translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This opening statement, known as the Bismillah, is a declaration of faith in the one true God, Allah, who is described as the Most Gracious and the Most Merciful. It serves as an invocation to seek Allah's blessings and guidance throughout the recitation of the Qur'an and the performance of any act. The Bismillah reminds believers of Allah's infinite mercy and compassion, and encourages them to approach all matters with a spirit of humility, reverence, and reliance on the divine.
orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

translation: All praise is [due] to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse expresses gratitude and praise to Allah, the Creator and Sustainer of the entire universe. It acknowledges that all good and blessings come from Allah, and that He alone is worthy of worship and praise. This verse sets the tone for the Qur'an, establishing Allah's sovereignty and the need for human beings to submit to Him with humility and appreciation.
orig: الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
interpretation: This verse establishes the fundamental attributes of Allah - that He is the Most Gracious, showering His creation with boundless mercy and compassion, and the Most Merciful, forgiving and overlooking the shortcomings of His servants. It sets the tone for the entire Quran, reminding us that the message it contains is rooted in the infinite mercy and benevolence of the Divine.
orig: الرحمن الرحيم

translation: Master of the Day of Recompense
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah as the sole Sovereign and Judge on the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions in this life. It emphasizes that Allah alone has the power and authority to determine the fate of every individual on that momentous day, and that no one else can influence or interfere with His judgment.
orig: مالك يوم الدين

translation: You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the core of Islamic belief - worshipping and seeking help from God alone, without associating any partners with Him. It reflects the fundamental tenet of monotheism (tawhid) in Islam, which is the belief in the oneness and sovereignty of God. The verse teaches Muslims to direct all their devotion, obedience, and reliance towards Allah, the Almighty, and to reject any form of polytheism or idolatry.
orig: إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين

translation: Guide us to the straight path
interpretation: This verse is a supplication, asking Allah (God) to guide us to the right and righteous path. The "straight path" refers to the path of truth, justice, and virtue - the path that leads to Allah's pleasure and eternal success in the Hereafter. This verse emphasizes the human need for divine guidance, as we cannot find the right way on our own. It reflects our humility and dependence on Allah to show us the way to live a life pleasing to Him.
orig: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم

translation: The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the straight path that leads to the pleasure of Allah. It describes the characteristics of those who are on this path - they are the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed His favor, not those who have incurred His anger or gone astray. The interpretation is that one should strive to follow the path of the righteous, the guided ones, and avoid the path of those who have deviated from the truth and earned Allah's displeasure.
orig: صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These are the opening letters of the Qur'an, known as the "Muqatta'at" or "Isolated Letters". Their exact meaning and significance have been the subject of much scholarly debate, but they are generally understood to be a way of emphasizing the divine and miraculous nature of the Qur'an, and to signify the depth and complexity of its message.
orig: الم

translation: This is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guidance for those conscious of Allah.
interpretation: This verse affirms the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, which is a book of guidance for those who are righteous and God-conscious. It emphasizes the certainty and reliability of the Qur'an, which is free from any doubt or ambiguity, and serves as a source of guidance for those who seek to live in a way that pleases Allah.
orig: ذلك الكتاب لا ريب فيه هدى للمتقين

translation: Those who believe in the unseen and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith in the unseen, maintaining a spiritual connection through prayer, and being charitable with one's wealth. It suggests that true believers are those who trust in God's guidance despite not being able to see it, who devote themselves to worship, and who contribute to the welfare of others using the resources God has bestowed upon them.
orig: الذين يؤمنون بالغيب ويقيمون الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And those who believe in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you, and of the Hereafter they are certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of believing in the divine revelations sent down to the Prophet Muhammad, as well as the previous prophets and scriptures. It also highlights the certainty of belief in the Hereafter, which is a core tenet of Islamic faith. The verse encourages steadfastness in faith and a holistic approach to religious belief.
orig: والذين يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك وبالآخرة هم يوقنون

translation: Those are upon [right] guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who follow the guidance and teachings of their Lord will be successful and prosperous in this life and the hereafter. It emphasizes that the path of righteousness and submission to God's will is the way to true and lasting fulfillment.
orig: أولئك على هدى من ربهم وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have rejected faith in God and chosen disbelief will not be affected by whether they are warned or not. Their hearts are sealed, and they will not believe regardless of the efforts made to guide them. The verse highlights the reality that faith is a matter of the heart, and no external force can compel someone to believe if they have already made the choice to reject the truth.
orig: إن الذين كفروا سواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their vision is a veil. And for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of those who have persistently rejected faith and closed their hearts and minds to the truth. The "seal" on their hearts and senses represents a spiritual blindness and deafness that prevents them from perceiving and accepting the divine guidance. This willful rejection of faith leads to a "great punishment" in the Hereafter.
orig: ختم الله على قلوبهم وعلى سمعهم وعلى أبصارهم غشاوة ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: And of the people are some who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of some people who claim to be believers in Allah and the Hereafter, but their actions and beliefs do not align with true faith. They may outwardly profess belief, but their hearts and deeds do not reflect genuine faith. This verse serves as a warning against such superficial and insincere belief, and encourages believers to strive for a deeper and more authentic faith in Allah and the Hereafter.
orig: ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله وباليوم الآخر وما هم بمؤمنين

translation: They seek to deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive not except themselves and perceive (it) not.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against those who try to deceive Allah and the believers. They may think they are fooling others, but in reality, they are only deceiving themselves, as they are unaware of the consequences of their actions.
orig: يخادعون الله والذين آمنوا وما يخدعون إلا أنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: In their hearts is disease, so Allah has increased their disease; and for them is a painful punishment because they [habitually] used to lie.
interpretation: This verse refers to those whose hearts are filled with doubts, hypocrisy and insincerity towards their faith. As a result, Allah increases their spiritual disease, leading them further away from the truth. They will face a severe punishment for their persistent rejection of the divine message and their deceitful ways.
orig: في قلوبهم مرض فزادهم الله مرضا ولهم عذاب أليم بما كانوا يكذبون

translation: And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are but reformers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and self-deception of those who claim to be reformers, but in reality, their actions lead to corruption and destruction. They refuse to acknowledge their wrongdoing and instead justify their actions, believing themselves to be righteous and beneficial to society. This verse serves as a warning against such misguided individuals who prioritize their own interests over the well-being of the community and the environment.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم لا تفسدوا في الأرض قالوا إنما نحن مصلحون

translation: Unquestionably, it is they who are the corrupters, but they perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who engage in corruption and mischief are unaware of their own wrongdoing. They are blind to the negative impact of their actions on society and do not realize that they are the true source of corruption, despite their own perception of themselves as upright individuals.
orig: ألا إنهم هم المفسدون ولكن لا يشعرون

translation: And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people have believed," they say, "Should we believe as the foolish have believed?" Unquestionably, it is they who are the foolish, but they do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and close-mindedness of those who reject faith, as they look down on the beliefs of others and consider themselves superior. The interpretation is that true wisdom lies in humility and openness to the guidance of faith, rather than in the conceit of those who think themselves wise but are in fact foolish and ignorant.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم آمنوا كما آمن الناس قالوا أنؤمن كما آمن السفهاء ألا إنهم هم السفهاء ولكن لا يعلمون

translation: And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their evil ones, they say, "Indeed, we are with you; we were only mockers."
interpretation: This verse describes the hypocrites who pretend to believe in public but secretly mock the faith and associate with those who oppose it. The interpretation is that true faith requires sincerity and consistency, not just outward displays of belief.
orig: وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم قالوا إنا معكم إنما نحن مستهزئون

translation: Allah mocks them and prolongs their transgression; they wander blindly.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah punishes those who persist in their arrogance and disbelief by allowing them to continue in their misguided ways, further increasing their deviation from the truth. Their blindness to the guidance of Allah is a consequence of their own stubborn refusal to accept the truth.
orig: الله يستهزئ بهم ويمدهم في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: Those are the ones who have exchanged guidance for error, and their transaction has brought no profit, nor were they [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who knowingly reject the truth and guidance of God, and instead choose to follow the path of error and misguidance. Their actions are likened to a fruitless business transaction, where they have traded away the valuable guidance of God for the worthless pursuit of falsehood. This highlights the futility and foolishness of such a choice, as they have gained nothing of value and remain lost and unguided.
orig: أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى فما ربحت تجارتهم وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: Their example is like that of one who kindled a fire, but when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness [so] they could not see.
interpretation: This verse is a metaphor describing the fate of those who reject faith and guidance. Just as a fire initially illuminates its surroundings but then is extinguished, leaving the person in darkness, those who reject faith will be deprived of the light of guidance and left in the darkness of misguidance, unable to see the truth.
orig: مثلهم كمثل الذي استوقد نارا فلما أضاءت ما حوله ذهب الله بنورهم وتركهم في ظلمات لا يبصرون

translation: Deaf, dumb and blind - so they will not return [to the right path].
interpretation: This verse describes those who are willfully ignorant and refuse to accept the guidance of Allah. They are spiritually deaf, mute, and blind, and thus unable to comprehend the truth and turn back to the right path.
orig: صم بكم عمي فهم لا يرجعون

translation: Or [it is] like a rainstorm from the sky within which is darkness, thunder and lightning. They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps in dread of death. And Allah is encompassing of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse draws a powerful analogy to illustrate the state of those who reject faith. Just as people instinctively try to shield themselves from the dangers of a violent thunderstorm, those who disbelieve in God try to shut out the truth of His message, out of fear of the consequences of their actions. However, Allah's power and knowledge encompasses all, even the disbelievers, leaving them with no escape.
orig: أو كصيب من السماء فيه ظلمات ورعد وبرق يجعلون أصابعهم في آذانهم من الصواعق حذر الموت والله محيط بالكافرين

translation: The lightning almost snatches away their sight; whenever it [gives] light to them, they walk therein; but when darkness comes over them, they stand [still]. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse describes the fleeting and transient nature of human perception and understanding. Just as lightning flashes briefly and then disappears, our ability to comprehend the signs of Allah is often limited and temporary. We may be able to see and understand certain truths when they are made clear to us, but when darkness returns, we are left uncertain and unable to proceed. This highlights our dependence on Allah and the fact that He alone has the power to grant us true and lasting insight. The verse reminds us to remain humble and to seek guidance from Allah, who is all-powerful and all-knowing.
orig: يكاد البرق يخطف أبصارهم كلما أضاء لهم مشوا فيه وإذا أظلم عليهم قاموا ولو شاء الله لذهب بسمعهم وأبصارهم إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse calls upon all of humanity to worship and submit to the One true God, the Creator of all things. It emphasizes that the purpose of our creation is to live a righteous life in devotion to God, following the guidance and example of those who came before us. The ultimate goal is to attain God-consciousness and piety, which will lead to salvation and eternal felicity.
orig: يا أيها الناس اعبدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم والذين من قبلكم لعلكم تتقون

translation: It is He who made the earth a bed [spread out] for you and the sky a ceiling and sent down from the sky, rain and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not attribute to Allah equals while you know [that there is nothing similar to Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the blessings and provisions that Allah has bestowed upon us, such as the earth as a comfortable place to live, the sky as a protective canopy, and the rain that brings forth fruits and sustenance. The interpretation is that we should be grateful to Allah for these blessings and not associate partners with Him, as He is the sole Creator and Provider.
orig: الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا والسماء بناء وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرج به من الثمرات رزقا لكم فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا وأنتم تعلمون

translation: And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our Servant [Muhammad], then produce a surah the like thereof and call upon your witnesses other than Allah, if you should be truthful.
interpretation: This verse challenges those who doubt the divine origin of the Qur'an to produce a single chapter (surah) that is comparable to it. The Qur'an is presented as a miraculous text that cannot be replicated by human beings, thus affirming its divine authorship. The verse invites skeptics to seek the help of their "witnesses" (i.e., deities or authorities) other than Allah, but emphasizes that they will not be able to produce anything like the Qur'an if they are truthful in their doubts.
orig: وإن كنتم في ريب مما نزلنا على عبدنا فأتوا بسورة من مثله وادعوا شهداءكم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And if you do not do it - and you [i.e., people] will never be able to do it - then fear the Fire, whose fuel is people and stones, prepared for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fearing and avoiding the punishment of the Hellfire, which is prepared for those who reject faith in God and His teachings. It suggests that even if one is unable to fulfill a certain obligation, they should still strive to avoid the consequences of disbelief and disobedience.
orig: فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا فاتقوا النار التي وقودها الناس والحجارة أعدت للكافرين

translation: And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens [in Paradise] beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with a provision of fruit therefrom, they will say, "This is what we were provided with before." And it is given to them in likeness. And they will have therein purified spouses, and they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse promises a blissful afterlife for those who believe in God and do good deeds. The gardens with flowing rivers symbolize the peace, abundance, and eternal life that awaits the righteous in the hereafter. The familiarity of the fruits they receive in Paradise suggests a continuity between this life and the next, where the blessings they enjoy are a fulfillment of their righteous aspirations in this world. The purified spouses and eternal abode further emphasize the perfection and permanence of the reward for the faithful.
orig: وبشر الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أن لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار كلما رزقوا منها من ثمرة رزقا قالوا هذا الذي رزقنا من قبل وأتوا به متشابها ولهم فيها أزواج مطهرة وهم فيها خالدون

translation: Indeed, Allah is not timid to present an example - that of a mosquito or what is smaller than it. And those who have believed know that it is the truth from their Lord. But as for those who disbelieve, they say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And none will know the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And this [i.e., the Qur'an] is not but a reminder to mankind.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Almighty, is not hesitant to use even the smallest of examples, such as a mosquito, to convey profound truths. It highlights the contrasting responses of the believers and the disbelievers. The believers recognize the wisdom and truth in Allah's examples, while the disbelievers question and reject them, leading to their own misguidance. This verse reminds us that Allah's guidance is a mercy, and it is He alone who decides whom to guide and whom to leave astray based on their own choices and dispositions.
orig: إن الله لا يستحيي أن يضرب مثلا ما بعوضة فما فوقها فأما الذين آمنوا فيعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم وأما الذين كفروا فيقولون ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا يضل به كثيرا ويهدي به كثيرا وما يضل به إلا الفاسقين

translation: Those who break the covenant of Allah after contracting it and sever that of which Allah has ordered to be joined and spread corruption on earth - it is those who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who break their promises and covenants with Allah, and who sever the ties and relationships that Allah has commanded to be maintained. They are the ones who spread corruption and disorder on the earth, and they will be the ultimate losers in the Hereafter.
orig: الذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه ويقطعون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life? Then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you [back] to life, and then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and sovereignty of Allah, the Creator, who has the ability to give life and cause death. It questions how one can deny the existence of Allah when they have experienced this cycle of life, death, and resurrection. The verse serves as a reminder that all people will ultimately return to Allah for judgment, and that denying His existence is illogical given the clear signs of His power in the cycle of life.
orig: كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: It is He who created for you all that is in the earth. Then He directed Himself to the heaven, [His being above all creation], and made them seven heavens, and He is of all things Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and knowledge as the sole Creator of the universe. He created everything on earth for the benefit of humanity, and then established Himself as the sovereign ruler over the seven heavens. This highlights God's absolute authority and omniscience, as He has perfect knowledge and control over all things.
orig: هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا ثم استوى إلى السماء فسواهن سبع سماوات وهو بكل شيء عليم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority." They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption in it and sheds blood, while we declare Your praise and sanctify You?" [Allah] said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know."
interpretation: This verse describes a dialogue between God and the angels regarding the creation of a human being as a 'khalifah' or successor on earth. The angels express concerns about the potential for corruption and bloodshed by this new creation, but God assures them that He knows what they do not. This highlights God's wisdom and the limitations of the angels' knowledge, as He alone knows the purpose behind creating humanity on earth.
orig: وإذ قال ربك للملائكة إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة قالوا أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك قال إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون

translation: And He taught Adam the names - all of them. Then He showed them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the unique status of Adam (peace be upon him) among God's creation. Allah (SWT) endowed Adam with the knowledge of the names of all things, demonstrating his superiority over the angels. This knowledge is a sign of the honor and trust bestowed upon Adam, and it underscores the responsibility he has to use this knowledge in a way that pleases his Creator.
orig: وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها ثم عرضهم على الملائكة فقال أنبئوني بأسماء هؤلاء إن كنتم صادقين

translation: They said, "Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, it is You who is the Knowing, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse expresses the humility and acknowledgment of the limited knowledge of the servants of Allah in comparison to His infinite knowledge and wisdom. It highlights that true wisdom and understanding can only come from Allah, the All-Knowing and the All-Wise, and that we as human beings should submit to His guidance and not claim to have knowledge beyond what He has taught us.
orig: قالوا سبحانك لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا إنك أنت العليم الحكيم

translation: He said, 'O Adam, inform them of their names.' And when he had informed them of their names, [Allah] said, 'Did I not tell you that I know the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth? And I know what you reveal and what you have concealed.'
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's omniscience and the limited knowledge of human beings. When Allah commanded Adam to inform the angels of the names of things, it demonstrated that Allah had endowed Adam with a special knowledge that the angels did not possess. This serves to establish Allah's superiority and the fact that He alone has complete and perfect knowledge of all things, both visible and invisible. The verse emphasizes that Allah is aware of all that is revealed and all that is concealed, reinforcing the idea that He is the All-Knowing, All-Seeing, and All-Wise.
orig: قال يا آدم أنبئهم بأسمائهم فلما أنبأهم بأسمائهم قال ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم غيب السماوات والأرض وأعلم ما تبدون وما كنتم تكتمون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except for Iblis. He refused and was arrogant and became of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disobedience and arrogance of Iblis (Satan) when he refused to prostrate before Adam, despite the command given by Allah. It emphasizes that Iblis, due to his pride and rejection of Allah's order, became a disbeliever and was excluded from the ranks of the angels.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس أبى واستكبر وكان من الكافرين

translation: And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat therefrom in [ease and] abundance from wherever you will. But do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse instructs Adam and his wife to reside in Paradise and enjoy its abundance, but warns them not to approach a particular tree, lest they become among the wrongdoers. This highlights the importance of obeying God's commands and avoiding that which is prohibited, in order to maintain a state of righteousness and avoid falling into sin.
orig: وقلنا يا آدم اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة وكلا منها رغدا حيث شئتما ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة فتكونا من الظالمين

translation: But Satan caused them to slip out of it and removed them from that [condition] in which they had been. And We said, "Go down, with hatred toward one another. And for you on the earth is a place of settlement and provision for a time."
interpretation: This verse describes how Satan tempted Adam and Eve, causing them to disobey God and be removed from the Garden of Eden. It then states that God commanded them to descend to Earth, where they would live in opposition to one another, but with the provision of sustenance for a limited time.
orig: فأزلهما الشيطان عنها فأخرجهما مما كانا فيه وقلنا اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين

translation: And Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse refers to Adam being forgiven by Allah after his initial disobedience. It highlights Allah's compassion and willingness to accept repentance from those who sincerely turn back to Him, even after committing mistakes. The interpretation is that Allah is the All-Forgiving and the Most Merciful, and that sincere repentance can lead to forgiveness and restoration of one's relationship with the Divine.
orig: فتلقى آدم من ربه كلمات فتاب عليه إنه هو التواب الرحيم

translation: We said, "Descend, with enmity between yourselves. And if there should come to you guidance from Me - then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray [in the world] nor suffer [in the Hereafter]."
interpretation: This verse is instructing mankind to descend from the elevated state they were in, with enmity and discord among them. However, if they follow the guidance that comes from God, they will be protected from going astray in this world and from suffering in the Hereafter. The interpretation emphasizes that those who follow God's guidance will be safe and secure, free from fear and grief.
orig: قلنا اهبطوا منها جميعا فإما يأتينكم مني هدى فمن تبع هداي فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith in God and deny the truth of the Qur"anic revelations will be condemned to the eternal punishment of the Hellfire. It highlights the grave consequences of disbelief and rejection of God"s guidance.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: O Children of Israel! Remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and fulfill (your obligations to) My covenant (with you), so that I fulfill (My obligations to) your covenant (with Me), and fear [only] Me.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the Children of Israel to remember the blessings and favors that God has bestowed upon them, and to fulfill their covenant with God. In return, God will fulfill His covenant with them and they should fear only Him. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of gratitude, fulfilling one's obligations, and having a reverent fear of God.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم وإياي فارهبون

translation: And believe in what I have sent down, confirming that which is [already] with you, and be not the first to disbelieve in it. And do not exchange My verses for a small price, and fear [only] Me.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have faith in the revelations of the Qur"an, which confirm and validate the previous scriptures. It warns against being the first to reject the Qur"an and cautions against trading the verses of Allah for worldly gains. The central message is to revere and fear Allah alone.
orig: وآمنوا بما أنزلت مصدقا لما معكم ولا تكونوا أول كافر به ولا تشتروا بآياتي ثمنا قليلا وإياي فاتقون

translation: And do not mix the truth with falsehood or conceal the truth while you know [it].
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to be truthful and transparent, and not to obscure or hide the truth. It emphasizes the importance of upholding honesty and integrity, and avoiding any deception or falsehood, even if it might seem advantageous in the short term. The verse highlights the moral obligation to speak the truth and not to conceal it, even when it may be difficult or inconvenient to do so.
orig: ولا تلبسوا الحق بالباطل وتكتموا الحق وأنتم تعلمون

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah and bow with those who bow [in worship].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling the core religious obligations of performing the ritual prayer, paying the obligatory charity (zakah), and joining the community of believers in acts of worship and submission to God.
orig: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة واركعوا مع الراكعين

translation: Do you order righteousness of the people and forget yourselves while you recite the Scripture? Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who preach righteousness and morality to others, but fail to apply the same standards to themselves. It highlights the hypocrisy of those who recite the Scriptures but do not practice what they preach. The verse encourages self-reflection and calls upon people to apply the same principles they demand of others to their own lives.
orig: أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم وأنتم تتلون الكتاب أفلا تعقلون

translation: And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is difficult except for the humble [before Allah]
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to seek help and strength through patience and prayer, as these are powerful tools to overcome challenges. However, it acknowledges that being steadfast and humble before Allah is not easy, and requires sincere devotion and submission to Him.
orig: واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة وإنها لكبيرة إلا على الخاشعين

translation: Those who think that they will meet their Lord and that they will return to Him.
interpretation: This verse refers to believers who have faith in the afterlife and the Day of Judgment, when they will stand before God and be held accountable for their actions. The interpretation is that these people have a strong conviction that they will ultimately return to their Lord and face the consequences of their deeds in this life.
orig: الذين يظنون أنهم ملاقو ربهم وأنهم إليه راجعون

translation: O Children of Israel! Remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds
interpretation: This verse calls upon the Children of Israel to remember the blessings and favors that God has bestowed upon them, and to acknowledge that God has chosen and elevated them above all other peoples. It is a reminder to be grateful for God's grace and to live up to the responsibilities that come with this privileged status.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأني فضلتكم على العالمين

translation: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it, nor will they be aided.
interpretation: This verse warns about the Day of Judgment, when each person will be held accountable for their own actions and no one will be able to help or intercede for another. On that day, no amount of wealth, power or influence will be able to save a person from the consequences of their deeds. The only thing that will matter is one's own righteous conduct and submission to God.
orig: واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ولا يقبل منها شفاعة ولا يؤخذ منها عدل ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst torment - killing your [newborn] sons and keeping your females alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers of God's deliverance of the Israelites from the oppression of Pharaoh and his people. It highlights the severe persecution they faced, with the killing of their male children and the subjugation of their women. This was a great trial from God, testing the faith and patience of the Israelites, but ultimately leading to their liberation and the downfall of the tyrants.
orig: وإذ نجيناكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب يذبحون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We parted the sea for you and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power and His deliverance of the Israelites from the oppression of Pharaoh. It reminds us that God can intervene in the course of events to save the righteous and punish the wicked, even in the most extraordinary circumstances. The verse encourages believers to have faith in God's ability to help them, even when they are facing seemingly insurmountable challenges.
orig: وإذ فرقنا بكم البحر فأنجيناكم وأغرقنا آل فرعون وأنتم تنظرون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We made an appointment with Moses for forty nights. Then you took [for worship] the calf after him, while you were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the incident when God appointed Moses for a period of forty nights to receive the Commandments, during which the Israelites worshipped the golden calf in his absence. The verse emphasizes that the people were wrongdoers for abandoning their faith and turning to idolatry, despite the clear guidance they had received from God through Moses.
orig: وإذ واعدنا موسى أربعين ليلة ثم اتخذتم العجل من بعده وأنتم ظالمون

translation: Then We forgave you after that so that you might be grateful.
interpretation: This verse suggests that after the believers had committed a sin or transgression, Allah forgave them, so that they may express gratitude and appreciation for His mercy and forgiveness.
orig: ثم عفونا عنكم من بعد ذلك لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We gave Moses the Scripture and criterion that perhaps you would be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an, like the previous scripture given to Moses, is a guide and criterion for distinguishing between truth and falsehood. It is revealed so that people may be rightly guided and find the path to salvation.
orig: وإذ آتينا موسى الكتاب والفرقان لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Moses said to his people, "O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf [for worship]. So repent to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is best for you in the sight of your Creator." And He accepted your repentance; indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of repentance and taking responsibility for one's actions. When the Israelites worshipped the golden calf, Moses admonished them for wronging themselves. He instructed them to repent and even to go so far as to kill themselves, emphasizing the gravity of their sin. However, God ultimately accepted their repentance, demonstrating His mercy and willingness to forgive those who sincerely turn back to Him. The verse underscores that true repentance is the best course of action, as it leads to God's acceptance and forgiveness.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم إنكم ظلمتم أنفسكم باتخاذكم العجل فتوبوا إلى بارئكم فاقتلوا أنفسكم ذلكم خير لكم عند بارئكم فتاب عليكم إنه هو التواب الرحيم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when you said, 'O Moses, we will not believe you until we see Allah outright,' so the thunderbolt took you while you were looking on.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the people of the past who demanded to see Allah directly, despite being warned that it would not be possible. Their demand led to their destruction by the thunderbolt, as they witnessed the power and might of Allah. This serves as a lesson that one should not make unreasonable demands of Allah, and should instead have faith and trust in Him.
orig: وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة فأخذتكم الصاعقة وأنتم تنظرون

translation: Then We revived you after your death, that you might be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the resurrection and the afterlife, reminding people that they will be brought back to life after death so that they may show gratitude to God for His blessings and guidance.
orig: ثم بعثناكم من بعد موتكم لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And We shaded you with clouds and sent down to you manna and quails, [saying], "Eat from the good [things] with which We have provided you." And they wronged Us not, but they were [only] wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of God's blessings and care for the Israelites during their journey in the wilderness. Despite their ungrateful and rebellious behavior, God continued to provide for them and protect them. The interpretation is that even when we turn away from God, He still extends His mercy and sustenance to us. However, it is we who wrong ourselves by not recognizing and appreciating God's favors.
orig: وظللنا عليكم الغمام وأنزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم وما ظلمونا ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We said, "Enter this city [i.e., Jerusalem] and eat from it wherever you will in [ease and] abundance, and enter the gate bowing humbly and say, 'Relieve us of our burdens." - We will [then] forgive your sins for you, and We will increase the doers of good [in goodness and reward].
interpretation: This verse describes God's instructions to the Israelites to enter the holy city of Jerusalem, partake of its abundant provisions, and humbly submit to God through prayer and supplication. The key message is that obedience and humility before God will lead to the forgiveness of sins and an increase in divine blessings and rewards for the righteous.
orig: وإذ قلنا ادخلوا هذه القرية فكلوا منها حيث شئتم رغدا وادخلوا الباب سجدا وقولوا حطة نغفر لكم خطاياكم وسنزيد المحسنين

translation: So We substituted in place of the ones who wronged a better [i.e., different] word than that which had been said to them, and We sent down upon the wrongdoers a punishment from the sky because they were defiantly disobeying.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that befell those who rejected the message of the Prophets and persisted in their wrongdoing. It suggests that when people refuse to heed the divine guidance and continue in their sinful ways, Allah may substitute their words with a more severe punishment as a consequence of their defiant disobedience.
orig: فبدل الذين ظلموا قولا غير الذي قيل لهم فأنزلنا على الذين ظلموا رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Moses prayed for water for his people, so We said, "Strike with your staff the stone." And there gushed forth from it twelve springs, and each people knew its watering place. [Moses said], "Eat and drink from the provision of Allah, and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption."
interpretation: This verse describes a miraculous event during the time of Prophet Moses, where he struck a rock with his staff and twelve springs of water gushed forth, providing sustenance for his people. The interpretation is that Allah can provide for His people in times of need, and that they should be grateful for His provision and not engage in corruption or misuse of the resources He has granted them. The verse emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah and being responsible stewards of the earth and its resources.
orig: وإذ استسقى موسى لقومه فقلنا اضرب بعصاك الحجر فانفجرت منه اثنتا عشرة عينا قد علم كل أناس مشربهم كلوا واشربوا من رزق الله ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when you said, "O Moses, we will never be patient [enduring] of [living on] one [kind of] food. So call upon your Lord to bring forth for us from the earth its green herbs and its cucumbers and its garlic and its lentils and its onions." [Moses] said, "Would you exchange what is better for what is less? Go down [to Egypt] with [your] dignity insulted and needy, and you have [already] incurred wrath from your Lord." And they were covered with humiliation and poverty and returned with anger from Allah [upon them]. That was because they [repeatedly] disbelieved in the signs of Allah and killed the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and were [habitually] transgressing.
interpretation: This verse describes the Israelites complaining to Moses about the monotonous food they were given and demanding a variety of vegetables. Moses admonishes them for wanting to exchange the better sustenance they had been provided for something less desirable. The verse highlights the Israelites' ingratitude and disobedience, which led to their being humiliated and facing Allah's wrath. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of being content with what Allah provides and not demanding more than is good for us, lest we incur His displeasure.
orig: وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نصبر على طعام واحد فادع لنا ربك يخرج لنا مما تنبت الأرض من بقلها وقثائها وفومها وعدسها وبصلها قال أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير اهبطوا مصرا فإن لكم ما سألتم وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة وباءوا بغضب من الله ذلك بأنهم كانوا يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون النبيين بغير الحق ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: Indeed, those who believe and those who are Jews and the Christians and the Sabeans - whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteousness - will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the path to salvation is not limited to any one religious tradition, but is open to all who have faith in God and the Afterlife, and who live righteously. It conveys a message of inclusivity, highlighting that God's mercy and reward are available to believers from diverse religious backgrounds, as long as they have faith and do good deeds. The verse offers reassurance that those who fulfill these conditions will be free from fear and sorrow in the Hereafter.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والنصارى والصابئين من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وعمل صالحا فلهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We took your covenant and raised over you the mount, [saying], "Take what We have given you with determination and remember what is in it that you might fear Allah."
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers to adhere to the covenant they made with God and to follow the teachings of the Qur'an with determination. The "mount" refers to Mount Sinai, where God spoke to Moses and the Israelites, emphasizing the gravity and importance of the covenant. The interpretation is that believers should strive to fulfill their obligations to God, remember the guidance in the Qur'an, and live in a way that demonstrates their fear and reverence of God.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم ورفعنا فوقكم الطور خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واذكروا ما فيه لعلكم تتقون

translation: Then you turned away after that. If not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have been among the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and steadfastness in faith. Even after being guided by Allah, the people may still turn away from the path of righteousness. However, Allah's grace and mercy are always available to those who seek His guidance. Without this divine favor, the people would be among the losers, facing the consequences of their own actions. The verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to be grateful for Allah's blessings.
orig: ثم توليتم من بعد ذلك فلولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته لكنتم من الخاسرين

translation: And you had already known about those who transgressed among you concerning the Sabbath, and We said to them, 'Be apes, despised.'
interpretation: This verse refers to a group of people who violated the sanctity of the Sabbath, and as a result, were transformed into apes as a punishment. The interpretation suggests that those who transgress against the commandments of God and disregard their religious obligations will face divine retribution, which can manifest in the form of humiliation and degradation.
orig: ولقد علمتم الذين اعتدوا منكم في السبت فقلنا لهم كونوا قردة خاسئين

translation: And We made it a deterrent example for what is before it and what is to come and an admonition for the God-fearing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the punishment or consequence of wrongdoing serves as a deterrent and warning to both those who have committed the sin and those who may be tempted to do so in the future. It also serves as a lesson and reminder for the righteous to remain steadfast in their faith and avoid such transgressions.
orig: فجعلناها نكالا لما بين يديها وما خلفها وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Moses said to his people, 'Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow.' They said, 'Do you take us in ridicule?' He said, 'I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the dialogue between Moses and his people regarding the command from Allah to slaughter a cow. The people initially reacted with skepticism and mockery, to which Moses responded by seeking refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant. This passage emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah's commands, even when they may seem unusual or difficult to comprehend, and the need to approach such matters with humility and reverence.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه إن الله يأمركم أن تذبحوا بقرة قالوا أتتخذنا هزوا قال أعوذ بالله أن أكون من الجاهلين

translation: They said, "Invoke for us your Lord to make clear to us what it is." [Moses] said, "[Allah] says, 'It is a cow which is neither old nor young, but medium [in age].' So do what you are commanded."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following Allah's commands without questioning or hesitation. When the Israelites asked Moses to clarify the details of the cow they were commanded to sacrifice, he simply relayed Allah's instructions to them without elaborating further. This teaches us to submit to Allah's will and execute His commands, even if we do not fully understand the wisdom behind them.
orig: قالوا ادع لنا ربك يبين لنا ما هي قال إنه يقول إنها بقرة لا فارض ولا بكر عوان بين ذلك فافعلوا ما تؤمرون

translation: They said, "Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what is its color." [Allah] said, "Indeed, He says it is a yellow cow, bright in color, pleasing to the observers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking clarity and understanding from God. The people asked Moses to pray to God to clarify the specific characteristics of the cow they were instructed to sacrifice, and God responded by providing a detailed description. This emphasizes that when we have questions or uncertainties, we should turn to God for guidance and seek to understand His instructions clearly.
orig: قالوا ادع لنا ربك يبين لنا ما لونها قال إنه يقول إنها بقرة صفراء فاقع لونها تسر الناظرين

translation: They said, "Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what it is." [As for] the cow, it bewilders us. And indeed, if Allah wills, we will be [rightly] guided.
interpretation: The people asked the Prophet to pray to God to clarify the details of the cow they were commanded to sacrifice, as the specifics were confusing to them. They expressed their trust that if God wills, they will follow the guidance provided.
orig: قالوا ادع لنا ربك يبين لنا ما هي إن البقر تشابه علينا وإنا إن شاء الله لمهتدون

translation: He said, "Indeed, he says it is a cow which is neither trained to plow the earth nor to water the crop, one free from fault, with no spot upon her." They said, "Now you have come with the truth." So they slaughtered her, though they were near to not doing it.
interpretation: This verse describes a dialogue between the Israelites and Prophet Moses regarding the sacrifice of a cow. The Israelites were commanded to sacrifice a cow, but they were reluctant to do so. Prophet Moses described the cow in detail, emphasizing that it was free from any defect or blemish. Upon hearing this, the Israelites acknowledged that Moses had spoken the truth, and they proceeded to sacrifice the cow. The interpretation suggests that the Israelites were initially hesitant to follow the divine command, but ultimately they complied with it after being convinced of its validity.
orig: قال إنه يقول إنها بقرة لا ذلول تثير الأرض ولا تسقي الحرث مسلمة لا شية فيها قالوا الآن جئت بالحق فذبحوها وما كادوا يفعلون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when you killed a man and disputed about it, but Allah was to bring out that which you were concealing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being truthful and transparent, even in difficult situations. It suggests that Allah is aware of all that we try to conceal and will ultimately bring it to light. The verse encourages us to be honest and accountable for our actions, rather than trying to cover them up.
orig: وإذ قتلتم نفسا فادارأتم فيها والله مخرج ما كنتم تكتمون

translation: And We said, 'Strike him with part of it.' Thus does Allah bring the dead to life, and He shows you His signs that you might reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has the power to bring the dead back to life, and that He shows His signs to humanity so that they may reflect and understand the truth.
orig: فقلنا اضربوه ببعضها كذلك يحيي الله الموتى ويريكم آياته لعلكم تعقلون

translation: Then your hearts became hardened after that, being like stones or even harder. For indeed, there are stones from which rivers burst forth, and there are some of them that split open and water comes out of them. And there are some of them that fall down for fear of Allah. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the hardening of the hearts of people after they have been exposed to the guidance of Allah. The hearts become like stones, or even harder, unable to be softened by the truth. However, the verse also highlights that there are some stones that can be sources of life-giving water, just as there are some hearts that can be softened by the fear of Allah. The verse serves as a warning to the people to not let their hearts become hardened, and to remain receptive to the guidance of Allah, who is ever-watchful of their actions.
orig: ثم قست قلوبكم من بعد ذلك فهي كالحجارة أو أشد قسوة وإن من الحجارة لما يتفجر منه الأنهار وإن منها لما يشقق فيخرج منه الماء وإن منها لما يهبط من خشية الله وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: Do you then hope that they would believe in you, and a party of them used to hear the Word of Allah [the Qur'an], then they used to change it [i.e. the Word of Allah] knowingly after they had understood it?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the notion that the disbelievers would accept faith, despite the fact that some of them had heard the Word of Allah [the Qur'an] and then knowingly distorted it after understanding it. The implication is that their rejection of faith is not due to lack of knowledge or understanding, but rather a willful decision to turn away from the truth.
orig: أفتطمعون أن يؤمنوا لكم وقد كان فريق منهم يسمعون كلام الله ثم يحرفونه من بعد ما عقلوه وهم يعلمون

translation: And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We have believed." But when they are alone with their evil ones, they say, "Indeed, we are with you; we were only mockers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to believe but do not truly have faith in their hearts. They outwardly profess belief when in the company of believers, but when alone with their associates, they admit to only mocking the faith. This verse encourages believers to scrutinize the sincerity of those who claim to share their beliefs, and to rely on the true substance of faith rather than outward displays.
orig: وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا قالوا آمنا وإذا خلا بعضهم إلى بعض قالوا أتحدثونهم بما فتح الله عليكم ليحاجوكم به عند ربكم أفلا تعقلون

translation: Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Almighty, is all-knowing and has complete knowledge of everything, both what people keep hidden and what they openly express. It serves as a reminder that we cannot hide anything from Allah, and that He is aware of our thoughts, intentions, and actions, whether they are kept secret or made public.
orig: أولا يعلمون أن الله يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون

translation: And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Scripture except in wishful thinking, and they do not but guess.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who claim knowledge of the Scripture without having truly studied and understood it. They rely on hearsay and conjecture rather than on genuine understanding. This highlights the importance of seeking authentic knowledge and not being content with superficial or baseless beliefs.
orig: ومنهم أميون لا يعلمون الكتاب إلا أماني وإن هم إلا يظنون

translation: Woe to those who write the "Book" with their own hands and then say, "This is from Allah," to exchange it for a small price. Woe to them for what their hands have written and woe to them for what they earn.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who falsely attribute their own writings to divine revelation in order to gain a small worldly benefit. It warns them of the grave consequences of this deception, both for what they have written and the earnings they have acquired through this means. The verse emphasizes the gravity of misrepresenting one's own work as divine, and the severe punishment that awaits those who engage in such practices.
orig: فويل للذين يكتبون الكتاب بأيديهم ثم يقولون هذا من عند الله ليشتروا به ثمنا قليلا فويل لهم مما كتبت أيديهم وويل لهم مما يكسبون

translation: And they say, "Never will the Fire touch us except for [a few] numbered days." Say, "Have you taken a covenant with Allah? For Allah will never break His covenant. Or do you say about Allah that which you do not know?"
interpretation: This verse addresses the false belief held by some that they will only be punished in the Hellfire for a limited time, and that they will eventually be forgiven and admitted into Paradise. The verse refutes this notion, stating that Allah will never break His covenant or promise of eternal punishment for those who disbelieve. It also warns against making claims about Allah's judgement without proper knowledge, as that would be a grave sin.
orig: وقالوا لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودة قل أتخذتم عند الله عهدا فلن يخلف الله عهده أم تقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Nay, but whoever earns evil and his sin has surrounded him - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who commit sins and are engulfed by them will be condemned to the eternal punishment of Hell. It serves as a warning to the believers to abstain from wrongdoing and to seek forgiveness and repentance, as the consequences of persistent sinfulness are severe.
orig: بلى من كسب سيئة وأحاطت به خطيئته فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have faith in God and do good deeds will be rewarded with eternal life in Paradise. It highlights the importance of both belief and righteous action, as the two are inseparable in achieving salvation. The verse conveys the message that the true believers will be granted the ultimate reward of residing in Paradise forever.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We took the covenant from the Children of Israel, [enjoining upon them]: Do not worship except Allah; and to parents do good and to relatives, orphans, and the needy. And speak to people good [words] and establish prayer and give zakah." Then you turned away, [all] except a few of you, and you were refusing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping only Allah, being kind to one's parents and relatives, caring for the orphans and the needy, and speaking good words to people. It also highlights the obligation to establish prayer and give charity. The verse laments that the Children of Israel, despite being given this covenant, turned away from it, except for a few of them.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل لا تعبدون إلا الله وبالوالدين إحسانا وذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وقولوا للناس حسنا وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة ثم توليتم إلا قليلا منكم وأنتم معرضون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We took your covenant, [saying], "Do not shed each other's blood or evict one another from your homes." Then you acknowledged [this] while you were witnessing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting human life and the sanctity of one's home. It reminds the believers of the covenant they made with God, to abstain from shedding each other's blood and forcibly removing one another from their homes. The verse underscores the gravity of this covenant, which the people acknowledged and witnessed, highlighting the need for them to uphold these principles in their lives.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم لا تسفكون دماءكم ولا تخرجون أنفسكم من دياركم ثم أقررتم وأنتم تشهدون

translation: Then, there you are - you [people] killing one another and evicting a party of your [own selves] from their homes, cooperating against them in sin and aggression. And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, although their eviction [of them] was forbidden to you. So do you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part? Then what is the recompense for those who do that among you except disgrace in worldly life; and on the Day of Resurrection they will be sent back to the severest of punishment. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse condemns the hypocritical behavior of the people, who on one hand claim to believe in the Quran, but on the other hand engage in acts of violence, oppression and injustice against their own people. The verse highlights the contradiction between professing faith and committing sinful acts, and warns that such behavior will lead to disgrace in this life and severe punishment in the Hereafter. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of living in accordance with the teachings of the Quran and not selectively believing in parts of it while rejecting others.
orig: ثم أنتم هؤلاء تقتلون أنفسكم وتخرجون فريقا منكم من ديارهم تظاهرون عليهم بالإثم والعدوان وإن يأتوكم أسارى تفادوهم وهو محرم عليكم إخراجهم أفتؤمنون ببعض الكتاب وتكفرون ببعض فما جزاء من يفعل ذلك منكم إلا خزي في الحياة الدنيا ويوم القيامة يردون إلى أشد العذاب وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: Those are the ones who have exchanged the Hereafter for the worldly life, so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be aided.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have prioritized the fleeting pleasures of this world over the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. They have made a poor trade, sacrificing their eternal salvation for the temporary gains of this life. As a result, they will face the full consequences of their choices, with no relief or assistance in the Hereafter.
orig: أولئك الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the Book and followed up after him with [a succession of] messengers. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Pure Spirit. [But] is it [not] that every time a messenger came to you, [O Children of Israel], with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant? And a party [of you] you denied, and another party you killed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the long history of God's guidance to humanity through a succession of messengers, including Moses and Jesus. It emphasizes that despite the clear signs and proofs brought by these messengers, the people often responded with arrogance and rejection, denying some messengers and even killing others. The verse serves as a reminder that true guidance requires humility and an openness to accept the truth, even when it may not align with one's desires.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب وقفينا من بعده بالرسل وآتينا عيسى ابن مريم البينات وأيدناه بروح القدس أفكلما جاءكم رسول بما لا تهوى أنفسكم استكبرتم ففريقا كذبتم وفريقا تقتلون

translation: And they say, "Our hearts are wrapped in coverings." But, [in fact], Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is it that they believe.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who make excuses for their rejection of faith, claiming that their hearts are "wrapped in coverings" and thus they are unable to understand the truth. However, the Qur'an states that it is Allah who has cursed them for their disbelief, and as a result, they have little faith.
orig: وقالوا قلوبنا غلف بل لعنهم الله بكفرهم فقليلا ما يؤمنون

translation: And when there came to them a Book from Allah confirming that which was with them - although before they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved - but [then] when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah will be upon the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who rejected the Qur'an despite recognizing its truth, despite previously praying for divine support against the disbelievers. It highlights the hypocrisy of those who refused to accept the new revelation from God, even though it confirmed the previous scriptures they possessed. The curse of God is upon those who stubbornly reject the truth out of arrogance or selfish motives, after it has been made clear to them.
orig: ولما جاءهم كتاب من عند الله مصدق لما معهم وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به فلعنة الله على الكافرين

translation: Wretched is that for which they have sold themselves - that they would disbelieve in what Allah has revealed through [their] outrage that Allah would send down His favor upon whom He wills from among His servants. So they have returned with anger [i.e., God's anger] upon anger, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who reject the revelations of Allah out of arrogance and envy, rather than accepting them with humility and gratitude. It warns that such rejection will incur the wrath of Allah, leading to a humiliating punishment for the disbelievers. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of submitting to Allah's will and guidance, and the consequences of turning away from it.
orig: بئسما اشتروا به أنفسهم أن يكفروا بما أنزل الله بغيا أن ينزل الله من فضله على من يشاء من عباده فباءوا بغضب على غضب وللكافرين عذاب مهين

translation: And when it is said to them, "Believe in what Allah has revealed," they say, "We believe [only] in what was revealed to us." And they disbelieve in what came after it, while it is the truth confirming that which is with them. Say, "Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were [indeed] believers?"
interpretation: This verse criticizes the hypocrisy of those who claim to believe, but only in what was revealed to them previously, and reject the new revelation that confirms the truth of what they already have. The verse challenges them by asking why they killed the prophets of Allah if they were truly believers, implying that their rejection of the new revelation is a sign of their lack of true faith.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم آمنوا بما أنزل الله قالوا نؤمن بما أنزل علينا ويكفرون بما وراءه وهو الحق مصدقا لما معهم قل فلم تقتلون أنبياء الله من قبل إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And Moses had certainly come to you with clear signs, then you took the calf [in worship] after that, while you were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that despite the clear signs and guidance provided by Moses, the people still turned to worshipping the calf, which was a grave injustice and deviation from the true path. It serves as a warning against succumbing to temptations and idolatry, even in the face of divine guidance.
orig: ولقد جاءكم موسى بالبينات ثم اتخذتم العجل من بعده وأنتم ظالمون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We took your covenant and raised over you the mount, [saying], "Take what We have given you with determination and listen." They said [instead], "We have heard and disobeyed." And their hearts absorbed [the worship of] the calf because of their disbelief. Say, "How wretched is that which your faith commands you, if you should [in fact] be believers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the disobedience and ingratitude of the Israelites, despite the covenant they made with God and the favors He bestowed upon them. They were commanded to accept the teachings of the Qur'an with determination and obedience, but they instead chose to rebel and worship the calf. This verse serves as a warning to believers to not follow in the footsteps of those who turned away from God's guidance, and to instead embrace faith wholeheartedly.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم ورفعنا فوقكم الطور خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واسمعوا قالوا سمعنا وعصينا وأشربوا في قلوبهم العجل بكفرهم قل بئسما يأمركم به إيمانكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: Say, "If the home of the Hereafter with Allah is for you alone and not the [other] people, then wish for death, if you are truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who claim that the Hereafter is exclusively for them and not for others. It calls on them to wish for death if they are truly sincere in their belief, as the Hereafter would then be theirs alone. The verse serves as a test of their conviction and highlights the importance of humility and inclusivity in one's faith.
orig: قل إن كانت لكم الدار الآخرة عند الله خالصة من دون الناس فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forth. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the wrongdoers will never desire death or the afterlife, because of their misdeeds in this life. They are fully aware of their sins and the consequences they will face, and Allah is all-knowing of their transgressions.
orig: ولن يتمنوه أبدا بما قدمت أيديهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: And you will surely find them the most greedy of people for life - [even] more than those who associate others with Allah. One of them wishes that he could be granted life a thousand years, but it would not remove him in the least from the [coming] punishment. And Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to cling to life and avoid death, even among those who associate partners with Allah. It emphasizes that no matter how much one may desire to live longer, it will not save them from the punishment they deserve for their misdeeds. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is all-knowing and sees everything we do, and that we will be held accountable for our actions in the Hereafter.
orig: ولتجدنهم أحرص الناس على حياة ومن الذين أشركوا يود أحدهم لو يعمر ألف سنة وما هو بمزحزحه من العذاب أن يعمر والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: Say, "Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - it is [none but] he who has brought the Qur'an down upon your heart, [O Muhammad], by permission of Allah, confirming that which was before it and as guidance and good tidings for the believers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) through the angel Gabriel, by the permission of Allah. The Qur'an is a confirmation of the previous scriptures and a guidance and good news for the believers. It refutes the notion of anyone being an enemy to Gabriel, who was the means of delivering the divine revelation.
orig: قل من كان عدوا لجبريل فإنه نزله على قلبك بإذن الله مصدقا لما بين يديه وهدى وبشرى للمؤمنين

translation: Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael - then indeed, Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are hostile and antagonistic towards Allah, His angels, His messengers, and the archangels Gabriel and Michael, will have Allah as their enemy. This is a clear warning to the disbelievers that their enmity towards the divine will be met with Allah's own enmity and opposition.
orig: من كان عدوا لله وملائكته ورسله وجبريل وميكال فإن الله عدو للكافرين

translation: And We have certainly sent down to you verses [which are] clear proofs, and no one will deny them except the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has revealed clear and unambiguous signs ("verses") to the Prophet Muhammad, and that only those who are rebellious and disobedient will reject these signs. It highlights the clarity and undeniability of the divine revelations, placing the responsibility for disbelief squarely on those who willfully turn away from the truth.
orig: ولقد أنزلنا إليك آيات بينات وما يكفر بها إلا الفاسقون

translation: And whenever they make a covenant, a party of them throws it away. Rather, most of them do not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the lack of sincerity and commitment among many people when it comes to upholding their promises and covenants. It suggests that even when agreements are made, a group of them will disregard and abandon them, and that most people do not truly believe in fulfilling their obligations.
orig: أوكلما عاهدوا عهدا نبذه فريق منهم بل أكثرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And when there came to them a Messenger from Allah, confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Scripture of Allah behind their backs as if they did not know [it].
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn rejection of some people towards the truth, even when it is presented to them clearly. When a Messenger from Allah came to them, confirming the previous scriptures they possessed, a group of them deliberately turned away from the message, disregarding the divine scripture as if they had no knowledge of it.
orig: ولما جاءهم رسول من عند الله مصدق لما معهم نبذ فريق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب كتاب الله وراء ظهورهم كأنهم لا يعلمون

translation: And they followed [instead] what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon. It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and that which was revealed to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut. But the two angels do not teach anyone unless they say, "We are a trial, so do not disbelieve [by practicing magic]." And [yet] they learn from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife. But they do not harm anyone through it except by permission of Allah . And the people learn what harms them and does not benefit them. But the Children of Israel certainly knew that whoever purchased the magic would not have in the Hereafter any share. And wretched is that for which they sold themselves, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse warns against the practice of magic, which is attributed to the devils during the reign of King Solomon, and to the two angels Harut and Marut in Babylon. The verse emphasizes that magic is a trial and temptation, and that those who learn it will not benefit in the Hereafter. It also highlights that magic can be used to cause separation between a husband and wife, but this can only be done with Allah's permission. The verse ultimately condemns the practice of magic as harmful and a rejection of the Hereafter.
orig: واتبعوا ما تتلو الشياطين على ملك سليمان وما كفر سليمان ولكن الشياطين كفروا يعلمون الناس السحر وما أنزل على الملكين ببابل هاروت وماروت وما يعلمان من أحد حتى يقولا إنما نحن فتنة فلا تكفر فيتعلمون منهما ما يفرقون به بين المرء وزوجه وما هم بضارين به من أحد إلا بإذن الله ويتعلمون ما يضرهم ولا ينفعهم ولقد علموا لمن اشتراه ما له في الآخرة من خلاق ولبئس ما شروا به أنفسهم لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And if they had believed and feared Allah, then the reward from Allah would have been [far] better, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that if the people had truly believed in God and lived righteously, the reward they would have received from God would have been far superior to anything they could have attained in this world. However, they lacked this knowledge and understanding, which prevented them from seeking the higher and more lasting rewards that come from faith and piety.
orig: ولو أنهم آمنوا واتقوا لمثوبة من عند الله خير لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: O you who believe! Do not say 'Ra'ina' but say 'Unthurna' and listen. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to be mindful of their speech and to avoid using certain words that could be misunderstood or misinterpreted. The word "Ra'ina" could be understood as an insult, so believers are told to instead use the word "Unthurna" which means "look at us" or "have consideration for us". The verse also emphasizes the importance of listening and being attentive, and warns that the disbelievers will face a painful punishment.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقولوا راعنا وقولوا انظرنا واسمعوا وللكافرين عذاب أليم

translation: Neither those who disbelieve from among the People of the Book nor the polytheists wish that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord. But Allah selects for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that neither the disbelievers among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) nor the polytheists wish for any good to be sent down to the believers from their Lord. However, Allah selects whomever He wills for His mercy, and He is the Possessor of great bounty. This highlights that the guidance and blessings of Allah are not limited to any particular group, but are bestowed upon those whom He chooses, regardless of their religious affiliation or background.
orig: ما يود الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب ولا المشركين أن ينزل عليكم من خير من ربكم والله يختص برحمته من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: And whatever We have repealed of a verse or caused to be forgotten, We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it. Do you not know that Allah is over all things competent?
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has the power to replace or abrogate previous verses of the Quran with new ones that are either better or similar in meaning. This reflects God's sovereignty and ability to guide humanity through progressive revelation, as He sees fit. The interpretation emphasizes that God's knowledge and power are absolute, and He alone determines the appropriate guidance for humanity at different times.
orig: ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها نأت بخير منها أو مثلها ألم تعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Did you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and [that] you have not besides Allah any protector or any helper?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone is the sovereign and supreme ruler of the heavens and the earth. It reminds us that we have no one to turn to for protection or assistance besides Allah, and that we should place our trust and reliance solely in Him.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Or do you wish to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before? And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has certainly gone astray from the soundness of the way.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against the desire to question the Prophet (peace be upon him) in the same manner that the Israelites questioned Prophet Moses (peace be upon him). It emphasizes that those who exchange faith for disbelief have strayed from the right path and gone astray.
orig: أم تريدون أن تسألوا رسولكم كما سئل موسى من قبل ومن يتبدل الكفر بالإيمان فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back to disbelief after you have believed, out of envy from themselves, [even] after the truth has become clear to them. So pardon and overlook until Allah delivers His command. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against the envy and resentment of the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who wish to turn the believers back to disbelief, even after the truth of Islam has been made clear to them. The believers are instructed to pardon and overlook the hostility of the People of the Book until Allah delivers His command, as Allah has power over all things.
orig: ود كثير من أهل الكتاب لو يردونكم من بعد إيمانكم كفارا حسدا من عند أنفسهم من بعد ما تبين لهم الحق فاعفوا واصفحوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره إن الله على كل شيء قدير
