translation: And establish prayer and give zakah, and whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of two core Islamic practices - performing regular prayer (salat) and giving charity (zakah). It also highlights that any good deeds we perform will be rewarded by Allah, as He is all-knowing and aware of our actions. The verse encourages us to be proactive in doing good and preparing for the afterlife, as the rewards will be found with Allah.
orig: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله إن الله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And they say, "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian." That is [merely] their wishful thinking. Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse addresses the claims made by some Jews and Christians that only those who follow their respective faiths will enter Paradise. The Qur'an refutes this notion, stating that it is merely their wishful thinking and not based on any divine revelation or solid evidence. The verse challenges them to provide proof for their exclusivist claims, if they are indeed truthful.
orig: وقالوا لن يدخل الجنة إلا من كان هودا أو نصارى تلك أمانيهم قل هاتوا برهانكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Nay, whoever submits his whole self to Allah and is a doer of good, he will get his reward with his Lord, and no fear will there be upon them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who truly submit to Allah and do good deeds will be rewarded by Allah, and they will be free from fear and grief. It encourages believers to sincerely devote themselves to Allah and do righteous actions, as this will lead to their salvation and well-being in the Hereafter.
orig: بلى من أسلم وجهه لله وهو محسن فله أجره عند ربه ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And the Jews say, "The Christians have nothing [true] to stand on," and the Christians say, "The Jews have nothing to stand on," although they [both] recite the Scripture. Thus do those who know not speak the same as their words. But Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the religious disputes and disagreements between the Jews and the Christians, despite the fact that they both claim to follow divine scriptures. The verse emphasizes that those who lack true knowledge often make similar claims against each other, but ultimately, it is Allah who will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection regarding the matters they differed upon.
orig: وقالت اليهود ليست النصارى على شيء وقالت النصارى ليست اليهود على شيء وهم يتلون الكتاب كذلك قال الذين لا يعلمون مثل قولهم فالله يحكم بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who prevents [the mention of] the name of Allah in His mosques and strives for their ruin? It is not for them to enter them except in fear. For them in this world is disgrace, and they will have in the Hereafter a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who prevent the remembrance of Allah in His mosques and work towards their destruction. Such people have no right to enter these places of worship except in a state of fear, as they will face disgrace in this world and a severe punishment in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the gravity of interfering with the sanctity of mosques and the worship of Allah.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه وسعى في خرابها أولئك ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين لهم في الدنيا خزي ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: And to Allah belong the east and the west. So wherever you [might] turn, there is the Face of Allah. Indeed, Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the Creator and Sustainer of the entire universe, and that His presence is everywhere. No matter which direction one turns, one will find Allah's presence, for He is all-encompassing and all-knowing. This serves to remind us of Allah's omnipresence and omniscience, and that we should always be conscious of His watchful gaze over us.
orig: ولله المشرق والمغرب فأينما تولوا فثم وجه الله إن الله واسع عليم

translation: And they say, "Allah has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him.
interpretation: This verse refutes the belief that Allah has taken a son. It affirms that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, and all are submissive and obedient to Him. The verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and oneness of Allah, and rejects the notion of Allah having a son or any partners.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الله ولدا سبحانه بل له ما في السماوات والأرض كل له قانتون

translation: The Originator of the heavens and the earth. And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and authority as the Creator of the universe. He is the One who originates and brings into existence the heavens and the earth, and when He wills something to happen, He merely commands it to "be" and it comes into existence immediately. This emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and the ease with which He can create and command the universe according to His will.
orig: بديع السماوات والأرض وإذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And those who do not know say, "Why does Allah not speak to us or there come to us a sign?" Thus spoke those before them like their words. Their hearts resemble each other. We have certainly made clear the signs for a people who are certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse addresses those who are skeptical about the divine origin of the Qur'an and the signs of Allah. It compares their attitude to that of previous generations who made similar demands for direct communication from God or miraculous signs. The verse suggests that their hearts are similar in their lack of certainty and openness to the clear signs and revelations that Allah has provided. The interpretation is that true faith requires a sincere and receptive heart, not the demand for extraordinary proofs.
orig: وقال الذين لا يعلمون لولا يكلمنا الله أو تأتينا آية كذلك قال الذين من قبلهم مثل قولهم تشابهت قلوبهم قد بينا الآيات لقوم يوقنون

translation: Indeed, We have sent you, [O Muhammad], with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and you will not be asked about the companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Prophet Muhammad was sent by God with the truth, to convey the message of Islam as a bearer of good news for those who believe and a warner for those who reject it. It also assures the Prophet that he will not be held accountable for the fate of those who reject the message and end up in Hell, as that is ultimately up to God to decide.
orig: إنا أرسلناك بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا ولا تسأل عن أصحاب الجحيم

translation: And the Jews and the Christians will never be pleased with you until you follow their religion. Say, "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance." And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would have against Allah no protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Jews and Christians will never be satisfied with the followers of Islam until they abandon their faith and adopt the beliefs of the Jews or Christians. The verse instructs the Prophet (peace be upon him) to declare that the true guidance is that which comes from Allah, not the desires or religions of others. It warns that if one were to follow the whims and desires of others after receiving the knowledge of the truth, they would have no one to protect or support them against Allah.
orig: ولن ترضى عنك اليهود ولا النصارى حتى تتبع ملتهم قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم بعد الذي جاءك من العلم ما لك من الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Those to whom We have given the Book, they recite it with the right recitation. They [are the ones who] believe in it. And whoever disbelieves in it - it is those who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reciting and believing in the divine scripture that has been revealed. Those who have been given the Book, referring to the Qur'an, are expected to recite it properly and with due reverence. This act of recitation with sincerity is a sign of true faith. In contrast, those who reject or disbelieve in the Qur'an are the ones who will suffer the consequences of their loss in the Hereafter.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يتلونه حق تلاوته أولئك يؤمنون به ومن يكفر به فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: O Children of Israel! Remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the Children of Israel to remember the blessings and favors that God has bestowed upon them, and to recognize that God has chosen them and preferred them over all other people. It is a reminder of their special status and the responsibility that comes with it.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأني فضلتكم على العالمين

translation: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all, and no compensation will be accepted from it, nor will any intercession benefit it, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being prepared for the Day of Judgement, when each person will be held accountable for their own actions. On that day, no one will be able to help or intercede for another, and no amount of wealth or status will be able to save a person from the consequences of their deeds. It reminds us to live our lives in a way that pleases Allah and prepares us for the ultimate reckoning.
orig: واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ولا يقبل منها عدل ولا تنفعها شفاعة ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham was tried by his Lord with commands and he fulfilled them [to perfection]. [Allah] said, "Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people." [Abraham] said, "And of my descendants?" [Allah] said, "My covenant does not include the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse describes a pivotal moment in the life of the Prophet Abraham, when he was tested by God with various commandments and he fulfilled them perfectly. In response, God promised to make Abraham a leader for all people. However, when Abraham asked if this promise would extend to his descendants, God clarified that His covenant does not include the wrongdoers. This highlights the importance of individual righteousness and that God's blessings are not automatically inherited, but must be earned through one's own actions and adherence to God's teachings.
orig: وإذ ابتلى إبراهيم ربه بكلمات فأتمهن قال إني جاعلك للناس إماما قال ومن ذريتي قال لا ينال عهدي الظالمين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We made the House a place of return for the people and [a place of] security. And take, [O believers], from the standing place of Abraham a place of prayer. And We charged Abraham and Ishmael, [saying], "Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who are staying [for worship] and those who bow and prostrate [in prayer]"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the House (the Kaaba) as a sacred place of worship and a sanctuary for the people. It instructs the believers to take the standing place of Abraham as a place of prayer, and charges Abraham and Ishmael to purify the House for those who perform Tawaf (circumambulation), stay for worship, and bow and prostrate in prayer. The verse highlights the sanctity of this holy site and the obligation of maintaining its purity for the devotion of the believers.
orig: وإذ جعلنا البيت مثابة للناس وأمنا واتخذوا من مقام إبراهيم مصلى وعهدنا إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل أن طهرا بيتي للطائفين والعاكفين والركع السجود

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide for its people from the fruits, [he who believes] in Allah and the Last Day." [Allah] said, "And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination."
interpretation: This verse highlights the prayer of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) for the city of Mecca to be a secure and prosperous place, where the believers in Allah and the Hereafter would be provided for. However, it also warns that those who disbelieve will be granted a temporary enjoyment, but will ultimately face the punishment of the Hellfire, which is a terrible destination. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith in Allah and the Hereafter, and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب اجعل هذا بلدا آمنا وارزق أهله من الثمرات من آمن منهم بالله واليوم الآخر قال ومن كفر فأمتعه قليلا ثم أضطره إلى عذاب النار وبئس المصير

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House and [with him] Ishmael, [saying], 'Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of Prophet Abraham and his son Ishmael in the construction of the Ka'bah, the sacred house of worship in Mecca. It shows their humility and devotion as they ask Allah to accept their efforts, acknowledging that He is the All-Hearing and All-Knowing. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's acceptance and guidance in all our endeavors.
orig: وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت وإسماعيل ربنا تقبل منا إنك أنت السميع العليم

translation: Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to Allah, the Almighty, requesting guidance and submission. The key elements are: 1) a plea for Allah to make the supplicant and their descendants devoted Muslims, 2) a request to be shown the proper rites and rituals of Islam, and 3) an acknowledgment of Allah's attribute as the Acceptor of repentance and the Merciful. The overall theme is a desire for individual and collective submission to Allah, along with a seeking of His guidance and forgiveness.
orig: ربنا واجعلنا مسلمين لك ومن ذريتنا أمة مسلمة لك وأرنا مناسكنا وتب علينا إنك أنت التواب الرحيم

translation: Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to Allah, the Almighty, to send a messenger from among the people to guide them. The messenger will recite the verses of the Qur'an, teach them the Book (the Qur'an) and wisdom, and purify them. This is a request for guidance and spiritual upliftment of the people, as Allah is the All-Mighty and the All-Wise.
orig: ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم يتلو عليهم آياتك ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة ويزكيهم إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: And who would be averse to the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself. And We had chosen him in this world, and indeed he, in the Hereafter, will be among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the religion of Abraham, which is the foundation of Islam. It suggests that anyone who rejects or turns away from this religion is only harming themselves and acting foolishly. The verse also highlights that God has chosen Abraham as a righteous person, and that he will be among the righteous in the Hereafter as well. This serves as a reminder to believers to emulate the example of Abraham and adhere to the principles of his faith.
orig: ومن يرغب عن ملة إبراهيم إلا من سفه نفسه ولقد اصطفيناه في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: When his Lord said to him, "Submit", he said, "I have submitted [in Islam] to the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse refers to the prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) and his submission to the will of God. It highlights the essence of Islam, which is the complete surrender and devotion to the One true God, the Lord of all creation. The verse emphasizes the importance of unconditional submission to the divine will, as exemplified by Abraham's response of willingly accepting God's command.
orig: إذ قال له ربه أسلم قال أسلمت لرب العالمين

translation: And this [religion of Islam] Abraham enjoined upon his sons and [so did] Jacob, [saying], "O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of submitting to the will of God (being a Muslim) until the end of one's life. It highlights how the prophets Abraham and Jacob passed on this belief to their children, underscoring the continuity of this divine message. The interpretation is that one should strive to maintain their faith in Allah and live as a true Muslim throughout their life.
orig: ووصى بها إبراهيم بنيه ويعقوب يا بني إن الله اصطفى لكم الدين فلا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون

translation: Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac - one God. And we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining the worship of the One True God, even after the passing of a prophet or religious leader. It highlights the continuity of monotheistic belief and submission to God (Islam) across generations, as exemplified by the response of Jacob's sons. The verse reinforces the unity of God and the obligation of all believers to worship Him alone.
orig: أم كنتم شهداء إذ حضر يعقوب الموت إذ قال لبنيه ما تعبدون من بعدي قالوا نعبد إلهك وإله آبائك إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق إلها واحدا ونحن له مسلمون

translation: That is a nation which has passed on. It will have [the consequence of] what it earned, and you will have what you have earned. And you will not be asked about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that each person is responsible for their own actions and will be held accountable for them. It suggests that we should not concern ourselves with the deeds of others, but rather focus on our own conduct and the consequences of our choices. The verse encourages us to take responsibility for our own actions and not to judge or criticize others for theirs.
orig: تلك أمة قد خلت لها ما كسبت ولكم ما كسبتم ولا تسألون عما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they say, "Be Jews or Christians [so] you will be guided." Say, "Rather, [we follow] the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the tendency of some people to claim that one must follow a specific religious tradition (Judaism or Christianity) in order to be guided. The Qur'an rejects this claim and instead directs the believers to follow the religion of Abraham, which is a monotheistic faith that rejects polytheism. The interpretation is that the true path to guidance is not found in adhering to a particular religious label, but in following the pure monotheistic faith of Abraham.
orig: وقالوا كونوا هودا أو نصارى تهتدوا قل بل ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: Say, "We have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Descendants and what was given to Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to declare their faith in Allah and in all the divine revelations and messengers that He has sent, without making any distinction between them. It emphasizes the unity of faith and the importance of submitting to Allah alone, as true Muslims. The verse highlights the inclusive nature of the Islamic faith, which recognizes the legitimacy of previous prophets and scriptures, and calls for unity among all believers.
orig: قولوا آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وما أنزل إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وما أوتي موسى وعيسى وما أوتي النبيون من ربهم لا نفرق بين أحد منهم ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And if they believe in the like of that which you believe, then they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, then they are only in opposition, and Allah will suffice you against them. And He is the Hearer, the Knower.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be patient and steadfast in their faith, even if others do not believe. It assures that those who believe in the same way will be rightly guided, while those who turn away are in opposition. Allah will protect the believers and is All-Hearing and All-Knowing.
orig: فإن آمنوا بمثل ما آمنتم به فقد اهتدوا وإن تولوا فإنما هم في شقاق فسيكفيكهم الله وهو السميع العليم

translation: The Tint of Allah, and who is better than Allah in tinting? And we are His worshippers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the true believers are those who have been "tinted" or transformed by the guidance and teachings of Allah. It suggests that there is no better "tint" or way of life than the one prescribed by Allah, and that the true purpose of the believers is to worship and submit to Allah alone.
orig: صبغة الله ومن أحسن من الله صبغة ونحن له عابدون

translation: Say, "Do you argue with us about Allah while He is our Lord and your Lord? For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. And we are sincere [in worship and obedience] to Him."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental differences between the believers and the disbelievers in their relationship with Allah. It establishes that Allah is the sole Lord and Creator, to whom both the believers and disbelievers are accountable for their actions. The verse encourages the believers to maintain their sincerity and devotion to Allah, and to not engage in fruitless arguments with those who reject faith, as each person will be judged by their own deeds.
orig: قل أتحاجوننا في الله وهو ربنا وربكم ولنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم ونحن له مخلصون

translation: Or do you say that [the founders of] Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Descendants were Jews or Christians? Say, "Is it you who know better or is it Allah?" And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from Allah? And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion that the Prophets of Islam, such as Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob, were followers of Judaism or Christianity. It emphasizes that only Allah knows the true nature of their faith, and that it is unjust to conceal any testimony about their religion that one may have received from Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that one should not make claims about the religious affiliations of the Prophets without proper knowledge, as that would be an act of injustice.
orig: أم تقولون إن إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط كانوا هودا أو نصارى قل أأنتم أعلم أم الله ومن أظلم ممن كتم شهادة عنده من الله وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: That is a community which has passed on. It will have [the consequence of] what it earned, and you will have what you have earned. And you will not be asked about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that each community or individual will be held accountable for their own actions and deeds. It suggests that we should not concern ourselves with the actions of others, but rather focus on our own conduct and its consequences. The verse encourages personal responsibility and accountability, reminding us that we will not be held responsible for the actions of those who have come before us.
orig: تلك أمة قد خلت لها ما كسبت ولكم ما كسبتم ولا تسألون عما كانوا يعملون

translation: The foolish among the people will say, "What has turned them away from their qiblah (direction of prayer) which they used to face?" Say, "To Allah belong the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path."
interpretation: This verse addresses those who question the change of the qiblah (direction of prayer) from Jerusalem to Mecca. It affirms that the direction of prayer is not an end in itself, but a means to guide people towards Allah. The true guidance comes from Allah, who is the Lord of the east and the west, and He alone can lead people to the straight path.
orig: سيقول السفهاء من الناس ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها قل لله المشرق والمغرب يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And thus We have made you a moderate community so that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you. And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who follows the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. And indeed, it is difficult except for those whom Allah has guided. And never would Allah have caused you to lose your faith. Indeed Allah is, to the people, Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the role of the Muslim community as a moderate and balanced community, tasked with bearing witness over all of humanity. It also explains the purpose behind the change in the direction of prayer (qiblah) from Jerusalem to Mecca, which was to distinguish those who truly follow the Prophet Muhammad from those who would turn away. The verse emphasizes that this change is difficult except for those guided by Allah, and that Allah would never cause the believers to lose their faith, for He is Kind and Merciful towards all people.
orig: وكذلك جعلناكم أمة وسطا لتكونوا شهداء على الناس ويكون الرسول عليكم شهيدا وما جعلنا القبلة التي كنت عليها إلا لنعلم من يتبع الرسول ممن ينقلب على عقبيه وإن كانت لكبيرة إلا على الذين هدى الله وما كان الله ليضيع إيمانكم إن الله بالناس لرءوف رحيم

translation: We have certainly seen the turning of your face, [O Muhammad], toward the heaven, and We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you [believers] are, turn your faces toward it [in prayer]. And indeed, those who have been given the Scripture well know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse establishes the direction of prayer (qiblah) for Muslims, which is the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca. It emphasizes that the Qur'an is the truth revealed by God, and that those who have received previous scriptures (Jews and Christians) know this to be true. The verse also highlights God's awareness of all human actions, which should motivate believers to conduct themselves righteously.
orig: قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وحيث ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره وإن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ليعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم وما الله بغافل عما يعملون

translation: And if you bring to those who were given the Scripture every sign, they will not follow your qiblah. Nor will you be a follower of their qiblah. Nor would one part of them be followers of the qiblah of another. And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, indeed, you would then be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that even if the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) are shown clear signs and evidence, they will not follow the qiblah (direction of prayer) of the Muslims. Similarly, the Muslims will not follow the qiblah of the People of the Book, nor will the various sects among the People of the Book follow each other's qiblah. The verse warns the Prophet Muhammad that if he were to follow the desires and beliefs of the People of the Book after the knowledge and guidance he has received, he would be considered among the wrongdoers.
orig: ولئن أتيت الذين أوتوا الكتاب بكل آية ما تبعوا قبلتك وما أنت بتابع قبلتهم وما بعضهم بتابع قبلة بعض ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم من بعد ما جاءك من العلم إنك إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their own sons. But a party of them surely conceal the truth while they know (it).
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of the Book, namely the Jews and Christians, who are familiar with the teachings of the Qur"an and recognize it as the truth, just as they recognize their own children. However, some of them deliberately conceal the truth about the Qur"an and its message, despite their knowledge of it.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an and the message it conveys is the absolute truth revealed by God. It instructs the believers to have unwavering faith in this truth and not to harbor any doubts about its divine origin and authenticity.
orig: الحق من ربك فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: And for every [religious following] is a [particular] direction to which it faces. So race to [all that is] good. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you forth [for judgement] all together. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to compete in doing good deeds, regardless of their religious affiliation or background. It emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate judge and that He has power over all things, so one should focus on righteous actions rather than differences. The verse promotes unity and cooperation in pursuing what is good and pleasing to Allah.
orig: ولكل وجهة هو موليها فاستبقوا الخيرات أين ما تكونوا يأت بكم الله جميعا إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And from wherever you go out, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram, and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it [in prayer]. And indeed, those who have been given the Scripture well know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to face the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca, the most sacred site in Islam, when performing their daily prayers. It emphasizes that this is the truth revealed by God, and that He is fully aware of the actions of His worshippers. The verse highlights the importance of unity and direction in Islamic worship, as well as God's omniscience and the authenticity of the religious teachings.
orig: ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وإنه للحق من ربك وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: And from wherever you go out [for prayer, O Muhammad], turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram [in Makkah], and wherever you [believers] may be, turn your faces toward it [during prayer] in order that the people will have no argument against you, except for those of them who commit wrong; so fear them not but fear Me, and [it is] so I may complete My favor upon you and that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of facing the direction of the Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Mosque in Makkah) during prayer, regardless of one's location. It serves to unify the Muslim community and prevent any disputes or arguments about the proper direction of prayer. The verse also reminds believers to fear and submit to Allah alone, not to those who do wrong, so that Allah's blessings and guidance may be complete upon them.
orig: ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وحيث ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره لئلا يكون للناس عليكم حجة إلا الذين ظلموا منهم فلا تخشوهم واخشوني ولأتم نعمتي عليكم ولعلكم تهتدون

translation: Just as We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves reciting to you Our verses and purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom and teaching you that which you did not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God has sent a messenger from among the people to guide them. This messenger recites the verses of the Qur'an, purifies the people, and teaches them the Book (the Qur'an) and wisdom. He also teaches them things they did not previously know. This highlights the importance of the messenger in guiding the people and imparting divine knowledge to them.
orig: كما أرسلنا فيكم رسولا منكم يتلو عليكم آياتنا ويزكيكم ويعلمكم الكتاب والحكمة ويعلمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون

translation: So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to remember and worship Allah, as He will in turn remember and bless them. It emphasizes the importance of gratitude and warns against ingratitude and denial of Allah's favors.
orig: فاذكروني أذكركم واشكروا لي ولا تكفرون

translation: O you who believe! Seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to seek help and strength through patience and prayer. It emphasizes that Allah is with those who are steadfast and persevere in the face of difficulties. The interpretation suggests that by cultivating patience and maintaining a consistent prayer life, believers can find the support and guidance they need from Allah to overcome challenges and remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا استعينوا بالصبر والصلاة إن الله مع الصابرين

translation: And do not say about those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers not to consider those who have died in the cause of Allah as dead, but rather as alive in the sight of Allah. Though they may have physically died, their souls live on in the afterlife. This is a reminder that the true believers who sacrifice their lives for their faith are not to be mourned as dead, but rather celebrated as alive in the eternal realm.
orig: ولا تقولوا لمن يقتل في سبيل الله أموات بل أحياء ولكن لا تشعرون

translation: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient,
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah will test the believers with various trials and tribulations, such as fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives, and crops. However, the believers who remain patient and steadfast in their faith will be rewarded with good news and glad tidings.
orig: ولنبلونكم بشيء من الخوف والجوع ونقص من الأموال والأنفس والثمرات وبشر الصابرين

translation: Those who, when disaster strikes them, say, "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have patience and steadfastness in the face of adversity. It reminds them that everything ultimately belongs to Allah, and that they will return to Him. This attitude of submission and trust in Allah's plan can provide solace and strength during difficult times.
orig: الذين إذا أصابتهم مصيبة قالوا إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون

translation: Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And it is those who are the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who have received the guidance of Allah and have been granted His blessings and mercy. They are the ones who have found the right path and are being led by Allah towards eternal success.
orig: أولئك عليهم صلوات من ربهم ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون

translation: Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes pilgrimage to the House or performs umrah - there is no blame upon him for walking between them. And whoever does good voluntarily - then indeed, Allah is appreciative and knowing.
interpretation: This verse encourages the ritual of walking between the hills of al-Safa and al-Marwah as part of the pilgrimage to the Kaaba in Mecca. This act symbolizes the search for truth and the willingness to exert effort in one's spiritual journey. The verse emphasizes that this ritual is a part of the religious rites and that those who perform it, whether for the Hajj or the Umrah, will not be held accountable. Furthermore, the verse encourages voluntary good deeds, as Allah is appreciative of such actions and has full knowledge of them.
orig: إن الصفا والمروة من شعائر الله فمن حج البيت أو اعتمر فلا جناح عليه أن يطوف بهما ومن تطوع خيرا فإن الله شاكر عليم

translation: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We have made it clear for the people in the Scripture - those are cursed by Allah and cursed by those who curse
interpretation: This verse condemns those who knowingly hide or conceal the clear guidance and proofs that have been revealed in the Quran. It suggests that such people will be cursed by Allah and by all those who are in a position to pronounce curses, as they are denying the truth and misleading others.
orig: إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزلنا من البينات والهدى من بعد ما بيناه للناس في الكتاب أولئك يلعنهم الله ويلعنهم اللاعنون

translation: Except for those who repent, correct themselves, and make evident [the truth], for those I will accept repentance, and I am the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse conveys Allah's compassion and willingness to forgive those who sincerely repent, correct their wrongdoings, and openly acknowledge the truth. It emphasizes that Allah is the Acceptor of repentance and the Most Merciful, ready to forgive those who turn back to Him with genuine remorse and a desire to amend their ways.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا وبينوا فأولئك أتوب عليهم وأنا التواب الرحيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - upon them will be the curse of Allah and of the angels and the people, all together.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith and die in that state will face the eternal curse of Allah, the angels, and all of humanity. It underscores the severe consequences of disbelief and the importance of maintaining faith until the end of one's life.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وماتوا وهم كفار أولئك عليهم لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين

translation: Abiding therein. The punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the punishment for those who reject faith and do not repent. The punishment will not be reduced or alleviated, and they will not be given any respite or opportunity to escape it. It highlights the severity and permanence of the consequences for those who turn away from God's guidance.
orig: خالدين فيها لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And your god is one God. There is no deity except Him, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental belief in the oneness and uniqueness of God. It affirms that there is only one true deity, and that this deity is the All-Merciful and the Especially Compassionate. This highlights the core tenet of Islamic monotheism, which is the belief in a single, all-powerful, and all-loving God who is the sole object of worship and devotion.
orig: وإلهكم إله واحد لا إله إلا هو الرحمن الرحيم

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the [great] ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what Allah has sent down from the heavens of rain, giving life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness and [by] dispersing therein every [kind of] moving creature, and [in His] directing of the winds and the clouds controlled between the heaven and the earth are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the various signs and wonders of Allah’s creation, which are meant to be contemplated by those who use their reason. It points to the intricate balance and order in the universe, from the heavens and the earth, to the alternation of night and day, the ships that sail the seas, the rain that gives life to the earth, and the winds and clouds that are under Allah’s control. These are all meant to be signs that guide people to recognize the power, wisdom, and mercy of the Creator.
orig: إن في خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار والفلك التي تجري في البحر بما ينفع الناس وما أنزل الله من السماء من ماء فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها وبث فيها من كل دابة وتصريف الرياح والسحاب المسخر بين السماء والأرض لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And of the people are some who take besides Allah other deities, loving them as they love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah. And if only those who have wronged would consider [that] when they see the punishment, [they will be certain] that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the common human tendency to worship or love things other than God, such as idols, wealth, power, or status. However, the verse emphasizes that true believers love God above all else, with a stronger and more sincere love. The verse also warns that those who have wronged will realize on the Day of Judgment that all power and authority belongs to God alone, and that He is severe in His punishment of those who associate partners with Him.
orig: ومن الناس من يتخذ من دون الله أندادا يحبونهم كحب الله والذين آمنوا أشد حبا لله ولو يرى الذين ظلموا إذ يرون العذاب أن القوة لله جميعا وأن الله شديد العذاب

translation: When those who were followed disassociate themselves from those who followed [them], and they [all] see the punishment, and cut off from them are the [friendly] ties.
interpretation: This verse describes a scenario on the Day of Judgment when those who were followed (leaders, scholars, etc.) will disassociate themselves from those who blindly followed them, and they will all witness the punishment that awaits them. The close ties and relationships that existed between them in the worldly life will be severed, as they will no longer be able to help or support one another.
orig: إذ تبرأ الذين اتبعوا من الذين اتبعوا ورأوا العذاب وتقطعت بهم الأسباب

translation: And those who followed will say, "If only we had one more chance to return [to the world], we would disassociate ourselves from them as they have disassociated themselves from us." Thus will Allah show them their deeds as regrets upon them, and they are never to emerge from the Fire.
interpretation: This verse describes the regret and desperation of those who followed the disbelievers, wishing they could return to the world and disassociate themselves from their previous associates. However, Allah will show them their evil deeds as a source of deep regret, and they will be unable to escape the punishment of the Hellfire.
orig: وقال الذين اتبعوا لو أن لنا كرة فنتبرأ منهم كما تبرءوا منا كذلك يريهم الله أعمالهم حسرات عليهم وما هم بخارجين من النار

translation: O mankind, eat from whatever is on earth [that is] lawful and good and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to consume only that which is lawful and wholesome, and to avoid following the temptations of Satan, who is an open enemy of humanity. The message is to live a life in accordance with the guidance of Allah, and to refrain from engaging in unlawful or harmful activities.
orig: يا أيها الناس كلوا مما في الأرض حلالا طيبا ولا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: He only commands you to evil and immorality and to say about Allah what you do not know.
interpretation: This verse warns against following the commands of Satan, who only directs people towards evil and immorality, and making false claims about Allah without proper knowledge. It emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance from Allah and refraining from blindly following the whispers of the devil.
orig: إنما يأمركم بالسوء والفحشاء وأن تقولوا على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed," they say, "Rather, we will follow that upon which we found our fathers." Even if their fathers understood nothing, nor were they guided?
interpretation: This verse condemns the blind adherence to the traditions and practices of one's ancestors, even if those traditions are devoid of any rational or spiritual foundation. It calls for the people to follow the guidance revealed by Allah, rather than simply following the ways of their forefathers without question. The verse implies that one should not blindly accept the beliefs and practices of the past, but rather use reason and seek the true path of guidance from the divine revelation.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اتبعوا ما أنزل الله قالوا بل نتبع ما ألفينا عليه آباءنا أولو كان آباؤهم لا يعقلون شيئا ولا يهتدون

translation: And the example of those who disbelieve is like that of one who calls out to those [animals] that hear nothing but calls and cries. [They are] deaf, dumb and blind, so they do not understand.
interpretation: This verse draws a powerful analogy between those who disbelieve in God and animals that are incapable of comprehending human speech. Just as animals cannot understand the calls and cries of a human, the disbelievers are spiritually deaf, dumb and blind, unable to grasp the profound truths of the Qur"an. This emphasizes that faith is not merely an intellectual exercise, but requires a deeper spiritual understanding that the disbelievers lack.
orig: ومثل الذين كفروا كمثل الذي ينعق بما لا يسمع إلا دعاء ونداء صم بكم عمي فهم لا يعقلون

translation: O you who believe, eat from the good things which We have provided for you and be grateful to Allah if it is [indeed] Him that you worship.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to consume the good and wholesome provisions that Allah has granted them, and to express gratitude to Allah for these blessings. The verse emphasizes that this gratitude should be sincere, arising from a genuine desire to worship and serve Allah alone.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم واشكروا لله إن كنتم إياه تعبدون

translation: He has only forbidden to you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes certain dietary restrictions for Muslims, prohibiting the consumption of carrion, blood, pork, and anything dedicated to deities other than Allah. However, it also provides an exception for those who are compelled by necessity to partake of these forbidden foods, as long as they do not do so out of desire or transgression. This reflects Allah's mercy and forgiveness, as He understands the challenges and hardships that people may face in their lives.
orig: إنما حرم عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل به لغير الله فمن اضطر غير باغ ولا عاد فلا إثم عليه إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book and exchange it for a small price - those consume not in their bellies except the Fire, and Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them. And they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who conceal or hide the teachings of the Quran, the book revealed by Allah, and instead choose to gain a small worldly benefit by doing so. The interpretation is that such people will be punished severely in the afterlife, as they will be consumed by the Fire of Hell, and Allah will not speak to them or purify them on the Day of Judgment, and they will face a painful punishment.
orig: إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزل الله من الكتاب ويشترون به ثمنا قليلا أولئك ما يأكلون في بطونهم إلا النار ولا يكلمهم الله يوم القيامة ولا يزكيهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Those are the ones who have exchanged guidance for error and punishment for forgiveness, and how patient they are for [entering] the Fire
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who have willfully chosen to reject the truth and guidance of Islam in favor of falsehood and misguidance, and who have preferred the punishment of the Hellfire over the forgiveness and mercy of Allah. It highlights their stubbornness and unwillingness to accept the truth, even in the face of the severe consequences they will face in the Hereafter.
orig: أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى والعذاب بالمغفرة فما أصبرهم على النار

translation: That is because Allah has sent down the Book in truth. And indeed, those who differ over the Book are in extreme dissension.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an has been revealed by Allah with truth and certainty. Those who dispute or disagree about the teachings and guidance of the Qur'an are in a state of deep discord and division, far removed from the truth.
orig: ذلك بأن الله نزل الكتاب بالحق وإن الذين اختلفوا في الكتاب لفي شقاق بعيد

translation: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but [true] righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets and gives wealth, in spite of love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask [for help], and for the freeing of slaves; [and who] establishes prayer and gives zakah; [and who] fulfill their promise when they promise; and [who] are patient in poverty and hardship and during battle. Those are the ones who have been true, and it is those who are the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true righteousness is not merely about the outward display of religious observances, such as the direction one faces during prayer. Rather, it is about the inward state of the heart and the outward manifestation of faith in one's actions. The key aspects of righteousness mentioned here include belief in the fundamental tenets of Islam, charitable giving, fulfillment of promises, and steadfastness in the face of adversity. The verse highlights that those who embody these qualities are the truly righteous ones.
orig: ليس البر أن تولوا وجوهكم قبل المشرق والمغرب ولكن البر من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر والملائكة والكتاب والنبيين وآتى المال على حبه ذوي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل والسائلين وفي الرقاب وأقام الصلاة وآتى الزكاة والموفون بعهدهم إذا عاهدوا والصابرين في البأساء والضراء وحين البأس أولئك الذين صدقوا وأولئك هم المتقون

translation: O you who believe! Prescribed for you is legal retribution for those murdered - the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. But whoever overlooks from his brother [i.e., the killer] anything, then there should be a suitable follow-up and payment to him with good conduct. This is an alleviation from your Lord and a mercy. But whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of legal retribution, or "an eye for an eye", as a means of ensuring justice and deterring murder. However, it also encourages forgiveness and reconciliation, allowing the victim's family to accept compensation in lieu of retaliation. This reflects a balance between the need for justice and the possibility of mercy, which is seen as an act of compassion from God.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كتب عليكم القصاص في القتلى الحر بالحر والعبد بالعبد والأنثى بالأنثى فمن عفي له من أخيه شيء فاتباع بالمعروف وأداء إليه بإحسان ذلك تخفيف من ربكم ورحمة فمن اعتدى بعد ذلك فله عذاب أليم

translation: And there is for you in legal retribution [saving of] life, O you [people] of understanding, that you may become righteous.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the practice of legal retribution, or qisas, serves a higher purpose of preserving life and promoting righteousness among people. It calls upon those with wisdom and discernment to understand and uphold this principle, as it is a means to achieve a more just and morally upright society.
orig: ولكم في القصاص حياة يا أولي الألباب لعلكم تتقون

translation: It is prescribed for you, when death approaches any of you, if he leaves wealth, that he make a bequest to parents and near relatives according to reasonable manners. [This is] a duty upon the righteous.
interpretation: This verse instructs that when one is facing death, if they have wealth to leave behind, they should make a will that bequeaths it to their parents and close relatives in a fair and reasonable manner. This is an obligation upon the righteous and God-fearing.
orig: كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين بالمعروف حقا على المتقين

translation: And whoever alters it [i.e., the Qur'an] after he has heard it - the sin is only upon those who have altered it. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of preserving the original message of the Qur'an. It warns against altering or changing the Qur'an after one has heard and understood it. The sin of such alteration lies with those who make the changes, not with the one who has heard the original message. This underscores the divine nature of the Qur'an and the responsibility of believers to uphold its integrity.
orig: فمن بدله بعدما سمعه فإنما إثمه على الذين يبدلونه إن الله سميع عليم

translation: But if one fears from the testator [some] bias or sin and corrects that between them, there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages the resolution of disputes and conflicts that may arise from the distribution of inheritance. If there is a concern that the testator has acted unfairly or committed a sin in their will, then it is permissible for the heirs to amicably resolve the matter amongst themselves, without incurring any sin. This is because Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, and desires for His servants to resolve their differences in a peaceful manner.
orig: فمن خاف من موص جنفا أو إثما فأصلح بينهم فلا إثم عليه إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fasting as a spiritual practice that has been ordained for believers throughout history. The purpose of fasting is to cultivate righteousness, self-discipline, and God-consciousness within the individual. By abstaining from food, drink, and other physical desires, the believer is able to focus on their relationship with the Divine and strive to become a more virtuous person.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كتب عليكم الصيام كما كتب على الذين من قبلكم لعلكم تتقون

translation: For a few numbered days. But whoever among you is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days [are to be made up]. And upon those who are able [to fast, but with hardship] - a ransom [as substitute] of feeding a poor person [each day]. And whoever volunteers excess - it is better for him. And to fast is better for you, if you should know.
interpretation: This verse outlines the rules for fasting during the month of Ramadan. It allows for exceptions for those who are ill or traveling, and provides an alternative of feeding a poor person for those who are unable to fast. The verse encourages voluntarily fasting as a virtuous act, as it is ultimately better for the believers if they can do so.
orig: أياما معدودات فمن كان منكم مريضا أو على سفر فعدة من أيام أخر وعلى الذين يطيقونه فدية طعام مسكين فمن تطوع خيرا فهو خير له وأن تصوموا خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: The month of Ramadhan [is that] in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for the people and clear proofs of the guidance and the criterion. So whoever sights [the new moon of] the month, let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [wants] for you to complete the period and to glorify Allah for that [to] which He has guided you; and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the month of Ramadan, during which the Qur'an was revealed as a guidance for humanity. It encourages fasting during this sacred month, while also providing flexibility for those who are ill or traveling. The verse highlights Allah's desire for ease and not hardship, and calls upon the believers to complete the fast, glorify Allah, and be grateful for the guidance provided.
orig: شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن هدى للناس وبينات من الهدى والفرقان فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه ومن كان مريضا أو على سفر فعدة من أيام أخر يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر ولتكملوا العدة ولتكبروا الله على ما هداكم ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And when My servants ask you, [O Muhammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's closeness and responsiveness to those who call upon Him. It encourages believers to have faith in God and to respond to His call, as this will lead to their guidance and salvation.
orig: وإذا سألك عبادي عني فإني قريب أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان فليستجيبوا لي وليؤمنوا بي لعلهم يرشدون

translation: It has been made lawful for you the night preceding the fast to go to your wives [for sexual relations]. They are a garment for you and you are a garment for them. Allah knows that you used to deceive yourselves, so He turned to you and forgave you. So now, have relations with them and seek that which Allah has decreed for you. And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the night. And do not have relations with them as long as you are staying for worship in the mosques. These are the limits [set by] Allah , so do not approach them. Thus does Allah make clear His ordinances to the people that they may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse outlines the permissibility of intimacy between spouses during the nights of Ramadan fasting. It emphasizes that spouses are a source of comfort and protection for one another, and that Allah has forgiven any past transgressions. The verse also clarifies the time frame for eating and drinking before the fast, as well as the prohibition of intimacy during the day while in the mosque for worship. The overall message is one of Allah's guidance and compassion, encouraging righteousness and adherence to the limits He has set.
orig: أحل لكم ليلة الصيام الرفث إلى نسائكم هن لباس لكم وأنتم لباس لهن علم الله أنكم كنتم تختانون أنفسكم فتاب عليكم وعفا عنكم فالآن باشروهن وابتغوا ما كتب الله لكم وكلوا واشربوا حتى يتبين لكم الخيط الأبيض من الخيط الأسود من الفجر ثم أتموا الصيام إلى الليل ولا تباشروهن وأنتم عاكفون في المساجد تلك حدود الله فلا تقربوها كذلك يبين الله آياته للناس لعلهم يتقون

translation: And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly or send it [in bribery] to the rulers in order that [they might aid] you [to] consume a portion of the wealth of the people in sin, while you know [it is unlawful].
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of using wealth unjustly, such as through bribery, to gain unfair advantage or to consume the wealth of others unlawfully. It emphasizes that believers should not engage in such sinful activities, even if they are aware of their unlawfulness.
orig: ولا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل وتدلوا بها إلى الحكام لتأكلوا فريقا من أموال الناس بالإثم وأنتم تعلمون

translation: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj." And it is not righteousness to enter houses from the back, but righteousness is [in] one who fears Allah. And enter houses from their doors and fear Allah that you may succeed."
interpretation: This verse addresses a question about the new moons, which were used to determine the timing of religious practices like Hajj (pilgrimage). The Qur'an clarifies that these lunar phases are meant to be markers of time for people, not objects of worship or superstition. The verse then emphasizes that true righteousness comes not from outward actions, but from fearing and obeying Allah. It encourages people to enter their homes through the proper entrances, as a symbol of humility and reverence before God. The ultimate goal is to achieve success (falah) in this life and the Hereafter by living a life of God-consciousness and righteous conduct.
orig: يسألونك عن الأهلة قل هي مواقيت للناس والحج وليس البر بأن تأتوا البيوت من ظهورها ولكن البر من اتقى وأتوا البيوت من أبوابها واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you but do not transgress. Indeed. Allah does not like transgressors.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to defend themselves against those who attack them, but to do so without exceeding the bounds of justice and moderation. It emphasizes that Allah does not approve of those who transgress and act unjustly, even in the course of defending their faith.
orig: وقاتلوا في سبيل الله الذين يقاتلونكم ولا تعتدوا إن الله لا يحب المعتدين

translation: And kill them wherever you overtake them and expel them from wherever they have expelled you, and fitnah is worse than killing. And do not fight them at al-Masjid al- Haram until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Muslims who were being persecuted and expelled from their homes by the disbelievers. It instructs the Muslims to fight back against their oppressors, but to avoid fighting at the sacred Masjid al-Haram unless the disbelievers initiate the fight there. The interpretation is that the Muslims are allowed to defend themselves and their faith, but should avoid instigating violence at the most sacred place of worship.
orig: واقتلوهم حيث ثقفتموهم وأخرجوهم من حيث أخرجوكم والفتنة أشد من القتل ولا تقاتلوهم عند المسجد الحرام حتى يقاتلوكم فيه فإن قاتلوكم فاقتلوهم كذلك جزاء الكافرين

translation: And if they cease, then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages forgiveness and mercy. If those who have wronged you cease their actions, then Allah is forgiving and merciful towards them. It emphasizes the importance of forgiveness and not seeking revenge, as Allah is the One who can ultimately judge and forgive.
orig: فإن انتهوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And fight them until there is no [more] fitnah and [until] the religion, all of it, is for Allah. And if they cease - then indeed, Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to fight against those who persecute them or prevent them from practicing their faith, until there is no more oppression and the religion of Islam is freely practiced. However, the verse also instructs that if the opponents cease their hostility, the believers should not continue fighting them, except against those who remain oppressive and unjust.
orig: وقاتلوهم حتى لا تكون فتنة ويكون الدين لله فإن انتهوا فلا عدوان إلا على الظالمين

translation: The sacred month for the sacred month, and [all] sacred things are [subject to] retribution. So whoever has assaulted you, then assault him in the same way that he has assaulted you. And fear Allah and know that Allah is with those who fear Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of the sacred months and the principle of just retaliation. It instructs that any violation of the sacred months should be met with a similar response, but also calls for fear of Allah and reminds that Allah is with those who are righteous and God-conscious.
orig: الشهر الحرام بالشهر الحرام والحرمات قصاص فمن اعتدى عليكم فاعتدوا عليه بمثل ما اعتدى عليكم واتقوا الله واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين

translation: And spend in the way of Allah and do not throw [yourselves] with your [own] hands into destruction [by refraining]. And do good; indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to spend and contribute financially in the cause of Allah, and to avoid actions that could lead to their own destruction or ruin. It also emphasizes the importance of doing good deeds, as Allah loves those who are righteous and benevolent.
orig: وأنفقوا في سبيل الله ولا تلقوا بأيديكم إلى التهلكة وأحسنوا إن الله يحب المحسنين

translation: And complete the Hajj and 'Umrah for Allah. But if you are prevented, [then offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal has reached its place of slaughter. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head [making shaving necessary] must offer a ransom of fasting [three days] or charity or sacrifice. And when you are secure, then whoever performs 'Umrah [during the Hajj months] followed by Hajj [offers] what can be obtained with ease of the sacrificial animals. And whoever cannot find [or afford such an animal] - then a fast of three days during Hajj and of seven when you have returned [home]. That is ten [complete] days. This is for those whose family is not in the area of al-Masjid al-Haram. And fear Allah and know that Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse outlines the obligations and rituals that must be fulfilled during the Hajj and 'Umrah pilgrimages. It emphasizes the importance of completing these acts of worship for Allah, and provides guidance on the sacrificial animals, hair-shaving, and fasting requirements for those who are prevented from fully participating. The verse also highlights the need to fear Allah and be aware of His severe punishment for those who do not fulfill their obligations.
orig: وأتموا الحج والعمرة لله فإن أحصرتم فما استيسر من الهدي ولا تحلقوا رءوسكم حتى يبلغ الهدي محله فمن كان منكم مريضا أو به أذى من رأسه ففدية من صيام أو صدقة أو نسك فإذا أمنتم فمن تمتع بالعمرة إلى الحج فما استيسر من الهدي فمن لم يجد فصيام ثلاثة أيام في الحج وسبعة إذا رجعتم تلك عشرة كاملة ذلك لمن لم يكن أهله حاضري المسجد الحرام واتقوا الله واعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب

translation: The Hajj is (during) well-known months. So whoever has obligated upon himself the Hajj (pilgrimage therein), then there is (to be) no sexual relations and no disobedience and no disputing during the Hajj. And whatever good you do - Allah knows it. And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of Allah. And fear Me, O you of understanding.
interpretation: This verse outlines the etiquette and guidelines for performing the Hajj pilgrimage. It emphasizes that during the Hajj months, the pilgrims must abstain from sexual relations, disobedience, and disputes. Instead, they should focus on performing good deeds, which Allah is aware of. The verse also encourages the pilgrims to take provisions for the journey, but stresses that the best provision is God-consciousness and fear of Allah. This highlights the spiritual nature of the Hajj and the importance of maintaining a righteous state of mind throughout the pilgrimage.
orig: الحج أشهر معلومات فمن فرض فيهن الحج فلا رفث ولا فسوق ولا جدال في الحج وما تفعلوا من خير يعلمه الله وتزودوا فإن خير الزاد التقوى واتقون يا أولي الألباب

translation: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord [during Hajj]. And when you depart from 'Arafat, remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram. And remember Him, as He has guided you, for indeed, you were before that among those astray.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to seek the bounty and blessings of Allah during the Hajj pilgrimage. It emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah at the sacred sites, such as al-Mash'ar al-Haram, and to continue remembering Him as He has guided you, for you were once among the misguided. The verse highlights the spiritual aspect of the Hajj journey and the need to be mindful of Allah's guidance throughout the pilgrimage.
orig: ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم فإذا أفضتم من عرفات فاذكروا الله عند المشعر الحرام واذكروه كما هداكم وإن كنتم من قبله لمن الضالين

translation: Then depart from the place from where [all] the people depart and ask forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages pilgrims to the holy sites to depart from the same place where the masses depart, and to seek forgiveness from Allah. The interpretation is that one should not try to distinguish oneself or stand out from the crowd during religious rituals, but rather join the community in a spirit of humility and devotion. The verse also emphasizes that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, so pilgrims should seek His forgiveness with sincerity and hope.
orig: ثم أفيضوا من حيث أفاض الناس واستغفروا الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And when you have completed your rites, remember Allah like your [remembrance of] your fathers or with [much] greater remembrance. And of the people is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," and he will have in the Hereafter no share.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to remember and glorify Allah after completing their religious rites, such as the pilgrimage to Mecca. The remembrance of Allah should be as strong or even stronger than the remembrance of one's own ancestors. However, the verse also warns against those who are only concerned with the worldly life and do not have any concern for the Hereafter. Such people will have no share in the Hereafter.
orig: فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا فمن الناس من يقول ربنا آتنا في الدنيا وما له في الآخرة من خلاق

translation: And among them is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."
interpretation: This verse describes those who pray to Allah for both worldly and spiritual blessings. They seek goodness and prosperity in this life as well as salvation and eternal bliss in the Hereafter. The verse highlights the balanced and comprehensive nature of their supplication, seeking a positive outcome in both realms - the temporal and the eternal.
orig: ومنهم من يقول ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار

translation: Those are the ones who will have [a share of] what they have earned, and Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have done good deeds will be rewarded for their efforts, and that Allah is quick to hold people accountable for their actions. It serves as a reminder that we will be held responsible for our choices and that we should strive to do what is right.
orig: أولئك لهم نصيب مما كسبوا والله سريع الحساب

translation: And remember Allah during [specified] numbered days. So whoever hastens [his departure] in two days - there is no sin upon him; and whoever delays [until the third] - there is no sin upon him - for [those] who fear Allah. And fear Allah and know that unto Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to remember and worship Allah during the specific days of Hajj, such as the days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah). It emphasizes that there is no sin upon those who depart early or delay their departure, as long as they fear and are conscious of Allah. The overall message is to be mindful of Allah and to know that we will all be held accountable before Him on the Day of Judgment.
orig: واذكروا الله في أيام معدودات فمن تعجل في يومين فلا إثم عليه ومن تأخر فلا إثم عليه لمن اتقى واتقوا الله واعلموا أنكم إليه تحشرون

translation: And of the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life, and he calls Allah to witness about what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who appear pious and righteous in their speech and outward behavior, but whose hearts are filled with malice, opposition, and hostility towards others. They may impress people with their words, but Allah knows the true nature of their hearts. This highlights the importance of looking beyond the superficial and examining the sincerity and intentions of those who claim to be believers.
orig: ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه وهو ألد الخصام

translation: And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption in it and destroy the crops and animals. And Allah does not like corruption.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who turn away from the guidance of Allah and instead seek to spread corruption and destruction in the land. It emphasizes that Allah does not approve of such behavior, which harms the natural order and the well-being of people. The verse serves as a warning against engaging in actions that disrupt the harmony and balance of the world that Allah has created.
orig: وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها ويهلك الحرث والنسل والله لا يحب الفساد

translation: And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," pride in the sin takes hold of him. Sufficient for him is Hell, and how wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who are arrogant and prideful when they are advised to be God-conscious and righteous. Their ego and attachment to sin prevents them from heeding the call to fear and obey Allah. This verse warns that such people will ultimately face the punishment of Hell, which is a terrible destination.
orig: وإذا قيل له اتق الله أخذته العزة بالإثم فحسبه جهنم ولبئس المهاد

translation: And among the people is he who sells himself, [seeking to please] the approval of Allah. And Allah is kind to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse speaks of those who willingly sacrifice their own desires and interests in order to please Allah. They are willing to put the will of Allah above their own, demonstrating their sincere devotion and trust in Him. The verse emphasizes that Allah is compassionate and caring towards His servants, rewarding those who make such sacrifices.
orig: ومن الناس من يشري نفسه ابتغاء مرضات الله والله رءوف بالعباد

translation: O you who believe! Enter into Islam completely [and perfectly] and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse urges believers to fully embrace the teachings and way of life of Islam, without compromise or deviation. It warns against following the temptations and deceptions of Satan, who is described as a clear and open enemy of the faithful. The interpretation is that one must wholeheartedly commit to the religion of Islam and avoid any influences or actions that would lead them astray from the righteous path.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ادخلوا في السلم كافة ولا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: And if you slip after clear proofs have come to you, then know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: If you deviate from the truth after the clear signs have been presented to you, then know that Allah is Mighty and Wise in His judgement and decision-making. This verse serves as a warning to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not to stray from the path of righteousness, for Allah has the power to hold them accountable and His wisdom in doing so is beyond human comprehension.
orig: فإن زللتم من بعد ما جاءتكم البينات فاعلموا أن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: Do they await but that Allah should come to them in covers of clouds and the angels [as well] and the matter is [then] decided? And [all] matters are returned to Allah.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have faith in God and His divine plan, rather than waiting for tangible signs or miraculous events. It suggests that the ultimate resolution of all matters rests with God, and that one should focus on submitting to His will rather than seeking external validation or dramatic occurrences.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا أن يأتيهم الله في ظلل من الغمام والملائكة وقضي الأمر وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: Ask the Children of Israel how many a Sign of power We have shown them! But if anyone, after Allah's favour has come to him, substitutes (something else), Allah is strict in punishment.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad to ask the Children of Israel about the many clear signs and miracles that Allah had bestowed upon them, yet they still turned away from faith. It serves as a warning that those who reject or substitute the blessings of Allah after they have been made clear will face severe punishment from Allah.
orig: سل بني إسرائيل كم آتيناهم من آية بينة ومن يبدل نعمة الله من بعد ما جاءته فإن الله شديد العقاب

translation: Beautified for those who disbelieve is the life of this world, and they ridicule those who believe. But those who fear Allah will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. And Allah gives provision to whom He wills without account.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the worldly life and the life of the Hereafter. Those who reject faith find the worldly life attractive and are disdainful towards the believers. However, on the Day of Judgment, the righteous will be elevated above the disbelievers, and Allah will provide sustenance to whomever He wills without measure.
orig: زين للذين كفروا الحياة الدنيا ويسخرون من الذين آمنوا والذين اتقوا فوقهم يوم القيامة والله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب

translation: Mankind was [of] one religion [before their deviation]; then Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners and sent down with them the Scripture in truth to judge between the people concerning that in which they differed. And none differed over it [i.e., the Scripture] except those who were given it - after the clear proofs had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. And Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they had differed, by His permission. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all of humanity was originally united in faith, but differences and disputes arose. Allah then sent the prophets with divine scriptures to guide people and resolve their disputes. However, even after receiving clear guidance, some people still differed out of jealousy and animosity. Allah then guided the believers to the truth, by His will and permission. This highlights the importance of unity, following divine guidance, and resolving disputes through righteous means.
orig: كان الناس أمة واحدة فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين وأنزل معهم الكتاب بالحق ليحكم بين الناس فيما اختلفوا فيه وما اختلف فيه إلا الذين أوتوه من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات بغيا بينهم فهدى الله الذين آمنوا لما اختلفوا فيه من الحق بإذنه والله يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you? They were touched by poverty and hardship and were shaken until [even their] messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that entering Paradise is not guaranteed without facing trials and tribulations, similar to what the previous generations of believers had to endure. It reminds us that hardship, poverty, and challenges are part of the journey towards attaining Allah's help and victory, which is ultimately near for those who remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: أم حسبتم أن تدخلوا الجنة ولما يأتكم مثل الذين خلوا من قبلكم مستهم البأساء والضراء وزلزلوا حتى يقول الرسول والذين آمنوا معه متى نصر الله ألا إن نصر الله قريب

translation: They ask you, [O Muhammad], what they should spend. Say, "Whatever you spend of good is [to be] for parents and relatives and orphans and the needy and the traveler. And whatever you do of good - indeed, Allah is Knowing of it."
