interpretation: This verse encourages believers to spend their wealth in charitable ways, particularly for the benefit of their parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, and travelers. It emphasizes that whatever good one does, Allah is aware of it and will reward it accordingly.
orig: يسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل ما أنفقتم من خير فللوالدين والأقربين واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل وما تفعلوا من خير فإن الله به عليم

translation: Fighting has been enjoined upon you while it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allah Knows, while you know not.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that while fighting may be undesirable, it is sometimes necessary for the greater good. It reminds us that our own desires and perceptions may not always align with what is truly best for us, and that we should trust in Allah's superior knowledge and wisdom. The verse encourages us to be open-minded and accept that which may initially seem unpleasant, as it may in fact be beneficial for us in the long run.
orig: كتب عليكم القتال وهو كره لكم وعسى أن تكرهوا شيئا وهو خير لكم وعسى أن تحبوا شيئا وهو شر لكم والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein. Say, "Fighting therein is a great [sin], but averting [people] from the way of Allah and disbelief in Him and [preventing access to] al-Masjid al-Haram and the expulsion of its people therefrom are greater [evil] in the sight of Allah. And [trial by] disbelief is worse than killing." And they will continue to fight you until they turn you back from your religion if they are able. And whoever of you reverts from his religion [to disbelief] and dies while he is a disbeliever - for those, their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of fighting during the sacred month, which is considered a great sin. However, it also highlights that preventing people from the way of Allah, disbelief in Him, preventing access to the sacred Masjid al-Haram, and expelling its people are even greater evils in the sight of Allah. The verse also warns that disbelief is worse than killing. It further states that the disbelievers will continue to fight the believers until they turn them back from their religion, if they are able. The verse concludes by warning that those who revert from their religion and die as disbelievers will have their deeds rendered worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and they will be the companions of the Fire, abiding in it eternally.
orig: يسألونك عن الشهر الحرام قتال فيه قل قتال فيه كبير وصد عن سبيل الله وكفر به والمسجد الحرام وإخراج أهله منه أكبر عند الله والفتنة أكبر من القتل ولا يزالون يقاتلونكم حتى يردوكم عن دينكم إن استطاعوا ومن يرتدد منكم عن دينه فيمت وهو كافر فأولئك حبطت أعمالهم في الدنيا والآخرة وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and fought in the cause of Allah - those expect the mercy of Allah. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have truly believed in Allah, who have made sacrifices by leaving their homes to spread the message of Islam, and who have strived and fought for the cause of Allah, are the ones who can hope for Allah's mercy and forgiveness. It highlights that Allah is indeed Forgiving and Merciful towards those who sincerely follow His path.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله أولئك يرجون رحمت الله والله غفور رحيم

translation: They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, "In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit." And they ask you what they should spend. Say, "The excess [beyond needs]." Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses [of ordinance] that you might give thought.
interpretation: This verse addresses two common practices of the time - the consumption of alcohol ("wine") and gambling ("gambling"). The Qur'an acknowledges that there may be some benefits to these activities, but states that the harms and sins associated with them outweigh any potential benefits. The verse then addresses the question of what people should spend or donate, instructing them to give from their excess wealth, beyond their basic needs. The overall message is one of moderation and prioritizing the spiritual and moral well-being of the community over indulgence in harmful practices.
orig: يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع للناس وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تتفكرون

translation: And they ask you concerning the orphans. Say: "To improve their condition is best. And if you mix your affairs with theirs, they are your brothers. And Allah knows the one who means mischief from the one who means good. And if Allah had willed, He could have put you in difficulty. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of caring for and improving the condition of orphans. It encourages Muslims to treat orphans as their own brothers, and reminds that Allah knows those who intend harm from those who intend good. The verse also suggests that Allah could have made the situation more difficult, but in His wisdom, has not done so. The overall message is one of compassion, justice and trust in Allah's plan.
orig: في الدنيا والآخرة ويسألونك عن اليتامى قل إصلاح لهم خير وإن تخالطوهم فإخوانكم والله يعلم المفسد من المصلح ولو شاء الله لأعنتكم إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist, even though she might please you. And do not marry polytheistic men [to your women] until they believe. And a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even though he might please you. Those invite [you] to the Fire, but Allah invites to Paradise and to forgiveness, by His permission. And He makes clear His verses to the people that perhaps they may remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of marrying fellow believers, rather than those who associate partners with Allah (polytheists). The verse highlights that a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even if the polytheist is more attractive. This is because polytheists are inviting one to the Fire, whereas Allah invites to Paradise and forgiveness. The verse encourages believers to heed Allah's clear signs and reminders, so that they may remember and strengthen their faith.
orig: ولا تنكحوا المشركات حتى يؤمن ولأمة مؤمنة خير من مشركة ولو أعجبتكم ولا تنكحوا المشركين حتى يؤمنوا ولعبد مؤمن خير من مشرك ولو أعجبكم أولئك يدعون إلى النار والله يدعو إلى الجنة والمغفرة بإذنه ويبين آياته للناس لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And they ask you about menstruation. Say, "It is harm, so keep away from wives during menstruation. And do not approach them until they are pure. And when they have purified themselves, then come to them from where Allah has ordained for you. Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves."
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the proper conduct during a woman's menstrual cycle. It instructs men to abstain from sexual relations with their wives during this time, as menstruation is considered a state of impurity. The verse emphasizes the importance of purification and cleanliness, and encourages both men and women to maintain a state of purity and repentance before Allah. The interpretation highlights the sensitivity and care that should be exercised in marital relations during this period, in order to uphold the principles of modesty and respect in the Islamic faith.
orig: ويسألونك عن المحيض قل هو أذى فاعتزلوا النساء في المحيض ولا تقربوهن حتى يطهرن فإذا تطهرن فأتوهن من حيث أمركم الله إن الله يحب التوابين ويحب المتطهرين

translation: Your wives are as a tilth unto you; so approach your tilth when or how ye will; but do some good act for your souls beforehand; and fear Allah. And know that ye are to meet Him (in the Hereafter), and give (these) good tidings to those who believe.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the relationship between husbands and wives, and the importance of maintaining a healthy and respectful intimacy within marriage. The analogy of the wife being like a "tilth" or cultivated land suggests that the husband should approach his wife with care, respect, and consideration, just as one would tend to a precious crop. The verse encourages husbands to "approach their tilth when or how they will", indicating the importance of mutual consent and the avoidance of coercion or exploitation. However, the verse also emphasizes the importance of doing "some good act for your souls beforehand", reminding husbands to maintain their spiritual and moral obligations even within the context of intimate relationships. Ultimately, the verse reminds all believers that they will be held accountable before Allah, and encourages them to live righteous lives and share this good news with others who believe.
orig: نساؤكم حرث لكم فأتوا حرثكم أنى شئتم وقدموا لأنفسكم واتقوا الله واعلموا أنكم ملاقوه وبشر المؤمنين

translation: And do not make [your oath by] Allah an excuse against being righteous and fearing Allah and making peace among people. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse cautions against using oaths or vows to Allah as an excuse to avoid doing what is righteous and just. Rather, one should strive to be God-fearing, do good deeds, and promote peace and reconciliation among people. Allah is all-Hearing and all-Knowing, and will hold people accountable for their actions and intentions.
orig: ولا تجعلوا الله عرضة لأيمانكم أن تبروا وتتقوا وتصلحوا بين الناس والله سميع عليم

translation: Allah will not impose blame upon you for what is meaningless in your oaths, but He will impose blame upon you for [breaking] what you intended of oaths. And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that they will not be held accountable for casual or unintentional oaths, but rather for breaking oaths that they had deliberately made. It emphasizes Allah's forgiveness and patience, encouraging believers to be mindful of their words and actions without being overly burdened by unintended slip-ups.
orig: لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما كسبت قلوبكم والله غفور حليم

translation: For those who swear abstinence from their wives, a waiting period of four months is prescribed; but if they go back (on their word), verily, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation where a husband swears an oath of abstinence from his wife. The prescribed waiting period is four months, during which the wife must wait to see if the husband will return to her. If the husband does return to his wife during this period, Allah is Oft-Forgiving and Most Merciful towards them.
orig: للذين يؤلون من نسائهم تربص أربعة أشهر فإن فاءوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And if they decide on divorce, then indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that if a couple decides to divorce, they should know that Allah is all-hearing and all-knowing of their decision and the circumstances surrounding it. This serves as a reminder that divorce should not be taken lightly, as Allah is aware of the situation and will hold the parties accountable for their actions.
orig: وإن عزموا الطلاق فإن الله سميع عليم

translation: And divorced women shall wait (as regards their marriage) for three menstrual periods, and it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs, if they believe in Allah and the Last Day. And their husbands have the better right to take them back in that period, if they wish for reconciliation. And they (women) have rights (over their husbands as regards living expenses, etc.) similar (to those of their husbands) over them (as regards obedience and respect, etc.) to what is reasonable, but men have a degree (of responsibility) over them. And Allah is All-Mighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the waiting period (iddah) for divorced women, during which they cannot remarry. It emphasizes the importance of transparency regarding pregnancy, as this is a divine creation. The verse also affirms the rights and responsibilities of both the husband and wife in a marriage, with the husband having a degree of authority, but also requiring him to provide for and treat his wife reasonably. Overall, the verse promotes fairness, accountability, and the preservation of the family unit.
orig: والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء ولا يحل لهن أن يكتمن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن إن كن يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر وبعولتهن أحق بردهن في ذلك إن أرادوا إصلاحا ولهن مثل الذي عليهن بالمعروف وللرجال عليهن درجة والله عزيز حكيم

translation: Divorce is permissible twice. [After that], either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment. And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them [i.e., the wives] unless both fear that they will not be able to keep [within] the limits [imposed by] Allah. But if you fear that they will not keep [within] the limits [imposed by] Allah, then there is no blame upon either of them concerning that by which she ransoms herself [i.e., gives something to the husband for her release]. These are the limits [set by] Allah, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah - it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse outlines the process and guidelines for divorce in Islam. It emphasizes that divorce should be a last resort, and that even after divorce, the parties should treat each other with kindness and respect. The verse also prohibits taking back the dowry or other gifts given to the wife, except in cases where both spouses fear they cannot uphold the limits set by Allah. Ultimately, the verse stresses the importance of respecting the limits and boundaries established by Allah, and warns against transgressing them.
orig: الطلاق مرتان فإمساك بمعروف أو تسريح بإحسان ولا يحل لكم أن تأخذوا مما آتيتموهن شيئا إلا أن يخافا ألا يقيما حدود الله فإن خفتم ألا يقيما حدود الله فلا جناح عليهما فيما افتدت به تلك حدود الله فلا تعتدوها ومن يتعد حدود الله فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: And if he has divorced her [for the third time], then she is not lawful to him afterward until [after] she marries a husband other than him. And if the latter husband divorces her [or dies], there is no blame upon the former husband and her [to remarry] if they believe that they will keep [within] the limits of Allah. And these are the limits of Allah, which He makes clear to a people who know.
interpretation: This verse establishes the conditions for a woman to remarry her previous husband after being divorced three times. It stipulates that the woman must first marry another man and then be divorced or widowed from him, before she can remarry her original husband. This is to ensure that the limits and sanctity of marriage are upheld, and that the decision to remarry is not taken lightly. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of respecting the limits set by Allah, which are made clear for those who have knowledge and understanding.
orig: فإن طلقها فلا تحل له من بعد حتى تنكح زوجا غيره فإن طلقها فلا جناح عليهما أن يتراجعا إن ظنا أن يقيما حدود الله وتلك حدود الله يبينها لقوم يعلمون

translation: And when you divorce women and they have [nearly] fulfilled their term, either retain them according to acceptable terms or release them according to acceptable terms, and do not keep them, intending harm, to transgress [against them]. And whoever does that has certainly wronged himself. And do not take the verses of Allah in jest. And remember the favor of Allah upon you and what has been revealed to you of the Book and wisdom by which He instructs you. And fear Allah and know that Allah is to all things Knowing.
interpretation: This verse outlines the proper conduct in divorce proceedings. It emphasizes that divorced women should be treated with respect, either by retaining them on fair terms or releasing them amicably, without any intention to harm or transgress against them. It warns against taking Allah's signs and revelations lightly, and reminds the believers to be mindful of Allah's blessings and the guidance provided in the Quran and wisdom. The overall message is to uphold justice, compassion and reverence for Allah's commands in matters of divorce and family relations.
orig: وإذا طلقتم النساء فبلغن أجلهن فأمسكوهن بمعروف أو سرحوهن بمعروف ولا تمسكوهن ضرارا لتعتدوا ومن يفعل ذلك فقد ظلم نفسه ولا تتخذوا آيات الله هزوا واذكروا نعمت الله عليكم وما أنزل عليكم من الكتاب والحكمة يعظكم به واتقوا الله واعلموا أن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And when you divorce women and they have [nearly] fulfilled their term, either retain them according to acceptable terms or release them according to acceptable terms, and do not keep them, intending harm, to transgress [against them]. And whoever does that has certainly wronged himself. And do not take the verses of Allah in jest. And remember the favor of Allah upon you and what has been revealed to you of the Book and wisdom by which He instructs you. And fear Allah and know that Allah is to all things Competent.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on how to handle the divorce process with dignity and fairness. It emphasizes that once the divorce period has lapsed, the divorced woman should either be retained on reasonable terms or released amicably, without any intention to harm or transgress against her. The verse also reminds believers to uphold the teachings of Allah and be mindful of His wisdom, which is meant to guide and instruct them. Ultimately, this verse promotes compassion, justice and reverence for the divine commandments in matters of divorce.
orig: وإذا طلقتم النساء فبلغن أجلهن فلا تعضلوهن أن ينكحن أزواجهن إذا تراضوا بينهم بالمعروف ذلك يوعظ به من كان منكم يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر ذلكم أزكى لكم وأطهر والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: And the mothers shall suckle their children for two whole years; (this is) for those who wish to complete the suckling. The duty of feeding and clothing them (the mothers) in a seemly manner is upon the father of the child. No person shall have a burden laid on him greater than he can bear. No mother shall be treated unfairly on account of her child, nor (shall) a father (be treated unfairly) on account of his child. And on the (father's) heir is incumbent the like of that (which was incumbent on the father). And if they both decide on weaning, by mutual consent, and (after) due consultation, there is no sin on them. And if you wish to engage a wet-nurse for your children, there is no sin on you, provided you pay what you promised for in a fair manner. And fear Allah and know that Allah is All-Seer of what you do.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the rights and responsibilities of parents regarding breastfeeding and caring for their children. It emphasizes that mothers should breastfeed their children for two full years if they wish to complete the suckling period. The father is responsible for providing food and clothing for the mother and child during this time. The verse also stresses that no person should be burdened beyond their capacity, and that neither the mother nor the father should be treated unfairly due to their child. It allows for the parents to mutually agree to wean the child before the two-year period, and permits the hiring of a wet-nurse if necessary, as long as the agreed-upon terms are fulfilled. The overall message is one of balance, fairness, and consideration for the well-being of both the parents and the child, with a reminder to fear and be conscious of Allah, who is All-Seeing of our actions.
orig: والوالدات يرضعن أولادهن حولين كاملين لمن أراد أن يتم الرضاعة وعلى المولود له رزقهن وكسوتهن بالمعروف لا تكلف نفس إلا وسعها لا تضار والدة بولدها ولا مولود له بولده وعلى الوارث مثل ذلك فإن أرادا فصالا عن تراض منهما وتشاور فلا جناح عليهما وإن أردتم أن تسترضعوا أولادكم فلا جناح عليكم إذا سلمتم ما آتيتم بالمعروف واتقوا الله واعلموا أن الله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And those who are taken in death among you and leave wives behind - they, [the wives, shall] wait four months and ten [days]. And when they have fulfilled their term, then there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable way. And Allah is [fully] Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse outlines the waiting period for widowed women in Islam. It instructs that a woman whose husband has passed away must observe a period of 'Iddah' for four months and ten days, during which she is not permitted to remarry. This is to ensure that any pregnancy is clearly established, and to provide the woman with a period of mourning and reflection. Once this period has elapsed, the woman is free to remarry or live her life as she chooses, as long as it is done in an acceptable and virtuous manner. The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of the actions of people.
orig: والذين يتوفون منكم ويذرون أزواجا يتربصن بأنفسهن أربعة أشهر وعشرا فإذا بلغن أجلهن فلا جناح عليكم فيما فعلن في أنفسهن بالمعروف والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: And there is no blame upon you for that to which you [indirectly] allude concerning a proposal of marriage to women or for what you conceal within yourselves. Allah knows that you will have them in mind. But do not promise them secretly except for saying a proper and recognized statement. And do not determine to undertake a marriage contract until the decreed period reaches its end. And know that Allah knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him and know that Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the etiquette and proper conduct regarding proposals of marriage. It emphasizes that there is no blame or sin in a man expressing his interest in a woman, even if he does not directly propose marriage. Allah knows what is in the hearts of people. However, the verse cautions against making secret promises or commitments to women before the proper time. It instructs that any communication should be done in a recognized and proper manner. The verse also advises waiting until the prescribed waiting period has ended before finalizing a marriage contract. The underlying message is that Allah is All-Knowing of people's thoughts and intentions, so one should be mindful of Him and conduct oneself with propriety and restraint in such matters, as Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
orig: ولا جناح عليكم فيما عرضتم به من خطبة النساء أو أكننتم في أنفسكم علم الله أنكم ستذكرونهن ولكن لا تواعدوهن سرا إلا أن تقولوا قولا معروفا ولا تعزموا عقدة النكاح حتى يبلغ الكتاب أجله واعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في أنفسكم فاحذروه واعلموا أن الله غفور حليم

translation: There is no blame upon you if you divorce women you have not touched nor specified for them an obligation. But give them [a gift of] maintenance - the wealthy according to his capability and the poor according to his capability - a provision according to what is acceptable, [this is] a duty upon the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse outlines the Islamic teachings regarding divorce, particularly when the marriage has not been consummated. It emphasizes that there is no blame or sin upon the husband if he decides to divorce his wife in such a situation. However, the verse also instructs the husband to provide a gift of maintenance to the divorced wife, according to his means and financial capability. This is considered a righteous and charitable act, expected of those who do good deeds.
orig: لا جناح عليكم إن طلقتم النساء ما لم تمسوهن أو تفرضوا لهن فريضة ومتعوهن على الموسع قدره وعلى المقتر قدره متاعا بالمعروف حقا على المحسنين

translation: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them an obligation, then [there is due to them] half of what you specified - unless they forego it or the one in whose hand is the marriage contract foregoes it. And to forego it is nearer to righteousness. And do not forget graciousness between you. Indeed, Allah, of whatever you do, is Seeing.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the financial obligations and rights of a divorced couple, particularly in cases where the marriage has not been consummated. It emphasizes the importance of fairness, graciousness, and righteousness in handling such matters. The interpretation highlights the need to uphold the rights of the divorced spouse, while also acknowledging the role of forgiveness and compromise in maintaining a just and harmonious relationship, as Allah is aware of all that we do.
orig: وإن طلقتموهن من قبل أن تمسوهن وقد فرضتم لهن فريضة فنصف ما فرضتم إلا أن يعفون أو يعفو الذي بيده عقدة النكاح وأن تعفوا أقرب للتقوى ولا تنسوا الفضل بينكم إن الله بما تعملون بصير

translation: Guard strictly your (habit of) prayers, especially the Middle Prayer, and stand before Allah in a devout (frame of mind).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a consistent prayer life, particularly the "Middle Prayer" which is believed to be the Asr prayer. It calls upon believers to stand humbly before God in a state of submission and devotion.
orig: حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى وقوموا لله قانتين

translation: And if you fear [an enemy, then send] a squadron [of cavalry] or those [fighters] on foot. And when you are secure, then remember Allah , just as He has taught you that which you did not [previously] know.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to be prepared for battle, whether on foot or on horseback, when facing an enemy. However, when a state of security is achieved, they are commanded to remember and glorify Allah, acknowledging that He has granted them knowledge and guidance that they did not possess before.
orig: فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله كما علمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون

translation: And those of you who die and leave behind wives - for their wives is a bequest: maintenance for a year without turning [them] out. But if they leave [of their own accord], then there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable way. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse outlines the Islamic guidelines regarding the maintenance and inheritance rights of widows. It establishes that a deceased husband must provide for his wife's maintenance for a year after his death, without forcing her to leave the marital home. However, if the widow chooses to remarry or leave of her own accord, there is no blame on the heirs. This reflects the Qur'an's emphasis on compassion, fairness, and the protection of widows' rights, while also respecting their autonomy and choices.
orig: والذين يتوفون منكم ويذرون أزواجا وصية لأزواجهم متاعا إلى الحول غير إخراج فإن خرجن فلا جناح عليكم في ما فعلن في أنفسهن من معروف والله عزيز حكيم

translation: And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of the righteous to provide for divorced women in a manner that is considered acceptable and reasonable. It establishes a moral obligation upon the community to ensure that divorced women are taken care of and not left without means of support.
orig: وللمطلقات متاع بالمعروف حقا على المتقين

translation: Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you might use reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of using one's intellect to understand the signs (ayat) of Allah revealed in the Qur'an. It encourages people to ponder and reflect upon the divine teachings, so that they may gain deeper insight and wisdom.
orig: كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تعقلون

translation: Have you not considered those who left their homes in many thousands, fearing death? Allah said to them, "Die," and then He restored them to life. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of the people do not show gratitude.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and mercy of Allah. It describes a group of people who fled their homes out of fear of death, but Allah commanded them to die, and then He restored them to life. This demonstrates Allah's absolute control over life and death, and His ability to bring people back to life after they have died. The verse also emphasizes that Allah is full of bounty and grace towards humanity, but most people do not show gratitude for this. The interpretation suggests that this verse is a reminder of Allah's sovereignty and the importance of being thankful for His blessings.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين خرجوا من ديارهم وهم ألوف حذر الموت فقال لهم الله موتوا ثم أحياهم إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: And fight in the cause of Allah and know that Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse calls upon believers to strive and fight in the cause of Allah, which can be understood as defending the faith, fighting oppression, and upholding justice. The verse also reminds us that Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, emphasizing that our actions and intentions are known to Him and that we will be held accountable for them.
orig: وقاتلوا في سبيل الله واعلموا أن الله سميع عليم

translation: Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? And it is Allah who withholds and grants abundance, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to make charitable donations, which are likened to a "goodly loan" to Allah. The promise is that Allah will multiply the reward for such donations many times over. The verse also reminds that Allah is the ultimate provider of wealth and that all will return to Him in the Hereafter.
orig: من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا فيضاعفه له أضعافا كثيرة والله يقبض ويبسط وإليه ترجعون

translation: Have you not considered the assembly of the Children of Israel after [the time of] Moses when they said to a prophet of theirs, "Appoint for us a king, that we may fight in the way of Allah"? He said, "Would you perhaps, if fighting was prescribed for you, not fight?" They said, "And why should we not fight in the cause of Allah when we have been driven out from our homes and from our children?" But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except for a few of them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reluctance of the Israelites to fight in the cause of Allah, despite their initial request for a king to lead them in battle. The verse suggests that the Israelites were more concerned with their own comfort and safety than with fulfilling their religious duty to defend their faith. The verse emphasizes that Allah is aware of the wrongdoers, implying that those who shirk their responsibilities will be held accountable.
orig: ألم تر إلى الملإ من بني إسرائيل من بعد موسى إذ قالوا لنبي لهم ابعث لنا ملكا نقاتل في سبيل الله قال هل عسيتم إن كتب عليكم القتال ألا تقاتلوا قالوا وما لنا ألا نقاتل في سبيل الله وقد أخرجنا من ديارنا وأبنائنا فلما كتب عليهم القتال تولوا إلا قليلا منهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: And their prophet said to them, "Indeed, Allah has appointed for you Talut as a king." They said, "How can he have kingship over us while we are more worthy of kingship than him and he has not been given any measure of wealth?" [The prophet] said, "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and has increased him abundantly in knowledge and stature. And Allah gives His sovereignty to whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing [in favor] and all-Knowing."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the appointment of Talut (Saul) as the king over the Israelites, despite their objections. The key points are: 1) Allah has chosen Talut to be the king, not the people; 2) Talut has been given additional knowledge and physical stature by Allah, making him more qualified than the people; 3) Allah gives kingship to whomever He pleases, not based on the people's preferences. This emphasizes that Allah's wisdom and plan supersede human desires and perceptions of worthiness.
orig: وقال لهم نبيهم إن الله قد بعث لكم طالوت ملكا قالوا أنى يكون له الملك علينا ونحن أحق بالملك منه ولم يؤت سعة من المال قال إن الله اصطفاه عليكم وزاده بسطة في العلم والجسم والله يؤتي ملكه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: And their prophet said to them, "Indeed, the sign of his kingship is that the ark will come to you in which is assurance from your Lord and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron had left, the angels carrying it. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers."
interpretation: This verse is describing the sign that will be given to the Israelites to confirm the kingship of their prophet. The sign is the arrival of the Ark of the Covenant, which contains the remnants of the legacy of Moses and Aaron, carried by angels. This sign is meant to affirm the truth of the prophet's message and to strengthen the faith of the believers among the Israelites.
orig: وقال لهم نبيهم إن آية ملكه أن يأتيكم التابوت فيه سكينة من ربكم وبقية مما ترك آل موسى وآل هارون تحمله الملائكة إن في ذلك لآية لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And when Talut (Saul) set out with the army, he said: "Verily! Allah will try you by a river. So whoever drinks thereof, he is not of me, and whoever tastes it not, he is of me, except him who takes (thereof) in the hollow of his hand." Yet, they drank thereof, all, except a few of them. So when he had crossed it (the river), he and those who believed with him, they said: "We have no power this day against Goliath and his hosts." But those who knew with certainty that they were to meet Allah, said: "How often a small group overcame a mighty host by Allah's Leave?" And Allah is with the patient ones.
interpretation: This verse describes a trial that the army of Prophet Talut (Saul) faced before the battle against Goliath. The trial involved a river, and those who drank from it were deemed unfit to fight, except for a few who took only a handful of water. This was a test of their discipline and faith. The verse then contrasts the reaction of those who doubted their ability to overcome Goliath's army with the reaction of those who had certainty in Allah's help and victory. It emphasizes that Allah's help and patience are with the believers, even when they face seemingly overwhelming odds.
orig: فلما فصل طالوت بالجنود قال إن الله مبتليكم بنهر فمن شرب منه فليس مني ومن لم يطعمه فإنه مني إلا من اغترف غرفة بيده فشربوا منه إلا قليلا منهم فلما جاوزه هو والذين آمنوا معه قالوا لا طاقة لنا اليوم بجالوت وجنوده قال الذين يظنون أنهم ملاقو الله كم من فئة قليلة غلبت فئة كثيرة بإذن الله والله مع الصابرين

translation: And when they went forth to [meet] Goliath and his soldiers, they said, "Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people."
interpretation: This verse reflects the believers' supplication to Allah for steadfastness, patience, and divine assistance in their confrontation with the disbelieving enemy. It highlights the importance of relying on Allah and seeking His help in the face of adversity, rather than solely relying on one's own strength or resources.
orig: ولما برزوا لجالوت وجنوده قالوا ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وثبت أقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين

translation: And they defeated them by the permission of Allah. And David killed Goliath, and Allah gave him the kingship and wisdom and taught him from that which He wills. And if it were not for Allah's repelling some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted, but Allah is full of bounty to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power of Allah's permission and guidance in enabling the believers to defeat their enemies. It also emphasizes that all blessings, such as kingship and wisdom, come from Allah, who teaches and bestows them upon whomever He wills. Additionally, the verse underscores the importance of Allah's intervention in maintaining balance and preventing corruption on earth, as He uses some people to repel others. This demonstrates Allah's boundless grace and favor upon all of creation.
orig: فهزموهم بإذن الله وقتل داوود جالوت وآتاه الله الملك والحكمة وعلمه مما يشاء ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض لفسدت الأرض ولكن الله ذو فضل على العالمين

translation: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you, [O Muhammad], in truth. And indeed, you are from among the messengers.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'anic verses being recited to the Prophet Muhammad are the divine revelations of Allah, and that the Prophet is truly one of the messengers sent by God to guide humanity.
orig: تلك آيات الله نتلوها عليك بالحق وإنك لمن المرسلين

translation: Those were the messengers. We have preferred some of them over others. Among them are those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised some of them in degree. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs, and We supported him with the Pure Spirit. If Allah had willed, those [generations] succeeding them would not have fought each other after the clear proofs had come to them. But they differed, and some of them believed and some of them disbelieved. And if Allah had willed, they would not have fought each other, but Allah does what He intends.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between the messengers of Allah, and how some were granted higher ranks and closer communication with God. It also emphasizes that even after the clear proofs and guidance were provided, people still differed in their beliefs and engaged in conflict. However, this was not Allah's ultimate desire, as He has the power to prevent such divisions if He so willed. The verse underscores that Allah's will prevails, and He acts according to His wisdom and purpose.
orig: تلك الرسل فضلنا بعضهم على بعض منهم من كلم الله ورفع بعضهم درجات وآتينا عيسى ابن مريم البينات وأيدناه بروح القدس ولو شاء الله ما اقتتل الذين من بعدهم من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات ولكن اختلفوا فمنهم من آمن ومنهم من كفر ولو شاء الله ما اقتتلوا ولكن الله يفعل ما يريد

translation: O you who have believed, spend [in the way of Allah ] from that which We have provided for you before a Day comes in which there is no exchange [i.e., ransom] and no [personal] friendships and no intercession. And the disbelievers - they are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to spend and give in the way of Allah before the Day of Judgment arrives, when there will be no opportunity to make amends or seek intercession. It emphasizes the importance of charitable giving and righteous deeds during one's lifetime, as the disbelievers who do not heed this call will be the true wrongdoers on that day.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا مما رزقناكم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا بيع فيه ولا خلة ولا شفاعة والكافرون هم الظالمون

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is present before them and what is behind them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Throne extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute sovereignty and divinity of Allah. It emphasizes that He alone is the true God, the Ever-Living and the Sustainer of all existence. Allah is free from any human weaknesses like drowsiness or sleep, and He has dominion over all that exists in the heavens and the earth. No one can intercede with Him except by His permission, as He has perfect knowledge of the past, present, and future. His power and knowledge are limitless, and the preservation of the heavens and the earth does not burden Him in the least. This verse highlights the supreme majesty and greatness of Allah, the One worthy of all worship and obedience.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم لا تأخذه سنة ولا نوم له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض من ذا الذي يشفع عنده إلا بإذنه يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يحيطون بشيء من علمه إلا بما شاء وسع كرسيه السماوات والأرض ولا يئوده حفظهما وهو العلي العظيم

translation: There is no compulsion in religion. The right course has become clear from the wrong. So whoever disbelieves in Taghut and believes in Allah has grasped the most trustworthy handhold with no break in it. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that faith in Islam is a matter of personal choice, not compulsion. It highlights that the path of guidance (Rushd) has become clear from the path of misguidance (Ghayy). Whoever rejects false deities (Taghut) and believes in Allah has firmly grasped the most secure and unbreakable connection (Al-'Urwah Al-Wuthqa) to Allah. This is because Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, and He will guide and protect those who believe in Him.
orig: لا إكراه في الدين قد تبين الرشد من الغي فمن يكفر بالطاغوت ويؤمن بالله فقد استمسك بالعروة الوثقى لا انفصام لها والله سميع عليم

translation: Allah is the Protector of those who have faith: from the depths of darkness He will lead them forth into light. Of those who reject faith, the patrons are the Evil Ones: from light they will lead them forth into the depths of darkness. They will be companions of the fire, to dwell therein (for ever).
interpretation: This verse contrasts the fate of those who have faith in Allah versus those who reject faith. The believers are guided by Allah from the darkness of ignorance and sin into the light of faith and righteousness. In contrast, the disbelievers are led by the forces of evil from the light of guidance into the depths of darkness and misguidance. The ultimate destination for the disbelievers is the Fire of Hell, where they will abide eternally.
orig: الله ولي الذين آمنوا يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور والذين كفروا أولياؤهم الطاغوت يخرجونهم من النور إلى الظلمات أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord [merely] because Allah had given him kingship? [And yet], when Abraham said, "My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death," he [the king] said, "I give life and cause death." [Abraham] said, "Indeed, Allah brings up the sun from the east, so bring it up from the west." Then the disbeliever was overwhelmed [by astonishment], and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the debate between Abraham and a powerful ruler who claimed to have the power of life and death. Abraham refutes the ruler's claim by pointing out that only Allah has the power to give life and take it away. He then challenges the ruler to demonstrate his power by making the sun rise from the west, which the ruler is unable to do. This demonstrates the futility of claiming divine powers and the importance of acknowledging the sovereignty of Allah, the true Creator and Sustainer of all life.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه أن آتاه الله الملك إذ قال إبراهيم ربي الذي يحيي ويميت قال أنا أحيي وأميت قال إبراهيم فإن الله يأتي بالشمس من المشرق فأت بها من المغرب فبهت الذي كفر والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Or [the state of such a person] is like the one who passed by a township which had fallen into ruin. He said, "How will Allah bring this to life after its death?" So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years; then He revived him. [Allah] said, "How long have you remained?" [The man] said, "I have remained a day or part of a day." [Allah] said, "Rather, you have remained one hundred years. Look at your food and your drink; it has not rotted. And look at your donkey; and We will make you a sign for the people. And look at the bones [of the donkey] - how We assemble them and then We cover them with flesh." And when it became clear to him, he said, "I know that Allah is over all things competent."
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's power over life and death, and His ability to resurrect the dead. The man who passed by the ruined township was amazed at the idea of Allah bringing it back to life after its destruction. As a lesson, Allah caused the man to die for a hundred years, then revived him, to demonstrate that resurrection is within Allah's power. The man's food and drink remained untouched, and his donkey was also resurrected, showing that nothing is impossible for Allah. This verse emphasizes the importance of believing in Allah's omnipotence and the reality of the Hereafter.
orig: أو كالذي مر على قرية وهي خاوية على عروشها قال أنى يحيي هذه الله بعد موتها فأماته الله مائة عام ثم بعثه قال كم لبثت قال لبثت يوما أو بعض يوم قال بل لبثت مائة عام فانظر إلى طعامك وشرابك لم يتسنه وانظر إلى حمارك ولنجعلك آية للناس وانظر إلى العظام كيف ننشزها ثم نكسوها لحما فلما تبين له قال أعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." [Allah] said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied." [Allah] said, "Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then [after slaughtering them] place on each mountain a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise."
interpretation: This verse illustrates Abraham`s desire to understand the power of God in giving life to the dead. Though Abraham already believed, he sought a deeper understanding and reassurance of God`s abilities. The instruction to take four birds, slaughter them, and scatter their parts on the mountains, then call them back, was a demonstration of God`s power to give life. This teaches that God is all-powerful and all-wise, and that true faith requires not just belief, but a desire to deepen one`s understanding of the divine.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب أرني كيف تحيي الموتى قال أولم تؤمن قال بلى ولكن ليطمئن قلبي قال فخذ أربعة من الطير فصرهن إليك ثم اجعل على كل جبل منهن جزءا ثم ادعهن يأتينك سعيا واعلم أن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a seed [of grain] which grows seven spikes; in each spike is a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies [His reward] for whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse provides an analogy to illustrate the virtue of spending one's wealth in the way of Allah. Just as a single seed can produce a bountiful harvest, the act of charitable giving can yield manifold rewards from Allah. This emphasizes the immense generosity and grace of Allah, who multiplies the rewards for those who spend in His cause. The interpretation suggests that the faithful should be encouraged to give freely, as Allah is all-encompassing in His knowledge and power to bless those who do so.
orig: مثل الذين ينفقون أموالهم في سبيل الله كمثل حبة أنبتت سبع سنابل في كل سنبلة مائة حبة والله يضاعف لمن يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: Those who spend their wealth [in Allah's way] and then do not follow up what they have spent with reminders [of it] or [other] injury, for them their reward is with their Lord, and there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to spend their wealth in the way of Allah without expecting any praise or acknowledgment from others. It promises that those who do so will be rewarded by Allah, and will not have to fear or grieve, as Allah will take care of them. The key message is that charitable giving should be done sincerely for the sake of Allah, without any ulterior motives or desire for recognition.
orig: الذين ينفقون أموالهم في سبيل الله ثم لا يتبعون ما أنفقوا منا ولا أذى لهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Kind speech and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. And Allah is Free of need and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to engage in kind speech and forgiveness rather than charity that is followed by harm or injury to the recipient. The key message is that the quality of one's actions is more important than the quantity, and that Allah is self-sufficient and merciful, not in need of our material offerings but appreciative of our sincere intentions and good character.
orig: قول معروف ومغفرة خير من صدقة يتبعها أذى والله غني حليم

translation: O you who believe! Do not invalidate your charities by reproach and injury, like one who spends his wealth to be seen by the people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day. His example is like a [hard] smooth rock upon which is [some] dust and is hit by a downpour - and it leaves it bare. [No wealth remains with them.] They are unable to keep anything of what they have earned. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against invalidating their charitable acts by reminding the recipient of the favor or causing them harm. It condemns those who give charitably only to be seen by others, rather than out of sincere faith in Allah and the Hereafter. Their deeds are likened to a barren rock, which cannot retain any vegetation despite heavy rain, just as the wealth of the ostentatious giver cannot benefit them. The verse emphasizes that Allah does not guide those who disbelieve, as their actions are devoid of true faith and sincerity.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى كالذي ينفق ماله رئاء الناس ولا يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فمثله كمثل صفوان عليه تراب فأصابه وابل فتركه صلدا لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا والله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking means to the pleasure of Allah and assuring [stability for] themselves is like a garden on high ground which is hit by a downpour - so it yields its fruits in double. And [even] if it is not hit by a downpour, then a [gentle] rain. And Allah, of what you do, is Seeing.
interpretation: This verse draws a beautiful analogy to illustrate the rewards of spending one's wealth for the pleasure of Allah. Just as a garden on high ground that receives heavy rainfall yields its fruits in double, those who spend their wealth seeking Allah's pleasure will be rewarded abundantly, even if their deeds do not immediately bear fruit. The verse emphasizes that Allah is All-Seeing of our actions, and will bestow His blessings accordingly.
orig: ومثل الذين ينفقون أموالهم ابتغاء مرضات الله وتثبيتا من أنفسهم كمثل جنة بربوة أصابها وابل فآتت أكلها ضعفين فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: Would any of you wish to have a garden of palm trees and vines with streams flowing beneath it, with all kinds of fruits for him therein, and he is given old age, with weak offspring, then a whirlwind with fire in it strikes it so it is burnt? Thus does Allah make clear to you [His] verses that you might give thought.
interpretation: This verse presents a metaphorical scenario to illustrate the transience of worldly pleasures and the importance of focusing on the hereafter. The lush garden with abundant fruits and flowing streams represents the material comforts and blessings that one may desire in this life. However, the old age and weak offspring suggest the inevitable decline and vulnerability that comes with this worldly existence. The sudden whirlwind and fire that destroys the garden symbolize the unpredictable and destructive nature of life's trials and tribulations. The verse encourages the reader to reflect on Allah's signs and lessons, as conveyed through this parable, in order to gain wisdom and perspective on the true purpose of life.
orig: أيود أحدكم أن تكون له جنة من نخيل وأعناب تجري من تحتها الأنهار له فيها من كل الثمرات وأصابه الكبر وله ذرية ضعفاء فأصابها إعصار فيه نار فاحترقت كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تتفكرون

translation: O you who believe, spend from the good things you have earned and from that which We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim toward the defective therefrom, spending [from that], while you would not take it [yourself] except with closed eyes. And know that Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to spend from the good and lawful provisions they have earned, and from what Allah has provided for them from the earth. It warns against spending from impure or unlawful sources, even if one would not accept such provisions for oneself. The verse emphasizes that Allah is self-sufficient and praiseworthy, and that believers should strive to please Him through their righteous conduct, including their spending habits.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أنفقوا من طيبات ما كسبتم ومما أخرجنا لكم من الأرض ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون ولستم بآخذيه إلا أن تغمضوا فيه واعلموا أن الله غني حميد

translation: Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality, but Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse warns against the deceptive promises of Satan, who tries to instill fear of poverty and incite people to engage in immoral and sinful acts. In contrast, Allah promises forgiveness and abundant blessings for those who turn to Him. The verse emphasizes that Allah is all-encompassing in His knowledge and His mercy, and that one should not be deceived by Satan's empty threats.
orig: الشيطان يعدكم الفقر ويأمركم بالفحشاء والله يعدكم مغفرة منه وفضلا والله واسع عليم

translation: He gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good. And none will remember except those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that wisdom is a gift from God, bestowed upon those He chooses. Those who are granted wisdom have been given a great blessing, as wisdom leads to much good. However, only those with understanding and discernment will truly appreciate and benefit from this wisdom.
orig: يؤتي الحكمة من يشاء ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا وما يذكر إلا أولو الألباب

translation: And whatever you spend in expenditure or whatever you pledge as a vow - indeed, Allah knows it; and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and aware of every act of charity or vow made by believers. It also serves as a warning to those who do wrong, that they will have no helpers or supporters on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وما أنفقتم من نفقة أو نذرتم من نذر فإن الله يعلمه وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: If you disclose your charitable expenditures, it is good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you, and He will remove from you some of your misdeeds [thereby]. And Allah, with what you do, is [fully] Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse encourages the giving of charity, whether it is done openly or secretly. Openly giving charity is good, as it can inspire others to do the same. However, giving charity in secret, without seeking recognition, is even better. This is because the intention behind the act of charity is more important than the outward display. By giving in secret, one is doing it solely for the sake of pleasing Allah, without any worldly motives. Furthermore, such secret charity can help conceal one's sins and misdeeds, as Allah is aware of all that we do.
orig: إن تبدوا الصدقات فنعما هي وإن تخفوها وتؤتوها الفقراء فهو خير لكم ويكفر عنكم من سيئاتكم والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: It is not [proper] upon you [i.e., Prophet Muhammad] to guide them [i.e., the people], but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever you spend in good, it is [of benefit] to yourselves, and you do not spend except seeking the countenance of Allah. And whatever you spend in good - it will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that guidance is in the hands of Allah, not the Prophet. It encourages believers to spend in good causes, not for worldly gain, but solely to seek Allah's pleasure. The verse also promises that any good spending will be fully rewarded by Allah without any injustice.
orig: ليس عليك هداهم ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء وما تنفقوا من خير فلأنفسكم وما تنفقون إلا ابتغاء وجه الله وما تنفقوا من خير يوف إليكم وأنتم لا تظلمون

translation: For the poor who have been restricted [in the cause] of Allah , unable to move about in the land. An ignorant [person] would think them self-sufficient because of their restraint, [but] you will know them by their [characteristic] sign. They do not ask people persistently. And whatever you spend of good - indeed, Allah is Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the poor who are restricted in their ability to move about and earn a living, due to their dedication to the cause of Allah. They may appear self-sufficient to the ignorant, but those who are aware can recognize them by their signs. These people do not persistently beg from others, and whatever good they are given, Allah is aware of it. The verse emphasizes the virtue of these poor individuals and the importance of supporting them, even though their situation may not be outwardly apparent.
orig: للفقراء الذين أحصروا في سبيل الله لا يستطيعون ضربا في الأرض يحسبهم الجاهل أغنياء من التعفف تعرفهم بسيماهم لا يسألون الناس إلحافا وما تنفقوا من خير فإن الله به عليم

translation: Those who spend their wealth [in Allah's way] by night and by day, secretly and publicly - they will have their reward with their Lord. And no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to spend their wealth in the way of Allah, whether it is done openly or secretly. The reward for such charitable acts is that the believers will have no fear or grief, as Allah will protect and care for them. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of selfless giving and the spiritual benefits it brings.
orig: الذين ينفقون أموالهم بالليل والنهار سرا وعلانية فلهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those who consume interest will not stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity. That is because they say, "Trade is [just] like interest." But Allah has permitted trade and has forbidden interest. So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists may have what is past, and his affair rests with Allah. But whoever returns [to dealing in interest or usury] - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide eternally therein.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of usury or interest-based transactions, and highlights the grave consequences of engaging in such activities. The metaphor of one who is "beaten by Satan into insanity" emphasizes the delusional and irrational nature of those who justify interest as being equivalent to trade. The verse makes a clear distinction between the permissibility of trade and the prohibition of interest, warning those who persist in usury that they will be condemned to the eternal Fire. The verse encourages those who have received guidance to desist from such practices and seek forgiveness, as their ultimate fate rests with Allah.
orig: الذين يأكلون الربا لا يقومون إلا كما يقوم الذي يتخبطه الشيطان من المس ذلك بأنهم قالوا إنما البيع مثل الربا وأحل الله البيع وحرم الربا فمن جاءه موعظة من ربه فانتهى فله ما سلف وأمره إلى الله ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: Allah destroys interest and gives increase for charities. And Allah does not like every sinning disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah does not approve of usury or interest-based transactions, but instead encourages charitable giving, which He will bless and increase. It also warns that Allah does not love those who persistently disbelieve and commit sins.
orig: يمحق الله الربا ويربي الصدقات والله لا يحب كل كفار أثيم

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and establish prayer and give zakah will have their reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have true faith in God, do good deeds, perform their religious obligations like prayer and charitable giving, will be rewarded by God and will be free from fear and sorrow in the hereafter. It highlights the importance of both belief and righteous action as the path to attaining God's pleasure and eternal bliss.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة لهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: O you who believe! Fear Allah and give up what remains [due to you] of interest, if you should be believers.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to refrain from usury or interest-based transactions, as they are incompatible with the principles of Islamic faith. It calls upon the faithful to turn away from any remaining interest-based practices, as they are displeasing to Allah and contrary to the beliefs of true believers.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And if you do not, then be informed of a war [against you] from Allah and His Messenger. But if you repent, you will have [the rights to] the principal [i.e., capital] of your wealth. You do not wrong, nor are you wronged.
interpretation: This verse warns those who refuse to pay back their debts or fulfill their financial obligations that they will face the wrath of Allah and His Messenger. However, it also offers a way out - if they repent and pay back what they owe, they will be entitled to keep the principal amount of their wealth without being wronged or wronging others.
orig: فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم لا تظلمون ولا تظلمون

translation: And if someone is in hardship, then [let there be] postponement until [a time of] ease. And if you [choose to] give charity, it is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse encourages compassion and leniency towards those who are in financial difficulty. It instructs that if someone is facing hardship, they should be granted an extension or postponement of their debt until they are in a better financial position. Additionally, it emphasizes that giving charity is better for the giver, if they only understood the spiritual and material benefits it brings.
orig: وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة وأن تصدقوا خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah. Then every soul will be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse reminds us to be mindful of the Day of Judgment, when we will all be held accountable for our actions in this life. It emphasizes that on that day, each person will be fairly compensated for their deeds, without any injustice or unfairness. This serves as a call to live a righteous life and prepare for the ultimate reckoning before God.
orig: واتقوا يوما ترجعون فيه إلى الله ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: O you who believe! When you contract a debt for a fixed term, write it down. And let a scribe write it down in justice between you. Let not the scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him. So let him write. And let the one who has the obligation (i.e. the debtor) dictate. And let him fear Allah, his Lord, and diminish not anything of it. But if the one who has the obligation is of limited understanding or weak or is unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate in justice. And get two witnesses out of your own men. And if there are not two men (available), then a man and two women, such as you agree for witnesses, so that if one of them (two women) errs, the other can remind her. And the witnesses should not refuse when they are called on (for evidence). And be not averse to writing down (the contract) for a fixed period, be it small or big, and include the time of its repayment. That is more just in the sight of Allah and stronger for testimony and more convenient to prevent doubt among yourselves, except when it is a present trade which you carry out on the spot among yourselves, in that case there is no sin on you if you do not write it down. But take witnesses whenever you make a commercial contract. And let no scribe and no witness suffer harm, and if you do (such harm), it would be wickedness in you. And fear Allah; and Allah teaches you. And Allah is All-Knower of each and everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of proper documentation and witnessing in financial transactions, in order to prevent disputes and maintain justice. It instructs believers to write down their debts, have a scribe record the transaction, and provide witnesses - either two men or one man and two women. The purpose is to ensure the accuracy of the record and prevent any party from being harmed or taken advantage of. The verse also cautions against refusing to write down the contract or to act as a witness, as that would be considered a sin. Overall, the interpretation highlights the Qur'an's emphasis on transparency, fairness, and the preservation of rights in financial dealings between Muslims.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى فاكتبوه وليكتب بينكم كاتب بالعدل ولا يأب كاتب أن يكتب كما علمه الله فليكتب وليملل الذي عليه الحق وليتق الله ربه ولا يبخس منه شيئا فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها أو ضعيفا أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو فليملل وليه بالعدل واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم فإن لم يكونا رجلين فرجل وامرأتان ممن ترضون من الشهداء أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا ولا تسأموا أن تكتبوه صغيرا أو كبيرا إلى أجله ذلكم أقسط عند الله وأقوم للشهادة وأدنى ألا ترتابوا إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة تديرونها بينكم فليس عليكم جناح ألا تكتبوها وأشهدوا إذا تبايعتم ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد وإن تفعلوا فإنه فسوق بكم واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then a security deposit [should be] taken. And if one of you entrusts another, then let him who is entrusted discharge his trust [faithfully] and let him fear Allah, his Lord. And do not conceal testimony. And whoever conceals it - his heart is indeed sinful, and Allah is Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty, trust, and transparency in financial and legal transactions, even when traveling or in the absence of a scribe. It instructs that if a written contract is not possible, a security deposit should be taken as a guarantee. Further, it commands that if one person entrusts another, the trustee must fulfill the trust faithfully and be mindful of Allah. The verse also prohibits concealing testimony, warning that to do so is a sin, for Allah is All-Knowing of our actions.
orig: وإن كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كاتبا فرهان مقبوضة فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته وليتق الله ربه ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه والله بما تعملون عليم

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will account for it. Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all creation, both in the heavens and on earth. It reminds us that Allah is aware of everything, even the thoughts and intentions we keep hidden within ourselves. Ultimately, we will be held accountable for our actions, and Allah alone has the authority to forgive or punish as He wills. This verse underscores the need for believers to be conscious of their thoughts and deeds, as Allah has complete control and knowledge over all things.
orig: لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers, [saying], "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say, "We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the [final] destination."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of faith among the believers, who do not discriminate between the different messengers of God. They accept all of God's messengers and scriptures, and pledge to obey and seek forgiveness from the Lord. This reflects the importance of having a comprehensive and unwavering faith in the divine, without any doubts or reservations.
orig: آمن الرسول بما أنزل إليه من ربه والمؤمنون كل آمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله لا نفرق بين أحد من رسله وقالوا سمعنا وأطعنا غفرانك ربنا وإليك المصير

translation: Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. [They prayed]: "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah does not burden a person beyond their capacity. Each person is responsible for their own actions and will be held accountable accordingly. The verse also includes a supplication, where the believers ask Allah not to hold them accountable for unintentional mistakes, and to not burden them with more than they can bear. They seek Allah's forgiveness, mercy and protection against the disbelievers. The overall message is one of divine justice, compassion and the importance of relying on Allah.
orig: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به واعف عنا واغفر لنا وارحمنا أنت مولانا فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These are among the 'mysterious letters' (al-muqatta'at) that appear at the beginning of some Qur'anic chapters. Their precise meaning is not entirely clear, but they are believed to be a part of the divine wisdom and knowledge contained within the Qur'an. They serve as a reminder of the profound and inscrutable nature of the Qur'anic revelation.
orig: الم

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence.
interpretation: This verse affirms the oneness and sovereignty of Allah, the Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It emphasizes that Allah alone is worthy of worship and that He is the source of all life and the one who maintains and governs all existence. This highlights the importance of belief in the uncompromising monotheism of Islam and the need to submit to Allah's will.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم

translation: The Book has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], in truth, confirming what was before it, and He revealed the Torah and the Gospel.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an is the final revelation from God, which confirms and fulfills the previous scriptures of the Torah and the Gospel. It highlights the divine origin and truthfulness of the Qur'an, which serves as a guide and a testament to the authenticity of the earlier revealed books.
orig: نزل عليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه وأنزل التوراة والإنجيل

translation: Before this was, as a guidance to people, and He has sent down the Criterion. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah will have a severe punishment, and Allah is Exalted in Might, the Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Quran is a guidance for all people, and it serves as a criterion to distinguish between truth and falsehood. It warns that those who reject the signs and revelations of Allah will face a severe punishment, as Allah is Mighty and the One who inflicts retribution on those who defy Him.
orig: من قبل هدى للناس وأنزل الفرقان إن الذين كفروا بآيات الله لهم عذاب شديد والله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: Indeed, Allah is not unaware of what you do
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and nothing is hidden from Him, whether on Earth or in the heavens. It serves as a reminder that our actions and thoughts are known to Allah, and we will be held accountable for them.
orig: إن الله لا يخفى عليه شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء

translation: It is He who forms you in the wombs as He wills. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and wisdom of God in creating and shaping human beings. It affirms that God alone has the authority to determine the form and nature of each individual, as He wills. This serves to remind us of God's sovereignty and the need to submit to His will, as He is the Exalted in Might and the Wise.
orig: هو الذي يصوركم في الأرحام كيف يشاء لا إله إلا هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: He it is who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book; in it are verses [that are] precise - they are the foundation of the Book - and others unspecific. As for those in whose hearts is deviation [from truth], they will follow of its unspecific part, seeking discord and seeking an interpretation [suitable to them]. And no one knows its [true] interpretation except Allah. But those firm in knowledge say, "We believe in it. All [of it] is from our Lord." And no one will be reminded except those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse highlights the nature of the Qur'an, with some verses being clear and unambiguous ("precise"), forming the foundation of the Book, while others are more ambiguous or open to interpretation ("unspecific"). It warns against those who have deviation in their hearts, who follow the ambiguous verses in order to sow discord and find interpretations that suit their own desires. The verse emphasizes that only Allah knows the true interpretation of the ambiguous verses, and that those who are firmly grounded in knowledge affirm their belief in the entire Qur'an as being from their Lord. The verse concludes by stating that only those of understanding will truly take heed and be reminded by the Qur'an.
orig: هو الذي أنزل عليك الكتاب منه آيات محكمات هن أم الكتاب وأخر متشابهات فأما الذين في قلوبهم زيغ فيتبعون ما تشابه منه ابتغاء الفتنة وابتغاء تأويله وما يعلم تأويله إلا الله والراسخون في العلم يقولون آمنا به كل من عند ربنا وما يذكر إلا أولو الألباب

translation: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.
interpretation: This verse expresses a supplication to God, asking Him to keep the hearts of the believers steadfast in their faith and to grant them His mercy. It reflects the recognition that guidance comes from God alone, and the need for His continued support and blessing to remain on the right path. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of relying on God's mercy and grace, as He is the ultimate Bestower of all blessings.
orig: ربنا لا تزغ قلوبنا بعد إذ هديتنا وهب لنا من لدنك رحمة إنك أنت الوهاب

translation: Our Lord, indeed You are the Gatherer of mankind for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the One who will gather all of humanity on the Day of Judgment, a day about which there can be no doubt. It affirms that Allah never breaks His promise and that the Day of Judgment will surely come to pass as He has decreed.
orig: ربنا إنك جامع الناس ليوم لا ريب فيه إن الله لا يخلف الميعاد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - never will their wealth or their children avail them against Allah at all, and it is they who are fuel for the Fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the wealth and children of those who reject faith in Allah will not protect them from Allah's punishment. Their wealth and children will be of no use to them on the Day of Judgment, and they will be the fuel for the eternal Fire of Hell.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا وأولئك هم وقود النار

translation: Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, they denied Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins. And Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse draws a parallel between the fate of the people of Pharaoh and those who came before them, who all rejected the signs and messages of Allah. As a result, Allah punished them for their sins. This serves as a warning that those who deny the truth and persist in their wrongdoing will face the severe consequences of Allah's retribution.
orig: كدأب آل فرعون والذين من قبلهم كذبوا بآياتنا فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم والله شديد العقاب

translation: Say to those who disbelieve, "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject faith in God and His message. It conveys that the disbelievers will ultimately be defeated and brought to the eternal punishment of Hell, which is a terrible destination. The interpretation suggests that those who turn away from the truth will face the consequences of their choices in the Hereafter.
orig: قل للذين كفروا ستغلبون وتحشرون إلى جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: There has already been for you a sign in the two armies [who] met - one fighting in the cause of Allah and another of disbelievers. They saw them [to be] twice their [own] number by [their] eyesight. But Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith and reliance on Allah in the face of adversity. It reminds believers that even when they are outnumbered by their enemies, Allah can grant them victory through His divine support. The lesson here is that true strength comes from one's faith and trust in Allah, not from material might or numbers alone. This verse encourages believers to steadfastly fight for the cause of Allah, knowing that He will aid them in their struggle.
orig: قد كان لكم آية في فئتين التقتا فئة تقاتل في سبيل الله وأخرى كافرة يرونهم مثليهم رأي العين والله يؤيد بنصره من يشاء إن في ذلك لعبرة لأولي الأبصار

translation: Beautified for people is the love of that which they desire - of women and sons, heaped-up sums of gold and silver, fine branded horses, and cattle and [cultivated] land. That is the enjoyment of worldly life, but Allah has with Him the best return [i.e., Paradise].
interpretation: This verse highlights the temporary and fleeting nature of the worldly pleasures and desires, such as the love of women, children, wealth, and material possessions. While these things may be attractive and enjoyable in this life, they are ultimately transient and cannot provide true and lasting fulfillment. The verse encourages people to look beyond the allure of the material world and to seek the eternal rewards that Allah has promised in the Hereafter, which are far superior to the temporary pleasures of this life.
orig: زين للناس حب الشهوات من النساء والبنين والقناطير المقنطرة من الذهب والفضة والخيل المسومة والأنعام والحرث ذلك متاع الحياة الدنيا والله عنده حسن المآب

translation: Say, "Shall I inform you of [something] better than that?
