For those who fear Allah will be gardens in the presence of their Lord beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and [there are] purified spouses for them and approval from Allah. And Allah is Seeing of [His] servants."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to seek the rewards of the Hereafter, which are far superior to the fleeting pleasures of this world. The interpretation suggests that those who fear and revere Allah will be granted eternal abode in the Gardens of Paradise, where they will live in peace and tranquility, surrounded by pure and righteous companions, and enjoying the pleasure and approval of Allah. This emphasizes the importance of piety, righteousness, and seeking the pleasure of Allah as the path to attaining the ultimate bliss in the Hereafter.
orig: قل أؤنبئكم بخير من ذلكم للذين اتقوا عند ربهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وأزواج مطهرة ورضوان من الله والله بصير بالعباد

translation: Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to seek forgiveness from Allah and protection from the punishment of the Fire. It highlights the importance of acknowledging one's sins and turning to Allah with humility and sincerity, seeking His mercy and guidance.
orig: الذين يقولون ربنا إننا آمنا فاغفر لنا ذنوبنا وقنا عذاب النار

translation: The patient, the truthful, the obedient, the spenders [in the way of Allah], and the ones who seek forgiveness before dawn.
interpretation: This verse highlights several virtuous qualities that are pleasing to Allah. The "patient" are those who endure trials and tribulations with steadfastness. The "truthful" are those who are honest and sincere in their words and deeds. The "obedient" are those who submit to Allah's commands. The "spenders" are those who give charitably from their wealth. The "ones who seek forgiveness before dawn" are those who humbly turn to Allah for forgiveness during the early hours of the morning. These are the types of people who are beloved to Allah and will be rewarded in the Hereafter.
orig: الصابرين والصادقين والقانتين والمنفقين والمستغفرين بالأسحار

translation: Allah witnesses that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge - [that He is] maintaining [creation] in justice. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and sovereignty of God. It states that God Himself, the angels, and those with knowledge all bear witness to the fact that there is no deity worthy of worship except for the One true God. This God is described as the Exalted in Might and the Wise, indicating His power, authority, and perfect wisdom in governing the universe. The verse also highlights that God maintains justice and equity in all of His creation, further reinforcing His divine attributes.
orig: شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو والملائكة وأولو العلم قائما بالقسط لا إله إلا هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam. And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the verses of Allah, then indeed, Allah is swift in [taking] account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the true religion in the sight of God is Islam. It states that even those who were given the previous scriptures (Jews and Christians) only differed after knowledge had come to them, out of jealousy and animosity towards one another. The verse warns that whoever rejects the signs and revelations of God will be held accountable swiftly by Him.
orig: إن الدين عند الله الإسلام وما اختلف الذين أوتوا الكتاب إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم ومن يكفر بآيات الله فإن الله سريع الحساب

translation: So if they argue with you, say, "I have submitted myself to Allah [in Islam], and [so have] those who follow me." And say to those who were given the Scripture and [to] the unlearned, "Have you submitted yourselves?" And if they submit [in Islam], they are [rightly] guided; but if they turn away, then upon you is only the [duty of] notification. And Allah is Seeing of [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers to remain steadfast in their submission to Allah, even in the face of arguments or opposition from others. It emphasizes that the true guidance comes from surrendering oneself to Allah, and that the role of the Prophet is to convey the message, not to force it upon anyone. The verse also highlights Allah's awareness and oversight of all His servants, underscoring the importance of sincere devotion and obedience to Him.
orig: فإن حاجوك فقل أسلمت وجهي لله ومن اتبعن وقل للذين أوتوا الكتاب والأميين أأسلمتم فإن أسلموا فقد اهتدوا وإن تولوا فإنما عليك البلاغ والله بصير بالعباد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah and kill the prophets without right and kill those who order justice among the people - give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who reject the signs and messages of Allah, and who unjustly kill the prophets and those who call for justice and righteousness among the people. It warns them of a severe punishment in the Hereafter for their transgressions.
orig: إن الذين يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون النبيين بغير حق ويقتلون الذين يأمرون بالقسط من الناس فبشرهم بعذاب أليم

translation: Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and for them there are no helpers.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have rejected faith and done evil deeds. Their actions in this life have been rendered futile and they will face no support or assistance on the Day of Judgment. They have lost both this life and the Hereafter.
orig: أولئك الذين حبطت أعمالهم في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who are invited to the Book of Allah that it should judge between them; then a party of them turns away, and they are averse?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question directed at the Prophet Muhammad, asking him if he has not seen those who were given a portion of the divine scriptures, such as the Jews and Christians, who are invited to refer to the Qur'an to settle their disputes, but a group of them turns away and rejects it, being averse to its teachings and guidance.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يدعون إلى كتاب الله ليحكم بينهم ثم يتولى فريق منهم وهم معرضون

translation: That is because they say, "Never will the Fire touch us except for [a few] numbered days," and [because] they are deluded in their religion.
interpretation: This verse refers to the false belief held by some people that they will only be punished in the Hellfire for a short, limited period of time, and that they will ultimately be forgiven and admitted to Paradise. The verse condemns this delusion, indicating that it is a result of their own fabrications and misguided understanding of their faith.
orig: ذلك بأنهم قالوا لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودات وغرهم في دينهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Then how [will it be] when We have gathered them for a Day about which there is no doubt? And every soul will be compensated [in full for] what it earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions in life. It conveys the message that on that Day, every person will receive the just consequences of their deeds, without any injustice or wrongdoing. The interpretation highlights the inevitability and fairness of the final reckoning, where each individual will be rewarded or punished according to their own merits.
orig: فكيف إذا جمعناهم ليوم لا ريب فيه ووفيت كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Say, "O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humiliate whom You will. In Your hand is [all] good. Indeed, You are over all things competent."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah. He is the sole Owner and Disposer of all authority and dominion in the universe. He bestows kingship and honor upon whomever He wills, and He can also take it away from whomever He wills. All good is in His Hands, and He has power over all things. This verse encourages believers to recognize Allah's supreme control and to submit to His will, as He is the ultimate source of all power and authority.
orig: قل اللهم مالك الملك تؤتي الملك من تشاء وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء وتعز من تشاء وتذل من تشاء بيدك الخير إنك على كل شيء قدير

translation: He causes the night to enter the day, and He causes the day to enter the night, and He brings the living out of the dead, and He brings the dead out of the living, and He provides for whom He wills without account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of God over the cycles of day and night, life and death, and the provision of sustenance. It highlights that God alone controls these natural phenomena and that His will and wisdom govern all aspects of existence. The interpretation suggests that we should humbly submit to God's authority and trust in His infinite knowledge and care for His creation.
orig: تولج الليل في النهار وتولج النهار في الليل وتخرج الحي من الميت وتخرج الميت من الحي وترزق من تشاء بغير حساب

translation: The believers do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. And whoever [of you] does that has nothing [i.e., no association] with Allah, except when taking precaution against them in prudence. And Allah warns you of Himself, and to Allah is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers not to form alliances or close relationships with those who disbelieve in Allah and reject the faith of Islam. The only exception is when a believer must outwardly show friendship or alliance to disbelievers in order to protect themselves or their faith. Ultimately, the believers must be mindful of Allah and return to Him.
orig: لا يتخذ المؤمنون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين ومن يفعل ذلك فليس من الله في شيء إلا أن تتقوا منهم تقاة ويحذركم الله نفسه وإلى الله المصير

translation: Say, "Whether you hide what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it. And He knows that which is in the heavens and that which is in the earth. And Allah is over all things competent."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and all-powerful. Whether we conceal our thoughts and feelings or openly express them, Allah is aware of them. Nothing is hidden from His knowledge, as He has knowledge of all that exists in the heavens and the earth. This serves as a reminder that we should be mindful of our actions and thoughts, as Allah has the power to hold us accountable for them.
orig: قل إن تخفوا ما في صدوركم أو تبدوه يعلمه الله ويعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present [before it], and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between itself and that [evil] was a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Day of Judgment, when each person will be held accountable for their deeds, both good and bad. The person will wish that they had distanced themselves from the evil they had done, highlighting the importance of being mindful of one's actions in this life. The verse also serves as a warning from Allah to His servants, reminding them of His power and the need to be righteous, while also emphasizing Allah's compassion and kindness towards His creation.
orig: يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه والله رءوف بالعباد

translation: Say, "If you love Allah, then follow me, [so] Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to follow the teachings and example of the Prophet Muhammad in order to earn Allah's love and forgiveness. It suggests that true love for Allah is demonstrated through obedience and adherence to His commands as revealed through the Prophet. By following the Prophet, believers can attain Allah's love, have their sins forgiven, and experience His mercy and compassion.
orig: قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: Say, "Obey Allah and the Messenger." But if they turn away - then indeed, Allah does not like the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to obey Allah and His Messenger. It warns that if they turn away from this command, then Allah does not love those who reject faith and disbelieve in Him.
orig: قل أطيعوا الله والرسول فإن تولوا فإن الله لا يحب الكافرين

translation: Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has chosen certain individuals and lineages to be honored and elevated above all others. The specific individuals mentioned - Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Imran - were selected by Allah to receive His special favor and guidance. This highlights the importance of these figures in Islam and the unique status they hold in the sight of the Divine.
orig: إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران على العالمين

translation: Offspring, some of them from others, and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all human beings are part of the same lineage, descended from a common ancestry. It highlights the interconnectedness of humanity, reminding us that we are all related and that Allah, as the All-Hearing and All-Knowing, is aware of our relationships and connections.
orig: ذرية بعضها من بعض والله سميع عليم

translation: When the wife of 'Imran said, "My Lord, indeed I have pledged to You what is in my womb, consecrated [for Your service], so accept this from me. Indeed, it is You who is the Hearing, the Knowing."
interpretation: This verse highlights the piety and devotion of the mother of Mary, the mother of Jesus. She had made a vow to dedicate her child to the service of God, even before the child was born. The verse conveys the importance of fulfilling one's vows and commitments to God, and the trust that God will accept such offerings, as He is All-Hearing and All-Knowing.
orig: إذ قالت امرأت عمران رب إني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا فتقبل مني إنك أنت السميع العليم

translation: And when she had given birth to her, she said, "My Lord, I have given birth to a female," and Allah was most knowing of what she had given birth to, "and the male is not like the female. And I have named her Mary, and I seek refuge for her in You and [for] her descendants from Satan, the expelled [from the mercy of Allah]."
interpretation: This verse speaks of the birth of the Prophet Maryam (Mary), peace be upon her. When she was born, her mother expressed her disappointment that the child was not a son, as sons were more highly valued in that society. However, Allah knows best what He has created, and the female is not inferior to the male. Maryam's mother then named her Maryam and sought Allah's protection for her and her descendants from the influence of Satan. This highlights the piety and devotion of Maryam's mother, and the special status of Maryam herself, who was chosen by Allah to be the mother of the Prophet Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him.
orig: فلما وضعتها قالت رب إني وضعتها أنثى والله أعلم بما وضعت وليس الذكر كالأنثى وإني سميتها مريم وإني أعيذها بك وذريتها من الشيطان الرجيم

translation: And her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good manner and put her in the care of Zechariah. Every time Zechariah entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found with her provision. [He] said, "O Mary, from where is this [coming] to you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account."
interpretation: This verse speaks of the miraculous upbringing of the Virgin Mary, and how she was cared for by the prophet Zechariah. It highlights God's special providence for Mary, providing her with sustenance and blessings in a supernatural way. The interpretation is that God has the power to care for and provide for those He chooses, in ways that defy human understanding, as a testament to His absolute sovereignty and generosity.
orig: فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن وأنبتها نباتا حسنا وكفلها زكريا كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب وجد عندها رزقا قال يا مريم أنى لك هذا قالت هو من عند الله إن الله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب

translation: There Zakariyya called upon his Lord, saying, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication."
interpretation: This verse describes the supplication of the prophet Zakariyya (Zechariah) to Allah, asking Him for a righteous child. The interpretation is that Zakariyya humbly and sincerely sought a good offspring from Allah, recognizing that Allah is the All-Hearing and Responsive to supplications.
orig: هنالك دعا زكريا ربه قال رب هب لي من لدنك ذرية طيبة إنك سميع الدعاء

translation: And the angels called to him as he was standing in prayer in the chamber: 'Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of John, confirming a word from Allah and [who will be] a master and abstaining [from women], and a prophet from among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse describes how the angels appeared to Zechariah and announced the good news of the birth of his son, John the Baptist. The message conveys that John will be a righteous and pious man, a leader and a prophet who will confirm the word of God. The description of him as 'abstaining [from women]' suggests that he will live a life of chastity and devotion to God's service.
orig: فنادته الملائكة وهو قائم يصلي في المحراب أن الله يبشرك بيحيى مصدقا بكلمة من الله وسيدا وحصورا ونبيا من الصالحين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, how can I have a son when I have reached old age and my wife is barren?' [The angel] said, 'Thus [it will be]; Allah does what He wills.'
interpretation: This verse conveys the message that Allah's power and will are absolute. Even in situations that seem impossible from a human perspective, such as an elderly man having a child with a barren wife, Allah can make it happen according to His will and plan. It emphasizes the need for believers to trust in Allah's wisdom and ability to bring about what He desires, even when it defies human logic or expectations.
orig: قال رب أنى يكون لي غلام وقد بلغني الكبر وامرأتي عاقر قال كذلك الله يفعل ما يشاء

translation: He said, "My Lord, make for me a sign." [Allah] said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture. And remember your Lord much and exalt [Him with praise] in the evening and the morning."
interpretation: This verse describes the sign that Allah gave to the prophet Zechariah, who was made mute for three days as a sign of the birth of his son, the prophet John. The interpretation is that sometimes Allah gives signs to his prophets and messengers, and that one should remember and glorify Allah frequently, both in the evening and morning.
orig: قال رب اجعل لي آية قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاثة أيام إلا رمزا واذكر ربك كثيرا وسبح بالعشي والإبكار

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse highlights the high status and honor that Allah bestowed upon the Virgin Mary, by choosing her and purifying her, and elevating her above all the women of the world. It emphasizes her exceptional virtue and the divine favor she received, which set her apart from others.
orig: وإذ قالت الملائكة يا مريم إن الله اصطفاك وطهرك واصطفاك على نساء العالمين

translation: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate and bow with those who [regularly] bow [in prayer].
interpretation: This verse is a command to Mary to be steadfast in her worship and devotion to Allah, and to join in the communal prayer alongside the believers. It emphasizes the importance of humility, submission, and unity in religious practice.
orig: يا مريم اقنتي لربك واسجدي واركعي مع الراكعين

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muhammad]. And you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should be responsible for Mary. Nor were you with them when they disputed.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the information being conveyed is from the realm of the unseen, which Allah has revealed to the Prophet Muhammad. It also indicates that the Prophet was not present when the people were deciding who would be responsible for caring for Mary, nor when they were disputing about this matter. This emphasizes that the knowledge being imparted is from Allah, not something the Prophet witnessed directly.
orig: ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary - distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near [to Allah]".
interpretation: This verse announces the miraculous birth of Jesus, the Messiah, to the Virgin Mary. It highlights that Jesus will be a highly esteemed and honored figure, both in this world and the Hereafter, and will be among the closest to Allah. This emphasizes the special status and divine nature of Jesus, who was born without a human father through the power of Allah.
orig: إذ قالت الملائكة يا مريم إن الله يبشرك بكلمة منه اسمه المسيح عيسى ابن مريم وجيها في الدنيا والآخرة ومن المقربين

translation: And he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity and among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse refers to Jesus (peace be upon him), who was given the ability to speak as a child in the cradle, and then later in life as a mature man. It also indicates that he will be counted among the righteous people.
orig: ويكلم الناس في المهد وكهلا ومن الصالحين

translation: She said: "O my Lord! How shall I have a son when no man has touched me?" He said: "Even so: Allah createth what He willeth: When He hath decreed a plan, He but saith to it, 'Be,' and it is!"
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and ability of Allah to create without the need for conventional means. When Allah wills something to happen, He simply commands it, and it comes into existence. This demonstrates the divine nature of Allah and His absolute sovereignty over all creation.
orig: قالت رب أنى يكون لي ولد ولم يمسسني بشر قال كذلك الله يخلق ما يشاء إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And He will teach him the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel
interpretation: This verse indicates that God will teach the Prophet Muhammad the divine scriptures and wisdom. The "Book" refers to the Qur'an, while the "Torah" and "Gospel" refer to the previous revelations given to Moses and Jesus, respectively. The "wisdom" signifies the Prophet's deep understanding and ability to interpret these sacred texts. This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Prophet's knowledge and his role as a recipient and teacher of God's guidance.
orig: ويعلمه الكتاب والحكمة والتوراة والإنجيل

translation: And [I have come to you] confirming what was before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse describes the mission of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) to the Children of Israel. He was sent to confirm the previous divine revelations, particularly the Torah, and to clarify and make lawful some matters that were previously forbidden to them. Furthermore, Jesus was given miraculous signs from God to demonstrate his prophethood, such as the ability to create a bird-like creature from clay, heal the blind and the leper, and raise the dead. These signs were meant to affirm his message and call the people to have faith in God and obey his teachings.
orig: ورسولا إلى بني إسرائيل أني قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم أني أخلق لكم من الطين كهيئة الطير فأنفخ فيه فيكون طيرا بإذن الله وأبرئ الأكمه والأبرص وأحيي الموتى بإذن الله وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون في بيوتكم إن في ذلك لآية لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And [I have come] confirming what was before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Quran confirms the previous scriptures, such as the Torah, and that it permits some things that were previously forbidden. It also emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah and obeying the Prophet Muhammad, as he has come with a sign (a miracle or proof) from Allah.
orig: ومصدقا لما بين يدي من التوراة ولأحل لكم بعض الذي حرم عليكم وجئتكم بآية من ربكم فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God, and calls upon all people to worship and submit to the one true God. It establishes that Allah is the Lord and Creator of all, and therefore deserving of our devotion and obedience. The verse also describes the path of righteousness and salvation as a "straight path" - a clear and direct way to please God and attain His pleasure.
orig: إن الله ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: But when Jesus felt [persistence in] disbelief from them, he said, 'Who are my supporters for [the cause of] Allah?' The disciples said, 'We are supporters for Allah. We have believed in Allah and testified that we are Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the steadfast faith and commitment of Jesus' disciples to supporting him and the cause of Allah. Despite facing disbelief and opposition, the disciples affirm their belief in Allah and declare their submission to Him as Muslims. This demonstrates the strength of their conviction and their unwavering loyalty to the divine message that Jesus brought.
orig: فلما أحس عيسى منهم الكفر قال من أنصاري إلى الله قال الحواريون نحن أنصار الله آمنا بالله واشهد بأنا مسلمون

translation: Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed and have followed the Messenger, so register us among the witnesses.
interpretation: This verse expresses the sincere belief and commitment of the believers to follow the teachings of the Qur'an and the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It is a supplication to Allah, asking Him to count them among the righteous witnesses who testify to the truth of the divine message. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith, obedience, and bearing witness to one's beliefs.
orig: ربنا آمنا بما أنزلت واتبعنا الرسول فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين

translation: And they planned, and Allah planned. And Allah is the best of planners.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that while the disbelievers may plot and scheme against the believers, Allah is the ultimate Planner and His plan will prevail over theirs. It reminds us that Allah is the Wisest and Most Powerful, and that we should trust in His plan rather than being distressed by the plots of those who oppose the truth.
orig: ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين

translation: When Allah said, "O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve and make those who follow you [in submission to Allah] superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that in which you used to differ."
interpretation: This verse speaks of Allah's plan for Jesus (peace be upon him). Allah informs Jesus that He will take him up to Himself, purify him from the disbelievers, and make those who follow Jesus superior to the disbelievers until the Day of Resurrection. This indicates that Jesus will be exalted and his true followers will be victorious, despite the opposition of the disbelievers. Ultimately, all will return to Allah for judgement on the matters they differed about during their lifetimes.
orig: إذ قال الله يا عيسى إني متوفيك ورافعك إلي ومطهرك من الذين كفروا وجاعل الذين اتبعوك فوق الذين كفروا إلى يوم القيامة ثم إلي مرجعكم فأحكم بينكم فيما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: But as for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse conveys a stern warning to those who reject faith in God and His teachings. It suggests that those who persistently deny the truth will face a severe and painful punishment, both in this life and in the Afterlife. The verse emphasizes that such individuals will have no one to support or defend them, highlighting the dire consequences of their choices.
orig: فأما الذين كفروا فأعذبهم عذابا شديدا في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: And as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them in full their rewards, and Allah does not like the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have faith and do good deeds will be rewarded by Allah. It also highlights that Allah does not approve of those who act unjustly or wrongfully.
orig: وأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيوفيهم أجورهم والله لا يحب الظالمين

translation: That is what We recite to you, [O Muhammad], of the verses and the precise [divine] message.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an and its teachings are being revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by Allah. It affirms the divine origin and wisdom of the Qur'anic verses, which the Prophet is tasked with conveying to humanity.
orig: ذلك نتلوه عليك من الآيات والذكر الحكيم

translation: Indeed, the example of Jesus to Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was.
interpretation: This verse draws a parallel between the creation of Jesus and the creation of Adam, both of whom were created by the divine power of Allah without a biological father. Just as Allah created Adam from dust, He created Jesus without a father, demonstrating His ability to bring about life in extraordinary ways. This emphasizes the divine nature of Jesus and his creation, and the fact that he was not the son of God, but rather a prophet of God, similar to Adam.
orig: إن مثل عيسى عند الله كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب ثم قال له كن فيكون

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an and the message it conveys is the absolute truth revealed by God. It instructs the believers to have unwavering faith in this truth and not to be among those who doubt or question it.
orig: الحق من ربك فلا تكن من الممترين

translation: But whoever argues with you about it after [this] knowledge has come to you - say, "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then supplicate [together] and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars [among us]."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to engage in a solemn invocation and mutual cursing with those who dispute the truth after it has been made clear to them. It suggests that the truth can be established through a sincere and humble supplication to God, where both sides call upon Him to curse the party that is being dishonest. This reflects the gravity of the matter and the importance of seeking the truth, even if it means confronting those who oppose it.
orig: فمن حاجك فيه من بعد ما جاءك من العلم فقل تعالوا ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم ثم نبتهل فنجعل لعنت الله على الكاذبين

translation: Indeed, this is the true narration. And there is no deity except Allah. And indeed, Allah is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms the truth and authenticity of the Qur'anic narratives, and emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of Allah as the only true deity worthy of worship. It also highlights Allah's attributes of power and wisdom, conveying that He alone possesses the ultimate authority and that His decisions and actions are guided by profound wisdom.
orig: إن هذا لهو القصص الحق وما من إله إلا الله وإن الله لهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: But if they turn away, then indeed, Allah is Knowing of the corrupters.
interpretation: If the people turn away from the guidance and truth of Allah, then Allah is fully aware of those who spread corruption and mischief in the land. He will hold them accountable for their misdeeds.
orig: فإن تولوا فإن الله عليم بالمفسدين

translation: Say, "O People of the Book, come to a word that is equitable between us and you - that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allah." But if they turn away, then say, "Bear witness that we are Muslims [submitting to Him]."
interpretation: This verse calls upon the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) to come to a common word, a shared belief, between them and the Muslims. That common word is the worship of one God, Allah, without associating any partners with Him. It rejects the idea of worshipping anyone or anything other than Allah, including taking other human beings as lords. If the People of the Book refuse this call, then the Muslims are to bear witness that they themselves are those who have submitted to Allah.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم ألا نعبد إلا الله ولا نشرك به شيئا ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله فإن تولوا فقولوا اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون

translation: O People of the Book! Why do you argue about Abraham, when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until [long] after him? Do you not understand?
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) and questions their arguments about the status of Prophet Abraham. The verse suggests that they should not argue about Abraham, as the Torah and the Gospel were revealed long after him. The implication is that they should use reason and understanding to comprehend the true nature of Abraham's role and status in Islam, rather than engaging in futile debates.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تحاجون في إبراهيم وما أنزلت التوراة والإنجيل إلا من بعده أفلا تعقلون

translation: Here you are - those who have argued about that of which you have [some] knowledge. But why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge? And Allah knows, while you know not.
interpretation: This verse admonishes those who argue about matters they have no knowledge of. It encourages people to focus on what they know, rather than speculate about things beyond their understanding. The verse emphasizes that Allah alone has complete knowledge, while humans have limited knowledge, and should therefore be humble and refrain from making claims about things they do not truly understand.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء حاججتم فيما لكم به علم فلم تحاجون فيما ليس لكم به علم والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a true monotheist, a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Abraham was a pure monotheist, not affiliated with any particular religious group. He followed the true path of worshipping one God, which is the essence of Islam. This verse serves to highlight the universal nature of Abraham's faith, which transcends the boundaries of later religious affiliations.
orig: ما كان إبراهيم يهوديا ولا نصرانيا ولكن كان حنيفا مسلما وما كان من المشركين

translation: Indeed, the most worthy of Abraham among the people are those who followed him [in submission to Allah ] and this prophet, and those who [genuinely] believe [in his message]. And Allah is the protector of the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the closest people to the Prophet Abraham are those who follow his teachings and beliefs, as well as the Prophet Muhammad and his followers. It highlights that Allah is the guardian and supporter of the believers, who have embraced the true faith.
orig: إن أولى الناس بإبراهيم للذين اتبعوه وهذا النبي والذين آمنوا والله ولي المؤمنين

translation: And a party of the People of the Book wish to lead you astray. But they lead astray not except themselves, and they perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against the deceptive efforts of some People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who wish to mislead the believers. However, their attempts to mislead others will only lead to their own downfall, as they are unaware of the consequences of their actions.
orig: ودت طائفة من أهل الكتاب لو يضلونكم وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah while you witness [to their truth]?
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book, referring to the Jews and Christians, and questions why they reject the signs and revelations of Allah despite being aware of their truth. It suggests that they have knowledge of the divine signs, yet they choose to disbelieve in them, which is a grave sin.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تكفرون بآيات الله وأنتم تشهدون

translation: O People of the Book! Why do you confound the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know [it]?
interpretation: This verse calls upon the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) to be honest and truthful in their dealings, and not to mix truth with falsehood or conceal the truth that they possess. It emphasizes the importance of sincerity and transparency in matters of faith and belief.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تلبسون الحق بالباطل وتكتمون الحق وأنتم تعلمون

translation: And a faction of the People of the Book say, "Believe in that which was revealed to the believers at the beginning of the day and reject it at its end, so perhaps they will return [from Christianity]".
interpretation: This verse refers to a group of Jews or Christians who sought to confuse the early Muslims by encouraging them to believe in the Qur'an in the morning but reject it by the evening, in the hope that they would abandon their faith. The interpretation is that this was a deceptive tactic to undermine the faith of the believers, which the Qur'an condemns.
orig: وقالت طائفة من أهل الكتاب آمنوا بالذي أنزل على الذين آمنوا وجه النهار واكفروا آخره لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And do not believe [i.e., follow] except the one who follows your religion [i.e., Islam]. Say, "Indeed, the [true] guidance is the guidance of Allah. [Do you fear] lest someone be given [knowledge] like you were given or that they would [thereby] argue with you before your Lord?" Say, "Indeed, [all] bounty is in the hand of Allah - He grants it to whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Wise."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the true guidance comes from Allah alone, and that one should not follow anyone except those who follow the religion of Islam. It cautions against arrogance, as the guidance and bounty of Allah are not limited to any particular group. The verse reminds that all good is in the hands of Allah, who bestows it upon whomever He wills, and that He is all-encompassing in His knowledge and wisdom.
orig: ولا تؤمنوا إلا لمن تبع دينكم قل إن الهدى هدى الله أن يؤتى أحد مثل ما أوتيتم أو يحاجوكم عند ربكم قل إن الفضل بيد الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: He selects for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's mercy and blessings are not distributed equally among all people, but rather He chooses to bestow His mercy upon whomever He wills. This highlights the fact that Allah's wisdom and divine plan are beyond human comprehension, and that we should be grateful for the blessings we receive without questioning Allah's choices. The verse also affirms that Allah is the source of all great bounty and favor, which He grants to His creation as He sees fit.
orig: يختص برحمته من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: And among the People of the Book are some who, if you entrust him with a great amount [of wealth], he will [continually] return it to you. And among them are some who, if you entrust him with a [single] coin, he will not return it to you unless you are constantly standing over him. That is because they say, "There is no blame upon us concerning the unlearned." And they speak untruth about Allah while they know [it].
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrasting attitudes and behaviors of some among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) when it comes to honesty and trustworthiness. Some of them can be trusted with great wealth, faithfully returning it as entrusted. Others, however, cannot be trusted even with a small amount, as they will only return it if the owner constantly oversees them. This is because they claim that there is no blame on them regarding the unlearned (i.e., the gentiles or non-believers), and they speak lies about Allah, knowing that what they say is false.
orig: ومن أهل الكتاب من إن تأمنه بقنطار يؤده إليك ومنهم من إن تأمنه بدينار لا يؤده إليك إلا ما دمت عليه قائما ذلك بأنهم قالوا ليس علينا في الأميين سبيل ويقولون على الله الكذب وهم يعلمون

translation: Nay, [but] whoever fulfills his commitment and fears [Allah] - then indeed, Allah loves those who fear Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's commitments and being God-conscious. It states that those who honor their pledges and are mindful of Allah are beloved to Him. The interpretation is that true faith is demonstrated through righteous actions and a sincere devotion to Allah, which is pleasing to Him.
orig: بلى من أوفى بعهده واتقى فإن الله يحب المتقين

translation: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their [own] oaths for a small price - those will have no share in the Hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them or look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them; and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who forsake their covenant with Allah and their solemn oaths for a trivial worldly gain. It emphasizes that such people will be deprived of Allah's mercy and blessings in the Hereafter. They will not be addressed by Allah, nor will He look upon them with favor on the Day of Judgment. They will not be purified of their sins, and instead, they will face a painful punishment.
orig: إن الذين يشترون بعهد الله وأيمانهم ثمنا قليلا أولئك لا خلاق لهم في الآخرة ولا يكلمهم الله ولا ينظر إليهم يوم القيامة ولا يزكيهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And indeed, there is among them a party who alter the Scripture with their tongues so you may think it is from the Scripture, but it is not from the Scripture; and they say, "This is from Allah," but it is not from Allah. And they speak untruth about Allah while they know [it].
interpretation: This verse warns against those who distort the teachings of the Qur'an, either by misinterpreting its verses or by fabricating false statements and attributing them to Allah. It emphasizes the importance of relying on the authentic and original teachings of the Qur'an, and not being deceived by those who seek to mislead people through their own twisted interpretations or fabrications. The verse highlights the grave sin of lying about Allah and His revelations, which is a clear violation of the principles of the Qur'an.
orig: وإن منهم لفريقا يلوون ألسنتهم بالكتاب لتحسبوه من الكتاب وما هو من الكتاب ويقولون هو من عند الله وما هو من عند الله ويقولون على الله الكذب وهم يعلمون

translation: It is not for a human [prophet] that Allah should give him the Scripture and authority and prophethood and then he would say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than Allah," but [rather, he would say], "Be pious scholars of the Lord because of what you have been teaching of the Scripture and because of what you have been studying."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is not befitting for a prophet of God to ask people to worship him instead of God. Rather, the role of a prophet is to teach people to be devoted servants of God, and to be righteous scholars who guide others based on their knowledge of the divine scriptures and teachings. The true purpose of prophethood is to lead people towards God, not to establish one's own authority or status.
orig: ما كان لبشر أن يؤتيه الله الكتاب والحكم والنبوة ثم يقول للناس كونوا عبادا لي من دون الله ولكن كونوا ربانيين بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب وبما كنتم تدرسون

translation: And He does not order you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Would He order you to disbelieve after you have submitted?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah does not command believers to worship or revere the angels and prophets as deities or lords. Rather, the true devotion and submission should be directed towards Allah alone, as the believers have already accepted Islam and submitted to the will of Allah.
orig: ولا يأمركم أن تتخذوا الملائكة والنبيين أربابا أيأمركم بالكفر بعد إذ أنتم مسلمون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Allah took the covenant of the prophets, [saying], "Whatever I give you of the Scripture and wisdom and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you [must] believe in him and support him." [Allah] said, "Have you acknowledged and taken upon that My commitment?" They said, "We have acknowledged it." [Allah] said, "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."
interpretation: This verse speaks of the covenant that Allah took from the prophets, to believe in and support the final prophet, Muhammad (peace be upon him), who would come and confirm the previous scriptures. The prophets acknowledged and accepted this covenant, and Allah calls them to bear witness to this on the Day of Judgment. This verse emphasizes the importance of accepting and supporting the final messenger sent by Allah.
orig: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين لما آتيتكم من كتاب وحكمة ثم جاءكم رسول مصدق لما معكم لتؤمنن به ولتنصرنه قال أأقررتم وأخذتم على ذلكم إصري قالوا أقررنا قال فاشهدوا وأنا معكم من الشاهدين

translation: And whoever turns away after that - then those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who turn away from the guidance of the Qur'an and the teachings of Islam after having received it are considered to be transgressors and sinful individuals. The interpretation suggests that true believers must steadfastly adhere to the faith and not deviate from it, lest they be counted among the disobedient.
orig: فمن تولى بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: Do they then seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him submit all creatures in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the religion of Allah is the only true and universal religion, to which all of creation - in the heavens and the earth - submits, either willingly or unwillingly. It is a rhetorical question that challenges the idea of seeking any religion other than the one ordained by Allah, as all will ultimately return to Him.
orig: أفغير دين الله يبغون وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وإليه يرجعون

translation: Say, "We have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Descendants and what was given to Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have faith in Allah and all the prophets and revelations that He has sent, without making any distinctions between them. It emphasizes the importance of submitting to Allah and following His guidance as revealed through the different prophets and scriptures. The verse promotes a universal and inclusive approach to faith, where believers recognize the common origins and messages of the various divine teachings.
orig: قل آمنا بالله وما أنزل علينا وما أنزل على إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وما أوتي موسى وعيسى والنبيون من ربهم لا نفرق بين أحد منهم ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And whoever desires other than Islam as religion - never will it be accepted from him, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Islam is the only true and acceptable religion in the sight of God. It warns that anyone who seeks a religion other than Islam will not have it accepted, and they will be among the losers in the Hereafter. This underscores the importance of submitting to the will of God and following the teachings of Islam as the path to salvation.
orig: ومن يبتغ غير الإسلام دينا فلن يقبل منه وهو في الآخرة من الخاسرين

translation: How shall Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and had witnessed that the Messenger is true and clear signs had come to them? And Allah guides not the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of rejecting faith after having accepted it. It suggests that those who turn away from the truth after being guided are unlikely to be guided again, as Allah does not guide those who have chosen the path of wrongdoing. The verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith and the consequences of abandoning it.
orig: كيف يهدي الله قوما كفروا بعد إيمانهم وشهدوا أن الرسول حق وجاءهم البينات والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Those - their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah and the angels and the people, all together.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who have earned the curse of Allah, the angels, and all of humanity will face a severe punishment and consequences for their misdeeds. It emphasizes the gravity of their actions and the universality of the condemnation they face.
orig: أولئك جزاؤهم أن عليهم لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين

translation: Abiding therein. The punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse conveys the eternal and unrelenting nature of the punishment for those who reject faith and commit grave sins. It emphasizes that there will be no respite or reduction in their suffering, and they will not be granted any reprieve or chance to escape their fate. The interpretation suggests that the consequences of one's actions in the afterlife are final and inescapable.
orig: خالدين فيها لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينظرون

translation: Except for those who repent after that and reform, for indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse offers hope and encouragement to those who have strayed or committed sins. It emphasizes that Allah is forgiving and merciful towards those who sincerely repent and make amends for their wrongdoings. The verse suggests that no matter how grave the sin, Allah's forgiveness is always available to those who truly turn back to Him and strive to improve themselves.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من بعد ذلك وأصلحوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve after they had believed, then increase in disbelief - never will their [claimed] repentance be accepted, and they are the ones astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of apostasy and the rejection of faith after having believed. It states that the repentance of those who turn away from their faith and increase in disbelief will not be accepted. They are considered to be truly lost and misguided.
orig: إن الذين كفروا بعد إيمانهم ثم ازدادوا كفرا لن تقبل توبتهم وأولئك هم الضالون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - never would the [whole] wealth of the earth in gold be accepted from one of them if he would [seek to] ransom himself with it. For them is a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the grave consequences of disbelief and dying in a state of rejection of faith. Even if a disbeliever were to offer the entire wealth of the earth as ransom, it would not be accepted from them. They are destined for a painful punishment, and they will have no one to help or support them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وماتوا وهم كفار فلن يقبل من أحدهم ملء الأرض ذهبا ولو افتدى به أولئك لهم عذاب أليم وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: You will not attain the [reward of] righteousness until you [willingly] spend [in the way of Allah] from that which you love. And whatever you spend - indeed, Allah is Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of charitable giving and selflessness in attaining righteousness. It suggests that true piety and virtue are not achieved merely through outward displays or empty rituals, but through the sincere sacrifice of that which one holds dear. The verse encourages believers to give from their wealth and possessions, even if it is something they themselves cherish, as this demonstrates a true devotion to Allah and a willingness to put the needs of others before one's own desires. The verse also reminds that Allah is all-knowing and is aware of the intentions and sacrifices of the believers, which will be duly rewarded.
orig: لن تنالوا البر حتى تنفقوا مما تحبون وما تنفقوا من شيء فإن الله به عليم

translation: All food was lawful for the Children of Israel, except what Israel had made unlawful for itself before the Torah was revealed. Say, "Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the dietary restrictions placed on the Children of Israel were not imposed by God, but were self-imposed by the Israelites themselves prior to the revelation of the Torah. The verse challenges the Israelites to bring forth the Torah and recite it, if they claim to be truthful about the origins of these dietary restrictions. This suggests that the Qur'an is questioning the validity of certain Israelite traditions and practices, and calling for a return to the original teachings of the Torah.
orig: كل الطعام كان حلا لبني إسرائيل إلا ما حرم إسرائيل على نفسه من قبل أن تنزل التوراة قل فأتوا بالتوراة فاتلوها إن كنتم صادقين

translation: So whoever invents a lie about Allah after that - it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who falsely attribute lies or falsehoods to Allah are the true wrongdoers. It serves as a stern warning against misrepresenting or distorting the teachings and messages of Allah, as that would be a grave sin.
orig: فمن افترى على الله الكذب من بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: Say, "Allah has spoken the truth. So follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists."
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to follow the true religion of Abraham, which is monotheism and devotion to the One God. It emphasizes that Abraham was not a polytheist, and that the believers should emulate his unwavering faith in the Oneness of God and his rejection of idolatry.
orig: قل صدق الله فاتبعوا ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah - blessed and a guidance for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse establishes the sanctity and importance of the Ka'bah in Makkah as the first place of worship established for all of humanity. It is a blessed and sacred site, and a source of guidance for the entire world.
orig: إن أول بيت وضع للناس للذي ببكة مباركا وهدى للعالمين

translation: In it are clear signs [such as] the standing place of Abraham. And whoever enters it shall be safe. And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House - for whoever is able to find thereto a way. But whoever disbelieves - then indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.
interpretation:
This verse emphasizes the significance of the Kaaba in Makkah, which is the holiest site in Islam. It highlights the following key points;
1) The Kaaba contains clear signs and symbols of faith, including the standing place of Prophet Abraham.
2) Those who enter the Kaaba's sacred precincts are granted a sense of security and protection.
3) It is an obligation upon all able-bodied Muslims to perform the pilgrimage (Hajj) to the Kaaba at least once in their lifetime.
4) Disbelief in the importance of the Kaaba does not diminish its status, as Allah is self-sufficient and independent of the beliefs of people.
orig: فيه آيات بينات مقام إبراهيم ومن دخله كان آمنا ولله على الناس حج البيت من استطاع إليه سبيلا ومن كفر فإن الله غني عن العالمين

translation: Say, "O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah while Allah is Witness over what you do?"
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the People of the Book, referring to the Jews and Christians, who were rejecting the message of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse calls upon them to reflect on their rejection of the divine signs and verses, reminding them that Allah is a Witness to their actions and beliefs. The implication is that they will be held accountable for their rejection of the truth.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لم تكفرون بآيات الله والله شهيد على ما تعملون

translation: Say, "O People of the Book, why do you avert from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it [seem] crooked, while you are witnesses [to the truth]? And Allah is not unaware of what you do."
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who were hindering the believers from following the path of Allah. The verse condemns their actions, as they were aware of the truth but still sought to mislead the believers and make the path of Allah appear crooked. The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of their deeds and will hold them accountable.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لم تصدون عن سبيل الله من آمن تبغونها عوجا وأنتم شهداء وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: O you who believe! If you obey a group of those who were given the Scripture, they would (indeed) render you disbelievers after you have believed.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against blindly following the directives of those who have received previous scriptures, such as the Jews and Christians, as they may lead the believers astray from their faith. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining one's own faith and not being easily swayed by the opinions or commands of others, even if they are perceived as religious authorities.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تطيعوا فريقا من الذين أوتوا الكتاب يردوكم بعد إيمانكم كافرين

translation: And how can you disbelieve while to you are being recited the verses of Allah and among you is His Messenger? And whoever holds firmly to Allah has [indeed] been guided to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absurdity of disbelieving in Allah when the signs of His existence and guidance are so clear, and when the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is present among the people. It calls on the believers to hold firmly to Allah and follow the straight path that He has shown them, for this is the path to true guidance and success.
orig: وكيف تكفرون وأنتم تتلى عليكم آيات الله وفيكم رسوله ومن يعتصم بالله فقد هدي إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: O you who believe! Fear Allah as He should be feared, and die not except in a state of Islam.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to have a deep reverence and consciousness of Allah, and to submit to Him completely, even to the point of death. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining one's faith and devotion to Allah throughout one's life, and not to die except in a state of complete surrender and obedience to Him.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون

translation: And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided. And remember the favor of Allah upon you - when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together and you became, by His favor, brothers. And you were on the edge of a pit of the Fire, and He saved you from it. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses so that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse encourages unity and solidarity among the believers. It reminds them of the blessings of Allah in bringing them together and saving them from the Fire. The interpretation is that Muslims should hold fast to their faith and remain united, remembering the favors of Allah upon them, so that they may continue to be guided on the right path.
orig: واعتصموا بحبل الله جميعا ولا تفرقوا واذكروا نعمت الله عليكم إذ كنتم أعداء فألف بين قلوبكم فأصبحتم بنعمته إخوانا وكنتم على شفا حفرة من النار فأنقذكم منها كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And let there be [arising] from you a nation inviting to [all that is] good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and those will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse encourages the formation of a community that actively promotes good, commands what is right, and forbids what is wrong. This community will be the ones who achieve true success and prosperity.
orig: ولتكن منكم أمة يدعون إلى الخير ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And do not be like those who became divided and differed after the clear proofs had come to them. And those will have a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse encourages unity and discourages division and disagreement among believers. It warns against the fate of those who let differences and disputes arise after clear guidance has been provided. The interpretation is that Muslims should strive to maintain unity, avoid divisiveness, and submit to the truth of the Qur"an and the teachings of the Prophet.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين تفرقوا واختلفوا من بعد ما جاءهم البينات وأولئك لهم عذاب عظيم

translation: The Day when some faces will be whitened and some faces will be blackened. As for those whose faces will be blackened, [to them it will be said], "Did you disbelieve after your belief? Then taste the punishment for what you used to reject."
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when people will be divided based on their faith and deeds. Those whose faces are whitened have embraced faith and done good, while those whose faces are blackened have rejected faith after believing and will taste the punishment for their disbelief.
orig: يوم تبيض وجوه وتسود وجوه فأما الذين اسودت وجوههم أكفرتم بعد إيمانكم فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: As for those whose faces have become white, they will be within the mercy of Allah; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the righteous will be distinguished by the whiteness of their faces, a sign of their purity and virtue. They will be granted eternal life in the mercy and grace of Allah, enjoying the bliss of Paradise without end.
orig: وأما الذين ابيضت وجوههم ففي رحمة الله هم فيها خالدون

translation: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you, [O Muhammad], in truth; and Allah does not want any injustice for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the verses of the Qur'an are the divine revelations of Allah, which are recited to the Prophet Muhammad with truth and authenticity. It further affirms that Allah does not desire any form of injustice or oppression for all of humanity and the entire creation.
orig: تلك آيات الله نتلوها عليك بالحق وما الله يريد ظلما للعالمين

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And to Allah are [all] matters returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and dominion of Allah over the entire universe, both in the heavens and on earth. It affirms that all things ultimately belong to Allah and will return to Him for judgment and accountability. This serves as a reminder of Allah's supreme power and authority, and that all affairs and decisions must be referred back to Him.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: You are the best nation produced [as an example] for mankind. You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah. If only the People of the Book had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the noble status of the Muslim community as the best nation, chosen to guide humanity towards righteousness and faith in Allah. It emphasizes the responsibility of Muslims to promote good and forbid evil, and laments the lack of faith among the People of the Book, who could have greatly benefited from belief in Allah if only they had accepted it. The verse underscores the importance of faith and righteous conduct as the hallmarks of a truly virtuous community.
orig: كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس تأمرون بالمعروف وتنهون عن المنكر وتؤمنون بالله ولو آمن أهل الكتاب لكان خيرا لهم منهم المؤمنون وأكثرهم الفاسقون

translation: They will not harm you except for [some] annoyance. And if they fight you, they will show you their backs; then they will not be aided.
interpretation: This verse reassures the believers that their enemies will not be able to inflict serious harm upon them, and that even if they try to fight, they will ultimately be defeated and abandoned by their supporters. The message is one of reassurance and encouragement for the believers to remain steadfast in the face of adversity.
orig: لن يضروكم إلا أذى وإن يقاتلوكم يولوكم الأدبار ثم لا ينصرون

translation: They have been overtaken by humiliation wherever they are found, except for a covenant from Allah and a covenant from the people. And they have drawn upon themselves anger from Allah and have been struck with poverty. That is because they disbelieved in the signs of Allah and killed the prophets without right. That is because they disobeyed and were [habitually] transgressing.
interpretation: This verse describes the consequences that the disbelievers and those who reject the signs of Allah and kill the prophets will face. They will be overtaken by humiliation and poverty, having drawn the anger of Allah upon themselves. This is a result of their disbelief, disobedience, and transgressions against the commandments of Allah.
orig: ضربت عليهم الذلة أين ما ثقفوا إلا بحبل من الله وحبل من الناس وباءوا بغضب من الله وضربت عليهم المسكنة ذلك بأنهم كانوا يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون الأنبياء بغير حق ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: Not equal are the People of the Book. Among them are those who are upright, reciting the verses of Allah during the periods of the night and prostrating [in worship].
interpretation: This verse highlights that the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) are not all the same. There are among them those who are steadfast in their faith, reciting the verses of Allah during the night and prostrating in worship. This suggests that those who are devoted and sincere in their religious practices are not to be equated with those who are not.
orig: ليسوا سواء من أهل الكتاب أمة قائمة يتلون آيات الله آناء الليل وهم يسجدون

translation: They believe in Allah and the Last Day, and they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and hasten to good deeds. And those are the righteous.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of the righteous believers. They have faith in Allah and the Day of Judgment, they command others to do good and forbid them from evil, and they are eager to perform good deeds. This shows that true faith is not just a matter of belief, but must be accompanied by righteous actions and concern for others.
orig: يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر ويسارعون في الخيرات وأولئك من الصالحين

translation: And whatever good they do - never will it be denied [their reward]. And Allah is Knowing of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of the good deeds performed by the righteous, and that He will not deny them their just reward. It encourages people to do good works, as Allah is all-knowing and will recognize and appreciate their efforts.
orig: وما يفعلوا من خير فلن يكفروه والله عليم بالمتقين

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - never will their wealth or their children avail them against Allah at all, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide in it eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the wealth and children of those who reject faith in Allah will not protect them from the punishment of the Hereafter. Their material possessions and familial ties will be of no avail on the Day of Judgment, as they will be condemned to the eternal fire of Hell as a consequence of their disbelief.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: The example of what they spend in this worldly life is like that of a wind containing frost which strikes the harvest of a people who have wronged themselves and destroys it. And Allah has not wronged them, but they wrong themselves.
interpretation: This verse draws a powerful analogy between the fleeting and destructive nature of worldly wealth and the ultimate consequences of misusing it. Just as a frost-laden wind can devastate a harvest, the wealth that is spent selfishly and without regard for others can ultimately destroy the one who hoards it. The key message is that wrongdoing and injustice against oneself and others will only lead to ruin, and that true success lies in aligning one's actions with the will of God.
orig: مثل ما ينفقون في هذه الحياة الدنيا كمثل ريح فيها صر أصابت حرث قوم ظلموا أنفسهم فأهلكته وما ظلمهم الله ولكن أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: O you who believe! Do not take [for counsel] intimates other than yourselves, [since] they will not fail to corrupt you. They wish you would have difficulty. Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater. We have certainly made clear to you the signs, if you will use reason.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against taking close confidants or advisors from among those who are not believers. It cautions that such people will try to lead the believers astray and cause them harm, even though they may outwardly appear friendly. The verse highlights that the disbelievers harbor deep resentment and animosity towards the believers, which is evident from their words and behavior, even though they may try to conceal the true extent of their hostility. The verse encourages the believers to carefully consider the signs and guidance provided by Allah, and to use their reason and discernment in order to avoid the pitfalls of taking untrustworthy confidants.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا بطانة من دونكم لا يألونكم خبالا ودوا ما عنتم قد بدت البغضاء من أفواههم وما تخفي صدورهم أكبر قد بينا لكم الآيات إن كنتم تعقلون

translation: Here you are loving them but they do not love you, and you believe in the whole of the Book. And when they meet you, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage. Say, "Die in your rage. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts."
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to believe but do not truly love the believers. It warns against being deceived by their outward show of faith, as they harbor resentment and anger towards the believers in private. The verse instructs the believers to be steadfast in their faith, and to recognize that Allah is fully aware of the hidden thoughts and intentions of people's hearts.
orig: ها أنتم أولاء تحبونهم ولا يحبونكم وتؤمنون بالكتاب كله وإذا لقوكم قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا عضوا عليكم الأنامل من الغيظ قل موتوا بغيظكم إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: If good befalls you, it grieves them, but if harm strikes you, they rejoice at it. And if you are patient and [fear Allah], their plot will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the jealous and malicious nature of those who wish harm upon the believers. It emphasizes that the believers should remain steadfast, patient and God-conscious in the face of such adversity, as Allah's protection will shield them from the schemes of their enemies. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of the actions of both the believers and their adversaries.
orig: إن تمسسكم حسنة تسؤهم وإن تصبكم سيئة يفرحوا بها وإن تصبروا وتتقوا لا يضركم كيدهم شيئا إن الله بما يعملون محيط

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when you went forth from your family in the early morning to post the believers at their stations for the battle [of Uhud] - and Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Battle of Uhud, where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) led the Muslim army against the Quraysh. The verse highlights the Prophet's foresight and strategic planning in positioning the believers at their battle stations, demonstrating his wisdom and Allah's guidance. It also emphasizes that Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, implying that He is aware of all the actions and intentions of the believers, and will judge them accordingly.
orig: وإذ غدوت من أهلك تبوئ المؤمنين مقاعد للقتال والله سميع عليم

translation: When two groups among you were about to lose courage, but Allah was their protector. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to put their trust in Allah, even in times of difficulty or uncertainty. It reminds them that Allah is their protector and supporter, and that they should rely on Him rather than becoming discouraged or losing hope.
orig: إذ همت طائفتان منكم أن تفشلا والله وليهما وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And Allah had already given you victory at [the battle of] Badr while you were few in number. So fear Allah that you may [truly] be grateful.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers that their victory at the Battle of Badr was a gift from Allah, despite their numerical inferiority. It encourages them to remain mindful of Allah’s favor and to express gratitude through obedience and righteous conduct.
orig: ولقد نصركم الله ببدر وأنتم أذلة فاتقوا الله لعلكم تشكرون

translation: When you said to the believers, 'Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?'
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to have faith and trust in God's support, as He is capable of providing them with supernatural assistance in times of need. The interpretation suggests that the believers should not be discouraged or lose hope, as God is able to strengthen them with the help of angels, if necessary.
orig: إذ تقول للمؤمنين ألن يكفيكم أن يمدكم ربكم بثلاثة آلاف من الملائكة منزلين

translation: Yes, if you are patient and conscious of Allah and the enemy comes upon you [attacking] in rage, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels having marks [of distinction].
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be patient and God-conscious, even in the face of adversity and attacks from their enemies. It promises that if they do so, Allah will support them with a powerful angelic force, emphasizing the divine assistance and protection available to those who remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: بلى إن تصبروا وتتقوا ويأتوكم من فورهم هذا يمددكم ربكم بخمسة آلاف من الملائكة مسومين

translation: And Allah has not made it (i.e., your dream, O Muhammad, of entering Makkah) except as a good tiding and so that your hearts would be assured thereby. And victory is not but from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the dream of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) entering Makkah was a divine sign and a good tiding, meant to reassure the hearts of the believers. It also affirms that true victory comes only from Allah, the Almighty and All-Wise, not from human efforts alone.
orig: وما جعله الله إلا بشرى لكم ولتطمئن قلوبكم به وما النصر إلا من عند الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: That He may cut off a portion of those who disbelieve, or abase them so that they turn back disappointed.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the divine retribution that may befall those who persistently reject faith and disbelieve in God. The interpretation suggests that God may either eliminate a portion of the disbelievers or humiliate them, causing them to retreat in failure and disappointment from their opposition to the truth.
orig: ليقطع طرفا من الذين كفروا أو يكبتهم فينقلبوا خائبين

translation: Not upon you, [O Muhammad], is [responsibility for] their guidance, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever good you spend is for yourselves, and you do not spend except seeking the countenance of Allah. And whatever you spend of good - it will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad is not responsible for the guidance of people, but rather it is Allah who guides whom He wills. It also encourages believers to do good deeds and spend in the way of Allah, as they will be fully rewarded for their actions, and not be wronged.
orig: ليس لك من الأمر شيء أو يتوب عليهم أو يعذبهم فإنهم ظالمون

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over the entire universe. He alone has the right to forgive or punish whomever He wills, as He is the All-Knowing and All-Wise. This reminds us that we should seek Allah's forgiveness and mercy, and submit to His will, for He is the most Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who believe! Do not consume interest, doubled and multiplied, but fear Allah that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse prohibits the practice of usury or interest-based transactions, as it can lead to the exploitation of the poor and the accumulation of wealth by the wealthy. The verse encourages believers to fear Allah and avoid such practices, in order to attain success and prosperity in this life and the hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تأكلوا الربا أضعافا مضاعفة واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And fear the Fire that has been prepared for the disbelievers
interpretation: This verse calls upon believers to be mindful of the consequences of disbelief and to strive to avoid the eternal punishment of the Hellfire, which has been prepared for those who reject faith in God and His guidance.
orig: واتقوا النار التي أعدت للكافرين

translation: And obey Allah and the Messenger that you may obtain mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger (Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him) as a means to attain Allah's mercy and forgiveness. It suggests that by submitting to the divine commandments and following the teachings of the Prophet, one can hope to receive Allah's compassion and be saved from punishment.
orig: وأطيعوا الله والرسول لعلكم ترحمون

translation: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and earth, prepared for the righteous
