interpretation: This verse encourages believers to strive for Allah's forgiveness and the reward of Paradise. It emphasizes the vastness of Paradise, which encompasses the heavens and the earth, and is prepared for those who are mindful of Allah and live righteously.
orig: وسارعوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم وجنة عرضها السماوات والأرض أعدت للمتقين

translation: Those who spend [in the cause of Allah ] during ease and hardship and who restrain anger and who pardon the people - and Allah loves the doers of good
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to be generous and charitable, both in times of prosperity and hardship. It also emphasizes the importance of self-control, forgiveness, and compassion towards others. The interpretation is that Allah loves those who are kind, patient, and forgiving, as these are virtues that bring out the best in people and strengthen the bonds of the community.
orig: الذين ينفقون في السراء والضراء والكاظمين الغيظ والعافين عن الناس والله يحب المحسنين

translation: And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves [by transgression], remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins - and who can forgive sins except Allah? - and [who] do not persist in what they have done while they know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness from Allah. Even when people commit sins or wrong themselves, if they remember Allah and sincerely seek His forgiveness, Allah is the only one who can forgive their sins. The verse encourages people not to persist in their wrongdoings, but to acknowledge their mistakes and turn back to Allah, knowing that He is the Most Merciful and Forgiving.
orig: والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم ومن يغفر الذنوب إلا الله ولم يصروا على ما فعلوا وهم يعلمون

translation: Those - their reward is with their Lord: Gardens of Eternity, beneath which rivers flow, they will abide therein forever. And excellent is the reward of the [righteous] workers.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward for the righteous believers in the Hereafter. They will be granted forgiveness from their Lord and will reside in the Gardens of Paradise, where rivers flow beneath them, to dwell there eternally. This is an excellent and supreme reward for those who have done righteous deeds in this life.
orig: أولئك جزاؤهم مغفرة من ربهم وجنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ونعم أجر العاملين

translation: There have already been examples [of punishment] before you, so travel through the earth and observe how was the end of those who denied.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to learn from the fate of those who denied the truth in the past. By observing the consequences faced by the deniers, the believers can gain wisdom and strengthen their faith. The verse emphasizes the importance of reflection and understanding the lessons from history, rather than simply denying the truth.
orig: قد خلت من قبلكم سنن فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: This is a clear statement for mankind and a guidance and instruction for those conscious of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a clear and comprehensive message for all of humanity, providing guidance and instruction for those who seek to live righteously and fear Allah.
orig: هذا بيان للناس وهدى وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And do not weaken or be sad, and you will be superior if you are [true] believers.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to remain steadfast, strong and hopeful in the face of adversity. It reminds them that if they maintain their faith, they will ultimately prevail over their enemies and obstacles. The message is one of spiritual and moral superiority through unwavering belief in God.
orig: ولا تهنوا ولا تحزنوا وأنتم الأعلون إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: If a wound has touched you, [so too] has a similar wound touched the [opposing] people. And these days [of varying conditions] We alternate among the people so that Allah may make evident those who believe and [may] take to Himself from among you martyrs - and Allah does not like the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the trials and tribulations faced by the believers are not unique to them, but are common experiences shared by all people. It suggests that adversity is a part of life, and that Allah allows these conditions to alternate among the people in order to test their faith and reveal those who truly believe. The verse also highlights that Allah does not favor the wrongdoers, and that those who give their lives for the cause of faith will be honored as martyrs.
orig: إن يمسسكم قرح فقد مس القوم قرح مثله وتلك الأيام نداولها بين الناس وليعلم الله الذين آمنوا ويتخذ منكم شهداء والله لا يحب الظالمين

translation: And [that] Allah may purify the believers [through trials] and destroy the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah tests the faith of believers through trials and tribulations, in order to purify and strengthen their belief. Meanwhile, the disbelievers who reject faith will be destroyed or eliminated. The interpretation is that Allah's plan involves both the purification of the faithful and the elimination of those who reject faith.
orig: وليمحص الله الذين آمنوا ويمحق الكافرين

translation: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who fight in His cause and made evident the steadfast?
interpretation: This verse questions the assumption that one can simply enter Paradise without having been tested and proven steadfast in their faith and commitment to the cause of Allah. It suggests that Allah will distinguish those who have truly strived and persevered in their faith from those who have not, before granting them entry into Paradise.
orig: أم حسبتم أن تدخلوا الجنة ولما يعلم الله الذين جاهدوا منكم ويعلم الصابرين

translation: And indeed, you used to wish for death before you met it, and you have [now] seen it as you looked [at it].
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who had previously wished for death and martyrdom in the cause of Allah, but when they faced it, they saw it as it truly is - a difficult and challenging experience. The verse emphasizes that the believers had a strong desire for the afterlife and were willing to sacrifice their lives for their faith, but when confronted with the reality of death, they were able to witness it directly, which made them realize the gravity of their decision.
orig: ولقد كنتم تمنون الموت من قبل أن تلقوه فقد رأيتموه وأنتم تنظرون

translation: Muhammad is not but a messenger. [Other] messengers have passed on before him. So if he was to die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels [to unbelief]? And he who turns back on his heels will never harm Allah at all; but Allah will reward the grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is a messenger of God, just like the messengers who came before him. It reminds the believers that even if Prophet Muhammad were to die or be killed, they should not turn away from their faith. Those who turn back on their faith will not harm God in any way, but God will reward those who are grateful and steadfast in their belief.
orig: وما محمد إلا رسول قد خلت من قبله الرسل أفإن مات أو قتل انقلبتم على أعقابكم ومن ينقلب على عقبيه فلن يضر الله شيئا وسيجزي الله الشاكرين

translation: And no soul can die except by permission of Allah at a decree determined. And whoever desires the reward of this world - We will give him thereof; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter - We will give him thereof. And we will surely reward the grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the timing of a person's death is determined by Allah, not by human will. It also highlights that those who seek the rewards of this world or the Hereafter will be granted what they desire, but that the grateful will be especially rewarded by Allah.
orig: وما كان لنفس أن تموت إلا بإذن الله كتابا مؤجلا ومن يرد ثواب الدنيا نؤته منها ومن يرد ثواب الآخرة نؤته منها وسنجزي الشاكرين

translation: And how many a prophet [fought and] with him fought many religious scholars. But they never lost determination because of what afflicted them in the cause of Allah, nor did they weaken or submit. And Allah loves the steadfast.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and perseverance in the face of adversity, even when facing overwhelming odds. It highlights that the true believers, represented by the prophets and their companions, did not lose their determination or give in to weakness, despite the trials and tribulations they faced in the cause of Allah. This serves as an encouragement for the believers to remain steadfast and patient, as Allah loves those who persevere.
orig: وكأين من نبي قاتل معه ربيون كثير فما وهنوا لما أصابهم في سبيل الله وما ضعفوا وما استكانوا والله يحب الصابرين

translation: And their saying was not but that they said, "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and the excess [commitment] in our affairs, and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people."
interpretation: This verse expresses the humble supplication of the believers, acknowledging their sins and excesses, and seeking forgiveness, steadfastness and divine assistance against the disbelievers. It highlights the importance of repentance, reliance on God, and seeking His help in the face of adversity.
orig: وما كان قولهم إلا أن قالوا ربنا اغفر لنا ذنوبنا وإسرافنا في أمرنا وثبت أقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين

translation: So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the good [reward] of the Hereafter, and Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah rewards those who do good deeds in both this life and the Hereafter. The "reward of this world" refers to the blessings and prosperity that Allah bestows upon the righteous in their earthly lives, while the "good [reward] of the Hereafter" refers to the eternal bliss and rewards awaiting them in the afterlife. The verse concludes by stating that Allah loves and cherishes those who strive to be benevolent and do good for others.
orig: فآتاهم الله ثواب الدنيا وحسن ثواب الآخرة والله يحب المحسنين

translation: O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will [then] become losers.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against obeying the disbelievers, as it would lead them astray and cause them to lose their faith and the rewards of the Hereafter. The believers are urged to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the influence of those who reject the truth of Islam.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تطيعوا الذين كفروا يردوكم على أعقابكم فتنقلبوا خاسرين

translation: Rather, Allah is your protector, and He is the best of helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the true protector and helper of the believers, and that He is the best and most reliable source of support. It encourages the believers to turn to Allah for guidance and assistance, rather than relying on their own strength or the help of others.
orig: بل الله مولاكم وهو خير الناصرين

translation: We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve for what they have associated with Allah of which He had not sent down [any] authority. And their refuge will be the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject faith in God and associate partners with Him will have fear and terror cast into their hearts, as they have no divine authority for their beliefs and actions. Their ultimate abode will be the Fire of Hell, which is a terrible fate for the wrongdoers.
orig: سنلقي في قلوب الذين كفروا الرعب بما أشركوا بالله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا ومأواهم النار وبئس مثوى الظالمين

translation: And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing the enemy by His permission until [the time] when you lost courage and fell to disputing about the order [given by the Prophet] and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love. Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you back from them [defeated] to test you. And He has already forgiven you, and Allah is the possessor of bounty for the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of steadfastness and unity among believers, even in the face of adversity. It reminds us that Allah's promise will be fulfilled, but that we must remain steadfast and obedient to His commands. The verse also acknowledges the human tendency to be distracted by worldly desires, and the need to focus on the Hereafter. Ultimately, Allah tests us to strengthen our faith, and He is the source of bounty and forgiveness for the believers.
orig: ولقد صدقكم الله وعده إذ تحسونهم بإذنه حتى إذا فشلتم وتنازعتم في الأمر وعصيتم من بعد ما أراكم ما تحبون منكم من يريد الدنيا ومنكم من يريد الآخرة ثم صرفكم عنهم ليبتليكم ولقد عفا عنكم والله ذو فضل على المؤمنين

translation: When you were ascending [the mountain] and did not turn toward anyone while the Messenger of Allah was calling you from behind, so He imposed upon you distress after [your] distress that you might not grieve over what had escaped you or [for] what had struck you. And Allah is [fully] Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Muslims who were ascending the mountain during a battle, and did not turn back to assist the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) who was calling them from behind. As a result, they experienced distress and hardship, which was a consequence of their disobedience. The verse emphasizes that this was to prevent them from grieving over what they had missed out on or what had befallen them. It also highlights that Allah is fully aware of their actions and will hold them accountable.
orig: إذ تصعدون ولا تلوون على أحد والرسول يدعوكم في أخراكم فأثابكم غما بغم لكيلا تحزنوا على ما فاتكم ولا ما أصابكم والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Then after the distress, He sent down upon you security [in the form of] drowsiness, [overtaking] a party of you, while another party worried about themselves, thinking of Allah other than the truth - the thought of ignorance, saying, "Is there anything for us [to have done] in this matter?" Say, "Indeed, the matter belongs completely to Allah." They conceal within themselves what they will not reveal to you. They say, "If there was anything for us to have [in this] matter, we would not have been killed here." Say, "Even if you had remained in your houses, those decreed to be killed would have gone out to the places of their [final] rest." [It was] so that Allah might test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts. And Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse describes the situation after the battle of Uhud, where the Muslims suffered a setback. It highlights how some were overcome by drowsiness while others were anxious, doubting Allah's plan. The verse emphasizes that the matter belongs entirely to Allah, and that He tests and purifies the hearts of the believers. The interpretation is that even in times of distress, we must trust in Allah's wisdom and not give in to doubts or anxiety, for He is All-Knowing of what is in our hearts.
orig: ثم أنزل عليكم من بعد الغم أمنة نعاسا يغشى طائفة منكم وطائفة قد أهمتهم أنفسهم يظنون بالله غير الحق ظن الجاهلية يقولون هل لنا من الأمر من شيء قل إن الأمر كله لله يخفون في أنفسهم ما لا يبدون لك يقولون لو كان لنا من الأمر شيء ما قتلنا هاهنا قل لو كنتم في بيوتكم لبرز الذين كتب عليهم القتل إلى مضاجعهم وليبتلي الله ما في صدوركم وليمحص ما في قلوبكم والله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Indeed, those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met [at Uhud] - it was Satan who caused them to slip because of some [of the sins] they had earned. But Allah has already forgiven them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers who retreated during the Battle of Uhud, when the Muslim army was defeated by the Quraysh. The verse explains that it was Satan who caused them to slip and retreat, due to some of their sins. However, Allah has forgiven them, as He is Forgiving and Forbearing. The interpretation suggests that even when believers falter, Allah is willing to forgive them if they repent and return to the right path.
orig: إن الذين تولوا منكم يوم التقى الجمعان إنما استزلهم الشيطان ببعض ما كسبوا ولقد عفا الله عنهم إن الله غفور حليم

translation: O you who believe! Do not be like those who disbelieved and said of their brothers when they traveled through the land or went out to fight: "If they had been with us, they would not have died or have been killed," so Allah makes that [misconception] a regret within their hearts. And it is Allah who gives life and causes death, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have strong faith and trust in Allah's plan, and not to be like the disbelievers who questioned Allah's decree. The disbelievers expressed regret over the deaths of their comrades, as if their presence could have prevented it. This verse reminds us that life and death are in Allah's hands, and we should not question His wisdom. Instead, we should have unwavering faith and submit to Allah's will.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تكونوا كالذين كفروا وقالوا لإخوانهم إذا ضربوا في الأرض أو كانوا غزى لو كانوا عندنا ما ماتوا وما قتلوا ليجعل الله ذلك حسرة في قلوبهم والله يحيي ويميت والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And if you are killed in the cause of Allah or die - then forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than whatever they accumulate [in this world].
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be steadfast in their faith and not fear death, as the forgiveness and mercy of Allah are far more valuable than any worldly possessions or gains. It reminds us that the true reward lies in the hereafter, not in this temporary life.
orig: ولئن قتلتم في سبيل الله أو متم لمغفرة من الله ورحمة خير مما يجمعون

translation: And whether you die or are killed, unto Allah you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that regardless of how one's life ends, whether through natural death or martyrdom, all people will ultimately be held accountable before God on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder to live one's life in a way that is pleasing to God, as we will all return to Him.
orig: ولئن متم أو قتلتم لإلى الله تحشرون

translation: So by mercy from Allah, [O Muhammad], you were lenient with them. And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh in heart, they would have disbanded from about you. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult them in the matter. And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah. Indeed, Allah loves those who rely [upon Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of compassion, forgiveness, and consultation in leadership. It teaches that a leader should be gentle and merciful, even towards those who may have opposed them. By being lenient and forgiving, the leader can maintain the loyalty and support of their followers. At the same time, the leader should also seek the counsel of others and rely on Allah's guidance when making decisions, as this is the way of the righteous.
orig: فبما رحمة من الله لنت لهم ولو كنت فظا غليظ القلب لانفضوا من حولك فاعف عنهم واستغفر لهم وشاورهم في الأمر فإذا عزمت فتوكل على الله إن الله يحب المتوكلين

translation: If Allah helps you, no one can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there, after Him, that can help you? And upon Allah let the believers put their trust.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah for help and victory. It conveys that if Allah supports the believers, no one can defeat them. Conversely, if Allah withdraws His support, no one else can provide the necessary help. Therefore, the believers should put their complete trust in Allah, as He is the ultimate source of support and victory.
orig: إن ينصركم الله فلا غالب لكم وإن يخذلكم فمن ذا الذي ينصركم من بعده وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And it is not [attributable] to any prophet that he would [intentionally] deceive. And whoever deceives - he will bring what he deceived on the Day of Resurrection. Then will every soul be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be treated unjustly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and integrity for prophets and all believers. It warns against any form of deception or misappropriation of resources, as the perpetrator will be held accountable on the Day of Judgment. The verse also reaffirms the principle of individual responsibility, where each person will be judged based on their own actions and not subjected to any injustice.
orig: وما كان لنبي أن يغل ومن يغلل يأت بما غل يوم القيامة ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Then is one who follows the approval of Allah [to be considered] like one who has incurred the wrath of Allah, and whose refuge is Hell? And wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between those who seek the pleasure and approval of Allah, and those who incur His wrath. The former will be rewarded with eternal bliss, while the latter will be condemned to the torment of Hell, which is a terrible destination. The verse encourages believers to strive for Allah's pleasure and avoid His displeasure, as the consequences are vastly different.
orig: أفمن اتبع رضوان الله كمن باء بسخط من الله ومأواه جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: They are [of] varying degrees in the sight of Allah, and Allah is Seeing of whatever they do.
interpretation: This verse indicates that people have different ranks and statuses in the sight of Allah, based on their faith, deeds, and level of obedience. Allah is All-Knowing and All-Seeing, and He is fully aware of the actions and intentions of every person.
orig: هم درجات عند الله والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: Certainly has Allah conferred [great] favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although they had been before in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense blessing and favor that God has bestowed upon the believers by sending them a Messenger from among themselves. The Messenger recites God's verses to them, purifies them spiritually, and teaches them the Book (the Quran) and wisdom. This is particularly significant because the believers were previously in a state of manifest error, and God has guided them to the right path through this Messenger.
orig: لقد من الله على المؤمنين إذ بعث فيهم رسولا من أنفسهم يتلو عليهم آياته ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين

translation: And when a misfortune befalls you, you say, "How is this?" Say, "This is from yourselves." Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the trials and tribulations that befall us are a result of our own actions and choices. It encourages us to take responsibility for our circumstances, rather than blaming external factors. The verse also reminds us that Allah has power over all things, and that ultimately, our fate is in His hands.
orig: أولما أصابتكم مصيبة قد أصبتم مثليها قلتم أنى هذا قل هو من عند أنفسكم إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And whatever [calamity] has struck you - it was not to cause you failure but [is] that Allah may make evident the [true] believers
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing that any hardship or calamity that befalls the believers is not a sign of their failure, but rather a means for Allah to distinguish the true believers from those who are weak in their faith. It serves to test and purify the believers, strengthening their resolve and trust in Allah's plan.
orig: وما أصابكم يوم التقى الجمعان فبإذن الله وليعلم المؤمنين

translation: And let those who oppose the Messenger [Muhammad] know that for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who pretend to be believers but in reality are disbelievers. It warns them that their true nature will be exposed and they will face a painful punishment for their hypocrisy and opposition to the Prophet Muhammad. The verse emphasizes that Allah knows what they are hiding in their hearts, even if they try to conceal it with their words.
orig: وليعلم الذين نافقوا وقيل لهم تعالوا قاتلوا في سبيل الله أو ادفعوا قالوا لو نعلم قتالا لاتبعناكم هم للكفر يومئذ أقرب منهم للإيمان يقولون بأفواههم ما ليس في قلوبهم والله أعلم بما يكتمون

translation: Those who said about their brethren while they themselves sat [at home]: "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed." Say, "Then avert death from yourselves if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who remained passive and did not support their brethren who went out to fight. They are being admonished for their inaction and for making excuses. The interpretation is that one should not simply sit back and make claims about what could have been, but rather take responsibility and action to avert harm if they truly believe in their position.
orig: الذين قالوا لإخوانهم وقعدوا لو أطاعونا ما قتلوا قل فادرءوا عن أنفسكم الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And never think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are martyred while fighting for the cause of Allah are not to be considered dead, but rather they are alive with their Lord and being provided for. This conveys the idea that martyrdom is not a cause for grief, but rather a means of attaining a higher spiritual state and eternal life in the hereafter.
orig: ولا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون

translation: Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty, and they receive good tidings about those [to be granted] after them who have not yet joined them - no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the believers who are rejoicing in the blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon them. They are also receiving good news about those who have not yet joined them in faith, indicating that these people will also be granted Allah's bounty and blessings. The verse emphasizes that the believers will have no fear or grief, as they are secure in their faith and the knowledge of Allah's protection and guidance.
orig: فرحين بما آتاهم الله من فضله ويستبشرون بالذين لم يلحقوا بهم من خلفهم ألا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: They rejoice in a grace from Allah and [His] bounty. And that Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of believers.
interpretation: This verse conveys a message of hope and reassurance for the believers. It suggests that those who have faith in Allah will be rewarded for their deeds, and that Allah's grace and blessings will not be lost or wasted. The verse encourages the believers to rejoice in Allah's favor and to have confidence that their righteous actions will be acknowledged and rewarded.
orig: يستبشرون بنعمة من الله وفضل وأن الله لا يضيع أجر المؤمنين

translation: Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after injury had struck them and who do good among them and fear Allah - for them is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith even in the face of adversity. It promises a great reward for those who respond to the call of Allah and the Prophet, and who continue to do good deeds and fear Allah, despite having faced hardship or injury. The verse emphasizes the importance of perseverance, faith, and righteous conduct, even in challenging circumstances.
orig: الذين استجابوا لله والرسول من بعد ما أصابهم القرح للذين أحسنوا منهم واتقوا أجر عظيم

translation: Those to whom the people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them." But it [merely] increased them in faith, and they said, "Sufficient for us is Allah, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs."
interpretation: This verse speaks of the steadfastness and trust in Allah displayed by the believers when faced with adversity. Despite the threats from their opponents, the believers' faith was strengthened, and they placed their complete trust in Allah as their Protector and Guardian. This verse encourages Muslims to maintain their faith and reliance on Allah, even in the face of challenges and opposition.
orig: الذين قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم فاخشوهم فزادهم إيمانا وقالوا حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل

translation: So they returned with favor from Allah and bounty, no harm having touched them. And they followed the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who follow the guidance of Allah and seek His pleasure will be rewarded with His blessings and protection. They will be granted favor and bounty from Allah, and will be spared from harm or suffering. The verse highlights Allah's great generosity and the importance of submitting to His will.
orig: فانقلبوا بنعمة من الله وفضل لم يمسسهم سوء واتبعوا رضوان الله والله ذو فضل عظيم

translation: That is only Satan who frightens [you of] his supporters. So fear them not, but fear Me, if you are [indeed] believers.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers not to be afraid of Satan's supporters, but rather to fear Allah alone. It emphasizes that the threats and fears instilled by Satan should not deter the faithful from following the path of righteousness. The true believers are called to have faith in Allah and to place their trust in Him, rather than being intimidated by the schemes of the devil and his followers.
orig: إنما ذلكم الشيطان يخوف أولياءه فلا تخافوهم وخافون إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And let not those grieve you who hasten into disbelief. Indeed, they will never harm Allah at all. [It is] Allah's will to not to assign them a portion in the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that he should not be distressed by those who rush to disbelieve in Allah and reject the message of Islam. Their disbelief cannot harm Allah in any way, as Allah is All-Powerful and All-Knowing. Rather, Allah has decreed that those who disbelieve will have no share in the rewards of the Hereafter, and they will face a severe punishment for their rejection of faith.
orig: ولا يحزنك الذين يسارعون في الكفر إنهم لن يضروا الله شيئا يريد الله ألا يجعل لهم حظا في الآخرة ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: Indeed, those who have exchanged disbelief for faith will not harm Allah at all, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have chosen disbelief over faith will not be able to harm or diminish the power of Allah in any way. Instead, they will face a painful punishment for their choice. The message is that faith in Allah is the only true path, and those who reject it will face severe consequences.
orig: إن الذين اشتروا الكفر بالإيمان لن يضروا الله شيئا ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And let not those who disbelieve ever think that [because] We extend their time [of enjoyment] it is better for them. We only extend it for them so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against the mistaken belief that the delay in punishment for the disbelievers is a sign of Allah's favor. Rather, the respite given to them is to allow them to increase in their sins, leading to a more severe and humiliating punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا أنما نملي لهم خير لأنفسهم إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما ولهم عذاب مهين

translation: Allah would not leave the believers in that [state] you are in [i.e., senseless] until He separates the evil from the good. And Allah would not inform you of the unseen. But Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills, so believe in Allah and His messengers. And if you believe and fear Allah, then for you is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah will test and distinguish the believers from the unbelievers, and that He alone has knowledge of the unseen. It encourages believers to have faith in Allah and His messengers, and promises a great reward for those who believe and are righteous.
orig: ما كان الله ليذر المؤمنين على ما أنتم عليه حتى يميز الخبيث من الطيب وما كان الله ليطلعكم على الغيب ولكن الله يجتبي من رسله من يشاء فآمنوا بالله ورسله وإن تؤمنوا وتتقوا فلكم أجر عظيم

translation: And let not those who [greedily] withhold of what Allah has given them of His bounty ever think that it is better for them. Rather, it is worse for them. Their wealth will be tied to their necks on the Day of Resurrection. And to Allah belongs the heritage of the heavens and the earth. And Allah, with what you do, is [fully] Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse warns against the sin of miserliness and greed. It states that those who hoard their wealth and do not spend it in the way of Allah will find that their wealth will be a burden to them on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes that all wealth ultimately belongs to Allah, and that He is fully aware of our actions and will hold us accountable for how we use the resources He has provided us.
orig: ولا يحسبن الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله هو خيرا لهم بل هو شر لهم سيطوقون ما بخلوا به يوم القيامة ولله ميراث السماوات والأرض والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: Certainly Allah has heard the statement of those who say, "Indeed, Allah is poor, while we are rich." We will record what they said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire."
interpretation: This verse condemns the arrogance and disbelief of those who claim that they are wealthy while Allah is poor. It highlights that Allah has heard their blasphemous statements and will hold them accountable for their rejection of the truth and their unjust persecution of the prophets. The verse warns them of the severe punishment they will face in the Hereafter for their transgressions.
orig: لقد سمع الله قول الذين قالوا إن الله فقير ونحن أغنياء سنكتب ما قالوا وقتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق ونقول ذوقوا عذاب الحريق

translation: That is because of what your hands have put forth [of evil], and indeed, Allah is not unjust to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the consequences people face are a result of their own actions and choices. Allah is not unjust, but rather people are accountable for their deeds. The interpretation suggests that one should take responsibility for their decisions and actions, as Allah is fair and just in His judgement.
orig: ذلك بما قدمت أيديكم وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد

translation: Those who say, "Indeed, Allah has enjoined upon us not to believe in any messenger until he brings us an offering which fire [from heaven] will consume." Say, "There have already come to you messengers before me with clear signs and [even] that of which you speak. So why did you kill them, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse addresses a group of people who demanded a specific sign, namely that a messenger should bring an offering which fire from heaven would consume, as a condition for them to believe in the messenger. The verse rejects this demand and reminds them that previous messengers had already brought clear signs, but the people had killed them instead of believing. The interpretation suggests that faith should not be conditional on specific miraculous signs, but rather on the merits of the message and the character of the messenger.
orig: الذين قالوا إن الله عهد إلينا ألا نؤمن لرسول حتى يأتينا بقربان تأكله النار قل قد جاءكم رسل من قبلي بالبينات وبالذي قلتم فلم قتلتموهم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then already have those before you been denied when they came with clear proofs and written ordinances and the enlightening Scripture.
interpretation: This verse is reassuring the Prophet Muhammad that if his people reject his message, it is not something unique to him, as previous messengers before him were also rejected by their people despite bringing clear proofs, scriptures, and guidance. This serves to console the Prophet and remind him that the rejection of the message is not a reflection on him, but rather a pattern that has occurred throughout history.
orig: فإن كذبوك فقد كذب رسل من قبلك جاءوا بالبينات والزبر والكتاب المنير

translation: Every soul will taste death, and you will only be given your [full] compensation on the Day of Resurrection. So he who is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained [his desire]. And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of death, and that the true reward for one's deeds will be given on the Day of Resurrection. It highlights that the ultimate success is to be saved from the Fire and admitted into Paradise, which is the true and lasting abode. In contrast, the life of this world is described as a mere "enjoyment of delusion", suggesting its transient and deceptive nature compared to the eternal life in the Hereafter.
orig: كل نفس ذائقة الموت وإنما توفون أجوركم يوم القيامة فمن زحزح عن النار وأدخل الجنة فقد فاز وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور

translation: You will surely be tested in your possessions and in yourselves. And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah much abuse. But if you are patient and fear Allah - indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of determination.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be steadfast and patient in the face of trials and tribulations, whether related to their wealth and possessions or their own selves. It also warns that they will face much abuse and opposition from those who have received divine scriptures before them, as well as from those who associate partners with Allah. However, the verse emphasizes that if the believers remain patient and God-conscious, this is a sign of their strong determination and resolve.
orig: لتبلون في أموالكم وأنفسكم ولتسمعن من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الذين أشركوا أذى كثيرا وإن تصبروا وتتقوا فإن ذلك من عزم الأمور

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Allah took the covenant of the [people of the] Scripture, [saying], "Inform the people and do not conceal it." But they threw it away behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price. And wretched is that which they purchased.
interpretation: This verse condemns the actions of those who were entrusted with divine scriptures, such as the Jews and Christians, for concealing or distorting the truth that was revealed to them. They had a responsibility to convey the message faithfully to the people, but instead they hid or altered it for their own gain, trading it for a meager worldly benefit. This is a grave sin, as they have betrayed their trust and deprived humanity of the guidance that was meant for them.
orig: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب لتبيننه للناس ولا تكتمونه فنبذوه وراء ظهورهم واشتروا به ثمنا قليلا فبئس ما يشترون

translation: Do not consider those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they did not do, as being exempt from the punishment, for they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who boast about their accomplishments and seek praise for things they did not actually do. It cautions that such people will not escape punishment, and they will face a painful consequence for their deception and vanity.
orig: لا تحسبن الذين يفرحون بما أتوا ويحبون أن يحمدوا بما لم يفعلوا فلا تحسبنهم بمفازة من العذاب ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over the entire universe. It emphasizes that Allah is the sole owner and ruler of the heavens and the earth, and that He has complete control and authority over all things. This serves to remind us of the greatness and supremacy of Allah, and that we should submit to His will and seek His guidance in all aspects of our lives.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the creation of the heavens and the earth, as well as the alternation of night and day, are clear signs and evidence of the existence, power, and wisdom of God. These signs are meant to be contemplated and understood by those who possess intellect and wisdom, in order to deepen their faith and awareness of the divine.
orig: إن في خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار لآيات لأولي الألباب

translation: Those who remember Allah while standing or sitting or [lying] on their sides and give thought to the creation of the heavens and the earth, [saying], "Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly; exalted are You [above such a thing]; then protect us from the punishment of the Fire."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to constantly remember and reflect upon Allah and His creation. It highlights the importance of engaging in dhikr (remembrance of Allah) in various postures, whether standing, sitting, or lying down. The act of contemplating the wonders of the heavens and the earth is also emphasized, as it leads to a deeper understanding of Allah's power, wisdom, and purpose. The verse culminates in a supplication, where the believers humbly ask Allah to protect them from the punishment of the Hellfire, recognizing that the creation of the universe was not in vain, but rather a manifestation of Allah's glory and a means for believers to seek His guidance and forgiveness.
orig: الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم ويتفكرون في خلق السماوات والأرض ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا سبحانك فقنا عذاب النار

translation: Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire - You have [already] disgraced him, and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are condemned to Hell have already been disgraced by Allah, and that the wrongdoers have no one to help or support them. It serves as a warning against wrongdoing and a reminder of Allah's ultimate authority and justice.
orig: ربنا إنك من تدخل النار فقد أخزيته وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, [saying], 'Believe in your Lord,' and we have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds and [cause us to] die with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse expresses the believers' response to the call to faith. They acknowledge that they have heard the call to believe in God, and they have responded by believing in Him. They then ask God to forgive their sins, remove their misdeeds, and allow them to die alongside the righteous people. This shows the believers' humility, their desire for forgiveness and purification, and their hope to be counted among the righteous in the Hereafter.
orig: ربنا إننا سمعنا مناديا ينادي للإيمان أن آمنوا بربكم فآمنا ربنا فاغفر لنا ذنوبنا وكفر عنا سيئاتنا وتوفنا مع الأبرار

translation: Our Lord, and grant us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail in [Your] promise.
interpretation: This verse expresses a supplication to Allah, the Almighty, to fulfill His promise that He has made to the believers through His messengers. It reflects the believers' desire to be granted the rewards and blessings that Allah has promised, and to be spared the disgrace and humiliation on the Day of Resurrection. The verse also affirms the believers' trust in Allah's faithfulness and that He will never fail to keep His promise.
orig: ربنا وآتنا ما وعدتنا على رسلك ولا تخزنا يوم القيامة إنك لا تخلف الميعاد

translation: So their Lord responded to them, "Never will I allow to be lost the work of [any] worker among you, whether male or female; you are of one another. So those who emigrated or were driven out from their homes or were harmed in My cause or fought or were killed - I will surely remove from them their misdeeds, and I will surely admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow as reward from Allah, and Allah has with Him the best of rewards."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah will not let the good deeds of any believer, whether male or female, go to waste. It promises that those who have suffered for the sake of their faith - whether by emigrating, being driven out of their homes, being harmed, fighting, or being killed - will be forgiven their sins and admitted to the gardens of Paradise as a reward from Allah, who has the best of rewards.
orig: فاستجاب لهم ربهم أني لا أضيع عمل عامل منكم من ذكر أو أنثى بعضكم من بعض فالذين هاجروا وأخرجوا من ديارهم وأوذوا في سبيلي وقاتلوا وقتلوا لأكفرن عنهم سيئاتهم ولأدخلنهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ثوابا من عند الله والله عنده حسن الثواب

translation: Let not the [free] movement of the disbelievers throughout the land deceive you.
interpretation: This verse cautions against being deceived by the apparent prosperity and freedom of movement enjoyed by those who disbelieve in God. It reminds that their worldly success is not an indication of their righteousness or a sign of God's approval, and that ultimately they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: لا يغرنك تقلب الذين كفروا في البلاد

translation: A brief enjoyment, then their abode is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse conveys the fleeting nature of worldly pleasures and the ultimate fate of those who indulge in them without regard for the Hereafter. It suggests that the temporary enjoyments of this life are insignificant compared to the eternal punishment of Hell, which is an unpleasant and uncomfortable place for those who have failed to live righteously.
orig: متاع قليل ثم مأواهم جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: But those who feared their Lord will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein, a hospitality from Allah. And that which is with Allah is best for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are pious and fear Allah will be rewarded with eternal bliss in the Hereafter. They will be granted gardens with flowing rivers, where they will dwell forever as honored guests of Allah. This is the best reward that Allah can bestow upon the righteous, as nothing that is with Allah can be surpassed in its goodness and value.
orig: لكن الذين اتقوا ربهم لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها نزلا من عند الله وما عند الله خير للأبرار

translation: And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in Allah and what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, [being] humbly submissive to Allah. They do not exchange the verses of Allah for a small price. Those - for them is their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse highlights that there are righteous people among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who believe in Allah and the revelations sent to them, as well as the Qur'an revealed to Prophet Muhammad. These people are humble and devoted in their submission to Allah, and they do not trade away the verses of Allah for a meager worldly gain. For such people, there is a great reward from their Lord, as Allah is swift in holding people accountable for their deeds.
orig: وإن من أهل الكتاب لمن يؤمن بالله وما أنزل إليكم وما أنزل إليهم خاشعين لله لا يشترون بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا أولئك لهم أجرهم عند ربهم إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: O you who believe, be patient and encourage one another in patience and stand firm and fear Allah that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be steadfast, persevere, and support one another in the face of adversity. It emphasizes the importance of fearing and obeying Allah in order to attain success and prosperity in this life and the hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed Allah is to you ever an Observer.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of humanity, as all people are descended from a single soul. It also highlights the importance of family and kinship ties, reminding people to be mindful of their responsibilities towards their relatives. The verse underscores that Allah is ever-watchful over His creation, and that people should be conscious of this in their actions and interactions with others.
orig: يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة وخلق منها زوجها وبث منهما رجالا كثيرا ونساء واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا

translation: And give to the orphans their properties and do not substitute the defective [of your own] for the good [of theirs]. And do not consume their wealth along with your own. Indeed, that is a great sin.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to manage the wealth of orphans with care, honesty and integrity. It prohibits taking advantage of orphans by substituting their good wealth with one's own inferior wealth, or consuming their wealth along with one's own. Doing so is considered a grave sin, as the wealth of orphans must be protected and preserved for their rightful benefit.
orig: وآتوا اليتامى أموالهم ولا تتبدلوا الخبيث بالطيب ولا تأكلوا أموالهم إلى أموالكم إنه كان حوبا كبيرا

translation: And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry those that please you of [other] women, two or three or four. But if you fear that you will not be just, then [marry only] one or those your right hands possess. That is more suitable that you may not incline [to injustice].
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of caring for orphan girls and the importance of treating them justly. It encourages marrying other women, up to four, if one fears not being able to deal fairly with orphan girls. However, it emphasizes that if one cannot ensure justice, then one should marry only one wife or those whom one's right hand possesses (i.e., female slaves). This is a more suitable approach to avoid inclining towards injustice.
orig: وإن خفتم ألا تقسطوا في اليتامى فانكحوا ما طاب لكم من النساء مثنى وثلاث ورباع فإن خفتم ألا تعدلوا فواحدة أو ما ملكت أيمانكم ذلك أدنى ألا تعولوا

translation: And give the women [upon marriage] their [bridal] gifts graciously. But if they give up willingly to you anything of it, then take it in satisfaction and ease.
interpretation: This verse instructs men to give women their bridal gifts willingly and graciously. If the women choose to forgo part of the gift, the men may accept it with satisfaction and ease, without any coercion or pressure.
orig: وآتوا النساء صدقاتهن نحلة فإن طبن لكم عن شيء منه نفسا فكلوه هنيئا مريئا

translation: And do not give the foolish your wealth which Allah has made a means of sustenance for you. But provide for them with it and clothe them and speak to them words of kindness.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers not to entrust their wealth to those who are incapable of managing it wisely. Instead, they should use their wealth to support and care for the less fortunate, providing for their needs and speaking to them with kindness and compassion. The underlying message is that wealth is a trust from Allah to be used responsibly for the benefit of the community, not merely for personal gain or indulgence.
orig: ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم التي جعل الله لكم قياما وارزقوهم فيها واكسوهم وقولوا لهم قولا معروفا

translation: And test the orphans [in their abilities] until they reach marriageable age. Then if you perceive in them sound judgement, release their wealth to them. And do not consume it excessively and quickly, [anticipating] that they will grow up. And whoever is wealthy - let him refrain [from taking, i.e., using, the orphan's wealth]. And whoever is poor - let him consume [from it] in an acceptable manner. And when you release their wealth to them, bring witnesses upon them. And sufficient is Allah as Accountant.
interpretation: This verse instructs the guardians of orphans to carefully assess the orphans' maturity and ability to manage their own wealth before releasing it to them. The guardians should not consume the orphans' wealth excessively or quickly, but rather preserve it for when the orphans come of age. The verse also encourages the wealthy to refrain from using the orphans' wealth, and the poor to consume it in a reasonable manner. Finally, it emphasizes the importance of having witnesses present when the wealth is returned to the orphans, and that ultimately, Allah is the best judge of one's actions.
orig: وابتلوا اليتامى حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح فإن آنستم منهم رشدا فادفعوا إليهم أموالهم ولا تأكلوها إسرافا وبدارا أن يكبروا ومن كان غنيا فليستعفف ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف فإذا دفعتم إليهم أموالهم فأشهدوا عليهم وكفى بالله حسيبا

translation: For men is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, and for women is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, be it little or much - an obligatory share.
interpretation: This verse establishes the inheritance rights of men and women. It states that both genders have a rightful share in the inheritance of their parents and close relatives, regardless of whether the inheritance is little or much. This is an obligatory share that must be respected and upheld.
orig: للرجال نصيب مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون وللنساء نصيب مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون مما قل منه أو كثر نصيبا مفروضا

translation: And when [other] relatives and orphans and the needy are present at the [time of] division, then provide for them [something] out of it [i.e., the wealth] and speak to them words of appropriate kindness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of caring for one's relatives, orphans, and the needy when distributing wealth. It instructs the believers to not only provide for them financially, but also to speak to them with kindness and compassion. The verse encourages a sense of social responsibility and concern for the less fortunate within the community.
orig: وإذا حضر القسمة أولو القربى واليتامى والمساكين فارزقوهم منه وقولوا لهم قولا معروفا

translation: And let those [executors and guardians] fear [Allah] who, if they left behind them [children who are] weak, would be afraid for them. So let them fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.
interpretation: This verse encourages those in positions of responsibility and authority to be mindful of the well-being of those who are weak and vulnerable, especially children. It exhorts them to fear Allah and speak words that are just and righteous, in order to protect the interests of those who may be left behind and unable to fend for themselves.
orig: وليخش الذين لو تركوا من خلفهم ذرية ضعافا خافوا عليهم فليتقوا الله وليقولوا قولا سديدا

translation: Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly are but consuming fire, and they will be burned in a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse condemns the exploitation and misuse of the wealth and property of orphans. It emphasizes that those who engage in such unjust practices are essentially consuming fire, which is a metaphor for the severe punishment they will face in the Hereafter. The interpretation underscores the gravity of this offense and the importance of safeguarding the rights and well-being of the vulnerable in society.
orig: إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما إنما يأكلون في بطونهم نارا وسيصلون سعيرا

translation: Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females. But if there are [only] daughters, two or more, for them is two-thirds of one's estate. And if there is only one daughter, for her is half. And for his [deceased] parents, each one of them is a sixth of his estate if he left children. But if he had no children and his parents [alone] inherit from him, then for his mother is one-third. And if he had brothers [or sisters], for his mother is a sixth, after any bequest he [may have] made or debt. Your parents and your children - you know not which of them are nearest to you in benefit. [These shares are] an obligation [imposed] by Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever All-Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse outlines the Islamic inheritance laws, which aim to ensure a fair distribution of a deceased person's estate among their heirs. The key points are: 1) For male heirs, the share is equal to that of two female heirs; 2) If there are two or more daughters, they receive two-thirds of the estate; 3) If there is only one daughter, she receives half the estate; 4) The parents of the deceased receive a sixth each if the deceased had children, or the mother receives a third if the deceased had no children; 5) The shares are set by Allah and must be followed, as He is All-Knowing and Wise.
orig: يوصيكم الله في أولادكم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين فإن كن نساء فوق اثنتين فلهن ثلثا ما ترك وإن كانت واحدة فلها النصف ولأبويه لكل واحد منهما السدس مما ترك إن كان له ولد فإن لم يكن له ولد وورثه أبواه فلأمه الثلث فإن كان له إخوة فلأمه السدس من بعد وصية يوصي بها أو دين آباؤكم وأبناؤكم لا تدرون أيهم أقرب لكم نفعا فريضة من الله إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: And for you is half of what your wives leave if they have no child. But if they have a child, for you is one fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they [may have] made or debt. And for them [i.e., the wives] is one fourth if you have no child. But if you have a child, then for them is the eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you [may have] made or debt. And if a man or woman leaves neither ascendants nor descendants but has a brother or a sister, then for each one of them is the sixth. But if they are more than two, they share a third, after any bequest which was made or debt, as long as there is no detriment [caused]. [This is] an ordinance from Allah, and Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse outlines the inheritance shares for spouses and siblings in the case of death. The key points are: 1) The husband is entitled to half of the wife's estate if she has no children, and a quarter if she has children. 2) The wife is entitled to a quarter of the husband's estate if he has no children, and an eighth if he has children. 3) If the deceased has no descendants, their siblings inherit a sixth each if there is only one, or a third if there are more than two. This distribution is an ordinance from Allah, who is all-knowing and forbearing.
orig: ولكم نصف ما ترك أزواجكم إن لم يكن لهن ولد فإن كان لهن ولد فلكم الربع مما تركن من بعد وصية يوصين بها أو دين ولهن الربع مما تركتم إن لم يكن لكم ولد فإن كان لكم ولد فلهن الثمن مما تركتم من بعد وصية توصون بها أو دين وإن كان رجل يورث كلالة أو امرأة وله أخ أو أخت فلكل واحد منهما السدس فإن كانوا أكثر من ذلك فهم شركاء في الثلث من بعد وصية يوصى بها أو دين غير مضار وصية من الله والله عليم حليم

translation: These are the limits [set by] Allah, and whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be admitted by Him to gardens [in Paradise] under which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. And that is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obeying the limits and commands set by Allah. Those who follow Allah and His Messenger will be rewarded with eternal life in the Gardens of Paradise, a great and glorious achievement.
orig: تلك حدود الله ومن يطع الله ورسوله يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits - He will put him into the Fire, wherein he will abide eternally, and he will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of disobeying Allah and His Messenger. It warns that those who transgress the limits set by Allah will be punished by being consigned to the eternal Fire of Hell, where they will face a humiliating and degrading punishment. The message is clear: obedience to Allah and His Messenger is essential, and those who defy this will face severe consequences.
orig: ومن يعص الله ورسوله ويتعد حدوده يدخله نارا خالدا فيها وله عذاب مهين

translation: And those who commit unlawful sexual intercourse from among your women - bring against them four [witnesses] from among you. And if they testify, confine the guilty women to their houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them [another] way.
interpretation: This verse outlines the process for dealing with cases of adultery or fornication among Muslim women. It requires four witnesses to testify against the accused, and if the testimony is confirmed, the woman is to be confined to her home until she dies or Allah provides another way for her. The purpose is to ensure justice and prevent the spread of immorality in the community.
orig: واللاتي يأتين الفاحشة من نسائكم فاستشهدوا عليهن أربعة منكم فإن شهدوا فأمسكوهن في البيوت حتى يتوفاهن الموت أو يجعل الله لهن سبيلا

translation: And the two who commit it among you - punish them both. But if they repent and correct themselves, leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the punishment for adultery or fornication. It instructs that the two individuals involved should be punished, but if they repent and reform their behavior, then they should be forgiven and left alone. This highlights God's mercy and willingness to accept repentance, even for grave sins, as long as the person truly turns back to the right path.
orig: واللذان يأتيانها منكم فآذوهما فإن تابا وأصلحا فأعرضوا عنهما إن الله كان توابا رحيما

translation: Repentance is only [accepted] from Allah for those who do wrong in ignorance [or carelessness] and then repent soon after. It is those to whom Allah will turn in forgiveness, and Allah is Ever All-Knower, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true repentance is accepted by Allah for those who commit sins out of ignorance or carelessness, and then promptly turn back to Him in sincere repentance. Allah, being All-Knowing and All-Wise, will forgive those who repent, as He is the Most Merciful and Compassionate.
orig: إنما التوبة على الله للذين يعملون السوء بجهالة ثم يتوبون من قريب فأولئك يتوب الله عليهم وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And repentance is not [accepted] for those who [continue to] do evil deeds up until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now," or for those who die while they are disbelievers. For them We have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true repentance requires a sincere change of heart and actions, not just words spoken at the time of death. Repentance is not accepted from those who continue to commit evil deeds until the moment of death, or from those who die in a state of disbelief. For such people, a severe punishment has been prepared in the Hereafter.
orig: وليست التوبة للذين يعملون السيئات حتى إذا حضر أحدهم الموت قال إني تبت الآن ولا الذين يموتون وهم كفار أولئك أعتدنا لهم عذابا أليما

translation: O you who believe! It is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion. And do not make difficulties for them in order to take [part of] what you have given them [in dowry] unless they commit a clear immorality. And live with them in kindness. For if you dislike them - perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to treat women with respect and kindness, and not to take advantage of them or oppress them. It prohibits the practice of inheriting women against their will, and also forbids making things difficult for them in order to take back the dowry given to them, unless they have committed a clear moral transgression. Instead, believers are commanded to live with women in kindness, even if they dislike them, as Allah may have placed much good in that situation.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا يحل لكم أن ترثوا النساء كرها ولا تعضلوهن لتذهبوا ببعض ما آتيتموهن إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة وعاشروهن بالمعروف فإن كرهتموهن فعسى أن تكرهوا شيئا ويجعل الله فيه خيرا كثيرا

translation: And if you wish to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a great amount [in gifts], do not take [back] from it anything. Would you take it in injustice and manifest sin?
interpretation: This verse prohibits the practice of taking back the dowry or gifts given to a wife in the event of a divorce or replacement of one wife with another. It emphasizes that such an act would be unjust and a clear sin, as the dowry belongs to the wife and should not be taken back from her.
orig: وإن أردتم استبدال زوج مكان زوج وآتيتم إحداهن قنطارا فلا تأخذوا منه شيئا أتأخذونه بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: And how could you take it while you have gone in unto each other and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of marriage and the marital covenant. It questions how one could betray the trust and intimacy of the marital relationship, given the solemn promise and commitment that has been made between the spouses. The verse serves as a reminder to honor and uphold the marriage vows, and not to violate the trust and intimacy that is central to the marital bond.
orig: وكيف تأخذونه وقد أفضى بعضكم إلى بعض وأخذن منكم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: And do not marry those [women] whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred. Indeed, it was an immorality and hateful [to Allah] and an evil way.
interpretation: This verse prohibits marrying the wives of one's father, except for what has already occurred in the past. This practice was considered immoral, detestable, and a bad path in the pre-Islamic Arab society. The verse aims to establish a clear moral and ethical standard for marriage, rejecting customs that were seen as unacceptable.
orig: ولا تنكحوا ما نكح آباؤكم من النساء إلا ما قد سلف إنه كان فاحشة ومقتا وساء سبيلا

translation: Forbidden to you [for marriage] are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your father's sisters, your mother's sisters, your brother's daughters, your sister's daughters, your [milk] mothers who nursed you, your sisters through nursing, your wives' mothers, and your step-daughters under your guardianship [born] of your wives unto whom you have gone in. But if you have not gone in unto them, then there is no sin upon you. And [also prohibited are] the wives of your sons who are from your [own] loins, and that you take [in marriage] two sisters simultaneously, except for what has already occurred. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the prohibited relationships for marriage in Islam. It establishes that one cannot marry their close blood relatives such as mothers, daughters, sisters, aunts, and nieces. It also prohibits marrying the mothers of one's wives, as well as the wives of one's sons. The verse also clarifies that a man cannot marry two sisters simultaneously, except for any past marriages that have already occurred. The verse emphasizes that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, indicating that these prohibitions are out of care for the believers.
orig: حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم وبناتكم وأخواتكم وعماتكم وخالاتكم وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت وأمهاتكم اللاتي أرضعنكم وأخواتكم من الرضاعة وأمهات نسائكم وربائبكم اللاتي في حجوركم من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن فإن لم تكونوا دخلتم بهن فلا جناح عليكم وحلائل أبنائكم الذين من أصلابكم وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين إلا ما قد سلف إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And [also prohibited to you are all] married women except those your right hands possess. [This is] the decree of Allah upon you. And lawful to you are [all others] beyond these, [provided] that you seek them [in marriage] with [gifts from] your wealth, desiring chastity, not unlawful sexual intercourse. So for whatever you enjoy [of marriage] from them, give them their due compensation as an obligation. And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree to beyond the obligation. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the permissibility of marriage with women beyond those already married, except for those whom one's right hand possesses (i.e. female slaves). It emphasizes that such marriages should be sought with the intention of chastity, not unlawful sexual intercourse, and that the dowry must be paid to the women as an obligation. The verse also indicates that there is no blame in mutually agreeing to terms beyond the obligatory dowry, as Allah is All-Knowing and Wise in His rulings.
orig: والمحصنات من النساء إلا ما ملكت أيمانكم كتاب الله عليكم وأحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم أن تبتغوا بأموالكم محصنين غير مسافحين فما استمتعتم به منهن فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة ولا جناح عليكم فيما تراضيتم به من بعد الفريضة إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever among you cannot [find] the means to marry free, believing women, then [he may marry] from those whom your right hands possess of believing slave girls. And Allah is most knowing about your faith. You [believers] are of one another. So marry them with the permission of their people and give them their due compensation [i.e., mahr] in a good manner, they being chaste, neither [of those who commit] unlawful intercourse randomly nor [of those who take] secret lovers. And if when married they should commit adultery, then for them is half the punishment for free [unmarried] women. This [allowance] is for him among you who fears sin, but to be patient is better for you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the Islamic guidelines for marriage, particularly for those who cannot afford to marry free, believing women. It permits marrying believing slave girls, provided that their owners and families give permission, and the marriage is conducted honorably. The verse emphasizes the importance of chastity and discourages illicit relationships. It also prescribes a lesser punishment for married slave women who commit adultery, compared to free women. The overall message is one of compassion and understanding, encouraging patience and forgiveness for those who struggle to fulfill their marital obligations.
orig: ومن لم يستطع منكم طولا أن ينكح المحصنات المؤمنات فمن ما ملكت أيمانكم من فتياتكم المؤمنات والله أعلم بإيمانكم بعضكم من بعض فانكحوهن بإذن أهلهن وآتوهن أجورهن بالمعروف محصنات غير مسافحات ولا متخذات أخدان فإذا أحصن فإن أتين بفاحشة فعليهن نصف ما على المحصنات من العذاب ذلك لمن خشي العنت منكم وأن تصبروا خير لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: Allah intends to make clear to you [the lawful from the unlawful] and guide you to the [good] practices of those before you and to accept your repentance. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah desires to guide and instruct the believers, to show them the righteous ways of those who came before them, and to accept their repentance. The verse highlights Allah's knowledge and wisdom in leading people towards the straight path.
orig: يريد الله ليبين لكم ويهديكم سنن الذين من قبلكم ويتوب عليكم والله عليم حكيم

translation: And Allah intends for you to repent, but those who follow [their] passions want you to digress [into] a great deviation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah desires for people to repent and return to the righteous path, but those who are consumed by their desires and worldly temptations want others to stray far away from the truth and guidance.
orig: والله يريد أن يتوب عليكم ويريد الذين يتبعون الشهوات أن تميلوا ميلا عظيما

translation: Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship, and [He] has made the human being weak.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah desires ease and comfort for His servants, not hardship. It also acknowledges the inherent weakness and limitations of the human being, which is a reminder of our need for Allah's guidance and support.
orig: يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا

translation: O you who believe! Do not consume one another's wealth unjustly but [only [lawful] business by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves [or one another]. Indeed, Allah to you is ever Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of conducting financial transactions with honesty, fairness and mutual consent. It prohibits the unlawful consumption of others' wealth, whether through fraud, exploitation or other unjust means. Additionally, it forbids self-harm or the harming of others, reminding that Allah is merciful and desires only good for His believers.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل إلا أن تكون تجارة عن تراض منكم ولا تقتلوا أنفسكم إن الله كان بكم رحيما

translation: And whoever does that in aggression and injustice - We will drive him into a Fire. And that, for Allah, is [always] easy.
interpretation: This verse warns against committing acts of aggression and injustice, as those who do so will be punished by being cast into the Fire. It emphasizes that for Allah, the punishment of such wrongdoers is an easy matter, as He has power and control over all things.
orig: ومن يفعل ذلك عدوانا وظلما فسوف نصليه نارا وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your lesser sins and admit you to a noble entrance [to Paradise].
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to avoid major sins and transgressions. If they do so, God will forgive their minor sins and grant them a noble and honorable entrance into Paradise. The emphasis is on the importance of repentance and turning away from major sins in order to attain God's forgiveness and eternal bliss.
orig: إن تجتنبوا كبائر ما تنهون عنه نكفر عنكم سيئاتكم وندخلكم مدخلا كريما

translation: And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others. For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned. And ask Allah of His bounty. Indeed Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of equality and justice in Islam. It discourages people from coveting what others have been blessed with, whether it be wealth, status, or other worldly possessions. Instead, it encourages individuals to focus on their own efforts and earnings, and to be grateful for what they have been given. The verse also highlights that both men and women have a rightful share in the fruits of their labor, and that they should seek the bounty of Allah through supplication, as He is All-Knowing of the circumstances of each person.
orig: ولا تتمنوا ما فضل الله به بعضكم على بعض للرجال نصيب مما اكتسبوا وللنساء نصيب مما اكتسبن واسألوا الله من فضله إن الله كان بكل شيء عليما

translation: And for all, We have made heirs to what parents and relatives leave. And to those with whom your right hands have made a pledge, give them their share. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, a Witness.
interpretation: This verse establishes the Islamic principles of inheritance, where the deceased's wealth is distributed among their heirs, including both family members and those with whom a pledge or covenant has been made. It emphasizes that Allah is a witness to all of these transactions, and that the distribution of wealth should be carried out according to the divine guidelines.
orig: ولكل جعلنا موالي مما ترك الوالدان والأقربون والذين عقدت أيمانكم فآتوهم نصيبهم إن الله كان على كل شيء شهيدا

translation: Men are in charge of women by [right of] what Allah has given one over the other and what they spend [for maintenance] from their wealth. So righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in [the husband's] absence what Allah would have them guard. But those [wives] from whom you fear arrogance - [first] advise them; [then if they persist], forsake them in bed; and [finally], strike them. But if they obey you [once more], seek no means against them. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Grand.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of male authority and responsibility over women, based on the natural differences between the sexes and the role of men as providers. It calls on women to be obedient and faithful to their husbands, and outlines a gradual disciplinary process for dealing with disobedience, starting with advice, then separation, and finally, if necessary, light physical discipline. The overall intent is to preserve the family structure and maintain harmony in the relationship, while upholding the dignity and rights of both partners.
orig: الرجال قوامون على النساء بما فضل الله بعضهم على بعض وبما أنفقوا من أموالهم فالصالحات قانتات حافظات للغيب بما حفظ الله واللاتي تخافون نشوزهن فعظوهن واهجروهن في المضاجع واضربوهن فإن أطعنكم فلا تبغوا عليهن سبيلا إن الله كان عليا كبيرا

translation: And if you fear dissension between the two, send an arbitrator from his people and an arbitrator from her people. If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will cause it between them. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Acquainted [with all things].
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to seek reconciliation between a couple who are experiencing discord and conflict in their marriage. It advises appointing an arbiter from each side of the family to mediate and facilitate a resolution, as Allah has the knowledge and ability to bring about reconciliation between the two if they genuinely desire it. The verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and expertise in resolving such matters.
orig: وإن خفتم شقاق بينهما فابعثوا حكما من أهله وحكما من أهلها إن يريدا إصلاحا يوفق الله بينهما إن الله كان عليما خبيرا

translation: And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and to parents do good, and to relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbor, the [distant] neighbor, the companion at your side, the traveler, and [those whom] your right hands possess. Indeed, Allah does not like anyone who is self-deluded and boastful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone without associating any partners with Him. It also highlights the duty to treat one's parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, and neighbors with kindness and compassion. Additionally, it reminds us to be mindful of those under our care, such as servants, and to avoid arrogance and pride, as Allah does not like those who are self-conceited and boastful.
orig: واعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا وبالوالدين إحسانا وبذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين والجار ذي القربى والجار الجنب والصاحب بالجنب وابن السبيل وما ملكت أيمانكم إن الله لا يحب من كان مختالا فخورا

translation: Those who are stingy and enjoin upon [other] people stinginess and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty - and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who are miserly and greedy, and who encourage others to be the same. They hide the blessings that God has bestowed upon them, instead of using their wealth and resources to help others. The Qur'an warns that a humiliating punishment awaits those who engage in such selfish and uncharitable behavior.
orig: الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل ويكتمون ما آتاهم الله من فضله وأعتدنا للكافرين عذابا مهينا
