translation: And those who spend their wealth to be seen by the people and believe not in Allah nor in the Last Day. And he to whom Satan is a companion - then evil is he as a companion.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who give charity or spend their wealth merely to show off and gain the praise of others, rather than out of sincere faith in Allah and the Hereafter. It warns that such people have taken Satan as their companion, which is a terrible fate. The true spirit of charity and good deeds should be to please Allah, not to seek the approval of others.
orig: والذين ينفقون أموالهم رئاء الناس ولا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر ومن يكن الشيطان له قرينا فساء قرينا

translation: And what [harm would come] upon them if they believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent out of what Allah has provided for them? And Allah is to them All-Knower.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have faith in Allah and the Day of Judgment, and to be charitable with the wealth that Allah has provided them. The interpretation is that those who have faith and are generous with their wealth will be rewarded by Allah, who is all-knowing of their deeds.
orig: وماذا عليهم لو آمنوا بالله واليوم الآخر وأنفقوا مما رزقهم الله وكان الله بهم عليما

translation: Indeed, Allah does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom's weight; while if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute justice and fairness. He will not overlook even the smallest good deed, but will reward it abundantly. Conversely, He will not punish anyone unjustly, even to the slightest degree. This highlights the importance of doing good deeds, as they will be recognized and generously rewarded by Allah.
orig: إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما

translation: Then how [will it be] when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad], against these [people] as a witness?
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will bring forth a witness from each community to testify against its members. Furthermore, the Prophet Muhammad will be a witness against all of humanity. This emphasizes the gravity of the accountability that each person will face on that momentous day, as they will be held responsible for their beliefs and actions in this life.
orig: فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد وجئنا بك على هؤلاء شهيدا

translation: That Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish they could be covered by the earth. And they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers who rejected the message of the Prophet will wish that the earth would swallow them up, to escape the punishment and humiliation they will face. They will not be able to hide or conceal anything from Allah, as He is All-Knowing and will hold them accountable for their deeds and misdeeds.
orig: يومئذ يود الذين كفروا وعصوا الرسول لو تسوى بهم الأرض ولا يكتمون الله حديثا

translation: O you who believe! Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying, nor while in a state of ritual impurity, except those passing through [a place of prayer], until you have washed [your whole body]. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and your hands [with it]. Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of ritual purity and sobriety when approaching prayer in Islam. It prohibits praying while intoxicated or in a state of ritual impurity, such as after sexual relations, until one has performed the necessary ablutions. The verse also provides exceptions for those who are ill, traveling, or unable to find water, allowing them to perform a dry ablution (tayammum) instead. The overall message is one of reverence and respect for the ritual of prayer, as well as Allah"s compassion and forgiveness towards those who strive to fulfill their religious obligations.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى حتى تعلموا ما تقولون ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل حتى تغتسلوا وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط أو لامستم النساء فلم تجدوا ماء فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم إن الله كان عفوا غفورا

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who buy error [in exchange for it] and wish you would lose the [right] way?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question directed at the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), asking him to reflect on the attitude of those who have been given a portion of the divine scriptures, such as the Jews and Christians. These people are willing to forsake the truth and embrace falsehood, and they even wish for the believers to stray from the right path. The verse highlights the perverse behavior of those who have been entrusted with divine guidance but choose to reject it in favor of their own desires and selfish interests.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يشترون الضلالة ويريدون أن تضلوا السبيل

translation: And Allah is most knowing of your enemies. And sufficient is Allah as an ally, and sufficient is Allah as a helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has full knowledge of one's enemies, and that He is a sufficient protector and helper for the believers. It reassures the faithful that they can rely on Allah's guidance and support, rather than needing to fear or worry about their adversaries.
orig: والله أعلم بأعدائكم وكفى بالله وليا وكفى بالله نصيرا

translation: Among those who are Jews, there are some who distort words from their [proper] usages and say, "We hear and we disobey" and "Hear, but be not heard" and "Ra‘ina," twisting their tongues and defaming the religion. And if they had said [instead], "We hear and we obey" and "Wait for us [to understand]," it would have been better for them and more suitable. But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse condemns the Jews who deliberately distort the words of God and their religious obligations. They claim to hear the message but then disobey it, or make statements that mock the religion. If they had instead expressed a sincere willingness to listen and obey, it would have been better for them. But because of their disbelief, Allah has cursed them, and only a few among them truly believe.
orig: من الذين هادوا يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه ويقولون سمعنا وعصينا واسمع غير مسمع وراعنا ليا بألسنتهم وطعنا في الدين ولو أنهم قالوا سمعنا وأطعنا واسمع وانظرنا لكان خيرا لهم وأقوم ولكن لعنهم الله بكفرهم فلا يؤمنون إلا قليلا

translation: O People of the Book! Believe in what We have (now) revealed, confirming what was (already) with you, before We change the face and fame of some (of you) beyond all recognition, and turn them hindwards, or curse them as We cursed the Sabbath-breakers, for the decision of Allah must be carried out.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the People of the Book, referring to the Jews and Christians who were given previous scriptures. It calls upon them to believe in the Quran, which confirms and affirms the previous revelations. The verse warns that if they do not believe, Allah may punish them by changing their faces or cursing them, just as He had cursed the Sabbath-breakers. This is a strong admonition to the People of the Book to accept the new revelation brought by Prophet Muhammad, as Allah's decree must be carried out.
orig: يا أيها الذين أوتوا الكتاب آمنوا بما نزلنا مصدقا لما معكم من قبل أن نطمس وجوها فنردها على أدبارها أو نلعنهم كما لعنا أصحاب السبت وكان أمر الله مفعولا

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of associating partners with Allah, which is considered the greatest sin in Islam. It states that Allah will not forgive this act of shirk (polytheism), but may forgive other, lesser sins for those He wills. The interpretation is that one must have complete and unwavering belief in the oneness of Allah, and that associating any other entity with Him is a severe transgression that cannot be forgiven.
orig: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ومن يشرك بالله فقد افترى إثما عظيما

translation: Have you not seen those who claim themselves to be pure? Nay, Allah purifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged [so much as] the thread [in the long slit of a date seed].
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of self-righteousness and the importance of recognizing that true purification comes from Allah alone. It emphasizes that one should not boast about one"s own purity, as it is Allah who decides whom to purify. The verse also assures that Allah"s judgment is fair and that no one will be wronged, even to the slightest degree.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم بل الله يزكي من يشاء ولا يظلمون فتيلا

translation: Look how they invent lies about Allah, and that is sufficient as a manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse is a call to reflect on how some people fabricate and spread false claims about Allah, which is a grave sin. It emphasizes that the mere act of inventing lies against Allah is a clear and manifest sin that is sufficient to condemn those who engage in it.
orig: انظر كيف يفترون على الله الكذب وكفى به إثما مبينا

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, believing in superstition and false objects of worship and saying about the disbelievers, "These are better guided than the believers as to the way"?
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who claim to follow revealed scriptures, yet believe in superstitions and false deities, and even consider the disbelievers to be more rightly guided than the believers. This highlights the hypocrisy and delusion of those who have strayed from the true teachings of their scriptures.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يؤمنون بالجبت والطاغوت ويقولون للذين كفروا هؤلاء أهدى من الذين آمنوا سبيلا

translation: Those are the ones who are cursed by Allah , and whoever is cursed by Allah - you will never find for him a helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are cursed by Allah, meaning they have incurred His displeasure and wrath, will have no one to support or defend them. It serves as a warning that when Allah withdraws His protection and favor, the individual is left without any recourse or assistance, underscoring the importance of seeking Allah's pleasure and avoiding His curse.
orig: أولئك الذين لعنهم الله ومن يلعن الله فلن تجد له نصيرا

translation: Or have they a share in the dominion? Then [if that were so], they would not give the people [even as much as] the speck on a date seed.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who claim authority or power do not truly have a share in the dominion, as they fail to provide even the smallest measure of justice and care for the people. It is a critique of those who seek power for their own benefit rather than for the welfare of the community.
orig: أم لهم نصيب من الملك فإذا لا يؤتون الناس نقيرا

translation: Or do they envy people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? But we had already given the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom and conferred upon them a great kingdom.
interpretation: This verse addresses the tendency of some people to be envious of others who have been blessed by Allah. It reminds us that Allah bestows His bounty upon whomever He wills, and that the family of Abraham were recipients of great blessings, including the Scripture, wisdom, and a mighty kingdom. The implication is that we should not be envious of others, but rather grateful for the blessings Allah has given us.
orig: أم يحسدون الناس على ما آتاهم الله من فضله فقد آتينا آل إبراهيم الكتاب والحكمة وآتيناهم ملكا عظيما

translation: And among them are those who have believed in it, and among them are those who have turned away from it. And sufficient is Hell as a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse highlights the different responses of people to the message of the Qur'an. Some have accepted it and believed, while others have rejected and turned away from it. The verse emphasizes that the punishment of Hell is sufficient for those who disbelieve and reject the guidance of the Qur'an.
orig: فمنهم من آمن به ومنهم من صد عنه وكفى بجهنم سعيرا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses - We will drive them into a Fire. Every time their skins are [partly] burned, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse warns those who reject the signs and messages of Allah that they will be punished in the Hellfire. The repeated burning and replacement of their skins symbolizes the eternal and severe nature of their torment, as they will continually experience the pain of the punishment. This emphasizes that Allah is All-Powerful and All-Wise in His judgement and retribution against those who stubbornly deny the truth.
orig: إن الذين كفروا بآياتنا سوف نصليهم نارا كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها ليذوقوا العذاب إن الله كان عزيزا حكيما

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever. For them therein are purified spouses, and We will admit them to deepening shade.
interpretation: This verse promises eternal paradise in the Hereafter for those who have faith in God and do good deeds. They will be granted entry into lush gardens with flowing rivers, where they will dwell forever. In this blissful abode, they will be accompanied by pure and virtuous spouses, and will enjoy the comfort and protection of a deep and shading canopy.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سندخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا لهم فيها أزواج مطهرة وندخلهم ظلا ظليلا

translation: Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice. Excellent is that which Allah instructs you. Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty, integrity, and fairness in our dealings with others. It calls upon us to fulfill our responsibilities and obligations, whether they are formal trusts or simply the trust placed in us by others. Additionally, it instructs us to judge and make decisions with justice, without bias or favoritism, for Allah is All-Hearing and All-Seeing, and will hold us accountable for our actions.
orig: إن الله يأمركم أن تؤدوا الأمانات إلى أهلها وإذا حكمتم بين الناس أن تحكموا بالعدل إن الله نعما يعظكم به إن الله كان سميعا بصيرا

translation: O you who believe! Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is the best [way] and best in result.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah, the Prophet Muhammad, and those in authority among the believers. It encourages the faithful to resolve any disputes by referring to the guidance of Allah and the Prophet, as this is the best course of action for those who believe in Allah and the Day of Judgment. The interpretation highlights the need for unity, submission to divine authority, and the proper resolution of differences within the community of believers.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول وأولي الأمر منكم فإن تنازعتم في شيء فردوه إلى الله والرسول إن كنتم تؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر ذلك خير وأحسن تأويلا

translation: Have you not seen those who claim to have believed in what was revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you? They wish to refer legislation to Taghut, while they were commanded to reject it; and Satan wishes to lead them far astray.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who outwardly claim to believe in the revelations sent down to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the previous Prophets, but in reality they seek to have their disputes and conflicts adjudicated by false authorities and idolatrous systems, rather than the divine guidance. The verse warns that this is a deception of Satan, who seeks to lead them far astray from the truth.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين يزعمون أنهم آمنوا بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك يريدون أن يتحاكموا إلى الطاغوت وقد أمروا أن يكفروا به ويريد الشيطان أن يضلهم ضلالا بعيدا

translation: And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to [the words of] the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turning away from you in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to be believers but turn away from the guidance of Allah and His Messenger. It suggests that true faith requires submitting to the teachings of the Qur'an and the Prophet Muhammad, rather than selectively accepting what aligns with one's own desires. The verse serves as a warning against hypocrisy and a call to sincerely embrace the message of Islam.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا إلى ما أنزل الله وإلى الرسول رأيت المنافقين يصدون عنك صدودا

translation: How then, when a disaster befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth, then they come to you swearing by Allah, "We intended nothing but good will and conciliation."
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to make excuses and claim good intentions when faced with the consequences of their own actions. It suggests that when people experience misfortune or hardship, they may try to absolve themselves by swearing that they only intended good, even if their actions suggest otherwise. The verse encourages critical reflection on one's own deeds and taking responsibility for the outcomes, rather than making empty oaths.
orig: فكيف إذا أصابتهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم ثم جاءوك يحلفون بالله إن أردنا إلا إحسانا وتوفيقا

translation: Those are the ones whose hearts Allah knows what is in them, so turn away from them and admonish them and speak to them a far-reaching word.
interpretation: This verse refers to those whose true intentions and feelings are known to Allah. The instruction is to turn away from them, admonish them, and speak to them in a profound and impactful way. The emphasis is on addressing their inner state rather than their outward appearance or actions.
orig: أولئك الذين يعلم الله ما في قلوبهم فأعرض عنهم وعظهم وقل لهم في أنفسهم قولا بليغا

translation: And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by permission of Allah. And if, when they had wronged themselves, they had come to you, [O Muhammad], and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obeying the messengers sent by Allah, as they are sent with His permission. It also highlights the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, who is willing to accept the repentance of those who have wronged themselves, if they seek forgiveness from both Allah and His messenger.
orig: وما أرسلنا من رسول إلا ليطاع بإذن الله ولو أنهم إذ ظلموا أنفسهم جاءوك فاستغفروا الله واستغفر لهم الرسول لوجدوا الله توابا رحيما

translation: But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in [full, willing] submission.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of submitting to the judgement and authority of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It indicates that true faith requires not only verbal acceptance, but also a willingness to accept the rulings of the Prophet in matters of dispute. The verse suggests that true believers will find no difficulty in accepting the Prophet's judgements, and will submit to them wholeheartedly.
orig: فلا وربك لا يؤمنون حتى يحكموك فيما شجر بينهم ثم لا يجدوا في أنفسهم حرجا مما قضيت ويسلموا تسليما

translation: And if We had decreed upon them, "Kill yourselves" or "Leave your homes," they would not have done it, except for a few of them. But if they had done what they were instructed, it would have been better for them and a firmer position [for them in faith].
interpretation: This verse highlights the difficulty of getting people to make significant sacrifices, even when commanded by God. It suggests that most people are reluctant to make major changes or sacrifices, even if it would be better for them spiritually. The verse encourages steadfastness and obedience to God's commands, as this would lead to a stronger faith and position.
orig: ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم أن اقتلوا أنفسكم أو اخرجوا من دياركم ما فعلوه إلا قليل منهم ولو أنهم فعلوا ما يوعظون به لكان خيرا لهم وأشد تثبيتا

translation: And when We give them a bountiful provision from Us, they [then] deny it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that when Allah bestows upon people a great reward or blessing, they often become ungrateful and deny the source of that provision. It serves as a warning against the tendency of humans to take Allah's gifts for granted and fail to acknowledge His generosity.
orig: وإذا لآتيناهم من لدنا أجرا عظيما

translation: And We have guided them to the straight path.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has provided guidance and direction to people, leading them to the righteous and true path. The 'straight path' refers to the path of Islam, which is the correct and most suitable way of life that leads to success in this world and the Hereafter.
orig: ولهديناهم صراطا مستقيما

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger - those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth, the martyrs and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to obey Allah and His Messenger, as those who do so will be in the company of the most noble and righteous people in the Hereafter - the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. This is a promise of the highest reward and companionship in the Afterlife for those who faithfully follow the guidance of Allah and His Messenger.
orig: ومن يطع الله والرسول فأولئك مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين وحسن أولئك رفيقا

translation: That is the bounty from Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the blessings and favors bestowed upon people are from Allah alone. It also affirms that Allah is All-Knowing, and His knowledge encompasses all things.
orig: ذلك الفضل من الله وكفى بالله عليما

translation: O you who believe! Take your precautions and then go forth, whether in heavy or light companies, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of Allah. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be vigilant and prepared, whether they go forth in small or large groups, and to strive with their wealth and lives for the cause of Allah. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of being cautious and united in the face of challenges, while dedicating one's efforts to the service of the divine.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا خذوا حذركم فانفروا ثبات أو انفروا جميعا

translation: And indeed, among you is he who lingers behind. And if disaster strikes you, he says, 'Allah has favored me in that I was not present with them.'
interpretation: This verse condemns those who avoid participating in important matters and responsibilities, and then try to justify their absence when calamity strikes. It highlights the hypocrisy of those who seek to absolve themselves of blame and claim divine favor, rather than taking responsibility for their actions or inactions.
orig: وإن منكم لمن ليبطئن فإن أصابتكم مصيبة قال قد أنعم الله علي إذ لم أكن معهم شهيدا

translation: And if you are granted a bounty from Allah, they would surely say, as if there had never been any affection between you and them. Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I could have attained a great attainment.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the human tendency to be jealous and ungrateful when others are blessed with good fortune. It suggests that those who are not favored may resent and distance themselves from those who are, as if the previous bond of affection never existed. The verse also expresses a longing to have been among the blessed, in order to have shared in their good fortune. The interpretation is that we should be grateful for the blessings bestowed upon us by God, and not let envy or resentment cloud our relationships with others.
orig: ولئن أصابكم فضل من الله ليقولن كأن لم تكن بينكم وبينه مودة يا ليتني كنت معهم فأفوز فوزا عظيما

translation: Let those fight in the cause of Allah who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter. And he who fights in the cause of Allah and is killed or achieves victory - We will bestow upon him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to fight in the cause of Allah, as those who do so are trading the temporary pleasures of this world for the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. It promises a great reward for those who are killed or emerge victorious in this struggle, emphasizing the importance of faith and sacrifice in the path of God.
orig: فليقاتل في سبيل الله الذين يشرون الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة ومن يقاتل في سبيل الله فيقتل أو يغلب فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: And why do you not fight in the cause of Allah and [for] the oppressed among men, women, and children who say, "Our Lord, take us out of this city of oppressive people and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper"?
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to fight in the cause of Allah and to defend the oppressed, including men, women, and children who are calling out for help and deliverance from their oppressors. It highlights the duty of the believers to support and protect the weak and vulnerable, and to strive for justice and liberation from tyranny.
orig: وما لكم لا تقاتلون في سبيل الله والمستضعفين من الرجال والنساء والولدان الذين يقولون ربنا أخرجنا من هذه القرية الظالم أهلها واجعل لنا من لدنك وليا واجعل لنا من لدنك نصيرا

translation: Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of Taghut (false deities). So fight against the allies of Satan. Indeed, the plot of Satan has ever been [but] weak.
interpretation: This verse draws a clear distinction between the believers and the disbelievers, and their respective motivations for fighting. The believers fight for the sake of Allah, while the disbelievers fight for the sake of false deities or "Taghut". The verse then commands the believers to fight against the allies of Satan, as the plot of Satan is ultimately weak and ineffective.
orig: الذين آمنوا يقاتلون في سبيل الله والذين كفروا يقاتلون في سبيل الطاغوت فقاتلوا أولياء الشيطان إن كيد الشيطان كان ضعيفا

translation: Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands [from fighting] and establish prayer and give zakah"? But then when fighting was ordained for them, at once a party of them feared people as they fear Allah or with [even] greater fear. They said, "Our Lord, why have You decreed upon us fighting? If only You had postponed [it for] us to a near term." Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for he who fears Allah. And injustice will not be done to you, [even] as much as a thread [in the eyeball]."
interpretation: This verse highlights the struggle of those who are commanded to worship and obey Allah, but then find themselves faced with the obligation of fighting in battle. The verse suggests that while some may initially be hesitant or fearful, their ultimate duty is to Allah and the Hereafter, not the fleeting pleasures of this world. The interpretation emphasizes that the Hereafter is far more important than the temporary trials of this life, and that those who fear and obey Allah will be justly rewarded, without the slightest injustice.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين قيل لهم كفوا أيديكم وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فلما كتب عليهم القتال إذا فريق منهم يخشون الناس كخشية الله أو أشد خشية وقالوا ربنا لم كتبت علينا القتال لولا أخرتنا إلى أجل قريب قل متاع الدنيا قليل والآخرة خير لمن اتقى ولا تظلمون فتيلا

translation: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be in towers raised high. But if good comes to them, they say, "This is from Allah"; and if adversity befalls them, they say, "This has come to us from you." Say, "All [things] are from Allah." So what is [the matter] with those people that they can hardly understand any statement?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that death is inevitable, regardless of one's circumstances or location. It highlights the tendency of people to attribute good fortune to Allah, but misfortune to others. The verse encourages the acceptance that all things, both good and bad, ultimately come from Allah, and urges the people to have a deeper understanding of this reality.
orig: أينما تكونوا يدرككم الموت ولو كنتم في بروج مشيدة وإن تصبهم حسنة يقولوا هذه من عند الله وإن تصبهم سيئة يقولوا هذه من عندك قل كل من عند الله فمال هؤلاء القوم لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا

translation: Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil reaches you is from yourself. And We have sent you, [O Muhammad], to the people as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all good that comes to a person is from Allah, while any evil or misfortune is a result of one's own actions. It also affirms that the Prophet Muhammad was sent as a messenger to all of humanity, and that Allah is the ultimate witness and judge of one's deeds.
orig: ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك وأرسلناك للناس رسولا وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah; but those who turn away - We have not sent you over them as a guardian.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obeying the Prophet Muhammad, as obedience to him is equivalent to obedience to Allah. It also clarifies that the Prophet was not sent as a guardian or watcher over people, but rather to convey the message of Islam. The verse encourages believers to follow the teachings of the Prophet, while also respecting the free will of those who choose not to believe.
orig: من يطع الرسول فقد أطاع الله ومن تولى فما أرسلناك عليهم حفيظا

translation: And they say, "Obedience." But when they leave you, a group of them spend the night determining other than what you say. And Allah records what they plan by night. So turn away from them and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of some individuals who outwardly profess obedience, but secretly plot and scheme against the Prophet's (peace be upon him) instructions. The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of their hidden intentions and actions, and the believers should turn away from them and put their trust in Allah, who is the best disposer of affairs.
orig: ويقولون طاعة فإذا برزوا من عندك بيت طائفة منهم غير الذي تقول والله يكتب ما يبيتون فأعرض عنهم وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an? If it had been from [any] other than Allah, they would have found within it much contradiction.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect deeply on the Qur'an and recognize its divine origin. The absence of any contradictions or inconsistencies in the Qur'an is a clear sign that it is from Allah, and not from any human source. This highlights the Qur'an's perfection and the wisdom behind its teachings.
orig: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا

translation: And when there comes to them information about [any] security or fear, they spread it around. But if they had referred it back to the Messenger or to those of authority among them, then the ones who [can] draw correct conclusions from it would have known about it. And if not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few [of you].
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to verify information, especially regarding matters of security and fear, before spreading it. It emphasizes the importance of referring to the Prophet Muhammad and those in authority to properly understand and interpret such information. The verse also highlights Allah's grace and mercy in guiding the believers away from following Satan's temptations, which they would have otherwise done without Allah's favor.
orig: وإذا جاءهم أمر من الأمن أو الخوف أذاعوا به ولو ردوه إلى الرسول وإلى أولي الأمر منهم لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته لاتبعتم الشيطان إلا قليلا

translation: So fight in the cause of Allah; you are not held responsible except for yourself. And encourage the believers [to join you] that perhaps Allah will restrain the [military] might of those who disbelieve. And Allah is greater in might and stronger in [exemplary] punishment.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to fight in the cause of Allah, not for their own personal gain or glory, but to uphold the truth and defend the faith. It emphasizes that each person is responsible for their own actions and that the believers should encourage one another to remain steadfast. The verse also suggests that Allah has the power to restrain the might of those who disbelieve, and that His punishment is severe and exemplary.
orig: فقاتل في سبيل الله لا تكلف إلا نفسك وحرض المؤمنين عسى الله أن يكف بأس الذين كفروا والله أشد بأسا وأشد تنكيلا

translation: Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share thereof, and whoever intercedes with an evil intercession will have a portion thereof. And Allah is ever All-Encompassing over everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of accountability and the consequences of one's actions. It teaches that the one who intercedes on behalf of another with a good intention and a righteous cause will be rewarded for their intercession, while the one who intercedes with an evil or unjust intention will be held accountable for their actions. The verse also affirms that Allah is All-Encompassing and has complete control over all things, and that He will judge each person's deeds accordingly.
orig: من يشفع شفاعة حسنة يكن له نصيب منها ومن يشفع شفاعة سيئة يكن له كفل منها وكان الله على كل شيء مقيتا

translation: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet [in return] with one better than it or [at least] return [it similarly]. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, an Accountant.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to respond to a greeting in a manner that is better or at least equal to the greeting received. It emphasizes that Allah is ever-watchful and will hold people accountable for their actions, including how they respond to greetings from others.
orig: وإذا حييتم بتحية فحيوا بأحسن منها أو ردوها إن الله كان على كل شيء حسيبا

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. He will surely assemble you for [account on] the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And who is more truthful than Allah in statement.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and affirms that He alone is worthy of worship. It also reminds us that we will all be gathered before God on the Day of Judgment, a day that is certain to come. The verse further highlights that there is no one more truthful than God in His words and promises.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو ليجمعنكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه ومن أصدق من الله حديثا

translation: What is [the matter] with you [that you are] two groups concerning the hypocrites? Allah has "overthrown" them for what they earned. Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has sent astray? And he whom Allah sends astray - for him you will never find a way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of trying to guide those whom Allah has sent astray. The hypocrites have been condemned by Allah for their misdeeds, and it is not for believers to try and guide them. Rather, believers should focus their efforts on those who are open to guidance, as Allah alone has the power to guide or misguide whomever He wills.
orig: فما لكم في المنافقين فئتين والله أركسهم بما كسبوا أتريدون أن تهدوا من أضل الله ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be alike. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate for the cause of Allah . But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them and take not from among them any ally or helper.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against aligning themselves with the disbelievers. It states that the disbelievers wish for the believers to disbelieve as they have, so that they may be equal. However, the believers are instructed not to take the disbelievers as allies until they emigrate for the cause of Allah. If the disbelievers refuse to do so, the believers are commanded to seize and kill them wherever they are found, and not to take them as allies or helpers.
orig: ودوا لو تكفرون كما كفروا فتكونون سواء فلا تتخذوا منهم أولياء حتى يهاجروا في سبيل الله فإن تولوا فخذوهم واقتلوهم حيث وجدتموهم ولا تتخذوا منهم وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: Except for those who join a people between whom and you there is a treaty (of peace), or (those who) come unto you, their hearts restraining them from (fighting) you as well as (fighting) their own people. And if Allah had willed, He could have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. So if they withdraw from you and fight not against you, and offer you peace, then Allah hath opened no way for you (to war against them).
interpretation: This verse outlines an exception to the general rule of fighting against those who oppose Islam. It states that if there is a treaty or peace agreement between a group and the Muslims, or if a group comes to the Muslims seeking peace, then the Muslims should not fight against them. This is because Allah could have given these people power over the Muslims, but He has chosen not to do so. Therefore, if they withdraw from fighting and offer peace, the Muslims should accept it and not seek to fight them.
orig: إلا الذين يصلون إلى قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق أو جاءوكم حصرت صدورهم أن يقاتلوكم أو يقاتلوا قومهم ولو شاء الله لسلطهم عليكم فلقاتلوكم فإن اعتزلوكم فلم يقاتلوكم وألقوا إليكم السلم فما جعل الله لكم عليهم سبيلا

translation: You will find others who wish to be secure from you and secure from their own people. Whenever they are returned to temptation, they plunge into it. So if they do not withdraw from you and offer you peace and restrain their hands, then take them and kill them wherever you overtake them. And those - We have made for you against them a clear authorization.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers about those who seek to gain the trust of both the believers and their own people, but in reality, they are inclined towards disbelief and temptation. The verse instructs the believers to kill those who do not withdraw from them, offer peace, and restrain their hands, as the believers have been given clear authority over them.
orig: ستجدون آخرين يريدون أن يأمنوكم ويأمنوا قومهم كل ما ردوا إلى الفتنة أركسوا فيها فإن لم يعتزلوكم ويلقوا إليكم السلم ويكفوا أيديهم فخذوهم واقتلوهم حيث ثقفتموهم وأولئكم جعلنا لكم عليهم سلطانا مبينا

translation: And it is not [fitting] for a believer to kill a believer except [that it be] by mistake. And whoever kills a believer by mistake - then the freeing of a believing slave and a compensation payment presented to the deceased's family [is required] unless they give [up their right as] charity. But if the deceased was from a people at war with you and he was a believer - then [only] the freeing of a believing slave [is required]. And if he was from a people with whom you have a treaty - then a compensation payment presented to his family and the freeing of a believing slave. And whoever does not find [one or cannot afford to buy one] - then [instead], a fast for two consecutive months [is required] as repentance before Allah, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the Islamic principles regarding the unintentional killing of a believer. It emphasizes the gravity of such an act, and outlines the atonement required - the freeing of a believing slave and a compensation payment to the deceased's family. The verse also provides different rulings depending on whether the deceased was from a warring tribe or a people with whom there was a treaty. Overall, the verse highlights the sanctity of a believer's life and the need for sincere repentance and atonement in cases of unintentional homicide.
orig: وما كان لمؤمن أن يقتل مؤمنا إلا خطأ ومن قتل مؤمنا خطأ فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة ودية مسلمة إلى أهله إلا أن يصدقوا فإن كان من قوم عدو لكم وهو مؤمن فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة وإن كان من قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق فدية مسلمة إلى أهله وتحرير رقبة مؤمنة فمن لم يجد فصيام شهرين متتابعين توبة من الله وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever kills a believer intentionally - his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and Allah has become angry with him and has cursed him and has prepared for him a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of intentionally killing a believer. The punishment for such an act is eternal damnation in Hell, accompanied by the wrath and curse of Allah. This serves as a stern warning against premeditated murder of a fellow Muslim, underscoring the sanctity of human life in Islam.
orig: ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا فجزاؤه جهنم خالدا فيها وغضب الله عليه ولعنه وأعد له عذابا عظيما

translation: O you who believe! When you go forth (to fight) in the Cause of Allah, verify (the truth), and say not to anyone who greets you (by embracing Islam): "You are not a believer"; seeking the perishable goods of the worldly life. There are much more profits and booties with Allah. Even thus were you yourselves before, till Allah conferred on you His Favours (i.e. guided you to Islam), therefore, be cautious in discrimination. Verily, Allah is Ever All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse exhorts the believers to be cautious and discerning when engaging in warfare for the sake of Allah. It warns against hastily judging those who greet them with the salutation of peace, as they may in fact be believers. The verse emphasizes that the true rewards lie with Allah, not the perishable gains of this world. It reminds the believers that they too were once in a state of ignorance, until Allah guided them to the truth of Islam. Therefore, the believers are called upon to exercise caution and avoid discrimination, as Allah is fully aware of their actions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ضربتم في سبيل الله فتبينوا ولا تقولوا لمن ألقى إليكم السلام لست مؤمنا تبتغون عرض الحياة الدنيا فعند الله مغانم كثيرة كذلك كنتم من قبل فمن الله عليكم فتبينوا إن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: Not equal are those believers who sit [at home] - except the disabled - and the mujahideen who strive in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred the mujahideen through their wealth and their lives over those who sit [at home], by degrees. And to all [i.e., both] Allah has promised the best [reward]. But Allah has preferred the mujahideen over those who sit [at home] with a great reward
interpretation: This verse establishes a distinction between those believers who actively engage in jihad (struggle) in the cause of Allah, and those who remain at home, except for those who are disabled. The mujahideen, who strive with their wealth and lives, are granted a higher status and greater reward by Allah. This highlights the importance of active participation in the defense and promotion of the faith, rather than mere passive belief. The verse emphasizes that both groups will be rewarded by Allah, but the mujahideen will receive an even greater reward for their sacrifices and efforts.
orig: لا يستوي القاعدون من المؤمنين غير أولي الضرر والمجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم فضل الله المجاهدين بأموالهم وأنفسهم على القاعدين درجة وكلا وعد الله الحسنى وفضل الله المجاهدين على القاعدين أجرا عظيما

translation: And degrees [of higher position] from Him and forgiveness and mercy. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the rewards and blessings that Allah bestows upon those who believe in Him and do righteous deeds. The "degrees" refer to the elevated ranks and stations that believers will attain in the Hereafter. The "forgiveness and mercy" indicate that Allah is always willing to forgive those who repent and seek His forgiveness, and that He showers His mercy and compassion upon His servants. This verse emphasizes Allah's boundless forgiveness and compassion, which are central to His nature.
orig: درجات منه ومغفرة ورحمة وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: Indeed, those whom the angels take [in death] while they are wronging themselves - [the angels] will say, "In what [condition] were you?" They will say, "We were oppressed in the land." [The angels] will say, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious [enough] for you to emigrate therein?" And those are the ones whose refuge is Hell - and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who die while engaging in wrongful acts against themselves. When the angels come to take their souls, the angels ask them about their condition. The people respond that they were oppressed and oppressed in the land. The angels then rebuke them, asking if the earth of Allah was not spacious enough for them to emigrate and seek a better life. Ultimately, the destination for such people is the hellfire, which is a terrible end.
orig: إن الذين توفاهم الملائكة ظالمي أنفسهم قالوا فيم كنتم قالوا كنا مستضعفين في الأرض قالوا ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها فأولئك مأواهم جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: Except for the weak among men and women and children who cannot devise a plan nor are they directed to a way
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's forgiveness and mercy extend to those who are weak and powerless, unable to find a way out of their difficulties. It suggests that these individuals are not held accountable to the same degree as those who have the means and ability to make choices, as they lack the capacity to devise a plan or find the right path.
orig: إلا المستضعفين من الرجال والنساء والولدان لا يستطيعون حيلة ولا يهتدون سبيلا

translation: And it may be that Allah will pardon them, and Allah is Oft-Pardoning, Most Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even those who have committed sins may be forgiven by Allah, as He is the Most Forgiving and Oft-Pardoning. It encourages believers to have hope in Allah's mercy and to seek His forgiveness, as He is willing to pardon those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: فأولئك عسى الله أن يعفو عنهم وكان الله عفوا غفورا

translation: And whoever emigrates for the cause of Allah will find on the earth many [alternative] locations and abundance. And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger and then death overtakes him - his reward has already become incumbent upon Allah. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to emigrate for the sake of Allah, promising that they will find ample opportunities and provisions in their new lands. It also assures those who die during this emigration that their reward is guaranteed by Allah, who is Forgiving and Merciful. The verse highlights the virtue of sacrificing one's comforts and leaving one's home to support the cause of Islam.
orig: ومن يهاجر في سبيل الله يجد في الأرض مراغما كثيرا وسعة ومن يخرج من بيته مهاجرا إلى الله ورسوله ثم يدركه الموت فقد وقع أجره على الله وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, [especially] if you fear that those who disbelieve may disrupt [or attack] you. Indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse allows for the shortening of the obligatory prayers when one is traveling, especially if there is a fear of harm from the disbelievers. This concession is a mercy from Allah, as the traveler may face hardship and difficulty in performing the full prayers. The verse also emphasizes the enmity of the disbelievers towards the believers, which necessitates caution and vigilance during travel.
orig: وإذا ضربتم في الأرض فليس عليكم جناح أن تقصروا من الصلاة إن خفتم أن يفتنكم الذين كفروا إن الكافرين كانوا لكم عدوا مبينا

translation: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand [in prayer] with you and let them carry their arms. And when they have prostrated, let them be [in position] behind you and have the other group come forward which has not [yet] prayed and let them pray with you, taking their precautions and their arms. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and your baggage so they could come down upon you in one [single] attack. But there is no blame upon you, if you are troubled by rain or are ill, for putting down your arms, but take your precautions. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse provides instructions for Muslims to maintain vigilance and preparedness even during times of prayer, in order to guard against potential attacks from disbelievers. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a state of readiness and caution, while also allowing for necessary accommodations due to adverse conditions or illness. The key message is that the believers should never let their guard down, for the disbelievers seek to take advantage of any perceived weakness or negligence.
orig: وإذا كنت فيهم فأقمت لهم الصلاة فلتقم طائفة منهم معك وليأخذوا أسلحتهم فإذا سجدوا فليكونوا من ورائكم ولتأت طائفة أخرى لم يصلوا فليصلوا معك وليأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم ود الذين كفروا لو تغفلون عن أسلحتكم وأمتعتكم فيميلون عليكم ميلة واحدة ولا جناح عليكم إن كان بكم أذى من مطر أو كنتم مرضى أن تضعوا أسلحتكم وخذوا حذركم إن الله أعد للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, or [lying] on your sides. But when you become secure, re-establish [regular] prayer. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to remember and invoke Allah in various states, whether standing, sitting, or lying down, after completing the obligatory prayer. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a continuous remembrance of Allah and re-establishing the regular performance of the prayer, which is a duty prescribed for the believers at specific times.
orig: فإذا قضيتم الصلاة فاذكروا الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبكم فإذا اطمأننتم فأقيموا الصلاة إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا

translation: And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy. If you should be suffering - so are they suffering as you are suffering, but you expect from Allah that which they do not expect. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to persevere and not become discouraged in the face of adversity or hardship. It reminds us that our enemies also suffer, and that we should have faith that Allah will provide for us, even if our enemies do not expect it. The verse emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and wise in His judgments and plans.
orig: ولا تهنوا في ابتغاء القوم إن تكونوا تألمون فإنهم يألمون كما تألمون وترجون من الله ما لا يرجون وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth so you may judge between the people by that which Allah has shown you. And do not be for the deceitful an advocate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Quran was revealed to Prophet Muhammad as a guide for humanity, so that he may judge and rule between people based on the truth and wisdom that Allah has bestowed upon him. It also warns the Prophet not to be an advocate or supporter of those who are deceitful or treacherous.
orig: إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق لتحكم بين الناس بما أراك الله ولا تكن للخائنين خصيما

translation: And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages seeking forgiveness from Allah, as He is the Most Forgiving and the Most Merciful. It reminds us that no matter how great our sins may be, Allah is always willing to forgive us if we sincerely repent and turn back to Him.
orig: واستغفر الله إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And do not argue about those who deceive themselves. Indeed, Allah does not like everyone self-conceited and boastful.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims not to argue or engage in disputes with those who are deceitful and arrogant, as Allah does not love those who are conceited and sinful. The focus should be on personal spiritual development and avoiding unnecessary conflicts with those who are unwilling to acknowledge their own faults.
orig: ولا تجادل عن الذين يختانون أنفسهم إن الله لا يحب من كان خوانا أثيما

translation: They hide from the people but they cannot hide from Allah, and He is with them when they spend the night in such as He does not accept of speech, and Allah is ever All-Aware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who try to conceal their misdeeds from people, but fail to realize that Allah is fully aware of their actions. It emphasizes that one cannot hide from the all-knowing and all-encompassing presence of Allah, even when engaging in unacceptable speech or behavior in private. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is ever-vigilant and that our actions, even those hidden from others, will be accounted for.
orig: يستخفون من الناس ولا يستخفون من الله وهو معهم إذ يبيتون ما لا يرضى من القول وكان الله بما يعملون محيطا

translation: Here you are - you have disputed on their behalf in the life of this world, but who will dispute with Allah for them on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be a guardian over them?
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of arguing on behalf of others in this world, as on the Day of Judgment, no one can argue or advocate for them before Allah. It emphasizes that each person is ultimately responsible for their own actions and will be held accountable before Allah, the Supreme Judge.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء جادلتم عنهم في الحياة الدنيا فمن يجادل الله عنهم يوم القيامة أم من يكون عليهم وكيلا

translation: And whoever does a wrong or wrongs himself, but then seeks forgiveness of Allah, he will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of Allah. It teaches that even if someone commits a sin or wrongs themselves, if they sincerely repent and seek Allah's forgiveness, they will find Allah to be Forgiving and Merciful. This encourages people to turn to Allah and seek His pardon, as He is willing to forgive those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم نفسه ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And whoever earns [i.e., commits] a sin only earns it against himself, and Allah is Ever All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the consequences of one's actions are borne by the individual alone. When a person commits a sin, they are the only ones responsible for it, not others. This reinforces the notion of individual accountability before Allah, who is All-Knowing and All-Wise in His judgments and decrees.
orig: ومن يكسب إثما فإنما يكسبه على نفسه وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever earns [i.e., commits] a sin or a wrong, and then blames it on an innocent [person], then he has taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse condemns the act of falsely accusing an innocent person of wrongdoing. It emphasizes that the one who commits a sin or a wrong and then tries to shift the blame to an innocent party has taken on a grave sin of slander and a clear transgression. The verse highlights the moral responsibility of owning up to one's own misdeeds rather than unjustly implicating others.
orig: ومن يكسب خطيئة أو إثما ثم يرم به بريئا فقد احتمل بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: And if not for the favor of Allah upon you, and His mercy, a [certain] group of them would have determined to mislead you. But they do not mislead except themselves, and they will not harm you at all. And [that is because] Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom and has taught you that which you did not know. And ever has the favor of Allah upon you been great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of Allah's grace and mercy in protecting the Prophet Muhammad from the schemes of those who sought to mislead him. It highlights that the true harm of such schemes is to the perpetrators themselves, as they cannot actually harm the Prophet. The verse also underscores that Allah has bestowed the Prophet with the Quran and wisdom, and has granted him knowledge that he did not possess before, all of which is a testament to Allah's immense favor upon him.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته لهمت طائفة منهم أن يضلوك وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم وما يضرونك من شيء وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب والحكمة وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما

translation: There is no good in most of their secret conversations, except [in] one who enjoins charity or that which is right or conciliation between people. And whoever does that, seeking means to the approval of Allah - then We will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that most secret conversations among people are not beneficial, unless they involve encouraging good deeds, righteousness, or reconciliation between people. The verse encourages believers to engage in such positive actions, done with the intention of seeking Allah's pleasure, for which they will be greatly rewarded.
orig: لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس ومن يفعل ذلك ابتغاء مرضات الله فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse warns against turning away from the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and following a path other than that of the believers. It indicates that those who do so will be held accountable and face a severe punishment in the Hereafter, as they have rejected the clear truth that was presented to them.
orig: ومن يشاقق الرسول من بعد ما تبين له الهدى ويتبع غير سبيل المؤمنين نوله ما تولى ونصله جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of associating partners with Allah (shirk), which is the unforgivable sin in Islam. It indicates that while Allah is merciful and may forgive other sins, He will not forgive the sin of shirk for those who persist in it. The interpretation suggests that the ultimate consequence of shirk is being led far astray from the path of truth and righteousness.
orig: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ومن يشرك بالله فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those they invoke besides Him are not [actual] deities. They [i.e., the invokers] are not but [like] demons [to whom] they [falsely, out of ignorance] associate [with Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the idols and false deities that people worship besides Allah are not true deities, but rather demons and evil spirits that have misled people into associating them with Allah. The verse highlights the futility and error of worshipping anything other than the one true God, Allah.
orig: إن يدعون من دونه إلا إناثا وإن يدعون إلا شيطانا مريدا

translation: May Allah curse him, and he [i.e., Satan] will say, "I will surely take from among Your servants a specific portion [of them]."
interpretation: This verse is a warning against the deception of Satan, who seeks to lead people astray and turn them away from the path of righteousness. The verse emphasizes that Satan is cursed by Allah and has the audacity to claim that he will take a portion of Allah's servants for himself. This serves as a reminder to believers to be vigilant and resist the temptations of Satan, who seeks to lead them astray from the guidance of Allah.
orig: لعنه الله وقال لأتخذن من عبادك نصيبا مفروضا

translation: And I will surely mislead them and will surely arouse in them [false] desires and will surely command them so they will slit the ears of the cattle and I will surely command them so they will change the creation of Allah". And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly sustained a clear loss.
interpretation: This verse warns against the deception and temptations of Satan, who seeks to lead people astray from the path of Allah. It emphasizes that those who follow Satan's commands, such as mutilating animals or changing the natural order created by Allah, will suffer a clear and devastating loss. The verse serves as a reminder to remain steadfast in faith and to seek refuge in Allah rather than succumbing to Satan's influence.
orig: ولأضلنهم ولأمنينهم ولآمرنهم فليبتكن آذان الأنعام ولآمرنهم فليغيرن خلق الله ومن يتخذ الشيطان وليا من دون الله فقد خسر خسرانا مبينا

translation: He promises them and arouses desire in them. But Satan does not promise them except delusion.
interpretation: This verse warns against the deceptions of Satan, who makes false promises and arouses false hopes in people, leading them astray from the truth. The interpretation is that one should not be deceived by Satan's temptations and empty promises, but rather seek guidance and fulfillment from Allah.
orig: يعدهم ويمنيهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا

translation: Those - their refuge is Hell, and they will not find from it any way of escape.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have rejected faith and done evil deeds. They will be condemned to the eternal punishment of Hell, from which there will be no way out or relief.
orig: أولئك مأواهم جهنم ولا يجدون عنها محيصا

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever. [It is] the promise of Allah, [which is] truth, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement.
interpretation: This verse promises that those who believe in God and do good deeds will be granted eternal life in Paradise, where they will dwell in gardens with flowing rivers. This is a true and unwavering promise from God, who is the most truthful of all.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سندخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا وعد الله حقا ومن أصدق من الله قيلا

translation: It is not [achieved] by your wishful thinking nor by that of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does a wrong will be recompensed for it, and he will not find besides Allah a protector or a helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that salvation and success are not achieved merely by wishful thinking or by following the beliefs of others, but rather by one's own righteous deeds. It warns that whoever commits a sin or wrong will be held accountable for it, and they will not find any protector or helper besides Allah to save them from the consequences of their actions.
orig: ليس بأمانيكم ولا أماني أهل الكتاب من يعمل سوءا يجز به ولا يجد له من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer - those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, [even as much as] the speck on a date-stone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that in Islam, both men and women are equally capable of performing good deeds and earning the reward of Paradise. It highlights that one's gender does not determine one's spiritual standing, but rather, it is one's faith and righteous actions that matter. The verse also conveys that those who believe and do good will be justly rewarded, without any discrimination or injustice.
orig: ومن يعمل من الصالحات من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون نقيرا

translation: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the best religion is one where the person submits themselves fully to Allah, while also doing good deeds and following the true faith of Abraham. It highlights that Allah chose Abraham as His close friend, indicating the high status of those who truly surrender to the divine will and live righteously.
orig: ومن أحسن دينا ممن أسلم وجهه لله وهو محسن واتبع ملة إبراهيم حنيفا واتخذ الله إبراهيم خليلا

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And ever is Allah, encompassing all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah. It conveys that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, and He has complete control and knowledge over all things. This highlights the importance of worshiping and submitting to Allah alone, as He is the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكان الله بكل شيء محيطا

translation: And they ask you concerning [the affairs of] women. Say, "Allah instructs you concerning them, and [instructs you concerning] what has been recited to you in the Book about the orphan girls to whom you do not give what is decreed for them - and [yet] you desire to marry them - and about the [other] weak among children. And [He commands] that you maintain justice for orphans."
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the proper treatment of women, particularly orphan girls and other vulnerable groups like children. It instructs that Allah has ordained certain rights and responsibilities regarding women, which should be upheld. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining justice and fairness, especially towards orphans and the weak. It condemns the practice of desiring to marry orphan girls without fulfilling their rightful entitlements. The overall message is one of compassion, equity and upholding the rights of those who are vulnerable in society.
orig: ويستفتونك في النساء قل الله يفتيكم فيهن وما يتلى عليكم في الكتاب في يتامى النساء اللاتي لا تؤتونهن ما كتب لهن وترغبون أن تنكحوهن والمستضعفين من الولدان وأن تقوموا لليتامى بالقسط وما تفعلوا من خير فإن الله كان به عليما

translation: And if a woman fears from her husband contempt or evasion, there is no sin upon them if they make terms of settlement between them - and settlement is best. And present in [human] souls is stinginess. But if you do good and fear Allah - then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Aware.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on how to resolve marital conflicts, particularly when the wife fears her husband's contempt or evasion. It encourages the couple to seek reconciliation, as settlement is better than conflict. The verse also acknowledges the human tendency towards selfishness and stinginess, but emphasizes that if the couple do good and fear Allah, then Allah is fully aware of their actions.
orig: وإن امرأة خافت من بعلها نشوزا أو إعراضا فلا جناح عليهما أن يصلحا بينهما صلحا والصلح خير وأحضرت الأنفس الشح وإن تحسنوا وتتقوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: And you will never be able to be equal [in feeling] between wives, even if you should strive [to do so]. So do not incline completely [toward one] and leave another hanging. And if you amend [your affairs] and fear Allah - then indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the inherent difficulty in treating multiple wives equally, and advises against leaning too heavily towards one wife at the expense of the others. Instead, it encourages seeking to maintain balance and fairness, while acknowledging that Allah is forgiving and merciful towards those who strive to do so.
orig: ولن تستطيعوا أن تعدلوا بين النساء ولو حرصتم فلا تميلوا كل الميل فتذروها كالمعلقة وإن تصلحوا وتتقوا فإن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And if they separate, Allah will enrich each [of them] from His abundance. And ever is Allah Encompassing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse encourages spouses to be patient and seek reconciliation if they have differences, as Allah will provide for each of them from His abundant provision. It emphasizes that Allah is All-Encompassing in His knowledge and Wise in His judgments, and that He will take care of those who trust in Him.
orig: وإن يتفرقا يغن الله كلا من سعته وكان الله واسعا حكيما

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And We had already enjoined upon those who were given the Scripture before you and upon you [as well] to fear Allah. But if you disbelieve - then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and ever is Allah Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the entire universe. It reminds the believers, as well as those who were given the Scripture before them, to fear and revere Allah, as He is the sole Owner and Sustainer of all that exists in the heavens and the earth. The verse also makes it clear that disbelief does not diminish Allah's dominion, for He is Self-Sufficient and Praiseworthy regardless of the state of His creation.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ولقد وصينا الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم وإياكم أن اتقوا الله وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكان الله غنيا حميدا

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and authority of Allah over the entire universe, both in the heavens and on earth. It affirms that everything belongs to Allah, and that He alone is the Disposer of all affairs, the One who oversees and manages all creation. This is a declaration of Allah's power, control, and sufficiency, and a reminder to believers to rely solely on Him.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: If He wills, He can do away with you, O people, and bring others [in your place]. And Allah is over that all-Powerful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute sovereignty and power. He has the ability to replace one group of people with another, should He so desire. It serves as a reminder that human existence and prosperity are ultimately dependent on God's will, not our own. This should instill a sense of humility and motivate us to seek God's pleasure and guidance in our lives.
orig: إن يشأ يذهبكم أيها الناس ويأت بآخرين وكان الله على ذلك قديرا

translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world - then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who seek worldly rewards and gains should realize that the ultimate reward lies with Allah, both in this life and the Hereafter. Allah is All-Hearing and All-Seeing, and He is the One who will judge and reward people according to their intentions and actions.
orig: من كان يريد ثواب الدنيا فعند الله ثواب الدنيا والآخرة وكان الله سميعا بصيرا

translation: O you who believe! Be steadfast for Allah, bearing witness with justice, and let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah. Verily, Allah is Well-Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse exhorts believers to be steadfast in upholding justice and fairness, even if it goes against their own interests or those of their family and close ones. It emphasizes that justice should be the guiding principle, not personal desires or biases. The verse reminds that Allah is fully aware of our actions and will hold us accountable, so we must strive to be just and righteous in our conduct.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط شهداء لله ولو على أنفسكم أو الوالدين والأقربين إن يكن غنيا أو فقيرا فالله أولى بهما فلا تتبعوا الهوى أن تعدلوا وإن تلووا أو تعرضوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: O you who believe! Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and the Book (the Qur'an) which He has sent down to His Messenger, and the Scripture which He sent down to those before (him), and whosoever disbelieves in Allah, His Angels, His Books, His Messengers, and the Last Day, then indeed he has strayed far away (i.e. in error).
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to have faith and belief in the fundamental tenets of Islam - belief in the oneness of Allah, His Messengers, His revealed Books, and the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that those who reject any of these core beliefs have strayed far from the path of truth and guidance.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا آمنوا بالله ورسوله والكتاب الذي نزل على رسوله والكتاب الذي أنزل من قبل ومن يكفر بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief - never will Allah forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of repeatedly turning away from faith and increasing in disbelief. Those who cycle between belief and disbelief, ultimately rejecting the truth, have sealed their own fate and will not be forgiven by Allah nor guided to the right path. This serves as a stern warning against wavering in one's faith and the consequences of such behavior.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم ازدادوا كفرا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم سبيلا

translation: Inform the hypocrites that there is for them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to warn the hypocrites, those who outwardly profess faith in Islam but inwardly conceal disbelief, that they will face a severe and painful punishment in the Hereafter for their insincerity and deception.
orig: بشر المنافقين بأن لهم عذابا أليما

translation: Those who take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, do they seek with them honor [through power]? But indeed, honor belongs to Allah entirely.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of Muslims seeking alliances and support from non-believers instead of other believers. It emphasizes that true honor and power belongs to Allah alone, and that seeking it from disbelievers is misguided. The interpretation is that Muslims should maintain their loyalty and allegiance to their faith and fellow believers, rather than compromising their principles in pursuit of worldly power or status.
orig: الذين يتخذون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أيبتغون عندهم العزة فإن العزة لله جميعا

translation: And it has already come down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah [recited] being disbelieved in and ridiculed, do not sit with them until they enter into another conversation. Indeed, you would then be like them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers in Hell all together
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to avoid associating with those who mock or disbelieve in the verses of the Quran. The interpretation is that Muslims should not participate in or condone such behavior, as it would make them complicit in the disbelief. The verse also warns that those who engage in such mockery will be gathered with the hypocrites and disbelievers in Hell on the Day of Judgement.
orig: وقد نزل عليكم في الكتاب أن إذا سمعتم آيات الله يكفر بها ويستهزأ بها فلا تقعدوا معهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره إنكم إذا مثلهم إن الله جامع المنافقين والكافرين في جهنم جميعا

translation: Those who wait (and watch) for (some misfortune to befall) you: if you have a victory from Allah, they say: "Were we not with you?" But if the disbelievers have a success, they say (to them): "Did we not gain an advantage over you and did we not guard you from the believers?" But Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will not grant to the disbelievers a way (to triumph) over the believers.
interpretation: This verse condemns the hypocrites who claim to be believers but in reality are waiting and watching for the misfortune of the true believers. When the believers have success, the hypocrites try to take credit for it, but when the disbelievers have success, the hypocrites gloat over the believers. However, Allah will judge between the believers and the hypocrites on the Day of Resurrection, and will not allow the disbelievers to have authority over the believers.
orig: الذين يتربصون بكم فإن كان لكم فتح من الله قالوا ألم نكن معكم وإن كان للكافرين نصيب قالوا ألم نستحوذ عليكم ونمنعكم من المؤمنين فالله يحكم بينكم يوم القيامة ولن يجعل الله للكافرين على المؤمنين سبيلا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites [think to] deceive Allah, but Allah is [fully] aware of what they are doing. And when they stand for prayer, they stand with laziness, showing [themselves to] the people and not remembering Allah except a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive nature of the hypocrites, who try to mislead Allah but are ultimately known by Him. It also describes their outward show of piety in prayer, which is done with laziness and for the sake of appearing righteous before others, rather than out of a genuine remembrance of Allah.
orig: إن المنافقين يخادعون الله وهو خادعهم وإذا قاموا إلى الصلاة قاموا كسالى يراءون الناس ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا

translation: Wavering between this [and that], [belonging] neither to these [i.e., the believers] nor to those [i.e., the disbelievers]. And whoever Allah leaves astray - for him you will never find a way.
interpretation: This verse describes those who are indecisive and wavering in their faith, not fully committing to either belief or disbelief. They belong neither to the believers nor the disbelievers, and are unable to find the right path. Ultimately, it is Allah who guides people, and those whom He leaves astray will have no way to find the truth.
orig: مذبذبين بين ذلك لا إلى هؤلاء ولا إلى هؤلاء ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: O you who believe! Do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah against yourselves a clear case?
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers not to ally themselves with the disbelievers, as this would go against their faith and give the disbelievers power over them. The believers should instead seek the company and support of other believers, as this will strengthen their faith and please Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أتريدون أن تجعلوا لله عليكم سلطانا مبينا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire - and never will you find for them a helper.
