interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe punishment that awaits the hypocrites in the afterlife. Hypocrites are those who outwardly profess faith in Islam but inwardly conceal disbelief or opposition to it. They will be condemned to the lowest level of Hell, the most severe and eternal punishment, and they will have no one to come to their aid or support them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار ولن تجد لهم نصيرا

translation: Except for those who repent, correct themselves, hold fast to Allah, and are sincere in their religion for Allah. For those will be with the believers. And Allah is going to give the believers a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere repentance, correcting one's actions, holding firmly to the faith in Allah, and being devoted to Allah alone in one's religious practice. Those who do so will be counted among the believers and will be granted a great reward by Allah.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله فأولئك مع المؤمنين وسوف يؤت الله المؤمنين أجرا عظيما

translation: What would God do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And ever is God Appreciative and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if people are grateful to God and have faith in Him, then God will not punish them. Instead, God is appreciative of their gratitude and faith, and has complete knowledge of their actions. The implication is that through gratitude and belief, one can avoid punishment and earn God's appreciation.
orig: ما يفعل الله بعذابكم إن شكرتم وآمنتم وكان الله شاكرا عليما

translation: Allah does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. And Allah is ever Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah dislikes the public expression of evil or wrongdoing, except in the case of someone who has been unjustly treated. In such situations, the public mention of the wrongdoing may be justified. However, even then, one should be mindful that Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, and that ultimately, justice will be served.
orig: لا يحب الله الجهر بالسوء من القول إلا من ظلم وكان الله سميعا عليما

translation: If you disclose good or conceal it or pardon an offense - indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Powerful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of good deeds, whether they are openly displayed or kept hidden. It also highlights the forgiving nature of Allah, who is both Pardoning and Powerful. The verse encourages believers to do good, even if it is not publicly known, and to pardon the wrongs of others, as Allah is the ultimate Judge and Forgiver.
orig: إن تبدوا خيرا أو تخفوه أو تعفوا عن سوء فإن الله كان عفوا قديرا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to discriminate between Allah and His messengers and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and wish to adopt a way in between -
interpretation: This verse condemns those who selectively believe in some parts of the divine message while rejecting others. It emphasizes the importance of accepting the entirety of Allah's revelations and the messengers He has sent, without discrimination or picking and choosing. The interpretation is that true faith requires a complete and unwavering belief in Allah and all of His prophets, without any division or compromise.
orig: إن الذين يكفرون بالله ورسله ويريدون أن يفرقوا بين الله ورسله ويقولون نؤمن ببعض ونكفر ببعض ويريدون أن يتخذوا بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: Those are the disbelievers, truly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith in God and His message are truly disbelievers. It also warns that a humiliating punishment has been prepared for them in the Hereafter as a consequence of their disbelief and rejection of the truth.
orig: أولئك هم الكافرون حقا وأعتدنا للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not discriminate between any of them - to them He will give their rewards, and Allah is Ever All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of believing in Allah and all of His messengers without making any distinction between them. Those who do so will be rewarded by Allah, who is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful. The interpretation suggests that true faith requires accepting all of Allah’s messengers, not just some of them, and that this is the path to attaining Allah’s rewards and blessings.
orig: والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله ولم يفرقوا بين أحد منهم أولئك سوف يؤتيهم أجورهم وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven. But they asked [even] greater than that of Moses [when] they said, "Show us Allah directly." So the thunderbolt took them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf [for worship] after clear evidences had come to them, and We pardoned that. And We gave Moses a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse highlights the audacity and unreasonable demands of the People of the Book, who asked the Prophet Muhammad to bring down a book from the heavens, something even greater than what they had demanded from Prophet Moses. Their request to see Allah directly resulted in them being struck by the thunderbolt due to their wrongdoing. Even after clear signs were given to them, they still worshipped the calf, but were pardoned by Allah. The verse emphasizes that Allah has given clear authority and guidance through the Prophets, which the people should follow.
orig: يسألك أهل الكتاب أن تنزل عليهم كتابا من السماء فقد سألوا موسى أكبر من ذلك فقالوا أرنا الله جهرة فأخذتهم الصاعقة بظلمهم ثم اتخذوا العجل من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات فعفونا عن ذلك وآتينا موسى سلطانا مبينا

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We raised the mountain above them as if it was a dark cloud and they were certain that it would fall upon them, [and We said], "Hold firmly to what We have given you and remember what is in it that you might fear Allah."
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah raised the mountain over the Israelites as a sign of His power and authority, compelling them to enter the gate in submission. It emphasizes the importance of adhering firmly to the covenant and commandments given to them, including observing the Sabbath, in order to fear and obey Allah.
orig: ورفعنا فوقهم الطور بميثاقهم وقلنا لهم ادخلوا الباب سجدا وقلنا لهم لا تعدوا في السبت وأخذنا منهم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: So it is because of their breach of their covenant, and their disbelieving in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the Prophets without right, and their saying: "Our hearts are wrapped (with coverings)",- nay, Allah hath set a seal on their hearts because of their rejection (of Faith), so they understand not.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reasons for the punishment that the disbelievers will face. They had broken their covenant with Allah, rejected His signs, unjustly killed the Prophets, and claimed that their hearts were sealed, unable to understand the truth. This indicates their arrogance and unwillingness to accept the guidance of Allah, which has led to Allah sealing their hearts, making it difficult for them to believe except for a few.
orig: فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم وكفرهم بآيات الله وقتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق وقولهم قلوبنا غلف بل طبع الله عليها بكفرهم فلا يؤمنون إلا قليلا

translation: And [for] their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander
interpretation: This verse condemns the disbelief of those who made false accusations against the Virgin Mary. It highlights the gravity of their slander, which was a grave sin and an affront to her honor and purity.
orig: وبكفرهم وقولهم على مريم بهتانا عظيما

translation: And [for] their saying, "Indeed, we have killed the Messiah, Jesus the son of Mary, the messenger of Allah." And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but [another] was made to resemble him to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him, for certain.
interpretation: This verse refutes the claim that the Jews killed Jesus. It states that they did not actually kill or crucify him, but rather someone was made to resemble him. The verse emphasizes that those who dispute this matter are in doubt, as they do not have definitive knowledge, only conjecture. The verse asserts that Jesus was not killed, affirming his life and status as a messenger of God.
orig: وقولهم إنا قتلنا المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وما قتلوه وما صلبوه ولكن شبه لهم وإن الذين اختلفوا فيه لفي شك منه ما لهم به من علم إلا اتباع الظن وما قتلوه يقينا

translation: Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms the elevated status of Jesus (peace be upon him) and his closeness to Allah. It indicates that Allah raised Jesus to Himself, rather than allowing him to be killed on the cross. This highlights the wisdom and power of Allah, who is Exalted in Might and Wise in His decisions and actions.
orig: بل رفعه الله إليه وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: And there is none of the People of the Book but will believe in him before his death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even those who have received previous divine scriptures, such as the Jews and Christians, will ultimately come to believe in the Prophet Muhammad before they die. On the Day of Judgment, the Prophet will testify against them for their rejection of his message during their lifetimes.
orig: وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته ويوم القيامة يكون عليهم شهيدا

translation: And [We had prohibited] because of the wrongdoing of those who became Jews, to whom We had prohibited certain [previously] lawful good things that had been made lawful for them, and [many of them] averting [people] from the way of Allah
interpretation: This verse highlights how the Jews were prohibited from certain good and lawful things due to their own wrongdoing and transgressions. It also indicates that they turned people away from the path of Allah, which is a grave sin.
orig: فبظلم من الذين هادوا حرمنا عليهم طيبات أحلت لهم وبصدهم عن سبيل الله كثيرا

translation: And [for] their taking of usury while they had been forbidden it, and their consuming of the people`s wealth unjustly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of usury (riba) and the unjust consumption of people`s wealth. It warns that those who engage in such practices, despite being forbidden from doing so, will face a severe punishment from Allah.
orig: وأخذهم الربا وقد نهوا عنه وأكلهم أموال الناس بالباطل وأعتدنا للكافرين منهم عذابا أليما

translation: But those firm in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you, and the establishers of prayer and the givers of zakah and the believers in Allah and the Last Day - those We will give a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the true believers are those who are firmly grounded in knowledge, who believe in the revelations sent down to the Prophet Muhammad and the previous Prophets, who establish regular prayer and give charity, and who have faith in Allah and the Day of Judgment. These are the ones who will be greatly rewarded by Allah.
orig: لكن الراسخون في العلم منهم والمؤمنون يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك والمقيمين الصلاة والمؤتون الزكاة والمؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر أولئك سنؤتيهم أجرا عظيما

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And We revealed [something] to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the [twelve] tribes [of Israel], and [to] Jesus and Job and Jonah and Aaron and Solomon, and to David We gave the Psalms.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the revelation of the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad is part of a continuous line of divine guidance that has been sent to various prophets throughout history. It highlights the universality of the divine message and the common foundation shared by the different prophetic traditions. The verse serves to affirm the legitimacy of Prophet Muhammad's prophethood and the divine origin of the Qur'an, as it is situated within this broader context of God's revelations to His messengers.
orig: إنا أوحينا إليك كما أوحينا إلى نوح والنبيين من بعده وأوحينا إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وعيسى وأيوب ويونس وهارون وسليمان وآتينا داوود زبورا

translation: And [We have sent] messengers about whom We have related [their stories] to you before, and messengers about whom We have not related to you. And Allah spoke to Moses with [direct] speech.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the prophets and messengers sent by Allah to guide humanity. It acknowledges that some of these messengers have been mentioned in the Quran, while others have not. The verse also highlights the unique and direct communication between Allah and the prophet Moses, underscoring the special status of this prophet.
orig: ورسلا قد قصصناهم عليك من قبل ورسلا لم نقصصهم عليك وكلم الله موسى تكليما

translation: Messengers as bearers of good tidings and as warners, in order that mankind might have no argument against Allah after the (coming of) messengers. Allah was ever Mighty, Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the prophets and messengers sent by Allah to guide humanity. They were sent as both bearers of good news and as warners, so that people would have no excuse or argument against Allah after the coming of these messengers. Allah is All-Mighty and All-Wise in His decision to send these messengers to guide and instruct mankind.
orig: رسلا مبشرين ومنذرين لئلا يكون للناس على الله حجة بعد الرسل وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: But Allah bears witness to that which He has revealed to you. He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness [as well]. And sufficient is Allah as Witness.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad by Allah, and that the angels also bear witness to its divine origin. It emphasizes that Allah Himself is the ultimate Witness and Testimony to the truth of the Qur'an, which was sent down with His perfect knowledge and authority.
orig: لكن الله يشهد بما أنزل إليك أنزله بعلمه والملائكة يشهدون وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah have certainly gone astray in [far] error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith in Allah and prevent others from following the path of righteousness have strayed far from the truth and are deeply misguided. Their rejection of faith and attempts to lead others astray will only result in their own eternal loss and misery.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله قد ضلوا ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and commit wrong - Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith and engage in wrongdoing will not be forgiven by Allah, nor will they be guided to the right path. It underscores the gravity of disbelief and unrighteousness, and the consequences of such actions in the sight of the Almighty.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وظلموا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم طريقا

translation: Except the way to Hell, abiding therein forever. And that, for Allah, is [always] easy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the only path available for those who reject faith is the eternal torment of Hell. It highlights that this outcome is inevitable and easily accomplished by Allah, the All-Powerful.
orig: إلا طريق جهنم خالدين فيها أبدا وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: O mankind, there has to come to you the Messenger with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you. And if you disbelieve - then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth. And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse encourages all of humanity to believe in the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad, as it is the truth from God. Believing in this message is better for one's own wellbeing. Even if some choose to disbelieve, everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God, who is all-knowing and all-wise.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم الرسول بالحق من ربكم فآمنوا خيرا لكم وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات والأرض وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: O People of the Book! Do not exaggerate in your religion, and do not say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary and a soul [created at a command] from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And do not say, "Three"; desist - it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is but one God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of moderation in religious beliefs and rejecting exaggerations or false claims about Allah and the nature of Jesus Christ. It calls on the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) to believe in the oneness of Allah and to not ascribe divinity to Jesus or claim a Trinity. The verse affirms that Jesus was a messenger of Allah and not the son of Allah. The interpretation highlights the message of monotheism, rejecting polytheism and the concept of the Trinity, and emphasizing that Allah alone is the Sovereign and Disposer of all affairs.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم ولا تقولوا على الله إلا الحق إنما المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وكلمته ألقاها إلى مريم وروح منه فآمنوا بالله ورسله ولا تقولوا ثلاثة انتهوا خيرا لكم إنما الله إله واحد سبحانه أن يكون له ولد له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: The Messiah will never be averse to being a servant of Allah, nor will the angels near [to Him]. And whoever is averse to His worship and is arrogant - [to] them He will gather all together to Himself.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humility and servitude of the Messiah (Jesus) and the angels towards Allah. It suggests that no one, not even the most exalted beings, should be arrogant or refuse to worship Allah. Those who are arrogant and reject worship of Allah will be gathered to Him on the Day of Judgment, where they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: لن يستنكف المسيح أن يكون عبدا لله ولا الملائكة المقربون ومن يستنكف عن عبادته ويستكبر فسيحشرهم إليه جميعا

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them in full their rewards and increase for them of His bounty. But as for those who disdain and are arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrasting fates of two groups of people: those who believe and do good deeds, and those who are arrogant and reject faith. The former will be rewarded by Allah and granted additional blessings, while the latter will face a painful punishment and will have no one to protect or help them. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith, righteousness, and humility before Allah, and the consequences of arrogance and rejection of faith.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيوفيهم أجورهم ويزيدهم من فضله وأما الذين استنكفوا واستكبروا فيعذبهم عذابا أليما ولا يجدون لهم من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: O mankind, there has to come to you a convincing proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light.
interpretation: This verse calls upon all of humanity to heed the guidance and clear proof that has come to them from God. The "convincing proof" refers to the Qur'an and the message of Islam, which provides clear and unambiguous guidance for how to live a righteous life. The "clear light" is the light of faith and divine wisdom that has been revealed through the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad. This verse urges people to accept this guidance and follow the path that leads to God's pleasure and salvation.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم برهان من ربكم وأنزلنا إليكم نورا مبينا

translation: But those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him - He will admit them to mercy from Himself and [give them] bounty and guide them to Himself on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse promises that those who have true faith in Allah and steadfastly hold on to their belief will be granted Allah's mercy, grace, and guidance. They will be led on a straight and righteous path that leads to Allah. This emphasizes the importance of unwavering faith and devotion to Allah as the means to attain His blessings and eternal guidance.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا بالله واعتصموا به فسيدخلهم في رحمة منه وفضل ويهديهم إليه صراطا مستقيما

translation:
They ask you for a [legal] ruling. Say, "Allah gives you a ruling concerning one having neither descendants nor ascendants [as heirs].
If a man dies, leaving no child but [only] a sister, she will have half of what he left. And he inherits from her if she [dies and] has no child. But if there are two sisters [or more], they will have two-thirds of what he left. And if the siblings are men and women, the male has the share of two females. Allah makes clear to you [His law], lest you go astray. And Allah is Knowing of all things."
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the inheritance laws in Islam, specifically regarding the case of someone who dies without direct descendants or ascendants. It establishes the shares of inheritance for a sister or sisters, and the relative shares between male and female siblings. The interpretation is that Allah has laid out these clear rules to prevent confusion and ensure a just distribution of the deceased's wealth, and that Allah has perfect knowledge of all matters.
orig: يستفتونك قل الله يفتيكم في الكلالة إن امرؤ هلك ليس له ولد وله أخت فلها نصف ما ترك وهو يرثها إن لم يكن لها ولد فإن كانتا اثنتين فلهما الثلثان مما ترك وإن كانوا إخوة رجالا ونساء فللذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين يبين الله لكم أن تضلوا والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: O you who believe! Fulfill [all] obligations. Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock except for that which is recited to you [in this Qur'an] - hunting [animals] while you are in the state of ihram [i.e., pilgrimage] is prohibited. Indeed, Allah ordains what He intends.
interpretation: This verse exhorts the believers to fulfill their obligations, whether they are religious, social, or contractual. It then clarifies that the animals of grazing livestock are lawful for consumption, except for those that are prohibited during the state of pilgrimage (ihram). This highlights the importance of following the divine commandments and respecting the sanctity of the sacred rituals. Ultimately, the verse reminds us that Allah has the absolute authority to ordain what He wills, and we must submit to His decree.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أوفوا بالعقود أحلت لكم بهيمة الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم غير محلي الصيد وأنتم حرم إن الله يحكم ما يريد

translation: O you who believe! Do not violate the sanctity of the symbols of Allah, nor of the Sacred Month, nor of the animals brought for sacrifice, nor the garlanded animals, nor those coming to the Sacred House, seeking the bounty and pleasure of their Lord. But when you have completed the pilgrimage, you may hunt. And do not let the hatred of a people - for having obstructed you from the Sacred Mosque - incite you to transgress. And help one another in righteousness and piety, but do not help one another in sin and transgression. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting the sanctity of Allah's symbols, such as the Sacred Months, the animals brought for sacrifice, and the Sacred House (the Kaaba). It instructs believers not to violate these sacred things, even if they have been prevented from accessing the Sacred Mosque. Instead, the verse encourages believers to help one another in righteousness and piety, and to refrain from sin and transgression. The verse also reminds believers that Allah is severe in punishment, and that they should fear Him.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحلوا شعائر الله ولا الشهر الحرام ولا الهدي ولا القلائد ولا آمين البيت الحرام يبتغون فضلا من ربهم ورضوانا وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا ولا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم أن صدوكم عن المسجد الحرام أن تعتدوا وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان واتقوا الله إن الله شديد العقاب

translation: Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and [those animals] killed by strangling or by a violent blow or by a head-long fall or by the goring of horns, and those from which a wild animal has eaten, except what you [are able to] slaughter [before its death], and those which are sacrificed on stone altars, and [forbidden is] that you seek decision through divining arrows. That is grave disobedience. This day those who disbelieve have despaired of [defeating] your religion; so fear them not, but fear Me. This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion. But whoever is forced [by necessity], without willful disobedience or transgressing due limits - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines various prohibitions and permissible practices related to food and religious rituals. It forbids the consumption of dead animals, blood, pork, and animals not slaughtered in the name of Allah. It also prohibits certain methods of animal slaughter and divination through arrows. The verse emphasizes that this religion (Islam) has been perfected and approved by Allah, and that those who disbelieve should not be feared. However, it also provides an exception for those who are forced by necessity to consume otherwise prohibited foods, as Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: حرمت عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل لغير الله به والمنخنقة والموقوذة والمتردية والنطيحة وما أكل السبع إلا ما ذكيتم وما ذبح على النصب وأن تستقسموا بالأزلام ذلكم فسق اليوم يئس الذين كفروا من دينكم فلا تخشوهم واخشون اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم وأتممت عليكم نعمتي ورضيت لكم الإسلام دينا فمن اضطر في مخمصة غير متجانف لإثم فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: They ask you, [O Muhammad], what has been made lawful for them. Say, "Lawful for you are [all] good foods and [game caught by] what you have trained of hunting animals which you train as Allah has taught you. So eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of Allah upon it, and fear [i.e., be aware of] Allah." Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers on what is lawful (halal) for them to consume. It permits the consumption of good, pure foods as well as game animals that have been trained for hunting. The key aspects are that the name of Allah is invoked upon the food, and that the believers remain conscious of and fear (be aware of) Allah, as He is swift in calling people to account for their actions.
orig: يسألونك ماذا أحل لهم قل أحل لكم الطيبات وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين تعلمونهن مما علمكم الله فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم واذكروا اسم الله عليه واتقوا الله إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: This day [all] good [lawful] things have been made lawful for you. And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them. And [lawful in marriage are] chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you have given them their [bridal] dues, [and you seek them in marriage] not in unlawful sexual intercourse, nor [taking them as] mistresses. And whoever denies the faith - his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse outlines several important rulings regarding what is permissible (halal) and what is not. It states that all good and pure things have been made lawful for Muslims. It also allows Muslims to consume the food of the People of the Book (Jews and Christians), and vice versa. Furthermore, it permits Muslim men to marry chaste women from among the believers as well as chaste women from the People of the Book, as long as the proper marital dues are given and the relationship is not one of unlawful sexual intercourse or concubinage. Finally, it warns that whoever rejects faith will have their deeds rendered worthless and they will be among the losers in the Hereafter.
orig: اليوم أحل لكم الطيبات وطعام الذين أوتوا الكتاب حل لكم وطعامكم حل لهم والمحصنات من المؤمنات والمحصنات من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم إذا آتيتموهن أجورهن محصنين غير مسافحين ولا متخذي أخدان ومن يكفر بالإيمان فقد حبط عمله وهو في الآخرة من الخاسرين

translation: O you who believe! When you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows and wipe over your heads and [wash] your feet to the ankles. And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the ritual ablution (wudu) that Muslims must perform before engaging in prayer. It details the specific steps to be followed, including washing the face, arms, head, and feet. It also addresses situations where water is not available, allowing for the use of clean earth (tayammum) as a substitute. The overall purpose is to purify oneself and prepare for the spiritual act of prayer, with Allah's intention being to make this process easy and to cleanse the believer, so that they may be grateful.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا قمتم إلى الصلاة فاغسلوا وجوهكم وأيديكم إلى المرافق وامسحوا برءوسكم وأرجلكم إلى الكعبين وإن كنتم جنبا فاطهروا وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط أو لامستم النساء فلم تجدوا ماء فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم منه ما يريد الله ليجعل عليكم من حرج ولكن يريد ليطهركم وليتم نعمته عليكم لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, "We hear and we obey." And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers to be grateful for the blessings and guidance that Allah has bestowed upon them, and to be mindful of the covenant they have made with Allah to obey Him. The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah and acknowledging that He is all-knowing, even of the secrets within one's heart. The interpretation encourages the believers to maintain a sincere and humble relationship with Allah, staying true to their commitment to hear and obey Him.
orig: واذكروا نعمة الله عليكم وميثاقه الذي واثقكم به إذ قلتم سمعنا وأطعنا واتقوا الله إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: O you who believe! Stand out firmly for justice, as witnesses to Allah, even as against yourselves, or your parents, or your kin, and whether it be (against) rich or poor: for Allah can best protect both. Follow not the lusts (of your hearts), lest you swerve, and if you distort (your witness) or decline to do justice, verily Allah is well-acquainted with all that you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and fairness in all situations, even if it goes against one's own interests or those of family and friends. It calls upon believers to be steadfast in their commitment to justice, and to not let personal biases or emotions sway them from doing what is right. The verse reminds that Allah is all-knowing and will hold people accountable for their actions, and that true piety lies in doing what is just and righteous, not in succumbing to personal desires or prejudices.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين لله شهداء بالقسط ولا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم على ألا تعدلوا اعدلوا هو أقرب للتقوى واتقوا الله إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds [that] for them there is forgiveness and great reward.
interpretation: This verse conveys a promise from God to those who have faith in Him and do good deeds. It assures them of God's forgiveness and a great reward in the Hereafter as a result of their righteous actions and beliefs. The interpretation highlights the connection between faith, good conduct, and the divine reward that awaits the believers.
orig: وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة وأجر عظيم

translation: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - those are the companions of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith in God and deny the truth of the divine revelations (the Qur'anic "signs") will be condemned to the eternal punishment of Hell. It serves as a warning to those who turn away from the guidance provided in the Qur'an and choose to live in disbelief and denial of God's signs and messages.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: O you who believe! Remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people were about to stretch out their hands [in aggression] against you, but He withheld their hands from you; and fear Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be grateful to Allah for His protection and blessings. It reminds them that when they were threatened by an enemy, Allah intervened and prevented harm from befalling them. The verse exhorts the believers to put their trust in Allah and be mindful of Him, as He is the source of their security and well-being.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا نعمت الله عليكم إذ هم قوم أن يبسطوا إليكم أيديهم فكف أيديهم عنكم واتقوا الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And Allah had already taken a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We delegated from among them twelve leaders. And Allah said, "Indeed, I am with you, if you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and loan Allah a goodly loan, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever of you disbelieves after that has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way."
interpretation: This verse highlights the covenant that Allah made with the Children of Israel, where He appointed twelve leaders from among them and promised to forgive their sins and grant them entry into Paradise if they upheld certain conditions. The key conditions were establishing prayer, paying zakah, believing in and supporting the messengers of Allah, and lending a goodly loan to Allah. This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's obligations to Allah and serving Him, and warns that those who disbelieve after this covenant will have strayed from the right path.
orig: ولقد أخذ الله ميثاق بني إسرائيل وبعثنا منهم اثني عشر نقيبا وقال الله إني معكم لئن أقمتم الصلاة وآتيتم الزكاة وآمنتم برسلي وعزرتموهم وأقرضتم الله قرضا حسنا لأكفرن عنكم سيئاتكم ولأدخلنكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار فمن كفر بعد ذلك منكم فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: And for their breaking of the covenant We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their [proper] usages and have forgotten a portion of that of which they were reminded. And you will still observe deceit among them, except a few of them. But pardon them and overlook [their misdeeds]. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of breaking a covenant with God. The people in question are cursed and their hearts are hardened, leading them to distort the words of God and forget the guidance they were given. Despite this, the verse instructs the Prophet (peace be upon him) to pardon them and overlook their misdeeds, as God loves those who do good. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of upholding covenants, the dangers of hardening one's heart, and the mercy and forgiveness of God towards those who repent and do good.
orig: فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم لعناهم وجعلنا قلوبهم قاسية يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه ونسوا حظا مما ذكروا به ولا تزال تطلع على خائنة منهم إلا قليلا منهم فاعف عنهم واصفح إن الله يحب المحسنين

translation: And from those who say, "We are Christians" We took their covenant; but they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded. So We caused among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah is going to inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse refers to the covenant that Allah took from the Christians, but they forgot and neglected a portion of what they were reminded of. As a result, Allah caused animosity and hatred to arise among them, which will continue until the Day of Resurrection. On that Day, Allah will inform them about their actions and hold them accountable for their transgressions.
orig: ومن الذين قالوا إنا نصارى أخذنا ميثاقهم فنسوا حظا مما ذكروا به فأغرينا بينهم العداوة والبغضاء إلى يوم القيامة وسوف ينبئهم الله بما كانوا يصنعون

translation: O People of the Book, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and overlooking much. There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book, referring to the Jews and Christians, and invites them to accept the message of Prophet Muhammad. It states that the Prophet has come to explain and clarify much of what they had concealed or distorted in their scriptures, and to overlook many of their past transgressions. The verse also describes the Qur'an as a "light" and a "clear Book" that has been sent down from Allah, providing guidance and clarity.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم كثيرا مما كنتم تخفون من الكتاب ويعفو عن كثير قد جاءكم من الله نور وكتاب مبين

translation: Allah guides to His Light whom He wills. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who guides people to the path of righteousness and enlightenment. He chooses to guide those who seek His pleasure and submit to His will. Through His guidance, He leads them out of the darkness of ignorance and sin into the light of faith and truth, and directs them towards the straight and righteous path.
orig: يهدي به الله من اتبع رضوانه سبل السلام ويخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور بإذنه ويهديهم إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary." Say, "Then who could prevent Allah at all if He had intended to destroy the Messiah, the son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on the earth?" And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of Allah, the Almighty. It refutes the notion that Jesus (peace be upon him) is the son of God, and affirms that Allah alone has power and control over all creation. The verse serves as a reminder that no one and nothing can prevent Allah from doing as He wills, and that all power and authority belong to Him alone.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم قل فمن يملك من الله شيئا إن أراد أن يهلك المسيح ابن مريم وأمه ومن في الأرض جميعا ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما يخلق ما يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And the Jews and the Christians say, "We are the children of Allah and His beloved." Say, "Then why does He punish you for your sins? Rather, you are human beings from among those He has created. He forgives whom He wills, and He punishes whom He wills. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the [final] destination."
interpretation: This verse addresses the claims made by the Jews and Christians that they are the chosen people of God and His beloved. The Qur'an refutes this notion, stating that all humans are equal in the sight of God, and that He punishes or forgives whomever He wills, regardless of their religious affiliation. The verse emphasizes that God's dominion extends over the entire universe, and that all will ultimately return to Him for judgment. The interpretation highlights the Qur'anic message of the oneness of God and the equality of all people before Him.
orig: وقالت اليهود والنصارى نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه قل فلم يعذبكم بذنوبكم بل أنتم بشر ممن خلق يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما وإليه المصير

translation: O People of the Book, Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you [the religion] after a period [of suspension] of the messengers, lest you say, 'There came not to us any bringer of good tidings or a warner.' So there has come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the People of the Book, referring to the Jews and Christians. It states that a new messenger, the Prophet Muhammad, has come to them to clarify the religion after a period when no messenger had been sent. This was to prevent them from claiming that no one had come to warn them or bring them good news. The verse emphasizes that this new messenger, the Prophet Muhammad, has indeed come to them as a bearer of good tidings and a warner, and that Allah has power over all things.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم على فترة من الرسل أن تقولوا ما جاءنا من بشير ولا نذير فقد جاءكم بشير ونذير والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Moses said to his people, 'O my people, remember the favor of Allah upon you when He appointed among you prophets and made you sovereigns and gave you that which He had not given to anyone among the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the blessings that Allah bestowed upon the people of Moses. He appointed prophets among them, made them sovereigns, and granted them favors that were not given to any other people. This is a reminder to the people to be grateful for these blessings and to remember the grace of Allah upon them.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ جعل فيكم أنبياء وجعلكم ملوكا وآتاكم ما لم يؤت أحدا من العالمين

translation: O my people, enter the holy land which Allah has assigned to you and do not turn back [from fighting in Allah's cause], for then you will turn back [as] losers.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the Israelites to enter and conquer the holy land of Canaan, which God has promised them. It warns them against turning back or retreating from this divine command, as that would lead to their defeat and loss. The verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and perseverance in fulfilling God's will, even in the face of adversity.
orig: يا قوم ادخلوا الأرض المقدسة التي كتب الله لكم ولا ترتدوا على أدباركم فتنقلبوا خاسرين

translation: They said, 'O Moses, indeed within it is a people of tyrannical strength, and indeed, we will never enter it until they leave it; and if they leave it, then we will enter.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the fear and hesitation of the Israelites to enter the Promised Land, as they were intimidated by the powerful inhabitants living there. Their unwillingness to confront the challenges ahead reflects a lack of faith and trust in God's promise, which Moses had conveyed to them. This passage serves as a lesson about the importance of overcoming fear, embracing faith, and having the courage to face difficulties in order to achieve the desired outcome.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إن فيها قوما جبارين وإنا لن ندخلها حتى يخرجوا منها فإن يخرجوا منها فإنا داخلون

translation: Two men from among those who feared [Allah] upon whom Allah had bestowed favor said, "Enter upon them through the gate, for when you have entered it, you will be the predominant. And upon Allah rely, if you should be believers."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have faith and trust in Allah, even when facing daunting challenges. The two men who feared Allah advised their people to enter the city with courage and conviction, knowing that with Allah's help, they would prevail. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah and having unwavering faith, which can lead to success even in the face of seemingly insurmountable obstacles.
orig: قال رجلان من الذين يخافون أنعم الله عليهما ادخلوا عليهم الباب فإذا دخلتموه فإنكم غالبون وعلى الله فتوكلوا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: They said, "O Moses, indeed we will not enter it, ever, as long as they are within it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are remaining right here."
interpretation: This verse highlights the reluctance and cowardice of the Israelites when faced with the prospect of entering and conquering the Promised Land. They make excuses and refuse to fight, instead asking Moses and God to do it for them. This reflects a lack of faith, courage, and willingness to fulfill their divine destiny. The interpretation is that true believers must be willing to make sacrifices and take action, rather than passively expecting others to do the difficult work for them.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إنا لن ندخلها أبدا ما داموا فيها فاذهب أنت وربك فقاتلا إنا هاهنا قاعدون

translation: He said, "My Lord, indeed I do not possess [power over] except myself and my brother, so distinguish between us and the defiantly disobedient people."
interpretation: This verse expresses the helplessness of the Prophet Musa (Moses) in the face of the Pharaoh and his people. Musa acknowledges that he has no power or authority except over himself and his brother Harun (Aaron). He asks Allah to distinguish between them and the wicked, corrupt people who have rejected the truth.
orig: قال رب إني لا أملك إلا نفسي وأخي فافرق بيننا وبين القوم الفاسقين

translation: He said, 'It is forbidden to them for forty years; in distraction they will wander through the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the Israelites who were condemned to wander in the wilderness for 40 years as a punishment for their disobedience and lack of faith. The interpretation is that one should not be distressed by the actions of those who persistently defy God's commands, for they will face the consequences of their choices.
orig: قال فإنها محرمة عليهم أربعين سنة يتيهون في الأرض فلا تأس على القوم الفاسقين

translation: And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam [i.e., Cain and Abel] in truth. When they both offered a sacrifice [to Allah], and it was accepted from one of them but not accepted from the other. [The latter] said, "I will surely kill you." [The former] said, "Indeed, Allah only accepts from the righteous [who fear Him]."
interpretation: This verse recounts the story of Cain and Abel, the two sons of Adam, and how their offerings to God were received differently. The interpretation is that God only accepts the offerings and deeds of those who are righteous and fear Him, not those who are wicked or do not have faith. The lesson is that we must strive to be righteous and God-fearing in our actions and intentions in order for them to be accepted by God.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق إذ قربا قربانا فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر قال لأقتلنك قال إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين

translation: If you stretch out your hand to kill me, I shall not stretch out my hand to kill you. For I fear Allah, the Lord of the Worlds.
interpretation: This verse expresses the principle of non-aggression and trust in God's judgment. Even when faced with a threat of violence, the believer is called to refrain from retaliation and instead put their faith in Allah, the Sovereign Lord. This teaches us to respond to harm with patience, forgiveness and reliance on divine justice rather than taking matters into our own hands.
orig: لئن بسطت إلي يدك لتقتلني ما أنا بباسط يدي إليك لأقتلك إني أخاف الله رب العالمين

translation: Indeed, I want you to [carry] my sin and your sin so you will be among the companions of the Fire. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse expresses the desire of the wrongdoer to have others share in their sin and punishment, rather than bearing the consequences of their own actions. It highlights the tendency of the unjust to shift blame and seek to involve others in their misdeeds, rather than taking responsibility for their own choices. The interpretation is that this attitude leads to the Fire, which is the just recompense for those who oppress and wrong others.
orig: إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك فتكون من أصحاب النار وذلك جزاء الظالمين

translation: And his soul permitted to him the murder of his brother, so he killed him and became of the losers.
interpretation: This verse describes how the soul of a person can become corrupted and lead them to commit a grave sin, such as the murder of their own brother. The interpretation is that one should be wary of the temptations of the soul and strive to control one's base desires, lest they lead to disastrous consequences and eternal loss.
orig: فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه فقتله فأصبح من الخاسرين

translation: Then Allah sent a crow searching [i.e., scratching] in the ground to show him [the man] how to hide the disgrace of his brother. [The man] said, "O woe to me! Have I failed to be like this crow and hide the disgrace of my brother?" And he became of the regretful.
interpretation: This verse teaches us the importance of compassion and helping others, even in difficult situations. The man who killed his brother initially struggled to understand how to properly bury the body, until he observed a crow burying another dead bird. This made him realize his own shortcoming and he felt deep regret for not being able to properly care for his brother's remains. The verse highlights how we should strive to help and support one another, even when it is challenging, and that failing to do so can lead to profound regret.
orig: فبعث الله غرابا يبحث في الأرض ليريه كيف يواري سوءة أخيه قال يا ويلتا أعجزت أن أكون مثل هذا الغراب فأواري سوءة أخي فأصبح من النادمين

translation: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption [done] in the land - it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves one - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And Our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs. Then indeed many of them, [even] after that, throughout the land, were transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of human life and the gravity of unjustly taking a life. It states that whoever kills an innocent person, it is as if they have killed all of humanity. Conversely, whoever saves a life, it is as if they have saved all of humanity. The verse also mentions that God's messengers came with clear proofs, yet many of the Children of Israel still transgressed. The interpretation highlights the importance of preserving and respecting human life, and the consequences of disregarding this fundamental principle.
orig: من أجل ذلك كتبنا على بني إسرائيل أنه من قتل نفسا بغير نفس أو فساد في الأرض فكأنما قتل الناس جميعا ومن أحياها فكأنما أحيا الناس جميعا ولقد جاءتهم رسلنا بالبينات ثم إن كثيرا منهم بعد ذلك في الأرض لمسرفون

translation: The only punishment of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to make mischief in the land is that they should either be killed or crucified or their hands and their feet should be cut off on opposite sides or they should be imprisoned. That is a disgrace for them in this world, and in the Hereafter they shall have a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse outlines the severe consequences for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger, and who seek to spread corruption and mischief in the land. The punishments mentioned - execution, crucifixion, amputation of limbs, and exile - are intended to serve as a deterrent and to protect the social order. The verse emphasizes that these individuals will face disgrace in this life and a great punishment in the Hereafter, underscoring the gravity of their crimes against the divine order.
orig: إنما جزاء الذين يحاربون الله ورسوله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا أن يقتلوا أو يصلبوا أو تقطع أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف أو ينفوا من الأرض ذلك لهم خزي في الدنيا ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: Except for those who repent before you overcome them and know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and God's forgiveness. It suggests that those who repent before they are overpowered or defeated will be forgiven by Allah, who is both Forgiving and Merciful. The verse encourages people to seek forgiveness and turn back to God, even if they have committed wrongs in the past, as Allah is willing to pardon them.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من قبل أن تقدروا عليهم فاعلموا أن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who believe! Fear Allah and seek the means [of nearness] to Him and strive in His cause that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to have a deep reverence and consciousness of Allah, to seek ways to draw closer to Him, and to exert effort in His cause. The ultimate goal is to attain success, both in this life and the Hereafter, through this righteous conduct.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وابتغوا إليه الوسيلة وجاهدوا في سبيله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - if they had whatever is on the earth entirely and the like of it with it by which to ransom themselves from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it will not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith in God will not be able to escape the punishment of the Day of Judgment, even if they possessed the entire wealth of the world and more. Their wealth and possessions will be of no avail on that Day, as God will not accept any ransom from them. Instead, they will face a painful and severe punishment for their disbelief and rejection of faith.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لو أن لهم ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه ليفتدوا به من عذاب يوم القيامة ما تقبل منهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: They wish to get out of the Fire, but they will never get out of it, and they will have a lasting punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the eternal nature of the punishment in the Hellfire for those who reject faith and do evil deeds. Despite their desire to escape the torment, they will be unable to do so, as their punishment is permanent and unending.
orig: يريدون أن يخرجوا من النار وما هم بخارجين منها ولهم عذاب مقيم

translation: And [as for] the thief, the male and the female, amputate their hands in recompense for what they committed as a deterrent [punishment] from Allah. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the punishment for theft - the amputation of the hands of the male and female thief. This severe punishment is meant to serve as a deterrent to discourage theft and protect the rights and property of others. The verse emphasizes that this is a decree from Allah, who is All-Powerful and All-Wise in His judgments.
orig: والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما جزاء بما كسبا نكالا من الله والله عزيز حكيم

translation: And whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, indeed, Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages repentance and reform after committing wrongdoing. It emphasizes that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, and that He will accept the repentance of those who turn back to Him and make amends for their past misdeeds. The verse highlights the importance of sincere repentance and a commitment to righteous actions, as this is the path to Allah's forgiveness and mercy.
orig: فمن تاب من بعد ظلمه وأصلح فإن الله يتوب عليه إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over the entire universe. He alone has the authority to punish or forgive whomever He pleases, for He is the Almighty, All-Powerful, and All-Knowing. This serves as a reminder to believers that they should submit to Allah's will and seek His forgiveness, for He is the ultimate Judge and Disposer of all affairs.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض يعذب من يشاء ويغفر لمن يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: O Messenger! Let not those grieve you who hasten into disbelief - of such as say "We believe" with their mouths but their hearts believe not, and of the Jews: listeners to falsehood, listeners to another people who have not come to you. They distort words from their [proper] usages, saying "If you are given this, take it; but if you are not given it, then beware." And he for whom Allah intends fitnah - never will you have [any] authority over him at all. Those are the ones for whom Allah does not intend to purify their hearts. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and instructing him not to be saddened by those who rush into disbelief. It warns against the hypocrites who outwardly profess faith but whose hearts do not truly believe, as well as the Jews who distort the words of the Qur'an and try to mislead people. The verse emphasizes that those whom Allah intends to lead astray cannot be guided, and that they will face disgrace in this life and a severe punishment in the Hereafter. The key message is to remain steadfast in faith and not be distressed by the actions of those who reject the truth.
orig: يا أيها الرسول لا يحزنك الذين يسارعون في الكفر من الذين قالوا آمنا بأفواههم ولم تؤمن قلوبهم ومن الذين هادوا سماعون للكذب سماعون لقوم آخرين لم يأتوك يحرفون الكلم من بعد مواضعه يقولون إن أوتيتم هذا فخذوه وإن لم تؤتوه فاحذروا ومن يرد الله فتنته فلن تملك له من الله شيئا أولئك الذين لم يرد الله أن يطهر قلوبهم لهم في الدنيا خزي ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: They are avid listeners to falsehood, devourers of [what is] unlawful. So if they come to you, [O Muhammad], judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them - never will they harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: This verse cautions against those who are eager to listen to and spread falsehoods, and who engage in unlawful practices. The Prophet (peace be upon him) is instructed to either judge between them with justice or to turn away from them, as their harm will not affect him. The key message is that a just and impartial judgment is required, for Allah loves those who act with fairness and equity.
orig: سماعون للكذب أكالون للسحت فإن جاءوك فاحكم بينهم أو أعرض عنهم وإن تعرض عنهم فلن يضروك شيئا وإن حكمت فاحكم بينهم بالقسط إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: And how could they judge you when they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah? Then they turn away, [even] after that, and those are not [in fact] believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to follow the teachings of the Torah, yet turn away from the judgments of Allah contained within it. It suggests that true believers should adhere to the divine guidance provided in the scriptures, rather than selectively choosing what to follow based on their own desires.
orig: وكيف يحكمونك وعندهم التوراة فيها حكم الله ثم يتولون من بعد ذلك وما أولئك بالمؤمنين

translation: Indeed, We have sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to Allah] judged by it for the Jews, as did the rabbis and scholars by that with which they were entrusted of the Scripture of Allah, and they were witnesses thereto. So do not fear the people but fear Me, and do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Torah, which was revealed as a guide and source of light. It highlights that the prophets, rabbis, and scholars were entrusted with the Scripture and were witnesses to its truth. The verse calls upon the people to fear and obey Allah alone, rather than fearing others, and to not compromise their faith for worldly gains. It also warns that those who do not judge by the revelations of Allah are disbelievers.
orig: إنا أنزلنا التوراة فيها هدى ونور يحكم بها النبيون الذين أسلموا للذين هادوا والربانيون والأحبار بما استحفظوا من كتاب الله وكانوا عليه شهداء فلا تخشوا الناس واخشون ولا تشتروا بآياتي ثمنا قليلا ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الكافرون

translation: And We have prescribed for them therein a life for a life, and an eye for an eye, and a nose for a nose, and an ear for an ear, and a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds is legal retribution. But whoever gives [up his right as] charity, it is an expiation for him. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of just retribution, known as Qisas, where the punishment should be proportional to the crime committed. It serves as a deterrent against violence and upholds the rule of law. However, the verse also encourages forgiveness and charitable acts as a means of atonement, which can lead to a more harmonious society. Ultimately, this verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the laws and teachings revealed by Allah, as those who do not judge accordingly are considered wrongdoers.
orig: وكتبنا عليهم فيها أن النفس بالنفس والعين بالعين والأنف بالأنف والأذن بالأذن والسن بالسن والجروح قصاص فمن تصدق به فهو كفارة له ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: And We sent, following in their footsteps, Jesus, the son of Mary, confirming that which came before him in the Torah; and We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light and confirming that which preceded it of the Torah as guidance and instruction for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Jesus, the son of Mary, was sent by God as a prophet, confirming the previous revelations in the Torah. The Gospel given to him provided guidance, light, and further confirmation of the teachings in the Torah for the righteous people.
orig: وقفينا على آثارهم بعيسى ابن مريم مصدقا لما بين يديه من التوراة وآتيناه الإنجيل فيه هدى ونور ومصدقا لما بين يديه من التوراة وهدى وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the followers of the Gospel (i.e. Christians) to judge and rule according to the teachings and commandments revealed by Allah in the Gospel. Those who do not judge by what Allah has revealed in the Gospel are considered to be defiantly disobedient and have strayed from the true path.
orig: وليحكم أهل الإنجيل بما أنزل الله فيه ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: And We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations away from what has come to you of the truth. To each of you We have prescribed a law and a method. Had Allah willed, He would have made you one nation [united in religion], but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you; so race to [all that is] good. To Allah is your return all together, and He will [then] inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Quran as the final revealed scripture, which confirms and supersedes the previous scriptures. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to judge between people based on the revelations from Allah, and not to follow their personal desires or whims. The verse also acknowledges the diversity of religious laws and practices among people, while highlighting that Allah could have made all people follow one religion if He had so willed. However, the purpose of this diversity is to test people and encourage them to compete in good deeds, as ultimately everyone will return to Allah and He will inform them about their differences.
orig: وأنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه من الكتاب ومهيمنا عليه فاحكم بينهم بما أنزل الله ولا تتبع أهواءهم عما جاءك من الحق لكل جعلنا منكم شرعة ومنهاجا ولو شاء الله لجعلكم أمة واحدة ولكن ليبلوكم في ما آتاكم فاستبقوا الخيرات إلى الله مرجعكم جميعا فينبئكم بما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And judge, [O Muhammad], between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations and beware of them, lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. And if they turn away - then know that Allah only intends to afflict them with some of their [own] sins. And indeed, many among the people are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the divine guidance revealed in the Quran, rather than succumbing to the whims and desires of the people. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to judge between people based on the revelations from Allah, and to be wary of those who may try to lead him astray from the path of truth. The verse also suggests that those who turn away from the divine guidance will be afflicted by their own sins, as a consequence of their disobedience. The interpretation highlights the need for steadfastness in following the Quran and the importance of resisting temptations that may lead one away from the straight path.
orig: وأن احكم بينهم بما أنزل الله ولا تتبع أهواءهم واحذرهم أن يفتنوك عن بعض ما أنزل الله إليك فإن تولوا فاعلم أنما يريد الله أن يصيبهم ببعض ذنوبهم وإن كثيرا من الناس لفاسقون

translation: Do they then seek the judgment of (the days of) Ignorance? And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who have firm Faith.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to seek guidance and judgment from Allah, rather than from the ignorant practices and customs of the pre-Islamic era. It emphasizes that Allah's judgment is superior to any human judgment, for those who have firm faith in Him.
orig: أفحكم الجاهلية يبغون ومن أحسن من الله حكما لقوم يوقنون

translation: O you who believe! Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you - then indeed, he is [one] of them. Indeed, Allah guides not the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against taking the Jews and Christians as allies or close friends. It emphasizes that the Jews and Christians are allies of one another, and that any Muslim who allies with them is considered to be one of them. The verse indicates that Allah does not guide those who do wrong by allying with the enemies of Islam.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء بعضهم أولياء بعض ومن يتولهم منكم فإنه منهم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: And you see those in whose hearts is disease hastening into [association with] them, saying, "We are afraid a misfortune may strike us." But perhaps Allah will bring conquest or a decision from Him, and they will become, over what they have been concealing within themselves, regretful.
interpretation: This verse describes those who have doubts and hypocrisy in their hearts. They are quick to associate with the believers, claiming they fear harm, but in reality they are concealing their true intentions. The verse suggests that Allah may grant victory or a decree that will expose their hidden motives, causing them to become regretful for what they have concealed within themselves.
orig: فترى الذين في قلوبهم مرض يسارعون فيهم يقولون نخشى أن تصيبنا دائرة فعسى الله أن يأتي بالفتح أو أمر من عنده فيصبحوا على ما أسروا في أنفسهم نادمين

translation: And those who believe will say, "Are these the ones who swore by Allah their strongest oaths that they were with you?" Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites who outwardly professed faith but inwardly harbored disbelief. They swore oaths to the believers, claiming to be on their side, but their actions and deeds were ultimately worthless and they suffered the consequences of their betrayal. The verse serves as a warning against hypocrisy and the importance of sincerity in one"s faith.
orig: ويقول الذين آمنوا أهؤلاء الذين أقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم إنهم لمعكم حبطت أعمالهم فأصبحوا خاسرين

translation: O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - Allah will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him [who are] humble toward the believers, powerful against the disbelievers; they strive in the cause of Allah and do not fear the blame of a critic. That is the favor of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast in their faith, and warns those who may be tempted to abandon it. It promises that Allah will replace those who turn away with a people who are devoted to Him and His cause. These new believers will be humble and compassionate towards the faithful, but firm and unyielding against the disbelievers. They will strive tirelessly in the path of Allah, undeterred by the criticism of others. This is a special favor from Allah, granted to those He chooses, and He is all-knowing and all-encompassing in His wisdom and power.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا من يرتد منكم عن دينه فسوف يأتي الله بقوم يحبهم ويحبونه أذلة على المؤمنين أعزة على الكافرين يجاهدون في سبيل الله ولا يخافون لومة لائم ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: Your guardian is none but Allah and [therefore] His Messenger and those who have believed - those who establish prayer and give zakah, and they bow [in worship].
interpretation: This verse establishes the true authority and guardianship over the believers. It is Allah and His Messenger, and those who have truly believed and demonstrate their faith through regular prayer and the giving of zakah, even while in the state of humility and submission (bowing in worship).
orig: إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم راكعون

translation: And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed - then the party of Allah will be the predominant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who ally themselves with Allah, His Messenger, and the believers will ultimately prevail and be victorious. It highlights the importance of loyalty and allegiance to the divine and the community of faith, which will lead to triumph and success.
orig: ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون

translation: O you who believe! Do not take as allies those who take your religion in ridicule and amusement among the ones who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers. And fear Allah if you should [truly] be believers.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against taking as allies those who mock and make light of their religion. It includes both the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) and the disbelievers. The believers are commanded to fear and be mindful of Allah if they truly have faith, and not to be influenced by those who ridicule their beliefs.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الذين اتخذوا دينكم هزوا ولعبا من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم والكفار أولياء واتقوا الله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And when you call to prayer, they take it in ridicule and amusement. That is because they are a people who do not use reason.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who treat the call to prayer with disrespect and mockery, rather than recognizing it as a sacred duty. It suggests that their behavior stems from a lack of understanding and an unwillingness to use their intellect to appreciate the significance of the prayer.
orig: وإذا ناديتم إلى الصلاة اتخذوها هزوا ولعبا ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعقلون

translation: Say, "O People of the Book, do you resent us except [for the fact] that we have believed in Allah and what was revealed to us and what was revealed before, and that most of you are defiantly disobedient?"
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book, referring to the Jews and Christians, and challenges them to consider why they harbor resentment towards the believers in Islam. The verse suggests that the main reason for their resentment is the fact that the Muslims have believed in Allah and the revelations sent down to them, as well as the previous revelations. The verse also points out that most of the People of the Book are defiantly disobedient, implying that their resentment is not justified and stems from their own lack of faith and obedience to Allah.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب هل تنقمون منا إلا أن آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وما أنزل من قبل وأن أكثركم فاسقون

translation: Say, 'Shall I inform you of [what is] worse than that as penalty from Allah? [It is that of] those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry and made of them apes and pigs and slaves of Taghut. Those are the worst in position and farthest astray from the sound way.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences of disbelief and disobedience to Allah. It warns that the worst fate is to be cursed by Allah, incur His wrath, and be transformed into the most despicable creatures - apes, pigs, and slaves of false deities. This serves as a strong admonition for people to avoid such a fate by submitting to Allah and following the righteous path.
orig: قل هل أنبئكم بشر من ذلك مثوبة عند الله من لعنه الله وغضب عليه وجعل منهم القردة والخنازير وعبد الطاغوت أولئك شر مكانا وأضل عن سواء السبيل

translation: And when they come to you, they say, 'We believe.' But they have entered with disbelief, and they have departed with it, and Allah is most knowing of what they were concealing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to believe in Islam but in reality harbor disbelief and conceal their true intentions. They may outwardly profess faith when it is convenient, but their hearts and actions betray their true state of disbelief. Allah, the All-Knowing, is aware of what they conceal within themselves.
orig: وإذا جاءوكم قالوا آمنا وقد دخلوا بالكفر وهم قد خرجوا به والله أعلم بما كانوا يكتمون

translation: And you see many of them hastening into sin and aggression and the devouring of [what is] unlawful. How wretched is what they are doing.
interpretation: This verse condemns the actions of those who eagerly and quickly engage in sinful and transgressive behaviors, as well as the consumption of ill-gotten gains. It highlights the reprehensible nature of their actions and the poor state in which they find themselves due to their misdeeds.
orig: وترى كثيرا منهم يسارعون في الإثم والعدوان وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Were it not for the rabbis and the priests forbidding them from uttering sin and consuming unlawful gain, how wretched is that which they were doing.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the religious leaders of the time for not properly guiding and restraining their followers from engaging in sinful and unlawful practices. The implication is that the people were engaging in wrongdoing, but the religious authorities failed to adequately prohibit and prevent it, which is condemned as a grave failure on their part.
orig: لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يصنعون

translation: And the Jews say, "The hand of Allah is chained." Chained are their hands, and cursed are they for what they say. Rather, both His hands are extended; He spends however He wills. And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. And We have cast among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. [It is] whenever they kindled fire for war [that] Allah extinguished it. And they strive throughout the land [causing] corruption, and Allah does not like corrupters.
interpretation: This verse addresses the false claim made by the Jews that Allah's hands are chained, implying that He is stingy and unable to provide. The Qur'an refutes this by stating that Allah's hands are extended, and He spends as He wills. The verse also highlights that the revelation of the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad will only increase the transgression and disbelief of many Jews, leading to animosity, hatred, and corruption among them. This verse emphasizes Allah's unlimited power and generosity, as well as the consequences of rejecting His guidance.
orig: وقالت اليهود يد الله مغلولة غلت أيديهم ولعنوا بما قالوا بل يداه مبسوطتان ينفق كيف يشاء وليزيدن كثيرا منهم ما أنزل إليك من ربك طغيانا وكفرا وألقينا بينهم العداوة والبغضاء إلى يوم القيامة كلما أوقدوا نارا للحرب أطفأها الله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا والله لا يحب المفسدين

translation: And if only the People of the Book had believed and feared God, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse encourages the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) to believe in God and be righteous. If they do so, God will forgive their sins and grant them entry into Paradise. It emphasizes the importance of faith and piety, and the rewards that await those who follow the path of righteousness.
orig: ولو أن أهل الكتاب آمنوا واتقوا لكفرنا عنهم سيئاتهم ولأدخلناهم جنات النعيم

translation: And if only they had upheld [the law of] the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to them from their Lord, they would have consumed [provision] from above them and from beneath their feet. Among them are a moderate community, but many of them - evil is that which they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the divine teachings revealed in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. If the people had adhered to these teachings, they would have been provided with abundant blessings and sustenance from above and below. However, the verse also acknowledges that among them are some who are moderate and righteous, while many others engage in harmful and evil deeds. The verse encourages adherence to the divine guidance as a means of attaining prosperity and well-being.
orig: ولو أنهم أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أنزل إليهم من ربهم لأكلوا من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم منهم أمة مقتصدة وكثير منهم ساء ما يعملون

translation: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Messenger (peace be upon him) conveying the message of Islam to the people. It assures the Messenger that Allah will protect him from the harm of the disbelievers, as long as he fulfills his duty of delivering the divine message.
