The interpretation highlights that the Messenger's primary responsibility is to convey the teachings of Islam without fear or hesitation, and that Allah will safeguard him in this endeavor.
orig: يا أيها الرسول بلغ ما أنزل إليك من ربك وإن لم تفعل فما بلغت رسالته والله يعصمك من الناس إن الله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: Say, "O People of the Book, you are [standing] on nothing until you uphold [the practice of] the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to you from your Lord." And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) to uphold the teachings and commandments of their own scriptures, the Torah and the Gospel, as well as what has been revealed to them from their Lord. It suggests that unless they do so, they are not truly following their own religious traditions. The verse also warns that the revelation of the Quran to the Prophet Muhammad will increase the transgression and disbelief of many among the People of the Book, and thus the Prophet should not be saddened by their rejection of the truth.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لستم على شيء حتى تقيموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أنزل إليكم من ربكم وليزيدن كثيرا منهم ما أنزل إليك من ربك طغيانا وكفرا فلا تأس على القوم الكافرين

translation: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews or Christians or Sabeans - those [among them] who believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteousness - will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that salvation and the promise of no fear or grief is not limited to any one religious group, but is open to all who believe in Allah and the Last Day, and do righteous deeds. It promotes a message of inclusivity and tolerance, highlighting that faith and good works, rather than religious affiliation, are the criteria for attaining Allah's pleasure and protection.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئون والنصارى من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وعمل صالحا فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And We had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel and had sent to them messengers. Whenever there came to them a messenger with what their souls did not desire, a party [of them] denied, and another party they killed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the repeated rejection and persecution of the prophets sent by God to the Children of Israel. Despite being given a covenant and guidance, they would often deny the messengers and even kill them when the message did not align with their desires and expectations. This reflects the human tendency to reject truth in favor of personal preferences, and serves as a warning against such obstinance in the face of divine guidance.
orig: لقد أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل وأرسلنا إليهم رسلا كلما جاءهم رسول بما لا تهوى أنفسهم فريقا كذبوا وفريقا يقتلون

translation: And they thought that there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf. Then Allah turned to them in forgiveness, but [again] many of them became [yet] blind and deaf. And Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn rejection of the truth by some people, who refused to see the signs of Allah and listen to His message. Despite being shown the truth, they persisted in their blindness and deafness, only to be forgiven by Allah. However, many of them continued in their state of denial, unable to comprehend the reality. This verse emphasizes the importance of being receptive to the guidance of Allah and not allowing one's own biases and preconceptions to cloud one's judgment.
orig: وحسبوا ألا تكون فتنة فعموا وصموا ثم تاب الله عليهم ثم عموا وصموا كثير منهم والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: Certainly, they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary." And the Messiah has said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." Indeed, he who associates others with Allah - Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers.
interpretation: This verse condemns the belief that Jesus is the son of God, and affirms that he was a prophet who called people to worship the one true God. It warns that those who associate partners with God will be denied Paradise and face the punishment of Hell, as they have committed a grave sin of polytheism.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم وقال المسيح يا بني إسرائيل اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم إنه من يشرك بالله فقد حرم الله عليه الجنة ومأواه النار وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Allah is the third of three." And there is no deity except one Allah. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, there will surely afflict the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse denounces the Christian doctrine of the Trinity, which asserts that God is three divine persons in one. The Qur'an firmly rejects this belief, declaring that God is One and Unique, and that any association of partners with Him is a grave sin. The verse warns that those who persist in this belief will be subject to a severe punishment from Allah.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله ثالث ثلاثة وما من إله إلا إله واحد وإن لم ينتهوا عما يقولون ليمسن الذين كفروا منهم عذاب أليم

translation: Do they not turn to Allah and seek forgiveness from Him? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to turn to Allah in repentance and seek His forgiveness. It highlights the fact that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, and is willing to accept the repentance of those who sincerely turn to Him. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness, as it is a path to His mercy and grace.
orig: أفلا يتوبون إلى الله ويستغفرونه والله غفور رحيم

translation: The Messiah, son of Mary, was not but a messenger; [other] messengers have passed on before him. And his mother was a supporter of truth. They both used to eat food. Look how We make clear to them the signs; then look how they are deluded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Jesus (peace be upon him) was a messenger of God, like other messengers before him. It reminds us that he was human, who ate food and had a mother, Mary, who was a truthful and righteous woman. The verse directs us to observe how God makes His signs and messages clear, yet people still turn away from the truth.
orig: ما المسيح ابن مريم إلا رسول قد خلت من قبله الرسل وأمه صديقة كانا يأكلان الطعام انظر كيف نبين لهم الآيات ثم انظر أنى يؤفكون

translation: Say, 'Do you worship besides Allah that which cannot harm you or benefit you, and Allah - it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping anything other than Allah, the Almighty. It questions the practice of worshipping idols or false deities that have no power to harm or benefit the worshippers. The verse highlights that Allah alone is the All-Hearing and All-Knowing, and therefore, He is the only worthy object of worship.
orig: قل أتعبدون من دون الله ما لا يملك لكم ضرا ولا نفعا والله هو السميع العليم

translation: Say, "O People of the Book, do not exaggerate in your religion or say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary and a soul [created at a command] from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And do not say, "Three"; desist - it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is but one God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs."
interpretation: This verse calls upon the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) to not exaggerate or go to extremes in their religious beliefs, and to instead adhere to the truth about Allah and the Messiah, Jesus. It emphasizes that Jesus was a messenger of Allah, not the son of Allah, and that Allah is the one and only God. The verse encourages the People of the Book to believe in Allah and His messengers, and to refrain from the belief in the Trinity, which is considered a deviation from the truth.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم غير الحق ولا تتبعوا أهواء قوم قد ضلوا من قبل وأضلوا كثيرا وضلوا عن سواء السبيل

translation: Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and of Jesus, the son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and [habitually] transgressed.
interpretation: This verse condemns the disbelievers among the Children of Israel, who were cursed by the prophets David and Jesus for their disobedience and transgressions. It highlights how rejection of faith and persistent wrongdoing can lead to divine punishment and condemnation.
orig: لعن الذين كفروا من بني إسرائيل على لسان داوود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: They did not forbid one another from the evil that they were doing. Wretched is what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who do not speak out against or prevent wrongdoing, even when they are aware of it. It suggests that by not taking a stand against evil, one becomes complicit in it and shares in the blame for the harmful actions. The interpretation is that it is a moral obligation to actively oppose and discourage unethical behavior, rather than passively accepting it.
orig: كانوا لا يتناهون عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون

translation: You see many of them taking those who disbelieve as allies. How wretched is that which they have put forth for themselves in that Allah has become angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who ally themselves with disbelievers, turning away from the guidance of Allah. It warns that such actions will incur the wrath of Allah, and that those who persist in this will face eternal punishment. The verse emphasizes the grave consequences of forsaking one's faith and aligning with those who reject it.
orig: ترى كثيرا منهم يتولون الذين كفروا لبئس ما قدمت لهم أنفسهم أن سخط الله عليهم وفي العذاب هم خالدون

translation: And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of true faith in Allah and the Prophet Muhammad. It suggests that those who claim to believe, yet ally themselves with those who oppose Allah and His messenger, are in fact disobedient and lack true faith. The interpretation is that true believers should not seek alliances with those who reject the teachings of Islam, but should remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: ولو كانوا يؤمنون بالله والنبي وما أنزل إليه ما اتخذوهم أولياء ولكن كثيرا منهم فاسقون

translation: You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers [to be] the Jews and those who associate others with Allah , and you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the varying degrees of animosity and affection towards the believers (Muslims) from different religious groups. The Jews and polytheists are described as the most intense in their enmity towards the believers, while the Christians are the most affectionate and closest to them. This is because the Christians, unlike the Jews and polytheists, have religious leaders (priests and monks) who are humble and not arrogant, which makes them more receptive to the message of Islam.
orig: لتجدن أشد الناس عداوة للذين آمنوا اليهود والذين أشركوا ولتجدن أقربهم مودة للذين آمنوا الذين قالوا إنا نصارى ذلك بأن منهم قسيسين ورهبانا وأنهم لا يستكبرون

translation: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of believers when they hear the Qur'an being recited. They are moved to tears because they recognize the truth in the divine message and wish to be counted among those who bear witness to it. The verse highlights the sincerity and devotion of the believers, who humbly submit to Allah and seek to be included among the righteous.
orig: وإذا سمعوا ما أنزل إلى الرسول ترى أعينهم تفيض من الدمع مما عرفوا من الحق يقولون ربنا آمنا فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين

translation: And why should we not believe in Allah and what has come to us of the truth? And we aspire that our Lord will admit us [to Paradise] with the righteous people.
interpretation: This verse expresses the desire of the believers to have faith in Allah and the truth that has been revealed to them. It reflects their aspiration to be admitted by Allah into Paradise along with the righteous people. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the hope for salvation in the Hereafter.
orig: وما لنا لا نؤمن بالله وما جاءنا من الحق ونطمع أن يدخلنا ربنا مع القوم الصالحين

translation: So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens [in Paradise] beneath which rivers flow, [where] they will abide eternally, and that is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah rewards those who do good deeds and speak righteously. The "gardens beneath which rivers flow" is a metaphor for the eternal bliss and abundance that the righteous will enjoy in the Hereafter. This is the just recompense for those who strive to please Allah and do good in this life.
orig: فأثابهم الله بما قالوا جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء المحسنين

translation: And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - those are the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith in God and deny the divine revelations will be condemned to the eternal punishment of Hell, referred to as "the Blaze". It highlights the severe consequences of disbelief and rejection of God's guidance.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: O you who believe! Do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like any self-conceited boaster
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to enjoy the good and lawful things that Allah has provided, and not to deprive themselves or others of these blessings. It warns against transgressing the bounds set by Allah, as He does not like those who are arrogant and self-conceited.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحرموا طيبات ما أحل الله لكم ولا تعتدوا إن الله لا يحب المعتدين

translation: And eat of what Allah has provided for you [which is] lawful and good. And fear Allah, in whom you are believers.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to consume only that which is lawful and pure, as provided by Allah. It also reminds them to be mindful of their faith in Allah and to live according to His commands.
orig: وكلوا مما رزقكم الله حلالا طيبا واتقوا الله الذي أنتم به مؤمنون

translation: Allah will not impose blame upon you for your [incorrect] oaths, but He will impose blame upon you for [breaking] what your hearts have pledged. And its [i.e., the oath's] expiation is the feeding of ten needy people from the average of that which you feed your [own] families or clothing them or the freeing of a slave. And whoever cannot find [or afford it] - then a fast of three days [is required]. That is the expiation for oaths when you have sworn. And guard your oaths. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses [i.e., ordinances] that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the Islamic teachings regarding oaths and their expiation. It emphasizes that Allah will not punish you for taking oaths carelessly, but rather for breaking the oaths that you have committed to. The expiation for breaking an oath is to feed ten needy people, clothe them, or free a slave. If one cannot afford this, then a three-day fast is required. The verse encourages believers to be mindful of their oaths and to fulfill them, as this demonstrates gratitude to Allah and obedience to His teachings.
orig: لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما عقدتم الأيمان فكفارته إطعام عشرة مساكين من أوسط ما تطعمون أهليكم أو كسوتهم أو تحرير رقبة فمن لم يجد فصيام ثلاثة أيام ذلك كفارة أيمانكم إذا حلفتم واحفظوا أيمانكم كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تشكرون

translation: O you who believe! Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters [to other than Allah], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to abstain from intoxicants, gambling, idolatrous practices, and divination, as these are considered impure and originating from the work of Satan. The believers are encouraged to avoid these practices in order to attain success and prosperity in this life and the hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إنما الخمر والميسر والأنصاب والأزلام رجس من عمل الشيطان فاجتنبوه لعلكم تفلحون

translation: Satan only wants to cause animosity and hatred between you through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not desist?
interpretation: This verse warns against the dangers of intoxicants and gambling, as they can lead to enmity and hatred among people, and distract them from remembering Allah and performing their religious duties. The interpretation is that one should refrain from such activities in order to maintain harmony in society and focus on their spiritual well-being.
orig: إنما يريد الشيطان أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء في الخمر والميسر ويصدكم عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة فهل أنتم منتهون

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and beware. And if you turn away - then know that upon Our Messenger is only [the responsibility for] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger. It warns against turning away from this obedience, and clarifies that the Messenger's responsibility is to convey the message clearly, not to compel belief. The interpretation is that true believers must submit to the commands of Allah and His Messenger, and that rejecting this obedience has consequences, though the Messenger's role is to deliver the message, not to force acceptance.
orig: وأطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول واحذروا فإن توليتم فاعلموا أنما على رسولنا البلاغ المبين

translation: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds concerning what they have consumed [of foods], as long as they fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe, then fear Allah and do good; and Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that believers who perform good deeds are not to be blamed for what they consume, as long as they maintain their faith, fear Allah, and continue to do good. The verse encourages believers to constantly increase in their devotion to Allah and their righteous conduct, as Allah loves those who excel in doing good.
orig: ليس على الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جناح فيما طعموا إذا ما اتقوا وآمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ثم اتقوا وآمنوا ثم اتقوا وأحسنوا والله يحب المحسنين

translation: O you who believe! Allah will surely test you through [something] from the game that your hands and spears [can] reach, [it is] that Allah may make evident those who fear Him unseen. And whoever transgresses after that - for him is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be steadfast in their faith, even when faced with trials and tribulations. The test mentioned here refers to the hunting of game, which was a common practice at the time. The verse suggests that through such tests, Allah will distinguish those who truly fear Him, even in private. Those who transgress after being tested will face a severe punishment.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ليبلونكم الله بشيء من الصيد تناله أيديكم ورماحكم ليعلم الله من يخافه بالغيب فمن اعتدى بعد ذلك فله عذاب أليم

translation: O you who believe! Do not kill game while you are in the state of Ihram. And whoever of you kills it intentionally, the penalty is an offering, brought to the Kaaba, of an eatable animal equivalent to the one he killed, as adjudged by two just men among you; or, for expiation, he should feed poor persons, or its equivalent in fasting, that he may taste the heinous consequences of his deed. Allah has forgiven what is past; but whoever returns to it, Allah will exact retribution from him. And Allah is Exalted in Might, the Lord of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of the state of Ihram (ritual consecration) during the pilgrimage, where hunting and killing animals is strictly prohibited. The verse outlines the penalty for intentionally killing game while in the state of Ihram, which is to offer an animal of equivalent value to the one killed, as determined by two just men. Alternatively, the offender can expiate the sin by feeding the poor or fasting. The verse also reminds that Allah has forgiven past transgressions, but those who repeat the offense will face divine retribution, as Allah is Mighty and the Lord of Retribution.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقتلوا الصيد وأنتم حرم ومن قتله منكم متعمدا فجزاء مثل ما قتل من النعم يحكم به ذوا عدل منكم هديا بالغ الكعبة أو كفارة طعام مساكين أو عدل ذلك صياما ليذوق وبال أمره عفا الله عما سلف ومن عاد فينتقم الله منه والله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: Lawful to you is [the hunting of] sea animals and their food as provision for you and the travelers, but unlawful to you is [the hunting of] land animals as long as you are in the state of ihram. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse permits the consumption of seafood and other marine life as sustenance for people, including travelers. However, it prohibits the hunting of land animals while in the state of ihram (a sacred state during the pilgrimage). This command emphasizes the importance of fearing and obeying Allah, as all people will ultimately be gathered before Him on the Day of Judgment.
orig: أحل لكم صيد البحر وطعامه متاعا لكم وللسيارة وحرم عليكم صيد البر ما دمتم حرما واتقوا الله الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: Allah has made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, a means of support for the people, and [also] the sacred month and the sacrificial animals and the garlands [by which they are identified]. That is so you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth and that Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Kaaba, the sacred month, the sacrificial animals, and the garlands are all means established by Allah to guide and support the people. It serves as a reminder that Allah has complete knowledge of all that exists in the heavens and the earth, and that He is All-Knowing. This highlights the importance of submitting to Allah's divine wisdom and guidance, as He alone possesses the ultimate knowledge and authority.
orig: جعل الله الكعبة البيت الحرام قياما للناس والشهر الحرام والهدي والقلائد ذلك لتعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وأن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Know that Allah is severe in penalty and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that while Allah is capable of severe punishment for those who disobey Him, He is also infinitely forgiving and merciful towards those who repent and seek His guidance. It encourages us to be mindful of Allah's power and justice, while also having hope in His compassion and willingness to pardon our sins.
orig: اعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب وأن الله غفور رحيم

translation: The Messenger`s duty is only to convey (the message). And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet`s role is to convey the message of Islam, while the responsibility of the people is to accept and follow it. Allah is all-knowing and is aware of both our outward actions and our inner thoughts and intentions.
orig: ما على الرسول إلا البلاغ والله يعلم ما تبدون وما تكتمون

translation: Say, "Not equal are the bad and the good, although the abundance of the bad might impress you." So fear Allah, O you of understanding, that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the distinction between the righteous and the wicked, and cautions against being impressed by the apparent abundance or success of the wicked. It calls upon those with understanding to fear Allah and strive for success in the Hereafter, rather than being swayed by the material prosperity of the unrighteous.
orig: قل لا يستوي الخبيث والطيب ولو أعجبك كثرة الخبيث فاتقوا الله يا أولي الألباب لعلكم تفلحون

translation: O you who believe! Do not ask about things which, if they were made known to you, would trouble you. But if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made clear to you. Allah has forgiven that, and Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to avoid asking about matters that, if revealed, would cause them distress or trouble. It suggests that some questions are best left unasked, as the answers may be difficult to bear. The verse also indicates that if such questions are asked during the revelation of the Qur'an, they will be addressed and clarified. Ultimately, Allah is forgiving and forbearing, and believers should trust in His wisdom and guidance.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تسألوا عن أشياء إن تبد لكم تسؤكم وإن تسألوا عنها حين ينزل القرآن تبد لكم عفا الله عنها والله غفور حليم

translation: Certainly have people asked [such questions] before you, and then became by them disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse indicates that some people in the past had asked questions about the divine messages and revelations, but then they rejected and disbelieved in them. This serves as a warning that one should not let their curiosity or questioning lead them to disbelief, but rather to seek understanding and submit to the truth.
orig: قد سألها قوم من قبلكم ثم أصبحوا بها كافرين

translation: Allah has not appointed [such innovations as] bahirah or sa'ibah or wasilah or ham, but those who disbelieve invent falsehood about Allah, and most of them do not reason.
interpretation: This verse rejects the pagan Arab practices of designating certain animals as sacred and prohibiting their use. It emphasizes that Allah has not ordained such superstitions, but rather the disbelievers fabricate lies about Allah. The verse encourages people to use their reason and not blindly follow traditions without divine sanction.
orig: ما جعل الله من بحيرة ولا سائبة ولا وصيلة ولا حام ولكن الذين كفروا يفترون على الله الكذب وأكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to [the example of] the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers." Even though their fathers knew nothing, and were not guided?"
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who blindly follow the traditions and practices of their ancestors, without questioning their validity or seeking guidance from the revelations of Allah and the example of the Prophet Muhammad. It suggests that following ancestral traditions is not a sufficient basis for guidance, especially if those traditions are not grounded in knowledge or divine guidance. The verse encourages people to seek the truth and guidance from the Qur'an and the Prophet's teachings, rather than simply adhering to the practices of their forefathers.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا إلى ما أنزل الله وإلى الرسول قالوا حسبنا ما وجدنا عليه آباءنا أولو كان آباؤهم لا يعلمون شيئا ولا يهتدون

translation: O you who believe! Take care of your own selves. If you follow the right guidance, no hurt can come to you from those who are in error.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to focus on their own spiritual development and not be overly concerned with the actions of those who have gone astray. It emphasizes that if one follows the guidance of God, they need not fear the consequences of others' misguidance, as God will ultimately judge all people based on their deeds.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم إلى الله مرجعكم جميعا فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, testimony [should be given] among you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest - [that of] two just men from among you or two others from outside if you are traveling through the land and the disaster of death should strike you. Detain them after the prayer and let them both swear by Allah if you are in doubt, [saying], "We will not exchange it [i.e., our testimony] for a price, even if he [i.e., the beneficiary] should be a near relative, and we will not withhold testimony for Allah. Indeed, we would then be of the sinful."
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to have two just witnesses from among themselves or from outside their community to testify in the event of a death and the distribution of the deceased's estate. The witnesses must swear by Allah that they will not conceal or alter the testimony, even if the beneficiary is a relative. This ensures the fair and just distribution of the deceased's wealth according to Islamic principles, and prevents any unethical behavior or tampering with the will.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا شهادة بينكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت حين الوصية اثنان ذوا عدل منكم أو آخران من غيركم إن أنتم ضربتم في الأرض فأصابتكم مصيبة الموت تحبسونهما من بعد الصلاة فيقسمان بالله إن ارتبتم لا نشتري به ثمنا ولو كان ذا قربى ولا نكتم شهادة الله إنا إذا لمن الآثمين

translation: And if it is found that the two of them have deserved [punishment for] sin, let two others stand in their place [who are] from among those who have a claim against the two who defaulted. And let them swear by Allah, `Our testimony is truer than their testimony, and we have not transgressed. Indeed, we would then be of the wrongdoers.`
interpretation: This verse outlines a process for resolving a dispute where two people have been accused of wrongdoing. It states that if it is determined that the two accused parties are indeed guilty, then two other people who have a legitimate claim against the accused should step forward and swear an oath that their testimony is more truthful than that of the accused. This serves as a check against false accusations, ensuring that justice is served and the rights of all parties are protected.
orig: فإن عثر على أنهما استحقا إثما فآخران يقومان مقامهما من الذين استحق عليهم الأوليان فيقسمان بالله لشهادتنا أحق من شهادتهما وما اعتدينا إنا إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: That is more suitable that they should come with testimony as it ought to be. And they were afraid that (other) oaths would be taken after their oaths. So fear Allah and listen (O mankind), and Allah guides not the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to provide testimony that is truthful and accurate, without any attempt to conceal or distort the facts. It also warns against taking oaths lightly or making false oaths, as this can undermine the credibility of one's testimony. The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah and listening to His guidance, as He does not guide those who persistently reject faith and disobey His commands.
orig: ذلك أدنى أن يأتوا بالشهادة على وجهها أو يخافوا أن ترد أيمان بعد أيمانهم واتقوا الله واسمعوا والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: The Day when Allah will gather the [whole of the] Messengers and say: "What was the response you received (from your people)?" They will say: "We have no knowledge (of that). Verily, You, only You (O Allah), are the All-Knower of all that is hidden (from us)."
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment when all the Messengers of Allah will be gathered before Him, and He will ask them about the response they received from their respective peoples. The Messengers will humbly acknowledge that they have no knowledge of the unseen, and that only Allah is the All-Knower of the hidden. This highlights the complete dependence of the Messengers on Allah's knowledge and wisdom, and the importance of submitting to Allah's authority on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يوم يجمع الله الرسل فيقول ماذا أجبتم قالوا لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Allah said, "O Jesus, the son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother when I supported you with the Pure Spirit and you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity; and [remember, O Jesus] when I taught you writing and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel; and when you designed from clay [what was] like the form of a bird with My permission, then you breathed into it, and it became a bird with My permission; and you healed the blind and the leper with My permission; and when you brought forth the dead with My permission; and [mention, O Muhammad], when I restrained the Children of Israel from [killing] you when you came to them with clear proofs, and those who disbelieved among them said, "This is not but obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse highlights the various miracles and blessings that were bestowed upon Jesus (peace be upon him) by Allah. It emphasizes that Jesus was supported by the Holy Spirit, spoke as a child and an adult, was taught various religious scriptures and wisdom, was given the ability to create a bird from clay, heal the blind and lepers, and raise the dead - all by the permission and power of Allah. The verse also mentions how the Children of Israel were restrained from harming Jesus when he came to them with clear proofs, yet some of them still rejected him as a practitioner of "obvious magic". This underscores the divine nature of Jesus' miracles and the rejection of some despite the clear evidence.
orig: إذ قال الله يا عيسى ابن مريم اذكر نعمتي عليك وعلى والدتك إذ أيدتك بروح القدس تكلم الناس في المهد وكهلا وإذ علمتك الكتاب والحكمة والتوراة والإنجيل وإذ تخلق من الطين كهيئة الطير بإذني فتنفخ فيها فتكون طيرا بإذني وتبرئ الأكمه والأبرص بإذني وإذ تخرج الموتى بإذني وإذ كففت بني إسرائيل عنك إذ جئتهم بالبينات فقال الذين كفروا منهم إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when I inspired to the disciples, "Believe in Me and in My messenger [Jesus]." They said, "We have believed, so bear witness that indeed we are Muslims [in submission to Allah]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith in Allah and His messenger, Jesus. The disciples, upon receiving the divine inspiration, professed their belief in Allah and His messenger, and declared themselves to be Muslims, i.e., those who submit to the will of Allah. This highlights the unity of the message of Islam, which was conveyed through various prophets throughout history.
orig: وإذ أوحيت إلى الحواريين أن آمنوا بي وبرسولي قالوا آمنا واشهد بأننا مسلمون

translation: When the disciples said, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table [spread with food] from the heaven?' [Jesus] said, 'Fear Allah, if you should be believers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith and trust in Allah. The disciples asked Jesus if his Lord could send down a table of food from the heavens, which suggests they were seeking a miraculous sign to confirm their belief. However, Jesus responds by urging them to fear (be mindful of) Allah, indicating that true faith requires more than just witnessing signs and wonders. Rather, it requires a sincere devotion and submission to Allah, which should be the foundation of one's belief.
orig: إذ قال الحواريون يا عيسى ابن مريم هل يستطيع ربك أن ينزل علينا مائدة من السماء قال اتقوا الله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: They said, "We desire to eat from it and let our hearts be reassured and know that you have been truthful to us, and we will be of the witnesses [to that]."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the desire of the Israelites to partake in the bounty that God has provided, as a means of affirming their faith and trust in the message of the prophet. It highlights the importance of seeking reassurance and certainty in one's beliefs, while also being willing to bear witness to the truth of what has been conveyed to them.
orig: قالوا نريد أن نأكل منها وتطمئن قلوبنا ونعلم أن قد صدقتنا ونكون عليها من الشاهدين

translation: Jesus, the son of Mary, said: 'O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table [spread with food] from the heaven to be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You, and provide for us, and You are the best of providers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights Jesus' (peace be upon him) humble request to Allah for a sign and provision. He asks Allah to send down a table of food from the heavens as a festival and a sign for the people, both the first and the last. This reflects Jesus' reliance on Allah as the ultimate provider, acknowledging that Allah is the best of providers.
orig: قال عيسى ابن مريم اللهم ربنا أنزل علينا مائدة من السماء تكون لنا عيدا لأولنا وآخرنا وآية منك وارزقنا وأنت خير الرازقين

translation: Allah said, "Indeed, I will send it down to you, but whoever disbelieves among you - then indeed, I will punish him with a punishment such as I have not punished anyone among the worlds."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of disbelief in the message that Allah will reveal. It serves as a stern warning that those who reject this divine revelation will face a severe punishment, the likes of which has never been inflicted upon anyone else in the world. This highlights the importance of accepting and adhering to the teachings of Allah.
orig: قال الله إني منزلها عليكم فمن يكفر بعد منكم فإني أعذبه عذابا لا أعذبه أحدا من العالمين

translation: And [beware, O believers], when Allah will say, "O Jesus, Son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?'" He will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, it is You who is [the full] Knower of the unseen."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah and the status of Jesus as a messenger, not a deity. Jesus humbly denies ever claiming divinity for himself or his mother, and acknowledges that Allah alone has knowledge of the unseen. The verse highlights the importance of maintaining the correct understanding of the relationship between the Creator and the created, and the need to submit to Allah's will and authority.
orig: وإذ قال الله يا عيسى ابن مريم أأنت قلت للناس اتخذوني وأمي إلهين من دون الله قال سبحانك ما يكون لي أن أقول ما ليس لي بحق إن كنت قلته فقد علمته تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك إنك أنت علام الغيوب

translation: I said not to them except what You commanded me - to worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Observer over them, and You are, over all things, Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet as a messenger of God, who conveyed only what he was commanded to say - to worship the one true God. He was a witness over the people as long as he was among them, but after his departure, God Himself became the Witness and Observer over them. This highlights the divine authority and oversight that God maintains over His creation, even after the departure of His messengers.
orig: ما قلت لهم إلا ما أمرتني به أن اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم وكنت عليهم شهيدا ما دمت فيهم فلما توفيتني كنت أنت الرقيب عليهم وأنت على كل شيء شهيد

translation: If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and wisdom of Allah. Even if the people have committed sins, they are still Allah's servants, and it is up to Him whether to punish or forgive them. This highlights the need for humans to submit to Allah's will and judgment, and to have faith in His infinite wisdom and mercy.
orig: إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك وإن تغفر لهم فإنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: Allah says, "This is the Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness. For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, [in] eternal abode. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is the great attainment."
interpretation: This verse describes the reward for the truthful believers on the Day of Judgment. Their truthfulness and sincerity in faith will earn them eternal paradise, where they will live in peace and contentment, with Allah's pleasure and their own satisfaction. This is the ultimate success and triumph that the believers can aspire to attain.
orig: قال الله هذا يوم ينفع الصادقين صدقهم لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is within them, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all creation. It affirms that Allah is the sole owner and ruler of the heavens, the earth, and everything within them. This highlights His supreme authority and ability to control and govern all aspects of the universe, making Him the only true deity worthy of worship and obedience.
orig: لله ملك السماوات والأرض وما فيهن وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: All praise is [due] to Allah, who has created the heavens and the earth and made the darkness and the light. Then those who disbelieve equate [others] with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all praise and gratitude belongs to Allah alone, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and the one who created both darkness and light. It then contrasts this with those who associate partners with Allah, which is the gravest sin in Islam.
orig: الحمد لله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وجعل الظلمات والنور ثم الذين كفروا بربهم يعدلون

translation: It is He who created you from clay and then decreed a term - and a specified term is with Him - then [still] you are in doubt.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God is the sole Creator of mankind, having created us from clay. He has also decreed a fixed term for our lives, which is known only to Him. Despite this clear evidence of His power and knowledge, people still doubt and question the truth of God's existence and the purpose of their creation.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من طين ثم قضى أجلا وأجل مسمى عنده ثم أنتم تمترون

translation: And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secret and your public [affairs], and He knows that which you earn.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the One and Only God, present in the heavens and on the earth. He has complete knowledge of both our hidden and our outward actions, as well as our deeds and earnings. This serves as a reminder of Allah's omniscience and that we are accountable to Him for our conduct.
orig: وهو الله في السماوات وفي الأرض يعلم سركم وجهركم ويعلم ما تكسبون

translation: And there does not come to them any sign from the verses of their Lord except that they are from it turning away.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people are turning away from the clear signs and evidence of God's existence and power that are presented to them in the Qur"an and in the natural world. They are willfully ignoring the guidance and reminders that are being provided to them, and thus remain in a state of heedlessness and rejection of the truth.
orig: وما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين

translation: But they have denied the truth when it has come to them, so they will be informed about what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who reject the truth and mock it when it is presented to them will eventually be informed about the consequences of their actions. They will be held accountable for their disbelief and derision towards the divine message.
orig: فقد كذبوا بالحق لما جاءهم فسوف يأتيهم أنباء ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We have destroyed before them, whom We had established in the earth as We have not established you, and We sent [successive] rain from the sky upon them in abundance and made rivers flow beneath them? Then We destroyed them for their sins and brought forth after them a generation of others.
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on the fate of previous generations who were destroyed due to their sins and transgressions, despite having been established and provided for by God. It serves as a warning to the current generation to learn from the past and avoid a similar fate through righteous conduct and obedience to God.
orig: ألم يروا كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من قرن مكناهم في الأرض ما لم نمكن لكم وأرسلنا السماء عليهم مدرارا وجعلنا الأنهار تجري من تحتهم فأهلكناهم بذنوبهم وأنشأنا من بعدهم قرنا آخرين

translation: And if We had sent down to you, [O Muhammad], a written scripture on paper and they touched it with their hands, the disbelievers would say, "This is not but obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn rejection of the disbelievers, who would dismiss the Qur'an as mere "obvious magic" even if it were to be delivered to them in a physical, written form. Their refusal to accept the divine revelation stems from their unwillingness to acknowledge the truth and their tendency to rationalize their unbelief.
orig: ولو نزلنا عليك كتابا في قرطاس فلمسوه بأيديهم لقال الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And they say, 'Why was there not sent down to him an angel?' But if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided; then they would not be reprieved.
interpretation: The verse addresses the skepticism of the disbelievers who demand a physical manifestation of God's messenger in the form of an angel. The interpretation is that if an angel had been sent down, the matter would have been settled conclusively, leaving no room for further questioning or delay in accepting the message. However, God's wisdom is to test people's faith through the human messengers, rather than through extraordinary displays of power.
orig: وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه ملك ولو أنزلنا ملكا لقضي الأمر ثم لا ينظرون

translation: And if We had willed, We could have made him an angel, but We would have made him [as] a man, and [thus] We would have confused them with that in which they are confusing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if God had willed, He could have created the Prophet as an angel instead of a human. However, by making him a human, God intended to show that prophets are not supernatural beings, but rather ordinary people chosen by God to convey His message. This serves to make the message more relatable and accessible to humanity, rather than something distant and unattainable.
orig: ولو جعلناه ملكا لجعلناه رجلا وللبسنا عليهم ما يلبسون

translation: And indeed, [O Muhammad], messengers before you were ridiculed, but those who mocked them were enveloped by that which they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who mock and ridicule the Prophets of God will be punished by the very thing they mocked. It is a reminder that one should not underestimate the power and authority of God's messengers, as they are protected and supported by the Almighty.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فحاق بالذين سخروا منهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Say, 'Travel through the land and observe how was the end of the deniers.'
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the fate of those who rejected the truth and the consequences of their disbelief. By observing the historical accounts of previous nations and civilizations, one can learn valuable lessons about the importance of faith, righteousness, and the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض ثم انظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: Say, "To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?" Say, "To Allah." He has decreed upon Himself [the] mercy. He will surely assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. Those who have lost themselves - it is they who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah alone. It also highlights that Allah has decreed mercy upon Himself, and that He will gather all people on the Day of Resurrection, which is an undeniable truth. Those who have lost themselves by rejecting faith in Allah are the ones who do not believe.
orig: قل لمن ما في السماوات والأرض قل لله كتب على نفسه الرحمة ليجمعنكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه الذين خسروا أنفسهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has dominion over all that exists, whether it is during the day or the night. He is the All-Hearing and the All-Knowing, and nothing is hidden from His knowledge and awareness. This serves to remind us of Allah's absolute sovereignty and that we are accountable to Him at all times.
orig: وله ما سكن في الليل والنهار وهو السميع العليم

translation: Say, "Is it other than Allah I should take as a protector, Creator of the heavens and the earth, while it is He who feeds and is not fed?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and supremacy of God. It challenges the notion of taking any other being as a protector or deity, as God is the sole Creator of the heavens and the earth, and the one who provides sustenance to all, without needing sustenance Himself. The verse directs the Prophet (peace be upon him) to declare his commitment to being the first to submit to God and to avoid associating partners with Him.
orig: قل أغير الله أتخذ وليا فاطر السماوات والأرض وهو يطعم ولا يطعم قل إني أمرت أن أكون أول من أسلم ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: Say, "Indeed, I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah (God) and the fear of facing severe punishment on the Day of Judgment for those who disobey Him. It serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and all believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to strive to follow Allah's commands, as disobedience will lead to a severe and dreadful consequence on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: قل إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: And whoever is protected from the Hellfire on that Day - [he is] the successful one. And that is the manifest success.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are saved from the punishment of the Hereafter on the Day of Judgment are the truly successful ones. This is the ultimate triumph and the clearest sign of Allah's mercy and favor upon them.
orig: من يصرف عنه يومئذ فقد رحمه وذلك الفوز المبين

translation: And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him. And if He intends for you good, then there is no repeller of His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah. It conveys that Allah alone has the ability to bring about both adversity and prosperity in the lives of people. No one can prevent or undo what Allah has decreed, whether it is hardship or blessings. This serves as a reminder to have complete trust and reliance in Allah, for He is the Almighty, the All-Powerful, and the One who determines the affairs of His creation.
orig: وإن يمسسك الله بضر فلا كاشف له إلا هو وإن يمسسك بخير فهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And He is the Supreme over His servants, and He is the Wise, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute sovereignty and authority over His creation. He is the Almighty, the One who has power and control over all His servants. At the same time, He is the Wise, possessing perfect knowledge and understanding, and the Acquainted, being fully aware of all things. This highlights God's supreme wisdom and intimate knowledge of His creation, which guides His actions and decisions.
orig: وهو القاهر فوق عباده وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: Say, "What thing is greatest in testimony?" Say, "Allah is witness between me and you. And this Qur'an was revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches. Do you [not] testify that with Allah there are other deities?" Say, "I will not testify [with you]." Say, "Indeed, He is but one God, and indeed, I am free of what you associate [with Him]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and supremacy of Allah. It challenges the polytheistic beliefs of the time by asking what testimony could be greater than that of Allah Himself. The Qur'an was revealed to warn people against associating partners with Allah, and the believer is instructed to bear witness to Allah's absolute unity and divinity, and to dissociate from all forms of polytheism.
orig: قل أي شيء أكبر شهادة قل الله شهيد بيني وبينكم وأوحي إلي هذا القرآن لأنذركم به ومن بلغ أئنكم لتشهدون أن مع الله آلهة أخرى قل لا أشهد قل إنما هو إله واحد وإنني بريء مما تشركون

translation: Those to whom We have given the Book recognize him as they recognize their own sons. Those who have lost their own souls - so they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse speaks of those who have been given the divine scripture, such as the Torah or the Gospel, and how they recognize the truth of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) just as they recognize their own children. However, those who have lost their own souls through arrogance and rejection of faith, they refuse to believe in the Qur'an and the message it brings.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم الذين خسروا أنفسهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies His verses? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the most unjust and reprehensible act is to fabricate lies about Allah or to reject and deny the signs and revelations of Allah. Those who engage in such behavior will not be successful, as they have chosen the path of injustice and wrongdoing.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], the Day when We will gather them all together - then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, "Where are your 'partners' that you used to claim [had share in Allah's divinity]?"
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, Allah will gather all people, including those who associated partners with Him. He will then ask the polytheists where are the deities they used to worship besides Allah, challenging the validity of their beliefs and exposing the falsehood of their claims.
orig: ويوم نحشرهم جميعا ثم نقول للذين أشركوا أين شركاؤكم الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: Then their trial was not but that they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not those who associated others with Allah."
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who were tested or tried will ultimately recognize and affirm their belief in the oneness of God, and deny any association of partners with Him. It emphasizes the importance of sincere faith and the rejection of polytheism or idolatry, even in the face of adversity or tribulation.
orig: ثم لم تكن فتنتهم إلا أن قالوا والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين

translation: Look how they lie against themselves! And lost from them is what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the self-deception and falsehoods that people often engage in. It suggests that individuals can become so consumed by their own fabrications and delusions that they lose sight of the truth and become disconnected from reality. The verse serves as a warning against the dangers of self-deception and the importance of being honest with oneself.
orig: انظر كيف كذبوا على أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears is deafness. And if they should see every sign, they will not believe in it. And when they come to you, [O Muhammad], they argue with you; those who disbelieve say, "This is not but legends of the former peoples."
interpretation: This verse describes a group of people who outwardly listen to the Qur'an, but inwardly their hearts and minds are veiled, preventing them from truly understanding and accepting its message. Despite the clear signs and evidence presented to them, they stubbornly refuse to believe and instead dismiss the Qur'an as mere "legends of the former peoples". This highlights the importance of having an open and receptive heart and mind in order to comprehend the divine guidance of the Qur'an.
orig: ومنهم من يستمع إليك وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإن يروا كل آية لا يؤمنوا بها حتى إذا جاءوك يجادلونك يقول الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: And they forbid [others] from it and go away from it, and they [themselves] do not destroy except their [own] selves, but they perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and self-deception of those who prohibit others from doing something, while they themselves indulge in the same behavior. They are blind to their own faults and the consequences of their actions, which ultimately lead to their own destruction, though they are unaware of it.
orig: وهم ينهون عنه وينأون عنه وإن يهلكون إلا أنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: And if you could but see when they will be made to stand before the Fire and will say, "Oh, would that we could be returned [to life on earth] and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers."
interpretation: This verse describes the regret and despair that the disbelievers will feel on the Day of Judgment when they are confronted with the reality of Hell. They will wish that they had been given another chance to believe in God's signs and become true believers, rather than deny the truth. This highlights the importance of faith and righteous deeds in this life, as the consequences of disbelief and rejection of God's guidance will be severe in the Hereafter.
orig: ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على النار فقالوا يا ليتنا نرد ولا نكذب بآيات ربنا ونكون من المؤمنين

translation: Nay, but that which they used to hide before has [now] appeared to them. And even if they were returned, they would return to that [which they were] forbidden; and indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the truth about the wrongdoings of the disbelievers has now been exposed, despite their previous attempts to conceal it. Even if they were given another chance, they would return to their old ways of denying the truth and engaging in deception. The verse emphasizes the futility of their claims and the certainty of their falsehood.
orig: بل بدا لهم ما كانوا يخفون من قبل ولو ردوا لعادوا لما نهوا عنه وإنهم لكاذبون

translation: And they say, "There is not but our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected."
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelief of those who deny the Hereafter and the resurrection. They dismiss the idea of an afterlife, believing that this worldly life is all there is. This interpretation suggests that the verse is addressing those who reject the concept of divine judgment and accountability in the Hereafter.
orig: وقالوا إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا وما نحن بمبعوثين

translation: And if you could see when they will be made to stand before their Lord. [Allah] will say, "Is this not the truth?" They will say, "Yes, by our Lord." [Allah] will say, "Then taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve."
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers will be confronted with the truth they denied in life. They will be forced to acknowledge the reality of God and their own accountability, but their admission will come too late to save them from the punishment they have earned through their rejection of faith.
orig: ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على ربهم قال أليس هذا بالحق قالوا بلى وربنا قال فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: Certainly, those who deny the meeting with Allah have lost, until when the Hour (of Resurrection) comes upon them unexpectedly, they will say, "Woe to us that we neglected it," and they will bear their burdens on their backs. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of denying the Day of Judgment and the meeting with Allah. Those who reject the reality of the Hereafter will face a rude awakening when the Hour of Resurrection arrives unexpectedly. On that day, they will be overwhelmed with regret and anguish, realizing the gravity of their neglect and the burdens they have accumulated. This verse serves as a warning to those who disbelieve, emphasizing the importance of acknowledging the accountability before Allah and preparing for the Hereafter.
orig: قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله حتى إذا جاءتهم الساعة بغتة قالوا يا حسرتنا على ما فرطنا فيها وهم يحملون أوزارهم على ظهورهم ألا ساء ما يزرون

translation: And the worldly life is but amusement and diversion; but the home of the Hereafter is best for those who fear Allah, so will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the life of this world is temporary and fleeting, like a game or play. The true and lasting life is the Hereafter, which is better for those who are conscious of and fear Allah. The verse encourages people to use their reason and intellect to understand the true purpose of life and prepare for the Hereafter.
orig: وما الحياة الدنيا إلا لعب ولهو وللدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون

translation: We certainly know that what they say grieves you, [O Muhammad], but they do not call you a liar. Rather, the wrongdoers reject the verses of Allah.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that the disbelievers' rejection of his message does not mean they consider him a liar. Rather, their rejection stems from their own wrongdoing and unwillingness to accept the clear signs and guidance of Allah. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet should not be distressed by their rejection, as it is not a reflection on his truthfulness, but rather on their own stubborn refusal to acknowledge the divine truth.
orig: قد نعلم إنه ليحزنك الذي يقولون فإنهم لا يكذبونك ولكن الظالمين بآيات الله يجحدون

translation: And indeed, [many] messengers before you were denied, but they were patient over [the effects of] denial, and they were harmed until Our victory came to them. And none can alter the words of Allah. And there has certainly come to you some information about the [previous] messengers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perseverance and steadfastness of the previous prophets in the face of rejection and persecution. Despite the hardships they faced, they remained patient and continued to convey the message of Allah. The verse also affirms the inviolability of Allah's words, highlighting that no one can alter or change the divine teachings. This serves as a reassurance and encouragement for the Prophet Muhammad and his followers, who may have faced similar challenges in their mission to spread the message of Islam.
orig: ولقد كذبت رسل من قبلك فصبروا على ما كذبوا وأوذوا حتى أتاهم نصرنا ولا مبدل لكلمات الله ولقد جاءك من نبإ المرسلين

translation: And if their turning away is hard on you, then if you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder to the sky so that you may bring them a sign, [do so]. But if Allah had willed, He would have united them upon guidance. So do not be of the ignorant.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to seek ways to guide those who have turned away from the message of Islam, even if it is difficult. It suggests exploring all possible means to provide them with signs and evidence that may lead them to the truth. However, it also acknowledges that guidance ultimately rests in the hands of Allah, and one should not become frustrated or ignorant by trying to force people to believe. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience, perseverance, and reliance on Allah in the face of opposition to the message of Islam.
orig: وإن كان كبر عليك إعراضهم فإن استطعت أن تبتغي نفقا في الأرض أو سلما في السماء فتأتيهم بآية ولو شاء الله لجمعهم على الهدى فلا تكونن من الجاهلين

translation: Only those who listen will respond. As for the dead, Allah will resurrect them, and to Him they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that only those who are receptive and willing to listen will respond to the message of the Qur'an. The dead, in a spiritual sense, are those who are heedless and unresponsive to the divine call. However, Allah has the power to resurrect them and bring them back to Him for judgment and accountability.
orig: إنما يستجيب الذين يسمعون والموتى يبعثهم الله ثم إليه يرجعون

translation: And they say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, Allah is Able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know."
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers who demanded a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as proof of his prophethood. The response is that Allah has the power to send down such a sign, but the majority of people lack the understanding to comprehend the wisdom behind it. This emphasizes that faith should not be based solely on miracles, but on a sincere search for the truth and an openness to Allah's guidance.
orig: وقالوا لولا نزل عليه آية من ربه قل إن الله قادر على أن ينزل آية ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And there is no creature on [or within] the earth or bird that flies with its wings except [that they are] communities like you. We have not neglected in the Register a thing. Then unto their Lord they will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all creatures, whether on the earth or in the air, are communities like humans. They are all part of Allah's creation and are subject to His will. The verse also suggests that Allah has knowledge of all things, and that all creatures will ultimately be gathered before Him for judgment.
orig: وما من دابة في الأرض ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه إلا أمم أمثالكم ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء ثم إلى ربهم يحشرون

translation: And those who deny Our verses are deaf and dumb within the darknesses. Whomever Allah wills - He sends him astray, and whomever He wills - He puts him on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who reject and deny the signs and messages of Allah. It suggests that their rejection has made them spiritually deaf and dumb, unable to perceive the truth. The verse further emphasizes that it is Allah who guides people, and He may choose to lead some astray or put others on the right path according to His will and wisdom. This highlights the importance of submitting to Allah and being open to His guidance.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا صم وبكم في الظلمات من يشإ الله يضلله ومن يشأ يجعله على صراط مستقيم

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if there came to you the punishment of Allah or there came to you the Hour - is it other than Allah you would invoke, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to reflect on their faith and actions. It challenges them to consider whether they would truly turn to Allah for help and salvation if they were faced with Allah's punishment or the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the importance of having sincere faith in Allah and not relying on anything or anyone else for deliverance.
orig: قل أرأيتكم إن أتاكم عذاب الله أو أتتكم الساعة أغير الله تدعون إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Nay, you call upon Him, and He removes that for which you call upon Him if He wills, and you forget your [associating of] partners.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to call upon Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him. It suggests that when people call upon Allah, He may remove their difficulties if He wills, but people often forget about their previous associations of partners with Allah.
orig: بل إياه تدعون فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء وتنسون ما تشركون

translation: And We have certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you, [O Muhammad]; then We seized them with poverty and hardship that perhaps they might humble themselves [to Us].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that sending messengers to guide people is a consistent practice of Allah. When previous nations rejected the messengers, Allah subjected them to hardship and adversity, with the hope that they would turn to Him in humility and repentance. This serves as a lesson for all people that turning away from Allah's guidance has consequences, but that Allah desires for people to humble themselves before Him.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا إلى أمم من قبلك فأخذناهم بالبأساء والضراء لعلهم يتضرعون

translation: Then why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts became hardened, and Satan made attractive to them that which they were doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to only turn to God in times of distress, but then quickly revert to their old ways once the hardship has passed. It serves as a warning that we should not wait for calamity to humble ourselves before the Almighty, but rather maintain a constant state of humility and repentance. The verse also reminds us of Satan's role in making our misdeeds seem appealing, and the importance of guarding our hearts against such temptations.
orig: فلولا إذ جاءهم بأسنا تضرعوا ولكن قست قلوبهم وزين لهم الشيطان ما كانوا يعملون

translation: But when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the doors of every [good] thing until, when they rejoiced in that which they were given, We seized them suddenly, and they were [then] in despair.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and being grateful for the blessings that God has bestowed upon us. When people forget the guidance and reminders they have received, and become complacent or arrogant, God may open the doors of prosperity and success for them. However, this prosperity can lead to a false sense of security and self-reliance, causing them to forget their dependence on God. Ultimately, God can suddenly take away these blessings, leaving them in a state of despair and regret for having forgotten their true purpose and relationship with the divine.
orig: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون

translation: And the remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off. And [all] praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the wrongdoers were ultimately destroyed, and that all praise and glory belongs to Allah, the Lord of all creation. It suggests that justice will prevail and that those who transgress will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: فقطع دابر القوم الذين ظلموا والحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should take away your hearing and your sight and set a seal upon your hearts, which deity other than Allah could bring them [back] to you?" Look how We diversify the verses; then they [still] turn away.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all aspects of human existence. It challenges the idea of worshipping any deity other than Allah, as only Allah has the ability to take away or restore one's senses and guide the heart. The verse also highlights how Allah presents His signs and verses, yet people still turn away from faith and guidance.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أخذ الله سمعكم وأبصاركم وختم على قلوبكم من إله غير الله يأتيكم به انظر كيف نصرف الآيات ثم هم يصدفون

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if there came to you the punishment of Allah or there came to you the Hour - is it that you would call upon other than Allah, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse calls upon the disbelievers to reflect on the consequences of their actions. It asks them to consider what they would do if they were to face the punishment of Allah or the Day of Judgment. The implication is that they would then turn to Allah for help, acknowledging His power and authority. The verse emphasizes that only the wrongdoers will be destroyed, suggesting that those who believe and do good deeds will be spared.
orig: قل أرأيتكم إن أتاكم عذاب الله بغتة أو جهرة هل يهلك إلا القوم الظالمون

translation: And We send not the Messengers but as bearers of good tidings and warners, and those who disbelieve contend with falsehood, that they may refute the Truth thereby. And they take My Revelations and that wherewith they are warned as a jest.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Messengers sent by God, who bring glad tidings and warnings. Those who believe and do righteous deeds have no fear or grief, as they will be granted salvation. The verse also highlights the tendency of disbelievers to use falsehood to refute the truth, and to treat God's revelations and warnings with disdain.
orig: وما نرسل المرسلين إلا مبشرين ومنذرين فمن آمن وأصلح فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And those who deny Our verses - the punishment will touch them for their defiant disobedience.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject the signs and messages of Allah will be punished for their wicked and sinful behavior. The punishment is a consequence of their defiant rejection of the truth and their persistent disobedience to Allah's commands.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا يمسهم العذاب بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: Say, "I do not tell you that I have the depositories [containing the provision] of Allah or that I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me." Say, "Are the blind and the seeing equal? Then will you not give thought?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is a messenger who follows the revelation from Allah, and does not possess any special powers or knowledge of the unseen. It also draws a comparison between the blind and the seeing, suggesting that those who are guided by the revelation are not equal to those who are spiritually blind. The verse encourages people to reflect and use their reason to understand the truth.
orig: قل لا أقول لكم عندي خزائن الله ولا أعلم الغيب ولا أقول لكم إني ملك إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي قل هل يستوي الأعمى والبصير أفلا تتفكرون

translation: And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered before their Lord - for them there is no protector or intercessor besides Him - that they might become righteous.
interpretation: This verse is calling the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to warn those who fear being held accountable before God on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that they have no one to protect or intercede for them on that day except God Himself. The purpose of this warning is to encourage them to become righteous and God-fearing, so that they may be saved from the punishment they fear.
orig: وأنذر به الذين يخافون أن يحشروا إلى ربهم ليس لهم من دونه ولي ولا شفيع لعلهم يتقون

translation: And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and afternoon, seeking His countenance. Not upon you is anything of their account and not upon them is anything of your account that you should drive them away, and so you would be of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse encourages us to be inclusive and welcoming towards those who sincerely seek God, regardless of their social status or background. It reminds us that we should not judge others or drive them away, as that would be an act of injustice. Instead, we should be patient and accepting, leaving the judgment of others to God alone.
orig: ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء وما من حسابك عليهم من شيء فتطردهم فتكون من الظالمين

translation: And thus We have tried some of them by others so that they [i.e., the disbelievers] might say, "Is it these [people] whom Allah has favored among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah tests some people through others, so that the disbelievers may question whether those who have been favored by Allah are truly worthy of such favor. The implication is that Allah knows best who is truly grateful and deserving of His blessings, and that we should not judge based on outward appearances or worldly status.
orig: وكذلك فتنا بعضهم ببعض ليقولوا أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا أليس الله بأعلم بالشاكرين

translation: And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy: that any of you who does wrong out of ignorance and then repents after that and corrects himself - indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to greet one another with peace and kindness. It also highlights Allah's mercy and forgiveness - that even if someone commits a wrong out of ignorance, if they subsequently repent and correct their ways, Allah will forgive them, for He is Forgiving and Merciful. The verse emphasizes that Allah's mercy extends to all who believe and seek forgiveness, regardless of their past mistakes.
orig: وإذا جاءك الذين يؤمنون بآياتنا فقل سلام عليكم كتب ربكم على نفسه الرحمة أنه من عمل منكم سوءا بجهالة ثم تاب من بعده وأصلح فأنه غفور رحيم

translation: And thus do We detail the verses, and so the way of the criminals will become clear.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah explains His signs and messages in detail, so that the path of the wrongdoers becomes evident. It suggests that through the clear exposition of Allah's teachings, the true nature and course of action of the sinful and criminal will be revealed.
orig: وكذلك نفصل الآيات ولتستبين سبيل المجرمين

translation: Say, "Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you call upon besides Allah." Say, "I will not follow your desires, for I would then have gone astray, and I would not be of the [rightly] guided."
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet Muhammad to declare that he has been forbidden from worshiping any deities other than Allah. He is instructed to not follow the desires and whims of the people, as that would lead him astray from the right path. The verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping only Allah and not succumbing to false beliefs or practices.
orig: قل إني نهيت أن أعبد الذين تدعون من دون الله قل لا أتبع أهواءكم قد ضللت إذا وما أنا من المهتدين

translation: Say, "Indeed, I am on clear evidence from my Lord, and you have denied it. I do not have that for which you are impatient. The decision is only for Allah . He relates the truth, and He is the best of deciders."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad is acting upon clear evidence and divine guidance from Allah, and that those who reject his message are denying the truth. It also reminds that the ultimate decision and judgment rests with Allah alone, who will judge fairly and determine the truth.
orig: قل إني على بينة من ربي وكذبتم به ما عندي ما تستعجلون به إن الحكم إلا لله يقص الحق وهو خير الفاصلين
