translation: Say, "If what you are impatient for were with me, the matter would have been decided between you and me. And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse is a response to those who demand immediate punishment for their wrongdoing. The Qur'an reminds us that Allah is all-knowing and will judge the wrongdoers in due time. It encourages patience and trust in Allah's wisdom, rather than rushing to judgment or retribution.
orig: قل لو أن عندي ما تستعجلون به لقضي الأمر بيني وبينكم والله أعلم بالظالمين

translation: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it. And no grain is there within the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry [thing] but that it is [recorded] in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of God, who has complete knowledge of the unseen and all that exists in the universe, both on land and in the sea. Nothing, not even the falling of a leaf or the smallest thing in the earth, escapes His knowledge. All is recorded in a clear and evident record, affirming God's absolute sovereignty and control over all creation.
orig: وعنده مفاتح الغيب لا يعلمها إلا هو ويعلم ما في البر والبحر وما تسقط من ورقة إلا يعلمها ولا حبة في ظلمات الأرض ولا رطب ولا يابس إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: And it is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day. Then He revives you therein that a specified term may be fulfilled. Then to Him is your return, and He will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omniscience and control over our lives. He knows our actions and thoughts, both during the day and night. He takes our souls during sleep, then revives us to fulfill our appointed term on earth. Ultimately, we will return to Him, and He will inform us of our deeds, holding us accountable for our actions. This highlights the importance of living a righteous life in accordance with God's will.
orig: وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل ويعلم ما جرحتم بالنهار ثم يبعثكم فيه ليقضى أجل مسمى ثم إليه مرجعكم ثم ينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And He is the Irresistible, above His slaves, and He sends guardians over you, until when death approaches one of you, Our messengers take his soul, and they never neglect their duty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and power of God over His creation. He is the Irresistible, the One who has complete control and authority over all His servants. He sends guardian angels to watch over and protect people until the time of their death, at which point the angels take the soul. This highlights God's omnipotence and the inevitability of death, which is carried out by His appointed messengers without any negligence.
orig: وهو القاهر فوق عباده ويرسل عليكم حفظة حتى إذا جاء أحدكم الموت توفته رسلنا وهم لا يفرطون

translation: Then they will be returned to Allah, their true Lord. Unquestionably, His is the judgment, and He is the swiftest of accountants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all people will ultimately be held accountable before Allah, the true Sovereign and Judge. He alone has the authority to pass judgment, and He is the swiftest in calling people to account for their actions and beliefs. This serves as a reminder of the need to live righteously and prepare for the Day of Reckoning.
orig: ثم ردوا إلى الله مولاهم الحق ألا له الحكم وهو أسرع الحاسبين

translation: Say, "Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and sea [when] you call upon Him imploring [Him] and in secret, 'If He should save us from this [crisis], we will surely be among the thankful.'"
interpretation: This verse encourages people to turn to God in times of distress, whether on land or at sea. It emphasizes the importance of humility and sincerity in seeking God's help, and promises that those who are saved will be grateful and thankful. The verse highlights God's power to rescue and deliver people from difficult situations, and calls upon them to acknowledge and appreciate this divine intervention.
orig: قل من ينجيكم من ظلمات البر والبحر تدعونه تضرعا وخفية لئن أنجانا من هذه لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: Say, "Allah will save you from it and from every distress, then [afterward] you associate [other deities] with Him."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to turn to Allah alone for salvation and relief from distress, and to avoid associating partners with Him. The interpretation suggests that Allah is the sole source of protection and deliverance, and that any form of polytheism or idolatry is a rejection of this fundamental truth.
orig: قل الله ينجيكم منها ومن كل كرب ثم أنتم تشركون

translation: Say, 'He is the [one] Able to send upon you affliction from above you or from beneath your feet and to confuse you [so you become] sects and make you taste the violence of one another." See how We diversify the signs that they might understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute power and ability to punish and test the people in various ways, whether from above or below. It also highlights how God can divide people into different sects and make them experience the violence and conflict among themselves. The purpose of this is to make people reflect on the signs and lessons in the Qur'an, so that they may understand and submit to God's will.
orig: قل هو القادر على أن يبعث عليكم عذابا من فوقكم أو من تحت أرجلكم أو يلبسكم شيعا ويذيق بعضكم بأس بعض انظر كيف نصرف الآيات لعلهم يفقهون

translation: And your people have denied it while it is the truth. Say, 'I am not a guardian over you.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the message of the Qur'an is the truth, yet the people have rejected it. The Prophet is instructed to declare that he is not responsible for their guidance, as they have the free will to accept or reject the truth.
orig: وكذب به قومك وهو الحق قل لست عليكم بوكيل

translation: For every news (that happens) is a [fixed] term, and you will [soon] know.
interpretation: This verse suggests that every event or piece of news has a predetermined time and outcome, and that in due course, the truth about it will become known. It encourages patience and trust in God's plan, as all things will be revealed in their own time.
orig: لكل نبإ مستقر وسوف تعلمون

translation: And when you see those who engage in [idle] discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them until they enter into another conversation. And if Satan should cause you to forget, then do not remain after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to avoid engaging with those who mock or ridicule the verses of the Quran. Instead, he should turn away from them until they change the subject. If Satan causes the Prophet to forget this command, he should not then sit with the wrongdoers.
orig: وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا فأعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره وإما ينسينك الشيطان فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم الظالمين

translation: And upon those who fear Allah is no responsibility concerning them, but [only] a reminder - that perhaps they will fear Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are righteous and fear Allah are not burdened with any accountability or responsibility, as their faith and devotion to Allah are already pleasing to Him. The verse serves as a reminder to them, encouraging them to continue on the path of righteousness and God-consciousness, so that they may maintain their piety and earn the pleasure of Allah.
orig: وما على الذين يتقون من حسابهم من شيء ولكن ذكرى لعلهم يتقون

translation: And leave those who take their religion as amusement and diversion and whom the worldly life has deluded. And remind [them] thereby lest a soul be produced [for punishment] through what it has earned, having other than Allah no protector and no intercessor. And if it should offer every compensation, it would not be taken from it. Those are the ones who are given to evil for what they have earned; for them is a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to deny.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who treat their religion as a mere game or entertainment, and who have been deluded by the pleasures of this worldly life. It reminds that each person will be held accountable for their actions, and that they will have no one to protect or intercede for them on the Day of Judgment, even if they were to offer every possible compensation. Those who have earned evil through their deeds will be punished with a drink of scalding water and a painful torment, due to their denial of the truth.
orig: وذر الذين اتخذوا دينهم لعبا ولهوا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا وذكر به أن تبسل نفس بما كسبت ليس لها من دون الله ولي ولا شفيع وإن تعدل كل عدل لا يؤخذ منها أولئك الذين أبسلوا بما كسبوا لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: Say, "Shall we invoke instead of Allah that which neither benefits us nor harms us and be turned back on our heels after Allah has guided us? [We would then be] like one whom the devils have enticed away from his senses in the land, [causing him to be] confused, although he has companions who invite him to guidance, [calling], 'Come to us.'" Say, "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance; and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to rely solely on the guidance of Allah and not to turn to false deities or superstitions that can neither benefit nor harm them. It warns against being misled by the devil, who can confuse people and lead them astray, even if they have companions who try to guide them back to the right path. The verse emphasizes that the true guidance comes only from Allah, and that believers must submit to Him as the Lord of all the worlds.
orig: قل أندعو من دون الله ما لا ينفعنا ولا يضرنا ونرد على أعقابنا بعد إذ هدانا الله كالذي استهوته الشياطين في الأرض حيران له أصحاب يدعونه إلى الهدى ائتنا قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى وأمرنا لنسلم لرب العالمين

translation: And establish prayer and fear Him and to Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of establishing regular prayer and maintaining a conscious awareness of God. It reminds us that we will ultimately be held accountable to God and gathered before Him on the Day of Judgment. The interpretation is that we should make prayer a central part of our lives, and live with the consciousness that we will one day return to God.
orig: وأن أقيموا الصلاة واتقوه وهو الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in truth. And the Day He says, "Be," and it is, His word is the truth. And His is the dominion [on] the Day the Horn is blown. [He is] Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He is the Wise, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and sovereignty of God. He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and His word is the absolute truth. On the Day of Resurrection, when the Horn is blown, His dominion will be established. He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He is the Wise and Acquainted with all things.
orig: وهو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق ويوم يقول كن فيكون قوله الحق وله الملك يوم ينفخ في الصور عالم الغيب والشهادة وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as deities? Indeed, I see you and your people to be in manifest error."
interpretation: This verse highlights Abraham's rejection of idolatry and his call to his father and people to worship the one true God. It emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the need to avoid the worship of false deities, which Abraham perceives as a clear deviation from the truth.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه آزر أتتخذ أصناما آلهة إني أراك وقومك في ضلال مبين

translation: And thus did We show Abraham the realm of the heavens and the earth that he would be among the certain [in faith]
interpretation: This verse indicates that God revealed to the prophet Abraham the vastness and grandeur of the heavens and the earth, in order to strengthen his faith and conviction in the oneness and power of the Creator. The experience of witnessing the divine kingdom instilled in Abraham a deep certainty and unwavering belief in God's existence and sovereignty.
orig: وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السماوات والأرض وليكون من الموقنين

translation: And when the night covered him [with darkness], he saw a star. He said, 'This is my lord.' But when it set, he said, 'I like not those that disappear.'
interpretation: This verse describes the journey of the prophet Abraham in discovering the oneness of God. He initially thought the star was his lord, but when it disappeared, he realized that it could not be the true, eternal God. This represents the process of moving from polytheism to monotheism, and the understanding that the true God is not a physical object that can vanish, but the eternal, all-powerful Creator.
orig: فلما جن عليه الليل رأى كوكبا قال هذا ربي فلما أفل قال لا أحب الآفلين

translation: And when he saw the moon rising, he said, "This is my Lord." But when it set, he said, "Unless my Lord guides me, I will surely be among the people gone astray."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the importance of not worshipping false gods or idols, and the need for divine guidance. The person initially mistook the moon for his "Lord", but upon seeing it set, he realized his error and acknowledged that he would be "among the people gone astray" without the guidance of the true Lord. This emphasizes the need to seek the right path and not be misled by worldly things that may appear divine, but are ultimately transient and cannot provide true guidance.
orig: فلما رأى القمر بازغا قال هذا ربي فلما أفل قال لئن لم يهدني ربي لأكونن من القوم الضالين

translation: And when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord; this is greater." But when it set, he said, "O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate with Allah."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the folly of worshipping the sun or other celestial bodies. The person initially thought the sun was his lord because of its grandeur, but when it set, he realized it was not worthy of worship as it was subject to change and could not be the eternal, all-powerful God. This highlights the importance of worshipping the one true God who is not limited by time or space.
orig: فلما رأى الشمس بازغة قال هذا ربي هذا أكبر فلما أفلت قال يا قوم إني بريء مما تشركون

translation: Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse expresses the speaker's firm belief and devotion to the One true God, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. It conveys a sense of sincerity and a rejection of polytheism or associating partners with God. The speaker affirms their commitment to the straight path, turning away from false deities and worshiping God alone.
orig: إني وجهت وجهي للذي فطر السماوات والأرض حنيفا وما أنا من المشركين

translation: And he argued with his people. He said, 'Do you argue with me concerning Allah while He has guided me? And I do not fear what you associate with Him [and will not be harmed] unless my Lord should will something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge; then will you not remember?'
interpretation: This verse expresses the steadfastness and conviction of the Prophet in his belief in the oneness of God, despite the opposition and polytheistic beliefs of his people. It emphasizes that he does not fear their false deities, as he has been guided by God, whose knowledge encompasses all things. The verse encourages reflection and remembrance of God's guidance and power.
orig: وحاجه قومه قال أتحاجوني في الله وقد هدان ولا أخاف ما تشركون به إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا وسع ربي كل شيء علما أفلا تتذكرون

translation: And how should I fear what you have associated while you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has not sent down to you a authority? [So] which of the two parties has more right to security, if you know?
interpretation: This verse highlights the absurdity of fearing idols or false gods when the true God, Allah, is the only one worthy of worship. It challenges the polytheists to consider who is more deserving of security and protection - those who worship Allah, or those who associate partners with Him without any divine authority. The verse emphasizes that the true believers in Allah's oneness are the ones who should feel secure, for they have the right to be protected by the Almighty.
orig: وكيف أخاف ما أشركتم ولا تخافون أنكم أشركتم بالله ما لم ينزل به عليكم سلطانا فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: Those who believe and do not mix their faith with injustice - those will have security, and they are [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true believers are those who not only have faith in God, but also refrain from committing injustice or wrongdoing. Such believers will be granted a sense of security and guidance, as they have purified their faith from any association with oppression or unrighteousness.
orig: الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم أولئك لهم الأمن وهم مهتدون

translation: And that was Our [conclusive] argument which We gave Abraham against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the argument or proof that Allah gave to Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) against his people was conclusive and decisive. Allah raises the ranks and degrees of whomever He wills, based on His wisdom and knowledge. This suggests that Allah's decisions and plans are wise and all-knowing, and should be accepted with submission.
orig: وتلك حجتنا آتيناها إبراهيم على قومه نرفع درجات من نشاء إن ربك حكيم عليم

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob; each [of them] We guided. And Noah, We guided before; and among his descendants, David and Solomon and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron. Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights how God has guided and rewarded many righteous individuals from among the descendants of Abraham, including his son Isaac, grandson Jacob, as well as other prominent prophets such as Noah, David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, and Aaron. The verse emphasizes that God rewards those who do good deeds and live righteously.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب كلا هدينا ونوحا هدينا من قبل ومن ذريته داوود وسليمان وأيوب ويوسف وموسى وهارون وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], Zechariah, John, Jesus, and Elias - and all were of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse mentions several righteous prophets of God - Zechariah, John, Jesus, and Elias. It emphasizes that they were all among the righteous, highlighting the virtue and piety of these important figures in Islamic tradition.
orig: وزكريا ويحيى وعيسى وإلياس كل من الصالحين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], Ishmael and Elisha and Jonah and Lot - and all [of them] We preferred over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the Prophets Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah, and Lot were all favored and chosen by Allah over the rest of humanity. It emphasizes the high status and divine selection of these Prophets, who were entrusted with guiding their people and conveying the message of Islam.
orig: وإسماعيل واليسع ويونس ولوطا وكلا فضلنا على العالمين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], their forefathers and their descendants and their brothers - and We chose them and We guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has chosen certain people and guided them to the right path. It suggests that faith and guidance can be passed down through generations, from forefathers to descendants, and that Allah selects those who will receive His guidance and direction.
orig: ومن آبائهم وذرياتهم وإخوانهم واجتبيناهم وهديناهم إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whomever He wills of His servants. And if they had associated others with Allah, then what they were doing would have been worthless for them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the guidance provided in the Qur’an is from Allah, and He bestows it upon whomever He wills among His servants. Even if those who are guided were to associate others with Allah in worship, their deeds would become futile and worthless in the sight of Allah.
orig: ذلك هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء من عباده ولو أشركوا لحبط عنهم ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Those are the ones to whom We have given the Scripture and authority and prophethood. But if they [i.e., the disbelievers] deny it, then We have entrusted it to a people who are not therein disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the divine guidance in the form of scripture, wisdom, and prophethood has been given to certain people. However, if those people reject this guidance, then it will be entrusted to others who will not deny it. This suggests that the acceptance and adherence to the divine message is more important than the lineage or identity of the recipients.
orig: أولئك الذين آتيناهم الكتاب والحكم والنبوة فإن يكفر بها هؤلاء فقد وكلنا بها قوما ليسوا بها بكافرين

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, so follow their guidance. Say, "I ask of you no payment for it. It is not but a reminder for the worlds."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have been guided by Allah are the ones to be followed. The Prophet (peace be upon him) is instructed to convey that he does not seek any reward or payment for delivering this message, as it is simply a reminder for all of humanity.
orig: أولئك الذين هدى الله فبهداهم اقتده قل لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إن هو إلا ذكرى للعالمين

translation: And they did not appraise Allah with true appraisal when they said, "Allah has not revealed to a human being anything." Say, "Who revealed the Scripture that Moses brought as light and guidance to the people? You [Jews] make it into pages, disclosing [some of] it and concealing much. And you were taught that which you knew not - [neither] you nor your fathers." Say, "Allah [revealed it]." Then leave them in their [empty] discourse, amusing themselves.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who deny the divine revelation and authority of the Qur'an and Prophet Muhammad. It reminds them that Allah has revealed scriptures before, such as the Torah revealed to Moses, and that the people have a responsibility to properly understand and uphold these divine teachings, rather than distorting or concealing them. The verse encourages the believers to have faith in Allah's wisdom and authority, and not to be swayed by the empty rhetoric of those who reject the truth.
orig: وما قدروا الله حق قدره إذ قالوا ما أنزل الله على بشر من شيء قل من أنزل الكتاب الذي جاء به موسى نورا وهدى للناس تجعلونه قراطيس تبدونها وتخفون كثيرا وعلمتم ما لم تعلموا أنتم ولا آباؤكم قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم يلعبون

translation: And this is a Book which We have revealed [to you, O Muhammad], blessed and confirming what was before it, and to warn those who dwell in the Mother of Cities [i.e., Makkah] and those around it. And those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are maintaining their prayers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and blessings of the Qur'an, which was revealed by Allah to the Prophet Muhammad. The Qur'an confirms and validates the previous divine scriptures, and it serves as a warning to the people of Makkah and the surrounding regions. The verse also highlights that those who believe in the Hereafter will have faith in the Qur'an and will be diligent in performing their prayers.
orig: وهذا كتاب أنزلناه مبارك مصدق الذي بين يديه ولتنذر أم القرى ومن حولها والذين يؤمنون بالآخرة يؤمنون به وهم على صلاتهم يحافظون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or says, "I have been inspired," while he has not been inspired with anything, and [who] says, "I will reveal [something] like what Allah has revealed"? And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are in the overwhelming pangs of death while the angels extend their hands, [saying], "Discharge your souls! Today you will be awarded the punishment of [extreme] humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth and [because] you were, toward His verses, being arrogant."
interpretation: This verse condemns those who falsely claim divine inspiration or revelation, and those who arrogantly reject the signs and messages of Allah. It warns that on the Day of Judgment, the wrongdoers will face a humiliating punishment for their lies and arrogance against the truth of Allah's words.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو قال أوحي إلي ولم يوح إليه شيء ومن قال سأنزل مثل ما أنزل الله ولو ترى إذ الظالمون في غمرات الموت والملائكة باسطو أيديهم أخرجوا أنفسكم اليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تقولون على الله غير الحق وكنتم عن آياته تستكبرون

translation: And you have certainly come to Us alone as We created you the first time, and you have left whatever We bestowed upon you behind your backs. And We do not see with you your 'intercessors' which you had claimed were among you as partners [with Allah]. It has [all] been severed between you, and lost from you is what you used to claim.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, people will be brought before Allah alone, without any of the worldly possessions, relationships or alleged intercessors that they had relied upon in this life. It serves as a reminder that one's ultimate accountability is to Allah alone, and that all the claims and associations made in this world will be of no avail on that day.
orig: ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة وتركتم ما خولناكم وراء ظهوركم وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء لقد تقطع بينكم وضل عنكم ما كنتم تزعمون

translation: Indeed, Allah is the cleaver of grain and date seeds. He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living. That is Allah; so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and wisdom of Allah in creating life from death and death from life. It is a reminder that Allah is the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe, and that one should not be deluded by false beliefs or idols, but rather turn to Allah in sincere worship and submission.
orig: إن الله فالق الحب والنوى يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي ذلكم الله فأنى تؤفكون

translation: And [it is He] who causes the dawn to break and makes the night dark and the sun and the moon to be in calculation. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of Allah, the Creator. He is the one who brings about the dawn, makes the night dark, and sets the sun and moon in their orbits. This is a testament to His absolute authority and wisdom, as the Exalted in Might and the Knowing.
orig: فالق الإصباح وجعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر حسبانا ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: And it is He who has made for you the stars to guide you through the darknesses of the land and sea. We have detailed the signs for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has created the stars as a means of guidance for humanity, both on land and at sea. The stars serve as beacons that help people navigate through the darkness, providing direction and orientation. This is a sign of Allah's power and wisdom, and a testament to His care for His creation. The verse is directed towards "a people who know", implying that those who possess knowledge and understanding will recognize and appreciate the significance of this divine provision.
orig: وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: And it is He who has created you from one soul and [created] from it its mate that he might dwell in security with her.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of humanity, as we are all created from a single soul. It also highlights the importance of companionship and security in relationships, as the creation of a mate for the individual is described as a means for them to "dwell in security with her". The verse then states that God has "detailed the signs" for those who understand, suggesting that this message of unity and the value of relationships holds deeper meaning and significance.
orig: وهو الذي أنشأكم من نفس واحدة فمستقر ومستودع قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يفقهون

translation: And it is He who sends down rain from the sky; We produce thereby the growth of all things. We bring forth from it greenery from which We produce grains arranged in layers. And from the palm trees - of its emerging fruit are clusters hanging low. And [We produce] gardens of grapevines and olives and pomegranates, similar yet varied. Look at [each of] its fruit when it yields and [at] its ripening. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and providence in providing sustenance for all living beings through the cycle of rain, growth, and the production of diverse fruits and vegetation. It invites the believers to reflect on these signs of God's creation and to strengthen their faith in Him as the sole provider and sustainer of life.
orig: وهو الذي أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به نبات كل شيء فأخرجنا منه خضرا نخرج منه حبا متراكبا ومن النخل من طلعها قنوان دانية وجنات من أعناب والزيتون والرمان مشتبها وغير متشابه انظروا إلى ثمره إذا أثمر وينعه إن في ذلكم لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And they have attributed to Allah partners - the jinn, while He has created them. And they have fabricated for Him sons and daughters without [any] knowledge. Exalted is He and high above what they describe [concerning Him].
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of associating partners with Allah, such as attributing divinity to jinn or fabricating the idea of Allah having children. It emphasizes that Allah is far above and exalted from such associations, which are made without any true knowledge or justification.
orig: وجعلوا لله شركاء الجن وخلقهم وخرقوا له بنين وبنات بغير علم سبحانه وتعالى عما يصفون

translation: The Originator of the heavens and the earth. How can He have a son when He has no wife? And He created all things and is the All-Knower of everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique nature of God as the Creator of the universe, who is free from any need for a spouse or offspring. It affirms that God is the Originator, or the Source, of all existence, and that He has complete knowledge and control over all things.
orig: بديع السماوات والأرض أنى يكون له ولد ولم تكن له صاحبة وخلق كل شيء وهو بكل شيء عليم

translation: That is Allah, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is Disposer of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of Allah as the sole deity and Creator of all things. It calls upon the believers to worship and submit to Allah alone, as He is the Disposer and Controller of all affairs in the universe.
orig: ذلكم الله ربكم لا إله إلا هو خالق كل شيء فاعبدوه وهو على كل شيء وكيل

translation: Vision perceives Him not, but He perceives [all] vision; and He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence and omniscience of God. He is beyond the reach of human perception, yet He is fully aware of all that is perceived. This underscores the idea that God is not limited by the constraints of the physical world, and that His knowledge and understanding far exceed that of His creation. The verse also highlights God's subtle and all-encompassing nature, as He is described as "the Subtle, the Acquainted." This suggests that God's workings are not always immediately apparent, but that He has an intimate knowledge of all things.
orig: لا تدركه الأبصار وهو يدرك الأبصار وهو اللطيف الخبير

translation: There has come to you enlightenment from your Lord. So whoever sees does so for [the benefit of] his own soul, and whoever is blind [suffers] against it. And I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the guidance and enlightenment from God has been provided, and now it is up to the individual to choose to accept and follow it. Those who choose to see and understand the truth will benefit themselves, while those who choose to remain blind will suffer the consequences. The Prophet is not responsible for forcing people to believe, but rather he has delivered the message from God.
orig: قد جاءكم بصائر من ربكم فمن أبصر فلنفسه ومن عمي فعليها وما أنا عليكم بحفيظ

translation: And thus do We diversify the verses [i.e., the Qur'anic verses], that they [i.e., the disbelievers] may say, "You have studied," and that We may make it [i.e., the Qur'an] clear for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah diversifies the verses of the Qur'an in order to challenge the disbelievers and to make the message clear for those who have knowledge and understanding. The disbelievers may try to dismiss the Qur'an as something that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) has studied, but Allah makes it clear that the Qur'an is a divine revelation that is meant to be understood by those who possess knowledge and wisdom.
orig: وكذلك نصرف الآيات وليقولوا درست ولنبينه لقوم يعلمون

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord. There is no deity except Him, and turn away from those who associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet Muhammad to follow the divine revelation he has received from God, and to turn away from those who associate partners with God in worship. The message is one of strict monotheism, rejecting any form of polytheism or idolatry, and affirming the absolute oneness and sovereignty of God.
orig: اتبع ما أوحي إليك من ربك لا إله إلا هو وأعرض عن المشركين

translation: And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated. And We have not made you over them a guardian, and you are not responsible for them.
interpretation: This verse suggests that people's choices to associate partners with Allah are ultimately subject to Allah's will. However, the Prophet Muhammad is not responsible for their choices, nor is he a guardian over them. His role is to convey the message, not to force belief upon them.
orig: ولو شاء الله ما أشركوا وما جعلناك عليهم حفيظا وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: And do not insult those they invoke other than Allah, lest they insult Allah in enmity without knowledge. Thus We have made pleasing to every community their deeds. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse cautions against insulting or mocking the deities or objects of worship of others, as it may lead them to retaliate by insulting Allah in ignorance. It emphasizes that Allah has made the actions of every community seem pleasing to them, but ultimately, all will return to their Lord, who will inform them of their deeds.
orig: ولا تسبوا الذين يدعون من دون الله فيسبوا الله عدوا بغير علم كذلك زينا لكل أمة عملهم ثم إلى ربهم مرجعهم فينبئهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they swear by Allah with their strongest oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say, "The signs are only with Allah, and what will make you perceive that even if a sign came, they would not believe?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim they would believe if a sign or miracle were to come to them. The Qur'an asserts that the signs or proofs of Allah's existence and power are with Allah alone, and that even if such a sign were to come, those who are unwilling to believe would still not accept it. The verse underscores the importance of faith being a matter of the heart and not dependent on external signs or wonders.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن جاءتهم آية ليؤمنن بها قل إنما الآيات عند الله وما يشعركم أنها إذا جاءت لا يؤمنون

translation: And We will turn their hearts and their eyes away [from guidance], as they refused to believe in it the first time. And We will leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who persistently reject faith and guidance will be deprived of understanding and insight. Their hearts and minds will be turned away from the truth, leaving them to wander in their own confusion and misguidance as a consequence of their stubborn rejection of God's signs and messages.
orig: ونقلب أفئدتهم وأبصارهم كما لم يؤمنوا به أول مرة ونذرهم في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: And even if We had sent down to them the angels [with the message] and the dead spoke to them and We gathered together every [created] thing in front of them, they would not believe unless Allah should will. But most of them, [of that], are ignorant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that belief in God and His message is ultimately a matter of divine will, not just a result of seeing miracles or signs. Even if the people were presented with the most overwhelming evidence, they would still not believe unless Allah willed it. This highlights the importance of humility and submission to God's sovereignty in matters of faith.
orig: ولو أننا نزلنا إليهم الملائكة وكلمهم الموتى وحشرنا عليهم كل شيء قبلا ما كانوا ليؤمنوا إلا أن يشاء الله ولكن أكثرهم يجهلون

translation: And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy - devils from among humans and jinn, inspiring to one another decorative speech in delusion. But if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and that which they invent.
interpretation: This verse teaches that every prophet of God faces opposition and enmity from evil forces, both human and supernatural. These forces try to undermine the prophet's message by spreading deceptive and alluring speech. However, it is ultimately God's will that determines whether these forces succeed or not. The verse instructs the prophet to disregard their fabrications and falsehoods, and to focus on conveying the divine message.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا شياطين الإنس والجن يوحي بعضهم إلى بعض زخرف القول غرورا ولو شاء ربك ما فعلوه فذرهم وما يفترون

translation: And let the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter incline to it and let them be pleased with it and let them commit what they are committing.
interpretation: This verse encourages those who do not believe in the Hereafter to turn their hearts towards the Qur'an and to accept its teachings. It suggests that they should be pleased with the Qur'an and commit themselves to the actions and deeds that it prescribes, even though they do not believe in the Hereafter.
orig: ولتصغى إليه أفئدة الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وليرضوه وليقترفوا ما هم مقترفون

translation: Is it other than Allah I should seek as judge while it is He who has revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book explained in detail?" And those to whom We [previously] gave the Scripture know that it is the truth from your Lord [O Muhammad]. So be not [among] the doubters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the only true judge and lawgiver, and that the Quran which He has revealed is the ultimate source of guidance. It warns against seeking guidance or judgment from any source other than Allah, and affirms that those who have received the previous scriptures recognize the truth of the Quran. The verse exhorts the believers not to have any doubts about the divine origin and authority of the Quran.
orig: أفغير الله أبتغي حكما وهو الذي أنزل إليكم الكتاب مفصلا والذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعلمون أنه منزل من ربك بالحق فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: And the word of your Lord has been completed in truth and justice. None can alter His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse affirms the completeness, truth, and justice of the words of Allah. It emphasizes that Allah's words cannot be changed or altered, and that He is All-Hearing and All-Knowing. This verse underscores the divine authority and infallibility of the Qur'anic revelation, and the importance of submitting to Allah's commands and guidance.
orig: وتمت كلمت ربك صدقا وعدلا لا مبدل لكلماته وهو السميع العليم

translation: And if you obey most of those upon the earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah. They follow not except assumption, and they are not but falsifying.
interpretation: This verse warns against blindly following the majority, as they may lead one astray from the path of Allah. It emphasizes that people often follow mere conjecture and speculation rather than the truth, and that their claims may be baseless and untrue.
orig: وإن تطع أكثر من في الأرض يضلوك عن سبيل الله إن يتبعون إلا الظن وإن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Lord, is the One who knows best who has gone astray from the right path and who has found guidance. It affirms that Allah's knowledge is comprehensive and that He is aware of the spiritual state of all people, whether they are misguided or rightly guided.
orig: إن ربك هو أعلم من يضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: So eat of that [meat] upon which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His verses.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to consume only the meat of animals upon which the name of Allah has been invoked during the slaughter. This is a command to eat only halal meat, as consuming anything not dedicated to Allah is forbidden for the faithful. The verse emphasizes that this is for those who truly believe in the signs and revelations of Allah.
orig: فكلوا مما ذكر اسم الله عليه إن كنتم بآياته مؤمنين

translation: And why should you not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has been mentioned [in supplication], while He has explained in detail to you what has been forbidden to you, excepting that to which you are compelled? And indeed do many lead [others] astray through their [own] desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord - He is most knowing of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to consume only what has been permitted by Allah, and to avoid what has been forbidden, except in cases of dire necessity. It also warns against following one's own desires without knowledge, as that can lead others astray. The verse emphasizes that Allah knows best who the transgressors are.
orig: وما لكم ألا تأكلوا مما ذكر اسم الله عليه وقد فصل لكم ما حرم عليكم إلا ما اضطررتم إليه وإن كثيرا ليضلون بأهوائهم بغير علم إن ربك هو أعلم بالمعتدين

translation: And leave what is apparent of sin and what is concealed thereof. Indeed, those who consume interest - they will not stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to not only avoid outward sins, but also the hidden and secret sins. It reminds that those who engage in usury and interest-based transactions will be held accountable on the Day of Judgment, as if they are possessed by Satan. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of purifying one's heart and intentions, not just outward actions.
orig: وذروا ظاهر الإثم وباطنه إن الذين يكسبون الإثم سيجزون بما كانوا يقترفون

translation: And do not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed, it is grave disobedience. And indeed do the devils inspire their allies [among men] to dispute with you. And if you were to obey them, indeed, you would be associators [of others with Allah].
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to not consume food that has not been slaughtered in the name of Allah. Consuming such food is considered a grave sin, as it is associating partners with Allah. The verse also warns that the devils inspire their followers to argue with and dispute the believers, and if the believers were to obey them, they would be considered as those who associate others with Allah.
orig: ولا تأكلوا مما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه وإنه لفسق وإن الشياطين ليوحون إلى أوليائهم ليجادلوكم وإن أطعتموهم إنكم لمشركون

translation: And is one who was dead [in sins] and We gave him life and made for him light by which to walk among the people [like one who remains] in darkness, unable to emerge? Thus it has been made pleasing to the disbelievers that which they were doing.
interpretation: This verse draws a contrast between those who were spiritually dead and have been revived by Allah, and those who remain in the darkness of disbelief. The former have been guided by the light of faith, while the latter are content with their misguided ways. The interpretation highlights how Allah can transform the spiritually dead into those who walk in the light, in contrast to the disbelievers who are pleased with their own actions despite being in darkness.
orig: أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها كذلك زين للكافرين ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And thus We have placed within every city the greatest of its criminals that they may conspire therein. But they conspire not except against themselves, and they perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse suggests that in every community, the most wicked and corrupt individuals often rise to positions of power and influence. However, their scheming and machinations ultimately only harm themselves, as they are unaware of the consequences of their actions.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا في كل قرية أكابر مجرميها ليمكروا فيها وما يمكرون إلا بأنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: And when a Sign comes to them, they say: "We will not believe until we receive the like of what the Messengers of Allah have received." Allah knows best where to place His Message. Humiliation from Allah and a severe punishment will befall the criminals for their scheming.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who refuse to believe in the Qur'an and the message of Islam until they are shown miracles similar to those given to the previous Messengers of Allah. The verse emphasizes that Allah knows best where and how to convey His message, and that those who reject the truth will face humiliation and severe punishment from Allah due to their deceptive schemes against the faith.
orig: وإذا جاءتهم آية قالوا لن نؤمن حتى نؤتى مثل ما أوتي رسل الله الله أعلم حيث يجعل رسالته سيصيب الذين أجرموا صغار عند الله وعذاب شديد بما كانوا يمكرون

translation: So whoever Allah wants to guide - He expands his breast to [contain] Islam; and whoever He wants to misguide - He makes his breast tight and constricted as though he were climbing into the sky. Thus does Allah place defilement upon those who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse explains that Allah guides those whom He wills to Islam by expanding their hearts and making them receptive to the faith. Conversely, He misguides those whom He wills by making their hearts constricted and averse to accepting Islam, as if they are struggling to ascend to the heavens. This illustrates that Allah places a state of spiritual impurity and rejection upon those who refuse to believe.
orig: فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام ومن يرد أن يضله يجعل صدره ضيقا حرجا كأنما يصعد في السماء كذلك يجعل الله الرجس على الذين لا يؤمنون

translation: And this is the path of your Lord, [leading] straight. We have detailed the verses for a people who remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the path shown by Allah is the straight and righteous path. Allah has explained His signs and messages in detail for those who reflect and remember.
orig: وهذا صراط ربك مستقيما قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يذكرون

translation: For them will be the Home of Peace with their Lord. And He will be their Protecting Friend because of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse conveys that those who believe and do righteous deeds will be granted eternal peace and security in the Hereafter, under the protection and guardianship of their Lord. This is a reward for their faithful actions in this life.
orig: لهم دار السلام عند ربهم وهو وليهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And the Day when He will gather them all together [and say], "O company of jinn, you have [misled] many of mankind." And their allies among mankind will say, "Our Lord, some of us made use of others, and we have [now] reached our term which you appointed for us." [Allah] will say, "The Fire is your residence, wherein you will abide eternally, except for what Allah wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing."
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when humans and jinn will be gathered together. The jinn will be accused of having misled many humans, and the human allies of the jinn will admit that they had taken advantage of one another. In response, Allah will decree that the Fire shall be their eternal abode, except for whatever Allah wills. This emphasizes Allah's sovereignty and wisdom in His judgment, which is based on perfect knowledge.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم جميعا يا معشر الجن قد استكثرتم من الإنس وقال أولياؤهم من الإنس ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض وبلغنا أجلنا الذي أجلت لنا قال النار مثواكم خالدين فيها إلا ما شاء الله إن ربك حكيم عليم

translation: And thus We will make some of the wrongdoers allies of others for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who engage in wrongdoing will be made to face the consequences of their actions, as they will be made allies of other wrongdoers. The implication is that the wrongdoers will be held accountable for their misdeeds and that their actions will lead to their own downfall.
orig: وكذلك نولي بعض الظالمين بعضا بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?" They will say, "We bear witness against ourselves." And the worldly life had deluded them, and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse addresses both jinn and humans, reminding them that messengers were sent to them to convey the signs (verses) of Allah and warn them about the Day of Judgment. On that Day, they will testify against themselves, acknowledging their disbelief and the fact that they were deluded by the worldly life. This highlights the accountability of all beings before Allah on the Day of Judgment, where no one can escape the consequences of their actions.
orig: يا معشر الجن والإنس ألم يأتكم رسل منكم يقصون عليكم آياتي وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا قالوا شهدنا على أنفسنا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا وشهدوا على أنفسهم أنهم كانوا كافرين

translation: That is because your Lord would not destroy the cities for wrongdoing while their people were unaware.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God does not punish or destroy a community unless its people have been warned and are aware of their wrongdoing. It implies that God is just and merciful, and does not mete out punishment without first providing guidance and an opportunity for people to reform themselves.
orig: ذلك أن لم يكن ربك مهلك القرى بظلم وأهلها غافلون

translation: And for all there will be degrees [of reward or punishment] for what they have done. And your Lord is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everyone will be held accountable for their actions, and that they will be rewarded or punished accordingly. It also affirms that God is fully aware of all that people do, and nothing escapes His knowledge or goes unnoticed.
orig: ولكل درجات مما عملوا وما ربك بغافل عما يعملون

translation: And your Lord is the Free of need, the Owner of Mercy. If He wills, He can do away with you and give succession after you to whomever He wills, just as He produced you from the descendants of another people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Lord, is the One who is self-sufficient and possesses infinite mercy. He has the power to replace one people with another if He so wills, just as He created the current people from the descendants of others. This serves as a reminder that Allah's will and power are supreme, and that humans should remain humble and grateful before Him.
orig: وربك الغني ذو الرحمة إن يشأ يذهبكم ويستخلف من بعدكم ما يشاء كما أنشأكم من ذرية قوم آخرين

translation: Indeed, that which you are promised is coming, and you will not cause failure [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the promises and warnings mentioned in the Quran will certainly come to pass, and that humans cannot escape or prevent the fulfillment of Allah's decrees. It serves as a reminder that we must be accountable for our actions and prepare for the Day of Judgment, as we cannot escape Allah's judgment.
orig: إن ما توعدون لآت وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: Say, "O my people, work according to your position, [for] indeed, I am working. And you are going to know to whom will come a punishment that will disgrace him and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment."
interpretation: This verse encourages people to act according to their own abilities and circumstances, and warns that the wrongdoers will ultimately face the consequences of their actions. It emphasizes that everyone will be held accountable for their deeds, and that those who oppress others will not succeed in the end.
orig: قل يا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل فسوف تعلمون من تكون له عاقبة الدار إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And they have attributed to Allah from that which He created of crops and livestock a share, and they say, "This is for Allah," by their claim, "and this is for our [pagan] partners [of Allah]." But what is for their "partners" does not reach Allah, and what is for Allah - this reaches their "partners." Evil is that which they decide.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of the polytheists who would allocate a portion of their agricultural and livestock produce to their false deities, while claiming that the remaining portion was for Allah. The verse highlights the absurdity of this practice, as the share allocated to the false deities could not reach Allah, while the share allocated to Allah would end up benefiting the false deities. This is a clear example of the flawed logic and injustice in the polytheists' beliefs and practices, which are strongly criticized in this verse.
orig: وجعلوا لله مما ذرأ من الحرث والأنعام نصيبا فقالوا هذا لله بزعمهم وهذا لشركائنا فما كان لشركائهم فلا يصل إلى الله وما كان لله فهو يصل إلى شركائهم ساء ما يحكمون

translation: And thus have We made for many of the polytheists their deeds pleasing to them. And they have obstructed [people] from the [right] way. And those who disbelieve in the Hereafter - We have prepared for them a punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights how Satan and the polytheists have made their evil deeds appear pleasing to them, leading them to commit further sins such as killing their own children. This has led them astray from the right path. However, if Allah had willed, they would not have done these things. Therefore, the believers should ignore their false claims and accusations, and focus on following the guidance of Allah.
orig: وكذلك زين لكثير من المشركين قتل أولادهم شركاؤهم ليردوهم وليلبسوا عليهم دينهم ولو شاء الله ما فعلوه فذرهم وما يفترون

translation: And they say, "These animals and crops are forbidden; no one may eat from them except whom we will" - [they claim] - and there are those [camels] whose backs are forbidden [for burden], and those [animals] upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned [at the time of slaughter] - [all of this] as an invention toward Allah. He will surely recompense them for what they had been inventing.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the pagan Arabs who had made arbitrary restrictions on certain animals and crops, claiming that these were forbidden for anyone except those they allowed. They also prohibited the use of certain animals for riding or carrying burdens, and failed to invoke the name of Allah when slaughtering animals, all of which were fabrications not sanctioned by Allah. The verse emphasizes that Allah will hold them accountable for these false claims and practices.
orig: وقالوا هذه أنعام وحرث حجر لا يطعمها إلا من نشاء بزعمهم وأنعام حرمت ظهورها وأنعام لا يذكرون اسم الله عليها افتراء عليه سيجزيهم بما كانوا يفترون

translation: And they say, "What is in the bellies of these animals is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our females. But if it is [born] dead, then they all have share therein." He will punish them for their description. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of some Arab tribes who would reserve the meat of certain animals only for the men, and forbid the women from consuming it. This was an unjust and discriminatory practice that the Quran rejects. The verse emphasizes that Allah is All-Wise and All-Knowing, and will punish those who engage in such unfair and biased treatment. The Quran promotes equality and justice, and this verse is a clear rejection of any gender-based discrimination.
orig: وقالوا ما في بطون هذه الأنعام خالصة لذكورنا ومحرم على أزواجنا وإن يكن ميتة فهم فيه شركاء سيجزيهم وصفهم إنه حكيم عليم

translation: Certainly lost are those who have killed their children in foolishness without knowledge and have forbidden what Allah has provided for them, inventing about Allah. They have gone astray and were not [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of infanticide, which was common in pre-Islamic Arabia. It highlights the grave sin of killing one's own children out of ignorance and without any justification. The verse also condemns the practice of prohibiting certain foods or resources that Allah has provided, simply based on superstition or false beliefs about Allah. The overall message is that such actions are a result of being misguided and deviating from the path of truth and righteousness.
orig: قد خسر الذين قتلوا أولادهم سفها بغير علم وحرموا ما رزقهم الله افتراء على الله قد ضلوا وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: And it is He who produces gardens, with trellises and without, and palm trees and crops of different [kinds of] food and olives and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Eat of [their] fruit when it yields and give [due] respect on the day of its harvest. And be not excessive. Indeed, He likes not those who commit excess.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's creation of a diverse array of agricultural bounties for the benefit of humanity. It encourages us to partake of these fruits and crops in moderation, expressing gratitude to God on the day of harvest, and avoiding wasteful or excessive consumption. The verse reminds us that God does not approve of those who are extravagant or indulgent, and calls us to be mindful and responsible in our use of the resources provided to us.
orig: وهو الذي أنشأ جنات معروشات وغير معروشات والنخل والزرع مختلفا أكله والزيتون والرمان متشابها وغير متشابه كلوا من ثمره إذا أثمر وآتوا حقه يوم حصاده ولا تسرفوا إنه لا يحب المسرفين

translation: And of the cattle, [He created] burden-bearers and [those fit for] slaughter. Eat of what Allah has provided for you and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to consume the sustenance provided by Allah, such as livestock, but to do so in a responsible manner and without following the temptations of Satan. It reminds that Satan is an open enemy, and that one should not heed his deceptions or be led astray by his schemes.
orig: ومن الأنعام حمولة وفرشا كلوا مما رزقكم الله ولا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: Eight mates - two of the sheep and two of the goats. Say, "Has He forbidden the two males or the two females or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the practice of the pagan Arabs who would prohibit certain types of livestock, such as male sheep or female goats, from being consumed. The verse challenges this practice by asking whether Allah has truly forbidden the consumption of certain genders or offspring of these animals. The verse encourages the people to provide evidence for their claims, if they are truthful, rather than blindly following traditions without a sound basis. The underlying message is to rely on knowledge and reason rather than blind adherence to customs, and to question practices that may not have a firm grounding in divine law.
orig: ثمانية أزواج من الضأن اثنين ومن المعز اثنين قل آلذكرين حرم أم الأنثيين أما اشتملت عليه أرحام الأنثيين نبئوني بعلم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And of camels, two [males], and of cattle, two [males]. Say, "Is it the two males He has forbidden or the two females, or [is it] that which the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge, if you are truthful." And of the camels, two [males], and of cattle, two [males] - Say, "Is it the two males He has forbidden or the two females or [is it] that which the wombs of the two females contain? Were you witnesses when Allah charged you with this? Then who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah to mislead the people by [something] other than knowledge? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse addresses the practice of certain Arab tribes during the pre-Islamic era, who would prohibit the consumption of certain livestock, such as camels and cattle, based on their gender or the contents of the female's womb. The verse challenges this practice, asking whether it was the males, the females, or the contents of the female's womb that were forbidden. The verse emphasizes that such prohibitions were not based on divine instruction, but rather on the people's own conjecture and misinformation. The verse ultimately condemns those who make false claims about God's commands in order to mislead others, stating that God does not guide the wrongdoers.
orig: ومن الإبل اثنين ومن البقر اثنين قل آلذكرين حرم أم الأنثيين أما اشتملت عليه أرحام الأنثيين أم كنتم شهداء إذ وصاكم الله بهذا فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا ليضل الناس بغير علم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Say, "I do not find within that which was revealed to me [anything] forbidden to one who would eat it unless it be a dead animal or blood spilled out or the flesh of swine - for indeed, it is impure - or it be [that slaughtered in] disobedience, dedicated to other than Allah". But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the permissible and prohibited foods in Islam. It establishes that the consumption of dead animals, blood, pork, and meat sacrificed to other than Allah is forbidden. However, if one is forced by necessity to consume such foods, without desire or transgression, then Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: قل لا أجد في ما أوحي إلي محرما على طاعم يطعمه إلا أن يكون ميتة أو دما مسفوحا أو لحم خنزير فإنه رجس أو فسقا أهل لغير الله به فمن اضطر غير باغ ولا عاد فإن ربك غفور رحيم

translation: And upon those who are Jews We have prohibited every [animal] with uncloven hoof, and of the cattle and the sheep We have prohibited to them their fat, except what adheres to their backs or the entrails or what is joined with bone. [By] that [prohibition] We repaid them for their injustice. And indeed, We are truthful.
interpretation: This verse outlines certain dietary restrictions placed upon the Jewish people as a consequence of their past transgressions. The prohibition of animals with uncloven hooves, as well as the restriction on consuming the fat of cattle and sheep, except for certain parts, is presented as a form of divine retribution for their unjust actions. The verse emphasizes that these rulings are based on truth and divine wisdom.
orig: وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا كل ذي ظفر ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عليهم شحومهما إلا ما حملت ظهورهما أو الحوايا أو ما اختلط بعظم ذلك جزيناهم ببغيهم وإنا لصادقون

translation: And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then say, "Your Lord is the Possessor of vast mercy, but His punishment cannot be repelled from the people who are criminals."
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad to remain steadfast in his message, even if his people reject it. It reminds him that Allah's mercy is vast and all-encompassing, but that the punishment of the wrongdoers cannot be averted. This serves as a warning to those who persist in their disbelief and sinful ways, while also reassuring the Prophet that Allah's support and mercy will always be with him.
orig: فإن كذبوك فقل ربكم ذو رحمة واسعة ولا يرد بأسه عن القوم المجرمين

translation: Those who associate others with Allah will say, "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated [anything] and neither would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything." Likewise did those before them deny until they tasted Our punishment. Say, "Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? You follow not except assumption, and you do not do but lie."
interpretation: This verse addresses those who associate partners with Allah, and it refutes their claims that they were compelled to do so by Allah's will. The verse emphasizes that their association of partners with Allah is a lie and that they are merely following assumptions and conjecture, rather than any genuine knowledge. The verse also draws a parallel between their claims and the denials of previous generations, who only acknowledged the truth when they faced Allah's punishment. The interpretation suggests that the verse serves to challenge the validity of the polytheists' beliefs and to call them to account for their actions.
orig: سيقول الذين أشركوا لو شاء الله ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا ولا حرمنا من شيء كذلك كذب الذين من قبلهم حتى ذاقوا بأسنا قل هل عندكم من علم فتخرجوه لنا إن تتبعون إلا الظن وإن أنتم إلا تخرصون

translation: Say, "Then, to Allah is the conclusive argument. And if He had willed, He would have guided you all."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the ultimate truth and authority belongs to Allah. Even though He could have guided all of humanity, He has given people the free will to choose between belief and disbelief. The responsibility lies with each individual to use their reason and faculties to recognize the truth of Allah's message.
orig: قل فلله الحجة البالغة فلو شاء لهداكم أجمعين

translation: Say, "Bring your witnesses who can testify that Allah has forbidden this." And if they testify, do not testify with them. And do not follow the desires of those who deny Our verses and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, while they equate [others] with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet Muhammad to challenge those who claim that Allah has forbidden certain things, and to demand that they produce witnesses to support their claim. If they do produce witnesses, the Prophet is instructed not to join them in their testimony, nor to follow the desires of those who deny the verses of the Qur'an and who do not believe in the Hereafter, but instead equate others with Allah. The interpretation suggests that the Prophet should not accept the claims of those who prohibit things without proper evidence, and should remain steadfast in his faith and the teachings of the Qur'an, even in the face of opposition from those who reject it.
orig: قل هلم شهداءكم الذين يشهدون أن الله حرم هذا فإن شهدوا فلا تشهد معهم ولا تتبع أهواء الذين كذبوا بآياتنا والذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وهم بربهم يعدلون

translation: Say, "Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you. [He commands] that you not associate anything with Him, and to parents, good treatment, and do not kill your children out of poverty; We will provide for you and them. And do not approach immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed. And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden [to be killed] except by [legal] right. This has He instructed you that you may use reason."
interpretation: This verse outlines several key moral and ethical principles that believers are commanded to uphold. The primary message is to avoid associating partners with God and to treat one's parents with kindness and respect. It also prohibits the killing of children out of poverty, as God will provide for the family. Additionally, it forbids engaging in immoral acts, whether openly or in secret, as well as unjustly taking a life. The purpose of these instructions is to encourage people to use their reason and wisdom to live righteously.
orig: قل تعالوا أتل ما حرم ربكم عليكم ألا تشركوا به شيئا وبالوالدين إحسانا ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق نحن نرزقكم وإياهم ولا تقربوا الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ذلكم وصاكم به لعلكم تعقلون

translation: And do not approach the wealth of the orphan except in the way that is best until he reaches maturity. And give full measure and weight in justice. We do not charge any soul except [with that within] its capacity. And when you speak, be just, even if [it concerns] a near relative. And the covenant of Allah fulfill. This has He instructed you that you may remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of protecting and managing the wealth of orphans in a just and responsible manner. It instructs us to approach the wealth of orphans only in the best way, until they reach adulthood. Additionally, it emphasizes the importance of fairness and honesty in all dealings, including the giving of full measure and weight. The verse also reminds us that we are only accountable for what is within our capacity, and that we should speak justly even when it concerns a close relative. Ultimately, the verse exhorts us to fulfill the covenant of Allah, as this is what He has instructed us to do, so that we may remember and be mindful of our duties.
orig: ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن حتى يبلغ أشده وأوفوا الكيل والميزان بالقسط لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها وإذا قلتم فاعدلوا ولو كان ذا قربى وبعهد الله أوفوا ذلكم وصاكم به لعلكم تذكرون

translation: And [moreover], this is My path, which is straight, so follow it; and do not follow [other] ways, for you will be separated from His way. This has He instructed you that you may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the straight path that God has prescribed, and not deviating from it by following other ways. The straight path represents the true guidance and righteous way of living, as opposed to the ways that lead to division and separation from God's path. The verse encourages adherence to God's instructions, which are meant to help people attain righteousness and God-consciousness.
orig: وأن هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل فتفرق بكم عن سبيله ذلكم وصاكم به لعلكم تتقون

translation: Then We gave Moses the Book, completing [Our favor] upon the one who did good and as a detailed explanation of all things and as guidance and mercy that perhaps in [the matter of] the meeting with their Lord they would believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Quran, which was given to Prophet Moses, is a complete and detailed guidance from God, providing instruction and mercy for those who believe in the meeting with their Lord.
orig: ثم آتينا موسى الكتاب تماما على الذي أحسن وتفصيلا لكل شيء وهدى ورحمة لعلهم بلقاء ربهم يؤمنون

translation: And this is a blessed Book which We have revealed, so follow it and fear Allah that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the Qur’an, which is a blessed book revealed by Allah. It calls upon people to adhere to the teachings and guidance of the Qur’an, and to fear and be conscious of Allah, so that they may receive His mercy and blessings.
orig: وهذا كتاب أنزلناه مبارك فاتبعوه واتقوا لعلكم ترحمون

translation: That you [people] may not say, "The Scripture was only sent down upon the two groups [i.e., the Jews and the Christians] before us, and indeed we were of their study unaware."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the people, reminding them not to claim that the revealed Scripture (the Qur`an) was only sent down to the previous religious communities (the Jews and Christians), and that they were unaware of the teachings of those scriptures. The implication is that the Qur`an has been revealed to guide all of humanity, not just the previous religious communities, and that the Muslims are responsible for studying and understanding its teachings.
orig: أن تقولوا إنما أنزل الكتاب على طائفتين من قبلنا وإن كنا عن دراستهم لغافلين

translation: Or [you could] say, "If only a Book had been revealed to us, we would have been better guided than they." Has there not come to you a clear evidence from your Lord - and guidance and mercy? And who is more unjust than one who denies the verses of Allah and turns away from them? We will recompense those who turn away from Our verses with the worst of punishment for their having turned away.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who make excuses for not following the guidance of the Qur'an, saying that if a book had been revealed to them, they would have been better guided. However, the verse points out that clear evidence, guidance and mercy have already come to them through the Qur'an, revealed by their Lord. It is a grave injustice to deny these divine signs and turn away from them. Those who do so will face the severest punishment for their rejection of Allah's guidance.
orig: أو تقولوا لو أنا أنزل علينا الكتاب لكنا أهدى منهم فقد جاءكم بينة من ربكم وهدى ورحمة فمن أظلم ممن كذب بآيات الله وصدف عنها سنجزي الذين يصدفون عن آياتنا سوء العذاب بما كانوا يصدفون

translation: Do they await only that the angels should come to them, or that your Lord should come, or that there should come some of the signs of your Lord? The Day that some of the signs of your Lord do come, no good will it do to a soul to believe in them then, if it believed not before nor earned good (by deeds of righteousness) through its Faith. Say: "Wait ye: we too are waiting."
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast in their faith, and not to wait for dramatic signs or events before believing. It emphasizes that true faith is not merely a reaction to extraordinary occurrences, but a lifelong commitment to righteousness and good deeds. The verse warns that belief at the last moment, when the signs of God become evident, will not be of any benefit to the soul. Rather, the believers are urged to continue waiting patiently, as God is also waiting to see the fruits of their faith.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا أن تأتيهم الملائكة أو يأتي ربك أو يأتي بعض آيات ربك يوم يأتي بعض آيات ربك لا ينفع نفسا إيمانها لم تكن آمنت من قبل أو كسبت في إيمانها خيرا قل انتظروا إنا منتظرون

translation: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - you, [O Muhammad], are not [associated] with them in anything. Their affair is only [left] to Allah; then He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have divided their religion into different sects and groups are not part of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) community. Their matter is ultimately with Allah, who will inform them about their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: إن الذين فرقوا دينهم وكانوا شيعا لست منهم في شيء إنما أمرهم إلى الله ثم ينبئهم بما كانوا يفعلون

translation: Whoever comes [to Allah] with a good deed will have ten times the like thereof [to his credit], and whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except [as much as] the like thereof, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of just and equitable retribution in the afterlife. It states that those who perform good deeds will be rewarded manifold, receiving ten times the reward for their virtuous actions. Conversely, those who commit evil deeds will be held accountable, but their punishment will be limited to the exact measure of their transgressions. This highlights the fairness and justice of Allah's judgment, where no one will be wronged or treated unfairly.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله عشر أمثالها ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى إلا مثلها وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Say, "Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path - a correct religion, the way of Abraham, inclining toward truth. And he was not of the polytheists."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the straight path of true religion, as exemplified by the faith of Abraham. The speaker declares that God has guided them to this righteous way, which rejects polytheism and idolatry in favor of a pure, monotheistic belief system.
orig: قل إنني هداني ربي إلى صراط مستقيم دينا قيما ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: Say, "Indeed, my prayer, my rite of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of dedicating one's entire life to the worship and service of Allah. The believer is instructed to declare that their prayer, their rituals, their way of living, and even their death are all for the sake of Allah, the Lord of all creation. This affirms the centrality of Allah in the life of a Muslim and the need to submit completely to His will.
orig: قل إن صلاتي ونسكي ومحياي ومماتي لله رب العالمين

translation: He has no partner, and with that I have been commanded, and I am the first [among you] of the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and sovereignty of God, with no partners or associates. It also indicates that the Prophet Muhammad was commanded by God to convey this message of pure monotheism, and that he was the first to submit to God and embrace Islam.
orig: لا شريك له وبذلك أمرت وأنا أول المسلمين

translation: Say, 'Shall I seek a Lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of all things?' And no soul earns [anything] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of Allah as the Lord and Creator of all things. It reminds us that each person is responsible for their own actions and will be held accountable for them. No one can bear the burden of another's sins. Ultimately, all people will return to Allah, who will judge them based on their beliefs and deeds, and clarify the matters over which they differed in this life.
orig: قل أغير الله أبغي ربا وهو رب كل شيء ولا تكسب كل نفس إلا عليها ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ثم إلى ربكم مرجعكم فينبئكم بما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And it is He who has made you successors upon the earth and has raised some of you above others in degrees [of rank] that He may try you through what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty; but indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God is the one who has made humans the successors on earth, and has elevated some above others in status and rank. This is to test them in how they use the blessings and resources that God has bestowed upon them. While God is swift in meting out punishment for misdeeds, He is also Forgiving and Merciful towards those who repent and strive to do good.
orig: وهو الذي جعلكم خلائف الأرض ورفع بعضكم فوق بعض درجات ليبلوكم في ما آتاكم إن ربك سريع العقاب وإنه لغفور رحيم

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem, Sad.
interpretation: This combination of letters at the beginning of the Surah (chapter) is known as one of the "Muqatta'at" or "Disconnected Letters" in the Quran.
