The exact meaning and significance of these letters is not entirely clear, and scholars have offered various interpretations. Some suggest they represent a divine secret or a challenge to humanity to produce something similar to the Quran. Others interpret them as a way to draw the reader's attention to the importance and miraculous nature of the Qur'anic text.
orig: المص

translation: This is a Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that you might bring mankind out of darknesses into the light by permission of their Lord - to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation sent down to the Prophet Muhammad to guide humanity towards the light of faith and righteousness. The Qur'an is not a burden, but rather a source of guidance and a reminder for the believers to follow the path of the Almighty, who is All-Powerful and Worthy of all praise.
orig: كتاب أنزل إليك فلا يكن في صدرك حرج منه لتنذر به وذكرى للمؤمنين

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord and do not follow other than Him any allies. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to follow the guidance and teachings revealed in the Quran, and not to rely on or follow other authorities or allies besides Allah. It emphasizes the importance of remembering and adhering to Allah's instructions, as people often tend to forget or neglect them.
orig: اتبعوا ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم ولا تتبعوا من دونه أولياء قليلا ما تذكرون

translation: And how many a city have We destroyed while it was committing wrong, so it is [now] fallen into ruin, and [how many] an abandoned well and [how many] a lofty palace.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of wrongdoing and injustice. It suggests that Allah (God) can swiftly and decisively punish societies that engage in oppression and corruption, causing their destruction and leaving behind only remnants of their former prosperity, such as abandoned wells and grand palaces. The verse serves as a warning to those who disregard Allah's commands and a reminder of the importance of righteousness and accountability.
orig: وكم من قرية أهلكناها فجاءها بأسنا بياتا أو هم قائلون

translation: And their plea did not cease except that they said, 'Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: When the punishment of Allah came upon the disbelievers, they had no choice but to admit their wrongdoing and acknowledge their guilt. This verse highlights the fact that even the most stubborn and arrogant people will be forced to recognize their sins when faced with the consequences of their actions.
orig: فما كان دعواهم إذ جاءهم بأسنا إلا أن قالوا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: So We will surely question those [people] to whom [a messenger] was sent, and We will surely question the messengers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will hold all people accountable for how they responded to the messengers and messages He sent to them. The people who received the messengers will be questioned about their acceptance or rejection of the divine guidance, and the messengers themselves will be questioned about how they conveyed the message and fulfilled their responsibilities.
orig: فلنسألن الذين أرسل إليهم ولنسألن المرسلين

translation: Then We will surely relate [their story] to them with [certain] knowledge, and We were not [at all] absent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge of all events, and that He will inform the people of what they did, as He was never unaware or absent from their actions. It underscores the omniscience and omnipresence of Allah, and that He will hold people accountable for their deeds on the Day of Judgment.
orig: فلنقصن عليهم بعلم وما كنا غائبين

translation: And the weighing [of deeds] that Day will be the truth. So those whose scales are heavy - it is they who will be the successful.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, the weighing of people's deeds and actions will be done with absolute fairness and justice. Those whose good deeds outweigh their bad deeds will be the successful ones, the ones who will attain salvation and eternal bliss.
orig: والوزن يومئذ الحق فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And as for him whose scales (of good deeds) are light, those are they who have lost their ownselves, in that they used to wrong Our signs.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those whose good deeds are found to be lacking on the Day of Judgment will have lost their own souls, as they had wronged the signs and teachings of Allah by not living according to them.
orig: ومن خفت موازينه فأولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم بما كانوا بآياتنا يظلمون

translation: And We have certainly established you upon the earth and made for you therein [means of] livelihood. Little are you grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has granted humans the ability to live and thrive on Earth, providing them with the means to sustain themselves. However, it laments that people often fail to express gratitude for these blessings, as they are "little" in their appreciation of Allah's favors.
orig: ولقد مكناكم في الأرض وجعلنا لكم فيها معايش قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: And We have certainly created you, [O Mankind], and given you [human] form. Then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except for Iblis. He was not of those who prostrated.
interpretation: This verse highlights the creation and exaltation of humanity. God first created mankind and gave us our distinct form. He then commanded the angels to prostrate before Adam, which they did, except for Iblis (Satan) who refused out of arrogance. This demonstrates the special status and honor bestowed upon humanity by God.
orig: ولقد خلقناكم ثم صورناكم ثم قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس لم يكن من الساجدين

translation: He [Allah] said, "What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?" [Satan] said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and pride of Satan, who refused to prostrate before Adam as commanded by Allah. Satan claimed that he was superior to Adam because he was created from fire, which he perceived as a more noble substance than the clay from which Adam was created. This arrogance and refusal to obey Allah's command led to Satan's downfall and expulsion from the heavenly abode.
orig: قال ما منعك ألا تسجد إذ أمرتك قال أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين

translation: He [Allah] said, "Then descend from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein. So get out; indeed, you are of the debased."
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the arrogant Iblis (Satan) to descend from the heavens and not to be arrogant. It emphasizes that arrogance and pride have no place in the sight of Allah, and that Iblis, by refusing to prostrate to Adam, has become one of the debased and disgraced.
orig: قال فاهبط منها فما يكون لك أن تتكبر فيها فاخرج إنك من الصاغرين

translation: He (Iblis) said, "Then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and defiance of Iblis (Satan) towards Allah. Despite being commanded to prostrate before Adam, Iblis refused, claiming that he was superior to Adam because he was created from fire while Adam was created from clay. This verse shows Iblis' attempt to delay his punishment and avoid the Day of Resurrection, when all beings will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: قال أنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: He said, 'Indeed, you are of those reprieved'
interpretation: This verse refers to the dialogue between God and Satan, where Satan is granted a respite until the Day of Judgment. The interpretation is that Satan is given a chance to continue his efforts to mislead and tempt humanity, but ultimately, he will be held accountable for his actions on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: قال إنك من المنظرين

translation: He said, "Because You have put me in the wrong, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path,"
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and defiance of Satan, who blames God for his own misguidance and vows to mislead humanity from the righteous path. It serves as a warning against the deceptive nature of evil and the importance of steadfastly following the guidance of God.
orig: قال فبما أغويتني لأقعدن لهم صراطك المستقيم

translation: Then We will surely come upon them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left, and You will not find most of them grateful [to You].
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has complete control and knowledge over His creation, as He can surround them from all sides. The implication is that people should be grateful to Allah for His blessings and guidance, but most of them are not thankful.
orig: ثم لآتينهم من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم وعن أيمانهم وعن شمائلهم ولا تجد أكثرهم شاكرين

translation: He (Allah) said: 'Get out of it, despised and expelled. Whoever of them follows you, I will surely fill Hell with you, all together.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of following Satan and rejecting the guidance of Allah. It emphasizes that those who choose to follow Satan will be condemned and punished in Hell, along with Satan himself. The verse serves as a warning to mankind to avoid the path of disobedience and instead seek the guidance of Allah.
orig: قال اخرج منها مذءوما مدحورا لمن تبعك منهم لأملأن جهنم منكم أجمعين

translation: And O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat from wherever you will but do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse instructs Adam and his wife to reside in Paradise and enjoy its bounties, but warns them against approaching a particular tree, as doing so would make them among the wrongdoers. The interpretation suggests that there are certain limits and boundaries that should not be crossed, and that obedience to God's commands is essential for attaining a blissful existence.
orig: ويا آدم اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة فكلا من حيث شئتما ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة فتكونا من الظالمين

translation: Then the Satan whispered to them to reveal to them that which was concealed from them of their private parts. And he said, "Your Lord did not forbid you this tree except that you become angels or become of the immortal."
interpretation: The Satan tempted Adam and Eve by suggesting that the forbidden tree would grant them divine powers and immortality, which was a deceptive lie to mislead them into disobeying God's command.
orig: فوسوس لهما الشيطان ليبدي لهما ما ووري عنهما من سوآتهما وقال ما نهاكما ربكما عن هذه الشجرة إلا أن تكونا ملكين أو تكونا من الخالدين

translation: And he swore to them, "Indeed, I am to you a sincere advisor."
interpretation: This verse conveys the message of sincerity and trustworthiness. The speaker is swearing to the listeners that he is truly a well-wishing advisor, someone who has their best interests at heart and is offering guidance with honesty and good intentions. It emphasizes the importance of building trust and establishing a relationship of mutual understanding and support.
orig: وقاسمهما إني لكما لمن الناصحين

translation: Then the Shaytan (Satan) whispered suggestions to them both in order to uncover that which was hidden from them of their private parts (before); and he said: "Your Lord did not forbid you this tree save you should become angels or become of the immortals." And he [Shaytan (Satan)] swore by Allah to them both (saying): "Verily, I am one of the sincere well-wishers for you both." So he misled them with deception. Then when they tasted of the tree, that which was hidden from them of their shame (private parts) became manifest to them and they began to cover themselves with the leaves of Paradise (in order to cover their shame). And their Lord called out to them (saying): "Did I not forbid you that tree and tell you: Verily, Shaytan (Satan) is an avowed enemy unto you?"
interpretation: This verse describes how Satan deceived Adam and Eve, leading them to disobey Allah's command and eat from the forbidden tree. Satan whispered to them, claiming that Allah had forbidden the tree only to prevent them from becoming angels or immortals. He swore that he was sincerely advising them, but this was a deception. When they ate from the tree, their private parts became exposed, and they began to cover themselves with leaves. Allah then called out to them, reminding them that He had forbidden them from that tree and warned them that Satan was their avowed enemy.
orig: فدلاهما بغرور فلما ذاقا الشجرة بدت لهما سوآتهما وطفقا يخصفان عليهما من ورق الجنة وناداهما ربهما ألم أنهكما عن تلكما الشجرة وأقل لكما إن الشيطان لكما عدو مبين

translation: They said, "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."
interpretation: This verse reflects the humility and repentance of those who have recognized their own shortcomings and mistakes. By acknowledging their wrongdoing and seeking forgiveness and mercy from God, they demonstrate a sincere desire to turn away from their past transgressions and become righteous. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of seeking divine forgiveness and compassion, without which one risks being among the losers in the hereafter.
orig: قالا ربنا ظلمنا أنفسنا وإن لم تغفر لنا وترحمنا لنكونن من الخاسرين

translation: He said, "Go down, with enmity between yourselves. And for you on the earth is a place of settlement and enjoyment for a time."
interpretation: This verse indicates that when Adam and Eve were asked to descend to the earth, they were to live with a sense of enmity and rivalry between themselves. However, the earth was also designated as a place of settlement and enjoyment for them, though only for a limited period of time.
orig: قال اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين

translation: He said: "Therein you will live, and therein you will die, and from it you will be brought forth."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the cyclical nature of life and death, and the ultimate return to the Creator. It suggests that our earthly existence is temporary, and that we will ultimately be resurrected and held accountable for our actions.
orig: قال فيها تحيون وفيها تموتون ومنها تخرجون

translation: O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and [as] adornment. But the clothing of righteousness - that is best. That is from the signs of Allah that perhaps they will remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of modesty and righteousness in one's attire. The clothing provided by Allah serves two purposes - to conceal one's private parts and to be a means of adornment. However, the most important aspect of clothing is the "clothing of righteousness", which is the best form of attire. This is a sign from Allah, a reminder for people to be mindful of their conduct and to prioritize spiritual purity over physical appearance.
orig: يا بني آدم قد أنزلنا عليكم لباسا يواري سوآتكم وريشا ولباس التقوى ذلك خير ذلك من آيات الله لعلهم يذكرون

translation: O children of Adam! Let not Satan deceive you, as he removed your (first) parents from the Garden, stripping them of their raiment to show them their private parts. Verily, he and Qabīluhu (his soldiers from the jinns or his tribe) see you from where you cannot see them. Verily, We have made the Shayâtîn (devils) Auliyâ' (protectors and helpers) for those who believe not.
interpretation: This verse warns the children of Adam (humanity) against the deception of Satan. It reminds us that Satan was able to tempt and mislead our first parents, Adam and Eve, causing them to be expelled from Paradise. Satan's aim is to expose our private parts and shame us. Though we may not see Satan and his followers, they can see us. The verse emphasizes that Allah has made the devils protectors and helpers for those who do not believe, highlighting the need for believers to be vigilant against Satan's schemes.
orig: يا بني آدم لا يفتننكم الشيطان كما أخرج أبويكم من الجنة ينزع عنهما لباسهما ليريهما سوآتهما إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم إنا جعلنا الشياطين أولياء للذين لا يؤمنون

translation: And when they commit an immorality, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has ordered us to do it." Say, "Indeed, Allah does not order immorality. Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?"
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of blindly following tradition and customs, even if they are immoral, by claiming that Allah has commanded them. It emphasizes that Allah does not order or approve of indecent or immoral acts, and that one should not attribute such commands to Allah without proper knowledge and justification.
orig: وإذا فعلوا فاحشة قالوا وجدنا عليها آباءنا والله أمرنا بها قل إن الله لا يأمر بالفحشاء أتقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Say, "My Lord has ordered justice, and that you direct your faces [i.e., yourselves] at every masjid, and invoke Him, sincere to Him in religion." As He originated you, you will [again] return [to Him].
interpretation: This verse commands Muslims to uphold justice and equity, to worship Allah sincerely at every place of worship, and to return to Him on the Day of Resurrection just as He created them in the first place. It emphasizes the importance of directing one's whole being towards Allah in all aspects of life, with complete devotion and sincerity.
orig: قل أمر ربي بالقسط وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد وادعوه مخلصين له الدين كما بدأكم تعودون

translation: A party [of them] He guided, and a party [of them] the misguidance had become binding upon - [for] indeed, they had taken the devils as allies instead of Allah while they thought that they were [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the division among people, where some are guided by Allah while others have misguidance bound upon them. Those who have taken the devils as allies instead of Allah, thinking that they are rightly guided, are in fact misguided. This emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance from Allah alone and not following the temptations of the devil.
orig: فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة إنهم اتخذوا الشياطين أولياء من دون الله ويحسبون أنهم مهتدون

translation: O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of worship, and eat and drink, but be not excessive. Indeed, He likes not those who commit excess.
interpretation: This verse encourages moderation and balance in one's conduct. It reminds the believers to dress appropriately and with dignity when attending places of worship, and to eat and drink in moderation, without excess or wastefulness. The verse emphasizes that Allah does not approve of those who indulge in extravagance or exceed proper limits in their behavior.
orig: يا بني آدم خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد وكلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا إنه لا يحب المسرفين

translation: Say, "Who has forbidden the adornment of [i.e., provided by] Allah which He has produced for His servants and the good [lawful] things of [His] provision?" Say, "They are for those who believe during the worldly life [but] exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection." Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the blessings and provisions granted by Allah are not to be forbidden or prohibited, but are meant to be enjoyed by the believers during their worldly life. The verse highlights that these adornments and good things of sustenance are exclusively for the believers on the Day of Resurrection, as a reward for their faith and righteous deeds in this life. The verse encourages a deeper understanding of Allah's signs and blessings, which are detailed for those who possess knowledge and wisdom.
orig: قل من حرم زينة الله التي أخرج لعباده والطيبات من الرزق قل هي للذين آمنوا في الحياة الدنيا خالصة يوم القيامة كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: Say, "My Lord has only forbidden immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed - and sin, and oppression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has not sent down authority, and that you say about Allah that which you do not know."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding immoral and sinful behaviors, both those that are openly visible and those that are hidden. It forbids associating partners with Allah without divine authority, as well as making claims about Allah without proper knowledge. The verse underscores the need to obey Allah's commands and refrain from unrighteous actions.
orig: قل إنما حرم ربي الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن والإثم والبغي بغير الحق وأن تشركوا بالله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا وأن تقولوا على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: And for every nation is a [specified] term. So when their time has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that every community or nation has a predetermined lifespan, and when their appointed time comes, they will neither be able to delay it nor hasten it. It underscores the divine decree and the certainty of the end of each nation's existence according to God's plan.
orig: ولكل أمة أجل فإذا جاء أجلهم لا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

translation: O children of Adam, if there come to you messengers from among you relating to you My verses [i.e., teachings and evidence], then whoever fears Allah and reforms - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the message of the Prophets sent by God. It reassures those who fear Allah and strive to do good that they have no need to fear or grieve, for they will be protected and provided for by God. The verse encourages people to have faith in the divine guidance and to live righteously in order to attain peace and security.
orig: يا بني آدم إما يأتينكم رسل منكم يقصون عليكم آياتي فمن اتقى وأصلح فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And those who deny Our signs and are arrogant toward them - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide in it eternally.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who reject the signs and messages of God, and who are arrogant and prideful in their rejection. It warns that such people will be consigned to the Fire of Hell, where they will remain forever. The interpretation is that arrogance and rejection of divine guidance leads to eternal punishment and separation from God.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا واستكبروا عنها أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies His verses? Those will attain their portion [i.e., share] of the [Holy] Book [i.e., the Qur'an] until when Our messengers come to them to take them in death, they [i.e., the disbelievers] will say, "Where are those you used to invoke besides Allah?" They will say, "They have departed from us," and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who fabricate lies about Allah or reject the signs and revelations of Allah. It warns that they will receive their share of punishment in the Hereafter, when the angels of death come to take their souls and they realize the futility of worshiping other than Allah. Their own actions and beliefs will testify against them, confirming that they were disbelievers.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته أولئك ينالهم نصيبهم من الكتاب حتى إذا جاءتهم رسلنا يتوفونهم قالوا أين ما كنتم تدعون من دون الله قالوا ضلوا عنا وشهدوا على أنفسهم أنهم كانوا كافرين

translation: He will say, "Enter among communities that have passed on before you from among the jinn and mankind into the Fire." Every time a [new] community enters, it will curse its sister [community] until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say about the first of them, "Our Lord, these had misled us, so give them a double punishment of the Fire."
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who have disbelieved and rejected the truth. They will be gathered together in the Hellfire, where each group will curse the other for leading them astray. The last of them will ask for a double punishment for the first, acknowledging their own culpability in following the wrong path. This highlights the importance of individual responsibility and the consequences of choosing to reject faith and guidance.
orig: قال ادخلوا في أمم قد خلت من قبلكم من الجن والإنس في النار كلما دخلت أمة لعنت أختها حتى إذا اداركوا فيها جميعا قالت أخراهم لأولاهم ربنا هؤلاء أضلونا فآتهم عذابا ضعفا من النار قال لكل ضعف ولكن لا تعلمون

translation: And the first of them will say to the last of them, "And you had over us no [actual] authority. So taste the punishment for what you used to earn."
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and blame that the wrongdoers will express towards one another on the Day of Judgment. The first group will reproach the last, acknowledging that they had no real authority or power over them, and that they are now reaping the consequences of their own misdeeds. The message is a stark reminder that each person is responsible for their own actions and will be held accountable for them.
orig: وقالت أولاهم لأخراهم فما كان لكم علينا من فضل فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكسبون

translation: Indeed, those who deny Our verses and are arrogant toward them - the gates of Heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel enters into the eye of a needle. And thus do We recompense the criminals.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject the signs and guidance of Allah with arrogance and pride will be denied entry into Paradise. The metaphor of a camel passing through the eye of a needle is used to convey the impossibility of such individuals attaining salvation, highlighting the severe consequences of their disbelief and arrogance. The verse serves as a warning to those who turn away from the truth and a reminder of the ultimate justice that will be meted out to the criminals on the Day of Judgment.
orig: إن الذين كذبوا بآياتنا واستكبروا عنها لا تفتح لهم أبواب السماء ولا يدخلون الجنة حتى يلج الجمل في سم الخياط وكذلك نجزي المجرمين

translation: For them is a bed of Hell, and over them coverings [of fire]. And thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse conveys that those who commit wrongdoing and injustice will be punished in the Hereafter. They will be subjected to the torment of Hell, which is described as a "bed" and "coverings" of fire. This punishment is a just recompense for their misdeeds in this life, as Allah promises to hold the wrongdoers accountable for their actions.
orig: لهم من جهنم مهاد ومن فوقهم غواش وكذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will not impose upon a soul except [within] its capacity. Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah does not burden a person beyond their ability. Those who believe and do good deeds will be rewarded with Paradise, where they will dwell forever. The interpretation highlights the justice and mercy of Allah, who expects only what a person can reasonably accomplish.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: And We will have removed whatever is in their breasts of [feelings of] hatred, [while] flowing beneath them are rivers. And they will say, "Praise to Allah, who has guided us to this; and we would never have been guided if Allah had not guided us. Certainly the messengers of our Lord had come with the truth." And they will be called, "This is Paradise, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the believers in the Hereafter, where they will be free from any feelings of hatred or resentment towards others. They will be in a state of contentment and gratitude, acknowledging that it was only through the guidance of Allah that they were able to attain this blissful state. The verse also emphasizes that the believers will inherit Paradise as a reward for their righteous deeds in this life.
orig: ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل تجري من تحتهم الأنهار وقالوا الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا وما كنا لنهتدي لولا أن هدانا الله لقد جاءت رسل ربنا بالحق ونودوا أن تلكم الجنة أورثتموها بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And the companions of Paradise will call to the companions of the Fire, "We have already found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?" They will say, "Yes." Then an announcer will announce among them, "The curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers,"
interpretation: This verse describes the interaction between the inhabitants of Paradise and the inhabitants of Hell on the Day of Judgment. The people of Paradise will call out to the people of Hell, confirming that what their Lord had promised them is true. The people of Hell will acknowledge that what their Lord had promised them is also true. Then, an announcer will proclaim that the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers, those who rejected faith and did evil deeds in this life.
orig: ونادى أصحاب الجنة أصحاب النار أن قد وجدنا ما وعدنا ربنا حقا فهل وجدتم ما وعد ربكم حقا قالوا نعم فأذن مؤذن بينهم أن لعنة الله على الظالمين

translation: Those who turn [others] away from the path of Allah and seek to make it [seem] deviant while they, concerning the Hereafter, are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who actively try to turn people away from the path of God and seek to make it appear crooked or distorted. It highlights that such individuals are disbelievers in the Hereafter, indicating that their actions are not only misguided but also a rejection of the true faith.
orig: الذين يصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا وهم بالآخرة كافرون

translation: And between them is a partition, and on [its] elevated places are men who recognize all by their marks. And they call to the companions of Paradise, "Peace be upon you." They have not [yet] entered it, but they long for it.
interpretation: This verse describes the separation between the dwellers of Paradise and the dwellers of Hell, with a partition or barrier in between them. On this barrier are men who can recognize the inhabitants of both sides by their distinctive features or marks. These men on the elevated places call out greetings of peace to the companions of Paradise, even though they have not yet entered Paradise themselves, but they eagerly desire to do so.
orig: وبينهما حجاب وعلى الأعراف رجال يعرفون كلا بسيماهم ونادوا أصحاب الجنة أن سلام عليكم لم يدخلوها وهم يطمعون

translation: And when they turn their eyes towards the companions of the Fire, they say: 'Our Lord! Place us not with the people who are Zalimun (polytheists and wrong-doers)'.
interpretation: This verse describes the supplication of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment when they see the punishment of the people of Hell. They will ask Allah not to be grouped with the wrongdoers and to save them from that fate. This highlights the fear of the consequences of their misdeeds and their desire to be spared from the same punishment as the unjust.
orig: وإذا صرفت أبصارهم تلقاء أصحاب النار قالوا ربنا لا تجعلنا مع القوم الظالمين

translation: And the companions of the Heights will call to men whom they will know by their marks, saying: "What did your multitude and your arrogance avail you?"
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the companions of the Heights (a place between Paradise and Hell) will call out to those who were arrogant and proud in this world. They will remind them that their wealth, power, and arrogance did not benefit them on that Day, when all that matters is one's deeds and faith.
orig: ونادى أصحاب الأعراف رجالا يعرفونهم بسيماهم قالوا ما أغنى عنكم جمعكم وما كنتم تستكبرون

translation: Are these the ones about whom you had sworn that Allah would never grant them mercy? [Enter Paradise], "No fear will there be concerning you, nor will you grieve."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who had sworn that Allah would never show mercy to the believers. The verse reassures the believers that they have no need to fear or grieve, as they will enter Paradise where they will be safe and secure.
orig: أهؤلاء الذين أقسمتم لا ينالهم الله برحمة ادخلوا الجنة لا خوف عليكم ولا أنتم تحزنون

translation: And the companions of the Fire will call to the companions of Paradise, "Pour upon us some water or from whatever [provisions] Allah has provided you." [The inhabitants of Paradise] will say, "Indeed, Allah has forbidden them both to the disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse describes the interaction between the inhabitants of Hell and the inhabitants of Paradise on the Day of Judgment. The disbelievers in Hell will plead with the believers in Paradise to share their blessings, but the believers will respond that Allah has forbidden the disbelievers from partaking in the bounties of Paradise as a punishment for their disbelief and rejection of faith.
orig: ونادى أصحاب النار أصحاب الجنة أن أفيضوا علينا من الماء أو مما رزقكم الله قالوا إن الله حرمهما على الكافرين

translation: Those who have taken their religion as distraction and amusement and whom the worldly life has deluded - this Day We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs, and for having rejected Our verses.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who treat their religion as a mere pastime or entertainment, and who have been deluded by the allure of the worldly life. On the Day of Judgment, they will be forgotten by God just as they had forgotten the reality of that Day and rejected the signs and messages of God.
orig: الذين اتخذوا دينهم لهوا ولعبا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا فاليوم ننساهم كما نسوا لقاء يومهم هذا وما كانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: And We have certainly brought them a Book which We have explained in detail - a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Quran is a revealed scripture from God, which has been clearly explained and presented as a guide and source of mercy for those who have faith and believe in its teachings.
orig: ولقد جئناهم بكتاب فصلناه على علم هدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Do they await except its [final] explanation? The Day its explanation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, "The messengers of our Lord had come with the truth, so are there [now] any intercessors to intercede for us or could we be sent back to do other than we used to do?" They will have lost themselves, and lost from them is what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who deny the truth and refuse to believe in the Qur'an and the Day of Judgment. It suggests that they will be left without any excuse on the Day when the true meaning and consequences of their actions are revealed. They will then realize their error and seek help, but it will be too late. The verse emphasizes the importance of believing in the Qur'an and acting upon its teachings in this life, as the consequences of denying the truth will be severe in the Hereafter.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا تأويله يوم يأتي تأويله يقول الذين نسوه من قبل قد جاءت رسل ربنا بالحق فهل لنا من شفعاء فيشفعوا لنا أو نرد فنعمل غير الذي كنا نعمل قد خسروا أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He covers the night with the day, [another night] chasing it rapidly; and [He created] the sun, the moon, and the stars, subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command; blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It highlights that Allah alone has the authority to command and control all of creation, from the heavens and the earth to the celestial bodies like the sun, moon, and stars. The verse also affirms Allah's continuous oversight and regulation of the natural cycles, such as the alternation of day and night. The concluding statement "blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds" is a declaration of Allah's supreme status and the blessings that flow from His dominion over all creation.
orig: إن ربكم الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش يغشي الليل النهار يطلبه حثيثا والشمس والقمر والنجوم مسخرات بأمره ألا له الخلق والأمر تبارك الله رب العالمين

translation: Call upon your Lord in humility and privately. Indeed, He does not like transgressors.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to call upon God with humility and in private, without arrogance or ostentation. It emphasizes that God does not love those who transgress or exceed the proper bounds in their behavior and actions.
orig: ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية إنه لا يحب المعتدين

translation: And do not cause corruption upon the earth after its reformation. And invoke Him in fear and aspiration. Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to avoid causing corruption or disruption in the world after it has been set in order. Instead, it calls upon them to worship and invoke Allah with a combination of fear and hope, as Allah's mercy is close to those who do good deeds.
orig: ولا تفسدوا في الأرض بعد إصلاحها وادعوه خوفا وطمعا إن رحمت الله قريب من المحسنين

translation: And it is He who sends the winds as bearers of good tidings before His mercy, and We send down from the sky pure water. That We may bring to life thereby a dead land and give it as drink to those We created of numerous livestock and men. And We have certainly distributed it among them that they might be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and mercy in sending the winds as a precursor to the rain that brings life to the dead land. The rain revives the land and provides sustenance for all of God's creations, from livestock to humans. This serves as a reminder of God's ability to bring the dead back to life on the Day of Resurrection, just as He brings life to the barren land through the rain.
orig: وهو الذي يرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته حتى إذا أقلت سحابا ثقالا سقناه لبلد ميت فأنزلنا به الماء فأخرجنا به من كل الثمرات كذلك نخرج الموتى لعلكم تذكرون

translation: And the good land - its vegetation emerges by permission of its Lord. But that which is bad - nothing emerges from it except with difficulty. Thus do We diversify the signs for a people who are grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between a fertile, productive land and a barren, unproductive one. The fertile land, described as "the good land", is able to produce vegetation abundantly by the permission and will of God. In contrast, the "bad" land can only produce vegetation with great difficulty. This analogy is used to illustrate how God's signs and blessings are diversified for those who are grateful and willing to appreciate them.
orig: والبلد الطيب يخرج نباته بإذن ربه والذي خبث لا يخرج إلا نكدا كذلك نصرف الآيات لقوم يشكرون

translation: We had certainly sent Noah to his people, and he said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the message of monotheism and the importance of worshipping only Allah. It highlights the role of the prophet Noah in calling his people to this belief, warning them of the severe punishment that awaits those who reject it. The interpretation underscores the urgency and gravity of the message, as the Day of Judgment is described as "a tremendous Day" which should motivate people to heed the call to worship the one true God.
orig: لقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فقال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: The eminent among his people said, "Indeed, we see you in clear error."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and dismissive attitude of the elite members of the community towards the Prophet's message. They viewed his teachings as a clear deviation from the accepted norms and beliefs, refusing to acknowledge the truth he brought. This verse serves as a reminder that those in positions of power and influence often resist change and new ideas, even when they are divinely inspired.
orig: قال الملأ من قومه إنا لنراك في ضلال مبين

translation: He said, 'O my people, I am not astray, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse conveys the message that the prophet is not misguided, but rather he is a messenger sent by the Lord of all creation. This emphasizes the divine origin of the prophet's message and his authority to guide the people.
orig: قال يا قوم ليس بي ضلالة ولكني رسول من رب العالمين

translation: I convey to you the messages of my Lord and advise you, and I know from Allah what you do not know.
interpretation: This verse expresses the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger of Allah, conveying the divine revelations and providing guidance to the people. It highlights the prophet's unique position of receiving knowledge directly from Allah, which surpasses the knowledge of the common people. The verse emphasizes the importance of accepting and following the prophet's teachings, as they are based on the divine wisdom that he has been entrusted with.
orig: أبلغكم رسالات ربي وأنصح لكم وأعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Are you astonished that there has come to you a reminder from your Lord through a man from among you, that he may warn you and that you may fear Allah and perhaps you will receive mercy?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the message of the Qur'an has come through a human messenger, which should not be a source of astonishment for the people. The purpose of this reminder is to warn the people and encourage them to be mindful of Allah, so that they may receive His mercy.
orig: أوعجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل منكم لينذركم ولتتقوا ولعلكم ترحمون

translation: But they denied him, so We saved him and those who were with him in the ship and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people blind [to the truth].
interpretation: This verse describes the story of Prophet Noah and the flood. The people of Noah rejected his message and warnings, so God saved Noah and his followers who believed, and drowned those who rejected the signs and guidance of God. This serves as a lesson that those who stubbornly deny the truth will face the consequences of their actions, while those who have faith and follow the righteous path will be saved.
orig: فكذبوه فأنجيناه والذين معه في الفلك وأغرقنا الذين كذبوا بآياتنا إنهم كانوا قوما عمين

translation: And to 'Aad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear [Him]?'
interpretation: This verse calls the people of 'Aad to worship Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him. The message emphasizes the oneness of God and the importance of fearing and obeying Him. The verse encourages the people to reflect on the fact that they have no deity worthy of worship other than Allah, and to consequently abandon any false deities or idols they may have been worshipping.
orig: وإلى عاد أخاهم هودا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره أفلا تتقون

translation: The eminent among the people who disbelieved from his [i.e., Noah's] people said, "Indeed, we see you in foolishness, and indeed, we think you are of the liars."
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and disbelief of the elite members of Noah's people, who dismissed him as a foolish liar for calling them to believe in God. Their rejection of Noah's message stemmed from their pride and unwillingness to submit to the truth, highlighting the human tendency to dismiss prophetic guidance when it challenges one's worldview and privileges.
orig: قال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه إنا لنراك في سفاهة وإنا لنظنك من الكاذبين

translation: He said, 'O my people, I am not a fool, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the Worlds.'
interpretation: This verse expresses the Prophet's response to his people who accused him of being a fool or madman for his message. He affirms that he is not a fool, but rather a messenger sent by the Lord of all creation, emphasizing the divine origin and authority of his message.
orig: قال يا قوم ليس بي سفاهة ولكني رسول من رب العالمين

translation: I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I am to you a trustworthy advisor.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger of God, conveying the divine revelations to humanity. It also highlights his sincerity and trustworthiness in delivering this message, as he is a "trustworthy advisor" to his people.
orig: أبلغكم رسالات ربي وأنا لكم ناصح أمين

translation: Are you amazed that there has come to you a reminder from your Lord through a man from among you, to warn you and that you may remember, and [that you may] recall when He made you successors after the people of Noah and increased you in stature? So remember the favors of Allah that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon them. It reminds them that the Qur'an and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) have been sent as a reminder from Allah to guide them towards success and prosperity. The verse also reminds the people that they have been made successors on the earth after the people of Prophet Noah, and that Allah has increased them in stature and abilities. Therefore, the people are urged to remember and be grateful for these blessings, so that they may attain success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: أوعجبتم أن جاءكم ذكر من ربكم على رجل منكم لينذركم واذكروا إذ جعلكم خلفاء من بعد قوم نوح وزادكم في الخلق بسطة فاذكروا آلاء الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: They said, "Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful."
interpretation: This verse represents the response of the disbelievers to the call of the Prophet to worship only Allah and abandon the worship of their forefathers` idols. They challenged the Prophet to bring the punishment he had warned them about if he was truthful in his message.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لنعبد الله وحده ونذر ما كان يعبد آباؤنا فأتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, 'Certainly, a scourge and wrath from your Lord have fallen upon you. Do you dispute with me about [mere] names which you and your fathers have made up? Allah has not sent down any authority for them. Then wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait.'
interpretation: This verse conveys a stern warning from God to those who engage in futile disputes over names and attributes that have no divine sanction. The message is that when God's punishment and displeasure descend, there is no room for such arguments. Instead, the proper response is to wait patiently and submit to God's will, for He is with those who do so.
orig: قال قد وقع عليكم من ربكم رجس وغضب أتجادلونني في أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما نزل الله بها من سلطان فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: And We saved him and those with him by a mercy from Us. And We cut off the roots of those who denied Our signs, and they were not believers.
interpretation: This verse describes how God saved Prophet Noah and his followers from the flood, while destroying those who rejected his message and refused to believe in God's signs. It emphasizes God's mercy towards the believers and His punishment of the disbelievers, highlighting the consequences of faith and disbelief.
orig: فأنجيناه والذين معه برحمة منا وقطعنا دابر الذين كذبوا بآياتنا وما كانوا مؤمنين

translation: And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you a clear proof from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah [sent] to you as a sign. So leave her to eat within the land of Allah and do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse calls upon the people of Thamud to worship only Allah, the one true God, and to heed the clear signs and guidance that have come to them through the prophet Salih. It emphasizes the miraculous she-camel as a sign from Allah, and commands the people not to harm it, lest they incur a painful punishment. The interpretation is that one must submit to the will of Allah and heed the guidance of His messengers, for to do otherwise will lead to severe consequences.
orig: وإلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره قد جاءتكم بينة من ربكم هذه ناقة الله لكم آية فذروها تأكل في أرض الله ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب أليم

translation: And remember when He made you successors after the people of 'Aad and settled you in the land, [and] you take for yourselves palaces from its plains and carve from the mountains, homes. So remember the favors of Allah and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.
interpretation: This verse reminds the people to be grateful to Allah for the blessings He has bestowed upon them. He has made them the successors of the previous nations, and has provided them with the means to build prosperous lives for themselves. However, the verse also cautions them against misusing these blessings and engaging in corruption and abuse on the earth. The call to remember the favors of Allah is a reminder to be thankful and to use the resources provided in a responsible and righteous manner.
orig: واذكروا إذ جعلكم خلفاء من بعد عاد وبوأكم في الأرض تتخذون من سهولها قصورا وتنحتون الجبال بيوتا فاذكروا آلاء الله ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: Said the eminent ones who had scorned among his people to those who were oppressed - to [any of] those who had believed among them, "Do you [actually] know that Salih is sent from his Lord?" They said, "Indeed we, in that with which he has been sent, are believers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the division between the leaders of the people of Thamud and the believers among them. The arrogant leaders questioned whether the people truly believed that Salih was a messenger sent by God, while the believers affirmed their faith in the message he brought. This reflects the common dynamic where the powerful and influential are often resistant to accepting the truth, while the oppressed and marginalized are more receptive to it.
orig: قال الملأ الذين استكبروا من قومه للذين استضعفوا لمن آمن منهم أتعلمون أن صالحا مرسل من ربه قالوا إنا بما أرسل به مؤمنون

translation: Those who were arrogant said: "Indeed, we are disbelievers in that which you believe."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and rejection of faith by those who refuse to accept the truth of the message of Islam. Their dismissive attitude towards the believers reflects their own pride and unwillingness to humble themselves before the divine guidance.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا إنا بالذي آمنتم به كافرون

translation: Then they hamstrung her and turned arrogant toward the command of their Lord and said, 'O Salih, bring us what you promise us, if you are of the messengers.'
interpretation: This verse describes the rejection and defiance of the people of Thamud towards the prophet Salih and his message. They deliberately disobeyed God's command not to harm the she-camel that Salih had brought as a sign, and demanded that he bring them the punishment he had warned them about if they did not believe. This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the guidance of God's messengers.
orig: فعقروا الناقة وعتوا عن أمر ربهم وقالوا يا صالح ائتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من المرسلين

translation: And the earthquake seized them, and they became motionless corpses in their homes.
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment that befell a people who rejected the message of their prophet. The "earthquake" represents a divine judgment that struck them, causing them to perish in their own homes. The interpretation suggests that those who stubbornly refuse to heed the guidance of God's messengers will face severe consequences in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: So he turned away from them and said, 'O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not love advisors.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection and dismissal that the prophets often faced when delivering the message of God to their people. The prophet, in this case, had faithfully conveyed the divine message and provided sincere counsel, but the people refused to heed the advice, as they did not appreciate those who sought to guide them. This serves as a reminder that the role of the prophet is to deliver the truth, even if it is not readily accepted by the people.
orig: فتولى عنهم وقال يا قوم لقد أبلغتكم رسالة ربي ونصحت لكم ولكن لا تحبون الناصحين

translation: And [We had sent] Lot when he said to his people, 'Do you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds?'
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of homosexuality and other forms of sexual immorality, which were prevalent among the people of Lot. The verse emphasizes that this behavior was unprecedented and unheard of among the nations of the world at that time, highlighting its deviant and unnatural nature.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه أتأتون الفاحشة ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين

translation: Indeed, you approach men with desire, instead of women. Rather, you are a transgressing people.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of homosexuality, which is considered a grave sin in Islam. The interpretation suggests that engaging in sexual relations with men instead of women is a form of excess and transgression against the natural order established by God.
orig: إنكم لتأتون الرجال شهوة من دون النساء بل أنتم قوم مسرفون

translation: And the only response of his people was that they said, "Expel them from your city. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."
interpretation: This verse refers to the response of the people to the Prophet's message. They rejected the Prophet and his followers, and demanded that they be expelled from the city, simply because the believers were striving to purify themselves and their faith. The verse highlights the closed-mindedness and intolerance of the rejecters, who could not accept those who sought to improve themselves spiritually.
orig: وما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا أخرجوهم من قريتكم إنهم أناس يتطهرون

translation: So We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was of those who remained [with the disbelievers].
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Lot (peace be upon him), who was saved from the destruction of his people along with his family, except for his wife who remained with the disbelievers and was destroyed with them. The interpretation is that even close family ties cannot save one from the consequences of disbelief and disobedience to God.
orig: فأنجيناه وأهله إلا امرأته كانت من الغابرين

translation: And We rained upon them a [torrential] rain, and see how was the end of the criminals.
interpretation: This verse is a reference to the destruction of the people of Lut (Lot) who were punished by Allah for their grave sins and moral depravity. The verse emphasizes the ultimate fate of those who persist in wrongdoing, highlighting the consequences they face. It serves as a warning to heed the message of the Qur'an and avoid the path of the criminals, lest one suffer a similar fate.
orig: وأمطرنا عليهم مطرا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المجرمين

translation: And to Madyan, We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. So fulfill the measure and weight and do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption."
interpretation: This verse calls upon the people of Madyan to worship only Allah, the one true God, and to fulfill their duties and obligations towards others in a just and fair manner. It emphasizes the importance of honesty, integrity, and avoiding corruption and abuse in all aspects of life. The interpretation is that one should worship Allah alone, be just and fair in their dealings with others, and refrain from engaging in any activities that harm society or the environment.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره قد جاءتكم بينة من ربكم فأوفوا الكيل والميزان ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تفسدوا في الأرض بعد إصلاحها ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And do not sit on every path, threatening and preventing from the way of Allah those who believe in Him, and seeking to make it [seem] crooked. And remember when you were few and He increased you. And see how was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse warns against obstructing the path of those who believe in Allah and seek to turn them away from the straight path. It reminds the believers that they were once few in number but Allah increased them, and it calls upon them to reflect on the fate of those who sought to corrupt and mislead others. The overall message is to remain steadfast in faith, not be deterred by those who seek to hinder the believers, and to trust in Allah's plan and support.
orig: ولا تقعدوا بكل صراط توعدون وتصدون عن سبيل الله من آمن به وتبغونها عوجا واذكروا إذ كنتم قليلا فكثركم وانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المفسدين

translation: And if a party of you have believed in that with which I was sent and a party have not believed, then be patient until Allah judges between us; and He is the best of judges.
interpretation: This verse encourages patience and steadfastness in the face of division and disbelief. It reminds the believers that Allah will ultimately judge between them and the disbelievers, and that He is the best of judges. The verse calls for the believers to remain patient and trust in Allah's justice, rather than taking matters into their own hands.
orig: وإن كان طائفة منكم آمنوا بالذي أرسلت به وطائفة لم يؤمنوا فاصبروا حتى يحكم الله بيننا وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: The eminent ones who were arrogant from among his people said, "We will surely evict you, O Shu'ayb, and those who have believed with you from our town, or you must return to our religion." [Shu'ayb] said, "Even if we were unwilling?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between the arrogant leaders of the people and the Prophet Shu'ayb, who had called them to worship only Allah and abandon their corrupt practices. The arrogant leaders threatened to expel Shu'ayb and his followers from their town if they did not return to their religion. However, Shu'ayb's response, "Even if we were unwilling?", demonstrates his firm resolve and unwavering faith in the truth he was preaching, despite the threats and intimidation from the powerful elite.
orig: قال الملأ الذين استكبروا من قومه لنخرجنك يا شعيب والذين آمنوا معك من قريتنا أو لتعودن في ملتنا قال أولو كنا كارهين

translation: We have indeed invented a lie against Allah, if we return to your religion after Allah has delivered us from it. And it is not for us to return to it except that Allah, our Lord, should will. Our Lord comprehends all things in knowledge. Upon Allah we have relied. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of those who give decision.
interpretation: This verse expresses a strong commitment to the truth of the Islamic faith and a rejection of any return to previous religious beliefs. It emphasizes that the decision to follow Islam is not one to be taken lightly, and that any reversal would be a grave betrayal of Allah. The verse also conveys a deep trust in Allah's knowledge and power, and a plea for His guidance and judgment in resolving conflicts with those who oppose the faith.
orig: قد افترينا على الله كذبا إن عدنا في ملتكم بعد إذ نجانا الله منها وما يكون لنا أن نعود فيها إلا أن يشاء الله ربنا وسع ربنا كل شيء علما على الله توكلنا ربنا افتح بيننا وبين قومنا بالحق وأنت خير الفاتحين

translation: And the eminent among his people who disbelieved said, "If you should follow Shu'ayb, then indeed, you would be losers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disbelief of the leaders of the people towards the message of Prophet Shu'ayb. They dismissed the call to believe in God and follow His guidance, perceiving it as a path to loss and ruin. This reflects the tendency of those in power to resist change and maintain the status quo, even when it goes against the truth.
orig: وقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه لئن اتبعتم شعيبا إنكم إذا لخاسرون

translation: Then the earthquake seized them, and they became within their home [corpses] fallen prone.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of a people who rejected the message of the Prophet. The earthquake that struck them was a divine punishment for their disbelief and disobedience. The verse emphasizes that they were destroyed in their own homes, highlighting the severity and suddenness of their demise. This serves as a warning to those who turn away from the guidance of God and His messengers.
orig: فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: Those who denied Shu'aib, it was as if they had never dwelt there. Those who denied Shu'aib - they were the losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of those who rejected the message of the prophet Shu'aib. It suggests that their denial of Shu'aib was so complete that it was as if they had never even lived in that land. They were the ultimate losers, having rejected the guidance that could have saved them.
orig: الذين كذبوا شعيبا كأن لم يغنوا فيها الذين كذبوا شعيبا كانوا هم الخاسرين

translation: So he turned away from them and said, "O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, so how [can] I grieve for a disbelieving people?"
interpretation: The verse expresses the frustration and sorrow of the prophet upon seeing the rejection of his people towards the message of God. Despite his sincere efforts to guide them, they chose to disbelieve, and the prophet is left with no choice but to turn away from them. The verse highlights the importance of delivering the divine message, even in the face of rejection, and the prophet's duty to convey the truth without being burdened by the consequences of people's choices.
orig: فتولى عنهم وقال يا قوم لقد أبلغتكم رسالات ربي ونصحت لكم فكيف آسى على قوم كافرين

translation: And We did not send into any city a prophet [who was rejected] except that We seized its people with poverty and hardship that they might humble themselves [to Us].
interpretation: This verse suggests that when a prophet is sent to a community, the people are often tested with hardship and adversity, so that they may turn to Allah in humility and submission. The purpose of these trials is to guide the people towards repentance and a closer relationship with their Creator.
orig: وما أرسلنا في قرية من نبي إلا أخذنا أهلها بالبأساء والضراء لعلهم يضرعون

translation: Then We substituted in place of the evil, good, until they became abundant and said, 'Hardship and ease have touched our fathers.' So We seized them suddenly while they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God may replace evil with good for people who repent and do righteous deeds, until they become prosperous. However, if they then become arrogant and forget the blessings they received, God may suddenly punish them without warning, as they were unaware of their wrongdoing.
orig: ثم بدلنا مكان السيئة الحسنة حتى عفوا وقالوا قد مس آباءنا الضراء والسراء فأخذناهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And if only the people of the cities had believed and feared Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth; but they denied [the messengers], so We seized them for what they were earning.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if the people had believed in God and followed His commands, they would have been granted abundant blessings from the heavens and the earth. However, they rejected the message of the prophets, and as a result, they were punished for their misdeeds. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and righteousness, and how they can lead to divine favor and prosperity.
orig: ولو أن أهل القرى آمنوا واتقوا لفتحنا عليهم بركات من السماء والأرض ولكن كذبوا فأخذناهم بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Then, do the people of the cities feel secure from Our punishment coming to them at night while they are asleep?
interpretation: This verse suggests that people should not feel secure from the punishment of Allah, as it can come upon them unexpectedly, even while they are sleeping. It serves as a warning to be vigilant and prepared, as the consequences of one's actions can manifest at any time.
orig: أفأمن أهل القرى أن يأتيهم بأسنا بياتا وهم نائمون

translation: Or do the people of the cities feel secure from Our punishment coming to them in the morning while they are at play?
interpretation: This verse questions whether the people of the cities feel safe from Allah's punishment coming to them unexpectedly while they are engaged in frivolous activities. It serves as a warning that one should not become complacent and neglect their religious duties, as the consequences of such behavior can be severe.
orig: أوأمن أهل القرى أن يأتيهم بأسنا ضحى وهم يلعبون

translation: Then do they feel secure from the plan of Allah? But no one feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people.
interpretation: This verse warns that no one can feel safe from the consequences of their misdeeds or the punishment of Allah. Only those who have lost their way and are destined for failure would feel secure from Allah's plan and judgment.
orig: أفأمنوا مكر الله فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون

translation: Has it not been shown to those who inherit the earth after its (previous) possessors, that if We will, We can afflict them for their sins, and seal up their hearts so that they cannot hear?
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who inherit the earth after its previous inhabitants should be aware that if Allah wills, He can punish them for their sins and make their hearts impervious to guidance, so that they do not listen and heed the message. It serves as a warning to the inheritors of the earth to be righteous and not to repeat the mistakes of the previous generations.
orig: أولم يهد للذين يرثون الأرض من بعد أهلها أن لو نشاء أصبناهم بذنوبهم ونطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يسمعون

translation: These are the towns whose news We relate to you. And certainly their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe in that which they had denied before. Thus does Allah seal over the hearts of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights how even when clear signs and messengers are sent to the disbelievers, they still refuse to believe due to their hardened hearts and rejection of the truth. It emphasizes that Allah seals the hearts of those who persistently disbelieve, making it difficult for them to accept the guidance.
orig: تلك القرى نقص عليك من أنبائها ولقد جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذبوا من قبل كذلك يطبع الله على قلوب الكافرين

translation: And We found not among them any firm commitment. And indeed, We found most of them to be defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the people being referred to lacked commitment and were mostly disobedient to the commandments of God. The interpretation suggests that the people were lacking in their adherence to their covenants and obligations, and were inclined towards sinful behavior.
orig: وما وجدنا لأكثرهم من عهد وإن وجدنا أكثرهم لفاسقين

translation: Then We sent after them Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, but they were unjust toward them. So see how was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: After the previous generations, We sent Moses with Our clear signs and miracles to Pharaoh and his people. But they were unjust and rejected the signs, leading to their ultimate downfall. This serves as a lesson and a warning to those who engage in corruption and oppression - their end will be equally disastrous.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعدهم موسى بآياتنا إلى فرعون وملئه فظلموا بها فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المفسدين

translation: And Moses said, "O Pharaoh, indeed I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse highlights the authority and divine mission of the Prophet Moses. He addresses the powerful Pharaoh, asserting that he is a messenger sent by the Lord of all the worlds, emphasizing the divine origin and legitimacy of his message. This establishes Moses' role as a prophet with a higher purpose beyond the earthly realm, challenging the arrogance and false claims of Pharaoh's divinity.
orig: وقال موسى يا فرعون إني رسول من رب العالمين

translation: It is truly right that I should not say about Allah except the truth. I have come to you with clear evidence from your Lord, so send with me the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of speaking the truth about Allah and not making false claims. The Prophet is affirming that he has come with clear proof and evidence from Allah, and he calls upon the Israelites to accompany him in following the guidance revealed by their Lord.
orig: حقيق على أن لا أقول على الله إلا الحق قد جئتكم ببينة من ربكم فأرسل معي بني إسرائيل

translation: He (Pharaoh) said, 'If you have come with a sign, then bring it forth if you are of the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse is a challenge from Pharaoh to Prophet Moses, demanding that he provide a miraculous sign as proof of his truthfulness and divine mission. It reflects Pharaoh's arrogance and unwillingness to accept the message of monotheism brought by Moses, unless it is accompanied by a clear supernatural demonstration of God's power.
orig: قال إن كنت جئت بآية فأت بها إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: And he threw down his staff, and suddenly it was a serpent, manifest [in its nature].
interpretation: This verse refers to the miracle of Prophet Moses, where he threw down his staff and it transformed into a clear and visible serpent. This miracle was a sign of God's power and a demonstration of Moses' prophethood to Pharaoh and his people, as it defied the natural laws and showed the divine intervention in Moses' mission.
orig: فألقى عصاه فإذا هي ثعبان مبين

translation: And he drew out his hand; and behold, it was white [with radiance] for the observers.
interpretation: This verse describes the miracle of Prophet Moses, when he drew out his hand from his garment and it shone with a brilliant white light. This was a sign of God's power and a demonstration of Moses' prophethood to the Pharaoh and his people. The radiant white hand was a testament to the divine nature of Moses' mission and the truth of his message.
orig: ونزع يده فإذا هي بيضاء للناظرين

translation: The eminent among the people of Pharaoh said, "Indeed, this is a learned magician."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and dismissive attitude of Pharaoh's elite towards Prophet Moses, whom they perceived as a skilled magician rather than a true messenger of God. Their refusal to acknowledge the divine nature of Moses' miracles and message reflects their unwillingness to submit to the truth, blinded by their own pride and worldly power.
orig: قال الملأ من قوم فرعون إن هذا لساحر عليم

translation: He wants to drive you out of your land, so what do you order?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the believers, who are being threatened with expulsion from their land by their enemies. The interpretation is that the believers should stand firm, unite, and decide on a course of action to defend their land and rights against those who seek to drive them out. The verse encourages the believers to take a decisive and unified stance in the face of this threat.
orig: يريد أن يخرجكم من أرضكم فماذا تأمرون

translation: They said, "Keep him and his brother and send among the cities recruiters,"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the request made by Pharaoh and his people to keep Prophet Moses and his brother Aaron, and to send recruiters to the cities to gather people against them. This suggests a powerful opposition against the message of Prophet Moses, and the desire to suppress it through force and coercion.
orig: قالوا أرجه وأخاه وأرسل في المدائن حاشرين

translation: They bring to you every skilled enchanter.
interpretation: This verse refers to the efforts of the disbelievers to challenge the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by bringing forth their most skilled magicians and enchanters to compete with the miracles of the Qur'an. However, the Qur'an is a divine revelation that cannot be matched by human endeavors, no matter how skilled the practitioners may be.
orig: يأتوك بكل ساحر عليم

translation: And the magicians came to Pharaoh; they said, "Indeed, for us is a reward if we are the predominant."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and self-confidence of the magicians who came to challenge Moses before Pharaoh. They believed that they would emerge victorious and demanded a reward for their triumph, indicating their desire for worldly gains and recognition rather than a sincere search for the truth.
orig: وجاء السحرة فرعون قالوا إن لنا لأجرا إن كنا نحن الغالبين

translation: He (Allah) said: 'Yes, and you are indeed among those brought near (to Me)'.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who are close to Allah, the Almighty, will be granted the honor and privilege of being in His presence. It suggests that through righteous deeds, devotion, and submission to Allah, one can attain a close relationship with the Divine, which is a source of great blessing and distinction.
orig: قال نعم وإنكم لمن المقربين

translation: They said, "O Moses, either you throw [your staff], or we will be the ones to throw [first]."
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between Moses and Pharaoh's magicians. The magicians challenged Moses to either throw his staff first or they would throw theirs, confident in their own abilities. This reflects the arrogance and defiance of Pharaoh's followers, who sought to undermine Moses' divine message and authority.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إما أن تلقي وإما أن نكون نحن الملقين

translation: He (Musa) said, "Throw (your staffs)." And when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and struck terror into them, and they presented a great [feat of] magic.
interpretation: This verse describes the confrontation between Prophet Musa (Moses) and the sorcerers of Pharaoh. When Musa commanded the sorcerers to throw down their staffs, they displayed an impressive feat of magic that bewildered the people and instilled fear in them. This verse highlights the power of the sorcerers' magic, which Musa would later overcome through the miracle of his staff turning into a serpent and swallowing the sorcerers' illusions.
orig: قال ألقوا فلما ألقوا سحروا أعين الناس واسترهبوهم وجاءوا بسحر عظيم

translation: And We inspired to Moses, "Throw down your staff," and at once it swallowed up what they were falsifying.
interpretation: This verse refers to the miracle performed by Prophet Moses when he threw down his staff, which then transformed into a serpent and swallowed up the illusions and deceptions of the magicians of Pharaoh. This signifies the power of truth over falsehood, and the ability of divine guidance to overcome the machinations of those who seek to mislead and deceive.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى أن ألق عصاك فإذا هي تلقف ما يأفكون

translation: And the truth has come, and falsehood has departed. Indeed, falsehood is [by nature] everbound to depart.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the truth has prevailed and the falsehood that people were involved in has been abolished. It signifies that the truth is eternal and will always triumph over falsehood, which is inherently bound to disappear.
orig: فوقع الحق وبطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they were overcome there and became debased.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that those who opposed the truth and the righteous were defeated and humiliated. It suggests that arrogance, pride, and opposition to the divine will ultimately lead to downfall and humiliation.
orig: فغلبوا هنالك وانقلبوا صاغرين

translation: And the magicians fell down in prostration
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the Egyptian magicians when they witnessed the miracle performed by Prophet Moses. They recognized the superiority of Moses' power and the truth of his message, and they prostrated themselves before God in submission and acknowledgment of their faith.
orig: وألقي السحرة ساجدين

translation: They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse expresses the response of the believers who have accepted and submitted to the one true God, the Lord of all creation. It signifies their faith and trust in the Almighty, acknowledging Him as the sole Sovereign and deserving of worship.
orig: قالوا آمنا برب العالمين

translation: The Lord of Moses and Aaron
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah as the Lord and Sustainer of the Prophets Moses and Aaron. It emphasizes that Allah is the supreme authority and the source of guidance for these two great Prophets, who were sent to guide their people.
orig: رب موسى وهارون

translation: Pharaoh said, "Have you believed in him before I give you permission? Indeed, this is a conspiracy which you have conspired in the city to expel its people from it, but you are going to know."
interpretation: This verse highlights Pharaoh's arrogance and refusal to accept the message of Prophet Moses. Pharaoh accuses the people of conspiring against him and his authority, and threatens them with consequences if they do not obey his commands. The interpretation suggests that Pharaoh was unwilling to acknowledge the truth and instead resorted to oppression and intimidation to maintain his power.
orig: قال فرعون آمنتم به قبل أن آذن لكم إن هذا لمكر مكرتموه في المدينة لتخرجوا منها أهلها فسوف تعلمون

translation: I will surely cut off your hands and your feet from opposite sides, then I will surely crucify you all.
interpretation: This verse conveys a stern warning and threat of severe punishment for those who defy the commands of God and engage in wrongdoing. The imagery of cutting off hands and feet and crucifixion represents the gravity of the consequences faced by those who persist in their transgressions. It serves as a deterrent against disobedience and a call to adhere to the righteous path.
orig: لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ثم لأصلبنكم أجمعين

translation: They say, "Indeed, we are to our Lord returning."
interpretation: This verse expresses the belief that all people will ultimately return to God on the Day of Judgment, where they will be held accountable for their actions in this life. It emphasizes the transient nature of this world and the importance of preparing for the afterlife by living a righteous life.
orig: قالوا إنا إلى ربنا منقلبون

translation: And they resent us only because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. [Our Lord], pour upon us patience and let us die as Muslims [in submission to You].
interpretation: This verse expresses the believers' response to those who resent them for their faith in God and His signs.
