The believers humbly ask God to grant them patience and to take them in a state of submission to Him (as Muslims). This highlights the believers' reliance on God and their desire to remain steadfast in their faith, despite the opposition they face.
orig: وما تنقم منا إلا أن آمنا بآيات ربنا لما جاءتنا ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين

translation: And the eminent among the people of Pharaoh said, "Will you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption in the land and abandon you and your gods?" [Pharaoh] said, "We will kill their sons and keep their women alive; and indeed, we are subjugators over them."
interpretation: This verse depicts the dialogue between Pharaoh and his elite advisors regarding their plan to suppress the growing influence of Prophet Moses and his people. The advisors suggest that Pharaoh should eliminate Moses and his followers to prevent them from causing disruption and abandoning the worship of Pharaoh's gods. Pharaoh's response reveals his tyrannical and oppressive intentions, as he proposes a strategy of killing the male children and enslaving the women of the Israelites, asserting his absolute power over them.
orig: وقال الملأ من قوم فرعون أتذر موسى وقومه ليفسدوا في الأرض ويذرك وآلهتك قال سنقتل أبناءهم ونستحيي نساءهم وإنا فوقهم قاهرون

translation: Moses said to his people, "Seek help through Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah. He causes to inherit it whom He wills of His servants. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous."
interpretation: This verse encourages the people to seek Allah's help and be patient, as the earth and its resources belong to Allah alone. He decides who will inherit the land, and the ultimate success is for those who are righteous and fear Allah.
orig: قال موسى لقومه استعينوا بالله واصبروا إن الأرض لله يورثها من يشاء من عباده والعاقبة للمتقين

translation: They said, "We were harmed before you came to us and after you have come to us." [Moses] said, "Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and grant you succession in the land so He may see how you will do."
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and doubt that the Israelites had towards Moses, even after he had been sent to them by God. They complained that they had been harmed both before and after Moses had come to them, implying that they did not believe his message or trust in God's plan. In response, Moses reassures them that God may destroy their enemies and grant them succession in the land, so that they can prove themselves worthy by their actions. This verse emphasizes the importance of faith, trust, and obedience to God's commands, even in the face of adversity or doubt.
orig: قالوا أوذينا من قبل أن تأتينا ومن بعد ما جئتنا قال عسى ربكم أن يهلك عدوكم ويستخلفكم في الأرض فينظر كيف تعملون

translation: And We had certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine and a deficiency in fruits that perhaps they might remember.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah punished the people of Pharaoh with years of drought and famine, as well as a reduction in the yield of their crops, in order to make them reflect on their wrongdoings and turn back to Allah. The purpose was to remind them of their dependence on Allah and the consequences of their arrogance and rejection of the truth.
orig: ولقد أخذنا آل فرعون بالسنين ونقص من الثمرات لعلهم يذكرون

translation: And when good comes to them, they say, "This is ours." And if a bad [condition] afflicts them, they see an evil omen in Moses and those with him. Unquestionably, their fortune is [determined] with Allah , but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickle and inconsistent nature of the disbelievers' attitude towards the Prophet Moses and his followers. When they experience good fortune, they attribute it to their own merits, but when faced with hardship, they superstitiously blame it on Moses and his companions. The verse emphasizes that their fate is ultimately in the hands of Allah, though most of them are unaware of this fact.
orig: فإذا جاءتهم الحسنة قالوا لنا هذه وإن تصبهم سيئة يطيروا بموسى ومن معه ألا إنما طائرهم عند الله ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And they said, "Whatever signs you may bring to us to bewitch us with them - we will not be believers [in] you."
interpretation: This verse reflects the stubborn rejection of the disbelievers, who refuse to accept the truth of the Qur'anic revelations despite the clear signs and miracles presented to them. Their unwillingness to believe stems from their arrogance and preconceived notions, rather than an objective consideration of the evidence. This highlights the importance of an open and sincere heart in accepting the guidance of the Qur'an.
orig: وقالوا مهما تأتنا به من آية لتسحرنا بها فما نحن لك بمؤمنين

translation: And We sent upon them the flood and the locusts and the lice and the frogs and the blood - [as] signs [i.e., warnings], detailed and manifest; but they were arrogant and were a criminal people.
interpretation: This verse describes the various plagues that were sent upon the people of Pharaoh as a warning and a sign, but they remained arrogant and did not heed the message. The interpretation is that those who are arrogant and reject the signs of God will face severe consequences.
orig: فأرسلنا عليهم الطوفان والجراد والقمل والضفادع والدم آيات مفصلات فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما مجرمين

translation: And when the punishment descended upon them, they said, 'O Moses, invoke for us your Lord by what He has promised you. If you [can] remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe you, and we will send with you the Children of Israel.'
interpretation: This verse describes the people's response when they were afflicted with a punishment from God. They pleaded with Moses to pray to God to remove the punishment, and in return they promised to believe in Moses and allow the Israelites to leave with him. This demonstrates the people's tendency to make promises to God in times of distress, but their faith often wanes once the hardship is lifted.
orig: ولما وقع عليهم الرجز قالوا يا موسى ادع لنا ربك بما عهد عندك لئن كشفت عنا الرجز لنؤمنن لك ولنرسلن معك بني إسرائيل

translation: And when We removed the punishment from them until a term which they should reach, behold, they broke [their word].
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to break their promises and commitments, even after being granted respite or relief from a difficult situation. It suggests that individuals may take their blessings for granted and revert to their previous ways, rather than fulfilling their obligations.
orig: فلما كشفنا عنهم الرجز إلى أجل هم بالغوه إذا هم ينكثون

translation: So We took retribution from them and drowned them in the sea because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.
interpretation: This verse conveys that those who reject the divine signs and remain heedless of them will face the consequences of their actions. The punishment of drowning in the sea serves as a reminder that those who turn away from the truth will not be spared from Allah's justice.
orig: فانتقمنا منهم فأغرقناهم في اليم بأنهم كذبوا بآياتنا وكانوا عنها غافلين

translation: And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed. And the fair promise of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their endurance. And We destroyed [all] that Pharaoh and his people were producing and [all] that they had been building.
interpretation: This verse highlights how God granted the Israelites dominion over the blessed lands after they had been oppressed, as a reward for their patience and endurance. It also describes how God destroyed the power and structures that Pharaoh and his people had built, emphasizing God's ultimate power and justice.
orig: وأورثنا القوم الذين كانوا يستضعفون مشارق الأرض ومغاربها التي باركنا فيها وتمت كلمت ربك الحسنى على بني إسرائيل بما صبروا ودمرنا ما كان يصنع فرعون وقومه وما كانوا يعرشون

translation: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came upon a people intent upon [worshipping] their idols. They [the Children of Israel] said, "O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods." [Moses] said, "Indeed, you are a people who are ignorant."
interpretation: This verse describes the Israelites' demand for idols after being saved from Pharaoh, despite witnessing the power of the one true God. Moses' response highlights their ignorance and lack of understanding, as they were rejecting the guidance they had received in favor of false deities. The verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith and rejecting the temptation to revert to idolatry, even in the face of social pressure.
orig: وجاوزنا ببني إسرائيل البحر فأتوا على قوم يعكفون على أصنام لهم قالوا يا موسى اجعل لنا إلها كما لهم آلهة قال إنكم قوم تجهلون

translation: Indeed, these [disbelievers] are in loss, and their deeds are void.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith and engage in misdeeds are doomed to failure and that their actions are futile and without merit. It serves as a warning to those who stray from the path of righteousness and encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and righteous conduct.
orig: إن هؤلاء متبر ما هم فيه وباطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Say, "Is it other than Allah I should desire as a lord while He has favored you over the worlds?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness and supremacy of Allah as the only true Lord and deity worthy of worship. It challenges the notion of seeking any other god or lord besides Allah, who has bestowed His favors and blessings upon all of creation. The verse affirms Allah's absolute sovereignty and the futility of turning to any other source of guidance or power.
orig: قال أغير الله أبغيكم إلها وهو فضلكم على العالمين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst torment - killing your [newborn] sons and keeping your women alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.
interpretation: This verse recounts the miraculous deliverance of the Israelites from the oppression of Pharaoh, who subjected them to severe persecution, killing their sons and sparing their women. This was a great trial from Allah, testing the faith and patience of the Israelites, but ultimately leading to their liberation and the downfall of their oppressors.
orig: وإذ أنجيناكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب يقتلون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them by [the addition of] ten; so the term of his Lord was completed as forty nights. And Moses said to his brother Aaron, "Replace me among my people and do right [by them] and do not follow the way of the corrupters."
interpretation: This verse describes the time when God appointed Moses for a meeting with Him, which lasted for a total of forty nights. During this time, Moses left his brother Aaron in charge of the Israelites, instructing him to guide the people and not follow the ways of those who seek to corrupt. The verse highlights the importance of righteous leadership and the need to avoid the path of those who seek to do harm.
orig: وواعدنا موسى ثلاثين ليلة وأتممناها بعشر فتم ميقات ربه أربعين ليلة وقال موسى لأخيه هارون اخلفني في قومي وأصلح ولا تتبع سبيل المفسدين

translation: And when Moses arrived at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, "My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You." [Allah] said, "You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it should remain in its place, then you will see Me." But when his Lord appeared to the mountain, He rendered it level, and Moses fell unconscious. And when he awoke, he said, "Exalted are You! I have repented to You, and I am the first [among my people] of the believers."
interpretation: This verse describes the profound encounter between Moses and God. When Moses requested to see God directly, he was told that this was not possible, as the human eye cannot withstand the full splendor of the divine. Instead, Moses was instructed to look at the mountain, which would serve as a metaphor for God's power and majesty. When God's presence was manifested, the mountain was reduced to rubble, and Moses was overwhelmed, falling unconscious. Upon regaining consciousness, Moses expressed his awe and reverence for God, declaring his repentance and affirming his faith as the first among his people to believe.
orig: ولما جاء موسى لميقاتنا وكلمه ربه قال رب أرني أنظر إليك قال لن تراني ولكن انظر إلى الجبل فإن استقر مكانه فسوف تراني فلما تجلى ربه للجبل جعله دكا وخر موسى صعقا فلما أفاق قال سبحانك تبت إليك وأنا أول المؤمنين

translation: He said, "O Moses, I have chosen you over the people with My messages and My words. So take what I have given you and be among the grateful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God has chosen Moses to convey His messages and words to the people. It is a declaration of Moses' elevated status and the responsibility bestowed upon him. The verse encourages Moses to accept what God has granted him and to be grateful for this honor and privilege.
orig: قال يا موسى إني اصطفيتك على الناس برسالاتي وبكلامي فخذ ما آتيتك وكن من الشاكرين

translation: And We had written for him within the Tablets the instruction of all things and detailed explanation for all things, [so] "Take them with determination and order your people to take the best of it. I will show you the home of the defiantly disobedient."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the completeness and detail of the guidance provided in the Tablets given to Moses. It instructs him to firmly adhere to this guidance and to encourage his people to follow the best of it. The verse also warns that the home of the defiantly disobedient will be shown, indicating the consequences of not following the divine guidance.
orig: وكتبنا له في الألواح من كل شيء موعظة وتفصيلا لكل شيء فخذها بقوة وأمر قومك يأخذوا بأحسنها سأريكم دار الفاسقين

translation: I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right. And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it. And if they see the way of consciousness, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way. That is because they have denied Our signs and they were heedless of them.
interpretation: This verse conveys that Allah will turn away those who are arrogant and reject the truth, even in the face of clear signs and guidance. Their arrogance and disbelief in Allah's signs will lead them to choose the path of error over the path of righteousness. This is because they have denied Allah's revelations and been heedless of them.
orig: سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق وإن يروا كل آية لا يؤمنوا بها وإن يروا سبيل الرشد لا يتخذوه سبيلا وإن يروا سبيل الغي يتخذوه سبيلا ذلك بأنهم كذبوا بآياتنا وكانوا عنها غافلين

translation: And those who deny Our verses and the meeting of the Hereafter - their deeds have become worthless. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject the signs and messages of Allah, and deny the reality of the Hereafter, will have their deeds rendered worthless. They will be judged and held accountable only for their own actions, and will receive the consequences of what they have done in this life.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا ولقاء الآخرة حبطت أعمالهم هل يجزون إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And the people of Moses made, after [his departure], from their ornaments a calf - a [lifeless] body that had a lowing sound. Did they not see that it could neither speak to them nor guide them to a way? They took it [for worship], and they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse describes how the Israelites, in the absence of Moses, turned to worshiping a golden calf that they had fashioned from their ornaments. Despite the calf being a lifeless object that could neither speak nor guide them, they still took it as an object of worship, demonstrating their wrongdoing and deviation from the true teachings of Moses. This highlights the human tendency to be easily misled and to fall into idolatry, even in the face of clear signs of the futility of such practices.
orig: واتخذ قوم موسى من بعده من حليهم عجلا جسدا له خوار ألم يروا أنه لا يكلمهم ولا يهديهم سبيلا اتخذوه وكانوا ظالمين

translation: And when it fell into their hands [i.e., the idols] and they saw that they were unable to attain any [power of] speech, they said, "If our Lord had not guided us, we would have been among the misled."
interpretation: This verse highlights the realization by the idolaters that their idols are powerless and unable to speak or help them. They acknowledge that it is only through the guidance of Allah that they have been saved from being among the misguided. This serves as a lesson that true guidance and salvation can only come from Allah, and not from false deities or idols.
orig: ولما سقط في أيديهم ورأوا أنهم قد ضلوا قالوا لئن لم يرحمنا ربنا ويغفر لنا لنكونن من الخاسرين

translation: And when Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, he said, "How wretched is that by which you have replaced me after [my departure]. Were you impatient over the matter of your Lord?" And he threw down the tablets and seized his brother by [the hair of] his head, pulling him toward him. [Aaron] said, "O son of my mother, indeed the people oppressed me and were about to kill me, so let not the enemies rejoice over me and do not place me with the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse describes Moses' reaction upon returning to his people and finding them worshipping a golden calf in his absence. His anger and grief are palpable, as he confronts them for their haste in abandoning the commands of God. The verse highlights the tension between Moses and his brother Aaron, who had been left in charge but was unable to prevent the people from their transgressions. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith, even in the face of adversity, and the need to avoid succumbing to the temptations of the world.
orig: ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا قال بئسما خلفتموني من بعدي أعجلتم أمر ربكم وألقى الألواح وأخذ برأس أخيه يجره إليه قال ابن أم إن القوم استضعفوني وكادوا يقتلونني فلا تشمت بي الأعداء ولا تجعلني مع القوم الظالمين

translation: He said, "My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy, for You are the most merciful of the merciful."
interpretation: This verse expresses the supplication of the Prophet Moses, asking his Lord to forgive him and his brother Aaron, and to admit them into the divine mercy. It highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and relying on the boundless mercy of Allah, the Most Merciful, as the ultimate source of salvation and grace.
orig: قال رب اغفر لي ولأخي وأدخلنا في رحمتك وأنت أرحم الراحمين

translation: Indeed, those who took the calf [for worship] will receive anger from their Lord and humiliation in the worldly life.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who worshipped the golden calf instead of Allah. It indicates that they will face the wrath of Allah and be humiliated in this life as a consequence of their idolatry. The verse emphasizes that Allah will punish those who fabricate lies and associate partners with Him.
orig: إن الذين اتخذوا العجل سينالهم غضب من ربهم وذلة في الحياة الدنيا وكذلك نجزي المفترين

translation: And those who commit misdeeds and then repent after that and believe - indeed, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of God towards those who have committed sins but then repent and believe. It conveys the message that no matter how grave the sins, if one sincerely turns back to God and believes, they will be forgiven and granted God's mercy.
orig: والذين عملوا السيئات ثم تابوا من بعدها وآمنوا إن ربك من بعدها لغفور رحيم

translation: And when the anger subsided in Moses, he took up the Tablets; and in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who are in awe of their Lord.
interpretation: This verse indicates that after Moses' anger subsided, he took up the Tablets which contained divine guidance and mercy for those who fear and revere Allah. The Tablets served as a source of direction and compassion for the believers who humbly submit to the will of their Lord.
orig: ولما سكت عن موسى الغضب أخذ الألواح وفي نسختها هدى ورحمة للذين هم لربهم يرهبون

translation: And Moses chose seventy men of his people for Our appointed time; and when the earthquake seized them, he said, 'My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me [as well]. Would You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? This is not but Your trial by which You send astray whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of forgivers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights Moses` plea to Allah after a group of seventy men he had chosen to accompany him were seized by an earthquake. Moses acknowledges that Allah could have destroyed them all, but asks for forgiveness, recognizing that the foolish actions of some should not lead to the punishment of all. He affirms Allah`s sovereignty in guiding and misguiding whomever He wills, and seeks His protection, forgiveness and mercy - for Allah is the best of forgivers.
orig: واختار موسى قومه سبعين رجلا لميقاتنا فلما أخذتهم الرجفة قال رب لو شئت أهلكتهم من قبل وإياي أتهلكنا بما فعل السفهاء منا إن هي إلا فتنتك تضل بها من تشاء وتهدي من تشاء أنت ولينا فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الغافرين

translation: And write for us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is good]; indeed, we have turned back to You." [Allah] said, "My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will, but My mercy encompasses all things." So I will decree it [especially] for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses -
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking both worldly and spiritual blessings from Allah. It highlights that those who turn to Allah with sincerity and faith will be granted His mercy and forgiveness, while His punishment is reserved for those who disobey Him. The verse also stresses the virtues of fearing Allah, giving charity, and believing in the signs of Allah.
orig: واكتب لنا في هذه الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة إنا هدنا إليك قال عذابي أصيب به من أشاء ورحمتي وسعت كل شيء فسأكتبها للذين يتقون ويؤتون الزكاة والذين هم بآياتنا يؤمنون

translation: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written about in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil and relieves them of their burden and the shackles which were upon them. So they who have believed in him, honored him, supported him and followed the light which was sent down with him - it is those who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse describes the followers of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as those who believe in him, support him, and follow the divine guidance he brought. It highlights that the Prophet was foretold in the previous scriptures, the Torah and the Gospel, and that he came to guide people towards what is right and away from what is wrong. The verse also emphasizes that the Prophet's teachings brought relief and liberation from the burdens and shackles that had previously weighed upon the people. Ultimately, it is those who embrace this message and follow the light revealed through the Prophet who will attain true success.
orig: الذين يتبعون الرسول النبي الأمي الذي يجدونه مكتوبا عندهم في التوراة والإنجيل يأمرهم بالمعروف وينهاهم عن المنكر ويحل لهم الطيبات ويحرم عليهم الخبائث ويضع عنهم إصرهم والأغلال التي كانت عليهم فالذين آمنوا به وعزروه ونصروه واتبعوا النور الذي أنزل معه أولئك هم المفلحون

translation: Say, "O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all, [from Him] to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death." So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered prophet, who believes in Allah and His words, and follow him that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse is a call to all of humanity to believe in the oneness of God and to follow the Prophet Muhammad, who is the final messenger of God. It emphasizes that God is the sole sovereign of the heavens and the earth, and that He alone has the power to give life and cause death. The verse then urges people to believe in God and His Messenger, the unlettered prophet, who believes in God and His words, and to follow him in order to be guided towards the right path.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس إني رسول الله إليكم جميعا الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض لا إله إلا هو يحيي ويميت فآمنوا بالله ورسوله النبي الأمي الذي يؤمن بالله وكلماته واتبعوه لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And among the people of Moses is a community [of followers] who guide by truth and by it act with justice.
interpretation: This verse highlights that among the followers of Prophet Moses, there was a righteous community that guided people based on the truth revealed to them, and they acted justly according to the divine guidance. This emphasizes the importance of adhering to the truth and implementing it in a just manner in one's personal and societal conduct.
orig: ومن قوم موسى أمة يهدون بالحق وبه يعدلون

translation: And We divided them into twelve descendant tribes [as distinct] nations. And We inspired to Moses when his people asked him for water, "Strike with your staff the stone," and [from it] there gushed forth twelve springs. Every people knew its watering place. And We shaded them with clouds and sent down upon them manna and quails, [saying], "Eat from the good things with which We have provided you." And they wronged Us not, but they were [themselves] doing wrong.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah divided the Israelites into twelve tribes and provided for them in the wilderness, including by making water gush forth from a rock when Moses struck it, and sending down manna and quails for them to eat. The interpretation is that Allah cares for and provides sustenance to His people, even when they are in difficult circumstances, but they must remain grateful and faithful to Him.
orig: وقطعناهم اثنتي عشرة أسباطا أمما وأوحينا إلى موسى إذ استسقاه قومه أن اضرب بعصاك الحجر فانبجست منه اثنتا عشرة عينا قد علم كل أناس مشربهم وظللنا عليهم الغمام وأنزلنا عليهم المن والسلوى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم وما ظلمونا ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And when it was said to them, "Dwell in this city and eat from it wherever you will and say, `Relieve [us of] our burdens,` and enter the gate bowing humbly; [then] We will forgive your sins for you, and We will increase the doers of good [in reward]."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Children of Israel, instructing them to settle in a city and eat freely from it, while also humbly asking for forgiveness of their sins. The verse emphasizes the importance of humility, obedience, and doing good deeds, which will be rewarded by God with the forgiveness of sins and an increase in the reward for the righteous.
orig: وإذ قيل لهم اسكنوا هذه القرية وكلوا منها حيث شئتم وقولوا حطة وادخلوا الباب سجدا نغفر لكم خطيئاتكم سنزيد المحسنين

translation: So We substituted in place of the ones who wronged, another people; and the heaven above them was not allowed to rain, and the earth was not allowed to grow [anything].
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah punished those who wronged and rejected the message by replacing them with another people, and by withholding rain and sustenance from them as a consequence of their wrongdoing.
orig: فبدل الذين ظلموا منهم قولا غير الذي قيل لهم فأرسلنا عليهم رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يظلمون

translation: And ask them about the town that was by the sea - when they transgressed in [the matter of] the Sabbath - when their fish came to them openly on the Sabbath day, and the day they had no Sabbath they did not come to them. Thus did We give trial to the people, for they were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse refers to a town that was located by the sea, where the people would transgress the sanctity of the Sabbath. On the Sabbath, the fish would come to them openly, but on the days when they did not observe the Sabbath, the fish would not come. This was a test from God to see if the people would obey His commands, but they were defiantly disobedient.
orig: واسألهم عن القرية التي كانت حاضرة البحر إذ يعدون في السبت إذ تأتيهم حيتانهم يوم سبتهم شرعا ويوم لا يسبتون لا تأتيهم كذلك نبلوهم بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And when a group among them said, "Why do you advise [or warn] a people whom Allah is [about] to destroy or to punish with a severe punishment?" [The righteous among them] said, "To be absolved before your Lord and perhaps they may fear [Him]."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of advising and warning people, even if their fate seems sealed. The righteous believers recognized that their role was to convey the message and counsel, not to judge the outcome. They sought to fulfill their duty to Allah, in the hope that the people may still turn to Him and be saved from punishment.
orig: وإذ قالت أمة منهم لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا قالوا معذرة إلى ربكم ولعلهم يتقون

translation: But when they forgot that with which they had been reminded, We saved those who had prevented evil, and We seized those who had wronged, with a wretched punishment, because they were defiantly disobeying.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of forgetting the guidance and reminders provided by God. When people neglect the teachings they have received, those who had been promoting good and preventing evil are saved, while those who had wronged others are seized with a severe punishment due to their defiant disobedience.
orig: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به أنجينا الذين ينهون عن السوء وأخذنا الذين ظلموا بعذاب بئيس بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: But when they insolently persisted in what they had been forbidden, We said to them: "Be you apes, despised and rejected."
interpretation: This verse describes how some people stubbornly continued to disobey God's commands, despite being warned. As a result, God punished them by transforming them into apes, a state of humiliation and disgrace.
orig: فلما عتوا عن ما نهوا عنه قلنا لهم كونوا قردة خاسئين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord will say to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to send upon the people of Sodom a punishment from the sky." Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine punishment that will befall the people of Sodom on the Day of Resurrection for their transgressions and immorality. It emphasizes that Allah is swift in His retribution, yet also Forgiving and Merciful towards those who repent and seek His forgiveness. The verse serves as a warning to humanity to abstain from sinful and unrighteous deeds, while also conveying the message of Allah's compassion towards those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: وإذ تأذن ربك ليبعثن عليهم إلى يوم القيامة من يسومهم سوء العذاب إن ربك لسريع العقاب وإنه لغفور رحيم

translation: And We have divided them throughout the earth as [various] communities - among them are the righteous, and among them are other than that. And We have tried them with good [times] and bad that perhaps they would return [to obedience].
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah has divided humanity into different communities, some of which are righteous and others are not. The purpose of this division is to test people with both good and bad circumstances, so that they may turn back to Allah in repentance and obedience.
orig: وقطعناهم في الأرض أمما منهم الصالحون ومنهم دون ذلك وبلوناهم بالحسنات والسيئات لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And there followed them successors who inherited the Scripture [while] taking the commodities of this lower life and saying, "It will be forgiven for us." And if an offer like it comes to them, they will [again] take it. Was the covenant of the Scripture not taken upon them that they would not say about Allah except the truth, and they studied what was in it? And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, so will you not use reason?
interpretation: This verse describes a group of people who have inherited the divine scripture, but instead of studying it and living by its teachings, they are more concerned with pursuing the fleeting pleasures and commodities of this worldly life. They believe that they will be forgiven for their transgressions, and they are quick to seize any opportunity for personal gain, even if it means compromising their principles. The verse emphasizes that the covenant of the scripture requires them to speak the truth about Allah and to reflect deeply on its teachings. It also highlights that the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, encouraging the readers to use their reason and understand the true purpose of life.
orig: فخلف من بعدهم خلف ورثوا الكتاب يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى ويقولون سيغفر لنا وإن يأتهم عرض مثله يأخذوه ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق ودرسوا ما فيه والدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون

translation: And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer - indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of the reformers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastly adhering to the teachings of the Quran and maintaining a consistent prayer life. It conveys the promise that those who strive to reform themselves and society will not have their efforts go unrewarded by God. The verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and good deeds, as God will ensure that their righteous work is not in vain.
orig: والذين يمسكون بالكتاب وأقاموا الصلاة إنا لا نضيع أجر المصلحين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We raised the mountain over them as if it was a dark cloud and they were certain that it would fall upon them, [and We said], "Hold firmly to what We have given you and remember what is in it that you might fear Allah."
interpretation: This verse describes a pivotal moment in the story of the Israelites, when God raised the mountain over them as a warning to accept the commandments He was about to give them. The imagery of the mountain looming overhead like a dark cloud conveys the gravity of the situation and the Israelites" fear that the mountain would fall on them. The interpretation is that God requires unwavering adherence to His teachings, and remembrance of His commands, in order to achieve righteousness and God-consciousness.
orig: وإذ نتقنا الجبل فوقهم كأنه ظلة وظنوا أنه واقع بهم خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واذكروا ما فيه لعلكم تتقون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord took from the children of Adam - from their loins - their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying to them], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] - lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware."
interpretation: This verse refers to the primordial covenant (al-mithaq) between God and humanity, in which God extracted from the loins of Adam all of his descendants and made them testify that He is their Lord. This covenant establishes the fundamental relationship between God and man, and serves as a basis for human accountability on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes that no one can claim ignorance of this covenant, as all of humanity bore witness to it.
orig: وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم وأشهدهم على أنفسهم ألست بربكم قالوا بلى شهدنا أن تقولوا يوم القيامة إنا كنا عن هذا غافلين

translation: Or [you say], "Our forefathers were associate-worshippers before, and we are [merely their] descendants after them. Then would You destroy us for what the falsifiers have done?"
interpretation: This verse addresses the argument that people sometimes make to justify their own idolatry or polytheism - that they are simply following the practices of their ancestors. The Qur'an rejects this excuse, indicating that people are responsible for their own actions and beliefs, not those of their forefathers. The verse suggests that people should not assume they will be saved from punishment simply by virtue of being the descendants of those who worshipped false gods.
orig: أو تقولوا إنما أشرك آباؤنا من قبل وكنا ذرية من بعدهم أفتهلكنا بما فعل المبطلون

translation: And thus do We detail the verses, and [that] perhaps they will return [to faith].
interpretation: This verse suggests that God presents His signs and messages in a clear and detailed manner, in the hope that people will reflect on them and return to the path of righteousness.
orig: وكذلك نفصل الآيات ولعلهم يرجعون

translation: And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave [knowledge of] Our signs, but he detached himself from them; so Satan pursued him, and he became of the deviators.
interpretation: This verse speaks of a person who was given divine signs and guidance, but he turned away from them and followed the temptations of Satan, becoming one of the misguided. The interpretation is that we should heed the guidance of Allah and not be swayed by the deceptions of Satan, lest we too become among the deviators.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها فأتبعه الشيطان فكان من الغاوين

translation: And if We had willed, We could have elevated him by means of the signs, but he adhered [to disbelief] to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, [he still] pants. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories that perhaps they will give thought.
interpretation: This verse presents a parable about a person who rejects the signs and guidance of God, and instead follows his own desires and inclinations. The verse compares such a person to a dog, which pants and is distracted regardless of whether it is chased or left alone. The interpretation is that those who deny God's signs and messages are like this, and their example is meant to encourage people to reflect and consider the truth, rather than blindly following their own whims and desires.
orig: ولو شئنا لرفعناه بها ولكنه أخلد إلى الأرض واتبع هواه فمثله كمثل الكلب إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث ذلك مثل القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فاقصص القصص لعلهم يتفكرون

translation: Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs and themselves they were wronging.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who reject the signs and messages of God, and in doing so, they wrong and harm themselves. The verse suggests that those who deny the truth of God's revelations are making a grave mistake that will ultimately lead to their own downfall.
orig: ساء مثلا القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا وأنفسهم كانوا يظلمون

translation: Whoever Allah guides - he is the [rightly] guided. And whoever He sends astray - it is those who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that guidance is solely in the hands of Allah. Those whom Allah guides will find the right path, while those whom He leaves to stray will be the ultimate losers. It highlights the importance of seeking Allah's guidance and submitting to His will, as He alone has the power to guide or misguide.
orig: من يهد الله فهو المهتدي ومن يضلل فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. It is they who are the heedless.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that many people, both from among the jinn and humans, have been destined for Hell due to their spiritual blindness and deafness. They possess the faculties of understanding, sight, and hearing, but they fail to use them to perceive and comprehend the truth. They are likened to cattle, or even more astray, because they are heedless and indifferent to the guidance and signs that have been provided to them. The interpretation suggests that the ultimate responsibility for one's spiritual state lies within the individual, and that those who neglect to use their God-given faculties to seek the truth will be held accountable.
orig: ولقد ذرأنا لجهنم كثيرا من الجن والإنس لهم قلوب لا يفقهون بها ولهم أعين لا يبصرون بها ولهم آذان لا يسمعون بها أولئك كالأنعام بل هم أضل أولئك هم الغافلون

translation: And to Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them. And leave [the company of] those who practice deviation concerning His names. They will be recompensed for what they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of invoking Allah by His beautiful and perfect names, and avoiding those who deviate from the proper understanding and use of these names. The interpretation is that we should seek to know and call upon Allah using the names that describe His perfect attributes, and avoid the company of those who misuse or distort the understanding of Allah's names.
orig: ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه سيجزون ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And among those We created is a community which guides by truth and thereby acts justly.
interpretation: This verse highlights that among the people created by God, there is a community that follows the truth and acts righteously. It suggests that there are those who strive to guide others towards the path of truth and justice, and who themselves adhere to the principles of fairness and equity in their conduct.
orig: وممن خلقنا أمة يهدون بالحق وبه يعدلون

translation: And those who deny Our signs - We will progressively lead them [to destruction] from where they do not know.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who reject the signs and messages of Allah will be gradually led to their downfall, even though they may not be aware of it. It suggests that Allah has a plan to guide people towards the truth, and those who choose to reject it will ultimately face the consequences of their actions, even if they do not realize it at the time.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون

translation: And I will give them respite. Indeed, My plan is firm.
interpretation: This verse expresses Allah's power and control over all affairs. It suggests that even though the disbelievers may plot against the believers, Allah's plan is unshakable and He will grant the disbelievers a period of respite before delivering His judgment. The interpretation highlights Allah's sovereignty and the futility of any schemes against His will.
orig: وأملي لهم إن كيدي متين

translation: Have they not considered that there is no madness in their companion [i.e., the Prophet]? He is but a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the Prophet Muhammad's message, which is one of clear guidance and warning, rather than considering him to be insane or possessed. It emphasizes that he is a messenger sent by God to guide humanity, not someone who is mentally unstable or delusional.
orig: أولم يتفكروا ما بصاحبهم من جنة إن هو إلا نذير مبين

translation: Have they not contemplated the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what Allah has created of [all] things and that perhaps their appointed time has come near? So in what statement hereafter will they believe?
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the wonders of the heavens and the earth, and the creation of all things by Allah. It suggests that the appointed time for people to meet their Lord may be near, and questions what other message they would believe in if they do not believe in the signs of Allah’s power and the imminence of the Hereafter.
orig: أولم ينظروا في ملكوت السماوات والأرض وما خلق الله من شيء وأن عسى أن يكون قد اقترب أجلهم فبأي حديث بعده يؤمنون

translation: Whomever Allah sends astray - for him there is no guide. And He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are led astray by Allah have no one to guide them back to the right path. They are left to wander in their own state of arrogance and misguidance, unable to see the truth.
orig: من يضلل الله فلا هادي له ويذرهم في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival? Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal its time except Him. It lays heavily upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come upon you except unexpectedly." They ask you as if you are familiar with it. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most of the people do not know."
interpretation: This verse addresses the human tendency to seek knowledge about the timing of the Day of Resurrection, known as the "Hour" in Islamic theology. The Qur'an emphasizes that the exact timing of this momentous event is known only to God, and that it will come unexpectedly, without any advance warning. The verse also highlights the limited nature of human knowledge, as even the Prophet Muhammad, the recipient of divine revelation, was not privy to this information. The interpretation underscores the importance of focusing on one's spiritual preparedness for the Hereafter, rather than obsessing over the unknowable details of its timing.
orig: يسألونك عن الساعة أيان مرساها قل إنما علمها عند ربي لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو ثقلت في السماوات والأرض لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة يسألونك كأنك حفي عنها قل إنما علمها عند الله ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: Say, "I possess not for myself [the power of] benefit or harm, except what Allah has willed. And if I knew the unseen, I could have acquired much wealth, and no harm would have touched me. I am not except a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limited power of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and all human beings. It reminds us that we have no control over the outcomes in our lives, as that power belongs to Allah alone. The verse also indicates that if the Prophet had the ability to see the unseen, he could have used that knowledge to his own benefit, but he was not given that power. Instead, his role is to warn people of the consequences of disbelief and to bring good news to those who have faith in Allah.
orig: قل لا أملك لنفسي نفعا ولا ضرا إلا ما شاء الله ولو كنت أعلم الغيب لاستكثرت من الخير وما مسني السوء إن أنا إلا نذير وبشير لقوم يؤمنون

translation: It is He who created you from one soul and created from it its mate that he might dwell in security with her. And when he covers her, she carries a light burden and continues therein. And when it becomes heavy, they both invoke Allah, their Lord, "If You should give us a good [child], we will surely be among the grateful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the creation of mankind from a single soul, and the pairing of each person with a spouse for companionship and security. It describes the process of pregnancy, where the burden starts light but grows heavier, leading the couple to turn to Allah in gratitude should they be blessed with a righteous child. The verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude to Allah for His blessings and the sanctity of the marital relationship.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة وجعل منها زوجها ليسكن إليها فلما تغشاها حملت حملا خفيفا فمرت به فلما أثقلت دعوا الله ربهما لئن آتيتنا صالحا لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: But when He gave them a sound (child), they attributed partners to Him in that which He had given them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to associate partners with God, even when they have been blessed with good things. The verse suggests that when people receive blessings from God, they may be inclined to attribute those blessings to other sources or to share the credit with others, rather than acknowledging God as the sole provider. The verse serves as a reminder to be grateful to God and to avoid the sin of associating partners with Him.
orig: فلما آتاهما صالحا جعلا له شركاء فيما آتاهما فتعالى الله عما يشركون

translation: Do they associate with Him those who create nothing and are themselves created?
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of associating partners with Allah, the One true Creator. It highlights the absurdity of worshiping or ascribing divinity to created beings who have no power to create anything themselves, while Allah is the Sole Creator of all things. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing Allah's unique and unparalleled status as the Supreme Creator, and the futility of worshiping anything else.
orig: أيشركون ما لا يخلق شيئا وهم يخلقون

translation: And they cannot help them, nor can they help themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the helplessness and inability of those who associate partners with Allah to provide any assistance or support, either to themselves or to others. It underscores the futility of relying on anything or anyone other than Allah for help and guidance.
orig: ولا يستطيعون لهم نصرا ولا أنفسهم ينصرون

translation: And if you invite them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is all the same for you whether you invite them or you are silent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that even if one invites others to the right path, they may not necessarily follow. The guidance of Allah is not something that can be forced upon people, as each individual has the free will to choose their own path. The verse conveys that the messenger's responsibility is to deliver the message, not to compel others to accept it. Whether the messenger invites them or remains silent, the outcome is the same if the people refuse to listen and follow the guidance.
orig: وإن تدعوهم إلى الهدى لا يتبعوكم سواء عليكم أدعوتموهم أم أنتم صامتون

translation: Indeed, those you [polytheists] call upon besides Allah are servants like you. So call upon them and let them respond to you, if you should be truthful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the idols and false gods that polytheists worship are not divine, but rather mere servants and creations of Allah, just like humans. It challenges the polytheists to call upon these false gods and see if they can respond, which would prove the validity of their worship. The verse suggests that the polytheists' claims of these gods' divinity are false, and that true worship and supplication should be directed towards Allah alone.
orig: إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عباد أمثالكم فادعوهم فليستجيبوا لكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Have they feet wherewith they walk? Or have they hands wherewith they hold? Or have they eyes wherewith they see? Or have they ears wherewith they hear? Say (O Muhammad): "Call your (so-called) partners (of Allâh) and then plot (your worst) against me, and give me no respite!"
interpretation: This verse is challenging the idolaters to prove the existence and power of their false deities. It is asking them whether these deities have the basic physical faculties like feet, hands, eyes, and ears that would enable them to interact with the world and assist their worshippers. The verse then commands the Prophet Muhammad to challenge the idolaters to call upon their supposed partners of Allah and plot against him, implying that their deities are powerless and unable to help them. The overall message is to affirm the oneness and supremacy of Allah over all false gods.
orig: ألهم أرجل يمشون بها أم لهم أيد يبطشون بها أم لهم أعين يبصرون بها أم لهم آذان يسمعون بها قل ادعوا شركاءكم ثم كيدون فلا تنظرون

translation: Indeed, my protector is Allah, who has revealed the Book; and He is the ally of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the true guardian and protector of the believers, as He has revealed the Qur'an, the divine scripture. He is the ally and supporter of the righteous - those who strive to live according to His guidance and commands.
orig: إن وليي الله الذي نزل الكتاب وهو يتولى الصالحين

translation: And those you invoke besides Him are unable to help you, nor can they help themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that any deities or objects worshipped besides Allah are powerless and incapable of providing any assistance or support. They cannot help the believers, nor can they even help themselves. This highlights the futility of idolatry and the need to worship only the One true God, Allah, who alone has the power to help and guide His creation.
orig: والذين تدعون من دونه لا يستطيعون نصركم ولا أنفسهم ينصرون

translation: And if you invite them to guidance, they will not hear; and you will see them looking at you while they do not see.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual blindness and deafness of those who reject the guidance of the Qur'an. Even when the truth is presented to them, they are unable or unwilling to perceive it, as if they are physically blind and deaf. This suggests that their rejection of faith is not due to a lack of evidence, but rather a hardening of their hearts and a turning away from the truth.
orig: وإن تدعوهم إلى الهدى لا يسمعوا وتراهم ينظرون إليك وهم لا يبصرون

translation: Accept what is best, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant.
interpretation: This verse encourages us to be forgiving and tolerant, to promote good values and practices, and to avoid engaging with those who are ignorant or act in an unwise manner. It emphasizes the importance of taking the high road, focusing on what is best, and not getting drawn into conflicts with those who lack understanding.
orig: خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين

translation: And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse instructs us to seek refuge in Allah whenever we are tempted by the whispers or evil suggestions of Satan. It reminds us that Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, and that by turning to Him, we can find protection and guidance against the deceptions of the devil.
orig: وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ فاستعذ بالله إنه سميع عليم

translation: Indeed, those who fear Allah - when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [Him] and at once they have insight.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are mindful of Allah and seek to please Him, when they are tempted or influenced by Satan, they quickly remember Allah and regain their spiritual clarity and insight. It highlights the importance of maintaining a strong connection with Allah and being vigilant against the whispers and temptations of Satan.
orig: إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم مبصرون

translation: And their brothers extend them in error; then they do not stop.
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people are led astray by their own kinsmen or associates, who encourage them to persist in their misguided ways. The interpretation is that one should be cautious of those who may influence us negatively and lead us down the wrong path, even if they are close to us. We should strive to make our own informed decisions and not blindly follow others.
orig: وإخوانهم يمدونهم في الغي ثم لا يقصرون

translation: And if you do not bring them a sign, they say, "Why have you not brought it?" Say, "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. This [Qur'an] is enlightenment from your Lord and guidance and mercy for a people who believe."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is simply conveying the message revealed to him by God, and is not responsible for producing miracles or signs to convince the disbelievers. The Qur'an itself is a sufficient "sign" or proof of its divine origin, as it provides enlightenment, guidance, and mercy for those who believe. The responsibility lies with the people to reflect on the Qur'an and accept the message, rather than demanding external proofs.
orig: وإذا لم تأتهم بآية قالوا لولا اجتبيتها قل إنما أتبع ما يوحى إلي من ربي هذا بصائر من ربكم وهدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And when the Qur'an is recited, then listen to it and pay attention that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to listen attentively and with reverence when the Qur'an is being recited, as this act of listening with humility and focus can lead to the attainment of God's mercy and blessings.
orig: وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا لعلكم ترحمون

translation: And remember your Lord within yourself in humility and in fear and without being loud in speech - in the mornings and the evenings. And be not among the heedless.
interpretation: This verse encourages the remembrance of God in a state of humility, reverence and without ostentation. It emphasizes the importance of remembering God both in the mornings and evenings, and to avoid being heedless or negligent in this regard. The interpretation is that one should strive to maintain a constant awareness and connection with the divine, expressed through a sincere and humble heart, rather than through outward displays or loud proclamations.
orig: واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة ودون الجهر من القول بالغدو والآصال ولا تكن من الغافلين

translation: Indeed, those who are with your Lord are not arrogant toward His worship, but they exalt Him and prostrate to Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humility and devotion of the believers in the presence of Allah. They do not show arrogance or pride in their worship, but rather they glorify and submit to Allah with complete humility and reverence. This is the ideal attitude that all believers should strive to emulate in their relationship with the Divine.
orig: إن الذين عند ربك لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ويسبحونه وله يسجدون

translation: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the bounties [of war]. Say, "The [decision concerning] bounties is for Allah and the Messenger. So fear Allah and amend that which is between you and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you should be believers."
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to seek guidance from Allah and the Prophet regarding the distribution of war spoils ("the bounties"). It emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah, resolving disputes amongst themselves, and obeying Allah and His Messenger - as these are the hallmarks of true faith.
orig: يسألونك عن الأنفال قل الأنفال لله والرسول فاتقوا الله وأصلحوا ذات بينكم وأطيعوا الله ورسوله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith; and upon their Lord they rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the characteristics of true believers. When the name of Allah is mentioned, their hearts are filled with reverence and awe, as they recognize the greatness and power of the Almighty. Furthermore, when the verses of the Qur'an are recited to them, their faith is strengthened and increased. These believers place their trust and reliance solely in their Lord, seeking guidance and support from Him alone.
orig: إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم وإذا تليت عليهم آياته زادتهم إيمانا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: Those who establish prayer and spend [in charity] from what We have provided them
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be steadfast in their religious practices, such as performing the obligatory prayers, and to be generous in sharing the blessings they have received from God with others in need. It emphasizes the importance of both spiritual devotion and practical charity as essential elements of a life of faith.
orig: الذين يقيمون الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: Those are the [true] believers, with degrees [of high position] from their Lord and forgiveness and a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who truly believe in Allah and live according to His teachings will be rewarded with elevated spiritual stations, forgiveness of their sins, and a bountiful provision from Allah. It highlights the elevated status of the true believers in the sight of their Lord.
orig: أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا لهم درجات عند ربهم ومغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: Just as your Lord brought you out of your home with the truth, and indeed, a party among the believers were unwilling.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad was sent by God with the truth, even though some believers were initially reluctant to accept it. It highlights the divine nature of the Prophet's mission and the importance of faith and submission to God's will, even when it may be challenging for some.
orig: كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق وإن فريقا من المؤمنين لكارهون

translation: They argue with you about the truth after it has been made clear, as if they are being driven to death while they are looking on.
interpretation: This verse describes the stubbornness and denial of those who reject the truth even when it is clearly presented to them. They argue against the truth, as if they are being forcefully led to their own demise, yet they remain indifferent and unwilling to accept the guidance.
orig: يجادلونك في الحق بعدما تبين كأنما يساقون إلى الموت وهم ينظرون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Allah promised you one of the two groups - that it would be yours - and you wished that the unarmed one would be yours. But Allah intended to establish the truth by His words and to eliminate the disbelievers
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad and the early Muslim community. It refers to the Battle of Badr, where the Muslims were outnumbered but were promised victory by Allah. The verse emphasizes that Allah's will prevails, even if it does not align with human desires or expectations. The interpretation is that Allah's plan will always triumph, and the truth will be established through His words, even if it means the defeat of the disbelievers.
orig: وإذ يعدكم الله إحدى الطائفتين أنها لكم وتودون أن غير ذات الشوكة تكون لكم ويريد الله أن يحق الحق بكلماته ويقطع دابر الكافرين

translation: That the truth may be manifested and the falsehood may be brought to naught, though the guilty dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the truth will prevail and falsehood will be eradicated, even if the wrongdoers dislike it. It is a reassurance that justice and righteousness will ultimately triumph over injustice and corruption, no matter the opposition faced.
orig: ليحق الحق ويبطل الباطل ولو كره المجرمون

translation: When you were crying out to your Lord, so He responded to you, "Indeed, I will reinforce you with a thousand from the angels, following one another."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking help and guidance from Allah, the Almighty. When the believers were facing a difficult situation, they cried out to their Lord for assistance, and Allah responded by promising to send a thousand angels to support them. This divine aid reflects the power and mercy of Allah, who is ever-ready to help those who turn to Him in times of need. The interpretation suggests that the believers should have unwavering faith in Allah's ability to provide support and victory, even in the face of overwhelming challenges.
orig: إذ تستغيثون ربكم فاستجاب لكم أني ممدكم بألف من الملائكة مردفين

translation: And Allah has not made it (i.e., the slaughter of the enemy) except [a matter of] good tidings for you and to reassure your hearts thereby. And victory is not except from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the military victory granted by Allah is not merely a means of destruction, but rather a source of good news and reassurance for the believers. It is a reminder that true victory comes only from Allah, the Almighty and All-Wise, and not from human efforts alone. This encourages the believers to trust in Allah's plan and to seek guidance from Him, rather than relying solely on their own strength or strategies.
orig: وما جعله الله إلا بشرى ولتطمئن به قلوبكم وما النصر إلا من عند الله إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: When He overwhelmed you with drowsiness [giving] security from Him and sent down upon you from the sky, rain by which to purify you and remove from you the evil [suggestions] of Satan and to make steadfast your hearts and plant firmly thereby your feet.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah provides comfort and protection to the believers during times of difficulty or distress. The drowsiness that overcomes them is a sign of security and tranquility from Allah, as He sends down rain from the sky to purify them and remove the evil whisperings of Satan. This allows the believers to have firm hearts and steadfast feet, strengthening their faith and resolve.
orig: إذ يغشيكم النعاس أمنة منه وينزل عليكم من السماء ماء ليطهركم به ويذهب عنكم رجز الشيطان وليربط على قلوبكم ويثبت به الأقدام

translation: When your Lord inspired to the angels, "I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike [them] upon the necks and strike from them every fingertip."
interpretation: This verse describes God's command to the angels to strengthen the believers and instill fear in the hearts of the disbelievers. The interpretation suggests that God will support the believers and grant them victory over those who reject faith, even to the point of inflicting severe punishment upon them.
orig: إذ يوحي ربك إلى الملائكة أني معكم فثبتوا الذين آمنوا سألقي في قلوب الذين كفروا الرعب فاضربوا فوق الأعناق واضربوا منهم كل بنان

translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who defy and disobey Allah and His Messenger will face severe consequences. It serves as a warning to those who choose to go against the commands and guidance of Allah, as He is the Almighty and will not tolerate such defiance.
orig: ذلك بأنهم شاقوا الله ورسوله ومن يشاقق الله ورسوله فإن الله شديد العقاب

translation: This is what you desired, so taste it, and indeed for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and persist in disbelief. It conveys the message that the consequences of disbelief and rejection of God's guidance will be the eternal punishment of the Fire. The verse emphasizes that the disbelievers will have to face the consequences of their own choices and actions, and they will be made to taste the punishment they have earned through their rejection of the truth.
orig: ذلكم فذوقوه وأن للكافرين عذاب النار

translation: O you who believe! When you meet those who disbelieve in battle, do not turn to them [your] backs.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to stand firm and face their enemies in battle, rather than fleeing or turning their backs. It emphasizes the importance of courage, steadfastness, and unwavering commitment to the cause of faith when confronted by those who reject it.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا لقيتم الذين كفروا زحفا فلا تولوهم الأدبار

translation: And whoever turns his back to them on that Day, unless swerving [as a strategy] for war or joining [another] company, has certainly returned with anger [upon him] from Allah, and his refuge is Hell - and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse warns against deserting one's comrades in battle. It states that anyone who turns their back on their fellow fighters, except for a tactical withdrawal or to join another group, will incur the wrath of Allah and be destined for Hell. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and loyalty in the face of adversity, even in the context of war.
orig: ومن يولهم يومئذ دبره إلا متحرفا لقتال أو متحيزا إلى فئة فقد باء بغضب من الله ومأواه جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: And you did not kill them, but it was Allah who killed them, and you did not throw when you threw, but it was Allah who threw, that He might test the believers with a good trial. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that victory in battle is not achieved through human effort alone, but rather by the will and power of Allah. It serves to remind the believers that their success is ultimately dependent on Allah's guidance and support, and that they should not take credit for their achievements. The verse also suggests that trials and tribulations faced by the believers are a means by which Allah tests their faith and strengthens their resolve.
orig: فلم تقتلوهم ولكن الله قتلهم وما رميت إذ رميت ولكن الله رمى وليبلي المؤمنين منه بلاء حسنا إن الله سميع عليم

translation: That [is so], and [moreover], Allah weakens the plot of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has the power to thwart the schemes and machinations of those who disbelieve in Him. It is a reassurance to the believers that their faith in Allah is not in vain, as He will ultimately undermine the efforts of the disbelievers to harm them.
orig: ذلكم وأن الله موهن كيد الكافرين

translation: If you [believers] seek the decision [of success], the decision has come to you. And if you desist [from hostility], it is better for you; but if you return [to war], We will return, and never will you be availed by your [large] company at all, even if it should increase; and [that is because] Allah is with the believers.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to seek Allah's help and decision, and to desist from hostility if it is better for them. It warns that if they return to war, Allah will also return to punish them, and their large numbers will not avail them, for Allah is with the believers. The verse emphasizes that the believers should trust in Allah's support and guidance, and avoid returning to conflict if it is not in their best interest.
orig: إن تستفتحوا فقد جاءكم الفتح وإن تنتهوا فهو خير لكم وإن تعودوا نعد ولن تغني عنكم فئتكم شيئا ولو كثرت وأن الله مع المؤمنين

translation: O you who believe! Obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him while you hear [his order].
interpretation: This verse commands the believers to obey Allah and His Messenger without hesitation or turning away, even when they hear the Messenger's instructions. It emphasizes the importance of complete submission and adherence to the divine guidance provided through the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أطيعوا الله ورسوله ولا تولوا عنه وأنتم تسمعون

translation: And do not be like those who say, "We have heard," but they do not listen.
interpretation: This verse cautions against being like those who claim to listen and understand, but in reality do not truly comprehend or act upon what they have heard. It emphasizes the importance of not only hearing the message, but also actively engaging with it and allowing it to transform one's thoughts and actions.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين قالوا سمعنا وهم لا يسمعون

translation: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not use reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the worst of God's creation are those who are spiritually deaf and dumb, unable to comprehend the signs of God and use their intellect to understand the truth. They are condemned for their willful rejection of faith and reason, which are the hallmarks of a true believer.
orig: إن شر الدواب عند الله الصم البكم الذين لا يعقلون

translation: And if Allah had known [any] good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would [still] have turned away, while they are averse.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah knows what is best for people, and if there was any good in those who turned away from the message, Allah would have guided them to hear and accept it. However, their rejection of the truth was due to their own aversion and unwillingness to listen, not a lack of guidance from Allah.
orig: ولو علم الله فيهم خيرا لأسمعهم ولو أسمعهم لتولوا وهم معرضون

translation: O you who believe! Respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart and that to Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to respond to the call of Allah and His Messenger, as this will bring them life and guidance. It also reminds them that Allah has power over their hearts and that they will ultimately be held accountable to Him on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا استجيبوا لله وللرسول إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه وأنه إليه تحشرون

translation: And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively, and know that Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse warns against the consequences of wrongdoing, which can affect not only the wrongdoers but also the wider community. It emphasizes the need to be mindful of Allah's punishment, which can be severe, and to avoid actions that could lead to trials or tribulations that may impact everyone, not just the perpetrators. The verse encourages people to be righteous and to be aware of the far-reaching effects of their actions.
orig: واتقوا فتنة لا تصيبن الذين ظلموا منكم خاصة واعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب

translation: And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that people might abduct you, but He sheltered you and supported you with His victory and provided you with good things that you might be grateful.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers of their humble beginnings when they were few in number and oppressed, fearing persecution from their enemies. However, Allah protected them, strengthened them, and provided for them, so that they may be grateful for His blessings. This serves as a lesson that even in times of weakness and hardship, Allah can elevate and support the believers if they remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: واذكروا إذ أنتم قليل مستضعفون في الأرض تخافون أن يتخطفكم الناس فآواكم وأيدكم بنصره ورزقكم من الطيبات لعلكم تشكرون

translation: O you who believe! Do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts while you know [the consequence].
interpretation: This verse urges believers to be faithful and trustworthy in their dealings with Allah and His Messenger, as well as in fulfilling the responsibilities and obligations entrusted to them. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining integrity and honesty, even when it may be tempting to act otherwise. The verse serves as a reminder that betrayal of trust is a grave sin that carries consequences, and believers must strive to uphold their commitments and duties with full knowledge of their actions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تخونوا الله والرسول وتخونوا أماناتكم وأنتم تعلمون

translation: And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial and that Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that our worldly possessions and offspring are a test from Allah, and that the true reward lies with Him in the Hereafter. It cautions us against becoming overly attached to the material aspects of life, and encourages us to focus on our spiritual development and pleasing Allah, as that is where the greatest reward can be found.
orig: واعلموا أنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة وأن الله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: O you who believe! If you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion and will remove from you your misdeeds and forgive you. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be mindful of Allah (God) and to fear displeasing Him. In return, Allah will grant them the ability to discern truth from falsehood, forgive their sins, and bestow upon them His great bounty and mercy. The key message is that by fearing and obeying Allah, believers can attain guidance, forgiveness, and Allah's abundant grace.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تتقوا الله يجعل لكم فرقانا ويكفر عنكم سيئاتكم ويغفر لكم والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when those who disbelieved plot against you to restrain you or kill you or evict you. But they plan, and Allah plans. And Allah is the best of planners.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the plots and schemes of the disbelievers against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They sought to undermine his mission, either by arresting him, killing him, or expelling him from Makkah. However, Allah, the Almighty, is the best of planners, and He will thwart the plans of the disbelievers and protect His Messenger. This verse emphasizes the sovereignty of Allah and His ultimate control over all affairs, even in the face of adversity and opposition.
orig: وإذ يمكر بك الذين كفروا ليثبتوك أو يقتلوك أو يخرجوك ويمكرون ويمكر الله والله خير الماكرين

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard this. If we willed, we could say the like of this. This is not but legends of the former peoples."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of those who reject the Qur"anic revelations. They claim that they could produce something similar to the Qur"an if they wished, dismissing it as mere "legends of the former peoples". This reflects their unwillingness to acknowledge the divine origin and miraculous nature of the Qur"an, and their refusal to submit to its guidance.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا قالوا قد سمعنا لو نشاء لقلنا مثل هذا إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when they said, "O Allah, if this should be the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disbelief of those who challenged the Prophet Muhammad to bring down a punishment from Allah as proof of the truth of his message. Their demand for a miraculous sign demonstrated their unwillingness to accept the Qur'an and the Prophet's teachings based on faith and reason. This verse serves as a warning against such arrogance and a call to submit to the will of Allah with humility and sincerity.
orig: وإذ قالوا اللهم إن كان هذا هو الحق من عندك فأمطر علينا حجارة من السماء أو ائتنا بعذاب أليم

translation: And Allah would not punish them while you, [O Muhammad], are among them, and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and forgiveness. As long as the believers are seeking forgiveness and repentance, Allah will not punish them, even if they have committed sins. The presence of the Prophet Muhammad among them is also a factor in Allah's decision not to punish them, as the Prophet's guidance and intercession help the believers to seek forgiveness and turn back to the right path.
orig: وما كان الله ليعذبهم وأنت فيهم وما كان الله معذبهم وهم يستغفرون

translation: And why should Allah not punish them while they obstruct [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram and they were not [fit to be] its guardians? Its [true] guardians are not but the righteous, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who obstruct people from accessing the sacred Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, which is the holiest site in Islam. It states that these people are not fit to be the guardians of this sacred place, as that role belongs only to the righteous and God-fearing.
