The verse suggests that most of those who obstruct access to the Masjid al-Haram do not truly understand the sanctity of this site and the responsibility that comes with being its guardian.
orig: وما لهم ألا يعذبهم الله وهم يصدون عن المسجد الحرام وما كانوا أولياءه إن أولياؤه إلا المتقون ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And their prayer at the House was not except whistling and clapping. So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse condemns the insincere and hypocritical prayers of those who perform religious rituals without true faith and devotion. The "whistling and clapping" refers to the superficial and ostentatious nature of their worship, which lacks the humility and reverence required in the presence of the Divine. The verse warns them that they will face the consequences of their disbelief and insincerity, and urges them to truly repent and return to a genuine spiritual connection with God.
orig: وما كان صلاتهم عند البيت إلا مكاء وتصدية فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of Allah. So they will spend it; then it will become for them a [source of] regret, and they will be overcome. And those who have disbelieved - unto Hell they will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse warns those who disbelieve and spend their wealth to turn people away from the path of Allah. It states that their wealth will be spent, but it will ultimately become a source of regret for them, and they will be overcome. The verse also emphasizes that those who have disbelieved will be gathered to Hell.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ينفقون أموالهم ليصدوا عن سبيل الله فسينفقونها ثم تكون عليهم حسرة ثم يغلبون والذين كفروا إلى جهنم يحشرون

translation: That Allah may separate the wicked from the good and place the wicked one upon another and heap them together and put them into Hell. It is those who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's ability to distinguish between the righteous and the wicked, and to punish the wicked accordingly. The interpretation suggests that Allah will gather the wicked together and consign them to Hell, which is the ultimate loss for those who have chosen a path of wickedness.
orig: ليميز الله الخبيث من الطيب ويجعل الخبيث بعضه على بعض فيركمه جميعا فيجعله في جهنم أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: Say to those who disbelieve, "If they cease, what has previously occurred will be forgiven for them. But if they return [to hostility] - then the precedent of the former [rebellious] peoples has already taken place."
interpretation: This verse encourages the disbelievers to cease their hostility and rejection of faith, with the promise that their past sins will be forgiven if they do so. However, it also warns that if they return to their previous ways of rejecting the truth, they will face the same fate as those who rejected the message of God in the past.
orig: قل للذين كفروا إن ينتهوا يغفر لهم ما قد سلف وإن يعودوا فقد مضت سنت الأولين

translation: And fight them until there is no [more] fitnah and [until] the religion, all of it, is for Allah. And if they cease - then indeed, Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse commands Muslims to fight against those who persecute them and prevent them from practicing their faith, until there is no more oppression and the religion of Islam is freely practiced. However, if the opposing party ceases hostilities, then Muslims should cease fighting as well, for Allah is aware of all that they do.
orig: وقاتلوهم حتى لا تكون فتنة ويكون الدين كله لله فإن انتهوا فإن الله بما يعملون بصير

translation: And if they turn away, then know that Allah is your protector; an excellent protector, and an excellent helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that even if people turn away from the message of Islam, Muslims should know that Allah is their protector and supporter. It assures believers that Allah is the best guardian and helper, and they can rely on Him for guidance and assistance.
orig: وإن تولوا فاعلموا أن الله مولاكم نعم المولى ونعم النصير

translation: And know that whatever you obtain of war booty - then indeed, for Allah is one fifth of it and for the Messenger and for [his] near relatives and the orphans, the needy, and the [stranded] traveler, if you have believed in Allah and in that which We sent down to Our Servant on the day of the Criterion - the day when the two armies met. And Allah, over all things, is competent.
interpretation: This verse instructs that a portion of any war booty or spoils of war should be set aside for Allah, the Prophet, and various groups in need such as relatives, orphans, the poor, and travelers. This is a command to honor the rights of others and to use wealth in a way that benefits the community. The verse also refers to the decisive battle of Badr, which was a major victory for the early Muslim community, and affirms that Allah has power over all things.
orig: واعلموا أنما غنمتم من شيء فأن لله خمسه وللرسول ولذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل إن كنتم آمنتم بالله وما أنزلنا على عبدنا يوم الفرقان يوم التقى الجمعان والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: When you were on the nearer side (of the valley), and they were on the farther side, and the caravan was lower (in position) than you. And if you had made a mutual appointment, you would certainly have failed in the appointment, but (it was) so that Allah might accomplish a matter which was to be done, that he who perished (on that day) might perish by clear proof (and) he who survived might survive by clear proof. And verily, Allah is All-Hearer, All-Knower.
interpretation: This verse describes a situation during the Battle of Badr, where the Muslim forces were positioned on the nearer side of the valley, while the disbelievers were on the farther side, and the caravan was lower in position. The verse suggests that if the Muslims had made a mutual appointment with the disbelievers, they would have failed in the appointment. However, this was part of Allah's plan, so that those who were destined to perish would do so with clear proof, and those who were destined to survive would do so with clear proof. This emphasizes that Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, and His plan is unfolding according to His will.
orig: إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا وهم بالعدوة القصوى والركب أسفل منكم ولو تواعدتم لاختلفتم في الميعاد ولكن ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا ليهلك من هلك عن بينة ويحيى من حي عن بينة وإن الله لسميع عليم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Allah showed them to you in your dream as few; and if He had shown them to you as many, you [believers] would have lost courage and would have disputed in the matter [of whether to fight], but Allah saved [you from that]. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has the power to control what is shown to us, whether it be in dreams or in reality. If Allah had shown the believers a larger number of the enemy forces, they may have lost courage and disputed about whether to fight. However, Allah saved them from that by only showing them a small number, demonstrating His knowledge and wisdom in guiding the believers. The interpretation is that we should trust in Allah's plan and judgement, even when we cannot fully understand it.
orig: إذ يريكهم الله في منامك قليلا ولو أراكهم كثيرا لفشلتم ولتنازعتم في الأمر ولكن الله سلم إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And [remember, O Muhammad], when He showed them to you, when you met them, as few in your eyes, and He made you [appear] as few in their eyes so that Allah might accomplish a matter already destined. And to Allah are [all] matters returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the outcome of a battle or conflict is ultimately in the hands of Allah. He can make the enemy appear fewer in number to the believers, or make the believers appear fewer in number to the enemy, in order to fulfill His divine plan. Regardless of the apparent circumstances, the true power and control lies with Allah, to whom all matters return.
orig: وإذ يريكموهم إذ التقيتم في أعينكم قليلا ويقللكم في أعينهم ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: O you who believe! When you meet a force, be firm, and remember Allah much that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to remain steadfast and have faith in Allah when facing adversity or a challenging situation. By remembering Allah frequently, one can find the strength and guidance to overcome obstacles and ultimately achieve success.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا لقيتم فئة فاثبتوا واذكروا الله كثيرا لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute and [thus] lose courage and [then] your strength would depart; and be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, as well as the need for unity and patience. It warns against disputes and division, which can lead to a loss of courage and strength. The interpretation suggests that by obeying Allah and His Messenger, and maintaining patience and unity, believers can receive the support and assistance of Allah, who is with those who are steadfast.
orig: وأطيعوا الله ورسوله ولا تنازعوا فتفشلوا وتذهب ريحكم واصبروا إن الله مع الصابرين

translation: And do not be like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen by people and avert [them] from the way of Allah. And Allah is encompassing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse cautions against acting with arrogance, vanity, and a desire for public display, rather than sincerely following the path of Allah. It reminds us that Allah is fully aware of our actions and intentions, and that we should strive to please Him, not seek the admiration of others.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين خرجوا من ديارهم بطرا ورئاء الناس ويصدون عن سبيل الله والله بما يعملون محيط

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Satan made their deeds pleasing to them and said, "No one can overcome you today from among the people, and indeed, I am a protector for you." But when the two armies sighted each other, he turned on his heels and said, "Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I see what you do not see; indeed, I fear Allah. And Allah is severe in penalty."
interpretation: This verse describes how Satan deceived the disbelievers by making their actions seem pleasing to them and promising them victory, but when the two armies faced each other, Satan abandoned them and declared his disassociation from them. The interpretation is that Satan tries to mislead people and make their evil actions appear good, but in the end, he will abandon them and they will face the severe punishment of Allah for their misdeeds.
orig: وإذ زين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم وقال لا غالب لكم اليوم من الناس وإني جار لكم فلما تراءت الفئتان نكص على عقبيه وقال إني بريء منكم إني أرى ما لا ترون إني أخاف الله والله شديد العقاب

translation: When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease say, "Allah and His Messenger have not given us anything [i.e., wealth or spoils of war] except delusion." And when it is said to them, "Make provision for yourselves and your families [in preparation for the campaign]," they say, "If only we could return [home]." And it [i.e., their excuse] pleases them. And Allah has made their hearts yield. And Allah guides not the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse condemns the hypocrites and those with a disease in their hearts (i.e., spiritual weakness) who make excuses to avoid participating in the cause of Allah. They claim that the Prophet and Allah have not given them anything, when in reality they are being called to make sacrifices for the faith. Their excuses please them, but Allah has sealed their hearts, for He does not guide those who persistently disobey Him. The lesson here is to beware of hypocrisy and weakness of faith, and to wholeheartedly devote oneself to the service of Allah.
orig: إذ يقول المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض غر هؤلاء دينهم ومن يتوكل على الله فإن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: And if you could but see when the disbelievers are made to stand before the Fire and [it is said], "Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire."
interpretation: This verse paints a vivid picture of the fate that awaits those who reject faith in God. It describes the angels striking the faces and backs of the disbelievers as they are forced to confront the torment of the Hellfire. The imagery conveys the utter humiliation and suffering they will experience, a stark warning to those who turn away from the truth.
orig: ولو ترى إذ يتوفى الذين كفروا الملائكة يضربون وجوههم وأدبارهم وذوقوا عذاب الحريق

translation: That is because of what your hands have put forth [of evil], and indeed, Allah is not unjust to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the consequences people face are a result of their own actions and choices. Allah is not unjust, but rather people are accountable for their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder that we are responsible for our own actions and their outcomes.
orig: ذلك بما قدمت أيديكم وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد

translation: Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, they disbelieved in the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and severe in [His] penalty.
interpretation: This verse draws a parallel between the disbelief and rejection of Allah's signs by the people of Pharaoh and those who came before them. It emphasizes that Allah punished them for their sins, highlighting His power and the severity of His retribution against those who deny His signs and guidance.
orig: كدأب آل فرعون والذين من قبلهم كفروا بآيات الله فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم إن الله قوي شديد العقاب

translation: That is because Allah would not change a favor which He had bestowed upon a people until they change what is within themselves. And indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah does not change the blessings and favors He has bestowed upon a people until they themselves change what is in their own hearts and minds. It suggests that the people’s own transformation and change is a prerequisite for Allah to alter the state of their circumstances. The verse also affirms that Allah is all-Hearing and all-Knowing, implying that He is aware of the people’s innermost thoughts and actions.
orig: ذلك بأن الله لم يك مغيرا نعمة أنعمها على قوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم وأن الله سميع عليم

translation: Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, they denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins, and We drowned the people of Pharaoh. And all [of them] were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse draws a parallel between the fate of the people of Pharaoh and those who came before them, who all denied the signs and messages of their Lord. As a result, they were destroyed for their sins, and the people of Pharaoh were drowned. This serves as a warning that those who reject divine guidance and persist in wrongdoing will face severe consequences.
orig: كدأب آل فرعون والذين من قبلهم كذبوا بآيات ربهم فأهلكناهم بذنوبهم وأغرقنا آل فرعون وكل كانوا ظالمين

translation: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve, [who] will not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the worst of all creatures in the sight of Allah are those who reject faith and refuse to believe in Him. Their disbelief and rejection of the truth is the most abhorrent state in the eyes of the Almighty.
orig: إن شر الدواب عند الله الذين كفروا فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant every time, and they do not fear [Allah].
interpretation: This verse is a warning against those who make covenants or agreements but then repeatedly break them without any fear of the consequences. It emphasizes the importance of honoring one's commitments and the need to be mindful of one's obligations to Allah.
orig: الذين عاهدت منهم ثم ينقضون عهدهم في كل مرة وهم لا يتقون

translation: And if you gain dominance over them in war, then disperse with [them] those [of them] whom you fear [will remain behind], that perhaps they will remember.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to disperse and scatter their enemies during war, in order to instill fear and cause them to reflect on their actions. The goal is not just military victory, but to make the enemy realize the consequences of their hostility and hopefully lead them to change their ways.
orig: فإما تثقفنهم في الحرب فشرد بهم من خلفهم لعلهم يذكرون

translation: And if you fear from a people betrayal, throw [their covenant] to them [with clarity]. Indeed, Allah likes not the treacherous.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to be cautious of potential betrayal from others, and to make their position clear to them. It emphasizes that Allah does not approve of those who act in a treacherous manner.
orig: وإما تخافن من قوم خيانة فانبذ إليهم على سواء إن الله لا يحب الخائنين

translation: And let not those who disbelieve think that they can outrun (i.e. escape from the punishment). Verily, they will never be able to save themselves (from Allah's Punishment).
interpretation: This verse warns those who disbelieve in Allah and reject His message that they cannot escape the consequences of their actions. No matter how they try to evade or outrun the punishment, they will never be able to avoid it, as Allah's power and authority are absolute.
orig: ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا سبقوا إنهم لا يعجزون

translation: And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know [but] whom Allah knows. And whatever you spend in the cause of Allah will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to prepare military strength and resources to deter and defend against their enemies. It highlights the importance of being ready to confront threats, both known and unknown, in the cause of Allah. The verse also promises that any expenditure made in this effort will be rewarded by Allah, emphasizing that the believers will not be wronged in this endeavor.
orig: وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة ومن رباط الخيل ترهبون به عدو الله وعدوكم وآخرين من دونهم لا تعلمونهم الله يعلمهم وما تنفقوا من شيء في سبيل الله يوف إليكم وأنتم لا تظلمون

translation: And if they incline to peace, then incline to it [also] and rely upon Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to be inclined towards peace and reconciliation, even if the other party is not initially receptive. It instructs believers to reciprocate a peaceful overture, and to put their trust in Allah, who hears and knows all things. The interpretation is that Muslims should strive for peace and conflict resolution, while maintaining faith in the divine guidance and wisdom.
orig: وإن جنحوا للسلم فاجنح لها وتوكل على الله إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: And if they intend to deceive you - then sufficient for you is Allah. He it is who supported you with His help and with the believers
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that if his enemies try to deceive or betray him, Allah will be sufficient for him and will support him with His help and the help of the believers. It emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate protector and that the believers will stand by the Prophet against any attempts to undermine him.
orig: وإن يريدوا أن يخدعوك فإن حسبك الله هو الذي أيدك بنصره وبالمؤمنين

translation: And He has united their (believers') hearts. If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have united their hearts, but Allah has united them. Indeed, He is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the unity and harmony among the believers is a gift from Allah, not something that can be achieved through human efforts or material means alone. It is Allah who has the power to unite the hearts of people, and this unity is a sign of His might and wisdom. The verse encourages believers to rely on Allah's guidance and grace to maintain their unity, rather than trying to achieve it through their own means.
orig: وألف بين قلوبهم لو أنفقت ما في الأرض جميعا ما ألفت بين قلوبهم ولكن الله ألف بينهم إنه عزيز حكيم

translation: O Prophet, sufficient for you is Allah and those who have followed you of the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) should rely on Allah and the believers who follow him, rather than seeking the approval or support of others. It conveys the message that the Prophet's true strength and guidance comes from his faith in Allah and the devotion of his followers.
orig: يا أيها النبي حسبك الله ومن اتبعك من المؤمنين

translation: O Prophet, encourage the believers to fight. If there are among you twenty [who are] steadfast, they will overcome two hundred. And if there are among you one hundred [who are] steadfast, they will overcome a thousand of those who have disbelieved because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to fight against the disbelievers, even if they are outnumbered. It emphasizes that the steadfastness and courage of the believers, even in small numbers, can lead to victory over a larger force of disbelievers. The reason for this is that the disbelievers "do not understand", implying that they lack the faith and understanding that gives the believers their strength and determination.
orig: يا أيها النبي حرض المؤمنين على القتال إن يكن منكم عشرون صابرون يغلبوا مائتين وإن يكن منكم مائة يغلبوا ألفا من الذين كفروا بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: Now Allah has lightened [the hardship] for you, and He knows that among you is weakness. So if there are from you one hundred [who are] patient, they will overcome two hundred. And if there are among you a thousand, they will overcome two thousand by permission of Allah. And Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be patient and steadfast in the face of adversity. It assures them that Allah has made their burdens lighter, and that He knows of their weaknesses. The verse then goes on to state that even a small number of patient believers can overcome a much larger force, with Allah's permission and support. This is a message of hope and reassurance, reminding the faithful that their perseverance and trust in Allah will ultimately lead to victory.
orig: الآن خفف الله عنكم وعلم أن فيكم ضعفا فإن يكن منكم مائة صابرة يغلبوا مائتين وإن يكن منكم ألف يغلبوا ألفين بإذن الله والله مع الصابرين

translation: It is not for a prophet to have captives [of war] until he inflicts defeat throughout the land. You [i.e., the Muslims] desire the commodities of this world, but Allah desires [for you] the Hereafter. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is not appropriate for a prophet to take prisoners of war until they have thoroughly defeated the enemy. The verse suggests that the desire for worldly gains should not be the primary motivation for a prophet, but rather the pursuit of the Hereafter, which is the ultimate goal that Allah desires for his followers. The verse also highlights that Allah is all-Powerful and All-Wise in His judgments and commands.
orig: ما كان لنبي أن يكون له أسرى حتى يثخن في الأرض تريدون عرض الدنيا والله يريد الآخرة والله عزيز حكيم

translation: If it were not for a decree from Allah that had preceded, you would have been touched for what you took by a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of Allah's divine decree and plan. It suggests that the believers were spared from a severe punishment due to Allah's prior decree, which protected them from the consequences of their actions. The interpretation highlights the idea that Allah's will and guidance are paramount, and that believers should trust in His wisdom and mercy.
orig: لولا كتاب من الله سبق لمسكم فيما أخذتم عذاب عظيم

translation: So consume what you have obtained of [lawful] good things and be conscious of Allah about whom you believe.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to consume the spoils of war that have been obtained through lawful means, and to be mindful of Allah and His commands. It emphasizes the importance of being conscious of Allah and seeking His forgiveness, as He is Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: فكلوا مما غنمتم حلالا طيبا واتقوا الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O Prophet, say to those who are captives in your hands: "If Allah knows [any] good in your hearts, He will give you [something] better than what was taken from you, and He will forgive you; and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and it instructs him to convey a message to the prisoners of war who are in the custody of the Muslims. The message is that if Allah sees any good in the hearts of these captives, He will reward them with something better than what was taken from them, and He will forgive them. This verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, and it encourages the captives to have faith and turn to Allah, as He is the Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: يا أيها النبي قل لمن في أيديكم من الأسرى إن يعلم الله في قلوبكم خيرا يؤتكم خيرا مما أخذ منكم ويغفر لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: And if they intend to deceive you - then indeed, Allah is sufficient for you. It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that if those who oppose the Prophet (peace be upon him) intend to betray or deceive him, they have already betrayed Allah by rejecting His guidance. Allah is fully aware of their schemes and will protect His Messenger, and the believers who support him, with His wisdom and power.
orig: وإن يريدوا خيانتك فقد خانوا الله من قبل فأمكن منهم والله عليم حكيم

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and emigrated and fought in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank in the sight of Allah. And it is those who are the achievers [of success]. Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him and approval and of gardens for them wherein is enduring pleasure. [They will be] abiding therein forever. Indeed, Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the high status and reward of those who have truly believed in Allah, made sacrifices by leaving their homes (emigrating), and strived (fought) in Allah's cause with their wealth and lives. They are the ones who have attained true success in the sight of Allah. Allah has promised them His mercy, approval, and everlasting pleasure in the Gardens of Paradise. This highlights the importance of faith, sacrifice, and striving in the path of Allah as the means to attain Allah's pleasure and the ultimate success in the Hereafter.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله والذين آووا ونصروا أولئك بعضهم أولياء بعض والذين آمنوا ولم يهاجروا ما لكم من ولايتهم من شيء حتى يهاجروا وإن استنصروكم في الدين فعليكم النصر إلا على قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And those who disbelieve are allies of one another. If you do not do so, there will be fitnah (discord) on the earth and great corruption.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity and avoiding alliances with those who disbelieve. It warns that such alliances can lead to discord and widespread corruption in society. The interpretation is that believers should maintain their faith and avoid compromising it by forming close ties with those who reject the truth of Islam.
orig: والذين كفروا بعضهم أولياء بعض إلا تفعلوه تكن فتنة في الأرض وفساد كبير

translation: And those who believed and emigrated and fought in the cause of Allah and those who gave shelter and aided - it is they who are the believers, truly. For them is forgiveness and noble provision.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith, migration, and striving in the cause of Allah. It emphasizes that true believers are those who not only believe but also take action by emigrating and fighting for the sake of Allah. Additionally, it promises forgiveness and noble provision for those who fulfill these criteria, indicating the rewards that await the steadfast believers.
orig: والذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله والذين آووا ونصروا أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: And those who believed after [the initial emigration] and emigrated and fought with you - they are of you. But those of [blood] relationship are more entitled [to inheritance] in the decree of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever, about all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith, migration, and striving alongside the believers, which establishes a bond of brotherhood that supersedes even blood relations. It highlights that in the sight of Allah, those who share this spiritual kinship have a greater claim on one another than those connected by mere blood ties. This teaches us that the ties of faith and common purpose are the strongest and most enduring.
orig: والذين آمنوا من بعد وهاجروا وجاهدوا معكم فأولئك منكم وأولو الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض في كتاب الله إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: A declaration from Allah and His Messenger to those of the Mushrikun (polytheists, pagans, idolaters, disbelievers in the Oneness of Allah) with whom you made a treaty.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah and His Messenger are free from any obligation or treaty with the polytheists, as they had violated the terms of the treaty. It signifies the end of the truce and the beginning of a new phase in the relationship between the believers and the disbelievers.
orig: براءة من الله ورسوله إلى الذين عاهدتم من المشركين

translation: So travel freely, [O disbelievers], throughout the land for four months and know that you cannot escape Allah and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse instructs the disbelievers to freely move about the land for four months, acknowledging that they cannot escape the power and judgment of Allah. It emphasizes that Allah will ultimately disgrace and punish those who reject faith in Him.
orig: فسيحوا في الأرض أربعة أشهر واعلموا أنكم غير معجزي الله وأن الله مخزي الكافرين

translation: And [it is] an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage that Allah is disassociated from the disbelievers, and [so is] His Messenger. So if you repent, that is best for you; but if you turn away - then know that you will not cause failure [to] Allah. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse conveys Allah's disassociation from the disbelievers and polytheists, and calls upon them to repent and embrace the true faith. It warns that those who persist in disbelief will face a painful punishment, and that they cannot escape Allah's will. The verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and submission to Allah as the path to salvation.
orig: وأذان من الله ورسوله إلى الناس يوم الحج الأكبر أن الله بريء من المشركين ورسوله فإن تبتم فهو خير لكم وإن توليتم فاعلموا أنكم غير معجزي الله وبشر الذين كفروا بعذاب أليم

translation: Except for those with whom you made a treaty among the polytheists and then they have not been deficient toward you in anything or supported anyone against you; so complete for them their treaty until their term [has ended]. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous [who fear Him].
interpretation: This verse establishes that treaties and agreements made with non-Muslims should be honored, as long as they do not break the terms of the treaty. It emphasizes that Allah loves those who are righteous and fulfill their obligations, even towards those who do not share their faith.
orig: إلا الذين عاهدتم من المشركين ثم لم ينقصوكم شيئا ولم يظاهروا عليكم أحدا فأتموا إليهم عهدهم إلى مدتهم إن الله يحب المتقين

translation: And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them and capture them and besiege them and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they should repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, let them [go] on their way. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the treatment of polytheists (those who associate partners with Allah) during the sacred months, a time when fighting was traditionally prohibited. The verse instructs Muslims to kill the polytheists wherever they are found, capture them, besiege them, and lie in wait for them. However, if the polytheists repent, establish prayer, and give zakah (obligatory charity), then they are to be left alone, as Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. The interpretation suggests that the command to fight the polytheists is conditional on their refusal to accept Islam and perform the basic religious obligations, and that the ultimate goal is their guidance and salvation.
orig: فإذا انسلخ الأشهر الحرم فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم وخذوهم واحصروهم واقعدوا لهم كل مرصد فإن تابوا وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فخلوا سبيلهم إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the words of Allah. Then deliver him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to provide safe passage and protection to polytheists who seek refuge, so that they may hear the message of Islam. The rationale given is that the polytheists "do not know", implying that they are ignorant and should be given the opportunity to learn about the true faith. The verse emphasizes the importance of compassion and understanding, even towards those who do not share the same beliefs.
orig: وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك فأجره حتى يسمع كلام الله ثم أبلغه مأمنه ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعلمون

translation: How can there be for the polytheists a treaty with Allah and with His Messenger, except for those with whom you made a treaty at al-Masjid al-Haram? So as long as they are upright toward you, be upright toward them. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous [who fear Him].
interpretation: This verse establishes that the polytheists cannot have a treaty with Allah and His Messenger, except for those who have made a treaty with the Muslims at the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram). As long as the polytheists with whom a treaty has been made remain true to their agreement, the Muslims must also uphold the treaty. This is because Allah loves those who are righteous and fulfill their obligations.
orig: كيف يكون للمشركين عهد عند الله وعند رسوله إلا الذين عاهدتم عند المسجد الحرام فما استقاموا لكم فاستقيموا لهم إن الله يحب المتقين

translation: And if they prevail over you, they would be to you as enemies and extend against you their hands and their tongues with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse warns that even if the disbelievers gain power over the believers, they will not show any mercy or loyalty. They will use their words to deceive the believers, while their hearts harbor enmity. The majority of them are morally corrupt.
orig: كيف وإن يظهروا عليكم لا يرقبوا فيكم إلا ولا ذمة يرضونكم بأفواههم وتأبى قلوبهم وأكثرهم فاسقون

translation: They have exchanged the signs of Allah for a small price and have averted [people] from His way. Indeed, it was evil that they were doing.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who sell the teachings and signs of Allah for a small worldly gain, and in doing so, lead others astray from the path of Allah. It emphasizes that such actions are evil and displeasing to Allah.
orig: اشتروا بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا فصدوا عن سبيله إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: They do not regard any tie of kinship or covenant in respect of a believer. And it is they who are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the disbelievers do not honor any ties of kinship or any covenant or agreement, even with believers. They violate these sacred bonds and are thus considered the transgressors, those who exceed the limits of proper conduct.
orig: لا يرقبون في مؤمن إلا ولا ذمة وأولئك هم المعتدون

translation: But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion. And We detail the verses for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who repent, establish regular prayer, and give the obligatory charity (zakah) are considered brothers in faith. It highlights the importance of these core Islamic practices as a means of strengthening the bonds of brotherhood and community among believers. The verse also indicates that the Qur'anic verses are explained in detail for those who seek knowledge and understanding.
orig: فإن تابوا وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فإخوانكم في الدين ونفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: And if they break their oaths after their treaty and revile your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief, for indeed, they have no [binding] oaths, that they might cease.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to fight against the leaders of disbelief if they break their oaths and attack the religion of Islam. The interpretation suggests that the believers should not tolerate such betrayal and should confront the disbelievers in order to put an end to their hostility and aggression.
orig: وإن نكثوا أيمانهم من بعد عهدهم وطعنوا في دينكم فقاتلوا أئمة الكفر إنهم لا أيمان لهم لعلهم ينتهون

translation: Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths and determined to expel the Messenger, and they had begun [the attack upon] you the first time? Do you fear them? But Allah has more right that you should fear Him, if you are [truly] believers.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to fight against those who have broken their oaths, plotted to expel the Prophet, and initiated hostilities against the believers. The verse emphasizes that the believers should fear Allah more than they fear their enemies, as Allah has a greater right to be feared if they are truly believers.
orig: ألا تقاتلون قوما نكثوا أيمانهم وهموا بإخراج الرسول وهم بدءوكم أول مرة أتخشونهم فالله أحق أن تخشوه إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and satisfy the breasts of a believing people
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to fight against those who oppose the faith. It promises that Allah will punish the disbelievers through the hands of the believers, and that the believers will be victorious and their hearts will be satisfied. The verse emphasizes the need for the believers to take an active role in defending their faith against those who seek to undermine it.
orig: قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم ويخزهم وينصركم عليهم ويشف صدور قوم مؤمنين

translation: And He will remove the rancor from their hearts. And Allah will turn in forgiveness to whom He wills, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse speaks of Allah's ability to remove the anger and resentment from the hearts of people, and His power to forgive whomever He chooses. It emphasizes Allah's knowledge and wisdom in His decisions regarding forgiveness and guidance.
orig: ويذهب غيظ قلوبهم ويتوب الله على من يشاء والله عليم حكيم

translation: Or did you think that you would be left [alone] while Allah has not yet made evident those among you who strive [for His cause] and do not take other than Allah, His Messenger and the believers as intimates? And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse questions whether people think they will be left alone without being tested, when Allah has not yet made clear those among them who strive for His cause and do not take anyone other than Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as their close confidants. Allah is fully aware of what they do.
orig: أم حسبتم أن تتركوا ولما يعلم الله الذين جاهدوا منكم ولم يتخذوا من دون الله ولا رسوله ولا المؤمنين وليجة والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah [while] witnessing against themselves with disbelief. [For] those, their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who associate partners with Allah (polytheists) have no right to maintain or frequent the mosques, as they are in a state of disbelief. Their actions and deeds will be rendered worthless, and they will be condemned to an eternal punishment in the Hellfire.
orig: ما كان للمشركين أن يعمروا مساجد الله شاهدين على أنفسهم بالكفر أولئك حبطت أعمالهم وفي النار هم خالدون

translation: The mosques of Allah are to be maintained by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, perform the prayer, and give the zakah and fear none but Allah. It is they who are expected to be on [right] guidance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the mosques are to be maintained and cared for by those who have true faith in Allah and the Hereafter, who regularly perform their prayers, give the obligatory charity (zakah), and fear none but Allah. These are the people who are expected to be rightly guided and on the path of salvation.
orig: إنما يعمر مساجد الله من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وأقام الصلاة وآتى الزكاة ولم يخش إلا الله فعسى أولئك أن يكونوا من المهتدين

translation: Have you made the providing of water for the pilgrims and the maintenance of al-Masjid al-Haram equal to [the deeds of] one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in the cause of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah. And Allah guides not the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse draws a distinction between those who engage in charitable acts, such as providing water for pilgrims or maintaining the sacred mosque, and those who have true faith in Allah and strive in His cause. The verse emphasizes that these two groups are not equal in the sight of Allah, as the latter group's deeds hold greater value and merit. The implication is that faith and righteous struggle are more important than outward acts of charity, and that Allah does not guide those who are wrongdoers, even if they engage in charitable acts.
orig: أجعلتم سقاية الحاج وعمارة المسجد الحرام كمن آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وجاهد في سبيل الله لا يستوون عند الله والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Those who have believed and emigrated and fought in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank in the sight of Allah. And it is those who are the attainers [of success].
interpretation: This verse highlights the high status and reward that Allah bestows upon those who have truly embraced faith, made sacrifices by leaving their homes, and strived in the cause of Allah through their wealth and lives. These individuals are described as being of the greatest rank before Allah, and they are the ones who will attain ultimate success and salvation.
orig: الذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم أعظم درجة عند الله وأولئك هم الفائزون

translation: Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him and [of] approval and [of] gardens for them wherein is enduring pleasure.
interpretation: This verse conveys the good news that Allah, the Lord of the believers, will bestow upon them His mercy, pleasure, and the eternal bliss of Paradise. The believers will enjoy a state of permanent and uninterrupted delight in the Gardens of Paradise.
orig: يبشرهم ربهم برحمة منه ورضوان وجنات لهم فيها نعيم مقيم

translation: Abiding therein forever. Indeed, Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse conveys the eternal nature of the reward in the Hereafter for those who believe and do righteous deeds. It emphasizes that Allah's reward is immense and beyond measure, as He has a "great reward" in store for His faithful servants.
orig: خالدين فيها أبدا إن الله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: O you who believe! Do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies if they have preferred disbelief over belief. And whoever of you does that - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to prioritize their faith over familial or tribal loyalties. It warns against blindly following one's relatives if they have chosen disbelief over belief, as that would be a form of injustice and wrongdoing. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining one's integrity and commitment to Islam, even if it means going against the preferences of those closest to you.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا آباءكم وإخوانكم أولياء إن استحبوا الكفر على الإيمان ومن يتولهم منكم فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: Say, "If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your relatives, wealth which you have obtained, commerce wherein you fear decline, and dwellings with which you are pleased are more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger and jihad in His cause, then wait until Allah executes His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing one's love and devotion to Allah and His cause over worldly attachments and desires. It warns against allowing family, wealth, or comfort to become more important than one's commitment to Allah and the struggle (jihad) in His path. The interpretation suggests that if a person's love for these worldly things surpasses their love for Allah and His Messenger, they will be left waiting for Allah's judgment, as He does not guide those who are defiantly disobedient.
orig: قل إن كان آباؤكم وأبناؤكم وإخوانكم وأزواجكم وعشيرتكم وأموال اقترفتموها وتجارة تخشون كسادها ومساكن ترضونها أحب إليكم من الله ورسوله وجهاد في سبيله فتربصوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: Certainly, Allah has helped you in many battlefields and [even] on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth was confining for you with [i.e., despite] its vastness, and you turned back [in retreat].
interpretation: This verse highlights how Allah's help and support can be crucial in battle, even when one's own strength and numbers appear overwhelming. The day of Hunayn is referenced, where the large Muslim army was initially overconfident, but this did not ultimately bring them victory. Instead, they faced difficulty and had to retreat, despite the vastness of the earth. This serves as a lesson that true success comes from Allah's aid, not just human capabilities alone.
orig: لقد نصركم الله في مواطن كثيرة ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم فلم تغن عنكم شيئا وضاقت عليكم الأرض بما رحبت ثم وليتم مدبرين

translation: Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down soldiers [i.e., angels] you did not see and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights how Allah provides His divine support and reassurance ("tranquility") to the Prophet and the believers, even when they face adversity from the disbelievers. It also emphasizes that Allah will punish those who reject faith, as that is the just consequence for their disbelief. The verse conveys the idea that Allah is always present, supporting the faithful and holding the disbelievers accountable.
orig: ثم أنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين وأنزل جنودا لم تروها وعذب الذين كفروا وذلك جزاء الكافرين

translation: Then Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills after that, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of Allah. After people have committed sins, Allah may still choose to forgive them if they sincerely repent. This highlights the compassionate nature of the Divine, who is willing to pardon those who seek His forgiveness, even after they have strayed from the righteous path.
orig: ثم يتوب الله من بعد ذلك على من يشاء والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who believe! The polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this their [final] year. And if you fear privation, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of ritual purity and the sanctity of the Sacred Mosque in Mecca. It declares that polytheists, who associate partners with Allah, are spiritually impure and should not be allowed to approach the Sacred Mosque. The verse also reassures the believers that if they fear poverty or hardship, Allah will provide for them from His abundant bounty, as He is All-Knowing and All-Wise in His decisions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إنما المشركون نجس فلا يقربوا المسجد الحرام بعد عامهم هذا وإن خفتم عيلة فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله إن شاء إن الله عليم حكيم

translation: Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture - [fight] until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to fight those who reject faith in Allah and the Day of Judgment, and who do not follow the rulings of Allah and His Messenger. It refers specifically to the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who are required to pay the jizyah tax and accept a subordinate status in the Islamic state.
orig: قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر ولا يحرمون ما حرم الله ورسوله ولا يدينون دين الحق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

translation: The Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." That is their statement from their mouths; they imitate the saying of those who disbelieved [before them]. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse condemns the claims made by the Jews and Christians that Ezra and the Messiah (Jesus) are the sons of God. It states that these are merely statements from their mouths, and they are imitating the disbelievers who made similar claims in the past. The verse expresses Allah's displeasure with these false claims and asks how the people can be so deluded to believe such falsehoods.
orig: وقالت اليهود عزير ابن الله وقالت النصارى المسيح ابن الله ذلك قولهم بأفواههم يضاهئون قول الذين كفروا من قبل قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون

translation: They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah, and [also] the Messiah, the son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of worshipping religious scholars and monks as gods, or elevating them to a status equal to God. It emphasizes that the true purpose of religion is to worship one God alone, the Almighty, who is free from any partners or associates. The verse serves as a reminder to focus one's devotion and obedience solely on the divine, and not to ascribe divinity to any created being, no matter how revered they may be.
orig: اتخذوا أحبارهم ورهبانهم أربابا من دون الله والمسيح ابن مريم وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا إلها واحدا لا إله إلا هو سبحانه عما يشركون

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This verse expresses that the disbelievers will try to suppress and undermine the truth of Islam, but Allah's light (guidance) will prevail and be perfected despite their efforts. It emphasizes that the truth of Islam will ultimately triumph over the opposition of the disbelievers.
orig: يريدون أن يطفئوا نور الله بأفواههم ويأبى الله إلا أن يتم نوره ولو كره الكافرون

translation: It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, although those who associate others with Allah dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has sent His Messenger (Prophet Muhammad) with the true guidance and the religion of truth (Islam) to make it prevail over all other religions, even if the polytheists and disbelievers dislike it. It is a declaration of the ultimate triumph of Islam over all other belief systems.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون

translation: O you who believe, indeed many of the scholars and the monks consume the wealth of people unjustly and avert [them] from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and spend it not in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns the greed and corruption of some religious leaders who misuse their positions to amass wealth and power at the expense of the people. It warns that those who hoard wealth instead of using it for the betterment of society will face a severe punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن كثيرا من الأحبار والرهبان ليأكلون أموال الناس بالباطل ويصدون عن سبيل الله والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله فبشرهم بعذاب أليم

translation: The Day when it will be heated in the Fire of Hell and their foreheads, their sides, and their backs will be branded with it. [This is] what you had hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard.
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment that awaits those who hoard wealth and do not fulfill their obligations to society. On the Day of Judgment, their ill-gotten gains will be used to brand and torment them in the Fire of Hell. This serves as a warning to those who prioritize worldly possessions over spiritual well-being and the welfare of others.
orig: يوم يحمى عليها في نار جهنم فتكوى بها جباههم وجنوبهم وظهورهم هذا ما كنزتم لأنفسكم فذوقوا ما كنتم تكنزون

translation: Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve [lunar] months in the register of Allah [from] the day He created the heavens and the earth; of these, four are sacred. That is the correct religion, so do not wrong yourselves during them. And fight against the disbelievers collectively as they fight against you collectively. And know that Allah is with the righteous [who fear Him].
interpretation: This verse establishes the Islamic lunar calendar, which has 12 months, 4 of which are sacred months. It emphasizes the importance of respecting these sacred months and not wronging oneself during them. It also calls upon the believers to fight against the disbelievers collectively, as the disbelievers fight against the believers. The verse ends with a reassurance that Allah is with the righteous who fear Him.
orig: إن عدة الشهور عند الله اثنا عشر شهرا في كتاب الله يوم خلق السماوات والأرض منها أربعة حرم ذلك الدين القيم فلا تظلموا فيهن أنفسكم وقاتلوا المشركين كافة كما يقاتلونكم كافة واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين

translation: The postponement (of a sacred month) is indeed an addition to disbelief: thereby the disbelievers are led astray. They allow it one year and forbid it (another) year, that they may agree in the number (of months) which Allah hath made sacred, and thus make lawful what Allah hath made unlawful. Evil seems fair to them. And Allah guideth not the disbelieving folk.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of postponing the sacred months, which was a pre-Islamic tradition among the Arabs. The postponement was done to accommodate their calendars and interests, but it was considered an addition to disbelief as it allowed them to make unlawful what Allah had made lawful, and vice versa. This practice led the disbelievers astray, as they would make their own decisions about the sanctity of the months based on their own whims, rather than following Allah's commandments. The verse emphasizes that Allah does not guide those who disbelieve and engage in such practices that go against His teachings.
orig: إنما النسيء زيادة في الكفر يضل به الذين كفروا يحلونه عاما ويحرمونه عاما ليواطئوا عدة ما حرم الله فيحلوا ما حرم الله زين لهم سوء أعمالهم والله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: O you who believe! What is [the matter] with you that, when you are told to go forth in the cause of Allah, you cling heavily to the earth? Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? But what is the enjoyment of worldly life compared to the Hereafter except a [very] little.
interpretation: This verse admonishes the believers for being reluctant to go forth and fight in the cause of Allah (i.e., participate in jihad). It criticizes them for being overly attached to the comforts and pleasures of this worldly life, at the expense of striving for the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes that the enjoyments of this world are insignificant compared to the rewards and blessings of the Hereafter, and that the believers should not be content with the temporary and fleeting nature of worldly life.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ما لكم إذا قيل لكم انفروا في سبيل الله اثاقلتم إلى الأرض أرضيتم بالحياة الدنيا من الآخرة فما متاع الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة إلا قليل

translation: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to participate in jihad and other efforts to support the cause of Islam. It warns that those who do not go forth will be punished, and that Allah will replace them with others who will carry out His will. The verse also emphasizes that believers cannot harm Allah in any way, as He is all-powerful and in control of all things.
orig: إلا تنفروا يعذبكم عذابا أليما ويستبدل قوما غيركم ولا تضروه شيئا والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: If you do not aid him - [i.e., the Prophet] - Allah has already aided him when those who disbelieved had driven him out [of Makkah] as one of two, when they were in the cave and he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." And Allah sent down his tranquility upon him and supported him with angels you did not see and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah - that is the highest. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse refers to the event when the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was forced to migrate from Makkah to Medina, and his close companion Abu Bakr accompanied him. They hid in a cave, and Allah protected them from their pursuers by sending down tranquility and angels to support them. This demonstrates that Allah is with those who believe in Him and support His cause, and that the ultimate victory belongs to the believers, no matter how dire the circumstances may seem. The interpretation highlights Allah's power, wisdom, and protection of the believers, as well as the ultimate triumph of the truth over falsehood.
orig: إلا تنصروه فقد نصره الله إذ أخرجه الذين كفروا ثاني اثنين إذ هما في الغار إذ يقول لصاحبه لا تحزن إن الله معنا فأنزل الله سكينته عليه وأيده بجنود لم تروها وجعل كلمة الذين كفروا السفلى وكلمة الله هي العليا والله عزيز حكيم

translation: Go forth, whether light or heavy, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of Allah. That is best for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to participate in jihad, whether they are physically fit or not, and to contribute their wealth and themselves to the cause of Allah. The interpretation is that this is the best course of action for the believers, if they only understood the true value and rewards of such sacrifices.
orig: انفروا خفافا وثقالا وجاهدوا بأموالكم وأنفسكم في سبيل الله ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: If it had been a near gain and an easy journey, they would have followed you, but the distance was too far for them. And they will swear by Allah, "If we had been able to, we would have gone forth with you." They destroy themselves, and Allah knows that they are liars.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who made excuses for not joining the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in a military expedition, despite being able-bodied and financially capable. The verse suggests that their reluctance was not due to genuine hardship, but rather a lack of sincerity and commitment to the cause. It highlights how they would make false oaths, claiming they would have joined if they could, when in reality they were simply unwilling to make the necessary sacrifices. The verse emphasizes that Allah knows the truth about their motives and that they are ultimately harming themselves by their deception.
orig: لو كان عرضا قريبا وسفرا قاصدا لاتبعوك ولكن بعدت عليهم الشقة وسيحلفون بالله لو استطعنا لخرجنا معكم يهلكون أنفسهم والله يعلم إنهم لكاذبون

translation: May Allah pardon you [O Muhammad]; why did you give them permission [to remain behind]? [You should not have] until it had become clear to you who were truthful and [until] you knew [who were] the liars.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of discernment and patience in dealing with people, especially in matters of faith and allegiance. It suggests that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) should not have given permission to some people to remain behind until he had clearly identified the truthful from the liars among them. The verse encourages careful assessment of people's intentions and actions, rather than hasty decisions or unwarranted leniency.
orig: عفا الله عنك لم أذنت لهم حتى يتبين لك الذين صدقوا وتعلم الكاذبين

translation: Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission [to be excused] from striving with their wealth and their lives. And Allah is Knowing of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true believers in God and the Hereafter do not seek exemption from the obligation to strive and sacrifice for the sake of their faith. They willingly and eagerly participate in jihad (spiritual and physical struggle) with their wealth and their lives, as this is a sign of their devotion and submission to the will of Allah. The verse also highlights that Allah is fully aware of those who are righteous and committed to His cause.
orig: لا يستأذنك الذين يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر أن يجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم والله عليم بالمتقين

translation: They only ask leave of thee who believe not in Allah and the Last Day, and whose hearts are in doubt, so that in their doubt they waver.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who do not believe in Allah and the Day of Judgment are the ones who seek permission from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to be exempted from certain religious obligations or responsibilities. Their hearts are filled with doubt and uncertainty, causing them to waver in their faith and commitment.
orig: إنما يستأذنك الذين لا يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر وارتابت قلوبهم فهم في ريبهم يترددون

translation: And if they had intended to go forth, they would have prepared for it [some] preparation. But Allah disliked their being sent, so He kept them back, and they were told, "Remain [behind] with those who remain."
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who were reluctant to participate in jihad should remain behind with those who are not able to fight, rather than making excuses to avoid their duty. Allah disapproved of their unwillingness to fight, and so they were told to stay behind with the non-combatants.
orig: ولو أرادوا الخروج لأعدوا له عدة ولكن كره الله انبعاثهم فثبطهم وقيل اقعدوا مع القاعدين

translation: If they had come out among you, they would not have increased you except in confusion, and they would have been active among you, seeking [to cause] you fitnah. And among you are avid listeners to them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who seek to sow discord and cause division within the community. It suggests that even if they were to join the community, their presence would not benefit it, but rather lead to confusion and strife. The verse also highlights the danger of those who would lend an ear to such disruptive elements, emphasizing that Allah is fully aware of the wrongdoers and their schemes.
orig: لو خرجوا فيكم ما زادوكم إلا خبالا ولأوضعوا خلالكم يبغونكم الفتنة وفيكم سماعون لهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: They had sought to cause dissension before, and they had upset matters for you until the truth came and the command of Allah appeared, while they were averse.
interpretation: This verse refers to the efforts of the disbelievers to create discord and obstacles for the Prophet Muhammad and the spread of Islam. Despite their attempts, the truth of Islam prevailed, and the command of Allah was established, even though they were unwilling to accept it.
orig: لقد ابتغوا الفتنة من قبل وقلبوا لك الأمور حتى جاء الحق وظهر أمر الله وهم كارهون

translation: And among them is he who says, "Permit me [to remain at home], and do not put me to trial." Unquestionably, into trial they have fallen. And indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse describes those who seek exemption from participating in the defense of the faith, fearing that they may be put to trial. However, the verse warns that by avoiding the trial, they have already fallen into the trial of cowardice and neglect of duty. The encompassing of the disbelievers by Hell is a consequence of their failure to stand firm in the face of adversity.
orig: ومنهم من يقول ائذن لي ولا تفتني ألا في الفتنة سقطوا وإن جهنم لمحيطة بالكافرين

translation: If good befalls you, it grieves them, but if a misfortune befalls you, they say: 'We took our precaution beforehand' and they turn away rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and envy of those who are quick to criticize and distance themselves from the believers when they face hardship, while taking pleasure in their misfortunes. It serves as a reminder that true faith and steadfastness are tested in times of difficulty, and that believers should remain steadfast in their beliefs regardless of the reactions of others.
orig: إن تصبك حسنة تسؤهم وإن تصبك مصيبة يقولوا قد أخذنا أمرنا من قبل ويتولوا وهم فرحون

translation: Say, "Never will we be struck except by what Allah has decreed for us; He is our protector." And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to put their trust in Allah and accept His divine decree. It reminds us that nothing can happen to us without Allah's permission, and that He is our protector and guardian. The interpretation emphasizes that the believers should rely on Allah and submit to His will, as He alone has control over our lives and destinies.
orig: قل لن يصيبنا إلا ما كتب الله لنا هو مولانا وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: Say, "Do you await for us except one of the two best things [i.e., martyrdom or victory], while we await for you that Allah will afflict you with punishment from Himself or at our hands? So wait; indeed, we are with you, waiting."
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the disbelievers who were persecuting the early Muslims. It conveys a message of steadfastness and determination from the Muslims, who are confident that they will either achieve victory or martyrdom, which are both considered "the best things" in the sight of God. The verse challenges the disbelievers to wait and see what will happen, as the Muslims are also waiting and prepared to face the consequences, whether it be punishment from God or at the hands of the believers. The interpretation emphasizes the unwavering faith and resolve of the Muslims in the face of adversity.
orig: قل هل تربصون بنا إلا إحدى الحسنيين ونحن نتربص بكم أن يصيبكم الله بعذاب من عنده أو بأيدينا فتربصوا إنا معكم متربصون

translation: Say, "Spend willingly or unwillingly; it will not be accepted from you. Indeed, you have been a defiantly disobedient people."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah does not accept any act of charity or good deeds if they are done unwillingly or with a reluctant heart. True faith and obedience to Allah require a willing and sincere submission, not just outward compliance. The verse also describes the people being addressed as "defiantly disobedient", indicating that their actions were not motivated by a genuine desire to please Allah, but rather by a rebellious spirit.
orig: قل أنفقوا طوعا أو كرها لن يتقبل منكم إنكم كنتم قوما فاسقين

translation: And what prevented their expenditures from being accepted from them is but that they have disbelieved in Allah and in His Messenger and that they come not to prayer except while they are lazy, and that they do not spend [for the cause of Allah] except while they are unwilling.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reasons why the expenditures of certain people were not accepted by Allah. The key reasons mentioned are: 1) Their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger, 2) Their laziness and reluctance in performing their obligatory prayers, and 3) Their unwillingness to spend in the cause of Allah. This indicates that true faith and sincerity are necessary prerequisites for one's deeds and charitable spending to be accepted by Allah.
orig: وما منعهم أن تقبل منهم نفقاتهم إلا أنهم كفروا بالله وبرسوله ولا يأتون الصلاة إلا وهم كسالى ولا ينفقون إلا وهم كارهون

translation: So let not their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through them in worldly life and that their souls should depart [at death] while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse cautions against being impressed or deceived by the wealth and children of the disbelievers. It explains that Allah intends to punish them through these worldly blessings, as their attachment to them will lead to the destruction of their souls in the afterlife due to their disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder that true worth is not measured by material possessions or family, but by one's faith and righteous deeds.
orig: فلا تعجبك أموالهم ولا أولادهم إنما يريد الله ليعذبهم بها في الحياة الدنيا وتزهق أنفسهم وهم كافرون

translation: And they swear by Allah that they are indeed of you. But they are not of you. Rather, they are a people who are afraid.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who outwardly claim to be part of the Muslim community, but inwardly harbor doubts and are afraid to fully commit to the faith. The verse emphasizes that their oaths of allegiance are not sincere, and that they are not truly a part of the believers, but rather a separate group who are driven by their own fears and insecurities.
orig: ويحلفون بالله إنهم لمنكم وما هم منكم ولكنهم قوم يفرقون

translation: And if they had found a refuge or caverns or a place to enter, they would have turned straight towards it while they rush headlong.
interpretation: This verse suggests that people often seek refuge or a safe place to escape from difficulties or dangers, even if it means acting hastily or recklessly. It highlights the human tendency to prioritize personal safety and security, even at the expense of caution or prudence.
orig: لو يجدون ملجأ أو مغارات أو مدخلا لولوا إليه وهم يجمحون

translation: And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities. If they are given from them, they are pleased; but if they are not given from them, at once they become angry.
interpretation: This verse describes the hypocritical attitude of some people towards charitable donations. They only approve of the charity when they themselves receive a share, but if they are not given anything, they become angry and critical. This highlights the need for sincerity and selflessness in acts of charity, rather than expecting personal benefit.
orig: ومنهم من يلمزك في الصدقات فإن أعطوا منها رضوا وإن لم يعطوا منها إذا هم يسخطون

translation: And if they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them and said, "Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us of His bounty, and [so will] His Messenger, [then] we will be satisfied."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be content with what Allah and His Messenger have provided, and to trust that Allah will grant them more from His bounty. It emphasizes the importance of being satisfied with one"s circumstances and having faith that Allah will provide for them, rather than being discontent or demanding more than what has been given.
orig: ولو أنهم رضوا ما آتاهم الله ورسوله وقالوا حسبنا الله سيؤتينا الله من فضله ورسوله إنا إلى الله راغبون

translation: Zakah expenditures are only for the poor and for the needy and for those employed to collect [zakah] and for bringing hearts together [for Islam] and for freeing captives [or slaves] and for those in debt and for the cause of Allah and for the [stranded] traveler - an obligation [imposed] by Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse outlines the legitimate recipients of zakah (obligatory Islamic charity). It emphasizes that zakah should be distributed to the poor, the needy, those employed to collect it, those whose hearts are to be reconciled to Islam, those in bondage, those in debt, those fighting for the cause of Allah, and the stranded traveler. This is an obligation prescribed by Allah, and He is All-Knowing and Wise in His commandments.
orig: إنما الصدقات للفقراء والمساكين والعاملين عليها والمؤلفة قلوبهم وفي الرقاب والغارمين وفي سبيل الله وابن السبيل فريضة من الله والله عليم حكيم

translation: And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say, "He is an ear [i.e., he listens to everyone]." Say, "[He is] an ear of goodness for you - he believes in Allah and believes the believers and is a mercy to those who believe among you." And for those who harm the Messenger of Allah, there is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who harm the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and accuse him of being someone who listens to everyone without discernment. The Qur'an refutes this claim, stating that the Prophet is an "ear of goodness" - he believes in Allah and the believers, and is a mercy to those who believe. However, it also warns that those who harm the Messenger of Allah will face a painful punishment. This highlights the importance of respecting and honoring the Prophet, as he is a conduit of Allah's guidance and mercy to humanity.
orig: ومنهم الذين يؤذون النبي ويقولون هو أذن قل أذن خير لكم يؤمن بالله ويؤمن للمؤمنين ورحمة للذين آمنوا منكم والذين يؤذون رسول الله لهم عذاب أليم

translation: They swear by Allah to you [Muslims] to please you, but Allah and His Messenger are more worthy for them to please, if they should [truly] be believers.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against being swayed by the oaths and claims of hypocrites who seek to win the believers' favor, even though their true allegiance should be to Allah and His Messenger. The true test of faith is not in outward displays of piety, but in sincerely submitting to the will of Allah and His Messenger.
orig: يحلفون بالله لكم ليرضوكم والله ورسوله أحق أن يرضوه إن كانوا مؤمنين

translation: Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger - that for him is the fire of Hell, wherein he will abide eternally? That is the great humiliation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who defy and oppose Allah and His Messenger will be condemned to the eternal punishment of Hell, which is the ultimate disgrace and humiliation. The verse serves as a stark warning against defiance and rebellion against the divine commands and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad.
orig: ألم يعلموا أنه من يحادد الله ورسوله فأن له نار جهنم خالدا فيها ذلك الخزي العظيم

translation: The hypocrites are afraid that a surah will be sent down about them, informing them of what is in their hearts. Say, "Mock, for indeed, Allah will expose what you fear."
interpretation: This verse warns the hypocrites, who outwardly profess faith but inwardly harbor disbelief, that they should not fear the revelation of a surah that will expose the true state of their hearts. The interpretation is that Allah will inevitably bring to light the hidden realities within the hypocrites, and they should not think they can conceal their true nature from Him.
orig: يحذر المنافقون أن تنزل عليهم سورة تنبئهم بما في قلوبهم قل استهزئوا إن الله مخرج ما تحذرون

translation: And if you ask them, they will surely say, "We were only conversing and playing." Say, "Is it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?"
interpretation: This verse condemns those who make light of the signs and messages of Allah, treating them as mere entertainment or idle chatter. The interpretation is that one should take the teachings of Islam seriously and not dismiss them as mere play or jest, for to do so is to mock the divine.
orig: ولئن سألتهم ليقولن إنما كنا نخوض ونلعب قل أبالله وآياته ورسوله كنتم تستهزئون

translation: Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief. If We pardon a party of you, We will punish another party because they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of disbelief after having accepted faith. It suggests that there is no room for making excuses, as disbelief after belief is a serious offense. The verse indicates that some may be forgiven, while others will be punished for their criminal actions, highlighting the consequences of turning away from faith.
orig: لا تعتذروا قد كفرتم بعد إيمانكم إن نعف عن طائفة منكم نعذب طائفة بأنهم كانوا مجرمين

translation: The hypocrites, men and women, are from one another. They enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right and close their hands. They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them. Indeed, the hypocrites - it is they who are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of the hypocrites, those who outwardly profess faith but inwardly conceal disbelief. They work together to promote evil and prevent good, being stingy with their wealth and support. They have forgotten Allah, and as a result, Allah has forsaken them. This verse emphasizes that the hypocrites are the truly disobedient ones, far from the path of righteousness.
orig: المنافقون والمنافقات بعضهم من بعض يأمرون بالمنكر وينهون عن المعروف ويقبضون أيديهم نسوا الله فنسيهم إن المنافقين هم الفاسقون

translation: Allah has promised the hypocrites, men and women, and the disbelievers, the Fire of Hell, wherein they will abide eternally. It is sufficient for them. And Allah has cursed them, and for them is an enduring punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the hypocrites and disbelievers, who will face an eternal punishment in the Fire of Hell. Their fate is sealed, and they will have no escape from this torment, which is a fitting consequence for their rejection of faith and their deeds. The verse emphasizes the finality and severity of their punishment, which is a result of Allah's curse and condemnation.
orig: وعد الله المنافقين والمنافقات والكفار نار جهنم خالدين فيها هي حسبهم ولعنهم الله ولهم عذاب مقيم

translation: Like those before you; they were mightier than you in power and had more wealth and children. So they enjoyed their portion [of worldly pleasures], and you have enjoyed your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion, and you have engaged [in vanities] like that in which they engaged. [Thus] those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and in the Hereafter, and it is they who are the [actual] losers.
interpretation: This verse draws a parallel between the previous generations and the current one, highlighting that both have indulged in the pursuit of worldly pleasures and neglected the more important spiritual aspects of life.
