The verse serves as a warning that such a lifestyle leads to the nullification of one's deeds, both in this life and the Hereafter, resulting in ultimate loss. The message is to learn from the mistakes of the past and focus on righteous actions that will benefit one in the afterlife.
orig: كالذين من قبلكم كانوا أشد منكم قوة وأكثر أموالا وأولادا فاستمتعوا بخلاقهم فاستمتعتم بخلاقكم كما استمتع الذين من قبلكم بخلاقهم وخضتم كالذي خاضوا أولئك حبطت أعمالهم في الدنيا والآخرة وأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: Has there not reached them the news of those before them - the people of Noah and [the tribes of] 'Aad and Thamud and the people of Abraham and the companions of Madyan and the overturned cities? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. And Allah would not have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the fate that befell previous nations who rejected the messengers sent to them by Allah. It emphasizes that these nations were not wronged by Allah, but rather they wronged themselves by disbelieving and disobeying the divine guidance. The verse encourages the reader to learn from the lessons of history and not to repeat the mistakes of those who came before, lest they suffer a similar fate.
orig: ألم يأتهم نبأ الذين من قبلهم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود وقوم إبراهيم وأصحاب مدين والمؤتفكات أتتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those - Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and mutual support among the believers, both men and women. It outlines the key characteristics of the believers, including their commitment to promoting good, forbidding evil, performing their religious obligations such as prayer and charity, and obeying Allah and His Messenger. This mutual support and righteous conduct will be rewarded with Allah's mercy, as He is All-Mighty and All-Wise in His judgments.
orig: والمؤمنون والمؤمنات بعضهم أولياء بعض يأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر ويقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة ويطيعون الله ورسوله أولئك سيرحمهم الله إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and blessed dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence, and approval from Allah is greater. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse promises the believers, both men and women, that they will be granted eternal abode in the Gardens of Paradise, where they will dwell forever. The Gardens will be filled with blessings, including flowing rivers and beautiful dwellings. This is the greatest achievement and success that one can attain, as it comes with the approval and pleasure of Allah, the Almighty.
orig: وعد الله المؤمنين والمؤمنات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ورضوان من الله أكبر ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: O Prophet, fight against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse calls on the Prophet Muhammad to confront and fight against those who openly reject faith in God (the disbelievers) as well as those who outwardly profess faith but inwardly harbor doubts and opposition (the hypocrites). The Prophet is instructed to be firm and unyielding in his dealings with them, as their ultimate destination is the eternal torment of Hell, which is a most wretched end.
orig: يا أيها النبي جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: They swear by Allah that they did not say [anything against the Prophet], while they had said the word of disbelief, and they disbelieved after their [pretense of] Islam and planned that which they were not [able to] attain. And they were not resentful except [for the fact] that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty. So if they repent, it will be better for them; but if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will not have in the earth any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse condemns the hypocrites who swear falsely by Allah, claiming they did not speak against the Prophet, when in fact they had uttered words of disbelief and turned away from Islam. Their true motive was jealousy and resentment that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them. The verse warns that if they do not repent, they will face a painful punishment in this life and the Hereafter, as they will have no one to protect or help them.
orig: يحلفون بالله ما قالوا ولقد قالوا كلمة الكفر وكفروا بعد إسلامهم وهموا بما لم ينالوا وما نقموا إلا أن أغناهم الله ورسوله من فضله فإن يتوبوا يك خيرا لهم وإن يتولوا يعذبهم الله عذابا أليما في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم في الأرض من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And among them is he who makes a covenant with Allah, [saying], "If He should give us from His bounty, we will surely spend in charity, and we will surely be among the righteous."
interpretation: This verse speaks of those who make a promise to Allah that if He bestows His blessings upon them, they will give in charity and strive to be among the righteous. It highlights the importance of gratitude and doing good deeds in response to the favors received from Allah.
orig: ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا من فضله لنصدقن ولنكونن من الصالحين

translation: But when He gave them of His bounty, they hoarded it and turned away, and they are averse.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of some people to become stingy and turn away from God when they are granted His blessings and provisions. It suggests that true gratitude and humility should accompany the reception of God's gifts, rather than greed and self-absorption.
orig: فلما آتاهم من فضله بخلوا به وتولوا وهم معرضون

translation: And He caused hypocrisy to follow into their hearts until the Day they will meet Him - for what they had [gradually] broken of their [own] promises and because they were liars.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the people who broke their promises to God and were liars were subsequently afflicted with hypocrisy in their hearts. This hypocrisy will remain with them until the Day of Judgment, when they will have to account for their deeds. The interpretation suggests that breaking one's word to God and being dishonest are grave sins that can lead to the development of hypocrisy within the heart, which is a spiritual disease that will have lasting consequences.
orig: فأعقبهم نفاقا في قلوبهم إلى يوم يلقونه بما أخلفوا الله ما وعدوه وبما كانوا يكذبون

translation: Have they not known that Allah knows their secret and their private conversation, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has knowledge of all things, even the most private and hidden aspects of people's lives. It serves as a reminder that we cannot hide anything from Allah, and that He is aware of our innermost thoughts, secrets, and conversations. This knowledge should inspire us to be mindful of our actions and to seek Allah's pleasure in all that we do.
orig: ألم يعلموا أن الله يعلم سرهم ونجواهم وأن الله علام الغيوب

translation: Those who criticize the charitable contributors among the believers and [thus] mock those who find nothing [to spend] except their [meager] efforts - so Allah has mocked them, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who mock or criticize believers who contribute charitably according to their means, even if their contributions are small. It emphasizes that Allah will mock those who mock the sincere efforts of the believers, and they will face a painful punishment.
orig: الذين يلمزون المطوعين من المؤمنين في الصدقات والذين لا يجدون إلا جهدهم فيسخرون منهم سخر الله منهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Whether you ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them, if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them. That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of disbelief in Allah and His Messenger. Even if the Prophet (peace be upon him) were to seek forgiveness for the disbelievers seventy times, Allah would not forgive them. This is because their rejection of faith is a fundamental rejection of Allah and His guidance, and Allah does not guide those who persistently disobey Him.
orig: استغفر لهم أو لا تستغفر لهم إن تستغفر لهم سبعين مرة فلن يغفر الله لهم ذلك بأنهم كفروا بالله ورسوله والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: Those who lagged behind [in the Jihad] rejoiced in their staying [at home] behind the Messenger of Allah and disliked to strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah and said, "Do not go forth in the heat." Say, "The fire of Hell is more intense in heat" - if they would but understand.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who refused to participate in the jihad (holy struggle) alongside the Prophet Muhammad, and instead preferred to remain behind. They were unwilling to sacrifice their wealth and lives for the cause of Allah. The verse emphasizes that the torment of Hell is far more severe than the heat they feared, if only they had the wisdom to understand.
orig: فرح المخلفون بمقعدهم خلاف رسول الله وكرهوا أن يجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله وقالوا لا تنفروا في الحر قل نار جهنم أشد حرا لو كانوا يفقهون

translation: Then let them laugh a little and [then] weep much as a recompense for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who have earned punishment in the afterlife will first laugh a little, perhaps out of denial or disbelief, but then will weep extensively as they face the consequences of their misdeeds. The laughter is short-lived, while the weeping is prolonged, indicating the gravity of their situation and the severity of the recompense they will receive.
orig: فليضحكوا قليلا وليبكوا كثيرا جزاء بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And if Allah brings you back to [contact with] a party of them [i.e., the hypocrites] and they ask your permission to go out [to battle], say, "You will not go out with me, ever, and you will never fight with me against an enemy. Indeed, you were satisfied with sitting [at home] the first time, so sit [now] with those who stay behind."
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, instructing him on how to deal with the hypocrites who had previously refused to join him in battle. The verse emphasizes that if these hypocrites ever seek permission to join the fighting, the Prophet should deny them, as they had already shown their unwillingness to participate and their preference to remain behind. The interpretation suggests that the Prophet should not trust these individuals or allow them to join the fighting, as their past actions have demonstrated their lack of commitment to the cause.
orig: فإن رجعك الله إلى طائفة منهم فاستأذنوك للخروج فقل لن تخرجوا معي أبدا ولن تقاتلوا معي عدوا إنكم رضيتم بالقعود أول مرة فاقعدوا مع الخالفين

translation: And do not pray [the funeral prayer, O Muhammad], over any of them who has died - ever - or stand at his grave. Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died while they were defivers.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to pray the funeral prayer over those who disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and not to stand at their graves. This is because they died in a state of disbelief and disobedience to Allah, and thus do not deserve the prayers and supplications of the believers.
orig: ولا تصل على أحد منهم مات أبدا ولا تقم على قبره إنهم كفروا بالله ورسوله وماتوا وهم فاسقون

translation: And let not their wealth and their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through them in worldly life and that their souls should depart [at death] while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against being impressed or deceived by the material wealth and offspring of the disbelievers. It emphasizes that Allah uses these worldly possessions as a means to punish them in this life, as their souls will depart while they remain in a state of disbelief. The true believers should not be distracted by the outward appearances of the disbelievers, but rather focus on their ultimate fate in the Hereafter.
orig: ولا تعجبك أموالهم وأولادهم إنما يريد الله أن يعذبهم بها في الدنيا وتزهق أنفسهم وهم كافرون

translation: And when a surah is revealed, [in which it is said], "Believe in Allah and fight alongside His Messenger," the wealthy among them ask your permission [to be exempted] and say, "Leave us [i.e., exempt us] to be with those who remain [behind]."
interpretation: This verse highlights the reluctance of the wealthy and privileged members of society to participate in the struggle (jihad) alongside the Prophet and the believers. They seek exemption, preferring to remain behind with those who do not take part in the fight for the cause of Allah. This reflects a lack of commitment and a desire to prioritize their own comfort and status over the demands of faith and the needs of the community.
orig: وإذا أنزلت سورة أن آمنوا بالله وجاهدوا مع رسوله استأذنك أولو الطول منهم وقالوا ذرنا نكن مع القاعدين

translation: They were pleased to be with those who remained behind, and their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand.
interpretation: This verse describes those who were content to remain behind and not participate in the struggle for the faith. Their hearts were sealed, meaning they were unable to comprehend the deeper spiritual significance of the situation. This suggests a lack of understanding and commitment to the true principles of Islam.
orig: رضوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالف وطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يفقهون

translation: But the Messenger and those who believed with him fought with their wealth and their lives. And those are the ones who will have [all that is] good, and it is those who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sacrifice and struggle in the path of faith. It highlights that the Prophet Muhammad and his companions not only believed in the message, but also actively fought and sacrificed their wealth and lives for its sake. This level of commitment and dedication is what leads to true success and the attainment of all that is good, both in this life and the hereafter.
orig: لكن الرسول والذين آمنوا معه جاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم وأولئك لهم الخيرات وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse promises the believers a reward in the Hereafter - the eternal bliss of Paradise, where they will live forever in gardens with flowing rivers. This is the ultimate success and triumph that awaits those who have faith and do righteous deeds.
orig: أعد الله لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And the desert Arabs came to make excuses; and they who had lied to Allah and His Messenger sat (at home). A painful punishment will afflict those of them who disbelieved.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Bedouin Arabs who made excuses for not participating in the battles against the disbelievers. It highlights the contrast between those who made excuses and those who outright rejected the message of Islam. The interpretation is that those who reject the truth of Islam will face a painful punishment from Allah.
orig: وجاء المعذرون من الأعراب ليؤذن لهم وقعد الذين كذبوا الله ورسوله سيصيب الذين كفروا منهم عذاب أليم

translation: There is not upon the weak or upon the ill or upon those who do not find anything to spend any discomfort when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger. And there is not upon the doers of good any cause [for blame]. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are unable to contribute financially, such as the weak, the ill, or the poor, are not held accountable if they are sincere in their faith and devotion to Allah and His Messenger. The verse also reassures the doers of good that they will not be blamed, as Allah is Forgiving and Merciful towards those who strive to please Him.
orig: ليس على الضعفاء ولا على المرضى ولا على الذين لا يجدون ما ينفقون حرج إذا نصحوا لله ورسوله ما على المحسنين من سبيل والله غفور رحيم

translation: Nor [is there blame] upon those who, when they came to you that you might give them mounts, you said, "I can find nothing for you to ride upon." They turned back while their eyes overflowed with tears out of grief that they could not find something to spend [for the cause of Allah].
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation where people came to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) seeking his help and support, but he was unable to provide them with what they needed. The verse emphasizes that there is no blame on those who were unable to contribute financially to the cause of Allah, even though they wished to do so. The verse highlights the sincerity of their intentions and the sorrow they felt at not being able to participate, as evidenced by their tears. The interpretation is that Allah understands the constraints and limitations of His servants, and does not hold them accountable for what they are unable to do, as long as their intentions are pure.
orig: ولا على الذين إذا ما أتوك لتحملهم قلت لا أجد ما أحملكم عليه تولوا وأعينهم تفيض من الدمع حزنا ألا يجدوا ما ينفقون

translation: The blame is only upon those who ask your permission [to not participate] while they are rich. They have been satisfied to be with those who stay behind, and Allah has sealed over their hearts, so they do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the blame and responsibility falls upon those who, despite being wealthy and capable of contributing, seek exemption from participating in righteous causes or fulfilling their duties. They are content to remain with those who stay behind, and Allah has sealed their hearts, preventing them from understanding the importance of their obligations.
orig: إنما السبيل على الذين يستأذنونك وهم أغنياء رضوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالف وطبع الله على قلوبهم فهم لا يعلمون

translation: They will make excuses to you when you have returned to them. Say, "Make no excuses; we will never believe you. Allah has already made known to us your circumstances." And Allah will observe your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger; then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the believers, instructing them not to accept the excuses of those who had turned away from the faith. The interpretation is that Allah and His Messenger are fully aware of the circumstances and actions of the people, and that they will ultimately be held accountable for their deeds, whether hidden or apparent. The believers are advised to remain firm in their faith and not be swayed by the insincere pleas of those who had previously rejected the truth.
orig: يعتذرون إليكم إذا رجعتم إليهم قل لا تعتذروا لن نؤمن لكم قد نبأنا الله من أخباركم وسيرى الله عملكم ورسوله ثم تردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: They will swear by Allah to you, [O believers], when you return to them, that you may turn away from them. So turn away from them. Indeed, they are unclean, and their refuge is Hell, as recompense for what they had been earning.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against the hypocrites who will swear oaths to them in order to turn them away from the truth. The believers are instructed to turn away from them, for the hypocrites are spiritually impure and their ultimate destination is Hell, which they have earned through their misdeeds.
orig: سيحلفون بالله لكم إذا انقلبتم إليهم لتعرضوا عنهم فأعرضوا عنهم إنهم رجس ومأواهم جهنم جزاء بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: They swear to you that you may be pleased with them, but if you are pleased with them - indeed, Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse warns against being deceived by the oaths and outward displays of those who claim to be believers, but whose actions and inner states are corrupt. Even if they manage to convince you of their sincerity, Allah is not pleased with those who are defiantly disobedient and whose hearts are not truly aligned with faith.
orig: يحلفون لكم لترضوا عنهم فإن ترضوا عنهم فإن الله لا يرضى عن القوم الفاسقين

translation: The desert Arabs are the most stubborn in disbelief and hypocrisy, and more likely to be ignorant of the limits [i.e., laws] which Allah has revealed to His Messenger. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual condition of the desert Arabs, who are described as being the most stubborn in their disbelief and hypocrisy. They are also more likely to be ignorant of the divine laws and commandments revealed by Allah to His Messenger. The verse emphasizes that Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise, and His judgment of the desert Arabs is based on His perfect knowledge and wisdom.
orig: الأعراب أشد كفرا ونفاقا وأجدر ألا يعلموا حدود ما أنزل الله على رسوله والله عليم حكيم

translation: And among the bedouins are some who consider what they spend as a loss and await for your misfortunes. Upon them will be the [entire] misfortune. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse condemns those hypocrites among the nomadic Arabs who view their charitable contributions as a burden and eagerly await calamities to befall the believers. However, the verse warns that the misfortune will ultimately return to them, for Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing of their malicious intentions.
orig: ومن الأعراب من يتخذ ما ينفق مغرما ويتربص بكم الدوائر عليهم دائرة السوء والله سميع عليم

translation: And among the bedouins are some who believe in Allah and the Last Day and take what they spend as [means of] nearness to Allah and the invocations of the Messenger. Unquestionably, it is a [means of] nearness for them. [The] Allah will admit them into His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights that even among the nomadic Arab tribes, there are those who sincerely believe in Allah and the Day of Judgment, and they spend their wealth charitably as a means of seeking closeness to Allah and honoring the teachings of the Prophet. This act of charity and devotion will be a means of attaining Allah's mercy and forgiveness, for Allah is all-Forgiving and all-Merciful.
orig: ومن الأعراب من يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر ويتخذ ما ينفق قربات عند الله وصلوات الرسول ألا إنها قربة لهم سيدخلهم الله في رحمته إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And the first forerunners [in the faith] among the Muhajireen and the Ansar and those who followed them with good conduct - Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the highest and most virtuous of the Prophet's companions - the first to accept Islam, the Muhajireen (those who migrated with the Prophet from Mecca to Medina) and the Ansar (the Medinans who welcomed and supported the Muhajireen). It praises their steadfast faith, their good deeds, and the mutual pleasure between them and Allah. As a reward, Allah has prepared for them the eternal bliss of Paradise, where they will dwell forever. This highlights the great status and reward for those who are the earliest and most devoted followers of the Prophet.
orig: والسابقون الأولون من المهاجرين والأنصار والذين اتبعوهم بإحسان رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه وأعد لهم جنات تجري تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And among those around you of the bedouins are hypocrites, and [also] from the people of Medina. They have become accustomed to hypocrisy. You, [O Muhammad], do not know them. [But] We know them. We will punish them twice [in this world]; then they will be returned to a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the prevalence of hypocrisy among the bedouins and the people of Medina. It indicates that some of them have become habitual hypocrites, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) is not fully aware of their true nature. However, Allah knows them well and will punish them twice in this world, before they face a severe punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: وممن حولكم من الأعراب منافقون ومن أهل المدينة مردوا على النفاق لا تعلمهم نحن نعلمهم سنعذبهم مرتين ثم يردون إلى عذاب عظيم

translation: And [there are] others who have acknowledged their sins. They had mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad. Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse speaks of those who have acknowledged their sins, but have also done some good deeds along with their wrongdoings. The verse suggests that Allah may forgive them, as He is Forgiving and Merciful. The interpretation is that even those who have a mix of good and bad deeds in their lives can be forgiven by Allah, if they sincerely repent and seek His forgiveness.
orig: وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Take, [O Muhammad], from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to increase, and invoke [Allah 's blessings] upon them. Indeed, your invocations are reassurance for them. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to collect charity from the wealth of the people, which will purify them from their sins and increase their good deeds. The Prophet (peace be upon him) is instructed to pray for them, as his prayers will provide them with peace and tranquility. Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, and He is aware of the intentions and actions of the people.
orig: خذ من أموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها وصل عليهم إن صلاتك سكن لهم والله سميع عليم

translation: Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and receives [voluntary] charities and that it is Allah who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the One who accepts the repentance of His servants and receives their charitable donations. It highlights Allah"s attribute of being the Oft-Returning, the Merciful, who readily forgives those who turn to Him in sincere repentance and who appreciates the good deeds of His servants.
orig: ألم يعلموا أن الله هو يقبل التوبة عن عباده ويأخذ الصدقات وأن الله هو التواب الرحيم

translation: And say, "Do [as you will], for Allah will see your deeds, and [so, will] His Messenger and the believers. And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to do good deeds, as they will be held accountable for their actions. It reminds us that Allah, His Messenger, and the believers are all aware of our deeds. Ultimately, we will all return to Allah, who knows both the seen and unseen, and He will inform us of what we used to do in this life.
orig: وقل اعملوا فسيرى الله عملكم ورسوله والمؤمنون وستردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And [there are] others who are awaiting the decree of Allah. Either He will punish them or He will turn to them [in forgiveness]. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are uncertain about their fate, whether they will be punished or forgiven by Allah. It emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and wise in His judgement, and that the ultimate decision rests with Him. The verse encourages believers to have faith in Allah's justice and to strive to please Him, rather than being complacent about their spiritual state.
orig: وآخرون مرجون لأمر الله إما يعذبهم وإما يتوب عليهم والله عليم حكيم

translation: And those who took for themselves a mosque for causing harm and disbelief and division among the believers and as a station for whoever had warred against Allah and His Messenger before. And they will surely swear, "We intended only the best." And Allah testifies that indeed they are liars.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who have built a mosque with the intention of causing harm, disbelief, and division among the believers, as well as providing a base for those who have fought against Allah and His Messenger. Despite their claims of good intentions, Allah testifies that they are liars, as their actions clearly demonstrate their true motives.
orig: والذين اتخذوا مسجدا ضرارا وكفرا وتفريقا بين المؤمنين وإرصادا لمن حارب الله ورسوله من قبل وليحلفن إن أردنا إلا الحسنى والله يشهد إنهم لكاذبون

translation: Never stand in it. A mosque founded on righteousness from the first day is more worthy for you to stand in. Within it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves.
interpretation: This verse encourages the establishment and frequenting of mosques that are built upon the principles of piety and righteousness. It suggests that such mosques are more deserving of one's presence and devotion, as they attract people who are committed to spiritual purification and cleanliness, which is pleasing to Allah.
orig: لا تقم فيه أبدا لمسجد أسس على التقوى من أول يوم أحق أن تقوم فيه فيه رجال يحبون أن يتطهروا والله يحب المطهرين

translation: Is one who founds his building on righteousness [with fear] of Allah and [His] approval better or one who founds his structure on the edge of a bank about to collapse, so it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse draws a clear contrast between two types of people: those who build their lives on a foundation of righteousness and God's approval, and those who build on a shaky foundation of sin and worldly pursuits. The former is described as better, as their structure will stand firm, while the latter will inevitably collapse into the fire of Hell. This highlights the importance of building one's life on a solid spiritual foundation, grounded in the fear and approval of Allah, rather than on the shifting sands of transient desires and worldly attachments.
orig: أفمن أسس بنيانه على تقوى من الله ورضوان خير أم من أسس بنيانه على شفا جرف هار فانهار به في نار جهنم والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Their building which they built will not cease to be a cause of skepticism in their hearts until their hearts are torn [i.e., they die]. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the doubts and skepticism that the disbelievers harbor in their hearts regarding the truth of Islam will persist until their death, as their hearts are not inclined to accept the truth. Allah, being All-Knowing and All-Wise, is aware of their condition and will judge them accordingly.
orig: لا يزال بنيانهم الذي بنوا ريبة في قلوبهم إلا أن تقطع قلوبهم والله عليم حكيم

translation: Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties [in exchange] for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed. [It is] a true promise [binding] upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than Allah? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And that is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that Allah has made a covenant with the believers, wherein they pledge their lives and wealth in His cause, and in return, they are promised Paradise. The believers are encouraged to fight in the way of Allah, even if it means that they may be killed or kill others. This promise is affirmed in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an, making it a binding and true commitment from Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's covenant with Allah, and the believers are exhorted to rejoice in this transaction, as it will lead to the greatest success and attainment.
orig: إن الله اشترى من المؤمنين أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة يقاتلون في سبيل الله فيقتلون ويقتلون وعدا عليه حقا في التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن ومن أوفى بعهده من الله فاستبشروا ببيعكم الذي بايعتم به وذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers, the travelers, the bowers, the prostrators, the enjoiners of what is right and the forbidders of what is wrong, and the keepers of the limits [set by] Allah. And give good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of the faithful believers. They are those who constantly repent and seek forgiveness, who are devoted in their worship and praise of God, who are ever-traveling in the path of God, who humbly bow and prostrate before God, and who strive to promote good and forbid evil in society. They are the ones who uphold the limits and boundaries set by God, and for them, the believers, there is a glad tiding of success and reward in the Hereafter.
orig: التائبون العابدون الحامدون السائحون الراكعون الساجدون الآمرون بالمعروف والناهون عن المنكر والحافظون لحدود الله وبشر المؤمنين

translation: It is not (proper) for the Prophet and those who believe to ask Allah's forgiveness for the Mushrikun (polytheists, idolaters, pagans, disbelievers in the Oneness of Allah), even though they be of kin, after it has become clear to them that they are the dwellers of the (Hell) Fire.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers are not permitted to seek forgiveness for those who associate partners with Allah, even if they are their close relatives. This is because it has become clear that those who commit shirk (polytheism) are destined for the Hellfire, and it would not be appropriate to ask for forgiveness on their behalf.
orig: ما كان للنبي والذين آمنوا أن يستغفروا للمشركين ولو كانوا أولي قربى من بعد ما تبين لهم أنهم أصحاب الجحيم

translation: And Abraham's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Abraham was compassionate and patient.
interpretation: This verse highlights Abraham's compassion and patience, even towards his own father. Initially, Abraham had promised his father that he would seek forgiveness for him. However, when it became clear that his father was an enemy of Allah, Abraham disassociated himself from him. This demonstrates Abraham's unwavering commitment to the truth and his willingness to put his faith above familial ties. The verse also emphasizes Abraham's compassionate and patient nature, as he continued to seek forgiveness for his father despite the latter's rejection of the true faith.
orig: وما كان استغفار إبراهيم لأبيه إلا عن موعدة وعدها إياه فلما تبين له أنه عدو لله تبرأ منه إن إبراهيم لأواه حليم

translation: And Allah would not let a people stray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah does not lead people astray after guiding them, unless they choose to stray themselves. Allah provides clear guidance to people so that they may know what to avoid and what to follow. This highlights Allah's mercy and justice, as He does not punish people without first making the path of righteousness clear to them.
orig: وما كان الله ليضل قوما بعد إذ هداهم حتى يبين لهم ما يتقون إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Indeed, Allah has sovereignty over the heavens and the earth; He gives life and causes death, and you have not besides Allah any protector or any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over the entire universe. He alone has the authority to give life and cause death, and there is no one else who can provide protection or assistance besides Him. This affirms the belief in the Oneness of Allah and the need to worship and submit to Him alone.
orig: إن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض يحيي ويميت وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Indeed, Allah has already forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajirun and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of difficulty after the hearts of a party of them had almost inclined [to doubt], and then He forgave them. Indeed, He is to them Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse speaks of Allah's forgiveness and mercy towards the Prophet Muhammad, the Muhajirun (the early Muslim emigrants from Mecca to Medina), and the Ansar (the Medinan supporters of the Prophet). Despite the difficulties they faced, and the doubts that crept into the hearts of some of them, Allah forgave them and showed them His kindness and mercy. This highlights the importance of perseverance and faith in times of hardship, and the boundless compassion of Allah towards those who strive in His cause.
orig: لقد تاب الله على النبي والمهاجرين والأنصار الذين اتبعوه في ساعة العسرة من بعد ما كاد يزيغ قلوب فريق منهم ثم تاب عليهم إنه بهم رءوف رحيم

translation: And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind [and regretted their error] to the point that the earth closed in on them despite its vastness, and their souls confined them, and they were certain that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them so they could repent. Indeed, it is Allah who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse describes the forgiveness that Allah extended to three individuals who had initially failed to join the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in a military campaign. Despite their initial reluctance, they later realized their mistake and felt remorse. The verse emphasizes that even when the situation seems dire and one feels trapped, true repentance and turning to Allah can lead to His forgiveness and mercy.
orig: وعلى الثلاثة الذين خلفوا حتى إذا ضاقت عليهم الأرض بما رحبت وضاقت عليهم أنفسهم وظنوا أن لا ملجأ من الله إلا إليه ثم تاب عليهم ليتوبوا إن الله هو التواب الرحيم

translation: O you who believe! Fear Allah and be with those who are true (in word and deed).
interpretation: This verse calls upon believers to be mindful of Allah and to associate with those who are truthful and sincere in their faith. It encourages believers to cultivate righteousness, integrity and honesty in their conduct, and to seek the company of others who embody these virtues.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وكونوا مع الصادقين

translation: It was not [proper] for the people of Medina and those surrounding them of the bedouins that they remain behind [from fighting] the Messenger of Allah or that they prefer themselves over his self. That is because they are not struck by thirst or fatigue or hunger in the cause of Allah, nor do they tread on any ground that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they inflict upon an enemy any infliction but that it is registered for them as a righteous deed. Indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the duty of the people of Medina and the surrounding bedouins to support the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in his mission. It highlights that they should not hesitate to join him in his endeavors, as they will be rewarded for their efforts and sacrifices in the cause of Allah. The verse also stresses that those who support the Prophet will not suffer any hardship, as Allah will protect and reward them for their good deeds. The interpretation underscores the importance of unwavering loyalty and commitment to the Prophet and the Islamic cause.
orig: ما كان لأهل المدينة ومن حولهم من الأعراب أن يتخلفوا عن رسول الله ولا يرغبوا بأنفسهم عن نفسه ذلك بأنهم لا يصيبهم ظمأ ولا نصب ولا مخمصة في سبيل الله ولا يطئون موطئا يغيظ الكفار ولا ينالون من عدو نيلا إلا كتب لهم به عمل صالح إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: And they do not spend [in the cause of Allah] any small or large amount, and they do not cross a valley but that it is registered for them; that Allah may reward them for the best of what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that no good deed, whether small or large, goes unnoticed by Allah. It suggests that Allah keeps track of all the righteous actions of the believers, and will reward them accordingly. The interpretation is that even the smallest acts of charity, kindness, or devotion to Allah are valued and will be compensated in the Hereafter.
orig: ولا ينفقون نفقة صغيرة ولا كبيرة ولا يقطعون واديا إلا كتب لهم ليجزيهم الله أحسن ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And it is not [proper] for the believers to go forth [to battle] all at once. So why should not a company from every division of them go forth to [attain] understanding in the religion and to warn their people when they return to them that they might be cautious?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having a group of believers dedicated to studying and understanding the religion, while the rest of the believers can focus on other aspects of their faith. The verse encourages a balanced approach where a group of believers dedicates themselves to gaining religious knowledge and then sharing it with their community, so that the entire community can be cautious and vigilant in their faith.
orig: وما كان المؤمنون لينفروا كافة فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا في الدين ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون

translation: O you who believe! Fight those of the disbelievers who are close to you and let them find harshness in you. And know that Allah is with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to fight against the disbelievers who are closest to them, and to show firmness and severity in doing so. The interpretation is that the believers should not hesitate to confront those who disbelieve and threaten their faith, as Allah is with those who are righteous and fear Him.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا قاتلوا الذين يلونكم من الكفار وليجدوا فيكم غلظة واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين

translation: And when a Surah is revealed, some of them say, "Which of you has this increased in faith?" As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the different reactions of people when a new chapter (Surah) of the Quran is revealed. Some people question whether the revelation has increased the faith of others, while those who truly believe find that it strengthens their faith and brings them joy. The verse suggests that the Quran has the power to deepen the faith of those who approach it with sincerity and openness.
orig: وإذا ما أنزلت سورة فمنهم من يقول أيكم زادته هذه إيمانا فأما الذين آمنوا فزادتهم إيمانا وهم يستبشرون

translation: But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it has [only] increased them in evil [in addition] to their [previous] evil. And they have died while they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have a spiritual disease or sickness in their hearts, such as hypocrisy, doubt, or a lack of faith. Their disbelief and evil deeds only increase their state of impurity and distance from God. They die in a state of disbelief, without having attained true faith and salvation.
orig: وأما الذين في قلوبهم مرض فزادتهم رجسا إلى رجسهم وماتوا وهم كافرون

translation: Do they not see that they are tried every year once or twice, but then they do not repent nor do they remember?
interpretation: This verse suggests that people often face trials and tribulations, but they fail to learn from these experiences and turn back to God in repentance. Instead, they continue in their sinful ways without reflecting on their actions or seeking forgiveness. The verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and remembrance of God, as these are essential for spiritual growth and salvation.
orig: أولا يرون أنهم يفتنون في كل عام مرة أو مرتين ثم لا يتوبون ولا هم يذكرون

translation: And when a surah is revealed, they look at each other, [as if saying], "Does anyone see you?" then they dismiss themselves. Allah has dismissed their hearts because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and lack of faith of those who profess belief in Islam but do not truly understand or follow its teachings. When a new revelation is brought to them, they look around nervously, as if afraid of being seen, and then turn away, unwilling to accept the truth. This indicates that their hearts have been turned away by Allah because they are a people who do not comprehend the deeper meanings and significance of the divine message.
orig: وإذا ما أنزلت سورة نظر بعضهم إلى بعض هل يراكم من أحد ثم انصرفوا صرف الله قلوبهم بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; [he is] concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the personal connection between the Prophet Muhammad and the believers. He is one of them, deeply concerned for their wellbeing and suffering, and compassionate towards them. The Messenger is not a distant, impersonal figure, but a caring guide who shares in the experiences of the community.
orig: لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم عزيز عليه ما عنتم حريص عليكم بالمؤمنين رءوف رحيم

translation: But if they turn away, then say, "Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne."
interpretation: If the people turn away from your message, then declare that Allah alone is sufficient for you. He is the only true God, and it is upon Him that you place your trust. He is the Sovereign Lord, the Possessor of the Magnificent Throne.
orig: فإن تولوا فقل حسبي الله لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وهو رب العرش العظيم

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book.
interpretation: This verse introduces the Qur'an as the "Wise Book" and emphasizes its divine origin and authority. The combination of letters "Alif, Lam, Ra" is one of the "mysterious letters" found at the beginning of certain Qur'anic chapters, which signify the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and its revelation.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب الحكيم

translation: Has it been a wonder to the people that We have revealed to a man from among them, [saying], "Warn mankind and give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a [firm] precedence of honor with their Lord"? [But] the disbelievers say, "Indeed, this is an obvious magician."
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the revelation he received from God. It highlights that it should not be a wonder or surprise that God chose a human messenger from among the people to convey His message and warn humanity, as well as give good news to the believers. The disbelievers, however, dismiss the Prophet as a mere magician, unable to comprehend the divine nature of the revelation. The verse emphasizes that the believers will have a firm standing and honor before their Lord, despite the rejection and accusations of the disbelievers.
orig: أكان للناس عجبا أن أوحينا إلى رجل منهم أن أنذر الناس وبشر الذين آمنوا أن لهم قدم صدق عند ربهم قال الكافرون إن هذا لساحر مبين

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne, arranging the matter [of His creation]. There is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Then will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and power of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It highlights that Allah alone has the authority to govern the affairs of His creation, and that no one can intercede on behalf of others without His permission. The verse calls upon the believers to worship Allah alone, as a reminder of His greatness and the need to submit to Him.
orig: إن ربكم الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش يدبر الأمر ما من شفيع إلا من بعد إذنه ذلكم الله ربكم فاعبدوه أفلا تذكرون

translation: To Him is your return, all of you. [It is] the promise of Allah in truth. Indeed, He begins the [process of] creation and then repeats it that He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds in justice. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to deny.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Resurrection and the Final Judgment, where all people will return to Allah and be held accountable for their beliefs and actions in this life. It highlights that Allah is the Creator who initiates and repeats the cycle of creation, and that He will justly reward the believers and punish the disbelievers. The interpretation underscores the importance of faith, righteous deeds, and the ultimate consequences of one's choices in this world.
orig: إليه مرجعكم جميعا وعد الله حقا إنه يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات بالقسط والذين كفروا لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light and determined for it phases - that you may know the number of years and the account [of time]. Allah has not created this except in truth. He details the signs for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and wisdom in creating the sun and the moon, and establishing their movements and phases. This allows humans to measure time, keep track of the years, and understand the calendar. The purpose of this is not just for practical reasons, but also to reflect on God's signs and the truth of His creation, for those who possess knowledge and understanding.
orig: هو الذي جعل الشمس ضياء والقمر نورا وقدره منازل لتعلموا عدد السنين والحساب ما خلق الله ذلك إلا بالحق يفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day and [in] what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth are signs for a people who fear [Him].
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the signs of Allah's power and wisdom in the creation of the universe, such as the alternation of night and day. These signs are meant to guide those who have consciousness of Allah and seek to live righteously.
orig: إن في اختلاف الليل والنهار وما خلق الله في السماوات والأرض لآيات لقوم يتقون

translation: Indeed, those who do not expect the meeting with Us and are satisfied with the life of this world and feel secure in it and those who are heedless of Our signs
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who are content with the pleasures of this world and do not believe in the Hereafter, and who are negligent of Allah's signs and guidance, will be deprived of the eternal bliss of the Afterlife.
orig: إن الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ورضوا بالحياة الدنيا واطمأنوا بها والذين هم عن آياتنا غافلون

translation: Those - their refuge is the Fire, for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who have rejected faith and done evil deeds. Their ultimate destination is the Fire of Hell, which they will be consigned to as a punishment for their misdeeds and the sins they have committed.
orig: أولئك مأواهم النار بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - their Lord will guide them because of their faith. Beneath them rivers will flow in Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have true faith in God and do good deeds will be guided by God and rewarded with the blissful abode of Paradise, where they will enjoy eternal peace and contentment.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات يهديهم ربهم بإيمانهم تجري من تحتهم الأنهار في جنات النعيم

translation: Their call therein will be, "Exalted are You, O Allah," and their greeting therein will be, "Peace." And the last of their calls will be, "Praise to Allah, Lord of the Worlds."
interpretation: This verse describes the nature of the supplications and greetings of the inhabitants of Paradise. They will glorify and exalt Allah, declaring His perfection and transcendence. Their greetings to one another will be "Peace", reflecting the harmony and tranquility of the abode. Finally, their ultimate supplication will be to praise Allah as the Lord of all the worlds, acknowledging His sovereignty and worthiness of all praise.
orig: دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم وتحيتهم فيها سلام وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: And if Allah were to hasten for the people the evil [they invoke] as He hastens for them the good, their term would have been ended for them. So We leave those who do not expect the meeting with Us, in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse highlights that if Allah were to punish people as quickly as He rewards them, their lives would be cut short. However, Allah is merciful and gives people time to repent and turn back to Him. Those who do not believe in the Hereafter and continue in their transgression are left to wander aimlessly, blind to the truth.
orig: ولو يعجل الله للناس الشر استعجالهم بالخير لقضي إليهم أجلهم فنذر الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: And when affliction touches man, he calls upon Us - whether lying on his side or sitting or standing. But when We remove from him his affliction, [he continues] as if he had never called upon Us to [remove] an affliction that touched him. Thus is made pleasing to the transgressors that which they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to turn to God in times of distress, but then quickly forget their reliance on Him once the hardship is removed. It serves as a reminder that we should maintain our connection with God, not just when we are in need, but at all times. The verse also cautions against the allure of transgressions, which can become normalized and accepted by those who indulge in them.
orig: وإذا مس الإنسان الضر دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما فلما كشفنا عنه ضره مر كأن لم يدعنا إلى ضر مسه كذلك زين للمسرفين ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We had already destroyed generations before you when they wronged, and their messengers had come to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.
interpretation: This verse highlights that previous generations who committed injustice and oppression were destroyed, despite the fact that clear signs and messengers were sent to them. This serves as a warning that those who persist in wrongdoing and reject faith will be punished accordingly, just as the criminal people of the past were recompensed.
orig: ولقد أهلكنا القرون من قبلكم لما ظلموا وجاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات وما كانوا ليؤمنوا كذلك نجزي القوم المجرمين

translation: Then We made you successors in the land after them to see how you will do.
interpretation: This verse suggests that after the previous generations, Allah has appointed the present generation as successors on Earth to see how they will conduct themselves and what they will do with the responsibilities entrusted to them. It implies a test or trial for the present generation to demonstrate their worthiness and obedience to Allah through their actions and choices.
orig: ثم جعلناكم خلائف في الأرض من بعدهم لننظر كيف تعملون

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect the [event of] meeting Us say, "Bring us a Qur'an other than this or change it." Say, [O Muhammad], "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of accepting the Qur'an as it is, without any attempt to change or alter it. It highlights that the Qur'an is a divine revelation, and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is simply a messenger who conveys it, not one who can modify it. The verse also warns against rejecting the Qur'an and calls upon the believers to have faith in the meeting with God and the accountability on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ائت بقرآن غير هذا أو بدله قل ما يكون لي أن أبدله من تلقاء نفسي إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Say, "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you, for I had remained among you a lifetime before it [i.e., the Qur'an]. Then will you not reason?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation, not something fabricated by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It suggests that if Allah had not willed for the Qur'an to be revealed, the Prophet would not have been able to recite it or make it known to the people. The verse then poses a rhetorical question, asking if the people will not use their reason to understand that the Qur'an is a true revelation from God, not something the Prophet himself invented.
orig: قل لو شاء الله ما تلوته عليكم ولا أدراكم به فقد لبثت فيكم عمرا من قبله أفلا تعقلون

translation: Then who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of fabricating lies about Allah or rejecting the divine signs and revelations. It conveys that those who engage in such wrongdoing will not attain success or prosperity, as they have strayed from the path of truth and righteousness.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته إنه لا يفلح المجرمون

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them, and they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah." Say, "Do you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens and the earth?" Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of worshipping idols and false gods, which can neither harm nor benefit the worshippers. It also criticizes the belief that these idols can act as intercessors with Allah. The verse emphasizes that Allah alone has complete knowledge of the heavens and the earth, and that associating partners with Him is an act of blasphemy. The interpretation highlights the futility of worshipping anything other than the one true God, and the importance of maintaining a pure and exclusive devotion to Allah.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا يضرهم ولا ينفعهم ويقولون هؤلاء شفعاؤنا عند الله قل أتنبئون الله بما لا يعلم في السماوات ولا في الأرض سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And the people were not but one community [united in religion], but [then] they differed. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them [immediately] concerning that over which they differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights that mankind was originally one community united in faith, but later they differed and divided into various groups and sects. However, the verse also suggests that if it were not for God's decree to give people a chance to choose and be tested, the differences would have been resolved immediately. The interpretation is that God allows for differences to exist as a test for humanity, but ultimately the truth will prevail as per His plan.
orig: وما كان الناس إلا أمة واحدة فاختلفوا ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم فيما فيه يختلفون

translation: And they say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "The unseen is only for Allah [to administer], so wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait."
interpretation: This verse addresses those who demand a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad as proof of his prophethood. The response is that the knowledge of the unseen belongs solely to Allah, and it is not for humans to dictate the terms of divine revelation. Rather, the believers are encouraged to patiently wait for Allah's guidance and signs, with the assurance that the Prophet is with them in this waiting period.
orig: ويقولون لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه فقل إنما الغيب لله فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: And when We let the people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, at once they conspire against Our verses. Say, "Allah is swifter in strategy." Indeed, Our messengers record that which you conspire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to become ungrateful and turn against God's signs and messages when they experience relief from hardship. It warns that Allah is swifter in His plans and that the angels record all the conspiracies and schemes of those who turn away from the truth. The interpretation is that people should be mindful of their actions and maintain gratitude towards God, even in times of ease, lest they incur His displeasure.
orig: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة من بعد ضراء مستهم إذا لهم مكر في آياتنا قل الله أسرع مكرا إن رسلنا يكتبون ما تمكرون

translation: It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea, until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good [i.e., favourable] wind, and they rejoice therein, there comes a storm wind, and the waves come upon them from everywhere, and they assume that they are surrounded [i.e., doomed], [at that point] they supplicate Allah, [saying], "If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the human condition of being subject to the forces of nature, and how in times of ease and prosperity, we tend to forget our reliance on Allah, but when faced with hardship and danger, we turn to Him in sincere supplication. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining an attitude of gratitude and humility before Allah, who controls all aspects of our lives, both on land and at sea.
orig: هو الذي يسيركم في البر والبحر حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك وجرين بهم بريح طيبة وفرحوا بها جاءتها ريح عاصف وجاءهم الموج من كل مكان وظنوا أنهم أحيط بهم دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين لئن أنجيتنا من هذه لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: And when He has saved them, at once they commit injustice upon the earth without right. O mankind, your injustice is only against yourselves. [In] the enjoyment of this worldly life. Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that after being saved from a difficult situation, people often turn to injustice and wrongdoing without any justification. It reminds us that our actions and transgressions are ultimately against ourselves, not others. The verse also highlights that the enjoyment of this worldly life is temporary, and we will all return to God, who will inform us about our deeds.
orig: فلما أنجاهم إذا هم يبغون في الأرض بغير الحق يا أيها الناس إنما بغيكم على أنفسكم متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم إلينا مرجعكم فننبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: The life of this world is but the enjoyment of deception. It is like a rain whose [resulting] plant growth pleases the tillers; then it dries up and you see it turned yellow, then it becomes [scattered] debris. And in the Hereafter is severe punishment or forgiveness from Allah, and [what is] the life of this world is not but [temporary] enjoyment of delusion.
interpretation: This verse paints a vivid metaphor for the fleeting and deceptive nature of worldly life. It compares the life of this world to a rain that causes the earth to sprout vegetation, which initially pleases the farmers, but then quickly withers and turns to dust. Just as this vegetation is temporary, so too is the enjoyment and splendor of this world. The true test lies in the Hereafter, where one will face either severe punishment or the forgiveness of Allah. This serves as a reminder that the life of this world is but a temporary deception, and one should focus on preparing for the eternal life to come through faith and righteous deeds.
orig: إنما مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض مما يأكل الناس والأنعام حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها وازينت وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها أتاها أمرنا ليلا أو نهارا فجعلناها حصيدا كأن لم تغن بالأمس كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And Allah invites to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah calls people to the abode of peace, which is Paradise, and guides whomever He wishes to the straight path, which is the path of righteousness and salvation. It highlights Allah's role as the ultimate guide and the one who directs people towards eternal peace and well-being.
orig: والله يدعو إلى دار السلام ويهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: For those who have done good is the best [reward] and extra. And no darkness will cover their faces, nor humiliation. They are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse promises a great reward for those who have done good deeds - not only the best reward, but an additional reward beyond that. Their faces will not be covered in darkness or humiliation, but rather they will be honored as the companions of Paradise, dwelling therein forever.
orig: للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة ولا يرهق وجوههم قتر ولا ذلة أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: And those who have earned [blame for] evil deeds - the recompense of an evil deed is its equivalent, and they will be humbled. They will have no protector from [the wrath of] Allah. It will be as if their faces are covered in the darkness of night. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who have committed evil deeds. Their punishment will be commensurate with their crimes, and they will be humbled and have no one to protect them from the wrath of Allah. Their state will be like being enveloped in the darkness of night, indicating the hopelessness and despair they will experience. They are destined to be the companions of the Fire, condemned to dwell in it eternally.
orig: والذين كسبوا السيئات جزاء سيئة بمثلها وترهقهم ذلة ما لهم من الله من عاصم كأنما أغشيت وجوههم قطعا من الليل مظلما أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And the Day We will gather them all together - then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, "Where are your 'partners' that you used to claim [were associated with Him]?"
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment when all people will be gathered before God. Those who associated others with God will be questioned about their false deities and idols that they worshipped. This emphasizes that on that Day, the false gods will disown their worshippers, highlighting the futility of polytheism and the need to worship God alone.
orig: ويوم نحشرهم جميعا ثم نقول للذين أشركوا مكانكم أنتم وشركاؤكم فزيلنا بينهم وقال شركاؤهم ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون

translation: And sufficient is Allah as Witness between us and you, that we were certainly unaware of your worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate witness between the believers and the disbelievers, and that the believers were unaware of the disbelievers' worship of other deities. It serves as a reminder that Allah is the sole deity worthy of worship and that He is aware of all that transpires, even if the believers were not previously cognizant of the disbelievers' practices.
orig: فكفى بالله شهيدا بيننا وبينكم إن كنا عن عبادتكم لغافلين

translation: There every soul will become [fully] aware of what it has done, and they will be returned to Allah , their true Lord, and lost from them is whatever they had invented.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, every person will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs. They will be returned to God, the true Lord and Master, and all the falsehoods they had invented or believed in will be revealed as such and will no longer have any power over them.
orig: هنالك تبلو كل نفس ما أسلفت وردوا إلى الله مولاهم الحق وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Say, "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who controls the hearing and the sight, and who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living, and who arranges [every] matter?" They will say, "[All that is] Allah." Say, "Then will you not fear Him?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and power of Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. It challenges the reader to reflect on the signs of Allah's existence and control over all things, from the provision of sustenance to the cycle of life and death. The verse invites the reader to acknowledge Allah's authority and to live in reverence and fear of Him, as the rightful response to these profound realities.
orig: قل من يرزقكم من السماء والأرض أمن يملك السمع والأبصار ومن يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ومن يدبر الأمر فسيقولون الله فقل أفلا تتقون

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, the Truth. And what can be beyond truth except error? So how are you averted?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the absolute truth, and there is nothing beyond the truth except error or falsehood. It calls upon people to not be misled by anything other than the truth revealed by Allah, and to remain steadfast in their faith and submission to Him.
orig: فذلكم الله ربكم الحق فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال فأنى تصرفون

translation: Thus the word of your Lord has come into effect upon those who defiantly disobeyed - that they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the decree of God has been established against those who have rejected faith and rebelled against His commandments. They will not be granted belief, as they have chosen to turn away from the truth.
orig: كذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين فسقوا أنهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Say, "Is there of your 'partners' any who begins creation and then repeats it?" Say, "Allah begins creation and then repeats it, so how are you deluded?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists to show if any of their false gods can create and then re-create, as Allah does. The implication is that only Allah has the power to originate life and then resurrect it, and so worship of any other deity is misguided and delusional.
orig: قل هل من شركائكم من يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده قل الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده فأنى تؤفكون

translation: Say, "Is there any of your 'partners' who guides to the truth?" Say, "Allah guides to the truth. So is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed or he who guides not unless he is guided? Then what is [wrong] with you - how do you judge?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists to compare the guidance provided by their false deities to the guidance provided by Allah. It emphasizes that only Allah truly guides people to the truth, while false deities cannot guide anyone unless Allah Himself guides them first. The verse then questions the polytheists' judgment in choosing to follow false deities instead of the One True God who alone is worthy of being followed.
orig: قل هل من شركائكم من يهدي إلى الحق قل الله يهدي للحق أفمن يهدي إلى الحق أحق أن يتبع أمن لا يهدي إلا أن يهدى فما لكم كيف تحكمون

translation: And most of them follow not except assumption. Indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that most people follow their own assumptions and speculations rather than the truth. Assumptions and guesses cannot replace the truth, as Allah is all-knowing of what people do. The verse encourages seeking knowledge and truth rather than blindly following assumptions or hearsay.
orig: وما يتبع أكثرهم إلا ظنا إن الظن لا يغني من الحق شيئا إن الله عليم بما يفعلون

translation: And this Qur'an is not such as could ever be produced by other than Allah; but it is a confirmation of (the revelation) that went before it, and a full explanation of the Book - wherein there is no doubt - from the Lord of the Worlds.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an is a divine revelation from Allah, and not something that could have been produced by any human being. It is a confirmation and explanation of the previous scriptures, providing a complete and authoritative guidance that is free from any doubt, coming from the Lord of all the worlds.
orig: وما كان هذا القرآن أن يفترى من دون الله ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين

translation: Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "Then bring a surah like it and call upon [for assistance] whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers who accused the Prophet Muhammad of fabricating the Qur'an. It calls upon them to produce a single chapter (surah) that can match the eloquence and content of the Qur'an, if they truly believe it is a human invention. The verse emphasizes that they should seek help from anyone they can besides Allah, demonstrating the divine origin of the Qur'an.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل فأتوا بسورة مثله وادعوا من استطعتم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Nay, they have rejected the truth when it has come to them, so they are in a state of confusion.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers have rejected the truth of the Qur`an and the message of Islam, even though they do not fully comprehend its meaning and significance. It draws a parallel between their rejection and the rejection of previous generations, and warns them of the consequences of their wrongdoing.
orig: بل كذبوا بما لم يحيطوا بعلمه ولما يأتهم تأويله كذلك كذب الذين من قبلهم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين

translation: And among them are those who believe in it and among them are those who do not believe in it. And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity of human responses to faith and belief. Some people will accept and believe in the message of the Qur’an, while others will reject it. Ultimately, it is Allah who knows best the true nature and intentions of all people, including those who seek to corrupt or undermine the faith.
orig: ومنهم من يؤمن به ومنهم من لا يؤمن به وربك أعلم بالمفسدين

translation: And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then say, "For me are my deeds, and for you are your deeds. You are disassociated from what I do, and I am disassociated from what you do."
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad to maintain his composure and steadfastness in the face of rejection and denial from his opponents. It emphasizes that each person is responsible for their own actions and beliefs, and that the Prophet should not be concerned with the actions of those who reject his message. The verse underscores the importance of maintaining one's own moral integrity and commitment to one's beliefs, regardless of the actions of others.
orig: وإن كذبوك فقل لي عملي ولكم عملكم أنتم بريئون مما أعمل وأنا بريء مما تعملون

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, but can you make the deaf hear, even though they will not use reason?
interpretation: This verse highlights that some people may listen to the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet, but they are still unable to comprehend the deeper meaning and significance of the message. Just as it is impossible for the physically deaf to hear, those who refuse to use their reasoning and intellect are also unable to truly understand the guidance being conveyed. The verse emphasizes the importance of using one's faculties of reason and contemplation to fully appreciate the divine teachings.
orig: ومنهم من يستمعون إليك أفأنت تسمع الصم ولو كانوا لا يعقلون

translation: And among them are those who look at you, [O Muhammad]. But can you guide the blind when they will not [choose to] see?
interpretation: This verse highlights that some people are unwilling to see the truth, even when it is presented to them clearly. The Prophet Muhammad cannot guide those who are willfully blind to the message of Islam, as they have chosen to reject it despite the evidence.
orig: ومنهم من ينظر إليك أفأنت تهدي العمي ولو كانوا لا يبصرون

translation: Indeed, Allah does not do injustice to people, but it is the people who are unjust to themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is Just and does not wrong anyone. Any injustice or suffering experienced by people is a result of their own actions and choices, not due to any unfairness on Allah's part. It encourages individuals to take responsibility for their own conduct and decisions, rather than blaming Allah for the consequences of their own wrongdoing.
orig: إن الله لا يظلم الناس شيئا ولكن الناس أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And the Day when He will gather them as if they had not remained [in the world] but an hour of the day, [and] they will recognize one another. Those will have lost who denied the meeting with Allah and were not guided.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when people will be gathered before Allah. On that day, time will seem to have passed so quickly that it will feel like just an hour. The people will recognize each other, but those who denied the existence of Allah and did not follow the right path will have lost, for they will face the consequences of their disbelief and misguided actions.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم كأن لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من النهار يتعارفون بينهم قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: And whether We show you (Muhammad) some of what We promise them (the disbelievers) or take you (unto Us), verily, to Us is their return, and (in any case) Allah is the witness over what they do.
interpretation: This verse conveys the certainty that the disbelievers will face the consequences of their actions, whether the Prophet (peace be upon him) witnesses it or not. Ultimately, all people will return to Allah, who is the witness over their deeds. This emphasizes the accountability that all humans have before their Creator.
orig: وإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإلينا مرجعهم ثم الله شهيد على ما يفعلون

translation: And for every nation is a messenger. So when their messenger has come, it will be judged between them in justice, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God has sent a messenger to guide every community or nation. When the messenger comes, the people will be judged fairly and impartially, and they will not be subjected to any injustice or oppression.
orig: ولكل أمة رسول فإذا جاء رسولهم قضي بينهم بالقسط وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of those who deny the promise of the Hereafter and resurrection. They challenge the believers to provide evidence for the fulfillment of this promise, doubting its veracity. The verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to respond to such skepticism with patience and wisdom.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "I possess not for myself [the power of] harm or benefit except what Allah has willed. And for every nation is a [specified] term. When their time has come, then they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that we have no power over our own harm or benefit, and that everything is ultimately in the hands of Allah.
