It also highlights that every nation has a predetermined term, and when that time comes, they cannot delay or hasten it even for a moment. This serves as a reminder of our limited control and the need to submit to Allah's will.
orig: قل لا أملك لنفسي ضرا ولا نفعا إلا ما شاء الله لكل أمة أجل إذا جاء أجلهم فلا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if His punishment should come to you by night or by day - for which [aspect] would the criminals be impatient?'
interpretation: This verse encourages the listener to reflect on the inevitability of divine punishment, regardless of when it may come. The question posed challenges the arrogance and impatience of the wrongdoers, who cannot escape the consequences of their misdeeds, whether they come during the day or night.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أتاكم عذابه بياتا أو نهارا ماذا يستعجل منه المجرمون

translation: Then is it that when it has [actually] occurred you will believe in it? [No], now you ask to hasten it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that people often demand the fulfillment of God's promises or warnings before they are ready to believe. However, once the promised event occurs, they then believe in it. The verse cautions against this attitude, and encourages people to have faith in God's words without needing to witness their immediate realization.
orig: أثم إذا ما وقع آمنتم به آلآن وقد كنتم به تستعجلون

translation: Then it will be said to those who wronged, 'Taste the punishment of eternity. Are you recompensed except for what you used to earn?'
interpretation: This verse conveys a stern warning to those who have wronged others. It suggests that on the Day of Judgment, the wrongdoers will be made to taste the eternal punishment for their misdeeds. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes that they will be recompensed only for the actions they committed in their worldly lives, highlighting the inescapable consequences of their choices.
orig: ثم قيل للذين ظلموا ذوقوا عذاب الخلد هل تجزون إلا بما كنتم تكسبون

translation: And they ask you, [O Muhammad], is it true? Say, "Yes, by my Lord. Indeed, it is the truth; and you will not be able to cause failure [to Allah]."
interpretation: This verse affirms the truthfulness of the Qur'an and the message that Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is conveying. It emphasizes that the revelation he receives is the absolute truth from God, and that no one can prevent or undermine the divine plan. The verse serves to reassure the Prophet and strengthen the believers' faith in the veracity of the Qur'anic teachings.
orig: ويستنبئونك أحق هو قل إي وربي إنه لحق وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: And if every soul that has wronged were to offer all that is in the earth, it would not be accepted from them. And they will [secretly] feel regret when they see the punishment, and they will be judged in justice, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, no amount of wealth or possessions will be able to redeem a soul that has committed wrongdoing. Even if they were to offer everything on earth, it would not be accepted from them. When they witness the punishment, they will feel deep regret, but it will be too late. The judgment will be fair and just, and they will not be wronged in any way.
orig: ولو أن لكل نفس ظلمت ما في الأرض لافتدت به وأسروا الندامة لما رأوا العذاب وقضي بينهم بالقسط وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Unquestionably, the promise of Allah is truth, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all that exists in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, the Almighty. It also affirms that the promise of Allah is true, but most people are unaware of this fundamental truth.
orig: ألا إن لله ما في السماوات والأرض ألا إن وعد الله حق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of God over life and death. He alone has the authority to give life and take it away, and ultimately, all people will return to Him for judgment and accountability. This underscores the need for humans to live in accordance with God's will and to prepare for the afterlife, where they will face the consequences of their actions in this world.
orig: هو يحيي ويميت وإليه ترجعون

translation: O mankind, there has to come to you instruction from your Lord and healing for what is in the breasts and guidance and mercy for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine guidance and source of healing for the spiritual and emotional ailments of the human soul. It serves as an instruction from God to lead the believers towards righteousness and His mercy.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءتكم موعظة من ربكم وشفاء لما في الصدور وهدى ورحمة للمؤمنين

translation: Say, "By the grace of Allah and by His mercy - so let them rejoice; that is better than what they accumulate."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to rejoice in the grace and mercy of Allah, rather than being consumed by the material possessions and wealth they may accumulate. The true source of happiness and fulfillment is found in Allah's blessings, not in worldly gains.
orig: قل بفضل الله وبرحمته فبذلك فليفرحوا هو خير مما يجمعون

translation: Say, "Have you considered what provision Allah has sent down for you and have made [part of it] unlawful and [part of it] lawful?" Say, "Has Allah permitted you [to do so], or do you invent [something] about Allah?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the practice of declaring certain foods or provisions as unlawful or lawful without any divine authority. It emphasizes that only Allah has the right to determine what is permissible and what is not, and that humans should not make such declarations based on their own whims or desires. The verse encourages people to reflect on the provisions Allah has granted them and to refrain from making arbitrary rulings about their lawfulness or unlawfulness.
orig: قل أرأيتم ما أنزل الله لكم من رزق فجعلتم منه حراما وحلالا قل آلله أذن لكم أم على الله تفترون

translation: And what do those who invent lies about Allah think the Day of Resurrection [will be like]? Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of them are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse warns those who fabricate lies and attribute them to Allah. On the Day of Resurrection, they will face the consequences of their actions. Despite Allah's abundant blessings and grace upon humanity, most people fail to express gratitude and appreciation for these blessings.
orig: وما ظن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب يوم القيامة إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثرهم لا يشكرون

translation: And you are not [engaged] in any matter and you do not recite of the Qur'an and you [people] do not do any [good] deed except that We are witness over you when you are involved in it. And not [even] an atom's weight in the earth or in the heaven is hidden from your Lord - and not [what is] less than that or greater than that, but it is [all] in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and all-seeing. Nothing that a person does, whether it is a recitation of the Qur'an, a worldly activity, or a good deed, escapes Allah's knowledge and observation. Even the smallest particle on earth or in the heavens is known to Allah, and everything is recorded in the clear register. This serves as a reminder to people to be mindful of their actions and to strive to please Allah, as He is aware of everything they do.
orig: وما تكون في شأن وما تتلو منه من قرآن ولا تعملون من عمل إلا كنا عليكم شهودا إذ تفيضون فيه وما يعزب عن ربك من مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: Unquestionably, [for] the allies of Allah there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse reassures the believers that those who are close to Allah (God) and have faith in Him will not experience fear or sorrow. They are under Allah's protection and care, and can trust in His guidance and plan for them.
orig: ألا إن أولياء الله لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those who believe and are conscious of God
interpretation: This verse speaks of the believers who have faith in God and strive to live righteously by being mindful of and submitting to the will of God. It emphasizes the importance of both belief and righteous conduct for those who seek to please God and attain His pleasure.
orig: الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: For them is good tidings in the worldly life and in the Hereafter. There is no change in the words of Allah. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse conveys the promise of good news and success for those who believe in and follow the teachings of Allah. It emphasizes the immutability of Allah's words, highlighting the certainty and permanence of the rewards and blessings that await the believers, both in this life and the Hereafter. The "great attainment" refers to the ultimate triumph and salvation that is granted to those who remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: لهم البشرى في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة لا تبديل لكلمات الله ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: And let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, all [power, honor, and glory] belongs to Allah. He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he should not be saddened by the words and criticisms of the disbelievers. It reminds him that all power, honor, and glory belong to Allah alone, and that Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing. This is a call to trust in Allah's plan and not to be distressed by the opposition of those who reject the message of Islam, for Allah is in control and will ultimately prevail.
orig: ولا يحزنك قولهم إن العزة لله جميعا هو السميع العليم

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And those who invoke other than Allah do not [actually] follow [His] 'partners'. They follow not except assumption, and they are not but falsifying.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone is the sovereign of the heavens and the earth, and that those who worship other deities besides Allah are not truly following partners, but are instead following mere speculation and conjecture. It reaffirms the absolute oneness and supremacy of Allah over all creation.
orig: ألا إن لله من في السماوات ومن في الأرض وما يتبع الذين يدعون من دون الله شركاء إن يتبعون إلا الظن وإن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: It is He who made for you the night to rest therein and the day, giving sight. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the one who created the alternation of night and day for the benefit of humanity. The night provides a time for rest and relaxation, while the day allows people to see and engage in their daily activities. This cycle is a sign of Allah's power and wisdom, and should be appreciated by those who listen and reflect on the divine signs in creation.
orig: هو الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يسمعون

translation: They say, "Allah has taken a son." Exalted is He; He is the [one] Free of all needs. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. You have no authority for this [claim]. Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?
interpretation: This verse condemns the notion that Allah has taken a son, which is a belief held by some religious groups. The verse emphasizes that Allah is the One who is free from all needs and that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. It challenges the people to provide any authority or evidence for their claim about Allah having a son, as such a claim is made without any knowledge or justification.
orig: قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا سبحانه هو الغني له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض إن عندكم من سلطان بهذا أتقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Say, "Indeed, those who invent falsehood about Allah will not succeed."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who fabricate lies and attribute them to Allah will not be successful in their endeavors. It serves as a warning against making false claims in the name of the divine, as such deception will ultimately lead to failure and disappointment.
orig: قل إن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب لا يفلحون

translation: Enjoyment in the world, then to Us is their return, then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the temporary nature of worldly pleasures and the ultimate accountability before God. The disbelievers may enjoy the material comforts of this life, but they will ultimately be held responsible for their rejection of faith and will face severe punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: متاع في الدنيا ثم إلينا مرجعهم ثم نذيقهم العذاب الشديد بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: And recite to them the news of Noah, when he said to his people, "O my people, if my presence has become burdensome to you and my reminding you of the signs of Allah - then upon Allah I have relied. So prepare your plan and [call upon] your associates, then let not your plan be obscure to you. Then carry it out upon me and do not delay me."
interpretation: This verse recounts the story of the prophet Noah, who called his people to worship Allah alone. When his people found his message burdensome, he reminded them to rely on Allah and prepare their plan to oppose him. However, he urged them to carry out their plan openly without hiding it, as he was confident in Allah's support and protection.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ نوح إذ قال لقومه يا قوم إن كان كبر عليكم مقامي وتذكيري بآيات الله فعلى الله توكلت فأجمعوا أمركم وشركاءكم ثم لا يكن أمركم عليكم غمة ثم اقضوا إلي ولا تنظرون

translation: But if you turn away, I have not asked you for any payment. My reward is only from Allah, and I have been commanded to be of the [submitting] Muslims.
interpretation: If you choose to reject my message, I do not demand any reward or payment from you. My only reward is from Allah, and I have been commanded to be among those who submit to Him and live in accordance with His will.
orig: فإن توليتم فما سألتكم من أجر إن أجري إلا على الله وأمرت أن أكون من المسلمين

translation: But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the ship and made them successors, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. So see how was the end of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse describes the story of Prophet Noah and the people who rejected his message. Despite their rejection, God saved Noah and his followers in the ark, while those who denied his signs were drowned. This serves as a lesson and warning to those who reject the guidance of God's messengers, as their end will be similar to those who were warned before them.
orig: فكذبوه فنجيناه ومن معه في الفلك وجعلناهم خلائف وأغرقنا الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المنذرين

translation: Then We sent, after them, messengers to their people, and they came to them with clear proofs. But they were not to believe in that which they had denied before. Thus We seal over the hearts of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse describes how even after previous messengers were rejected, God continued to send more messengers to guide people, but the people stubbornly refused to believe, having already rejected the truth. This shows God's patience and persistence in guiding humanity, but also how those who repeatedly turn away from the truth become hardened in their rejection, with God sealing their hearts as a consequence of their own choices.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعده رسلا إلى قومهم فجاءوهم بالبينات فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذبوا به من قبل كذلك نطبع على قلوب المعتدين

translation: Then We sent after them Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his establishment with Our signs, but they were arrogant and were a criminal people.
interpretation: This verse describes how after the previous generations, Allah sent the Prophets Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his people, with clear signs and evidence of the truth of Allah's message. However, Pharaoh and his people responded with arrogance and rejected the message, despite its clarity, and they were a criminal and sinful people.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعدهم موسى وهارون إلى فرعون وملئه بآياتنا فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما مجرمين

translation: And when the truth has come to them from Us, they say, "This is obvious magic."
interpretation: When the truth and guidance from Allah came to the people, they rejected it and dismissed it as mere magic, rather than acknowledging its divine origin and accepting it.
orig: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا إن هذا لسحر مبين

translation: Moses said, "Do you say [this] about the truth when it has come to you? Is this magic? But the magicians will not succeed."
interpretation: This verse is a response by the prophet Moses to the Pharaoh and his people who accused him of practicing magic when he presented them with the signs and miracles given to him by God. Moses affirms that what he has brought is the truth, not magic, and that the magicians will ultimately fail in their attempts to compete with the divine power manifested through him.
orig: قال موسى أتقولون للحق لما جاءكم أسحر هذا ولا يفلح الساحرون

translation: They said, "Have you come to us to turn us away from what we found our fathers following, and [to have] for yourselves grandeur in the land? And we are not for you [i.e., your people] believers."
interpretation: This verse reflects the response of the people when the Prophets called them to worship God alone and abandon the false deities they had inherited from their ancestors. The people accused the Prophets of seeking power and status for themselves, rather than guiding the people to the truth. This highlights the common human tendency to resist change and cling to tradition, even when it is false. The interpretation is that people often reject the truth when it challenges their established beliefs and way of life.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لتلفتنا عما وجدنا عليه آباءنا وتكون لكما الكبرياء في الأرض وما نحن لكما بمؤمنين

translation: And Pharaoh said, "Bring to me every learned magician."
interpretation: This verse highlights Pharaoh's arrogance and his desire to challenge the power of God. By summoning the "learned magicians", Pharaoh seeks to demonstrate his own authority and refute the miracles performed by Moses, who was sent by God. This reflects Pharaoh's rejection of the divine message and his attempt to assert his own supremacy over the will of the Almighty.
orig: وقال فرعون ائتوني بكل ساحر عليم

translation: And when the sorcerers came, Moses said to them, "Throw down what you will throw."
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between Moses and the sorcerers summoned by Pharaoh. It demonstrates Moses' confidence and authority, as he challenges the sorcerers to display their skills, knowing that the truth of his message from God will prevail over their deceptions.
orig: فلما جاء السحرة قال لهم موسى ألقوا ما أنتم ملقون

translation: And when they had thrown, Moses said, "What you have brought is [only] magic. Indeed, Allah will expose its worthlessness. Indeed, Allah does not amend the work of corrupters."
interpretation: This verse indicates that the magicians who were summoned by the Pharaoh to challenge Moses were unable to match the miracle performed by Moses, which was the staff turning into a real snake. Moses then declares that their magic is false and that Allah will expose its falsehood, for Allah does not guide or support the work of those who seek to corrupt and mislead people.
orig: فلما ألقوا قال موسى ما جئتم به السحر إن الله سيبطله إن الله لا يصلح عمل المفسدين

translation: And Allah will establish the truth by His words, even if the criminals dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's truth and justice will prevail, regardless of the opposition or dislike from those who commit crimes and sins. It affirms that Allah's words and decrees are absolute and cannot be altered or prevented, even by the wrongdoers.
orig: ويحق الله الحق بكلماته ولو كره المجرمون

translation: And none believed Moses except [some] offspring [i.e., youth] among his people, for fear of Pharaoh and his establishment, that they would persecute them. And indeed, Pharaoh was arrogant within the land, and indeed, he was of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse highlights the lack of faith and courage among the people of Moses, who were afraid to openly believe in him due to the tyranny and oppression of Pharaoh and his elite. It suggests that only the younger generation, the "offspring" of the people, were willing to take the risk and follow Moses, while the majority remained fearful. The verse also emphasizes Pharaoh's arrogance and corruption, which made him a formidable adversary for Moses and his followers.
orig: فما آمن لموسى إلا ذرية من قومه على خوف من فرعون وملئهم أن يفتنهم وإن فرعون لعال في الأرض وإنه لمن المسرفين

translation: And Moses said, 'O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then rely upon Him if you are Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to put their trust in Allah, the Almighty, and to submit to His will completely if they truly believe in Him. It emphasizes that true faith must be accompanied by reliance on Allah and a willingness to surrender one's will to Him, which is the essence of being a Muslim.
orig: وقال موسى يا قوم إن كنتم آمنتم بالله فعليه توكلوا إن كنتم مسلمين

translation: And they said, "Upon Allah we have relied. Our Lord, do not make us [objects of] trial for the wrongdoing people,"
interpretation: This verse expresses the believers' reliance on Allah and their plea to Him not to make them a trial or test for the wrongdoing people. The interpretation is that the believers are seeking Allah's protection and guidance, and asking Him not to allow them to be subjected to the persecution or temptations of the unjust people.
orig: فقالوا على الله توكلنا ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للقوم الظالمين

translation: And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse implores Allah to save the believers from the influence and harm of those who reject faith in Him. It reflects the desire of the faithful to be protected from the negative effects of disbelief and to be guided towards the path of righteousness through Allah's mercy and compassion.
orig: ونجنا برحمتك من القوم الكافرين

translation: And We inspired to Moses and his brother, "Settle your people in Egypt in houses and make your houses [facing the prayer direction] and establish prayer and give good tidings to the believers."
interpretation: This verse instructs Moses and his brother Aaron to settle the Israelites in Egypt, and to make their homes facing the direction of prayer (qibla). They are also commanded to establish regular prayer and to give good news to the believers.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى وأخيه أن تبوآ لقومكما بمصر بيوتا واجعلوا بيوتكم قبلة وأقيموا الصلاة وبشر المؤمنين

translation: And Moses said: "Our Lord! You have indeed bestowed on Pharaoh and his chiefs splendor and wealth in the life of this world, our Lord, that they may lead men astray from Your Path. Our Lord! Destroy their wealth, and harden their hearts, so that they will not believe until they see the painful torment."
interpretation: This verse expresses Moses' plea to God to punish the arrogance and disbelief of Pharaoh and his people. Moses acknowledges that God has granted Pharaoh and his people worldly wealth and power, but he asks God to use that against them by making them arrogant and leading them astray from the true path. Moses then asks God to destroy their wealth and harden their hearts, so that they will only believe in God's message when they face the painful torment of punishment.
orig: وقال موسى ربنا إنك آتيت فرعون وملأه زينة وأموالا في الحياة الدنيا ربنا ليضلوا عن سبيلك ربنا اطمس على أموالهم واشدد على قلوبهم فلا يؤمنوا حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: He said, 'Your supplication has been answered. So remain on a right course and do not follow the way of those who do not know.'
interpretation: This verse conveys the message that when one sincerely supplicates to Allah, their prayers are answered. The verse then instructs the believers to remain steadfast on the right path and not to follow the ways of those who lack knowledge and understanding of the truth.
orig: قال قد أجيبت دعوتكما فاستقيما ولا تتبعان سبيل الذين لا يعلمون

translation: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them in tyranny and enmity until, when drowning overtook him, he said, "I believe that there is no deity except that in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims."
interpretation: This verse describes the Israelites' miraculous crossing of the Red Sea and the subsequent drowning of Pharaoh and his army. It highlights how even Pharaoh, in the face of certain death, professed belief in the One God of the Israelites, acknowledging the truth of their faith. This serves as a powerful lesson that no one can escape the consequences of their actions, and that true faith must be sincere, not just a reaction to dire circumstances.
orig: وجاوزنا ببني إسرائيل البحر فأتبعهم فرعون وجنوده بغيا وعدوا حتى إذا أدركه الغرق قال آمنت أنه لا إله إلا الذي آمنت به بنو إسرائيل وأنا من المسلمين

translation: But now you have disobeyed before, and you were among the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse is a reprimand from God to a person who has disobeyed Him in the past and was among those who spread corruption on Earth. The verse serves as a reminder that past misdeeds cannot be undone, and the person must now strive to rectify their ways and avoid further corruption.
orig: آلآن وقد عصيت قبل وكنت من المفسدين

translation: So this Day We will save you in your body that you may be to those after you a sign. And indeed, many among the people, of Our signs, are heedless.
interpretation: This verse indicates that God will save Prophet Jonah's body from the whale, so that his miraculous survival can serve as a sign and lesson for future generations. However, the verse also suggests that many people remain heedless and unaware of God's signs and wonders in the world around them.
orig: فاليوم ننجيك ببدنك لتكون لمن خلفك آية وإن كثيرا من الناس عن آياتنا لغافلون

translation: And We had certainly given the Children of Israel a noble dwelling and provided for them of the good things, and they did not differ until knowledge had come to them. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings that God bestowed upon the Children of Israel, including providing them with a noble dwelling and good sustenance. However, it also notes that they did not differ until knowledge had come to them. This suggests that their differences arose after they had been guided, and that on the Day of Resurrection, God will judge them over the matters they had differed about. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of following knowledge and guidance, and that ultimately, God will be the final arbiter of our actions and beliefs.
orig: ولقد بوأنا بني إسرائيل مبوأ صدق ورزقناهم من الطيبات فما اختلفوا حتى جاءهم العلم إن ربك يقضي بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: And if you (Muhammad) are in doubt concerning that which We have revealed unto you, then ask those who are reading the Scripture (the Tawrah and the Injeel) before you. Verily, the truth has come to you from your Lord. So be not of those who doubt (it).
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad to seek confirmation of the truth of the Qur'an from those who have previously received divine scriptures, such as the Jews and Christians. It assures him that the Qur'an is the truth revealed by God, and he should not doubt it. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and verification, even for a prophet, and not being among those who are uncertain about the divine origin of the Qur'an.
orig: فإن كنت في شك مما أنزلنا إليك فاسأل الذين يقرءون الكتاب من قبلك لقد جاءك الحق من ربك فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: And do not be among those who deny the verses of Allah and [thus] be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse warns against denying or rejecting the signs and revelations of Allah. It cautions that those who do so will end up as losers, both in this life and the Hereafter. The message is to have faith in Allah's guidance and not to be among those who disbelieve and reject it, as that will lead to their ultimate downfall.
orig: ولا تكونن من الذين كذبوا بآيات الله فتكون من الخاسرين

translation: Indeed, the word of your Lord has come into effect upon those who disbelieved, [in that] they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who have been destined to disbelieve will not accept faith, no matter how much they are invited or exposed to the truth. It suggests that faith is a matter of divine decree, and those who are meant to believe will do so, while those who are meant to disbelieve will persist in their rejection of the truth.
orig: إن الذين حقت عليهم كلمت ربك لا يؤمنون

translation: And even if they were brought every sign until they see the painful punishment
interpretation: This verse suggests that even if the disbelievers were shown every possible miraculous sign, they would still refuse to believe until they actually witness the painful punishment of the Hereafter. It emphasizes the stubbornness and unwillingness of some people to accept the truth, even in the face of clear evidence.
orig: ولو جاءتهم كل آية حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: So why was there not a city that believed so that its faith would benefit it except the people of Jonah? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in worldly life and gave them enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith and its ability to bring about positive change. It contrasts the people of Jonah, who believed and were saved from punishment, with other cities that did not believe. The verse emphasizes that faith can protect a people from disgrace and bring them enjoyment, even if only for a limited time. The lesson is that true faith and belief in God can lead to salvation and a better life, both in this world and the hereafter.
orig: فلولا كانت قرية آمنت فنفعها إيمانها إلا قوم يونس لما آمنوا كشفنا عنهم عذاب الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ومتعناهم إلى حين

translation: And if your Lord had willed, all those who are on the earth would have believed, all of them. Then, [O Muhammad], would you compel the people in order that they become believers?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that faith is a matter of choice, not coercion. God has the power to make all people believers, but He has given them the free will to choose their own path. The verse suggests that it is not the role of the Prophet or any other person to force belief upon others, as true faith can only come from an individual's own conviction and willingness to accept it.
orig: ولو شاء ربك لآمن من في الأرض كلهم جميعا أفأنت تكره الناس حتى يكونوا مؤمنين

translation: And it is not for a soul to believe except by permission of Allah. And He will place defilement upon those who will not use reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that faith in Allah is a gift granted by Allah, not something that can be attained solely through human effort. It also suggests that those who do not use their intellect and reason to understand the signs of Allah will be subject to spiritual impurity and corruption.
orig: وما كان لنفس أن تؤمن إلا بإذن الله ويجعل الرجس على الذين لا يعقلون

translation: Say, "Look at what is in the heavens and earth." But of no avail will be signs or warners to a people who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to observe and reflect on the signs of God's creation in the heavens and the earth. However, it also acknowledges that such signs and warnings will not benefit those who stubbornly refuse to believe. The message is that faith and belief cannot be forced, but must come from within through sincere contemplation and openness to the truth.
orig: قل انظروا ماذا في السماوات والأرض وما تغني الآيات والنذر عن قوم لا يؤمنون

translation: Are they waiting except for [what occurred to] the days of those who passed on before them? Say, "Then wait, for I am with you among those who wait."
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to be patient and steadfast, just as those before them were. It reminds them that they are not alone in their struggles, and that God is with them as they wait for the ultimate fulfillment of His promises.
orig: فهل ينتظرون إلا مثل أيام الذين خلوا من قبلهم قل فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: Then We save Our messengers and those who have believed. [It is] incumbent upon Us to save the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God will save and protect His messengers and those who have faith in Him. It is an affirmation of God's promise to deliver the believers from harm and distress, as it is incumbent upon Him to do so.
orig: ثم ننجي رسلنا والذين آمنوا كذلك حقا علينا ننج المؤمنين

translation: Say, "O people, if you are in doubt about my religion, then I do not worship those you worship besides Allah, but I worship Allah, who causes your death. And I have been commanded to be of the believers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having a firm belief in the oneness of God (Allah) and the necessity of worshipping Him alone. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is instructed to convey this message clearly to the people, even if they are doubtful about his religion. The interpretation suggests that true faith and worship should be directed solely towards Allah, the Creator and Sustainer of all existence, who has power over life and death.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في شك من ديني فلا أعبد الذين تعبدون من دون الله ولكن أعبد الله الذي يتوفاكم وأمرت أن أكون من المؤمنين

translation: And direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. And never be of those who associate others with Allah
interpretation: This verse calls for a sincere and unwavering devotion to the true religion of Islam, free from any form of polytheism or idolatry. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a pure and upright faith, turning one's attention solely towards the worship of the One true God, and avoiding any association with false deities or practices.
orig: وأن أقم وجهك للدين حنيفا ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: And do not invoke besides Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you did, then indeed you would be of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse advises against worshiping or seeking help from anything other than Allah, as these false deities can neither benefit nor harm you. Seeking help or worship from anything besides Allah is considered an act of injustice and wrongdoing.
orig: ولا تدع من دون الله ما لا ينفعك ولا يضرك فإن فعلت فإنك إذا من الظالمين

translation: And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him. And if He intends for you [any] good, then there is no repeller of His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and power of Allah over all affairs. It highlights that only Allah can remove any adversity or hardship that may befall a person, and that only He can bestow any good or blessing. The verse also underscores Allah's wisdom and mercy in choosing whom to favor with His bounty, and that He is the Forgiving and Merciful towards His servants.
orig: وإن يمسسك الله بضر فلا كاشف له إلا هو وإن يردك بخير فلا راد لفضله يصيب به من يشاء من عباده وهو الغفور الرحيم

translation: Say, "O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord, so whoever is guided is only [guided] for [the benefit of] his soul, and whoever goes astray only goes astray [in violation] of it. And I am not over you a manager."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the truth has been revealed by God, and that each person is responsible for their own guidance or misguidance. Those who accept the truth will benefit themselves, while those who reject it will harm themselves. The Prophet is not responsible for people's choices, as they have been given the ability to discern the truth for themselves.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم الحق من ربكم فمن اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها وما أنا عليكم بوكيل

translation: And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah decides. And He is the best of judges.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain steadfast in following the divine revelation and to be patient until Allah's judgment is delivered. It reminds that Allah is the best of judges, and His judgment is always just and wise.
orig: واتبع ما يوحى إليك واصبر حتى يحكم الله وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. [This is] a Book whose verses have been perfected and then presented in detail from [one who is] Wise and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse introduces the Qur'an as a divinely revealed book whose verses have been perfected and presented in detail by the Wise and All-Knowing God. It emphasizes the Qur'an's authority, clarity, and divine origin, guiding the reader to approach it with reverence and contemplation.
orig: الر كتاب أحكمت آياته ثم فصلت من لدن حكيم خبير

translation: Worship none but Allah. Verily, I (Muhammad) am unto you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief that God (Allah) alone is worthy of worship. It also highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger sent by God to warn people against disbelief and to give them the good news of salvation through faith and righteous deeds.
orig: ألا تعبدوا إلا الله إنني لكم منه نذير وبشير

translation: And [that] you seek forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him [in confidence]. He will [then] provide you with a good provision for a specified term and give every owner of grace [his] grace. But if you turn away, then indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great Day.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to seek forgiveness from Allah and then turn to Him in repentance. It promises that those who do so will be provided with good sustenance for a specified period, and that Allah will grant His grace to those who deserve it. However, it also warns that those who turn away from Allah will face the punishment of a momentous Day of Judgment.
orig: وأن استغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه يمتعكم متاعا حسنا إلى أجل مسمى ويؤت كل ذي فضل فضله وإن تولوا فإني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم كبير

translation: To Allah is your return, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that ultimately, all people will return to Allah for judgment, and that Allah has the power and ability to control all things in the universe. It serves as a reminder of our accountability to Allah and His sovereignty over all creation.
orig: إلى الله مرجعكم وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: Unquestionably, they turn away their chests to hide from Him. Unquestionably, [even] when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they declare. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and aware of the innermost thoughts and intentions of people, even when they try to hide them. It serves as a reminder that one cannot escape the knowledge and judgment of Allah, and that one should be mindful of one's actions and thoughts, as Allah is aware of them all.
orig: ألا إنهم يثنون صدورهم ليستخفوا منه ألا حين يستغشون ثيابهم يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And there is no creature on [or within] the earth or bird that flies with its wings except [that they are] communities like you. We have not neglected in the Register a thing. Then unto their Lord they will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the provider and sustainer of all living beings on Earth. He knows the dwelling place and resting place of every creature, and all of this is recorded in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). This highlights Allah's omniscience and control over all of creation.
orig: وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها ويعلم مستقرها ومستودعها كل في كتاب مبين

translation: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days - and His Throne had been upon water - that He might test you as to which of you is best in deed. And if you say, "Indeed, you are resurrected after death," those who disbelieve will surely say, "This is not but obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power as the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and establishes that He has sovereignty over all creation. The reference to His Throne being upon water suggests His dominion and control over the universe. The verse then states that God created all of this as a test for humanity, to see who will do the best deeds. Finally, it addresses the disbelievers who will reject the concept of resurrection, dismissing it as "obvious magic". The interpretation underscores God's supreme authority, the purpose of creation as a test, and the skepticism of those who deny the afterlife.
orig: وهو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام وكان عرشه على الماء ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا ولئن قلت إنكم مبعوثون من بعد الموت ليقولن الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And if We delay the punishment for them until a limited time, they will surely say, "What detains it?" Unquestionably, on the Day it comes to them, it will not be averted from them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse warns those who deny the Day of Judgment and mock the idea of divine punishment. It suggests that even if Allah delays the punishment for a limited time, the disbelievers will question why it has not come yet. However, on the Day of Judgment, the punishment will not be averted from them, and they will be enveloped by the very thing they used to ridicule. This emphasizes the certainty of divine retribution and the futility of denying or mocking it.
orig: ولئن أخرنا عنهم العذاب إلى أمة معدودة ليقولن ما يحبسه ألا يوم يأتيهم ليس مصروفا عنهم وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And if We give man a taste of mercy from Us and then withdraw it from him, indeed, he is despairing and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to be ungrateful and despairing when faced with the withdrawal of Allah's blessings and mercy. It suggests that people often take Allah's favors for granted and become disheartened when they are removed, rather than turning to Allah in gratitude and seeking His continued guidance and support.
orig: ولئن أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة ثم نزعناها منه إنه ليئوس كفور

translation: And if We let him taste a favor after an adversity has touched him, he will surely say, "Bad times have gone away from me." Indeed, he is exultant and boastful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of some people to become arrogant and boastful when they experience good fortune after facing hardship. It suggests that they may forget the difficulties they have overcome and attribute their success solely to their own abilities, rather than acknowledging the role of God's blessings and guidance. The verse serves as a reminder to maintain humility and gratitude even in times of prosperity.
orig: ولئن أذقناه نعماء بعد ضراء مسته ليقولن ذهب السيئات عني إنه لفرح فخور

translation: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds - those will have a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have faith in God and do good deeds will be forgiven and receive a great reward from God. The key message is that belief and righteous actions are essential for attaining God's mercy and eternal bliss.
orig: إلا الذين صبروا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: So perhaps, [O Muhammad], you would leave part of what is revealed to you and your breast will be constrained by it because they say, "Why has a treasure not been sent down upon him or [why does] an angel not come with him?" But you are only a warner, and Allah is over all things a [perfect] Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad to remain steadfast in his message, despite the demands of the disbelievers for miracles or material wealth. The interpretation suggests that the Prophet should not be distressed by their skepticism, as his role is to be a warner, and Allah is the ultimate Disposer of all affairs.
orig: فلعلك تارك بعض ما يوحى إليك وضائق به صدرك أن يقولوا لولا أنزل عليه كنز أو جاء معه ملك إنما أنت نذير والله على كل شيء وكيل

translation: Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "Then bring ten suras like it and call upon [for help] whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who accuse the Prophet Muhammad of inventing the Qur'an to produce even ten chapters similar to it. The Qur'an is a miracle, and no human being can produce anything comparable to it, as it is the word of God revealed to the Prophet. This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and the inability of humans to replicate it, even if they sought help from others besides Allah.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل فأتوا بعشر سور مثله مفتريات وادعوا من استطعتم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And if they do not respond to you, then know that it [i.e., the Qur'an] was revealed [in truth] with the knowledge of Allah and that there is no deity except Him. So will you [not] submit?
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have faith in the divine origin of the Qur'an, even if some people reject its message. It reminds us that the Qur'an was revealed by Allah and that there is no god worthy of worship except Him. The verse then poses a question, challenging the reader to submit to Allah and embrace Islam.
orig: فإلم يستجيبوا لكم فاعلموا أنما أنزل بعلم الله وأن لا إله إلا هو فهل أنتم مسلمون

translation: Whoever desires the life of this world and [its] adornments - We will fully give them their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are solely focused on the material and worldly aspects of life, and seek only its pleasures and adornments, will be given what they desire in this life. However, they will not be deprived of the consequences of their actions, as they will be fully accountable for them in this world. The verse suggests that true fulfillment and reward comes from seeking a higher purpose beyond the fleeting pleasures of this world.
orig: من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها نوف إليهم أعمالهم فيها وهم فيها لا يبخسون

translation: Those are the ones for whom there will be nothing [of reward] in the Hereafter, and their deeds in this world are lost, and they are, in the Hereafter, among the losers.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have rejected faith and turned away from the guidance of Allah. They will have no share in the rewards of the Hereafter, and their deeds in this world will be in vain, as they were not done for the sake of Allah. They will be among the ultimate losers on the Day of Judgement.
orig: أولئك الذين ليس لهم في الآخرة إلا النار وحبط ما صنعوا فيها وباطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Is he who is upon clear evidence from his Lord like him to whom the evil of his deed has been made pleasing and they follow their [own] desires? [Is] the description of Paradise, which the righteous are promised, [not that] wherein are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk the taste of which never changes, and rivers of wine delicious to those who drink, and rivers of honey purified? And for them therein are all [kinds of] fruits and forgiveness from their Lord. [Are they] like him who abides eternally in the Fire and are given to drink scalding water that will sever their intestines?
interpretation: This verse contrasts those who have clear guidance from God, and those who follow their own desires. The former are promised Paradise, with its pure and delightful rivers, while the latter are condemned to eternal punishment in the Fire. The verse emphasizes that the truth from God is clear, and that those who reject it will face severe consequences, but most people still do not believe.
orig: أفمن كان على بينة من ربه ويتلوه شاهد منه ومن قبله كتاب موسى إماما ورحمة أولئك يؤمنون به ومن يكفر به من الأحزاب فالنار موعده فلا تك في مرية منه إنه الحق من ربك ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah? Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, "These are the ones who lied against their Lord." Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who falsely attribute lies and falsehoods to Allah. It emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, these people will be brought before their Lord, and the witnesses (the angels, prophets, and righteous people) will testify against them, confirming that they had lied about Allah. The verse concludes by declaring that the curse of Allah is upon those who commit such a grave injustice.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أولئك يعرضون على ربهم ويقول الأشهاد هؤلاء الذين كذبوا على ربهم ألا لعنة الله على الظالمين

translation: Those who turn [others] away from the way of Allah and seek to make it [seem] deviant while they, concerning the Hereafter, are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who actively work to turn people away from the path of Allah and seek to distort the true religion. It suggests that such individuals, despite their outward claims, are in reality disbelievers who do not truly believe in the Hereafter and the accountability that comes with it.
orig: الذين يصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: Those were not able to escape [destruction] upon the earth, and they had not besides Allah any protectors. For them the punishment will be doubled. They were not able to hear, nor did they see.
interpretation: This verse conveys that those who reject faith and disbelieve in Allah will not be able to escape the consequences of their actions on earth. They will have no one to protect them from the punishment of Allah. Their punishment will be doubled as they had the faculties of hearing and sight but chose to misuse them. The verse emphasizes that disbelievers will face severe retribution for their denial of faith and refusal to heed the signs of Allah.
orig: أولئك لم يكونوا معجزين في الأرض وما كان لهم من دون الله من أولياء يضاعف لهم العذاب ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع وما كانوا يبصرون

translation: Those are the ones who have lost themselves, and lost from them is what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have lost their way and strayed from the path of truth. They have been deluded by their own fabrications and false beliefs, which have ultimately led to their own spiritual and moral downfall.
orig: أولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Undoubtedly, they will be the greatest losers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith and do not believe in the Hereafter will be the greatest losers. They will suffer eternal punishment and deprivation in the Afterlife, which is far more severe than any worldly losses they may have experienced.
orig: لا جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds and humbled themselves to their Lord - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true believers who combine faith with righteous actions and humility before God will be rewarded with eternal life in Paradise. The key to attaining this blessed state is the combination of sincere belief, good deeds, and a humble and submissive attitude towards the Almighty.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وأخبتوا إلى ربهم أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: The example of the two parties is like the blind and deaf, and the seeing and hearing. Are they equal in comparison? Will you not then remember?
interpretation: This verse draws a comparison between those who believe in God and those who reject faith. The believers, who can see the truth and hear the guidance, are like those who can see and hear. In contrast, the disbelievers, who are blind and deaf to the signs of God, are like those who cannot see or hear. The verse emphasizes that these two groups cannot be considered equal, and it calls upon the people to reflect and remember this distinction.
orig: مثل الفريقين كالأعمى والأصم والبصير والسميع هل يستويان مثلا أفلا تذكرون

translation: And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, [saying], "Indeed, I am to you a clear warner,"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah sent the prophet Noah to his people as a clear warner, calling them to worship Allah alone and abandon idolatry. The verse underscores the importance of prophets in delivering the divine message and guiding people towards the right path.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه إني لكم نذير مبين

translation: That you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful Day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping and submitting only to Allah, the One true God. It warns against associating partners with Allah, as that would incur a severe punishment on the Day of Judgment. The interpretation is a call to monotheism and a reminder of the consequences of idolatry and polytheism.
orig: أن لا تعبدوا إلا الله إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم أليم

translation: The eminent among his people who disbelieved said, "We do not see you but as a man like ourselves, and we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us, [and] at first suggestion. And we do not see in you any merit over us; rather, we think you are liars."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the disbelieving leaders of the people to the prophet's message. They dismissed him as just a regular man like themselves, and they saw his followers as the lowest and most insignificant members of society. They did not see any merit or superiority in the prophet, and they accused him of being a liar. This reflects the arrogance and close-mindedness of those who rejected the prophet's message out of hand, without considering it objectively.
orig: فقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه ما نراك إلا بشرا مثلنا وما نراك اتبعك إلا الذين هم أراذلنا بادي الرأي وما نرى لكم علينا من فضل بل نظنكم كاذبين

translation: He said, "O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has provided me with a mercy from Himself...?"
interpretation: This verse expresses the frustration of a prophet or messenger who has received clear guidance and a divine mercy, yet his people stubbornly reject it. The interpretation is that even when presented with undeniable truth and blessings from God, some people may still refuse to accept it out of arrogance or bias. The prophet is questioning why he should have to force his people to accept what they are unwilling to accept, highlighting the futility of compulsion in matters of faith.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي وآتاني رحمة من عنده فعميت عليكم أنلزمكموها وأنتم لها كارهون

translation: And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth in return [for my message]. My reward is only from Allah, and I will not drive away those who have believed. Indeed, they will meet their Lord, but I see that you are a people behaving ignorantly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet does not seek any material reward for conveying the message of Islam. His only reward is from Allah. He also affirms that he will not turn away those who have believed, as they will meet their Lord. However, the Prophet sees his people as behaving ignorantly, not recognizing the truth of the message he has brought.
orig: ويا قوم لا أسألكم عليه مالا إن أجري إلا على الله وما أنا بطارد الذين آمنوا إنهم ملاقو ربهم ولكني أراكم قوما تجهلون

translation: And O my people, who will help me against Allah if I drive them away? Then will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse encourages the people to reflect on their actions and seek guidance from Allah, rather than turning away from Him. It reminds them that they cannot find true help or protection without Allah's support, and that they should remember this fact and not forget it.
orig: ويا قوم من ينصرني من الله إن طردتهم أفلا تذكرون

translation: And I do not say to you that I have the treasuries of Allah or that I know the unseen. And I do not say that I am an angel, and I do not say of those whom your eyes look down upon that Allah will never grant them good - Allah is most knowing of what is within them. Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humility and honesty of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in his message. He does not claim to have access to the divine treasuries or the knowledge of the unseen, nor does he claim to be an angel. He also does not look down upon or dismiss those whom others may consider insignificant, for Allah knows best what is in their hearts. This teaches us to be humble, honest, and compassionate in our dealings with others, and to refrain from making claims or judgments that are beyond our knowledge and capabilities.
orig: ولا أقول لكم عندي خزائن الله ولا أعلم الغيب ولا أقول إني ملك ولا أقول للذين تزدري أعينكم لن يؤتيهم الله خيرا الله أعلم بما في أنفسهم إني إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: They said, "O Noah, you have disputed with us and prolonged the dispute, so bring us what you threaten us with, if you should be of the truthful."
interpretation: The people challenged Noah to bring about the punishment he had warned them about if he was truly a messenger of God. They were skeptical of his message and wanted him to prove the truth of what he was saying.
orig: قالوا يا نوح قد جادلتنا فأكثرت جدالنا فأتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He (the Messenger) says, "Verily, it is Allah Who brings it (the Qur'an) down to you. And if He wills, He will keep you from believing in it."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, not something fabricated by the Prophet Muhammad. It also suggests that belief in the Qur'an is ultimately a matter of Allah's will - He can guide people to believe in it, or He can withhold that guidance if He so chooses. The verse serves as a reminder that human beings are not able to escape or overpower Allah's decree.
orig: قال إنما يأتيكم به الله إن شاء وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: And my advice will not benefit you if I intend to advise you if Allah intends to send you astray. He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that even if one tries to advise or guide others, it is ultimately up to Allah's will whether that guidance will be accepted or not. The verse suggests that human efforts alone are not sufficient, as Allah has the power to guide or misguide people as He wills. It reminds us that we should submit to Allah's sovereignty and plan, and that our ultimate return is to Him.
orig: ولا ينفعكم نصحي إن أردت أن أنصح لكم إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم هو ربكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "If I have invented it, then upon me is [the consequence of] my crime, but I am innocent of what [crimes] you commit."
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusation that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) had invented the Qur'an. The response given is that even if that were the case, the responsibility for such an act would be upon the Prophet himself, but he is innocent of the crimes that the disbelievers commit by rejecting the message of the Qur'an. This affirms the authenticity of the Qur'an as a divine revelation and places the burden of proof on those who deny it.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل إن افتريته فعلي إجرامي وأنا بريء مما تجرمون

translation: And it was revealed to Noah that no one from your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed by what they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse conveys the message that Prophet Noah was informed by divine revelation that only a few from his people would believe in the message of monotheism and the worship of one God. The rest would persist in their disbelief and rejection. Noah is advised not to be saddened or distressed by the actions of those who refuse to accept the truth, as this was a predetermined outcome.
orig: وأوحي إلى نوح أنه لن يؤمن من قومك إلا من قد آمن فلا تبتئس بما كانوا يفعلون

translation: And construct the ship under Our observation and Our inspiration and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are [to be] drowned.
interpretation: This verse instructs Prophet Noah to build the ark under the direct supervision and guidance of God. It also warns Noah not to plead with God on behalf of the wrongdoers, as they are destined to be drowned in the flood. The verse emphasizes God's omniscience and power in directing the events, as well as the inevitability of punishment for those who have transgressed against Him.
orig: واصنع الفلك بأعيننا ووحينا ولا تخاطبني في الذين ظلموا إنهم مغرقون

translation: And he constructs the ship, and whenever a group of his people passes by him, they ridicule him. [Noah] said, "If you ridicule us, then we will ridicule you just as you ridicule [us]."
interpretation: This verse highlights the response of Prophet Noah to the ridicule and mockery he faced from his people as he built the ship in preparation for the coming flood. Despite the scorn and derision, Noah remained steadfast in his faith and warned his people that their mockery would be met with divine retribution, just as they mocked him and his followers.
orig: ويصنع الفلك وكلما مر عليه ملأ من قومه سخروا منه قال إن تسخروا منا فإنا نسخر منكم كما تسخرون

translation: So you will come to know who it is to whom will come a punishment that will disgrace him and upon whom will descend an enduring punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and persist in their wrongdoing. It suggests that they will eventually face a punishment that will humiliate them and bring upon them a lasting and severe chastisement. The verse emphasizes the certainty of divine retribution for those who defy the teachings of the Qur'an and refuse to submit to the will of God.
orig: فسوف تعلمون من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ويحل عليه عذاب مقيم

translation: Until when Our command came and the oven overflowed, We said, "Embark therein of each [creature] two males and two females, and your family, except those about whom the word has preceded, and [include] those who have believed." And none had believed with him, except a few.
interpretation: This verse describes the events leading up to the Great Flood during the time of the Prophet Noah. It indicates that when the time of the flood came and the oven began to overflow, Noah was commanded to board the ark with his family and two of every kind of animal, except those who had already been condemned and a few believers who had faith in Noah's message. This verse highlights God's power in deciding the fate of those who reject the truth and the importance of faith in times of great calamity.
orig: حتى إذا جاء أمرنا وفار التنور قلنا احمل فيها من كل زوجين اثنين وأهلك إلا من سبق عليه القول ومن آمن وما آمن معه إلا قليل

translation: And he said, 'Embark therein, in the name of Allah, its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to place their trust in Allah, the Merciful and Forgiving, when undertaking a journey or any endeavor. It reminds us to invoke Allah's name and seek His protection, as He is the One who guides and safeguards us throughout our lives.
orig: وقال اركبوا فيها بسم الله مجراها ومرساها إن ربي لغفور رحيم

translation: And it sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Noah called to his son while he was separated [from them]: "O my son, come aboard with us and be not with the disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse describes the tumultuous journey of Noah's ark during the great flood. Despite the treacherous waves, the ark sailed on, carrying Noah and the believers. Yet, Noah's own son remained separated from them, refusing to join. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the need to disassociate from disbelief, even in the face of familial ties.
orig: وهي تجري بهم في موج كالجبال ونادى نوح ابنه وكان في معزل يا بني اركب معنا ولا تكن مع الكافرين

translation: He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain to protect me from the water." [God] said, "There is no protector today from the decree of Allah except for whom He gives mercy." And the waves came between them, and he was among the drowned.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of seeking refuge in worldly things when faced with the decree of Allah. The person sought refuge on a mountain, thinking it would protect him, but Allah made it clear that only His mercy can save someone from His decree. The verse serves as a reminder that true protection and salvation comes from Allah alone, not from any physical or material means.
orig: قال سآوي إلى جبل يعصمني من الماء قال لا عاصم اليوم من أمر الله إلا من رحم وحال بينهما الموج فكان من المغرقين

translation: And it was said, 'O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain].' And the water subsided, and the matter was accomplished, and the ship came to rest on the [mount] Judiyy. And it was said, 'Away with the wrongdoing people!'
interpretation: This verse describes the culmination of the flood that destroyed the wrongdoing people during the time of Prophet Noah. The earth is commanded to swallow its water, the sky to withhold its rain, and the flood waters recede, allowing the ship to come to rest on Mount Judiyy. The verse conveys a message of divine justice, as the wrongdoing people are condemned and removed from the earth, making way for a new beginning.
orig: وقيل يا أرض ابلعي ماءك ويا سماء أقلعي وغيض الماء وقضي الأمر واستوت على الجودي وقيل بعدا للقوم الظالمين

translation: And Noah called to his Lord and said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed, Your promise is true, and You are the most just of judges."
interpretation: This verse reflects Noah's grief and concern for his son, who did not believe and was therefore not saved from the flood. Noah acknowledges God's promise of salvation for his family, but recognizes that God is the ultimate judge in determining who is worthy. The verse highlights the tension between familial ties and divine judgment, and Noah's submission to God's wisdom.
orig: ونادى نوح ربه فقال رب إن ابني من أهلي وإن وعدك الحق وأنت أحكم الحاكمين

translation: He (Allah) said: 'O Nuh (Noah)! Verily, he is not of your family; verily, his work is unrighteous, so ask Me not about that which you have no knowledge of. I admonish you lest you should be one of the ignorant.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that a person's relationship with Allah is not determined by their family ties, but rather by their deeds and faith. It warns against making assumptions or requests without proper knowledge, and encourages seeking guidance from Allah to avoid ignorance.
orig: قال يا نوح إنه ليس من أهلك إنه عمل غير صالح فلا تسألن ما ليس لك به علم إني أعظك أن تكون من الجاهلين

translation: He (Moses) said, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking that of which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers."
interpretation: This verse reflects the humility and wisdom of the Prophet Moses, as he recognizes the limitations of his own knowledge and understanding. He seeks refuge in Allah, acknowledging that he may ask for things without fully comprehending their implications. Moses implores Allah to forgive him and have mercy on him, lest he be among those who suffer loss. This verse teaches us to approach Allah with humility, acknowledging our own shortcomings, and seeking His guidance and forgiveness.
orig: قال رب إني أعوذ بك أن أسألك ما ليس لي به علم وإلا تغفر لي وترحمني أكن من الخاسرين

translation: It was said, "O Noah, disembark in peace from Us, and blessings upon you and upon nations [descending] from those with you. And [other] nations - We will grant them enjoyment; then there will touch them from Us a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse signifies that Noah and his followers will be granted a safe and peaceful disembarkment from the Ark, and that they will be blessed by God. It also suggests that other nations, who were not with Noah, will be allowed to enjoy their lives for a time, but will ultimately face a painful punishment from God for their disbelief and transgressions.
orig: قيل يا نوح اهبط بسلام منا وبركات عليك وعلى أمم ممن معك وأمم سنمتعهم ثم يمسهم منا عذاب أليم

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muhammad]. You knew it not, neither you nor your people, before this. So be patient; indeed, the [best] outcome is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the knowledge of the unseen and future events is a divine prerogative, which God reveals to His Messengers as He wills. It encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to be patient and steadfast in the face of adversity, as the ultimate outcome is for those who fear God and lead righteous lives.
orig: تلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيها إليك ما كنت تعلمها أنت ولا قومك من قبل هذا فاصبر إن العاقبة للمتقين

translation: And to [the tribe of] 'Ād [We sent] their brother Hūd. He said, 'O my people, worship Allāh; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear [Him]?'
interpretation: This verse calls upon the people of 'Ād to worship only Allāh, the one true God, and to abandon their false idols and deities. It emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle of Tawheed (the Oneness of God) and the rejection of polytheism. The verse serves as a warning to the people of 'Ād to fear Allāh and submit to Him, as He is the only worthy object of worship.
orig: وإلى عاد أخاهم هودا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره إن أنتم إلا مفترون

translation: O my people, I do not ask you for wealth in return [for my guidance]. My reward is only from the One who created me; so will you not reason?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the Prophet does not seek any material reward or compensation for conveying the message of God. His only reward is from the One who created him, i.e., God. This highlights the sincerity and selflessness of the Prophet’s mission, and calls upon the people to use their reason and intellect to understand and accept the divine guidance being offered to them.
orig: يا قوم لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إن أجري إلا على الذي فطرني أفلا تعقلون

translation: And O my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in showers and increase you in strength [added] to your [existing] strength, and do not turn away, [being] criminals.
interpretation: This verse encourages the people to seek forgiveness from God and repent, as this will lead to blessings such as abundant rain and increased strength. It warns against turning away and being criminals, which would result in the loss of these blessings.
orig: ويا قوم استغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا ويزدكم قوة إلى قوتكم ولا تتولوا مجرمين

translation: They said, "O Hud, you have not brought us with any clear proof, and we are not ones to abandon our gods on your say-so. And we are not believers in you."
interpretation: This verse reflects the stubborn rejection of Hud's message by his people. They demand clear proof and evidence to abandon their traditional beliefs and gods, which they are unwilling to do based solely on Hud's words. This highlights the challenge faced by prophets in convincing people to forsake their long-held religious practices and accept a new faith, even when it is the truth.
orig: قالوا يا هود ما جئتنا ببينة وما نحن بتاركي آلهتنا عن قولك وما نحن لك بمؤمنين

translation: Truly, we say nothing but that some of our gods have possessed you with evil.' He said: 'I call Allah to witness, and bear you witness, that I am free from that which you associate (with Allah).
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between the Prophet Muhammad and the polytheists of Mecca. The polytheists accused the Prophet of being possessed by some of their gods, which he firmly rejects. Instead, he declares his complete devotion to the One True God, Allah, and disassociates himself from their polytheistic beliefs and practices.
orig: إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء قال إني أشهد الله واشهدوا أني بريء مما تشركون

translation: Then plot against me all together and do not give me respite.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking refuge in God alone, and not relying on any other power or authority. It suggests that those who turn away from God and seek help from others will ultimately face the consequences of their actions, as they will be unable to escape the divine plan. The verse encourages believers to have faith in God and to seek His guidance and protection, rather than turning to worldly powers or authorities.
orig: من دونه فكيدوني جميعا ثم لا تنظرون

translation: Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its [moving] forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah, the Lord of all creation. It highlights that Allah has control over all creatures, and that He guides them on the straight path. The interpretation is that one should put their trust in Allah, as He is the ultimate authority and guide in the universe.
orig: إني توكلت على الله ربي وربكم ما من دابة إلا هو آخذ بناصيتها إن ربي على صراط مستقيم

translation: But if they turn away, [O Muhammad], I have already conveyed to you that with which I was sent to you. And my Lord will give succession to a people other than you, and you will not harm Him at all. Indeed, my Lord is, over all things, Guardian.
interpretation: If the people reject the message you have brought, O Muhammad, then you have fulfilled your duty by conveying it to them. My Lord will then replace you with another people who will accept the message. You cannot harm God in any way, for He is the Guardian over all things.
orig: فإن تولوا فقد أبلغتكم ما أرسلت به إليكم ويستخلف ربي قوما غيركم ولا تضرونه شيئا إن ربي على كل شيء حفيظ

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us. And We saved them from a harsh punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights how Allah (God) saved the Prophet Hud and his followers from a severe punishment due to their faith and belief in Him. It demonstrates Allah's mercy and protection for those who remain steadfast in their faith, even in the face of adversity.
orig: ولما جاء أمرنا نجينا هودا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا ونجيناهم من عذاب غليظ

translation: And that [was] 'Aad, who rejected the signs of their Lord and disobeyed His messengers and followed the order of every obstinate tyrant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of the 'Aad people, who rejected the signs and messages of God, and instead followed the orders of arrogant and tyrannical leaders. This serves as a warning that blindly following the commands of powerful but unjust rulers can lead to destruction, and that true guidance comes from submitting to the will of God and His messengers.
orig: وتلك عاد جحدوا بآيات ربهم وعصوا رسله واتبعوا أمر كل جبار عنيد

translation: And they were pursued by a curse in this world and [as well as] on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, Aad disbelieved in their Lord; so away with Aad, the people of Hud.
interpretation: This verse conveys a strong warning against disbelief and rejection of God. The people of Aad, who were the followers of the prophet Hud, were cursed in this life and will face further punishment on the Day of Resurrection for their denial of their Lord. The repeated use of the phrase "so away with Aad" emphasizes the severe consequences of their disbelief and the distance they have placed between themselves and God's guidance.
orig: وأتبعوا في هذه الدنيا لعنة ويوم القيامة ألا إن عادا كفروا ربهم ألا بعدا لعاد قوم هود

translation: And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. He has produced you from the earth and settled you in it, so ask forgiveness of Him and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive."
interpretation: This verse calls upon the people of Thamud to worship only Allah, the one true God, who created them and established them on the earth. It emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah and repenting to Him, as He is ever-present and responsive to those who turn to Him. The message is one of monotheism, humility, and the need for a direct relationship with the Divine.
orig: وإلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره هو أنشأكم من الأرض واستعمركم فيها فاستغفروه ثم توبوا إليه إن ربي قريب مجيب

translation: They said, "O Salih, you were among us a man of promise before this. Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped? And indeed we are, about that to which you invite us, in disquieting doubt."
interpretation: The people are questioning Salih and expressing their skepticism about abandoning the religion of their forefathers to follow his teachings. They are doubtful and uncertain about the new beliefs he is calling them to, seeing it as a departure from their established traditions.
orig: قالوا يا صالح قد كنت فينا مرجوا قبل هذا أتنهانا أن نعبد ما يعبد آباؤنا وإننا لفي شك مما تدعونا إليه مريب

translation: He said, 'O my people, have you considered: if I should be on clear evidence from my Lord and He has provided me with a mercy from Himself, who would protect me from Allah if I disobeyed Him? So you would not increase me except in loss.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of obedience to Allah and the consequences of disobedience. The speaker, who is likely a prophet, emphasizes that he is on clear evidence from his Lord and has been granted a mercy from Him. He then asks his people who would protect him from Allah's punishment if he were to disobey Him, implying that there is no one who can save him from Allah's wrath. The interpretation suggests that true guidance and mercy come from Allah, and that disobedience to Him will only lead to further loss and suffering.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي وآتاني منه رحمة فمن ينصرني من الله إن عصيته فما تزيدونني غير تخسير

translation: And O my people, this is the she-camel of Allah, [which is] to you a sign. So let her eat within the land of Allah and do not touch her with harm, lest you be seized by a near punishment.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the people to recognize the she-camel as a sign from Allah and to allow it to graze freely in the land without harming it. Disrespecting or harming the she-camel would result in a swift punishment from Allah.
