orig: ويا قوم هذه ناقة الله لكم آية فذروها تأكل في أرض الله ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب قريب

translation: So they hamstrung her, and woke up the next morning regretful. Then he said, "Enjoy yourselves in your home for three days. This is a promise [i.e., a threat] that will not be belied."
interpretation: This verse describes the aftermath of the people of Thamud rejecting and killing the she-camel sent as a sign by God. The interpretation is that the people were given a brief respite of three days before facing the consequences of their disobedience, which would surely come to pass as God's promise is inviolable.
orig: فعقروها فقال تمتعوا في داركم ثلاثة أيام ذلك وعد غير مكذوب

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Ṣāliḥ and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us and [saved them] from the disgrace of that Day. Indeed, it is your Lord who is the Powerful, the Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse highlights that when the divine command came to punish the people of Ṣāliḥ for their rejection of his message, God saved Ṣāliḥ and those who believed in him, out of His mercy. They were spared from the disgrace and punishment that befell the disbelievers on that fateful day. This demonstrates the power and might of God, who is able to protect and deliver those who have faith in Him, while destroying the arrogant and unrepentant.
orig: فلما جاء أمرنا نجينا صالحا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا ومن خزي يومئذ إن ربك هو القوي العزيز

translation: And the wrongdoers were seized by the Blast, and they became within their homes [laid] motionless.
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine punishment that befell those who persisted in their wrongdoing and oppression. The "Blast" is a metaphor for the calamity that struck them, rendering them lifeless and powerless within their own homes. The interpretation suggests that those who engage in oppression and injustice will ultimately face the consequences of their actions, as decreed by God.
orig: وأخذ الذين ظلموا الصيحة فأصبحوا في ديارهم جاثمين

translation: As if they had not remained there [at all]. Unquestionably, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord. Unquestionably [for], Thamud were removed.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people of Thamud were completely wiped out, as if they had never existed in that place. It emphasizes that the Thamud people had disbelieved in their Lord, and as a result, they were utterly destroyed and removed from existence.
orig: كأن لم يغنوا فيها ألا إن ثمود كفروا ربهم ألا بعدا لثمود

translation: And certainly Our messengers came to Abraham with good news. They said: 'Peace.' He said: 'Peace,' and he delayed not to bring a roasted calf.
interpretation: This verse describes the visit of God's messengers to the prophet Abraham, who received them with hospitality and peace. It highlights Abraham's quick response in preparing a meal for his guests, demonstrating his piety, generosity and reverence towards the divine messengers.
orig: ولقد جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم بالبشرى قالوا سلاما قال سلام فما لبث أن جاء بعجل حنيذ

translation: But when he saw their hands not reaching towards it, he mistrusted them and felt from them apprehension. They said, "Fear not. We have been sent to the people of Lot."
interpretation: This verse describes the encounter between the angels and Prophet Abraham. When the angels arrived at Abraham's home, he was initially suspicious of them and felt apprehension, as he did not see them reaching out to take the food he had prepared. However, the angels reassured him that they had been sent to the people of Lot, and that he need not fear them.
orig: فلما رأى أيديهم لا تصل إليه نكرهم وأوجس منهم خيفة قالوا لا تخف إنا أرسلنا إلى قوم لوط

translation: And his wife was standing, and she laughed. Then We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, [a child,] Jacob.
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of Abraham's wife, Sarah, upon receiving the news that she would give birth to a son, Isaac, and that Isaac would have a son, Jacob. The verse highlights the miraculous nature of this event, as Sarah was advanced in age and had previously been childless. The laughter of Sarah is interpreted as a sign of her joy and disbelief at the news, and the subsequent birth of Isaac and Jacob is seen as a fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham.
orig: وامرأته قائمة فضحكت فبشرناها بإسحاق ومن وراء إسحاق يعقوب

translation: She said, 'Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman, and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is a strange thing.'
interpretation: This verse expresses the surprise and disbelief of the Prophet Abraham's wife, Sarah, upon being informed that she would give birth to a son despite her advanced age and that of her husband. The interpretation suggests that the birth of a child to such an elderly couple was seen as an extraordinary and miraculous event, which prompted Sarah's exclamation of wonder and amazement.
orig: قالت يا ويلتى أألد وأنا عجوز وهذا بعلي شيخا إن هذا لشيء عجيب

translation: They said, "Do you wonder at the decree of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Honorable."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad and his family, affirming that the decree of Allah is not to be wondered at, but rather His mercy and blessings should be recognized and appreciated. The verse emphasizes that Allah is Praiseworthy and Honorable, and His actions are to be accepted with humility and gratitude.
orig: قالوا أتعجبين من أمر الله رحمت الله وبركاته عليكم أهل البيت إنه حميد مجيد

translation: And when the fright had left Abraham and the good tidings had reached him, he began to argue with Us concerning the people of Lot.
interpretation: This verse describes how, after the initial fear and distress that Abraham experienced, he was then comforted by the good news that he would be granted a son. However, he then proceeded to argue with God regarding the fate of the people of Lot, pleading for their deliverance despite their wickedness.
orig: فلما ذهب عن إبراهيم الروع وجاءته البشرى يجادلنا في قوم لوط

translation: Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, grieving, and [frequently] returning [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the noble character of the Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him). It describes him as "forbearing", meaning he was patient, tolerant, and forgiving even in the face of adversity. He was also "grieving", indicating his deep connection to Allah and his sorrow for those who rejected the truth. Finally, he is described as "frequently returning [to Allah]", highlighting his constant devotion, repentance, and turning back to Allah in all matters.
orig: إن إبراهيم لحليم أواه منيب

translation: O Abraham, turn away from this. Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and indeed, there will reach them a punishment that cannot be repelled.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the Prophet Abraham, instructing him to turn away from the unbelievers and their rejection of the message of Islam. It emphasizes that the decree of God has been issued, and that the disbelievers will face an inescapable punishment for their refusal to accept the truth.
orig: يا إبراهيم أعرض عن هذا إنه قد جاء أمر ربك وإنهم آتيهم عذاب غير مردود

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt for them great discomfort and said, 'This is a trying day.'
interpretation: This verse describes the arrival of God's messengers to the people of Lot, who was distressed and troubled by their presence, as he knew the people would react with hostility and rejection of the divine message. Lot's statement 'This is a trying day' reflects his anxiety and concern for the safety of the messengers, as he anticipated the impending punishment that would befall his people for their wicked and immoral behavior.
orig: ولما جاءت رسلنا لوطا سيء بهم وضاق بهم ذرعا وقال هذا يوم عصيب

translation: And his people came hastening to him, and before [this] they had been doing evil deeds. [Lot] said, "O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you. So fear Allah and do not disgrace me concerning my guests. Is there not among you a man of reason?"
interpretation: This verse describes the response of the people of Lot when he tried to warn them against their immoral practices. Lot reminds them that his daughters are purer and more virtuous, and he pleads with them to fear Allah and not to dishonor him by mistreating his guests. The verse emphasizes the importance of moral and righteous conduct, and the need for people to use their reason and wisdom to make the right choices.
orig: وجاءه قومه يهرعون إليه ومن قبل كانوا يعملون السيئات قال يا قوم هؤلاء بناتي هن أطهر لكم فاتقوا الله ولا تخزون في ضيفي أليس منكم رجل رشيد

translation: They said, "Verily, you know that we have no claim on your daughters, and certainly you know what we desire."
interpretation: This verse refers to the response of the people of Lot to his plea to not engage in the immoral practice of homosexuality. They acknowledged that Lot knew they had no legitimate claims on his daughters, but they persisted in their desires, which were contrary to the natural order.
orig: قالوا لقد علمت ما لنا في بناتك من حق وإنك لتعلم ما نريد

translation: He said: "If I had but power against you or could betake myself to some powerful support."
interpretation: This verse expresses the helplessness of the person speaking, who wishes they had the strength or support to resist their adversaries. It suggests that even the most powerful can feel vulnerable and in need of assistance when faced with a formidable opponent.
orig: قال لو أن لي بكم قوة أو آوي إلى ركن شديد

translation: They said, "O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. So set out with your family during a portion of the night and let not any among you look back - except your wife; indeed, she will be struck by that which strikes them. Indeed, their appointment is [for] the morning. Is not the morning near?"
interpretation: This verse describes the angels who were sent to the people of Lot to destroy them for their wicked ways. They informed Lot that they were messengers of God and that the people would not be able to harm Lot. They instructed Lot to leave the city with his family during the night, and not to look back, except for his wife, who would also be destroyed along with the wicked people. This interpretation emphasizes God's justice in punishing the wrongdoers, while protecting the righteous, and the inevitability of the divine punishment.
orig: قالوا يا لوط إنا رسل ربك لن يصلوا إليك فأسر بأهلك بقطع من الليل ولا يلتفت منكم أحد إلا امرأتك إنه مصيبها ما أصابهم إن موعدهم الصبح أليس الصبح بقريب

translation: So when Our command came, We made the highest part [of the city] its lowest and rained upon them stones of hard clay in succession.
interpretation: This verse describes the destruction of an evil society that had been warned but persisted in its wickedness. When God's judgment came, the entire city was turned upside down, and a rain of hard, brimstone-like stones poured down upon it, utterly destroying it. This serves as a warning that those who defy God's commands and reject His guidance will face severe consequences.
orig: فلما جاء أمرنا جعلنا عاليها سافلها وأمطرنا عليها حجارة من سجيل منضود

translation: Marked (for execution) by your Lord, and they are not (at all) far therefrom.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the wrongdoers will be held accountable for their misdeeds, and their punishment is imminent and inevitable. It conveys a sense of certainty and urgency regarding the consequences of unjust actions.
orig: مسومة عند ربك وما هي من الظالمين ببعيد

translation: And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb, who said: 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. And do not decrease in the measure and the scale. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, but indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing Day.'
interpretation: This verse calls the people of Madyan to worship only Allah, the one true God, and to be honest and fair in their dealings by not decreasing the measure and the scale. The Prophet Shu'ayb warns them that he sees them in prosperity, but fears they will face the punishment of a Day that will encompass them if they do not heed his message and repent from their wrongdoings.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره ولا تنقصوا المكيال والميزان إني أراكم بخير وإني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم محيط

translation: And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice and do not deprive the people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to be fair and just in their dealings, to give full measure and weight, and to not deprive others of what is rightfully theirs. It also warns against causing corruption and disruption on the earth. The underlying message is to uphold principles of honesty, fairness, and social responsibility in one's conduct.
orig: ويا قوم أوفوا المكيال والميزان بالقسط ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: What remains [i.e., what Allah gives] is better for you, if you should be believers. And I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to focus on what Allah provides, which is better than worldly possessions. It also clarifies that the Prophet is not responsible for people's faith, as that is a matter between the individual and Allah.
orig: بقيت الله خير لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين وما أنا عليكم بحفيظ

translation: They said, "O Shu'aib, does your prayer command you that we should leave what our fathers worship or not do with our wealth what we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the directed."
interpretation: This verse highlights the resistance and skepticism faced by the prophet Shu'aib from his people when he called them to worship God alone and to be just in their dealings. They questioned the validity of his teachings, implying that he was overstepping his bounds by telling them how to conduct their religious and financial affairs. The verse portrays the people as arrogant, unwilling to submit to God's guidance, and more concerned with their own desires than with moral and ethical conduct. In response, the verse describes Shu'aib as "the forbearing, the directed," suggesting that he remained patient and steadfast in the face of their opposition, and that his teachings were divinely inspired.
orig: قالوا يا شعيب أصلاتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد

translation: He said, "O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has provided me with a good provision from Him...? And I do not intend to differ from you in that which I have forbidden you; I only intend reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through [the assistance of] Allah. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I return [in repentance]."
interpretation: This verse expresses the mindset and approach of a righteous leader who is guiding his people. He affirms that he is acting upon clear guidance from God and has been provided with good provisions, yet he does not wish to differ from his people in matters he has forbidden them. Rather, his intent is to reform and improve their condition as much as he is able, recognizing that his success ultimately depends on the help and support of God, in whom he places his trust and to whom he submits.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي ورزقني منه رزقا حسنا وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه إن أريد إلا الإصلاح ما استطعت وما توفيقي إلا بالله عليه توكلت وإليه أنيب

translation: And O my people, let not your dissension from me cause you that there should befall you [the punishment] like what befell the people of Noah or the people of Hud or the people of Salih. And the people of Lot are not from you far away.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the people to not let their dissension and rejection of the Prophet`s message lead to a punishment similar to that which befell the previous nations who rejected their Prophets. It emphasizes that the fate of the people of Lot is not far from them, implying that they should heed the warning and return to the straight path before it is too late.
orig: ويا قوم لا يجرمنكم شقاقي أن يصيبكم مثل ما أصاب قوم نوح أو قوم هود أو قوم صالح وما قوم لوط منكم ببعيد

translation: And seek forgiveness of your Lord and repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Affectionate.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to seek forgiveness from Allah and to repent to Him. It emphasizes that Allah is Merciful and Loving, and that He readily accepts the repentance of those who turn to Him sincerely. The verse highlights the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness and returning to Him, as He is the source of mercy and compassion.
orig: واستغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه إن ربي رحيم ودود

translation: They said, 'O Shu'aib, we do not understand much of what you say, and indeed, we see that you are weak among us. And if not for your family, we would have stoned you. And you are not to us a powerful [protector].'
interpretation: This verse reflects the rejection and contempt that the people of Shu'aib had towards him and his message. They dismissed his teachings as incomprehensible and saw him as weak, implying that his message lacked authority. Their threat to stone him if not for his family's presence highlights their hostility and unwillingness to accept his guidance. This verse underscores the challenges faced by prophets in conveying the truth to people who are resistant to change and unwilling to heed the divine message.
orig: قالوا يا شعيب ما نفقه كثيرا مما تقول وإنا لنراك فينا ضعيفا ولولا رهطك لرجمناك وما أنت علينا بعزيز

translation: He said: 'O my people, is my family not dearer to you than Allah? But you have put Him behind your backs [in neglect].' Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing one's relationship with Allah over all else, even family ties. It serves as a reminder that Allah should be the primary focus and that neglecting Him in favor of worldly attachments is a grave mistake, as Allah is all-knowing and all-encompassing of our actions.
orig: قال يا قوم أرهطي أعز عليكم من الله واتخذتموه وراءكم ظهريا إن ربي بما تعملون محيط

translation: And O my people, work according to your position. Indeed, I am working, and you are going to know to whom will come a punishment that will disgrace him and who is a liar. And watch, for I am with you a watcher.
interpretation: This verse encourages the people to work and act according to their abilities and status. It warns that those who are liars and deceivers will be disgraced with a punishment, and that the speaker (likely a prophet) is watching over them as an observer. The verse emphasizes the importance of honesty, accountability, and doing one's duty.
orig: ويا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل سوف تعلمون من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ومن هو كاذب وارتقبوا إني معكم رقيب

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Shu'aib and those who believed with him, by a mercy from Us. And the thunderbolt seized those who had wronged, and they became within their homes [found] dead -
interpretation: This verse describes the divine punishment that befell the people of Shu'aib after they persistently rejected his message and continued in their wrongdoing. Despite Shu'aib's efforts to guide them, they remained defiant, and so Allah saved Shu'aib and his followers while destroying the disbelievers through a devastating thunderbolt. This serves as a lesson that those who persist in oppression and disbelief will face the consequences of their actions, while the believers are protected by Allah's mercy.
orig: ولما جاء أمرنا نجينا شعيبا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا وأخذت الذين ظلموا الصيحة فأصبحوا في ديارهم جاثمين

translation: As if they had never dwelt there. So away with Midian, just as Thamud were done away with.
interpretation: This verse conveys a sense of the complete destruction and abandonment of the people of Midian, just as the people of Thamud were destroyed before them. It suggests that the land of Midian will be left desolate, as if its inhabitants had never lived there, emphasizing the finality and severity of their punishment.
orig: كأن لم يغنوا فيها ألا بعدا لمدين كما بعدت ثمود

translation: And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God sent the Prophet Moses with clear signs and evidence to establish the truth of his message. The "clear authority" refers to the miracles and divine support that Moses was granted to validate his prophethood and the divine origin of his teachings.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

translation: To Pharaoh and his establishment, and they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blind obedience of Pharaoh's people to his commands, even when those commands were not righteous or well-guided. It serves as a warning against blindly following the directives of those in power, without critically examining their intentions and the morality of their actions.
orig: إلى فرعون وملئه فاتبعوا أمر فرعون وما أمر فرعون برشيد

translation: He will bring his people on the Day of Resurrection, and he will have caused them to descend into the Fire, and wretched is the place to which they are descended.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that awaits those who reject faith and lead others astray. On the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers will be presented before Allah, and they will be made to enter the hellfire, which is a terrible and wretched destination for them.
orig: يقدم قومه يوم القيامة فأوردهم النار وبئس الورد المورود

translation: And they follow [the decree of] this [world], and upon them will be [entered] a curse on the Day of Resurrection, and wretched is the gift [that will be] given [to them].
interpretation: This verse warns those who blindly follow the ways of this world, without regard for the Hereafter. They will be cursed on the Day of Judgment, and the reward they receive will be wretched and undesirable.
orig: وأتبعوا في هذه لعنة ويوم القيامة بئس الرفد المرفود

translation: That is from the news of the cities, which We relate to you, [O Muhammad]. And there had already come to them My messengers with clear proofs, but they were not to believe in that which they had denied before. Thus does Allah seal over the hearts of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the stories of the past nations and their rejection of the divine messages are a lesson for the people. It emphasizes that even though the messengers came to them with clear signs, the disbelievers refused to believe due to their hardened hearts. This serves as a warning that Allah seals the hearts of those who persistently reject the truth.
orig: ذلك من أنباء القرى نقصه عليك منها قائم وحصيد

translation: And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. So their gods they used to invoke besides Allah did not avail them at all when there came the command of your Lord, and they did not increase them in other than ruin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the punishment that befell the disbelievers was not an act of injustice by God, but rather a consequence of their own wrongdoing. Their false deities were unable to help them when God's command came to pass, and instead only led them to further ruin and destruction.
orig: وما ظلمناهم ولكن ظلموا أنفسهم فما أغنت عنهم آلهتهم التي يدعون من دون الله من شيء لما جاء أمر ربك وما زادوهم غير تتبيب

translation: And thus does your Lord seize the cities when He seizes them while they are committing wrong. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's punishment and retribution against unjust societies and individuals is severe and painful. It serves as a warning that those who persist in wrongdoing and oppression will face the consequences of their actions, as Allah has the power to punish them in a manner that is both painful and severe.
orig: وكذلك أخذ ربك إذا أخذ القرى وهي ظالمة إن أخذه أليم شديد

translation: Indeed in that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day for which the people will be collected, and that is a Day [that will be] witnessed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fearing the punishment of the Hereafter. The Day of Judgment, when all people will be gathered and held accountable for their actions, is a momentous event that should inspire awe and reverence in those who believe. This is a sign for those who are mindful of their ultimate destiny and the consequences of their choices in this life.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية لمن خاف عذاب الآخرة ذلك يوم مجموع له الناس وذلك يوم مشهود

translation: And We do not delay it except for a specified term.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the timing of events, including the Day of Judgment, is predetermined by Allah and will occur according to His plan. It implies that the delay in the arrival of certain events is not due to haphazard circumstances, but rather a part of Allah's wisdom and the fulfillment of a specific term or duration.
orig: وما نؤخره إلا لأجل معدود

translation: The Day will come when no soul will speak except by His permission. And among them will be the wretched and the blessed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to speak or act without the permission of Allah. The fate of people will be divided into two categories - the wretched, who will be destined for punishment, and the blessed, who will be granted salvation and eternal bliss.
orig: يوم يأت لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه فمنهم شقي وسعيد

translation: And as for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire. For them therein is [violent] exhaling and inhaling.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who have turned away from the path of righteousness and embraced evil. They will be condemned to the eternal torment of Hell, where they will experience the agonizing sounds of labored breathing and wailing as a consequence of their misdeeds in life.
orig: فأما الذين شقوا ففي النار لهم فيها زفير وشهيق

translation: Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord should will. Indeed, your Lord is an accomplisher of what He intends.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the reward for the believers in Paradise. They will dwell there forever, as long as the heavens and the earth exist, unless God wills otherwise. This highlights God's absolute sovereignty and His ability to do as He pleases, for He is the Accomplisher of all that He intends.
orig: خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك إن ربك فعال لما يريد

translation: As for those who are blessed, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord may will - a gift uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the eternal reward in the Hereafter for those who have done good deeds and lived righteously. They will reside in Paradise forever, unless God wills otherwise. This gift of Paradise is unending and uninterrupted, a testament to God's boundless mercy and generosity towards the righteous.
orig: وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك عطاء غير مجذوذ

translation: So do not be in doubt, [O Muhammad], about what these [polytheists] worship. They worship not except as their fathers worshipped before. And indeed, We will give them their share [of punishment] undiminished.
interpretation: This verse is instructing the Prophet Muhammad not to doubt or be uncertain about the worship of the polytheists, as they are simply following the practices of their ancestors. It also assures that they will receive their full share of punishment for their idolatry, without any reduction.
orig: فلا تك في مرية مما يعبد هؤلاء ما يعبدون إلا كما يعبد آباؤهم من قبل وإنا لموفوهم نصيبهم غير منقوص

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the Book, but it came to be disputed. And if not for a word that had preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them. And indeed they are, concerning the Qur'an, in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: This verse highlights that despite the clear guidance provided in the Book (the Torah) given to Moses, there was still dispute and doubt among the people. The verse suggests that if not for God's prior decree to give people time to decide and guide them further, the matter would have been settled between them. However, even with the Qur'an, people remain in doubt and uncertainty about its truth and divine origin.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فاختلف فيه ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم وإنهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: And indeed, [O Muhammad], each [of the believers and disbelievers] We will surely repay in full [for] their deeds. And indeed, [O Muhammad], He is Acquainted with what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah will fully recompense every person, whether believer or disbeliever, for their deeds. Allah is All-Knowing and Fully Aware of the actions of all people, and He will judge them accordingly on the Day of Resurrection.
orig: وإن كلا لما ليوفينهم ربك أعمالهم إنه بما يعملون خبير

translation: So stand firm as you have been commanded, and those who have turned back with you, and do not transgress. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad and his followers to remain steadfast in their faith and adherence to God's commands. It also warns against transgressing the bounds set by God, reminding that He is all-seeing and aware of their actions.
orig: فاستقم كما أمرت ومن تاب معك ولا تطغوا إنه بما تعملون بصير

translation: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, lest you be touched by the Fire, and you would not have besides Allah [any] protectors; then you would not be helped.
interpretation: This verse warns against allying with or leaning towards those who do wrong, as it can lead to being engulfed by the punishment of the Hellfire. It emphasizes that one should not seek protection or assistance from anyone other than Allah, as only He can truly help and save a person.
orig: ولا تركنوا إلى الذين ظلموا فتمسكم النار وما لكم من دون الله من أولياء ثم لا تنصرون

translation: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.
interpretation: This verse encourages the establishment of regular prayer, both at the beginning and end of the day, as well as during the night. It suggests that good deeds have the power to erase or "do away with" misdeeds, providing a reminder for those who reflect on and remember the guidance of Allah.
orig: وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات ذلك ذكرى للذاكرين

translation: And be patient, for indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be patient and steadfast in their good deeds, as Allah will not let the reward for their righteous actions go to waste. It emphasizes that those who do good will be duly compensated by Allah, even if the results are not immediately apparent.
orig: واصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: So why were there not among the generations before you those of enduring discrimination who would have forbidden corruption in the earth except a few of those We saved from among them? And the wrongdoers pursued what luxury they were given therein, and they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the lack of righteous people in previous generations who would have spoken out against corruption and wrongdoing. It suggests that if there had been more people of virtue and integrity, they could have prevented the spread of corruption. However, the majority of people were consumed by their own desires and indulgences, and thus became criminals. The verse is a call for people to be more vigilant and courageous in standing up against injustice and immorality in society.
orig: فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم أولو بقية ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض إلا قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه وكانوا مجرمين

translation: And your Lord would not have destroyed the cities unjustly while their people were reformers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God's justice and mercy are paramount. He would not punish a community if its people were righteous and working to improve their society. It suggests that God's judgment is fair and takes into account the true state of a people, not just outward appearances.
orig: وما كان ربك ليهلك القرى بظلم وأهلها مصلحون

translation: And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community [united in religion], but they will not cease to differ.
interpretation: This verse suggests that while God could have created all of humanity to follow one religion, He has instead allowed for diversity of belief and practice. This diversity is part of God's plan, and human beings will continue to hold different views and opinions. The interpretation is that religious pluralism is a divinely-ordained state of affairs, and that we should embrace and respect this diversity rather than seek to impose uniformity.
orig: ولو شاء ربك لجعل الناس أمة واحدة ولا يزالون مختلفين

translation: Except those upon whom your Lord has decreed [salvation]. And for that He created them. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that salvation and damnation are ultimately in the hands of God. It suggests that while Hell will be filled with both jinn and humans, those whom God has decreed to be saved will be spared. The verse highlights God's absolute sovereignty and the inevitability of His decree.
orig: إلا من رحم ربك ولذلك خلقهم وتمت كلمة ربك لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

translation: And [O Muhammad], We relate to you from the news of the messengers what We strengthen thereby your heart. And there has come to you, in this [Qur'an], the truth and an instruction and a reminder for the believers.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad to take solace in the stories of the previous Prophets, as these accounts strengthen his heart and resolve. The Qur'an contains the truth, moral guidance, and a reminder for the believers to hold fast to their faith.
orig: وكلا نقص عليك من أنباء الرسل ما نثبت به فؤادك وجاءك في هذه الحق وموعظة وذكرى للمؤمنين

translation: And say to those who do not believe, "Act according to your position, [for] indeed, we are acting."
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to tell those who do not believe in the message of Islam to continue with their ways, for the believers will continue to act according to the guidance of the Qur'an and the teachings of Islam. It is a call for patience and steadfastness in the face of disbelief, as the believers are assured that they are acting upon the truth and will ultimately prevail.
orig: وقل للذين لا يؤمنون اعملوا على مكانتكم إنا عاملون

translation: And wait, indeed, we [too] are waiting.
interpretation: This verse encourages patience and steadfastness in the face of adversity. It suggests that just as the believers are waiting for the fulfillment of God's promises, the disbelievers should also be prepared to face the consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes the need for faith and trust in God's plan, even when the outcome is not immediately apparent.
orig: وانتظروا إنا منتظرون

translation: And to Allah belongs the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth, and to Him will [all] the matters be returned. So worship Him and rely upon Him. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone has knowledge of the unseen realms of the heavens and the earth, and that all matters ultimately return to Him. Therefore, the appropriate response is to worship and rely solely upon Allah, as He is fully aware of all that we do.
orig: ولله غيب السماوات والأرض وإليه يرجع الأمر كله فاعبده وتوكل عليه وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: This verse introduces the Qur'an as a clear and self-evident book of guidance, revealed by God. The letters "Alif, Lam, Ra" at the beginning are part of the mysterious letters that precede certain chapters of the Qur'an, whose precise meaning is not fully known. The verse emphasizes the clarity and lucidity of the Qur'anic message, which is intended to guide humanity towards the truth.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب المبين

translation: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you might understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic language so that the people to whom it was first addressed could comprehend its message. The purpose of revealing the Qur'an in Arabic is to facilitate understanding and reflection upon its teachings, thereby guiding the people towards wisdom and sound reasoning.
orig: إنا أنزلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون

translation: We relate to you, [O Muhammad], the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur'an although you were, before it, among the unaware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an contains the best and most meaningful stories that God has revealed to the Prophet Muhammad. Prior to the revelation of the Qur'an, the Prophet was unaware of these stories, but now he is able to convey them to humanity as the divinely inspired messenger.
orig: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بما أوحينا إليك هذا القرآن وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين

translation: And [mention, O Muḥammad], when Joseph said to his father, "O my father, indeed I have seen [in a dream] eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me."
interpretation: This verse describes a dream that the prophet Joseph (peace be upon him) had, in which he saw eleven stars, the sun, and the moon prostrating to him. This dream was a sign of his future greatness and the high status he would attain, as the eleven stars represented his eleven brothers, and the sun and moon represented his parents. The interpretation of the dream was that Joseph would one day become a great leader, and his family would come to revere and submit to him.
orig: إذ قال يوسف لأبيه يا أبت إني رأيت أحد عشر كوكبا والشمس والقمر رأيتهم لي ساجدين

translation: He said: "O my son! Relate not your vision to your brothers, lest they should plot a plot against you, for Satan is to man an avowed enemy."
interpretation: This verse advises Prophet Yaqub (Jacob) to not share his son Yusuf's (Joseph) dream with his other sons, as they may become jealous and plot against him. The verse highlights the danger of revealing one's visions or dreams to those who may be envious, as the devil will use such information to incite enmity and harm.
orig: قال يا بني لا تقصص رؤياك على إخوتك فيكيدوا لك كيدا إن الشيطان للإنسان عدو مبين

translation: And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of narratives and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights how God chooses and guides the Prophet Muhammad, teaching him the interpretation of narratives and completing His favor upon him and his family, just as He did with the previous Prophets like Abraham and Isaac. This emphasizes that God is All-Knowing and All-Wise in His guidance and selection of His Messengers.
orig: وكذلك يجتبيك ربك ويعلمك من تأويل الأحاديث ويتم نعمته عليك وعلى آل يعقوب كما أتمها على أبويك من قبل إبراهيم وإسحاق إن ربك عليم حكيم

translation: There were signs in [the story of] Joseph and his brothers for those who ask [i.e., seek knowledge].
interpretation: This verse highlights that the story of Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him) and his brothers contains valuable lessons and insights for those who seek to learn and understand the wisdom behind the events. The story serves as a sign or a lesson for those who inquire and reflect on the divine plan and the lessons that can be derived from it.
orig: لقد كان في يوسف وإخوته آيات للسائلين

translation: When they said, "Verily, Yusuf (Joseph) and his brother (Benjamin) are more beloved to our father than we, while we are a strong group. Truly, our father is in a clear error."
interpretation: This verse highlights the jealousy and resentment felt by the brothers of Yusuf (Joseph) towards him and his brother Benjamin, whom their father loved more. The brothers felt that they were a strong group, yet their father was misguided in his preference for Yusuf and Benjamin. This verse reflects the complex family dynamics and the tensions that can arise when a parent shows favoritism towards certain children.
orig: إذ قالوا ليوسف وأخوه أحب إلى أبينا منا ونحن عصبة إن أبانا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: Kill Yusuf or cast him out to [another] land; the countenance of your father will [then] be only for you, and you will be after him of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse describes the plot of Yusuf's (Joseph's) brothers to get rid of him out of jealousy, so that their father would focus only on them and they could become righteous people after Yusuf is gone. It highlights the selfish and deceptive nature of the brothers' intentions, and the importance of overcoming such negative traits in order to become truly righteous.
orig: اقتلوا يوسف أو اطرحوه أرضا يخل لكم وجه أبيكم وتكونوا من بعده قوما صالحين

translation: Said a speaker among them, "Do not kill Joseph but throw him into the bottom of the well; some travelers will pick him up, if you are going to do [it]."
interpretation: This verse suggests that one of the brothers of Joseph proposed a plan to not kill him, but instead throw him into a well, so that he may be found by travelers and taken away, rather than being outright murdered. This shows a reluctance to directly kill Joseph, even though they were still planning to get rid of him. The interpretation is that there was some internal conflict and debate among the brothers about how to deal with Joseph, with one proposing a less severe option.
orig: قال قائل منهم لا تقتلوا يوسف وألقوه في غيابت الجب يلتقطه بعض السيارة إن كنتم فاعلين

translation: They said, "O our father, why do you not trust us with Joseph while indeed, we are to him sincere counselors?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the plea of Joseph's brothers to their father, Jacob, asking him to trust them with Joseph. They assure him that they are sincere in their desire to protect and counsel Joseph, and that he can rely on their good intentions towards him.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا ما لك لا تأمنا على يوسف وإنا له لناصحون

translation: Send him with us tomorrow that he may enjoy himself and play. And indeed, we will be his guardians.
interpretation: This verse encourages the nurturing and protection of children, allowing them to play and experience joy while also ensuring their safety and well-being. It emphasizes the importance of providing a supportive environment for children to grow and develop, with responsible adults serving as their guardians.
orig: أرسله معنا غدا يرتع ويلعب وإنا له لحافظون

translation: He said, 'Indeed, it saddens me that you should take him away, and I fear that a wolf would eat him while you are thereof heedless.'
interpretation: This verse expresses the deep concern and anxiety of Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob) for his son Yusuf (Joseph). He is saddened by the prospect of his son being taken away, and he fears that while he is unaware, a wolf may attack and devour him. This highlights the strong paternal love and worry that Prophet Ya'qub had for his beloved son.
orig: قال إني ليحزنني أن تذهبوا به وأخاف أن يأكله الذئب وأنتم عنه غافلون

translation: They said, "If the wolf should eat him while we are a [strong] clan, indeed, we would then be losers."
interpretation: This verse expresses the concern and fear of the brothers of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) that if the wolf were to devour him, they would be considered failures and losers in the eyes of their father and the community. It highlights their sense of responsibility and the importance they placed on protecting Yusuf, even though they had planned to get rid of him out of jealousy.
orig: قالوا لئن أكله الذئب ونحن عصبة إنا إذا لخاسرون

translation: And when they had taken him [and agreed to throw him into the well], they resolved [upon that] and they put him into the bottom of the well. And We inspired to him, "You will surely inform them [someday] about this affair of theirs while they do not perceive [it]."
interpretation: This verse describes the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) being thrown into a well by his brothers, who were jealous of him. However, God revealed to Yusuf that he would one day inform his brothers of their actions, even though they were unaware that he would do so. This highlights God's power and control over events, and that no matter how difficult a situation may seem, He has a plan and will ultimately reveal the truth.
orig: فلما ذهبوا به وأجمعوا أن يجعلوه في غيابت الجب وأوحينا إليه لتنبئنهم بأمرهم هذا وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And they came to their father at nightfall, weeping.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the sons of Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob) returned to him at night, expressing their grief and sorrow. It indicates that they were distressed and remorseful, perhaps over the loss of their brother Yusuf (Joseph). The verse conveys a sense of emotional turmoil and the strong bond between the family members.
orig: وجاءوا أباهم عشاء يبكون

translation: They said, "O our father, indeed we went racing and left Yusuf with our possessions, and a wolf ate him. But you would not believe us, even if we were truthful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceitfulness of Yusuf's brothers, who tried to cover up their betrayal of him by blaming a wolf. Their claim that they were "truthful" is contradicted by their own admission that they left Yusuf behind, which led to his disappearance. The verse emphasizes the lack of trust between Yaqub and his sons, as he did not believe their story, even if they were telling the truth.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا إنا ذهبنا نستبق وتركنا يوسف عند متاعنا فأكله الذئب وما أنت بمؤمن لنا ولو كنا صادقين

translation: And they came upon his shirt with false blood. [Jacob] said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And [it is] Allah whose help is sought against that which you describe."
interpretation: This verse describes the incident where Joseph's brothers came to their father Jacob with Joseph's shirt stained with false blood, claiming that he had been killed by a wolf. However, Jacob saw through their deception and attributed it to their own souls, urging patience and reliance on Allah in the face of such trials. The interpretation highlights the importance of maintaining composure, exercising patience, and trusting in Allah when facing difficult situations, even when they are caused by the deceitful actions of others.
orig: وجاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا فصبر جميل والله المستعان على ما تصفون

translation: And a caravan came, and they sent their water-drawer, and he let down his bucket. [The leader] said, "Good news! This is a boy." And they concealed him, [considering him], as merchandise, and Allah was Knowing of what they did.
interpretation: This verse describes the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), peace be upon him, when he was thrown into a well by his brothers and then found by a caravan passing by. The verse highlights how the brothers concealed Yusuf and treated him as a commodity, while Allah was fully aware of their actions. This emphasizes the importance of not exploiting or objectifying others, and that Allah sees all that we do.
orig: وجاءت سيارة فأرسلوا واردهم فأدلى دلوه قال يا بشرى هذا غلام وأسروه بضاعة والله عليم بما يعملون

translation: And they sold him for a reduced price - a few dirhams - and they were, concerning him, of those content with little.
interpretation: This verse describes the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), who was sold by his brothers for a meager price, even though they knew his true worth. It highlights the greed and lack of appreciation that the brothers had for Yusuf, as they were willing to let go of him for a small sum of money, despite him being a righteous and noble person. The verse emphasizes the contrast between the true value of Yusuf and the low price at which he was sold, suggesting that the brothers were content with this unjust and unethical transaction.
orig: وشروه بثمن بخس دراهم معدودة وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين

translation: And the one from Egypt who bought him said to his wife, "Give him a comfortable place. Perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son." And thus, We established Joseph in the land to teach him the interpretation of events. And Allah is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse describes the events after Joseph was sold into slavery in Egypt. The Egyptian who bought Joseph showed him kindness and compassion, treating him well and even considering adopting him as a son. This demonstrates that God was guiding the events, placing Joseph in a position where he could eventually interpret dreams and rise to a position of power. The interpretation highlights that God is in control of all affairs, even when it may not be apparent to people.
orig: وقال الذي اشتراه من مصر لامرأته أكرمي مثواه عسى أن ينفعنا أو نتخذه ولدا وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض ولنعلمه من تأويل الأحاديث والله غالب على أمره ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And when he reached maturity and was [mentally] complete, We gave him judgment and [religious] knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse indicates that when a person reaches the age of maturity and wisdom, Allah grants them the ability to make sound judgments and acquire religious knowledge. This is a reward for those who strive to do good deeds and live righteously.
orig: ولما بلغ أشده آتيناه حكما وعلما وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him. She closed the doors and said, "Come, you." [Joseph] said, "I seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, he is my master, who has made good my residence. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."
interpretation: This verse describes the attempt by the wife of the Egyptian official to seduce the Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him) when he was in her house. However, Joseph remained steadfast in his faith and refused her advances, seeking refuge in Allah and acknowledging that his master (the Egyptian official) had treated him well. The verse emphasizes that the wrongdoers, those who attempt to seduce others into sin, will not succeed in their endeavors.
orig: وراودته التي هو في بيتها عن نفسه وغلقت الأبواب وقالت هيت لك قال معاذ الله إنه ربي أحسن مثواي إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And she certainly determined [to seduce] him, and he would have inclined to her had he not seen the proof of his Lord. Thus [it was] that We may turn away from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants.
interpretation: This verse describes the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and the wife of the Aziz (the minister) who tried to seduce him. The verse emphasizes that Yusuf remained steadfast in his faith and did not succumb to the temptation, as he saw the clear proof of God's guidance. This is an example of how God protects the righteous and turns them away from evil and immorality, as Yusuf was one of God"s chosen, devoted servants.
orig: ولقد همت به وهم بها لولا أن رأى برهان ربه كذلك لنصرف عنه السوء والفحشاء إنه من عبادنا المخلصين

translation: And they both raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back, and they found her husband at the door. She said, "What is the recompense of one who intended evil for your wife but that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?"
interpretation: This verse describes a situation where a woman attempts to seduce a man, but when her husband returns, she tries to frame the man as the aggressor. The interpretation is that the verse highlights the importance of honesty and integrity, and the consequences of false accusations and attempts to deceive.
orig: واستبقا الباب وقدت قميصه من دبر وألفيا سيدها لدى الباب قالت ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا إلا أن يسجن أو عذاب أليم

translation: She sought to seduce me, and he (Joseph) is of the truthful ones
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him) and the wife of the Aziz (the high-ranking official in Egypt). The wife of the Aziz tried to seduce Joseph, but he refused her advances, recognizing that it would be a sin against God. The verse then states that a witness from her own household testified that Joseph's shirt was torn from the back, indicating that the wife of the Aziz was the one who had attempted to seduce Joseph, and that Joseph had been truthful in his account of the incident.
orig: قال هي راودتني عن نفسي وشهد شاهد من أهلها إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت وهو من الكاذبين

translation: And if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has told a lie and he is of the truthful
interpretation: This verse refers to a story in the Qur'an where a woman tries to seduce a man, and when her husband returns, she accuses the man of attempting to seduce her. However, the evidence shows that the man is innocent, as his shirt is torn from the back, indicating that he was trying to flee from the woman's advances. This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking the truth and not making false accusations, even in the face of apparent evidence.
orig: وإن كان قميصه قد من دبر فكذبت وهو من الصادقين

translation: And when he (Yusuf) saw his shirt torn from the back, he (Yaqub) said: "Verily, this is a plot of you women! Certainly, mighty is your plot!"
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom and insight of Prophet Ya`qub (Jacob) in understanding the deception that had been plotted against his son Yusuf (Joseph). When Ya`qub saw the torn shirt, he immediately recognized that it was not a result of a normal accident, but rather a calculated scheme orchestrated by the women involved. This verse emphasizes the power and cunning of the women's plot, which Ya`qub acknowledges as being "mighty" or formidable. The interpretation underscores the importance of discernment and the ability to see through deception, even in the face of seemingly convincing evidence.
orig: فلما رأى قميصه قد من دبر قال إنه من كيدكن إن كيدكن عظيم

translation: Joseph, turn away from this, and [O wife], ask forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you have been of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Joseph, peace be upon him, and his wife, regarding the incident where she had tried to seduce him. The verse commands Joseph to turn away from this temptation and instead seek forgiveness for his wife's sin, as she was among the wrongdoers in this situation. The interpretation is that one should avoid falling into sin, and if one does, they should sincerely repent and seek forgiveness from God.
orig: يوسف أعرض عن هذا واستغفري لذنبك إنك كنت من الخاطئين

translation: And women in the city said, "The wife of al-`Azeez is seeking to seduce her slave boy; he has impassioned her with love. Indeed, we see her [to be] in clear error."
interpretation: This verse highlights the gossip and rumor-mongering that surrounded the attempted seduction of the slave boy Yusuf by the wife of the powerful official, al-`Azeez. The women of the city recognized the impropriety and sinfulness of her actions, and condemned her for it, seeing it as a clear deviation from moral and ethical behavior.
orig: وقال نسوة في المدينة امرأت العزيز تراود فتاها عن نفسه قد شغفها حبا إنا لنراها في ضلال مبين

translation: And when she heard of their scheming, she sent for them and prepared for them a banquet and gave each one of them a knife and said [to Joseph], "Come out before them." And when they saw him, they greatly admired him and cut their hands [in amazement] and said, "Perfect is Allah! This is not a man; this is none but a noble angel."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the women who were invited by the wife of the Aziz (the minister) to see Joseph. When they saw Joseph, they were so amazed by his beauty and noble character that they cut their hands in astonishment, exclaiming that he was not a human but a noble angel. This highlights the high esteem in which Joseph was held, and the awe and reverence the women felt towards him.
orig: فلما سمعت بمكرهن أرسلت إليهن وأعتدت لهن متكأ وآتت كل واحدة منهن سكينا وقالت اخرج عليهن فلما رأينه أكبرنه وقطعن أيديهن وقلن حاش لله ما هذا بشرا إن هذا إلا ملك كريم

translation: She said, "This is the one about whom you blamed me. And I certainly sought to seduce him, but he firmly refused. And if he does not do what I command him, he will surely be imprisoned and will be of those debased."
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and the wife of the ruler (Potiphar). It shows how the wife tried to seduce Yusuf, but he refused to commit the sin. She then falsely accused him, threatening that if he did not obey her, he would be imprisoned. This highlights the importance of resisting temptation and standing firm in one's faith, even in the face of adversity.
orig: قالت فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه ولقد راودته عن نفسه فاستعصم ولئن لم يفعل ما آمره ليسجنن وليكونا من الصاغرين

translation: The (imprisoned) young man said: "O my Lord! The prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me. Unless You turn away their plot from me, I should (in my youthful folly) feel inclined towards them and become one of the ignorant."
interpretation: The young man in prison expresses his preference for imprisonment over the temptations and schemes of the women who are trying to seduce him. He recognizes his own vulnerability and asks God to protect him from falling into their trap, lest he become one of the ignorant who succumb to their wiles.
orig: قال رب السجن أحب إلي مما يدعونني إليه وإلا تصرف عني كيدهن أصب إليهن وأكن من الجاهلين

translation: And his Lord responded to him and removed from him his misfortune. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), peace be upon him. When Yusuf was falsely accused and imprisoned, he turned to Allah in supplication. This verse indicates that Allah heard Yusuf's prayer and removed the adversity he was facing, as Allah is the All-Hearing and the All-Knowing. The interpretation suggests that when one faces difficulties, they should turn to Allah with sincerity, and Allah will respond to their call and alleviate their troubles.
orig: فاستجاب له ربه فصرف عنه كيدهن إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: Then it appeared to them after they had seen the signs that they must imprison him [i.e., Joseph] for a time.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even after witnessing clear signs and evidence, the people still chose to imprison Joseph out of jealousy or other ulterior motives. This highlights how preconceived notions and personal interests can sometimes blind people to the truth, even in the face of clear proof. The verse encourages us to remain open-minded and objective when evaluating information, rather than letting our biases or selfish desires cloud our judgment.
orig: ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات ليسجننه حتى حين

translation: And there entered the prison with him two young men. One of them said, 'Indeed, I have seen myself [in a dream] pressing [grapes into] wine.' And the other said, 'Indeed, I have seen myself carrying upon my head [some] bread, and the birds were eating from it.' [They said], 'Inform us of the interpretation of this, for we see you to be of those who do good.'
interpretation: This verse describes two young men who were imprisoned with Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). One of them had a dream about pressing grapes into wine, and the other had a dream about carrying bread on his head that the birds were eating. They asked Prophet Yusuf to interpret their dreams, as they recognized him to be a righteous and insightful man. This verse highlights the importance of seeking guidance and interpretation from those who are knowledgeable and pious, and the ability of Prophet Yusuf to interpret dreams, which was a special gift granted to him by Allah.
orig: ودخل معه السجن فتيان قال أحدهما إني أراني أعصر خمرا وقال الآخر إني أراني أحمل فوق رأسي خبزا تأكل الطير منه نبئنا بتأويله إنا نراك من المحسنين

translation: He (the king) said: "I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you (in reality). This is (part) of that which my Lord has taught me. Verily, I have forsaken the religion of a people that believe not in Allah and are disbelievers in the Hereafter."
interpretation: The king is informing the prisoners that he will interpret their dreams before they come true, as this is part of the knowledge that Allah has granted him. He then explains that he has abandoned the religion of those who do not believe in Allah and deny the Hereafter, indicating his faith in Allah and the Hereafter.
orig: قال لا يأتيكما طعام ترزقانه إلا نبأتكما بتأويله قبل أن يأتيكما ذلكما مما علمني ربي إني تركت ملة قوم لا يؤمنون بالله وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. It is not for us to associate anything with Allah. That is from the favor of Allah upon us and upon the people, but most of the people do not show gratitude.
interpretation: This verse expresses the importance of following the monotheistic faith of the Abrahamic prophets, which rejects the association of any partners with Allah. It highlights that this pure faith is a blessing and favor from Allah upon humanity, but that most people fail to properly appreciate and be grateful for this guidance.
orig: واتبعت ملة آبائي إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب ما كان لنا أن نشرك بالله من شيء ذلك من فضل الله علينا وعلى الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: O my two companions of the prison, are many different lords better or Allah, the One, the Prevailing?
interpretation: This verse encourages the reader to reflect on the true nature of divinity. It contrasts the concept of many different lords or deities with the idea of one supreme, all-powerful God. The interpretation suggests that the worship of a single, omnipotent God is superior to the belief in multiple, fragmented divine authorities.
orig: يا صاحبي السجن أأرباب متفرقون خير أم الله الواحد القهار

translation: You worship not besides Him except [mere] names you have named them, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority. Legislation is not but for Allah. He has commanded that you worship not except Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse condemns the worship of idols and false deities, which are merely names given by people and their ancestors, without any divine sanction or authority. It emphasizes that the true legislation and right to be worshipped belongs to Allah alone, and that the correct religion is to worship Him exclusively. However, most people remain ignorant of this truth.
orig: ما تعبدون من دونه إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان إن الحكم إلا لله أمر ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه ذلك الدين القيم ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: O my two companions of the prison! As for one of you, he will give drink to his lord of wine; and as for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decreed concerning which you both inquire.
interpretation: This verse describes a dream that one of the prisoners had, in which he saw that one of them would be released and become a servant to the king, while the other would be crucified. The interpretation of the dream suggests that the affairs of people are ultimately in the hands of God, and that the prisoners should submit to God's decree rather than trying to change their fates through their own efforts.
orig: يا صاحبي السجن أما أحدكما فيسقي ربه خمرا وأما الآخر فيصلب فتأكل الطير من رأسه قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان

translation: And he said to the one whom he knew would be released [and saved from prison], "Remember me before your lord." But the devil made him forget the mention [to] his lord, so he remained in prison for a few years.
interpretation: This verse highlights the weakness of human nature and the power of Satan to distract and mislead us. The man who was freed from prison had promised to remember the other prisoner before their lord, but Satan caused him to forget this promise. This serves as a lesson that we must be vigilant against the temptations of Satan and remain steadfast in our devotion to God, even in the face of adversity.
orig: وقال للذي ظن أنه ناج منهما اذكرني عند ربك فأنساه الشيطان ذكر ربه فلبث في السجن بضع سنين

translation: And the king said, "Indeed, I have seen [in a dream] seven fat cows being eaten by seven [that were] lean, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry."
interpretation: This verse describes a dream seen by the king, in which he saw seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean cows, and seven green spikes of grain along with others that were dry. This dream is interpreted as a prophecy of a period of abundance followed by a period of scarcity. The interpretation of this dream is a key event in the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) in the Qur'an, as he is able to interpret the dream and advise the king accordingly.
orig: وقال الملك إني أرى سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات يا أيها الملأ أفتوني في رؤياي إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون

translation: They said, "Confused dreams, and we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams."
interpretation: This verse refers to the response of the people when Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him) interpreted their dreams. They dismissed his interpretation, claiming that dreams are merely confused thoughts and that they themselves have no knowledge of dream interpretation. This highlights the importance of seeking guidance from those who have knowledge and wisdom, rather than relying solely on one's own understanding.
orig: قالوا أضغاث أحلام وما نحن بتأويل الأحلام بعالمين

translation: And he of the two who was released and remembered after a time said, "I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth."
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the two prisoners who were imprisoned with Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). One of them was released and remembered the interpretation of Yusuf's dream after some time. This person then offered to interpret the dream of the king, which led to Yusuf's release from prison and his subsequent rise to power in Egypt. The verse highlights the importance of patience, faith, and the ability to interpret dreams and visions, which can lead to positive outcomes even in the most challenging circumstances.
orig: وقال الذي نجا منهما وادكر بعد أمة أنا أنبئكم بتأويله فأرسلون

translation: O Joseph, the truthful one! Explain to us [the dream of] seven fat cows whom seven [others, being] lean consume, and [of] seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that are] dry - that I may return to the people to know [what they could infer from this].
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Yusuf (Joseph), chapter 12, verse 46. It describes a dream that the king of Egypt had, which he asked the Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) to interpret. The dream involves seven fat cows being consumed by seven lean cows, and seven green spikes of grain alongside others that are dry. The interpretation of this dream, as given by Prophet Yusuf, foretells seven years of abundant harvest followed by seven years of famine. This interpretation allowed the king to prepare for the coming famine and save his people from its effects.
orig: يوسف أيها الصديق أفتنا في سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات لعلي أرجع إلى الناس لعلهم يعلمون

translation: He said, "You shall sow for seven years consecutively; and what you harvest, leave it in the ear, except a little from which you may eat."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and his interpretation of the king's dream. The interpretation suggests that there will be seven years of abundant harvest, followed by seven years of famine. The instruction is to store the surplus grain during the years of abundance, so that it can be used during the years of scarcity. This teaches the importance of planning, preparation, and prudent management of resources, especially during times of prosperity, in order to withstand periods of hardship.
orig: قال تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا فما حصدتم فذروه في سنبله إلا قليلا مما تأكلون

translation: Then there will come after that seven [years of] hardship which will consume what you have put aside for them, except a little from which you [will] store.
interpretation: This verse describes a period of seven years of intense hardship and scarcity that will follow a period of plenty. During this difficult time, the people will be forced to consume the resources they had previously stored, leaving only a small amount remaining. The interpretation suggests the importance of planning and preparing for future challenges, as prosperity can be followed by periods of adversity.
orig: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك سبع شداد يأكلن ما قدمتم لهن إلا قليلا مما تحصنون

translation: Then there will come after that a year in which the people will be given relief and in which they will press [olives and grapes].
interpretation: This verse speaks of a period of abundance and prosperity that will come after a period of hardship. The people will be granted relief from their difficulties and will be able to enjoy the fruits of their labor, such as pressing olives and grapes to produce oil and wine. This suggests a message of hope and the promise of better times ahead, even in the face of adversity.
orig: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون

translation: And the king said, "Bring him to me." But when the messenger came to him, [Joseph] said, "Return to your master and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plan."
interpretation: This verse highlights Joseph's wisdom and discernment. When the king summoned him, Joseph did not simply go to the king, but instead asked the messenger to return to the king and inquire about the women who had cut their hands. This showed Joseph's insight into the situation and his desire to understand the full context before engaging with the king. The interpretation is that Joseph was a man of wisdom who did not act hastily, but rather sought to thoroughly comprehend the circumstances before proceeding.
orig: وقال الملك ائتوني به فلما جاءه الرسول قال ارجع إلى ربك فاسأله ما بال النسوة اللاتي قطعن أيديهن إن ربي بكيدهن عليم

translation: He (the king) said: "What was your case, O you women, when you did seek (to seduce) Yusuf (Joseph)?" The women said: "Allah forbid! No evil know we against him!" The wife of Al-'Aziz said: "Now the truth is manifest (to all), it was I who sought to seduce him, and he is surely of the truthful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of honesty and truthfulness. When the king questioned the women about their attempts to seduce Joseph, they initially denied any wrongdoing, claiming they knew no evil against him. However, the wife of the king's minister, al-'Aziz, later admitted that she was the one who had tried to seduce Joseph, and that he had been truthful in his account. This demonstrates the value of acknowledging one's mistakes and being truthful, even in the face of pressure or social expectations.
orig: قال ما خطبكن إذ راودتن يوسف عن نفسه قلن حاش لله ما علمنا عليه من سوء قالت امرأت العزيز الآن حصحص الحق أنا راودته عن نفسه وإنه لمن الصادقين

translation: That [is so] he may know that I have not betrayed him in [his] absence and that Allah does not guide the plot of betrayers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God is aware of all actions, even those done in secret. It serves as a warning that betrayal and deception will not be hidden from God, and that He does not guide or support those who engage in such treacherous acts.
orig: ذلك ليعلم أني لم أخنه بالغيب وأن الله لا يهدي كيد الخائنين

translation: And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent tendency of the human soul towards evil and sin, and the need for divine mercy and forgiveness. It acknowledges that the self is inclined towards wrongdoing, but that those who are granted the mercy of God are able to overcome this inclination. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking God's forgiveness and relying on His compassion, as He is the Most Forgiving and the Most Merciful.
orig: وما أبرئ نفسي إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء إلا ما رحم ربي إن ربي غفور رحيم

translation: And the king said, 'Bring him to me; I will appoint him exclusively for myself.' And when he spoke to him, he said, 'Indeed, you are today with us established [in position] and trusted.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the high regard and trust that the king placed in Joseph (peace be upon him) after he was able to interpret the king's dream. The king recognized Joseph's abilities and wisdom, and appointed him to a position of authority and responsibility within the kingdom. This demonstrates the value of being righteous, trustworthy, and capable, which can lead to one being granted positions of influence and honor.
orig: وقال الملك ائتوني به أستخلصه لنفسي فلما كلمه قال إنك اليوم لدينا مكين أمين

translation: He said, "Place me over the treasures of the land. Indeed, I will be a knowing guardian."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the request made by Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) to the king of Egypt, after he had correctly interpreted the king's dream. Yusuf's request to be placed in charge of the treasures of the land reflects his trustworthiness, knowledge, and ability to manage the resources of the kingdom wisely. The interpretation suggests that those who are capable and possess the necessary knowledge and skills should be entrusted with positions of responsibility and authority, as they can effectively safeguard and utilize the resources for the benefit of the people.
orig: قال اجعلني على خزائن الأرض إني حفيظ عليم

translation: And thus We established Joseph in the land to settle therein wherever he willed. We touch with Our mercy whom We will, and We do not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how Allah granted Joseph authority and power in the land of Egypt, allowing him to reside and rule as he pleased. It emphasizes that Allah bestows His mercy upon whomever He wills, and that the reward for those who do good deeds will not be lost or wasted.
orig: وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض يتبوأ منها حيث يشاء نصيب برحمتنا من نشاء ولا نضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and have been fearing Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the reward in the Hereafter is superior to any worldly gains for those who have faith in Allah and strive to live righteously by fearing and obeying Him.
orig: ولأجر الآخرة خير للذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: And Joseph's brothers came and entered upon him, and he recognized them, but he was to them unknown.
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when Joseph's brothers, who had betrayed him years earlier, come to him in Egypt seeking food during a famine. Joseph recognizes them, but they do not recognize him due to the changes in his appearance and status. This highlights the theme of divine providence and the eventual reunion of the family, despite the past betrayal.
orig: وجاء إخوة يوسف فدخلوا عليه فعرفهم وهم له منكرون

translation: And when he had furnished them with their supplies, he said, "Bring me a [half] brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of accommodators?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates Joseph's (peace be upon him) wisdom and compassion as he tests his brothers to see if they have changed from their past behavior. By asking them to bring their younger brother, he is assessing whether they will treat him with the same jealousy and cruelty they had shown towards Joseph earlier. The verse also highlights Joseph's generosity and fairness in providing for his brothers, and his confidence in his ability to be a gracious host, as he assures them that he will "give full measure" and be "the best of accommodators".
orig: ولما جهزهم بجهازهم قال ائتوني بأخ لكم من أبيكم ألا ترون أني أوفي الكيل وأنا خير المنزلين

translation: But if you do not bring him to me, then no measure [of grain] will there be for you with me, nor will you approach [me].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's obligations and responsibilities. If the people fail to bring the requested individual, they will be denied further provisions and access to the authority figure. The verse serves as a warning that consequences will follow if commitments are not met.
orig: فإن لم تأتوني به فلا كيل لكم عندي ولا تقربون

translation: They said, "We will try to entice him away from his father, and indeed, we will be doers [of that]."
interpretation: This verse speaks of a group of people who conspired to separate the Prophet Joseph from his father Jacob, as they were envious of Joseph and wanted to remove him from his father's favor. The interpretation is that this verse highlights the lengths to which people can go to achieve their selfish desires, even at the expense of harming others and disrupting family relationships.
orig: قالوا سنراود عنه أباه وإنا لفاعلون

translation: And he said to his servants, "Place their merchandise in their saddlebags so they might recognize it when they return to their people that perhaps they will [again] return."
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), when he instructed his servants to secretly place the merchandise of his brothers back into their saddlebags, so that they may recognize it when they return home. This was a compassionate act by Yusuf, as he wanted his brothers to return to him and be reunited, despite their past transgressions against him.
orig: وقال لفتيانه اجعلوا بضاعتهم في رحالهم لعلهم يعرفونها إذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And when they returned to their father, they said: "O our father! The measure is denied us, so send with us our brother that we may obtain measure, and indeed, we will be guardians over him."
interpretation: This verse highlights the desperation of the brothers of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) to obtain more food provisions for their family. They had been denied the full measure of grain they were entitled to, and they pleaded with their father Ya'qub (Jacob) to send their brother Binyamin (Benjamin) with them so that they could obtain the full measure. They promised to be guardians over Binyamin, ensuring his safe return, in order to convince their father to let him go with them.
