orig: فلما رجعوا إلى أبيهم قالوا يا أبانا منع منا الكيل فأرسل معنا أخانا نكتل وإنا له لحافظون

translation: He (Jacob) said: "Will you trust him with me, except (when) as you did trust his brother (Joseph) aforetime? But Allah is the Best to take care (of him), and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy."
interpretation: This verse expresses Jacob's reluctance to let his son Benjamin go with his other sons to Egypt, as he had previously lost his son Joseph. However, Jacob acknowledges that Allah is the best protector and the Most Merciful, implying that he must trust in Allah's plan and providence, even when faced with difficult circumstances.
orig: قال هل آمنكم عليه إلا كما أمنتكم على أخيه من قبل فالله خير حافظا وهو أرحم الراحمين

translation: And when they opened their baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, "O our father, what [more] could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. And we will obtain supplies for our family and protect our brother and receive an additional camel's load; that is an easy measurement."
interpretation: This verse describes the brothers of Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him) finding their merchandise returned to them, which they had brought to Egypt. They were surprised and pleased, and saw it as a sign of good fortune. They wanted to return to their father with this good news, obtain more supplies for their family, ensure the safety of their brother (Benjamin), and even receive an additional camel's load of goods. This shows their gratitude, desire to care for their family, and hope for continued blessings from God.
orig: ولما فتحوا متاعهم وجدوا بضاعتهم ردت إليهم قالوا يا أبانا ما نبغي هذه بضاعتنا ردت إلينا ونمير أهلنا ونحفظ أخانا ونزداد كيل بعير ذلك كيل يسير

translation: He [Ya`qub] said, "I will not send him with you until you give me a solemn pledge in Allah's name that you will bring him [back] to me, unless you are surrounded [by enemies]." And when they had given him their solemn pledge, he said, "Allah is the Witness over what we say."
interpretation: This verse describes the reluctance of Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob) to send his son Binyamin (Benjamin) with his other sons to Egypt, until they give him a solemn pledge that they will bring Binyamin back to him. This reflects Ya'qub's deep love and concern for his son, and his desire to protect him. The verse also highlights Ya'qub's trust in Allah, as he states that Allah is the Witness over their pledge, indicating that he is relying on Allah's help and protection in this matter.
orig: قال لن أرسله معكم حتى تؤتون موثقا من الله لتأتنني به إلا أن يحاط بكم فلما آتوه موثقهم قال الله على ما نقول وكيل

translation: And he said, 'O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from different gates; and I cannot avail you against [the decree of] Allah at all. The decision is only for Allah; upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let those who would rely [indeed] rely.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of caution and prudence in one's actions. The father advises his sons to enter the city through different gates, rather than all together, to avoid drawing unwanted attention or potential harm. This suggests that one should take reasonable precautions and not rely solely on divine providence, but also exercise personal responsibility. The verse also highlights the ultimate sovereignty of God, who alone has the power to determine one's fate. The father's declaration of trust in God serves as an example of true reliance on the divine, which should be the foundation for all human endeavors.
orig: وقال يا بني لا تدخلوا من باب واحد وادخلوا من أبواب متفرقة وما أغني عنكم من الله من شيء إن الحكم إلا لله عليه توكلت وعليه فليتوكل المتوكلون

translation: And when they entered from where their father had ordered them, it did not avail them against Allah at all except [it was] a need within [the] soul of Jacob, which he satisfied. And indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights that even though the brothers followed their father's instructions, it did not protect them from the consequences of their actions. The only thing that mattered was the need within the soul of Jacob, which he fulfilled. This verse emphasizes that true knowledge comes from what Allah has taught, and most people are unaware of this fact.
orig: ولما دخلوا من حيث أمرهم أبوهم ما كان يغني عنهم من الله من شيء إلا حاجة في نفس يعقوب قضاها وإنه لذو علم لما علمناه ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his brother to himself and said, 'Indeed, I am your brother, so do not despair over what they used to do.'
interpretation: This verse conveys Joseph's compassion and forgiveness towards his brothers, who had previously betrayed him. Despite their past actions, Joseph embraces his brother and reassures him, reminding him not to be distressed or despair over what his brothers had done. The verse highlights Joseph's noble character and his ability to rise above the wrongs committed against him, demonstrating the power of forgiveness and reconciliation.
orig: ولما دخلوا على يوسف آوى إليه أخاه قال إني أنا أخوك فلا تبتئس بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And when he had furnished them with their provisions, he put the [gold measuring] cup into the bag of his brother. Then an announcer called out, 'O caravan, indeed you are thieves!'
interpretation: This verse describes how Joseph, after providing his brothers with provisions, hid his own drinking cup in his brother Benjamin's bag, and then had an announcer accuse the brothers of theft. This was a test to see if his brothers had changed since their previous betrayal of him, and to bring about a reunion with his family.
orig: فلما جهزهم بجهازهم جعل السقاية في رحل أخيه ثم أذن مؤذن أيتها العير إنكم لسارقون

translation: They said, 'And they turned to them, 'What do you miss?'
interpretation: This verse suggests a dialogue where a group of people are inquiring about something that is missing or lost. The implication is that they are seeking to understand the situation and find what is lacking or needed.
orig: قالوا وأقبلوا عليهم ماذا تفقدون

translation: They said, "We are missing the cup of the king. And for he who produces it is [the reward of] a camel's load, and I am responsible for it."
interpretation: This verse describes a scenario where the companions of the king have lost a valuable cup belonging to the king. They announce that whoever brings back the cup will be rewarded with a camel's load of provisions, and the speaker takes responsibility for this promise. The verse highlights the importance placed on recovering the lost item and the incentive offered to encourage its return.
orig: قالوا نفقد صواع الملك ولمن جاء به حمل بعير وأنا به زعيم

translation: They said, "By Allah, you have certainly known that we have not come to cause corruption in the land, and we have not been thieves."
interpretation: This verse reflects the response of those accused of causing corruption and theft, as they assert their innocence and swear by Allah that they had no such intentions. It emphasizes the importance of honesty, integrity, and defending one's reputation when faced with false accusations.
orig: قالوا تالله لقد علمتم ما جئنا لنفسد في الأرض وما كنا سارقين

translation: They said, "What is the recompense for this if you are liars?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to a situation where a group of people are accusing others of lying or making false claims. The verse poses a question asking what the punishment or consequence would be if the accused party is indeed found to be lying. The implication is that there should be a fitting punishment for those who make false accusations or spread lies, emphasizing the importance of truthfulness and honesty.
orig: قالوا فما جزاؤه إن كنتم كاذبين

translation: They said: "The recompense of him in whose bag (of corn) it is found shall be (that) he shall be held as a bondman to atone for it. Thus do We punish the wrong-doers."
interpretation: This verse describes a situation where someone is accused of stealing something, and the punishment for the wrongdoer is that he shall be held as a bondman to atone for his crime. The interpretation is that those who commit injustice and wrongdoing will be punished accordingly, as a warning and deterrent to others.
orig: قالوا جزاؤه من وجد في رحله فهو جزاؤه كذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: Then he began (the search) with their bags, before (he began) the bag of his brother: at length he brought it out of his brother's bag. Thus did We plan for Joseph. He could not take his brother by the law of the king except that Allah willed it (so). We raise to degrees (of wisdom) whom We please: but over all endued with knowledge is one, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse describes how Joseph, when searching the bags of his brothers, started with the bag of the brother other than Benjamin, before finding the cup in Benjamin's bag. This was part of God's plan for Joseph, who could not have taken his brother by the law of the king except by God's will. The verse emphasizes that God raises people to degrees of wisdom as He pleases, and that above all is the All-Knowing God.
orig: فبدأ بأوعيتهم قبل وعاء أخيه ثم استخرجها من وعاء أخيه كذلك كدنا ليوسف ما كان ليأخذ أخاه في دين الملك إلا أن يشاء الله نرفع درجات من نشاء وفوق كل ذي علم عليم

translation: They said, "If he steals, a brother of his had stolen before." But Joseph kept it within himself and disclosed it not to them. He said, "You are in a worse situation, and Allah is Most Knowing of what you describe."
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and double standards of Joseph's brothers. They accused Joseph of theft, but conveniently overlooked the fact that one of their own brothers had stolen before. Joseph, however, did not expose their past transgressions, but instead pointed out that they were in a worse moral position for making such accusations. The interpretation suggests that the verse cautions against passing judgement on others when one's own actions are not above reproach, and encourages introspection and acknowledging one's own shortcomings before criticizing others.
orig: قالوا إن يسرق فقد سرق أخ له من قبل فأسرها يوسف في نفسه ولم يبدها لهم قال أنتم شر مكانا والله أعلم بما تصفون

translation: They said, "O Exalted one, indeed he has a father [who is] an old man, so take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you as a doer of good."
interpretation: The brothers of Joseph, upon seeing his high status and authority, appealed to him to take one of them in place of their elderly father, Jacob, as they recognized Joseph as a righteous and benevolent person who would treat them well.
orig: قالوا يا أيها العزيز إن له أبا شيخا كبيرا فخذ أحدنا مكانه إنا نراك من المحسنين

translation: They said, "Far be it from us [to take] your son. If he had taken your wealth, we would not [then] have taken him."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and fairness. The people in this verse are asserting that they would not have taken the son if he had stolen their possessions, as that would be an unjust act. It highlights the principle that one should only be held accountable for their own actions, and not be punished for the misdeeds of others.
orig: قال معاذ الله أن نأخذ إلا من وجدنا متاعنا عنده إنا إذا لظالمون

translation: And when they despaired of him, they secluded themselves in private consultation. Their spokesman said, "Do you not know that your father has taken upon you an oath by Allah and [that] before [this], you had failed in [your duty to] Joseph? So I will never leave [this] land until my father permits me or Allah decides for me, and He is the best of judges."
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom and patience of the eldest brother, who reminds his siblings of the promise they had made to their father regarding Joseph. He resolves not to leave the land until their father permits it or until Allah decides their case, recognizing that Allah is the best judge. This demonstrates the importance of keeping one's word and trusting in the wisdom of Allah's judgement.
orig: فلما استيأسوا منه خلصوا نجيا قال كبيرهم ألم تعلموا أن أباكم قد أخذ عليكم موثقا من الله ومن قبل ما فرطتم في يوسف فلن أبرح الأرض حتى يأذن لي أبي أو يحكم الله لي وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: Return to your father and say, "O our father, indeed your son has stolen, and we did not testify except to what we knew. And we were not witnesses of the unseen."
interpretation: This verse instructs the brothers of Prophet Joseph to return to their father and confess that his son Joseph had stolen, but that they did not have any knowledge of the unseen and could only testify to what they had witnessed. This emphasizes the importance of honesty and acknowledging one's mistakes, even when it is difficult.
orig: ارجعوا إلى أبيكم فقولوا يا أبانا إن ابنك سرق وما شهدنا إلا بما علمنا وما كنا للغيب حافظين

translation: And ask the city in which we were and the caravan in which we came, and indeed, we are truthful.
interpretation: This verse encourages seeking knowledge and verifying information from reliable sources. It suggests that one should not rely solely on personal opinions or hearsay, but should instead seek out the facts and testimonies of those who were present or involved in the events being discussed. The verse emphasizes the importance of being truthful and honest in one's statements.
orig: واسأل القرية التي كنا فيها والعير التي أقبلنا فيها وإنا لصادقون

translation: He (Joseph) said: 'Nay, but your own selves have beguiled you into something. So (for me) patience is most fitting. And Allah (Alone) is the One Whose help can be sought against that (lie) which you describe.'
interpretation: This verse is spoken by the Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him) after his brothers falsely accused him of trying to seduce their wife. Joseph responds by saying that it is their own selves that have led them to this false accusation, and that he will exercise patience, trusting in Allah to ultimately bring the truth to light. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and reliance on Allah in the face of adversity and false accusations.
orig: قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا فصبر جميل عسى الله أن يأتيني بهم جميعا إنه هو العليم الحكيم

translation: And he turned away from them and said, 'Oh, my sorrow over Joseph,' and his eyes became white from grief, for he was [of those overtaken by] distress.
interpretation: This verse describes the emotional state of Prophet Jacob (peace be upon him) after being separated from his son Joseph (peace be upon him). The verse conveys the depth of Jacob's grief and sorrow, as he turns away from his other sons and expresses his anguish over the loss of Joseph. The whitening of his eyes is a metaphorical expression of the intensity of his grief, which has overwhelmed him to the point of distress. This verse highlights the profound love and attachment a parent can have for their child, and the immense pain felt when they are separated.
orig: وتولى عنهم وقال يا أسفى على يوسف وابيضت عيناه من الحزن فهو كظيم

translation: They said, "By Allah, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you become weakened by illness or become of those who perish."
interpretation: The brothers of Joseph, out of jealousy, accuse him of being obsessed with the memory of Joseph to the point that it will weaken him or lead to his demise. This highlights the envy and malice the brothers harbored towards Joseph, which ultimately led them to plot against him.
orig: قالوا تالله تفتأ تذكر يوسف حتى تكون حرضا أو تكون من الهالكين

translation: He said: "I only complain of my sadness and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah that which you do not know."
interpretation: The verse expresses the sentiment of a person who is going through a difficult time and is seeking solace in Allah. The person acknowledges that their sadness and grief are known to Allah, and they have a deeper understanding of the situation than those around them. This suggests that the person has a strong faith in Allah and is relying on divine wisdom to guide them through their troubles.
orig: قال إنما أشكو بثي وحزني إلى الله وأعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: O my sons, go and inquire about Joseph and his brother and despair not of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to have hope and trust in Allah even in times of difficulty. It instructs the sons of Prophet Jacob to search for their lost brother Joseph and his brother, and not to lose hope in Allah's mercy. The verse emphasizes that only the disbelievers can truly despair of Allah's help, as the believers should always maintain faith in Allah's ability to provide relief and guidance.
orig: يا بني اذهبوا فتحسسوا من يوسف وأخيه ولا تيأسوا من روح الله إنه لا ييأس من روح الله إلا القوم الكافرون

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, they said, "O Exalted one, adversity has touched us and our family, and we have come with goods poor in quality, but give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable."
interpretation: The brothers of Joseph, having been struck by hardship and famine, come to Joseph seeking his help. They acknowledge his high status and authority, and request that he be generous and charitable towards them. The verse emphasizes that those who are charitable will be rewarded by Allah, encouraging the audience to be compassionate and generous towards those in need.
orig: فلما دخلوا عليه قالوا يا أيها العزيز مسنا وأهلنا الضر وجئنا ببضاعة مزجاة فأوف لنا الكيل وتصدق علينا إن الله يجزي المتصدقين

translation: He (the king) said: "Do you know what you did with Yusuf (Joseph) and his brother when you were ignorant?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and his brother, where the brothers had plotted against Yusuf out of jealousy. The king, who had later appointed Yusuf as a treasurer, is questioning the brothers about their past actions, highlighting their ignorance and lack of wisdom in their treatment of Yusuf.
orig: قال هل علمتم ما فعلتم بيوسف وأخيه إذ أنتم جاهلون

translation: They said, "Are you indeed Joseph?" He said, "I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has certainly favored us. Indeed, he who fears Allah and is patient, then indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and faith in Allah. When Joseph revealed his identity to his brothers, they were surprised and questioned him. Joseph then affirmed that he was indeed Joseph, and that Allah had favored them. The verse emphasizes that those who fear Allah and are patient will be rewarded, as Allah does not let the good deeds of the righteous go to waste. This teaches us to have trust in Allah's plan and to persevere through trials and tribulations, knowing that our efforts will be rewarded in the end.
orig: قالوا أإنك لأنت يوسف قال أنا يوسف وهذا أخي قد من الله علينا إنه من يتق ويصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: They said, "By Allah, Allah has certainly preferred you over us, and indeed we have been sinners."
interpretation: This verse reflects the acknowledgment by the people that Allah has chosen and favored the Prophet Muhammad over them, despite their own shortcomings and sins. It is an expression of their humility and recognition of the Prophet's elevated status in the sight of Allah.
orig: قالوا تالله لقد آثرك الله علينا وإن كنا لخاطئين

translation: He said: "No reproach this day shall be on you; Allah will forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy."
interpretation: This verse is a statement of forgiveness and compassion from God. It conveys the idea that those who have done wrong or made mistakes should not be burdened with guilt or shame, as God is willing to forgive them and show them mercy. The interpretation suggests that God’s forgiveness and mercy are boundless, and that individuals should not be overly harsh on themselves or others when mistakes are made.
orig: قال لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم وهو أرحم الراحمين

translation: Go with this shirt of mine and cast it over the face of my father; he will come to see. And bring me all your family.
interpretation: This verse instructs the brothers of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) to take his shirt and place it over the face of their father, Ya`qub (Jacob), so that he may regain his sight and be able to see. It also commands them to bring their entire family to Yusuf, indicating a reunion and reconciliation after a long period of separation.
orig: اذهبوا بقميصي هذا فألقوه على وجه أبي يأت بصيرا وأتوني بأهلكم أجمعين

translation: And when the caravan departed [from Egypt], their father said, 'Indeed, I find the smell of Joseph [in the distance], if you did not think me weakened in mind.'
interpretation: This verse suggests that the father of Joseph, Jacob, was able to sense and perceive the presence of his son Joseph, even though the caravan had departed and Joseph was far away. This demonstrates the deep spiritual connection and intuition that Jacob had with his son, which allowed him to feel Joseph's presence despite the physical distance between them. The interpretation is that strong familial bonds and spiritual awareness can transcend physical separation.
orig: ولما فصلت العير قال أبوهم إني لأجد ريح يوسف لولا أن تفندون

translation: They said, "By Allah, you are indeed in your old error."
interpretation: The verse suggests that the disbelievers accused the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of being in a longstanding state of misguidance or error. This reflects their rejection of his message and their unwillingness to accept the truth of Islam.
orig: قالوا تالله إنك لفي ضلالك القديم

translation: And when the bearer of good tidings arrived, he cast it upon his face, and he returned [once again] seeing. [Jacob] said, "Did I not tell you that I know from Allah that which you do not know?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power of faith and trust in God. When the good news of Joseph's well-being reached Jacob, he was able to regain his sight, demonstrating that faith can overcome even the most difficult circumstances. The verse also highlights Jacob's wisdom and insight, as he had known all along that God would eventually reveal the truth to him.
orig: فلما أن جاء البشير ألقاه على وجهه فارتد بصيرا قال ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: They said, 'O our father, ask forgiveness for us for our sins; indeed, we have been sinners."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah for one's sins. The people in the verse recognize their wrongdoing and humbly request their father to intercede on their behalf and ask Allah for forgiveness. It emphasizes the need for self-reflection, repentance, and turning to Allah for guidance and mercy.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا استغفر لنا ذنوبنا إنا كنا خاطئين

translation: He said, 'I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the compassion and mercy of God, who is willing to forgive those who seek His forgiveness. It emphasizes that God is the source of forgiveness and that He is both Forgiving and Merciful towards His creation.
orig: قال سوف أستغفر لكم ربي إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself and said, "Enter Egypt, if Allah wills, in safety."
interpretation: This verse describes the emotional reunion between Joseph and his parents after a long separation. It emphasizes that Joseph welcomed his parents and assured them of their safety in Egypt, acknowledging that their arrival and safety was ultimately in the hands of Allah. This highlights Joseph's piety, gratitude, and concern for his family's well-being.
orig: فلما دخلوا على يوسف آوى إليه أبويه وقال ادخلوا مصر إن شاء الله آمنين

translation: And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration. And he said, "O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of the prison and brought you [here] from the bedouin life after Satan had induced [estrangement] between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse describes the fulfillment of Joseph's dream, where his parents and brothers prostrate before him. It highlights how God's plan for Joseph unfolded, delivering him from prison and reuniting him with his family, despite the discord sown by Satan. The verse emphasizes God's wisdom and subtlety in orchestrating these events, demonstrating His knowledge and power.
orig: ورفع أبويه على العرش وخروا له سجدا وقال يا أبت هذا تأويل رؤياي من قبل قد جعلها ربي حقا وقد أحسن بي إذ أخرجني من السجن وجاء بكم من البدو من بعد أن نزغ الشيطان بيني وبين إخوتي إن ربي لطيف لما يشاء إنه هو العليم الحكيم

translation: My Lord, You have given me [something] of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. [O] Creator of the heavens and earth, You are my protector in this world and in the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse is spoken by the Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him) as he reflects on the blessings and guidance that Allah has bestowed upon him. He acknowledges that it is Allah who has granted him authority and the ability to interpret dreams, and that it is Allah who is his protector in this life and the next. The verse expresses Joseph's desire to remain steadfast in his faith, to die as a Muslim, and to be reunited with the righteous in the Hereafter. It is a supplication for Allah's continued care and guidance.
orig: رب قد آتيتني من الملك وعلمتني من تأويل الأحاديث فاطر السماوات والأرض أنت وليي في الدنيا والآخرة توفني مسلما وألحقني بالصالحين

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muhammad]. And you were not with them when they put together their plan while they conspired.
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine knowledge that Allah imparts to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) about events and information that are beyond human perception. It indicates that the Prophet was not present when the disbelievers plotted against him, but Allah informed him of their schemes through revelation. This highlights the prophetic role of Muhammad (peace be upon him) in receiving and conveying the divine message.
orig: ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك وما كنت لديهم إذ أجمعوا أمرهم وهم يمكرون

translation: And most of the people, although you strive [for it], will not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that despite the Prophet's sincere efforts to guide people to the truth of Islam, the majority of people will still not believe. It highlights the reality that faith is a matter of the heart, which cannot be forced upon people. The verse reminds us that guidance is in the hands of Allah, and that we must continue to convey the message with patience and wisdom, leaving the outcome to the Almighty.
orig: وما أكثر الناس ولو حرصت بمؤمنين

translation: And you do not ask them for it any payment. It is not but a reminder to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) does not seek any material compensation for conveying the message of Islam. His mission is to provide a reminder and guidance to all of humanity, not to enrich himself. The Qur'an is a gift from God to the people, not a commodity to be traded.
orig: وما تسألهم عليه من أجر إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: And how many a sign within the heavens and earth do they pass over while they, therefrom, are turning away.
interpretation: This verse suggests that there are countless signs and evidence of God's power and wisdom in the universe, which people often ignore or overlook. It encourages reflection and contemplation of the natural world, as a means of recognizing the divine.
orig: وكأين من آية في السماوات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون

translation: And most of them believe not in Allah except while they associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse suggests that while many people claim to believe in Allah, their actions and beliefs often involve associating partners or deities with Him. This indicates a lack of true, sincere faith and a failure to fully submit to the oneness and sovereignty of Allah.
orig: وما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون

translation: Then do they feel secure from the coming upon them of the overwhelming [punishment] from Allah or the coming of the Hour suddenly while they do not perceive?
interpretation: This verse warns those who have rejected faith that they should not feel secure from the coming of Allah's punishment or the sudden arrival of the Day of Judgment, which they are unaware of. It emphasizes the need for constant vigilance and preparedness, as the consequences of disbelief can come unexpectedly.
orig: أفأمنوا أن تأتيهم غاشية من عذاب الله أو تأتيهم الساعة بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allah, and I am not of those who associate others with Him."
interpretation: This verse calls upon the Prophet Muhammad to invite people to the path of Allah with wisdom, clarity and conviction. It emphasizes that the Prophet and his followers are devoted exclusively to the worship of Allah, without associating any partners with Him. The verse highlights the importance of inviting others to the true faith with patience, knowledge and sincerity.
orig: قل هذه سبيلي أدعو إلى الله على بصيرة أنا ومن اتبعني وسبحان الله وما أنا من المشركين

translation: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed [the message], so ask the people of the message if you do not know. [We sent them] with clear signs and written ordinances, and We revealed to you the message that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them and that they might give thought.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the messengers sent by God throughout history have been human beings, not angels or supernatural beings. It encourages the people to reflect on the fate of previous nations and communities, and to understand that the ultimate success lies with those who are righteous and God-fearing. The verse also highlights the purpose of revelation, which is to provide guidance and clarity to the people so that they may contemplate and understand the divine message.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم من أهل القرى أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم ولدار الآخرة خير للذين اتقوا أفلا تعقلون

translation: Until, when the messengers gave up hope and were certain that they had been denied, there came to them Our victory, and whoever We willed was saved. And Our punishment cannot be repelled from the people who are criminals.
interpretation: This verse conveys that even in the face of seemingly insurmountable challenges, God's help and victory will ultimately prevail. It suggests that those who have faith and do good deeds will be saved, while the wrongdoers cannot escape God's punishment. The verse encourages steadfastness in the face of adversity and trust in God's plan, even when the situation appears bleak.
orig: حتى إذا استيأس الرسل وظنوا أنهم قد كذبوا جاءهم نصرنا فنجي من نشاء ولا يرد بأسنا عن القوم المجرمين

translation: There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding. It was not a narration which could be invented, but a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of all things and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authenticity and divine origin of the Qur’an. It states that the stories and narratives in the Qur’an contain valuable lessons and wisdom for those who possess understanding. The Qur’an is not a fabricated tale, but a confirmation and detailed explanation of the previous divine revelations, and a source of guidance and mercy for those who believe.
orig: لقد كان في قصصهم عبرة لأولي الألباب ما كان حديثا يفترى ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل كل شيء وهدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Book; and what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine origin of the Qur'an, which is the "Book" revealed to the Prophet Muhammad from God. It emphasizes that the Qur'an contains the absolute truth, but most people do not accept or believe in it. This highlights the importance of faith and submission to God's guidance, as opposed to blind rejection or denial of the divine message.
orig: المر تلك آيات الكتاب والذي أنزل إليك من ربك الحق ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: Allah is the One who raised the heavens without pillars that you [can] see; then He established Himself above the Throne, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, [all] running [their courses] for a specified term. He arranges [each] matter; He details the signs that you may, of the meeting with your Lord, be certain.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and sovereignty of Allah, the Creator of the universe. It highlights how Allah has created the heavens without visible supports, and how He has established Himself on the Throne, subjecting the sun and moon to follow their ordained courses. This demonstrates Allah's complete control and authority over all creation. The verse also indicates that Allah arranges and directs all matters, and provides clear signs to guide people towards certainty in the meeting with their Lord on the Day of Judgment.
orig: الله الذي رفع السماوات بغير عمد ترونها ثم استوى على العرش وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى يدبر الأمر يفصل الآيات لعلكم بلقاء ربكم توقنون

translation: And it is He who has extended the earth and placed therein firmly set mountains and rivers, and from all the fruits He has made therein two mates; He causes the night to cover the day. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and wisdom of God in creating the universe. The extension of the earth, the placement of mountains and rivers, the diversity of fruits, and the cycle of day and night all point to the divine design and providence. This is a call for people to reflect on these signs and recognize the oneness and majesty of the Creator.
orig: وهو الذي مد الأرض وجعل فيها رواسي وأنهارا ومن كل الثمرات جعل فيها زوجين اثنين يغشي الليل النهار إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And in the earth are neighboring plots and gardens of grapevines and crops and palm trees, [growing] several from a single root or otherwise, watered with one water; but We make some of them exceed others in [quality of] fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity and interconnectedness of the natural world, where different types of vegetation and crops coexist, all nourished by the same water source. Yet, despite this common resource, Allah has created variations in the quality and abundance of their fruits, demonstrating His wisdom and the signs of His power for those who reflect and use their intellect.
orig: وفي الأرض قطع متجاورات وجنات من أعناب وزرع ونخيل صنوان وغير صنوان يسقى بماء واحد ونفضل بعضها على بعض في الأكل إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And if you are amazed, [O Muhammad] - then [even] more amazing is their saying: "When we have become dust, will we indeed be [brought] into a new creation?" Those are the ones who have disbelieved in their Lord, and those will have shackles upon their necks, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide in it eternally.
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers who scoff at the idea of resurrection and a new creation after death. It emphasizes that the concept of resurrection, despite seeming amazing to them, is a reality that they will have to face. The verse also highlights the consequences of disbelief, where the disbelievers will be shackled and condemned to an eternal life in the Fire. The interpretation underscores the importance of belief in the Almighty and the afterlife, and the severe punishment that awaits those who reject this fundamental tenet of Islam.
orig: وإن تعجب فعجب قولهم أإذا كنا ترابا أإنا لفي خلق جديد أولئك الذين كفروا بربهم وأولئك الأغلال في أعناقهم وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And they ask you to hasten the punishment, while the [tormented] Punishment is already before them. And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people, despite their wrongdoing. And indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that people often demand immediate punishment for their misdeeds, rather than seeking forgiveness and repentance. However, Allah is merciful and forgiving, even towards those who have wronged others. At the same time, He is also severe in His punishment for those who persist in their wrongdoing without seeking His forgiveness.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالسيئة قبل الحسنة وقد خلت من قبلهم المثلات وإن ربك لذو مغفرة للناس على ظلمهم وإن ربك لشديد العقاب

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" You are only a warner, and for every people is a [direct] guide.
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers who demand a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as proof of his prophethood. The Qur'an responds by stating that the Prophet's role is that of a warner, and that for every people, there is a guide sent by God to lead them to the right path. The interpretation emphasizes that the Prophet's mission is to convey the message of Islam, and that people are responsible for their own guidance and acceptance of the truth.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه إنما أنت منذر ولكل قوم هاد

translation: Allah knows what every female bears and what the wombs lose [prematurely] or exceed. And everything with Him is by due measure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and control over all aspects of creation. He knows the secrets of the wombs, including what each female conceives and what is lost or gained in the process of pregnancy and childbirth. This highlights Allah's power and wisdom, as He is aware of even the most intimate details of His creation, and everything is according to His divine plan and measure.
orig: الله يعلم ما تحمل كل أنثى وما تغيض الأرحام وما تزداد وكل شيء عنده بمقدار

translation: The Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Grand, the Exalted
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme knowledge and power of God, who has knowledge of both the unseen (the spiritual realm) and the witnessed (the physical world). He is the Grand, the Exalted, transcending all creation and deserving of the utmost reverence and worship.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة الكبير المتعال

translation: Whether one of you conceals his speech or declares it, and whether one moves about at night or in the daytime
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is All-Knowing and All-Aware of our thoughts, words, and actions, whether they are done in secret or openly, during the night or the day. It serves as a reminder that we are accountable for our conduct, and that we should strive to live righteously, as Allah is ever-present and cognizant of our deeds.
orig: سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به ومن هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار

translation: For him are successive [angels] before and behind him who protect him by the decree of Allah. Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah intends for a people ill, there is no repelling it. And there is not for them besides Him any patron.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has appointed angels to watch over and protect people, and that Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves. It also states that if Allah intends harm for a people, there is no one who can stop it, and that Allah is the only true protector. The interpretation is that people's fate is ultimately determined by their own actions and choices, and that Allah's will and judgment are inescapable.
orig: له معقبات من بين يديه ومن خلفه يحفظونه من أمر الله إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم وإذا أراد الله بقوم سوءا فلا مرد له وما لهم من دونه من وال

translation: It is He who shows you lightning, [causing] fear and hope, and [who] amasses the heavy clouds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who controls the natural phenomena of lightning and clouds. The lightning can instill both fear and hope in people - fear of the potential destruction it can cause, and hope of the rain it may bring. The heavy clouds that Allah amasses are a sign of His power and the provision of water for the earth.
orig: هو الذي يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا وينشئ السحاب الثقال

translation: And the thunder exalts [Allah] with praise of Him, and the angels [as well], from fear of Him. And He sends thunderbolts and hits with them whom He wills, yet they dispute about Allah, and He is severe in assault.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the glory and power of Allah, as even the thunder and angels praise and revere Him out of fear. Allah has the ability to send down thunderbolts to strike whomever He wills, yet people still argue and dispute about the nature of Allah, despite His might and severity in dealing with those who defy Him.
orig: ويسبح الرعد بحمده والملائكة من خيفته ويرسل الصواعق فيصيب بها من يشاء وهم يجادلون في الله وهو شديد المحال

translation: To Him belongs the call to the truth, and those whom they call upon besides Him do not respond to them with anything, except like one who stretches forth his hands towards water [from afar, calling it] to reach his mouth, but it will not reach it [thus]. And the supplication of the disbelievers is not but in error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the true call and worship belongs to God alone. Those who call upon other deities or powers besides God will not receive any response, as their supplication is like a person trying to reach water from afar - it will never reach them. The verse highlights the futility of worshipping anything other than the one true God, and that the supplication of the disbelievers is nothing but misguidance.
orig: له دعوة الحق والذين يدعون من دونه لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه وما هو ببالغه وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and their shadows [as well] in the mornings and the afternoons.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all of creation, from the heavens to the earth, submits to the will of Allah, either willingly or unwillingly. Even the shadows of all creatures prostrate to Allah at different times of the day, highlighting the universal submission to the Divine.
orig: ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال

translation: Say, "Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?" Say, "[It is] Allah." Say, "Have you then taken besides Him allies who do not possess for themselves any benefit or any harm?" Say, "Are the blind and the seeing equal? Or are the darkness and the light equal? Or have they attributed to Allah partners while He has created [all] things? And He is the One, the Prevailing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Oneness and Sovereignty of Allah as the Creator and Sustainer of the heavens and the earth. It rejects the notion of associating any partners with Allah, as He alone has the power to benefit or harm. The verse also draws a contrast between those who are spiritually blind and those who can see the truth, as well as between darkness and light, to highlight the superiority of worshipping the One True God over false deities. The interpretation underscores the futility of seeking protectors or allies besides Allah, who alone is the Almighty and Omnipotent.
orig: قل من رب السماوات والأرض قل الله قل أفاتخذتم من دونه أولياء لا يملكون لأنفسهم نفعا ولا ضرا قل هل يستوي الأعمى والبصير أم هل تستوي الظلمات والنور أم جعلوا لله شركاء خلقوا كخلقه فتشابه الخلق عليهم قل الله خالق كل شيء وهو الواحد القهار

translation: He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the flood carries a rising foam. And from that [ore] which they heat in the fire, [seeking to make] jewelry or utensils, is a foam like it. Thus Allah presents [the example of] truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it vanishes, [being] cast off; but as for that which benefits the people, it remains on the earth. Thus does Allah present examples.
interpretation: This verse uses the analogy of water and foam to illustrate the distinction between truth and falsehood. The water that comes down from the sky and fills the valleys represents truth, which is constant and beneficial. The rising foam on the water's surface represents falsehood, which is temporary and worthless. Similarly, the foam that forms when metals are heated in fire for making jewelry or utensils is like falsehood - it vanishes, while the useful metal remains. This analogy teaches that truth is lasting and valuable, while falsehood is transient and devoid of substance.
orig: أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا ومما يوقدون عليه في النار ابتغاء حلية أو متاع زبد مثله كذلك يضرب الله الحق والباطل فأما الزبد فيذهب جفاء وأما ما ينفع الناس فيمكث في الأرض كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال

translation: For those who have responded to their Lord is the best [reward], but those who have not responded to Him - if they had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it, they would [attempt to] ransom themselves thereby. Those will have the worst account, and their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the fate of those who obey and respond to God's commands, and those who do not. The former will be rewarded with the best in the Hereafter, while the latter, even if they possessed all the wealth of the world, would not be able to ransom themselves from the punishment of Hell, which is a terrible abode.
orig: للذين استجابوا لربهم الحسنى والذين لم يستجيبوا له لو أن لهم ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه لافتدوا به أولئك لهم سوء الحساب ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: Is then one who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? Only those of understanding will remember.
interpretation: This verse contrasts those who recognize the truth of the Quranic revelation with those who remain blind to it. The former, possessing insight and understanding, will take heed and remember the guidance, while the latter will remain in darkness. The implication is that true believers, who know the Quran to be the word of God, are fundamentally different from those who reject or ignore it.
orig: أفمن يعلم أنما أنزل إليك من ربك الحق كمن هو أعمى إنما يتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: Those who fulfill their covenant with Allah and do not break the promise
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's commitments and promises to Allah. It encourages believers to be steadfast in their faith and to honor the covenants they have made with the Almighty. This speaks to the virtue of integrity, reliability, and faithfulness in one's relationship with the divine.
orig: الذين يوفون بعهد الله ولا ينقضون الميثاق

translation: And those who join that which Allah has ordered to be joined and fear their Lord and are afraid of the evil of [their] account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining strong family and social ties, as commanded by Allah. It encourages believers to uphold their responsibilities towards their kin and community, and to fear the consequences of neglecting these duties. The interpretation suggests that fulfilling these obligations, with a sense of reverence towards Allah, will lead to a favorable outcome in the Hereafter.
orig: والذين يصلون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويخشون ربهم ويخافون سوء الحساب

translation: And those who are patient, seeking the countenance of their Lord, and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them secretly and publicly and prevent evil with good - those will have the good consequence of [this] home.
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities of the righteous believers who are steadfast in their faith and devotion to Allah. They patiently endure trials and tribulations, seeking the pleasure and approval of their Lord. They are diligent in their religious obligations, such as performing the daily prayers, and they are generous in spending from the provisions Allah has granted them, both in private and in public. Additionally, they respond to evil with good, thereby repelling it and preventing its spread. This righteous conduct will be rewarded with the best consequence in the Hereafter, the abode of the Afterlife.
orig: والذين صبروا ابتغاء وجه ربهم وأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة أولئك لهم عقبى الدار

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence; they will enter them with whoever were righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants. And the angels will enter upon them from every gate.
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal abode of the righteous in the Hereafter - the Gardens of Paradise. The righteous will enter these gardens, accompanied by their righteous ancestors, spouses, and offspring. Furthermore, the angels will greet them and welcome them from every entrance, signifying the complete peace, tranquility, and honor that the inhabitants of Paradise will enjoy.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها ومن صلح من آبائهم وأزواجهم وذرياتهم والملائكة يدخلون عليهم من كل باب

translation: Peace be upon you for your patience, and excellent is the final home.
interpretation: This verse conveys a message of divine blessing and commendation for those who have endured patiently. It suggests that those who have persevered through trials and tribulations will be rewarded with a blissful and eternal abode in the Hereafter, which is described as an "excellent final home." The verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to face life's challenges with patience and resilience, as they will be ultimately rewarded for their fortitude.
orig: سلام عليكم بما صبرتم فنعم عقبى الدار

translation: And those who break the covenant of Allah after contracting it and sever that which Allah has ordered to be joined and spread corruption on earth - for them is the curse, and they will have the worst home.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who break their covenant with Allah and sever the ties that Allah has commanded to be maintained. They spread corruption on earth, for which they will be cursed and face a terrible fate in the Hereafter.
orig: والذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه ويقطعون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض أولئك لهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. And they rejoice in the worldly life, while the worldly life is not, compared to the Hereafter, except [brief] enjoyment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has control over the distribution of provisions and resources. He bestows them upon whomever He wills, and restricts them from others as He pleases. The verse also highlights that people often become overly attached to the fleeting pleasures of this world, forgetting that the Hereafter is the true and lasting abode. The enjoyment of this worldly life is insignificant compared to the eternal rewards and blessings of the Hereafter.
orig: الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر وفرحوا بالحياة الدنيا وما الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة إلا متاع

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him]"
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers who demand a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad as proof of his prophethood. The response given is that Allah guides whomever He wills, and leads astray those who turn away from Him. The interpretation is that faith is a matter of Allah's guidance, not a result of miraculous signs, and that those who sincerely turn to Allah will be guided, while those who persist in disbelief will be left to stray.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه قل إن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي إليه من أناب

translation: Those who believe and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts find rest.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the remembrance of Allah in finding inner peace and tranquility. It suggests that those who truly believe in Allah and keep Him in their hearts and minds will find their hearts at ease and content. The remembrance of Allah is the source of this spiritual comfort and solace, as it connects the believer to the divine and provides a sense of security and purpose.
orig: الذين آمنوا وتطمئن قلوبهم بذكر الله ألا بذكر الله تطمئن القلوب

translation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is [in the Hereafter] a good place of return.
interpretation: This verse conveys the promise of a blissful afterlife for those who have faith in God and do good deeds. The "good place of return" refers to the reward and eternal abode in the Hereafter that awaits the righteous believers.
orig: الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات طوبى لهم وحسن مآب

translation: Thus have We sent you to a community before whom [other] communities have passed on, that you might recite to them that which We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say, "He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him is my return."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad was sent as a messenger to a people who had already received previous prophets and messengers, but they had rejected the message of the Most Merciful God. The verse instructs the Prophet to declare his faith in the One true God, to rely on Him, and to submit to Him. This highlights the universality of the Qur'anic message and the importance of belief in the Oneness of God.
orig: كذلك أرسلناك في أمة قد خلت من قبلها أمم لتتلو عليهم الذي أوحينا إليك وهم يكفرون بالرحمن قل هو ربي لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وإليه متاب

translation: And if there was any Qur'an by which the mountains would be moved or the earth would be cloven asunder or the dead would be made to speak, [it would be this Qur'an], but to Allah belongs the affair entirely. Then have those who believed not yet accepted that if Allah had willed, He could have guided the people, all of them? And those who disbelieve do not cease to be struck, for what they have done, by calamity - or it will descend near their home - until the promise of Allah has come about. Indeed, Allah does not fail in [His] promise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is the word of Allah, and that He has the power to perform extraordinary feats through it, such as moving mountains, splitting the earth, or reviving the dead. However, the ultimate decision and authority lies with Allah alone. The verse also highlights that those who believe should not be disheartened, as Allah could have guided all of humanity if He so willed. It warns the disbelievers that they will continue to face calamities until the promise of Allah is fulfilled, for Allah never fails in His promise.
orig: ولو أن قرآنا سيرت به الجبال أو قطعت به الأرض أو كلم به الموتى بل لله الأمر جميعا أفلم ييأس الذين آمنوا أن لو يشاء الله لهدى الناس جميعا ولا يزال الذين كفروا تصيبهم بما صنعوا قارعة أو تحل قريبا من دارهم حتى يأتي وعد الله إن الله لا يخلف الميعاد

translation: And certainly messengers before you were mocked, but I gave respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them, and how [terrible] was My punishment.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that rejection and mockery of the prophets is not a new phenomenon. It has happened throughout history. However, Allah gives the disbelievers time and respite, but ultimately they will be seized and punished for their rejection of the truth. This serves as a warning to those who mock the prophets and the message of Islam.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فأمليت للذين كفروا ثم أخذتهم فكيف كان عقاب

translation: Is then He Who is the Disposer of every affair (and Who takes account of everything), (not) better than (your so-called) partners of Allah? Say: "Praise be to Allah!" But most of them understand not.
interpretation: This verse highlights the superiority of Allah over any partners or associates that people may ascribe to Him. It emphasizes that Allah alone is the Disposer of every affair and the One who takes account of everything, which makes Him far superior to any false deities or idols that people may worship. The verse calls on people to praise and acknowledge Allah alone, as most of them do not truly understand His greatness and oneness.
orig: أفمن هو قائم على كل نفس بما كسبت وجعلوا لله شركاء قل سموهم أم تنبئونه بما لا يعلم في الأرض أم بظاهر من القول بل زين للذين كفروا مكرهم وصدوا عن السبيل ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: For them is punishment in the worldly life, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe. And they will not have from Allah any protector.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences faced by those who reject the guidance of Allah. They will face punishment not only in this life, but also in the Hereafter, where the punishment will be even more severe. This emphasizes the importance of submitting to Allah and following His commands, as there is no one who can protect them from the ultimate reckoning on the Day of Judgment.
orig: لهم عذاب في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أشق وما لهم من الله من واق

translation: The description of Paradise which the righteous have been promised: Beneath it flow rivers, its food is perpetual, and [so is] its shade. That is the final home of those who feared Allah, and the home of the disbelievers is the Fire.
interpretation: This verse describes the rewards and blessings awaiting those who are righteous and fear Allah. The imagery of a paradise with flowing rivers, perpetual sustenance, and shade evokes a state of eternal peace, comfort and abundance. In contrast, the "home of the disbelievers is the Fire", emphasizing the stark difference between the fate of the righteous and the unbelievers. This highlights the importance of fearing and obeying Allah in order to attain the highest rewards in the Hereafter.
orig: مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون تجري من تحتها الأنهار أكلها دائم وظلها تلك عقبى الذين اتقوا وعقبى الكافرين النار

translation: And those to whom We have given the Book rejoice at what has been revealed to you, and of the [opposing] factions are those who deny part of it. Say, "I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate [anything] with Him. To Him I invite [all], and to Him is my return."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an and the Prophet Muhammad's mission. It highlights that those who have been given the previous scriptures (such as the Jews and Christians) should rejoice in the revelation of the Qur'an, as it confirms and builds upon the truths found in their own scriptures. However, it also acknowledges that there are those among the factions (such as the disbelievers) who reject parts of the Qur'an. The Prophet is commanded to worship Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him, and to invite all people to this pure monotheistic faith, as this is the path that leads to Allah.
orig: والذين آتيناهم الكتاب يفرحون بما أنزل إليك ومن الأحزاب من ينكر بعضه قل إنما أمرت أن أعبد الله ولا أشرك به إليه أدعو وإليه مآب

translation: And thus have We sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and if you should follow their inclinations after what has come to you of knowledge, you would not have against Allah any ally or any protector.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the revealed knowledge of the Qur'an, which has been sent down in the Arabic language. It warns against succumbing to personal desires and whims, which may lead one astray from the truth that has been made clear. The message is that one should not seek any protector or ally other than Allah, as He alone can guide and safeguard those who adhere to His teachings.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه حكما عربيا ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم بعدما جاءك من العلم ما لك من الله من ولي ولا واق

translation: And We have certainly sent [messengers] before you, [O Muhammad], and We assigned to them wives and descendants. And it was not for a messenger to come with a sign except by permission of Allah. For every term is a [decreed] time.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that sending messengers is a consistent pattern in God's plan, and that these messengers were not alone but had families and descendants. It also highlights that the messengers could only perform miracles by God's permission, and that everything has a predetermined time period. This suggests that God's will and plan are sovereign, and that the messengers are instruments in carrying out this plan.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك وجعلنا لهم أزواجا وذرية وما كان لرسول أن يأتي بآية إلا بإذن الله لكل أجل كتاب

translation: Allah eliminates what He wills or confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has the ultimate power and authority to decide what is to be eliminated or confirmed, as He is the Sovereign and the Originator of all things. The "Mother of the Book" refers to the divine knowledge and plan that resides with Allah, which is the source and foundation of all revealed scriptures and the divine will.
orig: يمحو الله ما يشاء ويثبت وعنده أم الكتاب

translation: And whether We show you some of what We promise them, [O Muhammad], or We take you in death, upon you is [only] the [duty of] notification, and upon Us is the account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the ultimate responsibility of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is to convey the message of Islam, and the consequences of accepting or rejecting that message are in the hands of Allah. The Prophet's duty is to deliver the message, not to ensure the outcome. The final judgment and reckoning belongs to Allah alone.
orig: وإن ما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإنما عليك البلاغ وعلينا الحساب

translation: Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders? And Allah judges; there is no adjuster of His judgment. And He is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that Allah has control over the Earth and its resources. He can expand or reduce the land as He wills, and His judgments are final and cannot be changed. This emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate authority and that He holds all beings accountable for their actions.
orig: أولم يروا أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها والله يحكم لا معقب لحكمه وهو سريع الحساب

translation: And those before them had plotted, but to Allah belongs [all] planning. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know for whom is the final [destination] of the Abode.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate planner and that no one can outwit Him. It warns the disbelievers that their plots and schemes will be futile, as Allah knows everything they do and will determine the final outcome. The interpretation is that one should not rely on their own plans and machinations, but rather put their trust in Allah, as He is the All-Knowing and All-Powerful.
orig: وقد مكر الذين من قبلهم فلله المكر جميعا يعلم ما تكسب كل نفس وسيعلم الكفار لمن عقبى الدار

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger." Say, "Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you, and [the witness of] whoever has knowledge of the Scripture."
interpretation: This verse addresses those who reject the Prophet Muhammad`s message, denying that he is a true messenger of God. In response, the Prophet is commanded to say that Allah Himself is a sufficient witness between them, and that those who have knowledge of the Scriptures can also testify to the truth of his prophethood.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لست مرسلا قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم ومن عنده علم الكتاب

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. [This is] a Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that you may bring mankind out of darknesses into the light by permission of their Lord - to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Quran is a divine revelation sent down to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to guide humanity from the darkness of ignorance, disbelief, and sin to the light of faith, guidance, and righteousness. It emphasizes that this guidance is by the permission and will of God, the Almighty and Praiseworthy, and leads people to the straight path that pleases Him.
orig: الر كتاب أنزلناه إليك لتخرج الناس من الظلمات إلى النور بإذن ربهم إلى صراط العزيز الحميد

translation: Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and dominion of Allah over the entire universe, both in the heavens and on earth. It serves as a warning to those who reject faith and disbelieve in Allah, that they will face a severe and painful punishment for their rejection of the truth.
orig: الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وويل للكافرين من عذاب شديد

translation: Those who love the worldly life over the Hereafter and avert [people] from the way of Allah and seek to make it [seem] deviant. Those are in extreme error.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who are overly attached to the material world and its pleasures, and who use their influence to lead others astray from the path of Allah. It suggests that such people are in a state of profound misguidance, having lost sight of the true purpose of life and the importance of the Hereafter.
orig: الذين يستحبون الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة ويصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا أولئك في ضلال بعيد

translation: And We have not sent any messenger except [speaking] in the language of his people to state clearly for them, and Allah sends astray [thereby] whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah sends messengers who speak the language of their people, so that they can clearly convey the message of Islam to them. However, Allah guides whomever He wills and leads astray whomever He wills, as He is the Almighty and the All-Wise. This highlights the sovereignty of Allah in guiding people to the truth.
orig: وما أرسلنا من رسول إلا بلسان قومه ليبين لهم فيضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs, [commanding him], "Bring out your people from the darknesses into the light and remind them of the days of Allah." Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine mission of Prophet Moses to guide his people from the darkness of ignorance and sin to the light of faith and righteousness. The "days of Allah" refer to the significant events in the history of the Israelites, where God`s power and guidance were manifested. The interpretation suggests that those who are patient and grateful in their faith will find guidance and wisdom in reflecting on these divine signs and lessons.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا أن أخرج قومك من الظلمات إلى النور وذكرهم بأيام الله إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Moses said to his people, "Remember the favor of Allah upon you when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst torment and were slaughtering your [newborn] sons and keeping your females alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord."
interpretation: This verse reminds the Israelites of the favor and blessing of Allah in delivering them from the oppression and cruelty of Pharaoh and his people. It highlights the hardships they endured, including being subjected to severe punishment, the slaughter of their newborn sons, and the preservation of their women. This was a great trial from Allah, but He saved them from this calamity, demonstrating His power and mercy. The verse encourages the people to remember and be grateful for Allah's blessings and deliverance.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ أنجاكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب ويذبحون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord proclaimed, 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.'"
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be grateful to Allah for His blessings, as He promises to increase those blessings if they express gratitude. Conversely, it warns that denying or rejecting Allah's favors will result in severe punishment. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of maintaining a thankful attitude towards Allah and the consequences of ingratitude.
orig: وإذ تأذن ربكم لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم ولئن كفرتم إن عذابي لشديد

translation: And Moses said, "If you should disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely - indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is self-sufficient and does not need the worship or belief of His creation. Even if all of humanity were to disbelieve, it would not diminish Allah's power, glory or the perfection of His attributes. This serves as a reminder that our faith and obedience to Allah is for our own benefit, not for Allah's, as He is the Praiseworthy and Free of all need.
orig: وقال موسى إن تكفروا أنتم ومن في الأرض جميعا فإن الله لغني حميد

translation: Has there not come to you the news of those before you - the people of Noah and 'Aad and Thamud and those after them? None knows them [i.e., their number] but Allah. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they returned their hands to their mouths and said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed we are, about that to which you invite us, in disquieting doubt."
interpretation: This verse reminds us that throughout history, many people have rejected the messengers and messages sent by God. The people of Noah, 'Aad, and Thamud all denied the clear signs and proofs brought to them, and expressed doubt and disbelief in the message. This serves as a warning that rejecting God's guidance can have severe consequences, and that we should heed the lessons of the past and submit to God's will.
orig: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين من قبلكم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود والذين من بعدهم لا يعلمهم إلا الله جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فردوا أيديهم في أفواههم وقالوا إنا كفرنا بما أرسلتم به وإنا لفي شك مما تدعوننا إليه مريب

translation: Their messengers said, "Is there any doubt about Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth? He invites you that He may forgive you of your sins, and give you respite for a specified term." They said, "You are not but human beings like us, who wish to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship. So bring us a clear authority."
interpretation: This verse highlights the response of the disbelievers to the call of the messengers of Allah. The messengers remind the people that there is no doubt about the existence and power of Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. They invite the people to believe in Allah so that He may forgive their sins and give them time to repent. However, the disbelievers reject this call, claiming that the messengers are merely human beings like themselves and that they are trying to turn them away from the beliefs of their forefathers. They demand a clear proof or authority to support the message of the messengers.
orig: قالت رسلهم أفي الله شك فاطر السماوات والأرض يدعوكم ليغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى قالوا إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا تريدون أن تصدونا عما كان يعبد آباؤنا فأتونا بسلطان مبين

translation: Their messengers said to them: "We are only human beings like you, but Allah bestows His grace on whom He wills of His servants. And it is not for us to bring you a proof [i.e., authorization] except by the permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the messengers of Allah are human beings like the people they are addressing, and that it is Allah alone who bestows His grace and guidance upon whomever He wills. The messengers do not have any inherent authority or power of their own, but rather they convey the message of Allah with His permission. Therefore, the believers are instructed to place their trust and reliance in Allah alone.
orig: قالت لهم رسلهم إن نحن إلا بشر مثلكم ولكن الله يمن على من يشاء من عباده وما كان لنا أن نأتيكم بسلطان إلا بإذن الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And why should we not put our trust in Allah while He has guided us to our [good] ways. And we will surely be patient with whatever harm you should cause us. For upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to put their trust in Allah, as He has guided them to the right path. It also instructs them to be patient in the face of any harm or persecution they may face, and to rely on Allah as the true source of support and guidance for those who believe.
orig: وما لنا ألا نتوكل على الله وقد هدانا سبلنا ولنصبرن على ما آذيتمونا وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون

translation: And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, "We will surely drive you out of our land, or you must return to our religion." But their Lord inspired to them: "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and intolerance of the disbelievers towards the messengers of God. They threatened to expel the messengers from their land unless they returned to the disbelievers' religion. However, God assured the messengers that He would destroy the wrongdoers, those who persecute and oppress the believers. This verse emphasizes God's power and justice, and His unwavering support for those who follow the truth.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لرسلهم لنخرجنكم من أرضنا أو لتعودن في ملتنا فأوحى إليهم ربهم لنهلكن الظالمين

translation: And We will cause you to dwell in the land after them. That is for he who fears My position and fears My threat.
interpretation: This verse suggests that after the previous nations, Allah will establish the believers in the land. This is for those who fear standing before Allah and are wary of His punishment and warnings.
orig: ولنسكننكم الأرض من بعدهم ذلك لمن خاف مقامي وخاف وعيد

translation: And they sought victory and [instead], every obstinate tyrant was disappointed.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who seek power and dominance through tyrannical means will ultimately be disappointed and defeated. It emphasizes that true victory comes not from force or arrogance, but from righteousness and humility before God.
orig: واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد

translation: Behind him is Hell, and he will be given a drink of purulent water.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who reject faith and do evil deeds. They will be condemned to Hell, a place of eternal punishment, and will be forced to drink a foul, putrid liquid as a torment for their misdeeds.
orig: من ورائه جهنم ويسقى من ماء صديد

translation: He will sip it unwillingly, and he will hardly be able to swallow it. And death will come to him from everywhere, but he is not to die. And before him, there is a massive punishment.
interpretation: This verse describes the torment of the disbelievers in the Hereafter. They will be forced to drink a bitter and unpalatable drink, which they will find extremely difficult to swallow. Death will come to them from all directions, but they will not be able to die, and they will face a severe and relentless punishment.
orig: يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه ويأتيه الموت من كل مكان وما هو بميت ومن ورائه عذاب غليظ

translation: The example of those who disbelieved in their Lord is [that] their deeds are like ashes upon which the wind blows forcefully on a [stormy] day; they are unable [to keep] from what they earned. That is the extreme error.
interpretation: This verse presents a metaphor for the futility of the deeds of those who disbelieve in God. Their actions, like ashes blown away by a strong wind, have no lasting substance or impact. They are unable to hold onto or benefit from what they have earned through their disbelief, as it is all ultimately worthless. This emphasizes the idea that true faith and righteous deeds are necessary for one's actions to have any lasting value or meaning.
orig: مثل الذين كفروا بربهم أعمالهم كرماد اشتدت به الريح في يوم عاصف لا يقدرون مما كسبوا على شيء ذلك هو الضلال البعيد

translation: Have you not seen that Allah has created the heavens and the earth in truth? If He wills, He can do away with you and bring [in your place] a new creation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the sole Creator of the universe, and that He has the power to replace humanity with a new creation if He so desires. It serves as a reminder of Allah's absolute sovereignty and the transient nature of our existence, encouraging us to live righteously and submit to His will.
orig: ألم تر أن الله خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأت بخلق جديد

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that nothing is too difficult or challenging for Allah, the Almighty. It emphasizes the limitless power and capability of God, and that He can accomplish any task with ease. This verse serves to reassure believers that Allah is in full control and that they can trust in His ability to fulfill His will, no matter how seemingly impossible a situation may appear.
orig: وما ذلك على الله بعزيز

translation: And they will all be presented before Allah. Then the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers, so can you avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?" They will say, "If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. It is all the same for us whether we show intolerance or are patient; there is for us no place of escape."
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when all people will be gathered before Allah. The weak and powerless will confront the arrogant and powerful, asking if they can provide any relief from the punishment of Allah. The arrogant will admit that they cannot, as they were also misguided and have no means of escape from the consequences of their actions. This highlights the futility of arrogance and the importance of humility and reliance on Allah's guidance.
orig: وبرزوا لله جميعا فقال الضعفاء للذين استكبروا إنا كنا لكم تبعا فهل أنتم مغنون عنا من عذاب الله من شيء قالوا لو هدانا الله لهديناكم سواء علينا أجزعنا أم صبرنا ما لنا من محيص

translation: And Satan will say, when the matter has been concluded, "Indeed, Allah had promised you the promise of truth. And I promised you, but I betrayed you.
