But I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; but blame yourselves. I cannot be called to your aid, and you cannot be called to my aid. Indeed, I had previously denied having any association with you." Indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse describes Satan\'s admission of his deception of mankind. He acknowledges that he had no real power over them, but only invited them to disbelieve and they willingly responded. Therefore, Satan absolves himself of blame and says that the people have only themselves to blame for their own choices. The verse emphasizes that the wrongdoers, those who followed Satan\'s temptations, will face a painful punishment from Allah for their actions.
orig: وقال الشيطان لما قضي الأمر إن الله وعدكم وعد الحق ووعدتكم فأخلفتكم وما كان لي عليكم من سلطان إلا أن دعوتكم فاستجبتم لي فلا تلوموني ولوموا أنفسكم ما أنا بمصرخكم وما أنتم بمصرخي إني كفرت بما أشركتمون من قبل إن الظالمين لهم عذاب أليم

translation: And admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally by permission of their Lord; their [entire] greeting therein will be "Peace."
interpretation: This verse promises eternal bliss in Paradise for those who believe in God and do good deeds. The gardens with flowing rivers symbolize the tranquility and abundance of the afterlife, where the believers will dwell forever by the will of their Lord. The greeting of "Peace" reflects the state of harmony, security, and contentment that the inhabitants of Paradise will experience.
orig: وأدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها بإذن ربهم تحيتهم فيها سلام

translation: Have you not considered how Allah presents an example? [He presents] a good word like a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed and its branches [high] in the sky.
interpretation: This verse presents a metaphor for the power and virtue of a good word or righteous deed. Just as a good tree has a strong foundation and flourishes, a good word or righteous action has lasting impact and influence that extends heavenward. This emphasizes the importance of speaking and acting with virtue, as these deeds can have far-reaching and enduring effects.
orig: ألم تر كيف ضرب الله مثلا كلمة طيبة كشجرة طيبة أصلها ثابت وفرعها في السماء

translation: It produces its fruit all the time, by permission of its Lord. And Allah presents examples for the people that they might remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuous provision and sustenance that Allah grants to His creation. Just as a fruitful tree bears fruit regularly, Allah's blessings and favors are continuously bestowed upon people. The verse also highlights that these examples are presented by Allah to remind and encourage people to reflect on His signs and be grateful.
orig: تؤتي أكلها كل حين بإذن ربها ويضرب الله الأمثال للناس لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And the example of a bad word is like a bad tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, not having any stability.
interpretation: This verse draws a comparison between a bad word or statement and a bad tree. Just as a bad tree that is uprooted from the ground has no stability or foundation, a bad word or statement is also devoid of any substance or permanence. It is easily dismissed and has no lasting impact, like a tree that has been removed from the earth.
orig: ومثل كلمة خبيثة كشجرة خبيثة اجتثت من فوق الأرض ما لها من قرار

translation: Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in worldly life and in the Hereafter. And Allah sends astray the wrongdoers. And Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah strengthens and supports the faith of those who truly believe in Him, both in this life and in the Hereafter. In contrast, Allah allows the wrongdoers to go astray, as He has absolute power and sovereignty to do as He pleases. The firm word refers to the unwavering belief and commitment to Allah, which He sustains in the hearts of the faithful.
orig: يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ويضل الله الظالمين ويفعل الله ما يشاء

translation: Have you not seen those who have exchanged the favor of Allah [for disbelief] and settled their people in the Abode of Ruin?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that calls on the reader to reflect on the actions of those who have rejected the blessings of Allah and instead embraced disbelief. The "Abode of Ruin" refers to the ultimate destination of those who have turned away from the path of righteousness, which is the punishment and destruction in the Hereafter.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمت الله كفرا وأحلوا قومهم دار البوار

translation: They will enter Hell. And wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse conveys that those who have disbelieved and rejected the truth will be condemned to the eternal punishment of Hell, which is a terrible and unwelcoming abode.
orig: جهنم يصلونها وبئس القرار

translation: And they have attributed to Allah partners to mislead [people] from His way. Say, "Enjoy [your life] for indeed, your destination is the Fire."
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of associating partners with Allah, which leads people astray from the true path. The interpretation is that those who worship false gods or idols will ultimately face the punishment of the Hellfire, and they should enjoy their worldly life while it lasts, as their ultimate destination is the Fire.
orig: وجعلوا لله أندادا ليضلوا عن سبيله قل تمتعوا فإن مصيركم إلى النار

translation: Say to My servants who have believed to establish prayer and spend [in My way] from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, before a Day comes in which there is no exchange [i.e., ransom] and no [personal] friendships.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to maintain their faith by performing their obligatory prayers and spending charitably from the provisions that God has granted them, both privately and publicly. This is to be done before the Day of Judgment arrives, when no amount of wealth or personal connections will be of any use, and the only thing that will matter is one's righteous deeds.
orig: قل لعبادي الذين آمنوا يقيموا الصلاة وينفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا بيع فيه ولا خلال

translation: It is Allah who has created the heavens and the earth and sent down rain from the sky and produced thereby some fruits as provision for you and subjected for you the ships to sail through the sea by His command and has subjected for you the rivers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah alone who has the power to create the universe, provide sustenance, and subject natural phenomena to serve humanity. It is a call to recognize and be grateful to Allah for His bountiful provisions and the natural resources He has made available for our benefit.
orig: الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرج به من الثمرات رزقا لكم وسخر لكم الفلك لتجري في البحر بأمره وسخر لكم الأنهار

translation: And He has subjected to you the sun and the moon, [both] diligently pursuing their courses, and He has subjected to you the night and the day.
interpretation: This verse highlights how Allah has made the celestial bodies and the cycle of day and night subservient to humanity. The sun and moon move in their ordained paths, and the alternation of night and day provide for the needs of humans. This is a sign of Allah's power and His blessings upon us, which we should be grateful for and use to worship Him.
orig: وسخر لكم الشمس والقمر دائبين وسخر لكم الليل والنهار

translation: And He has given you of all that you asked of Him. And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is [generally] most unjust and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's abundance in providing for His creation and the human tendency to be ungrateful and unjust. The interpretation is that we should be thankful for God's countless blessings, as we can never fully enumerate them. However, the human condition is often characterized by ingratitude and wrongdoing, which we must strive to overcome.
orig: وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه وإن تعدوا نعمت الله لا تحصوها إن الإنسان لظلوم كفار

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this city [Makkah] secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols'
interpretation: This verse highlights Abraham's prayer to Allah to make the city of Makkah a safe and secure place, and to protect him and his descendants from the worship of false idols. It reflects Abraham's devotion to the oneness of God and his desire to establish a place of pure monotheistic worship.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب اجعل هذا البلد آمنا واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام

translation: My Lord, indeed they have led astray many among the people. So whoever follows me - then he is of me, and whoever disobeys me - indeed, You are [yet], Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse expresses the Prophet's plea to God to guide those who have been led astray by false beliefs and practices. The interpretation is that those who follow the Prophet's guidance will be considered part of his community, while those who disobey him will still be forgiven by God, who is Merciful.
orig: رب إنهن أضللن كثيرا من الناس فمن تبعني فإنه مني ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم

translation: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they might be grateful.
interpretation: This verse expresses the supplication of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) for his descendants, whom he had settled in the uncultivated valley of Makkah, near the sacred House of Allah (the Ka'bah). He prays that they may establish regular prayer, and that the hearts of people may be inclined towards them, and that they may be provided sustenance from the fruits, so that they may be grateful to Allah.
orig: ربنا إني أسكنت من ذريتي بواد غير ذي زرع عند بيتك المحرم ربنا ليقيموا الصلاة فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم وارزقهم من الثمرات لعلهم يشكرون

translation: Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare, and nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and all-encompassing knowledge. It conveys that Allah, the Lord, is fully aware of everything - both what we hide and what we openly express. Nothing is hidden from Allah, whether on earth or in the heavens. This underscores the importance of being mindful of our actions and thoughts, as Allah is all-knowing and nothing can be concealed from Him.
orig: ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي وما نعلن وما يخفى على الله من شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء

translation: Praise be to Allah, who has granted me in my old age Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.
interpretation: This verse expresses the gratitude of the Prophet Abraham towards Allah for granting him children in his old age, namely Ishmael and Isaac. It highlights that Allah is the All-Hearing who responds to the prayers and supplications of His servants, even in the most difficult of circumstances.
orig: الحمد لله الذي وهب لي على الكبر إسماعيل وإسحاق إن ربي لسميع الدعاء

translation: My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.
interpretation: This verse expresses the desire of the Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to be steadfast in performing the obligatory prayers, and to have his descendants also follow in his footsteps. It also includes a supplication for Allah to accept his prayers and supplications.
orig: رب اجعلني مقيم الصلاة ومن ذريتي ربنا وتقبل دعاء

translation: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day of Account
interpretation: This verse expresses a supplication to Allah, seeking forgiveness not only for oneself but also for one's parents and the believers in general. The "Day of Account" refers to the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions. The verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah, not only for one's own sins but also for the sins of one's loved ones and the community of believers. It reflects a deep sense of humility, compassion, and concern for the wellbeing of others in the afterlife.
orig: ربنا اغفر لي ولوالدي وللمؤمنين يوم يقوم الحساب

translation: And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them [in this life] until a Day when eyes will stare [in horror].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of the actions of the wrongdoers, even if He does not immediately punish them. He delays their punishment until the Day of Judgment, when all will be held accountable and the true nature of their deeds will be revealed. This serves as a warning to the wrongdoers that they cannot escape Allah's judgment, and that they will ultimately face the consequences of their actions.
orig: ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار

translation: Hastening, with heads uplifted, their eyes not returning towards them, and their hearts vacant.
interpretation: This verse depicts the state of those who are hastening towards the Judgment Day, with their heads held high in pride and arrogance. Their eyes are fixed forward, unwilling to look back, and their hearts are empty, devoid of faith and humility before the Almighty.
orig: مهطعين مقنعي رءوسهم لا يرتد إليهم طرفهم وأفئدتهم هواء

translation: And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come to them and those who had wronged will say, 'Our Lord, delay us for a little time, and we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.' [But it will be said], 'Had you not sworn before [that] there would be no cessation for you?'
interpretation: This verse warns people about the impending Day of Judgment, when those who have wronged will plead for more time to respond to the call of faith and follow the messengers. However, they will be reminded that they had previously sworn that there would be no end to their disbelief and rejection of the truth. This emphasizes the importance of repentance and submission to God before it is too late.
orig: وأنذر الناس يوم يأتيهم العذاب فيقول الذين ظلموا ربنا أخرنا إلى أجل قريب نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل أولم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال

translation: And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We presented for you [many] examples.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to reflect on the fate of those who wronged themselves by rejecting the truth. By dwelling in the homes of those who were destroyed, the believers are reminded of God's justice and the consequences of disbelief. The examples provided serve as a lesson and a warning to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: وسكنتم في مساكن الذين ظلموا أنفسهم وتبين لكم كيف فعلنا بهم وضربنا لكم الأمثال

translation: And they had plotted their plot, but with Allah is [recorded] their plot, even if their plot had been [sufficient] to do away with the mountains.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that no matter how elaborate or powerful a plot or scheme against the believers may be, it is ultimately under the control and knowledge of Allah. Even the mightiest of plots cannot prevail against Allah's will and power.
orig: وقد مكروا مكرهم وعند الله مكرهم وإن كان مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال

translation: So do not think that Allah will fail in His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might - the Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah will never fail to fulfill His promises to His messengers. He is All-Powerful and Mighty, and has the ability to exact retribution against those who reject His message and disobey His commands.
orig: فلا تحسبن الله مخلف وعده رسله إن الله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: The Day when the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well], and they [all] will come forth to Allah, the One, the Prevailing
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Resurrection when the current world will be transformed, and all of creation will be presented before the Almighty God, the One who has complete power and dominance over all things.
orig: يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسماوات وبرزوا لله الواحد القهار

translation: And you will see the criminals that Day tied in shackles.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment, when they will be bound in chains and fetters as a punishment for their misdeeds. The image of the criminals being "tied in shackles" conveys a sense of humiliation, helplessness, and the inescapable consequences of their sinful actions.
orig: وترى المجرمين يومئذ مقرنين في الأصفاد

translation: Their garments will be of pitch, and fire will cover their faces.
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment of the disbelievers in the Hereafter. Their clothing will be made of tar, which is a thick, sticky substance that will burn their skin. The fire will also engulf their faces, causing them immense suffering and anguish for their rejection of faith and their evil deeds in the worldly life.
orig: سرابيلهم من قطران وتغشى وجوههم النار

translation: That Allah may recompense each soul for what it has earned. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah will justly reward or punish each person based on their deeds and actions. It highlights Allah's omniscience and ability to swiftly hold people accountable for their conduct in this life.
orig: ليجزي الله كل نفس ما كسبت إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: This is a message for the people, so that they may be warned by it and know that He is but one God, and that those of understanding may remember.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the Qur'an is a message for all of humanity, to warn them and inform them that there is only one true God. It is meant to encourage those with wisdom and discernment to reflect on and remember this fundamental truth.
orig: هذا بلاغ للناس ولينذروا به وليعلموا أنما هو إله واحد وليذكر أولو الألباب

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: This verse introduces the Qur'an as a clear and self-evident scripture, with the letters "Alif, Lam, Ra" serving as a mysterious opening that draws the reader's attention to the profound and miraculous nature of the Qur'anic revelation.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب وقرآن مبين

translation: Perhaps those who disbelieve wish that they had been Muslims.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who disbelieve may wish they had accepted Islam, as it is the true and righteous path. It implies that the disbelievers may come to regret their rejection of faith and desire to have been among the believers.
orig: ربما يود الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين

translation: Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves and be diverted by hope, for they are going to know.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to leave the disbelievers alone and allow them to continue in their heedless ways, indulging in worldly pleasures and being deluded by false hopes. However, they will ultimately face the consequences of their actions and come to realize the error of their ways.
orig: ذرهم يأكلوا ويتمتعوا ويلههم الأمل فسوف يعلمون

translation: And We have not destroyed any town but it had a decree known.
interpretation: This verse suggests that every community or society has a predetermined fate or destiny, which is known to God. The destruction or demise of a town or civilization is not arbitrary, but rather part of a larger divine plan that is known to God. This implies that the rise and fall of civilizations is not merely a matter of chance or human agency, but is ultimately under the control and knowledge of the Almighty.
orig: وما أهلكنا من قرية إلا ولها كتاب معلوم

translation: No community can hasten or delay its term.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that every community or people have a fixed term or appointed time that is decreed by Allah, and they cannot hasten or delay that term. It is a reminder that the timing of events is in the hands of Allah, and that humans do not have control over the timing of their own fate or the fate of their communities.
orig: ما تسبق من أمة أجلها وما يستأخرون

translation: And they say, "O you upon whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad."
interpretation: This verse refers to the skepticism and rejection that the Prophet Muhammad faced from his people when he began to preach the message of Islam. The unbelievers dismissed him as a madman, unable to comprehend the divine revelation he was receiving. This reflects the common human tendency to reject and ridicule that which challenges our preconceptions and comfort zones.
orig: وقالوا يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر إنك لمجنون

translation: If you do not bring us the angels, [we will not believe]
interpretation: This verse expresses the disbelievers' demand for tangible proof of the Messenger's truthfulness, in the form of angels appearing before them. It highlights their unwillingness to accept the message of Islam based on faith and the evidence presented in the Quran. The interpretation is that such demands for physical miracles often stem from a lack of sincerity and an unwillingness to submit to the truth.
orig: لو ما تأتينا بالملائكة إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: And the angels do not descend except with the truth, and they [i.e., the disbelievers] would not then be granted respite.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the angels only descend with the truth from Allah, and they do not come to give the disbelievers more time or respite. It suggests that the angels' descent is a sign of the coming of the Hour and the judgment, not a delay or extension of time for the disbelievers to repent.
orig: ما ننزل الملائكة إلا بالحق وما كانوا إذا منظرين

translation: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur'an and indeed, We will be its guardian.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an was revealed by Allah, and that He will protect and preserve it from any corruption or alteration. This is a reassurance to believers that the Qur'an is a divine scripture that will remain intact and unchanged, serving as a guide and source of guidance for all time.
orig: إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون

translation: And We have certainly sent [messengers] before you, [O Muhammad], among the people of old.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah has sent prophets and messengers to guide humanity throughout history, not just with the advent of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes the continuity of divine guidance and the universality of the message of Islam.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك في شيع الأولين

translation: And there does not come to them any messenger except that they ridicule him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the people often mock and ridicule the messengers and prophets sent to guide them, instead of accepting their message with humility and sincerity. It suggests that rejecting the divine guidance and mocking the messengers is a common human tendency that has persisted throughout history.
orig: وما يأتيهم من رسول إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Thus We insert it into the hearts of the criminals
interpretation: This verse suggests that God plants or instills the message of the Qur'an into the hearts of those who commit sins and transgressions, as a means of guiding them towards repentance and the right path. The implication is that even the most hardened of sinners are not beyond the reach of God's guidance, and that the divine message has the power to penetrate the most stubborn of hearts.
orig: كذلك نسلكه في قلوب المجرمين

translation: They do not believe in it, and the precedent of the former peoples has already passed.
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people do not believe in the message of the Qur'an, despite the fact that previous generations have already witnessed the consequences of rejecting divine guidance. The interpretation implies that those who refuse to believe in the Qur'an are following the same path as those who came before them, and that they will face similar consequences for their disbelief.
orig: لا يؤمنون به وقد خلت سنة الأولين

translation: And if We had willed, We could have sent down to them from the sky a sign, and their necks would have remained humbled before it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if Allah had willed, He could have sent down a clear sign from the heavens that would have compelled the disbelievers to submit and humble themselves before it. However, Allah chooses to test people's faith through less direct means, allowing them the freedom to choose belief or disbelief.
orig: ولو فتحنا عليهم بابا من السماء فظلوا فيه يعرجون

translation: They would have said, "Our eyes have become dazzled; rather, we are a people bewitched."
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people may try to dismiss or deny the truth of the Qur'an by claiming that they are "bewitched" or under a spell, rather than acknowledging the clarity and power of the divine message. The interpretation is that those who refuse to accept the truth often resort to making excuses or attributing their rejection to external factors, rather than taking responsibility for their own choices and beliefs.
orig: لقالوا إنما سكرت أبصارنا بل نحن قوم مسحورون

translation: And We have placed [fixed stars] in the heaven and have beautified it for the observers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the grandeur and beauty of the heavens, which God has adorned with celestial bodies for the benefit and enjoyment of those who observe them. It suggests that the universe is a testament to God's power, wisdom, and artistry, and that contemplating the heavens can lead to a deeper appreciation of the divine creation.
orig: ولقد جعلنا في السماء بروجا وزيناها للناظرين

translation: And We have guarded it from every accursed Satan
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Qur'an is protected from any corruption or distortion by Satan. It is a divine revelation that is safeguarded and preserved, ensuring its purity and authenticity for all generations.
orig: وحفظناها من كل شيطان رجيم

translation: Except [for] one who steals a hearing and is pursued by a clear burning flame.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who try to eavesdrop on divine secrets or the unseen, and are then pursued by a clear and evident punishment, such as a blazing fire.
orig: إلا من استرق السمع فأتبعه شهاب مبين

translation: And the earth - We have spread it out and cast therein firmly set mountains and caused to grow therein [something] of every beautiful kind
interpretation: This verse highlights God's creative power in fashioning the earth and all that is within it. The earth is described as being "spread out", indicating its vastness and expanse. The placement of "firmly set mountains" suggests the stability and order within the natural world. Furthermore, the verse emphasizes the diversity of life on earth, with God causing "something of every beautiful kind" to grow, reflecting the richness and harmony of the created order. This verse invites the reader to appreciate the wonders of God's creation and to recognize the wisdom and purpose behind it.
orig: والأرض مددناها وألقينا فيها رواسي وأنبتنا فيها من كل شيء موزون

translation: And We have made for you therein [means of] livelihood and [for] those for whom you are not providers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has provided various means of sustenance and livelihood not only for those who are able to provide for themselves, but also for those who are dependent on others, such as the poor, the needy, and the vulnerable. It highlights Allah's mercy and care for all of His creation, regardless of their economic status or ability to be self-sufficient.
orig: وجعلنا لكم فيها معايش ومن لستم له برازقين

translation: And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories, and We do not send it down except in a known measure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God is the ultimate source and sustainer of all things. All that exists is under His control and in His possession. He alone determines the measure and timing of what is revealed or provided, according to His perfect wisdom and plan.
orig: وإن من شيء إلا عندنا خزائنه وما ننزله إلا بقدر معلوم

translation: And We have sent the winds as fertilizers, and have sent down water from the sky, and have given you to drink of it. And you are not the ones to store it [in your control].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who controls the natural processes that sustain life, such as the winds that fertilize the clouds and the rain that provides water. Humans are not the ones who store or control this water, but rather it is a gift from Allah that we are entrusted to use responsibly.
orig: وأرسلنا الرياح لواقح فأنزلنا من السماء ماء فأسقيناكموه وما أنتم له بخازنين

translation: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritor.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the sole Creator and Sustainer of life and death. He alone has the power to give life and take it away. Furthermore, Allah is the ultimate Inheritor, as all things in the universe ultimately belong to Him and will return to Him.
orig: وإنا لنحن نحيي ونميت ونحن الوارثون

translation: And We have already known the [previous] generations before you, and We have already known the [latter] generations [to come].
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has full knowledge of all generations, past and future. It suggests that Allah is all-knowing and that nothing is hidden from Him. This knowledge of the past and future generations is a testament to Allah's omniscience and His ability to see beyond the confines of time.
orig: ولقد علمنا المستقدمين منكم ولقد علمنا المستأخرين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He will gather them. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Lord and Creator, has absolute control over the resurrection and gathering of all people on the Day of Judgment. He is All-Wise in His decisions and All-Knowing of the affairs of His creation.
orig: وإن ربك هو يحشرهم إنه حكيم عليم

translation: And We have certainly created man from [extracted] clay from an altered black mud.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has created man from the elements of the earth - clay and altered black mud. It highlights the humble origins of man, reminding us of our dependence on Allah and the need to be grateful for our creation.
orig: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: And the jinn, We created him before from scorching fire.
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of the jinn, a sentient being made of fire, before the creation of humans. It suggests that the jinn were created earlier and have a distinct nature and purpose in the divine plan.
orig: والجان خلقناه من قبل من نار السموم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay from an altered black mud."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God is the creator of human beings, who were created from clay and altered black mud. It highlights God's power and sovereignty in bringing forth life, and establishes that humans are created by God and not by any other entity.
orig: وإذ قال ربك للملائكة إني خالق بشرا من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: And when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul, then fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the creation of man, and the divine breath that was given to him. It emphasizes the sacred nature of human life, which was directly imbued with a part of God"s own spirit. This highlights the special status of humanity and the obligation to worship and submit to the Creator.
orig: فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين

translation: So the angels prostrated - all of them entirely.
interpretation: This verse indicates the absolute obedience and submission of the angels to the command of God. When God ordered the angels to prostrate before Adam, they all complied without any hesitation or reservation, demonstrating their complete devotion and loyalty to the divine will.
orig: فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون

translation: Except Iblis (Satan), he refused to be among the prostrators.
interpretation: This verse highlights the defiance and arrogance of Iblis (Satan) who refused to prostrate before Adam when commanded by Allah. It signifies that even in the face of a divine order, Iblis chose to disobey due to his pride and sense of superiority, setting him apart from the obedient angels who submitted to Allah's will.
orig: إلا إبليس أبى أن يكون مع الساجدين

translation: He said, "O Iblis, what prevents you from being with those who prostrate?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the incident when Allah asked Iblis (Satan) why he did not prostrate before Adam as the other angels did. The interpretation is that Allah was questioning Iblis about his refusal to obey the divine command, which stemmed from his arrogance and pride.
orig: قال يا إبليس ما لك ألا تكون مع الساجدين

translation: He (Iblis) said, "I am not one to prostrate myself to a human whom You have created from dry clay from altered black mud."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disobedience of Iblis (Satan) when he refused to prostrate before Adam, whom Allah had created. Iblis viewed himself as superior to a human being made from clay, and this led to his downfall and expulsion from the heavenly realm. The verse emphasizes the importance of humility, obedience, and submission to Allah's commands, even when they may challenge one's own ego or perceived superiority.
orig: قال لم أكن لأسجد لبشر خلقته من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: He (Allah) said: "Then get out of it, for verily, you are Rajim (cursed or rejected)."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Adam and Iblis (Satan). When Iblis refused to prostrate to Adam, Allah commanded him to leave the heavenly abode, as he had become cursed or rejected due to his disobedience and pride.
orig: قال فاخرج منها فإنك رجيم

translation: And upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense.
interpretation: This verse conveys a stern warning to those who reject the message of Islam and persistently oppose it. The curse mentioned here refers to the divine punishment and displeasure that will befall such individuals until the Day of Judgment, when they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: وإن عليك اللعنة إلى يوم الدين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea from a person to be given more time before the Day of Resurrection, when all people will be held accountable for their deeds. The interpretation suggests a desire for a delay in facing the consequences of one's actions, possibly out of fear or a wish for more time to prepare.
orig: قال رب فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: He said, 'So indeed, you are of those reprieved'
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Adam and Iblis (Satan) in the Qur'an. When Iblis refused to prostrate before Adam, Allah gave him a respite until the Day of Judgment. The interpretation of this verse is that Iblis was granted a delay in his punishment, allowing him to continue his attempts to mislead humanity until the appointed time.
orig: قال فإنك من المنظرين

translation: To the Day of the Appointed Time
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions. It emphasizes the certainty and predetermined nature of this momentous event, which will occur at a time known only to God.
orig: إلى يوم الوقت المعلوم

translation: He (Satan) said, "My Lord, because You have put me in error, I will surely make [disobedience] attractive to them on earth, and I will mislead them all."
interpretation: This verse highlights Satan's arrogance and defiance towards God. Even after being misguided, Satan refuses to take responsibility for his actions and instead blames God for his own shortcomings. The verse underscores Satan's determination to lead all of humanity astray, making sinful acts appear appealing and enticing. It serves as a warning against the deceptive nature of Satan and the importance of seeking guidance from God to avoid being misled.
orig: قال رب بما أغويتني لأزينن لهم في الأرض ولأغوينهم أجمعين

translation: Except Your [devoted] servants among them.
interpretation: This verse indicates that among the disbelievers, there are some who are sincere and devoted servants of Allah, and they will be exempted from the punishment that the others will face.
orig: إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين

translation: He said, "This is a straight path upon me."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following a righteous and unwavering path that leads to Allah. It suggests that the path of truth and guidance is clear and direct, and that one should strive to remain steadfast upon it.
orig: قال هذا صراط علي مستقيم

translation: Indeed, [O Messenger], My [faithful] servants - there is no authority for you over them, except those who follow you of the deviators.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad has no authority over Allah's faithful servants, except for those who have strayed from the path of righteousness and chosen to follow the Prophet. It highlights that true believers are under the protection and guidance of Allah, not subject to the will of any human being.
orig: إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان إلا من اتبعك من الغاوين

translation: And indeed, Hell is their appointment, all of them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Hell is the ultimate destination for all those who reject faith and engage in wrongdoing. It serves as a warning to humanity about the consequences of turning away from the guidance of Allah and living a life of sin and disbelief.
orig: وإن جهنم لموعدهم أجمعين

translation: It has seven gates, for every gate is a [specific] portion [assigned].
interpretation: This verse refers to the seven gates of Hell, each with a specific portion or group of people assigned to it based on their deeds and beliefs. The implication is that the punishment in Hell is tailored to the individual's transgressions, and there is no one-size-fits-all approach to the afterlife.
orig: لها سبعة أبواب لكل باب منهم جزء مقسوم

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who fear Allah and strive to live righteously will be rewarded with the blissful abode of Paradise, where they will enjoy eternal gardens and flowing springs.
orig: إن المتقين في جنات وعيون

translation: Enter it in peace, [O believers]
interpretation: This verse conveys a message of peace and security for the believers. It invites them to enter the abode of paradise with a sense of tranquility and safety, free from any fear or harm.
orig: ادخلوها بسلام آمنين

translation: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of [ill] will, [so they will be] brothers, on thrones facing each other.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the purification of the hearts of the believers in the Hereafter, where any feelings of malice or resentment towards one another will be removed, and they will be united as brothers, sitting facing each other in a state of harmony and mutual love.
orig: ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل إخوانا على سرر متقابلين

translation: There shall touch them no fatigue, nor shall they [ever] be removed from it.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the believers in the Hereafter will be free from any physical or mental exhaustion, and they will remain in Paradise eternally without ever being expelled from it.
orig: لا يمسهم فيها نصب وما هم منها بمخرجين

translation: Inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's attributes of forgiveness and mercy. It encourages the believers to seek God's pardon and compassion, as He is the One who readily forgives and shows kindness to His servants. The interpretation highlights that God's mercy and forgiveness are readily available to those who turn to Him in repentance and seek His grace.
orig: نبئ عبادي أني أنا الغفور الرحيم

translation: And that My punishment - it is the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and intensity of Allah's punishment for those who reject His guidance and disobey His commands. The phrase "My punishment" signifies that the punishment comes directly from Allah, and the description of it as "the painful punishment" underscores the agonizing and excruciating nature of the retribution awaiting those who persist in their wrongdoing. This serves as a stark warning to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and righteous conduct.
orig: وأن عذابي هو العذاب الأليم

translation: And inform them about the guests of Abraham.
interpretation: This verse is instructing the Prophet Muhammad to inform the people about the story of Abraham's guests. The story of Abraham's guests is mentioned in the Quran, where it is recounted how Abraham received three angelic visitors who brought him the good news of a son, despite his old age. This story serves as an example of Abraham's hospitality, faith, and the divine blessings he received.
orig: ونبئهم عن ضيف إبراهيم

translation: When they entered upon him and said, 'Peace.' [Abraham] said, 'Indeed, we are fearful [i.e., cautious] of you.'
interpretation: This verse describes the interaction between Abraham and his visitors, who were angels in human form. When the angels greeted Abraham with 'Peace,' he responded by saying that he was cautious of them, not knowing their true nature. This highlights Abraham's wisdom and discernment, as he was able to sense that his visitors were not ordinary people.
orig: إذ دخلوا عليه فقالوا سلاما قال إنا منكم وجلون

translation: They said, "Do not be afraid, we bring you good tidings of a learned boy."
interpretation: This verse conveys a message of reassurance and good news. The angels who visited the Prophet Abraham informed him that he would be blessed with a son, despite his old age. The emphasis on the child being "learned" suggests that he would be endowed with knowledge, wisdom, and understanding - a sign of divine favor and a source of pride for his parents.
orig: قالوا لا توجل إنا نبشرك بغلام عليم

translation: He said: "Do you give me good tidings in spite of [my] old age?" So of what [strange] thing do you inform me?
interpretation: This verse is a response by Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) to the angels who had given him the good news of the birth of his son Isaac, despite his old age. The interpretation is that Abraham was surprised by this news, as he was advanced in years, and he questioned the angels about how this could be possible.
orig: قال أبشرتموني على أن مسني الكبر فبم تبشرون

translation: They said, "We give you good tidings in truth, so be not of the despairing."
interpretation: This verse is conveying a message of hope and reassurance. The people who are speaking are delivering good news to someone, likely a prophet or messenger of God. They are telling this person not to lose hope or become despondent, but rather to have faith and trust in the truth that has been revealed to them. The interpretation suggests that even in difficult times, one should maintain a positive outlook and believe in the ultimate truth and justice that God will bring about.
orig: قالوا بشرناك بالحق فلا تكن من القانطين

translation: And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except for those astray?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that one should never lose hope in the mercy and compassion of God. Only those who have strayed from the right path would despair of God's forgiveness and grace. It encourages believers to maintain faith in the divine mercy, even in times of difficulty or hardship.
orig: قال ومن يقنط من رحمة ربه إلا الضالون

translation: He said, 'What is your mission, O messengers?'
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between the Prophet Abraham and the angels who visited him. The question 'What is your mission, O messengers?' reflects Abraham's curiosity about the purpose of their visit, as he recognized them as divine emissaries. The interpretation is that the verse highlights the importance of understanding the mission and purpose of those who claim to be messengers of God, and the need to engage in respectful dialogue to discern their true intentions.
orig: قال فما خطبكم أيها المرسلون

translation: They said, 'Indeed, we have been sent to a criminal people'
interpretation: This verse conveys the message that the messengers of God were sent to people who had strayed from the path of righteousness and committed grave sins. It suggests that the messengers faced a challenging task in guiding these people back to the right way, as they were deeply entrenched in their wrongdoing.
orig: قالوا إنا أرسلنا إلى قوم مجرمين

translation: Except the family of Lot. Indeed, We will save them all
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah will save the family of Prophet Lot from the punishment that befell the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, due to their wickedness and immorality. It emphasizes Allah's mercy and justice, as He spares the believers from the consequences of the wrongdoings of their community.
orig: إلا آل لوط إنا لمنجوهم أجمعين

translation: Except his wife; We destined that she should be of those who remain behind.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Lut (Lot), where his wife was destined to be among those who were destroyed along with the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, due to her disbelief and rejection of the message of her husband.
orig: إلا امرأته قدرنا إنها لمن الغابرين

translation: And when the messengers came to the family of Lot
interpretation: This verse refers to the arrival of the angels sent by God to the family of the prophet Lot, in order to warn them of the impending destruction of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah due to their wicked and immoral practices. The arrival of the messengers signifies God's justice and the accountability that awaits those who persist in sin and reject the divine guidance.
orig: فلما جاء آل لوط المرسلون

translation: He said: 'Indeed, you are a people unknown [to me].'
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being addressed were unfamiliar or strangers to the speaker, indicating a lack of prior relationship or knowledge about them. The interpretation implies that the speaker feels distant or disconnected from the group they are addressing, perhaps due to differences in background, beliefs, or experiences.
orig: قال إنكم قوم منكرون

translation: They said, "Rather, we have come to you with that [i.e., truth] about which they were in doubt."
interpretation: The verse suggests that the disbelievers came to the Prophet Muhammad with the truth that they had previously been skeptical about. It implies that they acknowledged the veracity of the message he brought, even if they had previously doubted it.
orig: قالوا بل جئناك بما كانوا فيه يمترون

translation: And We have brought you the truth, and indeed, We are truthful.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an is the revealed truth from God, and that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is truly a messenger of God who conveys this truth to humanity. It emphasizes the authenticity and veracity of the Qur'anic message.
orig: وأتيناك بالحق وإنا لصادقون

translation: So set out with your family during a portion of the night and follow behind them and let not anyone among you look back and proceed [directly] to where you are commanded.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Moses and his followers to leave secretly during the night, without looking back, and to go where they are commanded. The interpretation is that one should follow the guidance of God and the Prophet without hesitation or doubt, and not be distracted by worldly concerns or the opinions of others.
orig: فأسر بأهلك بقطع من الليل واتبع أدبارهم ولا يلتفت منكم أحد وامضوا حيث تؤمرون

translation: And We conveyed to him [i.e., Abraham] that matter [i.e., the destruction of the evil people] that the root [i.e., the last remnant] of those [people] would be cut off by morning.
interpretation: This verse conveys the divine decree that the evil and corrupt people would be destroyed completely, leaving no trace of them by the morning. It emphasizes the certainty and finality of the punishment that would befall them, as a consequence of their persistent wrongdoing and rejection of the truth.
orig: وقضينا إليه ذلك الأمر أن دابر هؤلاء مقطوع مصبحين

translation: And the people of the city came rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people of the city were filled with joy and excitement, perhaps upon the arrival of a significant event or figure. It conveys a sense of communal celebration and shared happiness within the community.
orig: وجاء أهل المدينة يستبشرون

translation: He said, "Indeed these are my guests, so do not disgrace me."
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) in the Qur'an. It expresses Lot's plea to his people not to dishonor him by mistreating his guests, who were actually angels sent by God in human form. The verse emphasizes the importance of hospitality and protecting one's guests, even in the face of societal pressure or temptation.
orig: قال إن هؤلاء ضيفي فلا تفضحون

translation: And fear Allah and do not be disgraced
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be mindful of Allah and to avoid any actions or behaviors that would bring shame or disgrace upon them. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining one's dignity and reputation by upholding the teachings of Islam and seeking Allah's pleasure.
orig: واتقوا الله ولا تخزون

translation: They said, 'Did we not forbid you [to associate] with everyone?'
interpretation: This verse refers to a dialogue between the disbelievers and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The disbelievers are questioning why the Prophet associated with all people, including the poor and weak, instead of only associating with the elite and powerful. The interpretation is that true faith and guidance should be open to all people, not just a select few.
orig: قالوا أولم ننهك عن العالمين

translation: He said, "These are my daughters, if you would be doers [of righteousness]."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) and his people. It is an appeal by Lot to his people to cease their immoral practices and instead accept the believing women (his daughters) as righteous companions. The interpretation is that one should seek to surround oneself with righteous people and avoid engaging in sinful activities, as this is the path to salvation.
orig: قال هؤلاء بناتي إن كنتم فاعلين

translation: By your life, they were certainly in their intoxication, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the people being referred to were in a state of confusion and disarray, unable to see the truth or find the right path. It suggests that they were intoxicated, either literally or metaphorically, and were wandering aimlessly, unable to discern reality from illusion.
orig: لعمرك إنهم لفي سكرتهم يعمهون

translation: So the shriek seized them as they were watching the sunrise.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the people who rejected the message of the Prophets and persisted in their disbelief. The "shriek" refers to a loud, terrifying sound that destroyed them, while they were going about their daily lives, unaware of the impending punishment. This serves as a warning that those who reject faith and guidance will face a severe consequence.
orig: فأخذتهم الصيحة مشرقين

translation: And We made its upper part its lower part, and We rained upon them stones of hard clay.
interpretation: This verse describes the destruction of a settlement that was turned upside down as a punishment from God. The interpretation is that God has the power to completely overturn and destroy even the most established of societies as a consequence for their wrongdoing.
orig: فجعلنا عاليها سافلها وأمطرنا عليهم حجارة من سجيل

translation: Indeed in that are signs for those who discern.
interpretation: This verse suggests that there are clear signs and lessons in the creation and workings of the universe that can be perceived and understood by those who observe and contemplate them with insight and wisdom.
orig: إن في ذلك لآيات للمتوسمين

translation: And indeed, it (the Qur'an) is a straight path
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a clear and unwavering guide, leading the believers towards the right path. It is a constant and steadfast source of direction, providing a clear and consistent way of life for those who follow it.
orig: وإنها لبسبيل مقيم

translation: Indeed in that is a sign for the believers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that in the natural phenomena and the signs of God's creation, there are clear indications and lessons for those who have faith in God. The believers should reflect on these signs to strengthen their belief and gain a deeper understanding of the divine wisdom behind the universe.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية للمؤمنين

translation: And indeed, the companions of the thicket were [also] wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse refers to a group of people known as the "companions of the thicket" who were guilty of wrongdoing. The interpretation suggests that even those who lived in a lush, forested area were not immune from committing transgressions and being considered unjust or oppressive.
orig: وإن كان أصحاب الأيكة لظالمين

translation: And We took retribution from them, and indeed, they are both [i.e., those destroyed and those saved] a clear sign.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's justice and power in punishing the wrongdoers while preserving the righteous. The destruction of the wicked serves as a clear lesson and warning to all, demonstrating the consequences of disobedience and the rewards of faith and righteous conduct.
orig: فانتقمنا منهم وإنهما لبإمام مبين

translation: And the companions of the Rock certainly denied the messengers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Madyan (or Midian), who rejected the message of the prophet Shu'aib. They were known as the 'companions of the Rock' because they lived among the rocky terrain of that region. The verse emphasizes that they denied and disbelieved the messengers sent to guide them, despite the clear signs and warnings they received.
orig: ولقد كذب أصحاب الحجر المرسلين

translation: And We had certainly given them Our signs, but they were turning away from them.
interpretation: This verse conveys that Allah had provided clear signs and guidance to the people, but they chose to turn away from it and reject it. It suggests that people sometimes ignore or disregard the divine messages and teachings, despite having been presented with them.
orig: وآتيناهم آياتنا فكانوا عنها معرضين

translation: And they used to carve from the mountains, houses [in which they felt] secure.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ingenuity and resourcefulness of the people, who were able to construct secure dwellings by carving them out of the mountains. It suggests that they were able to find safety and protection in these carefully crafted homes, which were likely well-fortified and shielded from external threats.
orig: وكانوا ينحتون من الجبال بيوتا آمنين

translation: Then the shriek seized them at sunrise
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that befell the people of Prophet Shu'ayb, who rejected his call to worship God alone and abandoned their corrupt practices. The "shriek" or a loud, terrifying sound from the sky seized them at the break of dawn, signifying the swiftness and severity of God's retribution against those who persistently defy His guidance and commands.
orig: فأخذتهم الصيحة مصبحين

translation: And what they used to earn availed them not.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the wealth and possessions that people accumulate in this world will not be of any use to them in the Hereafter. It emphasizes that the true value lies in one's righteous deeds and faith, not in material gains.
orig: فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and that between them in play.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the creation of the universe was not in vain or without purpose, but rather it was created with truth and justice. The mention of "the Hour" (i.e. the Day of Resurrection) suggests that there is a higher purpose and an ultimate reckoning for all that has been created. The command to "overlook (their misdeeds) with gracious forgiveness" implies that even though the creation has a serious purpose, believers should respond with patience and compassion towards others.
orig: وما خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وإن الساعة لآتية فاصفح الصفح الجميل

translation: Indeed, your Lord - He is the Creator, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the attributes of Allah as the Creator, who possesses infinite knowledge and wisdom. It affirms that Allah is the sole Creator of all things, and that He has complete and perfect knowledge of all that He has created. This serves to remind us of Allah's power, authority, and sovereignty, and encourages us to submit to Him and seek His guidance.
orig: إن ربك هو الخلاق العليم

translation: And We have certainly given you, [O Muhammad], seven of the often-repeated [verses] and the great Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse refers to the seven verses of the opening chapter of the Qur'an, known as Al-Fatihah, which are considered the most important and oft-recited verses in Islamic worship. The "seven of the often-repeated" refers to these seven verses, and the "great Qur'an" refers to the entire revealed scripture. This highlights the significance and centrality of the Qur'an in the life of a Muslim, as it is the primary source of guidance and wisdom.
orig: ولقد آتيناك سبعا من المثاني والقرآن العظيم

translation: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, nor grieve over them. And lower your wing [in kindness] to the believers.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to covet the worldly possessions or status of others, nor to grieve over those who have rejected the message of Islam. Instead, he is commanded to be kind and compassionate towards the believers, and to treat them with humility and gentleness.
orig: لا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم ولا تحزن عليهم واخفض جناحك للمؤمنين

translation: And say, "Indeed, I am the clear warner."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a clear and unambiguous warner, conveying the message of Islam to humanity. It highlights his duty to warn people about the consequences of disbelief and encourage them to embrace the true faith.
orig: وقل إني أنا النذير المبين

translation: Just as We sent down upon the dividers
interpretation: This verse refers to the revelation of the Qur'an upon those who divided and disputed the truth. It suggests that Allah has sent down the Qur'an to guide those who are inclined to argue and disagree, in order to bring them back to the straight path.
orig: كما أنزلنا على المقتسمين

translation: Those who have broken the Qur'an into parts
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have divided the Qur'an into different sections or parts, either by accepting some parts and rejecting others, or by interpreting it in a fragmented manner rather than as a cohesive whole. The implication is that they have failed to appreciate the Qur'an as a complete and unified revelation from God.
orig: الذين جعلوا القرآن عضين

translation: So, by your Lord, We will surely question them all
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accountability that all people will face before God on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder that no one will be spared from being questioned about their beliefs, actions, and intentions in this life.
orig: فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين

translation: About what they used to do
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, people will be questioned about their deeds and actions in this life. It implies that we will be held accountable for our choices and behaviors, and that we should strive to do good and avoid evil in order to be successful in the Hereafter.
orig: عما كانوا يعملون

translation: So proclaim what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to convey the message of Islam without fear or hesitation, and to turn away from those who associate partners with Allah. It emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and conviction in the face of opposition and rejection from those who reject the truth.
orig: فاصدع بما تؤمر وأعرض عن المشركين

translation: Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that Allah will protect him from the mockery and ridicule of his opponents. It conveys the message that Allah will take care of those who mock the Prophet and the divine message, and that the Prophet should not worry about them, but rather focus on delivering the message of Islam.
orig: إنا كفيناك المستهزئين

translation: Those who take a deity other than Allah - they will [soon] know.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who associate partners with Allah, the One true God. It conveys that those who worship false deities or idols will eventually realize the error of their ways and face the consequences of their actions. The interpretation suggests that the punishment or realization of their mistake will come to them, as they will come to know the truth about the oneness of Allah.
orig: الذين يجعلون مع الله إلها آخر فسوف يعلمون

translation: And We certainly know that your breast is constrained by what they say
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was distressed by the disbelief and rejection of his message by his people. However, Allah reassures him that He is aware of this and will provide him with the necessary support and guidance to overcome these challenges.
orig: ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون

translation: So glorify the praises of your Lord and be of those who prostrate themselves (in worship).
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to glorify and praise God, and to be among those who humbly submit to God through acts of worship such as prostration. It emphasizes the importance of worshiping and acknowledging God's greatness and sovereignty.
orig: فسبح بحمد ربك وكن من الساجدين

translation: And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty [of death].
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to continuously worship and serve God until the time of their death. The "certainty" refers to the inevitability of death, which is the ultimate certainty that all humans will face. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong and unwavering faith in God throughout one's life, as this is the path to achieving spiritual fulfillment and eternal salvation.
orig: واعبد ربك حتى يأتيك اليقين

translation: The command of Allah has come, so do not be impatient for it. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in Allah's plan. It reminds us that we should not be hasty or impatient in our expectations, as Allah's command will come to pass in its own time. The verse also affirms Allah's transcendence and supremacy, reminding us that He is above all that people associate with Him.
orig: أتى أمر الله فلا تستعجلوه سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: The angels descend with the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, [telling them], "Warn that there is no deity except Me; so fear Me."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and authority of God, who sends down the angels and the divine revelation (the Spirit) to His servants to convey the message that He is the only true God worthy of worship. It calls upon people to fear and revere God alone, and to obey His commands.
orig: ينزل الملائكة بالروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده أن أنذروا أنه لا إله إلا أنا فاتقون

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. High is He above what they associate [with Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and transcendence of God. He is the sole Creator of the universe, and everything in existence is a testament to His power, wisdom, and glory. The verse also rejects the notion of associating partners with God, as this would diminish His unique and unparalleled divinity.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق تعالى عما يشركون

translation: He created man from a sperm-drop; and behold, this same (man) becomes an open disputer.
interpretation: This verse highlights the humble origins of man, created from a mere sperm-drop, yet endowed with the ability to engage in complex reasoning and debate. It suggests that despite man's lowly beginnings, he is capable of becoming an "open disputer" - one who engages in intellectual discourse and challenges ideas. The verse serves as a reminder of the remarkable potential within the human being, and the need to approach discussions and debates with humility, recognizing our own limited nature.
orig: خلق الإنسان من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين

translation: And the cattle, He has created them for you; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings of God in creating livestock for the benefit of humanity. The animals provide warmth through their fur or wool, as well as various other practical uses and sustenance. This emphasizes the divine providence and the responsibility of humans to appreciate and make proper use of these resources.
orig: والأنعام خلقها لكم فيها دفء ومنافع ومنها تأكلون

translation: And for you in them is [beauty and] enjoyment when you bring them in [for the evening] and when you send them out [to pasture in the morning].
interpretation: This verse highlights the beauty and enjoyment that can be found in livestock, such as camels, sheep, or cattle. When you bring them back home in the evening and when you send them out to graze in the morning, there is a sense of tranquility and appreciation for the natural world that they represent. The verse encourages the appreciation of the blessings and provisions that these animals provide.
orig: ولكم فيها جمال حين تريحون وحين تسرحون

translation: And they carry your loads to a land you could not have reached except with difficulty to yourselves. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's compassion and care for His servants. It suggests that even when facing hardships and difficulties in life, God provides means and resources to help us reach our destinations. The verse encourages us to trust in God's mercy and kindness, as He facilitates our journey through life and supports us in overcoming the challenges we face.
orig: وتحمل أثقالكم إلى بلد لم تكونوا بالغيه إلا بشق الأنفس إن ربكم لرءوف رحيم

translation: And [He created] the horses, mules and donkeys for you to ride and [as] adornment. And He creates that which you do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings of Allah in creating various animals for the benefit of humanity. The horses, mules, and donkeys are not only for transportation and labor, but also serve as a means of adornment and beauty. Additionally, the verse suggests that Allah creates many other things that are beyond human knowledge and understanding, further emphasizing His power and wisdom.
orig: والخيل والبغال والحمير لتركبوها وزينة ويخلق ما لا تعلمون

translation: And upon Allah is the [responsibility for the] direction of the way, and among them [i.e., the ways] are those deviating. And if He willed, He could have guided you all.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the ultimate guidance and direction of the right path lies with Allah. While there are many paths and ways in life, some of which may be misguided or deviant, Allah has the power and ability to guide all of humanity to the straight path if He so chooses. The verse suggests that Allah's guidance is available, but people are responsible for choosing to follow it.
orig: وعلى الله قصد السبيل ومنها جائر ولو شاء لهداكم أجمعين

translation: It is He who sends down water from the sky; from it is drink, and from it are the shrubs upon which you feed your animals.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's provision and sustenance for His creation. The rain that comes from the sky provides drinking water for humans and nourishment for the vegetation that sustains livestock. This demonstrates God's care and wisdom in sustaining all life on Earth.
orig: هو الذي أنزل من السماء ماء لكم منه شراب ومنه شجر فيه تسيمون

translation: He produces for you thereby the crop and the olive and the palm trees and the grapevines and from all the fruits. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse highlights the abundance and variety of the natural provisions that God has created for the benefit of humankind. It encourages people to reflect on the signs of God's power and wisdom in the natural world, which should lead them to gratitude, faith, and a deeper understanding of the divine.
orig: ينبت لكم به الزرع والزيتون والنخيل والأعناب ومن كل الثمرات إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And He has subjected to you the night and the day and the sun and the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and sovereignty over the entire universe. The night and day, the sun, moon, and stars are all subjected to His command, and their orderly movements and cycles are signs for those who reflect and use their intellect to understand the divine wisdom behind the creation of these celestial bodies. This is an invitation to ponder upon Allah's might and to submit to Him in gratitude and obedience.
orig: وسخر لكم الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر والنجوم مسخرات بأمره إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And [He created] whatever He has multiplied for you in the earth of [varying] colors. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the diversity and variety of creation on Earth, which is a sign of God's power and wisdom for those who reflect and remember Him. The different colors and forms of the things He has created are a testament to His artistry and a reminder for people to appreciate and be grateful for the wonders of the natural world.
orig: وما ذرأ لكم في الأرض مختلفا ألوانه إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يذكرون

translation: And it is He who has subjected the sea for you to eat from it tender meat and to extract from it ornaments which you wear. And you see the ships plowing through it, and [He subjected it] that you may seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the bountiful provisions that God has made available to humanity through the sea. It emphasizes that God has subjected the sea to serve human needs, allowing us to extract from it both sustenance (tender meat) and adornments (ornaments) that we can use. The verse also points to the ships that traverse the sea, enabling us to seek God's bounty and provision. The underlying message is one of gratitude and appreciation for God's abundant blessings, which should motivate us to be thankful and acknowledge His sovereignty.
orig: وهو الذي سخر البحر لتأكلوا منه لحما طريا وتستخرجوا منه حلية تلبسونها وترى الفلك مواخر فيه ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And He has cast into the earth firmly set mountains, lest it shift with you, and [made] rivers and roads, that you may be guided,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's creation of mountains, rivers, and roads as a means to guide and stabilize humanity. The mountains are firmly set in the earth to prevent it from shaking or shifting, providing a stable foundation for human habitation. The rivers and roads serve as pathways for travel and communication, facilitating the guidance and direction of people. The verse suggests that these physical features of the earth are divinely ordained to help people find their way and be rightly guided.
orig: وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم وأنهارا وسبلا لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And [by] the stars, they are [also] guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of celestial bodies, particularly the stars, as a means of guidance and navigation for people. The stars have been used throughout history to help people find their way, both literally and metaphorically. This verse suggests that the stars can serve as a source of guidance and direction, not only for physical navigation but also for spiritual and intellectual guidance.
orig: وعلامات وبالنجم هم يهتدون

translation: Is then He Who creates like one who does not create? Will you not then remember?
interpretation: This verse draws a comparison between the Creator, Allah, and those who cannot create. It emphasizes that the One who has the power to create is vastly different from those who have no such ability. The rhetorical question "Will you not then remember?" is an invitation to reflect on the clear distinction between the Creator and the created, and to remember and acknowledge the greatness of Allah.
orig: أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق أفلا تذكرون

translation: And if you [try to] count the favors of Allah, you will not be able to enumerate them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless nature of Allah's blessings and favors upon humanity. No matter how much we try to count and enumerate them, we will never be able to fully comprehend the extent of Allah's generosity and compassion. This serves as a reminder to be grateful to Allah and to seek His forgiveness, as He is the Most Forgiving and the Most Merciful.
orig: وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها إن الله لغفور رحيم

translation: And Allah knows what you conceal and what you declare.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Almighty, is all-knowing and has complete awareness of our thoughts, actions, and intentions, whether they are hidden or openly expressed. It serves as a reminder that we should be mindful of our conduct, as Allah is aware of everything we do, even if it is not visible to others.
orig: والله يعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون

translation: And those they invoke besides Allah create nothing, and they [themselves] are created.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the false deities worshipped by people besides Allah have no power to create anything, as they themselves are created beings. It highlights the futility of associating partners with Allah, the One True Creator who alone has the power to create.
orig: والذين يدعون من دون الله لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون

translation: They are [but] dead, not living, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith are spiritually dead, unaware of the truth, and oblivious to the reality of the Hereafter and the Day of Resurrection. They are disconnected from the divine guidance and the ultimate purpose of their existence.
orig: أموات غير أحياء وما يشعرون أيان يبعثون

translation: Your God is one God. But those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts are in denial, and they are arrogant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God, and contrasts the belief in the Hereafter with those who deny it. The interpretation is that those who do not believe in the afterlife have hearts that are in a state of denial and are arrogant. This suggests that belief in the Hereafter is a fundamental aspect of faith, and that a lack of such belief is indicative of a hardened, prideful heart.
orig: إلهكم إله واحد فالذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة قلوبهم منكرة وهم مستكبرون

translation: Verily, Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He does not love the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge of all that people keep hidden in their hearts and all that they openly express. It conveys that Allah does not love those who are arrogant and full of pride, as such behavior is displeasing to Him.
orig: لا جرم أن الله يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون إنه لا يحب المستكبرين

translation: And when it is said to them, "What has your Lord sent down?" they say, "Legends of the former peoples,"
interpretation: This verse refers to those who dismiss the Qur'an as mere "legends of the former peoples" and do not recognize it as the revealed word of God. The interpretation is that such people are arrogant and unwilling to accept the truth of the Qur'an, preferring instead to dismiss it as mere fables or stories of the past.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم ماذا أنزل ربكم قالوا أساطير الأولين

translation: That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they misled without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of misguiding others without knowledge. Those who lead others astray will be held accountable not only for their own sins, but also for the sins of those they have misled. On the Day of Judgment, they will have to bear the full weight of their own burdens as well as the burdens of those they have led astray, which is a heavy and unjust burden to carry. This serves as a warning to be cautious in our teachings and to ensure that we are guiding others with knowledge and wisdom, rather than misleading them.
orig: ليحملوا أوزارهم كاملة يوم القيامة ومن أوزار الذين يضلونهم بغير علم ألا ساء ما يزرون

translation: Those before them had also plotted, but Allah struck at the foundations of their building, and the roof fell down upon them from above, and the punishment came to them from directions they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who schemed against the truth and plotted against the believers will ultimately be defeated. Allah, the Almighty, has the power to destroy the foundations of their plans, causing their structures to collapse upon them. The punishment will come from unexpected directions, emphasizing the futility of their schemes and the might of Allah.
orig: قد مكر الذين من قبلهم فأتى الله بنيانهم من القواعد فخر عليهم السقف من فوقهم وأتاهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون

translation: Then, on the Day of Resurrection, He will disgrace them and say, 'Where are My 'partners' for whose sake you used to oppose [Me]?' Those who were given knowledge will say, 'Indeed, disgrace this Day and evil are upon the disbelievers'
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of associating partners with Allah (God) on the Day of Resurrection.
