Those who worshipped false deities or idols alongside Allah will be disgraced, and Allah will question them about their misguided beliefs. The people of knowledge, referring to the believers, will affirm that the disgrace and punishment are rightfully upon the disbelievers who rejected the true faith.
orig: ثم يوم القيامة يخزيهم ويقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تشاقون فيهم قال الذين أوتوا العلم إن الخزي اليوم والسوء على الكافرين

translation: Those whom the angels take [in death] while they are wronging themselves - [the angels] will say, "Where [i.e., in what condition] were you?" They will say, "We were oppressed in the land." [The angels] will say, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious [enough] for you to emigrate therein?" - And those are the ones whom their refuge is Hell, and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who die while they are unjust to themselves. When the angels of death come to take their souls, they will ask them about their condition and why they did not migrate to a place where they could freely practice their religion. The verse emphasizes that the earth is spacious enough for people to find refuge, and that those who fail to do so will end up in Hell, which is a terrible destination.
orig: الذين تتوفاهم الملائكة ظالمي أنفسهم فألقوا السلم ما كنا نعمل من سوء بلى إن الله عليم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: So enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the arrogant, those who have pride and conceit in their hearts. It conveys that the ultimate destination for such individuals is the gates of Hell, where they will dwell eternally. The interpretation suggests that arrogance and pride are vices that lead to a wretched and miserable existence in the Hereafter.
orig: فادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فلبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: And it will be said to those who feared Allah, "What did your Lord send down?" They will say, "Good." For those who do good in this world is a good [reward] - and the home of the Hereafter is better. And how excellent is the home of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward and blessings that Allah (SWT) has in store for those who fear Him and do good deeds. When the righteous are asked about what Allah has sent down, they will simply reply "Good", indicating their contentment and satisfaction with Allah's decree. The verse then goes on to state that those who do good in this world will be rewarded with good in this life, and an even better reward in the Hereafter. The home of the righteous in the Hereafter is described as being "excellent", emphasizing the sublime and unparalleled nature of the abode that awaits the God-conscious.
orig: وقيل للذين اتقوا ماذا أنزل ربكم قالوا خيرا للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنة ولدار الآخرة خير ولنعم دار المتقين

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence; they will enter them, beneath which rivers flow. They will have therein whatever they wish. Thus does Allah reward the righteous.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward for the righteous in the Hereafter - they will be granted eternal gardens in Paradise, where they will have all that they desire. The rivers flowing beneath these gardens symbolize the abundance and tranquility of this eternal abode. This is how Allah rewards those who fear Him and strive to live righteously in this world.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها تجري من تحتها الأنهار لهم فيها ما يشاءون كذلك يجزي الله المتقين

translation: Those whom the angels take [in death] while they are good - they [the angels] will say, "Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who live righteous lives and die in a state of faith will be welcomed into Paradise by the angels. The angels will greet them with the salutation of peace, acknowledging their good deeds and virtuous conduct in life. This verse provides reassurance and encouragement for believers to strive for righteousness, as they will be rewarded with the eternal bliss of Paradise.
orig: الذين تتوفاهم الملائكة طيبين يقولون سلام عليكم ادخلوا الجنة بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Do they await but that the angels should come to them or there comes the command of your Lord? Thus did those do before them, and Allah wronged them not, but they were [themselves] wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to have faith in Allah and not to be distracted by waiting for extraordinary signs or events. It reminds them that previous generations also faced trials and tribulations, but it was their own misdeeds that led to their downfall, not any injustice from Allah. The interpretation is that one should focus on righteous conduct and trust in Allah's plan, rather than seeking miraculous interventions or blaming Allah for one's own shortcomings.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا أن تأتيهم الملائكة أو يأتي أمر ربك كذلك فعل الذين من قبلهم وما ظلمهم الله ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: So the evil consequences of what they did overtook them, and that at which they used to scoff surrounded them.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who engage in wrongdoing and mock the signs of God will ultimately face the consequences of their actions. Their arrogance and disbelief will be met with the very thing they scorned, as they are enveloped by the punishment they had denied.
orig: فأصابهم سيئات ما عملوا وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And those who associate others with Allah say, "If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped anything other than Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything through other than Him." Thus did those before them do; so are the messengers responsible for anything but clear notification?
interpretation: This verse addresses the polytheists who associate partners with Allah. They claim that if Allah had willed, they would not have worshipped anything other than Him, and they would not have forbidden anything except through Allah's command. The verse draws a parallel between the polytheists' argument and the actions of those who came before them, implying that the messengers are only responsible for conveying the clear message, not for the choices and actions of the people.
orig: وقال الذين أشركوا لو شاء الله ما عبدنا من دونه من شيء نحن ولا آباؤنا ولا حرمنا من دونه من شيء كذلك فعل الذين من قبلهم فهل على الرسل إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: And We have certainly sent among every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid Taghut (false deities)." And among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was [deservedly] decreed. So proceed through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of God's guidance, as He has sent a messenger to every nation to call people to worship God alone and avoid false deities. The verse highlights that some people accepted this guidance and were rightly guided, while others rejected it and were left to their error. The instruction to "proceed through the earth and observe" suggests that one can learn from the fate of those who denied the truth, and that the consequences of belief and disbelief are visible in the world.
orig: ولقد بعثنا في كل أمة رسولا أن اعبدوا الله واجتنبوا الطاغوت فمنهم من هدى الله ومنهم من حقت عليه الضلالة فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: Indeed, [O Muhammad], you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that guidance and faith are ultimately in the hands of Allah. Even though the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) deeply cared for the guidance of his people, he could not force them to believe. Allah alone decides who will receive His guidance, and no one can help those whom Allah has left to stray. The responsibility of the Prophet was to convey the message, not to make people accept it.
orig: إن تحرص على هداهم فإن الله لا يهدي من يضل وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: And they swear by Allah with their strongest oaths [that] Allah will not resurrect one who dies. But yes - it is a [binding] promise upon Him in truth, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of resurrection and the afterlife, despite the disbelief of many people. It highlights that Allah has made a binding promise to resurrect the dead, even though most people are unaware of this truth.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لا يبعث الله من يموت بلى وعدا عليه حقا ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: That He may make clear to them that [matter] over which they differ, and that those who have disbelieved may know that they were liars.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the purpose of the revelation of the Qur'an is to provide clarity and guidance on matters of dispute and disagreement among people, and to expose the falsehood of those who reject the truth and deny the divine message.
orig: ليبين لهم الذي يختلفون فيه وليعلم الذين كفروا أنهم كانوا كاذبين

translation: Indeed, Our word for a thing when We intend it is but that We say to it, "Be," and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and authority of Allah in creating things. When Allah wills something to come into existence, He simply says "Be," and it comes into being immediately without any delay or difficulty. This highlights the absolute sovereignty and omnipotence of Allah, who can bring anything into existence through His divine command.
orig: إنما قولنا لشيء إذا أردناه أن نقول له كن فيكون

translation: And those who emigrated for [the cause of] Allah after they had been wronged - We will surely settle them in this world in a good place; but the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers who have been persecuted or oppressed for their faith to migrate and seek refuge elsewhere. It promises that Allah will provide them a good life in this world, and an even greater reward in the Hereafter, if they remain steadfast in their faith. The interpretation emphasizes that the ultimate reward is in the afterlife, which should be the primary motivation for the believers, rather than worldly comforts or status.
orig: والذين هاجروا في الله من بعد ما ظلموا لنبوئنهم في الدنيا حسنة ولأجر الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: Those who are patient and rely upon their Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtues of patience and trust in Allah. It encourages believers to endure trials and tribulations with steadfastness, and to place their complete reliance and faith in the Almighty. By doing so, they will be rewarded with the guidance and support of Allah.
orig: الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed [the message], so ask the people of the message if you do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the messengers sent by God throughout history have always been human beings, not angels or supernatural beings. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to refer to the people of knowledge and wisdom, the "people of the message", if he is unsure about anything. This highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and learning from those who are knowledgeable, rather than relying solely on one's own understanding.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون

translation: With clear proofs and written ordinances. And We have sent down to you the Reminder [i.e., the Qur'an] that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them and that they might give thought.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has provided clear evidence and guidance through the Qur'an and other scriptures, which have been revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) so that he can explain to the people what has been sent down to them. The purpose is to encourage people to reflect and ponder over the divine teachings, in order to understand and implement them in their lives.
orig: بالبينات والزبر وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم ولعلهم يتفكرون

translation: Then, do those who have devised evil plots feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them or that the punishment will not come upon them from where they do not perceive?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who plot and scheme against the believers. It suggests that they should not feel secure, as Allah has the power to punish them in unexpected ways, whether by causing the earth to swallow them or by bringing upon them a punishment from a direction they do not anticipate. The message is that one should not underestimate the might and justice of Allah, and that those who engage in evil deeds will ultimately be held accountable.
orig: أفأمن الذين مكروا السيئات أن يخسف الله بهم الأرض أو يأتيهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون

translation: Or He may seize them gradually, and they will not be able to escape.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has the power to punish those who reject faith gradually, in ways they cannot escape or avoid. It serves as a warning to those who persist in disbelief and disobedience, that they cannot escape the consequences of their actions.
orig: أو يأخذهم في تقلبهم فما هم بمعجزين

translation: Or He may seize them gradually. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God may gradually take people to account for their misdeeds, rather than punishing them immediately. The interpretation is that God is patient and forgiving, and gives people time to repent and change their ways. The verse emphasizes that God is compassionate and merciful towards His creation.
orig: أو يأخذهم على تخوف فإن ربكم لرءوف رحيم

translation: Have they not looked at the things that Allah has created? Their shadows incline to the right and to the left, prostrating to Allah while they are humble.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the signs of Allah's creation, such as the shadows of objects that move and prostrate to Allah, as a means of recognizing the power and majesty of the Creator. It suggests that even inanimate objects like shadows demonstrate submission to Allah, which should inspire a similar attitude of humility and devotion in human beings.
orig: أولم يروا إلى ما خلق الله من شيء يتفيأ ظلاله عن اليمين والشمائل سجدا لله وهم داخرون

translation: And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth - the creatures and the angels, and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal submission and worship of Allah by all creation, including the angels. It highlights that all beings in the heavens and on the earth, whether animate or inanimate, prostrate and submit to Allah without any arrogance or pride. This serves as a reminder that we should emulate this attitude of humility and devotion in our own worship and relationship with the Divine.
orig: ولله يسجد ما في السماوات وما في الأرض من دابة والملائكة وهم لا يستكبرون

translation: They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fearing and obeying Allah (God) in all aspects of life. The believers are described as those who have a deep reverence and awe for their Lord, which motivates them to follow His commands and do what is pleasing to Him, without hesitation or resistance.
orig: يخافون ربهم من فوقهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون

translation: And Allah has said, "Do not take two deities. He is but one God, so fear Me."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental belief in the oneness of God. It rejects the notion of multiple deities and affirms that there is only one true God who deserves to be worshipped and feared. The verse calls upon believers to direct their reverence and devotion solely towards the one God, and to avoid any form of polytheism or associating partners with Him.
orig: وقال الله لا تتخذوا إلهين اثنين إنما هو إله واحد فإياي فارهبون

translation: And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him is [due] worship constantly. Then is it other than Allah that you fear?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the sole sovereign over the entire universe, both in the heavens and the earth. It is He alone who deserves worship and obedience from all of creation. The rhetorical question at the end challenges the reader to consider whether it is appropriate to fear or revere anything or anyone other than Allah, the Almighty.
orig: وله ما في السماوات والأرض وله الدين واصبا أفغير الله تتقون

translation: And whatever [good] you have - it is from Allah. Then when adversity touches you, to Him you cry for help.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all blessings and good things we have in life come from Allah. When we face hardship and difficulties, we should turn to Allah and seek His help, as He is the source of all provisions and the ultimate refuge.
orig: وما بكم من نعمة فمن الله ثم إذا مسكم الضر فإليه تجأرون

translation: Then when He removes the adversity from you, at once a party of you associate others with their Lord
interpretation: When Allah removes the hardship and difficulties from people, some of them start associating partners with Him and worshiping other than Him, instead of being grateful and worshiping Him alone.
orig: ثم إذا كشف الضر عنكم إذا فريق منكم بربهم يشركون

translation: That they may disbelieve in that which We have given them. So enjoy yourselves, for you are going to know.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject the blessings and guidance provided by God will be left to their own devices, and the consequences of their actions will become clear to them in due time. The interpretation implies that those who turn away from faith and God's teachings will eventually face the consequences of their choices, and they will come to realize the error of their ways.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم فتمتعوا فسوف تعلمون

translation: And they attribute to what they do not know a share of [Our] provision, [and] by Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to invent.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of attributing divine qualities or a share in God's provision to things that have no real knowledge or power. It serves as a warning that people will be held accountable for the false claims and beliefs they have fabricated.
orig: ويجعلون لما لا يعلمون نصيبا مما رزقناهم تالله لتسألن عما كنتم تفترون

translation: And they attribute to Allah daughters, and for them [i.e., themselves] is what they desire.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of the pagan Arabs who used to attribute female offspring to Allah, while preferring male children for themselves. The verse highlights the absurdity and hypocrisy of this belief, as they ascribed to Allah what they themselves did not want for their own families.
orig: ويجعلون لله البنات سبحانه ولهم ما يشتهون

translation: And when one of them is informed of [the birth of] a female, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unfortunate cultural practice of some Arabs at the time of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of being displeased and saddened by the birth of a daughter. The verse condemns this attitude, indicating that it is a sign of moral and spiritual weakness to be ashamed of having a female child. The interpretation is that one should embrace and celebrate the birth of both sons and daughters, as all human life is precious in the sight of God.
orig: وإذا بشر أحدهم بالأنثى ظل وجهه مسودا وهو كظيم

translation: He hides himself from the people because of the evil of that which he has been informed. Shall he keep it in humiliation or bury it [i.e., the girl] in the ground? Unquestionably, evil is that which they decide.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of female infanticide that was common in pre-Islamic Arabia. It criticizes the decision to either keep the newborn girl in a state of humiliation or bury her alive, describing such actions as "evil". The verse emphasizes the moral wrongness of this practice and calls for a change in societal attitudes towards women.
orig: يتوارى من القوم من سوء ما بشر به أيمسكه على هون أم يدسه في التراب ألا ساء ما يحكمون

translation: For those who do not believe in the Hereafter, the similitude of evil is made alluring to them (i.e. the fire of Hell or their saying: "There is only our life of this world, we die and we live and nothing destroys us except Time"), and for them is the supreme example (i.e. Allah), and He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those who believe in the Hereafter and those who do not. For the disbelievers, evil is made to appear attractive to them, whether it is the allure of the fire of Hell or the notion that there is only this worldly life and nothing else. In contrast, Allah is the supreme example, the All-Mighty and All-Wise, who will hold people accountable in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of believing in the Hereafter and following the guidance of Allah, the All-Wise.
orig: للذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة مثل السوء ولله المثل الأعلى وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And if Allah were to impose blame on the people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon the earth any creature, but He delays them for a specified term. And when their time has come, then indeed Allah is ever, of His servants, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and patience in dealing with the wrongdoings of humanity. Despite the prevalence of injustice and sin, Allah does not immediately punish all people, but rather gives them a chance to repent and reform. The verse suggests that if Allah were to hold people accountable for their misdeeds right away, there would be no one left on Earth. However, Allah grants a specified time period for people to make amends, and when that time comes, there is no delaying or hastening of the appointed hour of reckoning. This highlights the importance of using the time given by Allah wisely and turning to Him in repentance before it is too late.
orig: ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بظلمهم ما ترك عليها من دابة ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى فإذا جاء أجلهم لا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

translation: And they attribute to Allah what they dislike, and their tongues assert the lie that they will have the best [of the afterlife]. Unquestionably, for them is the Fire, and they will be [therein] neglected.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who attribute to Allah what they themselves dislike, such as associating partners with Him or denying His attributes. Their tongues assert falsehoods about the rewards they will receive in the Hereafter, when in reality they will be punished with the Fire of Hell due to their disbelief and neglect of their duties.
orig: ويجعلون لله ما يكرهون وتصف ألسنتهم الكذب أن لهم الحسنى لا جرم أن لهم النار وأنهم مفرطون

translation: By Allah, We have certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you, [O Muhammad], but Satan made their deeds attractive to them. And he is their [i.e., the disbelievers'] ally today [as well], and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has sent messengers to previous nations, but Satan had made their deeds seem attractive to them. Satan is their ally today, and they will face a painful punishment. This serves as a warning to the disbelievers that they should not be deceived by Satan's temptations, as they will ultimately face a severe consequence for their actions.
orig: تالله لقد أرسلنا إلى أمم من قبلك فزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم فهو وليهم اليوم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And We have not sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book [i.e., the Qur'an] except to clarify for them that in which they differ and as guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad to resolve the differences among people and to provide guidance and mercy for those who believe. It suggests that the Qur'an is a source of clarity and direction for the faithful, helping them navigate the complexities of faith and life.
orig: وما أنزلنا عليك الكتاب إلا لتبين لهم الذي اختلفوا فيه وهدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And Allah has sent down water from the sky and given life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who sends down the rain from the sky, which then revives the earth and brings it back to life after it had been lifeless and barren. This is a clear sign of Allah's power and His ability to give life and sustain it, for those who are willing to listen and reflect on His creation.
orig: والله أنزل من السماء ماء فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يسمعون

translation: And indeed, for you in the livestock there is a lesson. We give you drink from what is in their bellies - between excretion and blood - pure milk, palatable for drinkers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wonders of God's creation, specifically the livestock. It points to the nourishment and sustenance that can be derived from these animals, as they provide pure, wholesome milk for human consumption, despite the impurities that exist in their bodies. This is a sign of God's power and a lesson for mankind to reflect on the blessings and wisdom in the natural world.
orig: وإن لكم في الأنعام لعبرة نسقيكم مما في بطونه من بين فرث ودم لبنا خالصا سائغا للشاربين

translation: And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines you take intoxicant and [as] provision. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the blessings of God, such as the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines, which can be used for both intoxicants and wholesome sustenance. The verse suggests that those who use their reason and intellect will see the signs of God's wisdom and power in these natural resources.
orig: ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب تتخذون منه سكرا ورزقا حسنا إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يعقلون

translation: And your Lord inspired to the bee, "Take for yourself among the mountains, houses, and among the trees and [in] that which they construct."
interpretation: This verse encourages us to observe the remarkable engineering and architectural skills of the bees in constructing their hives. It highlights how the bees, under the guidance of God, are able to build intricate structures in the mountains, trees, and other places. This serves as a lesson for us to appreciate the wonders of God's creation and to learn from the ingenuity of the bees in our own endeavors.
orig: وأوحى ربك إلى النحل أن اتخذي من الجبال بيوتا ومن الشجر ومما يعرشون

translation: Then eat from all the fruits and follow the ways of your Lord with humility. There comes forth from their bellies a drink, varying in colors, in which there is healing for people. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to partake of the various blessings and bounties that God has provided, and to follow the path of God with humility and submission. The reference to the "drink, varying in colors" is understood to be a metaphor for the diversity and richness of God's creation, which contains remedies and healing for humanity. The verse thus highlights the importance of contemplating and reflecting on the signs of God's power and wisdom in the natural world.
orig: ثم كلي من كل الثمرات فاسلكي سبل ربك ذللا يخرج من بطونها شراب مختلف ألوانه فيه شفاء للناس إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And Allah created you and then will cause you to die. And among you is he who is reversed to the most decrepit [old] age so that he will not know anything after [having had] knowledge. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who has created us and it is He who will eventually cause us to die. It also highlights that some people are made to live to an extremely old age, to the point that they lose their mental faculties and ability to comprehend things they once knew. This serves as a reminder that Allah is all-knowing and all-powerful, and that our lives are ultimately in His hands.
orig: والله خلقكم ثم يتوفاكم ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر لكي لا يعلم بعد علم شيئا إن الله عليم قدير

translation: And Allah has favored some of you over others in provision. But those who were favored [with wealth] are not willing to give [a share] of their provision to those [slaves] whom their right hands possess so that they would be equal [in sharing]. Then is it the favor of Allah they reject?
interpretation: This verse highlights the inequality in the distribution of wealth and resources among people, and how those who have been blessed with wealth and abundance are often unwilling to share it with those who are less fortunate. The verse emphasizes that this unwillingness to share is a rejection of Allah's blessings and a denial of the true spirit of Islam, which calls for compassion, generosity, and equality among all believers.
orig: والله فضل بعضكم على بعض في الرزق فما الذين فضلوا برادي رزقهم على ما ملكت أيمانهم فهم فيه سواء أفبنعمة الله يجحدون

translation: And Allah has made for you from yourselves mates and has made for you from your mates sons and grandchildren and has provided for you from the good things. Then in falsehood do they believe and in the favor of Allah they disbelieve?
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon humanity, including the institution of marriage and the gift of children. It reminds us that these blessings come from Allah, and that to deny or disbelieve in them would be a grave error and ingratitude towards the Almighty.
orig: والله جعل لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا وجعل لكم من أزواجكم بنين وحفدة ورزقكم من الطيبات أفبالباطل يؤمنون وبنعمت الله هم يكفرون

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which does not possess for them [the ability to provide] sustenance from the heavens and the earth in anything, nor do they have [any] power.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that worshipping anything other than Allah is futile, as these false deities have no power to provide sustenance or any kind of benefit from the heavens and the earth. They are powerless and cannot influence the affairs of the universe in any way. This serves as a warning against associating partners with Allah and highlights the need to direct all worship and reliance towards the One true God, who is the sole Provider and Sustainer of all creation.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا يملك لهم رزقا من السماوات والأرض شيئا ولا يستطيعون

translation: So do not give examples for Allah. Indeed, Allah knows, and you do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that we should not make comparisons or give examples to illustrate the nature of Allah, as He is beyond human comprehension. We should refrain from trying to liken Allah to anything in the created world, as our knowledge is limited and Allah alone knows the true nature of His divine attributes.
orig: فلا تضربوا لله الأمثال إن الله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: Allah presents an example: a slave [who is] owned and unable to do anything of himself, and a [free] man whom We have provided with a good provision, so he spends from it secretly and publicly. Can they be equal? [No], praise to Allah. But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse presents a metaphor to illustrate the difference between a slave, who is completely dependent on his master and unable to do anything on his own, and a free man who has been provided with good sustenance from Allah. The free man is able to spend from this provision both secretly and openly, demonstrating his freedom and self-sufficiency. The verse then poses a rhetorical question asking if these two can be considered equal, with the answer being that they cannot, and that all praise is due to Allah. However, the verse notes that most people do not understand this distinction.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا عبدا مملوكا لا يقدر على شيء ومن رزقناه منا رزقا حسنا فهو ينفق منه سرا وجهرا هل يستوون الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And Allah has set forth an example: two men, one of them dumb, who has no power over anything, and he is a burden to his master; whichever way he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who enjoins justice and is himself on a straight path?
interpretation: This verse presents a metaphorical comparison between two types of people: one who is incapable and dependent, and another who is just and righteous. The first person is described as "dumb" and powerless, unable to contribute or bring any good, and is a burden to his master. The second person is one who enjoins justice and follows a straight path. The verse suggests that these two types of people are not equal, emphasizing the superiority of the one who upholds justice and righteousness over the one who is incapable and dependent.
orig: وضرب الله مثلا رجلين أحدهما أبكم لا يقدر على شيء وهو كل على مولاه أينما يوجهه لا يأت بخير هل يستوي هو ومن يأمر بالعدل وهو على صراط مستقيم

translation: And to Allah belongs the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. And the matter of the Hour is not but as a [single] glance of the eye or even nearer. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the knowledge of the unseen, including the timing of the Hour (the Day of Resurrection), belongs solely to Allah. The coming of the Hour will be sudden and unexpected, like the blink of an eye. This highlights Allah's absolute power and control over all things, and the need for humans to be ever-prepared for the final reckoning.
orig: ولله غيب السماوات والأرض وما أمر الساعة إلا كلمح البصر أو هو أقرب إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And Allah has extracted you from the wombs of your mothers while you know nothing, and He made for you hearing and vision and intellect that perhaps you would be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the one who created us and gave us the faculties of hearing, sight, and understanding, which we should be grateful for. It reminds us that we were born without any knowledge, and that all our abilities and knowledge come from Allah, which should lead us to appreciate and thank Him.
orig: والله أخرجكم من بطون أمهاتكم لا تعلمون شيئا وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة لعلكم تشكرون

translation: Have they not observed the birds [flying] in the atmosphere? They are sustained only by Allah. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to reflect on the wonders of Allah's creation, specifically the birds that fly in the sky. It emphasizes that the birds are sustained and controlled by Allah alone, which is a sign for those who have faith in Him. The interpretation suggests that observing the natural world can strengthen one's belief in the power and sovereignty of the Creator.
orig: ألم يروا إلى الطير مسخرات في جو السماء ما يمسكهن إلا الله إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And Allah has made for you from your homes a place of rest and made for you from the hides of the animals tents which you find light to carry on the day of your travel and the day of your encampment; and from their wool, fur, and hair is furnishing and enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: This verse highlights how Allah has provided various means for human comfort and convenience. The homes we live in provide a place of rest and shelter, while the hides, wool, fur, and hair of animals are used to make lightweight tents that can be easily transported during travel or encampment. These natural materials also serve as furnishings and other useful items for a period of time. The verse emphasizes Allah's blessings and how He has created the world to serve the needs of humanity.
orig: والله جعل لكم من بيوتكم سكنا وجعل لكم من جلود الأنعام بيوتا تستخفونها يوم ظعنكم ويوم إقامتكم ومن أصوافها وأوبارها وأشعارها أثاثا ومتاعا إلى حين

translation: And Allah has made for you from that which He has created, shadow and has made for you from the mountains, shelters and has made for you garments to protect you from the heat and garments [i.e., coats of mail] to protect you from your [enemy in] battle. Thus does He complete His favor upon you that you might submit [to Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's provision and care for humanity. He has created various blessings and means of protection for us, such as shade, shelters in the mountains, and clothing to shield us from heat and harm. These are signs of God's favor and mercy, intended to encourage our submission and gratitude to Him.
orig: والله جعل لكم مما خلق ظلالا وجعل لكم من الجبال أكنانا وجعل لكم سرابيل تقيكم الحر وسرابيل تقيكم بأسكم كذلك يتم نعمته عليكم لعلكم تسلمون

translation: And if they turn away, then only upon you is [responsibility for] the clear notification.
interpretation: If the people reject your message, O Prophet, your duty is only to convey the message clearly and plainly, without any ambiguity. The ultimate decision and guidance of the people rests with Allah, not with you.
orig: فإن تولوا فإنما عليك البلاغ المبين

translation: They recognize the favor of Allah; then they deny it, and most of them are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ingratitude and disbelief of many people who are aware of the blessings and favors bestowed upon them by Allah, yet they choose to deny and reject them. It serves as a reminder that true faith and gratitude should accompany the recognition of Allah's bounties, and that a lack of appreciation for these blessings is a sign of disbelief.
orig: يعرفون نعمت الله ثم ينكرونها وأكثرهم الكافرون

translation: And the Day We will resurrect from every nation a witness. Then it will not be permitted to the disbelievers [to apologize or make excuses], nor will they be asked to appease [Allah].
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Judgment, when every nation will be held accountable for their actions. On that day, a witness will be brought forth from each community to testify against them. The disbelievers will not be given a chance to make excuses or seek forgiveness, as their fate has already been sealed due to their rejection of faith and refusal to submit to Allah.
orig: ويوم نبعث من كل أمة شهيدا ثم لا يؤذن للذين كفروا ولا هم يستعتبون

translation: And when those who have wronged see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse conveys that on the Day of Judgment, those who have committed wrongdoings will face the full consequences of their actions. They will not be able to escape the punishment, nor will they be granted any respite or leniency. The verse emphasizes the certainty and severity of the punishment for those who have transgressed against God's laws and the rights of others.
orig: وإذا رأى الذين ظلموا العذاب فلا يخفف عنهم ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And when those who associate others with Allah see their 'partners', they say: 'Our Lord, these are our 'partners' whom we used to invoke besides You.' But they will throw back at them their word, [saying], 'Indeed, you are liars.'
interpretation: This verse describes the scene on the Day of Judgment when the polytheists will see the false deities they worshipped in this world. They will acknowledge that these were their 'partners' whom they used to worship alongside Allah. However, these false deities will reject their claims and declare them to be liars, as they were unable to provide any benefit or intercession for the polytheists on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وإذا رأى الذين أشركوا شركاءهم قالوا ربنا هؤلاء شركاؤنا الذين كنا ندعو من دونك فألقوا إليهم القول إنكم لكاذبون

translation: And they will submit to Allah on that Day, and what they used to invent will have disappeared from them.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, people will submit to Allah and the false beliefs and deities they used to worship will be exposed as worthless and will vanish from them.
orig: وألقوا إلى الله يومئذ السلم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah - We will increase them in punishment over [their] punishment for what they used to corrupt.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith and prevent others from the path of Allah will be subjected to an even greater punishment. Their punishment will be compounded due to their corrupt actions and attempts to lead others astray.
orig: الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله زدناهم عذابا فوق العذاب بما كانوا يفسدون

translation: And the Day when We will resurrect among every community a witness over them from themselves. And We will bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over those. And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things and as guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Judgment, when a witness from each community will be brought forth to testify about the deeds of its people. The Prophet Muhammad will be a witness over all these communities. The Qur'an is described as a comprehensive guide that clarifies all matters, provides guidance and mercy, and brings good news to the believers.
orig: ويوم نبعث في كل أمة شهيدا عليهم من أنفسهم وجئنا بك شهيدا على هؤلاء ونزلنا عليك الكتاب تبيانا لكل شيء وهدى ورحمة وبشرى للمسلمين

translation: Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving to relatives and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah commands us to uphold justice, do good deeds, and be kind to our relatives. He forbids us from engaging in immoral and unethical acts, as well as oppression. The purpose of these commands is to remind us to be righteous and mindful of Allah, so that we may remember and follow His guidance.
orig: إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى وينهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي يعظكم لعلكم تذكرون

translation: And fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have taken it, [O believers], and do not break oaths after their confirmation while you have made Allah, over you, a witness. Indeed, Allah knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one"s covenants and oaths made with Allah. It reminds believers that they have taken Allah as a witness to their promises, and that Allah is aware of all their actions. The verse encourages believers to be steadfast in their commitments and to not break their word, as this would be a breach of trust with Allah.
orig: وأوفوا بعهد الله إذا عاهدتم ولا تنقضوا الأيمان بعد توكيدها وقد جعلتم الله عليكم كفيلا إن الله يعلم ما تفعلون

translation: And do not be like the one who untwisted her spun thread after it was strong, [by] taking your oaths as [means of] deception between you because one community is more plentiful [in wealth or numbers] than another community. Indeed, Allah only tries you thereby. And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse cautions against breaking promises and oaths for personal gain or to gain advantage over others. It emphasizes that Allah tests people in this way, and will reveal the truth about their actions on the Day of Judgment. The key message is to be steadfast in one's commitments and not to use oaths deceitfully for worldly gains or to gain superiority over others.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالتي نقضت غزلها من بعد قوة أنكاثا تتخذون أيمانكم دخلا بينكم أن تكون أمة هي أربى من أمة إنما يبلوكم الله به وليبينن لكم يوم القيامة ما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And if Allah had willed, He could have made you [of] one religion, but He causes to stray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has the power and authority to guide people to the right path, but He also allows people to stray if they choose to do so. It suggests that individuals are responsible for their actions and will be held accountable for them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ولو شاء الله لجعلكم أمة واحدة ولكن يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء ولتسألن عما كنتم تعملون

translation: And do not make [your] oaths a [means of] deception between you so that a foot might slip after being firm, and [then] you would taste the evil [consequences] of [having barred] from the way of Allah, and you would have a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse cautions against using oaths as a means of deception or manipulation, as that can lead to a loss of firm footing and the tasting of evil consequences for turning away from the path of Allah. It emphasizes the need to be truthful and steadfast in one's commitments, and warns of the severe punishment that may result from such deceptive practices.
orig: ولا تتخذوا أيمانكم دخلا بينكم فتزل قدم بعد ثبوتها وتذوقوا السوء بما صددتم عن سبيل الله ولكم عذاب عظيم

translation: And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price. Indeed, what is with Allah is best for you, if you should know.
interpretation: This verse warns against betraying one's covenant or promise to Allah for the sake of worldly gains. It emphasizes that what Allah has to offer is far superior to any material wealth or benefit that one may acquire through such betrayal. The verse encourages believers to have faith in Allah and prioritize their spiritual well-being over temporary, fleeting gains.
orig: ولا تشتروا بعهد الله ثمنا قليلا إنما عند الله هو خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: And whatever you have of wealth - it will be depleted, but what Allah has is lasting. And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the wealth and possessions of this world are fleeting and temporary, while the rewards and blessings from Allah are eternal and lasting. It encourages believers to be patient and steadfast in their faith, as Allah will reward them for their good deeds in the best possible way.
orig: ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق ولنجزين الذين صبروا أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward [in the Hereafter] according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that in Islam, both men and women are equally capable of and encouraged to perform good deeds. It promises that those who believe and do righteous acts will be granted a blessed life in this world and a commensurate reward in the Hereafter. The verse highlights the principle of gender equality in Islam and the importance of faith and good works, regardless of one"s gender.
orig: من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فلنحيينه حياة طيبة ولنجزينهم أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون

translation: So when you recite the Qur'an, [first] seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the expelled [from His mercy].
interpretation: This verse instructs the reader of the Qur'an to seek refuge in Allah from the influence of Satan before reciting the Qur'an. It emphasizes the importance of seeking divine protection and guidance when engaging with the sacred scripture, in order to avoid being misled by the temptations and deceptions of the devil.
orig: فإذا قرأت القرآن فاستعذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم

translation: Indeed, he [i.e., Satan] has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Satan has no power or influence over those who have true faith in God and who put their trust in Him. The believers are protected from Satan's temptations and deceptions because of their unwavering reliance on the Almighty. This verse serves as a reassurance and encouragement for the faithful to remain steadfast in their belief and to not be swayed by the schemes of the devil.
orig: إنه ليس له سلطان على الذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the devil's (or Satan's) authority and influence is limited to those who choose to follow and ally themselves with him, as well as those who associate partners with Allah (God). It suggests that the devil has no power over those who remain steadfast in their faith and loyalty to Allah alone.
orig: إنما سلطانه على الذين يتولونه والذين هم به مشركون

translation: And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse - and Allah is most knowing of what He sends down - they say, "You, [O Muhammad], are but an inventor [of lies]". But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse addresses the attitude of those who reject the Qur'an and accuse the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of fabricating its verses. It emphasizes that Allah is the One who sends down the revelations, and that the Prophet is merely conveying the message, not inventing it. The verse also suggests that most of those who reject the Qur'an do so out of ignorance and lack of understanding, rather than any valid reason.
orig: وإذا بدلنا آية مكان آية والله أعلم بما ينزل قالوا إنما أنت مفتر بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Say, "The Pure Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth to make firm those who believe and as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an was revealed by the Holy Spirit (Gabriel) on behalf of God, in order to strengthen the faith of believers, provide guidance, and give good news to Muslims. It underscores the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, which serves to affirm the beliefs of the faithful and spread the message of Islam.
orig: قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق ليثبت الذين آمنوا وهدى وبشرى للمسلمين

translation: And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches the Prophet." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, and this [i.e., the Qur'an] is [in] a clear Arabic language.
interpretation: This verse addresses the claim made by the disbelievers that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was being taught the Qur'an by a human being, rather than receiving it directly from God. The verse refutes this claim by stating that the language of the person they are referring to is foreign, while the Qur'an is in a clear Arabic language. This serves to demonstrate that the Qur'an could not have been learned from a human source, but rather was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) directly by God.
orig: ولقد نعلم أنهم يقولون إنما يعلمه بشر لسان الذي يلحدون إليه أعجمي وهذا لسان عربي مبين

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the verses of Allah - Allah will not [choose to] guide them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject and refuse to believe in the signs and revelations of Allah will not receive guidance from Him. Instead, they will face a painful and severe punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: إن الذين لا يؤمنون بآيات الله لا يهديهم الله ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Only they invent falsehood who do not believe in the signs of Allah, and it is they who are the liars.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject the signs and messages of Allah are the ones who fabricate falsehoods. They are the true liars, as they deny the truth revealed by Allah and instead spread deception.
orig: إنما يفتري الكذب الذين لا يؤمنون بآيات الله وأولئك هم الكاذبون

translation: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief, [but] not [of] those who [willingly] open their breasts to disbelief, [for them is] a wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who consciously and willingly reject faith in Allah after having believed, except for those who are compelled to do so while their hearts remain firm in faith, will incur the wrath of Allah and face a severe punishment. The interpretation suggests that true faith cannot be forced, and that those who freely choose to abandon their belief will be held accountable for their decision.
orig: من كفر بالله من بعد إيمانه إلا من أكره وقلبه مطمئن بالإيمان ولكن من شرح بالكفر صدرا فعليهم غضب من الله ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: That is because they preferred the worldly life over the Hereafter, and that Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who prefer the temporary pleasures of this world over the eternal rewards of the Hereafter are disbelievers, and Allah will not guide them to the right path. It emphasizes the importance of prioritizing the Hereafter over the fleeting nature of this world.
orig: ذلك بأنهم استحبوا الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة وأن الله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: Those are the ones upon whose hearts and hearing and vision Allah has sealed, and those are the heedless.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have willfully turned away from the guidance of Allah, and as a result, their hearts, hearing, and vision have been sealed. They are heedless of the truth and have become oblivious to the signs of Allah in the universe and in their own selves.
orig: أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم وسمعهم وأبصارهم وأولئك هم الغافلون

translation: Undoubtedly, it is they who will be the losers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who disbelieve and reject the message of Islam will be the ultimate losers in the Hereafter. They will face the consequences of their actions and be deprived of the eternal rewards and blessings of the Afterlife.
orig: لا جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الخاسرون

translation: Then, indeed your Lord, to those who emigrated after they had been tried and then fought [for the cause of Allah ] and were patient - indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages those who have faced trials and tribulations for their faith, and have then migrated and fought for the cause of Allah, to be patient. It assures them that despite the hardships they have faced, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful towards them.
orig: ثم إن ربك للذين هاجروا من بعد ما فتنوا ثم جاهدوا وصبروا إن ربك من بعدها لغفور رحيم

translation: The Day every soul will come disputing [i.e., defending] for itself, and every soul will be fully compensated for what it did, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Judgment, when every person will be held accountable for their actions in life. On that day, each person will argue and defend their own actions, and they will be fully compensated - whether with reward or punishment - for what they did in the world. This emphasizes that there will be no injustice or unfairness on that Day, as each person will be judged fairly based on their own deeds.
orig: يوم تأتي كل نفس تجادل عن نفسها وتوفى كل نفس ما عملت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And Allah presents an example: a city which was safe and secure, its provision coming to it in abundance from every location, but it denied the favors of Allah. So Allah made it taste the envelopment of hunger and fear for what they had been doing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of ingratitude and disbelief in the face of Allah's blessings. The city was prosperous and secure, with abundant provision coming to it from all directions. However, the people denied and rejected Allah's favors, and as a result, they were made to suffer the hardship of hunger and fear as a punishment for their actions. The lesson here is that we must be grateful for Allah's blessings and not take them for granted, lest we face the consequences of our ingratitude.
orig: وضرب الله مثلا قرية كانت آمنة مطمئنة يأتيها رزقها رغدا من كل مكان فكفرت بأنعم الله فأذاقها الله لباس الجوع والخوف بما كانوا يصنعون

translation: And a messenger had certainly come to them from among themselves, but they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the people to whom a messenger was sent rejected the message, despite the messenger being one of their own. As a result, they were punished for their wrongdoing and injustice in rejecting the divine guidance brought to them.
orig: ولقد جاءهم رسول منهم فكذبوه فأخذهم العذاب وهم ظالمون

translation: So eat of what Allah has provided for you [which is] lawful and good. And be grateful for the favor of Allah if it is [indeed] Him that you worship.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to consume only what is lawful and wholesome, and to be grateful to Allah for the blessings He has provided. It reminds us that our worship of Allah should lead to gratitude and obedience, not just empty rituals.
orig: فكلوا مما رزقكم الله حلالا طيبا واشكروا نعمت الله إن كنتم إياه تعبدون

translation: He has only forbidden to you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the dietary restrictions in Islam, prohibiting the consumption of certain foods that are considered impure or unclean. The interpretation is that Allah has forbidden these items, but if a person is forced by necessity to consume them, without desire or transgression, then they are not sinful. This demonstrates the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, who understands the challenges and hardships that people may face.
orig: إنما حرم عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل لغير الله به فمن اضطر غير باغ ولا عاد فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And do not say about what your tongues assert of untruth, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to invent falsehood about Allah. Indeed, those who invent falsehood about Allah will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse warns against making claims about the lawfulness or unlawfulness of things based on one's own whims or desires, rather than on the clear teachings of the Qur'an and the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes that those who falsely attribute such rulings to Allah will not prosper, as they are engaging in a grave sin of fabricating lies against the Almighty.
orig: ولا تقولوا لما تصف ألسنتكم الكذب هذا حلال وهذا حرام لتفتروا على الله الكذب إن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب لا يفلحون

translation: A brief enjoyment, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the pleasures and comforts of this world are fleeting and temporary, and that those who indulge in them without regard for the Hereafter will face a severe and painful punishment.
orig: متاع قليل ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And upon those who became Jews We had imposed some of the [previous] prohibitions. But if they were to persist in their error, then indeed, your Lord, to those who have believed among them, would judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Jews had certain prohibitions and restrictions placed upon them by God, as a result of their own transgressions and wrongdoing. However, these prohibitions were not imposed upon them unjustly, but rather as a consequence of their own actions. The verse suggests that if the Jews were to persist in their erroneous ways, God would ultimately judge between the believers and non-believers among them on the Day of Resurrection, regarding the matters over which they differed.
orig: وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا ما قصصنا عليك من قبل وما ظلمناهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: Then, indeed your Lord - to those who have done wrong out of ignorance and then repented after that and corrected themselves - indeed, your Lord, [thereafter], is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's mercy and forgiveness towards those who have committed sins out of ignorance or mistake, but then repented and corrected their ways. It conveys the message that even if one has done wrong, they can still seek forgiveness from God and be granted it, as long as they sincerely turn back to the right path.
orig: ثم إن ربك للذين عملوا السوء بجهالة ثم تابوا من بعد ذلك وأصلحوا إن ربك من بعدها لغفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, Abraham was a [comprehensive] nation, [submitting] devoutly to Allah, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exemplary nature of Abraham's faith and devotion to Allah. It describes him as a comprehensive nation, meaning that he embodied the complete essence of true faith and submission to the Almighty. Abraham was a devout and upright servant of Allah, inclining towards the truth and rejecting the practice of associating partners with Allah, which is a form of polytheism.
orig: إن إبراهيم كان أمة قانتا لله حنيفا ولم يك من المشركين

translation: Grateful for His favors, He chose him and guided him to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being grateful to Allah for His blessings and guidance. It suggests that Allah has chosen and guided a person to the right path, and the appropriate response is to be thankful for this favor.
orig: شاكرا لأنعمه اجتباه وهداه إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And We have certainly given him [i.e., Abraham] good in this world, and indeed, he is in the Hereafter among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah bestowed upon the Prophet Abraham blessings and goodness in this worldly life, and that he will be among the righteous in the Hereafter. This highlights the virtue and status of Abraham as a prophet and a righteous servant of Allah, whose faith and deeds were pleasing to Allah both in this life and the next.
orig: وآتيناه في الدنيا حسنة وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], to follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to follow the pure monotheistic faith of Abraham, who worshipped God alone without associating partners with Him. The verse emphasizes that Abraham was not of those who committed polytheism or idolatry, and that the Prophet should emulate this example of pure, sincere devotion to the one true God.
orig: ثم أوحينا إليك أن اتبع ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: The Sabbath was only enjoined upon those who differed over it, and indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the observance of the Sabbath (Saturday) was a matter of disagreement and dispute among certain groups, and that ultimately, it is Allah who will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection regarding their differences on this matter. The implication is that the Sabbath was not a universal obligation, but rather a point of contention among certain people.
orig: إنما جعل السبت على الذين اختلفوا فيه وإن ربك ليحكم بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to invite others to the path of God with wisdom, good counsel, and the best form of dialogue. It emphasizes that God alone knows best who has strayed from the right path and who is rightly guided, so the believer's role is to convey the message in the most effective manner without passing judgment.
orig: ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: And if you punish [an enemy, O believers], punish with an equivalent of that with which you were harmed. But if you are patient - it is better for those who are patient.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to respond to harm with an equivalent punishment, but also highlights the virtue of patience and forbearance. It suggests that exercising restraint and enduring hardship is ultimately better for those who are steadfast in their faith.
orig: وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير للصابرين

translation: And be patient, and your patience is not but [through] Allah. And do not grieve over them and do not be in distress over what they conspire.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension all believers, to be patient and steadfast in the face of adversity and the plots of the disbelievers. The key message is that true patience and fortitude can only be achieved through reliance on and trust in Allah. The verse also reminds the believers not to be distressed or saddened by the schemes of their opponents, as Allah is in control and will ultimately prevail.
orig: واصبر وما صبرك إلا بالله ولا تحزن عليهم ولا تك في ضيق مما يمكرون

translation: Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is with those who are righteous and do good deeds. It suggests that those who have piety (taqwa) and engage in virtuous actions will be under Allah's protection and guidance.
orig: إن الله مع الذين اتقوا والذين هم محسنون

translation: Exalted is He who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse is a reference to the Night Journey (al-Isra’) of the Prophet Muhammad from Mecca to Jerusalem, and then his Ascension (al-Mi’raj) to the heavens. It highlights the divine power and authority of God, who transported His Messenger on this miraculous journey to show him some of His signs and wonders. The verse emphasizes God’s omniscience and omnipotence, as He is the All-Hearing and All-Seeing.
orig: سبحان الذي أسرى بعبده ليلا من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى الذي باركنا حوله لنريه من آياتنا إنه هو السميع البصير

translation: And We gave Moses the Book and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel [saying], 'Do not take other than Me as Disposer of affairs'.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Quran, which was revealed to Moses, was a guidance for the Children of Israel. It instructs them not to take any other besides God as their guardian, protector or disposer of their affairs. The verse highlights the importance of worshiping and relying solely on God, without associating partners with Him.
orig: وآتينا موسى الكتاب وجعلناه هدى لبني إسرائيل ألا تتخذوا من دوني وكيلا

translation: Offspring of those whom We carried [in the ship] with Noah. Indeed, he was a grateful servant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the blessed lineage of those who were saved from the flood during the time of the Prophet Noah. It highlights that the offspring of those who were carried in the ship with Noah were a righteous and grateful people, as Noah himself was described as a "grateful servant" of God.
orig: ذرية من حملنا مع نوح إنه كان عبدا شكورا

translation: And We had already written in the Psalm that the Children of Israel will spread corruption on the earth twice and will become tyrants of great arrogance.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the Children of Israel that they will commit corruption and arrogance on the earth twice. The first time refers to their corruption and oppression during the time of the Israelite kingdoms, and the second time refers to their corruption and arrogance after the advent of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him). This serves as a lesson that such behavior will not go unnoticed and will be met with consequences from Allah.
orig: وقضينا إلى بني إسرائيل في الكتاب لتفسدن في الأرض مرتين ولتعلن علوا كبيرا

translation: And when the promise of [one of] the two comes to pass, [We will send] your enemies to afflict you with severe torment, and they will enter the Mosque, as they entered it the first time, and to destroy whatever they come upon with [complete] destruction.
interpretation: This verse speaks of a divine promise that will come to pass, where the enemies of the believers will be sent to afflict them with severe punishment. The enemies will enter the sacred spaces of the believers, just as they had done before, and they will destroy everything in their path. This serves as a warning to the believers that they must remain steadfast in their faith, as the promise of God will ultimately be fulfilled.
orig: فإذا جاء وعد أولاهما بعثنا عليكم عبادا لنا أولي بأس شديد فجاسوا خلال الديار وكان وعدا مفعولا

translation: Then We gave you the turn to prevail over them. And We supported you with wealth and children and made you more numerous in manpower.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's continued support and empowerment of the believers, granting them victory, resources, and increasing their numbers to establish His religion. It encourages the believers to have faith in God's plan and to use the blessings bestowed upon them to further His cause.
orig: ثم رددنا لكم الكرة عليهم وأمددناكم بأموال وبنين وجعلناكم أكثر نفيرا

translation: If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, [it is] against yourselves. Then when the final [i.e., second] promise comes, [they will be ordered], "Distort your [once radiant] faces and taste the punishment of the Burning Fire."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the consequences of our actions, whether good or bad, ultimately affect ourselves. When we do good deeds, the benefits return to us, but when we do evil, the harm also falls upon us. The verse also warns that on the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers will suffer the punishment of the Hellfire, having their faces distorted in shame and regret for their past misdeeds.
orig: إن أحسنتم أحسنتم لأنفسكم وإن أسأتم فلها فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة ليسوءوا وجوهكم وليدخلوا المسجد كما دخلوه أول مرة وليتبروا ما علوا تتبيرا

translation: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy upon you, but if you return [to sin], We will return [to punishment]. And We have made Hell, for the disbelievers, a prison-bed.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah is merciful and willing to forgive those who repent, but warns that if they return to their sinful ways, they will face punishment. The verse also emphasizes that Hell is the ultimate destination for those who persistently reject faith and refuse to submit to Allah.
orig: عسى ربكم أن يرحمكم وإن عدتم عدنا وجعلنا جهنم للكافرين حصيرا

translation: Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable and gives good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an provides guidance and direction to the most upright and righteous path. It also gives glad tidings and a promise of a great reward to those believers who perform good deeds. The interpretation highlights the Qur'an's role as a source of guidance and motivation for the faithful to live righteously and earn the eternal reward in the Hereafter.
orig: إن هذا القرآن يهدي للتي هي أقوم ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم أجرا كبيرا

translation: And indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter - We have prepared for them a Painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject the belief in the afterlife will be subjected to a severe and painful punishment. It serves as a warning to those who deny the existence of the Hereafter, and underscores the importance of faith in the divine judgment that awaits us in the life to come.
orig: وأن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة أعتدنا لهم عذابا أليما

translation: And man supplicates for evil as he supplicates for good, and man is ever hasty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to be impatient and hasty, often supplicating for immediate gratification or relief from difficulties, even if it may not be in their best interest in the long run. It serves as a reminder that we should be measured and thoughtful in our prayers, seeking what is truly good for us, rather than being driven by impulse or a desire for quick results.
orig: ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير وكان الإنسان عجولا

translation: And We have made the night and the day as two [of Our] signs, and We have made the sign of the night obscure and made the sign of the day visible that you may seek bounty from your Lord and may know the number of years and the account [of time]. And all things We have set out in detail.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the alternation between night and day as signs of Allah's power and wisdom. The night is made obscure to allow people to rest and seek the bounty of Allah, while the day is made visible to facilitate their activities and to enable them to know the number of years and the account of time. This highlights the divine order and purpose behind the creation of the night and day, which serves as a means for human beings to recognize Allah's sovereignty and to organize their lives accordingly.
orig: وجعلنا الليل والنهار آيتين فمحونا آية الليل وجعلنا آية النهار مبصرة لتبتغوا فضلا من ربكم ولتعلموا عدد السنين والحساب وكل شيء فصلناه تفصيلا

translation: And every human being's fate have We attached to his neck, and We will bring forth for him, on the Day of Resurrection, a record which he will find spread open
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that each person is responsible for their own actions and will be held accountable on the Day of Judgment. The metaphor of "attaching one's fate to their neck" suggests that each person's deeds, whether good or bad, are inseparable from them and will be presented to them on the Day of Resurrection. The "record" that will be "spread open" represents the comprehensive documentation of a person's life and actions, which will be used to judge them.
orig: وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه ونخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه منشورا

translation: Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as accountant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of self-accountability. On the Day of Judgment, each person will be held responsible for their own actions and deeds, and their own record will be sufficient to judge them. The verse encourages individuals to carefully examine their own conduct and decisions, rather than relying on the judgment of others.
orig: اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا

translation: Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul. And whoever errs only errs against it. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And never would We punish until We have sent a messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes individual responsibility and accountability. It states that whoever chooses to be guided, does so for their own benefit, and whoever goes astray, does so to their own detriment. No one can bear the burden of another's sins or mistakes. Allah does not punish a people until He has sent them a messenger to guide them and make clear the path of truth.
orig: من اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وما كنا معذبين حتى نبعث رسولا

translation: And when We intend to destroy a city, We command its affluent but they defiantly disobey therein; so the word comes into effect upon it, and We destroy it with [complete] destruction.
interpretation: This verse suggests that when God intends to destroy a city or community, He first commands its wealthy and privileged members to obey and reform. However, if they persist in their defiance and corruption, then God's decree of punishment becomes inevitable and the city is destroyed completely.
orig: وإذا أردنا أن نهلك قرية أمرنا مترفيها ففسقوا فيها فحق عليها القول فدمرناها تدميرا

translation: And how many generations have We destroyed after Noah? And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs, Aware of the sins of His servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has the power to destroy civilizations and communities that turn away from Him, just as He destroyed many generations after the time of the Prophet Noah. It also affirms that Allah is fully aware of the sins and transgressions of His servants, and that He is the One who will hold them accountable.
orig: وكم أهلكنا من القرون من بعد نوح وكفى بربك بذنوب عباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: Whoever desires the immediate [i.e., this world] - We hasten for him from it what We will to whom We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will [enter to] burn, condemned and banished.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who are solely focused on the immediate pleasures and gains of this world, without consideration for the Hereafter. It indicates that while Allah may grant some people their worldly desires, the ultimate consequence for such a mindset is the punishment of Hell, which they will enter in a state of disgrace and rejection.
orig: من كان يريد العاجلة عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد ثم جعلنا له جهنم يصلاها مذموما مدحورا

translation: And whoever desires the Hereafter and exerts the effort due to it while he is a believer - it is those whose effort is ever appreciated [by Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving for the Hereafter with sincere faith and belief. It suggests that those who make the effort to do good deeds and prepare for the Afterlife, while maintaining their faith, will have their efforts appreciated and rewarded by Allah. The verse encourages believers to prioritize the Hereafter over the temporary pleasures of this world and to work diligently towards attaining Allah's pleasure and the rewards of the Afterlife.
orig: ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها وهو مؤمن فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا

translation: Nay, We supply (the necessities) to these as well as to those, the gifts of thy Lord. And the gifts of thy Lord are not, (in the least), restricted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God's bounty and provision are not limited to any particular group of people. Rather, God bestows His gifts and sustenance upon all, both the righteous and the wicked, without discrimination. This highlights the universality and impartiality of God's mercy and care for all of His creation.
orig: كلا نمد هؤلاء وهؤلاء من عطاء ربك وما كان عطاء ربك محظورا

translation: Look how We have preferred some over others. And the Hereafter is greater in degrees [of difference] and greater in distinction.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah has created people with different abilities, talents, and stations in life. Some are preferred over others, not due to any inherent superiority, but by Allah's wisdom and plan. The true distinction, however, lies in the Hereafter, where the degrees of difference and preference will be even greater, as the ultimate reward and punishment will be meted out according to one's deeds and faith.
orig: انظر كيف فضلنا بعضهم على بعض وللآخرة أكبر درجات وأكبر تفضيلا

translation: Do not set up with Allah another god, lest you sit condemned and forsaken.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping and believing in only one God, Allah. It warns against associating any other deity with Allah, as this would lead to condemnation and being forsaken. The interpretation suggests that true devotion and submission to the one true God is essential for a believer to avoid being condemned and abandoned.
