orig: لا تجعل مع الله إلها آخر فتقعد مذموما مخذولا

translation: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them reach old age [while] with you, say not to them [so much as], "Uff," and do not repel them but speak to them a noble word.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping only God and treating one's parents with kindness and respect, even as they grow old. It prohibits even the slightest expression of annoyance or irritation towards them, and instead commands speaking to them with gentleness and reverence. The verse underscores the duty of children to honor and care for their aging parents.
orig: وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه وبالوالدين إحسانا إما يبلغن عندك الكبر أحدهما أو كلاهما فلا تقل لهما أف ولا تنهرهما وقل لهما قولا كريما

translation: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of showing humility, compassion and gratitude towards one's parents. It instructs the believer to be humble and merciful towards their parents, and to pray for Allah's mercy upon them, in recognition of the care and upbringing they provided when the believer was young and dependent.
orig: واخفض لهما جناح الذل من الرحمة وقل رب ارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا

translation: Your Lord is most knowing of what is within yourselves. If you should be righteous, then indeed He is ever, to the often returning [to Him], Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God is all-knowing and aware of the innermost thoughts and intentions of human beings. It encourages people to be righteous, as God is forgiving towards those who frequently repent and turn back to Him.
orig: ربكم أعلم بما في نفوسكم إن تكونوا صالحين فإنه كان للأوابين غفورا

translation: And give the relative his right, and [also] the poor and the traveler, and do not spend wastefully.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to fulfill the rights of their relatives, the poor, and travelers, and to avoid wasteful spending. It emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's social and familial obligations, and practicing moderation and generosity in one's spending.
orig: وآت ذا القربى حقه والمسكين وابن السبيل ولا تبذر تبذيرا

translation: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, and ever has Satan been to his Lord ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are wasteful and extravagant in their spending are akin to the devils, as they share a similar disregard for the blessings of Allah and a lack of gratitude towards their Lord. The comparison highlights the notion that wastefulness and ingratitude are closely linked, and those who engage in such behavior are aligning themselves with the ways of Satan, who was forever ungrateful to Allah.
orig: إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين وكان الشيطان لربه كفورا

translation: And if you turn away from them seeking mercy from your Lord which you expect, then speak to them a gentle word.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet (peace be upon him) to be patient and gentle with people, even if they reject his message. It suggests that he should seek Allah's mercy and forgiveness, and then speak to them in a kind and compassionate manner, in the hope that they may be receptive to the message of Islam.
orig: وإما تعرضن عنهم ابتغاء رحمة من ربك ترجوها فقل لهم قولا ميسورا

translation: And do not make your hand [as] chained to your neck or extend it completely [i.e., outstretch it] and [thereby] become blamed and insolvent.
interpretation: This verse advises against two extremes in spending and generosity. It warns against being stingy, like chaining one's hand to one's neck, and against being excessively generous to the point of becoming impoverished. The ideal is to spend moderately and judiciously, avoiding both extremes.
orig: ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط فتقعد ملوما محسورا

translation: Indeed, your Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed, He is to His servants Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Lord, is the ultimate provider of sustenance and resources. He has the power to expand or restrict the provision for whomever He wills, according to His divine wisdom and knowledge. This serves as a reminder that we should trust in Allah's plan and not be overly concerned with the material aspects of life, as He is All-Knowing and All-Seeing of the needs of His servants.
orig: إن ربك يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: And do not kill your children out of fear of poverty. We provide for them and for you. Indeed, their killing is ever a great sin.
interpretation: This verse prohibits the killing of children out of fear of poverty, as God is the provider for all. The killing of children is considered a grave sin in Islam.
orig: ولا تقتلوا أولادكم خشية إملاق نحن نرزقهم وإياكم إن قتلهم كان خطئا كبيرا

translation: And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and is evil as a way.
interpretation: This verse commands Muslims to abstain from all forms of unlawful sexual relations, as it is a grave sin and an evil path to follow. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining moral and ethical boundaries in one"s personal life and relationships.
orig: ولا تقربوا الزنا إنه كان فاحشة وساء سبيلا

translation: And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority, but let him not exceed limits in [his] slaughter. Indeed, he has been supported [by the law].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of human life and the gravity of unjust killing. It forbids the taking of life except in cases where it is justified by law, such as in self-defense or as punishment for a serious crime. The verse also grants the heir of a person who is unjustly killed the authority to seek justice, but cautions against exceeding the bounds of law and justice in doing so. The overall message is one of respecting the value of human life and upholding the rule of law.
orig: ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ومن قتل مظلوما فقد جعلنا لوليه سلطانا فلا يسرف في القتل إنه كان منصورا

translation: And do not approach the wealth of the orphan except in the way that is best until he reaches maturity. And fulfill [every] commitment. Indeed, the commitment is ever [that about which one will be] questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of protecting and managing the wealth of orphans in a responsible manner, until they reach adulthood. It also stresses the need to fulfill all commitments and obligations, as one will be held accountable for them.
orig: ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن حتى يبلغ أشده وأوفوا بالعهد إن العهد كان مسئولا

translation: And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with an even balance. That is the best [way] and best in result.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fairness, honesty and integrity in commercial transactions. It instructs people to measure and weigh accurately, using a balanced and just scale. Doing so is not only the right thing to do, but it also leads to the best outcomes for all involved. This principle of fairness and honesty should be applied in all aspects of life, not just in business dealings.
orig: وأوفوا الكيل إذا كلتم وزنوا بالقسطاس المستقيم ذلك خير وأحسن تأويلا

translation: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse instructs us not to make claims or take actions based on incomplete or uncertain knowledge. We are accountable for how we use our faculties of hearing, sight and understanding. We must be careful to only speak and act upon what we truly know, and not make assumptions or speculations beyond our actual knowledge.
orig: ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا

translation: And do not walk upon the earth with [ostentatious] conceit. Indeed, Allah does not like any self-conceited boaster
interpretation: This verse advises against arrogance and self-conceit. It reminds us that we are limited in our abilities and cannot control or conquer the earth. We should walk with humility and modesty, recognizing that true power and greatness belong to Allah alone.
orig: ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا إنك لن تخرق الأرض ولن تبلغ الجبال طولا

translation: And all of that - its evil is ever, in the sight of your Lord, detested.
interpretation: This verse conveys that all forms of wrongdoing and sinful acts are displeasing and abhorrent to Allah. It emphasizes that Allah, the Lord, views such misdeeds with disdain and disapproval. The verse serves as a warning to believers to refrain from engaging in any evil or undesirable actions, as they are unacceptable in the sight of the Almighty.
orig: كل ذلك كان سيئه عند ربك مكروها

translation: That is from what your Lord has revealed to you, [O Muhammad], of wisdom. And do not make [as equal] with Allah another deity, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed and banished.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the wisdom that has been revealed to the Prophet Muhammad by Allah. It cautions against associating any other deity with Allah, as that would lead to being condemned and cast into Hell. The interpretation is that one should seek guidance solely from the wisdom revealed by Allah, and refrain from worshipping any other god, for that would be a grave sin.
orig: ذلك مما أوحى إليك ربك من الحكمة ولا تجعل مع الله إلها آخر فتلقى في جهنم ملوما مدحورا

translation: Has then your Lord (O pagans!) preferred for you sons, and taken for Himself from among the angels daughters? Verily, you indeed utter an awful saying.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the pagan Arabs who believed that God had daughters, while preferring sons for themselves. The verse is highlighting the absurdity of this belief, as it is inconceivable that the all-powerful, all-knowing God would have offspring, let alone female offspring which were considered inferior in that society. The verse is emphasizing that this is an "awful saying" and a grave error in their beliefs about the nature of God.
orig: أفأصفاكم ربكم بالبنين واتخذ من الملائكة إناثا إنكم لتقولون قولا عظيما

translation: And We have certainly diversified [the contents] in this Qur'an that mankind may be reminded, but it does not increase them except in aversion.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Qur'an has been presented in a variety of ways to remind and guide humanity, but rather than leading to increased faith and obedience, it often results in increased aversion and rejection from people. The Qur'an is a profound and multifaceted revelation, but its message is not always readily accepted by those who are inclined towards disbelief and turning away from the truth.
orig: ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن ليذكروا وما يزيدهم إلا نفورا

translation: Say, "If there had been with Him [any] gods, as they say, then they [each] would have sought to the Owner of the Throne a way [to Him]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and supremacy of God. It refutes the idea of multiple deities by stating that if there were other gods, they would have tried to find a way to the Owner of the Throne (i.e., the one true God). This suggests that the existence of a single, all-powerful God is the only rational explanation for the universe.
orig: قل لو كان معه آلهة كما يقولون إذا لابتغوا إلى ذي العرش سبيلا

translation: Exalted is He and high [above all] from what they say, [a great exaltation].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute transcendence and supremacy of Allah over all that is said or attributed to Him. It rejects any notion of Allah having partners, children, or being subject to human limitations or imperfections. The phrase "exalted is He" conveys the idea of Allah's infinite perfection, majesty, and freedom from all deficiencies that are associated with created beings.
orig: سبحانه وتعالى عما يقولون علوا كبيرا

translation: The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them exalt Him. And there is not a thing that does not exalt [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their [way of] exalting. Indeed, He is Ever-Forbearing and Oft-Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all of creation, from the heavens to the earth and everything in between, glorifies and praises Allah. Even things that we may not perceive as having the capacity to glorify Allah, like inanimate objects, do so in their own way. However, humans often fail to comprehend the manner in which all of creation worships and submits to the Almighty. This is because Allah is Forbearing and Forgiving, and does not demand that we understand the intricacies of His creation's worship, but rather that we focus on our own worship and submission to Him.
orig: تسبح له السماوات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم إنه كان حليما غفورا

translation: And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a concealed partition.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who do not believe in the Hereafter will not be able to fully comprehend the message of the Qur'an. There is a veil or barrier that prevents them from understanding the deeper spiritual and metaphysical truths contained in the Qur'anic revelation. This verse emphasizes the importance of faith in the Hereafter as a prerequisite for understanding the Qur'an.
orig: وإذا قرأت القرآن جعلنا بينك وبين الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة حجابا مستورا

translation: And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn back in aversion.
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people are unwilling to understand the message of the Qur'an due to their own biases and preconceptions. They have a mental and spiritual barrier that prevents them from comprehending the divine guidance. When the oneness of God is mentioned, they turn away in rejection, unable or unwilling to accept the truth.
orig: وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإذا ذكرت ربك في القرآن وحده ولوا على أدبارهم نفورا

translation: We know best what they listen to when they listen to you and when they are in private conversation. When the wrongdoers say, "You follow not but a man affected by magic."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah knows best what the disbelievers are thinking and saying about the Prophet Muhammad, even in their private conversations. It refutes the claim that the Prophet is simply a man under the influence of magic, and affirms that he is a true messenger of Allah.
orig: نحن أعلم بما يستمعون به إذ يستمعون إليك وإذ هم نجوى إذ يقول الظالمون إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا

translation: Look how they strike for you comparisons; but they have strayed, so they cannot [find] a way.
interpretation: This verse encourages us to reflect on how disbelievers try to distort the truth by drawing false analogies and comparisons to discredit the message of Islam. However, their attempts are misguided and they are unable to find a valid path, as they have strayed from the right guidance.
orig: انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال فضلوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلا

translation: And they say, "When we have become bones and crumbled particles, will we indeed be [re]created in a new creation?"
interpretation: This verse expresses the skepticism of the disbelievers regarding the resurrection and the afterlife. They find it hard to believe that after their bodies have decomposed and turned into dust, they will be resurrected and brought back to life in a new form. The Qur'an answers this skepticism by affirming the power of God to recreate and resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا

translation: Say, 'Be stones or iron,'
interpretation: This verse is a metaphorical expression calling for steadfastness, resilience, and strength in the face of adversity. The imagery of being like stones or iron suggests the need to be unyielding, unwavering, and impervious to the challenges and pressures one may face. The interpretation encourages the believers to adopt a resolute and determined attitude in their faith and actions, remaining firm and unshaken regardless of the circumstances.
orig: قل كونوا حجارة أو حديدا

translation: Or have they created [anything] that the creation [of Allah] has not produced? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain. Or have they the depositories of your Lord? Or are they the controllers [of them]?
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers to produce something that is not already created by Allah. It emphasizes that the creation of the heavens and the earth is beyond human capability, and that the disbelievers have no control over the treasures and resources of Allah. The verse also suggests that the disbelievers will be perplexed and doubtful when asked about the resurrection, and that they will express their uncertainty about it.
orig: أو خلقا مما يكبر في صدوركم فسيقولون من يعيدنا قل الذي فطركم أول مرة فسينغضون إليك رءوسهم ويقولون متى هو قل عسى أن يكون قريبا

translation: The Day He will call you, and you will respond with [words of] His praise and you will think that you had not remained [in the world] except for a little while.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Resurrection, when people will be summoned to account for their deeds. On that day, they will respond with praise and glorification of God, realizing that their worldly life was but a fleeting moment compared to the eternal Hereafter.
orig: يوم يدعوكم فتستجيبون بحمده وتظنون إن لبثتم إلا قليلا

translation: And tell My servants to say that which is best. Indeed, Satan induces [dissension] among them. Indeed, Satan is to man a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to speak in the most virtuous and beneficial manner, as Satan seeks to sow discord and enmity among people. It emphasizes that Satan is an avowed enemy of humanity, and that believers should be mindful of his schemes and avoid falling into his traps.
orig: وقل لعبادي يقولوا التي هي أحسن إن الشيطان ينزغ بينهم إن الشيطان كان للإنسان عدوا مبينا

translation: Your Lord is most knowing of you. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you or, if He wills, He will punish you. And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], over them as a guardian.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah (God) is all-knowing and has complete authority over the fate of His creation. He may choose to show mercy or punishment to people based on His divine will and wisdom. The verse also clarifies that the Prophet Muhammad was not sent as a guardian or overseer to coerce people, but rather as a messenger to convey the divine message.
orig: ربكم أعلم بكم إن يشأ يرحمكم أو إن يشأ يعذبكم وما أرسلناك عليهم وكيلا

translation: And your Lord is most knowing of whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And We have preferred some of the prophets over others, and to David We gave the Zabur.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Lord, has the ultimate knowledge and understanding of all that exists in the heavens and the earth. It also highlights that Allah has chosen to bestow certain prophets with a higher status and honor than others, and that He granted the Zabur (Psalms) to the prophet David.
orig: وربك أعلم بمن في السماوات والأرض ولقد فضلنا بعض النبيين على بعض وآتينا داوود زبورا

translation: Say, 'Call upon those you have claimed [as gods] besides Him, for they do not possess the [power to remove] adversity from you or [to] transfer [it].'
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to challenge the polytheists who worship false gods besides Allah, and to tell them that these gods have no power to remove harm or provide any benefit. It emphasizes that only Allah has the true power and authority to control the affairs of the universe.
orig: قل ادعوا الذين زعمتم من دونه فلا يملكون كشف الضر عنكم ولا تحويلا

translation: Those [who] call upon their Lord, seeking means to Him, [and] hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is ever feared.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the believers who sincerely seek closeness to Allah through righteous deeds and supplication. They hope for Allah's mercy and forgiveness, while also fearing His punishment. The interpretation is that the believers should have a balanced approach of seeking Allah's pleasure, being hopeful in His mercy, and being cautious of His punishment, as the punishment of the Lord is indeed a grave matter to be feared.
orig: أولئك الذين يدعون يبتغون إلى ربهم الوسيلة أيهم أقرب ويرجون رحمته ويخافون عذابه إن عذاب ربك كان محذورا

translation: And there is no city but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment. That has ever been in a register inscribed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute sovereignty and power over all creation. It suggests that no community or civilization is immune from divine judgment and punishment if they persist in wrongdoing and reject faith. The verse serves as a warning to humanity to live righteously and heed God's commands, lest they face the consequences of their actions on the Day of Resurrection.
orig: وإن من قرية إلا نحن مهلكوها قبل يوم القيامة أو معذبوها عذابا شديدا كان ذلك في الكتاب مسطورا

translation: And We did not send the signs except to warn and deter, but the former peoples denied them, and We gave Thamud the she-camel - [she was] a visible [sign], but they wronged her. And We do not send the signs except as a deterrence.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the signs and miracles sent by God are meant to warn and deter people, not to compel them to believe. However, even when such clear signs are provided, people often reject them out of stubbornness or arrogance, as was the case with the people of Thamud who wronged the she-camel sent to them as a sign. The verse suggests that God sends these signs not to force belief, but to provide a clear warning and deterrence against disbelief and wrongdoing.
orig: وما منعنا أن نرسل بالآيات إلا أن كذب بها الأولون وآتينا ثمود الناقة مبصرة فظلموا بها وما نرسل بالآيات إلا تخويفا

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We said to you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people." And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people and the tree [mentioned] in the Qur'an. And We threaten them, but it only increases them in great transgression.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's knowledge and power encompasses all of humanity. The vision shown to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was a test for the people, as was the mention of the 'accursed tree' in the Quran. Despite the warnings given to them, the people only increased in their arrogance and rebellion against Allah.
orig: وإذ قلنا لك إن ربك أحاط بالناس وما جعلنا الرؤيا التي أريناك إلا فتنة للناس والشجرة الملعونة في القرآن ونخوفهم فما يزيدهم إلا طغيانا كبيرا

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblees. He said, "Shall I prostrate to one You created from clay?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the disobedience of Iblees (Satan) who refused to prostrate to Adam, despite the command from God. Iblees saw himself as superior to Adam, who was created from clay, and thus refused to submit. This act of disobedience led to Iblees being cursed and expelled from the divine presence, demonstrating the importance of humility and obedience to God's commands.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس قال أأسجد لمن خلقت طينا

translation: He said, 'Have you seen this one whom You have honored above me? If You will delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely destroy his descendants, except for a few.'
interpretation: This verse depicts Satan's arrogance and jealousy towards the honor bestowed upon Adam by God. Satan threatens to mislead and corrupt Adam's descendants, except for a few who will remain steadfast in their faith, if God were to delay his punishment until the Day of Resurrection. The verse highlights Satan's determination to lead humanity astray and his resentment towards God's favoring of Adam.
orig: قال أرأيتك هذا الذي كرمت علي لئن أخرتن إلى يوم القيامة لأحتنكن ذريته إلا قليلا

translation: He said, 'Go, and whoever follows you among them - then indeed, Hell will be the recompense of you, [all], an ample recompense.'
interpretation: This verse is a warning from God to those who follow the path of evil and disobedience. It suggests that those who choose to follow the wrong path will be held accountable and face the severe punishment of Hell, which is a fitting and just recompense for their actions.
orig: قال اذهب فمن تبعك منهم فإن جهنم جزاؤكم جزاء موفورا

translation: And incite [to senselessness] whoever you can among them with your voice and assault them with your horses and foot soldiers and become a partner in their wealth and their children and promise them. But Satan does not promise them except delusion.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to use various means to confront and defeat the disbelievers, including using one's voice to incite them, deploying military forces, and becoming involved in their financial and family affairs. However, it also warns that Satan's promises to the disbelievers are nothing but deception and false hope.
orig: واستفزز من استطعت منهم بصوتك وأجلب عليهم بخيلك ورجلك وشاركهم في الأموال والأولاد وعدهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا

translation: Indeed, [O Muhammad], over My [faithful] servants you have no authority. And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) has no authority or control over the believers. Their faith and devotion belong solely to Allah, the Lord and Protector, who is sufficient as a Guardian and Disposer of all affairs.
orig: إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان وكفى بربك وكيلا

translation: Your Lord is the One who drives the ships for you through the sea so that you may seek of His bounty. Indeed, He has ever been to you a Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's providence and care for humanity. It highlights how God facilitates our ability to travel and seek provision and sustenance through the ships that sail on the seas. This is a manifestation of God's mercy and benevolence towards us, as He has made the world and its resources accessible for our benefit.
orig: ربكم الذي يزجي لكم الفلك في البحر لتبتغوا من فضله إنه كان بكم رحيما

translation: And when adversity touches you at sea, lost are [all] those you invoke except for Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away [from Him]. And ever is man ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to turn to God only in times of distress, but then to turn away from Him when the crisis has passed. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining faith and gratitude to God at all times, not just when facing difficulties.
orig: وإذا مسكم الضر في البحر ضل من تدعون إلا إياه فلما نجاكم إلى البر أعرضتم وكان الإنسان كفورا

translation: Then have you felt secure that [instead] He will not cause a part of the land to swallow you or send against you a storm of stones? Then you would not find for yourselves a guardian.
interpretation: This verse warns against a false sense of security and complacency. It reminds that Allah has the power to punish and destroy, and that we should not take His blessings for granted. The interpretation is that we must remain vigilant, humble and seek Allah's protection, for He alone can safeguard us from calamities.
orig: أفأمنتم أن يخسف بكم جانب البر أو يرسل عليكم حاصبا ثم لا تجدوا لكم وكيلا

translation: Or have you been given the assurance that when you are in the grave, you will be brought out [in resurrection]? Or do you feel secure that [from] the heaven [i.e., Allah] He will not send upon you a storm of stones? Or have you felt secure that [from] the heaven He will not send against you a wind carrying sediment [i.e., a thunderstorm] and you would then know how [severe] was My warning?
interpretation: This verse warns against complacency and overconfidence in one's security and survival. It reminds that the afterlife and the power of Allah are not to be taken lightly. The verse cautions that one can be easily destroyed by the forces of nature, which are under Allah's control, if one does not heed the warnings and remain mindful of one's accountability before Allah.
orig: أم أمنتم أن يعيدكم فيه تارة أخرى فيرسل عليكم قاصفا من الريح فيغرقكم بما كفرتم ثم لا تجدوا لكم علينا به تبيعا

translation: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the honor and dignity that God has bestowed upon humanity. He has granted us the ability to live and thrive on both land and sea, and has provided us with sustenance and good things. Moreover, God has preferred and exalted us above many of His other creations, demonstrating His special regard for mankind.
orig: ولقد كرمنا بني آدم وحملناهم في البر والبحر ورزقناهم من الطيبات وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا تفضيلا

translation: The Day We will call forth every people with their record [of deeds]. So whoever is given his record in his right hand - those will read their records, and they will not be wronged, [even as much as] a thread [in the long slit of a date seed].
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions in life. Those who are given their record of deeds in their right hand, indicating they have done good, will read their records and will not be wronged even in the slightest. This emphasizes the perfect justice and fairness of God's judgment, where no one will be treated unfairly.
orig: يوم ندعو كل أناس بإمامهم فمن أوتي كتابه بيمينه فأولئك يقرءون كتابهم ولا يظلمون فتيلا

translation: And whoever is blind in this [life] will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in [his] way.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are spiritually blind and unable to see the truth in this life will also be blind to the realities of the Hereafter, and will be even more lost and misguided in the afterlife.
orig: ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا

translation: And indeed, they were about to tempt you away from that which We revealed to you in order [for you] to invent about Us other than that, and then they would have taken you as an intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse warns the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that the disbelievers were trying to lead him astray from the revelation he had received from God, in order to make him fabricate something else in God's name. Had he succumbed to their temptation, they would have taken him as a close confidant.
orig: وإن كادوا ليفتنونك عن الذي أوحينا إليك لتفتري علينا غيره وإذا لاتخذوك خليلا

translation: And if We had not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined to them a little
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of Allah's guidance and support for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Without Allah's intervention, the Prophet might have been inclined to compromise with the unbelievers to some degree, even though this would have been a small concession. The verse underscores the Prophet's need for divine assistance to remain steadfast on the path of truth and not succumb to the temptations of the disbelievers.
orig: ولولا أن ثبتناك لقد كدت تركن إليهم شيئا قليلا

translation: Then if We should let you [O Muhammad] taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death, then [even then] you would not find for yourself any helper against Us.
interpretation: This verse conveys a stern warning that even if the Prophet Muhammad were to face double the punishment of life and death, he would still have no one to help him against the decree of Allah. It emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah, and the futility of seeking any protector or helper besides Him.
orig: إذا لأذقناك ضعف الحياة وضعف الممات ثم لا تجد لك علينا نصيرا

translation: And indeed, they were about to tempt you away from that by which We had revealed to you, in order to [make] you invent about Us something else; and then they would have taken you as a friend.
interpretation: This verse warns the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that his opponents were trying to seduce him away from the divine revelation he had received, in order to make him fabricate something false about God. However, their plot would not last long, as they would soon cease to have any influence over him.
orig: وإن كادوا ليستفزونك من الأرض ليخرجوك منها وإذا لا يلبثون خلافك إلا قليلا

translation: The way of those whom We have sent before you of Our messengers - and you will not find in Our way any alteration.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consistency and continuity of the divine message that has been revealed through the prophets throughout history. Just as previous messengers were sent by God to guide humanity, the current prophet (in this case, Prophet Muhammad) is also part of this divine tradition. The interpretation is that the fundamental principles and teachings of the divine message remain unchanged, as the way of God is eternal and immutable.
orig: سنة من قد أرسلنا قبلك من رسلنا ولا تجد لسنتنا تحويلا

translation: Establish prayer from the decline of the sun [from its meridian] until the darkness of the night and [also] the Qur'an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to perform the five daily prayers, from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night. It also mentions the special importance of the dawn prayer, which is witnessed by the angels.
orig: أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا

translation: And from [part of] the night, pray with it as additional [worship] for you; it is expected that your Lord will resurrect you to a praised station.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to engage in voluntary night prayers (tahajjud) as a means of drawing closer to God. The "praised station" refers to a lofty spiritual rank that the believer may attain through this supererogatory act of worship, which is pleasing to God and may lead to the person being raised to a high position on the Day of Resurrection.
orig: ومن الليل فتهجد به نافلة لك عسى أن يبعثك ربك مقاما محمودا

translation: And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority."
interpretation: This verse implores God to guide the believer to enter and exit life in a righteous manner, and to grant them divine authority and support to live a virtuous life. It reflects the desire for God's guidance and assistance in navigating the trials and tribulations of this world.
orig: وقل رب أدخلني مدخل صدق وأخرجني مخرج صدق واجعل لي من لدنك سلطانا نصيرا

translation: And say, "Truth has come, and falsehood has departed. Indeed is falsehood, [by nature], ever bound to depart."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the truth has prevailed and falsehood has been vanquished. It is a declaration that the truth is eternal and will always triumph over falsehood, which is inherently transient and bound to disappear. The message is one of hope and reassurance that righteousness will ultimately prevail.
orig: وقل جاء الحق وزهق الباطل إن الباطل كان زهوقا

translation: And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a source of healing and mercy for those who believe in it and follow its guidance. However, for those who persist in wrongdoing and rejection of the truth, the Qur'an does not bring them guidance and instead leads them to further loss and destruction.
orig: وننزل من القرآن ما هو شفاء ورحمة للمؤمنين ولا يزيد الظالمين إلا خسارا

translation: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; and when evil touches him, he is in despair.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of human beings to become ungrateful and complacent when they are blessed with good fortune, while becoming despondent and hopeless when faced with adversity. It suggests that the human condition is marked by a lack of steadfastness and a tendency to be easily swayed by the ups and downs of life, rather than maintaining a balanced and resilient attitude.
orig: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه وإذا مسه الشر كان يئوسا

translation: Say, "Each works according to his manner, but your Lord is most knowing of who is best guided."
interpretation: This verse encourages people to recognize that individuals have different ways of acting and behaving, and that God knows best who is on the right path. It suggests that one should not judge others harshly, but rather focus on one's own actions and strive to be guided in the right direction.
orig: قل كل يعمل على شاكلته فربكم أعلم بمن هو أهدى سبيلا

translation: And they ask you, [O Muhammad], about the soul. Say, "The soul is of the affair [i.e., concern] of my Lord. And you [i.e., mankind] have not been given of knowledge except a little."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limited nature of human knowledge, particularly regarding the soul. It suggests that the true nature of the soul is known only to God, and that humans have been given only a small fraction of the knowledge that God possesses. This serves to humble and remind us of our own limitations, and the need to turn to God for guidance and understanding on matters that are beyond our full comprehension.
orig: ويسألونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا

translation: And if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you. Then you would not find for yourself concerning Us any protector.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of God. It suggests that if God so wills, He can easily take away the revelation that has been given to the Prophet Muhammad. This serves as a reminder that the Qur'an and the message it contains are entirely dependent on the will and mercy of God, and that the Prophet has no power or authority over it. The verse also highlights the importance of the believers' reliance on God alone, and not on any other intermediary or protector.
orig: ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا

translation: Except as a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, His favor upon you has ever been great.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the guidance and blessings bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) are a mercy from Allah, the Almighty. It emphasizes that the Prophet’s mission and the revelation of the Qur’an are not due to his own merit, but rather a great favor and blessing from his Lord. This serves to remind us that all good that comes to us is ultimately a mercy and grace from Allah, and we should be grateful for His endless bounties.
orig: إلا رحمة من ربك إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا

translation: Say, "If mankind and the jinn gathered in order to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce the like of it, even if they were to each other assistants."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine and inimitable nature of the Qur'an. It challenges all of humanity and the jinn (supernatural beings) to produce a text that is comparable to the Qur'an in its eloquence, depth, and transformative power. The verse asserts that this is an impossible task, even if all of creation were to collaborate, as the Qur'an is a miraculous revelation from God that cannot be replicated by any created being.
orig: قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن لا يأتون بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا

translation: And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example, but most of the people refused [anything] except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an contains a wide variety of examples, parables, and guidance for humanity, but most people choose to reject and disbelieve it instead of accepting the truth it presents.
orig: ولقد صرفنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا

translation: And they say, "We will never believe you until you cause to gush forth for us from the ground a spring."
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and unwillingness of some people to believe in the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) without seeing a miraculous sign. It suggests that they were demanding a specific demonstration of divine power, rather than accepting the message based on its merits and the Prophet's own integrity. The interpretation is that true faith should not be conditional on the performance of miracles, but rather on the recognition of the truth and the willingness to submit to it.
orig: وقالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا

translation: Or you have a garden of palm trees and grapes and make the rivers flow abundantly through it
interpretation: This verse is encouraging the believer to strive for the hereafter and to not be content with the temporary pleasures of this world. The imagery of a lush garden with flowing rivers is used to represent the eternal bliss and abundance that awaits the righteous in the Afterlife. The message is to focus on attaining the pleasure of Allah and the rewards of the Hereafter, rather than being distracted by the fleeting delights of this world.
orig: أو تكون لك جنة من نخيل وعنب فتفجر الأنهار خلالها تفجيرا

translation: Or do the heavens fall upon us in fragments as you have claimed, or do you bring Allah and the angels as [an embodied] tribe?
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers who make outrageous claims against the truth of Islam. It questions whether they truly believe that the heavens will fall upon them in pieces, or that they can summon Allah and the angels to their aid as a tribe or group. The underlying message is that such claims are absurd and the disbelievers will be held accountable for their rejection of the truth.
orig: أو تسقط السماء كما زعمت علينا كسفا أو تأتي بالله والملائكة قبيلا

translation: Or you have a house of gold or you ascend into the heaven. And [even then] we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we may read." Say, "Exalted is my Lord! Was I ever but a human messenger?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers who demand extraordinary signs and miracles as a condition for their belief in the Prophet Muhammad. The verse emphasizes that even if the Prophet were to possess great wealth or ascend to the heavens, the disbelievers would still not believe in him unless he brought down a physical book from God. The Prophet's response is to glorify God and affirm that he is but a human messenger, not a divine being, and that his message comes from God alone.
orig: أو يكون لك بيت من زخرف أو ترقى في السماء ولن نؤمن لرقيك حتى تنزل علينا كتابا نقرؤه قل سبحان ربي هل كنت إلا بشرا رسولا

translation: And nothing has prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human messenger?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and resistance that some people had towards accepting the message of Islam, even when it was clearly presented to them. The verse suggests that the primary reason for their disbelief was their inability to accept that a human being could be chosen by God as a messenger. This reflects a common human tendency to be skeptical of the divine when it is manifested in a human form, rather than in some more extraordinary or supernatural way. The verse encourages us to overcome such biases and to be open-minded and receptive to the guidance that comes to us, regardless of the form it takes.
orig: وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى إلا أن قالوا أبعث الله بشرا رسولا

translation: Say, "If there were upon the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel [as a] messenger."
interpretation: This verse suggests that if there were angels living on the earth, God would have sent an angel messenger to them from the heavens, just as He has sent human messengers to guide humanity. This highlights the wisdom and mercy of God in choosing human messengers to convey His message, rather than angels, as humans can better relate to and understand the divine guidance.
orig: قل لو كان في الأرض ملائكة يمشون مطمئنين لنزلنا عليهم من السماء ملكا رسولا

translation: Say, "[Allah alone] is sufficient as Witness between me and you. Indeed, He is ever, concerning His servants, Aware and Seeing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone is the ultimate witness and judge between the Prophet Muhammad and his people. Allah is fully aware of all their actions and is all-seeing, so He is the only one who can truly judge the truth of the Prophet's message and the people's response to it. This serves to reassure the Prophet that he has fulfilled his duty and that the final judgment rests with Allah.
orig: قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: And whoever Allah guides - he is the [rightly] guided. And whoever He sends astray - you will never find for them protectors besides Him. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection [fallen] on their faces - blind, dumb and deaf. Their refuge is Hell, and whenever it subsides, We increase them in blazing fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of Allah in guiding people to the right path. Those whom Allah guides are rightly guided, while those whom He sends astray will have no one to protect them. On the Day of Resurrection, the disbelievers will be gathered before Allah in a state of utter helplessness and humiliation, blind, dumb, and deaf, with Hell as their final abode. Whenever the intensity of their punishment subsides, Allah will increase it further, highlighting the severity of their eternal torment.
orig: ومن يهد الله فهو المهتد ومن يضلل فلن تجد لهم أولياء من دونه ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا وبكما وصما مأواهم جهنم كلما خبت زدناهم سعيرا

translation: That is their recompense because they disbelieved in Our verses and said, "When we are bones and crumbled particles, will we [truly] be resurrected [in] a new creation?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the punishment of those who reject the signs and messages of God, and who doubt the reality of the Resurrection and the Afterlife. The verse emphasizes that their denial of these fundamental Islamic beliefs will result in a severe recompense, as they will be resurrected and held accountable for their disbelief and rejection of the truth.
orig: ذلك جزاؤهم بأنهم كفروا بآياتنا وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا

translation: Have they not considered that Allah who created the heavens and earth is [the one] Able to create the likes of them? And He has appointed for them a term, about which there is no doubt. But the wrongdoers refuse [anything] except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the power and ability of Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. Just as Allah has created the entire universe, He is also capable of creating human beings and giving them a set lifespan. However, the wrongdoers stubbornly refuse to acknowledge this truth and instead choose to disbelieve.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض قادر على أن يخلق مثلهم وجعل لهم أجلا لا ريب فيه فأبى الظالمون إلا كفورا

translation: Say, "If you possessed the treasures of the mercy of my Lord, you would [still] hold back out of fear of spending them." And ever has man been stingy."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that even if people had the treasures of God's mercy, they would still be reluctant to spend it out of stinginess and fear of running out. It highlights the inherent human tendency towards miserliness and unwillingness to part with wealth, even if it is abundant.
orig: قل لو أنتم تملكون خزائن رحمة ربي إذا لأمسكتم خشية الإنفاق وكان الإنسان قتورا

translation: And We had certainly given Moses nine clear signs. So ask the Children of Israel [about] when he came to them and Pharaoh said to him, "Indeed, I think, O Moses, that you are affected by magic."
interpretation: This verse highlights the miracles that God bestowed upon Moses to prove his prophethood, yet Pharaoh remained stubborn and accused Moses of being under the influence of magic. This underscores the hardness of heart and unwillingness to accept the truth that can afflict those in power, even in the face of clear divine signs.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى تسع آيات بينات فاسأل بني إسرائيل إذ جاءهم فقال له فرعون إني لأظنك يا موسى مسحورا

translation: He (Pharaoh) said: "Verily, I know that what these (two) have brought is but the truth from the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and I feel that you, O Pharaoh, are indeed going to be destroyed (in this life and the Hereafter)."
interpretation: This verse highlights the acknowledgment by Pharaoh that the message brought by Moses and Aaron is the truth from God, the Lord of the heavens and the earth. However, despite this recognition, Pharaoh still stubbornly refuses to submit to God's will, believing that he will ultimately be destroyed, both in this life and the Hereafter, due to his arrogance and rejection of the truth.
orig: قال لقد علمت ما أنزل هؤلاء إلا رب السماوات والأرض بصائر وإني لأظنك يا فرعون مثبورا

translation: And he intended to provoke them [i.e., the Israelites] from the land, but We drowned him and those with him all together.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Pharaoh, who sought to oppress and drive out the Israelites from Egypt. However, God punished Pharaoh and his army by drowning them in the sea, as a consequence of their tyranny and oppression against the believers.
orig: فأراد أن يستفزهم من الأرض فأغرقناه ومن معه جميعا

translation: And We said after him [i.e., Moses] to the Children of Israel, "Dwell in the land, and when there comes the promise of the Hereafter, We will bring you forth in [one] gathering."
interpretation: This verse conveys the message that after the time of Prophet Moses, God instructed the Children of Israel to settle in the land and establish themselves there. However, this is not their final destination, as when the promise of the Hereafter comes to pass, God will gather them all together to account for their deeds and determine their final abode in the Afterlife.
orig: وقلنا من بعده لبني إسرائيل اسكنوا الأرض فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة جئنا بكم لفيفا

translation: And with the truth We have sent it down, and with the truth it has descended. And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an was revealed by Allah with the truth, and that the Prophet Muhammad was sent as a bearer of good news and a warner to humanity. The truth of the Qur'an and the Prophet's message is emphasized, indicating that they are from Allah and not from any human source.
orig: وبالحق أنزلناه وبالحق نزل وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا

translation: And [it is] a Qur'an which We have separated [by intervals] that you might recite it to the people over a prolonged period, and We have sent it down progressively.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gradual and systematic revelation of the Qur'an, which was revealed to Prophet Muhammad over a period of time, rather than all at once. This allowed the people to gradually understand and internalize the teachings of the Qur'an, rather than being overwhelmed by its entirety. The verse also suggests that the Qur'an was revealed in a way that facilitated its recitation and study by the people, making it more accessible and understandable.
orig: وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ونزلناه تنزيلا

translation: Say, "Believe in it or do not believe [in it]. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it - when it is recited to them, they fall upon their faces in prostration."
interpretation: This verse encourages people to believe in the Qur'an, as even those who were given knowledge before its revelation prostrate before it when it is recited to them. It emphasizes the divine nature and authority of the Qur'an, which should compel people to accept it with humility and submission.
orig: قل آمنوا به أو لا تؤمنوا إن الذين أوتوا العلم من قبله إذا يتلى عليهم يخرون للأذقان سجدا

translation: And they say, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled."
interpretation: This verse expresses the belief and acknowledgment of the believers that God's promise will surely come to pass. It reflects their deep faith and trust in the divine decree, and their conviction that what God has promised will inevitably be fulfilled. This verse encourages steadfastness, patience, and reliance on God's plan, even in the face of challenges or difficulties.
orig: ويقولون سبحان ربنا إن كان وعد ربنا لمفعولا

translation: And they fall upon their faces, weeping, and the Qur'an increases them in humble submission.
interpretation: This verse describes the profound impact the Qur'an has on the hearts of those who hear it. When the Qur'anic verses are recited, the believers are overcome with a deep sense of humility and awe, causing them to prostrate themselves and weep out of reverence for the divine message. This reaction reflects the transformative power of the Qur'an, which increases the believers' devotion and submission to Allah.
orig: ويخرون للأذقان يبكون ويزيدهم خشوعا

translation: Say, "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful. Whichever [name] you call - to Him belong the best names." And do not recite [too] loudly in your prayer or [too] quietly but seek between that an [intermediate] course.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to invoke Allah by any of His beautiful names, as they all refer to the same Divine Being. It also advises against excessively loud or quiet prayer, and instead recommends a moderate approach. The underlying message is that one's relationship with the Divine should be sincere, humble and balanced, without unnecessary display or affectation.
orig: قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: And say, "Praise to Allah, who has not taken a son and has had no partner in [His] dominion and has not needed a protector out of weakness, and magnify Him with [great] magnification."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and supremacy of Allah. It states that Allah has no offspring, no partner in His dominion, and does not need a protector, as He is the Almighty and All-Powerful. The verse calls for praising and magnifying Allah, acknowledging His absolute sovereignty and perfection.
orig: وقل الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك ولم يكن له ولي من الذل وكبره تكبيرا

translation: All praise is [due] to Allah, who has sent down upon His Servant the Book and has not made therein any crookedness.
interpretation: This verse expresses gratitude and praise to Allah for revealing the Qur'an, the divine scripture, to His servant (the Prophet Muhammad). It emphasizes that the Qur'an is free from any distortion or crookedness, and is a perfect and straight guidance for humanity.
orig: الحمد لله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب ولم يجعل له عوجا

translation: To warn [the disbelievers] of a severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual purpose of the Qur'an - to warn those who reject faith of the severe punishment that awaits them, and to give glad tidings to the believers who do good deeds that they will be rewarded with a great reward. The Qur'an serves as a reminder and a guide, calling people to the path of righteousness and faith.
orig: قيما لينذر بأسا شديدا من لدنه ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم أجرا حسنا

translation: Abiding therein forever
interpretation: This verse conveys the eternal nature of the reward for the righteous in the Hereafter. It suggests that those who have lived virtuously and believed in God will reside in Paradise, enjoying its blessings and pleasures without end.
orig: ماكثين فيه أبدا

translation: And warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."
interpretation: This verse warns those who claim that Allah has a son. The Qur'an firmly rejects the notion of Allah having a son or any other divine partners, as it goes against the fundamental Islamic belief in the absolute oneness and uniqueness of God. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of upholding the concept of Allah's pure monotheism and rejecting any association of partners with Him.
orig: وينذر الذين قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا

translation: They have no knowledge thereof, nor had their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they speak naught but a lie.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who make claims without any knowledge or evidence to support them. It suggests that they are speaking falsehoods, and that their words carry great weight and significance, despite being baseless. The interpretation is that one should not make bold claims or pronouncements without proper justification and understanding.
orig: ما لهم به من علم ولا لآبائهم كبرت كلمة تخرج من أفواههم إن يقولون إلا كذبا

translation: So perhaps, [O Muhammad], you may exhaust yourself by worrying about their response if they do not believe in this message out of grief.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Prophet Muhammad may have been distressed and saddened by the lack of faith of his people. However, the verse advises him not to exhaust himself over this, as it is ultimately up to them to believe or not. The interpretation is that one should not be overly burdened by the responses or actions of others, and instead focus on one's own duty and responsibility.
orig: فلعلك باخع نفسك على آثارهم إن لم يؤمنوا بهذا الحديث أسفا

translation: Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them [as to] which of them is best in deed.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the various elements on Earth, such as natural resources, beauty, and opportunities, are meant to be a test for humanity. The purpose is to see which individuals or societies will make the best use of these blessings and live righteously, rather than engaging in wasteful or destructive behavior. The ultimate goal is to determine who is most deserving of Allah's pleasure and rewards in the Hereafter.
orig: إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا

translation: And indeed, We will make that which is upon it [i.e., the earth] barren ground.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the earth, which is currently inhabited and fertile, will one day be turned into a barren and desolate landscape. This could be interpreted as a reference to the Day of Judgment, when the world as we know it will come to an end and be transformed into a new, eternal realm.
orig: وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا

translation: Or have you thought that the companions of the cave and the inscription were, among Our signs, a wonder?
interpretation: This verse poses a rhetorical question, suggesting that the companions of the cave and the inscription were not a wonder or something extraordinary among the signs of Allah. Rather, they were part of the many wonders and signs that Allah has created, which should not be seen as isolated or unique events. The implication is that one should not be surprised or amazed by such occurrences, but rather recognize them as part of Allah's vast and intricate creation.
orig: أم حسبت أن أصحاب الكهف والرقيم كانوا من آياتنا عجبا

translation: When the youths took refuge in the cave and said, "Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance."
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when a group of young believers sought refuge in a cave, seeking guidance and mercy from Allah. Their supplication reflects a deep yearning for divine assistance in navigating the challenges they faced, demonstrating their reliance on God and their desire to follow the righteous path.
orig: إذ أوى الفتية إلى الكهف فقالوا ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا

translation: And We struck upon their ears in the cave for a number of years.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah struck the ears of the people in the cave, causing them to be deaf or unable to hear for a number of years. This could be interpreted as a miraculous event where Allah protected the people in the cave from being discovered or disturbed during their long slumber.
orig: فضربنا على آذانهم في الكهف سنين عددا

translation: Then We revived them to know which of the two factions was best at calculating what [period] they had remained [in that state].
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has the power to resurrect people in order to test and determine which group or faction is best able to understand and account for the duration of their time in the previous state. It implies that God has the knowledge and ability to assess the understanding and reasoning of different groups, and that this assessment is part of the divine plan.
orig: ثم بعثناهم لنعلم أي الحزبين أحصى لما لبثوا أمدا

translation: We relate to you, [O Muhammad], their story in truth. Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We had increased them in guidance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and guidance. It highlights that the story of the youths who believed in their Lord is being relayed truthfully, and that their faith was rewarded with increased guidance from Allah. The interpretation suggests that true belief and adherence to the path of righteousness can lead to spiritual growth and divine favor.
orig: نحن نقص عليك نبأهم بالحق إنهم فتية آمنوا بربهم وزدناهم هدى

translation: And We sealed their hearts when they stood up and said, 'Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. Never will we invoke besides Him any deity. [If we did], we would then have spoken an enormity.'
interpretation: This verse describes how God has sealed the hearts of those who have professed belief in His oneness and sovereignty over the heavens and the earth. They have recognized that it would be a grave error to worship any deity other than the one true God.
orig: وربطنا على قلوبهم إذ قاموا فقالوا ربنا رب السماوات والأرض لن ندعو من دونه إلها لقد قلنا إذا شططا

translation: These are our people who have taken gods besides Him. Why do they not bring for [them] a clear authority? And who is more unjust than one who invents about Allah a lie?
interpretation: This verse condemns those who worship idols and false gods instead of the one true God, Allah. It challenges them to provide a clear proof or authority for their worship of these false deities, as there can be no justification for such polytheism. The verse then poses a rhetorical question, asserting that there is no one more unjust than those who falsely attribute partners to Allah, the Almighty.
orig: هؤلاء قومنا اتخذوا من دونه آلهة لولا يأتون عليهم بسلطان بين فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا

translation: And when you have withdrawn from them and those they worship other than Allah, retreat to the cave. Your Lord will extend for you of His mercy and will prepare for you from your affair facility.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to separate themselves from those who worship false gods and idols, and instead take refuge in the worship of the One true God, Allah. By doing so, Allah will extend His mercy and blessings upon them, and make their affairs and circumstances easier to bear.
orig: وإذ اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته ويهيئ لكم من أمركم مرفقا

translation: And you see the sun when it rises, it passes away from their cave on the right, and when it sets, it leaves them on the left, while they are in a wide space thereof. That is from the Signs of Allah. He whom Allah guides, he is the [rightly] guided; but he whom He sends astray - for him you will never find a protecting guide.
interpretation: This verse describes the miraculous phenomenon of the sun's movement in relation to the cave where the people of the cave (Ashab al-Kahf) were sheltered. The sun's passage from right to left of the cave's entrance is a sign of Allah's power and wisdom. It also serves as a metaphor for guidance and misguidance - those whom Allah guides will find the right path, while those whom He leaves astray will have no protector to guide them. The verse emphasizes the importance of accepting Allah's guidance and submitting to His will.
orig: وترى الشمس إذا طلعت تزاور عن كهفهم ذات اليمين وإذا غربت تقرضهم ذات الشمال وهم في فجوة منه ذلك من آيات الله من يهد الله فهو المهتد ومن يضلل فلن تجد له وليا مرشدا

translation: And you would think them awake, while they are asleep. And We turn them to the right and to the left, and their dog [stretches out] his paws at the entrance. If you were to look at them, you would turn back from them in flight and be filled with terror of them.
interpretation: This verse describes the people of the Cave, who were protected by Allah while they slept for an extended period of time. The verse emphasizes that although they appear to be awake, they are in fact asleep, and Allah is controlling their movements and positioning. The mention of the dog guarding the entrance adds to the sense of mystery and divine protection surrounding these individuals. The verse suggests that if one were to encounter this sight, they would be filled with fear and flee, underscoring the extraordinary nature of this event.
orig: وتحسبهم أيقاظا وهم رقود ونقلبهم ذات اليمين وذات الشمال وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بالوصيد لو اطلعت عليهم لوليت منهم فرارا ولملئت منهم رعبا

translation: And thus have We revived them that they may question one another. [One] said, "How long have you remained [here]?" They said, "We have remained a day or part of a day." [The others] said, "Your Lord is most knowing of how long you remained. So send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city and let him look to which food is the purest and bring you provision from it and let him be cautious. And let no one be aware of you."
interpretation: This verse describes how God revived a group of people who had been asleep for a long period of time. When they awoke, they were confused about how much time had passed. The verse then describes how they decided to send one of their members to the nearby city to procure the purest food for them, while being cautious and discreet about their presence. The interpretation is that this verse highlights God's power to revive the dead, and the importance of caution and discretion when dealing with unfamiliar situations.
orig: وكذلك بعثناهم ليتساءلوا بينهم قال قائل منهم كم لبثتم قالوا لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم قالوا ربكم أعلم بما لبثتم فابعثوا أحدكم بورقكم هذه إلى المدينة فلينظر أيها أزكى طعاما فليأتكم برزق منه وليتلطف ولا يشعرن بكم أحدا

translation: Indeed, if they overcome you, they would be to you as enemies and extend against you their hands and their tongues with [intent of] evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers that if the disbelievers gain power over them, they will persecute and harm the believers in an attempt to make them abandon their faith. The believers are cautioned that they will not succeed in their efforts to turn away from Islam, no matter how much the disbelievers try to coerce them.
orig: إنهم إن يظهروا عليكم يرجموكم أو يعيدوكم في ملتهم ولن تفلحوا إذا أبدا

translation: And thus did We disclose them [i.e., the sleepers], that they might know that the promise of Allah is true and that of the Hour there is no doubt. [That was] when they disputed among themselves about their affair and [then] said, "Construct over them a structure. Their Lord is most knowing about them." Those who prevailed over their affair said, "We will surely take over them a masjid."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of believing in the promise of Allah and the certainty of the Day of Judgment. When the people who were asleep in the cave were discovered, it became clear that Allah's promise is true and that the Hour (the Day of Judgment) is inevitable. The verse also shows how people can have different perspectives and opinions on matters, and how those in power can make decisions that may not be in the best interest of others. The interpretation is that we should have unwavering faith in Allah's promises and be mindful of the Day of Judgment, and that we should strive to make decisions that are just and considerate of all people.
orig: وكذلك أعثرنا عليهم ليعلموا أن وعد الله حق وأن الساعة لا ريب فيها إذ يتنازعون بينهم أمرهم فقالوا ابنوا عليهم بنيانا ربهم أعلم بهم قال الذين غلبوا على أمرهم لنتخذن عليهم مسجدا

translation: They will say, "[They are] three, the fourth of them being their dog," and they will say, "[They are] five, the sixth of them being their dog," guessing at the unseen; and they will say, "[They are] seven, and the eighth of them is their dog." Say, "My Lord is most knowing of their number. None know them except a few. So do not argue about them except with an obvious argument and do not inquire about them among [the speculators] from anyone."
interpretation: This verse addresses the tendency of people to speculate and make claims about matters they have no certain knowledge of, such as the number of people in a particular story. The verse cautions against engaging in such idle speculation and instead encourages relying on what is known with certainty, as conveyed by the divine revelation. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of humility and restraint when discussing matters beyond one's direct knowledge.
orig: سيقولون ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم ويقولون خمسة سادسهم كلبهم رجما بالغيب ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم قل ربي أعلم بعدتهم ما يعلمهم إلا قليل فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا ولا تستفت فيهم منهم أحدا

translation: And do not say about anything, 'Indeed, I will do that [thing] tomorrow.'
interpretation: This verse advises against making definitive statements about future actions, as one cannot be certain of what will happen tomorrow. It encourages humility and acknowledging the uncertainty of the future, which is in the hands of God.
orig: ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا

translation: Except as your Lord wills. And remember your Lord when you forget and say, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right conduct."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of relying on God's will and seeking His guidance. It reminds us that our actions and choices are ultimately subject to God's will, and that we should turn to Him when we forget or lose our way. The verse also expresses hope that God may guide us to what is even more righteous and pleasing to Him.
orig: إلا أن يشاء الله واذكر ربك إذا نسيت وقل عسى أن يهدين ربي لأقرب من هذا رشدا

translation: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and [some] added nine.
interpretation: This verse describes the duration of time that the People of the Cave remained in their cave. The number of years, three hundred and nine, is a symbolic representation of a long period of time, rather than a precise numerical count. The verse suggests that the People of the Cave were protected and preserved by God during their time in the cave, a testament to the power and wisdom of the divine.
orig: ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا

translation: Say, "Allah is most knowing of how long they remained. To Him belong the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. How Clear-sighted and Hearing is He of His servants" - no protector have they besides Him, and He makes none to share in His Decision and Command.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that only Allah, the Almighty, has knowledge of the unseen aspects of the heavens and the earth. He is all-Seeing and all-Hearing, and no one besides Him has the authority to make decisions or share in His command. This underscores the absolute sovereignty and omniscience of Allah, and the need for believers to submit to Him alone without associating any partners with Him.
orig: قل الله أعلم بما لبثوا له غيب السماوات والأرض أبصر به وأسمع ما لهم من دونه من ولي ولا يشرك في حكمه أحدا

translation: And recite, [O Muhammad], what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord. There is no changer of His words, and never will you find in other than Him a refuge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and immutability of the Qur'an, which was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad. It assures that the words of the Qur'an cannot be changed or altered, and that God alone is the ultimate refuge and source of guidance for humanity. The verse reinforces the authority and sanctity of the Qur'anic revelation.
orig: واتل ما أوحي إليك من كتاب ربك لا مبدل لكلماته ولن تجد من دونه ملتحدا

translation: And keep yourself patient [by being] with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His countenance. And let not your eyes overlook them, desiring the adornments of the worldly life, and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire and whose affair is ever [in] neglect.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to be patient and steadfast in keeping company with those who are devoted to remembering and worshipping Allah, both in the morning and evening. It warns against being distracted by the allure of worldly pleasures and desires, and cautions against following those who have become heedless of Allah’s remembrance and have succumbed to their own selfish inclinations.
orig: واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ولا تعد عيناك عنهم تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه وكان أمره فرطا

translation: And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve." Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a fire whose walls will surround them. And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like murky oil, which scalds [their] faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the freedom of choice in matters of faith. It states that the truth has been revealed from God, and it is up to each individual to either believe or disbelieve. The verse then goes on to warn the wrongdoers of the punishment that awaits them in the Hereafter - a fire whose walls will surround them, and a torment that will be like scalding, murky water. This serves as a reminder that those who reject the truth will face severe consequences, while highlighting the importance of belief and righteous conduct.
orig: وقل الحق من ربكم فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر إنا أعتدنا للظالمين نارا أحاط بهم سرادقها وإن يستغيثوا يغاثوا بماء كالمهل يشوي الوجوه بئس الشراب وساءت مرتفقا

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of any who did well in deeds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have faith in God and do good deeds will be rewarded by God, and that their efforts will not be wasted or forgotten. It is a reassurance that God is just and will not neglect to acknowledge and recompense the righteous actions of His servants.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا

translation: Those will have gardens of perpetual residence; beneath them rivers will flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and will wear green garments of fine silk and brocade, reclining therein on adorned couches. Excellent is the reward, and good is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse describes the rewards and blessings that await the righteous in the Hereafter. It paints a vivid picture of the eternal gardens of Paradise, where the believers will dwell, surrounded by flowing rivers, adorned with golden bracelets, and dressed in the finest silk and brocade. They will recline on comfortable couches, enjoying the perfect rewards and the excellent resting place that God has prepared for them. This verse highlights the magnificence and splendor of the Afterlife, which serves as a powerful motivation for believers to strive for righteousness and earn the pleasure of God.
orig: أولئك لهم جنات عدن تجري من تحتهم الأنهار يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ويلبسون ثيابا خضرا من سندس وإستبرق متكئين فيها على الأرائك نعم الثواب وحسنت مرتفقا

translation: And present to them an example of two men: We granted to one of them two gardens of grapevines, and We bordered them with palm trees and placed between them [fields of] crops.
interpretation: This verse presents a parable of two men - one who was granted two gardens of grapevines, with palm trees bordering them and crops in between. This parable highlights the contrast between those who are blessed with worldly abundance and those who are not, and serves as a reminder that true success and fulfillment comes from faith and righteous deeds, not just material possessions.
orig: واضرب لهم مثلا رجلين جعلنا لأحدهما جنتين من أعناب وحففناهما بنخل وجعلنا بينهما زرعا

translation: Both the gardens brought forth their produce, and did not withhold anything thereof. And We caused a river to gush forth in their midst.
interpretation: This verse is describing the bounty and abundance that Allah has provided in the gardens of Paradise. The gardens are able to produce their full yield without any deficiency or shortcoming, and Allah has supplied them with flowing rivers to nourish and sustain them. This is a metaphor for the complete fulfillment and satisfaction that the believers will experience in the Hereafter.
orig: كلتا الجنتين آتت أكلها ولم تظلم منه شيئا وفجرنا خلالهما نهرا

translation: And he had fruit, and he said to his companion, while he was conversing with him, "I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in [personal] followers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and pride of a wealthy man who boasts about his material possessions and social status to his companion. It serves as a cautionary tale against the dangers of excessive wealth and self-importance, as these can lead to a disregard for others and a lack of humility.
orig: وكان له ثمر فقال لصاحبه وهو يحاوره أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا

translation: And he entered his garden while he was unjust to himself. He said, "I do not think that this will ever perish."
interpretation: This verse describes a person who enters his paradise or prosperous state while being unjust to his own soul. He is arrogant and believes that his wealth and prosperity will last forever, without considering the impermanence of worldly possessions and the consequences of his unjust actions. The interpretation highlights the importance of humility, gratitude, and acknowledging the transient nature of this life.
orig: ودخل جنته وهو ظالم لنفسه قال ما أظن أن تبيد هذه أبدا
