translation: And I do not think the Hour will occur. And [even] if I should be returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a return.
interpretation: This verse expresses the person's disbelief in the coming of the Day of Judgment, and their conviction that even if they were to return to their Lord, they would find something better than this worldly life. It highlights the shortsightedness and lack of faith in the Hereafter that can sometimes afflict people.
orig: وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رددت إلى ربي لأجدن خيرا منها منقلبا

translation: His companion said to him while he was arguing with him, "Have you disbelieved in the One who created you from dust and then from a sperm-drop and then proportioned you [as] a man?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of acknowledging and believing in the One who created us, Allah. The companion questions the disbelief of the other person, reminding him that he was created from the most humble of origins - dust and a sperm-drop - yet Allah shaped him into a complete human being. This serves as a call to reflect on the power and wisdom of the Creator, and to have faith in Him.
orig: قال له صاحبه وهو يحاوره أكفرت بالذي خلقك من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم سواك رجلا

translation: But He is Allah, my Lord; and I will not associate anyone with my Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of Allah as the true Lord, and the importance of worshipping Him alone without associating any partners with Him. It is a declaration of the speaker's unwavering faith in the absolute unity of God and a rejection of polytheism or idolatry.
orig: لكنا هو الله ربي ولا أشرك بربي أحدا

translation: And when you entered your garden, you said, 'What Allah wills [is what will occur]; there is no power except in Allah.' [But now], if you see me as less than you in wealth and children,
interpretation: This verse expresses the humility and acknowledgement of Allah's power and will that should be present in a believer's heart. When the owner of the garden was blessed with wealth and children, he recognized that it was by Allah's will and not due to his own power. This serves as a reminder that all blessings come from Allah, and one should not become arrogant or look down on others who may have less.
orig: ولولا إذ دخلت جنتك قلت ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله إن ترن أنا أقل منك مالا وولدا

translation: So perhaps my Lord will give me [something] better than your garden and will send upon it a [torment of] thunderbolt from the heaven, and it will become a smooth, dusty ground
interpretation: This verse suggests that one should not be overly attached to worldly possessions and pleasures, as they are fleeting and can be taken away at any moment. It implies that true fulfillment and blessings come from God, and that one should seek His pleasure and guidance rather than relying solely on material comforts.
orig: فعسى ربي أن يؤتين خيرا من جنتك ويرسل عليها حسبانا من السماء فتصبح صعيدا زلقا

translation: Or [that] its water should become consumed, and you would not be able to seek it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that a person should not rely solely on material resources, as they can be depleted or become inaccessible. It encourages seeking more permanent and reliable sources of sustenance, such as spiritual and moral guidance, which can provide lasting fulfillment and support.
orig: أو يصبح ماؤها غورا فلن تستطيع له طلبا

translation: And his fruits were encompassed [by ruin], so he began to wring his hands [in regret] over what he had spent on it, while it had collapsed upon its trellises, and [he said], "Oh, I wish I had not associated with my Lord anyone [in worship]!"
interpretation: This verse depicts the regret and remorse of someone who had invested heavily in a project that ultimately failed. The verse suggests that excessive attachment to worldly possessions and a lack of faith in God can lead to disappointment and a sense of loss. The interpretation is that one should not place their trust solely in material wealth, but rather seek a balance between worldly pursuits and spiritual devotion to God.
orig: وأحيط بثمره فأصبح يقلب كفيه على ما أنفق فيها وهي خاوية على عروشها ويقول يا ليتني لم أشرك بربي أحدا

translation: And he had no company to aid him other than Allah, nor could he defend himself.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the person had no supporters or helpers besides Allah, and was unable to defend himself on his own. It highlights the importance of relying on Allah and not seeking aid from others, as Allah is the ultimate source of help and protection.
orig: ولم تكن له فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان منتصرا

translation: The authority is for Allah, the True. He is best in reward and best in outcome.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the ultimate authority and sovereignty belongs to Allah alone. He is the True God, and His judgement and decisions are the most just and righteous. Seeking His pleasure and following His commands is the best path, as it leads to the most excellent reward in the Hereafter.
orig: هنالك الولاية لله الحق هو خير ثوابا وخير عقبا

translation: And present to them the example of the life of this world as rain which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it and [then] it becomes dry remnants, scattered by the winds. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse draws a parable of the fleeting nature of worldly life. Just as rain falls from the sky and nourishes the vegetation, only for it to wither and be scattered by the winds, so too is the life of this world - it is temporary and transient. This serves as a reminder that one should not become overly attached to the material world, but rather focus on the eternal life in the Hereafter, over which Allah has complete power and control.
orig: واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض فأصبح هشيما تذروه الرياح وكان الله على كل شيء مقتدرا

translation: Wealth and children are [but] adornment of the worldly life. But the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord for [eternal] reward and better for [one's] hope.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that material wealth and children, while providing temporary enjoyment and status in this world, are ultimately fleeting. The true and lasting value lies in one's righteous and enduring deeds, which will be rewarded by Allah in the Hereafter. These good deeds are superior to worldly possessions in terms of the eternal reward they bring and the hope they provide for the afterlife.
orig: المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير أملا

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], the Day We will remove the mountains and you will see the earth appearing, and We have gathered them, and We have not left behind from them anyone.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the mountains will be removed and the earth will be laid bare, and all of humanity will be gathered before Allah for accountability. The interpretation is that on that Day, no one will be left behind or excluded from the reckoning, as Allah will gather all of His creation to stand before Him.
orig: ويوم نسير الجبال وترى الأرض بارزة وحشرناهم فلم نغادر منهم أحدا

translation: And they will be presented before your Lord in rows. [And He will say], "You have certainly come to Us just as We created you the first time. But you claimed that We would never make for you an [appointed] time."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, all people will be held accountable before God. It suggests that the claims made by some that there will be no reckoning or resurrection are false, as God created them in the first place and will bring them back to account for their actions.
orig: وعرضوا على ربك صفا لقد جئتمونا كما خلقناكم أول مرة بل زعمتم ألن نجعل لكم موعدا

translation: And the Record [of deeds] will be placed [open], and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, "Oh, woe to us! What is this record that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present [before them], and your Lord does not do injustice to anyone.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the record of people's deeds will be presented before them. The criminals will be filled with dread and despair upon seeing the comprehensive and accurate record of their actions, both small and large. They will realize that nothing they did has been left out, and that they will be held accountable for everything. This emphasizes that on that day, no one will be able to escape the consequences of their own actions, and that Allah's judgment will be fair and just, without any injustice.
orig: ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه ويقولون يا ويلتنا مال هذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها ووجدوا ما عملوا حاضرا ولا يظلم ربك أحدا

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except for Iblis. He was of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord. Then will you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me while they are enemies to you? Wretched it is for the wrongdoers as an exchange.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disobedience of Iblis (Satan) when he refused to prostrate to Adam, despite the command from Allah. It serves as a warning against taking Iblis and his descendants as allies, as they are enemies to humanity and will lead them astray. The verse emphasizes that it is a wretched exchange for the wrongdoers to choose Iblis over Allah as their protector.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس كان من الجن ففسق عن أمر ربه أفتتخذونه وذريته أولياء من دوني وهم لكم عدو بئس للظالمين بدلا

translation: I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor [even] the creation of themselves, and I would not have taken the misguiders as assistants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God alone is the Creator of the heavens, the earth, and all of humanity. He did not require the assistance of any other being in this act of creation. The verse also suggests that God does not rely on those who have gone astray or misguided others, as they are not worthy of being God's assistants.
orig: ما أشهدتهم خلق السماوات والأرض ولا خلق أنفسهم وما كنت متخذ المضلين عضدا

translation: And the Day when He will call them and say, 'Where are My partners which you used to claim?',
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when Allah will call those who associated partners with Him and ask them where are the deities they worshipped. They will not be able to respond, as these false gods have no power to help them. This highlights the futility of polytheism and the need to worship only the one true God, Allah.
orig: ويوم يقول نادوا شركائي الذين زعمتم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم وجعلنا بينهم موبقا

translation: And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain [that they are to fall into it], and they will not find from it a [way of] avoidance.
interpretation: This verse conveys the inevitability of the punishment for the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment. They will be fully convinced of their impending doom in the Hellfire, but they will have no means to escape it. This emphasizes the certainty and inescapability of divine justice for those who have committed grave sins and transgressions.
orig: ورأى المجرمون النار فظنوا أنهم مواقعوها ولم يجدوا عنها مصرفا

translation: And We have certainly diversified [the contents] in this Qur'an for the people, but most of the people refuse [anything] except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Qur'an's comprehensive and diverse nature, as it provides guidance and examples for all of humanity. However, it also acknowledges the tendency of many people to reject this guidance and instead persist in disbelief and skepticism.
orig: ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن للناس من كل مثل وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا

translation: And what prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them and from asking forgiveness of their Lord except that there [come to] them the precedent of the former peoples or the punishment should come [to them] before?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the primary reason people do not believe and seek forgiveness from God is either their adherence to the ways of previous generations who rejected the truth, or their fear of the impending punishment that may come upon them. It highlights the importance of being open-minded and responsive to divine guidance, rather than being constrained by the traditions and beliefs of the past.
orig: وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى ويستغفروا ربهم إلا أن تأتيهم سنة الأولين أو يأتيهم العذاب قبلا

translation: And We send not the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners. And those who disbelieve dispute by [using] falsehood to [attempt to] invalidate thereby the truth and have taken My verses, and that of which they are warned, in ridicule.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the messengers sent by God, who are tasked with delivering both good news and warnings to people. It also highlights the tendency of those who reject faith to use falsehood and ridicule in an attempt to undermine the truth. The verse suggests that the messengers' teachings and the warnings they convey should be taken seriously, rather than being treated with scorn.
orig: وما نرسل المرسلين إلا مبشرين ومنذرين ويجادل الذين كفروا بالباطل ليدحضوا به الحق واتخذوا آياتي وما أنذروا هزوا

translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forth? Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if you invite them to guidance, they will never be directed.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who turn away from the signs and messages of God, despite being reminded of them. It suggests that their hearts and minds have been sealed, preventing them from understanding and accepting the guidance. Even if they are invited to the path of righteousness, they will remain steadfast in their rejection, unable to find the right direction.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن ذكر بآيات ربه فأعرض عنها ونسي ما قدمت يداه إنا جعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإن تدعهم إلى الهدى فلن يهتدوا إذا أبدا

translation: And your Lord is the Forgiving, the Possessor of Mercy. If He were to impose blame upon them for what they have earned, He would have hastened for them the punishment. But for them is an appointment, and they will never find an escape from it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of God. Even though people may commit sins, God is willing to forgive them if they repent and seek His forgiveness. The verse also suggests that God does not hastily punish people, but rather gives them time to mend their ways and return to the right path. Ultimately, there is no escape from God's judgment, and people will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: وربك الغفور ذو الرحمة لو يؤاخذهم بما كسبوا لعجل لهم العذاب بل لهم موعد لن يجدوا من دونه موئلا

translation: And those cities - We destroyed them when they wronged, and We made for their destruction a promised time.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah has the power to punish those who commit injustice and oppression. The destruction of the previous nations serves as a warning to those who persist in their wrongdoing, and a reminder that there is a predetermined time for their reckoning. It emphasizes the consequences of transgressing against the laws of Allah and the importance of upholding justice and righteousness.
orig: وتلك القرى أهلكناهم لما ظلموا وجعلنا لمهلكهم موعدا

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Moses said to his servant, "I will not cease [traveling] until I reach the junction of the two seas or continue for a long period."
interpretation: This verse refers to the journey of Prophet Moses and his servant to find the junction of the two seas, a symbolic place where they would encounter great wisdom. The verse highlights Moses' determination and perseverance in his quest for knowledge and understanding, even if it means continuing for a long period of time. It emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and not giving up, even in the face of challenges or difficulties.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لفتاه لا أبرح حتى أبلغ مجمع البحرين أو أمضي حقبا

translation: And when they had reached the junction between the two [bodies of] water, they forgot their fish, and it took its course into the sea, [inserting itself] into the water.
interpretation: This verse describes the encounter between Moses and his companion, who were traveling to find the knowledgeable person that Moses was seeking. When they reached the place where the two bodies of water met, they forgot about the fish they were carrying, and it swam away into the sea. This event marks the beginning of their journey to find the knowledgeable person, as the loss of the fish was a sign that they had reached their destination.
orig: فلما بلغا مجمع بينهما نسيا حوتهما فاتخذ سبيله في البحر سربا

translation: And when they had passed on (some distance), Moses said to his boy-servant: 'Bring us our morning meal; truly we have suffered much fatigue in this, our journey.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of taking breaks and nourishing oneself during a long and tiring journey. It teaches us to be mindful of our physical and mental well-being, and to seek sustenance when needed, in order to continue our path with renewed energy and focus.
orig: فلما جاوزا قال لفتاه آتنا غداءنا لقد لقينا من سفرنا هذا نصبا

translation: He said: "Did you see when we took refuge on the rock? Indeed, I forgot [there] the fish, and none made me forget it except Satan - that I should not mention it. And it took its course into the sea amazingly."
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to forget and be distracted, even from important matters. The protagonist, likely the prophet Moses, had forgotten about the miraculous fish that had been given to him, and he attributed this forgetfulness to the influence of Satan. The verse emphasizes the importance of being vigilant and not allowing Satan to lead us astray, even in seemingly insignificant matters.
orig: قال أرأيت إذ أوينا إلى الصخرة فإني نسيت الحوت وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان أن أذكره واتخذ سبيله في البحر عجبا

translation: He said: This is what we were seeking. So they both returned, retracing their footsteps.
interpretation: This verse expresses the sense of satisfaction and accomplishment felt by the two individuals upon finding what they were searching for. The repetition of "their footsteps" suggests a journey of discovery, where they retraced their steps to arrive at their desired destination. The interpretation conveys a message of perseverance, determination, and the reward that comes from diligently pursuing one's goals.
orig: قال ذلك ما كنا نبغ فارتدا على آثارهما قصصا

translation: And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and had taught him from Us [certain] knowledge.
interpretation: This verse refers to a righteous servant of God who was granted divine knowledge and mercy. The interpretation suggests that God bestows His blessings upon those who are devoted to Him, granting them wisdom and guidance from the divine source.
orig: فوجدا عبدا من عبادنا آتيناه رحمة من عندنا وعلمناه من لدنا علما

translation: Moses said to him, "May I follow you on [the condition] that you teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgement?"
interpretation: This verse depicts Moses' desire to learn from a knowledgeable person, in this case the character referred to as "him". Moses seeks to follow this individual on the condition that he is taught some of the wisdom and sound judgement that this person has acquired. The verse highlights Moses' humility and eagerness to gain knowledge from someone more experienced than himself.
orig: قال له موسى هل أتبعك على أن تعلمن مما علمت رشدا

translation: He said, 'Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me,
interpretation: This verse expresses the difficulty of maintaining patience and steadfastness when dealing with someone who has a different perspective or approach. It suggests that there may be challenges in finding common ground and working together, requiring a great deal of effort and understanding from both parties.
orig: قال إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا

translation: And how can you have patience about a matter of which you have no comprehensive knowledge?
interpretation: This verse encourages us to exercise patience and restraint in matters where our knowledge is limited. We should not make hasty judgments or decisions on issues that we do not fully understand. Instead, we should strive to gain more knowledge and perspective before reacting, as this will lead to wiser and more considered actions.
orig: وكيف تصبر على ما لم تحط به خبرا

translation: He said, "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient and I will not disobey you in [any] order."
interpretation: This verse expresses the servant's commitment to be patient and obedient to the commands of Allah and his master. It reflects a strong faith in Allah's will and a determination to fulfill one's duties, even in the face of challenges.
orig: قال ستجدني إن شاء الله صابرا ولا أعصي لك أمرا

translation: He said: 'If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself make mention of it to you.'
interpretation: This verse suggests that when following a wise teacher or guide, one should not constantly question or demand explanations, but rather trust in the teacher's judgment and wait patiently for the appropriate time when the teacher chooses to share more information. It emphasizes the importance of obedience, patience and deference to the one who has greater knowledge and wisdom.
orig: قال فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكرا

translation: And they set out, until when they had embarked on the ship, he [i.e., al-Khidr] tore it open. [Moses] said, "Have you torn it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the difference in understanding between the prophet Moses and the righteous servant al-Khidr. Al-Khidr, with his superior knowledge and wisdom, took an action that appeared destructive to Moses, who could not comprehend the deeper purpose behind it. This highlights the need for humility and trust in the face of Allah's plans, which may not always be immediately apparent to us.
orig: فانطلقا حتى إذا ركبا في السفينة خرقها قال أخرقتها لتغرق أهلها لقد جئت شيئا إمرا

translation: He said, 'Did I not say to you that you would not be able to have patience with me?'
interpretation: This verse is a statement made by Moses to his companion, likely referring to an earlier promise or agreement they had made. The interpretation is that Moses is reminding his companion that he had warned him that he would not be able to have the necessary patience and perseverance to accompany Moses on his journey, implying that the companion's lack of patience has now become evident.
orig: قال ألم أقل إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا

translation: He said, "Do not blame me for what I forgot and do not make my matter too difficult for me."
interpretation: This verse expresses a plea for mercy and leniency. The speaker acknowledges their forgetfulness and asks not to be held accountable for it. They also ask that their affairs not be made overly burdensome or difficult. This reflects a humble and vulnerable posture, seeking understanding and compassion from the one being addressed.
orig: قال لا تؤاخذني بما نسيت ولا ترهقني من أمري عسرا

translation: So they both proceeded, until when they met a boy, he killed him. [Moses] said, "Have you killed a pure soul without [cause for] a soul? You have certainly done a deplorable thing."
interpretation: This verse describes an incident where Moses and his companion encounter a young boy, and the companion kills him. Moses is shocked and questions the companion's action, stating that he has committed a grave and deplorable act by killing an innocent soul without justification. The interpretation here is that the verse emphasizes the sanctity of human life and condemns the unjustified taking of an innocent life, which is a grave moral transgression.
orig: فانطلقا حتى إذا لقيا غلاما فقتله قال أقتلت نفسا زكية بغير نفس لقد جئت شيئا نكرا

translation: He said, 'Did I not say to you that you would not be able to have patience with me?'
interpretation: This verse suggests that patience and perseverance are essential qualities for one to maintain in their relationship with the Divine. It implies that without these virtues, one may struggle to comprehend the wisdom and plan of God, and may become frustrated or impatient. The verse serves as a reminder to cultivate patience, trust, and submission in one's spiritual journey.
orig: قال ألم أقل لك إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا

translation: He said: "If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as a companion. You have obtained from me an excuse."
interpretation: This verse expresses the condition set by the person speaking, that if he asks about anything further after this, the other person should not keep him company anymore, as he has already obtained a sufficient excuse or justification from the speaker.
orig: قال إن سألتك عن شيء بعدها فلا تصاحبني قد بلغت من لدني عذرا

translation: So they went on until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. And they found therein a wall about to collapse, so he (al-Khidhr) set it up straight. [Musa] said, "If you wished, you could have taken for it a payment."
interpretation: This verse describes an encounter between Prophet Moses and al-Khidhr, where they came upon a town and asked the people for food, but were refused hospitality. They then found a wall about to collapse, and al-Khidhr repaired it without seeking any payment. The interpretation is that sometimes, we should do good deeds without expecting any reward or compensation, as the ultimate reward is with Allah.
orig: فانطلقا حتى إذا أتيا أهل قرية استطعما أهلها فأبوا أن يضيفوهما فوجدا فيها جدارا يريد أن ينقض فأقامه قال لو شئت لاتخذت عليه أجرا

translation: He said, "This is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience."
interpretation: This verse refers to a conversation between Prophet Moses and the knowledgeable man he had met, who had demonstrated abilities beyond Moses' understanding. The interpretation suggests that the parting of their ways was necessary, as the other man had knowledge that Moses could not patiently comprehend at that time. This highlights the humility required in the face of superior knowledge and wisdom.
orig: قال هذا فراق بيني وبينك سأنبئك بتأويل ما لم تستطع عليه صبرا

translation: As for the ship, it belonged to [some] poor people working at sea, so I intended to cause defect in it as there was behind them a king who was taking every [good] ship by force.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the Prophet Musa (Moses) acting out of compassion and wisdom. He intentionally damaged a ship belonging to poor fishermen, not out of malice, but to prevent it from being seized by a tyrannical king who was confiscating all good ships. This demonstrates how sometimes an action that appears harmful on the surface can actually be for the greater good, as Musa was protecting the livelihoods of the poor people.
orig: أما السفينة فكانت لمساكين يعملون في البحر فأردت أن أعيبها وكان وراءهم ملك يأخذ كل سفينة غصبا

translation: As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them with transgression and disbelief.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the righteous young man whom Prophet Moses and his companion encountered during their journey. The verse suggests that the boy's parents were believers, and the Prophet feared that the boy's actions might lead his parents to stray from their faith and commit acts of transgression and disbelief. This highlights the importance of parental influence and the need to protect children from going astray, even if their actions seem justified.
orig: وأما الغلام فكان أبواه مؤمنين فخشينا أن يرهقهما طغيانا وكفرا

translation: And we intended for their Lord to substitute for them [a child] better than him in purity and nearer to mercy.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God can replace something that is less desirable with something better and more pure, out of His mercy and compassion. The interpretation is that God can provide a superior alternative to what one currently has, if it is in the best interest of the individual.
orig: فأردنا أن يبدلهما ربهما خيرا منه زكاة وأقرب رحما

translation: As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was beneath it a treasure for them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord intended that they reach maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord. That is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience.
interpretation: This verse describes the story of a wall that contained a hidden treasure belonging to two orphan boys. The wall was repaired by the Prophet's companion, al-Khidr, as an act of mercy from God to help the orphans retrieve their treasure when they came of age. The interpretation emphasizes that God's plan is often hidden from human understanding, but is ultimately for the good of those involved, even if it is not immediately apparent.
orig: وأما الجدار فكان لغلامين يتيمين في المدينة وكان تحته كنز لهما وكان أبوهما صالحا فأراد ربك أن يبلغا أشدهما ويستخرجا كنزهما رحمة من ربك وما فعلته عن أمري ذلك تأويل ما لم تسطع عليه صبرا

translation: And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say, "I will recite to you about him a report."
interpretation: This verse introduces the story of Dhul-Qarnayn, a righteous and powerful ruler who is believed to have traveled to the east and west. The verse indicates that the people were curious about this figure, and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is instructed to share information about him.
orig: ويسألونك عن ذي القرنين قل سأتلو عليكم منه ذكرا

translation: Indeed, We have established him [i.e., Satan] in the earth and granted him from the means [i.e., wealth and children].
interpretation: This verse is a warning that Satan has been granted power and influence in the world, and has been provided with the means to tempt and mislead people. It serves as a reminder to believers to be vigilant and not to be deceived by the allures of this world, which can lead them astray from the path of righteousness.
orig: إنا مكنا له في الأرض وآتيناه من كل شيء سببا

translation: Then follow a way
interpretation: This verse encourages one to pursue a path or course of action that is righteous and leads to success. It suggests that one should not be content with the status quo, but should actively seek out and follow a path that is guided by wisdom and leads to positive outcomes.
orig: فأتبع سببا

translation: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it [as if] setting in a spring of dark mud, and he found near it a people. [Allah] said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish [them] or else you take among them [a way of] goodness."
interpretation: This verse describes the journey of Dhul-Qarnayn, a righteous and powerful ruler, as he reaches the westernmost point of the earth. There, he finds the sun setting in a dark, muddy spring, and encounters a people living nearby. The verse then presents Allah giving Dhul-Qarnayn a choice: either to punish the people for their misdeeds, or to treat them with kindness and compassion. This highlights the moral dilemma faced by leaders, who must balance justice and mercy in their dealings with their subjects.
orig: حتى إذا بلغ مغرب الشمس وجدها تغرب في عين حمئة ووجد عندها قوما قلنا يا ذا القرنين إما أن تعذب وإما أن تتخذ فيهم حسنا

translation: And as for him who does wrong, We shall punish him. Then he will be brought back to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the consequences for those who commit wrongdoing and injustice. It indicates that such individuals will face punishment, first in this life and then in the Hereafter when they are returned to their Lord. The "terrible punishment" refers to the severe and unpleasant nature of the punishment they will face, as a result of their misdeeds.
orig: قال أما من ظلم فسوف نعذبه ثم يرد إلى ربه فيعذبه عذابا نكرا

translation: But as for he who believes and does righteousness, for him is the best [reward], and we will speak to him from Our command with ease.
interpretation: This verse conveys that those who believe in God and do good deeds will be rewarded with the best in the Hereafter. Moreover, God will make their affairs in this life easy for them and provide them with guidance and assistance from His command.
orig: وأما من آمن وعمل صالحا فله جزاء الحسنى وسنقول له من أمرنا يسرا

translation: Then he will follow a way
interpretation: This verse suggests that after a person has made an effort or taken a certain course of action, they will then proceed to follow a particular path or course of action that is a result of their previous efforts. The implication is that one's actions and choices lead to certain outcomes or consequences, which the person then follows or pursues.
orig: ثم أتبع سببا

translation: Until, when he reached the rising of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had not made against it any shield.
interpretation: This verse describes the journey of a traveler who reaches the rising of the sun, and finds that it is shining upon a people who have no protection or shelter from its rays. This can be interpreted as a metaphor for the lack of guidance or spiritual protection for those who have not been provided with the light of divine revelation or the shield of faith.
orig: حتى إذا بلغ مطلع الشمس وجدها تطلع على قوم لم نجعل لهم من دونها سترا

translation: Thus [it was], and We had [already] encompassed [all] that he had of knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge and understanding of all things, including the knowledge and affairs of His servants. It suggests that Allah is all-knowing and has comprehensive awareness of everything, including what His servants possess in terms of knowledge, capabilities, and circumstances.
orig: كذلك وقد أحطنا بما لديه خبرا

translation: Then follow a way
interpretation: This verse encourages one to seek knowledge, pursue a path of righteousness, and strive towards a noble purpose in life. It suggests that one should not be complacent, but actively seek out and follow a meaningful course of action that leads to positive outcomes.
orig: ثم أتبع سببا

translation: Until, when he reached between the two mountains, he found before them a people who could hardly understand [his] speech.
interpretation: This verse describes a journey undertaken by a prophet or messenger, who reaches a place between two mountains and encounters a people who can barely comprehend his message. This suggests the challenges faced by those who seek to convey divine guidance to communities that may be unfamiliar with or resistant to it, highlighting the importance of patience, perseverance, and adaptability in the face of such barriers to understanding.
orig: حتى إذا بلغ بين السدين وجد من دونهما قوما لا يكادون يفقهون قولا

translation: They said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are [great] corrupters in the land. So may we assign for you an tribute on condition that you make between us and them a barrier?"
interpretation: This verse indicates that the people approached Dhul-Qarnayn, a powerful ruler, and requested him to construct a barrier between them and the tribes of Gog and Magog, who were known to be great corrupters and troublemakers on the earth. The people were willing to pay a tribute or tax in exchange for Dhul-Qarnayn's assistance in providing this protection.
orig: قالوا يا ذا القرنين إن يأجوج ومأجوج مفسدون في الأرض فهل نجعل لك خرجا على أن تجعل بيننا وبينهم سدا

translation: He said, "That in which my Lord has established me is better [than what you offer], so assist me with strength, and I will make between you and them a barrier."
interpretation: This verse expresses the confidence of the speaker in the provisions granted to him by his Lord, which are better than what is being offered. It calls for assistance and strength to establish a barrier or separation between the two parties, implying the need for a clear division or distinction between them.
orig: قال ما مكني فيه ربي خير فأعينوني بقوة أجعل بينكم وبينهم ردما

translation: Bring me blocks of iron" - until, when he had filled up the space between the two mountain-sides, he said, "Blow!" - until, when he had made it [glow like] fire, he said, "Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper."
interpretation: This verse describes the building of a great barrier or dam, likely by the figure known as Dhul-Qarnayn (the Two-Horned One). The verse highlights the technological and engineering prowess required to construct such a massive structure, as Dhul-Qarnayn commands the gathering of iron, the heating of it to a molten state, and the pouring of copper over it to fortify the barrier. This serves as an example of the power and capability that God grants to certain individuals, and the ability of humanity to overcome great challenges through determination and skill.
orig: آتوني زبر الحديد حتى إذا ساوى بين الصدفين قال انفخوا حتى إذا جعله نارا قال آتوني أفرغ عليه قطرا

translation: But they were unable to scale it or dig through it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers were unable to overcome the message of the Qur'an, either by openly opposing it or by trying to undermine it in a subtle way. It highlights the power and inimitability of the Qur'an, which the disbelievers could not overcome despite their efforts.
orig: فما اسطاعوا أن يظهروه وما استطاعوا له نقبا

translation: He said, "This is a mercy from my Lord. But when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and ever is the promise of my Lord true."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the blessings and provisions given by God are a mercy from Him. However, when the time of reckoning comes, all worldly things will be destroyed and made level. The promise of God is always true and will be fulfilled.
orig: قال هذا رحمة من ربي فإذا جاء وعد ربي جعله دكاء وكان وعد ربي حقا

translation: And We will leave some of them that day surging over others, and [then] the Horn will be blown, and We will gather them in a [single] gathering.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when people will be resurrected and gathered for judgment. On that day, some will be overwhelmed by the events, while others will be more composed. The blowing of the Horn signals the start of the final gathering of all humanity before God for the final reckoning and accounting of their deeds.
orig: وتركنا بعضهم يومئذ يموج في بعض ونفخ في الصور فجمعناهم جمعا

translation: And We will present Hell that Day to the disbelievers, on display
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that on the Day of Judgment, Hell will be presented before the disbelievers as a stark reminder of the consequences of their rejection of faith and righteous deeds. The display of Hell serves as a warning to those who turned away from the truth and embraced disbelief, highlighting the severity of their fate in the Hereafter.
orig: وعرضنا جهنم يومئذ للكافرين عرضا

translation: Those whose eyes had been within a cover away from My remembrance, and they were unable to hear.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are heedless of Allah's guidance and reminders, and are unable to comprehend the truth. Their spiritual senses are veiled, preventing them from recognizing and accepting the divine message.
orig: الذين كانت أعينهم في غطاء عن ذكري وكانوا لا يستطيعون سمعا

translation: Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as allies besides Me? Verily, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a dwelling.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who disbelieve in God should not think they can take God's servants as allies or protectors instead of God. It clearly states that God has prepared Hell as a dwelling place for the disbelievers, indicating that they will be punished for their rejection of faith and alliance with those other than God.
orig: أفحسب الذين كفروا أن يتخذوا عبادي من دوني أولياء إنا أعتدنا جهنم للكافرين نزلا

translation: Say, 'Shall we [believers] inform you of the greatest losers as to [their] deeds?'
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to reflect on those who have lost the most in their deeds and actions, in order to avoid their fate. The implication is that those who disbelieve and do not live according to the teachings of Islam are the greatest losers, as they will face eternal punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا

translation: Those whose efforts have been wasted in this life while they thought that they were acquiring good by their works.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have misguided their efforts and actions in this worldly life, believing that they are doing good deeds, when in reality their actions are futile and devoid of true purpose. It highlights the importance of aligning one's intentions and actions with the guidance of the Qur'an and the teachings of Islam, rather than being misled by one's own assumptions or the opinions of others.
orig: الذين ضل سعيهم في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا

translation: Those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord and [in the eventual] meeting with Him - so their deeds have become worthless, and We will not assign to them on the Day of Resurrection any weight [i.e., importance].
interpretation: This verse describes those who reject the signs and messages of Allah, and deny the Day of Resurrection and Judgement. Their deeds and actions in this life will be rendered meaningless and worthless, as they have chosen to turn away from the truth. On the Day of Judgement, their deeds will not be given any weight or consideration, as they have forfeited the chance to earn Allah's pleasure and reward through their disbelief and rejection of the faith.
orig: أولئك الذين كفروا بآيات ربهم ولقائه فحبطت أعمالهم فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا

translation: That is their recompense - Hell, because they disbelieved and took My signs and My messengers in ridicule.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the ultimate punishment for those who reject faith and mock the signs of God and His messengers is the eternal torment of Hell. It emphasizes that disbelief and mockery of divine guidance are grave sins that warrant severe consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: ذلك جزاؤهم جهنم بما كفروا واتخذوا آياتي ورسلي هزوا

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them are the Gardens of Paradise as accommodation.
interpretation: This verse conveys that those who have faith in God and do good deeds will be rewarded with the eternal bliss of Paradise as their dwelling place. It emphasizes the direct correlation between belief, righteous actions, and the attainment of the highest level of Paradise, referred to as "the Gardens of Paradise". The verse highlights the concept that faith and good works go hand-in-hand, and that those who possess both will be granted the ultimate reward in the Hereafter.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات كانت لهم جنات الفردوس نزلا

translation: Abiding therein eternally. They will not desire from it any shift.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the believers who enter Paradise will remain there forever, without any desire to leave or change their circumstances. Their state of eternal bliss and contentment in Paradise will be permanent and unchanging.
orig: خالدين فيها لا يبغون عنها حولا

translation: Say, "If the sea were ink for [writing] the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the infinite and boundless nature of God's knowledge and wisdom. Even if the entire ocean was used as ink to write down God's words, it would be exhausted before God's words are exhausted. This highlights the limitless and eternal nature of God's speech and the inability of human beings to fully encompass the depth and breadth of divine knowledge.
orig: قل لو كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي لنفد البحر قبل أن تنفد كلمات ربي ولو جئنا بمثله مددا

translation: Say, "I am only a man like you, to whom it has been revealed that your god is but one God. So whoever would hope for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad is a human being like others, but he has been chosen by God to receive divine revelation. It calls on people to believe in the oneness of God and to do good deeds, without associating partners with God in worship. The key message is the importance of worshipping God alone and living a righteous life in order to attain God's pleasure and the meeting with Him on the Day of Judgment.
orig: قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا

translation: Kaf, Ha, Ya, 'Ayn, Sad.
interpretation: These are among the 'mysterious letters' (al-huruf al-muqatta'at) that appear at the beginning of some Qur'anic chapters. Their precise meaning is not definitively known, but they are believed to be a way of emphasizing the divine origin and inimitability of the Qur'an.
orig: كهيعص

translation: Mention, [O Muhammad], the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zechariah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and compassion of God towards His servant Zechariah, who was granted a son (John the Baptist) in his old age, despite his previous barrenness. It serves as a reminder of God's ability to bestow blessings upon those who are steadfast in their faith and devotion to Him.
orig: ذكر رحمت ربك عبده زكريا

translation: When he called his Lord with a hidden call.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) who would engage in private supplication and communion with Allah, the Almighty. The "hidden call" suggests an intimate and sincere connection between the Prophet and his Lord, away from the distractions of the world.
orig: إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا

translation: He said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has filled with white, and I have never been in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy."
interpretation: This verse expresses the humility and reliance on God of the Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) in his old age. Despite the physical signs of aging, he remains steadfast in his devotion to God and confident that his supplications have not been in vain. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining faith and trust in God even in the face of life's challenges.
orig: قال رب إني وهن العظم مني واشتعل الرأس شيبا ولم أكن بدعائك رب شقيا

translation: And I have feared the successors after me, and my wife has been barren, so give me from Yourself an heir
interpretation: This verse expresses the concern of the Prophet Zakariyyah (peace be upon him) about his succession and the continuation of his lineage. He feared that after him, his people might stray from the right path, and he also worried about not having a son to carry on his legacy. Therefore, he prayed to Allah to grant him a child from Himself, as a means of continuing his righteous work and preserving his legacy.
orig: وإني خفت الموالي من ورائي وكانت امرأتي عاقرا فهب لي من لدنك وليا

translation: He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, and make him, my Lord, well-pleased [with me].
interpretation: This verse expresses the desire of the Prophet Zachariah to have a righteous son who will inherit his knowledge and piety, and who will be pleasing to Allah. The verse suggests that the son will be a continuation of the legacy of the family of the Prophet Jacob, and that he will be a source of Allah's pleasure and satisfaction.
orig: يرثني ويرث من آل يعقوب واجعله رب رضيا

translation: O Zechariah, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John. We have not assigned to him before [any] name similar [to it].
interpretation: This verse announces the glad tidings to the prophet Zechariah of the birth of a son, who will be named John (Yahya). The verse emphasizes that this name is unique and has not been given to anyone before, indicating the special status and purpose of this child.
orig: يا زكريا إنا نبشرك بغلام اسمه يحيى لم نجعل له من قبل سميا

translation: He said, 'My Lord, how can I have a son when my wife has already reached old age and I have become extremely old?'
interpretation: This verse expresses the surprise and disbelief of the Prophet Abraham upon being informed by God that he would have a son, despite his and his wife's advanced age. The interpretation is that even in the face of seemingly impossible circumstances, one should have faith in God's plan and power, as He is capable of accomplishing what may appear improbable to human understanding.
orig: قال رب أنى يكون لي غلام وكانت امرأتي عاقرا وقد بلغت من الكبر عتيا

translation: He said, "Thus has your Lord said, 'It is an easy matter for Me,'"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ease with which God creates and sustains all things. It reminds us that God is all-powerful and that nothing is difficult for Him, even the creation of human beings from nothing.
orig: قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين وقد خلقتك من قبل ولم تك شيئا

translation: He said, 'My Lord, make for me a sign.' [Allah] said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, [being] sound.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine sign given to the prophet Zechariah, in which he was instructed not to speak for three nights as a sign of the coming birth of his son, John the Baptist. The interpretation is that sometimes God gives us signs and tests of our faith, which we must accept with patience and trust in the divine plan.
orig: قال رب اجعل لي آية قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاث ليال سويا

translation: Then he came out to his people from the prayer chamber and signaled to them to exalt [Allah] in the morning and afternoon.
interpretation: This verse describes the prophet Zakariyyā (peace be upon him) emerging from the prayer chamber to his people, and instructing them to glorify and praise Allah in the morning and evening. This emphasizes the importance of constant remembrance and worship of the Almighty, not just during specific times, but throughout the day.
orig: فخرج على قومه من المحراب فأوحى إليهم أن سبحوا بكرة وعشيا

translation: O Yahya, take the Scripture with determination." And We gave him judgement [while yet] a boy.
interpretation: This verse encourages the prophet Yahya (John the Baptist) to firmly uphold and convey the teachings of the Scripture, even from a young age. It emphasizes that Yahya was granted wisdom and the ability to make sound judgements despite his youth, demonstrating God's special favor and guidance.
orig: يا يحيى خذ الكتاب بقوة وآتيناه الحكم صبيا

translation: And affection from Us and purity, and he was [of those who were] pious
interpretation: This verse speaks of the qualities of a righteous person, who is granted affection and purity from God, and who was known for their piety and God-consciousness.
orig: وحنانا من لدنا وزكاة وكان تقيا

translation: And dutiful to his parents, and he was not a disobedient tyrant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being dutiful and obedient to one's parents, and avoiding the traits of being a tyrannical and disobedient person. It highlights the virtues of filial piety and humility, which are highly valued in Islamic teachings.
orig: وبرا بوالديه ولم يكن جبارا عصيا

translation: And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he is raised alive.
interpretation: This verse is a declaration of peace and blessing upon the Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him). It highlights the significance of the three major events in his life: his birth, his death, and his resurrection. The verse emphasizes that peace and blessings are upon him on these momentous occasions, underscoring the divine favor and honor bestowed upon him.
orig: وسلام عليه يوم ولد ويوم يموت ويوم يبعث حيا

translation: And mention, [O Muhammad], in the Book [the story of] Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the Virgin Mary, who secluded herself in a private place to the east in order to devote herself to worship and prayer. The verse highlights Mary's piety and her desire to commune with God away from the distractions of the world.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب مريم إذ انتبذت من أهلها مكانا شرقيا

translation: So she took, in seclusion from them, a screen. Then We sent to her Our Angel, and he represented himself to her as a well-proportioned man.
interpretation: This verse describes the story of the Virgin Mary and the miraculous birth of Jesus. Mary secluded herself from her people and then the Angel Gabriel appeared to her in the form of a man to deliver the news of her immaculate conception. The interpretation is that God sent His Angel to Mary to inform her of the divine plan and the birth of Jesus, the Messiah.
orig: فاتخذت من دونهم حجابا فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشرا سويا

translation: She said, "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing [Allah]."
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Maryam (Mary) in the Qur'an. It shows Maryam's piety and her reliance on Allah's protection when confronted by a stranger. The interpretation is that one should seek refuge in Allah, the Most Merciful, when facing any difficulty or challenge, especially if the other person is righteous and God-fearing.
orig: قالت إني أعوذ بالرحمن منك إن كنت تقيا

translation: He said, "I am only a messenger of your Lord to give you [the gift of] a pure son."
interpretation: This verse is from the Quran, Surah Maryam (19:19). It is part of the story of the Annunciation, where the angel Gabriel appears to the Virgin Mary and informs her that she will give birth to a son, the Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him). The interpretation of this verse is that the angel is conveying to Mary that he is a messenger from God, sent to bestow upon her the gift of a pure, righteous son - the Messiah, Jesus Christ.
orig: قال إنما أنا رسول ربك لأهب لك غلاما زكيا

translation: She said, "How can I have a son when no man has touched me, and I have not been unchaste?"
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, and it is a response from the Virgin Mary to the angel who informed her that she would give birth to a son, despite her being a virgin. The interpretation of this verse is that it emphasizes the miraculous nature of the virgin birth of Jesus, as Mary is expressing her surprise and wonder at how this could be possible without a man's involvement. This highlights the divine nature of Jesus' conception and birth, and the power of God to create life in a way that defies human understanding.
orig: قالت أنى يكون لي غلام ولم يمسسني بشر ولم أك بغيا

translation: Thus has your Lord said, "It is an easy matter for Me," and [We will do it] that We may make him a sign for the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter [already] decreed."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ease with which Allah can accomplish His will, and that the birth of a child to the elderly couple (Zechariah and his wife) will serve as a sign and a mercy from Allah to the people. The matter has already been decreed by Allah, and will come to pass as He has willed.
orig: قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين ولنجعله آية للناس ورحمة منا وكان أمرا مقضيا

translation: And she carried him, and she withdrew with him to a remote place.
interpretation: This verse describes the birth of Jesus and how his mother Mary withdrew to a remote place to give birth to him. The interpretation suggests that Mary sought solitude and privacy during this significant event, away from the distractions and judgments of society.
orig: فحملته فانتبذت به مكانا قصيا

translation: And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, "Oh, I wish I had died before this and was in oblivion, forgotten."
interpretation: This verse describes the difficult experience of the Virgin Mary during the birth of Jesus. The pains of childbirth overwhelmed her, causing her to wish for death rather than face the challenges ahead. The interpretation suggests that even the most righteous individuals can face moments of despair and longing for an escape from their circumstances, highlighting the human experience of the Prophets.
orig: فأجاءها المخاض إلى جذع النخلة قالت يا ليتني مت قبل هذا وكنت نسيا منسيا

translation: Then the (angel) called her from below her, "Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream."
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Mary to not be saddened or distressed, as God has provided for her and her son Jesus a source of sustenance and comfort during their time of need. It symbolizes God's care and support for those who face difficulties in life.
orig: فناداها من تحتها ألا تحزني قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا

translation: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will let fall upon you fresh, ripe dates.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Mary to seek sustenance from the date palm tree during her time of need. The shaking of the tree and the falling of the ripe dates symbolize the provision and care that God will provide for those who trust in Him, even in the most difficult circumstances.
orig: وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة تساقط عليك رطبا جنيا

translation: So eat and drink and be contented. And if you see from among humanity anyone, say, 'Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak today to [any] man.'
interpretation: This verse encourages the addressee, often interpreted as the Virgin Mary, to take care of herself and her needs after the hardship of childbirth. It then instructs her to refrain from speaking to anyone, as she has vowed a fast to the Most Merciful (God). The interpretation suggests a focus on devotion, humility, and self-care in the face of extraordinary circumstances.
orig: فكلي واشربي وقري عينا فإما ترين من البشر أحدا فقولي إني نذرت للرحمن صوما فلن أكلم اليوم إنسيا

translation: Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, "O Mary, you have certainly done a remarkable thing."
interpretation: This verse describes the miraculous birth of Jesus to the Virgin Mary. When Mary returned to her people with the infant Jesus, they were astonished and acknowledged that she had done something extraordinary, as she had given birth without a father. This highlights the divine nature of Jesus' conception and birth, which was a sign of Allah's power and a testament to Mary's purity and faith.
orig: فأتت به قومها تحمله قالوا يا مريم لقد جئت شيئا فريا

translation: O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil nor was your mother unchaste.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to Prophet Maryam (Mary), the mother of Prophet Isa (Jesus). It is a reassurance from Allah that her lineage is pure and that she is not the daughter of a wicked man or an unchaste woman. This verse refutes any accusations or doubts about Maryam's noble ancestry and her own purity and righteousness.
orig: يا أخت هارون ما كان أبوك امرأ سوء وما كانت أمك بغيا

translation: Then she pointed to him. They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle a child?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the miraculous birth of Jesus, where the newborn Jesus spoke from the cradle, testifying to his prophethood. The people were astonished at this, questioning how they could converse with a child in the cradle. This demonstrates the divine power and wisdom of God, who can bestow extraordinary abilities upon His chosen messengers.
orig: فأشارت إليه قالوا كيف نكلم من كان في المهد صبيا

translation: He said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet."
interpretation: This verse expresses the humility and devotion of the prophet, who declares that he is a servant of Allah and that it is Allah who has bestowed upon him the Scripture and the status of a prophet. It emphasizes the divine origin of the prophet's mission and the fact that he is merely a conduit for Allah's message, not the source of it.
orig: قال إني عبد الله آتاني الكتاب وجعلني نبيا

translation: And He has made me blessed wherever I am and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and responsibilities bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes that he was made a blessed individual, with the divine favor and guidance following him wherever he went. Additionally, it underscores the importance of maintaining a steadfast commitment to prayer and charitable giving (zakah) throughout one's lifetime as a fundamental aspect of faith and devotion.
orig: وجعلني مباركا أين ما كنت وأوصاني بالصلاة والزكاة ما دمت حيا

translation: And dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a wretched tyrant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being dutiful and caring towards one's parents, particularly one's mother. It also highlights that the individual has not been made a wretched tyrant, suggesting that they have been guided towards righteous and humble conduct.
orig: وبرا بوالدتي ولم يجعلني جبارا شقيا

translation: And peace be upon me the day I was born and the day I die and the day I am raised alive.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of peace and tranquility in one's life, from the day of birth to the day of death and resurrection. It suggests that the individual should strive to maintain a state of peace and contentment throughout their life, regardless of the circumstances they face.
orig: والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حيا

translation: That is Jesus, the son of Mary - the word of truth about which they are in dispute.
interpretation: This verse affirms the status of Jesus as the son of Mary and the word of truth. It highlights the fact that there is dispute and disagreement among people regarding the nature and status of Jesus, which the Qur'an seeks to clarify and resolve.
orig: ذلك عيسى ابن مريم قول الحق الذي فيه يمترون

translation: It is not [befitting] for Allah to take a son; exalted is He. When He decrees an affair, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Almighty, is free from the need for a son or any other family relationship. He is the Supreme Being, who simply commands something to exist, and it comes into being immediately without any need for a son or any other intermediary. This highlights the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah, who is self-sufficient and not in need of any other being to carry out His will.
orig: ما كان لله أن يتخذ من ولد سبحانه إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the importance of worshiping Him alone. It reminds us that Allah is the Lord and Creator of all, and that the path of worshiping Him is the straight and true path to follow. It calls upon all people to devote themselves to Allah and submit to His will.
orig: وإن الله ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And the parties differed [i.e., separated] among themselves, and woe to those who disbelieved from the scene of a tremendous Day.
interpretation: This verse highlights the division and discord that will arise among the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. It conveys a sense of dread and anguish that the disbelievers will face when confronted with the immense and awe-inspiring nature of that momentous day.
orig: فاختلف الأحزاب من بينهم فويل للذين كفروا من مشهد يوم عظيم

translation: We hear them and see them the Day they come to Us, but the wrongdoers today are in clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, the wrongdoers will be fully aware of their misdeeds and the consequences they face, as Allah will make them hear and see the truth they had previously denied. However, in their current state, the wrongdoers are in a state of clear misguidance, unable to recognize the truth and heed the warnings.
orig: أسمع بهم وأبصر يوم يأتوننا لكن الظالمون اليوم في ضلال مبين

translation: And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be concluded, while they are in [a state of] heedlessness and while they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse warns the disbelievers of the Day of Regret, when they will realize the consequences of their disbelief and rejection of faith. On that day, the matter will be concluded, and they will be held accountable for their actions, even though they were heedless and did not believe in God's signs and the Day of Judgment.
orig: وأنذرهم يوم الحسرة إذ قضي الأمر وهم في غفلة وهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Indeed, it is We who will inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah is the ultimate owner and inheritor of the earth and all that is in it. All people and creation will eventually return to Allah, the All-Knowing and All-Powerful, for judgment and accountability.
orig: إنا نحن نرث الأرض ومن عليها وإلينا يرجعون

translation: And mention, [O Muhammad], in the Book [the story of] Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the high status of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) as a truthful and prophetic figure. It encourages the reader to reflect on the life and teachings of this great messenger of God, who exemplified sincerity, righteousness, and divine guidance.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and will not benefit you in anything?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Prophet Abraham questioning his father's worship of idols that cannot hear, see or provide any benefit. The interpretation is that one should not worship anything besides the one true God, as only God has the power to hear, see and provide for His creation.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه يا أبت لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنك شيئا

translation: O my father, indeed I have been given knowledge that has not come to you. So follow me; I will guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse conveys the importance of seeking and acquiring knowledge, and the responsibility to guide others towards the right path. The son has been granted knowledge that his father does not possess, and he urges his father to follow him in order to be guided along the straight and righteous path. This highlights the value of education and the duty to share one's knowledge for the benefit of others.
orig: يا أبت إني قد جاءني من العلم ما لم يأتك فاتبعني أهدك صراطا سويا

translation: O my father! Do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has been to the Most Merciful disobedient.
interpretation: This verse urges us to not worship or follow Satan, as Satan has been disobedient and rebellious towards the Most Merciful, God. It reminds us to turn away from Satan's temptations and instead submit to the will of God, who is the source of all mercy and guidance.
orig: يا أبت لا تعبد الشيطان إن الشيطان كان للرحمن عصيا

translation: O my father! I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you so you would become a companion to Satan.
interpretation: This verse expresses the concern of a son for his father, who is in danger of incurring the punishment of Allah due to his association with Satan. The son is urging his father to turn away from the path of Satan and towards the path of righteousness, lest he be subjected to the wrath of the Most Merciful.
orig: يا أبت إني أخاف أن يمسك عذاب من الرحمن فتكون للشيطان وليا

translation: He said, 'Do you turn away from my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so avoid me a great while.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the confrontation between the prophet Abraham and his people who worshipped idols. The verse highlights the hostility and intolerance that the people showed towards Abraham for rejecting their false gods and calling them to worship the one true God. The verse demonstrates the importance of steadfastness in faith and the willingness to face persecution for the sake of one's beliefs.
orig: قال أراغب أنت عن آلهتي يا إبراهيم لئن لم تنته لأرجمنك واهجرني مليا

translation: He said, 'Peace be upon you, I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He is to me the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse conveys the humility and repentance of a person seeking forgiveness from God. The speaker acknowledges God's mercy and willingness to accept repentance, expressing a desire to seek forgiveness on behalf of another. It highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and God's compassionate nature towards those who turn to Him in sincere repentance.
orig: قال سلام عليك سأستغفر لك ربي إنه كان بي حفيا

translation: And I will withdraw from you and those you invoke other than Allah, and I will call upon my Lord. I expect that I will not be in invocation to my Lord [ever] unhappy.
interpretation: This verse expresses the intention of the speaker to separate themselves from those who worship other gods besides Allah, and to devote themselves solely to the worship of their Lord. The speaker expresses the hope that in doing so, they will not be disappointed or unhappy in their supplications to their Lord.
orig: وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله وأدعو ربي عسى ألا أكون بدعاء ربي شقيا

translation: And when he had withdrawn from them and that which they were worshipping besides Allah, We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and each [of them] We made a prophet.
interpretation: This verse describes how the prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) turned away from the idols and false deities that his people were worshipping, and in return, Allah blessed him with two righteous sons, Isaac and Jacob, both of whom were also made prophets. This highlights how turning away from falsehood and dedicating oneself to the worship of the One True God is rewarded with divine guidance and prophethood.
orig: فلما اعتزلهم وما يعبدون من دون الله وهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وكلا جعلنا نبيا

translation: And We have granted them from Our mercy and made for them a tongue of honesty and high [reputation].
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has bestowed His mercy upon the believers and has granted them a high and truthful reputation. The "tongue of honesty" suggests that they are known for their truthfulness, sincerity, and good character, which has earned them a position of high esteem among the people.
orig: ووهبنا لهم من رحمتنا وجعلنا لهم لسان صدق عليا

translation: And mention, [O Muhammad], in the Book [the story of] Moses. Indeed, he was chosen and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the status and importance of the Prophet Moses in the Qur'an. It emphasizes that Moses was a chosen messenger of God, a prophet who was entrusted with conveying the divine message to his people. The verse underscores Moses' sincerity, dedication, and prophetic role, which serve as an example and inspiration for believers.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب موسى إنه كان مخلصا وكان رسولا نبيا

translation: And We called him from the right side of the Mount, and We brought him near, [to converse with Us].
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Moses, and the event of Allah calling him from the right side of Mount Sinai and bringing him close to have a direct conversation with Him. This represents the close and intimate relationship between Allah and His chosen prophet, and the importance of the divine revelation received by Moses.
orig: وناديناه من جانب الطور الأيمن وقربناه نجيا

translation: And We granted him, out of Our Mercy, his brother Aaron as a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine grace and mercy of Allah, who bestowed upon the Prophet Moses his brother Aaron as a prophet to assist and support him in his mission. The inclusion of Aaron as a prophet alongside Moses underscores the importance of unity, cooperation, and mutual support in carrying out the divine message.
orig: ووهبنا له من رحمتنا أخاه هارون نبيا

translation: And mention, [O Muhammad], in the Book [the story of] Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtues of the Prophet Ishmael, who was one of the prophets sent by God. It emphasizes that Ishmael was true to his promise, meaning that he fulfilled his duties and obligations as a prophet. The verse also affirms that Ishmael was a messenger and a prophet, underscoring his status as a divinely-appointed messenger who conveyed God's teachings to his people.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إسماعيل إنه كان صادق الوعد وكان رسولا نبيا

translation: And he used to enjoin on his people prayer and zakah, and he was to his Lord pleasing.
interpretation: This verse describes the righteous character of a person who encouraged his family and community to perform their religious obligations, such as prayer and charity. He was a person who was beloved and pleasing to Allah, the Almighty. This highlights the importance of not only fulfilling one's own religious duties, but also guiding and encouraging others to do the same, as this is a sign of a person who is beloved by Allah.
orig: وكان يأمر أهله بالصلاة والزكاة وكان عند ربه مرضيا

translation: And mention, [O Muhammad], in the Book [the story of] Idrees. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the status of the prophet Idrees (Enoch) as a truthful and righteous prophet of God. It encourages the remembrance and veneration of this noble messenger, who exemplified the qualities of truthfulness and prophethood.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إدريس إنه كان صديقا نبيا

translation: And We have raised him to a high station
interpretation: This verse refers to the exalted status and honor bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by Allah. It signifies that Allah has elevated the Prophet's rank and position, granting him a lofty and esteemed place among all of creation.
orig: ورفعناه مكانا عليا

translation: Those are the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among the prophets from the descendants of Adam and from those We carried [in the ship] with Noah, and from the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and from those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fall down in prostration and weeping.
interpretation: This verse highlights the high status of the prophets and those who have been guided and chosen by Allah. It emphasizes that the prophets, including those from the lineage of Adam, Noah, Abraham, and Israel, have been bestowed with Allah's favor and guidance. When the verses of the Qur'an, which represent the mercy of Allah, are recited to them, they respond with humility, prostration, and sincere emotion, demonstrating their deep faith and reverence for the divine message.
orig: أولئك الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين من ذرية آدم وممن حملنا مع نوح ومن ذرية إبراهيم وإسرائيل وممن هدينا واجتبينا إذا تتلى عليهم آيات الرحمن خروا سجدا وبكيا

translation: Then there followed them a posterity who lost their prayers and followed desires, so they will meet Ghayy.
interpretation: This verse describes a subsequent generation that neglected their religious obligations, such as performing the daily prayers, and instead pursued their own selfish desires. As a result, they will face the consequences of their actions, which are described as "Ghayy" - a state of loss, destruction, or wretchedness.
orig: فخلف من بعدهم خلف أضاعوا الصلاة واتبعوا الشهوات فسوف يلقون غيا

translation: Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work - those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged in the least.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the path to salvation is through repentance, faith, and righteous deeds. Those who follow this path will be granted entry into Paradise and will not be subjected to any injustice or unfair treatment.
orig: إلا من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون شيئا

translation: Gardens of Eden, which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen. Indeed, His promise has ever been a subject of arrival [i.e., fulfillment].
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal gardens of Paradise that God has promised to those who believe in Him and do righteous deeds, even though they cannot see it in this life. The interpretation is that God's promise of Paradise is certain to be fulfilled, as He is the Most Merciful and always keeps His word.
orig: جنات عدن التي وعد الرحمن عباده بالغيب إنه كان وعده مأتيا

translation: They will not hear therein any ill speech but only [greetings of] peace, and they will have their provision therein, morning and afternoon.
interpretation: This verse describes the tranquility and peace that will be experienced by the inhabitants of Paradise. They will not hear any idle or harmful speech, but only greetings of peace. Additionally, they will be provided for in abundance, receiving their sustenance and nourishment both in the morning and evening.
orig: لا يسمعون فيها لغوا إلا سلاما ولهم رزقهم فيها بكرة وعشيا

translation: That is the Garden which We will give as inheritance to those of Our servants who were fearing [Allah].
interpretation: This verse refers to the eternal Paradise that Allah will grant as an inheritance to those of His servants who were righteous and God-fearing in their worldly lives. It highlights that Paradise is not earned through one's own efforts, but is a gift bestowed by Allah upon those who have lived a life of piety and devotion to Him.
orig: تلك الجنة التي نورث من عبادنا من كان تقيا

translation: And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between, and your Lord is never forgetful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the revelation of the Qur'an and the events that unfold are all under the command and will of God. He has knowledge and control over the past, present, and future, and nothing happens without His decree. This serves to reassure believers that God is in complete control and that His plan will unfold as He wills, not as per human desires or whims.
orig: وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا وما بين ذلك وما كان ربك نسيا

translation: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so worship Him and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know of any similarity to Him?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and uniqueness of God, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. It calls upon the believer to worship and be steadfast in their devotion to God, as there is none comparable to Him.
