The rhetorical question "Do you know of any similarity to Him?" reinforces the idea that God is unparalleled and incomparable, and that the believer should focus their worship and allegiance solely on Him.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما فاعبده واصطبر لعبادته هل تعلم له سميا

translation: And the human says, "When I have died, will I surely be brought forth [to new] life?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and doubt that some people have about the afterlife and resurrection. The human being questions whether they will truly be brought back to life after death, expressing disbelief in the idea of life after death. This verse serves as a reminder that faith in the afterlife is a core tenet of Islamic belief, and that those who deny it will be held accountable on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويقول الإنسان أإذا ما مت لسوف أخرج حيا

translation: Does not man remember that We created him before, while he was nothing?
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on the origin of human existence. It reminds us that we were created by God from nothing, highlighting our dependence on the divine and the profound miracle of our creation. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of acknowledging our humble beginnings and the need to be grateful to the Creator.
orig: أولا يذكر الإنسان أنا خلقناه من قبل ولم يك شيئا

translation: So, by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils, and then We will bring them to be present around Hell, upon their knees.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity and the forces of evil will be gathered and presented before the eternal fire of Hell. The posture of being "upon their knees" suggests a state of humiliation, submission, and helplessness before the Almighty.
orig: فوربك لنحشرنهم والشياطين ثم لنحضرنهم حول جهنم جثيا

translation: Then We will surely extract from every sect those of them who were worst in rebellion against the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will separate the most rebellious and defiant individuals from each group or sect, and hold them accountable for their actions against the Most Merciful. It indicates that those who were the most arrogant and disobedient towards Allah will be singled out and punished accordingly.
orig: ثم لننزعن من كل شيعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتيا

translation: Then, We are most knowing of those who are most worthy of it [i.e., the Fire] to be burned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has the ultimate knowledge and wisdom in determining who deserves punishment in the Hellfire. It serves as a reminder that the judgment of people's deeds and their ultimate destinations in the Hereafter lies solely in the hands of the All-Knowing and All-Wise Allah, and not in the hands of humans.
orig: ثم لنحن أعلم بالذين هم أولى بها صليا

translation: And there is none of you but he shall come to it. That is with your Lord a decree that must be accomplished.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everyone will ultimately face the Day of Judgment, as it is a decree from God that must be fulfilled. It serves as a reminder to believers to prepare for the Hereafter and to live their lives in accordance with the teachings of Islam.
orig: وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا

translation: Then We will save those who feared Us, and We will leave the wrongdoers within it, [fallen] upon their knees.
interpretation: This verse indicates that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will save those who feared Him and lived righteously, while leaving the wrongdoers to face the consequences of their actions, humbled and defeated.
orig: ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Which of the two parties is best in position and best in association?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and dismissive attitude of the disbelievers towards the believers when the clear verses of the Qur'an are recited to them. The disbelievers challenge the believers, questioning which group is superior in terms of status, position, and companionship. This verse serves as a warning against the pride and conceit of the disbelievers, who fail to recognize the truth and guidance in the Qur'an.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا

translation: And how many generations have We destroyed before them who were better in wealth and appearance?
interpretation: This verse highlights that previous generations who were more prosperous and advanced in their worldly possessions and outward appearances were nonetheless destroyed by Allah. This serves as a reminder that material wealth and physical appearances are not the true measure of a society's worth, and that ultimately, all people and civilizations are subject to Allah's judgment and will.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا ورئيا

translation: Say, "Whoever is in error - let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension [in wealth and provision] until, when they see that which they were promised - either punishment or the Hour - they will know who is in more lasting position and who is weaker in soldiers."
interpretation: This verse encourages patience and perseverance in the face of disbelief and misguidance. It suggests that God will give those who are in error a chance to reflect and turn back to the right path, extending His mercy and provision to them. However, this extension is not indefinite, and ultimately they will face the consequences of their choices, whether it be punishment or the coming of the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes that the true position of strength and power lies with God and His believers, not with those who reject the truth.
orig: قل من كان في الضلالة فليمدد له الرحمن مدا حتى إذا رأوا ما يوعدون إما العذاب وإما الساعة فسيعلمون من هو شر مكانا وأضعف جندا

translation: And Allah increases in guidance those who are rightly guided, and the good deeds that endure are better to your Lord for reward and better for [one's] hope.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah rewards and increases the guidance of those who are righteous and follow the path of truth. The good deeds that a person performs and that endure, such as acts of charity, worship, and kindness, are the most valuable and will be rewarded by Allah in the best manner. This is better than the fleeting pleasures of this world and provides a more lasting and meaningful reward.
orig: ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا هدى والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير مردا

translation: Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children [in the Hereafter]?"
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question, challenging the disbeliever who rejects the signs and messages of Allah, and who claims that he will be granted wealth and children in the Hereafter as a reward for his disbelief. The interpretation is that such a person is deluded and misguided, for true success and salvation can only be attained through faith and righteous deeds, not through disbelief and arrogance.
orig: أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا وقال لأوتين مالا وولدا

translation: Has he [i.e., the disbeliever] been informed of the unseen, or has he taken from the Most Merciful a promise?
interpretation: This verse questions whether the disbeliever has been granted knowledge of the unseen or made a covenant with the Most Merciful. The implication is that the disbeliever has no such special knowledge or divine promise, and thus their rejection of faith is unfounded.
orig: أطلع الغيب أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا

translation: No! We will record what he says, and We will extend to him from the punishment [a prolonged length].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah will hold the disbelievers accountable for their words and deeds, and that they will face a severe and prolonged punishment for their rejection of the truth and their transgressions.
orig: كلا سنكتب ما يقول ونمد له من العذاب مدا

translation: And We will inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone.
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, a person will be held accountable for their words and actions, and they will stand alone before God, without any support or assistance from others. It emphasizes the individual responsibility and the importance of being mindful of one's speech and deeds, as they will be a witness against the person on that day.
orig: ونرثه ما يقول ويأتينا فردا

translation: And they have taken gods besides Allah that they might be to them a [source of] strength.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of worshipping other deities besides Allah, in the belief that they will provide strength and support. The Qur'an emphasizes that Allah alone is worthy of worship and that seeking power or assistance from any other source is misguided and futile.
orig: واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة ليكونوا لهم عزا

translation: Nay, they will [surely] deny their worship of them and be against them an opponent.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who worship false idols or deities will eventually come to deny their worship and turn against the very objects they once venerated. It implies that such beliefs and practices are ultimately futile and will be abandoned in the end.
orig: كلا سيكفرون بعبادتهم ويكونون عليهم ضدا

translation: Have you not considered that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them to [evil] with [constant] incitement?
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has sent the devils to incite and provoke the disbelievers, leading them further astray from the truth. The interpretation is that Allah allows the devils to tempt and deceive the disbelievers, as a means of testing their faith and resolve.
orig: ألم تر أنا أرسلنا الشياطين على الكافرين تؤزهم أزا

translation: So do not impatiently urge them. We only count out to them a [limited] number [of days].
interpretation: This verse advises against rushing or being impatient with those who reject the message of Islam. It suggests that Allah has a plan and a specific timeline for them, and that they will be held accountable in due course. The interpretation is that one should trust in Allah's wisdom and timing, and avoid the temptation to force the matter or seek immediate retribution.
orig: فلا تعجل عليهم إنما نعد لهم عدا

translation: The day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that on the Day of Judgment, the righteous people will be gathered and presented before the Most Merciful, Allah, in a dignified and honored manner, as a delegation or honored group.
orig: يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا

translation: And We will drive the criminals to [Hell], to [Hellfire], as cattle are driven to water.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the wrongdoers will be forcibly driven to the eternal punishment of Hell, just as cattle are herded to water. This conveys the inevitability and severity of the punishment that awaits those who reject faith and commit sins.
orig: ونسوق المجرمين إلى جهنم وردا

translation: They do not possess [the power of] intercession except [on behalf of] one who has taken from the Most Merciful a covenant.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the ability to intercede on behalf of others is limited to those who have a special covenant or relationship with the Most Merciful (Allah). It implies that there are no intermediaries or intercessors who can independently grant forgiveness or salvation, and that the ultimate authority rests with Allah alone.
orig: لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا من اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا

translation: And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken [for Himself] a son."
interpretation: This verse refutes the notion that God has taken a son, which was a belief held by some people at the time. The interpretation is that God, the Most Merciful, is self-sufficient and does not need a son or any other being. He is the sole Creator and Sustainer of all things.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا

translation: You have certainly come [with] something tremendous
interpretation: This verse expresses the astonishment and amazement of the disbelievers at the profound teachings and miraculous nature of the Qur'an. It suggests that the message of the Qur'an is something extraordinary and unprecedented, which challenges their preconceptions and demands a serious consideration of its truth.
orig: لقد جئتم شيئا إدا

translation: The heavens are about to burst from it and the earth to split open, and the mountains to collapse in detrition.
interpretation: This verse conveys the immense power and magnitude of God's message and the profound impact it can have on the very fabric of the universe. It suggests that the Qur'anic teachings are so profound and transformative that they can shake the foundations of the cosmos, causing the heavens to tremble, the earth to split, and the mountains to crumble. This emphasizes the gravity and importance of the divine message and the need for humankind to heed it with utmost reverence and sincerity.
orig: تكاد السماوات يتفطرن منه وتنشق الأرض وتخر الجبال هدا

translation: That they ascribe to the Most Merciful a son
interpretation: This verse is rejecting the notion of God having a son, which was a belief held by some people at the time. The interpretation is that the idea of God having a offspring is incompatible with the concept of God as the Most Merciful, All-Powerful and Unique Creator.
orig: أن دعوا للرحمن ولدا

translation: And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is not appropriate or befitting for God, the Most Merciful, to have a son. The concept of God having a son is rejected in Islam, as it contradicts the fundamental belief in the oneness and uniqueness of God (tawhid). The interpretation suggests that God is self-sufficient and does not need a son or any other being to be associated with Him.
orig: وما ينبغي للرحمن أن يتخذ ولدا

translation: Indeed, whoever is in the heavens and the earth will come to the Most Merciful as a servant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all of creation, whether in the heavens or on earth, will eventually submit to the Almighty and Merciful God as His servants. It highlights the universal sovereignty of Allah and the ultimate humility of all beings before their Creator.
orig: إن كل من في السماوات والأرض إلا آتي الرحمن عبدا

translation: He has counted them and numbered them precisely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omniscience and complete knowledge of all things, including the number of His creation. It suggests that nothing escapes God's awareness and that He has perfect knowledge of all that exists.
orig: لقد أحصاهم وعدهم عدا

translation: And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual and personal nature of the Day of Resurrection. On that day, each person will stand alone before God to account for their actions, without the support or influence of others. This underscores the importance of personal responsibility and the need for each individual to prepare for the ultimate reckoning.
orig: وكلهم آتيه يوم القيامة فردا

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them [i.e., grant them] affection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have faith in God and do good deeds will be granted the love and affection of the Most Merciful, God. It suggests that believers who lead righteous lives will be rewarded with a special closeness and bond with the Divine, which is a profound blessing and source of comfort and joy.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سيجعل لهم الرحمن ودا

translation: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Qur'an has been made easy to understand and remember, in order to convey the message of glad tidings to the righteous and to warn those who are stubborn and resistant to guidance.
orig: فإنما يسرناه بلسانك لتبشر به المتقين وتنذر به قوما لدا

translation: And how many generations have We destroyed before them? Can you perceive any of them, or hear from them a sound?
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of human civilizations and the inevitability of their demise. It suggests that the current generation should not be arrogant or complacent, as previous generations have been destroyed despite their apparent strength and prosperity. The verse encourages reflection on the ephemeral nature of worldly existence and the importance of preparing for the Hereafter.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هل تحس منهم من أحد أو تسمع لهم ركزا

translation: Ta, Ha.
interpretation: This is the opening of Surah Ta-Ha, one of the longer chapters of the Qur'an. The letters "Ta" and "Ha" are part of the group of "disconnected letters" that appear at the beginning of certain Qur'anic chapters. Their exact meaning is not definitively known, but they are believed to be a symbolic way of emphasizing the divine nature and authority of the Qur'an. The chapter that follows goes on to recount stories and teachings that are meant to guide and inspire the reader.
orig: طه

translation: We have not sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Qur'an that you be distressed
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that the revelation of the Qur'an was not intended to cause him hardship or distress. Rather, it was revealed to guide and benefit humanity. The Qur'an is a source of mercy, guidance, and ease, not a burden or source of difficulty. This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an was sent down to bring about the well-being and prosperity of the believers, not to cause them anguish or suffering.
orig: ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى

translation: Except as a reminder to whoever would fear [Allah]
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Qur'an is a reminder and guidance for those who fear and revere Allah. It is not meant to be a mere intellectual exercise, but a source of inspiration and motivation for those who seek to live a righteous life in accordance with the teachings of Islam. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a deep, reverent attitude towards Allah and being mindful of one's actions and their consequences.
orig: إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى

translation: A revelation from He who created the earth and the highest heavens.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a revelation from God, the Creator of the earth and the heavens above. It establishes the divine origin of the Qur'an, affirming that it is not the work of a human but rather a message revealed by the Almighty, the One who brought the entire universe into existence. This serves to reinforce the authority and truth of the Qur'anic teachings, as they come directly from the All-Knowing and All-Powerful Creator.
orig: تنزيلا ممن خلق الأرض والسماوات العلى

translation: The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme power and sovereignty of God, the Most Merciful. It affirms that God has established Himself above the Throne, which is a symbol of His absolute authority and control over the entire creation. This verse reminds us that God is the ultimate source of mercy and that His mercy extends to all of His creation. It also underscores the importance of submitting to God's will and seeking His guidance, as He alone has the power to govern the universe and determine the fate of all beings.
orig: الرحمن على العرش استوى

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is under the soil.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and dominion of God over all creation. It affirms that God is the sole owner and controller of the entire universe, including the heavens, the earth, and everything in between them, as well as what lies beneath the surface of the earth. This highlights the vastness of God's power and the extent of His authority, which is unparalleled and beyond human comprehension. It serves as a reminder to believers to submit to God's will and to acknowledge His supreme authority in all aspects of their lives.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وما بينهما وما تحت الثرى

translation: And if you speak aloud - then indeed, He knows the secret and what is [even] more hidden.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God is all-knowing and aware of even the most hidden thoughts and intentions of people. Whether one speaks openly or conceals their words, God is cognizant of all that is said and all that is hidden within the heart and mind. This serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and speech, as God is the ultimate witness and judge.
orig: وإن تجهر بالقول فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names.
interpretation: This verse affirms the oneness and supremacy of God. It states that Allah is the only true deity, and that all the most beautiful and perfect names and attributes belong to Him alone. This emphasizes the exclusive divinity and sovereignty of God, and calls upon believers to worship and glorify Him as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو له الأسماء الحسنى

translation: And has the story of Moses reached you?
interpretation: This verse is asking whether the story of the prophet Moses has reached the listener. The story of Moses is one of the most prominent narratives in the Qur'an, as it provides guidance and lessons for believers. The question implies that the story of Moses is an important one that everyone should be familiar with, as it contains valuable wisdom and insights.
orig: وهل أتاك حديث موسى

translation: When he saw a fire, he said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch or find at the fire some guidance."
interpretation: This verse describes the Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) seeing a fire while traveling with his family. He tells them to wait while he goes to investigate the fire, hoping to either bring back a torch to light their way or find some guidance from the fire. This represents Moses' initial encounter with the divine, as the fire will soon become the site of his calling to prophethood by God.
orig: إذ رأى نارا فقال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس أو أجد على النار هدى

translation: And when he came to it, he was called, 'O Moses!'
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when Moses approached the burning bush, and he was called out to by God. This was a pivotal moment in the life of Moses, as it marked the beginning of his divine mission to lead the Israelites out of Egypt. The calling of Moses by God signifies the start of his prophetic role and the unfolding of God's plan for him and his people.
orig: فلما أتاها نودي يا موسى

translation: Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) when he was called by Allah to prophethood at the sacred valley of Tuwa. The command to remove his sandals is a sign of reverence and humility in the presence of the Divine. The verse emphasizes the sacredness of the place and the importance of the encounter between Moses and his Lord, which would lead to his mission of freeing the Israelites from the tyranny of Pharaoh.
orig: إني أنا ربك فاخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى

translation: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed [to you].
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), indicating that God has chosen him to receive divine revelation. The verse encourages the Prophet to listen attentively and obediently to the Qur'an and other revelations that are being conveyed to him, as this is a great honor and responsibility. The interpretation suggests that we should also strive to listen to and follow the guidance provided in the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet, as they contain the truth and wisdom from the Almighty.
orig: وأنا اخترتك فاستمع لما يوحى

translation: Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute oneness and sovereignty of Allah (God). It calls upon the believers to worship Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him. The command to establish prayer is a means of remembering Allah and maintaining a close connection with Him. This verse emphasizes the fundamental principle of Islamic monotheism and the importance of worshiping the one true God.
orig: إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدني وأقم الصلاة لذكري

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - so that every soul may be recompensed for that which it strives to earn.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the coming of the Day of Judgment (the Hour), which is a fundamental belief in Islam. The verse suggests that even though the exact timing of the Hour is known only to God, it is inevitable and will come to pass. The purpose of this is so that every person will be held accountable for their actions and deeds in this life, and will be justly rewarded or punished based on what they have earned through their efforts and choices. This serves as a reminder to believers to live righteously and prepare for the Hereafter.
orig: إن الساعة آتية أكاد أخفيها لتجزى كل نفس بما تسعى

translation: So let not those who disbelieve therein turn you away from it and follow their [own] desires, lest you perish.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against being swayed by those who reject the message of the Qur"an and instead follow their own desires. It cautions the believer not to be deterred from the truth by those who do not believe, as that could lead to one"s own spiritual downfall and destruction.
orig: فلا يصدنك عنها من لا يؤمن بها واتبع هواه فتردى

translation: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between God and the prophet Moses. It is a question posed by God to Moses, asking him about the object he is holding in his right hand. This question is significant as it marks the beginning of God's communication with Moses and the start of his prophethood. The interpretation is that God is initiating a conversation with Moses, drawing his attention to the object in his hand, which will later be revealed to be the staff that Moses will use to perform miracles and lead the Israelites out of Egypt.
orig: وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى

translation: He said: "This is my staff; I lean upon it, and I beat down branches with it for my sheep, and I have other uses for it."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Taha, verse 18. It is part of the story of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) and his encounter with Allah at the Mount of Sinai. In this verse, Moses is describing the staff he carries, which he uses to support himself, to herd his sheep, and for other purposes. The interpretation of this verse is that it highlights the importance of using the tools and resources we have been given by Allah in a beneficial and productive manner, whether it is for our own needs or to assist others. It also suggests that we should not limit ourselves to the obvious or immediate uses of the things we possess, but be open to discovering other ways in which they can be utilized.
orig: قال هي عصاي أتوكأ عليها وأهش بها على غنمي ولي فيها مآرب أخرى

translation: He said, "Throw it, O Moses!"
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Taha, verse 19. It is part of the narrative where Allah commands Prophet Moses to throw down his staff, which then transforms into a serpent. This command signifies Allah's power and ability to bring about extraordinary events, demonstrating His sovereignty and the need for Moses to submit to His will. The interpretation suggests that we should be willing to obey Allah's commands, even if they seem extraordinary or beyond our understanding, as He is the All-Knowing and All-Powerful.
orig: قال ألقها يا موسى

translation: And he threw it, and suddenly it was a snake, slithering.
interpretation: This verse describes the miracle of Prophet Moses, when he threw down his staff and it transformed into a living snake. This event is a sign of Allah's power and Moses' prophethood. The swift movement of the snake represents the power and immediacy of Allah's creation, demonstrating His ability to transform the ordinary into the extraordinary.
orig: فألقاها فإذا هي حية تسعى

translation: He said: "Take it, and fear not. We shall return it to its former state."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) and the miraculous staff he was given by God. When Moses threw his staff on the ground, it turned into a snake, and God commanded him to "take it and fear not." This was a sign of God's power and a reassurance to Moses that he need not be afraid, as God would restore the staff to its original form. The interpretation is that God provides His servants with the means to overcome their challenges, and that they should trust in Him and not be afraid, as He will guide them and restore what was lost.
orig: قال خذها ولا تخف سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى

translation: And draw your hand close to your side; it will come out white without disease - another sign
interpretation: This verse is referring to the miracle of Prophet Moses, when he was commanded by God to put his hand into his garment and then withdraw it, and it would come out shining white without any disease or blemish. This was one of the signs that God gave to Moses to demonstrate His power and to convince Pharaoh and his people of the truth of Moses' message. The verse is encouraging the reader to seek signs and miracles from God as a means of strengthening their faith and belief.
orig: واضمم يدك إلى جناحك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء آية أخرى

translation: We will show you some of Our greatest signs.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah will reveal some of His most profound and awe-inspiring signs and wonders to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and, through him, to all of humanity. These signs may be in the form of miracles, profound teachings, or clear evidence of Allah's power and wisdom in the universe. The purpose is to strengthen the faith of believers and guide those who are seeking the truth.
orig: لنريك من آياتنا الكبرى

translation: Go to Pharaoh, indeed he has transgressed.
interpretation: This verse is a command from God to the Prophet Moses to go to Pharaoh, the ruler of Egypt at the time, and confront him. The verse indicates that Pharaoh has become arrogant and tyrannical, overstepping the bounds of his authority and oppressing the Israelites who were under his rule. The instruction to "go to Pharaoh" signifies that Moses should stand up to Pharaoh's oppression and call him to account for his transgressions against God's laws and the rights of the people.
orig: اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى

translation: He said, 'My Lord, expand for me my breast [with assurance]'
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Taha, verse 25. It is a supplication by the Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) to his Lord, asking for his heart and mind to be opened and expanded, so that he may receive and convey the divine message with ease and clarity. The interpretation is that when one is entrusted with a great responsibility, they should seek Allah's help and guidance to be able to fulfill it to the best of their abilities.
orig: قال رب اشرح لي صدري

translation: And ease for me my matter
interpretation: This verse is a supplication, where the person is asking Allah to make their affairs and tasks easy for them. It expresses a desire for Allah's assistance and guidance in navigating the challenges and complexities of life. The interpretation suggests that the person is seeking Allah's help and support to overcome difficulties and find success in their endeavors.
orig: ويسر لي أمري

translation: And ease my tongue [i.e., remove the difficulty] from [my speech]
interpretation: This verse is a supplication by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to Allah, asking Him to remove any impediment or difficulty in his speech and to make it easy for him to convey the message of Islam. It reflects the humility and reliance on God that the Prophet (peace be upon him) demonstrated, even though he was entrusted with the great responsibility of receiving and delivering the Qur'an. The interpretation suggests that one should seek God's help and guidance in overcoming any obstacles or challenges they face in effectively communicating and fulfilling their duties.
orig: واحلل عقدة من لساني

translation: That they may understand my speech
interpretation: This verse expresses the desire of the speaker, likely a prophet or messenger of God, for their audience to comprehend and grasp the meaning of what they are saying. The emphasis is on the importance of understanding the message being conveyed, rather than just hearing the words. The speaker wants their audience to truly internalize and apprehend the significance of the message, so that they may act upon it accordingly.
orig: يفقهوا قولي

translation: And appoint for me a minister from my family
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, and it is a supplication made by the Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) to Allah. In this verse, Moses is asking Allah to appoint a minister or assistant from among his own family members to help him in his mission of guiding the Israelites. The interpretation is that it is important to have trusted and capable individuals around us to support us in our endeavors, especially when it comes to matters of great importance. This teaches us the value of seeking help and guidance from those who are close to us and who share our goals and values.
orig: واجعل لي وزيرا من أهلي

translation: Harun is my brother
interpretation: This verse refers to the prophet Moses (peace be upon him) mentioning his brother Aaron (Harun) as his brother. This highlights the close relationship and support between the two prophets as they were both tasked with guiding the Israelites. The verse emphasizes the importance of brotherhood, unity and cooperation in carrying out the divine mission.
orig: هارون أخي

translation: Strengthen my back with him
interpretation: This verse is a supplication from the Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) to Allah, asking Him to strengthen his resolve and provide him with assistance in his mission. The phrase "strengthen my back with him" suggests that Moses is seeking the support and reinforcement of a companion or helper who can provide him with the strength and courage he needs to carry out his responsibilities. This verse highlights the importance of seeking divine aid and relying on Allah's support in times of challenge and difficulty.
orig: اشدد به أزري

translation: And include him in my matter
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to involve and consult his companion, likely referring to his close associate or advisor, in important matters and decisions. It emphasizes the importance of seeking counsel and collaboration, rather than acting alone, when faced with significant issues or tasks. The interpretation suggests that seeking input from trusted individuals can lead to better outcomes and decisions.
orig: وأشركه في أمري

translation: That we may glorify You much
interpretation: This verse expresses the desire to constantly praise and glorify Allah, the Almighty. It suggests that the purpose of our existence is to remember and revere God through abundant remembrance and glorification. The verse encourages us to devote ourselves to the remembrance of Allah, as this is a means of attaining spiritual fulfillment and closeness to the Divine.
orig: كي نسبحك كثيرا

translation: And remember Him often.
interpretation: This verse encourages the remembrance of God frequently. It suggests that one should constantly keep God in mind, through dhikr (remembrance) and other forms of worship. This helps to maintain a strong connection with the divine, and serves as a reminder of one"s purpose in life and the ultimate accountability before God.
orig: ونذكرك كثيرا

translation: Indeed, you have always been to us a Seer.
interpretation: This verse expresses the acknowledgment of the people towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as someone who has deep insight and awareness of their affairs. It conveys the idea that the Prophet was endowed with a profound understanding of the people, their needs, and their circumstances, which enabled him to guide them effectively. This verse highlights the Prophet's exceptional wisdom, foresight, and ability to perceive the truth, which were essential qualities for his role as a messenger of God.
orig: إنك كنت بنا بصيرا

translation: He said, "You have been granted your request, O Moses."
interpretation: This verse refers to God's response to Moses' request. Moses had asked God to appoint his brother Aaron as his helper and minister, and God granted this request. The interpretation is that God is responsive to the sincere requests of His servants and is willing to provide them with the support and assistance they need to carry out their divine mission.
orig: قال قد أوتيت سؤلك يا موسى

translation: And We have certainly conferred upon you, [O Muhammad], another favor.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the additional blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It suggests that Allah has granted him further guidance, wisdom, and support to carry out his mission of conveying the divine message to humanity. This verse emphasizes the continuous care and attention that Allah provides to His chosen messengers, ensuring they are equipped with the necessary means to fulfill their responsibilities.
orig: ولقد مننا عليك مرة أخرى

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We inspired to your mother what We inspired
interpretation: This verse refers to the time when Allah revealed to the mother of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to place him in a basket and set him afloat on the river, which ultimately led to him being found and raised by the family of Pharaoh. This was part of Allah's plan to protect the Prophet (peace be upon him) and prepare him for the great mission of prophethood.
orig: إذ أوحينا إلى أمك ما يوحى

translation: Cast him into the chest, then cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank; an enemy to Me and an enemy to him will take him. And I bestowed upon you love from Myself and that you would be brought up under My eye.
interpretation: This verse describes the command given by God to the mother of Prophet Moses to cast him into the river in a chest, so that he would be saved from the persecution of Pharaoh. God promises that an enemy of Pharaoh and an enemy of Moses would find and take care of him. Additionally, God bestowed His love upon Moses and ensured that he would be raised under His watchful eye. This verse highlights God's protection and care for His chosen prophets, even in the face of great adversity.
orig: أن اقذفيه في التابوت فاقذفيه في اليم فليلقه اليم بالساحل يأخذه عدو لي وعدو له وألقيت عليك محبة مني ولتصنع على عيني

translation: And when your sister went and said, "Shall I direct you to one who will be responsible for him?" So We restored you to your mother that she might be content and not grieve. And you killed a person, but We saved you from retaliation and tried you with a [severe] trial. And you remained [some] years among the people of Madyan. Then you came [here] at the decreed time, O Moses.
interpretation: This verse recounts key events from the life of the Prophet Moses (peace be upon him). It describes how when Moses was a child, his sister led Pharaoh's people to his mother, who then cared for him. It also mentions how Moses later killed a man, for which he was forgiven, and how he spent years among the people of Madyan before being called by God to his prophetic mission. The verse highlights God's guidance, protection and trials of Moses throughout his life, ultimately leading him to his destined purpose. The interpretation emphasizes God's hand in shaping the life of a prophet, and the importance of trusting in divine plan even through difficulty.
orig: إذ تمشي أختك فتقول هل أدلكم على من يكفله فرجعناك إلى أمك كي تقر عينها ولا تحزن وقتلت نفسا فنجيناك من الغم وفتناك فتونا فلبثت سنين في أهل مدين ثم جئت على قدر يا موسى

translation: And I have chosen you for Myself
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has chosen and prepared the individual for a special purpose or role. The interpretation is that the individual has been selected and molded by God for a divine plan or mission, which the individual is now entrusted to fulfill. This verse conveys a sense of divine election and purpose, where the individual is seen as being specially crafted and designated by God for a unique task or destiny.
orig: واصطنعتك لنفسي

translation: Go, you and your brother, with My signs and do not slacken in My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to Prophet Moses and his brother Aaron, instructing them to go forth with the signs and miracles that God has granted them, and to remain steadfast in their remembrance and worship of God. The emphasis is on the importance of maintaining a strong connection with the divine, even in the face of challenges or opposition. The verse highlights the need for unwavering faith and dedication in the pursuit of God's message and guidance.
orig: اذهب أنت وأخوك بآياتي ولا تنيا في ذكري

translation: Go to Pharaoh, indeed he has transgressed.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the Prophets Moses and Aaron, instructing them to go to the tyrannical ruler Pharaoh and call him to the path of righteousness. The word "طغى" (transgressed) implies that Pharaoh had exceeded all bounds of justice, morality, and obedience to God, and had become arrogant and oppressive in his rule. The command to "go to Pharaoh" signifies the duty of the Prophets to confront the oppressor and invite him to repent and submit to the will of God.
orig: اذهبا إلى فرعون إنه طغى

translation: And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear [Allah].
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers to speak to the disbelievers with kindness and compassion, rather than harshness or confrontation. The goal is to soften their hearts and make them receptive to the message of Islam, so that they may remember the truth and develop a reverence for Allah. This approach is more likely to lead to their guidance and salvation than a harsh or aggressive one.
orig: فقولا له قولا لينا لعله يتذكر أو يخشى

translation: They [Musa and Harun] said, "Our Lord, indeed we are afraid that he will hasten [punishment] against us or that he will transgress."
interpretation: In this verse, Musa (Moses) and Harun (Aaron) are expressing their fear that the Pharaoh may either rush to punish them or exceed all bounds in his tyranny and oppression. They are seeking refuge in Allah, their Lord, from the Pharaoh's potential excesses and injustice. This highlights the importance of relying on Allah and seeking His protection when facing powerful and unjust adversaries.
orig: قالا ربنا إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى

translation: He said, "Fear not, indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Taha, verse 46. It is part of the dialogue between Prophet Moses and God, where God reassures Moses and his brother Aaron that He is with them, hears their prayers, and sees their circumstances. This verse conveys the message that believers need not fear, for God is always present, watching over them and guiding them, even in the face of challenges and adversity.
orig: قال لا تخافا إنني معكما أسمع وأرى

translation: So go to him and say, "Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace will be upon he who follows the guidance."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Moses and Pharaoh. It instructs Moses and Aaron to go to Pharaoh and convey a message from God. The key points are: 1) Moses and Aaron are messengers of God, 2) they are to ask Pharaoh to let the Israelites go, 3) they should not be tortured, 4) they bring a sign (miracle) from God, and 5) peace will be upon those who follow God's guidance. The overall message is one of authority, compassion, and a call to faith in the one true God.
orig: فأتياه فقولا إنا رسولا ربك فأرسل معنا بني إسرائيل ولا تعذبهم قد جئناك بآية من ربك والسلام على من اتبع الهدى

translation: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment is upon he who denies the truth and turns away
interpretation: This verse conveys a stern warning from Allah to those who reject the truth of His message and teachings, and turn away from it. The punishment mentioned refers to the consequences and retribution that will befall those who stubbornly disbelieve and refuse to submit to the will of Allah. This serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to avoid the path of denial and turning away from the guidance provided in the Qur'an.
orig: إنا قد أوحي إلينا أن العذاب على من كذب وتولى

translation: He (Pharaoh) said, "Then who is the Lord of you two, O Moses?"
interpretation: This verse is part of the dialogue between Pharaoh and Moses. Pharaoh is challenging Moses and questioning his claim of being sent by a higher authority, the Lord. The interpretation is that Pharaoh is asserting his own power and authority, and is demanding that Moses acknowledge him as the supreme ruler. This exchange highlights the conflict between Pharaoh's arrogance and Moses' faith in the one true God.
orig: قال فمن ربكما يا موسى

translation: Our Lord is He who gave to each thing its creation and then guided [it].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the belief that God is the Creator of all things, and that He has also guided each creation towards its intended purpose. It suggests that God has a plan and purpose for all of His creations, and that He provides guidance to help them fulfill that purpose. The interpretation is that we should have faith in God's wisdom and trust that He has a plan for us, even if we do not always understand it.
orig: قال ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى

translation: He said, "What then is the case of the former generations?"
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between Prophet Moses and Pharaoh. The question posed by Pharaoh suggests a challenge to the message of Prophet Moses, implying that the previous generations had not been punished for their disbelief, and therefore the warnings of punishment were not credible. The interpretation is that Pharaoh is questioning the validity of the message and the consequences of rejecting it, by citing the apparent lack of divine punishment for earlier generations who had also disbelieved.
orig: قال فما بال القرون الأولى

translation: He said, "Its knowledge is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets."
interpretation: This verse refers to the knowledge of the Hour (the Day of Resurrection) and when it will occur. The speaker, believed to be the Prophet Muhammad, states that the exact timing of the Hour is known only to God, and that God does not make mistakes or forget anything. This emphasizes the certainty of the Hour's arrival, as well as God's absolute knowledge and power over all things.
orig: قال علمها عند ربي في كتاب لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى

translation: It is He who made for you the earth as a [firm] resting place and the sky as a [sustained] structure and sent down from the sky, rain and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not attribute to Allah equals while you know [that there is nothing similar to Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and providence in creating the Earth as a habitable place for humanity, providing water from the sky to sustain life, and bringing forth a variety of vegetation for our sustenance. It reminds us that we should not ascribe any partners or equals to God, as He alone is the Creator and Sustainer of all things.
orig: الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا وسلك لكم فيها سبلا وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به أزواجا من نبات شتى

translation: Eat and pasture your livestock. Indeed in that are signs for those of intelligence.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to enjoy the provisions that Allah has provided, such as food and livestock, while also reminding them to be mindful and appreciative of these blessings. The mention of "signs for those of intelligence" suggests that reflecting on the natural world and the way Allah sustains life can lead to a deeper understanding of the divine and the purpose of existence.
orig: كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى

translation: From the [earth] have We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will extract you [another] extraction.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the cyclical nature of human existence - that we are created from the earth, will return to it after death, and will then be resurrected from it on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder of our humble origins and the inevitability of our return to Allah, the Creator, who has the power to bring us back to life after death.
orig: منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم ومنها نخرجكم تارة أخرى

translation: And We have certainly shown him [i.e., man] Our signs, but he denied and refused.
interpretation: This verse refers to the human being's tendency to reject and deny the clear signs and evidence of God's existence and power that are manifest in the universe and in one's own self. Despite being presented with undeniable proofs of the Creator, the human being often chooses to disbelieve and disobey, out of arrogance, stubbornness or a desire to live according to their own whims and desires. This verse serves as a warning against such willful rejection of the truth and a call to reflect on the signs of God and submit to His guidance.
orig: ولقد أريناه آياتنا كلها فكذب وأبى

translation: He said, "Have you come to us to drive us out of our land by your magic, O Moses?"
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between the Pharaoh and Prophet Moses (peace be upon him). The Pharaoh accuses Moses of using magic to drive the people out of their land, which was a common accusation against prophets who called people to worship God alone. The Pharaoh's response reflects his arrogance and unwillingness to accept the truth of Moses' message, as he sees it as an attempt to undermine his power and authority.
orig: قال أجئتنا لتخرجنا من أرضنا بسحرك يا موسى

translation: So we will surely bring you magic the like of it, and appoint between us and you a meeting place that we will not fail to keep, neither we nor you.
interpretation: This verse is a challenge from the disbelievers to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to bring a miracle or magic similar to what they were doing. They proposed a meeting place where they would both demonstrate their abilities, and neither side would fail to show up. This was a test of the Prophet’s claim of prophethood and the truthfulness of the Qur’an.
orig: فلنأتينك بسحر مثله فاجعل بيننا وبينك موعدا لا نخلفه نحن ولا أنت مكانا سوى

translation: He said, 'Your appointment is the Day of Adornment, and the people shall be gathered at forenoon.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when all people will be gathered before God for judgment. The "Day of Adornment" suggests a day of great splendor and significance, when people will be resplendent in their appearance, either in the beauty of their righteous deeds or the shame of their misdeeds. The gathering "at forenoon" implies a time of clarity and visibility, when the truth will be made manifest and people will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: قال موعدكم يوم الزينة وأن يحشر الناس ضحى

translation: Then Pharaoh turned his back, and gathered (his power). Then he came (against Moses).
interpretation: This verse describes Pharaoh's reaction after Moses and Aaron delivered God's message to him. Pharaoh dismissed their call, and instead gathered his resources and forces to confront them. This represents Pharaoh's arrogance and unwillingness to submit to God's command, leading to his eventual downfall.
orig: فتولى فرعون فجمع كيده ثم أتى

translation: Moses said to them, "Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allah or He will destroy you with a punishment, and he has certainly failed who fabricates [a lie]."
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from Prophet Moses to his people not to fabricate lies about Allah or attribute false statements to Him. The consequence of such an action would be a severe punishment from Allah. The verse emphasizes that those who invent lies against Allah are doomed to fail, as they have strayed from the truth and will face the consequences of their deeds.
orig: قال لهم موسى ويلكم لا تفتروا على الله كذبا فيسحتكم بعذاب وقد خاب من افترى

translation: And they disputed about their affair among themselves and they concealed [their] private conversation.
interpretation: This verse describes a situation where a group of people were in disagreement and dispute about a certain matter. They kept their discussion and deliberation secret, not revealing it to others. This suggests that the matter was sensitive or controversial, and they wanted to keep it private. The interpretation is that when people are in disagreement, they should strive to resolve it through open and transparent dialogue, rather than resorting to secretive discussions and decision-making.
orig: فتنازعوا أمرهم بينهم وأسروا النجوى

translation: They said, "Indeed, these two are magicians who want to drive you out of your land by their magic and do away with your most exemplary way [of life]."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of Pharaoh and his people to the miracles performed by Moses and Aaron. They accused the two prophets of being magicians who sought to use their magic to overthrow the existing order and displace the people from their land. The interpretation suggests that the ruling elite saw the message of Moses and Aaron as a threat to their power and influence, and they sought to discredit the prophets by portraying them as deceitful sorcerers rather than true messengers of God.
orig: قالوا إن هذان لساحران يريدان أن يخرجاكم من أرضكم بسحرهما ويذهبا بطريقتكم المثلى

translation: So gather your plan and come [at once] in a line. And whoever gains the upper hand this Day will be successful.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the disbelievers to unite and gather their forces against the Prophet Muhammad and his followers. It is a challenge to them to come together in a united front and try to defeat the believers. The verse assures that whoever gains the upper hand on that day will be successful. The interpretation suggests that the ultimate victory belongs to those who are steadfast in their faith and trust in God, regardless of the apparent strength of their opponents.
orig: فأجمعوا كيدكم ثم ائتوا صفا وقد أفلح اليوم من استعلى

translation: They said, "O Moses, either you throw [your staff], or we will be the ones to throw [first]."
interpretation: This verse describes a confrontation between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh. The magicians challenged Moses to a contest, asking him to either cast his staff first or to allow them to cast theirs. This was a test of power and authority, as the magicians sought to demonstrate that their magic was superior to that of Moses. The verse highlights the arrogance and confidence of the magicians, who believed they could outperform the miracle performed by Moses.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إما أن تلقي وإما أن نكون أول من ألقى

translation: He said, "Rather, you throw." And suddenly their ropes and their staffs seemed to him from their magic to be moving [like snakes].
interpretation: This verse describes a scene from the story of Prophet Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh. When Moses was commanded by God to confront Pharaoh, the magicians of Pharaoh were summoned to challenge Moses. They threw down their ropes and staffs, which appeared to be moving like snakes through their magic. However, when Moses threw down his staff, it swallowed up their illusions, demonstrating the superiority of God's power over the magicians' tricks. This verse highlights the power of faith and truth over deception and falsehood.
orig: قال بل ألقوا فإذا حبالهم وعصيهم يخيل إليه من سحرهم أنها تسعى

translation: So Moses conceived a fear within himself.
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment when Moses encountered God at the burning bush. After God spoke to him and commanded him to go to Pharaoh, Moses felt a sense of fear and apprehension within himself. This fear likely stemmed from the weight of the responsibility God had placed upon him, as well as the potential dangers he would face in confronting the powerful Pharaoh. The verse highlights Moses' human emotions and doubts, even as he was chosen by God for this important mission.
orig: فأوجس في نفسه خيفة موسى

translation: We said, "Do not fear. Indeed, it is you who are the Superior."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, and it is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse reassures him that he has no need to fear, as he is the most exalted and superior among all people. This is a statement of encouragement and affirmation of the Prophet's high status and position in the sight of God. The interpretation conveys a message of confidence, strength, and divine favor bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad.
orig: قلنا لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى

translation: And throw down what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have created. They have only created the illusion of a snake, and the magician will not succeed wherever he may go.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the incident when Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) confronted the magicians of Pharaoh. When the magicians used their tricks to create the illusion of snakes, Moses was commanded to throw down his staff, which then swallowed up their illusions. This verse emphasizes that the tricks of the magicians were merely an illusion, and that true power lies with God. It also suggests that the efforts of those who engage in falsehood and deception will ultimately fail, no matter where they go.
orig: وألق ما في يمينك تلقف ما صنعوا إنما صنعوا كيد ساحر ولا يفلح الساحر حيث أتى

translation: So the magicians fell down in prostration. They said, "We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the magicians when they witnessed the miracle performed by Moses, which surpassed their own magical abilities. They recognized the power of God and prostrated themselves in submission, declaring their belief in the Lord of Aaron and Moses. This event marked a significant turning point, as the magicians acknowledged the truth of Moses' message and the superiority of the divine power he represented.
orig: فألقي السحرة سجدا قالوا آمنا برب هارون وموسى

translation: He said, "Have you believed in him before I gave you permission? Indeed, he is your chief who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet from opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in [punishment] and more enduring."
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between the Pharaoh and the magicians who had challenged Prophet Moses (peace be upon him). The Pharaoh is threatening the magicians with severe punishment for believing in Moses and his message, before the Pharaoh had given them permission to do so. The Pharaoh claims that he is the supreme authority, and that he had taught them magic, so they had no right to believe in Moses without his approval. The Pharaoh's threats of cutting off their limbs and crucifying them are a demonstration of his arrogance and cruelty, as he tries to assert his power and dominance over the magicians. The verse highlights the Pharaoh's tyrannical nature and his refusal to submit to the truth of God's message, even in the face of clear signs and miracles.
orig: قال آمنتم له قبل أن آذن لكم إنه لكبيركم الذي علمكم السحر فلأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل ولتعلمن أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى

translation: They said, "We will never prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and [over] He who created us. So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life."
interpretation: This verse reflects the response of the disbelievers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) when he called them to believe in the oneness of God and the message of Islam. The disbelievers refused to accept the Prophet's call, claiming that they would not give up their traditional beliefs and practices in favor of the clear proofs and guidance that the Prophet brought. They asserted that they would only follow the path that their forefathers had established, as they believed that was the true way. The verse emphasizes that the disbelievers' decision was limited to the worldly life and did not consider the consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: قالوا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات والذي فطرنا فاقض ما أنت قاض إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا

translation: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us [to do] of the magic. And Allah is the best and most enduring.
interpretation: This verse expresses the belief and faith of the people in their Lord, seeking His forgiveness for their sins and for being compelled to engage in magic, which is a prohibited act. The verse highlights that Allah is the best and most enduring, emphasizing the importance of seeking His mercy and guidance rather than relying on the temporary and deceptive nature of magic.
orig: إنا آمنا بربنا ليغفر لنا خطايانا وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر والله خير وأبقى

translation: Indeed, he who comes to his Lord as a criminal - then indeed, for him is Hell, in which he will neither die nor live.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who come before God having committed sins and wrongdoings will be condemned to the eternal torment of Hell, where they will neither find relief in death nor a state of living, but rather a perpetual state of suffering and punishment.
orig: إنه من يأت ربه مجرما فإن له جهنم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى

translation: And whoever comes to Him as a believer having done righteous deeds - for those will be the highest degrees [in position].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the highest degrees or ranks in the hereafter are reserved for those who come to God in a state of faith and have done good deeds. It suggests that faith and righteous actions are the keys to attaining the highest spiritual stations and nearness to God. The interpretation is that one's ultimate success and elevated status in the afterlife is dependent on both believing in God and actively doing good works.
orig: ومن يأته مؤمنا قد عمل الصالحات فأولئك لهم الدرجات العلى

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence, beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. And that is the reward of one who purifies himself.
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal paradise that is promised to those who purify themselves and live righteous lives. The gardens of Eden, with their flowing rivers, represent the blissful and everlasting nature of this reward for the believers. The key message is that the ultimate reward for spiritual purification and righteous conduct is the eternal abode in paradise.
orig: جنات عدن تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء من تزكى

translation: And We had inspired to Moses, "Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path through the sea, not fearing overtaking and not [being] afraid [of drowning]."
interpretation: This verse refers to the Israelites' exodus from Egypt under the leadership of Prophet Moses. God commanded Moses to lead the Israelites out of Egypt and through the Red Sea, which He would part to allow them to cross safely. The verse emphasizes that the Israelites should not fear being overtaken by Pharaoh's army or drowning in the sea, as God would protect them and provide a dry path for them to walk on. This is a testament to God's power and His ability to save those who believe in Him and follow His commands.
orig: ولقد أوحينا إلى موسى أن أسر بعبادي فاضرب لهم طريقا في البحر يبسا لا تخاف دركا ولا تخشى

translation: Then Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, and the sea overwhelmed them that which overwhelmed them
interpretation: This verse describes how Pharaoh and his army chased after the Israelites after they had been freed from slavery in Egypt. However, when they reached the sea, God caused the waters to overwhelm and drown Pharaoh's entire army, delivering the Israelites from their oppressors. This event is a powerful demonstration of God's might and His ability to save those who trust in Him, even from the most formidable of enemies.
orig: فأتبعهم فرعون بجنوده فغشيهم من اليم ما غشيهم

translation: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide [them].
interpretation: This verse highlights how Pharaoh misled and misguided his people, failing to provide them with proper guidance and direction. It suggests that Pharaoh's leadership was not focused on the well-being and guidance of his people, but rather on his own selfish interests and desires. The verse emphasizes the importance of righteous and benevolent leadership that seeks to guide and uplift the people, rather than lead them astray.
orig: وأضل فرعون قومه وما هدى

translation: O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a covenant with you on the right side of the Mount, and We sent down to you Manna and quails.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Children of Israel, reminding them of Allah's blessings and favors upon them. It highlights how Allah saved them from their enemies, made a covenant with them at the right side of Mount Sinai, and provided them with the sustenance of Manna and quails. This verse emphasizes Allah's guidance, protection, and provision for the Children of Israel, and serves as a reminder for them to be grateful and obedient to Allah.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل قد أنجيناكم من عدوكم وواعدناكم جانب الطور الأيمن ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى

translation: Eat of the good things We have provided for you, and do not transgress, lest My wrath should descend upon you. And he upon whom My wrath descends has indeed fallen into utter ruin.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to enjoy the blessings and provisions that God has bestowed upon them, but to do so in moderation and without excess or transgression. It warns that those who incur God's wrath by going beyond the bounds of what is permitted will face severe consequences. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of gratitude, moderation, and obedience to God's commands in order to avoid His displeasure and the resulting spiritual and worldly downfall.
orig: كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم ولا تطغوا فيه فيحل عليكم غضبي ومن يحلل عليه غضبي فقد هوى

translation: And indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver for whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah’s boundless mercy and forgiveness for those who sincerely repent, believe, and do good deeds, and then continue to follow the right path. It conveys the idea that no matter how grave one’s sins may be, Allah is always willing to forgive those who turn to Him with a genuine heart and a desire to reform their ways. The verse encourages believers to seek Allah’s forgiveness, have faith, and strive to do good, as this is the surest way to attain His pleasure and eternal salvation.
orig: وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى

translation: And what has made you hasten from your people, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse is addressing Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) and inquiring about his hasty departure from his people. The implication is that Moses had left his people in a hurry, perhaps due to a pressing matter or an urgent situation. The question suggests that there was a reason behind his hasty departure, which is being asked about. The verse encourages Moses to reflect on his actions and the circumstances that led him to leave his people so quickly.
orig: وما أعجلك عن قومك يا موسى

translation: He said: 'They are close upon my footsteps, and I have hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased.'
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Taha, verse 84. It depicts the words of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) when he returned to his people after receiving the commandments from Allah on Mount Sinai. The verse conveys that Moses hastened back to his people, hoping that Allah would be pleased with his actions and the guidance he brought to them. This highlights the importance of seeking Allah's pleasure and doing what is right, even when faced with challenges from one's own people.
orig: قال هم أولاء على أثري وعجلت إليك رب لترضى

translation: He said, 'Indeed, We have tried your people after you [i.e., your departure], and the Samiri has led them astray.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the incident when the Prophet Moses left his people for a period of time, and during his absence, a man named the Samiri led the people astray and made them worship a golden calf. The verse indicates that God had tested the people of Moses after he left them, and the Samiri was responsible for leading them into misguidance and idolatry.
orig: قال فإنا قد فتنا قومك من بعدك وأضلهم السامري

translation: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, "O my people, did not your Lord make you a good promise? Then, was the time [of its fulfillment] too long for you, or did you wish that displeasure from your Lord should descend upon you, so you broke your promise to me?"
interpretation: This verse describes Moses' reaction upon returning to his people and finding them worshipping the golden calf in his absence. He is angry and grieved, and he questions them about the promise their Lord had made to them. The interpretation is that Moses is admonishing his people for their lack of faith and their hasty decision to turn away from God's covenant, which had led to the displeasure of God descending upon them. He is reminding them of the good promise their Lord had made, and questioning whether they had grown impatient or whether they had deliberately sought God's wrath by breaking their promise to Moses.
orig: فرجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا قال يا قوم ألم يعدكم ربكم وعدا حسنا أفطال عليكم العهد أم أردتم أن يحل عليكم غضب من ربكم فأخلفتم موعدي

translation: They said, "We did not break our promise to you by our own authority, but we were made to carry [some of] the people's ornaments and we threw them [into the fire], and thus did the Samiri throw [them]."
interpretation: This verse describes the response of the Israelites to Prophet Moses when he returned and found them worshipping a golden calf. They claimed that they did not intentionally break their promise to Moses, but were coerced into contributing their ornaments, which were then used by the Samiri to create the idol. The interpretation suggests that the people were easily swayed by the Samiri's deception and lost their way, despite their earlier commitment to worship only Allah.
orig: قالوا ما أخلفنا موعدك بملكنا ولكنا حملنا أوزارا من زينة القوم فقذفناها فكذلك ألقى السامري

translation: And he extracted for them [the statue of] a calf which had a body, and it lowed. And they said, "This is your god and the god of Moses, but he has forgotten."
interpretation: This verse describes the incident when the Israelites worshipped a golden calf in the absence of Prophet Moses. The calf was created by Samiri, who had taken advantage of the people's weak faith and led them astray. The verse highlights the foolishness of the Israelites in worshipping an inanimate object, and their rejection of the true God and the message of Prophet Moses. It serves as a warning against idolatry and the importance of maintaining a steadfast faith in the One True God.
orig: فأخرج لهم عجلا جسدا له خوار فقالوا هذا إلهكم وإله موسى فنسي

translation: Do they not see that it [i.e., the Qur'an] returns not to them [any] word, and that they are not those who can [truly] harm or benefit them?
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who reject the message of the Qur'an and are unwilling to believe in it. It is pointing out that the Qur'an does not return to them with any word or message that they want to hear, but rather it conveys the truth that they are unwilling to accept. Additionally, it emphasizes that these rejecters have no power to harm or benefit the believers, as the ultimate power and control lies with Allah alone.
orig: أفلا يرون ألا يرجع إليهم قولا ولا يملك لهم ضرا ولا نفعا

translation: And Aaron had already told them before, 'O my people, you are only being tried by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the incident when Moses left his people in the care of his brother Aaron, and in his absence, the Israelites began worshipping a golden calf. Aaron had warned them against this, but they did not heed his advice. The verse emphasizes that this was a trial for the people, and that they should have followed Aaron's guidance and obeyed his commands, as their Lord is the Most Merciful and would have forgiven them if they had repented.
orig: ولقد قال لهم هارون من قبل يا قوم إنما فتنتم به وإن ربكم الرحمن فاتبعوني وأطيعوا أمري

translation: They said, "We will never cease being devoted to it [the calf] until Moses returns to us."
interpretation: This verse describes the Israelites who worshipped the golden calf in the absence of Moses. They were so enamored with the idol that they refused to abandon it, even after Moses returned, until he forced them to do so. This highlights the human tendency to be easily swayed by material objects and false gods, and the importance of steadfast faith and obedience to the true God, as represented by Moses and his teachings.
orig: قالوا لن نبرح عليه عاكفين حتى يرجع إلينا موسى

translation: He said, 'O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray?'
interpretation: This verse is from the Quran, Surah Ta-Ha, verse 92. It is part of the story of Prophet Moses and his brother Aaron. When Moses went up to Mount Sinai to receive the commandments, he left Aaron in charge of the Israelites. During his absence, the Israelites started worshipping a golden calf. When Moses returned and saw this, he asked Aaron what prevented him from stopping the people from going astray. The interpretation of this verse is that it emphasizes the responsibility of leaders and those in authority to guide and correct their people when they stray from the right path. It highlights the importance of taking action and not remaining passive in the face of wrongdoing.
orig: قال يا هارون ما منعك إذ رأيتهم ضلوا

translation: Will you not then follow me?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question posed by God, addressing the human being. It is a call to obedience and submission to God's commands. The verse suggests that disobedience to God's orders is a grave mistake that should be avoided. The interpretation is that one should follow and obey God's directives without hesitation or defiance.
orig: ألا تتبعن أفعصيت أمري

translation: He said, "O son of my mother, do not seize [me] by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You caused division among the Children of Israel, and you did not observe [or await] my word.'"
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Taha, verse 94. It is part of the story of Prophet Moses and his brother Aaron. The verse portrays the concern of Aaron that his actions might be misunderstood and lead to division among the Israelites, which he feared would displease Moses. The interpretation is that one should be mindful of the consequences of their actions and strive to maintain unity and harmony, even if their intentions are good. It emphasizes the importance of observing the guidance and instructions of righteous leaders.
orig: قال يا ابن أم لا تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي إني خشيت أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ولم ترقب قولي

translation: He said, "And what was your case, O Samiri?"
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Taha, verse 95. It is part of the story of the Prophet Moses and the Israelites. After Moses returns from the mountain, he finds that the Israelites have worshipped a golden calf in his absence. The verse is a question posed by Moses to the Samiri, the one who had led the Israelites astray and made the golden calf. The interpretation is that Moses is inquiring about the Samiri's motives and actions, seeking to understand why he had caused such a deviation from the true faith.
orig: قال فما خطبك يا سامري

translation: He (Moses) said: "I perceived something which they perceived not, and I have grasped a handful from the footprint of the Messenger, and that I have done (as my work). And I did it not of my own accord but it was done by the prompting of my heart."
interpretation: This verse describes an event from the life of Prophet Moses. It indicates that Moses perceived or understood something that others around him did not. He then took a handful of dust from the footprint of the Messenger (likely referring to Prophet Muhammad), and did something with it, which he acknowledges was prompted by his own soul or desires, rather than a direct command from God. This suggests that Moses acted based on his own interpretation or judgment, rather than clear divine guidance. The verse highlights the importance of following divine instructions carefully, rather than relying solely on one's own perceptions or inclinations.
orig: قال بصرت بما لم يبصروا به فقبضت قبضة من أثر الرسول فنبذتها وكذلك سولت لي نفسي

translation: He (Pharaoh) said: 'Go away! And indeed for you (in the life of this world) is (the promise of) not to be touched (i.e. you will be respited), and indeed, you have (another) appointment (in the Hereafter) which you cannot miss. And look at your god to whom you have been devoted. We will surely burn it and scatter its (particles in the sea).'
interpretation: This verse describes Pharaoh's response to Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) after Moses called him to believe in the One true God. Pharaoh arrogantly dismisses Moses, threatening that he will not be harmed in this life, but that he has an appointment with punishment in the Hereafter that he cannot escape. Pharaoh then mocks Moses' belief in God, saying he will burn the idol that Moses worships and scatter its remains in the sea. This verse highlights Pharaoh's stubborn rejection of the truth and his belief in his own power and divinity, which ultimately led to his destruction.
orig: قال فاذهب فإن لك في الحياة أن تقول لا مساس وإن لك موعدا لن تخلفه وانظر إلى إلهك الذي ظلت عليه عاكفا لنحرقنه ثم لننسفنه في اليم نسفا
