translation: Your God is but Allah, the One, there is no deity except Him. He encompasses all things in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of God, known as Allah in the Islamic tradition. It states that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, who is the sole creator and sustainer of the universe. The verse also highlights Allah's infinite knowledge and wisdom, as He encompasses all things with His knowledge. This reinforces the belief that Allah alone is worthy of worship and that He has complete control and understanding of all aspects of existence.
orig: إنما إلهكم الله الذي لا إله إلا هو وسع كل شيء علما

translation: Thus We relate to you, [O Muhammad], from the news of what has preceded [before], and We have given you from Us a reminder.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah is revealing to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) the stories and events of the past, which serve as a reminder and guidance for the people. The Quran is a revelation from Allah that contains the wisdom and knowledge needed for humanity to live a righteous life. By relating these past events, Allah is establishing the continuity of His message and the truthfulness of the Quran as the final revelation.
orig: كذلك نقص عليك من أنباء ما قد سبق وقد آتيناك من لدنا ذكرا

translation: And whoever turns away from it - then indeed, he will bear [on the Day of Resurrection] a burden [of sin]
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who turn away from the guidance and teachings of the Qur'an. It warns that on the Day of Judgment, they will bear the burden and consequences of their rejection and disobedience. The interpretation is that those who choose to ignore or reject the divine guidance revealed in the Qur'an will be held accountable for their actions and will face the punishment for their sins on the Day of Resurrection.
orig: من أعرض عنه فإنه يحمل يوم القيامة وزرا

translation: Abiding therein. And wretched for them is the Day of Resurrection as a load.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who reject faith and do evil deeds. They will be in the Fire of Hell forever, and the Day of Resurrection will be a heavy burden and punishment for them.
orig: خالدين فيه وساء لهم يوم القيامة حملا

translation: The Day when the Trumpet will be blown, and you will be gathered in groups,
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Resurrection, when the Trumpet will be blown, and all people will be gathered before God for judgment. The term "زرقا" (zurqa) refers to the discolored, lifeless eyes of the criminals on that Day, indicating their fear, distress, and hopelessness. The interpretation suggests that on the Day of Judgment, the wrongdoers will be gathered in a state of despair and dejection, facing the consequences of their misdeeds.
orig: يوم ينفخ في الصور ونحشر المجرمين يومئذ زرقا

translation: They converse in secret among themselves: "You have remained not but ten [days]."
interpretation: This verse refers to a group of people who were discussing the length of time that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his companions would remain in Medina. They were whispering to each other, believing that the Prophet's mission would not last more than ten days. This verse highlights the disbelief and skepticism of those who doubted the longevity and success of the Prophet's message, despite the clear signs and miracles that were being manifested.
orig: يتخافتون بينهم إن لبثتم إلا عشرا

translation: We are most knowing of what they say, when their best speaker says, "You have not remained [in the world] except for a day."
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah is all-knowing and aware of what people say, even their most eloquent statements. The verse suggests that the disbelievers claim that the life in this world is short and temporary, lasting only a day. However, this interpretation is flawed, as the true nature of the Hereafter and the Day of Judgment is far more significant and eternal than the fleeting life of this world.
orig: نحن أعلم بما يقولون إذ يقول أمثلهم طريقة إن لبثتم إلا يوما

translation: And they ask you, [O Muhammad], about the mountains, so say, "My Lord will scatter them [as] dust."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the end of the world, when the mountains will be scattered and reduced to dust. This is a powerful metaphor for the complete destruction and transformation of the physical world, as part of the Day of Judgment. The message is that all material things, no matter how seemingly permanent, are ultimately transient and will be swept away by the will of God. This serves as a reminder to focus on the eternal spiritual realm rather than the fleeting physical world.
orig: ويسألونك عن الجبال فقل ينسفها ربي نسفا

translation: And He will leave it a level plain
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah will destroy the earth and leave it as a flat, barren landscape. The term "قاعا صفصفا" conveys the idea of a completely flat, smooth, and featureless terrain, devoid of any hills, valleys, or other topographical features. This suggests that on the Day of Judgment, the entire world as we know it will be leveled, leaving behind a plain that is devoid of any life or vegetation. The interpretation is that Allah has the power to completely reshape the earth and reduce it to a state of utter desolation, as a sign of His might and the inevitability of the Day of Resurrection.
orig: فيذرها قاعا صفصفا

translation: You see not in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency. So return [your] vision [to the sky]; do you see any breaks?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the universe created by God is perfectly balanced and harmonious, without any flaws or imperfections. It encourages the reader to observe the heavens and the earth, and to reflect on the consistency and order that permeates the creation. The verse suggests that by contemplating the signs of God's power and wisdom in the universe, one can come to a deeper understanding of the divine and the perfection of the Creator.
orig: لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا

translation: On that Day, they will follow the Caller with no crookedness in him, and the voices will have humbled themselves before the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a soft whisper.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when people will be summoned by a Caller (the Angel Israfil) whose call will be clear and straightforward, without any deception or falsehood. On that day, all voices will be hushed and humbled before the Most Merciful (Allah), and only a soft, whispered sound will be heard, as people will be in a state of awe and reverence.
orig: يومئذ يتبعون الداعي لا عوج له وخشعت الأصوات للرحمن فلا تسمع إلا همسا

translation: That Day, intercession will not avail [anyone] except [for] one to whom the Most Merciful has given permission and whose speech He approves.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when no one's intercession will be of any benefit except for those whom Allah, the Most Merciful, has granted permission and whose words He is pleased with. This emphasizes that on that momentous day, only Allah's approval and permission will carry any weight, and no human intervention or recommendation will be of any use without the Almighty's consent.
orig: يومئذ لا تنفع الشفاعة إلا من أذن له الرحمن ورضي له قولا

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not encompass it with [their] knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitless knowledge and omniscience of God. He knows everything that has happened in the past and everything that will happen in the future, which is beyond the comprehension of human beings. It highlights the vast difference between the infinite knowledge of the Creator and the finite knowledge of His creation.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يحيطون به علما

translation: And the faces have humbled themselves before the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, and he has certainly failed who carried [a burden of] injustice.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that on the Day of Judgment, all people will humble themselves before the Almighty, the Eternal and Self-Subsisting God. It also suggests that those who have committed injustice and oppression will be disappointed and unsuccessful, as their deeds will be exposed and they will be held accountable for their wrongdoings.
orig: وعنت الوجوه للحي القيوم وقد خاب من حمل ظلما

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer - he will neither fear injustice nor deprivation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who believe in God and do good deeds have no reason to fear any kind of injustice or loss. Their faith and righteous actions will protect them from harm and ensure that they are treated fairly. The verse conveys a message of reassurance and comfort for the believers, encouraging them to continue doing good works without fear of being wronged or deprived of their rights.
orig: ومن يعمل من الصالحات وهو مؤمن فلا يخاف ظلما ولا هضما

translation: And thus have We sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and have diversified therein the warnings that perhaps they will avoid [sin] or it will cause them remembrance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic language, and that it contains various warnings and admonitions. The purpose of these warnings is to encourage people to be mindful of their actions and to turn towards God, so that they may attain righteousness and find guidance. The verse suggests that the Qur'an serves as a reminder and a means of awakening the human conscience, leading people to fear God and avoid sin.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه قرآنا عربيا وصرفنا فيه من الوعيد لعلهم يتقون أو يحدث لهم ذكرا

translation: So exalted is Allah, the Sovereign, the Truth. And, [O Muhammad], do not hasten with [recitation of] the Qur’an before its revelation is completed to you, and say, ‘My Lord, increase me in knowledge."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exalted status of Allah as the Sovereign and the Truth. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to rush in reciting the Qur’an before its complete revelation has been delivered to him. Instead, he is encouraged to pray to Allah to increase his knowledge and understanding. The verse highlights the importance of patience, humility, and seeking more knowledge in the process of receiving and understanding the divine revelation.
orig: فتعالى الله الملك الحق ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضى إليك وحيه وقل رب زدني علما

translation: And We had already taken a promise from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found not in him determination.
interpretation: This verse refers to the covenant that God made with Adam, the first human, before his creation. God commanded Adam to worship Him alone and not to disobey Him. However, Adam forgot this covenant and did not have the firm resolve to fulfill it. This highlights the human tendency to forget the divine commandments and the need for constant guidance and determination to remain steadfast in one's faith.
orig: ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم من قبل فنسي ولم نجد له عزما

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except for Iblis; he refused.
interpretation: This verse highlights the command from Allah to the angels to prostrate before Adam, which they all obeyed except for Iblis (Satan). Iblis' refusal to prostrate before Adam, despite being commanded to do so, was an act of disobedience and pride. This event marks the beginning of Iblis' rebellion against Allah and his subsequent expulsion from the ranks of the angels. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and humility before Allah's commands, even when they may seem challenging or contrary to one's own desires or beliefs.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس أبى

translation: And We said, 'O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife. So let him not remove you from Paradise so you would suffer.'
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to Adam and his wife, Eve, about the danger posed by Satan (the enemy referred to). Allah is advising them not to be deceived by Satan, as he seeks to remove them from the bliss of Paradise and cause them to suffer. The message is one of caution and guidance, urging Adam and Eve to remain steadfast in their faith and obedience to Allah in order to avoid the consequences of Satan's temptations.
orig: فقلنا يا آدم إن هذا عدو لك ولزوجك فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتشقى

translation: Indeed, you will not be hungry therein or be unclothed.
interpretation: This verse conveys the promise of God that the believers will be provided with all their needs in the Hereafter. They will never experience hunger or the lack of clothing, which are common hardships in this world. This is a reassurance of the abundant blessings and comforts that await the righteous in the Afterlife.
orig: إن لك ألا تجوع فيها ولا تعرى

translation: And [moreover], you will not be thirsty therein nor will you be exposed to the sun.
interpretation: This verse reassures the believers that in Paradise, they will not experience thirst or the scorching heat of the sun. It highlights the comfort and tranquility that awaits them in the afterlife, where they will be free from the discomforts and hardships of the worldly life.
orig: وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى

translation: Then Satan whispered to him; he said, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and [a kingdom] that will not deteriorate?"
interpretation: This verse describes how Satan tempted Adam to eat from the forbidden tree, promising him eternal life and a kingdom that would never decay. This represents Satan's attempt to lure Adam and Eve away from God's command and towards disobedience. The interpretation is that Satan uses deception and false promises to try to lead people astray from the righteous path.
orig: فوسوس إليه الشيطان قال يا آدم هل أدلك على شجرة الخلد وملك لا يبلى

translation: And they both ate of it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred.
interpretation: This verse describes the consequences of Adam and Eve's disobedience to God by eating from the forbidden tree in the Garden of Eden. As a result, their private parts became visible to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves from the Garden. The verse also states that Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray, leading to their expulsion from the Garden.
orig: فأكلا منها فبدت لهما سوآتهما وطفقا يخصفان عليهما من ورق الجنة وعصى آدم ربه فغوى

translation: Then his Lord chose him and turned to him and guided [him].
interpretation: This verse describes how God guided and forgave the Prophet Muhammad after he had initially strayed from the path. It shows God's mercy and willingness to guide those who sincerely repent and return to Him. The interpretation is that even the greatest of prophets can make mistakes, but God will forgive and guide them if they turn back to Him with sincerity.
orig: ثم اجتباه ربه فتاب عليه وهدى

translation: He said, "Descend, with enmity between yourselves. And if there should come to you guidance from Me - then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer misery."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Adam and Eve being sent down to Earth after they disobeyed God in the Garden of Eden. The verse highlights that even though they will now have to face challenges and enmity between each other, God has provided them with guidance that will lead them away from going astray and suffering, if they choose to follow it. The interpretation is that God's guidance, if accepted, can save us from the trials and tribulations of this world and lead us to a righteous path.
orig: قال اهبطا منها جميعا بعضكم لبعض عدو فإما يأتينكم مني هدى فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل ولا يشقى

translation: And whoever turns away from My remembrance - indeed, he will have a depressed life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.
interpretation: This verse warns those who turn away from the remembrance of Allah and His teachings. It states that such people will have a life of hardship and difficulty, as they have turned away from the guidance that could have provided them with a life of ease and fulfillment. Furthermore, on the Day of Resurrection, they will be raised blind, indicating that they were spiritually blind in this life, unable to perceive the truth and guidance that was available to them.
orig: ومن أعرض عن ذكري فإن له معيشة ضنكا ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى

translation: He will say, "My Lord, why have You raised me blind while I was [once] seeing?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the disbeliever will question God as to why he was resurrected blind, when he had the ability to see the truth during his worldly life. The interpretation is that the disbeliever had the capacity to see the signs of God and believe, but chose to be blind to the truth and reject faith. This highlights the importance of using one’s faculties to seek guidance and submit to God during one’s lifetime.
orig: قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا

translation: He said, "Thus did Our signs come to you, and you forgot them." And thus today are you forgotten.
interpretation: This verse is a reference to the story of the Pharaoh, who was warned by the signs and miracles shown to him by Prophet Moses, but he ignored them and continued in his arrogance and disbelief. The verse suggests that just as the Pharaoh forgot the signs, he too will be forgotten on the Day of Judgment, when he will face the consequences of his actions. The message is that those who reject the guidance and signs of Allah will ultimately be forgotten and abandoned, just as they had abandoned the truth.
orig: قال كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى

translation: And thus do We recompense he who transgresses and does not believe in the verses of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who transgress and reject the signs (verses) of God will face a severe and lasting punishment in the Hereafter. The interpretation is that those who live extravagantly, without faith in God's guidance, will be subject to a punishment that is more intense and eternal than the trials of this world.
orig: وكذلك نجزي من أسرف ولم يؤمن بآيات ربه ولعذاب الآخرة أشد وأبقى

translation: Have they not been guided by the example of those before them, whose remnants dwell in their dwelling places? Verily in that are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the fate of previous generations who were destroyed due to their disbelief and rejection of the truth. It suggests that by observing the ruins and remnants of those who came before, one can gain guidance and wisdom. The interpretation is that those who use their intellect and reason ('those of understanding') can learn valuable lessons from the examples of the past, and thereby be guided towards the right path.
orig: أفلم يهد لهم كم أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون يمشون في مساكنهم إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى

translation: And if it were not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been an obligation [upon Us], and [for] a specified term [their punishment would have come].
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah's mercy and wisdom have delayed the punishment of the disbelievers, even though they deserve it. It indicates that Allah has a plan and a specific time for everything, and that His decisions are not arbitrary, but based on His perfect knowledge and wisdom. The verse emphasizes that Allah's decisions are not subject to human will or timeframes, but are part of His divine plan.
orig: ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لكان لزاما وأجل مسمى

translation: So be patient over what they say and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and [in part] of the hours of the night [exalt Him] and at the ends of the day, that you may be pleased.
interpretation: This verse encourages patience and steadfastness in the face of criticism or opposition from others. It also emphasizes the importance of praising and glorifying Allah throughout the day, including before sunrise, before sunset, and during the hours of the night. By doing so, one may attain the pleasure and approval of Allah.
orig: فاصبر على ما يقولون وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى

translation: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, [its being but] the splendor of worldly life by which We test them. And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse advises against being envious or covetous of the material possessions and worldly luxuries enjoyed by others. It reminds us that the splendor and enjoyment of this worldly life is only a test from Allah, and that the true and lasting provision is that which comes from Allah, the Lord and Sustainer. The interpretation encourages us to focus on the eternal rewards in the Hereafter rather than being distracted by the temporary pleasures of this world.
orig: ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم زهرة الحياة الدنيا لنفتنهم فيه ورزق ربك خير وأبقى

translation: And enjoin prayer upon your family [and people] and be steadfast therein. We ask you not for provision; We provide for you, and the [best] outcome is for [those of] righteousness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prayer and steadfastness in it. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to enjoin prayer upon his family and people, and to be steadfast in performing it. The verse also assures the Prophet that Allah will provide for him and his people, and that the ultimate outcome is for those who are righteous and God-fearing.
orig: وأمر أهلك بالصلاة واصطبر عليها لا نسألك رزقا نحن نرزقك والعاقبة للتقوى

translation: And they say, "Why has a sign not been brought to him from his Lord?" Has there not come to them the clear evidence that is [contained] in the former scriptures?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who demand a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as proof of his prophethood. The response given is that the clear evidence and guidance already present in the previous scriptures, such as the Torah and the Gospel, should suffice as proof. The Qur'an is not meant to be a book of miracles, but rather a book of guidance and wisdom that builds upon the revelations that came before it.
orig: وقالوا لولا يأتينا بآية من ربه أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى

translation: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before him, they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced?"
interpretation: This verse suggests that if Allah had punished the people before sending a messenger, they would have complained and asked why a messenger was not sent to them first, so they could have followed the divine verses and avoided humiliation and disgrace. The interpretation is that Allah sends messengers to guide people and give them a chance to believe and reform, before subjecting them to punishment for their misdeeds.
orig: ولو أنا أهلكناهم بعذاب من قبله لقالوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا فنتبع آياتك من قبل أن نذل ونخزى

translation: Say, "Wait, indeed we [too] are waiting."
interpretation: This verse is instructing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to tell the disbelievers who are waiting for something bad to happen to the believers to go ahead and wait, for the believers are also waiting for the ultimate triumph of the truth. It suggests that the disbelievers will soon realize that the path of guidance and righteousness is the one followed by the believers, not them.
orig: قل كل متربص فتربصوا فستعلمون من أصحاب الصراط السوي ومن اهتدى

translation: Mankind's reckoning has drawn near, and they are turning away in heedlessness.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Day of Judgment is approaching, yet people remain heedless and neglectful of this impending reality. They are turning away from the signs and reminders of the Hereafter, preoccupied with the affairs of this worldly life. The verse serves as a warning to humanity to be mindful of the coming reckoning and to prepare for the accountability they will face before Allah.
orig: اقترب للناس حسابهم وهم في غفلة معرضون

translation: There does not come to them any new reminder from their Lord except that they listen to it while they are amusing themselves.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people often ignore or dismiss the reminders and guidance that come to them from God, as they are too preoccupied with their own worldly pursuits and pleasures. Instead of taking the divine messages seriously and reflecting on them, they treat them as mere entertainment or amusement, without any real intention to change their ways and submit to God's will. The verse highlights the human tendency to be distracted from the path of righteousness and to prioritize temporary, fleeting pleasures over the eternal guidance provided by the Creator.
orig: ما يأتيهم من ذكر من ربهم محدث إلا استمعوه وهم يلعبون

translation: Their hearts are distracted. And those who have wronged conceal their private conversations, [asking], "Is this [Prophet] not just a human being like you? So would you approach magic while you are seeing [it]?"
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who are skeptical of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the message of Islam. It suggests that their hearts are distracted from the truth, and they try to conceal their private conversations where they plot against the Prophet. They question whether he is just a human being like them, and they wonder how they can be expected to believe in the miracles and teachings he brings, even though they can see them with their own eyes. The verse is challenging their arrogance and unwillingness to accept the divine message, despite the clear signs and evidence presented to them.
orig: لاهية قلوبهم وأسروا النجوى الذين ظلموا هل هذا إلا بشر مثلكم أفتأتون السحر وأنتم تبصرون

translation: My Lord knows the speech in the heaven and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Lord, has knowledge of all speech and communication, whether it occurs in the heavens or on earth. He is the All-Hearing, who hears and comprehends all that is said, and the All-Knowing, who has perfect knowledge of all things. This highlights Allah’s omniscience and sovereignty, as He is aware of everything that is spoken or communicated, no matter where it takes place.
orig: قال ربي يعلم القول في السماء والأرض وهو السميع العليم

translation: Rather, they say, "[These are but] mixed dreams," and, "He has invented it," and, "He is a poet." So let him bring us a sign just as the former [messengers] were sent [with miracles].
interpretation: This verse is responding to the accusations made by the disbelievers against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Qur'an. They dismissed the Qur'an as "mixed dreams", meaning incoherent and meaningless, or as something the Prophet "invented" himself, or as the words of a "poet". The verse challenges them to bring a similar revelation if they doubt the divine origin of the Qur'an, just as previous prophets were sent with miracles to prove their message. This emphasizes the Qur'an's divine origin and the inability of the disbelievers to produce anything like it.
orig: بل قالوا أضغاث أحلام بل افتراه بل هو شاعر فليأتنا بآية كما أرسل الأولون

translation: And there was no town that believed [in its messengers] before them, and We would have destroyed them. So will these not believe?
interpretation: This verse highlights that the people of Makkah, who were rejecting the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), were not the first to disbelieve in the messengers of Allah. Rather, previous generations of people had also rejected the messengers sent to them, and as a result, Allah had destroyed those disbelieving societies. The verse then poses a rhetorical question, asking whether the people of Makkah will continue to disbelieve, despite the lessons of history. The implication is that they should learn from the fate of those who came before them and accept the message of the Qur’an.
orig: ما آمنت قبلهم من قرية أهلكناها أفهم يؤمنون

translation: And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed [Our message]. So ask the people of the message if you do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophets sent by God throughout history have been human beings, not supernatural or divine beings. It instructs the people to refer to the "people of the message" - the previous Prophets and their followers - to gain knowledge and understanding, if they themselves do not know the answers to their questions. This highlights the importance of seeking knowledge from reliable sources, rather than relying solely on one's own limited understanding.
orig: وما أرسلنا قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون

translation: And We did not make them [i.e., the messengers] bodies that did not eat food, nor were they immortal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the messengers of Allah were human beings, not supernatural or divine entities. They had physical bodies that required sustenance, just like other humans, and they were not immortal. This serves to dispel any notion of the messengers being superhuman or divine, and underscores the fact that they were chosen by Allah to convey His message to humanity as ordinary people. The verse highlights the humanity of the messengers, which makes their teachings and example more relatable and accessible to other human beings.
orig: وما جعلناهم جسدا لا يأكلون الطعام وما كانوا خالدين

translation: Then We fulfilled for them the promise, and We saved them and those We willed and destroyed the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah fulfilled His promise to the believers and saved them from their enemies, while destroying those who had transgressed and exceeded the limits. It highlights Allah's power and justice, as He rewards the righteous and punishes the wicked.
orig: ثم صدقناهم الوعد فأنجيناهم ومن نشاء وأهلكنا المسرفين

translation: We have certainly revealed to you a Book in which is your reminder. Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an, which has been revealed to the Prophet Muhammad, contains guidance and reminders for humanity. It encourages people to reflect and use their reasoning faculties to understand the divine message and its significance in their lives.
orig: لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم أفلا تعقلون

translation: And how many a township have We destroyed while it was given to wrongdoing, and they are [now] fallen into ruin, and [how many] a deserted well and [how many] a lofty palace.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and justice in destroying societies that engage in wrongdoing and oppression. It suggests that when a community becomes corrupt and refuses to heed the warnings of the prophets, Allah may punish them by destroying their way of life and replacing them with a new people. This serves as a lesson and a reminder that no one is beyond the reach of Allah's judgment, and that those who persist in wrongdoing will ultimately face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وكم قصمنا من قرية كانت ظالمة وأنشأنا بعدها قوما آخرين

translation: But when they felt Our punishment, behold, they started to flee from it.
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the people when they experienced the consequences of their wrongdoing. When they finally realized the severity of the punishment they were facing, they tried to escape it, but it was too late. The verse highlights how people often only become aware of their mistakes when it is too late to avoid the consequences, and emphasizes the importance of being proactive in doing good and avoiding evil.
orig: فلما أحسوا بأسنا إذا هم منها يركضون

translation: Do not rush, but return to what you were given in abundance, and to your homes - perhaps you will be asked.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to not rush or act hastily, but instead to return to the blessings and comforts they had been previously given. It suggests that they should reflect on their homes and lives, as they may be questioned about how they utilized those provisions. The message is to be mindful, appreciative, and accountable for the resources and opportunities one has been granted.
orig: لا تركضوا وارجعوا إلى ما أترفتم فيه ومساكنكم لعلكم تسألون

translation: They will say, "Woe to us! Indeed, we have been wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse describes the remorseful state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, when they will realize the gravity of their sins and transgressions against God and others. They will acknowledge their wrongdoing and express their regret, but it will be too late for them to seek forgiveness and redemption. This verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their sinful ways, encouraging them to repent and seek God's mercy before it is too late.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: And their cry did not cease until We made them [as] a harvest [cut down], extinguished [in death].
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who persistently rejected the message of the Prophets and continued in their disbelief. The verse suggests that their cries and pleas for mercy did not cease until they were destroyed and silenced, like a harvested crop that is cut down and no longer standing. This serves as a warning to those who stubbornly refuse to accept the truth and turn away from the guidance of God.
orig: فما زالت تلك دعواهم حتى جعلناهم حصيدا خامدين

translation: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and that between them in play.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the creation of the universe, including the heavens, the earth, and all that is between them, was not a frivolous or playful act. Rather, it was a deliberate and purposeful act by the Almighty Creator. The universe was not created in vain or without a greater meaning and significance. This verse serves as a reminder that the creation of the cosmos is a profound and meaningful act, and that humans should approach it with reverence, contemplation, and a desire to understand the deeper purpose behind it.
orig: وما خلقنا السماء والأرض وما بينهما لاعبين

translation: If We had willed to take a diversion, We could have taken it from [what is] with Us, if We were to do [such a thing].
interpretation: This verse suggests that if Allah had wanted to create something for amusement or entertainment, He could have done so easily, as He has the power and resources to create anything. However, Allah did not create the universe for mere amusement or diversion, but rather for a higher purpose - to test and guide humanity towards the path of righteousness. The verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate Creator and that everything in the universe serves a meaningful purpose in His divine plan.
orig: لو أردنا أن نتخذ لهوا لاتخذناه من لدنا إن كنا فاعلين

translation: Nay, We hurl the Truth against falsehood, and it destroys it, and behold, falsehood perishes! Ah! woe be to you for the (false) things ye ascribe (to Us).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the truth will always prevail over falsehood. God will strike down falsehood with the truth, and falsehood will be destroyed. The verse also warns against attributing false things to God, which will lead to a painful punishment.
orig: بل نقذف بالحق على الباطل فيدمغه فإذا هو زاهق ولكم الويل مما تصفون

translation: And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those [angels] near Him are not prevented by arrogance from His worship, nor do they tire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah. The angels who are closest to Allah do not feel superior or arrogant, and they worship Him without tiring. This teaches us that we should also worship Allah with humility and dedication, without arrogance or exhaustion.
orig: وله من في السماوات والأرض ومن عنده لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ولا يستحسرون

translation: They exalt [Him] night and day and do not slacken.
interpretation: This verse describes the angels and other spiritual beings who constantly praise and glorify Allah, without ever ceasing or becoming tired. It emphasizes the uninterrupted and perpetual nature of their worship and devotion to the Almighty. This serves as a reminder to believers that they should strive to emulate this state of continuous remembrance and glorification of Allah in their own lives, as much as possible.
orig: يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون

translation: Or have they taken deities from the earth who resurrect [the dead]?
interpretation: This verse is questioning whether people have taken gods from the earth, which they believe can resurrect the dead. The implication is that such beliefs are misguided, as only God has the power to resurrect the dead. The verse is challenging the notion of worshiping anything other than the one true God, who alone has the power of life and death.
orig: أم اتخذوا آلهة من الأرض هم ينشرون

translation: If there had been within the heavens and earth gods besides Allah, they both would have been ruined. So exalted is Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and supremacy of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It refutes the notion of multiple deities or gods, as that would lead to chaos and the destruction of the heavens and the earth. The verse highlights Allah's transcendence and perfection, as He is the Lord of the Throne, far above the flawed and limited descriptions that people ascribe to Him.
orig: لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا فسبحان الله رب العرش عما يصفون

translation: He is not to be questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and authority of God. He is not accountable to anyone for His actions, as He is the Creator and Sustainer of all things. In contrast, humans will be held accountable for their deeds and will be questioned about them on the Day of Judgment. This highlights the importance of submitting to God's will and living a righteous life, as we will ultimately be responsible for our choices and actions.
orig: لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسألون

translation: Or have they taken gods from the earth who resurrect [the dead]? Say, "Produce your proof. This [Qur'an] is the message for those with me and the message of those before me." But most of them do not know the truth, so they are turning away.
interpretation: This verse challenges the idea of worshipping gods other than Allah. It asks the disbelievers to provide proof for their belief in other deities, and reminds them that the Qur'an is a message from Allah that has been revealed to the Prophet Muhammad as well as to the prophets before him. The verse suggests that most people do not know the truth and are turning away from it, implying that they should reflect on the Qur'an and its message.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دونه آلهة قل هاتوا برهانكم هذا ذكر من معي وذكر من قبلي بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون الحق فهم معرضون

translation: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that, "There is no deity except Me, so worship Me."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the core message of Islam - the belief in the oneness of God (tawheed). It states that all the prophets and messengers sent by God have conveyed the same fundamental message: that there is no deity worthy of worship except the one true God, and that people should worship and submit to Him alone. This is the essence of the Islamic faith, and it is a message that has been consistent throughout the history of prophethood.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول إلا نوحي إليه أنه لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدون

translation: And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken [for Himself] a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are [but] honored servants.
interpretation: This verse refutes the notion that God has taken a son, which was a belief held by some people at the time. It asserts that God is exalted and transcendent, and that the servants of God are merely honored, not divine. The interpretation emphasizes God's absolute oneness and sovereignty, and the status of human beings as created and honored servants, not as equal to or part of the divine.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا سبحانه بل عباد مكرمون

translation: They do not speak before He speaks, and they act by His command.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the obedience and submission of the believers to Allah. They do not speak or act on their own accord, but rather they wait for Allah's command and then carry it out. This highlights the importance of humility, patience, and complete reliance on Allah in the life of a true believer.
orig: لا يسبقونه بالقول وهم بأمره يعملون

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they cannot intercede except for one whom He approves. And they, from His fear, are apprehensive.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, the Almighty. He has knowledge of all that is before people and all that is behind them - their past, present, and future. Furthermore, it highlights that the intercession of angels or other beings is only permitted for those whom Allah approves. The verse also conveys a sense of awe and reverence that the angels feel towards Allah, as they are "apprehensive" or in fear of Him.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يشفعون إلا لمن ارتضى وهم من خشيته مشفقون

translation: And whoever among them should say, "I am a god besides Him" - that one We will recompense with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse condemns the worship of any deity other than Allah. It warns that anyone who claims divinity or worships a god besides Allah will be punished with Hell. This emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of God (tawhid) and the rejection of polytheism or associating partners with Allah. The interpretation highlights that Allah alone is worthy of worship and that those who transgress this core tenet of Islam will face severe consequences.
orig: ومن يقل منهم إني إله من دونه فذلك نجزيه جهنم كذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: Have not those who disbelieve known that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them and made from water every living thing? Then will they not believe?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the power and wisdom of God in creating the universe. It suggests that those who reject faith should reflect on the fact that the heavens and the earth were once a single entity, which God then separated and from which He created all living things from water. The purpose is to encourage belief in God"s existence and His role as the Creator, who has the power to shape and sustain the universe and all life within it.
orig: أولم ير الذين كفروا أن السماوات والأرض كانتا رتقا ففتقناهما وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي أفلا يؤمنون

translation: And We have placed on the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with them, and We have made therein [mountain] passes and routes that they might be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's creation of mountains on the earth to provide stability and prevent it from shaking or shifting. The mountains also serve as pathways and routes for people to travel and find their way, guiding them in their journeys. The interpretation is that God has designed the earth in a way that provides both physical and spiritual guidance for humanity, allowing them to navigate the world and find the right path.
orig: وجعلنا في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بهم وجعلنا فيها فجاجا سبلا لعلهم يهتدون

translation: And We have made the heaven a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs, are turning away.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God has created the heavens as a protected and secure canopy for humanity. However, it also suggests that many people are heedless and turn away from the signs and wonders of the universe, failing to reflect on the divine wisdom and power displayed in the celestial bodies and phenomena.
orig: وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا وهم عن آياتها معرضون

translation: And it is He who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon; all [heavenly bodies] in an orbit are swimming.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over the universe. He is the One who created the night and day, the sun and the moon, and all the heavenly bodies that move in their designated orbits. The verse suggests that these celestial objects are in a state of constant motion, "swimming" in their respective paths, which is a testament to Allah's perfect design and control over the cosmos.
orig: وهو الذي خلق الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر كل في فلك يسبحون

translation: And We did not grant to any man before you eternity [in life]; so if you die - would they then be eternal?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mortality of human beings, including the Prophet Muhammad. It suggests that no human being before him was granted eternal life, and if he were to die, the people would not become immortal either. This is a reminder that death is an inevitable part of the human experience, and that true eternal life can only be found in the Hereafter.
orig: وما جعلنا لبشر من قبلك الخلد أفإن مت فهم الخالدون

translation: Every soul will taste death. And We test you with evil and with good as trial. And to Us you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of death, which is an inevitable experience for all living beings. It also highlights that in this life, we are tested by both good and evil circumstances as a means of trial and purification. Ultimately, all people will return to Allah, the Creator, for judgment and accountability.
orig: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ونبلوكم بالشر والخير فتنة وإلينا ترجعون

translation: And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you not except in ridicule. [Saying], "Is this the one who mentions your gods?" And they are, at the mention of the Most Merciful, disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). When they see him, they do not take him seriously, but rather mock and ridicule him. They question whether he is the one who speaks against their false gods, and they reject the mention of the Most Merciful (Allah), as they are disbelievers. This verse emphasizes the arrogance and closed-mindedness of the disbelievers, who refuse to acknowledge the truth and instead choose to mock and reject it.
orig: وإذا رآك الذين كفروا إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا أهذا الذي يذكر آلهتكم وهم بذكر الرحمن هم كافرون

translation: He created man from haste. I will show you My signs, so do not impatiently urge Me.
interpretation: This verse highlights the nature of human beings, who are often hasty and impatient. The Qur'an reminds us that Allah has created us from this tendency to rush and be impatient. However, the verse also assures us that Allah will reveal His signs in due time, and that we should not try to rush or demand them prematurely. The interpretation encourages patience, trust, and submission to Allah's plan, rather than giving in to our natural inclination towards haste and impatience.
orig: خلق الإنسان من عجل سأريكم آياتي فلا تستعجلون

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who mockingly ask when the promise of the Resurrection and Judgment Day will come to pass, challenging the believers to prove the truthfulness of their faith. The interpretation is that the disbelievers are arrogantly denying the reality of the Hereafter and demanding immediate proof, rather than having faith in Allah's plan and timing.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: If those who disbelieve knew the time when they will not [be able to] keep back the Fire from their faces and their backs and [that] they will not be aided.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who disbelieve in God and reject His message. It suggests that if the disbelievers were to know the true nature of the punishment they will face on the Day of Judgment, when they will be unable to escape the Fire or receive any help, they would immediately turn back to God in repentance. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment awaiting the disbelievers and the futility of their efforts to avoid it, as they will be completely powerless against it.
orig: لو يعلم الذين كفروا حين لا يكفون عن وجوههم النار ولا عن ظهورهم ولا هم ينصرون

translation: Rather, the Hour will come upon them unexpectedly, and it will befuddle them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be given respite.
interpretation: This verse refers to the suddenness and unexpectedness of the Day of Judgment, which will catch people by surprise and leave them unable to react or prepare for it. The interpretation is that people should not be complacent and should always be ready for the inevitable arrival of the Hour, as they will not have the chance to undo their actions or avoid the consequences of their deeds on that day.
orig: بل تأتيهم بغتة فتبهتهم فلا يستطيعون ردها ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And indeed, [many] messengers before you were ridiculed, but those who mocked them were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that the rejection and ridicule of God's messengers is not a new phenomenon. Throughout history, many prophets and messengers have been mocked and derided by those who refused to believe their message. However, the verse warns that those who scoffed and mocked the messengers ultimately faced the consequences of their actions, as they were enveloped by the very thing they had ridiculed. This serves as a cautionary tale, reminding us that we should not underestimate the gravity of rejecting divine guidance and that those who do so may ultimately face the consequences of their own actions.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فحاق بالذين سخروا منهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Say, "Who protects you in the night and the day from the Most Merciful?" But they, from the remembrance of their Lord, are turning away.
interpretation: This verse is calling upon the disbelievers to consider who is protecting them day and night, and to acknowledge the mercy and providence of Allah. However, it laments that they are turning away from the remembrance of their Lord and failing to appreciate His blessings and care for them. The verse encourages the people to reflect on Allah's attributes and to submit to Him, rather than remaining heedless and ungrateful.
orig: قل من يكلؤكم بالليل والنهار من الرحمن بل هم عن ذكر ربهم معرضون

translation: Or have they gods who can defend them against Us? They have no power to aid themselves, nor can they be defended from Us.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the notion of false deities or idols that some people may worship instead of the one true God, Allah. The verse is challenging the idea that these other gods have any real power or ability to protect or help their worshippers. It is stating that these false gods cannot even defend themselves, let alone provide any assistance or support to their followers. The implication is that Allah alone is the true and powerful deity, and that worshipping anything else is futile and powerless.
orig: أم لهم آلهة تمنعهم من دوننا لا يستطيعون نصر أنفسهم ولا هم منا يصحبون

translation: Nay, We gave the good things of this life to these men and their fathers until the period grew long for them; See they not that We gradually reduce the land (in their control) from its outlying borders? Is it then they who will win?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers have been given worldly pleasures and comforts, but they have become arrogant and complacent. The Qur'an warns them that Allah gradually reduces the land under their control, indicating that their power and dominance will not last forever. The implication is that they should not be deceived by their temporary prosperity and should instead focus on their relationship with Allah, as it is He who is the ultimate victor.
orig: بل متعنا هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى طال عليهم العمر أفلا يرون أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها أفهم الغالبون

translation: Say, "I only warn you by revelation." But the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is only delivering the message of God's revelation, and not speaking from his own desires. It also highlights that those who are "deaf" to the truth, who refuse to listen and heed the warnings, will not benefit from the call to faith. The interpretation is that people must open their hearts and minds to receive and act upon the divine guidance, otherwise they will remain spiritually deaf and unresponsive to the call of faith.
orig: قل إنما أنذركم بالوحي ولا يسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ما ينذرون

translation: And if they are touched by a breath of punishment from your Lord, they will surely say, "Woe to us! Indeed, we have been wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of those who disbelieve in God and reject His signs when they are afflicted with punishment. Despite their arrogance and denial during times of prosperity, when faced with the consequences of their own misdeeds, they will acknowledge their wrongdoing and express regret. This highlights the fact that even the most stubborn of disbelievers will eventually recognize their error when confronted with the might and justice of the Almighty.
orig: ولئن مستهم نفحة من عذاب ربك ليقولن يا ويلنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: And We shall set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so that not a soul will be dealt with unjustly in the least. And if there be [even] the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice and accountability on the Day of Resurrection. It assures that God will establish a fair and impartial system of judgment, where even the smallest of deeds, good or bad, will be taken into account. No one will be wronged, and even the slightest weight of a mustard seed will be accounted for. This serves as a reminder to humans to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held responsible for them on the Day of Judgment, and God is the ultimate and sufficient reckoner.
orig: ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة فلا تظلم نفس شيئا وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين

translation: And We had certainly given Moses and Aaron the Criterion and a light and a reminder for the righteous
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah (SWT) had bestowed upon the Prophets Moses and Aaron the "Furqan" (the Criterion or the Qur'an), which serves as a source of guidance and light for the righteous people. The "Furqan" helps distinguish between truth and falsehood, and provides a clear reminder for those who fear Allah (SWT) and strive to please Him.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى وهارون الفرقان وضياء وذكرا للمتقين

translation: Those who fear their Lord unseen and they are fearful of the Hour.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of the righteous believers. They fear Allah (God) even when they are not being watched by others, as they are conscious of Allah's presence and accountability. They are also fearful and apprehensive about the Day of Judgment, known as the "Hour", as they know they will be held responsible for their actions in this life.
orig: الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب وهم من الساعة مشفقون

translation: And this is a blessed Message which We have sent down: will ye then reject it?
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an, which is described as a "blessed Message" that has been revealed by God. The rhetorical question "will ye then reject it?" implies that rejecting the Qur'an, which contains guidance and blessings, would be an unreasonable and unjustified action. The verse encourages the believers to appreciate and accept the Qur'an as a divinely-revealed scripture.
orig: وهذا ذكر مبارك أنزلناه أفأنتم له منكرون

translation: And We had certainly given Abraham his guidance before, and We were of him, [that is, of Abraham] well-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah had guided and directed Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) towards the right path and the truth before this time. Allah was fully aware of Abraham"s character, beliefs, and actions, and had chosen him to be a prophet and a messenger.
orig: ولقد آتينا إبراهيم رشده من قبل وكنا به عالمين

translation: When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) questioning his father and people about their worship of idols and statues. It reflects Abraham's rejection of idolatry and his search for the true God. The verse highlights the importance of monotheism and the need to worship only the one true God, rather than false deities or objects of worship.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه وقومه ما هذه التماثيل التي أنتم لها عاكفون

translation: They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."
interpretation: This verse refers to a common argument used by people to justify their religious beliefs and practices. They claim that they are simply following the traditions and beliefs of their ancestors, without critically examining the validity or rationality of those beliefs. The Qur'an often challenges this line of thinking, emphasizing the importance of independent reasoning and not blindly following the practices of one's forefathers.
orig: قالوا وجدنا آباءنا لها عابدين

translation: He (Allah) will say: "Indeed, you have been, you and your forefathers, in manifest error."
interpretation: This verse indicates that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will confront the disbelievers and inform them that they and their forefathers were in a state of clear misguidance and deviation from the truth. It emphasizes the importance of following the right path and not blindly adhering to the beliefs and practices of one's ancestors, if they are not in accordance with the guidance of Allah.
orig: قال لقد كنتم أنتم وآباؤكم في ضلال مبين

translation: They said, "Have you come to us with the truth, or are you one of the triflers?"
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, and it is part of a dialogue between the prophet Moses and the Pharaoh and his people. The people are questioning whether Moses has come to them with the truth of God's message, or if he is simply playing games and deceiving them. The verse highlights the skepticism and resistance that prophets often face when delivering the divine message, as the people are unwilling to accept the truth and prefer to remain in their state of disbelief and ignorance.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا بالحق أم أنت من اللاعبين

translation: He (Pharaoh) said, "Nay, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Who created them, and I am one of the witnesses (to this)".
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between Pharaoh and Prophet Moses (peace be upon him). Pharaoh, despite seeing the clear signs and miracles shown by Moses, stubbornly refuses to believe in the Oneness of God and instead claims that he (Pharaoh) is the lord. However, in this verse, Pharaoh acknowledges that the true Lord is the One who created the heavens and the earth, and that he (Pharaoh) is a witness to this fact. This shows that even the most arrogant and stubborn of people can be compelled to recognize the truth of God's Lordship, but their pride and ego prevent them from submitting to it.
orig: قال بل ربكم رب السماوات والأرض الذي فطرهن وأنا على ذلكم من الشاهدين

translation: And by Allah, I will surely plan against your idols after you have turned and gone away.
interpretation: This verse expresses the Prophet Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) determination to destroy the idols of his people after they had turned away from him. It reflects his strong faith in God and his willingness to stand up against the false deities that his people worshipped. The verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping the one true God and rejecting all forms of idolatry.
orig: وتالله لأكيدن أصنامكم بعد أن تولوا مدبرين

translation: And He broke them into fragments, all except the largest of them, that they might return [to it].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the destruction of idols worshipped by the people. The verse indicates that the Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) broke all the idols except the largest one, in order to make the people realize the futility of worshipping lifeless objects and to turn back to the worship of the One true God.
orig: فجعلهم جذاذا إلا كبيرا لهم لعلهم إليه يرجعون

translation: They said, "Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse is referring to an incident where the idolaters discovered that their idols had been damaged or destroyed. They immediately accused someone of being responsible, calling that person a wrongdoer. This highlights the idolaters' attachment to their false gods and their unwillingness to question the validity of idol worship. The Qur'an uses this example to illustrate the folly of worshipping anything other than the one true God, Allah.
orig: قالوا من فعل هذا بآلهتنا إنه لمن الظالمين

translation: They said, "We heard a youth mention them, called Abraham."
interpretation: This verse refers to a conversation between some people who heard a young man, named Abraham, speaking about the idols that they worshipped. The verse suggests that the people were surprised to hear someone, particularly a young person, criticizing their religious beliefs and practices. This encounter likely foreshadows the conflict between Abraham and his people over the worship of false gods, which is a central theme in the Qur'an.
orig: قالوا سمعنا فتى يذكرهم يقال له إبراهيم

translation: They said, "Bring him before the eyes of the people that they may witness [him]."
interpretation: This verse refers to the demand made by the people to bring Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) before them, so that they could witness his case and pass judgment on him. The implication is that they wanted to publicly examine and scrutinize him, possibly to expose any wrongdoing or to validate the accusations made against him. The purpose was to have a public trial or hearing, where the people could observe the proceedings and bear witness to the outcome.
orig: قالوا فأتوا به على أعين الناس لعلهم يشهدون

translation: They said, "Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?"
interpretation: This verse is part of the Qur'anic narrative describing the confrontation between the Prophet Abraham and his people who worshipped idols. The people are questioning Abraham, accusing him of destroying their gods. This verse highlights the people's devotion to their false deities and their inability to comprehend the truth of monotheism that Abraham was preaching.
orig: قالوا أأنت فعلت هذا بآلهتنا يا إبراهيم

translation: He said, "Rather, this - the largest of them - did it. So ask them, if they can speak."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) and his confrontation with his people who were idol-worshippers. When Abraham destroyed the idols, he told his people to ask the largest idol, as if it could speak and explain what happened. This was a rhetorical device to expose the futility of idol-worship, as the idols were incapable of speech or action. The interpretation is that one should not blindly follow traditions or beliefs without questioning their validity and reasoning behind them.
orig: قال بل فعله كبيرهم هذا فاسألوهم إن كانوا ينطقون

translation: So they returned to [blaming] themselves and said, "Indeed, it is you who are the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse describes a situation where a group of people realize their own wrongdoing after initially blaming others. They come to the realization that they themselves are the ones who have acted unjustly or sinfully, and they acknowledge this fact. The verse highlights the importance of self-reflection and taking responsibility for one's actions, rather than shifting blame onto others.
orig: فرجعوا إلى أنفسهم فقالوا إنكم أنتم الظالمون

translation: Then they returned to their heads, [for] you had already known that they would speak.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers or opponents of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) tried to discredit him and his message, but their attempts were futile. The verse implies that the Prophet already knew that they would try to refute his teachings, but their arguments would not stand up to scrutiny. The interpretation is that the truth of Islam is evident, and the Prophet's opponents cannot shake this truth through their empty rhetoric or false accusations.
orig: ثم نكسوا على رءوسهم لقد علمت ما هؤلاء ينطقون

translation: He (i.e., Abraham) said: "Do you then worship, besides Allah, things that can neither profit you nor harm you?"
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between the Prophet Abraham and his people, who were idolaters. Abraham is questioning the logic and wisdom of worshipping deities that have no power to benefit or harm the worshippers. The interpretation is that one should only worship the one true God, Allah, who is the sole Creator and Sustainer of all things, and not false gods or idols that have no real power or influence. This emphasizes the importance of true and sincere monotheistic worship of Allah alone.
orig: قال أفتعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعكم شيئا ولا يضركم

translation: Woe to you and what you worship besides Allah. Do you not understand?
interpretation: This verse expresses a strong condemnation of idolatry and the worship of false deities. It suggests that those who worship anything other than the one true God, Allah, are foolish and lack understanding. The verse encourages critical thinking and rational contemplation of the futility of worshipping anything other than the Almighty Creator.
orig: أف لكم ولما تعبدون من دون الله أفلا تعقلون

translation: They said, "Burn him and support your gods, if you are to act."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), peace be upon him, when he was thrown into the fire by the disbelievers for rejecting their idols and worshiping the One True God. The disbelievers urged each other to burn Ibrahim and support their false gods, believing that their gods would protect them. This verse highlights the arrogance and ignorance of the disbelievers, who thought that their powerless idols could harm a prophet of God. It serves as a reminder that true faith and submission to the Almighty is the only path to salvation, and that no one and nothing can harm those who are under the protection of God.
orig: قالوا حرقوه وانصروا آلهتكم إن كنتم فاعلين

translation: We said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham."
interpretation: This verse describes the miraculous event when the Prophet Abraham was thrown into a blazing fire, but the fire was commanded by God to be cool and peaceful for him. This demonstrates God's power to protect and care for those who have faith in Him, even in the face of great danger. The interpretation is that God can transform the most threatening circumstances into a source of comfort and safety for those who trust in Him.
orig: قلنا يا نار كوني بردا وسلاما على إبراهيم

translation: And they planned a plan, but We planned a plan, while they perceived not.
interpretation: This verse refers to the attempts of the disbelievers to harm the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers. However, Allah (God) had a greater plan that would ultimately defeat their schemes and make them the "greatest losers". This verse emphasizes that Allah's plan is superior to any human plot or conspiracy, and that those who oppose the truth will ultimately fail.
orig: وأرادوا به كيدا فجعلناهم الأخسرين

translation: And We delivered him and Lot [his nephew] to the land which We had blessed for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse refers to the deliverance of the Prophets Abraham and Lot from the destruction that befell the people of Sodom and Gomorrah. The verse emphasizes that God had blessed the land to which Abraham and Lot were taken, indicating that it was a place of peace, prosperity, and divine favor. The interpretation suggests that God protects and provides for His righteous servants, even in the face of widespread corruption and wrongdoing.
orig: ونجيناه ولوطا إلى الأرض التي باركنا فيها للعالمين

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob in addition, and all [of them] We made righteous.
interpretation: This verse speaks of Allah's blessings upon the prophet Abraham. After granting him a son, Ishmael, Allah then also blessed him with two more sons, Isaac and Jacob. All three of these sons were made righteous and pious by Allah, continuing the legacy of their father Abraham. This shows Allah's abundant generosity in bestowing multiple righteous children upon the prophet Abraham, further strengthening his lineage and mission.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب نافلة وكلا جعلنا صالحين

translation: And We made them leaders guiding by Our command, and We inspired to them the doing of good deeds, establishment of prayer, and giving of zakah; and they were worshippers of Us.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah appointed the prophets and righteous leaders to guide people towards the path of righteousness. These leaders were inspired by Allah to perform good deeds, establish prayer, and give charity. They were devoted servants of Allah, worshipping Him alone.
orig: وجعلناهم أئمة يهدون بأمرنا وأوحينا إليهم فعل الخيرات وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وكانوا لنا عابدين

translation: And [We had sent] Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds? Indeed, you approach men with desire, instead of women. Rather, you are a transgressing people."
interpretation: This verse describes the story of the prophet Lot, who was sent to the people of Sodom and Gomorrah. It emphasizes that the people of Lot were engaged in immoral and unnatural sexual practices, such as homosexuality, which were unprecedented among the nations. The verse condemns their actions as a transgression against the natural order and the will of God.
orig: ولوطا آتيناه حكما وعلما ونجيناه من القرية التي كانت تعمل الخبائث إنهم كانوا قوم سوء فاسقين

translation: And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Jonah, who was swallowed by a whale and then rescued by Allah. The verse conveys that Allah forgave Jonah and accepted him back into His mercy, as Jonah was a righteous and faithful servant. This highlights Allah's compassion and willingness to forgive those who sincerely repent and return to the right path.
orig: وأدخلناه في رحمتنا إنه من الصالحين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], Noah, when he called [to Us] before, and We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great distress.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the Prophet Noah, who called upon God to save him and his family from the great flood that destroyed his people. God answered his call and rescued him and his family, delivering them from the immense hardship and calamity they were facing. This verse highlights God's responsiveness to the prayers of His servants and His power to save those who believe in Him, even in the face of overwhelming adversity.
orig: ونوحا إذ نادى من قبل فاستجبنا له فنجيناه وأهله من الكرب العظيم

translation: And We supported him against the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them all.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) and the destruction of his people who rejected his message and the signs of Allah. The verse highlights that Allah supported Noah against his people who denied the divine revelations, as they were an evil people. Ultimately, they were all drowned in the flood as a consequence of their disbelief and wickedness.
orig: ونصرناه من القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا إنهم كانوا قوم سوء فأغرقناهم أجمعين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field - when the sheep of [certain] people overgrazing [there] had pastured at night, and We were witness to their judgment.
interpretation: This verse refers to a case where David and Solomon, two of the prophets of God, were called upon to judge a dispute between people regarding the use of a field. The verse indicates that the sheep of some people had grazed in the field at night, causing damage. David and Solomon, as righteous and wise judges, were able to make a fair judgment in this case, and God Himself was a witness to their judgment.
orig: وداوود وسليمان إذ يحكمان في الحرث إذ نفشت فيه غنم القوم وكنا لحكمهم شاهدين

translation: And We made Sulaiman to understand (the case); and to each (of them) We gave wisdom and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains and the birds to glorify (Us) with Dawud, and We were the Doers.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah granted wisdom and knowledge to both Prophet Sulaiman (Solomon) and Prophet Dawud (David). It also mentions that Allah subjected the mountains and birds to glorify Him along with Prophet Dawud. This highlights Allah's power and ability to control all of creation, and the way in which He favored His Prophets by bestowing upon them special gifts and abilities.
orig: ففهمناها سليمان وكلا آتينا حكما وعلما وسخرنا مع داوود الجبال يسبحن والطير وكنا فاعلين

translation: And We taught him the art of making garments for you, that they may protect you from your (own) violence. Then will you not be grateful?
interpretation: This verse refers to the teaching of the skill of making protective garments, such as armor, to the Prophet. The purpose of this was to provide protection from the violence and harm that people might face. The verse then asks if the people will be grateful for this knowledge and the protection it provides. The interpretation suggests that the Qur'an encourages gratitude for the blessings and provisions that Allah has granted to humanity.
orig: وعلمناه صنعة لبوس لكم لتحصنكم من بأسكم فهل أنتم شاكرون

translation: And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind - its morning [course was] a month's [journey], and its afternoon [course was] a month's [journey], and We caused a flow of copper to pour forth for him, and among the jinn were those who worked for him by the permission of his Lord. And whoever deviated among them from Our command - We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse describes the supernatural powers granted to the Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him) by God. He was given control over the wind, which could travel vast distances in a short time, allowing him to quickly traverse his kingdom. Additionally, God made the jinn (supernatural beings) subservient to Solomon, to work for him by God's permission. This verse highlights the blessings and abilities bestowed upon Solomon by the Almighty, and serves as a reminder of God's supreme power and authority over all creation.
orig: ولسليمان الريح عاصفة تجري بأمره إلى الأرض التي باركنا فيها وكنا بكل شيء عالمين

translation: And of the devils are some who dive for him and [some] who do other work besides that, and We were of them keepers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the devils, or Shaitans, who dive into the sea to retrieve pearls and other valuable items for the people. However, some of the Shaitans also engage in other harmful or deceptive activities, which Allah is aware of and keeps watch over. The verse suggests that the Shaitans have a range of activities, some of which may be beneficial to people, while others may be harmful or misleading. The interpretation is that Allah is in control and is aware of all the activities of the Shaitans, both good and bad.
orig: ومن الشياطين من يغوصون له ويعملون عملا دون ذلك وكنا لهم حافظين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful."
interpretation: This verse describes the prophet Job (Ayyub) calling out to his Lord, Allah, in a time of distress and affliction. Despite the hardship he was facing, Job recognized that Allah is the Most Merciful and that He alone can provide relief and comfort. The verse emphasizes the importance of turning to Allah in times of difficulty, and having faith that He will respond with His infinite mercy and compassion.
orig: وأيوب إذ نادى ربه أني مسني الضر وأنت أرحم الراحمين

translation: So We responded to him and removed what distress was upon him. And We gave him [back] his family and the like thereof with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah responded to the supplication of Prophet Job (peace be upon him) and removed the distress and affliction that had befallen him. Allah then restored to him his family and possessions, as a sign of mercy and a reminder for those who worship and submit to Allah.
orig: فاستجبنا له فكشفنا ما به من ضر وآتيناه أهله ومثلهم معهم رحمة من عندنا وذكرى للعابدين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], Ishmael and Idris and Dhul-Kifl - all were of the patient.
interpretation: This verse mentions three prophets of God - Ishmael, Idris (Enoch), and Dhul-Kifl - and states that they were all among the patient and steadfast. This highlights the virtues of patience, perseverance, and steadfastness in the face of trials and tribulations, which are important qualities for a believer to possess. The verse encourages the reader to emulate the example of these prophets and strive to be patient and steadfast in their own lives.
orig: وإسماعيل وإدريس وذا الكفل كل من الصابرين

translation: And We shall admit them to Our Mercy: for he was of the Righteous.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah will admit the righteous people into His Mercy and Paradise. The phrase "We shall admit them to Our Mercy" suggests that Allah's Mercy is vast and encompasses those who have lived righteous lives. The phrase "for he was of the Righteous" further emphasizes that the individuals being referred to are those who have done good deeds and followed the path of righteousness. This verse provides a message of hope and reassurance for the believers, that if they strive to live righteously, they will be granted Allah's Mercy and enter Paradise.
orig: وأدخلناهم في رحمتنا إنهم من الصالحين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], the man of the fish [i.e., Jonah], when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him. And he called out within the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse refers to the prophet Jonah, who was swallowed by a whale after fleeing from his people.
