In his distress, Jonah called out to Allah, professing his belief in the Oneness of God and acknowledging his own wrongdoing. The verse emphasizes the importance of turning to Allah in times of difficulty and seeking His forgiveness, even when one has strayed from the righteous path. It serves as a reminder that Allah's mercy and forgiveness are always available to those who sincerely repent.
orig: وذا النون إذ ذهب مغاضبا فظن أن لن نقدر عليه فنادى في الظلمات أن لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين

translation: So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Yunus (Jonah), who was swallowed by a whale after abandoning his people. When he called out to God in the belly of the whale, God heard his plea and saved him. This verse emphasizes that God responds to the sincere calls of the believers and saves them from their distress, just as He saved Yunus. It is a reassurance that God will come to the aid of the faithful in times of difficulty.
orig: فاستجبنا له ونجيناه من الغم وكذلك ننجي المؤمنين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone [with no heir], while you are the best of inheritors."
interpretation: This verse refers to the prophet Zechariah, who prayed to Allah, asking Him not to leave him without an heir. Zechariah was concerned that he would not have a successor to carry on his legacy and mission. The verse emphasizes that Allah is the best of inheritors, implying that He can provide Zechariah with an heir in a way that only He can. This highlights the importance of relying on Allah and trusting in His plan, even when faced with personal concerns or uncertainties.
orig: وزكريا إذ نادى ربه رب لا تذرني فردا وأنت خير الوارثين

translation: So We responded to him, and We gave to him John, and We adjusted for him his wife. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us in hope and fear, and they were to Us humbly submissive.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah responded to the supplication of Zechariah, the father of the prophet John (Yahya), by granting him a son and adjusting his wife's condition so that she could bear children. It highlights that Zechariah and his family were people who eagerly pursued good deeds, and supplicated to Allah with both hope and fear, being humbly submissive to Him. This demonstrates the virtue and piety of this family, and how Allah rewards those who are devoted to Him.
orig: فاستجبنا له ووهبنا له يحيى وأصلحنا له زوجه إنهم كانوا يسارعون في الخيرات ويدعوننا رغبا ورهبا وكانوا لنا خاشعين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], the one who guarded her chastity, so We blew into her [garment] through Our [created] angel [Gabriel], and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse refers to the virgin Mary, the mother of Jesus (peace be upon him). It highlights that she was chaste and pure, and that God breathed His spirit into her through the angel Gabriel, causing her to conceive Jesus without a father. The verse then states that Mary and her son Jesus were made a sign and a miracle for all of humanity to witness and learn from.
orig: والتي أحصنت فرجها فنفخنا فيها من روحنا وجعلناها وابنها آية للعالمين

translation: Indeed, this, your religion, is one religion, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the divine message and the oneness of God. It conveys that all believers, regardless of time or place, are part of the same community of faith, and that their ultimate purpose is to worship and serve the one true God. The verse serves as a call to devotion and submission to the divine will, reminding the believers of their shared identity and their obligation to worship and obey their Lord.
orig: إن هذه أمتكم أمة واحدة وأنا ربكم فاعبدون

translation: And they have broken their affair among themselves, [but] to Us they will [all] return.
interpretation: This verse suggests that people often disagree and divide themselves over various matters, but ultimately, they will all return to God for judgment and accountability. It emphasizes the idea that human affairs are temporary and that the final reckoning will be with Allah, the Almighty.
orig: وتقطعوا أمرهم بينهم كل إلينا راجعون

translation: So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer - for such their effort is not denied, and indeed, We are recorders of it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who believe in God and do good deeds will be rewarded for their efforts. Their good works will not go unnoticed or unrecorded, as God keeps track of all that they do. This encourages believers to strive for righteousness and to have faith that their efforts will be acknowledged and appreciated by the Almighty.
orig: فمن يعمل من الصالحات وهو مؤمن فلا كفران لسعيه وإنا له كاتبون

translation: And it is forbidden for a town which We have destroyed that they [i.e., its people] would [ever] return.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that once a town or community has been destroyed by Allah due to their persistent disbelief and wrongdoing, they will never be able to return to their previous state. It emphasizes the finality and irreversibility of the punishment that befalls those who reject the guidance of Allah and persist in their sinful ways. The verse serves as a warning to heed Allah's commands and avoid the fate of those who were destroyed for their transgressions.
orig: وحرام على قرية أهلكناها أنهم لا يرجعون

translation: Until, when [the dam of] Gog and Magog has been opened and they, from every elevation, descend [upon the earth]
interpretation: This verse describes the eventual release of Gog and Magog, two tribes of destructive and chaotic people, who will be unleashed upon the world at the end of times. Their emergence from their confinement signals a major event in the lead up to the Day of Judgment, when the world will be engulfed in turmoil and chaos. The phrase "from every elevation" suggests that they will come from all directions, overwhelming and overrunning the earth.
orig: حتى إذا فتحت يأجوج ومأجوج وهم من كل حدب ينسلون

translation: And the true promise has approached, so suddenly the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring [in horror, awaiting it]. [They will say], "O woe to us; we had been unmindful of this - and indeed, we were wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, which is described as the "true promise" that is approaching. When that day arrives, the disbelievers will be struck with fear and horror, realizing that they had been heedless of it and had wronged themselves by rejecting faith. The verse conveys a sense of urgency and the inevitability of the coming of the Day of Judgment, which the disbelievers will face with regret for their past misdeeds.
orig: واقترب الوعد الحق فإذا هي شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا يا ويلنا قد كنا في غفلة من هذا بل كنا ظالمين

translation: Indeed, you [disbelievers] and what you worship other than Allah are the firewood of Hell. You will [all] be coming to it.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who worship deities other than Allah. It makes it clear that these false deities and their worshippers will all be consigned to the fires of Hell. The comparison to "firewood" suggests that they will be consumed by the flames, indicating the futility and worthlessness of their beliefs and practices. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of their fate, stating that they "will [all] be coming to it", leaving no room for doubt or escape.
orig: إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم أنتم لها واردون

translation: If these [false deities] were [true] gods, they would not have come to [i.e., entered] it, and all, [both worshippers and worshipped], therein would remain [forever].
interpretation: This verse suggests that the false deities worshipped by the people are not true gods, as they would not be subject to entering and leaving the world like ordinary beings. The fact that these deities are not eternal and do not remain forever in the world they are worshipped in is evidence that they are not worthy of being called gods. This verse encourages the rejection of false idols and the recognition of the one true God who is eternal and sovereign.
orig: لو كان هؤلاء آلهة ما وردوها وكل فيها خالدون

translation: For them therein is a [life of] sighing, and they therein will not hear [anything].
interpretation: This verse describes the torment of the disbelievers in the Hellfire, where they will be in a state of constant sighing and groaning, unable to hear anything but the sounds of their own suffering. It emphasizes the severe punishment that awaits those who reject faith and turn away from the guidance of Allah.
orig: لهم فيها زفير وهم فيها لا يسمعون

translation: Indeed, those for whom the best [reward] has preceded from Us - they are from it far removed.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have been blessed with the best reward from Allah, and they are far removed from the punishment or consequences of their sins. It suggests that those who have been granted the highest blessings and rewards by Allah will not be subjected to the punishments that others may face, as they have already been forgiven and have attained a high spiritual status.
orig: إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون

translation: They will not hear its slightest sound, and they will abide eternally in what their souls desired.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the state of the disbelievers in the Hereafter. They will not hear even the slightest sound of the torment in Hell, as they will be completely absorbed in the eternal enjoyment of their desires and lusts that they indulged in during their worldly lives. This indicates that the punishment of the Hellfire is so severe that the disbelievers will be completely oblivious to it, being preoccupied with their own selfish pleasures.
orig: لا يسمعون حسيسها وهم في ما اشتهت أنفسهم خالدون

translation: The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, [saying], "This is your Day which you have been promised."
interpretation: This verse provides a reassuring message to the believers on the Day of Judgment. It conveys that the believers will not be overcome by the greatest fear or terror on that day, as they will be welcomed by the angels. The angels will greet them, reminding them that this is the day they were promised, a day of triumph and reward for their faith and righteous deeds in this life.
orig: لا يحزنهم الفزع الأكبر وتتلقاهم الملائكة هذا يومكم الذي كنتم توعدون

translation: The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a [written] sheet for the records. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [That is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Resurrection, when the universe as we know it will be folded up and transformed, just as a written scroll is rolled up. This signifies the end of the current world and the beginning of the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes that this is a promise from God that will surely come to pass, just as He initiated the original creation of the universe, He will recreate it anew. This highlights God's power and control over all of creation, and the certainty of the Resurrection and the Hereafter.
orig: يوم نطوي السماء كطي السجل للكتب كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده وعدا علينا إنا كنا فاعلين

translation: And We have already written in the Psalms after the [previous] mention that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the righteous and pious servants of Allah will eventually inherit the earth. It suggests that the ultimate destiny of the earth is not for the unrighteous, but for those who live according to Allah's commands and strive to please Him. This interpretation highlights the idea that the righteous will be rewarded with the inheritance of the earth, which is a promise from Allah.
orig: ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون

translation: Indeed in this [Qur'an] is a message for a worshipping people.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Qur'an contains a clear and profound message for those who are devoted and submissive to Allah. The message is intended for those who worship and serve God sincerely, seeking guidance and spiritual nourishment from the divine revelation. The Qur'an is a source of guidance and inspiration for the believers, providing them with the means to deepen their faith and relationship with the Almighty.
orig: إن في هذا لبلاغا لقوم عابدين

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad was sent by God as a mercy and blessing to all of humanity, not just to a particular people or nation. The Prophet's mission was to guide and enlighten people, to bring them closer to God, and to establish justice, peace and compassion in the world. This verse highlights the universal and benevolent nature of the Prophet's prophethood, which was intended to benefit all of creation.
orig: وما أرسلناك إلا رحمة للعالمين

translation: Say, "Indeed, it is only revealed to me that your god is one God, so will you be Muslims [in submission to Him]?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental belief in the oneness of God (Tawheed) which is the core of the Islamic faith. It calls upon people to submit to the one true God and embrace Islam. The interpretation suggests that true submission to the one God is the essence of being a Muslim.
orig: قل إنما يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فهل أنتم مسلمون

translation: But if they turn away, then say: "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt [that struck] 'Aad and Thamud. And if you should turn away, I have already conveyed to you that with which I was sent to you, and my Lord will put in place of you a people other than you, and you will not harm Him at all. And my Lord is a Guardian over all things."
interpretation: This verse is a warning from the Prophet Muhammad to the people who have rejected his message and turned away from it. He tells them that if they continue to reject the message, they will face a punishment like that which befell the ancient peoples of 'Aad and Thamud, who were destroyed for their disbelief. The Prophet also reminds them that he has already conveyed the message to them, and that if they persist in their rejection, Allah will replace them with another people who will accept the message. This verse emphasizes the importance of accepting the divine message and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: فإن تولوا فقل آذنتكم على سواء وإن أدري أقريب أم بعيد ما توعدون

translation: Indeed, He knows the [most] apparent of speech and [what] is [concealed] within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has perfect knowledge of all that is said, both openly and in secret. He is aware of the outward expression of speech as well as the hidden thoughts and intentions of the heart. This serves as a reminder that we cannot hide anything from Allah, and that He is all-knowing and all-seeing.
orig: إنه يعلم الجهر من القول ويعلم ما تكتمون

translation: And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a [limited] time.
interpretation: This verse expresses the uncertainty of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding the purpose of a particular event or situation. He acknowledges that he does not know for sure whether it is a test or trial for the people, or whether it is a temporary source of enjoyment and pleasure. The interpretation suggests that the Prophet is cautious in making definitive judgments, recognizing that the true nature and purpose of events may not be fully known to him. This reflects the humility and wisdom of the Prophet, as he leaves room for the possibility that Allah's plan may be beyond human understanding at times.
orig: وإن أدري لعله فتنة لكم ومتاع إلى حين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, judge [between us] in truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the one whose help is sought against that which you describe.'
interpretation: This verse expresses a plea to Allah, the Lord, to judge with truth and justice. It acknowledges that Allah is the Most Merciful, and that He is the one whose help is sought against the false claims and descriptions made by people. The speaker is seeking a fair and righteous judgment from Allah, recognizing Him as the ultimate source of mercy and assistance.
orig: قال رب احكم بالحق وربنا الرحمن المستعان على ما تصفون

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the earthquake of the [final] Hour is a terrible thing.
interpretation: This verse calls upon all of humanity to be mindful of and submissive to God, the Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It warns that the coming of the Day of Judgment, signified by the "earthquake of the [final] Hour", is a momentous and terrifying event that all people must prepare for. The interpretation is that we should live our lives in a way that pleases God, by performing good deeds and avoiding sin, in order to be ready for the Day of Reckoning.
orig: يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم إن زلزلة الساعة شيء عظيم

translation: The Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from that [child] she was nursing, and every pregnant woman will abort her pregnancy, and you will see the people [as if] intoxicated while they are not intoxicated; but the punishment of Allah is severe.
interpretation: This verse describes the intensity and severity of the Day of Judgment, when the signs of its arrival will be so overwhelming that even the most natural and instinctive human behaviors will be disrupted. Nursing mothers will abandon their infants, pregnant women will miscarry, and people will appear to be in a state of intoxication, though they are not actually drunk. This conveys the profound impact and terror that will be experienced on that momentous day, reminding us of the need to prepare for the reckoning and punishment that Allah has in store for those who have disobeyed Him.
orig: يوم ترونها تذهل كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد

translation: And of the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who argue about the nature of God without having proper knowledge or understanding. It cautions against blindly following every deceptive and misguided entity, like the "rebellious devil", which can lead one astray from the truth. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance from reliable sources when it comes to matters of faith, rather than relying on unfounded opinions or being swayed by misleading influences.
orig: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ويتبع كل شيطان مريد

translation: It is written for him [i.e., upon him] that whoever takes him as an ally will surely be led astray and guided to the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who take Satan as their ally and protector, rather than Allah. It warns that such people will be led astray from the path of guidance and truth, and will ultimately be condemned to the punishment of the Hellfire. The message is that one should seek Allah's protection and guidance, and not rely on any other power or authority besides Him.
orig: كتب عليه أنه من تولاه فأنه يضله ويهديه إلى عذاب السعير

translation: O people, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then [consider that] indeed, We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, and then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed - that We may make clear to you. And We settle in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, then We bring you out as a child, and then [We develop you] that you may reach your [time of] maturity. And among you is he who is taken in [early] death, and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit [old] age so that he knows nothing after having known. And you see the earth barren, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells and grows [something] of every beautiful [kind].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and wisdom of God in the creation of human beings. It outlines the stages of human development, from dust to a fully formed individual, to illustrate the reality of the Resurrection. The verse also highlights how God controls the life cycle, with some dying young and others living to old age. Finally, it uses the analogy of the earth being barren until revived by rain to show how God can bring the dead back to life. The overall message is to affirm belief in the Resurrection and God's absolute authority over life and death.
orig: يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في ريب من البعث فإنا خلقناكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم من مضغة مخلقة وغير مخلقة لنبين لكم ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء إلى أجل مسمى ثم نخرجكم طفلا ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم ومنكم من يتوفى ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر لكيلا يعلم من بعد علم شيئا وترى الأرض هامدة فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and it is He Who gives life to the dead, and it is He Who is Able to do all things.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah is the absolute truth, the only true deity worthy of worship. It also emphasizes that Allah has the power to give life to the dead, which is a testament to His omnipotence. This serves as a reminder that Allah has the ability to do all things, and that He alone deserves our worship and submission.
orig: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأنه يحيي الموتى وأنه على كل شيء قدير

translation: And indeed, the Hour is coming - there is no doubt about it - and [that] Allah will resurrect those in the graves.
interpretation: This verse affirms the certainty of the coming of the Last Hour, the Day of Resurrection, when all people will be brought back to life to be held accountable for their deeds. It emphasizes that there is no doubt or uncertainty about the reality of the Resurrection, as it is a decree of Allah that will surely come to pass. The verse also highlights Allah's power to resurrect the dead, even those who have long been buried in their graves. This serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability that all people will face before their Creator.
orig: وأن الساعة آتية لا ريب فيها وأن الله يبعث من في القبور

translation: And of the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book.
interpretation: This verse is warning against those who engage in debates and arguments about Allah without having the proper knowledge, guidance, or divine revelation to support their claims. It cautions against speaking about matters of faith and theology without the necessary understanding and evidence. The verse emphasizes the importance of basing one's beliefs and discussions about Allah on authentic sources, such as the Quran and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad, rather than on personal opinions or unfounded claims.
orig: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ولا هدى ولا كتاب منير

translation: And the second is to turn [him] away from the way of Allah. For him in the world is disgrace, and We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the Burning Fire.
interpretation: This verse warns against the sin of turning others away from the path of Allah. It states that the one who does this will face disgrace in this world and severe punishment in the Hereafter, described as the "punishment of the Burning Fire". The interpretation is that we should strive to guide people towards Allah's path, not turn them away from it, as that is a grave sin with severe consequences.
orig: ثاني عطفه ليضل عن سبيل الله له في الدنيا خزي ونذيقه يوم القيامة عذاب الحريق

translation: That is because of what your hands have put forth [of evil], and indeed, Allah is not unjust to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the consequences of one's own actions. It suggests that the punishment or difficulties one faces are a result of their own misdeeds and wrongdoings. The verse emphasizes that Allah is not unjust, but rather, people reap what they sow. It serves as a reminder that we are responsible for our own actions and that Allah is fair in His judgment, not oppressing His servants.
orig: ذلك بما قدمت يداك وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد

translation: And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge. If he is touched by good, he is reassured by it. But if he is touched by trial, he turns on his [very] face [to the other direction]. He has lost [this] world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss.
interpretation: This verse describes a type of person who worships Allah only superficially, without true devotion and commitment. They are only interested in the benefits and rewards of faith, and their worship is conditional upon receiving worldly gains and prosperity. However, when faced with trials and tribulations, they quickly abandon their faith and turn away from Allah. This type of faith is unstable and leads to a loss in both this life and the Hereafter, which is the ultimate and most evident form of loss.
orig: ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف فإن أصابه خير اطمأن به وإن أصابته فتنة انقلب على وجهه خسر الدنيا والآخرة ذلك هو الخسران المبين

translation: He calls upon besides Allah that which neither harms him nor benefits him. That is the [very] straying error.
interpretation: This verse is warning against worshipping or seeking help from anything other than Allah, as that will only lead to being misguided and distant from the truth. It emphasizes that only Allah can truly benefit or harm a person, and that seeking aid from false deities or idols is a grave error that will only result in being further away from the right path.
orig: يدعو من دون الله ما لا يضره وما لا ينفعه ذلك هو الضلال البعيد

translation: He calls upon that whose harm is nearer than its benefit. Wretched is the protector and wretched is the associate.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against seeking help or relying on things that may cause more harm than good. It suggests that people sometimes turn to things or entities that are more likely to harm them than benefit them, which is a foolish and misguided action. The verse emphasizes that such a "protector" or "associate" is wretched and unworthy of one's trust or dependence.
orig: يدعو لمن ضره أقرب من نفعه لبئس المولى ولبئس العشير

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, Allah does what He intends.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Almighty, will grant eternal bliss in the Hereafter to those who have true faith in Him and who lead righteous lives by performing good deeds. The imagery of gardens with flowing rivers represents the tranquility and abundance that the believers will experience in Paradise. This verse also affirms that Allah has absolute power and authority, and He will fulfill His promises as He wills.
orig: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار إن الله يفعل ما يريد

translation: Whoever thinks that Allah will not support him [i.e., the Prophet] in this world and the Hereafter - let him extend a rope to the heaven; then let him cut [it] and see if his plan will remove that which enrages [him].
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who doubt that Allah will support the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his message. It is challenging them to try to find a way to prevent Allah's support and victory for the Prophet, as this is an impossible task. The verse is emphasizing that Allah's plan and support for His Messenger will prevail, no matter how much the disbelievers try to hinder it. The interpretation is that one should have faith in Allah's power and wisdom, and not doubt His ability to support and protect His chosen Messenger.
orig: من كان يظن أن لن ينصره الله في الدنيا والآخرة فليمدد بسبب إلى السماء ثم ليقطع فلينظر هل يذهبن كيده ما يغيظ

translation: And thus have We sent it down as clear verses, and that Allah guides whom He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an has been revealed by Allah as clear and unambiguous guidance for humanity. It also affirms that Allah alone has the power to guide people to the right path, and He chooses to guide those whom He wills. This highlights the importance of seeking Allah's guidance and submitting to His will, rather than relying solely on one's own understanding or desires.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه آيات بينات وأن الله يهدي من يريد

translation: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews or Christians or Sabeans - those [among them] who believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteousness - will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all those who believe in Allah and the Day of Judgment, and do righteous deeds, will be rewarded by Allah regardless of their religious background. It highlights the inclusiveness of Islam, which recognizes the validity of other faiths and the potential for people of different beliefs to attain salvation through faith and good works. The verse also reassures the believers that they need not fear or grieve, as Allah is witness to their actions and will judge them fairly on the Day of Resurrection.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئين والنصارى والمجوس والذين أشركوا إن الله يفصل بينهم يوم القيامة إن الله على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Have you not seen that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures and many of the people? But upon many the punishment has become due. And he whom Allah humiliates - for him there is no bestower of honor. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal submission to Allah, the Almighty Creator. It highlights that all of creation - from the celestial bodies like the sun, moon, and stars, to the natural elements like mountains and trees, and even the animals and many people - prostrate and submit to Allah. This is a testament to Allah's sovereignty and power, as He is the One who controls and commands all of existence. The verse also warns that those who reject this truth and refuse to submit to Allah will face punishment, as Allah is the ultimate authority and decides the fate of all. Ultimately, this verse reinforces the idea that Allah is the supreme and all-powerful being, and that true honor and dignity can only come from submitting to His will.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يسجد له من في السماوات ومن في الأرض والشمس والقمر والنجوم والجبال والشجر والدواب وكثير من الناس وكثير حق عليه العذاب ومن يهن الله فما له من مكرم إن الله يفعل ما يشاء

translation: These are two adversaries who have disputed over their Lord. But those who disbelieved will have cut out for them garments of fire. Poured upon their heads will be scalding water.
interpretation: This verse describes two groups of people - those who believe in God and those who reject faith. The believers and the disbelievers are in constant conflict, as they have opposing views about their Lord. The verse warns that the disbelievers will be punished in the Hereafter, where they will be clothed in garments of fire and have scalding water poured over their heads. This is a vivid depiction of the torment that awaits those who reject God's guidance and deny the truth.
orig: هذان خصمان اختصموا في ربهم فالذين كفروا قطعت لهم ثياب من نار يصب من فوق رءوسهم الحميم

translation: That by which He may melt what is in their bellies and [their] skins
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that the disbelievers will face on the Day of Judgment. The "that by which He may melt" is a metaphorical reference to the intense heat and torment that will be inflicted upon them, which will penetrate deep into their bodies, melting what is in their bellies and skins. This punishment is a consequence of their rejection of faith and their evil deeds in this world.
orig: يصهر به ما في بطونهم والجلود

translation: And for them are maces of iron.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The "maces of iron" symbolize the severe and painful torment that they will face, as a consequence of their rejection of faith and their wrongdoings in this life. The verse serves as a warning to those who turn away from the guidance of Allah, emphasizing the gravity of their actions and the inevitable retribution they will face.
orig: ولهم مقامع من حديد

translation: Whenever they want to get out of it [i.e., Hell] from anguish, they will be returned to it, and [it will be said], "Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire!"
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal nature of the punishment in Hell for those who disbelieve and reject faith. Whenever they try to escape the torment of Hell out of distress, they will be returned to it and made to experience the painful punishment of the Burning Fire. This emphasizes that there is no escape from the consequences of their misdeeds and that they will be condemned to an unending cycle of torment.
orig: كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها من غم أعيدوا فيها وذوقوا عذاب الحريق

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearl, and their garments therein will be silk.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward that Allah has prepared for those who believe in Him and do good deeds. The believers will be admitted to the gardens of Paradise, where they will enjoy eternal bliss. They will be adorned with beautiful jewelry, such as gold bracelets and pearls, and their clothing will be made of the finest silk. This imagery conveys the splendor and luxury of the afterlife that awaits the righteous, as a way of motivating believers to strive for faith and good works in this life.
orig: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير

translation: And they were guided to good speech, and they were guided to the path of the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the guidance that believers receive from Allah. They are guided to use good and righteous speech, and they are also guided to the straight path that leads to the Praiseworthy (Allah). This implies that believers are not only guided in their words but also in their actions, following the path that is pleasing to Allah and leads to His praise and approval.
orig: وهدوا إلى الطيب من القول وهدوا إلى صراط الحميد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah and [from] al-Masjid al-Haram, which We have made for the people, equal [for] the resident therein and the [temporary] visitor, and whoever inclines [to enter it] with an [unjust] inclination, [behind] him We will [soon] make him taste a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who disbelieve in Allah and prevent others from following the path of Allah, and from entering the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) in Mecca, which was established for all people, whether they are residents or visitors. It also warns those who seek to enter the Sacred Mosque with impure intentions or to cause harm, that they will be made to taste a painful punishment.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ويصدون عن سبيل الله والمسجد الحرام الذي جعلناه للناس سواء العاكف فيه والباد ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد بظلم نذقه من عذاب أليم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We designated for Abraham the site of the House [saying], "Do not associate anything with Me and purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who stand [in prayer] and those who bow and prostrate."
interpretation: This verse instructs Prophet Abraham to establish the House of Allah (the Kaaba) and to purify it for those who come to perform the rituals of Hajj and Umrah. The key message is to worship Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining the sanctity and purity of the House of Allah, which is to be a place of worship, devotion and submission to the One God.
orig: وإذ بوأنا لإبراهيم مكان البيت أن لا تشرك بي شيئا وطهر بيتي للطائفين والقائمين والركع السجود

translation: And proclaim to the people the Hajj [pilgrimage]; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every distant pass
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to announce the pilgrimage (Hajj) to the people. It promises that people will respond to this call and come to perform the Hajj, some on foot and others on camels, from all corners of the land. This verse emphasizes the importance of the Hajj as a central ritual in Islam, and the willingness of the people to undertake this spiritual journey despite the difficulties involved. It highlights the devotion and sacrifice of the pilgrims, who will come from far and wide to fulfill this religious obligation.
orig: وأذن في الناس بالحج يأتوك رجالا وعلى كل ضامر يأتين من كل فج عميق

translation: That they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah during known days over what He has provided for them of [sacrificial] animals. So eat of them and feed the miserable and poor.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to participate in the ritual of animal sacrifice during the known days of Eid al-Adha. The purpose is for them to witness the benefits and blessings that come from this act of worship, and to remember the name of Allah in gratitude for the provisions He has granted them. The verse also instructs them to eat from the sacrificed animals and to feed the needy and poor, promoting compassion and sharing with those less fortunate.
orig: ليشهدوا منافع لهم ويذكروا اسم الله في أيام معلومات على ما رزقهم من بهيمة الأنعام فكلوا منها وأطعموا البائس الفقير

translation: Then let them end their state of ritual impurity, fulfill their vows, and circumambulate the Ancient House.
interpretation: This verse is instructing the pilgrims who have completed the Hajj rituals to perform certain acts to conclude their pilgrimage. The "state of ritual impurity" refers to the state of consecration and ritual purity that the pilgrims enter during the Hajj. They are now instructed to "end their state of ritual impurity" by performing the necessary rites and rituals to exit this sacred state. They are also told to "fulfill their vows" - any promises or commitments they had made in relation to the Hajj. Finally, they are directed to "circumambulate the Ancient House" - the Kaaba in Mecca, which is considered the most sacred site in Islam. This final act of circumambulation is a way for the pilgrims to honor and show reverence to the House of God before completing their journey.
orig: ثم ليقضوا تفثهم وليوفوا نذورهم وليطوفوا بالبيت العتيق

translation: That [is so]. And whoever honors the symbols of Allah - indeed, it is from the piety of hearts. And for you in the cattle are lessons [i.e., signs]. We give you to drink from what is in their bellies - between excretion and blood - pure milk, palatable to drinkers. And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines you take intoxicant and [also] good provision. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honoring the sacred symbols of Allah, as it is a sign of the piety of the heart. It also mentions the blessings of livestock and fruits, which are provided for the benefit of humanity. The verse cautions against consuming intoxicants and impurities, and encourages people to use their reason to appreciate the signs of Allah's creation.
orig: ذلك ومن يعظم حرمات الله فهو خير له عند ربه وأحلت لكم الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان واجتنبوا قول الزور

translation: Inclining toward uprightness, not associating [anything] with Allah. And he who associates others with Allah - it is as though he had fallen from the sky, and the birds had snatched him or the wind had carried him away to a remote place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him. It compares the fate of those who commit shirk (associating partners with Allah) to someone falling from the sky, where they are snatched by birds or carried away by the wind to a distant and isolated place. This highlights the severity of the consequences of polytheism and the need to maintain a pure and unwavering belief in the Oneness of Allah.
orig: حنفاء لله غير مشركين به ومن يشرك بالله فكأنما خر من السماء فتخطفه الطير أو تهوي به الريح في مكان سحيق

translation: That [is so]. And whoever honors the symbols of Allah - indeed, it is from the piety of hearts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honoring and respecting the symbols and rituals of Allah. It suggests that doing so is a reflection of the piety and righteousness of one's heart. The verse encourages believers to revere and uphold the sacred practices and institutions established by Allah, as this is a sign of their devotion and closeness to Him.
orig: ذلك ومن يعظم شعائر الله فإنها من تقوى القلوب

translation: In them (i.e. the camels) for you is (a source of) benefit for a specified term; then their (final) resting place is the ancient House (i.e. the Ka'bah in Makkah).
interpretation: This verse refers to the camels that are used for transportation and other purposes. It indicates that the camels provide various benefits to humans for a specified duration, and that their ultimate destination is the ancient House, which is a reference to the Ka'bah in Makkah. This suggests that the camels, like other aspects of creation, ultimately serve the purpose of leading people to the worship of Allah and the sacred sites of Islam.
orig: لكم فيها منافع إلى أجل مسمى ثم محلها إلى البيت العتيق

translation: And for every nation We have appointed a rite [of sacrifice] that they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them of [sacrificial] animals. And your god is one God, so to Him submit. And, [O Muhammad], give good tidings to the humble [before their Lord].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has prescribed a way of worship and religious observance for every community, including the practice of animal sacrifice, so that they may remember and glorify the name of Allah for the sustenance He has provided them. It also affirms the oneness of God, and calls upon all people to submit to Him. The verse ends with a command to give good news to the humble and devout believers.
orig: ولكل أمة جعلنا منسكا ليذكروا اسم الله على ما رزقهم من بهيمة الأنعام فإلهكم إله واحد فله أسلموا وبشر المخبتين

translation: Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, and [to] the patient ones in what has afflicted them, and the establishers of prayer, and those who spend from what We have provided them.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of the righteous believers. When the name of Allah is mentioned, their hearts become filled with reverence and awe, recognizing the majesty and power of the Divine. They are patient and steadfast in the face of adversity, trusting in Allah's wisdom and plan. They are diligent in their prayers, maintaining a strong connection with their Creator. Additionally, they are generous in sharing the provisions that Allah has bestowed upon them, using their wealth to support good causes and help those in need. This verse highlights the qualities of true faith, humility, and compassion that are central to the Islamic way of life.
orig: الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم والصابرين على ما أصابهم والمقيمي الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And the camels [as well] - We have made them for you as among the symbols [appointed] of Allah; for you therein is good [i.e., benefit]. So mention the name of Allah upon them when lined up [for sacrifice]; and when they are [finally] stilled, eat from them and feed the [contented] beggar and the [desperate] petitioner. Thus have We subjected them to you that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to recognize the blessings of Allah and to express gratitude for them. The camels are mentioned as one of the symbols or signs of Allah, which have been provided for the benefit of humanity. The verse instructs the believers to invoke the name of Allah when the camels are lined up for sacrifice, and then to partake of the meat and share it with the needy. This act of gratitude and sharing is seen as a means of expressing thankfulness to Allah for the provision of these animals. The verse emphasizes that Allah has subjected the camels to serve humanity, and this should lead the believers to be grateful to Allah.
orig: والبدن جعلناها لكم من شعائر الله لكم فيها خير فاذكروا اسم الله عليها صواف فإذا وجبت جنوبها فكلوا منها وأطعموا القانع والمعتر كذلك سخرناها لكم لعلكم تشكرون

translation: It is not their meat nor their blood that reaches Allah, but it is the piety from you that reaches Him. Thus have We subjected them to you that you may glorify Allah for that [to] which He has guided you; and give good tidings to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the true essence of sacrifice is not in the physical act of slaughtering animals, but in the piety and devotion of the worshipper. The meat and blood of the sacrificed animals do not reach Allah directly, but rather it is the sincerity and reverence of the one who offers the sacrifice that is truly accepted. The verse encourages believers to focus on developing their inner spiritual state, as this is what truly pleases Allah. The animals are subjected to humans as a means for them to glorify and praise Allah, and to inspire them to do good deeds. The verse ends with a promise of good tidings for those who strive to be righteous and benevolent.
orig: لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم كذلك سخرها لكم لتكبروا الله على ما هداكم وبشر المحسنين

translation: Indeed, Allah defends those who have believed. Indeed, Allah does not like any treacherous ingrate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah protects and defends those who have true faith in Him. It also makes clear that Allah does not approve of or love those who are ungrateful and treacherous, betraying the trust placed in them. The verse serves as a reassurance to believers that Allah is on their side, and a warning to those who would seek to undermine or betray the faith.
orig: إن الله يدافع عن الذين آمنوا إن الله لا يحب كل خوان كفور

translation: Permission [to fight] has been given to those who are being fought, because they were wronged. And indeed, Allah is competent to give them victory.
interpretation: This verse grants permission to those who are being unjustly attacked to defend themselves and fight back. It emphasizes that Allah has the power to support and grant victory to those who are oppressed and wronged. The interpretation is that Islam allows for self-defense against aggression, but does not condone unprovoked violence or aggression.
orig: أذن للذين يقاتلون بأنهم ظلموا وإن الله على نصرهم لقدير

translation: Those who have been evicted from their homes without right - only because they say, "Our Lord is Allah." And were it not that Allah checks the people, some by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned. And Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of religious freedom and the protection of places of worship. It condemns the unjust expulsion of people from their homes solely because of their faith in Allah. The verse suggests that if Allah did not restrain people from harming one another, the places where His name is frequently mentioned, such as monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques, would be destroyed. However, Allah will support those who support Him, for He is Powerful and Exalted in Might. This verse underscores the divine protection and preservation of religious sites and the freedom to worship, regardless of one's faith.
orig: الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض لهدمت صوامع وبيع وصلوات ومساجد يذكر فيها اسم الله كثيرا ولينصرن الله من ينصره إن الله لقوي عزيز

translation: Those who, if We give them authority in the land, establish prayer and give zakah and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. And to Allah belongs the outcome of [all] matters.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of those who are given authority and power in the land. They are people who: 1) Establish regular prayer and worship of God, 2) Pay the obligatory charity (zakah) to support the less fortunate, 3) Promote and enjoin what is good and righteous, and 4) Forbid and prevent what is wrong and immoral. Ultimately, the final outcome and consequences of all matters belong to God alone.
orig: الذين إن مكناهم في الأرض أقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأمروا بالمعروف ونهوا عن المنكر ولله عاقبة الأمور

translation: And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then already have the people of Noah and [the tribes of] 'Aad and Thamud denied [their prophets] before them.
interpretation: This verse is reassuring the Prophet Muhammad that if the people reject his message, it is not the first time that a prophet has faced such rejection. Previous prophets like Noah, 'Aad, and Thamud also faced denial and rejection from their people. This serves as a reminder that the opposition faced by the Prophet is not unique, and that he should remain steadfast in his mission, just as the previous prophets did.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود

translation: And the people of Abraham and the people of Lot
interpretation: This verse refers to the communities of the Prophets Abraham and Lot, who were both sent to guide their respective peoples. The people of Abraham and the people of Lot represent two distinct communities that were challenged with rejecting idolatry and upholding moral and ethical standards. The verse highlights the importance of heeding the messages of the Prophets and following the righteous path they advocated.
orig: وقوم إبراهيم وقوم لوط

translation: And the companions of Midian and Moses was denied, so I gave respite to the disbelievers. Then I seized them, and how [terrible] was My reproach.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Midian, who rejected the message of the prophet Moses. Despite their rejection, God gave them time and respite, but then eventually seized them with a severe punishment. This serves as a warning that those who reject the truth and persist in disbelief will face the consequences of their actions, no matter how much time they are given to repent. The verse emphasizes God's justice and the ultimate fate of those who stubbornly refuse to believe.
orig: وأصحاب مدين وكذب موسى فأمليت للكافرين ثم أخذتهم فكيف كان نكير

translation: And how many a city have We destroyed that was wrongdoing - and they are [now] fallen upon their sides, and [how many] an abandoned well and [how many] a lofty palace?
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of societies that were destroyed due to their wrongdoing and injustice. It paints a vivid picture of the ruins left behind - abandoned wells, collapsed buildings, and grand palaces that have fallen into disrepair. The message is a warning that societies that stray from the path of righteousness and morality will ultimately face ruin and destruction, no matter how powerful or prosperous they may have been. The verse serves as a reminder to humanity to uphold justice, morality, and righteousness in order to avoid a similar fate.
orig: فكأين من قرية أهلكناها وهي ظالمة فهي خاوية على عروشها وبئر معطلة وقصر مشيد

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and have hearts by which to reason and ears by which to hear? For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the world around them and use their God-given faculties of reason and hearing to understand the signs of Allah's power and wisdom. The verse suggests that the real blindness is not of the physical eyes, but of the hearts and minds that fail to comprehend the deeper truths of the universe. It emphasizes the importance of cultivating spiritual insight and understanding, rather than merely relying on outward perception.
orig: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فتكون لهم قلوب يعقلون بها أو آذان يسمعون بها فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمى القلوب التي في الصدور

translation: And they ask you to hasten the punishment, and Allah will never fail in His [entire] promise. And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism and impatience of the disbelievers, who demand that the punishment they were warned about be brought upon them immediately. The verse reassures that Allah will never fail to fulfill His promise, but that the concept of time is different from the human perspective. A day in the sight of Allah is equivalent to a thousand years by human reckoning, indicating that the divine plan and timeline is not bound by human perception of time. This serves as a reminder that Allah's promise will be fulfilled in due course, even if it does not align with the impatient demands of the disbelievers.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالعذاب ولن يخلف الله وعده وإن يوما عند ربك كألف سنة مما تعدون

translation: And how many a city have We destroyed while it was doing wrong - so it is [now] fallen into ruin - and [how many] an abandoned well and [how many] a lofty palace!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God has destroyed many cities and civilizations that were oppressive and unjust. It serves as a warning that no society can escape the consequences of their wrongdoing, and that all will ultimately return to God for judgment. The verse encourages people to reflect on the fate of past nations and to strive for righteousness, as no one is immune from God's punishment of those who commit injustice.
orig: وكأين من قرية أمليت لها وهي ظالمة ثم أخذتها وإلي المصير

translation: Say, 'O people, I am to you only a clear warner'
interpretation: This verse is instructing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to convey to the people that his role is to clearly warn them about the consequences of rejecting faith and the importance of believing in the oneness of God and following His commands. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet is not asking for any reward or status, but is simply delivering the message of guidance from God as a warner, so that people may be aware of the right path and make the choice to follow it.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس إنما أنا لكم نذير مبين

translation: So those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is forgiveness and a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have faith in God and do good deeds will be granted forgiveness of their sins and will be provided with a generous and honorable sustenance. It highlights the importance of both belief and righteous actions, as they are the means to attain God's mercy and blessings in the hereafter.
orig: فالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: And those who strive against Our verses, [seeking] to frustrate them - those are the companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who reject the signs and messages of Allah (God) and actively try to undermine or disprove them. They are described as "companions of Hellfire", indicating that their rejection and opposition to the divine revelations will lead them to a punishment in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of accepting and submitting to the guidance provided in the Qur'an, rather than trying to "frustrate" or invalidate it.
orig: والذين سعوا في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke [the word], Satan threw [some misunderstanding] into that of his utterance, but Allah abolishes that which Satan throws in; then Allah makes precise His verses. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses the fact that even the previous prophets and messengers sent by God were not immune to the whisperings and temptations of Satan. When the prophets spoke the word of God, Satan would sometimes try to insert his own ideas and misunderstandings. However, God would then remove and abolish whatever Satan had tried to introduce, and make the divine message clear and precise. This demonstrates God's power and wisdom in preserving the integrity of His revelations, and the inability of Satan to truly corrupt the divine teachings. The verse reminds us that even the greatest of prophets were not free from the influences of Satan, and that it is only through God's protection that the true message can be maintained.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول ولا نبي إلا إذا تمنى ألقى الشيطان في أمنيته فينسخ الله ما يلقي الشيطان ثم يحكم الله آياته والله عليم حكيم

translation: That He may make what the devil throws in a trial for those in whose hearts is disease and those hard of heart. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah allows the temptations and deceptions of Satan to be a test for those whose hearts are diseased with doubts, hypocrisy, and hardness. The wrongdoers, who reject faith and persist in their evil ways, are in a state of profound discord and alienation from the truth.
orig: ليجعل ما يلقي الشيطان فتنة للذين في قلوبهم مرض والقاسية قلوبهم وإن الظالمين لفي شقاق بعيد

translation: And those who have been given knowledge may know that it (the Qur'an) is the truth from your Lord, so they may believe in it, and their hearts may humbly submit to Him. And indeed, Allah is the Guide of those who have believed to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge and its role in strengthening one's faith. It suggests that those who have been granted knowledge should recognize the Qur'an as the truth revealed by God, and that this recognition should lead them to believe in it wholeheartedly. The verse also highlights that such belief will result in the humility and submission of their hearts to God, and that God guides those who believe towards the straight path.
orig: وليعلم الذين أوتوا العلم أنه الحق من ربك فيؤمنوا به فتخبت له قلوبهم وإن الله لهاد الذين آمنوا إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it until the Hour comes upon them suddenly or there comes to them the punishment of a barren Day.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who continue to doubt and reject the message of Islam, even in the face of clear signs and evidence. The verse suggests that their doubt and rejection will persist until the Day of Judgment arrives, either suddenly or when they face the punishment of a "barren Day" - a day devoid of any relief or respite from the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: ولا يزال الذين كفروا في مرية منه حتى تأتيهم الساعة بغتة أو يأتيهم عذاب يوم عقيم

translation: The sovereignty on that Day will be that of Allah; He will judge between them. So those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, Allah alone will have absolute sovereignty and authority to judge all people. Those who believed in Allah and did good deeds will be rewarded with the eternal bliss of Paradise, while those who rejected faith and did evil will be punished. The verse highlights the importance of faith and righteous actions, which will determine one's fate in the Hereafter.
orig: الملك يومئذ لله يحكم بينهم فالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات في جنات النعيم

translation: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - for them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who reject faith in God and deny the truth of the Quranic revelations. The punishment awaiting them is described as "humiliating", indicating that it will be a severe and degrading consequence for their disbelief and rejection of the divine signs. The interpretation suggests that those who turn away from God's guidance and refuse to acknowledge the truth will face a shameful and disgraceful punishment in the hereafter.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا فأولئك لهم عذاب مهين

translation: And those who emigrate for the cause of Allah and then are killed or die - Allah will surely provide for them a good provision. And indeed, Allah is the best of providers.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to make sacrifices for the sake of their faith, even to the point of emigrating or losing their lives. It promises that Allah will reward such believers with a good provision, both in this life and the hereafter. The verse emphasizes that Allah is the best of providers, and that those who make sacrifices for His cause can trust in His care and generosity.
orig: والذين هاجروا في سبيل الله ثم قتلوا أو ماتوا ليرزقنهم الله رزقا حسنا وإن الله لهو خير الرازقين

translation: He will surely admit them to an entrance with which they will be pleased, and indeed, Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah will grant the righteous believers a satisfactory and pleasing entrance into Paradise. The verse also highlights that Allah is all-Knowing and Forbearing, implying that He is aware of the deeds and intentions of His servants and is patient and merciful in His dealings with them.
orig: ليدخلنهم مدخلا يرضونه وإن الله لعليم حليم

translation: That [is so]. And whoever has retaliated with an equivalent of that with which he was harmed and then has [again] been wronged, Allah will surely aid him. Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of proportionate retaliation, where one may respond to harm with an equivalent action. However, it also encourages forgiveness and pardoning, as Allah is the One who will ultimately aid and support the one who has been wronged, as He is Pardoning and Forgiving. The interpretation suggests that while retaliation may be justified, it is better to seek Allah's aid and forgiveness, as this is the more noble and virtuous path.
orig: ذلك ومن عاقب بمثل ما عوقب به ثم بغي عليه لينصرنه الله إن الله لعفو غفور

translation: That is because Allah causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night and because Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete control over the alternation of night and day. He causes the night to gradually transition into the day, and the day to gradually transition into the night. This is a sign of Allah's power and wisdom, as well as His constant observation and awareness of all that occurs in the universe. It serves as a reminder that Allah is the All-Hearing and the All-Seeing, and that He is in full command of the cosmos and its cycles.
orig: ذلك بأن الله يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وأن الله سميع بصير

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and that which they call upon other than Him is falsehood, and that Allah - He is the Most High, the Grand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental truth that Allah is the only true and real deity, and that all other objects of worship are false and have no real existence or power. It affirms that Allah is the Highest and the Greatest, and that He alone deserves worship and obedience. The verse serves to remind the believers to have unwavering faith in the oneness and supremacy of Allah, and to reject all forms of idolatry and polytheism.
orig: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأن ما يدعون من دونه هو الباطل وأن الله هو العلي الكبير

translation: Have you not seen that Allah sends down rain from the sky, and the earth becomes green? Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power and providence in providing for His creation. The rain that descends from the sky nourishes the earth, causing it to become lush and verdant. This is a sign of God's care and wisdom, as He is the Subtle and All-Knowing One who orchestrates the natural cycles that sustain life. The verse invites the reader to reflect on God's majesty and to recognize His role as the Sustainer of all things.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فتصبح الأرض مخضرة إن الله لطيف خبير

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over the entire universe, both in the heavens and on earth. It highlights that Allah is the sole possessor of all that exists, and that He is free from any need or dependence on His creation. This verse serves to remind us of Allah's grandeur, power, and self-sufficiency, and encourages us to worship and praise Him, as He is the only One worthy of praise and glorification.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإن الله لهو الغني الحميد

translation: Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and amply bestowed upon you His favors, [both] apparent and unapparent? But of the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book [from Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and mercy of Allah, who has subjected all of creation to serve humanity. It reminds us that we should be grateful for the blessings and favors bestowed upon us, both visible and invisible. The verse also cautions against those who dispute about Allah without proper knowledge, guidance or divine scripture. The interpretation is that we should recognize and appreciate Allah's sovereignty and benevolence, and avoid arrogance or ignorance in our understanding of the divine.
orig: ألم تر أن الله سخر لكم ما في الأرض والفلك تجري في البحر بأمره ويمسك السماء أن تقع على الأرض إلا بإذنه إن الله بالناس لرءوف رحيم

translation: And it is He who gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the One who gives life and causes death. He is the Sovereign over life and death, and ultimately, all people will return to Him for judgment. This highlights the need for humans to submit to Allah and live a righteous life, as they will be held accountable for their actions in the Hereafter. The verse also suggests that human beings can be ungrateful and denying of Allah's blessings, as indicated by the phrase "indeed, mankind is ungrateful." This serves as a reminder to be thankful and to worship Allah alone.
orig: وهو الذي أحياكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم إن الإنسان لكفور

translation: For every nation We have appointed a ritual sacrifice. So let them not dispute with you over the matter, but invite them to your Lord. Indeed, you are upon a straight guidance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of religious practices, as each community has been given its own set of rituals and ways of worshipping God. It encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to invite people to the straight path of Islam, without getting into disputes over differences in religious practices. The interpretation is that one should focus on the core message of monotheism and righteous living, rather than getting caught up in arguments over peripheral matters of ritual.
orig: لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا هم ناسكوه فلا ينازعنك في الأمر وادع إلى ربك إنك لعلى هدى مستقيم

translation: And if they argue with you, then say, "Allah is most knowing of what you do."
interpretation: This verse is instructing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) on how to respond to those who argue and dispute with him regarding the teachings of Islam. The verse emphasizes that Allah, the Almighty, is the All-Knowing and is fully aware of the actions and intentions of all people. Therefore, the appropriate response to those who argue is to simply state that Allah knows best what they are doing, whether it is out of sincerity or ulterior motives. This encourages the believers to maintain their faith and trust in Allah's knowledge and wisdom, rather than engaging in fruitless debates.
orig: وإن جادلوك فقل الله أعلم بما تعملون

translation: Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will settle all disputes and disagreements that people had in this world. It serves as a reminder that we will be held accountable for our actions and beliefs, and that ultimately, Allah is the One who will judge us fairly and justly, regardless of our differences.
orig: الله يحكم بينكم يوم القيامة فيما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and earth? Indeed, that is in a Record. Indeed, that for Allah is easy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has knowledge of all that exists in the heavens and the earth. This knowledge is recorded in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), which is a divine record of all that has been and will be. The verse also highlights that it is easy for Allah to have this comprehensive knowledge, as He is the All-Knowing and All-Powerful.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله يعلم ما في السماء والأرض إن ذلك في كتاب إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: And they worship besides Allah that for which He has not sent down authority and of which they have no knowledge. And for the wrongdoers there is no helper.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of worshipping false gods or idols without any divine sanction or justification. It emphasizes that such worship is baseless, as these deities have no real power or authority, and the worshippers have no true knowledge of them. The verse also highlights that those who engage in such wrongdoing will have no one to support or defend them.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا وما ليس لهم به علم وما للظالمين من نصير

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve, disapproval. They are almost on the verge of assaulting those who recite to them Our verses. Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that? [It is] the Fire which Allah has promised those who disbelieve, and wretched is the destination."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of those who disbelieve when the clear verses of the Quran are recited to them. Their faces show disapproval and they are almost ready to attack those who recite the verses to them. The verse then asks if the disbelievers should be informed of something even worse than this - the Fire of Hell that Allah has promised for those who disbelieve. This highlights the severe punishment that awaits those who reject the message of the Quran, and the importance of accepting and submitting to the truth it conveys.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات تعرف في وجوه الذين كفروا المنكر يكادون يسطون بالذين يتلون عليهم آياتنا قل أفأنبئكم بشر من ذلكم النار وعدها الله الذين كفروا وبئس المصير

translation: O people, an example is presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create [as much as] a fly, even if they gathered together for that [purpose]. And if the fly should steal from them a [tiny] thing, they could not recover it from him. Weak are the pursuer and the pursued.
interpretation: This verse presents an example to illustrate the powerlessness of false deities worshipped besides Allah. It emphasizes that these false gods are incapable of even creating the simplest of creatures, a fly. Moreover, if a fly were to take something from the worshippers of these false gods, they would be unable to retrieve it. This highlights the weakness and helplessness of both the worshippers and the worshipped, in contrast to the power and might of the one true God, Allah.
orig: يا أيها الناس ضرب مثل فاستمعوا له إن الذين تدعون من دون الله لن يخلقوا ذبابا ولو اجتمعوا له وإن يسلبهم الذباب شيئا لا يستنقذوه منه ضعف الطالب والمطلوب

translation: They have not appraised Allah with true appraisal. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Mighty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that people do not truly appreciate the greatness and power of Allah. It suggests that humans often fail to comprehend the full extent of Allah's might and majesty. The interpretation is that we should strive to have a deeper understanding and reverence for Allah, who is all-powerful and deserving of our utmost respect and submission.
orig: ما قدروا الله حق قدره إن الله لقوي عزيز

translation: Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among the people. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Almighty, selects and appoints messengers from both the angelic and human realms. The angels, being pure and exalted beings, are chosen by Allah to convey His messages, while He also selects human messengers from among the people. This highlights the divine wisdom in utilizing both celestial and earthly messengers to guide humanity. Furthermore, the verse affirms that Allah is All-Hearing and All-Seeing, implying that He is fully aware of all that transpires and is able to discern the innermost thoughts and actions of His creation.
orig: الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا ومن الناس إن الله سميع بصير

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and to Allah will all matters be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and sovereignty. He has knowledge of all that has come before and all that is yet to come. Nothing is hidden from Him, and ultimately, all affairs and decisions will return to Him for judgment and resolution. This serves as a reminder to believers that they should strive to live in accordance with Allah's will, as He is fully aware of their actions and intentions.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: O you who believe, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good - that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse is an exhortation to the believers to engage in acts of worship and righteous deeds. It calls upon them to bow and prostrate in prayer, to worship and obey their Lord, and to do good deeds. The purpose of these actions is to attain success, both in this life and the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of a complete submission to Allah and the performance of good works as a means of achieving prosperity and salvation.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اركعوا واسجدوا واعبدوا ربكم وافعلوا الخير لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. [It is] the religion of your father, Abraham. Allah named you "Muslims" before [in former scriptures] and in this [Qur'an] that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer and give zakah and hold fast to Allah. He is your protector; and excellent is the protector, and excellent is the helper.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to strive and exert their utmost effort in the cause of Allah, as is their duty. It emphasizes that Allah has chosen the believers and made their religion, Islam, easy and free from hardship. The religion of Islam is the same as that of the prophet Abraham, the father of the believers. Allah has named the believers "Muslims" before in previous scriptures, and in the Qur'an, so that the Prophet Muhammad can be a witness over the believers, and the believers can be witnesses over the people. The verse then commands the believers to establish regular prayer, pay the obligatory charity (zakah), and hold firmly to their allegiance to Allah, for He is their protector and the best helper.
orig: وجاهدوا في الله حق جهاده هو اجتباكم وما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج ملة أبيكم إبراهيم هو سماكم المسلمين من قبل وفي هذا ليكون الرسول شهيدا عليكم وتكونوا شهداء على الناس فأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة واعتصموا بالله هو مولاكم فنعم المولى ونعم النصير

translation: Certainly, the believers have succeeded.
interpretation: This verse is a declaration of the success and triumph of the believers. It conveys the idea that those who have true faith in God and live according to His teachings will ultimately achieve success, both in this life and the Hereafter. The success of the believers is not limited to material or worldly gains, but encompasses spiritual and eternal well-being. This verse serves as a source of encouragement and motivation for the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to strive for the attainment of God's pleasure and eternal bliss.
orig: قد أفلح المؤمنون

translation: Those who are humble in their prayers
interpretation: This verse is describing the characteristics of the believers. It states that the true believers are those who are humble and reverent in their prayers. They approach their prayers with a deep sense of awe and submission to Allah, not merely going through the motions. This humility and devotion in prayer is a sign of their sincere faith and their desire to connect with the divine.
orig: الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون

translation: And those who turn away from ill speech
interpretation: This verse refers to people who avoid and abstain from engaging in idle, vain, or frivolous talk. They are described as those who "turn away from ill speech", indicating a conscious effort to refrain from speech that is meaningless, harmful, or unproductive. This quality reflects a level of spiritual and moral discipline, where the individual prioritizes restraint and focus over indulging in idle chatter or gossip.
orig: والذين هم عن اللغو معرضون

translation: And those who give [i.e., pay] the zakah (obligatory charity).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of paying zakah, which is one of the five pillars of Islam. Zakah is a mandatory charitable contribution that Muslims are required to pay, typically 2.5% of their wealth, to help the less fortunate members of society. By fulfilling this obligation, Muslims demonstrate their commitment to social welfare and their desire to purify their wealth and themselves.
orig: والذين هم للزكاة فاعلون

translation: And those who guard their private parts
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sexual morality and chastity in Islam. It encourages believers to protect their intimate parts from unlawful or inappropriate acts, and to maintain their sexual purity. This is seen as a sign of one's faith and commitment to the teachings of the Qur'an.
orig: والذين هم لفروجهم حافظون

translation: Except with their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they are not to be blamed -
interpretation: This verse establishes that sexual relations are only permissible within the bounds of marriage or with one's slaves. It indicates that engaging in sexual activity outside of these sanctioned relationships is considered blameworthy and sinful.
orig: إلا على أزواجهم أو ما ملكت أيمانهم فإنهم غير ملومين

translation: And whoever seeks beyond that - it is those who are the transgressors.
