interpretation: This verse is referring to those who go beyond the limits set by Allah and engage in unlawful or immoral acts. The interpretation is that those who seek things beyond what is permitted by Allah are the ones who are transgressing and acting in a way that is contrary to the teachings of Islam.
orig: فمن ابتغى وراء ذلك فأولئك هم العادون

translation: And those who are to their trusts and their promises attentive
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being trustworthy and fulfilling one's promises. It highlights that the truly righteous people are those who are careful to uphold the trusts and covenants entrusted to them, whether they are obligations to God, to other people, or to society at large. This speaks to the core Islamic values of honesty, integrity, and accountability.
orig: والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون

translation: And those who carefully maintain their prayers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining and being diligent in one's prayers. It suggests that those who are steadfast in their religious obligations, such as performing their daily prayers, are among the righteous and will be rewarded by Allah. The interpretation is that maintaining one's prayers is a sign of faith and devotion, and it is a crucial aspect of one's spiritual life and relationship with the divine.
orig: والذين هم على صلواتهم يحافظون

translation: It is they who will be the inheritors
interpretation: This verse refers to those who believe in God and follow His guidance. They will be the ones who inherit the blessings of the Hereafter, such as eternal life in Paradise. This emphasizes that true success and fulfillment comes from submitting to God and living righteously, rather than from worldly pursuits and possessions.
orig: أولئك هم الوارثون

translation: Those who will inherit Paradise, they will dwell therein [forever].
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who will be granted Paradise as their eternal abode in the Hereafter. The term "those who inherit the Paradise" indicates that Paradise is a reward and a blessing bestowed upon the righteous, not something that is earned through one's own efforts alone. The phrase "they will dwell therein [forever]" emphasizes the permanence and perpetuity of their stay in Paradise, without any end or interruption.
orig: الذين يرثون الفردوس هم فيها خالدون

translation: And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God has created humans from a humble and simple substance - clay. This reminds us of our lowly origins and the fact that we are dependent on God for our existence. It also suggests that despite our humble beginnings, God has endowed us with the ability to rise above our physical limitations and achieve great things through the guidance and blessings of the divine.
orig: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين

translation: Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging.
interpretation: This verse describes the early stage of human development, where the human embryo is first created as a sperm-drop and then placed in a secure and protected environment within the mother's womb. This emphasizes God's power and wisdom in the creation of human life, as well as the care and nurturing that the embryo receives during this crucial stage of development.
orig: ثم جعلناه نطفة في قرار مكين

translation: Then We created the sperm-drop into a clinging clot, and We created the clot into a [fetal] lump, and We created the [fetal] lump into bones, and We covered the bones with flesh; then We developed it into another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.
interpretation: This verse describes the stages of human embryonic development, from the initial sperm-drop to the fully formed fetus. It highlights the intricate and remarkable process of creation, emphasizing God's power and wisdom as the best of creators. The verse invites the reader to reflect on the wonders of the human body and to appreciate the divine artistry behind its formation.
orig: ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة فخلقنا العلقة مضغة فخلقنا المضغة عظاما فكسونا العظام لحما ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين

translation: Then, after that, you will surely die.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of death for all human beings, regardless of their circumstances or status. It serves as a reminder that this life is temporary and that we must prepare for the afterlife. The verse encourages us to live righteously and focus on our spiritual well-being, as we will all eventually face the reality of death and be held accountable for our actions.
orig: ثم إنكم بعد ذلك لميتون

translation: Then, indeed you - on the Day of Resurrection - will be resurrected.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Resurrection, when all people will be brought back to life and held accountable for their actions in this world. It serves as a reminder that our earthly lives are not the end, and that we will all face the ultimate reckoning on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ثم إنكم يوم القيامة تبعثون

translation: And We have created above you seven paths, and never have We been of the creation unaware.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has created seven distinct paths or levels of existence above us, which could be interpreted as referring to the seven heavens or the various planes of existence. It also emphasizes that Allah is never unaware or ignorant of His creation, indicating His omniscience and sovereignty over all that He has created.
orig: ولقد خلقنا فوقكم سبع طرائق وما كنا عن الخلق غافلين

translation: And We send down water from the sky in [due] measure, and We settle it in the earth. And indeed, We are Able to take it away.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's control and power over the water cycle. He sends down rain from the sky in a measured and controlled manner, and He has the ability to take that water away. This highlights God's sovereignty and the fact that all natural resources are under His dominion. The interpretation suggests that humans should recognize God's authority and not take His blessings for granted, as He can withdraw them as He pleases.
orig: وأنزلنا من السماء ماء بقدر فأسكناه في الأرض وإنا على ذهاب به لقادرون

translation: And We produced for you thereby gardens of palm trees and grapevines in which for you are abundant fruits and from which you eat.
interpretation: This verse is describing how God has created gardens and orchards filled with date palms and grapevines, providing a bountiful harvest of fruits for people to enjoy and sustain themselves. It is a testament to God's provision and the abundance of the natural world that He has created for the benefit of humanity.
orig: فأنشأنا لكم به جنات من نخيل وأعناب لكم فيها فواكه كثيرة ومنها تأكلون

translation: And a tree that emerges from Mount Sinai which produces oil and [a relish] for those who eat.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the olive tree, which grows abundantly in the region of Mount Sinai. The olive tree is a blessed and sacred tree that provides nourishment and sustenance to those who consume its fruits and oil. The oil from the olive tree has numerous benefits, including being a source of healthy fats, vitamins, and antioxidants. The verse highlights the bountiful provision of God, who has created this remarkable tree to benefit humanity.
orig: وشجرة تخرج من طور سيناء تنبت بالدهن وصبغ للآكلين

translation: And indeed, for you in the livestock is a lesson. We give you drink from what is in their bellies, and for you in them are [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the many blessings and lessons that can be found in the livestock animals that Allah has provided for humanity. It teaches us that we should reflect on the wonders of these creatures, and how they can provide us with sustenance and other benefits. The verse encourages us to be grateful for these gifts from Allah, and to use them in a responsible and ethical manner.
orig: وإن لكم في الأنعام لعبرة نسقيكم مما في بطونها ولكم فيها منافع كثيرة ومنها تأكلون

translation: And upon it and upon the ship you will be carried.
interpretation: This verse suggests that humans will be carried and transported not only on land, but also on ships or boats. It highlights the capability of humans to travel and navigate across bodies of water, which was an important mode of transportation and exploration in the past. The verse can be interpreted as a statement about the technological and transportation advancements that humans have achieved, allowing them to travel and be carried on various means, including ships and vessels.
orig: وعليها وعلى الفلك تحملون

translation: And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, and he said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear [Him]?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping and submitting to the one true God, Allah, as taught by the prophet Noah. It highlights that there is no other deity worthy of worship besides Allah, and calls upon the people to fear and revere Him. The verse underscores the fundamental message of monotheism and the need to abandon all forms of idolatry and polytheism.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فقال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره أفلا تتقون

translation: And the eminent among his people who disbelieved said, "This is not but a human like you who wishes to take precedence over you. And if Allah had willed, He could have sent down angels. We have not heard of this among our forefathers."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers in the Prophet's community to his claim of prophethood. They dismissed him as a mere mortal like themselves, who was seeking to elevate himself above them. They argued that if Allah had truly chosen him as a prophet, He would have sent down angels instead of a human messenger. This reflects their arrogance and unwillingness to accept a human prophet, as they were accustomed to the traditions of their forefathers.
orig: فقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه ما هذا إلا بشر مثلكم يريد أن يتفضل عليكم ولو شاء الله لأنزل ملائكة ما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين

translation: He is not but a man possessed by a spirit, so wait concerning him for a time.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the accusations made by the disbelievers against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), claiming that he is possessed by a spirit or a jinn. The verse instructs the believers to be patient and wait for the truth to be revealed, as the true nature of the Prophet will become clear with time.
orig: إن هو إلا رجل به جنة فتربصوا به حتى حين

translation: He (Moses) said: "My Lord! Help me against the people who belie (me)."
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is calling upon his Lord, Allah, to help him against the people who have rejected and disbelieved his message. This reflects Moses' reliance on Allah and his desire for divine assistance in the face of opposition and rejection from his people. The verse highlights the importance of seeking Allah's help and support when facing challenges and adversity in one's efforts to convey the truth.
orig: قال رب انصرني بما كذبون

translation: So We inspired to him, "Construct the ship under Our observation and Our inspiration. And when Our command comes and the oven overflows, load therein of every [creature] two mates and your family, except those about whom the word has preceded, and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are [to be] drowned."
interpretation: This verse describes the story of Prophet Noah and the construction of the Ark. God inspires Noah to build the Ark under His guidance and observation. When the time comes and the flood begins, Noah is commanded to load the Ark with two mates of every creature and his family, except those who had already been condemned. Noah is instructed not to plead for those who have wronged, as they are destined to be drowned in the flood. The verse emphasizes God's power, wisdom, and justice in delivering His command and punishing the wrongdoers while saving the righteous through Noah and the Ark.
orig: فأوحينا إليه أن اصنع الفلك بأعيننا ووحينا فإذا جاء أمرنا وفار التنور فاسلك فيها من كل زوجين اثنين وأهلك إلا من سبق عليه القول منهم ولا تخاطبني في الذين ظلموا إنهم مغرقون

translation: And when you have embarked with those who are with you upon the ship and they sail, then say: "Praise be to Allah who has saved us from the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to express gratitude to Allah upon being saved from a dangerous situation. The "ship" here can be interpreted as a metaphor for any mode of transportation or circumstance that delivers one from harm. The "wrongdoing people" refers to those who seek to oppress or harm the believers. The instruction to "say" the praise highlights the importance of verbally acknowledging Allah's protection and deliverance.
orig: فإذا استويت أنت ومن معك على الفلك فقل الحمد لله الذي نجانا من القوم الظالمين

translation: And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority."
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to seek refuge in Allah, the Almighty, and to ask Him to guide and protect them in all their affairs. The request to be granted "a sound entrance and a sound exit" implies a desire for Allah's guidance and protection in all aspects of life, from beginning to end. The phrase "a supporting authority" suggests a request for divine assistance and empowerment, which can come in the form of knowledge, wisdom, or divine favor. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah and seeking His help and blessings in all of one's endeavors.
orig: وقل رب أنزلني منزلا مباركا وأنت خير المنزلين

translation: Indeed in that are signs, and indeed, We are ever putting [people] to test.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the trials and tribulations we face in life are a means for us to grow and develop our faith. The "signs" referred to are the lessons and guidance that can be found in our experiences, if we approach them with wisdom and humility. The verse reminds us that Allah is constantly testing us, not to punish us, but to strengthen our relationship with Him and to help us become better versions of ourselves.
orig: إن في ذلك لآيات وإن كنا لمبتلين

translation: Then We produced after them another generation.
interpretation: This verse suggests that after the previous generations, Allah created another generation of people. This implies the continuous cycle of life and the renewal of humanity, as Allah replaces one generation with another. The interpretation is that Allah has the power to create and sustain successive generations, demonstrating His divine authority and control over the affairs of the world.
orig: ثم أنشأنا من بعدهم قرنا آخرين

translation: So We sent to them a messenger from among themselves, [saying], "Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him; then will you not fear [Him]?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him. The Qur'an instructs the people to worship Allah, the One true God, and to abandon any false deities or idols. The verse also highlights the role of the messenger, who is sent from among the people to convey this message of monotheism and call them to fear and revere Allah, the Almighty.
orig: فأرسلنا فيهم رسولا منهم أن اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره أفلا تتقون

translation: And the eminent among his people who disbelieved and denied the Meeting of the Hereafter and whom We had provided with comfort in the worldly life said, "This is not but a man like yourselves. He eats of that from which you eat and drinks of what you drink.
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the disbelieving leaders of the Prophet's people to his message. They dismissed him as merely a human being like themselves, who eats and drinks as they do. They refused to accept that he could be a prophet sent by God, denying the reality of the Hereafter and the accountability before God. Their arrogance and attachment to the comforts of this world blinded them to the truth of the Prophet's message.
orig: وقال الملأ من قومه الذين كفروا وكذبوا بلقاء الآخرة وأترفناهم في الحياة الدنيا ما هذا إلا بشر مثلكم يأكل مما تأكلون منه ويشرب مما تشربون

translation: And if you obey a human being like yourselves, then indeed, you would be losers.
interpretation: This verse warns against blindly following or obeying a human being, even if they appear to be like you. It suggests that such obedience would lead to loss or failure, as humans are fallible and can make mistakes. The verse encourages critical thinking and not simply accepting the words of others without scrutiny, as that can result in being led astray.
orig: ولئن أطعتم بشرا مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون

translation: Does He promise you that when you have died and become [mere] dust and bones, you will be brought forth [to new life]?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the disbelievers who deny the concept of resurrection and life after death. It is challenging them to consider whether they truly believe that after they have died and their bodies have decomposed into dust and bones, they will be brought back to life and held accountable for their actions. The verse is emphasizing the power and ability of God to resurrect the dead, which is a fundamental belief in Islam. The interpretation is that God has the power to recreate and resurrect the dead, and this is a promise that will be fulfilled on the Day of Judgment.
orig: أيعدكم أنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجون

translation: Far, far away is that which you are promised.
interpretation: This verse expresses the idea that the promise of the afterlife and the Day of Judgment is very distant and far-removed from the disbelievers' comprehension. It suggests that they are skeptical and doubtful about the reality of the Hereafter, which they view as something unattainable or impossible. The repetition of the word "haihat" (far, far away) emphasizes the magnitude of the distance between their current state of disbelief and the promised events of the Hereafter.
orig: هيهات هيهات لما توعدون

translation: Verily, this worldly life is all that [we] have. We die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient nature of this worldly life. It suggests that our existence is limited to the life we experience in this world - we are born, we live, and we die. The verse also implies that the belief in an afterlife and resurrection is not accepted by some people, who think that nothing remains after death except the passage of time. The verse challenges this notion and calls on people to reflect on the purpose of their existence beyond the temporal nature of this world.
orig: إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا نموت ونحيا وما نحن بمبعوثين

translation: He is not but a man who has fabricated a lie about Allah, and we will not believe in him.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a person who falsely claims to receive revelations from Allah and speaks on His behalf. The Qur'an rejects such claims, stating that this person is simply a liar who has fabricated a lie against Allah. The believers are instructed not to believe in this individual, as he is not a true messenger of Allah.
orig: إن هو إلا رجل افترى على الله كذبا وما نحن له بمؤمنين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, support me against the people who deny.'
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Al-Mu'minun, verse 26. It is a supplication made by the Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) to Allah, asking for help and support against the people who rejected his message and accused him of falsehood. The interpretation is that when faced with opposition and disbelief, the righteous should turn to Allah, seek His help and guidance, and have faith that He will support them against those who deny the truth.
orig: قال رب انصرني بما كذبون

translation: He (Pharaoh) said: "Soon will you know (the consequences)! Then (it was said to his forces), "Will you dispute with him about what he has shown (as Signs)?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the confrontation between Prophet Moses and Pharaoh. Pharaoh arrogantly dismissed the signs and miracles shown by Moses, but the verse warns that soon Pharaoh and his people will realize the consequences of their rejection and disbelief. The interpretation suggests that those who deny the truth will eventually regret their actions when they face the consequences.
orig: قال عما قليل ليصبحن نادمين

translation: So the shriek seized them in truth, and We made them as [plant] stubble. So away with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the disbelievers who rejected the message of the Prophets. They were struck by a devastating punishment, likened to a "shriek" that seized them, as a consequence of their wrongdoing and injustice. The verse emphasizes that this punishment was justified and in accordance with the truth. The imagery of them being made "as [plant] stubble" conveys the idea that they were utterly destroyed and reduced to insignificance. The final statement "So away with the wrongdoing people" expresses a strong condemnation of the evildoers and distance from them.
orig: فأخذتهم الصيحة بالحق فجعلناهم غثاء فبعدا للقوم الظالمين

translation: Then We produced after them another generation
interpretation: This verse suggests that after the previous generations, Allah created and established another set of people on Earth. This implies that the cycle of life continues, with new generations succeeding the old ones. The verse emphasizes Allah's power and ability to create and sustain human life throughout the ages.
orig: ثم أنشأنا من بعدهم قرونا آخرين

translation: No community can advance its term, nor can they delay it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the lifespan and fate of a community or civilization is predetermined by Allah. No matter how much they try, they cannot hasten or delay their appointed time. This is a reminder of the sovereignty of Allah over all affairs and the need for humanity to submit to His will.
orig: ما تسبق من أمة أجلها وما يستأخرون

translation: Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Whenever their messenger came to a nation, they denied him, so We made some of them follow others [in succession] and We made them narrations. So away with a people who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah sent a succession of messengers to guide humanity, but many nations rejected their message. As a result, Allah caused those nations to be destroyed or dispersed, and their stories became mere "narrations" or historical accounts. This serves as a warning to those who refuse to believe in Allah's signs and messengers, that they too will face the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: ثم أرسلنا رسلنا تترى كل ما جاء أمة رسولها كذبوه فأتبعنا بعضهم بعضا وجعلناهم أحاديث فبعدا لقوم لا يؤمنون

translation: Then We sent Moses and his brother Aaron with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse refers to the sending of the Prophets Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and the Israelites. The "signs" mentioned are the miracles and proofs that were given to them to demonstrate the truth of their message. The "clear authority" indicates the divine mandate and power that they were granted to convey God's message and call people to worship Him alone. This verse highlights the importance of prophetic guidance and the need for people to heed the divine message brought by the Messengers of God.
orig: ثم أرسلنا موسى وأخاه هارون بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

translation: To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they behaved insolently, and they were a self-conceited people.
interpretation: This verse refers to the confrontation between Prophet Moses and the powerful ruler Pharaoh, along with his elite entourage. Despite the clear signs and miracles shown by Moses, Pharaoh and his followers responded with arrogance, pride, and a sense of superiority. They refused to submit to the truth and guidance brought by the prophet, choosing instead to maintain their positions of power and authority. This highlights the danger of ego, self-conceit, and a refusal to acknowledge the truth, even in the face of overwhelming evidence.
orig: إلى فرعون وملئه فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما عالين

translation: They said, "Do we believe in two human beings like ourselves while their people are to us subservient?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the response of the disbelievers when the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his companion were sent as messengers. The disbelievers questioned how they could believe in two human beings like themselves, when their people (the people of the messengers) were subservient to them. This reflects the arrogance and skepticism of the disbelievers, who could not accept that ordinary human beings could be chosen by God as messengers. The interpretation is that the Qur'an is highlighting the importance of humility and openness to God's guidance, rather than relying on one's own preconceptions and status.
orig: فقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا وقومهما لنا عابدون

translation: But they denied them, so they were of the destroyed.
interpretation: This verse refers to a group of people who rejected the messages and warnings delivered by the prophets sent to them. As a result, they faced destruction and were annihilated as a consequence of their disbelief and rejection. The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the guidance and warnings provided by the prophets, as those who reject them will ultimately face severe consequences.
orig: فكذبوهما فكانوا من المهلكين

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, that perhaps they would be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah had revealed the Scripture to Moses, the Torah, so that the people of Israel would be guided and follow the correct path. The purpose of the divine revelation was to provide guidance and direction for the Israelites, so that they may worship Allah alone and live according to His commands. The verse suggests that if the Israelites had followed the teachings of the Torah, they would have been rightly guided.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب لعلهم يهتدون

translation: And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign, and We gave them refuge on high ground with flowing water.
interpretation: This verse is referring to Jesus (peace be upon him) and his mother, Mary. It highlights their status as signs or miracles of Allah, and how they were provided with a place of refuge and sustenance. The "high ground with flowing water" symbolizes the protection and provision that Allah granted them, even in the face of adversity. This verse emphasizes the divine favor and care bestowed upon Jesus and Mary, and serves as a testament to Allah's power and mercy.
orig: وجعلنا ابن مريم وأمه آية وآويناهما إلى ربوة ذات قرار ومعين

translation: O Messengers, eat from the good things and work righteousness. Indeed, I, of what you do, am Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophets and Messengers of Allah, instructing them to consume only the good and pure things, and to engage in righteous deeds. It emphasizes that Allah is All-Knowing of their actions, and that they will be held accountable for what they do.
orig: يا أيها الرسل كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا إني بما تعملون عليم

translation: And indeed this, your religion, is one religion, and I am your Lord, so fear Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the Islamic faith, and the fact that all believers should submit to the one true God, Allah. It calls upon the faithful to be mindful of and obedient to their Lord, as He is the sole deity worthy of worship. The interpretation is that Muslims should strive for unity in their religious beliefs and practices, and maintain a constant awareness of their accountability to Allah.
orig: وإن هذه أمتكم أمة واحدة وأنا ربكم فاتقون

translation: Then they broke up their affair among themselves into (different) sects: each party rejoicing in that which is with itself.
interpretation: This verse describes how people often divide themselves into different factions and groups, each one rejoicing in their own beliefs and ideas rather than seeking unity. The interpretation is that this tendency towards division and self-satisfaction with one's own views is a source of discord and prevents people from coming together and finding common ground.
orig: فتقطعوا أمرهم بينهم زبرا كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون

translation: So leave them in their confusion for a time.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to leave the disbelievers alone and let them remain in their state of ignorance and misguidance until the appointed time when they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse suggests that the Prophet should not be distressed by their rejection of the message, but rather allow them to continue in their state of confusion and uncertainty until the Day of Judgment, when they will face the consequences of their choices.
orig: فذرهم في غمرتهم حتى حين

translation: Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children
interpretation: This verse is questioning the belief of those who think that the wealth and children they possess are a sign of Allah's pleasure and favor upon them. The verse suggests that this is a mistaken belief, as Allah may provide these things to test and try people, not necessarily as a sign of His approval.
orig: أيحسبون أنما نمدهم به من مال وبنين

translation: We hasten for them in the good deeds, but they perceive not.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah is guiding and leading people towards good deeds and righteous actions, even if they are unaware of it. The interpretation is that Allah is actively working to provide opportunities and blessings for people to do good, but some people may not recognize or appreciate this divine guidance and assistance.
orig: نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون

translation: Indeed, those who are apprehensive out of fear of their Lord
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who truly believe in God and are conscious of His presence are filled with a sense of awe and reverence for Him. They are not driven by fear, but rather by a deep respect and humility before the Almighty. This state of being "apprehensive out of fear of their Lord" motivates them to lead righteous lives, avoid sin, and strive to please God in all their actions.
orig: إن الذين هم من خشية ربهم مشفقون

translation: And those who believe in the signs of their Lord
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having faith in the signs and revelations of God. It suggests that true believers are those who wholeheartedly accept and trust in the divine messages and guidance provided in the Qur'an and other forms of divine communication. This unwavering belief in God's signs is a key characteristic of the faithful, as it forms the foundation of their spiritual journey and relationship with the divine.
orig: والذين هم بآيات ربهم يؤمنون

translation: And those who do not associate [anything] with their Lord
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him. It refers to the believers who are devoted to Allah and do not commit polytheism or idolatry. The interpretation is that true believers in Allah will not ascribe divinity to anyone or anything other than the one true God.
orig: والذين هم بربهم لا يشركون

translation: And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful because they will be returning to their Lord
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of the righteous believers. They are those who give charitably and perform good deeds, not out of a sense of pride or boastfulness, but out of a sincere fear and reverence for Allah. They are cognizant that they will ultimately return to their Lord and be held accountable for their actions. This mindset of humility and awareness of the Hereafter motivates them to do good and avoid evil, as they seek to please Allah and earn His pleasure.
orig: والذين يؤتون ما آتوا وقلوبهم وجلة أنهم إلى ربهم راجعون

translation: It is they who hasten to good deeds, and they who are foremost in them.
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous people who eagerly and swiftly perform good deeds, and are the first to do so. They are not hesitant or delayed in doing what is right and pleasing to God. This highlights the importance of being proactive and diligent in our pursuit of virtue and acts of goodness.
orig: أولئك يسارعون في الخيرات وهم لها سابقون

translation: And We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. And with Us is a record which speaks with [precise] truth; and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. He is just and fair, and will judge people based on what they are capable of doing. The Qur'an, which is described as a "record which speaks with [precise] truth", will be the basis for this judgment, and people will not be treated unjustly.
orig: ولا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها ولدينا كتاب ينطق بالحق وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Nay, but their hearts are plunged in ignorance of this (Qur'an), and they have other (evil) deeds, besides, which they are doing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the hearts of those who reject the Qur'an are veiled from understanding its message. They are preoccupied with other deeds and actions that are not in accordance with the guidance of the Qur'an. The verse implies that their rejection of the Qur'an is not due to a lack of understanding, but rather a result of their own choices and actions that keep them from recognizing the truth.
orig: بل قلوبهم في غمرة من هذا ولهم أعمال من دون ذلك هم لها عاملون

translation: Until, when We seize the affluent among them with punishment, at once they are crying out.
interpretation: This verse describes a scenario where the affluent and privileged people are punished by God. When they face the consequences of their actions, they cry out in despair, realizing the gravity of their situation. The verse suggests that those who have been arrogant and indulged in worldly pleasures will not be spared from divine retribution when the time comes.
orig: حتى إذا أخذنا مترفيهم بالعذاب إذا هم يجأرون

translation: Do not cry out this Day. Indeed, you will not be helped by Us.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to those who disbelieve and reject the message of Islam. It conveys the message that on the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers will not be able to seek help or protection from Allah, as they have turned away from Him during their worldly lives. The verse emphasizes the importance of submitting to Allah and following His guidance, as those who reject it will be left helpless on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: لا تجأروا اليوم إنكم منا لا تنصرون

translation: Certainly, My verses used to be recited to you, but you were turning back on your heels [in aversion].
interpretation: This verse expresses that God's revelations were recited to the people, but they turned away from them and refused to accept them. The verse suggests that the people were arrogant and stubborn, unwilling to listen and submit to the truth of God's message. It highlights the importance of humility and openness in approaching the divine teachings, rather than rejecting them out of hand.
orig: قد كانت آياتي تتلى عليكم فكنتم على أعقابكم تنكصون

translation: Arrogantly they go forth to it. Flee ye from it!
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people of Samaria, who were arrogant and proud in their rejection of the truth. The verse is calling upon the believers to flee from such arrogance and rejection, and to not be influenced by those who are stubborn in their disbelief.
orig: مستكبرين به سامرا تهجرون

translation: Have they not reflected upon the word, or has there come to them that which had not come to their forefathers of old?
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect and ponder upon the message of the Qur'an, as it is a revelation from God that has not been received by their ancestors before. The implication is that they should not reject the Qur'an simply because it is new to them, but rather they should carefully consider its teachings and the wisdom it contains.
orig: أفلم يدبروا القول أم جاءهم ما لم يأت آباءهم الأولين

translation: Or have they not recognized their messenger, so they are toward him disincliners?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people have failed to recognize or accept their prophet, and thus they have turned away from him and rejected his message. The interpretation is that those who do not acknowledge the prophet sent to them are turning away from the guidance and truth that he brings, and are denying or refusing to accept his authority and teachings.
orig: أم لم يعرفوا رسولهم فهم له منكرون

translation: Or do they say, "He has made it up"? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, [O Muhammad], that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you [so] perhaps they will be guided.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of those who reject the Qur'an, claiming that Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) has "made it up" or fabricated it. The Qur'an responds by affirming that it is the truth revealed by Allah, the Lord of the worlds, in order to warn a people who have not received a divine message before. The verse encourages the people to reflect on the Qur'an and be guided, as most of them are "averse to the truth".
orig: أم يقولون به جنة بل جاءهم بالحق وأكثرهم للحق كارهون

translation: And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been ruined. Rather, We have brought them their message, but they, from their message, are turning away.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the truth must be followed, even if it goes against people's desires and inclinations. It suggests that if people were to simply follow their own whims and desires, it would lead to the corruption and destruction of the entire universe. Instead, God has provided guidance and a reminder ("their message") for humanity, but many people choose to turn away from it and ignore it.
orig: ولو اتبع الحق أهواءهم لفسدت السماوات والأرض ومن فيهن بل أتيناهم بذكرهم فهم عن ذكرهم معرضون

translation: Or do you ask them for payment? But the provision of your Lord is better, and He is the best of providers.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers, asking whether they are seeking payment or reward from the people they are calling to Islam. The verse then states that the provision or reward from Allah is better than any worldly payment, and that Allah is the best of providers. The interpretation is that the believers should not be focused on receiving earthly rewards for their efforts in spreading the message of Islam, but rather they should seek the pleasure and reward of Allah, who is the ultimate Provider and the best of those who provide.
orig: أم تسألهم خرجا فخراج ربك خير وهو خير الرازقين

translation: And indeed, you [O Muhammad] invite them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is calling people to the straight and righteous path of Islam. It is a directive from God to the Prophet to guide humanity towards the path of truth, justice, and salvation. The "straight path" refers to the teachings and principles of the Qur'an, which lead to a life of faith, morality, and spiritual fulfillment.
orig: وإنك لتدعوهم إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the Path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject the belief in the Hereafter, the afterlife, are straying from the straight path that leads to salvation. By denying the existence of the Hereafter, they are deviating from the true guidance and the righteous way of living that is prescribed in the Qur'an. This highlights the importance of having faith in the Hereafter as it shapes one's worldview and determines the direction of one's life.
orig: وإن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة عن الصراط لناكبون

translation: And if We gave them mercy and removed what afflict them, they would still persist in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even if God were to show mercy and remove the hardships and afflictions from the people, they would still persist in their arrogance and rebellion. They would continue to wander aimlessly, blinded by their own stubbornness and refusal to heed the guidance of God.
orig: ولو رحمناهم وكشفنا ما بهم من ضر للجوا في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: And We had certainly seized them with punishment, but they did not submit to their Lord, nor did they humbly supplicate.
interpretation: This verse describes how despite facing punishment from Allah, the disbelievers did not humble themselves before Him nor did they sincerely supplicate to Him for forgiveness. It highlights their stubborn refusal to submit to the will of Allah, even in the face of adversity. The interpretation is that true humility and supplication to Allah is necessary for one to find guidance and salvation.
orig: ولقد أخذناهم بالعذاب فما استكانوا لربهم وما يتضرعون

translation: Until, when We open for them a gate of severe punishment, at once they will be therein in despair.
interpretation: This verse describes a scenario where Allah opens a gate of severe punishment for those who have rejected faith and persisted in their wrongdoing. When faced with this punishment, they will be in utter despair, realizing the consequences of their actions. The verse highlights the finality and inevitability of divine retribution for those who stubbornly reject the guidance and continue to disobey Allah.
orig: حتى إذا فتحنا عليهم بابا ذا عذاب شديد إذا هم فيه مبلسون

translation: And it is He who has created for you the hearing and the sight and the heart; little are you grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who has bestowed upon humanity the senses of hearing, sight, and understanding (the heart). However, despite these blessings, people tend to be ungrateful and fail to appreciate the gifts they have been given. The verse serves as a reminder to be thankful to Allah for the faculties that allow us to perceive and comprehend the world around us.
orig: وهو الذي أنشأ لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: And it is He who has produced you [i.e., created you] from the earth and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and sovereignty of God. He is the one who has created all of humanity and placed them on the earth. Ultimately, all people will be gathered before Him on the Day of Resurrection to be held accountable for their actions in this life. This serves as a reminder of God's power and the importance of living a righteous life in preparation for the Hereafter.
orig: وهو الذي ذرأكم في الأرض وإليه تحشرون

translation: And it is He who gives life and causes death, and to Him is [attributed] the alternation of the night and the day. Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the sole Creator and Sustainer of life and death, and that the alternation of night and day is a sign of His power and wisdom. It calls upon people to reflect and use their intellect to understand the profound meaning behind these natural phenomena, and to recognize the existence and oneness of Allah.
orig: وهو الذي يحيي ويميت وله اختلاف الليل والنهار أفلا تعقلون

translation: But they say the like of what the former [generations] said.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who reject the message of the Quran and make statements similar to those made by previous generations of disbelievers. It suggests that their rejection of the truth is not novel, but rather a repetition of the same patterns of denial and skepticism that have existed throughout history. The verse implies that their objections and excuses are not original, but rather a rehashing of arguments that have already been addressed and refuted.
orig: بل قالوا مثل ما قال الأولون

translation: They say, "When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected?"
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of some people regarding the concept of resurrection and the afterlife. They question how it is possible for them to be resurrected after they have died and their bodies have decomposed into dust and bones. This reflects a lack of understanding and belief in the power and wisdom of God, who has the ability to recreate and resurrect the dead. The interpretation of this verse is that God has the power to bring the dead back to life, and that the resurrection is a certainty that should be accepted by those who believe in God and His divine plan.
orig: قالوا أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمبعوثون

translation: Certainly, We and our forefathers have been promised this before. This is nothing but the legends of the ancients.
interpretation: This verse expresses the skepticism and disbelief of the people towards the message of the Qur'an, which they dismiss as nothing more than "legends of the ancients". They argue that they and their forefathers have heard similar claims and promises before, implying that the Qur'anic message is not new or unique. The verse highlights the resistance and rejection that the Prophet Muhammad faced from his people, who were unwilling to accept the divine revelation.
orig: لقد وعدنا نحن وآباؤنا هذا من قبل إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: Say, "To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you should know?"
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question to challenge the disbelievers and polytheists who associate partners with Allah. The implication is that the earth and everything in it belongs to Allah alone, the One true God, and not to any other deities or false gods that they may worship. The verse is inviting them to reflect and acknowledge the oneness and sovereignty of Allah over all creation.
orig: قل لمن الأرض ومن فيها إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: They will say, "[It is] for Allah." Say, "Then will you not remember?"
interpretation: This verse addresses those who attribute their wealth and blessings to Allah, but fail to show gratitude and live according to His teachings. The interpretation is that Allah is reminding them to reflect on the source of their blessings and to live a life that is pleasing to Him, rather than merely paying lip service to their faith.
orig: سيقولون لله قل أفلا تذكرون

translation: Say, "Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Great Throne?"
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the disbelievers to acknowledge the Oneness and Sovereignty of Allah. It emphasizes that Allah is the Lord and Sustainer of the entire universe, including the seven heavens and the Mighty Throne. This affirms Allah's supreme power, authority, and control over all creation, which should lead to worship and submission to Him alone.
orig: قل من رب السماوات السبع ورب العرش العظيم

translation: They will say, "[It is] for Allah." Say, "Then will you not fear [Him]?"
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who attribute their wealth and possessions to Allah, but do not fear Him or fulfill their obligations to Him. The interpretation is that one should not merely claim to believe in Allah, but should also demonstrate that belief through righteous actions and a God-fearing attitude. The question "Then will you not fear [Him]?" is meant to make them reflect on their lack of true devotion and commitment to Allah.
orig: سيقولون لله قل أفلا تتقون

translation: Say, "Who is it in whose hand is the dominion of all things? And He protects, but none can protect from Him, if you should know."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of God over all creation. It challenges the reader to recognize that God alone has dominion and control over the entire universe, and that no one and nothing can protect against His will or judgment. The interpretation suggests that this verse is a call to acknowledge God's supreme authority and to submit to Him, as only He can provide true protection and security.
orig: قل من بيده ملكوت كل شيء وهو يجير ولا يجار عليه إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: They will say, "[It is] for Allah." Say, "Then how are you deluded?"
interpretation: This verse addresses the common practice of people attributing their actions and possessions to Allah, while in reality they are being deluded and misguided. The interpretation suggests that the believer should challenge this notion and ask how they can be so deceived, as everything ultimately belongs to Allah and should be used in accordance with His will.
orig: سيقولون لله قل فأنى تسحرون

translation: Nay, We have brought them the Truth, and indeed they (themselves) are liars.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the people have been given the truth and guidance through the Qur'an, but they choose to reject it and continue in their falsehoods. It is a strong rebuke of those who deny the truth despite its clear presentation to them. The interpretation is that the people’s own lies and deceptions are the reason for their rejection of the truth, not any shortcoming in the truth itself.
orig: بل أتيناهم بالحق وإنهم لكاذبون

translation: Allah has not taken any son, nor has there ever been with Him any deity. [If there had been], then each deity would have taken what it created, and some of them would have sought to overcome others. Exalted is Allah above what they describe [concerning Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute unity and uniqueness of Allah. It rejects the notion of Allah having a son or any other deity associated with Him, as this would imply a division of power and authority, which is incompatible with the concept of a supreme, all-powerful God. The verse also suggests that if there were multiple deities, they would each seek to assert their own authority and compete with one another, which is contrary to the idea of a harmonious, unified divine order. By declaring Allah "exalted above what they describe", the verse affirms that Allah is beyond any human conception or association, and that He is free from the limitations and attributes that people may ascribe to Him.
orig: ما اتخذ الله من ولد وما كان معه من إله إذا لذهب كل إله بما خلق ولعلا بعضهم على بعض سبحان الله عما يصفون

translation: The Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, so high is He above what they associate [with Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme and transcendent nature of God, who has knowledge of both the unseen (the spiritual realm) and the witnessed (the physical world). It affirms that God is far above and beyond any association with partners or equals, which would diminish His absolute sovereignty and divinity.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة فتعالى عما يشركون

translation: Say, "My Lord, show me that which they are promised."
interpretation: This verse is a supplication by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to Allah, asking Him to show him the fulfillment of the promises made in the Qur'an, whether it be the punishment of the disbelievers or the reward of the believers. It reflects the Prophet's eagerness to see the divine plan unfold and his trust in Allah's promise. The interpretation suggests that the believer should have a strong desire to witness the triumph of truth and justice, while maintaining patience and reliance on Allah's wisdom and timing.
orig: قل رب إما تريني ما يوعدون

translation: My Lord, so do not place me among the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse expresses the supplication of the believer to Allah, asking to not be counted among the wrongdoers. It reflects a deep desire to avoid the company and fate of those who transgress against Allah's commands and oppress others. The interpretation is that the believer is seeking Allah's protection and guidance to remain on the righteous path, distancing themselves from the misguided and unjust.
orig: رب فلا تجعلني في القوم الظالمين

translation: And indeed, [O Muhammad], We are able to show you what We have promised them.
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah's power and ability to fulfill His promises, including showing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) the fate of those who disbelieve. It is a reassurance that Allah is in control and will bring about the events He has foretold, whether it is the punishment of the disbelievers or the triumph of the believers. The verse emphasizes that Allah has the power to make good on His promises, and the Prophet can be certain that what Allah has promised will come to pass.
orig: وإنا على أن نريك ما نعدهم لقادرون

translation: Repel [evil] by that [deed] which is better; and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity [will become] as though he was a devoted friend.
interpretation: This verse encourages responding to evil with good, as this can transform enmity into friendship. The idea is that by meeting aggression with patience and kindness, one can diffuse tension and potentially turn an enemy into an ally. The verse suggests that Allah knows best how to deal with those who speak ill, and that the righteous response is to counter negativity with positivity.
orig: ادفع بالتي هي أحسن السيئة نحن أعلم بما يصفون

translation: And say, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils,"
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to seek refuge in Allah from the whispers and temptations of the devils. The devils, or Satan and his followers, constantly try to lead people astray and encourage them to sin. By seeking refuge in Allah, the believer is protected from their harmful influence and is able to remain steadfast on the path of righteousness.
orig: وقل رب أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين

translation: And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present.
interpretation: This verse expresses the desire to seek refuge in Allah, the Lord, from the presence or influence of those who may harm or mislead the speaker. It reflects a deep reliance on Allah's protection and a recognition of the importance of seeking refuge from any negative forces or influences.
orig: وأعوذ بك رب أن يحضرون

translation: Until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "My Lord, send me back",
interpretation: This verse refers to the regret that some people will feel when they face the reality of death. They will wish to return to the world and have another chance to believe in God and do good deeds. However, this request will be denied, as death is the final stage of one's earthly life and there is no going back. The verse highlights the importance of being prepared for the afterlife and not delaying one's faith and righteous actions until the last moment.
orig: حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت قال رب ارجعون

translation: Perhaps I may do righteous deeds in that which I have left behind. No! Indeed, it is only a [worthless] word he is saying. And behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of righteous deeds and the futility of mere words. The person speaking expresses a desire to do good deeds in the future, but the Qur'an dismisses this as an empty statement. The verse also suggests that there is a barrier or separation between the living and the dead until the Day of Resurrection, when all will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت كلا إنها كلمة هو قائلها ومن ورائهم برزخ إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: And when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no relationships among them that Day, nor will they ask about one another.
interpretation: This verse describes the events of the Day of Resurrection, when the Trumpet will be blown to signal the end of the world. On that day, all human relationships and family ties will be severed, and people will be solely focused on their own accountability before God. There will be no opportunity for people to inquire about their relatives or loved ones, as everyone will be preoccupied with their own judgment.
orig: فإذا نفخ في الصور فلا أنساب بينهم يومئذ ولا يتساءلون

translation: So he whose scales are heavy [with good deeds] - it is they who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those whose good deeds outweigh their bad deeds on the Day of Judgment will be the ones who achieve success and salvation. It suggests that the ultimate measure of a person's worth is not their worldly status or accomplishments, but the weight of their good deeds in the sight of God. The successful are those who have lived righteous lives and will be rewarded accordingly.
orig: فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And as for him whose scales (of good deeds) are light, those are they who have lost their own selves, in Hell will they abide.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Judgment, where people's deeds will be weighed on a scale. Those whose good deeds are outweighed by their bad deeds will be condemned to eternal punishment in Hell. This serves as a warning to live a righteous life and strive to do more good than evil, lest one be among "those who have lost their own selves" and are doomed to an eternity in the Hellfire.
orig: ومن خفت موازينه فأولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم في جهنم خالدون

translation: Their faces will be blackened by the Fire, and they will be in it, their eyes cast down in humiliation.
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment of the disbelievers in the Hereafter. Their faces will be disfigured and blackened by the intense heat and flames of the Fire of Hell, and they will be in a state of constant anguish and distress, their eyes cast down in shame and humiliation.
orig: تلفح وجوههم النار وهم فيها كالحون

translation: Were not My verses recited to you, but you were turning back on your heels?
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who denied the signs and revelations of God, despite them being recited and presented to them. The verse expresses God's disappointment that despite the clear evidence and guidance provided, they stubbornly rejected the truth and turned away from it. It is a reminder that denying the divine signs and messages, even when they are made clear, is a grave offense against God.
orig: ألم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم فكنتم بها تكذبون

translation: They will say: "Our Lord! Our wretchedness overcame us, and we were (an) erring people."
interpretation: This verse describes the remorseful plea of those who have strayed from the righteous path and fallen into a state of wretchedness. They acknowledge that their own misguided choices and actions led them astray, and they now seek forgiveness from their Lord. The interpretation suggests that true repentance and a humble admission of one's mistakes are the first steps towards seeking guidance and redemption from the Almighty.
orig: قالوا ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين

translation: Our Lord, remove us from this [city whose] people are oppressors and grant us from Yourself a protector and grant us from Yourself a helper.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication from the believers, asking Allah to remove them from a place where the people are oppressors. They acknowledge that if they were to return to that place, they would be wrongdoers themselves. The verse highlights the importance of seeking refuge and protection from Allah, as well as seeking His help and guidance to avoid falling into oppression and wrongdoing.
orig: ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون

translation: He will say, "Depart into it and speak not to Me."
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. Allah will command them to enter Hell and will forbid them from speaking to Him, as they had rejected His signs and disobeyed His commands during their worldly life. This is a stern warning against disbelief and a reminder that those who turn away from Allah will face a severe and eternal punishment.
orig: قال اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون

translation: Indeed, there was a group of My servants who said, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful.'
interpretation: This verse speaks of a group of believers who acknowledge their faith in God and humbly ask for His forgiveness and mercy. The key message here is that even the most devout believers recognize their need for God's grace and compassion. It emphasizes the importance of humility, repentance, and reliance on God's infinite mercy, as the best of outcomes comes from the Most Merciful.
orig: إنه كان فريق من عبادي يقولون ربنا آمنا فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الراحمين

translation: And you took them in mockery until they made you forget My remembrance, while you used to laugh at them.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from God to those who mock and ridicule the believers. It suggests that by engaging in such behavior, they have forgotten God's remembrance and become distracted from their true purpose in life. The verse emphasizes that the act of mocking and laughing at the believers is a grave sin, as it leads to the neglect of one's spiritual obligations and the remembrance of God.
orig: فاتخذتموهم سخريا حتى أنسوكم ذكري وكنتم منهم تضحكون

translation: Indeed, I have rewarded them this Day for their patient endurance - that they are the successful.
interpretation: This verse conveys that those who have patiently endured trials and tribulations in this life will be rewarded by Allah on the Day of Judgment. Their steadfastness and faith have led them to success and triumph in the Hereafter. The interpretation suggests that patience and perseverance in the face of adversity are highly valued by Allah, and those who exhibit such qualities will be considered "the successful" in the end.
orig: إني جزيتهم اليوم بما صبروا أنهم هم الفائزون

translation: He (Allah) will say: 'For how many years did you remain on the earth?'
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when Allah will question the disbelievers about the duration of their stay on earth. The purpose of this question is to make them realize how short their worldly life was compared to the eternal life in the Hereafter, and to make them accountable for how they spent their time on earth.
orig: قال كم لبثتم في الأرض عدد سنين

translation: They will say, "We have remained for a day or part of a day, so ask those who keep account."
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when the disbelievers will be asked about the duration of their worldly life. They will claim that they only stayed for a day or part of a day, indicating their perception of the brevity of their earthly existence. However, the verse encourages them to ask "those who keep account", meaning the angels who record the deeds of people, to get the true measure of the time they spent in the world. This highlights the tendency of humans to underestimate the significance of their lives and the importance of the Hereafter, and the need to rely on divine knowledge rather than one's own limited perspective.
orig: قالوا لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم فاسأل العادين

translation: He will say, "How long did you remain on earth in number of years?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when people will be questioned about their time on earth. The interpretation is that if people had known the true nature of the afterlife, they would have realized that their time on earth was "only a little" compared to the eternal life in the hereafter. This is a reminder to focus on the everlasting life in the Hereafter rather than being consumed by the temporary pleasures of this world.
orig: قال إن لبثتم إلا قليلا لو أنكم كنتم تعلمون

translation: Did you think that We had created you in vain and that to Us you would not be returned?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, challenging the notion that human existence is meaningless or without purpose. The implication is that humans have been created with a higher purpose, and that they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions and return to God. The interpretation suggests that the purpose of life is not mere vanity or futility, but rather that there is a greater meaning and significance to our existence, which will be revealed in the hereafter.
orig: أفحسبتم أنما خلقناكم عبثا وأنكم إلينا لا ترجعون

translation: So exalted is Allah, the Sovereign, the Real. There is no deity except Him, the Lord of the Noble Throne.
interpretation: This verse affirms the supreme sovereignty and divinity of Allah. It emphasizes that Allah is the true and rightful Ruler, and that He alone deserves worship, as there is no other deity worthy of worship besides Him. The reference to the "Noble Throne" signifies Allah's power, majesty, and control over the entire universe.
orig: فتعالى الله الملك الحق لا إله إلا هو رب العرش الكريم

translation: And whoever invokes besides Allah another deity for which he has no proof - then his account is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping only Allah, the one true God, and not associating any other deities with Him. It warns that those who worship false gods without any proof or justification will be held accountable before their Lord. The interpretation is that true success and salvation can only be attained by those who believe in and worship Allah alone, and not by those who reject this fundamental belief in the oneness of God.
orig: ومن يدع مع الله إلها آخر لا برهان له به فإنما حسابه عند ربه إنه لا يفلح الكافرون

translation: And say, "My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful."
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to humbly ask Allah for forgiveness and mercy. It highlights that Allah is the most Merciful and the best of those who show mercy. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness and relying on His boundless mercy, as He is the ultimate source of compassion and grace.
orig: وقل رب اغفر وارحم وأنت خير الراحمين

translation: We have sent it down and imposed it, and We have sent down in it verses [which are] clear that you might remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an was revealed by God and its teachings were made obligatory for the believers. The verses of the Qur'an are clear and unambiguous, guiding people towards remembrance of God and righteous living. The purpose is to remind people of the truth and encourage them to reflect on the divine message, so that they may live according to God's will.
orig: سورة أنزلناها وفرضناها وأنزلنا فيها آيات بينات لعلكم تذكرون

translation: The [unmarried] woman or [unmarried] man found guilty of sexual intercourse - lash each one of them with a hundred lashes, and do not be taken by pity for them in the religion of Allah , if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes the punishment for adultery or fornication in Islam. The punishment is a hundred lashes for both the man and woman involved, to be carried out publicly as a deterrent and to uphold the moral standards of the religion. The verse emphasizes that this punishment should be carried out without any compassion or leniency, as it is a matter of upholding the laws of Allah. The public nature of the punishment also serves to reinforce the gravity of the offense and its consequences within the community of believers.
orig: الزانية والزاني فاجلدوا كل واحد منهما مائة جلدة ولا تأخذكم بهما رأفة في دين الله إن كنتم تؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر وليشهد عذابهما طائفة من المؤمنين

translation: The fornicator does not marry except a [female] fornicator or a polytheist, and the [female] fornicator does not marry except a fornicator or a polytheist. And that has been made unlawful to the believers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that a fornicator, whether male or female, should only marry another fornicator or a polytheist, and not a believer. This restriction is to protect the moral fabric of the Muslim community and prevent the spread of immorality. The verse highlights the importance of upholding moral standards and safeguarding the sanctity of marriage within the Islamic faith.
orig: الزاني لا ينكح إلا زانية أو مشركة والزانية لا ينكحها إلا زان أو مشرك وحرم ذلك على المؤمنين

translation: And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses - lash them with eighty lashes and do not accept from them testimony ever after. And those are the defisinners.
interpretation: This verse addresses the punishment for those who falsely accuse chaste women of adultery. The punishment is eighty lashes, and their testimony is to be rejected forever thereafter. This serves as a deterrent against making unsubstantiated accusations, which can severely damage a person's reputation and standing in the community. The verse emphasizes the importance of providing solid evidence before making such serious charges, and the need to protect the honor and dignity of innocent individuals.
orig: والذين يرمون المحصنات ثم لم يأتوا بأربعة شهداء فاجلدوهم ثمانين جلدة ولا تقبلوا لهم شهادة أبدا وأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: Except for those who repent after that and reform, for indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who have committed sins or wrongdoings can be forgiven by Allah if they sincerely repent and make amends. The verse emphasizes Allah's compassion and willingness to forgive those who turn back to Him and strive to improve their conduct. It encourages people to seek forgiveness and make positive changes in their lives, as Allah is "Forgiving and Merciful" towards those who do so.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من بعد ذلك وأصلحوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And those who accuse their wives [of adultery] and have no witnesses except themselves - then the testimony of one of them [shall be] four testimonies [by swearing] before Allah that indeed, he is of the truthful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the process for a husband to accuse his wife of adultery when there are no other witnesses. The husband must testify four times, swearing by Allah that he is telling the truth. This serves as a form of evidence in the absence of other witnesses, and places a high burden of proof on the husband making the accusation.
orig: والذين يرمون أزواجهم ولم يكن لهم شهداء إلا أنفسهم فشهادة أحدهم أربع شهادات بالله إنه لمن الصادقين

translation: And the fifth [oath] is that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars.
interpretation: This verse refers to the process of 'Lian' in Islamic law, which is a procedure where a husband can accuse his wife of adultery and the wife can deny the accusation. The verse describes the fifth oath that the husband must take, which is that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is lying about his accusation. This serves as a strong deterrent against false accusations and emphasizes the gravity of making such claims without proof.
orig: والخامسة أن لعنت الله عليه إن كان من الكاذبين

translation: And it will prevent punishment from her if she gives four testimonies [swearing] by Allah that indeed, he is of the liars.
interpretation: This verse refers to a situation where a woman is accused of adultery but denies the accusation. It provides a way for her to avoid punishment by taking four oaths, swearing by Allah that the accuser is lying. This procedure is known as "li'an" and is a means for the woman to clear her name and avoid the punishment for adultery, which is typically severe in Islamic law. The interpretation is that the Qur'an provides a just and merciful way for the woman to defend herself against a false accusation.
orig: ويدرأ عنها العذاب أن تشهد أربع شهادات بالله إنه لمن الكاذبين

translation: And the fifth [sign] is that the wrath of Allah will be upon her if he is of the truthful.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a sign or indication that can reveal the truthfulness of a person's claim. If a person is truthful in their claim, then the wrath or punishment of Allah will befall them if they are lying. This serves as a warning that Allah will not allow falsehood to go unchecked, and that those who are truthful have nothing to fear from the consequences of their actions.
orig: والخامسة أن غضب الله عليها إن كان من الصادقين

translation: And if not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is the Accepting of repentance and the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of Allah's grace and mercy towards His servants. It suggests that without Allah's favor and compassion, we would be lost. The verse also highlights that Allah is the One who accepts repentance and is All-Wise in His judgments and decisions. This serves as a reminder for us to be grateful for Allah's blessings, seek His forgiveness, and trust in His wisdom.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته وأن الله تواب حكيم

translation: Indeed, those who came with falsehood are a group among you. Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you. For every person among them is what [punishment] he has earned from the sin, and he who took upon himself the greater portion thereof - for him is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who spread false accusations and rumors within the community. It reminds the believers that such behavior should not be seen as something harmful, but rather as an opportunity for spiritual growth and purification. Each individual involved in spreading the falsehood will be held accountable for their own actions and the resulting consequences. The one who played a leading role in this will face a severe punishment.
orig: إن الذين جاءوا بالإفك عصبة منكم لا تحسبوه شرا لكم بل هو خير لكم لكل امرئ منهم ما اكتسب من الإثم والذي تولى كبره منهم له عذاب عظيم

translation: And why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not right for us to speak of this. Exalted are You, [O Allah]; this is a great slander"?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the believers, both men and women, who heard a slanderous rumor about one of the Prophet's wives, but did not immediately reject it and instead entertained doubts about her. The verse condemns this reaction, and calls on the believers to have a better opinion of themselves and to immediately dismiss such obvious falsehoods, recognizing them as a clear slander against the Prophet's household.
orig: لولا إذ سمعتموه ظن المؤمنون والمؤمنات بأنفسهم خيرا وقالوا هذا إفك مبين

translation: And if they had not brought to him four witnesses [to the accusation], then he [i.e., the slanderer] would be the liar before Allah among them. And if it had not been for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, you would have been touched by a great punishment for that [lie] which you uttered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of providing credible evidence and witnesses when making serious accusations against others. It condemns those who make false allegations without sufficient proof, declaring them as liars in the sight of God. The verse also highlights the mercy and grace of God, which protects people from the consequences of their wrongdoings, should they repent and seek forgiveness.
orig: لولا جاءوا عليه بأربعة شهداء فإذ لم يأتوا بالشهداء فأولئك عند الله هم الكاذبون

translation: And if not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have been among the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of Allah's grace and mercy in our lives. It suggests that without Allah's favor and compassion, we would face severe punishment and consequences for our actions. The verse encourages us to be grateful for Allah's blessings and to seek His forgiveness and guidance, as we are all susceptible to making mistakes and falling into sin. Ultimately, it reminds us of our dependence on Allah and the need to submit to His will.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته في الدنيا والآخرة لمسكم في ما أفضتم فيه عذاب عظيم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when you received it with your tongues and said with your mouths that of which you had no knowledge and thought it was insignificant while it was, in the sight of Allah, tremendous.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who spread rumors and gossip without having proper knowledge or understanding of the matter. It highlights how people can carelessly say things that they have no real basis for, and how such actions are viewed as grave in the sight of Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of being careful with one's speech, verifying information, and not making light of matters that may be of great significance to Allah.
orig: إذ تلقونه بألسنتكم وتقولون بأفواهكم ما ليس لكم به علم وتحسبونه هينا وهو عند الله عظيم

translation: And why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us to speak of this. Exalted are You, [O Allah]; this is a great slander."
interpretation: This verse is addressing a situation where people heard something that they should not have spoken about. The verse emphasizes that when faced with such situations, the proper response is to refrain from discussing it and instead glorify and exalt Allah, recognizing that what was said is a great falsehood or slander. The verse teaches that we should be careful with our speech, and not engage in or spread rumors or false information, but instead turn to Allah and acknowledge His greatness.
orig: ولولا إذ سمعتموه قلتم ما يكون لنا أن نتكلم بهذا سبحانك هذا بهتان عظيم

translation: Allah instructs you concerning [the obligation of] your wives. If they should leave [i.e., separate through divorce], do not prevent them from remarrying their [former] husbands if they agree among themselves on an acceptable basis.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting the rights of women in marriage and divorce. It instructs believers to not prevent their divorced wives from remarrying their former husbands, if that is the mutual agreement between the parties. The verse highlights Allah's guidance on maintaining fairness and justice in marital relationships, even in the event of a divorce.
orig: يعظكم الله أن تعودوا لمثله أبدا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And Allah makes clear to you the verses [of revelation], and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Almighty, provides clear guidance and signs to humanity through His revealed verses in the Qur'an. It underscores that Allah is all-Knowing and Wise in His actions and teachings, which are meant to lead people towards righteousness and the attainment of His pleasure.
orig: ويبين الله لكم الآيات والله عليم حكيم

translation: Indeed, those who like that immorality should be spread [or publicized] among those who have believed will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And Allah knows and you do not know.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who take pleasure in spreading or publicizing immoral and indecent behavior among the believers. It warns that they will face a painful punishment in this life and the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes that Allah has knowledge of all things, including the hidden motives and intentions of people, which may not be apparent to others.
