orig: إن الذين يحبون أن تشيع الفاحشة في الذين آمنوا لهم عذاب أليم في الدنيا والآخرة والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of Allah's grace and mercy towards humanity. It suggests that without Allah's favor and compassion, we would be in a dire situation. The verse highlights that Allah is both Compassionate (Rauf) and Merciful (Rahim), and that His kindness is essential for our well-being and salvation. This serves as a reminder to be grateful for Allah's blessings and to seek His forgiveness and guidance.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته وأن الله رءوف رحيم

translation: O you who believe! Do not follow the footsteps of Satan. And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan - indeed, he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing. And if not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would have been pure, ever, but Allah purifies whom He wills, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against following the ways of Satan, who commands people to engage in immoral and sinful acts. It emphasizes that without Allah's grace and mercy, no one would be able to purify themselves. However, Allah chooses to purify whomever He wills, as He is All-Hearing and All-Knowing. The interpretation highlights the importance of avoiding Satan's influence and relying on Allah's guidance and forgiveness for spiritual purification.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان ومن يتبع خطوات الشيطان فإنه يأمر بالفحشاء والمنكر ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم من أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء والله سميع عليم

translation: And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear not to give [aid] to their relatives and the needy and the emigrants for the cause of Allah, and let them pardon and overlook. Would you not love for Allah to forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages those who are wealthy and have the means to help others, to not withhold their assistance from their relatives, the needy, and those who have migrated for the sake of Allah. It calls upon them to be forgiving and overlook the faults of others, as they themselves desire Allah's forgiveness and mercy. The underlying message is that true virtue lies in compassion, generosity, and a willingness to pardon, rather than in merely abstaining from wrongdoing.
orig: ولا يأتل أولو الفضل منكم والسعة أن يؤتوا أولي القربى والمساكين والمهاجرين في سبيل الله وليعفوا وليصفحوا ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, those who [falsely] accuse chaste, unaware and believing women are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns the slanderous accusation of chaste and believing women. It underscores the gravity of such false accusations, which incur a severe punishment both in this life and the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of protecting the honor and reputation of righteous women, and warns against spreading malicious rumors or unfounded allegations against them.
orig: إن الذين يرمون المحصنات الغافلات المؤمنات لعنوا في الدنيا والآخرة ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will testify against them as to what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when people's own body parts will bear witness against them for their actions in life. The tongue, hands, and feet - which were used to commit sins and transgressions - will testify to the person's misdeeds. This emphasizes the comprehensive and inescapable nature of the accountability on that Day, as no one can hide or deny their wrongdoings. It serves as a warning to humans to be mindful of their actions in this life, as they will all be held responsible for them.
orig: يوم تشهد عليهم ألسنتهم وأيديهم وأرجلهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: That Day, Allah will pay them in full their [due] recompense, and they will know that Allah is the clear Truth.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when Allah will give each person their just reward for their deeds in this life. On that Day, people will fully realize that Allah is the absolute and undeniable Truth, and that His judgement is fair and righteous. The phrase "the clear Truth" emphasizes that Allah's existence, attributes, and commands are evident and indisputable.
orig: يومئذ يوفيهم الله دينهم الحق ويعلمون أن الله هو الحق المبين

translation: Evil women are for evil men, and evil men are for evil women. And good women are for good men, and good men are for good women. Those [good people] are declared innocent of what [the slanderers] say. For them is forgiveness and noble provision.
interpretation: This verse establishes a principle of compatibility and suitability between people of good character and those of bad character. It suggests that good people should associate with other good people, and evil people with other evil people. The verse also emphasizes that those who are falsely accused or slandered will be declared innocent, and they will be granted forgiveness and a noble provision from Allah.
orig: الخبيثات للخبيثين والخبيثون للخبيثات والطيبات للطيبين والطيبون للطيبات أولئك مبرءون مما يقولون لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: O you who believe! Do not enter houses other than your own until you have asked permission and greeted their inhabitants. That is best for you, that you may be reminded.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to seek permission before entering someone else's home, and to greet the inhabitants with a polite salutation. This is considered the best and most respectful way of interacting with others, as it shows consideration for their privacy and rights. The verse also suggests that following this etiquette serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their conduct and to treat others with respect.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا على أهلها ذلكم خير لكم لعلكم تذكرون

translation: And if you find no one therein, then do not enter it until permission has been given to you. And if it is said to you, "Go back," then go back; it is purer for you. And Allah is Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to seek permission before entering a dwelling, even if it appears unoccupied. It emphasizes the importance of respecting others' privacy and not intruding without proper authorization. The verse also encourages believers to heed instructions to withdraw, as this is considered a more virtuous course of action. Ultimately, this guidance reflects Allah's omniscience and the need for believers to conduct themselves in a manner that is pleasing to Him.
orig: فإن لم تجدوا فيها أحدا فلا تدخلوها حتى يؤذن لكم وإن قيل لكم ارجعوا فارجعوا هو أزكى لكم والله بما تعملون عليم

translation: There is no blame upon you for entering houses not inhabited in which there is convenience for you. And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the etiquette and rules around entering uninhabited houses. It states that there is no blame or sin in entering such houses, as long as they contain possessions or belongings that are of use or convenience to you. The verse emphasizes that Allah is aware of both what you openly express and what you keep hidden, indicating that one should maintain honesty and integrity in their actions.
orig: ليس عليكم جناح أن تدخلوا بيوتا غير مسكونة فيها متاع لكم والله يعلم ما تبدون وما تكتمون

translation: Tell the believing men to reduce [some] of their vision and guard their private parts. That is purer for them. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their chastity. The interpretation is that it is spiritually and morally beneficial for the believers to restrain their lustful desires and focus on purity of heart and mind. This helps them maintain a closer connection with God, who is fully aware of their actions and intentions.
orig: قل للمؤمنين يغضوا من أبصارهم ويحفظوا فروجهم ذلك أزكى لهم إن الله خبير بما يصنعون

translation: And tell the believing women to reduce [some] of their vision and guard their private parts and not expose their adornment except that which [necessarily] appears thereof and to wrap [a portion of] their headcovers over their chests and not expose their adornment except to their husbands, their fathers, their husbands' fathers, their sons, their husbands' sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, their sisters' sons, their women, their slaves, or their male attendants who lack desire, or children who are not yet aware of the private aspects of women. And let them not stamp their feet to make known what they conceal of their adornment. And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, that you might succeed.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believing women to observe modesty and decency in their conduct. They are commanded to lower their gaze, guard their private parts, and not display their adornments publicly, except for what is naturally visible. They are also told to cover their chests with their headcovers and not to reveal their adornments to anyone other than their close family members or those who are not interested in them. The verse emphasizes the importance of modesty and self-control, as well as the need for all believers to turn to Allah in repentance, in order to achieve success in the Hereafter.
orig: وقل للمؤمنات يغضضن من أبصارهن ويحفظن فروجهن ولا يبدين زينتهن إلا ما ظهر منها وليضربن بخمرهن على جيوبهن ولا يبدين زينتهن إلا لبعولتهن أو آبائهن أو آباء بعولتهن أو أبنائهن أو أبناء بعولتهن أو إخوانهن أو بني إخوانهن أو بني أخواتهن أو نسائهن أو ما ملكت أيمانهن أو التابعين غير أولي الإربة من الرجال أو الطفل الذين لم يظهروا على عورات النساء ولا يضربن بأرجلهن ليعلم ما يخفين من زينتهن وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا أيه المؤمنون لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male slaves and female slaves. If they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse encourages the practice of marriage, particularly for those who are unmarried, as well as for the righteous among the male and female slaves. It suggests that even if the prospective spouses are poor, Allah will provide for them from His bounty, as He is all-Encompassing and Knowing. The verse emphasizes the importance of marriage and the responsibility of the community to support those who seek to enter into this institution, regardless of their financial status.
orig: وأنكحوا الأيامى منكم والصالحين من عبادكم وإمائكم إن يكونوا فقراء يغنهم الله من فضله والله واسع عليم

translation: And let those who do not find [the means for] marriage keep themselves chaste until Allah enriches them from His bounty. And those who seek a contract [for eventual emancipation] from among whom your right hands possess - then make a contract with them if you know there is within them goodness and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you. And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity, to seek [thereby] the temporary interests of worldly life. And if someone should compel them, then indeed, Allah is [to them], after their compulsion, Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on several matters related to marriage and the treatment of slaves. It encourages those who cannot afford marriage to remain chaste until Allah provides for them. It also instructs that slaves who seek a contract for eventual emancipation should be given that opportunity if they demonstrate goodness. Importantly, it prohibits the compulsion of slave girls into prostitution, emphasizing that Allah is forgiving and merciful towards those who are compelled into such situations against their will.
orig: وليستعفف الذين لا يجدون نكاحا حتى يغنيهم الله من فضله والذين يبتغون الكتاب مما ملكت أيمانكم فكاتبوهم إن علمتم فيهم خيرا وآتوهم من مال الله الذي آتاكم ولا تكرهوا فتياتكم على البغاء إن أردن تحصنا لتبتغوا عرض الحياة الدنيا ومن يكرههن فإن الله من بعد إكراههن غفور رحيم

translation: And We have certainly sent down to you verses [which are] clear and an example from those who passed on before you and an admonition for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has revealed clear and evident signs ("آيات مبينات") to guide humanity, as well as examples and lessons from the experiences of previous generations. These revelations and examples are meant to serve as an admonition and guidance for the righteous ("للمتقين"), who seek to live their lives in accordance with Allah's teachings.
orig: ولقد أنزلنا إليكم آيات مبينات ومثلا من الذين خلوا من قبلكم وموعظة للمتقين

translation: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a brilliant star lit from [the oil of] a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse presents a metaphor for the divine light of Allah that illuminates the heavens and the earth. The metaphor likens this divine light to a lamp within a niche, with the lamp encased in glass that shines like a brilliant star. The oil that fuels this lamp comes from a blessed olive tree, neither from the east nor the west, and its light glows even without being touched by fire. This represents the self-sustaining and all-encompassing nature of Allah's divine guidance and wisdom. The verse concludes by stating that Allah presents such examples to guide people, for He has knowledge of all things.
orig: الله نور السماوات والأرض مثل نوره كمشكاة فيها مصباح المصباح في زجاجة الزجاجة كأنها كوكب دري يوقد من شجرة مباركة زيتونة لا شرقية ولا غربية يكاد زيتها يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار نور على نور يهدي الله لنوره من يشاء ويضرب الله الأمثال للناس والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: In houses which Allah has ordered to be raised and that His name be mentioned therein; exalting Him within them in the morning and the evenings
interpretation: This verse refers to the mosques or places of worship, where Allah has commanded that they be built and maintained, and that His name be remembered and glorified within them, both in the mornings and the evenings. It emphasizes the importance of establishing and frequenting these sacred spaces as a means of connecting with the divine and fulfilling one's religious obligations.
orig: في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال

translation: Men whom neither trade nor sale beguiles from the remembrance of Allah and the keeping up of prayer and the giving of poor-rate; they fear a day in which the hearts and eyes will be overturned.
interpretation: This verse describes men who are steadfast in their devotion to Allah, despite the distractions of commerce and business. They remain focused on remembering Allah, performing their prayers, and giving charity. They are aware of the Day of Judgment, when all hearts and eyes will be shaken, and they fear that day. This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining one's spiritual devotion and commitment to Allah, even in the face of worldly temptations and obligations.
orig: رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة يخافون يوما تتقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار

translation: That Allah may recompense them for the best of what they did and increase them of His bounty. And Allah gives provision to whom He wills without account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah will reward the righteous for their good deeds and increase them in His bounty. It highlights that Allah is the Provider who gives sustenance to whomever He wills, without limit or measure. The interpretation suggests that Allah's reward and provision are not based on human calculations or expectations, but rather on His infinite wisdom and generosity.
orig: ليجزيهم الله أحسن ما عملوا ويزيدهم من فضله والله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب

translation: And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a lowland which a thirsty one supposes to be water until, when he comes to it, he finds it is nothing, but he finds Allah with him, and He will pay him in full his due. And Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse draws a powerful metaphor to illustrate the futility of the deeds of those who disbelieve in God. Their actions are likened to a mirage - an illusion of water that appears real to a thirsty traveler, but vanishes when approached. Similarly, the disbelievers' deeds may seem meaningful and rewarding in this life, but they will ultimately amount to nothing. The verse emphasizes that God is the true source of reckoning and that He will hold everyone accountable for their actions, swiftly and justly. The interpretation highlights the importance of faith and righteous deeds, as opposed to the empty pursuits of those who reject God's guidance.
orig: والذين كفروا أعمالهم كسراب بقيعة يحسبه الظمآن ماء حتى إذا جاءه لم يجده شيئا ووجد الله عنده فوفاه حسابه والله سريع الحساب

translation: Or [they are] like darknesses within an unfathomable sea which is covered by waves, upon which are waves, over which are clouds - darknesses, some of them upon others. When one puts out his hand [therein], he can hardly see it. And he to whom Allah has not granted light - for him there is no light.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of darkness within an unfathomable sea to describe the state of those who have rejected faith and guidance from Allah. The layers of darkness - waves upon waves, clouds upon clouds - represent the depth and complexity of their spiritual blindness. Just as a person in such a sea would struggle to see their own hand, those without Allah's light are unable to perceive the truth and guidance. This highlights the importance of seeking and accepting the light that Allah provides through His revelations and teachings, without which one is left in profound spiritual darkness.
orig: أو كظلمات في بحر لجي يغشاه موج من فوقه موج من فوقه سحاب ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض إذا أخرج يده لم يكد يراها ومن لم يجعل الله له نورا فما له من نور

translation: Have you not seen that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the [heavenly] bodies, the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures and many of the people? But upon many the punishment has been justified. And he whom Allah humiliates - for him there is no bestower of honor. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal and comprehensive nature of Allah's sovereignty and worship. It highlights that all of creation - from the celestial bodies in the heavens to the creatures on earth - prostrate and submit to Allah, acknowledging His divine authority and power. The verse also suggests that while many people recognize and worship Allah, there are also those who have earned Allah's punishment due to their misdeeds and rejection of faith. The key message is that Allah is the ultimate sovereign, and all beings in the universe are subservient to Him, whether willingly or not.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يسبح له من في السماوات والأرض والطير صافات كل قد علم صلاته وتسبيحه والله عليم بما يفعلون

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone is the sovereign ruler of the heavens and the earth, and that all creation and all people will ultimately return to Him for judgment and accountability. It emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over all things, and the fact that our final destination is with Him.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وإلى الله المصير

translation: Have you not seen that Allah drives clouds? Then He brings them together, then He makes them into a mass, and you see the rain emerge from within it. And He sends down from the sky, mountains [of clouds] within which is hail, and He strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills. The flash of its lightning almost takes away the eyesight.
interpretation: This verse encourages us to reflect on the wonders of Allah's creation and His power over the natural world. It describes the process of cloud formation and rainfall, highlighting how Allah controls the movement and composition of clouds, and how He directs the rain and hail to fall where He wills. The verse also mentions the intensity of lightning, which can almost blind the eyes, further emphasizing Allah's might and dominion over all things. This serves to reinforce the message that Allah is the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe, and that we should worship and submit to Him alone.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يزجي سحابا ثم يؤلف بينه ثم يجعله ركاما فترى الودق يخرج من خلاله وينزل من السماء من جبال فيها من برد فيصيب به من يشاء ويصرفه عن من يشاء يكاد سنا برقه يذهب بالأبصار

translation: Allah alternates the night and the day. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have insight.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the One who controls the alternation of night and day. This is a sign of His power and wisdom for those who reflect and seek understanding. The regular cycle of night and day is a profound reminder of Allah's sovereignty and the order He has established in the universe. Those who possess insight and discernment can derive valuable lessons from observing this natural phenomenon, leading them to recognize Allah's greatness and to submit to Him.
orig: يقلب الله الليل والنهار إن في ذلك لعبرة لأولي الأبصار

translation: And Allah has created every [living] creature from water. And of them are those that move on their bellies, and of them are those that walk on two legs, and of them are those that walk on four. Allah creates what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine power and wisdom of Allah in creating a diverse array of living creatures, each with its own unique mode of locomotion. The verse highlights that all life originates from water, which is the fundamental building block of existence. The variety in the ways these creatures move, whether on their bellies, two legs, or four, is a testament to Allah's boundless creativity and control over all things. This serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and the wonders of His creation.
orig: والله خلق كل دابة من ماء فمنهم من يمشي على بطنه ومنهم من يمشي على رجلين ومنهم من يمشي على أربع يخلق الله ما يشاء إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: We have certainly sent down verses of clear evidence, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has revealed clear and unambiguous signs and guidance in the Quran, and that He alone has the power to guide people to the right path. It suggests that one should strive to understand and follow the guidance provided in the Quran, while ultimately recognizing that it is Allah who decides whom He will guide. The interpretation encourages believers to remain humble and seek Allah's guidance, rather than relying solely on their own understanding.
orig: لقد أنزلنا آيات مبينات والله يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And they say, "We have believed in Allah and in the Messenger, and we obey"; then a faction of them turns away after that. And those are not [true] believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to believe in Allah and His Messenger, but their actions do not match their words. They profess faith, but then turn away and disobey the teachings of Islam. This verse emphasizes that true believers are those who not only verbally accept the faith, but also demonstrate their commitment through their actions and obedience to Allah and His Messenger.
orig: ويقولون آمنا بالله وبالرسول وأطعنا ثم يتولى فريق منهم من بعد ذلك وما أولئك بالمؤمنين

translation: And when they are called to [the words of] Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, at once a party of them turns away [in refusal].
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of submitting to the judgment and guidance of Allah and His Messenger. When people are called to accept the rulings of Allah and His Messenger, some of them turn away and refuse to comply. This is a sign of arrogance and a rejection of divine authority. The verse encourages believers to humbly accept the judgments of Allah and His Messenger, even if they may not align with their personal desires or preferences.
orig: وإذا دعوا إلى الله ورسوله ليحكم بينهم إذا فريق منهم معرضون

translation: And if they have the right, they will come to it in submission.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if those who are being addressed have a legitimate claim or right, they should come to it willingly and with humility, without arrogance or resistance. It emphasizes the importance of acknowledging the truth and submitting to it, even if it goes against one's own desires or preconceptions.
orig: وإن يكن لهم الحق يأتوا إليه مذعنين

translation: Is there a disease in their hearts? Or have they doubted? Or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will wrong them? Nay, it is they who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who harbor doubts and suspicions about the truth of Islam and the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The Qur'an poses three questions to them: 1) Is there a disease in their hearts that prevents them from accepting the truth? 2) Do they doubt the authenticity of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad? 3) Do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will treat them unjustly if they accept Islam? The Qur'an then rejects these notions and declares that it is they who are the true wrongdoers, as they are denying the clear signs and guidance from Allah.
orig: أفي قلوبهم مرض أم ارتابوا أم يخافون أن يحيف الله عليهم ورسوله بل أولئك هم الظالمون

translation: The only statement of the [true] believers when they are called to [the words of] Allah and His Messenger to judge between them is that they say, "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and submission to Allah and His Messenger among the believers. When the believers are called to follow the teachings of the Qur'an and the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad, they should respond with a humble and sincere attitude, saying "We hear and we obey." This demonstrates their willingness to accept the divine commandments and submit to the will of Allah. The verse then states that those who exhibit this level of obedience and faith are the ones who will achieve success and prosperity in this life and the hereafter.
orig: إنما كان قول المؤمنين إذا دعوا إلى الله ورسوله ليحكم بينهم أن يقولوا سمعنا وأطعنا وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and fears Allah and is conscious of Him - it is those who are the attainers of success.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, as well as the fear and consciousness of Allah. Those who exhibit these qualities are the ones who will be successful in this life and the Hereafter. The verse highlights that true success is achieved through submitting to the will of Allah and living a life in accordance with His teachings.
orig: ومن يطع الله ورسوله ويخش الله ويتقه فأولئك هم الفائزون

translation: And they swear by Allah their strongest oaths that if you order them, they will surely go forth. Say, "Do not swear. [Such] obedience is known. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who would swear oaths of allegiance to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), but then fail to follow through on their promises. The verse instructs the Prophet to tell them that they do not need to swear oaths, as true obedience is known by one's actions, not just words. Allah is fully aware of what they do, and will judge them accordingly. The emphasis is on the importance of sincere, consistent obedience over empty oaths.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن أمرتهم ليخرجن قل لا تقسموا طاعة معروفة إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Say, "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, but if you turn away - then upon him is only that [duty] with which he has been charged, and upon you is that with which you have been charged. And if you obey him, you will be [rightly] guided. And there is not upon the Messenger except the [responsibility for] clear notification."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obeying both Allah and His Messenger, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It states that if people turn away from this obligation, the responsibility lies with them and not the Messenger, whose duty is only to convey the message clearly. However, if they obey the Messenger, they will be guided rightly. The verse highlights that the Messenger's role is to deliver the divine message, not to compel people to believe or obey.
orig: قل أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول فإن تولوا فإنما عليه ما حمل وعليكم ما حملتم وإن تطيعوه تهتدوا وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among you that He will surely grant them succession [to authority] upon the earth just as He granted it to those before them and that He will surely establish for them [therein] their religion which He has preferred for them and that He will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security, [for] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me. But whoever disbelieves after that - then those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse promises that Allah will grant authority and security in the land to those believers who do righteous deeds. It indicates that just as Allah established the previous nations, He will establish the believers and grant them the ability to practice their religion freely without fear. This is contingent on the believers worshipping Allah alone without associating partners with Him. Those who reject faith after this are considered disobedient.
orig: وعد الله الذين آمنوا منكم وعملوا الصالحات ليستخلفنهم في الأرض كما استخلف الذين من قبلهم وليمكنن لهم دينهم الذي ارتضى لهم وليبدلنهم من بعد خوفهم أمنا يعبدونني لا يشركون بي شيئا ومن كفر بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah and obey the Messenger - that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to perform the five daily prayers, pay the obligatory charity (zakah), and obey the teachings and commands of the Prophet Muhammad. By fulfilling these religious duties, believers can hope to receive Allah's mercy and forgiveness.
orig: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأطيعوا الرسول لعلكم ترحمون

translation: Do not think that those who disbelieve will escape [unharmed] in the land, and their refuge will be the Fire, and how wretched the destination.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who disbelieve in God and reject faith will not be able to escape divine punishment. Their ultimate destination is the Fire of Hell, which is a terrible and undesirable end. The verse emphasizes that the disbelievers cannot evade the consequences of their actions and that they will face the ultimate judgment of God.
orig: لا تحسبن الذين كفروا معجزين في الأرض ومأواهم النار ولبئس المصير

translation: O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those who have not [yet] reached puberty among you ask permission of you [before entering] three times: before the dawn prayer and when you put aside your clothing [for rest] at noon and after the night prayer. [These are] three times of privacy for you. There is no blame upon you nor upon them beyond these [periods], for they continually circulate among you - some of you, among others. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses; and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse outlines the etiquette and rules of privacy within the household. It instructs the believers to seek permission from their servants and children who have not reached puberty, before entering private spaces during three specific times of the day. This is to maintain the privacy and modesty of the household members. The verse emphasizes that this rule is not a burden, but rather a way to establish clear boundaries and facilitate smooth interactions within the home. The overall message is one of respecting the privacy and dignity of all members of the household.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ليستأذنكم الذين ملكت أيمانكم والذين لم يبلغوا الحلم منكم ثلاث مرات من قبل صلاة الفجر وحين تضعون ثيابكم من الظهيرة ومن بعد صلاة العشاء ثلاث عورات لكم ليس عليكم ولا عليهم جناح بعدهن طوافون عليكم بعضكم على بعض كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات والله عليم حكيم

translation: And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission [as do] those before them. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse instructs that when children reach the age of puberty, they should seek permission before entering private spaces, just as those before them were required to do. This is a guidance from Allah to maintain privacy and respect the sanctity of the home. The verse also emphasizes that Allah makes His signs and commandments clear, and that He is All-Knowing and All-Wise in His legislation.
orig: وإذا بلغ الأطفال منكم الحلم فليستأذنوا كما استأذن الذين من قبلهم كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته والله عليم حكيم

translation: And as for women past the age of menstruation among your women, for them the 'iddah (prescribed period) is three months, and [also for] those who have not menstruated. And for those with pregnancy, their term is until they give birth. And whoever fears Allah and keeps duty to Him, He will make a way for him (from every difficulty).
interpretation: This verse addresses the waiting period (iddah) for women who are no longer of childbearing age or have not yet reached that stage. It states that for such women, the iddah is three months, and that they are allowed to remove their outer garments, as long as they do not display their adornments. The verse emphasizes that it is better for them to observe modesty, and that Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing. The interpretation highlights the compassionate guidance provided in the Quran for women in different stages of life, while promoting virtues such as modesty and fear of Allah.
orig: والقواعد من النساء اللاتي لا يرجون نكاحا فليس عليهن جناح أن يضعن ثيابهن غير متبرجات بزينة وأن يستعففن خير لهن والله سميع عليم

translation: There is no blame upon the blind or upon the lame or upon the ill or upon yourselves if you eat from your [own] houses or the houses of your fathers or the houses of your mothers or the houses of your brothers or the houses of your sisters or the houses of your father's brothers or the houses of your father's sisters or the houses of your mother's brothers or the houses of your mother's sisters or [from houses] whose keys your right hands possess, or [from the house] of your friend. There is no blame upon you for what you eat [from these houses] all together or [in] separate groups. But when you enter houses, give greetings of peace upon each other - a greeting from Allah, blessed and good. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses [of ordinance] that you may understand.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of where one can eat, and it establishes that there is no blame or sin in eating from the houses of one's close family members or those under one's care. The verse encourages a spirit of hospitality, unity and mutual support within the community. It also emphasizes the importance of greeting others with a kind and blessed greeting, as this is a sign of the divine guidance that Allah provides to help people understand and live by His ordinances.
orig: ليس على الأعمى حرج ولا على الأعرج حرج ولا على المريض حرج ولا على أنفسكم أن تأكلوا من بيوتكم أو بيوت آبائكم أو بيوت أمهاتكم أو بيوت إخوانكم أو بيوت أخواتكم أو بيوت أعمامكم أو بيوت عماتكم أو بيوت أخوالكم أو بيوت خالاتكم أو ما ملكتم مفاتحه أو صديقكم ليس عليكم جناح أن تأكلوا جميعا أو أشتاتا فإذا دخلتم بيوتا فسلموا على أنفسكم تحية من عند الله مباركة طيبة كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تعقلون

translation: The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then doubt not but strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is those who are the truthful. When the believers are called to [the words of] Allah and His Messenger in order [for him] to judge between them, their [only] statement is, "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and fears Allah and is conscious of Him - it is those who are the attainers [of success].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the key characteristics of true believers - those who have faith in Allah and His Messenger, and who are steadfast in their devotion and obedience to Allah's commands. The believers are described as those who do not doubt, but rather strive with their wealth and lives in the cause of Allah, and who respond with complete submission when called to the words of Allah and His Messenger. This verse highlights the importance of unwavering faith, obedience, and fear of Allah as the hallmarks of the successful believers.
orig: إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله وإذا كانوا معه على أمر جامع لم يذهبوا حتى يستأذنوه إن الذين يستأذنونك أولئك الذين يؤمنون بالله ورسوله فإذا استأذنوك لبعض شأنهم فأذن لمن شئت منهم واستغفر لهم الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like your calling of one another. Allah knows those of you who slip away, concealed by others. And let those who dissent from his [i.e., the Prophet's] command beware, lest fitnah strike them or a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and honoring the status of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and not treating him like an ordinary person. It warns against those who try to slip away from the Prophet's guidance and commands, and cautions that those who go against his directives may face trials and severe punishment. The verse highlights the need to submit to the Prophet's authority and teachings, as he was divinely appointed to guide humanity.
orig: لا تجعلوا دعاء الرسول بينكم كدعاء بعضكم بعضا قد يعلم الله الذين يتسللون منكم لواذا فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره أن تصيبهم فتنة أو يصيبهم عذاب أليم

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. He already knows that which you are [engaged in], and [that Day] the Day they will be returned to Him, and He will inform them of what they have done. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah. He is fully aware of our actions and thoughts, and on the Day of Judgment, He will inform us of what we have done in our lives. This serves as a reminder that we are accountable to Allah for our deeds, and that He has perfect knowledge of all things.
orig: ألا إن لله ما في السماوات والأرض قد يعلم ما أنتم عليه ويوم يرجعون إليه فينبئهم بما عملوا والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Blessed is He who has sent down the Criterion upon His Servant that he may be to the worlds a warner
interpretation: This verse praises God for revealing the Qur'an, referred to as "the Criterion" (al-Furqan), to the Prophet Muhammad as a warning and guidance for all of humanity. The verse highlights the divine origin of the Qur'an and the Prophet's role as a warner to convey God's message to the entire world. It emphasizes the Qur'an's universal significance and the Prophet's mission to guide people towards the right path.
orig: تبارك الذي نزل الفرقان على عبده ليكون للعالمين نذيرا

translation: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and who has not taken a son and has not had a partner in dominion and has created each thing and determined it with [precise] determination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and oneness of God. It states that God is the sole owner and ruler of the heavens and the earth, and that He has no offspring or partners in His dominion. This underscores the idea of God's uniqueness and absolute power, as He has created all things and determined their nature and purpose with perfect precision.
orig: الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض ولم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك وخلق كل شيء فقدره تقديرا

translation: And they have taken besides Him gods which create nothing, while they are [themselves] created, and possess not for themselves any harm or benefit and possess not [power over] death or life or resurrection.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of worshiping idols or false gods, which are incapable of creating anything and have no power to harm or benefit people. It emphasizes that only the one true God, Allah, has the power of creation, life, death, and resurrection. The verse is a call to reject polytheism and idolatry and to worship Allah alone as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe.
orig: واتخذوا من دونه آلهة لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون ولا يملكون لأنفسهم ضرا ولا نفعا ولا يملكون موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "This is not but a falsehood he has invented, and another people assisted him in it." But they have committed an injustice and a lie.
interpretation: This verse responds to the claims made by the disbelievers who rejected the message of the Quran and accused the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of fabricating it with the help of others. The interpretation is that the disbelievers have made an unjust and false accusation, as the Quran is the word of God revealed to the Prophet, not a fabrication. Their claim is a lie and an injustice towards the Prophet and the believers.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا إفك افتراه وأعانه عليه قوم آخرون فقد جاءوا ظلما وزورا

translation: And they say, "Legends of the former peoples which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and afternoon."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the claims made by the disbelievers that the Qur'an is not a divine revelation, but rather a compilation of ancient legends and stories that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) had written down and was being dictated to him. The interpretation suggests that the disbelievers dismissed the Qur'an as mere fables and stories of the past, rather than recognizing it as a revelation from God. This verse refutes their claims and affirms the divine origin of the Qur'an.
orig: وقالوا أساطير الأولين اكتتبها فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: Say, "[O Muhammad], He who revealed it is the One who knows [all] the secrets within the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He has ever been Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Quran was revealed by God, who has knowledge of all that is hidden in the heavens and the earth. It affirms that God is Forgiving and Merciful, and that the Quran is a manifestation of these divine attributes. The interpretation suggests that the Quran is a divine revelation that contains wisdom and guidance, and that God is the source of all knowledge and the ultimate arbiter of forgiveness and mercy.
orig: قل أنزله الذي يعلم السر في السماوات والأرض إنه كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And they say, "What is this messenger that eats food and walks in the markets? Why was there not sent down to him an angel so he would be with him a warner?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and disbelief of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They questioned how a messenger of God could be a human being who eats food and walks in the markets like ordinary people. They expected the messenger to be an angel, not a human, and they could not understand why God did not send down an angel to accompany the Prophet as a warner. This verse highlights the tendency of the disbelievers to judge the Prophet based on their own limited understanding and preconceptions, rather than accepting the divine wisdom behind God's choice of a human messenger.
orig: وقالوا مال هذا الرسول يأكل الطعام ويمشي في الأسواق لولا أنزل إليه ملك فيكون معه نذيرا

translation: Or [the disbeliever is told], "Throw yourself down [from the sky], or we will bring down on you the angels [in charge of punishment]," and the disbelievers were not left with any [good] option. And they said, "You are but a man possessed by a demon."
interpretation: This verse describes the stubborn rejection of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They demand that he perform miraculous feats to prove his prophethood, such as being granted a treasure or a garden. However, the verse indicates that even if such signs were shown, the disbelievers would still reject the message and accuse the Prophet of being possessed by a demon. This highlights the hardness of their hearts and their unwillingness to accept the truth, no matter what evidence is presented to them.
orig: أو يلقى إليه كنز أو تكون له جنة يأكل منها وقال الظالمون إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا

translation: Look how they coin similitudes for thee, but they have gone astray, so they cannot find a way.
interpretation: This verse encourages the reader to reflect on how people often use analogies and examples to try to explain or understand divine truths, but in doing so, they can become misguided and lose their way. The implication is that one should not blindly accept such analogies, but rather seek the true path that leads to God.
orig: انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال فضلوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلا

translation: Blessed is He who, if He wills, can make for you [something] better than that - gardens beneath which rivers flow - and can make for you palaces.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense power and generosity of God, who can bestow upon the believers blessings and rewards that surpass their wildest dreams. The mention of "gardens beneath which rivers flow" and "palaces" symbolizes the luxurious and eternal abodes that God can provide for those who believe in and worship Him. The verse emphasizes that God has the absolute authority to grant whatever He wills, and that His blessings are limitless and beyond human comprehension. It encourages the faithful to have unwavering trust and faith in God's plan, knowing that He can always provide something better than what they currently possess or imagine.
orig: تبارك الذي إن شاء جعل لك خيرا من ذلك جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ويجعل لك قصورا

translation: But they have denied the Hour, and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who reject the Day of Judgment or the coming of the Hour. It states that Allah has prepared a severe punishment, described as a "Blaze", for those who deny the reality of the Hereafter and the Final Judgment. The implication is that those who reject this fundamental belief in Islam will face severe consequences in the Afterlife.
orig: بل كذبوا بالساعة وأعتدنا لمن كذب بالساعة سعيرا

translation: When they see them from a distant place, they will hear from them (i.e., the disbelievers) [calls of] anger and rage.
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they see the believers in the Hereafter. The disbelievers will hear the intense anger and rage of the believers towards them, as the believers witness the punishment the disbelievers are receiving for their rejection of faith and evil deeds in the worldly life. This highlights the severe consequences the disbelievers will face on the Day of Judgment for their opposition to the truth.
orig: إذا رأتهم من مكان بعيد سمعوا لها تغيظا وزفيرا

translation: And when they are thrown into a narrow place in it, bound in chains, they will call out thereupon for [their] destruction.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the disbelievers in the Hereafter, where they will be confined in a narrow and constricted space, bound in chains. In this state of utter helplessness and despair, they will call out for destruction, wishing for their existence to come to an end, as they are unable to bear the torment they are experiencing.
orig: وإذا ألقوا منها مكانا ضيقا مقرنين دعوا هنالك ثبورا

translation: Do not call for one destruction today, but call for much destruction.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against complacency and the tendency to downplay the severity of one's actions. The message is that we should not underestimate the consequences of our choices and behaviors, but rather be mindful of the potential for widespread and devastating impact. The verse encourages us to take a more serious and proactive approach to addressing the challenges we face, rather than dismissing them as insignificant or manageable. The call for "much destruction" is a metaphorical way of emphasizing the need to confront our problems head-on, rather than ignoring or minimizing them.
orig: لا تدعوا اليوم ثبورا واحدا وادعوا ثبورا كثيرا

translation: Say, "Is that [i.e., the worldly life] better or the Garden of Eternity which is promised to the righteous? It will be for them a [final] destination and [a place of] residence."
interpretation: This verse contrasts the temporary pleasures of this worldly life with the eternal bliss of the Hereafter, which is promised to the righteous. The interpretation suggests that the Garden of Eternity, the abode of the pious in the Afterlife, is far superior to the fleeting joys of this world. It emphasizes that the Hereafter is the ultimate destination and permanent residence for the righteous, where they will find true fulfillment and peace.
orig: قل أذلك خير أم جنة الخلد التي وعد المتقون كانت لهم جزاء ومصيرا

translation: For them therein is whatever they wish, [while] abiding eternally. [It is] ever upon your Lord a [standing] promise, [which must be] fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the believers in Paradise will have everything they desire and wish for, and they will reside there eternally. This is a promise from Allah that must be fulfilled, as it is a binding and inescapable decree.
orig: لهم فيها ما يشاءون خالدين كان على ربك وعدا مسئولا

translation: And the Day when He will gather them and what they worshipped besides Allah. And He will say, "Did you mislead these, My servants, or did they [themselves] stray from the way?"
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when all people will be gathered before Allah and held accountable for their beliefs and actions in this life. The verse highlights the responsibility of those who were worshipped besides Allah, whether they were idols, false deities, or human beings. Allah will question them, asking if they had misled the people or if the people had strayed on their own. This emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to escape responsibility for their choices and that Allah alone is worthy of worship.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم وما يعبدون من دون الله فيقول أأنتم أضللتم عبادي هؤلاء أم هم ضلوا السبيل

translation: They will say, "Exalted are You. It was not for us to take besides You any allies. But You provided for them and their fathers until they forgot the message and became a people ruined."
interpretation: This verse highlights the realization of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, where they will acknowledge that they were misguided in taking allies besides Allah. They will recognize that it was Allah who had provided for them and their forefathers, but they forgot the message and ultimately became a ruined people. The interpretation emphasizes the futility of seeking protectors and helpers other than Allah, and the importance of remembering and upholding the divine guidance.
orig: قالوا سبحانك ما كان ينبغي لنا أن نتخذ من دونك من أولياء ولكن متعتهم وآباءهم حتى نسوا الذكر وكانوا قوما بورا

translation: They have already denied you, but what you say cannot be turned away or supported. And whoever among you does wrong - We will let him taste a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who have rejected the message of the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It conveys that their rejection will not change the truth of the message, nor will it prevent its ultimate triumph. The verse also warns that those who commit injustice and wrongdoing will be severely punished. The interpretation suggests that one should remain steadfast in their faith and righteous conduct, as the truth will prevail despite opposition and rejection.
orig: فقد كذبوكم بما تقولون فما تستطيعون صرفا ولا نصرا ومن يظلم منكم نذقه عذابا كبيرا

translation: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], any of the messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. And We have made some of you [people] as trial for others - will you have patience? And ever is your Lord Perfect in Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the previous Prophets sent by God were human beings who had the same physical needs as other people, such as eating food and walking in the markets. This serves to remind us that the Prophets were not divine beings, but rather human messengers chosen by God to guide humanity. The verse also notes that people are a trial for one another, testing their patience and faith. Ultimately, God is all-knowing and all-seeing, and will judge people accordingly.
orig: وما أرسلنا قبلك من المرسلين إلا إنهم ليأكلون الطعام ويمشون في الأسواق وجعلنا بعضكم لبعض فتنة أتصبرون وكان ربك بصيرا

translation: And those who do not expect the meeting with Us say, "Why were not angels sent down to us, or [why] do we [not] see our Lord?" They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and [become] insolent with [great] insolence.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who do not believe in the Hereafter and the meeting with Allah. They demand to see angels or Allah Himself as a condition for their belief, out of arrogance and rejection of the signs and messengers that Allah has already sent. This attitude reflects their pride and unwillingness to submit to the truth, as they have become arrogant in their own selves and have transgressed greatly.
orig: وقال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة أو نرى ربنا لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتوا كبيرا

translation: The Day they see the angels - no good tidings will there be that Day for the criminals, and [the angels] will say, "Prevent [or Forbid]"
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the criminals will see the angels but will receive no good news on that Day. Instead, the angels will forbid them from entering Paradise and will tell them that their fate is sealed.
orig: يوم يرون الملائكة لا بشرى يومئذ للمجرمين ويقولون حجرا محجورا

translation: And We will approach what they have done of deeds and make them as dust dispersed.
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, all the deeds and actions of people will be examined, and whatever was done without sincerity or for the sake of Allah will be rendered worthless, like scattered dust. It emphasizes the importance of doing good deeds with the right intention and for the sake of pleasing Allah, rather than for worldly gain or recognition.
orig: وقدمنا إلى ما عملوا من عمل فجعلناه هباء منثورا

translation: The companions of Paradise, that Day, are the best in residence and the best in resting place.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the inhabitants of Paradise on the Day of Judgment. It conveys that the believers who have been granted Paradise will be in the best of accommodations and resting places, enjoying the ultimate comfort and peace in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the superior and blissful conditions that the righteous will experience in the eternal abode of Paradise, in contrast to the torment and suffering of the disbelievers.
orig: أصحاب الجنة يومئذ خير مستقرا وأحسن مقيلا

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], the Day when the heaven will split open with [emerging] clouds, and the angels will be sent down in successive descent.
interpretation: This verse describes the events that will occur on the Day of Judgment. The splitting open of the heavens with clouds signifies the dramatic changes that will take place in the cosmic order, as the world as we know it comes to an end. The descent of the angels in successive waves represents the arrival of the divine forces to oversee the final judgment of humanity. This verse emphasizes the magnitude and solemnity of the Day of Resurrection, when all people will be held accountable for their actions in life.
orig: ويوم تشقق السماء بالغمام ونزل الملائكة تنزيلا

translation: The sovereignty that Day will be the Truth [belonging] to the Most Merciful. And it will be for the disbelievers a difficult Day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, the absolute sovereignty and authority will belong to the Most Merciful, Allah. It will be a difficult and challenging day for those who rejected faith and disbelieved in Allah, as they will be held accountable for their actions and face the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: الملك يومئذ الحق للرحمن وكان يوما على الكافرين عسيرا

translation: And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands [in regret] he will say, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way."
interpretation: This verse describes the regret that a wrongdoer will feel on the Day of Judgment. They will wish that they had followed the path of the Messenger and submitted to God, rather than choosing a path of wrongdoing and injustice. The imagery of biting on one's hands conveys the intense remorse and self-reproach the wrongdoer will experience, realizing the opportunity they had missed to follow the right way. This serves as a warning to believers to heed the guidance of the Messenger and not to stray from the straight path.
orig: ويوم يعض الظالم على يديه يقول يا ليتني اتخذت مع الرسول سبيلا

translation: Woe is me! I wish I had not taken that one as an intimate friend!
interpretation: This verse expresses regret and remorse over having taken someone as a close friend or confidant. The phrase "Woe is me!" suggests deep anguish and disappointment, indicating that the relationship has led to negative consequences. The verse implies that the person made a poor choice in selecting this individual as a close companion, and now wishes they had not done so. The interpretation suggests that one should be cautious and discerning in choosing close friends, as the wrong choice can lead to regret and suffering.
orig: يا ويلتى ليتني لم أتخذ فلانا خليلا

translation: He led me astray from the Reminder after it had come to me. And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter.
interpretation: This verse expresses the regret of a person who was misled by Satan after receiving guidance from Allah. It highlights how Satan can cause a person to stray from the path of remembrance and righteous living, even after they have been guided. The verse serves as a warning against the deceptive nature of Satan and the importance of steadfastness in faith, even in the face of temptation.
orig: لقد أضلني عن الذكر بعد إذ جاءني وكان الشيطان للإنسان خذولا

translation: And the Messenger has said, 'O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as [a thing] abandoned.'
interpretation: This verse expresses the Prophet Muhammad's lament that his people have abandoned and neglected the Qur'an, failing to heed its guidance and teachings. It highlights the importance of the Qur'an as the divine revelation sent to humanity, and the responsibility of believers to engage with it and live by its principles. The interpretation suggests that the abandonment of the Qur'an leads to a disconnect from the divine message and a loss of spiritual direction.
orig: وقال الرسول يا رب إن قومي اتخذوا هذا القرآن مهجورا

translation: And thus have We made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals, but sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper.
interpretation: This verse indicates that every prophet sent by God has faced opposition and enmity from those who are criminals and reject the truth. However, the verse also reassures the prophet that their Lord, God, is sufficient as a guide and helper, providing them with the necessary support and guidance to overcome these challenges.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا من المجرمين وكفى بربك هاديا ونصيرا

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not revealed to him all at once?" Thus [it is] to let Our hearts become firm with it. And We have spaced it distinctly.
interpretation: This verse addresses the criticism of the disbelievers who questioned why the Qur'an was not revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) all at once, rather than in stages over a period of time. The interpretation is that the gradual revelation of the Qur'an was to strengthen the heart and faith of the Prophet, and to allow for its careful and methodical recitation and contemplation. The "spacing" or "spacing it distinctly" refers to the gradual and measured way in which the Qur'an was revealed, which allowed for its teachings to be firmly established in the hearts and minds of the believers.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك ورتلناه ترتيلا

translation: And they do not come to you with any argument except that We bring you the truth and the best explanation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the opponents of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) cannot bring any argument or evidence against the truth of the Qur'an and the message of Islam. Rather, Allah (God) provides the Prophet with the truth and the best interpretation and explanation of it, refuting any false claims or objections raised against it.
orig: ولا يأتونك بمثل إلا جئناك بالحق وأحسن تفسيرا

translation: Those who will be gathered on their faces to Hell, those are the worst in position and farthest astray in [their] way.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who will be punished on the Day of Judgment for their misdeeds and rejection of faith. They will be gathered and forced to crawl on their faces into the hellfire, which is the worst and most humiliating position. This indicates that they have strayed farthest from the right path and guidance, and will face the most severe consequences for their actions.
orig: الذين يحشرون على وجوههم إلى جهنم أولئك شر مكانا وأضل سبيلا

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture and appointed with him his brother Aaron as an assistant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah (God) bestowed the Scripture (the Torah) upon Moses and appointed his brother Aaron to assist him in his mission. This highlights the importance of having support and cooperation in carrying out the divine command, as well as the honor and responsibility that comes with being chosen by Allah to receive and convey His message.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب وجعلنا معه أخاه هارون وزيرا

translation: And We said, "Go to the people who denied Our signs." So We destroyed them with [complete] destruction.
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of a people who had rejected the signs and messages of Allah. It suggests that those who deny the truth and evidence of Allah's revelations will face severe consequences, as they were utterly destroyed. The interpretation emphasizes the consequences of disbelief and the importance of accepting and following Allah's guidance.
orig: فقلنا اذهبا إلى القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فدمرناهم تدميرا

translation: And the people of Noah - when they denied the messengers, We drowned them, and We made them for the people a sign. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the messengers of God. The people of Noah were destroyed for their disbelief and denial of the divine message. Their fate was a sign for humanity, demonstrating the consequences of turning away from God’s guidance. The verse also emphasizes that the wrongdoers will face a painful punishment, underscoring the importance of heeding the call of the messengers and living righteously.
orig: وقوم نوح لما كذبوا الرسل أغرقناهم وجعلناهم للناس آية وأعتدنا للظالمين عذابا أليما

translation: And [We destroyed] 'Aad and Thamud and the companions of the Well and many generations between them.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the destruction of various ancient peoples and civilizations who rejected the message of God and His prophets. 'Aad and Thamud were two ancient Arab tribes that were destroyed for their disbelief and disobedience. The "companions of the Well" likely refers to the people of Rass, who were also destroyed for their rejection of the divine message. The verse emphasizes that many generations between these peoples were also destroyed, highlighting God's punishment of those who turn away from the truth.
orig: وعادا وثمود وأصحاب الرس وقرونا بين ذلك كثيرا

translation: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example - but the human being is ever a [greater] dispute.
interpretation: This verse highlights the abundance of examples and parables presented in the Qur'an to guide and enlighten humanity. However, it also suggests that despite these clear teachings, human beings often engage in disputes and arguments, failing to fully comprehend the wisdom and guidance provided. The verse emphasizes the need for humility, open-mindedness, and a sincere desire to understand the profound lessons within the Qur'an, rather than being consumed by fruitless debates and disagreements.
orig: وكلا ضربنا له الأمثال وكلا تبرنا تتبيرا

translation: And they had certainly come upon the city that had been rained upon with an evil rain. So have they not seen it? But they were not expecting resurrection.
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of the people of Lot, who were punished by God for their immoral and unnatural practices. The "city that had been rained upon with an evil rain" is a reference to the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, which were destroyed by a rain of fire and brimstone. The verse suggests that despite witnessing the consequences of their actions, the people of Lot did not believe in the resurrection and the ultimate judgment of God. This serves as a warning to those who reject faith and engage in sinful behavior, that they will be held accountable for their actions in the afterlife.
orig: ولقد أتوا على القرية التي أمطرت مطر السوء أفلم يكونوا يرونها بل كانوا لا يرجون نشورا

translation: And when they see you, they take you not except in ridicule, [saying], "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They did not take him seriously and mocked him, questioning whether he was truly a messenger sent by Allah. This verse demonstrates the arrogance and rejection of the truth by those who refuse to accept the message of Islam, even in the face of clear evidence and signs.
orig: وإذا رأوك إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا

translation: Indeed, he almost led us astray from our gods had we not been steadfast upon them. And they are going to know, when they see the punishment, who is farthest astray in [his] way.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against those who try to lead people away from their beliefs and faith. It emphasizes that those who remain steadfast in their beliefs will be victorious, while those who stray from the right path will face the consequences of their actions. The verse suggests that those who mock or ridicule one's faith will eventually realize their mistake when they face the punishment for their misdeeds.
orig: إن كاد ليضلنا عن آلهتنا لولا أن صبرنا عليها وسوف يعلمون حين يرون العذاب من أضل سبيلا

translation: Have you seen the one who takes as his god his own desire? Then would you be responsible for him?
interpretation: This verse encourages us to be wary of those who worship their own desires and impulses rather than following the guidance of God. It suggests that we should not take responsibility for those who have chosen to follow their own whims, as they are accountable for their own choices. The verse emphasizes the importance of submitting to the will of God rather than succumbing to our own selfish desires.
orig: أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه أفأنت تكون عليه وكيلا

translation: Or do you think that most of them hear or understand? They are not except like livestock; rather, they are [even] more astray in [their] way.
interpretation: This verse is questioning whether most people truly listen and understand the message of the Qur'an. It compares them to livestock, suggesting that they are lost and misguided, even more so than animals who follow their natural instincts. The verse emphasizes that these people do not use their faculties of reason and comprehension to understand the divine guidance, and are therefore further astray from the right path.
orig: أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون إن هم إلا كالأنعام بل هم أضل سبيلا

translation: Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shadow? And if He willed, He could have made it stationary. Then We make the sun for it an indication.
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on the signs of Allah's power and wisdom in the natural world. The extension and movement of shadows is presented as an example of Allah's control over the physical world. The verse suggests that even though Allah could have made the shadows stationary, He chose to make them dynamic, using the sun as an indicator of their changing position. This is a sign of Allah's creative power and an invitation for people to contemplate His signs in the universe.
orig: ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل ولو شاء لجعله ساكنا ثم جعلنا الشمس عليه دليلا

translation: Then We took him up to Us in a light manner.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ascension of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the heavens, known as the "Isra' and Mi'raj" (Night Journey and Ascension). The verse suggests that Allah took the Prophet in a gentle and easy manner, indicating the honor and privilege bestowed upon him. This event is seen as a miraculous journey where the Prophet was able to witness the divine realm and receive guidance and instructions from Allah.
orig: ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضا يسيرا

translation: And it is He who has made for you the night to rest therein and the day, giving sight. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has created the cycle of day and night, and the ability to sleep and rest during the night, as signs of His power and wisdom. The night provides a peaceful respite from the activities of the day, while the day allows us to see and be active. These natural phenomena are evidence of Allah's creative design and should inspire gratitude and reflection among those who listen and ponder.
orig: وهو الذي جعل لكم الليل لباسا والنوم سباتا وجعل النهار نشورا

translation: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, and We send down from the sky pure water
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and mercy. The winds that bring good news and the pure water that comes down from the sky are signs of God's providence and care for His creation. The interpretation is that God controls the natural world and sends His blessings to sustain and purify His servants.
orig: وهو الذي أرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته وأنزلنا من السماء ماء طهورا

translation: That We may give life thereby to a dead land and give drink to those We created of numerous livestock and people.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the purpose of water is to revive a dead land and provide sustenance for both animals and humans. It highlights the divine provision and sustenance that Allah has created for all of His creation, emphasizing the importance of recognizing and being grateful for these blessings.
orig: لنحيي به بلدة ميتا ونسقيه مما خلقنا أنعاما وأناسي كثيرا

translation: And We have certainly diversified [the contents of] this Qur'an for the people, but most of the people refused [anything] except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has made the Qur'an easy to understand and has presented its teachings in various ways, so that people may reflect upon it and be guided. However, the majority of people have chosen to reject the message of the Qur'an and remain in a state of disbelief and ingratitude towards Allah.
orig: ولقد صرفناه بينهم ليذكروا فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا

translation: And if We had willed, We could have sent to every city a warner.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has the power and ability to send a messenger or warner to every single community if He so desires. However, He chooses to send messengers to specific places and people according to His wisdom and plan. This highlights the fact that guidance is ultimately in the hands of Allah, and He bestows it upon whomever He pleases.
orig: ولو شئنا لبعثنا في كل قرية نذيرا

translation: So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with the Qur'an a great striving.
interpretation: This verse commands the believers not to obey or follow the disbelievers, and to engage in a vigorous and determined struggle against them using the Qur'an. The "great striving" refers to the effort and dedication required to stand firm in one's faith and convey the message of the Qur'an to those who reject it. The Qur'an is presented as the primary weapon in this spiritual battle, as it contains the truth that can guide people away from disbelief and towards faith.
orig: فلا تطع الكافرين وجاهدهم به جهادا كبيرا

translation: And it is He who has released [simultaneously] the two seas, one fresh and sweet and one salty and bitter, and He placed between them a barrier and prohibiting partition.
interpretation: This verse describes God's power and wisdom in creating the two different types of bodies of water - the fresh, sweet water of rivers and lakes, and the salty, bitter water of the oceans. He has kept them separate, with a barrier or partition between them, preventing them from mixing. This demonstrates God's control over the natural world and His ability to maintain distinct elements within His creation.
orig: وهو الذي مرج البحرين هذا عذب فرات وهذا ملح أجاج وجعل بينهما برزخا وحجرا محجورا

translation: And it is He who has created from water a human being and made him [a relative by] lineage and marriage. And ever is your Lord competent [concerning creation].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and ability to create human beings from water. It also highlights the social and familial relationships that God has established among humans, such as lineage and marriage. The verse serves to remind us of God's sovereignty and the intricate ways in which He has designed the fabric of human society.
orig: وهو الذي خلق من الماء بشرا فجعله نسبا وصهرا وكان ربك قديرا

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which neither profits them nor harms them, and the disbeliever is ever a supporter [of misguidance] against his Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of worshipping anything other than Allah. It emphasizes that the objects of worship that people take besides Allah can neither benefit them nor harm them in any way. The verse also describes the disbeliever as being a supporter of misguidance against his Lord, indicating the misguided nature of their beliefs and actions.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعهم ولا يضرهم وكان الكافر على ربه ظهيرا

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a giver of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad was sent by God as a messenger to deliver the good news of guidance and salvation to those who believe, as well as to warn those who reject the message. His role was to convey the divine revelation and call people to worship God alone, not to compel them to accept the faith. The verse highlights the merciful and compassionate nature of the Prophet's mission, which was to guide humanity towards the path of righteousness and eternal bliss.
orig: وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا

translation: Say, "I do not ask you for this message any payment [but] only good will through kinship."
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to tell the people that he does not seek any material reward or payment for conveying the message of Islam. Rather, he only desires that people accept the faith out of their own free will and with the intention of seeking closeness to God. The verse emphasizes that the true reward for the Prophet is the people's willingness to follow the path that leads to God.
orig: قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر إلا من شاء أن يتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا

translation: And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and exalt [Him] with His praise. And sufficient is He to be, with the sins of His servants, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to put their trust in Allah, the Ever-Living who never dies. It instructs the believer to glorify and praise Allah, for He is fully aware of the sins and shortcomings of His servants. The interpretation is that the believer should have unwavering faith in Allah, seek His pleasure, and rely on Him alone, as He is the only One who can truly help and guide them.
orig: وتوكل على الحي الذي لا يموت وسبح بحمده وكفى به بذنوب عباده خبيرا

translation: It is He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days and then established Himself above the Throne - the Most Merciful, so ask about Him one well-informed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and majesty of God, the Creator of the heavens, the earth, and all that is between them. It affirms that God created the entire universe in six days and then established Himself on the Throne, which is a symbol of His sovereignty and authority. The verse also refers to God as the Most Merciful, encouraging the believers to seek knowledge and understanding about Him from those who are well-informed, such as the prophets and scholars. The overall message is a call to recognize and worship the one true God, the Creator of all things.
orig: الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش الرحمن فاسأل به خبيرا

translation: And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Should we prostrate to whatever you order us?" And it has [only] increased them in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn rejection of some people to submit to the commands of Allah, the Most Merciful. When they are called to prostrate and worship the One True God, they question the very concept of the Merciful, showing their lack of understanding and faith. This attitude only increases their distance from the truth and their aversion to the guidance of Allah.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اسجدوا للرحمن قالوا وما الرحمن أنسجد لما تأمرنا وزادهم نفورا

translation: Blessed is He who has placed in the sky great stars and has placed therein a [burning] lamp and a luminous moon.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and glory of God, the Creator of the universe.
