The "great stars" or "constellations" in the sky are a testament to God's majesty and the wonders of His creation. The "burning lamp" refers to the sun, which provides light and warmth to the earth, while the "luminous moon" is a source of reflected light that illuminates the night sky. This verse invites us to reflect on the beauty and order of the cosmos, which are signs of God's infinite wisdom and power.
orig: تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجا وجعل فيها سراجا وقمرا منيرا

translation: And it is He who has made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has created the alternation of night and day as a sign of His power and wisdom, and as an opportunity for humans to reflect, remember, and be grateful to Him. The night and day are a "khilfah" - a succession or alternation - which allows people to choose to remember Allah and be thankful to Him. This highlights that the cycle of night and day is not merely a natural phenomenon, but a deliberate creation by Allah to facilitate human spiritual growth and connection with the divine.
orig: وهو الذي جعل الليل والنهار خلفة لمن أراد أن يذكر أو أراد شكورا

translation: And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them [harshly], they say [words of] peace
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of the servants of the Most Merciful (God). They are humble in their conduct, walking on the earth with a sense of dignity and restraint. When they are confronted by the ignorant, who may speak to them harshly or insultingly, they respond with words of peace and composure, avoiding conflict and maintaining their composure. This verse teaches the importance of humility, patience, and grace in the face of adversity or provocation.
orig: وعباد الرحمن الذين يمشون على الأرض هونا وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما

translation: And those who spend [part of] the night to their Lord prostrating and standing [in prayer]
interpretation: This verse describes the righteous believers who dedicate a portion of their night to worshipping Allah through prostration and standing in prayer. It highlights the importance of devotion, humility and perseverance in one's spiritual life.
orig: والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما

translation: And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell, indeed, its punishment is ever adhering,"
interpretation: This verse refers to those who recognize the severity and permanence of the punishment of Hell, and humbly ask Allah to save them from it. The interpretation is that these people have a deep understanding of the gravity of the Hellfire and its unrelenting torment, and they sincerely seek Allah's forgiveness and protection from it.
orig: والذين يقولون ربنا اصرف عنا عذاب جهنم إن عذابها كان غراما

translation: Indeed, it (Hell) is an evil place of settlement and residence.
interpretation: This verse is referring to Hell as an evil and unpleasant place of dwelling for those who have rejected faith and done evil deeds. It emphasizes that Hell is a terrible abode and resting place for the wicked, in contrast to the blissful abode of Paradise for the righteous.
orig: إنها ساءت مستقرا ومقاما

translation: And [they are] those who, when they spend, do so not excessively or sparingly but are ever between that [extreme].
interpretation: This verse encourages a balanced approach to spending and financial management. It teaches that one should not be extravagant or miserly, but rather maintain a moderate and reasonable stance. The ideal is to spend in a measured way, without going to extremes of excess or stinginess. This promotes financial responsibility and prudence, which are virtues in Islam.
orig: والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا وكان بين ذلك قواما

translation: And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden [to be killed], except by [legal] right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever should do that will meet a penalty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping only Allah, respecting the sanctity of life, and abstaining from adultery or fornication. It highlights that those who follow these principles will be rewarded, while those who violate them will face consequences for their actions. The verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and moral conduct.
orig: والذين لا يدعون مع الله إلها آخر ولا يقتلون النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ولا يزنون ومن يفعل ذلك يلق أثاما

translation: He will have the punishment doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide in it humiliated.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who reject faith and commit grave sins. The punishment for such individuals will be doubled on the Day of Judgment, and they will remain in that state of humiliation and disgrace forever. The message is a stern warning to those who choose to turn away from the guidance of Allah and engage in wrongdoing, as they will face severe consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: يضاعف له العذاب يوم القيامة ويخلد فيه مهانا

translation: Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work - for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of repentance, faith, and righteous deeds. It promises that those who turn away from their past misdeeds, believe in Allah, and perform good works will have their sins forgiven and replaced with good deeds. This highlights Allah's boundless mercy and willingness to pardon those who sincerely seek His forgiveness and strive to live righteously.
orig: إلا من تاب وآمن وعمل عملا صالحا فأولئك يبدل الله سيئاتهم حسنات وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And whoever repents and does righteous good deeds, then indeed, he turns to Allah with true repentance.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to repent from their sins and do good deeds. It promises that those who truly repent and turn back to Allah with sincere remorse, and then strive to do good works, will be forgiven and accepted by Allah. The verse emphasizes that repentance is not just a one-time act, but a continuous process of turning back to Allah and improving one’s conduct.
orig: ومن تاب وعمل صالحا فإنه يتوب إلى الله متابا

translation: And those who do not testify to falsehood, and when they pass by ill speech, they pass by with dignity
interpretation: This verse describes the qualities of righteous believers. They do not participate in or bear witness to falsehood or deception. When they encounter vain or frivolous speech, they pass by with dignity and composure, refusing to engage in or validate such behavior. This demonstrates their commitment to truthfulness, integrity, and moral uprightness.
orig: والذين لا يشهدون الزور وإذا مروا باللغو مروا كراما

translation: And those who, when reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind
interpretation: This verse describes the believers who, when reminded of the verses (signs, teachings) of Allah, do not turn away from them in a state of deafness and blindness. Instead, they listen attentively, reflect upon the verses, and strive to understand and apply them in their lives. They are receptive to the guidance of Allah and seek to increase their faith and knowledge through the Qur"anic revelations.
orig: والذين إذا ذكروا بآيات ربهم لم يخروا عليها صما وعميانا

translation: And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us a leader for the righteous."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to pray to Allah for their spouses and children to be a source of joy and comfort, and for them to be righteous leaders who guide others towards piety and God-consciousness. It emphasizes the importance of having a pious family and being a positive role model for others in the community.
orig: والذين يقولون ربنا هب لنا من أزواجنا وذرياتنا قرة أعين واجعلنا للمتقين إماما

translation: Those will be given their reward for what they patiently endured, and they will be received therein with greetings and [words of] peace.
interpretation: This verse refers to the reward that will be given to those who persevered and remained steadfast in their faith. They will be welcomed into Paradise with greetings and peace, a testament to the blessings they have earned through their patient endurance. The verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and perseverance in the face of life's trials, as those who maintain their faith will be rewarded with the ultimate reward of eternal peace and contentment in the Hereafter.
orig: أولئك يجزون الغرفة بما صبروا ويلقون فيها تحية وسلاما

translation: Abiding therein. Excellent it is as a resting place and as a [goodly] abode.
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal abode in Paradise for the righteous believers. They will dwell in this blissful place permanently, finding it to be an excellent resting place and a wonderful abode. The verse conveys the idea of the eternal peace, comfort, and joy that the believers will experience in the Hereafter.
orig: خالدين فيها حسنت مستقرا ومقاما

translation: Say, "What would my Lord care for you if not for your [voluntary] supplication? But you [disbelievers] have already denied [the truth], so soon punishment will be [yours]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of supplication and seeking guidance from Allah. It suggests that the disbelievers will face punishment for their rejection of the truth, as Allah does not need their worship or acknowledgment. The verse encourages believers to maintain their devotion to Allah through sincere prayer and supplication, as this is what truly matters to the Lord.
orig: قل ما يعبأ بكم ربي لولا دعاؤكم فقد كذبتم فسوف يكون لزاما

translation: Taa, Seen, Meem.
interpretation: These are letters from the Arabic alphabet, known as "Huroof Muqatta'at" (Disjointed Letters). Their exact meaning and significance is not fully known, but they are believed to be a way for God to emphasize the miraculous nature of the Quran and to draw the reader's attention to the deeper meanings and messages within the text.
orig: طسم

translation: These are the verses of the clear Book
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Qur'an, which is described as the "clear Book". The Qur'an is a divine revelation that contains clear and unambiguous guidance for humanity. It is a book that provides clarity on matters of faith, ethics, and the purpose of life. The verses of the Qur'an are considered to be the "signs" or "evidence" of the divine origin of this scripture, as they demonstrate the wisdom, eloquence, and depth of the message it conveys.
orig: تلك آيات الكتاب المبين

translation: Perhaps, [O Muhammad], you would kill yourself with grief over them [i.e., the people] if they do not believe in this message [i.e., the Qur'an].
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to grieve excessively over those who reject the message of Islam. It suggests that he should not be overly concerned with whether people believe or not, as that is ultimately in the hands of Allah. The interpretation is that the Prophet should focus on conveying the message clearly, and leave the outcome to Allah, without causing himself undue distress over the choices of others.
orig: لعلك باخع نفسك ألا يكونوا مؤمنين

translation: If We willed, We could send down to them from the sky a sign, and their necks would remain humbled before it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if Allah willed, He could send down a clear and undeniable sign from the heavens that would compel people to submit and humble themselves before it. However, Allah chooses not to do so, as faith requires the exercise of free will and cannot be coerced. The verse emphasizes that Allah has the power to overwhelm people with evidence, but prefers to allow them the freedom to believe or disbelieve.
orig: إن نشأ ننزل عليهم من السماء آية فظلت أعناقهم لها خاضعين

translation: And there does not come to them any new reminder from the Most Merciful except that they turn away from it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people are constantly being reminded of Allah's signs and messages, but they choose to turn away and ignore them. They are indifferent and apathetic towards the guidance and reminders that come to them from the Most Merciful, Allah. This indicates a lack of willingness to accept and act upon the divine guidance, which is a common human tendency.
orig: وما يأتيهم من ذكر من الرحمن محدث إلا كانوا عنه معرضين

translation: So they have denied the truth, and the news of what they used to ridicule will soon reach them.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of the Quran and mock it. It suggests that the consequences of their disbelief and ridicule will soon become apparent to them, and they will be held accountable for their actions. The interpretation is that those who deny the truth will eventually face the consequences of their rejection, and the news of what they mocked will become a reality that they cannot escape.
orig: فقد كذبوا فسيأتيهم أنباء ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Have they not observed the earth - how much of every good [and useful] kind We have produced therein?
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the wonders of creation and the blessings that God has provided on earth. The diversity and abundance of life on earth, with its many species of plants and animals, is a sign of God's power, wisdom and generosity. This should inspire gratitude and faith in the Creator.
orig: أولم يروا إلى الأرض كم أنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them are not believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights that despite the clear signs and evidence of God's existence and the truth of Islam, most people still choose not to believe. It is a reminder that faith is a choice, and that even with clear guidance, many will still reject it out of arrogance, stubbornness or misguided beliefs. The verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith, as they are on the right path, even if the majority do not follow it.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the attributes of Allah as being All-Powerful ("the Exalted in Might") and All-Compassionate ("the Merciful"). It reminds us that despite His absolute power and authority, Allah is also infinitely kind and caring towards His creation. This speaks to the dual nature of Allah - He is both the Almighty Sovereign and the Loving Sustainer. The interpretation encourages believers to have faith in Allah's ability to protect and provide for them, while also finding solace in His mercy and compassion.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord called to Moses, [saying], "Go to the wrongdoing people"
interpretation: This verse refers to the time when Allah called upon the Prophet Moses to go to the Pharaoh and his people, who were oppressing and wronging the Israelites. It is a command from Allah to Moses to confront the tyrannical ruler and his people, and to call them to the path of righteousness and justice. This verse highlights the divine mandate given to the Prophets to stand up against oppression and to guide the people towards the truth.
orig: وإذ نادى ربك موسى أن ائت القوم الظالمين

translation: The people of Pharaoh. Do they not fear [Allah]?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the people of Pharaoh for their lack of fear and reverence for Allah. It suggests that despite the signs and warnings they have witnessed, they have not developed the God-consciousness (taqwa) that should lead them to submit to the One true God. The implication is that their arrogance and defiance of Allah will ultimately lead to their downfall, just as it did for Pharaoh himself.
orig: قوم فرعون ألا يتقون

translation: He said, 'My Lord, indeed I fear that they will deny me'
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Prophet Musa (Moses) in the Quran. It refers to the moment when Musa was sent by God to Pharaoh to invite him to believe in the One God and free the Israelites from slavery. Musa expressed his fear that Pharaoh and his people would not believe him and would instead reject his message. This highlights the challenges faced by prophets in conveying the divine message, as they often encounter resistance and denial from those in power. The verse teaches us that even the greatest messengers of God can experience apprehension, but that they must still have faith and trust in God's plan.
orig: قال رب إني أخاف أن يكذبون

translation: And my chest tightens, and my tongue is not loosened, so send [a message] to Aaron.
interpretation: This verse expresses the difficulty that the Prophet Moses experienced in speaking and conveying his message. He felt a tightness in his chest and a lack of fluency in his speech, so he requested that his brother Aaron be sent to assist him in delivering the message to Pharaoh. This reflects the human limitations that even the prophets faced, and the need for divine assistance in fulfilling their missions.
orig: ويضيق صدري ولا ينطلق لساني فأرسل إلى هارون

translation: And they have a sin upon them, so I fear that they will kill [me].
interpretation: This verse expresses the fear and concern of the speaker, who is aware that the people they are addressing have committed a sin or wrongdoing. The speaker is worried that this sin may lead the people to kill them, either out of retaliation, punishment, or some other reason. The verse conveys a sense of vulnerability and apprehension on the part of the speaker, who feels threatened by the potential consequences of the sin committed by the others.
orig: ولهم علي ذنب فأخاف أن يقتلون

translation: He said, "No! Go both of you with Our signs. Indeed, We are with you, listening."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Moses and his brother Aaron being sent by Allah to Pharaoh. When Pharaoh demanded a miracle, Allah commanded Moses and Aaron to go to him with the signs and miracles that Allah had granted them. The verse emphasizes that Allah is with them, listening and supporting them, and that they should not be afraid to convey the message to Pharaoh.
orig: قال كلا فاذهبا بآياتنا إنا معكم مستمعون

translation: So go to Pharaoh and say, "Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse is instructing the Prophets Moses and Aaron to go to Pharaoh and convey to him that they are messengers sent by the Lord of all the worlds. It emphasizes the divine authority and universal nature of their mission, as they are not just representatives of a local deity, but of the One True God who is the Sustainer of all creation. The verse sets the stage for the confrontation between the Prophets and the tyrant Pharaoh, where the former will call the latter to submit to the will of God and free the Israelites from oppression.
orig: فأتيا فرعون فقولا إنا رسول رب العالمين

translation: Send with us the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, where Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) is requesting the Pharaoh to let the Children of Israel go with him. The interpretation is that Moses is seeking permission from the Pharaoh to take the Israelites out of Egypt, as they were being oppressed and enslaved by the Egyptians. This verse represents the beginning of the journey of the Israelites towards the Promised Land, under the guidance of Prophet Moses.
orig: أن أرسل معنا بني إسرائيل

translation: He (Pharaoh) said, "Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for (many) years of your life?"
interpretation: This verse is part of the dialogue between Pharaoh and Prophet Moses (peace be upon him). Pharaoh is reminding Moses that he had been raised in Pharaoh's household as a child, and had lived among them for many years. This was Pharaoh's way of asserting his authority and questioning Moses' audacity to challenge him, despite the fact that he had been nurtured in Pharaoh's own home. The verse highlights the ingratitude and arrogance of Pharaoh, who failed to recognize the true status of Moses as a prophet of God.
orig: قال ألم نربك فينا وليدا ولبثت فينا من عمرك سنين

translation: And you did the deed which you did, and you are of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a past action or deed that the addressee had committed, which is described as the act of a disbeliever. The interpretation suggests that the addressee had engaged in an act of disbelief or rejection of faith, which is being condemned in this verse.
orig: وفعلت فعلتك التي فعلت وأنت من الكافرين

translation: He said, "I did it while I was of those astray."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Ash-Shu'ara (The Poets), verse 20. It is part of the story of Prophet Musa (Moses) and the Pharaoh. The Pharaoh had accused Musa of killing one of his people, and Musa admitted that he had done it while he was "of those astray" - meaning he had made a mistake and acted without proper guidance. This verse highlights the importance of acknowledging one's mistakes and seeking forgiveness, rather than trying to justify or cover up wrongdoing.
orig: قال فعلتها إذا وأنا من الضالين

translation: So I fled from you when I feared you. Then my Lord granted me wisdom and prophethood.
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, and it is spoken by the Prophet Moses (peace be upon him). It describes a time when he fled from the Pharaoh and his people out of fear, and then Allah (God) granted him wisdom and made him one of the Messengers. The interpretation is that even the greatest of Prophets can sometimes feel afraid, but Allah supports and empowers them to fulfill their mission. This verse teaches us to trust in Allah's plan, even when we face difficulties or fear.
orig: ففررت منكم لما خفتكم فوهب لي ربي حكما وجعلني من المرسلين

translation: And that is a favor which you bestow upon me that you have enslaved the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse expresses gratitude for the favor of having been given authority over the Children of Israel. The speaker acknowledges that this position of power and dominance over another people is a blessing bestowed upon them. The interpretation suggests a sense of entitlement and lack of empathy towards the subjugated people.
orig: وتلك نعمة تمنها علي أن عبدت بني إسرائيل

translation: Pharaoh said, "And what is the Lord of the worlds?"
interpretation: This verse depicts Pharaoh's arrogance and rejection of the concept of a supreme divine authority. Pharaoh, in his hubris, questions the very existence of a Creator and Sustainer of the entire universe, challenging the notion of a higher power that holds dominion over all creation. This verse highlights the dangers of ego, pride, and a refusal to acknowledge a power greater than oneself, which can lead to a dangerous denial of the divine and a rejection of faith.
orig: قال فرعون وما رب العالمين

translation: He said, 'My Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you should be convinced.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and authority of God over the entire universe, including the heavens, the earth, and everything in between. It is a call to the believers to have firm conviction and certainty in the Oneness of God, as the Creator and Sustainer of all creation. The verse encourages the people to have unwavering faith in God's power and control over the cosmos, which should lead them to submit to Him and live according to His guidance.
orig: قال رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إن كنتم موقنين

translation: He said to those around him, "Will you not listen?"
interpretation: This verse refers to a prophet or messenger of God who is trying to convey a message to his people. He is expressing his frustration that they are not listening or paying attention to what he is saying. It suggests the importance of being receptive and open-minded to the guidance and teachings being presented, rather than being dismissive or indifferent.
orig: قال لمن حوله ألا تستمعون

translation: Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old has said
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the message of Islam is not a new religion, but rather a continuation of the teachings of the previous prophets and messengers of God. It establishes the unity of God and the continuity of His guidance to humanity throughout history. The verse reminds the people that the same Lord who guided their ancestors is now speaking to them through the Qur'an, calling them to worship Him alone and follow His commandments.
orig: قال ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين

translation: He (the disbeliever) said: "Verily, your Messenger who has been sent to you is a madman."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who rejected the message of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and accused him of being a madman. The interpretation is that the disbelievers refused to accept the Prophet's message and divine revelation, and instead resorted to ridiculing and insulting him. This verse highlights the arrogance and closed-mindedness of those who reject the truth and choose to remain in their state of disbelief.
orig: قال إن رسولكم الذي أرسل إليكم لمجنون

translation: He said, "The Lord of the east and the west and whatever is between them, if you were to use reason."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) in the Qur'an. It emphasizes that the one true God is the Lord of the entire universe, from the east to the west, and everything in between. The verse encourages people to use their reason and intellect to recognize and worship this one God, rather than associating partners with Him. The implication is that if people were to ponder and reflect upon the wonders of the creation, they would come to the conclusion that there is only one Creator worthy of worship.
orig: قال رب المشرق والمغرب وما بينهما إن كنتم تعقلون

translation: He said, "If you take a god other than Me, I will surely place you among the imprisoned."
interpretation: This verse is a warning from God to those who would worship false gods or deities other than Him. The implication is that to worship anything other than the one true God is to imprison oneself, to be confined by the limitations of false beliefs and idolatry. The verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and supremacy of God, and the importance of devoting oneself entirely to the worship of the divine.
orig: قال لئن اتخذت إلها غيري لأجعلنك من المسجونين

translation: They said, "Have you come to us with something clear?"
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between Prophet Moses and the Pharaoh and his people. The Pharaoh and his people are challenging Moses, asking if he has come to them with a clear proof or evidence to support his claim of being a messenger of God. The verse highlights the skepticism and resistance that the Pharaoh and his people had towards Moses' message, and their demand for clear and tangible proof to validate his prophethood.
orig: قال أولو جئتك بشيء مبين

translation: He said, "Then bring it if you are of the truthful."
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Prophet Musa (Moses) and Pharaoh. Pharaoh challenged Musa to bring a clear sign of his prophethood, and Musa responded by throwing down his staff, which then turned into a snake. The interpretation is that when one makes a claim, they should be prepared to provide evidence to support it. This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and truthfulness, as Pharaoh demands that Musa back up his claim of being a prophet with a clear demonstration.
orig: قال فأت به إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: And [Musa] threw his staff, and suddenly it was a serpent, manifest.
interpretation: This verse describes a miracle performed by the prophet Musa (Moses), where he threw down his staff and it transformed into a clear, visible serpent. This was one of the signs Musa was given to demonstrate his prophethood to Pharaoh and the people of Egypt. The transformation of the staff into a serpent was a powerful display of Musa's connection to the divine and his ability to perform miracles, which would later help convince Pharaoh to let the Israelites leave Egypt.
orig: فألقى عصاه فإذا هي ثعبان مبين

translation: And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white [with radiance] for the observers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the miracle of Prophet Moses, where he drew out his hand from his garment and it shone with a bright, radiant whiteness. This was a sign of God's power and a proof of Moses' prophethood to the Pharaoh and his people. The whiteness of the hand symbolizes the purity, truth, and divine light that accompanies the message of God's prophets.
orig: ونزع يده فإذا هي بيضاء للناظرين

translation: He said to the assembly around him: "This is a learned magician."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Pharaoh's reaction to Moses and his miracles. The Pharaoh, in the presence of his advisors, dismisses Moses as a "learned magician" rather than acknowledging the divine nature of the miracles he has witnessed. This represents the Pharaoh's arrogance and unwillingness to submit to the truth of God's message, even in the face of clear signs and wonders.
orig: قال للملإ حوله إن هذا لساحر عليم

translation: He wants to drive you out of your land by his magic, so what do you advise?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the attempts of the Pharaoh to expel the Israelites from their land through the use of his sorcery and magic. The question posed is directed at the Israelites, asking them what they would advise in response to the Pharaoh's schemes. The interpretation is that the verse is highlighting the need for the believers to seek guidance and counsel from one another when faced with adversity, rather than succumbing to the manipulations of the oppressors.
orig: يريد أن يخرجكم من أرضكم بسحره فماذا تأمرون

translation: They said, "Keep him and his brother in suspense and send among the cities recruiters",
interpretation: This verse refers to the response of Pharaoh and his people when Prophet Moses demanded that they let the Children of Israel go. They decided to keep Moses and his brother Aaron in suspense and send messengers to the cities to gather more people against them. The interpretation suggests that the opponents of the truth often resort to delaying tactics and mobilizing support against the righteous, rather than heeding the call of God.
orig: قالوا أرجه وأخاه وابعث في المدائن حاشرين

translation: They come to you with [arguments from] every kind of sorcerer, [claiming] knowledgeable.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who would come to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) with various arguments and claims, presented by those they considered to be knowledgeable and skilled in sorcery, in an attempt to discredit the Prophet and the message of Islam. The verse suggests that these disbelievers were relying on the perceived expertise of these "knowledgeable sorcerers" to try to undermine the Prophet's message, but their efforts would ultimately be futile.
orig: يأتوك بكل سحار عليم

translation: So the magicians were assembled for a fixed appointment on a well-known day.
interpretation: This verse refers to the confrontation between Prophet Moses and the Egyptian sorcerers summoned by Pharaoh. The sorcerers were gathered at a predetermined time and place to demonstrate their magical abilities and challenge the message of Prophet Moses. This event symbolizes the clash between the truth of God's message and the falsehood of sorcery, which ultimately led to the sorcerers' acknowledgment of the superiority of Moses' miracle and their conversion to the true faith.
orig: فجمع السحرة لميقات يوم معلوم

translation: And it will be said to the people, "Are you assembled?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity will be gathered before Allah for the final reckoning. The question "Are you assembled?" is a rhetorical one, emphasizing the inevitability of this momentous event and the need for people to be prepared for it by living righteous lives in this world.
orig: وقيل للناس هل أنتم مجتمعون

translation: Perhaps we may follow the sorcerers if they are the predominant ones.
interpretation: This verse suggests a sense of uncertainty and a willingness to follow the sorcerers if they prove to be more powerful or successful. It reflects a desire to align with the perceived winners, even if their methods are questionable. The verse highlights the human tendency to be influenced by power and success, rather than by moral or ethical considerations.
orig: لعلنا نتبع السحرة إن كانوا هم الغالبين

translation: And when the magicians came, they said to Pharaoh, "Is there indeed for us a reward if we are the predominant?"
interpretation: This verse describes the interaction between Pharaoh and the magicians he had summoned to compete with Moses. The magicians, confident in their abilities, asked Pharaoh if they would be rewarded if they were victorious over Moses. This shows their arrogance and desire for worldly gains, rather than a sincere concern for the truth. The verse highlights the importance of humility and seeking the pleasure of God, rather than seeking personal glory or material rewards.
orig: فلما جاء السحرة قالوا لفرعون أئن لنا لأجرا إن كنا نحن الغالبين

translation: He (Allah) said: "Yes, and you shall be among those brought near (to Me)".
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between Allah and the angels, where Allah informs the angels that a human being (Adam) will be created and placed on Earth. The angels express their concern about the potential for corruption and bloodshed on Earth, and Allah reassures them that the human being (Adam) and his descendants who believe in Allah and obey Him will be among the ones who are brought close to Allah, honored, and granted a high status in the Hereafter.
orig: قال نعم وإنكم إذا لمن المقربين

translation: Moses said to them, "Throw what you are about to throw."
interpretation: This verse refers to the confrontation between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh. When the magicians challenged Moses to a display of power, Moses instructed them to go ahead and throw down what they were about to throw, which were their magical staffs. This was a test of power, where Moses demonstrated that his staff, transformed into a serpent, could swallow the staffs of the magicians, thus proving the superiority of the power granted to him by God over the magic of Pharaoh's sorcerers.
orig: قال لهم موسى ألقوا ما أنتم ملقون

translation: And they cast down their ropes and their staffs and said, 'By the might of Pharaoh, indeed it is we who are the superior.'
interpretation: This verse describes the confrontation between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh. The magicians cast down their ropes and staffs, boasting that they would defeat Moses through the power and might of Pharaoh. However, this verse foreshadows their eventual defeat, as the power of Pharaoh and his magicians is no match for the true power of God, which Moses represents.
orig: فألقوا حبالهم وعصيهم وقالوا بعزة فرعون إنا لنحن الغالبون

translation: And Moses threw his staff, and behold, it swallowed up what they were falsifying.
interpretation: This verse describes a miraculous event where Moses (peace be upon him) demonstrated the power of God by throwing down his staff, which then swallowed up the illusions and deceptions created by the magicians of Pharaoh. This event was a clear sign of God's authority and the truth of Moses' message, which exposed the falsehood of the magicians' practices. The verse emphasizes that God's power is supreme and can overcome any human attempts to deceive or mislead.
orig: فألقى موسى عصاه فإذا هي تلقف ما يأفكون

translation: So the magicians fell down in prostration.
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the magicians who were summoned by Pharaoh to compete against the miracles of Prophet Moses. When they witnessed the clear sign of God's power in the form of Moses' staff turning into a snake, they immediately recognized the truth and fell down in prostration, acknowledging the superiority of God's power over their own magical abilities.
orig: فألقي السحرة ساجدين

translation: They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse refers to the response of the people when they were invited to believe in the one true God, the Lord of all creation. By declaring their faith in the Lord of the worlds, they affirmed their belief in the oneness and sovereignty of Allah, rejecting any form of polytheism or idolatry. This statement of faith is a fundamental aspect of Islamic belief, emphasizing the importance of acknowledging and submitting to the one and only God.
orig: قالوا آمنا برب العالمين

translation: The Lord of Moses and Aaron
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah, the one true God, as the Lord and Protector of the prophets Moses and Aaron. It emphasizes that Allah is the supreme authority and the source of guidance for these two important figures in Islamic history. This verse underscores the belief that Allah is the sole deity worthy of worship and that He guides His chosen messengers to lead humanity towards righteousness and salvation.
orig: رب موسى وهارون

translation: He said: "Did you believe in him before I gave you permission? Surely he is your chief, who has taught you sorcery. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you all."
interpretation: This verse describes a powerful ruler who is angered that his subjects have believed in and followed a sorcerer without his permission. His threat to punish them severely, by cutting off their limbs and crucifying them, shows his arrogance and abuse of power. The verse highlights the dangers of blindly following charismatic figures who claim special powers, without proper scrutiny and authorization from rightful authorities. It serves as a warning against the misuse of power and the importance of exercising caution and discernment in matters of faith and belief.
orig: قال آمنتم له قبل أن آذن لكم إنه لكبيركم الذي علمكم السحر فلسوف تعلمون لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ولأصلبنكم أجمعين

translation: They said, "No harm. Indeed, to our Lord we will return."
interpretation: This verse expresses the steadfast faith and trust in God held by the believers, even in the face of adversity. The phrase "no harm" indicates their acceptance of whatever befalls them, as they are confident that their ultimate return is to God, who will judge and reward them justly. This verse highlights the importance of maintaining a strong relationship with the divine, and the belief that all things, both good and bad, ultimately lead back to the Creator.
orig: قالوا لا ضير إنا إلى ربنا منقلبون

translation: Indeed, we hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins, as we were the first of the believers.
interpretation: This verse expresses the hope and desire of the believers to be forgiven by Allah for their sins. The phrase "as we were the first of the believers" suggests a sense of humility and recognition that they were among the earliest to embrace the faith of Islam. The interpretation is that the believers are seeking Allah's forgiveness, acknowledging their past transgressions, and hoping to be counted among the faithful who were the first to accept the message of the Qur'an.
orig: إنا نطمع أن يغفر لنا ربنا خطايانا أن كنا أول المؤمنين

translation: And We inspired to Moses, "Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path through the sea. Do not fear being overtaken and do not be afraid."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Israelites' exodus from Egypt under the leadership of Prophet Moses. God commanded Moses to lead his people out of Egypt and travel by night, promising them a safe passage through the Red Sea. This was a miraculous event, as God parted the sea, allowing the Israelites to cross on dry land, while the Pharaoh's army was drowned when they tried to pursue them. The interpretation of this verse is that God can provide protection and deliverance to His servants, even in the face of seemingly insurmountable obstacles, if they put their trust in Him.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى أن أسر بعبادي إنكم متبعون

translation: And Pharaoh sent among the cities summoners
interpretation: This verse describes how Pharaoh, the ruler of Egypt at the time, dispatched messengers and officials to the various cities and towns under his control. These "summoners" were likely sent to gather resources, conscript people into labor, or enforce Pharaoh's authority over the populace. The verse suggests Pharaoh's power and reach, as he was able to mobilize people across his kingdom to serve his will.
orig: فأرسل فرعون في المدائن حاشرين

translation: Indeed, these are a small company
interpretation: This verse is referring to the small number of believers and followers of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) at the time. It emphasizes that despite their small numbers, they are a significant and important group. The interpretation suggests that the true worth of a group is not determined by its size, but by its faith, dedication, and the righteousness of its members.
orig: إن هؤلاء لشرذمة قليلون

translation: And indeed, they [i.e., the disbelievers] are to Us [i.e., Allah] a source of irritation.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the disbelievers and their rejection of faith are a source of distress and annoyance for Allah. It suggests that their persistent denial of the truth and their hostility towards the believers are displeasing to Allah, and that He is aware of their actions and attitudes.
orig: وإنهم لنا لغائظون

translation: And indeed, we are all cautious.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all people are in a state of vigilance and caution. It suggests that we should be mindful and careful in our actions and dealings, as we are all subject to the same uncertainties and potential dangers in life. The verse encourages a sense of collective responsibility and awareness, reminding us to be cautious and prudent in our conduct.
orig: وإنا لجميع حاذرون

translation: And We brought them out from gardens and springs
interpretation: This verse describes how God removed the disbelievers from the blessings and comforts they once enjoyed, such as the gardens and springs that were provided for them. This suggests that those who reject faith will be deprived of the rewards and bounties that believers will receive in the Hereafter.
orig: فأخرجناهم من جنات وعيون

translation: And treasures and a noble station
interpretation: This verse refers to the rewards and high status that Allah (God) will bestow upon the righteous in the Hereafter. The "treasures" symbolize the abundant blessings and provisions that the believers will enjoy in Paradise, while the "noble station" represents the elevated rank and honor they will attain in the sight of Allah. This verse encourages believers to strive for righteousness and obedience to Allah in order to earn these eternal rewards in the Afterlife.
orig: وكنوز ومقام كريم

translation: And thus We gave it [i.e., the land] as an inheritance to the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Israelites inheriting the land of Canaan, which was promised to them by Allah. It signifies that Allah fulfills His promises and grants blessings to those who believe in Him and follow His guidance. The inheritance of the land is a reward for the Israelites' faith and obedience, and a testament to Allah's power and mercy.
orig: كذلك وأورثناها بني إسرائيل

translation: And they pursued them at sunrise.
interpretation: This verse describes the Israelites pursuing their enemies, the Egyptians, at the break of dawn. The urgency and immediacy of this action suggests a determination to catch up with and overtake their adversaries without delay. The imagery of "sunrise" evokes a sense of a new beginning, a fresh start, and the start of a new chapter in the Israelites' journey. This verse highlights the Israelites' resolve and their unwavering commitment to achieving their goal, even in the face of a powerful foe.
orig: فأتبعوهم مشرقين

translation: And when the two groups saw one another, the companions of Moses said, 'Indeed, we are to be overtaken.'
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when the Israelites, led by Moses, saw the approaching Egyptian army pursuing them. The Israelites were fearful and felt that they would be caught and defeated by the Egyptians. This verse highlights the anxiety and uncertainty the Israelites experienced as they faced an overwhelming adversary, emphasizing their reliance on Moses and their faith in God's ultimate protection and deliverance.
orig: فلما تراءى الجمعان قال أصحاب موسى إنا لمدركون

translation: He (Musa) said: "Nay! Verily, with me is my Lord, He will guide me."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Ash-Shu'ara, verse 62. It is a response by the Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) to Pharaoh, who had challenged him and threatened him. Moses affirms that he is not alone, but that his Lord, Allah, is with him and will guide him. This verse conveys the importance of relying on and having faith in Allah, the Almighty, who will provide guidance and support to those who believe in Him, even in the face of adversity.
orig: قال كلا إن معي ربي سيهدين

translation: So We inspired to Moses, 'Strike with your staff the sea,' and it parted, and each part was like a great towering mountain.
interpretation: This verse describes how God commanded Moses to strike the sea with his staff, and the sea then parted, allowing the Israelites to cross through it. The verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of this event, describing how the parted waters were like "great towering mountains" on either side. This miracle demonstrated God's power and was a sign to the Israelites of His divine guidance and protection as they fled from Pharaoh.
orig: فأوحينا إلى موسى أن اضرب بعصاك البحر فانفلق فكان كل فرق كالطود العظيم

translation: And We advanced the last ones
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, those who were considered last or least in this world will be brought forward and honored. It implies that in the sight of Allah, the true worth of a person is not determined by their worldly status, but by their faith, deeds, and closeness to Allah. This verse encourages humility and the realization that Allah's judgment and rewards transcend the standards of this world.
orig: وأزلفنا ثم الآخرين

translation: And We saved Moses and all those who were with him, all together.
interpretation: This verse describes the miraculous deliverance of Prophet Moses and his followers from the Pharaoh and his army. It highlights God's power to save the righteous and faithful from their oppressors, and to punish the tyrants and disbelievers. The verse emphasizes the unity and solidarity of the believers who were saved together, underscoring the importance of community and mutual support in times of trial and adversity.
orig: وأنجينا موسى ومن معه أجمعين

translation: Then We drowned the others
interpretation: This verse refers to the drowning of Pharaoh and his army after they pursued the Israelites across the Red Sea. It signifies that those who oppose the truth and oppress the righteous will ultimately face divine punishment and destruction.
orig: ثم أغرقنا الآخرين

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them are not believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the signs and wonders of God's creation are clear evidence of His existence and power, yet most people remain in disbelief and do not accept the truth of Islam. It serves as a reminder that belief in God requires not just intellectual acknowledgment, but a sincere and committed faith that manifests in one's actions and way of life.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the attributes of Allah as being the Almighty, the Powerful, and the Most Merciful. It conveys that despite His absolute authority and sovereignty, Allah is also the source of compassion and kindness towards His creation. This highlights the balanced and comprehensive nature of Allah's attributes, where His power and might are complemented by His mercy and benevolence.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: And recite to them the news of Abraham.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to recite to the people the story and teachings of the Prophet Abraham. The story of Abraham is significant as he was a great prophet and messenger of God, and his life and teachings serve as an example for believers to follow. This verse emphasizes the importance of learning from the lives of the prophets and using their examples to guide one's own life.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ إبراهيم

translation: When he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) questioning his father and his people about their worship of idols and false deities. It highlights Abraham's rejection of idolatry and his search for the one true God. This verse emphasizes the importance of questioning one's beliefs and traditions, and seeking the truth through rational inquiry and spiritual reflection.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه وقومه ما تعبدون

translation: They said, "We will worship idols and remain devoted to them."
interpretation: This verse refers to the polytheistic beliefs of some people who worshipped idols and were devoted to them. The interpretation suggests that they were unwilling to abandon their false gods and superstitious practices, despite the call to worship the one true God. This highlights the importance of monotheism and rejecting the worship of any entity other than the Almighty.
orig: قالوا نعبد أصناما فنظل لها عاكفين

translation: He will say, "Do they hear you when you call?"
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will question the disbelievers about their rejection of faith, asking them if they could hear the call of the Prophets and Messengers when they were inviting them to believe in the Oneness of God. The implication is that the disbelievers had no excuse for their rejection, as they were able to hear the message but chose to ignore it.
orig: قال هل يسمعونكم إذ تدعون

translation: Or they may benefit you or they may do you harm.
interpretation: This verse suggests that people or things in one's life may either be beneficial or harmful. It encourages being cautious and discerning in one's relationships and dealings, as not everyone or everything will have one's best interests in mind. The verse emphasizes the need to carefully evaluate the potential consequences of one's choices and associations.
orig: أو ينفعونكم أو يضرون

translation: They said, "Rather, we found our fathers doing thus [as you command]."
interpretation: This verse reflects a common human tendency to follow traditions and customs of the past, even if they are not necessarily justified or beneficial. The people being addressed here are resistant to change and prefer to maintain the practices of their ancestors, rather than critically examining them. This verse highlights the importance of questioning long-held beliefs and traditions, and being open to new ideas and ways of thinking, rather than blindly following the past.
orig: قالوا بل وجدنا آباءنا كذلك يفعلون

translation: He said, "Have you then considered what you have been worshipping?"
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah An-Najm, verse 57. It is part of a dialogue between the Prophet Abraham and his people, who were idolaters. The verse is asking them to reflect on the objects of their worship - the idols they had been worshipping. The implication is that these idols are powerless and do not deserve to be worshipped, as they have no ability to benefit or harm the people. The verse encourages critical thinking and questioning the validity of their religious practices, leading them to the realization of the Oneness of God.
orig: قال أفرأيتم ما كنتم تعبدون

translation: You and your ancient forefathers
interpretation: This verse is addressing the people and their ancestors, implying that they have shared a long-standing tradition or way of life. The phrase "your ancient forefathers" suggests that the people being addressed have inherited certain beliefs, customs, or practices from their ancestors. The verse may be a call to reflect on the origins and foundations of their way of life, and to consider whether it is still relevant or in need of reevaluation.
orig: أنتم وآباؤكم الأقدمون

translation: Indeed, they are enemies to me, except for the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the enemies of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes that the only true Lord and protector is Allah, the Lord of all the worlds. The verse serves as a reminder that one should not fear the enmity of others, as long as they have the support and protection of Allah.
orig: فإنهم عدو لي إلا رب العالمين

translation: The One Who created me, and [it is] He who guides [me]
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the Creator of all things, including the speaker (the one reciting the verse). It also highlights that Allah is the One who guides and directs the person, providing them with the right path and direction in life. The verse conveys a sense of humility, gratitude and reliance on Allah as the source of guidance and leadership.
orig: الذي خلقني فهو يهدين

translation: And it is He who feeds me and gives me drink
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who provides for our sustenance and nourishment. He is the One who grants us food and water, the essential elements for our survival. This serves as a reminder that we are entirely dependent on Allah and should be grateful to Him for all that He bestows upon us.
orig: والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين

translation: And when I am ill, it is He who cures me.
interpretation: This verse expresses the belief that Allah is the one who provides healing and cure when a person is ill. It emphasizes the idea that Allah is the ultimate source of health and well-being, and that one should turn to Him for relief from illness and affliction.
orig: وإذا مرضت فهو يشفين

translation: And the One who causes me to die and then gives me life
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah as the One who has power over life and death. It emphasizes that Allah alone has the authority to take away life and restore it, demonstrating His absolute sovereignty and control over all creation. This serves as a reminder to humans of their dependence on Allah and the need to submit to His will.
orig: والذي يميتني ثم يحيين

translation: And the one who hopes that Allah will forgive him his sins on the Day of Recompense
interpretation: This verse expresses a person's hope and desire for Allah's forgiveness of their sins on the Day of Judgment. It highlights the importance of seeking Allah's mercy and pardon, as the Day of Reckoning is a time when one's deeds will be scrutinized and held accountable. The verse encourages a humble and repentant attitude, acknowledging one's shortcomings and relying on Allah's infinite grace and compassion to be forgiven.
orig: والذي أطمع أن يغفر لي خطيئتي يوم الدين

translation: My Lord, grant me wisdom and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to Allah, asking for wisdom and to be joined with the righteous. The interpretation is that the Prophet is seeking guidance and understanding from Allah, as well as the company and companionship of those who are righteous and virtuous. This reflects the Prophet's humility and desire to be close to Allah and to follow the path of the righteous.
orig: رب هب لي حكما وألحقني بالصالحين

translation: And grant me a reputation of honor among later generations
interpretation: This verse expresses a supplication to Allah to grant the speaker a good reputation and legacy among future generations. It reflects the desire to be remembered positively and to leave behind a lasting positive impact on others, even after one's lifetime. The "tongue of truth" refers to speaking and acting with honesty, integrity, and virtue, which will earn the speaker a respected standing among people in the future.
orig: واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين

translation: And make me an inheritor of the Garden of Bliss.
interpretation: This verse expresses a supplication to Allah, asking to be made among those who will inherit the Garden of Paradise, which is a place of eternal bliss and pleasure. The interpretation suggests that the speaker is seeking Allah's guidance and mercy to be counted among the righteous who will be granted entry into the blissful abode of the Hereafter.
orig: واجعلني من ورثة جنة النعيم

translation: And forgive my father, for indeed he is of those astray.
interpretation: This verse expresses a request by the Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) to forgive his father, who had worshipped idols. Despite his father's misguided beliefs, Ibrahim maintains a compassionate attitude and asks Allah to forgive him. This highlights the importance of maintaining familial ties and seeking forgiveness, even for those who have strayed from the right path. The verse emphasizes the virtue of mercy and the recognition that all people are susceptible to error, and thus deserve a chance at guidance and redemption.
orig: واغفر لأبي إنه كان من الضالين

translation: And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected
interpretation: This verse is asking Allah not to humiliate or disgrace the person on the Day of Resurrection, when all people will be held accountable for their deeds. It suggests a desire to be spared from any embarrassment or shame on that momentous day, when one's actions and beliefs will be laid bare. The verse reflects a plea for dignity and honor in the afterlife.
orig: ولا تخزني يوم يبعثون

translation: The Day when there will be no benefit [to anyone] from wealth or children
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when worldly possessions and familial ties will be of no avail. On that momentous day, the only thing that will matter is one's faith, good deeds, and relationship with the Almighty. Material wealth and social status will become insignificant, and people will be judged solely based on their spiritual and moral standing before God. This serves as a reminder to focus on the eternal life in the Hereafter, rather than being consumed by the fleeting pleasures of this world.
orig: يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون

translation: Except for one who comes to Allah with a sound heart
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having a pure and sincere heart when approaching Allah. It suggests that the only people who will be saved on the Day of Judgment are those who have purified their hearts and intentions, and have come to Allah with complete devotion and sincerity. The "sound heart" refers to a heart that is free from worldly attachments, hypocrisy, and evil intentions, and is instead filled with faith, righteousness, and a desire to please Allah.
orig: إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم

translation: And the Garden will be brought near to the righteous
interpretation: This verse conveys that on the Day of Judgment, the Garden (Paradise) will be brought close to the righteous and God-fearing people. This suggests that the rewards and blessings of the Hereafter will be easily accessible to those who have lived a life of piety, righteousness and devotion to Allah. The proximity of Paradise to the righteous emphasizes the certainty of their reward and the ease with which they will enter it, in contrast to the distance and difficulty faced by the wicked in reaching Hell.
orig: وأزلفت الجنة للمتقين

translation: And the Hellfire will be exposed for [all] the deviators
interpretation: This verse warns that on the Day of Judgment, the Hellfire will be made visible to all those who have strayed from the path of righteousness and fallen into sin and misguidance. It serves as a stark reminder of the consequences that await those who reject faith and choose to follow their desires instead of the guidance of Allah.
orig: وبرزت الجحيم للغاوين

translation: And it will be said to them, "Where are [all] those you used to worship?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when those who worshipped false deities or idols in their worldly life will be questioned about their misguided beliefs and practices. The verse suggests that on that day, the disbelievers will be made to realize the futility of their previous actions and the worthlessness of the objects they had worshipped, as they will be unable to provide any help or salvation.
orig: وقيل لهم أين ما كنتم تعبدون

translation: Can those [false deities] whom they call upon besides Allah give them help, or [can they] help themselves?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the ability of false deities or idols to provide any assistance or support to their worshippers. It challenges the notion that these gods can either help the people or even help themselves, implying that they are powerless and incapable of providing any real aid or protection. The verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping anything other than the one true God, Allah, and highlights His supreme power and sovereignty.
orig: من دون الله هل ينصرونكم أو ينتصرون

translation: Then they will be thrown into it, they and the deviators
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment of the disbelievers and those who have gone astray from the path of truth. They will be cast into the hellfire, along with the misguided ones who have led them astray. This is a warning to those who reject faith and follow their own desires, that they will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: فكبكبوا فيها هم والغاوون

translation: And the soldiers of Shaitaan (Satan) all together
interpretation: This verse refers to the forces of evil, led by Satan, that work to mislead and corrupt humanity. The interpretation is that Satan and his minions, who represent the forces of temptation, deception and sin, are united in their efforts to lead people astray from the path of righteousness and faith in God. The verse serves as a warning to believers to be vigilant and resist the schemes of Satan and his soldiers.
orig: وجنود إبليس أجمعون

translation: They will say, while they dispute therein
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when people will be gathered and held accountable for their actions. The verse depicts a scene where the people will be arguing and disputing with one another, as they stand before their Lord. This suggests that on that day, people will not be able to escape the consequences of their deeds, and they will have to face the reality of their choices and actions.
orig: قالوا وهم فيها يختصمون

translation: By Allah, we were indeed in manifest error
interpretation: This verse expresses the realization of those who had previously been in a state of clear misguidance and error. They acknowledge their previous state of being astray from the truth and recognize the need to return to the right path. The verse emphasizes the importance of self-reflection and acknowledging one's mistakes in order to seek guidance and find the right way.
orig: تالله إن كنا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: And when We made you equal with the Lord of the worlds
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all people are equal before God, the Lord of the worlds. It suggests that there is no distinction or superiority among humans based on their status, wealth, or other worldly factors. Rather, all are accountable to the same divine authority and are judged equally according to their deeds and faith.
orig: إذ نسويكم برب العالمين

translation: And none have led us astray except the criminals.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the wrongdoers and sinners are the ones who have misguided people and caused them to stray from the right path. It implies that the responsibility for people's misguidance lies with those who commit crimes and transgressions, not with God or the believers. The verse emphasizes that the true source of misguidance is the evil influence of the criminals, not any fault of the believers themselves.
orig: وما أضلنا إلا المجرمون

translation: So we have no intercessors
interpretation: This verse expresses the hopelessness and despair of those who rejected faith and will face the consequences of their actions on the Day of Judgment. They will have no one to intercede on their behalf or save them from the punishment they deserve.
orig: فما لنا من شافعين

translation: And no intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to help or intercede for another person. Even the closest of friends and loved ones will be powerless to assist each other, as each person will be held accountable for their own actions. This serves as a reminder to focus on our own deeds and relationship with God, rather than relying on others for salvation.
orig: ولا صديق حميم

translation: If only we had a share [in the decision], we would not have been among the slain.
interpretation: This verse expresses a sense of regret and a desire for a chance to change the outcome. The people speaking here wish they had been given a say or a role in the decision-making process, as they feel they would not have ended up among the casualties if they had been involved. The verse suggests a longing for agency and the ability to influence events, rather than being passive victims of circumstances beyond their control.
orig: فلو أن لنا كرة فنكون من المؤمنين

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them are not believers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that while there are clear signs and evidence of God's existence and power in the world around us, many people still choose not to believe. The verse highlights the contrast between the clarity of the signs and the lack of faith in most people. It suggests that the problem lies not in a lack of evidence, but in the human tendency to turn away from faith and to be skeptical or unbelieving, even in the face of clear signs.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Lord of the universe, is the Almighty, All-Powerful, and the Most Merciful. It conveys that despite His supreme power and authority, Allah is also infinitely compassionate and forgiving towards His creation. This highlights the dual nature of Allah - He is both the Exalted and the Merciful, and this should instill in believers a sense of awe, reverence, and hope in His divine attributes.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The people of Noah denied the messengers
interpretation: This verse refers to the rejection of the message of the prophet Noah by his own people. They refused to believe in the oneness of God and the call to righteousness that Noah brought to them. This verse highlights the common pattern of rejection that many prophets faced from their own communities, who were unwilling to accept the divine guidance and instead persisted in their disbelief and wrongdoing.
orig: كذبت قوم نوح المرسلين

translation: When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear [Allah]?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Noah, who was sent to guide his people to worship Allah alone. The verse highlights Noah's call to his people to have reverence and fear of Allah, and to turn away from their disbelief and wrongdoing. The interpretation suggests that Noah was urging his people to be mindful of Allah's commands and to live righteously, in order to avoid the consequences of their transgressions.
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم نوح ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: This verse conveys the message that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is a trustworthy messenger sent by God to guide humanity. It emphasizes the integrity and reliability of the Prophet as a messenger, assuring the people that his teachings and guidance can be trusted. This verse establishes the Prophet's credibility and authority as a divine messenger, calling upon the people to accept his message with confidence.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me
interpretation: This verse calls upon believers to be mindful of Allah and to obey the Prophet Muhammad. It emphasizes the importance of fearing (or revering) Allah and following the guidance and instructions given by the Prophet, who was sent by Allah to convey the divine message. The interpretation is that believers should strive to live in accordance with Allah's will and the teachings of the Prophet, as this is the path to righteousness and success in the afterlife.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And I do not ask you for wealth [in return]. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) does not seek any material reward or wealth from the people in return for conveying the message of Islam. His only reward is from Allah, the Lord of all the worlds. This underscores the selflessness and sincerity of the Prophet in his mission to guide humanity, without any personal agenda or desire for worldly gains.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse calls upon believers to be mindful of Allah and to obey the commands and teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes the importance of having faith in Allah and following His guidance as conveyed through the Prophet. The interpretation is that true believers should strive to live according to the principles of Islam, fearing Allah and submitting to His will by obeying the Prophet's teachings.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: They said, "Shall we believe in you when the lowest [of the people] follow you?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and resistance that the Prophet Muhammad faced from the elite and powerful members of society when he started preaching Islam. They questioned how they could believe in him when the poor, weak, and marginalized people were the ones who were following him. This verse highlights the tendency of the privileged to dismiss the message and the messenger based on the socioeconomic status of the followers, rather than the merits of the message itself. The interpretation suggests that true faith and guidance should not be judged by worldly status or popularity, but by the substance and truth of the message.
orig: قالوا أنؤمن لك واتبعك الأرذلون

translation: He said, 'And I am not aware of what they used to do.'
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Moses and the Israelites. When Moses returned from the mountain after receiving the commandments, he found his people worshipping a golden calf. In this verse, Moses expresses his lack of knowledge about their actions, indicating that he was unaware of their idolatry and had not sanctioned it. The interpretation is that sometimes, even the most righteous of people may be unaware of the wrongdoings of those under their care or influence, and they should not be held responsible for such actions.
orig: قال وما علمي بما كانوا يعملون

translation: Indeed, their account is only upon my Lord, if you could but perceive.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the ultimate judgment and reckoning of people's deeds is with God alone. Even though it may not be apparent to us now, God is fully aware of everyone's actions and will hold them accountable on the Day of Judgment. This serves as a reminder to be conscious of our conduct, as we will all return to God and be held responsible for our choices and behaviors in this life.
orig: إن حسابهم إلا على ربي لو تشعرون

translation: And I am not a dismisser of the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not someone who would reject or turn away the believers. Rather, he is a compassionate and caring leader who welcomes and embraces the believers. This verse serves to reassure the believers that the Prophet will not abandon or dismiss them, but will continue to guide and support them on their spiritual journey.
orig: وما أنا بطارد المؤمنين

translation: Indeed, I am but a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is a clear and evident warner, sent by God to guide humanity towards the truth and warn them against the consequences of disbelief and disobedience. It highlights the Prophet's role as a messenger, whose duty is to convey the divine message and caution people against the punishment that awaits those who reject it.
orig: إن أنا إلا نذير مبين

translation: They said, "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among the stoned."
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Prophet Noah in the Qur'an. The people of Noah had rejected his message and threatened him with stoning if he did not stop calling them to worship only Allah. This verse highlights the resistance and hostility that prophets often faced from their people when calling them to the truth. It serves as a reminder that standing firm in one's faith and convictions can come at a cost, but that the ultimate reward is with Allah.
orig: قالوا لئن لم تنته يا نوح لتكونن من المرجومين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, indeed my people have denied [the truth].'
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Al-Shu'ara, verse 117. It is the words of the Prophet Nuh (Noah), who is addressing his Lord, Allah, and expressing his frustration that his people have rejected the message of truth that he has conveyed to them. The interpretation is that when people stubbornly refuse to accept the guidance and truth that is presented to them, it can be a source of great distress for the messenger of that truth. However, the messenger's duty is to continue to convey the message, and to place his trust in Allah, knowing that the ultimate judgment lies with Him.
orig: قال رب إن قومي كذبون

translation: So open between me and them an opening and save me and those with me from the believers.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to Allah, asking for a resolution or opening between him and his opponents, and for protection for himself and his followers from the believers who have turned against him. It reflects the challenges the Prophet faced in his mission to spread the message of Islam, and his reliance on Allah's help and guidance to overcome these obstacles.
orig: فافتح بيني وبينهم فتحا ونجني ومن معي من المؤمنين

translation: And We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) and the great flood. It describes how God saved Noah and those who believed in him and joined him on the ark, while the disbelievers were destroyed. The "laden ship" or "ark" represents the vessel that carried the believers to safety, symbolizing God's protection and deliverance of the righteous in times of great calamity.
orig: فأنجيناه ومن معه في الفلك المشحون

translation: Then We drowned the remaining [people].
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Noah and the great flood. After Noah and his followers were saved in the ark, God then drowned all the disbelievers who had rejected Noah's message and refused to join him on the ark. This verse emphasizes God's power to punish those who stubbornly reject the truth and refuse to heed the warnings of the prophets.
orig: ثم أغرقنا بعد الباقين

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them are not believers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that there are clear signs of God's existence and power in the creation, but most people do not believe in Him. It implies that those who reflect on the wonders of the universe should be able to recognize the divine origin of creation, but many people choose not to believe despite the available evidence.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Lord of the universe, is both Almighty and Merciful. He has the power and authority to do as He wills, but He is also compassionate and kind towards His creation. This reminds us that we should have unwavering faith in Allah, and seek His forgiveness and mercy, even when faced with difficulties or challenges.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The people of 'Ad denied the messengers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ancient tribe of 'Ad, who rejected the message of the prophets sent to them. The people of 'Ad were known for their arrogance, disbelief and oppression, and they denied and rejected the warnings and guidance brought by the messengers of God. This serves as a lesson that those who reject the truth and defy the divine commands will face severe consequences for their actions.
orig: كذبت عاد المرسلين

translation: When their brother Hud said to them, "Will you not fear [Allah]?"
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, specifically from Surah Hud, verse 50. It describes the prophet Hud addressing his people, the 'Aad, and urging them to fear and worship Allah. The interpretation is that Hud, as a messenger of Allah, is calling his people to have taqwa (God-consciousness) and to submit to the will of the Almighty. He is reminding them that they should fear Allah and His punishment if they persist in their disbelief and disobedience.
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم هود ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the trustworthiness and reliability of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger of God. It conveys the idea that the Prophet is delivering the divine message with complete honesty and integrity, and that the people can have full confidence in him and the teachings he is conveying.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to be mindful of Allah and to obey the Prophet Muhammad. It emphasizes the importance of submitting to the will of Allah and following the guidance provided by the Prophet, who was sent as a messenger to convey the divine teachings. The verse highlights the need for believers to have a reverent fear of Allah and to demonstrate their faith through obedience to the Prophet's instructions, which are rooted in the Qur'anic teachings.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And I do not ask you for wealth [in return]. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not seek any material or worldly gain from his mission of conveying the message of Islam.
