His only reward and compensation was to be found with Allah, the Lord of all the worlds. This highlights the selflessness and sincerity of the Prophet, as he was not motivated by personal interests or desires, but solely by the desire to guide humanity to the truth and earn the pleasure of God.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: Do you build upon every elevation a [vain] structure? And take for yourselves [fine] dwellings?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the practice of building elaborate structures and dwellings solely for the purpose of vanity and ostentation, rather than for practical needs or the betterment of society. It suggests that such actions are frivolous and do not serve a meaningful purpose. The interpretation is that one should not engage in vain and wasteful activities, but rather focus on more constructive and beneficial endeavors.
orig: أتبنون بكل ريع آية تعبثون

translation: And you take factories, perhaps that you may abide [in them].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the human tendency to accumulate wealth and build structures that provide a sense of permanence and security. The phrase "you take factories" suggests that people often invest in industrial or commercial enterprises, not just for practical purposes, but also to create a lasting legacy and a sense of immortality. The phrase "perhaps that you may abide [in them]" implies that this pursuit of material wealth and physical structures is driven by a desire for longevity and a fear of mortality. The verse cautions against placing too much emphasis on these transient pursuits, as true and lasting fulfillment can only be found in the remembrance of God and the hereafter.
orig: وتتخذون مصانع لعلكم تخلدون

translation: And when you strike, you strike as tyrants.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against oppression and tyranny. It cautions those in power not to abuse their authority and to treat others with justice and compassion. The verse suggests that when people in positions of power use their strength to harm or subjugate others, they are acting like "tyrants" or oppressors. The message is to exercise restraint and moderation, and to avoid using one's power in a cruel or unjust manner.
orig: وإذا بطشتم بطشتم جبارين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse calls upon believers to be mindful of Allah and to obey the commands of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes the importance of fearing (or being conscious of) Allah, and following the guidance and instructions given by the Prophet, who was sent as a messenger to convey Allah's message. Obeying the Prophet is equated with obeying Allah, as the Prophet's teachings and commands are a reflection of Allah's will.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse calls upon believers to be mindful and conscious of Allah, the One who has provided them with all the knowledge and resources they possess. It reminds them that they will ultimately be held accountable before Allah, and thus they must live their lives in a way that pleases Him. The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing and revering Allah, as this will guide believers to make righteous choices and lead a life that is pleasing to the Almighty.
orig: واتقوا الذي أمدكم بما تعلمون

translation: And has supplied you with cattle and children
interpretation: This verse is referring to the blessings that God has bestowed upon the people. The "cattle" represent the material wealth and resources that God has provided, while the "children" represent the spiritual and familial blessings. The interpretation is that God has granted the people both physical and spiritual abundance, and they should be grateful for these gifts.
orig: أمدكم بأنعام وبنين

translation: And gardens and springs
interpretation: This verse refers to the bountiful rewards and pleasures that await the righteous in the Hereafter. The "gardens" symbolize the lush, paradisiacal environments that the believers will enjoy, while the "springs" represent the abundant sources of pure, refreshing water that will flow throughout these heavenly abodes. This imagery conveys the idea of a life of eternal bliss, tranquility, and fulfillment that God has prepared for those who have lived virtuously and submitted to His will.
orig: وجنات وعيون

translation: Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day.
interpretation: This verse expresses the Prophet's concern for his people and his fear that they will face a severe punishment on the Day of Judgment if they do not heed his message and repent from their misdeeds. The "tremendous Day" refers to the Day of Resurrection, when all people will be held accountable for their actions in life. The Prophet is warning his people to turn away from their disbelief and wrongdoing in order to avoid this impending punishment.
orig: إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: They say, "It is same to us whether you warn us or do not warn us."
interpretation: This verse expresses the attitude of those who are indifferent to the message of the Qur'an and the warnings of the Prophets. They consider it irrelevant whether they are warned or not, as they are unwilling to change their ways and beliefs. This verse highlights the importance of being receptive to the guidance provided by Allah through His Messengers, and the consequences of turning a blind eye to the truth.
orig: قالوا سواء علينا أوعظت أم لم تكن من الواعظين

translation: Indeed, this is not but a creation of the former [peoples].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Qur'an itself, indicating that it is not a new or novel creation, but rather a continuation of the divine revelations that have been sent down to the previous prophets and nations. The implication is that the Qur'an is part of the same divine tradition and carries the same essential message as the earlier scriptures, even though it may contain new laws, teachings, and guidance that are tailored to the specific needs and circumstances of the Prophet Muhammad's time and community.
orig: إن هذا إلا خلق الأولين

translation: And We are not to punish [anyone]
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah does not punish people without just cause. It suggests that Allah is merciful and does not arbitrarily inflict punishment, but rather holds people accountable for their actions in a fair and just manner.
orig: وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: But they denied him, so We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who rejected the message of the Prophets sent to them. Despite the clear signs and evidence provided, they stubbornly refused to believe and as a result, they were destroyed. This serves as a lesson and a sign for those who reflect, but the majority of people still choose not to believe. The verse emphasizes the importance of having faith and heeding the guidance of the Prophets, lest one suffers the same consequences as those who rejected the truth.
orig: فكذبوه فأهلكناهم إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the attributes of Allah as being "al-Aziz" (the Almighty, the Powerful) and "ar-Rahim" (the Most Merciful). It conveys that Allah is the Sovereign, the Dominant, the One with absolute power and authority, yet He is also the Most Compassionate, the Most Loving, and the Most Merciful towards His creation. This highlights the balance between Allah's majesty and His mercy, and reminds us that even in the face of His power and might, He is still the Merciful Lord who cares for His servants.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The Thamud denied the messengers
interpretation: This verse refers to the ancient tribe of Thamud, who rejected the message of the prophets sent to them. The Thamud were a prosperous people who lived in the northern region of the Arabian Peninsula. They were known for their impressive rock-cut architecture and advanced civilization. However, they turned away from the guidance of the messengers, refusing to believe in the oneness of God and the message of repentance and righteousness. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and deny the signs of God, as the Thamud were ultimately destroyed for their disbelief and arrogance.
orig: كذبت ثمود المرسلين

translation: When their brother Salih said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, and it is referring to the story of the prophet Salih and his people, the Thamud. The verse highlights Salih's call to his people to fear and worship Allah, the One True God. Salih's message was to reject idolatry and polytheism, and to live a righteous life in submission to Allah. The interpretation of this verse is that it emphasizes the importance of fearing and obeying Allah, and not falling into the trap of disbelief and disobedience.
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم صالح ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) as mentioned in the Qur'an. It conveys the message that Prophet Shu'ayb was sent by Allah as a messenger to his people, and that he was a trustworthy and reliable person who could be entrusted with the divine message. The verse emphasizes the importance of having faith in the messengers of Allah and following their teachings, as they are the conduits through which Allah communicates with humanity.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me
interpretation: This verse commands believers to have reverence and consciousness of Allah, and to obey the instructions and guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes the importance of submitting to the will of Allah and following the teachings of the Prophet, which lead to spiritual and moral purification.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And I do not ask you for wealth [in return]. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not seeking any worldly reward or compensation for his message. His only reward is from Allah, the Lord of all creation. This highlights the sincerity and selflessness of the Prophet's mission, as he is not motivated by personal gain but solely by the desire to convey Allah's guidance to humanity.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: Do you feel secure in what is here?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, implying that one should not feel secure or complacent in the temporary and fleeting nature of this worldly life. It suggests that true security and safety can only be found in one's relationship with the Almighty, and that one should not become overly attached to the transient pleasures and possessions of this world.
orig: أتتركون في ما هاهنا آمنين

translation: In gardens and springs.
interpretation: This verse refers to the bountiful rewards and pleasures awaiting the righteous in the Hereafter. The "gardens and springs" symbolize the lush, tranquil environments of Paradise, where the believers will reside in eternal bliss and contentment. This verse highlights the promise of a life of abundance, serenity, and spiritual fulfillment in the Afterlife for those who have lived virtuously in this world.
orig: في جنات وعيون

translation: And [there are] crops and palm trees, growing out of it, with trunks in layers
interpretation: This verse describes the abundance and variety of vegetation that grows in the lands created by God. The reference to "crops and palm trees" suggests a fertile and productive landscape, where different types of plants thrive. The phrase "growing out of it, with trunks in layers" conveys the idea of a layered or tiered structure of the vegetation, perhaps indicating the presence of different levels of growth, from the ground cover to the tall palm trees. This imagery evokes a sense of the richness and diversity of God's creation.
orig: وزروع ونخل طلعها هضيم

translation: And you carve out in the mountains, houses, [that are] grand.
interpretation: This verse refers to the human tendency to build grand and impressive structures, even in the most challenging of environments like mountainous regions. It suggests that people often seek to create elaborate dwellings, showcasing their skills and wealth, rather than living in more modest accommodations. The interpretation is that this verse cautions against excessive materialism and vanity, and encourages a more balanced and humble approach to living.
orig: وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتا فارهين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me
interpretation: This verse calls upon believers to be mindful of Allah and to obey the Prophet Muhammad. It emphasizes the importance of taqwa (God-consciousness) and obedience to the Messenger as a means of pleasing Allah and attaining success in this life and the Hereafter. The interpretation suggests that true faith requires both a reverence for the divine and a willingness to submit to the guidance provided by the Prophet, who was sent as a messenger to humanity.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And do not obey the order of the extravagant
interpretation: This verse instructs us not to follow the commands or directives of those who are wasteful, extravagant, and excessive in their behavior. It encourages us to be moderate and avoid the temptation to indulge in unnecessary luxuries or to squander resources. The interpretation is that we should be mindful of our actions and not blindly obey those who encourage profligacy, as this can lead to harmful consequences for ourselves and society.
orig: ولا تطيعوا أمر المسرفين

translation: Those who spread corruption in the land and do not amend.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who engage in sinful and destructive behaviors that harm society and the environment, without making any effort to improve or rectify their actions. It condemns those who sow discord, oppress others, and engage in activities that undermine the well-being of the community. The interpretation is that such individuals will be held accountable for their misdeeds and that true reform and betterment can only come through righteous and constructive actions.
orig: الذين يفسدون في الأرض ولا يصلحون

translation: They said, "You are but one of the deluded."
interpretation: This verse refers to a dialogue between the disbelievers and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The disbelievers accused the Prophet of being "one of the deluded" or "one of the bewitched", implying that he was under the influence of magic or delusion and not speaking the truth. This was a common accusation made by the opponents of the Prophet, who refused to accept the message of Islam and tried to discredit the Prophet's mission.
orig: قالوا إنما أنت من المسحرين

translation: You are not but a human being like us, so bring a sign if you are of the truthful.
interpretation: This verse is a response from the disbelievers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) when he claimed to be a messenger of God. They argued that he was just a human being like them, and challenged him to show a miraculous sign to prove his truthfulness. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet was a human being, not a divine being, and that he should provide evidence of his prophethood if he was indeed truthful.
orig: ما أنت إلا بشر مثلنا فأت بآية إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, "This is a she-camel. For her is a [time of] drink, and for you is a [time of] drink, [each] on a known day."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of the prophet Salih and his people. It describes how Salih presented a she-camel as a sign from God, and instructed his people to allow the camel to drink on one day, and for them to drink on another day. This was a test of their faith and obedience to God's commands. The interpretation is that God provides for all of His creation, but expects us to use His blessings responsibly and in accordance with His instructions.
orig: قال هذه ناقة لها شرب ولكم شرب يوم معلوم

translation: And do not touch it with harm, lest you be seized by a painful punishment on a tremendous Day.
interpretation: This verse warns against harming or misusing the divine revelations (the Qur'an) in any way. It emphasizes that those who mistreat the Qur'an will be subject to a severe punishment on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder to treat the Qur'an with the utmost respect and care, as it is the word of God revealed to humanity.
orig: ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: And they hamstrung her, so they became regretful.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the people of Thamud, who were punished for their rejection of the prophet Salih and their killing of the she-camel that was a sign from Allah. The verse describes how they hamstrung (cut the tendons of) the she-camel, and as a result, they became regretful and remorseful for their actions. This serves as a warning to those who defy the commands of Allah and engage in wrongdoing, as they will ultimately face the consequences of their actions.
orig: فعقروها فأصبحوا نادمين

translation: And the punishment seized them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights that those who rejected the message of the Prophets faced severe consequences for their disbelief. The "punishment" refers to the divine retribution that befell them, which serves as a "sign" or lesson for humanity. However, the majority of people still remained in a state of unbelief, unwilling to heed the warnings and guidance provided by the Prophets.
orig: فأخذهم العذاب إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes two key attributes of God - His might and His mercy. The term "al-Aziz" (the Exalted in Might) conveys that God is all-powerful, supreme, and unrivaled in His authority. The term "ar-Rahim" (the Merciful) conveys that God is compassionate, kind, and forgiving towards His creation. This combination of might and mercy highlights the dual nature of God - He is both the Almighty Sovereign and the Compassionate Sustainer. The verse reminds us that despite God's supreme power, He is also merciful and loving towards His servants, and that we can seek His help and guidance with confidence.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The people of Lot denied the messengers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the rejection of the prophet Lot (peace be upon him) and his message by the people of Sodom. They denied the existence of God and the truthfulness of Lot's warnings, leading to their ultimate destruction. This serves as a lesson that those who reject the divine message and persist in their sinful ways will face severe consequences.
orig: كذبت قوم لوط المرسلين

translation: When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear [Allah]?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Sodom, to whom the prophet Lot was sent as a messenger. Lot, their brother, admonished them to fear Allah and refrain from their immoral and wicked practices, such as homosexuality and other sins. The verse emphasizes the importance of having faith, being righteous, and fearing Allah in order to avoid His punishment.
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم لوط ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the trustworthiness and reliability of the messenger, who is conveying a message from God. It is a statement of the messenger's integrity and credibility, assuring the recipients that the message they are receiving can be trusted as it comes from a reliable source.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse calls upon believers to be mindful of Allah and to obey the Prophet Muhammad. It emphasizes the importance of fearing and revering Allah, as well as submitting to the guidance and commands provided by the Prophet. The interpretation is that believers should strive to live according to Allah's will and the teachings of the Prophet, as this is the path to pleasing Allah and attaining salvation.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And I do not ask you for wealth [in return]. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not seek any material gain or wealth from the people in return for conveying the message of Islam. His only reward and compensation was from Allah, the Lord of all the worlds. This highlights the sincerity and selflessness of the Prophet's mission, as he was not motivated by personal interests but rather by the desire to guide humanity towards the truth and the pleasure of Allah.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: Do you approach the males among the worlds?
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of homosexuality, which was prevalent in some ancient societies. The Qur'an emphasizes that sexual relations should be between a man and a woman within the institution of marriage, as this is the natural and divinely ordained way of human reproduction and the preservation of society. The verse strongly disapproves of engaging in sexual acts with members of the same sex, which is considered a deviation from the natural order and a violation of the teachings of Islam.
orig: أتأتون الذكران من العالمين

translation: And you leave what your Lord has created for you of mates?
interpretation: This verse is condemning the practice of abandoning or neglecting one's spouse, which was a common practice in pre-Islamic Arabia. The verse emphasizes that spouses are a creation of God, and that it is a duty for believers to honor and cherish their marital relationships. The interpretation suggests that abandoning one's spouse is a form of transgression and deviation from the natural order established by God.
orig: وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم بل أنتم قوم عادون

translation: They said, "If you do not desist, O Lot, you will be of those evicted."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people of Sodom who were threatening the Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) for preaching against their sinful practices of homosexuality and other moral deviations. They warned him that if he did not stop his preaching, he would be expelled from their land. This highlights the opposition and hostility that righteous people often face when they stand up against the wrongdoings of their society. The verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and courage in the face of such threats, as the Prophets demonstrated in their unwavering commitment to their divine mission.
orig: قالوا لئن لم تنته يا لوط لتكونن من المخرجين

translation: He said, "Indeed, I am of those who witness [your deeds]."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Shu'ayb, who was sent to the people of Madyan. The verse indicates that Shu'ayb affirmed his role as a witness to the actions and conduct of his people. He was not merely a passive observer, but an active participant who was aware of and accountable for their deeds. This suggests that as a prophet, Shu'ayb felt a responsibility to guide his people and hold them accountable for their actions, in order to lead them towards righteousness and the pleasure of God.
orig: قال إني لعملكم من القالين

translation: My Lord, save me and my family from [the consequences of] what they are doing.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication by the Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) to Allah, asking to be saved from the wicked actions of his people, who were engaged in immoral and unnatural practices. It reflects Lut's concern for his own salvation as well as that of his family, as he recognized the corrupting influence of his people's behavior. The verse highlights the importance of seeking Allah's protection and guidance, especially when faced with societal evils and temptations.
orig: رب نجني وأهلي مما يعملون

translation: And We saved him and his family - all together.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Nuh (Noah) and the flood. Allah saved Nuh and his family from the flood that destroyed the disbelievers. This verse emphasizes that Allah protects and saves the righteous people who believe in Him, while the disbelievers are destroyed. It is a lesson that those who have faith in Allah and follow His guidance will be saved, while those who reject the truth will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: فنجيناه وأهله أجمعين

translation: Except an old woman among those who remained behind.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the destruction of the people of Lut (Lot), who were punished by God for their immoral and unethical behavior. The verse indicates that the only person who was spared from this punishment was an old woman who remained behind, likely referring to Lut's wife who did not heed the warning and was therefore destroyed along with the rest of the people. This serves as a lesson that those who persist in their wrongdoing and reject the guidance of God will face severe consequences, while those who repent and turn to God may be saved.
orig: إلا عجوزا في الغابرين

translation: Then We destroyed the others.
interpretation: This verse suggests that after punishing the disbelievers, God then destroyed those who persisted in their rejection of faith and continued to oppress the believers. The interpretation is that God will ultimately destroy those who refuse to heed His warnings and continue to engage in wrongdoing.
orig: ثم دمرنا الآخرين

translation: And We rained upon them a [torrential] rain, and evil was the rain of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment that was inflicted upon the disbelievers who were warned by the Prophets, but they persisted in their rejection of the truth. The "torrential rain" is a metaphor for the severe and devastating consequences that befell them as a result of their defiance and disobedience. The interpretation suggests that those who are warned by the divine message, but choose to ignore it, will face the consequences of their actions, which can be dire and unpleasant.
orig: وأمطرنا عليهم مطرا فساء مطر المنذرين

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them are not believers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even though there are clear signs and evidence of God's existence and power in the universe, most people do not believe or have faith. The verse implies that people often fail to recognize or acknowledge the divine signs around them, and instead remain in a state of disbelief or skepticism.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Lord of the Prophet Muhammad, is the Almighty, the All-Powerful, and the Most Merciful. It conveys the idea that despite His absolute power and authority, Allah is also infinitely compassionate and forgiving towards His creation. This serves to instill in believers a sense of awe and reverence for God, as well as hope and trust in His mercy and benevolence.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The companions of the thicket denied the messengers
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Midian, who rejected the message of the prophets sent to them. The "companions of the thicket" (Ashab al-Aikah) were a group of people who lived in a wooded area and rejected the call of the messengers, denying their divine mission. This serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and refuse to believe in the messengers of God.
orig: كذب أصحاب الأيكة المرسلين

translation: When Shu'aib said to them, "Will you not fear [Allah]?"
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Al-A'raf, verse 85. It refers to the prophet Shu'aib (Jethro) addressing his people, urging them to fear and be mindful of Allah. The interpretation suggests that Shu'aib is calling his people to have a reverent attitude towards Allah, to be conscious of their actions and to avoid wrongdoing. This is a common theme in the Qur'an, where prophets call their people to worship Allah alone and to live righteously.
orig: إذ قال لهم شعيب ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the trustworthiness and reliability of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger of God. It conveys the message that the Prophet is a faithful and honest guide, deserving of the people's trust and acceptance of his teachings. The verse assures the listeners that the Prophet's words and actions are guided by divine wisdom and can be relied upon.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me
interpretation: This verse calls upon believers to have reverence and consciousness of Allah, and to obey the commands and guidance of the Prophet Muhammad. It emphasizes the importance of both having faith in Allah and submitting to His will, as well as following the teachings and example of the Prophet, who was sent as a messenger to guide humanity. The interpretation is that true piety and righteousness requires both a devotion to Allah and obedience to His appointed prophet.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And I do not ask you for wealth [in return]. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not seek any material reward or compensation from the people for conveying the message of Islam. His only reward and recompense was from Allah, the Lord of all the worlds. This highlights the sincerity and selflessness of the Prophet's mission, as he was not motivated by personal gain but rather by a desire to guide humanity towards the truth and the pleasure of Allah.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: Give full measure and do not be of those who cause loss.
interpretation: This verse commands people to be fair and just in their dealings, particularly when it comes to measures and weights. It emphasizes the importance of honesty and integrity in commercial transactions, and warns against cheating or defrauding others. The interpretation is that one should always strive to be fair and just, and not take advantage of others or engage in any deceitful practices, as that would be considered a form of "causing loss" or harming others.
orig: أوفوا الكيل ولا تكونوا من المخسرين

translation: And weigh with the straight balance.
interpretation: This verse instructs people to be just and fair in their dealings, to use accurate and honest measures when weighing or assessing things. It emphasizes the importance of integrity, honesty, and fairness in all aspects of life, whether in business, social interactions, or personal conduct. The "straight balance" refers to a balanced and impartial approach, free from bias or manipulation, in order to ensure equity and justice.
orig: وزنوا بالقسطاس المستقيم

translation: And do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.
interpretation: This verse instructs us not to withhold or diminish the rights and possessions of others, and to refrain from causing mischief and corruption in the world. It emphasizes the importance of fairness, honesty, and respecting the rights of all people, as well as maintaining a peaceful and harmonious society.
orig: ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: And fear the One who created you and [also] the former generations
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be mindful and reverent of Allah, the Creator, who has brought all of humanity into existence. It also reminds us to learn from the experiences and lessons of previous generations, and to avoid the mistakes and transgressions that they may have committed. By fearing and respecting Allah, and by reflecting on the examples of those who came before us, we can strive to live righteous and God-conscious lives.
orig: واتقوا الذي خلقكم والجبلة الأولين

translation: They said, "You are only of those bewitched."
interpretation: This verse refers to the response of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They accused him of being under the influence of magic or sorcery, rather than acknowledging the divine revelation he was receiving. The interpretation suggests that the disbelievers refused to accept the truth of the Prophet's message, and instead resorted to dismissing it as the result of some kind of enchantment or deception.
orig: قالوا إنما أنت من المسحرين

translation: And you are not but a human being like us, and we think you are of the liars.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and stating that he is a human being like the rest of humanity, and that the disbelievers doubt his prophethood and consider him to be a liar. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet is not a divine being, but a messenger sent by God to guide humanity. It serves as a reminder that prophets are human and should not be deified, while also acknowledging the skepticism and rejection faced by the Prophet from those who refused to believe in his message.
orig: وما أنت إلا بشر مثلنا وإن نظنك لمن الكاذبين

translation: Then cause a fragment from the sky to fall upon us, if you are of the truthful.
interpretation: This verse is a challenge from the disbelievers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to prove his prophethood by bringing down a piece of the sky as a sign. The interpretation is that this request is made in a mocking and disbelieving manner, as the disbelievers do not truly believe in the Prophet's message and are demanding an impossible miracle to test his truthfulness. The Qur'an does not respond to this request, as true faith cannot be based on such miraculous displays, but rather on the inherent truth and guidance of the Qur'anic teachings.
orig: فأسقط علينا كسفا من السماء إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: My Lord knows best what you do.
interpretation: This verse expresses the belief that Allah, the Lord, has perfect knowledge and understanding of all that His servants do. It emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and that He is aware of every action, thought, and intention of His creation. This serves as a reminder to believers that they are accountable to Allah for their deeds, and that they should strive to please Him in all their actions.
orig: قال ربي أعلم بما تعملون

translation: But they denied him, so the punishment of the day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed, that was the punishment of a great day.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the people of Prophet Shu'aib, who rejected his message and were punished by Allah with a severe punishment on the Day of the Canopy. The "day of the Canopy" is believed to refer to a day when the sky appeared to be like a canopy over the people, indicating the intensity of the punishment. This verse emphasizes the gravity of rejecting the message of the prophets and the consequences that come with it.
orig: فكذبوه فأخذهم عذاب يوم الظلة إنه كان عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even though there are clear signs and evidence of God's existence and power in the universe, most people still choose not to believe. It implies that faith is a matter of the heart and mind, not just outward observation. The verse encourages reflection on the signs around us, while acknowledging that belief ultimately requires an inner spiritual acceptance that not everyone achieves.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Lord of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), is the Almighty, the All-Powerful, and the Most Merciful. It conveys that despite His supreme power and authority, Allah is also infinitely compassionate and loving towards His creation. This combination of absolute might and boundless mercy is a core tenet of Islamic theology, highlighting the unique and unparalleled nature of the Divine.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: And indeed, it is the revelation of the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an is a divine revelation from Allah, the Lord and Sustainer of all the worlds. It emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, which was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a guidance for all of humanity.
orig: وإنه لتنزيل رب العالمين

translation: The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an being revealed by the Angel Gabriel, who is known as the "Trustworthy Spirit". It emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation, not the words of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) himself. The interpretation is that the Qur'an is a sacred text that has been faithfully delivered by the Angel Gabriel, who is a trusted messenger of God.
orig: نزل به الروح الأمين

translation: That it may be upon your heart, [O Muhammad], to be among the warners.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Quran has been revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) so that he may convey its message as a warner to humanity. The Quran is to be firmly established in the heart of the Prophet, so that he can effectively warn people about the consequences of disbelief and encourage them to believe in the oneness of God and lead a righteous life. The role of the Prophet is to be a bearer of glad tidings and a warner, guiding people towards the straight path.
orig: على قلبك لتكون من المنذرين

translation: In a clear Arabic language
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Quran was revealed in a clear and eloquent Arabic language, making it accessible and understandable to the Arabic-speaking people of the time. The clarity of the language used in the Quran is a testament to its divine origin, as it is a language that is free from ambiguity or obscurity. This language serves as a means of guidance and a tool for understanding the message of the Quran for those who speak Arabic.
orig: بلسان عربي مبين

translation: And indeed, it [i.e., the Qur'an] is [mentioned] in the scriptures of the former peoples.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the message of the Qur'an is not something new, but rather it is in line with the teachings and scriptures of the previous prophets and nations. It indicates that the Qur'an is a continuation and confirmation of the divine revelations that were sent before it, and that its teachings are consistent with the eternal truths found in the earlier scriptures.
orig: وإنه لفي زبر الأولين

translation: Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel recognize it?
interpretation: This verse is asking whether the disbelievers do not see the clear signs and evidence of the truth of the Qur'an, such as the fact that the learned scholars among the Jews recognize its divine origin and authenticity. The implication is that if even the scholars of the People of the Book can recognize the Qur'an as a revelation from God, then this should be a clear sign for the disbelievers to also accept and believe in it.
orig: أولم يكن لهم آية أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل

translation: And if We had sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of Allah. And these examples We present to the people that perhaps they will give thought.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound impact and power of the Qur'an. If the Qur'an were to be revealed upon a mountain, the mountain would humble itself and break apart out of reverence and fear for Allah. This serves as an example to humanity to reflect on the Qur'an and its divine origin, and to submit to its teachings with the same level of humility and awe.
orig: ولو نزلناه على بعض الأعجمين

translation: And he recited it to them, but they were not believers in it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even when the truth is presented to people, some may still choose not to believe it. The Qur'an was recited to those who were unwilling to accept it, despite the clarity and power of its message. This highlights the importance of free will and the individual's choice in matters of faith. The verse emphasizes that belief is not something that can be forced, but rather a personal decision that each person must make for themselves.
orig: فقرأه عليهم ما كانوا به مؤمنين

translation: And thus We have inserted it into the hearts of the criminals
interpretation: This verse suggests that the message of the Qur'an has been placed in the hearts of the wrongdoers, even though they may resist or reject it. The implication is that the truth of the Qur'an is so evident that it cannot be ignored, even by those who wish to deny it. The verse suggests that the Qur'an has a transformative power that can reach even the most hardened of hearts, if they are willing to open themselves to its guidance.
orig: كذلك سلكناه في قلوب المجرمين

translation: They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people will not believe in the message of the Qur'an or the warnings of the Hereafter until they actually experience the severe punishment that awaits those who reject faith. It implies that people often need to face the consequences of their actions before they are willing to accept the truth. The interpretation suggests that true faith should come from a sincere heart, not just from fear of punishment.
orig: لا يؤمنون به حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: And it will come to them suddenly while they perceive not.
interpretation: This verse refers to the suddenness and unexpectedness of the Day of Judgment. It suggests that the arrival of the Day of Judgment will catch people by surprise, as they will not be expecting it or prepared for it. The interpretation is that people should remain vigilant and ready for the inevitable arrival of the Day of Judgment, as it will come without warning.
orig: فيأتيهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And they will say, "Are we to be put in respite?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, who will be questioned about their denial of the truth and their rejection of faith. They will ask in a tone of surprise and disbelief whether they will be given more time or respite, implying that they were not fully aware of the consequences of their actions. This verse highlights the reality that on the Day of Judgment, there will be no more chances or delays, and the disbelievers will be held accountable for their choices in this life.
orig: فيقولوا هل نحن منظرون

translation: Then do they seek to hasten Our punishment?
interpretation: This verse is asking whether the disbelievers are hastening or demanding the punishment of Allah, as if they are eager for it to come. The implication is that they should not be so hasty, as Allah's punishment will come in due time and according to His wisdom. The verse serves as a warning to those who mock the message of Islam and challenge Allah's authority.
orig: أفبعذابنا يستعجلون

translation: Have you seen if We let them enjoy for years
interpretation: This verse is asking the reader to reflect on the temporary nature of worldly pleasures and luxuries. The verse suggests that even if people are allowed to enjoy a life of comfort and abundance for many years, it is ultimately fleeting and not a lasting source of true fulfillment. The implication is that one should not become overly attached to or rely on the temporary pleasures of this world, but rather focus on spiritual and eternal matters.
orig: أفرأيت إن متعناهم سنين

translation: Then there came to them that which they had been promised
interpretation: This verse refers to the eventual fulfillment of the promises and warnings that were given to the disbelievers. It suggests that the consequences they were warned about, whether blessings for the righteous or punishment for the wicked, will inevitably come to pass. The verse emphasizes the certainty of divine judgment and the inescapable nature of the consequences that await people based on their deeds and beliefs.
orig: ثم جاءهم ما كانوا يوعدون

translation: And of no avail to them will be whatever they used to enjoy.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the fate of those who disbelieved and rejected the message of God. It suggests that on the Day of Judgment, the worldly pleasures and possessions they had enjoyed in this life will be of no use or benefit to them. Their temporary enjoyment of material things will not save them from the consequences of their disbelief and wrongdoing. The verse emphasizes that true success and salvation can only be found through faith and righteous deeds, not through the mere accumulation of wealth and worldly pleasures.
orig: ما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يمتعون

translation: And We have not destroyed any city but that it had warners
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has always sent messengers and warners to every community to guide them towards the right path. He does not punish a people without first sending them a warner to remind them of their obligations and the consequences of their actions. This is a sign of Allah's mercy and justice, as He does not hold people accountable without first providing them with guidance and the opportunity to reform themselves.
orig: وما أهلكنا من قرية إلا لها منذرون

translation: A reminder, and We were not unjust.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that Allah's judgments are not unjust, but rather fair and righteous. It suggests that Allah's actions, even if they may seem difficult or challenging to us, are ultimately just and not a result of wrongdoing on His part. The verse emphasizes that Allah is not unjust, and that any perceived injustice is a result of our own limited understanding, not a reflection of Allah's true nature.
orig: ذكرى وما كنا ظالمين

translation: And the devils have not brought it down [i.e., the Qur'an]
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an was not brought down by the devils or evil spirits, but rather by the divine revelation from Allah. It serves to refute the claim made by the disbelievers that the Qur'an was the work of the devils or sorcerers, and to establish the Qur'an as a divine scripture revealed by Allah to the Prophet Muhammad.
orig: وما تنزلت به الشياطين

translation: And it is not for them, nor can they [ever]
interpretation: This verse suggests that there are certain things that are not appropriate or befitting for people, and there are also things that they are not capable of doing. It implies that there are limits to human abilities and that we should not overstep our bounds or try to achieve what is beyond our reach. The verse encourages us to be realistic and humble in our aspirations and actions, and to recognize the limitations of our human condition.
orig: وما ينبغي لهم وما يستطيعون

translation: Indeed, they [i.e., the disbelievers] are, about the Hearing, sequestered [from it].
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers are deaf to the truth and guidance of the Qur'an. They are isolated and cut off from hearing and understanding the divine message, either due to their arrogance, stubbornness, or spiritual blindness. The verse emphasizes that they have willfully turned away from the Hearing, which refers to the Qur'an and the guidance it provides.
orig: إنهم عن السمع لمعزولون

translation: So do not invoke with Allah another deity [or object of worship] or you will be among the punished.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping only Allah and not associating any other deities or objects with Him. It warns against the grave consequences of polytheism, which is the belief in or worship of multiple gods. The verse instructs the believers to refrain from worshiping any other deity besides Allah, as that would lead to punishment in the Hereafter. The interpretation underscores the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of God (tawheed) and the rejection of idolatry or associating partners with Allah.
orig: فلا تدع مع الله إلها آخر فتكون من المعذبين

translation: And warn your closest kindred.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to warn his closest relatives and family members about the consequences of disbelief and the importance of accepting Islam. It emphasizes the responsibility of the Prophet to convey the divine message to those closest to him, as they are the ones who will be most affected by his teachings. The verse highlights the importance of spreading the message of Islam within one's own community and family, as they are the ones who will be most receptive to the message.
orig: وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين

translation: And lower your wing to those who follow you of the believers
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to be gentle and humble towards the believers who follow him. It encourages a compassionate and inclusive approach in guiding and leading the believers, rather than a harsh or authoritarian one. The metaphor of "lowering your wing" suggests a protective and nurturing attitude, like a parent towards their child. This verse emphasizes the importance of humility, empathy and care in the leadership and guidance of the faithful.
orig: واخفض جناحك لمن اتبعك من المؤمنين

translation: And if they disobey you, then say, "Indeed, I am disassociated from what you do."
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to disassociate himself from the actions of those who disobey him and reject his message. It emphasizes that the Prophet is not responsible for the misdeeds of those who refuse to follow his guidance. The interpretation suggests that when faced with opposition, one should maintain a clear stance and distance oneself from the wrongful actions of others, while continuing to convey the truth.
orig: فإن عصوك فقل إني بريء مما تعملون

translation: And put your trust in the Exalted in Might, the Merciful
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to put their trust and reliance in Allah, who is the Mighty and Compassionate. It reminds us that Allah is the ultimate source of power and that He is also the Most Merciful, caring for His creation. By trusting in Allah, we can find strength and comfort, even in the face of difficulties. This trust should lead us to submit to Allah's will and seek His guidance in all our affairs.
orig: وتوكل على العزيز الرحيم

translation: The One who sees you when you stand [for prayer]
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah, the Almighty, who is all-seeing and all-knowing. It emphasizes that Allah is aware of our every action, even the most private ones like standing for prayer. This serves as a reminder to the believer to be conscious of Allah's presence and to conduct themselves in a manner that pleases Him, as He is ever-watchful over us.
orig: الذي يراك حين تقوم

translation: And your turning among those who prostrate
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his movements and actions among the believers who prostrate themselves in prayer. It suggests that the Prophet was present and actively engaged with the worshippers, setting an example and leading them in their devotion to Allah.
orig: وتقلبك في الساجدين

translation: Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the All-Hearing and the All-Knowing. He hears and knows everything, including our thoughts, actions, and the innermost secrets of our hearts. This serves as a reminder that we are always accountable to Allah, and that we should strive to live our lives in a manner that is pleasing to Him.
orig: إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, implying that the devils descend upon those who listen to them and follow their whispers. The verse is a warning against falling prey to the temptations of the devils, who aim to lead people astray from the path of righteousness and guidance.
orig: هل أنبئكم على من تنزل الشياطين

translation: It descends upon every sinful liar.
interpretation: This verse refers to the revelation of the Qur'an, which is sent down upon every person who is deceitful and engages in sinful behavior. The verse emphasizes that the Qur'anic guidance is universal, applicable to all people, regardless of their moral state. It serves as a warning to those who are dishonest and engage in wrongdoing, that they are not exempt from the divine message and its consequences.
orig: تنزل على كل أفاك أثيم

translation: They listen to the [recitation of the] Qur'an, and most of them are liars.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who outwardly appear to listen to the Qur'an, but in reality, they do not believe in it or accept its teachings. They are hypocrites who pretend to be believers, but their actions and intentions are deceitful. The verse suggests that while many people may claim to listen to the Qur'an, the majority of them are actually liars who do not truly accept its message and guidance.
orig: يلقون السمع وأكثرهم كاذبون

translation: And the poets - [only] the deviators follow them,
interpretation: This verse suggests that the poets are often followed by those who have gone astray or been misguided. The implication is that the poetry of the time was not necessarily truthful or beneficial, but rather led people away from the right path. The Qur'an cautions against blindly following the poets and their words, and encourages seeking guidance from the divine revelation instead.
orig: والشعراء يتبعهم الغاوون

translation: Have you not considered how they stray in every valley?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that points to the aimless and directionless wandering of those who have turned away from the guidance of God. The imagery of "straying in every valley" suggests a lack of purpose, a lack of a clear path, and a sense of being lost. The verse is inviting the reader to reflect on the consequences of rejecting the truth and following one's own desires without a clear moral compass.
orig: ألم تر أنهم في كل واد يهيمون

translation: And they say what they do not do.
interpretation: This verse is a criticism of those who make claims or promises that they do not fulfill. It highlights the hypocrisy of saying one thing but doing another. The verse emphasizes the importance of aligning one's words and actions, and being true to one's commitments.
orig: وأنهم يقولون ما لا يفعلون

translation: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and remember Allah often and defend themselves after being wronged. And those who have wronged are going to know to what [kind of] return they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the only ones who will be saved from punishment are those who have true faith, do good deeds, remember Allah frequently, and defend themselves when wronged. It warns that those who have wronged others will face the consequences of their actions and learn the outcome of their misdeeds.
orig: إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وذكروا الله كثيرا وانتصروا من بعد ما ظلموا وسيعلم الذين ظلموا أي منقلب ينقلبون

translation: Ta. Sin. These are the verses of the Qur'an and a clear Book
interpretation: This verse introduces the Qur'an as a clear and self-evident book of guidance revealed by God. The letters "Ta" and "Sin" at the beginning are part of the mysterious letters (al-Muqatta'at) that appear at the start of some Quranic chapters, the precise meaning of which is not definitively known. The verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a "clear Book" (kitabun mubin), meaning it is a divine scripture that provides clear and unambiguous guidance for humanity.
orig: طس تلك آيات القرآن وكتاب مبين

translation: Guidance and good tidings for the believers
interpretation: This verse is describing the Quran as a source of guidance and good news for those who believe in God and follow His teachings. The Quran provides direction and reassurance for the faithful, leading them towards righteous living and the promise of eternal reward in the Hereafter.
orig: هدى وبشرى للمؤمنين

translation: Those who establish prayer and give zakah, and they are certain of the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of true believers. It states that the believers are those who regularly perform their obligatory prayers (salat) and pay the purifying alms (zakah) due on their wealth. Additionally, they have firm conviction and certainty in the life of the Hereafter, where they will be held accountable for their actions in this world. This verse emphasizes the importance of both righteous deeds and unwavering faith in the Afterlife as essential components of a believer's spiritual life.
orig: الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم بالآخرة هم يوقنون

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter - We have made pleasing to them their deeds, so they wander blindly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the state of those who reject belief in the Afterlife. It suggests that their worldly actions and pursuits have been made attractive to them, causing them to be misguided and wander aimlessly, without a clear sense of purpose or accountability. The implication is that without the guiding light of faith in the Hereafter, people can become lost in the pursuit of fleeting pleasures and worldly gains, failing to recognize the true meaning and consequences of their actions.
orig: إن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة زينا لهم أعمالهم فهم يعمهون

translation: Those are the ones who will have the worst of punishment, and in the Hereafter they will be the greatest losers.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who have rejected faith and done evil deeds. They will face the worst punishment in the Hereafter, and they will be the greatest losers as they have lost the opportunity to attain eternal bliss and salvation. The verse emphasizes the severe consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing, and the importance of seeking guidance and doing good in order to secure a favorable outcome in the Hereafter.
orig: أولئك الذين لهم سوء العذاب وهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون

translation: And indeed, [O Muhammad], you receive the Qur'an from [the presence of] the Wise, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from the All-Wise and All-Knowing God. It emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, which is not the product of human authorship, but rather a revelation from the Almighty. The attributes of "Wise" and "Knowing" highlight the perfection and completeness of the Qur'an, as it comes from the One who possesses absolute wisdom and knowledge. This verse serves to strengthen the believers' faith in the Qur'an as the word of God, revealed to guide humanity.
orig: وإنك لتلقى القرآن من لدن حكيم عليم

translation: When Moses said to his family, "Indeed, I have perceived a fire. I will bring you from there information or will bring you a burning branch that you may warm yourselves."
interpretation: This verse describes a pivotal moment in the life of the Prophet Moses. While traveling with his family, Moses notices a fire in the distance and decides to investigate it. This event marks the beginning of Moses' prophetic mission, as he is about to encounter God and receive the divine call to lead the Israelites out of Egypt. The verse highlights Moses' curiosity and willingness to explore the unknown, which ultimately leads him to a transformative spiritual experience. The interpretation suggests that sometimes the most significant moments in our lives arise unexpectedly, and it is our openness to explore and seek guidance that can lead us to profound and life-changing encounters.
orig: إذ قال موسى لأهله إني آنست نارا سآتيكم منها بخبر أو آتيكم بشهاب قبس لعلكم تصطلون

translation: And when he came to it, he was called, "O Moses, indeed I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa. And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed [to you].
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when Moses approached the burning bush and heard the voice of God calling out to him. The key message here is that God has chosen Moses to be His messenger, and that Moses should listen attentively to the revelations that will be given to him. The verse emphasizes the sacredness of the place and the fact that God is the Lord of all the worlds.
orig: فلما جاءها نودي أن بورك من في النار ومن حولها وسبحان الله رب العالمين

translation: O Moses, indeed, it is I - the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse is spoken by God to the prophet Moses, affirming His divine attributes of power and wisdom. The verse emphasizes that God is the Almighty, the All-Wise, and that Moses should heed His commands and guidance. It is a reminder of God's sovereignty and the importance of submitting to His will.
orig: يا موسى إنه أنا الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: And throw down your staff!" And when he saw it writhing as if it were a snake, he turned in flight and did not look back. [Allah said], "O Moses, do not fear. Indeed, in My presence the messengers do not fear.
interpretation: This verse describes the miracle of Moses, where he is commanded to throw down his staff, and it transforms into a snake. This event is a sign of God's power and Moses' prophethood. The interpretation is that even in the face of such a miraculous and awe-inspiring sight, Moses initially recoiled in fear. However, God reassures him that the messengers need not fear in His presence, as He will protect them. This highlights God's omnipotence and the importance of faith and trust in Him, even when confronted with extraordinary circumstances.
orig: وألق عصاك فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان ولى مدبرا ولم يعقب يا موسى لا تخف إني لا يخاف لدي المرسلون

translation: Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work. For them Allah will replace their evil deeds with good. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and forgiveness. It indicates that those who have committed wrongdoings but then repent, believe, and do good deeds, will have their sins replaced with good deeds. This emphasizes that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, and that He readily accepts the repentance of those who turn back to Him in sincerity.
orig: إلا من ظلم ثم بدل حسنا بعد سوء فإني غفور رحيم

translation: And put your hand into your bosom; it will come forth white without disease - as another sign, That We may show you [some] of Our greater signs.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the miracle that Allah granted to Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) as a sign to Pharaoh and his people. When Moses put his hand into his garment, it would emerge shining white, without any blemish or disease. This was one of the nine signs that Allah commanded Moses to show to Pharaoh and his people, in order to prove the truth of his message and call them to worship Allah alone. However, despite these clear signs, Pharaoh and his people persisted in their disbelief and disobedience, for they were a wicked and rebellious people.
orig: وأدخل يدك في جيبك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء في تسع آيات إلى فرعون وقومه إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: And when Our visible signs came to them, they said, "This is a clear magic."
interpretation: This verse refers to the reaction of the disbelievers when they were presented with clear and undeniable signs and miracles from God. Instead of acknowledging the truth, they dismissed them as "clear magic", refusing to accept the divine origin of these signs. This highlights the tendency of some to reject the truth even in the face of overwhelming evidence, out of arrogance, stubbornness, or a desire to maintain their existing beliefs and worldview.
orig: فلما جاءتهم آياتنا مبصرة قالوا هذا سحر مبين

translation: And they rejected them, while their [own] souls were convinced by them, out of injustice and arrogance. So see how was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who deny the truth of God's revelations and signs, despite being inwardly convinced of their veracity. Their rejection is driven by injustice and arrogance, rather than reason or faith. The verse warns that the ultimate fate of such "corrupters" will be dire, inviting the reader to reflect on how their end will unfold.
orig: وجحدوا بها واستيقنتها أنفسهم ظلما وعلوا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المفسدين

translation: And We had certainly given to David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, "Praise [is due] to Allah, who has favored us over many of His believing servants."
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah granted knowledge and wisdom to the prophets David and Solomon. They recognized that this was a blessing from Allah and expressed gratitude, acknowledging that Allah had favored them over many of His believing servants. This teaches us to be thankful for the blessings and knowledge that Allah bestows upon us, and to recognize that it is a privilege that not everyone is granted.
orig: ولقد آتينا داوود وسليمان علما وقالا الحمد لله الذي فضلنا على كثير من عباده المؤمنين

translation: And Solomon inherited David. And he said, "O people, we have been taught the speech of birds, and we have been given from all things. This is indeed a clear bounty."
interpretation: This verse highlights the great knowledge and wisdom that was bestowed upon the Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him). He inherited the prophethood and the kingdom from his father, the Prophet David (peace be upon him). The verse then states that Solomon was taught the language of the birds, which is a metaphor for his ability to understand the speech and communication of all creatures. This signifies the depth of his knowledge and the extensive nature of the blessings he received from God. The verse concludes by emphasizing that this knowledge and these blessings are indeed a clear and manifest favor from God.
orig: وورث سليمان داوود وقال يا أيها الناس علمنا منطق الطير وأوتينا من كل شيء إن هذا لهو الفضل المبين

translation: And gathered for Solomon were his soldiers from the jinn and from the men and from the birds, and they were [marching] in rows.
interpretation: This verse describes how Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him) had a vast army composed of jinn (supernatural beings), humans, and birds, all organized and marching in an orderly fashion. This highlights Solomon"s immense power and authority, which was granted to him by God. The verse suggests that Solomon had control over a diverse range of creatures, demonstrating his wisdom and ability to command a multitude of forces.
orig: وحشر لسليمان جنوده من الجن والإنس والطير فهم يوزعون

translation: Until, when they came to the valley of the ants, an ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings that you not be crushed by Solomon and his soldiers while they perceive not."
interpretation: This verse describes a scene where Prophet Solomon and his army are passing through the valley of the ants. An ant, perceiving the approaching army, warns its fellow ants to take shelter in their dwellings to avoid being trampled upon. The interpretation suggests that even the smallest of creatures are under the protection of God, and that Prophet Solomon, despite his great power and authority, is mindful of not causing harm to them unintentionally. This highlights the importance of compassion and consideration for all of God's creation.
orig: حتى إذا أتوا على واد النمل قالت نملة يا أيها النمل ادخلوا مساكنكم لا يحطمنكم سليمان وجنوده وهم لا يشعرون

translation: Then he smiled, amused at her speech, and said, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve. And admit me by Your mercy into [the company of] Your righteous servants."
interpretation: This verse depicts the Prophet Solomon's reaction to the words of the Queen of Sheba. He is amused by her speech, but then humbly turns to God, asking for the ability to be grateful for the blessings God has bestowed upon him and his parents, and to do righteous deeds that are pleasing to God. He also asks God to admit him, through His mercy, into the company of the righteous servants. This verse highlights the importance of gratitude, righteousness, and seeking God's pleasure and mercy, even for the most powerful of God's prophets.
orig: فتبسم ضاحكا من قولها وقال رب أوزعني أن أشكر نعمتك التي أنعمت علي وعلى والدي وأن أعمل صالحا ترضاه وأدخلني برحمتك في عبادك الصالحين

translation: And he took stock of the birds and said, "Why do I not see the hoopoe - or is he among the absent?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him) taking an account of the birds under his command. He noticed the absence of the hoopoe (a type of bird) and inquired about its whereabouts, wondering if it was simply missing or had not shown up for some reason. This highlights Solomon's keen awareness and oversight of the creatures under his authority, as well as his desire to have all of them present and accounted for.
orig: وتفقد الطير فقال ما لي لا أرى الهدهد أم كان من الغائبين

translation: I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or I will surely slaughter him or let him bring me a clear authorization [from Allah].
interpretation: This verse expresses the threat and warning of a powerful ruler or tyrant towards a person who has defied his authority. The three options presented - severe punishment, slaughter, or providing clear authorization from Allah - suggest the ruler’s determination to deal harshly with the perceived transgression. The verse highlights the abuse of power and the lack of mercy, as well as the importance of seeking divine legitimacy for one’s actions.
orig: لأعذبنه عذابا شديدا أو لأذبحنه أو ليأتيني بسلطان مبين

translation: And he stayed not long, and he said: I have compassed that which thou hast not compassed, and I have come unto thee from Sheba with sure tidings.
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur’an, Surah An-Naml (The Ant), verse 22. It is spoken by the hoopoe bird, who had been sent by Prophet Sulaiman (Solomon) to gather information. The hoopoe is reporting back to Sulaiman that it has discovered something that Sulaiman was not aware of, and that it has brought him certain news from the land of Sheba. The interpretation suggests that the hoopoe, through its keen observation and investigation, has gained knowledge that surpasses even that of the wise Prophet Sulaiman, and is now sharing this newfound information with him.
orig: فمكث غير بعيد فقال أحطت بما لم تحط به وجئتك من سبإ بنبإ يقين

translation: Indeed, I found [there] a woman ruling them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Queen of Sheba, who ruled over her people with wisdom and authority. The verse highlights that she had been granted abundant resources and a powerful position, symbolized by her "great throne". This suggests that even in a patriarchal society, a woman could rise to a position of significant political and economic power through her own merits and capabilities.
orig: إني وجدت امرأة تملكهم وأوتيت من كل شيء ولها عرش عظيم

translation: And I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from the [right] way, so they are not guided,
interpretation: This verse describes the prophet finding a people who were worshipping the sun instead of Allah. The verse indicates that Satan has made their actions seem appealing to them, and has led them astray from the right path, so that they are not guided towards the truth.
orig: وجدتها وقومها يسجدون للشمس من دون الله وزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم فصدهم عن السبيل فهم لا يهتدون

translation: Do they not prostrate to Allah, who brings forth what is hidden within the heavens and the earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme power and knowledge of Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. It calls upon people to prostrate and submit to Allah, who has the ability to bring forth what is hidden and concealed, and who is aware of all that is hidden and all that is openly declared by His creation. This highlights the need for humility and acknowledgment of Allah's sovereignty and omniscience.
orig: ألا يسجدوا لله الذي يخرج الخبء في السماوات والأرض ويعلم ما تخفون وما تعلنون

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Lord of the Great Throne.
interpretation: This verse affirms the oneness and sovereignty of Allah. It establishes that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah, the Almighty Lord who reigns over the entire universe. This verse emphasizes the supreme power and authority of Allah, the Creator and Sustainer of all things.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو رب العرش العظيم

translation: He (Pharaoh) said, "We will see whether you have told the truth or are of the liars."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Al-Naml, verse 27. It is a response by Pharaoh to Prophet Moses, after Moses had presented his miracles as proof of his prophethood. Pharaoh's statement reflects his arrogance and unwillingness to accept the truth, as he demands to "see" whether Moses is truthful or a liar. This verse highlights the stubborn rejection of the truth by those who are blinded by their own ego and desire for power.
orig: قال سننظر أصدقت أم كنت من الكاذبين

translation: Go with this letter of mine and cast it upon them. Then turn away from them and see what [response] they will return.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to deliver a message to his opponents, then observe their reaction and response. It suggests that the Prophet should not be discouraged by their initial reaction, but rather wait and see how they ultimately react to the message. The verse encourages patience, detachment and observation in the face of opposition, rather than confrontation.
orig: اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم ثم تول عنهم فانظر ماذا يرجعون

translation: She (the Queen of Sheba) said, "O eminent ones, indeed there has been delivered to me a noble letter."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the Queen of Sheba upon receiving a letter from the Prophet Solomon. She acknowledges the importance and nobility of the letter, indicating that she recognizes the authority and wisdom of the one who sent it. This sets the stage for her subsequent interaction with Solomon and her eventual acceptance of his message and faith.
orig: قالت يا أيها الملأ إني ألقي إلي كتاب كريم

translation: Indeed, it is from Solomon, and indeed, it is [i.e., reads], "In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, and it is describing a letter that was sent by the Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him). The verse emphasizes that the letter originated from Solomon, and that it begins with the invocation "In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful." This opening is a common formula used in Islamic texts to seek the blessings and guidance of Allah at the start of any endeavor. The interpretation suggests that Solomon's actions and communications were done in the name of Allah and with the recognition of Allah's mercy and compassion.
orig: إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

translation: Do not exalt yourselves above me and come to me in submission.
interpretation: This verse is a command from God to the people, instructing them not to be arrogant or consider themselves superior to God, but rather to submit to Him in complete obedience and humility. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing God's supreme authority and the need for people to surrender themselves to His will.
orig: ألا تعلوا علي وأتوني مسلمين

translation: She (the Queen of Sheba) said, "O eminent ones, advise me in my affair. I would not decide a matter until you witness [for] me."
interpretation: This verse describes the Queen of Sheba seeking counsel from her advisors before making an important decision. She recognizes the value of seeking guidance and input from those around her, rather than acting unilaterally. This demonstrates wisdom, humility, and a desire to make a well-informed choice that has the support of her people. The interpretation is that leaders should seek counsel and not make important decisions alone, but rather involve those who can provide valuable perspectives and insight.
orig: قالت يا أيها الملأ أفتوني في أمري ما كنت قاطعة أمرا حتى تشهدون

translation: They said, "We are people of strength and of great might, and the command is thine, so see what thou wilt command."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur"an, and it is part of a larger narrative about the Prophet Musa (Moses) and his confrontation with the Pharaoh. The verse represents the response of the Pharaoh"s people to Musa"s call to worship the one true God. They boast of their strength and power, and they challenge Musa to do as he pleases, confident in their own might. This verse highlights the arrogance and defiance of those who reject the message of God, and it serves as a warning to those who would oppose the truth. The interpretation is that true power and might come from submitting to the will of God, not from relying on one"s own strength and resources.
orig: قالوا نحن أولو قوة وأولو بأس شديد والأمر إليك فانظري ماذا تأمرين

translation: She said: "Verily, when kings enter a town, they despoil it, and make the most honorable amongst its people the lowest. And thus they do."
interpretation: This verse refers to the tendency of powerful rulers and kings to abuse their authority and oppress the people when they conquer a new territory. They often plunder the wealth of the land, subjugate the local population, and demean the status of the respected and influential members of the society. This verse serves as a warning against the corrupting influence of power and the need to guard against the misuse of authority.
orig: قالت إن الملوك إذا دخلوا قرية أفسدوها وجعلوا أعزة أهلها أذلة وكذلك يفعلون

translation: And indeed, I am sending to them a gift and will see [what will be] the response of the messengers.
interpretation: This verse is from the story of the Queen of Sheba, who upon hearing about the wisdom and power of Prophet Solomon, decides to send him a gift to test his status. The verse expresses the Queen's intention to send a gift to Prophet Solomon and observe how he and his messengers will respond to it. This highlights the Queen's curiosity and desire to understand the true nature of Prophet Solomon's prophethood and authority.
orig: وإني مرسلة إليهم بهدية فناظرة بم يرجع المرسلون

translation: And when Solomon came, he said, "Do you intend to help me with wealth? But what Allah has given me is better than what He has given you. Rather, it is you who rejoice in your gift."
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and gratitude of Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him).
