When the people tried to impress him with their wealth and gifts, he reminded them that the blessings he has received from Allah are far greater than any material wealth. He acknowledged that their gifts, though impressive, are not as valuable as the spiritual and worldly blessings bestowed upon him by Allah. This teaches us to be grateful for Allah's favors and not to be distracted by the material possessions of others, for true wealth and success come from Allah alone.
orig: فلما جاء سليمان قال أتمدونن بمال فما آتاني الله خير مما آتاكم بل أنتم بهديتكم تفرحون

translation: Return to them, so We will surely bring forth to them soldiers [from the angels] whom they will not be able [to defeat], and they will be humbled.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the enemies of the believers who are arrogant and refuse to submit to the truth. Allah promises to send down His forces, which the disbelievers will not be able to withstand, and they will be forced to submit in a state of humiliation and disgrace.
orig: ارجع إليهم فلنأتينهم بجنود لا قبل لهم بها ولنخرجنهم منها أذلة وهم صاغرون

translation: He (Solomon) said, "O assembly [of jinn], which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?"
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah An-Naml (The Ant), verse 38. It describes a scene from the story of Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him) and the Queen of Sheba. Solomon, who had been gifted with the ability to understand the speech of birds and animals, challenges the assembly of jinn (supernatural creatures) to bring him the throne of the Queen of Sheba before she and her people come to him in submission. This demonstrates Solomon's power and wisdom, as he seeks to establish his authority over the Queen of Sheba's kingdom without confrontation, and to bring her to the true faith of Islam.
orig: قال يا أيها الملأ أيكم يأتيني بعرشها قبل أن يأتوني مسلمين

translation: A jinni of the [lower] world said, "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed, I am for that [task] strong and trustworthy."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, specifically Surah An-Naml (The Ant), verse 39. It describes a powerful jinni (a supernatural being) who boasts that he can bring the throne of the Queen of Sheba to the Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him) before he even stands up from his place. The jinni is expressing his confidence in his ability to accomplish this task quickly and reliably. This verse highlights the power and abilities of the jinn, who were created by Allah alongside humans and angels, and were sometimes commanded to assist the Prophets in their missions.
orig: قال عفريت من الجن أنا آتيك به قبل أن تقوم من مقامك وإني عليه لقوي أمين

translation: He who had knowledge of the Scripture said: "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." And when [Solomon] saw it placed before him, he said, "This is from the favor of my Lord to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful - his gratitude is only for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever is ungrateful - then indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous."
interpretation: This verse describes a scene where someone with knowledge of the Scripture promises to bring something to Solomon before he blinks. When Solomon sees it, he realizes it is a favor from his Lord, meant to test whether he will be grateful or ungrateful. The interpretation is that gratitude is for one's own benefit, while ingratitude does not diminish God's wealth and generosity. The verse emphasizes that true gratitude is an expression of one's own spiritual state, not a reflection on God.
orig: قال الذي عنده علم من الكتاب أنا آتيك به قبل أن يرتد إليك طرفك فلما رآه مستقرا عنده قال هذا من فضل ربي ليبلوني أأشكر أم أكفر ومن شكر فإنما يشكر لنفسه ومن كفر فإن ربي غني كريم

translation: He said, "Disguise her throne for her, we will see whether she will be guided or will be of those who are not guided."
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Prophet Sulaiman (Solomon) and the Queen of Sheba. It describes how Sulaiman wanted to test the Queen's wisdom and faith by disguising her throne, to see if she would recognize it or be misguided. The interpretation is that Sulaiman was trying to assess the Queen's intelligence, perceptiveness and spiritual guidance - whether she would be able to discern the truth or would be among those who are lost and unable to find the right path.
orig: قال نكروا لها عرشها ننظر أتهتدي أم تكون من الذين لا يهتدون

translation: And when she came, it was said, "Is your throne like this?" She said, "It is as though it was the same. And [our people] were submitted to Allah before me, and I was among the disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse describes the arrival of the Queen of Sheba to meet Prophet Solomon. When she saw the grand throne that Solomon had, she recognized its similarity to her own throne, acknowledging that she and her people had already submitted to Allah before this meeting. This indicates that she had prior knowledge of monotheism and the worship of the one true God, even though she had previously been among the disbelievers. The verse highlights her willingness to accept the truth of Islam after witnessing the power and wisdom of Prophet Solomon.
orig: فلما جاءت قيل أهكذا عرشك قالت كأنه هو وأوتينا العلم من قبلها وكنا مسلمين

translation: And it (the Fire) hindered her from (worshipping) what she used to worship besides Allah. Verily, she was of the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of the wife of Prophet Lut (Lot), who was punished along with the disbelieving people of Sodom and Gomorrah for her disbelief in Allah and her rejection of the message brought by her husband. The verse emphasizes that she was hindered from worshipping the false deities she used to worship, as she was a disbeliever who refused to accept the true faith in Allah.
orig: وصدها ما كانت تعبد من دون الله إنها كانت من قوم كافرين

translation: It was said to her, "Enter the palace." But when she saw it, she thought it was a body of water and uncovered her shins [to wade through]. [Solomon] said, "Indeed, it is a palace [whose floor is] made smooth with glass." [She said], "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon to Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse describes the encounter between Queen Sheba and Prophet Solomon. When she was invited to enter the palace, she mistook the smooth glass floor for water and uncovered her legs to wade through it. However, Solomon clarified that it was a palace made of glass. This incident led Queen Sheba to realize her error and acknowledge her wrongdoing, and she submitted herself to the worship of Allah, the Lord of the worlds, along with Prophet Solomon.
orig: قيل لها ادخلي الصرح فلما رأته حسبته لجة وكشفت عن ساقيها قال إنه صرح ممرد من قوارير قالت رب إني ظلمت نفسي وأسلمت مع سليمان لله رب العالمين

translation: And We had certainly sent to Thamud their brother Salih, [saying], "Worship Allah," but at once they were two parties conflicting.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah sent the prophet Salih to the people of Thamud, calling them to worship Allah alone. However, instead of heeding his message, the people of Thamud divided into two conflicting factions - those who believed in Salih's message and those who rejected it. This highlights the importance of unity in faith and the danger of division and discord within a community when it comes to matters of religion and belief.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا إلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا أن اعبدوا الله فإذا هم فريقان يختصمون

translation: He said, 'O my people, why do you hasten to [bring about] evil before [achieving] the good? Why do you not seek forgiveness of Allah that you may receive mercy?'
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of the prophet Shu'ayb, who was sent to the people of Madyan. He is advising his people not to rush towards evil deeds before doing good deeds, and instead to seek forgiveness from Allah so that they may receive His mercy. The verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness as a means to attain Allah's mercy and guidance.
orig: قال يا قوم لم تستعجلون بالسيئة قبل الحسنة لولا تستغفرون الله لعلكم ترحمون

translation: They said, "We augur ill of you and those with you." He said, "Your [i.e., your omen] is with Allah. Rather, you are a people being tried."
interpretation: The disbelievers accused the Prophet Muhammad and his followers of being a bad omen, bringing misfortune and calamity. The Prophet responded by saying that their fate is in the hands of Allah, and that they are being tested and tried by Allah through the message of Islam.
orig: قالوا اطيرنا بك وبمن معك قال طائركم عند الله بل أنتم قوم تفتنون

translation: And there were in the city nine [who were] causes of corruption in the land and would not reform.
interpretation: This verse refers to a group of nine people in a city who were causing harm and disruption in the land, and were unwilling to reform their ways. The Qur'an is highlighting the presence of those who spread corruption and refuse to improve themselves or their actions, which is a warning against such behavior and a call to work towards positive change in society.
orig: وكان في المدينة تسعة رهط يفسدون في الأرض ولا يصلحون

translation: They said, "Take a mutual oath by Allah that we will attack him and his family by night, and then we will say to his protector, 'We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed, we are truthful.'"
interpretation: This verse describes a conspiracy by a group of people to secretly attack and destroy the family of someone they consider an enemy. They plan to then claim innocence and deny any involvement in the attack, swearing an oath by Allah to support their lie. The interpretation suggests that this verse condemns such deceptive and treacherous behavior, where people are willing to resort to violence and false oaths to achieve their aims, rather than seeking justice through proper channels.
orig: قالوا تقاسموا بالله لنبيتنه وأهله ثم لنقولن لوليه ما شهدنا مهلك أهله وإنا لصادقون

translation: And they plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot, while they perceived not.
interpretation: This verse refers to the attempts of the disbelievers to undermine and harm the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. However, Allah (God) also devised a plan to protect and support the Prophet and the believers, which the disbelievers were unaware of. This verse emphasizes that Allah's plan is always superior to the plans of those who seek to harm the believers, and that He will ultimately prevail over their schemes.
orig: ومكروا مكرا ومكرنا مكرا وهم لا يشعرون

translation: So see how was the end of their plot - indeed, We destroyed them and [all of] their people, all together.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who plot and scheme against the believers. It reminds us that the ultimate outcome of such plots and schemes is destruction, as Allah has the power to utterly destroy those who oppose Him and His message. The verse encourages us to reflect on the fate of those who have gone before, and to learn from their example. It serves as a reminder that no one can escape the consequences of their actions, and that those who seek to harm the believers will ultimately face the wrath of Allah.
orig: فانظر كيف كان عاقبة مكرهم أنا دمرناهم وقومهم أجمعين

translation: So those are their houses, desolate because of the wrong they had done. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of those who committed injustice and wrongdoing. Their houses were left in ruins and desolate as a consequence of their misdeeds. This serves as a lesson and a sign for those who have knowledge and understanding, reminding them that wrongful actions have consequences and that justice will prevail.
orig: فتلك بيوتهم خاوية بما ظلموا إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يعلمون

translation: And We saved those who believed and were fearing Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God protects and saves those who have faith in Him and strive to live righteously. It suggests that belief in God and piety are the keys to attaining divine protection and deliverance from hardship. The verse implies that faith and God-consciousness are the foundations for a life of security and well-being.
orig: وأنجينا الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: And [We had sent] Lot when he said to his people, "Do you commit such immorality while you are seeing [i.e., aware]?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the prophet Lot, who was sent to the people of Sodom and Gomorrah. He admonished his people for engaging in the sin of homosexuality, which is considered a grave moral transgression in Islam. The verse emphasizes that the people were aware of the immorality of their actions, yet they persisted in them. This highlights the importance of upholding moral and ethical standards, even in the face of societal pressures or personal desires.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه أتأتون الفاحشة وأنتم تبصرون

translation: Do you indeed approach men with desire instead of women? Rather, you are a people behaving ignorantly.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of homosexuality, which was prevalent in some communities at the time. It emphasizes that the natural and intended order is for sexual relations to be between men and women, and that engaging in homosexual acts is a sign of ignorance and deviation from the natural order. The verse serves as a moral and spiritual guidance, calling people to follow the righteous path and avoid behaviors that are considered sinful and harmful to individuals and society.
orig: أئنكم لتأتون الرجال شهوة من دون النساء بل أنتم قوم تجهلون

translation: And the answer of his people was not but that they said, "Expel the family of Lot from your city. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."
interpretation: This verse describes the response of the people of Lot to his call to worship God alone. Instead of accepting his message, they demanded that Lot and his family be expelled from their city, accusing them of trying to purify themselves from their immoral practices. This highlights the stubborn rejection of the truth by those who are engrossed in their sinful ways and unwilling to change their ways.
orig: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا أخرجوا آل لوط من قريتكم إنهم أناس يتطهرون

translation: And We saved him and his family, except his wife; We destined her to be of those who remained behind.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the prophet Lot (peace be upon him) and his people. When Lot warned his people against their immoral practices, they rejected his message. As a result, God destroyed the town, but saved Lot and his family, except for his wife, who was destined to perish with the rest of the disbelievers. This verse emphasizes that even close family members may not be spared from divine punishment if they persist in their wrongdoing and reject the truth.
orig: فأنجيناه وأهله إلا امرأته قدرناها من الغابرين

translation: And We rained down upon them a [torrential] rain, and evil was the rain of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment that was inflicted upon the people who were warned but did not heed the warnings. The "torrential rain" is a metaphor for the severe and devastating consequences that befell them as a result of their disbelief and disobedience. The interpretation is that those who are warned but persist in their wrongdoing will face a terrible fate, just as the people in this verse experienced.
orig: وأمطرنا عليهم مطرا فساء مطر المنذرين

translation: Say, "Praise be to Allah, and peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen." Is Allah better or what they associate with Him?
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to praise and glorify Allah, and to acknowledge the blessings He has bestowed upon those whom He has chosen as His servants. It also poses a rhetorical question, challenging the notion of associating partners with Allah, as Allah is clearly superior and more deserving of worship than any other being or entity.
orig: قل الحمد لله وسلام على عباده الذين اصطفى آلله خير أما يشركون

translation: Is not He (better than your gods) Who created the heavens and the earth, and sends down for you water (rain) from the sky, wherewith We cause to grow wonderful gardens full of beauty and delight? It is not in your ability to cause the growth of the trees in them. (Is there any god with Allah?) Nay, but they are a people who ascribe equals (to Him).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and sovereignty of God as the sole Creator of the heavens and the earth, and the provider of life-sustaining resources like water. It contrasts this with the inability of any other deity or being to create or sustain the natural world, which is a testament to God's uniqueness and the foolishness of associating partners with Him. The verse invites the reader to reflect on the signs of God's power and providence, and to worship Him alone as the one true God.
orig: أمن خلق السماوات والأرض وأنزل لكم من السماء ماء فأنبتنا به حدائق ذات بهجة ما كان لكم أن تنبتوا شجرها أإله مع الله بل هم قوم يعدلون

translation: Is He [not best] who has made the earth a stable ground and placed within it rivers and made for it mountains and placed between the two seas a barrier? Is there a deity with Allah? [No], but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and wisdom of Allah in creating the earth and its various features. The mention of the earth being a "stable ground" suggests that it is a secure and dependable place for life to exist. The presence of rivers, mountains, and the barrier between the two seas demonstrates Allah's intricate design and control over the natural world. The rhetorical question "Is there a deity with Allah?" challenges the notion of any other divine being, emphasizing the uniqueness and supremacy of Allah. The verse concludes by noting that most people are unaware of this truth, implying the importance of recognizing and worshiping Allah alone.
orig: أمن جعل الأرض قرارا وجعل خلالها أنهارا وجعل لها رواسي وجعل بين البحرين حاجزا أإله مع الله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Is He [not best] who responds to the desperate one when he calls upon Him and removes evil and makes you inheritors of the earth? Is there a deity with Allah? Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and mercy of Allah, the one true God. It contrasts the ability of Allah to respond to those in distress, relieve their suffering, and make them inheritors of the earth, with the idea of there being any other deity worthy of worship alongside Allah. The verse encourages people to remember and reflect on the greatness of Allah, as they tend to do so only rarely.
orig: أمن يجيب المضطر إذا دعاه ويكشف السوء ويجعلكم خلفاء الأرض أإله مع الله قليلا ما تذكرون

translation: Is He [not best] who guides you through the darknesses of the land and sea and who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy? Is there a deity with Allah? Exalted is Allah above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and sovereignty of Allah, the one true God. It highlights how Allah guides and directs His creation, whether it be on land or sea, and how He sends the winds as a sign of His mercy and bounty. The verse then poses a rhetorical question, asking if there is any other deity worthy of worship besides Allah, the Exalted. This is a strong affirmation of the oneness and supremacy of Allah, and a rejection of associating partners with Him.
orig: أمن يهديكم في ظلمات البر والبحر ومن يرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته أإله مع الله تعالى الله عما يشركون

translation: Is not He (far better) who begins the creation, then repeats it, and who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Is there a deity with Allah? Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of polytheism and affirms the oneness of God. It highlights that the true God is the one who initiates and sustains all creation, providing for humanity from the heavens and the earth. The verse calls upon the disbelievers to provide evidence for their claim of other deities alongside God, emphasizing that true faith must be based on clear and rational proofs.
orig: أمن يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ومن يرزقكم من السماء والأرض أإله مع الله قل هاتوا برهانكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except Allah, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that only Allah, the Almighty, has knowledge of the unseen and the future. It is a reminder that humans, despite their efforts and knowledge, do not possess the ability to know the unseen or the exact time of the Resurrection. This verse encourages humility and a recognition of the limitless power and knowledge of Allah, the Creator of all things.
orig: قل لا يعلم من في السماوات والأرض الغيب إلا الله وما يشعرون أيان يبعثون

translation: Nay, their knowledge of the Hereafter is but scant. Nay, they are in doubt about it. Nay, they are blind to it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being addressed have only limited knowledge of the Hereafter, and are doubtful and uncertain about it. They are described as being "blind" to the reality of the Hereafter, indicating that they are unable or unwilling to see and understand the truth of the afterlife. The repetition of "nay" emphasizes the contrast between their limited understanding and the certainty of the Hereafter.
orig: بل ادارك علمهم في الآخرة بل هم في شك منها بل هم منها عمون

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "When we have become dust and our forefathers, will we indeed be brought forth [into new creation]?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and disbelief of those who reject the concept of resurrection and the afterlife. They question how it is possible that after they have turned to dust, they will be brought back to life. This reflects a lack of understanding and faith in the power of God, who has the ability to create and recreate all things.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا أإذا كنا ترابا وآباؤنا أئنا لمخرجون

translation: We and our fathers were promised this before. This is not but legends of the former peoples.
interpretation: This verse expresses the skepticism of the disbelievers towards the message of the Quran, claiming that it is not a divine revelation but rather "legends of the former peoples". The verse suggests that the disbelievers had heard similar messages before from their ancestors, and they dismissed them as mere "legends" or fabrications. The implication is that the Quran is being rejected on the basis of prejudice and a refusal to consider it objectively, rather than on the basis of reasoned examination of its content.
orig: لقد وعدنا هذا نحن وآباؤنا من قبل إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: Say, 'Travel through the land and observe how was the end of the criminals.'
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the fate of those who committed crimes and transgressions against God and humanity. By observing the consequences that befell the wrongdoers, one can learn valuable lessons and be deterred from following a similar path. The verse emphasizes the importance of critical thinking, introspection, and drawing lessons from historical events to understand the divine justice and the ultimate fate of those who choose to defy God's commands.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المجرمين

translation: And do not grieve over them or be in distress over what they conspire.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to be saddened or distressed by the plots and schemes of his opponents. It reminds him that he should not worry about their machinations, as Allah is in control and will protect him. The verse teaches us to have faith in Allah and not to be overly concerned with the actions of those who seek to harm us, as Allah is the ultimate protector and will guide us through any difficulties.
orig: ولا تحزن عليهم ولا تكن في ضيق مما يمكرون

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers who deny the promise of the Resurrection and the Day of Judgment. They challenge the believers, asking when this promise will come to pass, doubting its veracity. The interpretation is that the disbelievers are arrogantly questioning the truth of the Quranic teachings regarding the Hereafter, seeking to undermine the faith of the believers.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "Perhaps your Lord will give you something of what you are waiting for."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have patience and trust in Allah's plan. It suggests that what they are eagerly awaiting may come to pass, but in Allah's own time. The verse reminds us not to be hasty, but to have faith that Allah will provide in the way that is best for us, even if it does not align with our own expectations or timeline.
orig: قل عسى أن يكون ردف لكم بعض الذي تستعجلون

translation: And indeed, your Lord is full of bounty for the people, but most of them do not show gratitude.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah (God) is extremely generous and benevolent towards all people, providing them with countless blessings and favors. However, most people fail to recognize and appreciate these blessings, and do not express gratitude to Allah for all that they have been given. The verse encourages believers to be thankful and appreciative of Allah's grace and mercy, in contrast to those who remain ungrateful.
orig: وإن ربك لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثرهم لا يشكرون

translation: And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Lord, has complete knowledge and awareness of the innermost thoughts, intentions, and actions of people. He knows what they hide in their hearts as well as what they openly express and reveal. This affirms Allah's omniscience and serves as a reminder that we cannot hide anything from Him, and that we will be held accountable for our thoughts and deeds.
orig: وإن ربك ليعلم ما تكن صدورهم وما يعلنون

translation: And there is nothing hidden in the heavens and the earth but it is [recorded] in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of God, who has knowledge of all things in the universe, both visible and invisible. The "clear register" refers to the divine knowledge and record that encompasses all of creation. This highlights the idea that nothing escapes the sight and knowledge of God, who is all-knowing and all-seeing.
orig: وما من غائبة في السماء والأرض إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel most of that about which they disagree.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Qur'an provides detailed information about many of the disputes and disagreements that arose among the Children of Israel regarding various religious and spiritual matters. The Qur'an serves as a guide and clarification of these issues, shedding light on the differences that existed within the Jewish community and providing the correct understanding from the divine perspective.
orig: إن هذا القرآن يقص على بني إسرائيل أكثر الذي هم فيه يختلفون

translation: And indeed, it (the Qur'an) is a guidance and a mercy for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a source of divine guidance and a manifestation of Allah's mercy towards those who believe in it. The Qur'an provides direction for the believers, leading them on the path of righteousness and salvation. It also serves as a means of Allah's compassion and benevolence, offering solace, comfort, and spiritual nourishment to the faithful.
orig: وإنه لهدى ورحمة للمؤمنين

translation: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them by His judgment, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Lord of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), is the one who will judge between people on the Day of Judgment. His judgment is based on His wisdom and knowledge, and He is the Almighty, the All-Knowing. This verse serves as a reminder that the ultimate authority and justice reside with Allah, and that He alone has the power and wisdom to judge all of humanity.
orig: إن ربك يقضي بينهم بحكمه وهو العزيز العليم

translation: So rely upon Allah. Indeed, you are upon the clear truth.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension all believers, to place their trust and reliance in Allah alone. It assures them that they are following the clear and evident truth, and that they should have confidence in Allah's guidance and support. The interpretation is that one should have unwavering faith in Allah and not be swayed by doubts or the opinions of others, for the path of truth is clear and evident to those who believe.
orig: فتوكل على الله إنك على الحق المبين

translation: Indeed, you do not make hear the dead, nor do you make hear the deaf the call when they have turned, retreating.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) cannot guide or influence those who have turned away from the truth and have become spiritually dead or deaf to the call of faith. It is a reminder that guidance ultimately comes from Allah, and the Prophet can only convey the message - the acceptance or rejection of it lies with the individual.
orig: إنك لا تسمع الموتى ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ولوا مدبرين

translation: And you are not [responsible] to guide the blind from their error. You will only hear from those who believe in Our verses so they [themselves] will submit [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad is not responsible for guiding those who are spiritually blind and have strayed from the truth. The guidance can only be accepted by those who believe in the verses and signs of Allah, and willingly submit to Him. The verse highlights that faith and acceptance of the divine message is a prerequisite for guidance, and that the Prophet's role is to convey the message, not to force it upon those who are unwilling to believe.
orig: وما أنت بهادي العمي عن ضلالتهم إن تسمع إلا من يؤمن بآياتنا فهم مسلمون

translation: And when the word [i.e., decree] befalls them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them, [saying] that the people were, of Our signs, not certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse suggests that when the time of judgment arrives, Allah will bring forth a creature from the earth to confront the disbelievers and testify against them. This creature will speak to the people, informing them that they had rejected the clear signs and proofs of Allah's existence and sovereignty, and thus were not firm in their faith. The appearance of this creature is a sign of the coming of the Day of Judgment, when all will be held accountable for their beliefs and actions.
orig: وإذا وقع القول عليهم أخرجنا لهم دابة من الأرض تكلمهم أن الناس كانوا بآياتنا لا يوقنون

translation: And the Day We will gather from every nation a [single] witness, and We will say, "Bring your proof," and they will know that the truth is with Allah, and lost from them is that which they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Judgment, when people from every community will be gathered and held accountable for their beliefs and actions. Those who rejected the signs and messages of Allah will be asked to present their proof or justification, but they will realize that the truth lies with Allah and that their false claims and inventions have been exposed.
orig: ويوم نحشر من كل أمة فوجا ممن يكذب بآياتنا فهم يوزعون

translation: Until, when they come [before Him], [Allah] will say, "Did you deny My signs while you encompassed them not in knowledge, or what [was it that] you were doing?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when people will be held accountable for their actions in life. The verse suggests that some individuals may have denied the signs and messages of Allah, despite lacking true understanding and knowledge of them. The question "what [was it that] you were doing?" implies that their actions were not based on genuine comprehension, but rather on ignorance, arrogance, or other misguided motivations. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding the signs of Allah, rather than simply rejecting them out of hand.
orig: حتى إذا جاءوا قال أكذبتم بآياتي ولم تحيطوا بها علما أماذا كنتم تعملون

translation: And the word will have been decreed upon them for what they wronged, so they will not [be able to] speak.
interpretation: This verse indicates that on the Day of Judgment, those who committed wrongdoing will be held accountable and will not be able to defend themselves or make excuses for their actions. Their silence will be a testament to the justice of Allah's judgment, as they will be unable to deny or justify their misdeeds.
orig: ووقع القول عليهم بما ظلموا فهم لا ينطقون

translation: Have they not seen that We have made the night that they may rest therein, and the day sight-giving? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom and power of God in creating the alternation of night and day. The night is created for people to rest and find peace, while the day is made to provide light and vision. This pattern is a clear sign of God's design and a testament to His sovereignty for those who believe and reflect on His creation.
orig: ألم يروا أنا جعلنا الليل ليسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], the Day when the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified except whom Allah wills. And all will come to Him humbled.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Resurrection, when the trumpet will be blown to signal the end of the world. All beings in the heavens and on earth, except those whom Allah wills to be spared, will be seized with terror and will come before Allah in a state of humility and submission.
orig: ويوم ينفخ في الصور ففزع من في السماوات ومن في الأرض إلا من شاء الله وكل أتوه داخرين

translation: And you see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they will pass as the passing of clouds. [It is] the work of Allah, who perfected all things. Indeed, He is Acquainted with that which you do.
interpretation: This verse encourages us to reflect on the power and majesty of Allah, the Creator. The mountains, which appear to be rigid and immovable, are in fact passing away like clouds in the sky. This serves as a reminder that all things in this world are temporary and subject to change, and that only Allah is eternal and unchanging. The verse also emphasizes that Allah has created all things with perfection and wisdom, and that He is aware of all that we do. This should inspire us to live our lives in a way that is pleasing to Allah, and to trust in His plan for us.
orig: وترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمر مر السحاب صنع الله الذي أتقن كل شيء إنه خبير بما تفعلون

translation: Whoever comes [to Allah] with a good deed will have better than it, and they will be secure from the [overwhelming] terror of that Day.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to do good deeds, as they will be rewarded with something even better in the afterlife. Those who do good will be protected from the fear and anxiety of the Day of Judgment, as they will be "secure from the [overwhelming] terror of that Day". The verse emphasizes the importance of righteous actions and the promise of divine reward for those who strive to please Allah.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها وهم من فزع يومئذ آمنون

translation: And whoever comes with an evil deed - their faces will be overturned into the Fire. [And it will be said], "Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who commit evil deeds will be punished in the Hereafter. Their faces will be cast down into the Fire, and they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a warning to people to refrain from evil and instead do good deeds, as they will be recompensed accordingly on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ومن جاء بالسيئة فكبت وجوههم في النار هل تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who has made it sacred and to whom all things belong, and I have been commanded to be of those who submit [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental duty of a believer, which is to worship and submit to the One true God, the Lord of all creation. It highlights that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was commanded by God to worship the Lord of Mecca, the city that God has made sacred. This verse also affirms that everything belongs to God, and that the ultimate purpose of a believer is to submit to the will of God and become of those who willingly surrender themselves to Him.
orig: إنما أمرت أن أعبد رب هذه البلدة الذي حرمها وله كل شيء وأمرت أن أكون من المسلمين

translation: And that I may recite the Qur'an. And whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul. And whoever goes astray - [then] say, "I am only [one] of the warners."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the guidance provided by the Qur'an is for the benefit of the individual. Those who choose to follow the guidance will do so for their own spiritual and moral development, while those who reject it are responsible for their own misguidance. The Prophet's role is to convey the message as a warner, not to compel belief. The verse encourages personal responsibility and discourages coercion in matters of faith.
orig: وأن أتلو القرآن فمن اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ومن ضل فقل إنما أنا من المنذرين

translation: And say, "Praise to Allah. He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to praise and glorify Allah, as He will reveal His signs and wonders to them, allowing them to recognize His power, wisdom and majesty. It also emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of the actions and deeds of His creation, and that nothing escapes His knowledge and oversight. This serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their conduct, as Allah is ever-present and observing their activities.
orig: وقل الحمد لله سيريكم آياته فتعرفونها وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون

translation: Ta. Sin. Mim.
interpretation: These are letters from the Arabic alphabet, known as the 'Muqatta'at' or 'Isolated Letters', which appear at the beginning of some chapters of the Quran. The precise meaning and purpose of these letters is not definitively known, but they are believed to have symbolic or mystical significance, and to represent the divine nature and attributes of God.
orig: طسم

translation: These are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Qur'an, which is described as the "clear Book". The Qur'an contains clear and unambiguous signs, messages, and guidance from Allah for humanity. The term "these" in the verse indicates that the verses that follow are part of the Qur'an, which is a revelation that provides clarity, wisdom, and direction for those who seek to understand and follow the teachings of Islam.
orig: تلك آيات الكتاب المبين

translation: We relate to you, [O Muhammad], from the news of Moses and Pharaoh in truth for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse is informing the Prophet Muhammad that he will be reciting to the people the story of Moses and Pharaoh, which is a true and important narrative for those who have faith. The story of Moses and Pharaoh serves as a lesson and example for the believers, highlighting the conflict between truth and falsehood, and the ultimate triumph of righteousness over tyranny.
orig: نتلو عليك من نبإ موسى وفرعون بالحق لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions, oppressing a sector among them, slaughtering their [newborn] sons and keeping their females alive. Indeed, he was of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse describes the tyrannical rule of Pharaoh over the Israelites in Egypt. Pharaoh abused his power, oppressed the Israelites, and committed heinous acts such as killing their newborn sons while keeping their daughters alive. This verse portrays Pharaoh as a corrupt and oppressive ruler who sought to subjugate and control the Israelites for his own gain, rather than serving the people justly. The verse condemns Pharaoh's actions as those of a corrupter and oppressor.
orig: إن فرعون علا في الأرض وجعل أهلها شيعا يستضعف طائفة منهم يذبح أبناءهم ويستحيي نساءهم إنه كان من المفسدين

translation: And We want to confer favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them inheritors
interpretation: This verse expresses Allah's desire to bestow honor and leadership upon those who were previously oppressed and marginalized in society. The interpretation suggests that Allah intends to empower the weak and downtrodden, elevating them to positions of authority and making them the inheritors of the land. This reflects the Qur'anic principle of justice and the uplifting of the oppressed.
orig: ونريد أن نمن على الذين استضعفوا في الأرض ونجعلهم أئمة ونجعلهم الوارثين

translation: And We gave [strength] to Pharaoh and his soldiers through [their] wealth and children, and they were [thus] distracted.
interpretation: This verse highlights how worldly possessions and power can distract people from the remembrance of God. Pharaoh and his people were given wealth and authority, but they became arrogant and neglected their spiritual obligations. This serves as a warning that material success should not make one forget one's duty to the Creator.
orig: ونمكن لهم في الأرض ونري فرعون وهامان وجنودهما منهم ما كانوا يحذرون

translation: And We inspired to the mother of Moses, "Suckle him; but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him [one] of the messengers."
interpretation: This verse describes how God inspired the mother of Moses to suckle him, but when she feared for his safety, she was instructed to cast him into the river. God reassured her not to fear or grieve, as He would return Moses to her and make him one of the messengers. This highlights God's divine plan and protection for the prophet Moses, even from an early age. The mother's act of faith and trust in God's will is emphasized, as she obediently follows the divine command despite her natural maternal concerns.
orig: وأوحينا إلى أم موسى أن أرضعيه فإذا خفت عليه فألقيه في اليم ولا تخافي ولا تحزني إنا رادوه إليك وجاعلوه من المرسلين

translation: And the family of Pharaoh picked him up [out of the river] so that he would become to them an enemy and a [cause of] grief. Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers were deliberate sinners.
interpretation: This verse describes how the family of Pharaoh rescued the infant Moses from the river, not realizing that he would later become their enemy and a source of grief for them. The verse highlights the sinful nature of Pharaoh, Haman, and their armies, who were destined to be punished for their oppression and rejection of God's message.
orig: فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا إن فرعون وهامان وجنودهما كانوا خاطئين

translation: And the wife of Pharaoh said, "[He is] a comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son." And they perceived not.
interpretation: This verse describes the wife of Pharaoh pleading with her husband not to kill the infant Moses. She saw the child as a blessing and potential benefit to them, even suggesting they could adopt him as their own son. Her compassion and wisdom in this moment stood in contrast to Pharaoh's cruelty and paranoia, highlighting the moral complexities within the power structures of Pharaoh's household.
orig: وقالت امرأت فرعون قرت عين لي ولك لا تقتلوه عسى أن ينفعنا أو نتخذه ولدا وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And the heart of Moses' mother became empty [of patience or content]. She was about to disclose [the matter concerning] him had We not bound her heart that she would be of the believers.
interpretation: This verse describes the emotional state of Moses' mother after she had to hide her newborn son to protect him from Pharaoh's decree to kill all newborn boys. The verse conveys her inner turmoil and the difficulty of keeping such an important secret, to the point where she nearly revealed her son. However, God strengthened her faith and resolve, allowing her to remain steadfast in her belief and trust in God's plan, even in the face of such a challenging situation.
orig: وأصبح فؤاد أم موسى فارغا إن كادت لتبدي به لولا أن ربطنا على قلبها لتكون من المؤمنين

translation: And she said to his sister, "Follow him"; so she watched him from a distance while they perceived not.
interpretation: This verse describes the story of Moses' birth, when his mother placed him in a basket and sent his sister to follow and watch over him as he floated down the river. The interpretation is that this verse highlights the care and protection of a mother for her child, as well as the watchful eye of the sister who followed to ensure his safety, all while remaining unseen by those who sought to harm him.
orig: وقالت لأخته قصيه فبصرت به عن جنب وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And We had forbidden him [breastfeeding] foster mothers before, so she said, "Shall I direct you to a household that will be responsible for him for you while they are to him [i.e., the child] sincere advisors?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) as a child. After being placed in the river by his mother to protect him from Pharaoh's decree, he was found and raised by Pharaoh's family. However, God had forbidden Moses from being nursed by foster mothers before, so his mother devised a plan to have him returned to her to be nursed. The verse describes how she offered to find a household that would care for and advise the child sincerely, leading to Moses being returned to his own mother to be nursed.
orig: وحرمنا عليه المراضع من قبل فقالت هل أدلكم على أهل بيت يكفلونه لكم وهم له ناصحون

translation: And We restored him to his mother that she might be comforted and not grieve and that she might know that the promise of Allah is true. But most of them [i.e., the people] do not know.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Moses, where he was returned to his mother after being taken away as a child. The interpretation is that Allah restores what is dear to us, even after difficult trials, in order to comfort us, alleviate our grief, and affirm that His promises are true. However, most people do not fully understand or appreciate this divine wisdom.
orig: فرددناه إلى أمه كي تقر عينها ولا تحزن ولتعلم أن وعد الله حق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And when he reached maturity and was [mentally] complete, We gave him judgement and [religious] knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse describes the life of the Prophet Musa (Moses), peace be upon him. It indicates that when he reached adulthood and his faculties were fully developed, Allah granted him wisdom and knowledge. This is a sign of Allah's favor and a reward for Musa's righteous conduct. The verse teaches that Allah rewards those who do good deeds and strive to please Him.
orig: ولما بلغ أشده واستوى آتيناه حكما وعلما وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And he entered the city at a time of inattention of its people and found therein two men fighting: one from his faction and one from his enemy. And the one from his faction called for help against the one from his enemy, so Moses struck him and [unintentionally] killed him. [Moses] said, "This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is an enemy [to mankind], clear in his deception."
interpretation: This verse describes an incident where Moses (peace be upon him) unintentionally killed a man who was fighting with another person. The verse highlights how Satan can instigate conflict and violence between people, even those who are allies. The interpretation is that we should be wary of Satan's schemes to divide us and promote enmity, and instead seek to resolve disputes through peaceful means.
orig: ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من أهلها فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان هذا من شيعته وهذا من عدوه فاستغاثه الذي من شيعته على الذي من عدوه فوكزه موسى فقضى عليه قال هذا من عمل الشيطان إنه عدو مضل مبين

translation: He said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me." And He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness from Allah. The person in the verse acknowledges that he has wronged himself, and humbly asks Allah for forgiveness. The verse then states that Allah forgave him, emphasizing that Allah is the Forgiving and Merciful. This teaches us that no matter how grave our sins may be, if we sincerely repent and ask Allah for forgiveness, He will forgive us, for He is the Most Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: قال رب إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي فغفر له إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: He (Musa) said: "O my Lord! Because You have bestowed Your Grace on me, I shall never be a helper for the Mujrimun (criminals, disbelievers, polytheists, sinners, etc.)"
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) is expressing his gratitude to Allah for the blessings and guidance he has received. He declares that because of Allah's favor upon him, he will never support or assist the wrongdoers, criminals, or those who disbelieve in Allah. This demonstrates Moses' firm commitment to righteousness and his unwavering loyalty to Allah, even in the face of potential pressure or temptation to side with the unjust. The verse highlights the importance of gratitude, steadfastness, and a strong moral compass in the life of a believer.
orig: قال رب بما أنعمت علي فلن أكون ظهيرا للمجرمين

translation: And he became fearful in the city, looking around, when suddenly the one who had sought his help the day before was crying out to him. [Moses] said to him, "Indeed, you are an evident, [persistent] deviator."
interpretation: This verse describes Moses' experience after he had killed an Egyptian. He became fearful in the city, looking around nervously, when the same man he had helped the day before was now calling out to him for help. Moses rebuked him, calling him an "evident, [persistent] deviator", meaning that the man was clearly misguided and persistent in his wrongdoing. This highlights how one\'s good deed can be met with ingratitude, and how the righteous can face persecution even from those they have helped.
orig: فأصبح في المدينة خائفا يترقب فإذا الذي استنصره بالأمس يستصرخه قال له موسى إنك لغوي مبين

translation: But when he intended to strike the one who was an enemy to them both, he said, "O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed someone yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land and do not want to be of the amenders."
interpretation: This verse describes a scene where Moses (peace be upon him) was about to strike someone who was an enemy to both him and the person he was speaking to. The person then reminds Moses of his previous act of killing someone, and accuses him of wanting to be a tyrant in the land rather than being one who seeks to amend and improve things. The interpretation is that this verse highlights the importance of restraint, wisdom and seeking to reform and improve society, rather than resorting to violence and oppression, even when dealing with one's enemies.
orig: فلما أن أراد أن يبطش بالذي هو عدو لهما قال يا موسى أتريد أن تقتلني كما قتلت نفسا بالأمس إن تريد إلا أن تكون جبارا في الأرض وما تريد أن تكون من المصلحين

translation: And there came a man from the farthest end of the city, running. He said, "O Moses, indeed the eminent ones are conspiring against you to kill you, so leave [the city]; indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors."
interpretation: This verse describes a man who comes running from the outskirts of the city to warn Moses (peace be upon him) that the leaders of the people are plotting to kill him. The man is portrayed as a sincere advisor, urging Moses to leave the city for his own safety. This highlights the presence of those who are willing to stand up for the truth and protect the righteous, even in the face of powerful opposition. The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the advice of those who truly wish to guide and support us, even when the circumstances seem dire.
orig: وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى قال يا موسى إن الملأ يأتمرون بك ليقتلوك فاخرج إني لك من الناصحين

translation: And he left it, fearful and vigilant. He said, "My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse describes Moses' departure from Egypt after he had killed a man inadvertently. He was fearful of the consequences and vigilant, hoping to escape the wrath of the Pharaoh and his people. In his distress, he turned to God, pleading for salvation from the wrongdoers, recognizing his own vulnerability and the need for divine intervention.
orig: فخرج منها خائفا يترقب قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين

translation: And when he turned his face toward Madyan, he said, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the sound way."
interpretation: This verse describes the Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) turning his face towards the land of Madyan after fleeing from Egypt. In this moment of uncertainty, he expresses his hope and trust in Allah, saying "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the sound way." This demonstrates Moses' humility and reliance on Allah, seeking divine guidance and direction in the face of an unknown future. The verse highlights the importance of turning to Allah in times of difficulty and uncertainty, and trusting that He will provide the right path forward.
orig: ولما توجه تلقاء مدين قال عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل

translation: And when he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found thereat a crowd of people watering [their flocks], and he found aside from them two women driving back [their flocks]. He said, "What is your circumstance?" They said, "We do not water [our flocks] until the shepherds dispatch [their flocks]; and our father is an old man."
interpretation: This verse describes Prophet Moses' (peace be upon him) encounter with two women at the water source in Madyan. The verse highlights the social customs and norms of the time, where women were not expected to water their flocks alongside the men. The two women were waiting for the male shepherds to finish watering their flocks before they could do so. This shows the respect for social hierarchy and the deference given to the elder men in the community. The verse also suggests the vulnerability of the two women, as they needed to wait for the men to finish before they could water their own flocks. Moses' concern for their situation and his willingness to help them demonstrates his compassion and sense of justice.
orig: ولما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان قال ما خطبكما قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء وأبونا شيخ كبير

translation: Then he watered (their flocks) for them; then he turned back to the shade and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need."
interpretation: This verse describes a prophet (traditionally identified as Moses) who came upon two women tending their flocks and helped them by watering their animals. He then withdrew to the shade and prayed to Allah, acknowledging his need for Allah's provision and blessings. The interpretation is that even the righteous prophets recognize their dependence on God and humbly ask for His help and sustenance.
orig: فسقى لهما ثم تولى إلى الظل فقال رب إني لما أنزلت إلي من خير فقير

translation: Then one of the two women came to him, walking with shyness. She said, "Indeed, my father invites you that he may reward you for having watered for us." And when he came to him and related to him the story, [Moses] said, "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse describes an encounter between Prophet Moses and one of the daughters of the Prophet Shu'aib. After Moses helped the women by watering their flocks, one of the daughters came to him and invited him to meet her father, who wanted to reward Moses for his kindness. The verse emphasizes that the daughter approached Moses with shyness, indicating her modesty and propriety. Moses then went with her and recounted the story to her father, who reassured Moses that he no longer needed to fear the wrongdoers from whom he had fled. This episode highlights the virtues of kindness, hospitality, and protection that are encouraged in Islamic teachings.
orig: فجاءته إحداهما تمشي على استحياء قالت إن أبي يدعوك ليجزيك أجر ما سقيت لنا فلما جاءه وقص عليه القصص قال لا تخف نجوت من القوم الظالمين

translation: One of the two [women] said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Al-Qasas, verse 26. It describes an incident where one of the two daughters of Prophet Shu'aib (peace be upon him) recommends to her father to hire Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) as a shepherd, describing him as "the strong and the trustworthy". This highlights the importance of hiring individuals based on their competence and integrity, rather than on other superficial factors. The interpretation suggests that when seeking to employ someone, one should prioritize the person's strength, capability, and trustworthiness, as these are the most important qualities that will ensure the successful completion of the task at hand.
orig: قالت إحداهما يا أبت استأجره إن خير من استأجرت القوي الأمين

translation: He said, "Indeed, I wish to wed you one of these, my two daughters, on [the condition] that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be [as a favor] from you. And I do not wish to put you in difficulty. You will find me, if Allah wills, from among the righteous."
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Prophet Moses and the shepherd he met in Midian. The shepherd offers to marry one of his daughters to Moses if Moses agrees to work for him for 8 years. The shepherd expresses his desire to make the arrangement easy for Moses, and states that he hopes Moses will find him to be a righteous and upright person. This verse highlights the shepherd's generosity, fairness and piety in his dealings with Moses.
orig: قال إني أريد أن أنكحك إحدى ابنتي هاتين على أن تأجرني ثماني حجج فإن أتممت عشرا فمن عندك وما أريد أن أشق عليك ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين

translation: He said, "That [is agreed upon] between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I complete - there is no injustice to me, and Allah, over what we say, is Witness."
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) and the pious servant of Allah, as narrated in the Qur’an. It refers to an agreement made between them regarding the duration of Moses’ employment with the pious servant. The verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one’s commitments and maintaining justice in dealings, with Allah as the Witness over all that is said and done.
orig: قال ذلك بيني وبينك أيما الأجلين قضيت فلا عدوان علي والله على ما نقول وكيل

translation: And when Moses had completed the term and was traveling with his family, he perceived from the direction of the Mount [Sinai] a fire. He said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you from there [some] information or a burning fire log that you may warm yourselves."
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when Moses, after completing his time in Midian, was traveling with his family and perceived a fire from the direction of Mount Sinai. The verse highlights Moses' curiosity and concern for his family, as he asks them to wait while he investigates the fire, with the hope of bringing them information or a burning log to warm themselves. This event marks the beginning of Moses' encounter with God and his subsequent mission to free the Israelites from Pharaoh's oppression.
orig: فلما قضى موسى الأجل وسار بأهله آنس من جانب الطور نارا قال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر أو جذوة من النار لعلكم تصطلون

translation: And when he came to it, [a voice] was called from the right side of the valley in the blessed spot of the tree, "O Moses, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the Worlds."
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when Moses, while tending to his family's sheep, encounters the divine presence at the sacred site of the burning bush. The voice that calls out to him from the blessed spot affirms that he is in the presence of God, the Lord of all creation. This marks the beginning of Moses' prophetic mission, as God chooses him to lead the Israelites out of Egypt.
orig: فلما أتاها نودي من شاطئ الواد الأيمن في البقعة المباركة من الشجرة أن يا موسى إني أنا الله رب العالمين

translation: And [it was said], "Throw down your staff." But when he saw it writhing as if it was a snake, he turned in flight and did not return. [Allah said], "O Moses, fear not. Indeed, in My presence the messengers do not fear."
interpretation: This verse describes a miraculous event that occurred when God commanded Moses to throw down his staff. The staff transformed into a snake, causing Moses to flee in fear. However, God reassured Moses that he need not be afraid, as the messengers of God are protected in His presence. This event is a demonstration of God's power and a sign to Moses of his prophethood, as well as a reminder that the messengers of God are under His protection and should not fear.
orig: وأن ألق عصاك فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان ولى مدبرا ولم يعقب يا موسى أقبل ولا تخف إنك من الآمنين

translation: And put your hand into your bosom; it will come forth white without disease - another sign, That We may show you [some] of Our greater signs.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the miracles given to the prophet Moses as signs to Pharaoh and his people. The first miracle is when Moses puts his hand into his garment, and it comes out shining white, without any disease or blemish. This is a sign of God's power and Moses' prophethood. The second miracle is when Moses spreads his wing or arm, which is a sign of God's protection and support for him. These two miracles are meant to convince Pharaoh and his people of the truth of Moses' message, but they stubbornly rejected it, being a "wicked people".
orig: اسلك يدك في جيبك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء واضمم إليك جناحك من الرهب فذانك برهانان من ربك إلى فرعون وملئه إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: He said: "My Lord! I have killed a person from among them, and I fear that they will kill me."
interpretation: This verse is from the story of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) in the Qur'an. It describes a situation where Moses accidentally killed a person, and he was afraid that the people would retaliate and kill him in turn. The verse highlights Moses' sense of responsibility and his fear of the consequences of his action, even though it was unintentional. This teaches us that we should be mindful of our actions and their potential impact, and seek forgiveness and guidance from Allah when we make mistakes.
orig: قال رب إني قتلت منهم نفسا فأخاف أن يقتلون

translation: And my brother Aaron - he is more fluent than I in speech, so send him with me as a helper to confirm me. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me.
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, where Moses is speaking to God and requesting that his brother Aaron be sent with him as a helper to assist in conveying God's message to Pharaoh. Moses expresses his fear that the people will not believe him, so he asks for Aaron's support in delivering the message effectively. The interpretation is that even the most righteous and chosen individuals can feel a sense of inadequacy or fear when faced with a daunting task, and seeking help from others is a sign of wisdom and humility.
orig: وأخي هارون هو أفصح مني لسانا فأرسله معي ردءا يصدقني إني أخاف أن يكذبون

translation: He said, "We will strengthen your arm through your brother and make for you a position of authority, so they will not be able to reach you because of Our signs. You and those who follow you will be the predominant."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Moses and Aaron, where God promises to empower and support them in their mission to confront Pharaoh. The interpretation is that God will provide the necessary authority and divine signs to ensure that Moses and Aaron, along with their followers, will prevail over their opponents. The key message is that with God's support, the righteous will ultimately triumph over those who reject the divine signs and guidance.
orig: قال سنشد عضدك بأخيك ونجعل لكما سلطانا فلا يصلون إليكما بآياتنا أنتما ومن اتبعكما الغالبون

translation: And when Moses came to them with Our clear signs, they said, "This is not but invented magic, and we have not heard of this [religion] among our forefathers."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of Pharaoh and his people when Moses came to them with clear signs and miracles from God. Instead of accepting the truth, they dismissed it as invented magic and something they had not heard of from their ancestors. This reflects their arrogance, stubbornness, and unwillingness to accept the new guidance brought by Moses, even in the face of undeniable evidence. The verse highlights the tendency of some people to reject the truth out of blind adherence to tradition and a refusal to consider new ideas, even when they are supported by clear proofs.
orig: فلما جاءهم موسى بآياتنا بينات قالوا ما هذا إلا سحر مفترى وما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين

translation: And Moses said, "My Lord is most knowing of who has come with guidance from Him and who will have the final home. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."
interpretation: This verse expresses Moses' trust in God\'s wisdom and judgment. Moses acknowledges that God knows best who has truly come with divine guidance, and who will ultimately be successful in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes that the wrongdoers, those who act unjustly, will not succeed or prosper, as God\'s justice will prevail.
orig: وقال موسى ربي أعلم بمن جاء بالهدى من عنده ومن تكون له عاقبة الدار إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And Pharaoh said, "O eminent ones, I have not known you to have a god other than me. So ignite for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay and make for me a tower that I may look at the God of Moses. And indeed, I do think he is among the liars."
interpretation: This verse depicts Pharaoh's arrogance and rejection of the concept of any deity other than himself. Pharaoh dismisses the idea of the God of Moses, claiming that he has not known of any other god, and commands his minister Haman to build him a tower so that he can personally inspect the God of Moses and determine if he is a liar. This verse highlights Pharaoh's pride, his refusal to acknowledge the sovereignty of God, and his attempt to challenge the divine authority through his own worldly power and ambition.
orig: وقال فرعون يا أيها الملأ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين فاجعل لي صرحا لعلي أطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه من الكاذبين

translation: And he (Pharaoh) and his soldiers behaved arrogantly in the land, without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us.
interpretation: This verse describes the arrogance and hubris of Pharaoh and his army, who believed that they were all-powerful and would never be held accountable for their actions. They acted with impunity in the land, oppressing the people, without any justification or right to do so. However, the verse indicates that they were mistaken in their belief that they would never have to return to God and face judgment for their misdeeds. This serves as a warning against arrogance and a reminder that all people will ultimately be held accountable for their choices and actions.
orig: واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق وظنوا أنهم إلينا لا يرجعون

translation: And We took him and his soldiers and cast them into the sea, and see how was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Pharaoh and his army being drowned in the sea after pursuing the Israelites. It serves as a lesson that those who oppress and wrong others will face a dire end. The verse encourages the reader to reflect on the fate of the wrongdoers and take heed, as God's justice will prevail in the end.
orig: فأخذناه وجنوده فنبذناهم في اليم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين

translation: And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse refers to the leaders and authorities who misguide people and call them towards wrongdoing and the path of destruction. They will not receive any assistance or support on the Day of Judgment, when they will be held accountable for their actions and the consequences they have brought upon themselves and others.
orig: وجعلناهم أئمة يدعون إلى النار ويوم القيامة لا ينصرون

translation: And We have made them a curse in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have rejected faith and turned away from the guidance of Allah. They have been made a curse in this world, meaning that they are shunned and their actions are condemned by others. On the Day of Judgment, they will be among the despised, facing the consequences of their disbelief and misdeeds. This serves as a warning to those who choose to reject the truth and turn away from the path of righteousness.
orig: وأتبعناهم في هذه الدنيا لعنة ويوم القيامة هم من المقبوحين

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, after We had destroyed the former generations, as enlightenment for the people and guidance and mercy that they might be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah had revealed the Scripture (the Torah) to Moses after destroying the previous generations of people. The purpose of this revelation was to provide enlightenment, guidance and mercy to the people, so that they may be reminded of Allah’s teachings and commandments and live accordingly.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب من بعد ما أهلكنا القرون الأولى بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And you were not at the western side when We decreed for Moses the command, and you were not among the witnesses.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not present when God gave the commandments to Moses (peace be upon him). The verse suggests that the Prophet Muhammad did not witness the events surrounding the revelation of the Torah to Moses, and therefore his knowledge of these events came through divine revelation rather than personal experience. This underscores the fact that the Qur'an is a revelation from God, not something the Prophet Muhammad composed himself.
orig: وما كنت بجانب الغربي إذ قضينا إلى موسى الأمر وما كنت من الشاهدين

translation: But We brought forth generations [in succession], and prolonged was their duration. And you were not a resident among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were the senders [of this revelation].
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has created and brought forth successive generations of people, and that the lifespans of these generations have been prolonged. It also states that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not physically present among the people of Madyan to recite the verses of the Quran to them, but rather, Allah was the one who sent this revelation to him.
orig: ولكنا أنشأنا قرونا فتطاول عليهم العمر وما كنت ثاويا في أهل مدين تتلو عليهم آياتنا ولكنا كنا مرسلين

translation: And you were not at the side of the Mount when We called [Moses], but [We sent you as] a mercy from your Lord to warn a people to whom no warner had come before you that they might remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad was not present at the time when God called Moses at Mount Sinai, but that he was sent as a mercy from God to warn a people who had not received a prophet before him. The purpose of this warning is to remind the people and encourage them to remember and reflect on God's message.
orig: وما كنت بجانب الطور إذ نادينا ولكن رحمة من ربك لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير من قبلك لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And if not that a disaster should strike them for what their hands have put forth [of sins], and they would say, "Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses and been among the believers?"
interpretation: This verse suggests that people often only turn to God and seek guidance when they are faced with a calamity or hardship. It implies that if people were not afflicted with difficulties, they may not feel the need to seek divine guidance and submit to God. The verse encourages people to be proactive in their faith and to follow the teachings of God's messengers, rather than waiting for a crisis to spur them into belief and obedience.
orig: ولولا أن تصيبهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم فيقولوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا فنتبع آياتك ونكون من المؤمنين

translation: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?" Did they not disbelieve in that which was given to Moses before? They say, "Two works of magic, supporting each other," and they say, "Indeed, we are disbelievers [in all of it]."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when the truth (the Qur'an) came to them from God. They questioned why the Prophet Muhammad was not given the same miracles as Moses, even though they had previously rejected the miracles given to Moses. They dismissed the Qur'an and the Prophet as "two works of magic" and declared their disbelief in all of it. This highlights the stubborn rejection of the truth by those whose hearts are hardened against it, despite the clear evidence presented to them.
orig: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا لولا أوتي مثل ما أوتي موسى أولم يكفروا بما أوتي موسى من قبل قالوا سحران تظاهرا وقالوا إنا بكل كافرون

translation: Say, "Then bring a scripture from Allah which is more guided than either of them that I may follow it, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who reject the Qur'an to produce a scripture that is more divinely guided than the Qur'an and the Torah, if they truly believe in their own claims. It calls on them to provide evidence for their position, rather than simply rejecting the Qur'an without offering a superior alternative. The verse emphasizes the need for truthfulness and substantive arguments in religious discourse.
orig: قل فأتوا بكتاب من عند الله هو أهدى منهما أتبعه إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But if they do not respond to you, [O Muhammad], then know that they only follow their [own] desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that if people refuse to heed the guidance and teachings of the Prophet Muhammad, they are simply following their own desires and whims, rather than seeking the truth. It highlights that the worst state is to follow one's own desires without any divine guidance, as this leads to misguidance and injustice. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah does not guide those who have wronged themselves by rejecting the truth.
orig: فإن لم يستجيبوا لك فاعلم أنما يتبعون أهواءهم ومن أضل ممن اتبع هواه بغير هدى من الله إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: And We have already conveyed the Word to them, that they may remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has already conveyed His message and guidance to the people, in the form of the Qur'an and through His Messengers. The purpose of this is to remind them and encourage them to reflect on the message, so that they may remember Allah, appreciate His blessings, and follow the path of righteousness.
orig: ولقد وصلنا لهم القول لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: Those to whom We have given the Book before this, - they believe in it (the Qur'an).
interpretation: This verse refers to the people who were given the previous scriptures, such as the Torah and the Gospel, and they believe in the Qur'an as well. It suggests that the Qur'an is a continuation and confirmation of the earlier divine revelations, and that those who are familiar with the previous scriptures can recognize the truth in the Qur'an. This verse encourages a harmonious relationship between the followers of different faiths who share a common belief in the divine origin of their scriptures.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب من قبله هم به يؤمنون

translation: And when it is recited to them, they say, "We have believed in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were, [even] before it, among the Muslims."
interpretation: This verse highlights the response of people when the Qur'an is recited to them. They acknowledge that it is the truth from their Lord, and that they had already submitted to God (i.e., were Muslims) even before the revelation of the Qur'an. This suggests that the Qur'an is in harmony with the innate human disposition to believe in and worship one God, and that those who have an open and sincere heart will readily accept it as the truth.
orig: وإذا يتلى عليهم قالوا آمنا به إنه الحق من ربنا إنا كنا من قبله مسلمين

translation: Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured and [because] they avert evil with good, and from what We have provided them they spend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the rewards that believers will receive in the Hereafter for their good deeds and patient endurance. The "twice" reward suggests that they will be compensated not only for their righteous actions, but also for their ability to respond to evil with goodness. Furthermore, the verse emphasizes that the believers utilize the provisions they have been given by God to engage in charitable spending and benevolent acts. This demonstrates their gratitude, faith, and commitment to pleasing God.
orig: أولئك يؤتون أجرهم مرتين بما صبروا ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it and say, "For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace will be upon you; we seek not the ignorant."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to turn away from and avoid engaging with frivolous, idle or harmful speech. It emphasizes that each person is responsible for their own actions and deeds, and that believers should maintain a peaceful and respectful attitude, not seeking out or engaging with the ignorant or those who speak ill.
orig: وإذا سمعوا اللغو أعرضوا عنه وقالوا لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم سلام عليكم لا نبتغي الجاهلين

translation: Indeed, [O Muhammad], you do not guide whom you wish, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that guidance is in the hands of Allah alone.
