The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not the one who guides people, but rather it is Allah who guides whomever He wills. This is a reminder that the Prophet's role is to convey the message, but the ultimate decision to accept it and be guided rests with the individual. Allah knows best who will accept the guidance and who will not, and He directs His guidance accordingly.
orig: إنك لا تهدي من أحببت ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: And they say, "If we were to follow the guidance with you, we would be swept from our land." Have We not established for them a safe sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the skepticism and resistance of the disbelievers towards accepting the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They were afraid that if they were to follow the teachings of Islam, they would be driven out of their land and lose their power and influence. However, the verse reminds them that Allah has already established a safe sanctuary, the sacred precincts of Mecca, where all people can find refuge and sustenance. Yet, most of them are unaware of this divine provision and continue to reject the truth.
orig: وقالوا إن نتبع الهدى معك نتخطف من أرضنا أولم نمكن لهم حرما آمنا يجبى إليه ثمرات كل شيء رزقا من لدنا ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And how many a city have We destroyed that was insolent in its [way of] living, and those are their dwellings which have not been inhabited after them except briefly. And it is We who were the inheritors.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the destruction of communities that had become arrogant and complacent in their way of life. It suggests that these communities were destroyed, and their dwellings remained uninhabited for a long time afterwards, with only a few people returning to live there. The verse emphasizes that it is Allah who is the ultimate inheritor and decision-maker, and that He has the power to destroy and replace civilizations as He wills.
orig: وكم أهلكنا من قرية بطرت معيشتها فتلك مساكنهم لم تسكن من بعدهم إلا قليلا وكنا نحن الوارثين

translation: And your Lord would not have destroyed the cities until He had sent to their mother [i.e., principal city] a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would not have destroyed the cities except that their people were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah does not destroy a community until He has sent a messenger to warn them and convey His signs (verses) to them. The destruction only occurs when the people persist in their wrongdoing and reject the message. This highlights Allah's justice and mercy, as He gives people a chance to reform before facing consequences for their misdeeds.
orig: وما كان ربك مهلك القرى حتى يبعث في أمها رسولا يتلو عليهم آياتنا وما كنا مهلكي القرى إلا وأهلها ظالمون

translation: And whatever you have been given - it is [only for] the enjoyment of worldly life and its adornment. And what is with Allah is better and more lasting; so will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse reminds us that the material possessions and pleasures of this world are temporary and fleeting. While they may provide enjoyment and adornment, the true and lasting good is what is with Allah in the Hereafter. The verse encourages us to use our reason and intellect to recognize the superiority and permanence of the rewards in the Afterlife over the transient nature of worldly gains.
orig: وما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزينتها وما عند الله خير وأبقى أفلا تعقلون

translation: Is he to whom We have promised a good [reward] and he will reach it like he who We have provided enjoyment of worldly life [but] then he, on the Day of Resurrection, will be among the ones presented [for punishment]?
interpretation: This verse draws a contrast between two types of people: those who have been promised a good reward from Allah, and those who have been given the enjoyment of this worldly life. The verse suggests that the former, who have been promised a good reward, will ultimately attain it, while the latter, who have been given worldly pleasures, will be held accountable on the Day of Resurrection. The implication is that the true success lies in the hereafter, not in the fleeting pleasures of this world.
orig: أفمن وعدناه وعدا حسنا فهو لاقيه كمن متعناه متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم هو يوم القيامة من المحضرين

translation: And the Day He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' that you used to claim?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when Allah will call upon the disbelievers and ask them about the false deities and partners they associated with Him during their worldly life. The verse highlights the futility of polytheism and the fact that on that day, the disbelievers will have no one to help or defend them, as their alleged "partners" were mere fabrications and had no real power or divinity.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: Those for whom the [decree of] word has proved true will say, "Our Lord, these are the ones we led to error. We led them to error just as we were in error. We declare our disassociation [from them] to You. They did not used to worship [Us]."
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when those who led others astray will disassociate themselves from their followers, acknowledging that they themselves were in error and had misguided others. They will declare to Allah that their followers did not truly worship Allah, but rather the leaders themselves. This highlights the grave responsibility of those who misguide others, and the importance of guiding people towards the truth.
orig: قال الذين حق عليهم القول ربنا هؤلاء الذين أغوينا أغويناهم كما غوينا تبرأنا إليك ما كانوا إيانا يعبدون

translation: And it will be said, "Call upon your 'partners'" - and they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment. If only they had been guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of worshiping false gods or "partners" alongside Allah. When the disbelievers are called upon to invoke their deities, they will find that their gods are unable to respond or provide any help, and they will witness the punishment that befalls them. This serves as a lesson that true guidance and salvation can only be found in the worship of the one true God, Allah, and not in the worship of any other entities.
orig: وقيل ادعوا شركاءكم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم ورأوا العذاب لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون

translation: And the Day He will call them and say, "What did you answer the messengers?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when Allah will call upon people and ask them about how they responded to the messages and teachings brought by the prophets and messengers. It highlights the importance of accepting and following the guidance provided by Allah through His messengers, as people will be held accountable for their response on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول ماذا أجبتم المرسلين

translation: So the news has become obscured to them on that Day, and they will not [be able to] ask.
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, the news or information that was previously known to the people will become obscured or unclear to them. They will not be able to ask or inquire about what is happening, as they will be overwhelmed by the events unfolding before them. The verse implies that on that momentous day, people will be so preoccupied with their own fate that they will not have the presence of mind to seek information or clarification.
orig: فعميت عليهم الأنباء يومئذ فهم لا يتساءلون

translation: But as for he who repents, believes and does righteous deeds, perhaps he will be among the successful.
interpretation: This verse encourages repentance, faith, and righteous actions as a path to success and salvation. It suggests that those who turn back to God, embrace belief, and engage in good works may be counted among the prosperous and victorious in the Hereafter. The verse highlights the possibility of forgiveness and redemption for those who sincerely reform themselves.
orig: فأما من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فعسى أن يكون من المفلحين

translation: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; the people have not any choice. Exalted is Allah and high [above all] that they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of God. He creates whatever He wills, and He chooses whatever He desires, without any being having the right to object or question His decisions. This affirms the belief that God alone has the authority to determine the course of events and that humans have no right to claim any autonomy or independence from Him. The verse also highlights the transcendence and perfection of God, who is far above and beyond any association or comparison with created beings.
orig: وربك يخلق ما يشاء ويختار ما كان لهم الخيرة سبحان الله وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Lord and Creator, has complete knowledge and awareness of the innermost thoughts, feelings, and intentions of people, even those that are hidden from others. It serves as a reminder that we cannot hide anything from Allah, and that He is aware of both our public actions and our private thoughts and motivations. This knowledge should inspire us to be righteous and honest in our dealings, as Allah is All-Knowing and will hold us accountable for our deeds.
orig: وربك يعلم ما تكن صدورهم وما يعلنون

translation: And He is Allah, there is no deity except Him. To Him belongs [all] praise in the first [life] and the Hereafter, and His is the [final] decision, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse affirms the oneness and sovereignty of Allah. It emphasizes that He is the only true deity worthy of worship, and that all praise and glory belong to Him alone, both in this life and the Hereafter. It also underscores that Allah has complete authority and control over all matters, and that ultimately, all people will be accountable to Him and return to Him.
orig: وهو الله لا إله إلا هو له الحمد في الأولى والآخرة وله الحكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then hear?'
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question posed by God, challenging the disbelievers to consider the possibility of perpetual darkness and to acknowledge that only God has the power to provide light and sustenance. The verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping any deity other than Allah, as they would be unable to bring light and life to the world. The underlying message is a call to believe in the oneness and sovereignty of God, and to heed the guidance provided in the Quran.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم الليل سرمدا إلى يوم القيامة من إله غير الله يأتيكم بضياء أفلا تسمعون

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the day continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you the night in which you might rest? Then do you not see?"
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the notion of worshipping any deity other than Allah. It emphasizes the fact that Allah is the sole creator and sustainer of the day and night cycle, which is essential for human life and rest. The verse invites the listener to reflect on the absurdity of seeking guidance or assistance from any other source, as Allah alone has the power to control the natural order. The underlying message is to acknowledge Allah's sovereignty and to devote one's worship and allegiance to Him alone.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم النهار سرمدا إلى يوم القيامة من إله غير الله يأتيكم بليل تسكنون فيه أفلا تبصرون

translation: And from His mercy, He has made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and [that] you may seek from His bounty and [that] you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah’s mercy in creating the alternation of night and day, which allows humans to rest and seek provisions from Allah’s bounty. The purpose is to encourage gratitude and appreciation for Allah’s blessings.
orig: ومن رحمته جعل لكم الليل والنهار لتسكنوا فيه ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And the Day He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' that you used to claim?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when Allah will call the disbelievers and ask them about the false deities and idols they used to worship alongside Him. This is to demonstrate the futility of their polytheistic beliefs and to establish Allah's absolute sovereignty and oneness. The verse highlights the fact that on that Day, the idols and false gods they claimed to be partners of Allah will be of no help or avail to them, as they have no real power or divinity.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: And We will draw out from every nation a witness and say, "Produce your proof." And they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and lost from them is that which they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will call forth a witness from each community to testify about the people's deeds and beliefs. When asked to provide their proof, the people will realize that the truth belongs to Allah alone, and all the falsehoods they had invented will be exposed and abandoned.
orig: ونزعنا من كل أمة شهيدا فقلنا هاتوا برهانكم فعلموا أن الحق لله وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he oppressed them. And We had given him of treasures that its keys would burden a company of strong men. [And this was] when his people said to him, "Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like any self-conceited boaster."
interpretation: This verse describes the story of Qarun, who was a wealthy and powerful man from the people of Prophet Moses. Despite being blessed with great wealth and treasures, Qarun became arrogant and oppressed his own people. The verse emphasizes that the keys to Qarun's treasures were so heavy that they would burden a group of strong men, indicating the vastness of his wealth. However, his people warned him not to be arrogant and boastful about his possessions, as Allah does not love those who are conceited and self-glorifying. The lesson here is that wealth and power should not lead to arrogance and oppression, but rather to humility and using one's blessings to serve others and please Allah.
orig: إن قارون كان من قوم موسى فبغى عليهم وآتيناه من الكنوز ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة أولي القوة إذ قال له قومه لا تفرح إن الله لا يحب الفرحين

translation: And seek, through that which Allah has given you, the Home of the Hereafter; and [yet], do not forget your share of the world. And do good as Allah has done good to you. And desire not corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not like any self-conceited boaster.
interpretation: This verse encourages a balanced approach to life, where one should strive for the Hereafter while not neglecting one's worldly responsibilities. It emphasizes the importance of doing good and being grateful to Allah, and warns against corruption and arrogance. The interpretation suggests that one should seek the ultimate abode of the Hereafter through the means Allah has provided, while also fulfilling one's duties in this world. The verse calls for a harmonious approach that avoids extremes and upholds the principles of righteousness and moderation.
orig: وابتغ فيما آتاك الله الدار الآخرة ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك ولا تبغ الفساد في الأرض إن الله لا يحب المفسدين

translation: He said, "I was only given it because of knowledge I have." Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations who were greater than him in strength and greater in accumulation [of wealth and children]? But the criminals, about their sins, will not be asked.
interpretation: This verse is referring to Qârûn (Korah), who was a wealthy man among the Israelites during the time of Prophet Moses. Qârûn became arrogant and boastful about his wealth, claiming that he had attained it through his own knowledge and abilities. However, the verse reminds him that his wealth and power were ultimately granted by Allah, and that previous generations who were even more powerful and wealthy than him were destroyed due to their arrogance and misdeeds. The verse warns that the criminals will not be able to escape accountability for their sins before Allah, no matter how powerful or wealthy they may have been in this world.
orig: قال إنما أوتيته على علم عندي أولم يعلم أن الله قد أهلك من قبله من القرون من هو أشد منه قوة وأكثر جمعا ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون

translation: And he went forth among his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said, "Oh, how we wish we had like what was given to Qarun. Indeed, he is a possessor of great fortune."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the people to the wealth and luxuries enjoyed by Qarun, who was a wealthy and influential member of the community. The people were envious of Qarun's material possessions and wished they could have the same level of wealth and comfort. This verse highlights the human tendency to covet worldly possessions and the allure of material wealth, even at the expense of more important spiritual and moral values. The interpretation suggests that true contentment and fulfillment cannot be found solely in the pursuit of material gain, and that one should be mindful of the ephemeral nature of worldly possessions.
orig: فخرج على قومه في زينته قال الذين يريدون الحياة الدنيا يا ليت لنا مثل ما أوتي قارون إنه لذو حظ عظيم

translation: And those who were given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for one who believes and does righteousness. And none will receive it except the patient."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith, good deeds, and patience. It warns those who have knowledge against arrogance and complacency, and reminds them that the true reward from Allah is better than any worldly gain. The interpretation is that true believers, who combine faith with righteous actions and persevere through difficulties, will be the ones to attain the ultimate reward from Allah.
orig: وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن وعمل صالحا ولا يلقاها إلا الصابرون

translation: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. And there was for him no company to aid him other than Allah, and he was not of those who [could] defend themselves.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who defy the commands of Allah and reject faith. The earth swallowing up the person and their home is a metaphor for how the unrighteous will be destroyed and their worldly possessions will be of no avail. The verse emphasizes that there is no one who can save such individuals from the punishment of Allah, and they are powerless to defend themselves against divine retribution. The lesson here is to submit to Allah's will and live a righteous life, for there is no escape from His judgment.
orig: فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان من المنتصرين

translation: And those who had wished for his place the previous day began to say, "Oh, [how great is] Allah's sustenance to whom He wills of His servants. If only we had been given like what was given to him. Indeed, he is the great [one in] possession of good fortune."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of those who had wished to be in the position of the one who was blessed with Allah's sustenance. They now acknowledge that it is Allah who bestows His provision upon whomever He wills, and that if it were not for Allah's grace, they too would have been deprived. This highlights the importance of recognizing that all blessings come from Allah, and that one should not be envious of others' fortunes, but rather be grateful for what one has been given.
orig: وأصبح الذين تمنوا مكانه بالأمس يقولون ويكأن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر لولا أن من الله علينا لخسف بنا ويكأنه لا يفلح الكافرون

translation: That is the Hereafter, We will assign it to those who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth or corruption. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse describes the Hereafter as a place that will be granted to those who do not seek power, dominance or corruption on Earth. Instead, it will be given to the righteous and God-fearing people, whose ultimate outcome will be a favorable one.
orig: تلك الدار الآخرة نجعلها للذين لا يريدون علوا في الأرض ولا فسادا والعاقبة للمتقين

translation: Whoever comes [to Allah] with a good deed will have better than it, and they will be secure from the terror of that Day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of doing good deeds and avoiding evil. It promises that those who do good will be rewarded with something even better, while those who commit evil will only be punished for what they have done. The verse encourages people to strive to do what is right and avoid what is wrong, as they will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى الذين عملوا السيئات إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Indeed, He who has imposed upon you, [O Muhammad], the Qur'an will take you back to a destined place. Say, "My Lord is most knowing of who has brought guidance and who is in manifest error."
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that Allah, who has revealed the Qur'an to him, will eventually return him to a destined place, either in this life or the Hereafter. The verse also instructs the Prophet to say that Allah knows best who has received the guidance of the Qur'an and who has strayed from it. This is a reminder that the judgment of people's faith and actions belongs to Allah alone, and that the Prophet should focus on conveying the message without concerning himself with the ultimate fate of those who reject it.
orig: إن الذي فرض عليك القرآن لرادك إلى معاد قل ربي أعلم من جاء بالهدى ومن هو في ضلال مبين

translation: And you did not expect that the Book would be conveyed to you, but [it is] a mercy from your Lord. So do not be an assistant to the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the revelation of the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad was a pure act of divine mercy, not something he had expected or sought. It is a reminder that the Qur'an is a gift from God, not the result of human effort or planning. The verse also cautions the Prophet not to lend support to those who reject the message of the Qur'an, the disbelievers, as that would be contrary to the divine purpose behind its revelation.
orig: وما كنت ترجو أن يلقى إليك الكتاب إلا رحمة من ربك فلا تكونن ظهيرا للكافرين

translation: And do not be averted from the verses of Allah after they have been revealed to you, and invite to your Lord and do not be among the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain steadfast in his faith and not be swayed by those who reject the message of the Qur'an. It emphasizes the importance of calling people to the worship of the One true God, and avoiding any association with polytheism or idolatry. The verse serves as a reminder to all believers to hold firm to their faith, and to actively invite others to the path of guidance revealed in the Qur'an.
orig: ولا يصدنك عن آيات الله بعد إذ أنزلت إليك وادع إلى ربك ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: And do not invoke with Allah another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will be destroyed except His Face. His is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and supremacy of God (Allah). It commands the believers to worship none but Allah, as He is the only true deity and all else will perish. The verse also affirms that Allah is the sole judge and that all people will ultimately return to Him for accountability on the Day of Judgement.
orig: ولا تدع مع الله إلها آخر لا إله إلا هو كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه له الحكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: These are among the 'Disconnected Letters' (al-Muqatta'at) that appear at the beginning of some Qur'anic chapters. Their exact meaning and significance are not entirely clear, and there are various interpretations among Islamic scholars. Some believe they represent a challenge to humankind to produce something similar to the Qur'an, while others view them as a way to draw attention to the miraculous nature of the Qur'an. Ultimately, the deeper meaning of these letters remains a mystery, and Muslims are encouraged to ponder and reflect on them as part of the divine revelation.
orig: الم

translation: Do the people think that they will be left to say, "We believe" and they will not be tried?
interpretation: This verse suggests that simply claiming to have faith is not enough. True faith must be tested and demonstrated through one's actions and perseverance. The verse implies that those who merely profess belief without being willing to face trials and hardships are deceiving themselves. The true believers are those who are willing to be tested and to remain steadfast in their faith, even in the face of adversity.
orig: أحسب الناس أن يتركوا أن يقولوا آمنا وهم لا يفتنون

translation: And We had certainly tried those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars.
interpretation: This verse refers to the trials and tribulations that previous nations and communities faced, and how Allah tests the faith and sincerity of people. The verse assures that Allah will distinguish the truthful from the liars, and that the truth will ultimately prevail. It encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith, as Allah's judgment will expose the true nature of people's beliefs and actions.
orig: ولقد فتنا الذين من قبلهم فليعلمن الله الذين صدقوا وليعلمن الكاذبين

translation: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us? Evil is what they judge.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the notion that those who commit evil deeds can escape the consequences of their actions. The implication is that they cannot outrun the judgment and punishment of Allah. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in sinful behavior, reminding them that their actions will not go unnoticed or unpunished. The interpretation emphasizes the idea that evil actions will ultimately be met with a fitting retribution, as determined by the wisdom and justice of Allah.
orig: أم حسب الذين يعملون السيئات أن يسبقونا ساء ما يحكمون

translation: Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, then the term appointed by Allah will surely come. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to prepare for the meeting with Allah on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that the appointed time of one's death and the Day of Resurrection are certain and will come to pass, as Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing. The verse reminds us to live our lives in a way that pleases Allah, as we will be held accountable for our actions on that Day.
orig: من كان يرجو لقاء الله فإن أجل الله لآت وهو السميع العليم

translation: And whoever strives (in Allah's Cause) does so for his own self; verily, Allah is free of all wants from the 'Alamin (mankind, jinns, and all that exists).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the struggle or effort (jihad) in the cause of Allah is ultimately for one's own benefit. Allah, being the All-Sufficient and Independent, does not need or gain anything from the efforts of His servants. The true reward and benefit of striving in Allah's cause accrues to the individual themselves, as it purifies the soul, earns the pleasure of Allah, and secures eternal reward in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن جاهد فإنما يجاهد لنفسه إن الله لغني عن العالمين

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse promises that those who have faith in God and do good deeds will have their sins forgiven and will be rewarded for their righteous actions. It highlights the concept of God's mercy and justice, where believers are promised forgiveness and a reward commensurate with their good deeds. The verse emphasizes the importance of both faith and righteous actions in attaining God's pleasure and blessings.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنكفرن عنهم سيئاتهم ولنجزينهم أحسن الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: And We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honoring and caring for one's parents, but also establishes that this duty has limits. If the parents try to pressure the person to associate partners with God, which goes against the person's knowledge and belief, then they should not be obeyed in that regard. Ultimately, the person will return to God, who will inform them of their actions and hold them accountable.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه حسنا وإن جاهداك لتشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما إلي مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely admit them to the Righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have faith in God and do good deeds will be admitted to the company of the righteous in the Hereafter. It suggests that faith and righteous actions go hand-in-hand, and that those who possess both will be rewarded with a place among the virtuous and pious individuals. The verse highlights the importance of both belief and righteous conduct in order to attain salvation and a place in the company of the righteous.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لندخلنهم في الصالحين

translation: And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah," but when one [of them] is harmed for [the cause of] Allah, they consider the trial of the people as [if it were] the punishment of Allah. But if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you." Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of some people who claim to believe in Allah, but when they face adversity or persecution for the sake of their faith, they start to question Allah's wisdom and justice. They view the trials and tribulations they face as a punishment from Allah, rather than a test of their faith. However, when Allah grants them victory, they quickly claim to have been with the believers all along, seeking to gain favor and recognition. The verse emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and fully aware of the true intentions and sentiments within the hearts of all people.
orig: ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله فإذا أوذي في الله جعل فتنة الناس كعذاب الله ولئن جاء نصر من ربك ليقولن إنا كنا معكم أوليس الله بأعلم بما في صدور العالمين

translation: And [that] Allah may make evident those who believe and [may] make evident the hypocrites.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah will distinguish the true believers from the hypocrites. He will make it clear who has sincere faith and who is merely pretending. This allows the believers to identify and avoid the influence of the hypocrites, and it also serves as a warning to the hypocrites that their true nature will be exposed.
orig: وليعلمن الله الذين آمنوا وليعلمن المنافقين

translation: And those who disbelieved say to those who believed, "Follow our way, and we will carry your sins." But they will not carry anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive and hypocritical nature of the disbelievers. They try to lure the believers to follow their path, falsely promising to bear the burden of their sins. However, the verse makes it clear that the disbelievers cannot and will not actually carry the sins of the believers, as they are liars. The true burden of sin can only be borne by the individual, and the disbelievers' offer is merely a ploy to mislead the believers and turn them away from the truth.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا اتبعوا سبيلنا ولنحمل خطاياكم وما هم بحاملين من خطاياهم من شيء إنهم لكاذبون

translation: And they will surely carry their [own] burdens and [other] burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of fabricating lies and falsehoods against Allah and His teachings. Those who engage in such deception will not only bear the burden of their own sins but also the sins of those they have misled. On the Day of Judgment, they will be held accountable for their actions and the false claims they have made. This serves as a warning to people to be truthful and avoid spreading misinformation, as they will be held responsible for the consequences of their choices.
orig: وليحملن أثقالهم وأثقالا مع أثقالهم وليسألن يوم القيامة عما كانوا يفترون

translation: And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the lengthy duration of Prophet Noah"s mission to his people, which lasted for nearly a millennium. Despite his tireless efforts to guide them towards the path of righteousness, the people remained steadfast in their wrongdoing and disbelief. Ultimately, they were punished with the devastating flood, a consequence of their persistent rejection of God"s message and guidance.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فلبث فيهم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما فأخذهم الطوفان وهم ظالمون

translation: And We saved him and the companions of the ship, and We made it a sign for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Noah and the Flood. God saved Noah and his companions who were on the ark, and made this event a sign for all of humanity to reflect upon. The preservation of Noah and his followers through the Flood demonstrates God's power, mercy, and ability to save the righteous even in the face of great calamity. This event serves as a lesson and a reminder for all people to have faith in God and follow His guidance.
orig: فأنجيناه وأصحاب السفينة وجعلناها آية للعالمين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said to his people, "Worship Allah and fear Him. That is best for you, if you should know."
interpretation: This verse encourages the people to worship Allah alone and to be mindful of Him. The interpretation is that worshipping Allah and fearing Him is the best course of action for the people, if they only knew the truth. It emphasizes the importance of monotheism and piety in leading a righteous life.
orig: وإبراهيم إذ قال لقومه اعبدوا الله واتقوه ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: You only worship, besides Allah, idols, and you create a lie. Verily, those whom you worship besides Allah have no power to give you provision, so seek your provision from Allah, and worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be brought back.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of worshipping idols and false deities instead of the one true God, Allah. It emphasizes that these idols have no power to provide for or sustain the people, and that true provision and sustenance can only come from Allah. The verse encourages the people to seek their provisions from Allah, worship Him alone, and be grateful to Him, as ultimately all will return to Him.
orig: إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا وتخلقون إفكا إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه واشكروا له إليه ترجعون

translation: And if you deny, already have nations before you denied. And there is not upon the Messenger except [the duty of] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that disbelief or rejection of the message of the Messenger is not a new phenomenon. Previous nations and communities have also rejected the messages of their prophets and messengers. The Messenger's duty is to convey the message clearly and unambiguously, and it is up to the people to accept or reject it. The responsibility for accepting or rejecting the message lies with the people themselves, not with the Messenger.
orig: وإن تكذبوا فقد كذب أمم من قبلكم وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: Have they not considered how Allah originates creation and then repeats it? Indeed, that, for Allah, is [not difficult, but] easy.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on Allah's power and ability to create and resurrect. Just as Allah has the power to bring life into existence, He also has the power to resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment. This serves as a reminder that nothing is too difficult for Allah, and that He is in complete control of all creation.
orig: أولم يروا كيف يبدئ الله الخلق ثم يعيده إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: Say, "Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then Allah will produce the final creation. Indeed Allah, over all things, is Competent."
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the wonders of Allah's creation and the process of life. It invites us to observe the natural world and how Allah has brought it into existence, in order to appreciate His power and wisdom. The verse then states that Allah will bring about the final resurrection, emphasizing that He has power over all things. This is meant to instill faith in the Hereafter and the ultimate accountability before Allah.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف بدأ الخلق ثم الله ينشئ النشأة الآخرة إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah. He alone has the authority to punish or show mercy to whomever He wills, as He is the All-Knowing and All-Wise. It reminds us that we are ultimately accountable to Allah and will return to Him on the Day of Judgment, where we will be judged based on our actions and beliefs.
orig: يعذب من يشاء ويرحم من يشاء وإليه تقلبون

translation: And you will not cause failure [to Allah] upon the earth or in the heaven. And you have not besides Allah any protector or any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that humans are powerless and cannot escape the will of Allah, whether on earth or in the heavens. It reminds us that we have no one to protect or help us besides Allah, and that we must submit to His divine plan and authority.
orig: وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض ولا في السماء وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah and [in] the meeting with Him - those have despaired of My mercy, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns those who reject the signs and messages of Allah, and deny the Day of Judgment, that they have lost hope in Allah's mercy and will face a severe punishment. It emphasizes the importance of believing in Allah's revelations and the reality of the Hereafter, as those who reject these fundamental aspects of faith will be deprived of Allah's forgiveness and compassion.
orig: والذين كفروا بآيات الله ولقائه أولئك يئسوا من رحمتي وأولئك لهم عذاب أليم

translation: But the only response of his people was that they said, "Kill him or burn him." But Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the prophet Abraham and his confrontation with his people who were idolaters. When Abraham denounced their worship of idols and called them to worship the one true God, they responded with threats to kill or burn him. However, Allah protected Abraham from the fire, demonstrating His power and the truth of Abraham's message. This verse encourages believers to have faith in Allah and His prophets, even in the face of persecution and threats, as Allah will ultimately protect and vindicate those who believe in Him.
orig: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا اقتلوه أو حرقوه فأنجاه الله من النار إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And he (Pharaoh) said: "Verily, you have taken (for worship) idols besides Allah, solely to have (some) affection between you in the life of this world, but on the Day of Resurrection, you shall disown each other, and curse each other, and your abode will be the Fire, and you will have no helper."
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah through the words of Pharaoh, who is addressing the Israelites. He is criticizing their worship of idols, which he says is only for the sake of having affection and unity among themselves in this worldly life. However, on the Day of Judgment, they will turn against each other, disown one another, and curse each other. Their ultimate abode will be the Fire of Hell, with no one to help or save them. The interpretation emphasizes that worshiping idols or false gods, even if it may bring temporary unity, will ultimately lead to eternal punishment and separation from Allah on the Day of Resurrection.
orig: وقال إنما اتخذتم من دون الله أوثانا مودة بينكم في الحياة الدنيا ثم يوم القيامة يكفر بعضكم ببعض ويلعن بعضكم بعضا ومأواكم النار وما لكم من ناصرين

translation: And Lot believed him. [Abraham] said, "Indeed, I will migrate to [the service of] my Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse describes the response of the prophet Lot to the message of the prophet Abraham. Lot believed in Abraham's call to migrate to serve God, recognizing that God is the Almighty and All-Wise. The verse highlights the importance of faith, obedience, and trust in God's commands, even when they require leaving one's home and comfort zone.
orig: فآمن له لوط وقال إني مهاجر إلى ربي إنه هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and placed in his descendants prophethood and the Scripture, and We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, he is in the Hereafter among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and favors that Allah bestowed upon the Prophet Abraham. Allah granted him two righteous sons, Isaac and Jacob, and made prophethood and the revealed scriptures (such as the Torah and the Gospel) to continue in their descendants. Furthermore, Allah rewarded Abraham in this world, and he will be among the righteous in the Hereafter. This verse emphasizes the high status of Abraham and the continuation of his legacy through his progeny.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وجعلنا في ذريته النبوة والكتاب وآتيناه أجره في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], Lot, when he said to his people, "Indeed, you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds [i.e., peoples].
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the Prophet Lot, who condemned his people for engaging in the immoral practice of homosexuality, which was unprecedented in the history of humankind. The verse emphasizes the gravity of this sin, which sets the people of Lot apart from all other nations. The interpretation highlights the Qur’an’s condemnation of homosexuality as a grave moral transgression that was unique to Lot’s people.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه إنكم لتأتون الفاحشة ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين

translation: Do you indeed approach men [with such unnatural desire] and cut off the highway and commit in your meetings [every] evil?
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of homosexuality and other immoral acts. It suggests that the people being addressed were engaging in unnatural sexual acts, disrupting society, and committing other sinful acts in their gatherings. The verse then states that the only response the people had to this condemnation was to challenge the prophet to bring down God's punishment if he was telling the truth.
orig: أئنكم لتأتون الرجال وتقطعون السبيل وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, "My Lord, help me against the corrupt people."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, and it is spoken by the Prophet Nuh (Noah). He is calling upon his Lord, Allah, to help him and support him against the corrupt and evil people of his time who were rejecting his message and his call to worship only Allah. The verse reflects Nuh's reliance on Allah and his trust that Allah will provide him with the necessary help and victory against those who are causing corruption and mischief on the earth.
orig: قال رب انصرني على القوم المفسدين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good tidings, they said, "Indeed, we will destroy the people of this city. Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse describes how the angels (referred to as "Our messengers") came to Prophet Abraham and informed him that they would destroy the people of the city of Sodom, as the people there had been wrongdoers. This was a warning from God about the impending punishment that would befall the wicked people of that city.
orig: ولما جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم بالبشرى قالوا إنا مهلكو أهل هذه القرية إن أهلها كانوا ظالمين

translation: He (Abraham) said: "Verily, in it (the township) is Lut (Lot)." They said: "We know better who is there. We will verily save him (Lut) and his family, except his wife, she will be of those who remain behind (i.e. she will be destroyed)."
interpretation: This verse describes the response of the angels to Abraham when he mentioned that the town they were heading to contained Lot and his family. The angels assured Abraham that they knew best who was in the town and that they would save Lot and his family, except for his wife, who would be destroyed along with the rest of the disbelievers. This highlights God's mercy in saving the righteous and His justice in punishing the wicked.
orig: قال إن فيها لوطا قالوا نحن أعلم بمن فيها لننجينه وأهله إلا امرأته كانت من الغابرين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt for them great discomfort. And he said, "This is a distressful day." And his people came hastening to him, and before [this] they had been doing evil deeds. [Lot] said, "O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you. So fear Allah and do not disgrace me concerning my guests. Is there not among you a righteous man?"
interpretation: This verse describes the arrival of the angels (messengers) to the town of Lot, and Lot's distress at their presence, as he feared for their safety among his wicked people. The angels reassured Lot that they had come to save him and his family, except for his wife who would be left behind as she was among those who would be destroyed. The verse highlights Lot's concern for his guests and his plea to his people to fear Allah and not to disgrace him in front of his guests, indicating his righteous character.
orig: ولما أن جاءت رسلنا لوطا سيء بهم وضاق بهم ذرعا وقالوا لا تخف ولا تحزن إنا منجوك وأهلك إلا امرأتك كانت من الغابرين

translation: Indeed, We will send down to the people of this city a punishment from the sky because they were defiantly disobeying.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah will send down a severe punishment upon a community that has persistently engaged in sinful and disobedient behavior. The punishment is described as coming "from the sky", suggesting it may be in the form of a natural disaster or divine intervention. The key message is that Allah will not tolerate continued corruption and wickedness, and those who persist in such acts will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: إنا منزلون على أهل هذه القرية رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And indeed, We have left of it a clear sign for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the destruction of the people of Thamud, who were punished for their rejection of the prophet Salih and their mistreatment of the she-camel that was a sign from God. The "clear sign" left behind is a reminder to people to use their reason and intellect to understand the consequences of denying God's messengers and defying His commands.
orig: ولقد تركنا منها آية بينة لقوم يعقلون

translation: And to Madyan, [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb, and he said, 'O my people, worship Allah and expect the Last Day, and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.'
interpretation: This verse is about the prophet Shu'ayb being sent to the people of Madyan. He calls them to worship Allah alone, and to believe in the Day of Judgment. He also warns them against spreading corruption and causing mischief on the earth. The main message is to have faith in Allah, live righteously, and avoid evil and destructive behavior that harms society.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا فقال يا قوم اعبدوا الله وارجوا اليوم الآخر ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: But they denied him, so the earthquake seized them, and they became within their homes [laid] prone.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the people who rejected the message of the Prophet sent to them. They denied and disbelieved the Prophet, so they were punished by a severe earthquake that destroyed their homes and caused them to perish. This serves as a warning that those who reject the truth and the messengers of God will face divine retribution.
orig: فكذبوه فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: And [We destroyed] 'Aad and Thamud, and it has become clear to you from their [ruined] dwellings. And Satan had made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from the path, and they were endowed with insight.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the fate of the ancient peoples of 'Aad and Thamud, whose ruined dwellings serve as a lesson and warning to us. Despite being endowed with insight and understanding, they were deceived by Satan, who made their evil deeds seem attractive to them, leading them astray from the right path. This serves as a cautionary tale about the danger of being misled by the temptations of Satan and the importance of staying steadfast on the path of righteousness.
orig: وعادا وثمود وقد تبين لكم من مساكنهم وزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم فصدهم عن السبيل وكانوا مستبصرين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], Qarun and Pharaoh and Haman. And Moses had already come to them with clear evidences, but they were arrogant in the land and were not the first to believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and rejection of the truth by powerful leaders like Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman, despite the clear signs and guidance brought to them by the prophet Moses. It serves as a warning against the dangers of pride, arrogance, and unwillingness to accept the truth, even in the face of undeniable evidence. The verse emphasizes that these leaders were not the first to disbelieve, but rather they chose to be arrogant and reject the divine message, leading to their eventual downfall.
orig: وقارون وفرعون وهامان ولقد جاءهم موسى بالبينات فاستكبروا في الأرض وما كانوا سابقين

translation: And each [of them] We seized for his sin; and among them were [those upon] whom We sent a storm of stones, and among them were [those whom] the blast [from the sky] seized, and among them were [those whom] the earth swallowed, and among them were [those whom] We drowned. And it was not for Allah to wrong them, but it was they who were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah punished different groups of people for their sins, using various means such as storms, blasts, the earth swallowing them, and drowning. The key message is that Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves through their own misdeeds and sins. This serves as a warning to people to avoid sinful behavior and to hold themselves accountable for their actions.
orig: فكلا أخذنا بذنبه فمنهم من أرسلنا عليه حاصبا ومنهم من أخذته الصيحة ومنهم من خسفنا به الأرض ومنهم من أغرقنا وما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: The example of those who take allies other than Allah is like that of the spider who takes a home. And indeed, the weakest of homes is the home of the spider, if they but knew.
interpretation: This verse draws a powerful metaphor to illustrate the futility of relying on anything other than Allah for protection and guidance. Just as a spider's web is a fragile and unreliable shelter, those who seek help from false gods or idols are building their lives on an equally unstable foundation. The verse emphasizes that if people truly understood the weakness and impermanence of such alliances, they would not place their trust in anything other than the Almighty.
orig: مثل الذين اتخذوا من دون الله أولياء كمثل العنكبوت اتخذت بيتا وإن أوهن البيوت لبيت العنكبوت لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, Allah knows what they invoke besides Him of [anything], and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge and awareness of all that is invoked or worshipped besides Him. He is the Almighty, the All-Wise, and nothing escapes His knowledge. This serves as a reminder that Allah alone is worthy of worship, as He has power and wisdom that surpasses all else.
orig: إن الله يعلم ما يدعون من دونه من شيء وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And these examples We present to the people, but none will understand them except those of knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'anic parables and examples are meant to convey deep and profound truths, which can only be fully appreciated by those who possess true knowledge and understanding. The "people" referred to here are the general masses, who may not have the necessary intellectual and spiritual capacity to grasp the deeper meanings behind these parables. Only the "knowledgeable" ones, those who have attained a higher level of knowledge and wisdom, can truly comprehend the wisdom and insights embedded in these Qur'anic examples.
orig: وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس وما يعقلها إلا العالمون

translation: Allah has created the heavens and the earth in truth. Verily, in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the creation of the heavens and the earth by Allah is a purposeful and just act, not something haphazard or without meaning. The existence of this magnificent universe is a clear sign for those who believe in Allah, as it points to His power, wisdom, and divine plan. This should inspire the believers to reflect on the wonders of Allah's creation and to submit to Him in faith and worship.
orig: خلق الله السماوات والأرض بالحق إن في ذلك لآية للمؤمنين

translation: Recite, [O Muhammad], what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows that which you do.
interpretation: This verse encourages the recitation and study of the Qur'an, as well as the establishment of regular prayer. It emphasizes that prayer has a purifying effect, as it helps to prevent immoral and wrongful behavior, and reminds us of the greatness of Allah. The verse also reminds us that Allah is all-knowing and is aware of our actions, which should motivate us to live righteously.
orig: اتل ما أوحي إليك من الكتاب وأقم الصلاة إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر والله يعلم ما تصنعون

translation: And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best, except for those who commit injustice among them, and say, "We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you. And our God and your God is one; and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to engage in respectful and constructive dialogue with the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians), avoiding confrontational or argumentative approaches, except with those who are unjust. The focus should be on affirming the common belief in the one true God and the shared submission to Him, rather than on differences. The verse promotes a spirit of mutual understanding and cooperation between Muslims and the People of the Scripture.
orig: ولا تجادلوا أهل الكتاب إلا بالتي هي أحسن إلا الذين ظلموا منهم وقولوا آمنا بالذي أنزل إلينا وأنزل إليكم وإلهنا وإلهكم واحد ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And thus have We sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book [i.e., the Qur'an]. So those to whom We [previously] gave the Scripture believe in it [i.e., the Qur'an]. And among the [people of the Book] are those who believe in it. And none reject Our verses except the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the Qur'an has been revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the same way that previous Scriptures were revealed to other Prophets. It states that those who were given the previous Scriptures (such as the Torah and the Gospel) believe in the Qur'an, as it confirms and upholds the essential teachings of those Scriptures. However, it also acknowledges that some of them reject the Qur'an, and that only the disbelievers reject the verses of Allah without any justification.
orig: وكذلك أنزلنا إليك الكتاب فالذين آتيناهم الكتاب يؤمنون به ومن هؤلاء من يؤمن به وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا الكافرون

translation: And you were not reciting any scripture before it, nor did you inscribe one with your right hand. [If you had], the falsifiers would have had [cause for] doubt.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad did not learn the Qur'an from any previous scripture or write it himself, but rather received it through divine revelation. This serves as a proof that the Qur'an is not a human-made text, but a divine message, which the disbelievers cannot refute or cast doubt upon.
orig: وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك إذا لارتاب المبطلون

translation: Nay, but they are clear signs in the breasts of those who are given knowledge, and none but the wrongdoers deny Our signs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'anic verses are clear and self-evident signs of the truth, which are recognized by those who possess true knowledge. It suggests that only those who are unjust and wrongful in their conduct deny the divine signs and messages contained in the Qur'an, as their hearts and minds are blinded by their own biases and desires.
orig: بل هو آيات بينات في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا الظالمون

translation: And they say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "The signs are only with Allah, and I am but a clear warner."
interpretation: This verse addresses the skeptics who demanded that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) should be given miraculous signs from God to prove his prophethood. The response is that the signs and miracles are in the hands of God alone, and the Prophet's role is to clearly convey the divine message as a warner, not to perform extraordinary feats. The emphasis is on the fact that faith should be based on the message of the Quran, not on the display of supernatural powers.
orig: وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه آيات من ربه قل إنما الآيات عند الله وإنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: Has it not been enough for them that We have sent down to you the Book which is recited to them? Indeed in that is a mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the revelation of the Qur'an, which is recited to the people, should be sufficient for them as a guide and a source of mercy and remembrance for those who believe. The implication is that the people should accept and follow the guidance provided in the Qur'an, as it contains the wisdom and mercy of Allah.
orig: أولم يكفهم أنا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب يتلى عليهم إن في ذلك لرحمة وذكرى لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Say, "Sufficient is Allah between me and you as Witness. He knows what is in the heavens and earth. And they who have believed in falsehood and disbelieved in Allah - it is those who are the losers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate witness between the Prophet Muhammad and the disbelievers. Allah, who is all-knowing and all-seeing, is aware of the truth and the falsehood that the disbelievers have embraced. Those who have believed in falsehood and rejected faith in Allah are the ones who will ultimately suffer the consequences of their choices and be the true losers.
orig: قل كفى بالله بيني وبينكم شهيدا يعلم ما في السماوات والأرض والذين آمنوا بالباطل وكفروا بالله أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And they ask you to hasten the punishment, and had it not been for a [specified] term, the punishment would have come to them. But it will surely come to them suddenly while they perceive not.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who are challenging the Prophet (peace be upon him) to bring down the punishment they were warned about. The verse explains that the punishment will indeed come, but it will come at its appointed time, not when they demand it. The punishment will come suddenly, without them realizing it, as a consequence of their rejection of faith and persistent disbelief.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالعذاب ولولا أجل مسمى لجاءهم العذاب وليأتينهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed, Hell will be encompassing of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who are challenging the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to bring down the punishment that they were warned about. The verse assures that the punishment of Hell will indeed encompass and surround the disbelievers, despite their impatience and demands. It serves as a reminder that the punishment of the Hereafter is certain and that the disbelievers cannot escape it.
orig: يستعجلونك بالعذاب وإن جهنم لمحيطة بالكافرين

translation: The day when the punishment will cover them from above them and from under their feet, and [the command will be], "Taste [the result of] what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers and wrongdoers will be surrounded by the punishment of Allah from all sides. They will be held accountable for their actions in this life and will be commanded to taste the consequences of their misdeeds. The verse emphasizes the inescapability and severity of the punishment that awaits those who reject faith and engage in sinful acts.
orig: يوم يغشاهم العذاب من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم ويقول ذوقوا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship [only] Me.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to worship Allah alone, as the earth is vast and there is ample space for people to live and fulfill their religious obligations. It reminds believers that they should focus their devotion and service on Allah, the Creator, and not be distracted by the material world or false deities.
orig: يا عبادي الذين آمنوا إن أرضي واسعة فإياي فاعبدون

translation: Every soul will taste death, and then to Us you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal truth that all living beings will eventually experience death, which is an inevitable part of the human condition. It serves as a reminder that our earthly existence is temporary, and that ultimately, we will all be held accountable for our actions and return to God for judgment. This verse encourages believers to live a righteous life and prepare for the afterlife, as our ultimate destination is with the Creator.
orig: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ثم إلينا ترجعون

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely assign to them of Paradise [elevated] chambers beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. Excellent is the reward of [those] workers.
interpretation: This verse promises a lofty and elevated abode in Paradise for those who believe in God and do good deeds. The imagery of "chambers" beneath which rivers flow conveys a sense of tranquility, comfort and abundance in the Hereafter. The eternal nature of this reward highlights its permanence and the ultimate success of those who strive to please God through their faith and righteous actions. This verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to continuously engage in virtuous conduct, as they will be amply rewarded in the Afterlife.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنبوئنهم من الجنة غرفا تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها نعم أجر العاملين

translation: Those who are patient and rely upon their Lord
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who have steadfastness and trust in Allah. They endure trials and tribulations with patience and perseverance, and they place their complete reliance and faith in Allah, knowing that He is the ultimate source of guidance and support. This attitude of patience and trust in the divine is a hallmark of the true believers, and it is a quality that Allah rewards and appreciates.
orig: الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And how many a creature is there that carries not [provisions for] its [own] sustenance? [It is] Allah who provides for it and for you. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate provider for all creatures, including humans. It reminds us that we should not worry about our sustenance, as Allah will provide for us just as He provides for all other living beings. The verse also highlights Allah's attributes of being All-Hearing and All-Knowing, suggesting that He is aware of our needs and will provide for us accordingly.
orig: وكأين من دابة لا تحمل رزقها الله يرزقها وإياكم وهو السميع العليم

translation: And if you ask them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?" they will surely say, "Allah." Then how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the existence of the universe and the orderly functioning of the celestial bodies like the sun and the moon are clear signs of the existence and power of Allah. Even those who deny or turn away from Allah will acknowledge that Allah is the Creator when directly asked. The verse then questions how they can still be deluded and turn away from the truth that is so apparent in the creation around them.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض وسخر الشمس والقمر ليقولن الله فأنى يؤفكون

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts [it] for him. Indeed, Allah is to all things Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who controls the provision and sustenance of His servants. He grants abundance to whomever He wills, and restricts it for whomever He wills. This is a reflection of Allah's absolute power and knowledge, as the verse states that "Indeed, Allah is to all things Knowing." The interpretation suggests that one should have trust and reliance in Allah's wisdom and divine plan, rather than being preoccupied with the distribution of worldly resources.
orig: الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر له إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And if you ask them, "Who has sent down water from the sky and given life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness?" they will surely say, "Allah." Say, "[All] praise is [due] to Allah"; but most of them do not reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that even those who do not believe in Allah will acknowledge that it is He who sends down rain from the sky and revives the dead earth. However, despite this acknowledgment, most people do not truly ponder and reflect on the signs of Allah’s power and sovereignty. The verse encourages believers to give praise and thanks to Allah for His blessings, as this is the appropriate response for those who use their reason and understanding.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من نزل من السماء ماء فأحيا به الأرض من بعد موتها ليقولن الله قل الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And this worldly life is not but [mere] amusement and diversion; but the Home of the Hereafter is the [true] Life, if they but knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the life of this world is fleeting and insignificant compared to the eternal life of the Hereafter. It is a reminder that the true purpose of our existence is not found in the temporary pleasures and distractions of this world, but in the everlasting life that awaits us in the Hereafter. If only people would realize this, they would prioritize their efforts and focus on preparing for the Afterlife, which is the true abode of eternal life and fulfillment.
orig: وما هذه الحياة الدنيا إلا لهو ولعب وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And when they board ships, they invoke Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to turn to God in times of distress, such as when facing danger at sea, but then to forget or neglect their devotion to God once the crisis has passed. It serves as a reminder that true faith and sincerity to God should not be limited to moments of need, but should be a constant state of being, regardless of one's circumstances.
orig: فإذا ركبوا في الفلك دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر إذا هم يشركون

translation: That they may disbelieve in that which We have given them, and that they may enjoy [their worldly life], but they will come to know.
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people will choose to disbelieve in the blessings and guidance that God has provided them, and instead indulge in worldly pleasures. However, they will eventually come to realize the consequences of their choices.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم وليتمتعوا فسوف يعلمون

translation: Have they not seen that We have made [Makkah] a secure sanctuary, while people are being taken away all around them? Then is it in falsehood that they believe and in the favor of Allah they disbelieve?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the blessings and security that Allah has bestowed upon the people of Makkah, while those around them are facing hardship and persecution. Yet, despite these blessings, the people of Makkah are turning away from the truth of Islam and disbelieving in the favors of Allah. The verse is a rhetorical question, challenging the people to reflect on their ingratitude and rejection of the truth.
orig: أولم يروا أنا جعلنا حرما آمنا ويتخطف الناس من حولهم أفبالباطل يؤمنون وبنعمة الله يكفرون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a [sufficient] residence for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse condemns those who fabricate lies about Allah or reject the truth when it is presented to them. It emphasizes that Hell is the fitting abode for such disbelievers, highlighting the severity of their transgression against the divine.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه أليس في جهنم مثوى للكافرين

translation: And those who strive for Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to strive and make efforts in the way of Allah. It promises that those who do so will be guided by Allah to the right path. The verse also affirms that Allah is with those who do good deeds and act righteously.
orig: والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا وإن الله لمع المحسنين

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: This is one of the 'Muqatta'at' (Disconnected Letters) that appear at the beginning of some Quranic chapters. The precise meaning of these letters is not definitively known, and their interpretation has been the subject of much discussion among Islamic scholars. However, the general consensus is that they serve as a reminder of the miraculous nature of the Quran, and that they signify the divine origin and authority of the revealed text.
orig: الم

translation: The Romans have been defeated
interpretation: This verse refers to the defeat of the Byzantine (Roman) Empire by the Sassanid Persians in the early 7th century CE. The verse is seen as a prophecy that the Romans (Byzantines) would eventually prevail over the Persians, which came true when the Byzantine Emperor Heraclius defeated the Persians in 628 CE. The verse is interpreted as a sign of God's power and a reminder that ultimately, good will triumph over evil.
orig: غلبت الروم

translation: In the lowest land, and they, after their defeat, will be victorious.
interpretation: This verse refers to the early Muslims who were persecuted and oppressed in Makkah. Despite their difficult circumstances, the verse promises that they will eventually emerge victorious over their oppressors. The "lowest land" likely refers to the harsh conditions they faced, but the promise of their eventual triumph conveys a message of hope and resilience in the face of adversity.
orig: في أدنى الأرض وهم من بعد غلبهم سيغلبون

translation: In a few years. To Allah belongs the command before and after. And that day the believers will rejoice.
interpretation: This verse refers to the eventual victory of the believers over their enemies and the establishment of God's rule on Earth. The phrase "in a few years" suggests that this triumph will come about relatively quickly, despite the current difficulties faced by the believers. The verse emphasizes that the ultimate power and authority belongs to God, both before and after this event. On the day of this victory, the believers will rejoice, as their faith and perseverance will be rewarded.
orig: في بضع سنين لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد ويومئذ يفرح المؤمنون

translation: With the help of Allah, He grants victory to whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that victory and success come from Allah, not from one's own strength or efforts. It is Allah who grants victory to whomever He wills, out of His infinite power and wisdom. The verse also highlights that Allah is the Almighty, possessing absolute power and authority, as well as the Most Merciful, showering His blessings and compassion upon His creation. This serves as a reminder that one should seek Allah's help and rely on Him, rather than one's own abilities, in order to achieve success.
orig: بنصر الله ينصر من يشاء وهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: Allah has made a promise, and Allah does not fail in His promise, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah always fulfills His promises, but many people are unaware of this fact. It serves as a reminder that we should have faith in Allah's promises and not doubt His ability to deliver on what He has committed to. The interpretation suggests that we should trust in Allah's words and not be among those who are ignorant of His unwavering commitment to His promises.
orig: وعد الله لا يخلف الله وعده ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: They know only the outward (things) in the life of this world, and they are heedless of the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people are only concerned with the material aspects of this worldly life and are neglectful or unaware of the life in the Hereafter. They are focused on the superficial and transient aspects of this world, without giving due consideration to the eternal consequences of their actions and beliefs. The verse cautions against such heedlessness and encourages a more balanced and comprehensive understanding of life, one that takes into account both the worldly and the spiritual dimensions.
orig: يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون

translation: Have they not reflected within themselves? Allah has not created the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and for a specified term. And indeed, many of the people, in the meeting with their Lord, are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect and ponder upon the creation of the heavens and the earth, which Allah has created with a purpose and for a specific duration. It suggests that those who fail to recognize the truth of Allah's creation and deny the meeting with their Lord on the Day of Judgment are disbelievers.
orig: أولم يتفكروا في أنفسهم ما خلق الله السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وأجل مسمى وإن كثيرا من الناس بلقاء ربهم لكافرون

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power, and they [i.e., the former peoples] plowed the earth and built it up more than these [i.e., the Makkans] have built it up, and their messengers came to them with clear evidences. And Allah would not have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the fate of previous generations who were more powerful and prosperous than the present one. The verse suggests that those who came before were able to develop and cultivate the land to a greater extent, yet they were ultimately destroyed due to their own wrongdoing and injustice. The message is that people should not be arrogant or complacent, but rather learn from the examples of the past and avoid the same mistakes that led to their downfall. The verse emphasizes that Allah does not wrong people, but it is their own actions that lead to their demise.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم كانوا أشد منهم قوة وأثاروا الأرض وعمروها أكثر مما عمروها وجاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: Then the end of those who did evil was that they denied the signs of Allah and used to mock at them.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who reject and mock the signs and messages of Allah. Their ultimate end is one of punishment and destruction, as they have chosen to disbelieve in Allah's guidance and treat it with disdain. The verse serves as a warning to those who would follow a similar path, emphasizing the consequences of turning away from the truth and rejecting Allah's divine revelations.
orig: ثم كان عاقبة الذين أساءوا السوأى أن كذبوا بآيات الله وكانوا بها يستهزئون

translation: Allah originates the creation, then He will repeat it, then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the belief in the power and authority of God (Allah) over the universe. It states that Allah is the one who initiates the creation of all things, and that He has the ability to repeat or resurrect this creation. The verse also affirms that all people will ultimately return to Allah, implying that there will be a Day of Judgment where people will be held accountable for their actions in this life.
orig: الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: And the Day the Hour appears the criminals will be in despair.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the Hour (the end of the world) arrives. On that day, the criminals, those who committed sins and transgressions, will be in a state of utter despair and hopelessness. They will realize the consequences of their actions and the futility of their worldly pursuits, as they face the reckoning and punishment for their misdeeds.
