orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يبلس المجرمون

translation: And their partners had not any [power of] intercession, and they [themselves] were disbelievers in their partners.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the idols and false deities worshipped by the polytheists had no power to intercede or provide any benefit to them. It highlights the futility of associating partners with Allah, as the polytheists were in fact disbelievers in their own false gods, which had no divine status or authority.
orig: ولم يكن لهم من شركائهم شفعاء وكانوا بشركائهم كافرين

translation: And the Day the Hour appears - that Day the people will be separated [into categories].
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all people will be resurrected and divided into different groups based on their beliefs and deeds in this life. On that Day, the righteous will be separated from the wicked, and each group will be held accountable for their actions. This emphasizes the importance of living a righteous life in preparation for the ultimate reckoning before God.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يومئذ يتفرقون

translation: But as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, they will be in a Garden [of Paradise], rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for those who have faith in God and do good deeds. The "Garden" refers to Paradise, a place of eternal bliss and happiness. Those who believe and act righteously will be in a state of joy and contentment, free from any worries or suffering. This verse emphasizes the importance of combining faith with righteous actions, as both are necessary to attain the ultimate reward of Paradise.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فهم في روضة يحبرون

translation: And as for those who disbelieve and deny Our verses and the meeting of the Hereafter, those will be brought to the punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fate of those who reject faith in God and deny the truth of the Qur"anic revelations, as well as the reality of the Hereafter. They will be subjected to punishment and held accountable for their disbelief and denial. The verse serves as a warning to those who turn away from God"s guidance and the belief in the afterlife.
orig: وأما الذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا ولقاء الآخرة فأولئك في العذاب محضرون

translation: So exalted is Allah at evening and morning.
interpretation: This verse encourages the remembrance and glorification of Allah at all times, particularly at the beginning and end of the day. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a constant state of awareness and gratitude towards Allah throughout one"s daily life.
orig: فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون

translation: And to Him belongs [all] praise in the heavens and the earth and [at] evening and when you are at noon.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all praise and gratitude is due to God, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. It highlights that God is to be praised at all times, whether in the morning, evening, or throughout the day. This is a reminder to constantly remember and acknowledge God's blessings and sovereignty over all of creation.
orig: وله الحمد في السماوات والأرض وعشيا وحين تظهرون

translation: He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living and gives life to the earth after its lifelessness. And thus will you be brought forth [from the dead].
interpretation: This verse is highlighting Allah's power and ability to create life from death, and death from life. It is a reminder that just as Allah brings forth the living from the dead, and the dead from the living, He will also resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment. This is a testament to His omnipotence and serves as a call for people to believe in the Hereafter and the resurrection.
orig: يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها وكذلك تخرجون

translation: And of His signs is that He created you from dust, then, suddenly you are human beings dispersing [throughout the earth].
interpretation: This verse highlights the creation of humans from the basic element of dust, which is a common and humble substance. It emphasizes that despite this simple origin, humans are then transformed into complex, intelligent, and capable beings who spread throughout the earth. This serves as a sign of God's power and wisdom in creating life from the most basic of materials and elevating it to a higher state of existence.
orig: ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون

translation: And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in creating spouses for humans, so that they may find comfort, love, and compassion in their relationships. The verse suggests that the institution of marriage is a sign of God's mercy and a reflection of His care for humanity. It encourages people to reflect on the purpose and blessings of marriage, which can foster a sense of peace, mutual understanding, and emotional fulfillment.
orig: ومن آياته أن خلق لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا لتسكنوا إليها وجعل بينكم مودة ورحمة إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your languages and your colors. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the diversity in creation, such as the heavens, the earth, and the differences in human languages and physical appearances, are all signs of God's power, wisdom and glory. These variations are meant to be a source of wonder and contemplation for those who possess knowledge and understanding.
orig: ومن آياته خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف ألسنتكم وألوانكم إن في ذلك لآيات للعالمين

translation: And of His signs is your sleep by night and day and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who hear.
interpretation: This verse highlights two of God's signs that indicate His power and wisdom: your sleep by night and day, and your seeking of His bounty. Sleep, which is a state of rest and restoration, is a remarkable phenomenon that demonstrates God's care for His creation. Similarly, the human desire and ability to seek and obtain provisions from God's bounty is a testament to His providence. These signs should be recognized and appreciated by those who listen and reflect on the wonders of the universe.
orig: ومن آياته منامكم بالليل والنهار وابتغاؤكم من فضله إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يسمعون

translation: And of His signs is [that] He shows you the lightning [causing] fear and aspiration, and He sends down rain from the sky by which He gives life to the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights two of Allah's signs that demonstrate His power and wisdom. The first is the lightning, which can inspire both fear and hope in people. The lightning is a reminder of Allah's might, but also of His ability to provide for His creation. The second sign is the rain, which breathes life back into the earth after it has become barren and lifeless. This illustrates Allah's control over life and death, and His ability to sustain the world He has created. The verse encourages people to reflect on these signs and use their reason to recognize the oneness and sovereignty of Allah.
orig: ومن آياته يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا وينزل من السماء ماء فيحيي به الأرض بعد موتها إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And among His signs is that the heavens and the earth stand by His command. Then when He calls you with a [single] call from the earth, immediately you will come forth.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute power and authority of Allah over the entire universe. The heavens and the earth exist and function according to His command, demonstrating His sovereignty. When Allah summons humanity on the Day of Resurrection, people will emerge from the earth without delay, emphasizing the certainty of the Hereafter and the accountability of all human beings before their Creator.
orig: ومن آياته أن تقوم السماء والأرض بأمره ثم إذا دعاكم دعوة من الأرض إذا أنتم تخرجون

translation: And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. All are to Him devoutly obedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everything and everyone in the heavens and the earth belongs to and is subservient to God. It underscores the absolute sovereignty and dominion of God over all creation, leaving no room for any other deity or authority. The phrase "all are to Him devoutly obedient" implies that all beings, whether conscious or not, willingly or unwillingly, submit to the will and command of the Almighty. This verse reinforces the concept of divine unity and the idea that God alone deserves worship and obedience.
orig: وله من في السماوات والأرض كل له قانتون

translation: And it is He who originates the creation and then repeats it, and that is [even] easier for Him. And to Him belongs the highest attribute in the heavens and earth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and wisdom in creating the universe and all that is in it. He is the One who initiates the creation, and then brings it back to life again, which is an easy task for Him. God has the highest and most perfect attributes, and He is the Mighty and the Wise, whose knowledge and power are beyond human comprehension.
orig: وهو الذي يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده وهو أهون عليه وله المثل الأعلى في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: He has set forth for you a parable from yourselves. Do you have among those whom your right hands possess (i.e., your slaves) any partners in what We have provided for you so that you are equal therein [and] would fear them as your fear of one another [within your family]? Thus do We explain the verses that perhaps you may reason.
interpretation: This verse uses the example of slaves that one owns to illustrate a broader principle about God's Lordship. Just as you do not treat your slaves as equals to yourself, so too should you not consider any created being as an equal to God. You fear your slaves, but you should fear God even more, as He is the true Provider and Master. This verse encourages people to use their reason to understand God's signs and oneness, and not to ascribe partners to Him.
orig: ضرب لكم مثلا من أنفسكم هل لكم من ما ملكت أيمانكم من شركاء في ما رزقناكم فأنتم فيه سواء تخافونهم كخيفتكم أنفسكم كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: Nay, but those who do wrong follow their own lusts without knowledge. Who is able to guide him whom Allah has sent astray? And for such there are no helpers.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who follow their own desires and whims without any knowledge or guidance from Allah. It emphasizes that those who have gone astray cannot be guided by anyone other than Allah, and they have no one to help them. The verse serves as a warning to people not to blindly follow their own desires, but to seek knowledge and guidance from Allah in order to live a righteous life.
orig: بل اتبع الذين ظلموا أهواءهم بغير علم فمن يهدي من أضل الله وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a sincere and upright disposition in one's faith. It calls upon the believer to direct their entire being towards the true religion, which is the natural inclination (fitrah) that Allah has instilled in all people. The verse highlights that the creation of Allah is immutable, and that the true religion is the correct and unwavering path, even though most people are unaware of this fact.
orig: فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرت الله التي فطر الناس عليها لا تبديل لخلق الله ذلك الدين القيم ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: Turn to Him in repentance and fear Him, and establish prayer and do not be of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to turn to Allah in sincere repentance, to fear and revere Him, to establish regular prayer, and to avoid the sin of associating partners with Allah (shirk). It emphasizes the importance of a direct and devoted relationship with the One true God, without ascribing divinity to any other being or entity. The verse highlights the core tenets of Islamic faith - tawheed (belief in the oneness of God), tawbah (repentance), and salah (ritual prayer) - as the path to spiritual purification and nearness to the Divine.
orig: منيبين إليه واتقوه وأقيموا الصلاة ولا تكونوا من المشركين

translation: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - you, [O Muhammad], are not [in any way] of them. Their affair is only [left] to Allah; then He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who have divided their religion into different sects and groups, each of which is content with its own beliefs and practices. The message is that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not responsible for these divisions, as they are the result of people's own choices. Ultimately, it is Allah who will judge them for their actions.
orig: من الذين فرقوا دينهم وكانوا شيعا كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون

translation: And when affliction touches people, they call upon their Lord, turning to Him in repentance. But then, when He gives them a taste of mercy from Him, at once a party of them associate others with their Lord [in worship].
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to turn to God in times of distress, but then to often forget their devotion and commitment to Him when they experience His mercy and blessings. It serves as a reminder that true faith and worship of God should not be contingent on one's circumstances, but should be a constant state of being.
orig: وإذا مس الناس ضر دعوا ربهم منيبين إليه ثم إذا أذاقهم منه رحمة إذا فريق منهم بربهم يشركون

translation: That they may disbelieve in that which We have given them. So enjoy yourselves, for you are going to know.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject the guidance and blessings that God has provided them will be left to enjoy the temporary pleasures of this world. However, they will eventually come to realize the consequences of their disbelief and rejection of the truth.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم فتمتعوا فسوف تعلمون

translation: Or have We sent down to them an authority, and it is it that speaks of that which they associate with Him?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Qur'an itself is a clear authority and proof from God, which refutes the polytheistic beliefs and practices of the people. The Qur'an speaks directly to the falsehood of associating partners with God, providing guidance and evidence against such beliefs.
orig: أم أنزلنا عليهم سلطانا فهو يتكلم بما كانوا به يشركون

translation: And when We give the people a taste of mercy, they rejoice in it; but if evil afflicts them for what their hands have put forth, immediately they are in despair.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to be fickle and inconsistent in their response to God's actions. When people experience God's mercy and blessings, they are quick to rejoice and be grateful. However, when they face adversity or hardship, they become despondent and lose hope, forgetting that it is often a consequence of their own actions. The verse suggests that people should maintain a steadfast faith in God's wisdom and justice, regardless of the circumstances they find themselves in.
orig: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة فرحوا بها وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدمت أيديهم إذا هم يقنطون

translation: Have they not seen that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to reflect on Allah's power and wisdom in providing sustenance. It suggests that Allah's distribution of resources is not random, but rather based on His divine plan and knowledge. The verse invites people to have faith in Allah's judgment and to recognize the signs of His sovereignty in the way He grants and restricts provision. The interpretation emphasizes that this understanding should lead to belief and trust in Allah among those who reflect on it.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And give the relative his right, and [also] the poor and the traveler, and do not spend wastefully. Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, and ever has Satan been to his Lord ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to fulfill the rights of their relatives, the poor, and the travelers. It emphasizes that this is better for those who seek the pleasure of Allah, and they are the ones who will be successful. The verse also warns against wasteful spending, as those who are wasteful are like the devils, and Satan himself has always been ungrateful to his Lord.
orig: فآت ذا القربى حقه والمسكين وابن السبيل ذلك خير للذين يريدون وجه الله وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And whatever you give as interest to increase the wealth of people will not increase with Allah. But what you give in zakah, desiring the countenance of Allah - those are the multipliers.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of usury or interest-based lending, which was common in pre-Islamic Arabia. It states that any wealth gained through interest will not be blessed by Allah and will not truly increase the wealth of the people. In contrast, the verse encourages the practice of zakah (obligatory charity) as a means of seeking the pleasure of Allah, and promises that those who give zakah will be rewarded with their wealth being multiplied.
orig: وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس فلا يربو عند الله وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون

translation: Allah is the One who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, and then will give you life. Is there any of your "partners" who does anything of that? Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all aspects of human existence. He is the sole Creator, Sustainer, and Giver of life and death. The verse challenges the notion of associating partners with Allah, as none of these "partners" have any power or ability to perform these divine acts. The verse affirms the transcendence and uniqueness of Allah, who is free from any association or partnership with others.
orig: الله الذي خلقكم ثم رزقكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم هل من شركائكم من يفعل من ذلكم من شيء سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: Corruption has appeared throughout the land and sea by [reason of] what the hands of people have earned so He may let them taste part of [the consequence of] what they have done that perhaps they will return [to righteousness].
interpretation: This verse suggests that the corruption and destruction that has appeared on land and in the sea is a result of the misdeeds and wrongful actions of people. The purpose of this is to make people taste the consequences of their actions, in the hope that they will turn back to the path of righteousness and repentance.
orig: ظهر الفساد في البر والبحر بما كسبت أيدي الناس ليذيقهم بعض الذي عملوا لعلهم يرجعون

translation: Say, "Travel through the land and observe how was the end of those before. Most of them were associators [of others with Allah]."
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the fate of previous nations and civilizations who associated partners with Allah. The message is that those who rejected the oneness of God and engaged in polytheism ultimately faced a dire consequence. The instruction to "travel through the land" suggests that by observing the ruins and remnants of past societies, one can gain insight into the importance of upholding the belief in the sole divinity of Allah.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبل كان أكثرهم مشركين

translation: So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse is instructing the believers to firmly adhere to the true religion of Islam, which is the natural religion of mankind as created by Allah. It emphasizes that the religion of Islam is the correct and unchanging path, even though most people may not recognize this truth. The verse is a call to steadfastness in faith before the Day of Judgment arrives, when people will be held accountable for their beliefs and actions.
orig: فأقم وجهك للدين القيم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا مرد له من الله يومئذ يصدعون

translation: Whoever disbelieves - upon him is [the consequence of] his disbelief. And those who do righteous deeds - for themselves they are preparing [i.e., storing up good for themselves].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of individual responsibility and accountability. It states that whoever rejects faith in God and His teachings will bear the consequences of their disbelief. On the other hand, those who perform good deeds and righteous actions will be rewarded for their efforts, as they are preparing a good future for themselves. The verse highlights the fact that each person is responsible for their own choices and actions, and will be held accountable for them.
orig: من كفر فعليه كفره ومن عمل صالحا فلأنفسهم يمهدون

translation: That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds out of His bounty. Indeed, He does not like the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah will reward those who have faith in Him and do good deeds. The reward will come from Allah's grace and bounty, not as an entitlement. In contrast, Allah does not favor those who reject faith and refuse to do righteous acts.
orig: ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من فضله إنه لا يحب الكافرين

translation: And of His signs is [that] He sends the winds as bringers of good tidings and to let you taste of His mercy and so the ships may sail by His command and [that] you may seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights some of the signs of Allah`s power and mercy. The sending of the winds as bringers of good tidings, such as rain, is a sign of His power and provision. The fact that we can taste of His mercy, through the sustenance and blessings He provides, is another sign. The ability of ships to sail by His command is a further demonstration of His control over the natural world. And the opportunity to seek His bounty, through the resources and means He has provided, is a call to be grateful for His generosity. The overall message is one of recognizing Allah`s sovereignty, appreciating His blessings, and responding with thankfulness.
orig: ومن آياته أن يرسل الرياح مبشرات وليذيقكم من رحمته ولتجري الفلك بأمره ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And We have certainly sent [messengers] before you, [O Muhammad], to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs, and We took retribution from those who committed crimes, and [incumbent upon Us] was support of the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has sent messengers to various peoples throughout history, not just to the people of Muhammad (peace be upon him). These messengers came with clear proofs and evidence, but the disbelievers among their people rejected the message and committed crimes. Allah then took retribution against those who rejected the truth, and it is incumbent upon Allah to support and aid the believers who accept the message of the messengers.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك رسلا إلى قومهم فجاءوهم بالبينات فانتقمنا من الذين أجرموا وكان حقا علينا نصر المؤمنين

translation: It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a land that is dead, and revive the earth after its death. Thus is the Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over the natural world. He sends the winds that bring the clouds, and then He spreads those clouds in the sky as He wills. When the rain falls from those clouds, it brings life to the dead land, just as Allah will resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment. This is a sign of Allah's might and a reminder that He alone has the power to create and sustain all of creation.
orig: الله الذي يرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فيبسطه في السماء كيف يشاء ويجعله كسفا فترى الودق يخرج من خلاله فإذا أصاب به من يشاء من عباده إذا هم يستبشرون

translation: And if they had believed before that and had attained the blessings, they would have been [even] better off.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who believe in God and His revelations before the Qur'an was revealed would have been in an even better position had they accepted the truth earlier. It implies that faith and righteous deeds are rewarded, and that those who embrace the truth sooner are more fortunate than those who delay their belief.
orig: وإن كانوا من قبل أن ينزل عليهم من قبله لمبلسين

translation: So look at the effects of Allah's mercy, how He gives life to the earth after its death. Indeed, that [same one] will give life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse encourages us to reflect on the signs of Allah's mercy and power in the world around us. The revival of the earth after it has died and become barren is a testament to Allah's ability to give life and resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment. Just as Allah has the power to bring the earth back to life, He also has the power to resurrect all of humanity on the Day of Reckoning. This serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and the certainty of the Hereafter.
orig: فانظر إلى آثار رحمت الله كيف يحيي الأرض بعد موتها إن ذلك لمحيي الموتى وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And if We should send a [calamitous] wind and they saw [their crops] turned yellow, they would remain thereafter disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even if the disbelievers were to witness clear signs of Allah's power, such as a destructive wind that turns their crops yellow, they would still persist in their disbelief and rejection of faith. It highlights the stubborn nature of those who refuse to acknowledge the truth, even in the face of undeniable evidence.
orig: ولئن أرسلنا ريحا فرأوه مصفرا لظلوا من بعده يكفرون

translation: Indeed, you do not make the dead to hear, nor do you make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs [in flight].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad cannot make the dead or the deaf hear his message. It is a reminder that the message of Islam must be conveyed to those who are willing to listen and accept it, not those who have turned away from it. The verse suggests that the Prophet should focus his efforts on those who are receptive to his teachings, rather than wasting time on those who have already rejected them.
orig: فإنك لا تسمع الموتى ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ولوا مدبرين

translation: And you are not [responsible] to guide the blind from their error. You will only guide those who believe in Our verses so they are [willingly] submitting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad is not responsible for guiding those who stubbornly refuse to believe in the signs of Allah. Rather, he is only responsible for guiding those who willingly accept the message of Islam and submit to the will of Allah. The guidance of Allah is only for those who have faith in His revelations and are willing to follow them.
orig: وما أنت بهاد العمي عن ضلالتهم إن تسمع إلا من يؤمن بآياتنا فهم مسلمون

translation: Allah is the One who created you from weakness, then He appointed after weakness, strength, then He appointed after strength, weakness and grayness. He creates what He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute power and sovereignty in creating and shaping human beings. It emphasizes that Allah has complete control over our lives, taking us through various stages of strength and weakness, youth and old age. The verse reminds us that Allah creates whatever He wills, and He is the All-Knowing and All-Powerful, capable of doing anything. This serves as a reminder to us to submit to Allah's will and not to be arrogant about our own strength or abilities, as they are ultimately granted by Allah and can be taken away by Him.
orig: الله الذي خلقكم من ضعف ثم جعل من بعد ضعف قوة ثم جعل من بعد قوة ضعفا وشيبة يخلق ما يشاء وهو العليم القدير

translation: And the Day the Hour appears the criminals will swear they had remained but an hour. Thus they were deluded.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection. When the Hour arrives, the criminals will be shocked and will claim that they had only remained in the world for a short time, as if it was just an hour. This indicates that they were completely unaware of the true nature of the Hereafter and were deluded by the temporary pleasures of this world, failing to prepare for the eternal life to come.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يقسم المجرمون ما لبثوا غير ساعة كذلك كانوا يؤفكون

translation: And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, "You remained during the extent of the life of the world until the Day of Resurrection, and this is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not know."
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who have knowledge and faith, and those who do not. On the Day of Resurrection, the knowledgeable and faithful will realize that the disbelievers remained in the world until the Day of Judgment, but they did not know or acknowledge it. This emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and having faith, as it allows one to understand the true nature of reality and the afterlife.
orig: وقال الذين أوتوا العلم والإيمان لقد لبثتم في كتاب الله إلى يوم البعث فهذا يوم البعث ولكنكم كنتم لا تعلمون

translation: And that Day, the wrongdoers will not benefit from their [empty] excuses, nor will they be invited [to seek] forgiveness.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who committed injustice and wrongdoing will not be able to provide any justification or excuse for their actions. They will not be given the opportunity to seek forgiveness or make amends, as their time for repentance has passed.
orig: فيومئذ لا ينفع الذين ظلموا معذرتهم ولا هم يستعتبون

translation: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example. But, [O Muhammad], if you should bring them a sign, the disbelievers will surely say, "You [believers] are but falsifiers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an contains a wide variety of examples and parables to guide humanity. However, even if the Prophet Muhammad were to show the disbelievers a miraculous sign, they would still reject it and accuse the believers of falsehood. This highlights the stubbornness and closed-mindedness of those who refuse to accept the truth of the Qur'an and the message of Islam.
orig: ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل ولئن جئتهم بآية ليقولن الذين كفروا إن أنتم إلا مبطلون

translation: Thus does Allah seal over the hearts of those who do not know.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has the power to seal or close the hearts and minds of those who lack knowledge and understanding. It implies that those who do not seek knowledge or are unwilling to learn may be prevented from gaining deeper insight and wisdom. The verse serves as a warning that one should strive to acquire knowledge and understanding, lest their hearts become hardened and closed off from the guidance of Allah.
orig: كذلك يطبع الله على قلوب الذين لا يعلمون

translation: So be patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth, and let them not take conceit from those who are certain [of disbelief].
interpretation: This verse encourages patience and steadfastness in the face of adversity and disbelief. It reminds us that the promise of Allah is true and that we should not be swayed or discouraged by those who do not have firm faith. The interpretation suggests that we should remain steadfast in our beliefs and not be influenced by the arrogance or skepticism of those who reject the truth of Allah's message.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق ولا يستخفنك الذين لا يوقنون

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: The opening letters Alif, Lam, Meem are known as the 'Muqatta'at' or 'Disconnected Letters' that appear at the beginning of certain chapters of the Quran. Their exact meaning and significance is not entirely clear, but they are believed to be a part of the divine wisdom and a way for God to emphasize the miraculous nature of the Quran. These letters may represent the challenges facing the unbelievers in understanding the Quran, or they may be a symbolic reference to the divine attributes of God.
orig: الم

translation: These are the verses of the wise Book.
interpretation: This verse introduces the Qur'an as the "wise Book" - a reference to its divine origin, profound wisdom, and guidance for humanity. It establishes the Qur'an as a revealed scripture containing signs and messages from God that are worthy of contemplation and adherence.
orig: تلك آيات الكتاب الحكيم

translation: Guidance and mercy for the doers of good
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a source of guidance and mercy for those who strive to do good deeds and lead righteous lives. It suggests that the Qur'anic teachings are not just for the believers, but for all who seek to improve themselves and contribute positively to society. The verse highlights the inclusive and compassionate nature of the divine guidance revealed in the Qur'an.
orig: هدى ورحمة للمحسنين

translation: Those who establish prayer and give zakah, and they are certain of the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of two key pillars of Islamic faith: establishing regular prayer (salat) and giving obligatory charity (zakah). Those who faithfully uphold these practices are described as being "certain of the Hereafter", indicating that their belief in the life after death is firm and unwavering. This suggests that a true believer's actions are guided by a strong conviction in the reality of the Day of Judgment and the eternal life in the Hereafter. The verse highlights that these spiritual and charitable deeds are not just outward rituals, but are rooted in a deep inner certainty about the divine realities.
orig: الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم بالآخرة هم يوقنون

translation: Those are the ones who are [rightly] guided by their Lord, and it is those who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who are guided by Allah and will attain success in this life and the Hereafter. The phrase "those are the ones who are [rightly] guided by their Lord" indicates that they have received divine guidance and are following the path ordained by Allah. The following phrase, "and it is those who are the successful", suggests that their adherence to this guidance will lead them to triumph and prosperity, both spiritual and worldly. The verse emphasizes that true success and salvation can only be achieved by those who follow the righteous path laid out by Allah.
orig: أولئك على هدى من ربهم وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And of the people is he who buys the amusement of speech to mislead [others] from the way of Allah without knowledge and who takes it [i.e., His way] in ridicule. Those will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who indulge in idle talk and frivolous discussions that lead people astray from the path of Allah. They do this without any real knowledge or understanding, and they treat the truth of Allah's guidance with mockery and derision. The verse warns that such people will face a humiliating punishment for their actions.
orig: ومن الناس من يشتري لهو الحديث ليضل عن سبيل الله بغير علم ويتخذها هزوا أولئك لهم عذاب مهين

translation: And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away in pride, as if he had not heard them, as if in his ears was a deafness. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of those who arrogantly reject the signs and messages of Allah. They turn away in pride, acting as if they have not heard the verses being recited to them, as if they have a deafness in their ears. This is a warning that those who persist in this attitude of arrogance and rejection will be subject to a painful punishment.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليه آياتنا ولى مستكبرا كأن لم يسمعها كأن في أذنيه وقرا فبشره بعذاب أليم

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them are the Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse promises that those who have faith in God and do good deeds will be rewarded with the eternal bliss and delights of Paradise. It emphasizes that belief and righteous actions go hand-in-hand, and that the ultimate reward for such a combination is the highest level of paradise, referred to as "the Gardens of Pleasure". This verse encourages believers to strive for both spiritual and moral excellence in order to attain this sublime reward in the Hereafter.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم جنات النعيم

translation: Abiding therein eternally. [It is] the promise of Allah [which is] truth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the reward for the believers in the Hereafter. It affirms that the promise of Allah is true and that He is the Almighty, the All-Wise. The interpretation suggests that the believers can have complete confidence in Allah's promise of eternal life in the Hereafter, as He is the Sovereign and the All-Knowing, and His decree is just and wise.
orig: خالدين فيها وعد الله حقا وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: He created the heavens without pillars that you see, and has cast into the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with you, and dispersed therein from every [kind of] creature. And We sent down rain from the sky and caused to grow therein [plants] of every noble [kind].
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and majesty of God as the Creator of the universe. It describes how God created the heavens without any visible support, and how He placed firmly set mountains on the earth to prevent it from shaking and shifting. The verse also emphasizes God's provision for all living creatures, as He has dispersed various forms of life on the earth and sent down rain from the sky to nourish the growth of noble plants. This verse serves to remind us of God's infinite wisdom, power, and care for His creation.
orig: خلق السماوات بغير عمد ترونها وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم وبث فيها من كل دابة وأنزلنا من السماء ماء فأنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم

translation: This is the creation of Allah; so show Me what those besides Him have created. Rather, the wrongdoers are in clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the creation of the universe is the work of Allah alone, and challenges those who worship idols or associate partners with Allah to show what they have created. It highlights the fact that those who commit injustice and ascribe partners to Allah are clearly misguided and in a state of profound error.
orig: هذا خلق الله فأروني ماذا خلق الذين من دونه بل الظالمون في ضلال مبين

translation: And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom [and said], "Be grateful to Allah." And whoever is grateful is grateful for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever denies [His favor] - then indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and humility towards Allah. Luqman, known for his wisdom, was given this wisdom by Allah, and he was instructed to be grateful to Allah for this gift. The verse highlights that the act of gratitude ultimately benefits the individual, as it strengthens one's relationship with the Divine. Conversely, those who deny or are ungrateful for Allah's blessings only harm themselves, as Allah is self-sufficient and in no need of their gratitude. The verse encourages believers to cultivate an attitude of thankfulness and appreciation for the blessings bestowed upon them by the Almighty.
orig: ولقد آتينا لقمان الحكمة أن اشكر لله ومن يشكر فإنما يشكر لنفسه ومن كفر فإن الله غني حميد

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Luqman said to his son while he was instructing him, "O my son, do not associate [anything] with Allah. Indeed, association [with him] is great injustice."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the gravity of associating partners with Allah. Luqman, known for his wisdom, is advising his son to avoid the sin of shirk (polytheism) as it is a grave injustice. The interpretation highlights that worshipping or ascribing divinity to anything other than the one true God is a fundamental violation of the principle of tawheed (the oneness of God) and a grave moral and spiritual transgression.
orig: وإذ قال لقمان لابنه وهو يعظه يا بني لا تشرك بالله إن الشرك لظلم عظيم

translation: And We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents. His mother carried him, [increasing her] in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years. [He is commanded], "Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the [final] destination."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of caring for one's parents, especially the mother who endures great hardship in bearing and raising the child. It commands the child to be grateful to Allah and to their parents, as the final destination is with Allah.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه حملته أمه وهنا على وهن وفصاله في عامين أن اشكر لي ولوالديك إلي المصير

translation: And if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them but accompany them [in this world] with appropriate kindness and follow the way of those who turn back to Me [in repentance]. Then to Me will be your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of not associating any partners with Allah, even if those close to you try to persuade you to do so. It instructs the believer to maintain appropriate kindness and companionship with others, while following the path of those who repent and return to Allah. Ultimately, all will return to Allah, who will inform them of their deeds.
orig: وإن جاهداك على أن تشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما وصاحبهما في الدنيا معروفا واتبع سبيل من أناب إلي ثم إلي مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O my son, indeed if it [i.e., a wrong] should be the weight of a mustard seed, [and it is] within a rock or [anywhere] in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted [with all things].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and power of Allah. It conveys the message that no deed, no matter how small or insignificant it may seem, can escape the knowledge and judgment of Allah. Even if a wrongdoing is as small as a mustard seed, hidden within a rock or anywhere in the universe, Allah is aware of it and will bring it forth. This highlights the importance of being mindful of our actions, as Allah is All-Knowing and All-Powerful.
orig: يا بني إنها إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل فتكن في صخرة أو في السماوات أو في الأرض يأت بها الله إن الله لطيف خبير

translation: O my son, establish prayer and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, [all] that is of the matters [requiring] determination.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and calls upon him to instruct his followers to uphold the five daily prayers, to promote good and forbid evil, and to be steadfast in the face of adversity. The verse emphasizes that these are among the most important and resolute matters that a believer must adhere to. The interpretation is that a true believer must diligently fulfill their religious obligations, work to improve society, and remain patient and persevere through life's challenges, as these are the hallmarks of a strong faith.
orig: يا بني أقم الصلاة وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر واصبر على ما أصابك إن ذلك من عزم الأمور

translation: And do not turn your cheek in scorn toward people and do not walk through the earth exultantly. Indeed, Allah does not like every self-conceited boaster.
interpretation: This verse instructs us to not be arrogant or conceited in our interactions with others. We should not look down on people or walk with an air of superiority. Allah does not like those who are full of pride and self-importance. Instead, we should be humble and treat all people with respect, regardless of their status or position.
orig: ولا تصعر خدك للناس ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا إن الله لا يحب كل مختال فخور

translation: And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice; indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys.
interpretation: This verse encourages moderation and humility in one's conduct and speech. It advises to walk at a moderate pace and to speak in a lowered voice, as the braying of donkeys is considered the most unpleasant of sounds. The message is to avoid excessiveness, arrogance or boastfulness, and instead adopt a humble and restrained demeanor in one's daily life and interactions with others.
orig: واقصد في مشيك واغضض من صوتك إن أنكر الأصوات لصوت الحمير

translation: Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and amply bestowed upon you His favors, [both] apparent and unapparent? And [yet] of the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book.
interpretation: This verse encourages us to reflect on the blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon us, both visible and invisible. It reminds us that everything in the heavens and the earth has been subjected to our use, as a sign of Allah's generosity and care for us. However, it also warns against those who argue about Allah without any real knowledge, guidance or divine revelation to support their claims. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance from authentic sources, rather than relying on personal opinions or unfounded beliefs.
orig: ألم تروا أن الله سخر لكم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وأسبغ عليكم نعمه ظاهرة وباطنة ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ولا هدى ولا كتاب منير

translation: And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed," they say, "Rather, we will follow that upon which we found our fathers." Even if Satan was inviting them to the punishment of the Blaze?
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of some people to blindly follow the traditions and beliefs of their ancestors, even if they contradict the guidance revealed by Allah. It suggests that such adherence to ancestral practices can lead one to follow Satan and ultimately to the punishment of the Hellfire, rather than the path of righteousness prescribed by Allah. The verse encourages critical thinking and a willingness to follow the divine guidance, even if it differs from the established norms of one's society.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اتبعوا ما أنزل الله قالوا بل نتبع ما وجدنا عليه آباءنا أولو كان الشيطان يدعوهم إلى عذاب السعير

translation: And whoever submits his face [i.e., himself] to Allah while he is a doer of good - then he has grasped the most trustworthy handhold. And to Allah will be the [good] outcome of [all] matters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of submitting oneself completely to Allah while also doing good deeds. The "most trustworthy handhold" refers to the firm belief and trust in Allah, which will lead to the best outcome in all matters. This verse encourages believers to devote themselves to Allah and strive to do righteous actions, as this is the path to success in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: ومن يسلم وجهه إلى الله وهو محسن فقد استمسك بالعروة الوثقى وإلى الله عاقبة الأمور

translation: And whoever disbelieves - let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet (peace be upon him) not to be saddened by the disbelief of those who reject the message of Islam. It reminds us that all people will ultimately return to Allah, and He will inform them of their deeds and judge them accordingly. This verse emphasizes that Allah has full knowledge of what is in people's hearts and minds, and nothing is hidden from Him.
orig: ومن كفر فلا يحزنك كفره إلينا مرجعهم فننبئهم بما عملوا إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: We give them enjoyment for a little, then We will force them to a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject faith and engage in wrongdoing may be granted a temporary period of enjoyment and prosperity, but ultimately they will face a severe and unrelenting punishment. The Qur'an warns that such people should not be deceived by their temporary success, as they will be held accountable for their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: نمتعهم قليلا ثم نضطرهم إلى عذاب غليظ

translation: And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, "Allah." Say, "[All] praise is [due] to Allah." But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the innate understanding that most people have about the existence of God (Allah) as the Creator of the heavens and the earth. When asked directly about the origin of the universe, people will readily acknowledge that Allah is the Creator. However, the verse also suggests that despite this acknowledgment, many people do not truly understand or appreciate the implications of this belief. The verse encourages believers to give praise and gratitude to Allah, the One who has created all that exists.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله قل الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all that exists in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah alone. He is the One who is self-sufficient, not in need of anything or anyone, and is worthy of all praise and glorification. It underscores the absolute sovereignty and independence of Allah, the Creator and Sustainer of the universe, who is free from all needs and imperfections.
orig: لله ما في السماوات والأرض إن الله هو الغني الحميد

translation: And if all the trees on earth were pens and the sea [was ink], replenished thereafter by seven [more] seas, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the infinite nature of Allah's knowledge and power. Even if all the trees on earth were made into pens, and the entire ocean and seven more oceans were used as ink, the words and knowledge of Allah would still not be exhausted. This is a testament to the limitless wisdom and might of the Almighty. The verse serves to remind us of the unfathomable nature of Allah's creation and the insignificance of human knowledge in comparison to the divine.
orig: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام والبحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر ما نفدت كلمات الله إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: And He it is who created you and brought you into being, and to Him shall you be gathered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God is the sole Creator of all human beings, and that ultimately all people will be resurrected and gathered before Him for judgement. The phrase "as a single soul" suggests that all of humanity is interconnected, originating from a single source. The attributes of God mentioned, "All-Hearing" and "All-Seeing", indicate His omniscience and ability to hold people accountable for their actions.
orig: ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة إن الله سميع بصير

translation: Have you not seen that Allah causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term, and that Allah, with whatever you do, is Acquainted?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over the natural cycles of day and night, as well as the movement of the sun and moon. It suggests that Allah is the ultimate orchestrator of the universe, subjecting these celestial bodies to His will and plan. The verse also indicates that Allah is fully aware of and knowledgeable about all of our actions, reminding us of His constant surveillance and the need to live righteously.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري إلى أجل مسمى وأن الله بما تعملون خبير

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and that which they call upon other than Him is falsehood, and that Allah - He is the Most High, the Grand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the absolute and ultimate truth, while all other deities or objects of worship are false and worthless. It affirms Allah's supreme power, majesty, and authority as the Highest and the Greatest, deserving of all worship and obedience.
orig: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأن ما يدعون من دونه الباطل وأن الله هو العلي الكبير

translation: Have you not seen that the ships sail through the sea by the grace of Allah, that He may show you of His signs? Indeed in that are signs for every patient and grateful [servant].
interpretation: This verse encourages us to reflect on the wonders of Allah's creation, specifically the ships that sail through the sea. The verse highlights that the ships are able to sail due to the grace and power of Allah, not by their own might. This is a sign of Allah's greatness and an invitation for us to be patient and grateful in our faith. The interpretation suggests that by contemplating such signs, every person who is steadfast in their belief and thankful to Allah can find guidance and affirmation of their faith.
orig: ألم تر أن الفلك تجري في البحر بنعمت الله ليريكم من آياته إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And when a wave covers them like canopies, they call upon Allah, submitting to Him in faith. But when He delivers them to the land, [some] of them are moderate [in faith]. And none reject Our signs except everyone treacherous and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse describes the behavior of people when they face a crisis or danger, such as a storm at sea. In such situations, they sincerely call upon Allah, submitting to Him in faith and seeking His help. However, once they are delivered from the danger and reach land safely, some of them become moderate in their faith, while others completely reject Allah's signs and are ungrateful for the blessings they have received. This highlights the tendency of some people to turn away from Allah when they are no longer in immediate need of His help, despite the clear signs of His power and mercy.
orig: وإذا غشيهم موج كالظلل دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر فمنهم مقتصد وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا كل ختار كفور

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord and fear a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth, so let not the worldly life delude you and be not deceived about Allah by the Deceiver.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fearing and obeying Allah, the Almighty. It warns that on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to help or save another, not even a parent for their child or a child for their parent. This is because the promise of Allah is true and will come to pass. The verse cautions against being deluded by the fleeting pleasures of this worldly life and being deceived by Satan, who tries to turn people away from the path of righteousness. The ultimate accountability is to Allah, and one should strive to live a life that pleases Him.
orig: يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم واخشوا يوما لا يجزي والد عن ولده ولا مولود هو جاز عن والده شيئا إن وعد الله حق فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور

translation: Indeed, Allah [alone] has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. And no soul perceives what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul perceives in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing and Acquainted [with all things].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and power of Allah. He alone has knowledge of the appointed time of the Hour (the Day of Resurrection), and it is He who sends down the rain from the sky. Allah also knows the secrets of the wombs, including the gender, characteristics, and fate of the unborn. No one can know what they will earn or achieve in the future, nor can anyone know the time and place of their death. This highlights the complete sovereignty of Allah over all affairs and the need for humans to submit to His will and seek His guidance, as He alone is All-Knowing and Fully Aware of all things.
orig: إن الله عنده علم الساعة وينزل الغيث ويعلم ما في الأرحام وما تدري نفس ماذا تكسب غدا وما تدري نفس بأي أرض تموت إن الله عليم خبير

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: The letters Alif, Lam, and Meem are among the 'Muqatta'at' or 'Disconnected Letters' that appear at the beginning of some chapters of the Quran. Their exact meaning and significance are not definitively known, but they are believed to be a part of the divine wisdom and a way for God to emphasize the miraculous nature of the Quran. Some scholars interpret these letters as representing the names of God, or as symbols of the Quran's divine origin and the unity of God.
orig: الم

translation: The revelation of the Book, there is no doubt about it, is from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an is a revelation from God, the Lord of all creation, and that there is no doubt or uncertainty about its divine origin. It establishes the Qur'an as an authoritative and infallible scripture, which believers can trust and rely upon without any hesitation.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين

translation: Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, [O Muhammad], that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you [so] perhaps they will be guided.
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusation made by the disbelievers that the Qur'an was fabricated by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The Qur'an refutes this claim, stating that the Qur'an is the truth revealed by God to the Prophet, so that he may warn the people who have not received a messenger before him, in the hope that they may be guided to the right path.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه بل هو الحق من ربك لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير من قبلك لعلهم يهتدون

translation: Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then He established Himself above the Throne. You have not besides Him any protector or any intercessor; so will you not be reminded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme power and sovereignty of Allah as the sole Creator of the universe. It highlights that Allah alone has the authority to govern and guide His creation, and that there is no one else worthy of worship or able to intercede on behalf of people. The verse encourages people to reflect on this reality and be mindful of Allah, turning to Him alone for guidance and support.
orig: الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش ما لكم من دونه من ولي ولا شفيع أفلا تتذكرون

translation: He arranges [each] matter from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a Day, the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count.
interpretation: This verse speaks of God's absolute control and authority over all matters in the universe. He directs and manages the affairs of the heavens and the earth, and all of this will ultimately return to Him on the Day of Judgment. The reference to "a Day, the extent of which is a thousand years" suggests that the time in the Hereafter is vastly different from our earthly conception of time, emphasizing God's transcendence and the magnitude of the events to come.
orig: يدبر الأمر من السماء إلى الأرض ثم يعرج إليه في يوم كان مقداره ألف سنة مما تعدون

translation: That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah (God) is the All-Knowing, who has knowledge of both the seen and the unseen realms. He is the Mighty, the Powerful, and the Merciful, who extends His compassion and kindness to all His creation.
orig: ذلك عالم الغيب والشهادة العزيز الرحيم

translation: Who perfected everything which He created and began the creation of man from clay.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfection and completeness of God's creation, and how He began the creation of mankind from the most basic of materials - clay. This highlights God's power, wisdom and control over all of creation, as well as the humble origins of human beings. The verse encourages us to reflect on the wonders of God's creation and to recognize our own dependence on the Creator.
orig: الذي أحسن كل شيء خلقه وبدأ خلق الإنسان من طين

translation: Then He made his posterity from a extract of a liquid disdained.
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of human beings, and how God fashioned us from a humble and insignificant substance - a drop of semen. This emphasizes the lowly origins of mankind, and serves as a reminder of our dependence on God and our need to be grateful for the honor He has bestowed upon us by creating us in His image. The verse also highlights the miraculous nature of human creation, transforming a "liquid disdained" into the complex and wondrous form of the human being.
orig: ثم جعل نسله من سلالة من ماء مهين

translation: Then He proportioned him and breathed into him from His [created] soul and made for you hearing and vision and hearts; little are you grateful.
interpretation: This verse describes the creation of man by God. After fashioning the human form, God breathed into it a part of His own divine spirit, endowing man with the faculties of hearing, sight and understanding. However, despite these blessings, most people fail to show gratitude to their Creator.
orig: ثم سواه ونفخ فيه من روحه وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: And they say, "When we have become lost in the earth, will we indeed be [recreated] in a new creation?" Rather, they are, in [the matter of] the meeting with their Lord, disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers who deny the concept of resurrection and life after death. They question whether they will be recreated after being lost in the earth, implying that they do not believe in the Hereafter. The verse then states that these disbelievers are actually rejecting the meeting with their Lord, which is a fundamental tenet of Islamic faith.
orig: وقالوا أإذا ضللنا في الأرض أإنا لفي خلق جديد بل هم بلقاء ربهم كافرون

translation: Say, "The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will take your souls, and then to your Lord you will be returned."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that death is an inevitable reality that every human being will face, and that our ultimate destination is to return to God. It serves as a reminder to focus on our relationship with the divine and to prepare for the afterlife, rather than being consumed by the fleeting nature of this world.
orig: قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت الذي وكل بكم ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون

translation: And if you could but see when the criminals are hanging their heads before their Lord, [saying], "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to the world]; we will work righteousness. Indeed, we are [now] certain."
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment, when they will humbly bow their heads before their Lord, acknowledging their sins and asking to be sent back to the world so that they can make amends and do righteous deeds. This highlights the importance of repentance and the desire to seek forgiveness and redemption, even in the face of the ultimate reckoning. The verse emphasizes that true certainty in the afterlife can lead one to sincere remorse and a commitment to reform.
orig: ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءوسهم عند ربهم ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا فارجعنا نعمل صالحا إنا موقنون

translation: And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me has come into effect [that] 'I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute sovereignty and power. He could have guided all of humanity to the right path, but He has decreed that some will choose to reject faith and be condemned to Hell. This is a reflection of God's justice - He does not force guidance upon anyone, but holds people accountable for their choices. The verse also highlights the vastness of Hell, which will be filled not only with disobedient humans, but also with jinn (spiritual beings). Ultimately, this verse serves as a warning to humanity to heed God's guidance and avoid the eternal punishment of Hell.
orig: ولو شئنا لآتينا كل نفس هداها ولكن حق القول مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

translation: So taste [the punishment] because you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours. [And] indeed, We have [accordingly] forgotten you, and taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who neglected their duties and responsibilities towards God and humanity. It suggests that those who forget or ignore their accountability on the Day of Judgment will be made to taste the eternal punishment as a consequence of their misdeeds. The verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of one’s actions and their consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: فذوقوا بما نسيتم لقاء يومكم هذا إنا نسيناكم وذوقوا عذاب الخلد بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Only those believe in Our verses who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration and exalt [their Lord] with praise of Him, and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true believers are those who humbly and wholeheartedly submit to the signs and revelations of God. When they are reminded of God's verses, they respond with sincere prostration and praise, without any trace of arrogance or pride. This highlights the importance of a humble and reverent attitude towards the divine message, which is a key characteristic of the faithful.
orig: إنما يؤمن بآياتنا الذين إذا ذكروا بها خروا سجدا وسبحوا بحمد ربهم وهم لا يستكبرون

translation: Their sides turn away from (their) beds, they call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them, they spend.
interpretation: This verse describes the behavior of the righteous believers. They turn away from their beds, indicating that they are not preoccupied with worldly comforts and pleasures. Instead, they call upon their Lord with a sense of fear and hope, seeking His guidance and forgiveness. Furthermore, they spend from the provisions that God has granted them, demonstrating their generosity and commitment to using their wealth in a way that pleases God.
orig: تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the ultimate rewards and pleasures that Allah has prepared for the righteous in the Hereafter are beyond human imagination and comprehension. No one can fully fathom the extent of the bliss and joy that awaits those who have lived a life of faith and good deeds. This serves as a powerful motivation for believers to strive for the Hereafter, where they will be granted unimaginable rewards as a result of their righteous actions in this life.
orig: فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين جزاء بما كانوا يعملون

translation: Is one who is a believer like one who is a defiantly disobedient? They are not equal.
interpretation: This verse draws a clear distinction between the believer and the defiantly disobedient person. The believer, who submits to God and follows His guidance, is not equal to the one who rejects faith and engages in sinful acts. The verse emphasizes that they are fundamentally different in their spiritual standing and cannot be considered the same.
orig: أفمن كان مؤمنا كمن كان فاسقا لا يستوون

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them are the Gardens of Refuge as accommodation for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse promises a reward in the Hereafter for those who have faith in God and do good deeds. The "Gardens of Refuge" refers to the eternal paradise that awaits the righteous, where they will reside as a reward for their virtuous actions in this life. The interpretation emphasizes that belief and righteous conduct are the keys to attaining this blissful abode in the Afterlife.
orig: أما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فلهم جنات المأوى نزلا بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And as for those who defiantly disobeyed, their refuge is the Fire. Every time they wish to emerge from it, they will be returned to it while it is said to them, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who reject faith and disobey God. They will be condemned to the Fire of Hell, and whenever they try to escape it, they will be returned to it. This is a punishment for their denial of God's signs and rejection of the truth. The verse emphasizes the permanence and severity of their torment, as they are forced to "taste the punishment of the Fire" which they had previously denied.
orig: وأما الذين فسقوا فمأواهم النار كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها أعيدوا فيها وقيل لهم ذوقوا عذاب النار الذي كنتم به تكذبون

translation: And We will surely let them taste the nearer punishment before the greater punishment, that perhaps they will return [to righteousness].
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject faith and persist in their wrongdoing will be subjected to a lesser punishment first, as a warning and an opportunity to repent and return to the path of righteousness. The "nearer punishment" could refer to worldly consequences or trials, while the "greater punishment" likely refers to the ultimate punishment in the Hereafter. The purpose of this gradual approach is to give people a chance to reflect on their actions and change their ways, so that they may avoid the more severe consequences of their sins.
orig: ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them? Indeed, We, from the criminals, will take retribution.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of turning away from the guidance and signs of Allah after being reminded of them. It suggests that the most unjust and blameworthy individuals are those who are aware of Allah's revelations but choose to ignore and reject them. The verse warns that Allah will mete out punishment and retribution to those who persist in their criminal behavior and turn a blind eye to the truth.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن ذكر بآيات ربه ثم أعرض عنها إنا من المجرمين منتقمون

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the Book, so be not in doubt over his meeting, and We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah had revealed the Book, the Torah, to the Prophet Moses. It assures the Prophet Muhammad and the believers that they should not have any doubt about the meeting with Allah, as the previous prophets were also given divine scriptures to guide their people. The Qur'an is thus presented as a continuation of the divine guidance that was revealed to the Children of Israel through the Torah.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فلا تكن في مرية من لقائه وجعلناه هدى لبني إسرائيل

translation: And We made from them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and [when] they were certain of Our signs.
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who remained steadfast in their faith and conviction despite facing trials and tribulations. God appointed them as leaders to guide others, as a reward for their patience and unwavering belief in the divine signs and revelations. The interpretation suggests that true leadership is earned through steadfastness, certainty in one's beliefs, and a commitment to following God's commands.
orig: وجعلنا منهم أئمة يهدون بأمرنا لما صبروا وكانوا بآياتنا يوقنون

translation: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will make the final judgment between people regarding the matters in which they differed during their lives on earth. It is a reminder that the ultimate arbiter of truth is God, and that He will settle all disputes and disagreements on the Day of Judgment. The verse encourages believers to strive for unity and avoid divisiveness, as Allah will eventually judge between them and determine the truth.
orig: إن ربك هو يفصل بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: Have they not been guided [to see] how many generations We destroyed before them as they walk among their dwellings? Indeed in that are signs; then will they not listen?
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the fate of previous generations who rejected the message of God and were consequently destroyed. The verse suggests that the people of the time should heed the lessons of history and listen to the guidance of the Qur'an, lest they suffer a similar fate. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of learning from the past and being receptive to the divine guidance.
orig: أولم يهد لهم كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من القرون يمشون في مساكنهم إن في ذلك لآيات أفلا يسمعون

translation: Have they not seen that We drive the water to barren land and bring forth thereby crops from which their livestock eat and [they] themselves? Then do they not see?
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the signs of God's power and wisdom in the natural world. By bringing water to dry, barren land and causing crops to grow from it, God demonstrates His ability to sustain life and provide for His creation. The fact that both people and their livestock benefit from these crops is a testament to God's care and providence. The verse invites the reader to open their eyes and truly see these wonders, which should lead them to believe in and worship the One who has made all of this possible.
orig: أولم يروا أنا نسوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز فنخرج به زرعا تأكل منه أنعامهم وأنفسهم أفلا يبصرون

translation: And they say, "When is this conquest, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who are skeptical about the promise of the coming of the Day of Judgment and the establishment of God's kingdom on Earth. They challenge the believers to provide a specific timeline for this "conquest" or victory, implying that they do not believe it will ever happen. The interpretation is that the timing of the final triumph of truth and justice is known only to God, and the believers should have faith in God's plan rather than demanding a specific timeline from the Prophet.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الفتح إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "The Day of Judgement - that is the Day when their [professed] faith will not benefit those who disbelieved, nor will they be granted respite."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who disbelieve in God and reject the message of Islam. On the Day of Judgement, when the final reckoning takes place, their disbelief will not avail them, and they will not be given any more time or chance to believe. Their faith, if any, will be of no use to them on that day. The verse emphasizes the finality and gravity of the Day of Judgement, when there will be no more opportunities for repentance or salvation for those who stubbornly rejected the truth.
orig: قل يوم الفتح لا ينفع الذين كفروا إيمانهم ولا هم ينظرون

translation: So turn away from them and wait. Indeed, they are waiting.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to turn away from those who reject his message and to wait patiently, as they too are waiting for some sign or event that will confirm their beliefs. It suggests that the Prophet should not be distracted by their antagonism, but rather focus on his mission and trust that the truth will prevail in due time.
orig: فأعرض عنهم وانتظر إنهم منتظرون

translation: O Prophet, fear Allah and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to be mindful and conscious of Allah, and to not obey those who disbelieve in Allah or those who outwardly profess faith but inwardly harbor hypocrisy. The verse emphasizes that Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise, and that the Prophet should not be swayed by the demands or influence of the disbelievers and hypocrites, but rather remain steadfast in his faith and obedience to Allah.
orig: يا أيها النبي اتق الله ولا تطع الكافرين والمنافقين إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to follow the divine revelation that is being sent to him from his Lord, Allah. It emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of all that the people do, and nothing is hidden from Him. This serves as a reminder to the believers to always be conscious of Allah's presence and to strive to do what is pleasing to Him, as He is the All-Knowing and the All-Wise.
orig: واتبع ما يوحى إليك من ربك إن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: And rely upon Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to put their trust in Allah alone, and to rely on Him as the ultimate Guardian and Protector. It suggests that by entrusting one's affairs to Allah, the believer can find sufficient support and guidance, and need not seek help from any other source. The phrase "and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs" emphasizes that Allah is the One who controls and manages all matters, and that the believer should have complete faith and reliance in Him.
orig: وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: And Allah has not made for a man two hearts in his interior. And He has not made your wives whom you declare unlawful your mothers. And He has not made your adopted sons your [true] sons. That is [merely] your saying by your mouths, but Allah says the truth, and He guides to the [right] way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and truthfulness in one's relationships and beliefs. It refutes the practice of declaring one's wife as one's mother, which was a pre-Islamic custom, and also the concept of adopting children and considering them as one's own.
