interpretation: This verse is referring to the arrogance and self-deception of those who believe that their wealth and large families are a sign of divine favor, and that they will not be held accountable for their actions. The interpretation is that material prosperity and large families do not necessarily equate to righteousness or protection from punishment. True success and salvation lies in one's faith, deeds, and relationship with the Almighty.
orig: وقالوا نحن أكثر أموالا وأولادا وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: Say, "Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it], but most of the people do not know."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Lord, is the sole provider of sustenance and resources. He bestows His bounty upon whomever He wills, and He also restricts it as He pleases. However, most people are unaware of this fundamental truth and fail to recognize Allah's absolute control over all provisions.
orig: قل إن ربي يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And your wealth and your children are not but a trial for you, and Allah has with Him a great reward. So fear Allah as much as you are able and listen and obey and spend [in the way of Allah]; it is better for your souls. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that wealth and children are a test and trial for believers, not a means to gain proximity to Allah. The true measure of one's worth is not in material possessions or family, but in faith and righteous deeds. Those who believe and do good works will be rewarded in the Hereafter, while those who are stingy and selfish will not succeed. The key is to fear Allah, listen and obey His commands, and spend in His cause, as this is ultimately better for one's soul.
orig: وما أموالكم ولا أولادكم بالتي تقربكم عندنا زلفى إلا من آمن وعمل صالحا فأولئك لهم جزاء الضعف بما عملوا وهم في الغرفات آمنون

translation: And those who strive against Our verses, [seeking] to frustrate them - those will be brought into the Punishment.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who stubbornly reject the signs and messages of Allah (SWT) and try to undermine or discredit them. They will be held accountable and face the punishment in the Hereafter for their arrogance and defiance of the divine guidance.
orig: والذين يسعون في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك في العذاب محضرون

translation: Say, "Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts [it] for him. And whatever you spend of anything - it is He who replaces it, and He is the best of providers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who is the ultimate provider of sustenance and resources. He extends provision to whomever He wills, and restricts it from others as He sees fit. The verse also encourages believers to spend from what Allah has provided them, as He will replace and replenish what they have spent. This highlights Allah's generosity and His role as the best of providers.
orig: قل إن ربي يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر له وما أنفقتم من شيء فهو يخلفه وهو خير الرازقين

translation: And the Day when He will gather them all together and then say to the angels, "Were these the ones who used to worship you?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all people will be gathered before God. On that day, God will confront the disbelievers who had worshipped false deities or angels, asking the angels if these were the ones who were worshipped instead of God. This highlights the futility of worshipping anyone or anything other than the one true God, and emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, all will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم جميعا ثم يقول للملائكة أهؤلاء إياكم كانوا يعبدون

translation: They say: "Glory to Thee! our (relationship) is with Thee - and Thou art our Protector - not theirs. Nay, but they worshipped the Jinns; most of them believed in them."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the polytheists who worshipped idols and false deities besides Allah. They claim that their relationship is with Allah and that He is their Protector, but in reality, they worshipped the jinn (supernatural beings) and believed in them. This verse emphasizes that the true worship and allegiance should be directed towards Allah alone, and not towards any other created beings or false deities.
orig: قالوا سبحانك أنت ولينا من دونهم بل كانوا يعبدون الجن أكثرهم بهم مؤمنون

translation: So today no one of you can possess [any] benefit or harm for another, and We will say to those who wronged, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to help or harm another, as each person will be held accountable for their own actions. It serves as a warning to those who wronged others, that they will face the consequences of their misdeeds in the form of the punishment of the Hellfire, which they had previously denied or disbelieved in.
orig: فاليوم لا يملك بعضكم لبعض نفعا ولا ضرا ونقول للذين ظلموا ذوقوا عذاب النار التي كنتم بها تكذبون

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say, "This is not but a man who wishes to avvert you from that which your fathers were worshipping." And they say, "This is not except a lie invented." And those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, "This is not but obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when the clear verses of the Qur'an were recited to them. They dismissed the Qur'an as the work of a man who wanted to turn them away from the religion of their forefathers. They also accused the Qur'an of being a fabrication and a clear magic. This highlights the stubborn rejection of the truth by those who are unwilling to accept it due to their preconceived notions and biases.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قالوا ما هذا إلا رجل يريد أن يصدكم عما كان يعبد آباؤكم وقالوا ما هذا إلا إفك مفترى وقال الذين كفروا للحق لما جاءهم إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And We have not given them Scriptures which they could study, nor sent to them before you any warner.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people to whom the Qur'an was revealed had not been given any previous scriptures or messengers to guide them. The Qur'an was the first divine revelation they received, and Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was the first warner sent to them. This emphasizes the unique status of the Qur'an and the Prophet's mission, as they were the first to bring the message of Islam to this particular community.
orig: وما آتيناهم من كتب يدرسونها وما أرسلنا إليهم قبلك من نذير

translation: And those before them denied, and they (the people to whom this Messenger was sent) have not attained a tenth of what We had granted to those (of old), yet they denied My Messengers. Then how (terrible) was My rejection (of them)?
interpretation: This verse highlights that the disbelievers who came before the people to whom the Messenger was sent had also denied the truth, and they did not even attain a tenth of the blessings and bounties that were granted to those earlier nations. Yet, they still rejected the Messengers of Allah. This serves as a warning about the severe consequences of rejecting Allah's Messengers and the divine message.
orig: وكذب الذين من قبلهم وما بلغوا معشار ما آتيناهم فكذبوا رسلي فكيف كان نكير

translation: Say, "I only advise you of one [thing] - that you stand for Allah, [seeking truth] in pairs and individually, and then give thought." There is not in your companion [Muhammad] any madness. He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect and ponder upon the message of the Quran and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes that the Prophet is not a madman, but rather a warner who is conveying the message of Allah to save people from a severe punishment. The verse also instructs people to stand for Allah, either in pairs or individually, and to contemplate the message being delivered. This highlights the importance of personal reflection and seeking the truth, rather than blindly following others.
orig: قل إنما أعظكم بواحدة أن تقوموا لله مثنى وفرادى ثم تتفكروا ما بصاحبكم من جنة إن هو إلا نذير لكم بين يدي عذاب شديد

translation: Say, "Whatever fee I might have asked of you is yours. My reward is only from Allah, and He is witness over all things."
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to clarify that he is not seeking any personal gain or reward from the people for conveying the message of Islam. His only reward is from Allah, who is the witness over all things. This emphasizes the sincerity and selflessness with which the Prophet delivered the divine revelation, without any expectation of material compensation from the people.
orig: قل ما سألتكم من أجر فهو لكم إن أجري إلا على الله وهو على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Say, "Indeed, my Lord projects the truth. He is the [Perfect] Knower of the unseen."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the knowledge of the unseen world belongs solely to God. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to proclaim that his Lord, Allah, is the one who reveals the truth and has comprehensive knowledge of all that is hidden from human perception. This affirms the divine origin of the Qur'an and the Prophet's teachings, as they come from the All-Knowing God rather than being the product of human speculation or invention.
orig: قل إن ربي يقذف بالحق علام الغيوب

translation: Say, "The truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate [anything] nor reproduce [it]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the truth revealed in the Qur'an has come, and falsehood or falsehoods have no power to create or sustain themselves. The truth will prevail, and falsehood will be exposed and vanquished. This is a reassurance to the believers that the message of Islam is the truth, and it will ultimately triumph over any attempts to undermine or distort it.
orig: قل جاء الحق وما يبدئ الباطل وما يعيد

translation: Say, "If I have gone astray, I have only gone astray to [the detriment of] myself. And if I have been guided, it is by what my Lord has revealed to me. Indeed, He is Hearing and near."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the personal responsibility of the individual in matters of faith and guidance. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is instructed to say that if he has erred or gone astray, the consequences of that are borne by him alone. Conversely, if he has been rightly guided, it is due to the revelation and guidance from his Lord, who is All-Hearing and Ever-Near. This verse teaches that each person is accountable for their own choices and actions, and that true guidance comes from submitting to the will of God.
orig: قل إن ضللت فإنما أضل على نفسي وإن اهتديت فبما يوحي إلي ربي إنه سميع قريب

translation: And if you could see when they are terrified but there is no escape, and they will be seized from a place nearby
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, when they will be seized and there will be no way for them to escape the punishment. They will be taken from a place close to them, indicating that the punishment will be swift and inescapable. The imagery of being "terrified but there is no escape" conveys the hopelessness and despair of the disbelievers as they face the consequences of their actions in this life.
orig: ولو ترى إذ فزعوا فلا فوت وأخذوا من مكان قريب

translation: And they say, "We have believed in it," but how can they reach it from a distant place?
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who claim to have believed in the Quran, but their actions and distance from its teachings show that their faith is superficial. The verse suggests that true faith requires not just verbal affirmation, but a sincere and active engagement with the teachings of the Quran, which cannot be achieved from a distance. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of actively living by the principles of the Quran, rather than merely professing belief in it.
orig: وقالوا آمنا به وأنى لهم التناوش من مكان بعيد

translation: And they have disbelieved in it before. And they utter suggestions from a distant place.
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who reject the truth of the Qur'an and make unfounded accusations against it from a distant place, without any real knowledge or evidence. It suggests that their criticism and rejection of the Qur'an is not based on a sincere examination of its content, but rather on preconceived notions and biases.
orig: وقد كفروا به من قبل ويقذفون بالغيب من مكان بعيد

translation: And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, as was done with their kind before. Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: This verse describes how the disbelievers will be prevented from attaining their desires and worldly pleasures in the Hereafter, just as their predecessors were denied such things. This is a consequence of their state of doubt and uncertainty regarding the truth of the faith, which led them to reject it.
orig: وحيل بينهم وبين ما يشتهون كما فعل بأشياعهم من قبل إنهم كانوا في شك مريب

translation: Praise be to Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers having wings, two or three or four. He increases in creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and majesty of Allah as the Creator of the heavens and the earth. It highlights Allah's ability to create various forms of life, including the angels, who are described as having wings in different numbers. This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's infinite power and the wonders of His creation, which He increases as He wills. It underscores that Allah is all-powerful and has control over all things.
orig: الحمد لله فاطر السماوات والأرض جاعل الملائكة رسلا أولي أجنحة مثنى وثلاث ورباع يزيد في الخلق ما يشاء إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Whatever mercy Allah opens up for the people, none can withhold it. And whatever He withholds, none can release it thereafter. And He is the Exalted in Might, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah. He is the sole dispenser of His mercy and blessings to humanity. No one can prevent what Allah chooses to bestow, nor can anyone release what He chooses to withhold. This affirms Allah's complete control and wisdom in His decisions, which are guided by His infinite knowledge and power. The interpretation highlights that Allah alone decides the distribution of His mercy, and humans have no authority to interfere with or override His will.
orig: ما يفتح الله للناس من رحمة فلا ممسك لها وما يمسك فلا مرسل له من بعده وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O mankind, remember the favor of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and earth? There is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse calls upon all of humanity to remember and be grateful for the countless blessings and provisions that Allah has bestowed upon them. It challenges the notion that there could be any other deity or creator besides Allah who is capable of sustaining and providing for His creation. The verse aims to reaffirm the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and supremacy of Allah, and to remind people not to be deceived by false gods or ideologies that would lead them astray from the truth.
orig: يا أيها الناس اذكروا نعمت الله عليكم هل من خالق غير الله يرزقكم من السماء والأرض لا إله إلا هو فأنى تؤفكون

translation: And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then already have the messengers before you been denied, and to Allah are [all] matters returned.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that if his people reject his message, it is not something unique to him. Previous prophets and messengers have also faced rejection, and in the end, all matters will return to Allah, who will judge between the truth and falsehood. This verse encourages the Prophet to remain steadfast in his mission, despite the opposition he may face, as Allah is the ultimate arbiter.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذبت رسل من قبلك وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is truth, so let not the worldly life delude you and be not deceived about Allah by the Deceiver.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to all of humanity to not be deceived by the fleeting pleasures and allures of this worldly life, and to not be misled by the temptations of Satan. The promise of Allah is true and will come to pass, so one should not be distracted from the path of righteousness by the temporary attractions of this world. This emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and not being led astray by worldly desires or the deceptions of the devil.
orig: يا أيها الناس إن وعد الله حق فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور

translation: Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse warns us that Satan is our enemy and we should treat him as such. Satan tries to mislead people and lead them to the hellfire. We should be vigilant and not follow Satan's temptations, as he only wants to lead us astray and to the eternal punishment of the Hellfire.
orig: إن الشيطان لكم عدو فاتخذوه عدوا إنما يدعو حزبه ليكونوا من أصحاب السعير

translation: Those who disbelieve - for them is a severe punishment, and those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the fates of two groups of people - those who reject faith ("disbelieve") and those who have faith and do good works ("believe and do righteous deeds"). The former group will face "a severe punishment", while the latter group will receive "forgiveness and a great reward". This highlights the importance of belief in God and righteous conduct, which are rewarded in the Hereafter, in contrast to disbelief and evil, which are punished.
orig: الذين كفروا لهم عذاب شديد والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: Then is one to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive so he considers it good [like one rightly guided]? For indeed, Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let yourself perish over them in regret. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse warns against being deceived by the outward appearance of one's actions. Sometimes, a person may be misguided and find their evil deeds attractive, thinking they are good. However, Allah alone has the power to guide or misguide whomever He wills. The verse advises not to grieve excessively over those who are misguided, as Allah is All-Knowing of their actions. The focus should be on seeking Allah's guidance and doing what is right, rather than being consumed by regret over others' choices.
orig: أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسنا فإن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات إن الله عليم بما يصنعون

translation: And it is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land and give life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness. Thus is the resurrection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over the natural world. The winds that He sends bring about the formation of clouds, which are then directed to areas that are lifeless or barren. When the rain from these clouds falls on the land, it revives the earth and brings it back to life. This serves as an analogy for the resurrection, where Allah will bring the dead back to life on the Day of Judgment, just as He brings life to the dead land through the rain. The interpretation highlights Allah's ability to create and sustain life, as well as the certainty of the resurrection and the afterlife.
orig: والله الذي أرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فسقناه إلى بلد ميت فأحيينا به الأرض بعد موتها كذلك النشور

translation: Whoever desires honor [through power] - then to Allah belongs all honor. To Him ascends good speech, and righteous work raises it. But they who plot evil deeds will have a severe punishment, and the plotting of those - it will perish.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true honor and power comes from Allah alone. Those who seek honor and power through their own means and schemes will be disappointed, as only the worship of Allah and righteous deeds can lead to lasting honor. In contrast, those who plot evil will face severe punishment, as their schemes will ultimately fail and be destroyed.
orig: من كان يريد العزة فلله العزة جميعا إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب والعمل الصالح يرفعه والذين يمكرون السيئات لهم عذاب شديد ومكر أولئك هو يبور

translation: And Allah has created you from dust, then from a semen-drop; then He made you mates. And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. And no aged person is granted [additional] life nor is his lifespan diminished but that it is in a register. Indeed, that for Allah is easy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over the creation of human beings. It highlights that Allah created humans from the most basic elements, like dust, and then from a semen-drop. It also points out that Allah has created humans in pairs, as mates for one another. The verse further affirms that nothing in the life of a human being, including conception, birth, and lifespan, occurs without Allah's knowledge and will. This underscores the idea that Allah is the ultimate authority and controller of all aspects of human existence, and that nothing happens without His permission. The final statement that "that for Allah is easy" reinforces the notion of Allah's absolute power and ability to govern all affairs, even the most intricate details of human life.
orig: والله خلقكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم جعلكم أزواجا وما تحمل من أنثى ولا تضع إلا بعلمه وما يعمر من معمر ولا ينقص من عمره إلا في كتاب إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: And not are equal the two seas - this one fresh and sweet, palatable for drinking, and this one salty and bitter. And from them you eat tender meat and extract ornament which you wear. And you see the ships plowing through [them] that you may seek of His bounty and that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between two types of bodies of water - one that is fresh and sweet, suitable for drinking, and the other that is salty and bitter. It then goes on to describe how humans benefit from both types of seas, extracting food and adornments from them. The final part of the verse emphasizes how humans can utilize the resources of the seas through ships, in order to seek Allah's bounty, and be grateful for His provisions. The overall message is about the diversity of Allah's creation and how humans can appreciate and benefit from it in various ways.
orig: وما يستوي البحران هذا عذب فرات سائغ شرابه وهذا ملح أجاج ومن كل تأكلون لحما طريا وتستخرجون حلية تلبسونها وترى الفلك فيه مواخر لتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: He causes the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon - each running [its course] for a specified term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs sovereignty. And those you invoke other than Him do not possess [as much as] the membrane of a date seed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over the natural world. He controls the alternation of night and day, and the movement of the sun and moon, all according to a precise and measured plan. This highlights Allah's complete control and authority, in contrast to the false deities that people worship, which have no real power or dominion. The verse encourages believers to recognize and submit to the one true God, Allah, who alone deserves worship and obedience.
orig: يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك والذين تدعون من دونه ما يملكون من قطمير

translation: Indeed, if you invite them, they will not hear your call, and if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection, they will deny your association [of others with Allah]. And none can inform you like [He is] Acquainted [with all matters].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping anything other than Allah. It states that the idols or false deities that people may call upon will not hear their prayers or respond to them. Even on the Day of Judgment, these false deities will deny the association of partners with Allah, further highlighting their powerlessness. The verse also suggests that only Allah, who is All-Knowing, can truly inform and guide people about the reality of their beliefs and actions.
orig: إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم ولا ينبئك مثل خبير

translation: O mankind, you are those in need of Allah, while Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all of humanity is in need of Allah (God), while Allah is the One who is self-sufficient and worthy of all praise. It serves as a reminder that we are dependent on Allah for all our needs, whether material or spiritual, and that we should turn to Him with humility and gratitude, recognizing our own limitations and Allah's infinite power and perfection.
orig: يا أيها الناس أنتم الفقراء إلى الله والله هو الغني الحميد

translation: If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah. He has the ability to completely replace humanity with a new creation if He so desires. This serves as a reminder that we are entirely dependent on Allah, and that we should strive to live according to His will and commands, as He has the power to reshape the world as He pleases.
orig: إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأت بخلق جديد

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: This verse conveys the message that nothing is too difficult or impossible for Allah, the Almighty. It emphasizes the omnipotence and unlimited power of God, who can accomplish any task with ease. The verse serves to reassure believers that Allah is capable of fulfilling His promises and carrying out His will, no matter how challenging the situation may appear from a human perspective. This verse encourages trust, faith, and reliance on the divine power of God.
orig: وما ذلك على الله بعزيز

translation: And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to [carry some of] its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he should be a close relative. You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen and have established prayer. And whoever purifies himself only purifies himself. And to Allah is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of individual responsibility and accountability before God. It states that no one can bear the burden or sins of another person, even if that person is a close relative. Each person is responsible for their own actions and will be held accountable for them. The verse also encourages warning and guiding those who fear God and establish prayer, as they are the ones who will benefit from this message. Ultimately, it is up to each individual to purify themselves, as the final destination is with God.
orig: ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان ذا قربى إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب وأقاموا الصلاة ومن تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفسه وإلى الله المصير

translation: And not equal are the blind and the seeing
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental difference between those who have insight and understanding (the seeing) and those who are devoid of it (the blind). It suggests that individuals with vision and perception cannot be equated with those who lack awareness and discernment. The verse emphasizes the importance of possessing spiritual and intellectual sight, which allows one to navigate life's complexities and make informed decisions.
orig: وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير

translation: And not the darkness and not the light
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the contrast between darkness and light, which can be interpreted as a metaphor for the contrast between ignorance and knowledge, evil and good, or falsehood and truth. The Qur'an often uses this contrast to encourage believers to seek guidance and enlightenment from God, and to avoid the darkness of ignorance and sin.
orig: ولا الظلمات ولا النور

translation: And neither the shade nor the heat
interpretation: This verse speaks of the protection and comfort that Allah provides for the believers in the Hereafter. The shade and the heat, which can be burdensome in this world, will not affect the believers in the afterlife. This is a promise of the ultimate comfort and peace that awaits those who have faith in Allah.
orig: ولا الظل ولا الحرور

translation: And the living and the dead are not equal. Indeed, Allah causes to hear whom He wills, and you [O Muhammad] will not make hear those in the graves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the living and the dead are not equal in the sight of Allah. The living have the opportunity to hear and respond to the message of Allah, while the dead in their graves cannot hear the call. This highlights the importance of making the most of one's life and heeding the guidance of Allah before it is too late.
orig: وما يستوي الأحياء ولا الأموات إن الله يسمع من يشاء وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور

translation: You are not but a warner
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not a ruler or a king, but rather a messenger sent to warn and remind people of the consequences of their actions and to guide them towards the path of righteousness. His role is to convey the message of Islam and to encourage people to believe in and worship Allah alone, without any partners or associates.
orig: إن أنت إلا نذير

translation: Indeed, We have sent you, [O Muhammad], with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and there was no nation but that there had [previously] been a warner within it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad was sent by God with the truth, as a bearer of good news and a warner to all of humanity. It also highlights that every nation or community has had a warner or messenger sent to them in the past, to guide them towards the truth and warn them against disbelief and wrongdoing.
orig: إنا أرسلناك بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وإن من أمة إلا خلا فيها نذير

translation: And if they deny you, then those before them also denied. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs and with written ordinances and with the enlightening Scripture.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the disbelievers who reject his message. It is reminding them that this pattern of rejection is not new - previous Prophets and messengers were also denied by their people, despite bringing clear evidence and divine scriptures. This serves as a reassurance to the Prophet that his message is true, and that the rejection he faces is part of the pattern of human history. It also warns the disbelievers that they are following in the footsteps of those who came before them and suffered the consequences of their rejection.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذب الذين من قبلهم جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات وبالزبر وبالكتاب المنير

translation: Then We seized those who disbelieved, and how [terrible] was My reproach.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject faith and disbelieve in God. It suggests that those who turn away from the truth will face the consequences of their actions, and that God's punishment and disapproval will be severe. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of believing in and submitting to God, and the dire consequences of rejecting His guidance.
orig: ثم أخذت الذين كفروا فكيف كان نكير

translation: Have you not seen that Allah sends down rain from the sky, and We produce thereby fruits of varying colors? And in the mountains are tracts, white and red of varying shades and [some] extremely black.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and creativity in the natural world. The verse describes how Allah sends down rain from the sky, which then produces a variety of fruits with differing colors. It also mentions the diverse colors and shades found in the mountains, ranging from white and red to extremely black. This is a sign of Allah's infinite wisdom and the beauty of His creation, which should inspire believers to reflect on His greatness and to be grateful for His blessings.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به ثمرات مختلفا ألوانها ومن الجبال جدد بيض وحمر مختلف ألوانها وغرابيب سود

translation: And among people and moving creatures and grazing livestock are various colors. Similarly, only those fear Allah, from among His servants, who have knowledge. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity of creation, both among humans and animals, in their colors and appearances. It then emphasizes that true fear and reverence for Allah is found only in those who possess knowledge and understanding, for they recognize the power and majesty of the Creator. This suggests that knowledge and wisdom are essential for developing a deep, meaningful relationship with Allah, the Almighty and Forgiving.
orig: ومن الناس والدواب والأنعام مختلف ألوانه كذلك إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء إن الله عزيز غفور

translation: Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah and establish prayer and spend [in His cause] from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, [they] expect a transaction [i.e., profit] that will never perish.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of three key aspects of faith and devotion: reciting the Quran, establishing regular prayer, and spending charitably from one's wealth. Those who engage in these righteous deeds with sincerity, both privately and publicly, are promised a reward that will never diminish or be lost. This suggests that the true believers are those who dedicate themselves to the worship of Allah and the service of others, seeking the eternal rewards of the Hereafter rather than the fleeting gains of this world.
orig: إن الذين يتلون كتاب الله وأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية يرجون تجارة لن تبور

translation: That He may pay them in full their wages and increase them of His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative.
interpretation: This verse speaks of God's generosity and reward for those who believe and do righteous deeds. It conveys that God will ensure that they are fully compensated for their good works, and will further bless them with additional rewards from His grace. The verse highlights God's attributes of forgiveness and appreciation, indicating that He is merciful towards His servants and values their efforts and devotion.
orig: ليوفيهم أجورهم ويزيدهم من فضله إنه غفور شكور

translation: And that which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], of the Book is the truth, confirming what was before it. Indeed, Allah, concerning His servants, is Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is the truth and confirms the previous divine scriptures. It also emphasizes that Allah is All-Knowing and All-Seeing of His servants, meaning that He is fully aware of their actions and conditions, and nothing is hidden from Him.
orig: والذي أوحينا إليك من الكتاب هو الحق مصدقا لما بين يديه إن الله بعباده لخبير بصير

translation: Then We gave the Book as inheritance to those whom We elected of Our servants; and among them are some who wrong themselves, and of them are some who follow a middle course, and of them are some who are foremost in good deeds by Allah's permission. That is the great favor.
interpretation: This verse highlights that Allah has chosen certain individuals to inherit the divine scripture, the Qur'an. However, these chosen servants exhibit different levels of righteousness - some wrong themselves by sinning, others follow a moderate path, and some are at the forefront of performing good deeds with Allah's permission. This diversity in the spiritual states of the inheritors of the Book demonstrates the great favor and mercy of Allah, as He guides people according to their capacities and intentions.
orig: ثم أورثنا الكتاب الذين اصطفينا من عبادنا فمنهم ظالم لنفسه ومنهم مقتصد ومنهم سابق بالخيرات بإذن الله ذلك هو الفضل الكبير

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence; they will enter them, as well as bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be of silk.
interpretation: This verse describes the blessings and rewards that await the righteous in the Hereafter. The "Gardens of perpetual residence" refers to the eternal Paradise, where the believers will dwell. They will be adorned with beautiful jewelry such as "bracelets of gold and pearls", and their clothing will be made of the finest silk. This imagery conveys the idea of the splendor, luxury, and comfort that the inhabitants of Paradise will enjoy as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this life.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير

translation: And they say, "Praise to Allah, who has removed from us [all] sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative."
interpretation: This verse expresses the gratitude and praise of the believers towards Allah for relieving them of their sorrow and distress. It highlights that Allah is Forgiving, readily accepting the repentance and gratitude of His servants, and Appreciative, rewarding them for their faith and good deeds. The verse encourages a mindset of thankfulness and recognition of Allah's blessings, even in times of difficulty.
orig: وقالوا الحمد لله الذي أذهب عنا الحزن إن ربنا لغفور شكور

translation: He who has settled us in the home of duration out of His bounty - there touches us not in it any fatigue, and there touches us not in it weariness [of mind].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the blessings and comforts that God has bestowed upon the believers in the hereafter. The "home of duration" refers to Paradise, where the righteous will reside eternally without experiencing any physical or mental exhaustion. This verse highlights the tranquility and ease that the believers will enjoy in the afterlife, as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world.
orig: الذي أحلنا دار المقامة من فضله لا يمسنا فيها نصب ولا يمسنا فيها لغوب

translation: And those who disbelieve - for them is the fire of Hell. It will not be concluded upon them so they may die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who reject faith and disbelieve in God. They will be condemned to the eternal punishment of Hell, where they will not die and find relief, nor will their torment be lessened. This is the just recompense for those who are ungrateful and reject the guidance of God.
orig: والذين كفروا لهم نار جهنم لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا ولا يخفف عنهم من عذابها كذلك نجزي كل كفور

translation: And they will cry out therein, "Our Lord, remove us; we will do righteousness, [but] not [what] we used to do." But did We not grant you life enough for whoever would remember therein to remember, and the warner had come to you? So taste [the penalty], for there is not for the wrongdoers any helper.
interpretation: This verse describes the desperate pleas of the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment, as they realize the consequences of their misdeeds. They will beg to be removed from the punishment, promising to do good deeds instead of their previous evil actions. However, the verse reminds them that they were given ample time in this life to reflect and heed the warnings, but they chose to persist in their wrongdoing. Now, they must face the consequences of their choices, with no one to save them from the punishment they deserve.
orig: وهم يصطرخون فيها ربنا أخرجنا نعمل صالحا غير الذي كنا نعمل أولم نعمركم ما يتذكر فيه من تذكر وجاءكم النذير فذوقوا فما للظالمين من نصير

translation: Indeed, Allah is the Knower of the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is [fully] Aware of what is in the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has knowledge of all that is hidden and unseen, not only in the physical world of the heavens and the earth, but also in the innermost thoughts and intentions of people. It affirms that Allah is all-knowing and has complete awareness of the secrets and realities of all creation. This serves as a reminder that we cannot hide anything from Allah, and that He is aware of our deepest selves and the contents of our hearts.
orig: إن الله عالم غيب السماوات والأرض إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: He it is who has made you successors in the earth. So he who disbelieves, his disbelief will be upon him. And their disbelief does not increase the disbelievers with their Lord in anything except hatred; and their disbelief does not increase the disbelievers except in loss.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is God who has placed humankind as successors and caretakers of the earth. It reminds us that those who disbelieve in God will bear the consequences of their disbelief, which will only increase their hatred towards God and lead them to further loss. The interpretation suggests that disbelief is not only a personal matter, but also has cosmic implications, as it distances the disbeliever from God and leads to spiritual and worldly harm.
orig: هو الذي جعلكم خلائف في الأرض فمن كفر فعليه كفره ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم عند ربهم إلا مقتا ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم إلا خسارا

translation: Say, "Have you considered your 'partners' whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth, or have they a share in the heavens? Or have We given them a book so they are [standing] on evidence from it? [No], rather, the wrongdoers promise each other not but delusion."
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists to provide evidence for the existence and power of the gods they worship alongside Allah. It asks them to show what these 'partners' have created, or what share they have in the heavens. The verse suggests that the polytheists have no divine scripture or clear evidence to support their beliefs, and that their claims are merely delusional. The overall message is to affirm the oneness of Allah and reject the falsehood of polytheism.
orig: قل أرأيتم شركاءكم الذين تدعون من دون الله أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض أم لهم شرك في السماوات أم آتيناهم كتابا فهم على بينت منه بل إن يعد الظالمون بعضهم بعضا إلا غرورا

translation: Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them [in place] after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over the entire universe. He is the One who sustains the heavens and the earth, and without His constant support, they would cease to exist. Even if the heavens and the earth were to somehow cease, no one else could hold them in place after Allah. This verse highlights Allah's eternal and unparalleled authority, as well as His compassionate and forgiving nature, as He is described as "Forbearing and Forgiving".
orig: إن الله يمسك السماوات والأرض أن تزولا ولئن زالتا إن أمسكهما من أحد من بعده إنه كان حليما غفورا

translation: And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be more guided than [any of] the nations. But when a warner came to them, it did not increase them except in aversion.
interpretation: This verse describes the hypocritical attitude of some people who claim to be believers, but when a warner (a prophet or messenger) comes to them, they do not increase in faith and guidance, but rather turn away in aversion. They had sworn oaths that if a warner came, they would be more guided than any other nation, but their actions proved otherwise. This highlights the importance of sincerity and true faith, rather than just outward displays of religiosity.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن جاءهم نذير ليكونن أهدى من إحدى الأمم فلما جاءهم نذير ما زادهم إلا نفورا

translation: In arrogance in the land and evil plotting. But the evil plot will not encompass except its own people. So do they await except the way of the former peoples? But you will never find in the way of Allah any change, and you will never find in the way of Allah any alteration.
interpretation: This verse warns against arrogance, pride, and evil plotting, as these will only harm the ones who engage in them. It emphasizes that the consequences of such behavior will not be averted, as it is the established way of Allah and cannot be changed. The verse encourages people to learn from the fate of previous nations who engaged in similar misdeeds, and to realize that the laws and patterns set by Allah are immutable.
orig: استكبارا في الأرض ومكر السيئ ولا يحيق المكر السيئ إلا بأهله فهل ينظرون إلا سنت الأولين فلن تجد لسنت الله تبديلا ولن تجد لسنت الله تحويلا

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in impression left [upon the land], but God seized them for their sins, and they had from God no protector. That is because God is the Protector of those who have believed and [that] the disbelievers have no protector.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the fate of previous generations who were more powerful than the current one. It suggests that the ultimate outcome is not determined by worldly power, but by one's relationship with God. The verse emphasizes that God is all-knowing and all-powerful, and that He alone can protect those who believe in Him. It serves as a warning to the disbelievers that they have no true protector besides God.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم وكانوا أشد منهم قوة وما كان الله ليعجزه من شيء في السماوات ولا في الأرض إنه كان عليما قديرا

translation: And if Allah were to impose blame on the people for what they have earned, He would not leave upon the earth any creature. But He defers them for a specified term, and when their time has come - then indeed Allah is to His servants, All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and forbearance towards humanity. If Allah were to punish people immediately for their sins and misdeeds, there would be no one left on earth. However, Allah gives people time to repent and reform themselves, deferring their punishment until an appointed time. This demonstrates Allah's wisdom and deep knowledge of His servants, as He is All-Seeing and fully aware of their circumstances and the appropriate time for judgment.
orig: ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بما كسبوا ما ترك على ظهرها من دابة ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى فإذا جاء أجلهم فإن الله كان بعباده بصيرا

translation: Ya Sin.
interpretation: This is one of the Qur'anic chapters that begin with letters from the Arabic alphabet, known as the "Muqatta'at" or "Disconnected Letters". The meaning of "Ya Sin" is not definitively known, but it is believed to be a reference to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) or a symbolic representation of the Qur'an itself. The chapter goes on to discuss the oneness of God, the message of the Qur'an, and the importance of faith and righteous deeds.
orig: يس

translation: And the Wise Qur'an
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature and wisdom of the Qur'an, the holy scripture revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The Qur'an is described as "al-Qur'an al-Hakim" (the Wise Qur'an), highlighting its profound and comprehensive teachings that guide humanity towards truth, justice, and a righteous way of life. The wisdom of the Qur'an is manifested in its ability to address the spiritual, moral, and practical needs of mankind, providing guidance and solutions for all aspects of life.
orig: والقرآن الحكيم

translation: Indeed, you are from the messengers
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), affirming that he is one of the messengers of Allah. It emphasizes the divine origin of his prophethood and the authenticity of his message. The verse conveys the idea that the Prophet Muhammad is a true messenger of God, sent with a divine mission to guide humanity towards the path of righteousness and salvation.
orig: إنك لمن المرسلين

translation: On a straight path
interpretation: This verse suggests that the righteous path is a straight and clear one, without deviation or confusion. It implies that following the guidance of God and living according to His teachings leads to a life of purpose, direction, and spiritual fulfillment. The "straight path" represents the path of truth, justice, and virtue that leads to eternal success in the Hereafter.
orig: على صراط مستقيم

translation: The Revelation of the Almighty, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is the opening of the Qur'an, known as the Bismillah. It establishes the divine origin and attributes of the Qur'an. "The Almighty" refers to the absolute power and sovereignty of God, while "the Merciful" emphasizes God's compassion and benevolence towards His creation. This sets the tone for the Qur'an as a revelation from the All-Powerful yet All-Merciful God.
orig: تنزيل العزيز الرحيم

translation: That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are unaware.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the purpose of the Qur'an and the Prophet's mission is to warn a people who have not been warned before, so that they may become aware and attentive to the message of Islam. The verse suggests that previous generations were heedless and neglectful of the divine guidance, and now it is the responsibility of the Prophet and the believers to convey the message to those who have not been reached before, so that they may not remain in a state of unawareness and neglect.
orig: لتنذر قوما ما أنذر آباؤهم فهم غافلون

translation: The word has proved true against most of them, for they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the majority of people have rejected the message of the Qur'an and chosen not to believe in it. The "word" that has "proved true" refers to the divine decree or judgment that those who persist in disbelief will be held accountable for their actions. This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the consequences of rejecting the guidance provided in the Qur'an.
orig: لقد حق القول على أكثرهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Indeed, We have placed around their necks shackles, and they are to their chins, so they are with heads [kept] aloft.
interpretation: This verse is describing the state of those who reject the truth and stubbornly refuse to accept guidance. The "shackles" around their necks represent the constraints and limitations they have placed upon themselves by their own disbelief and arrogance. They are "to their chins", meaning that these shackles have become a part of their very existence, preventing them from seeing the truth and humbling themselves before God. As a result, they remain "with heads [kept] aloft", unwilling to acknowledge their own shortcomings and unwilling to submit to the guidance of the Almighty. This verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their rejection of the truth, highlighting the consequences of such obstinance.
orig: إنا جعلنا في أعناقهم أغلالا فهي إلى الأذقان فهم مقمحون

translation: And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah has placed barriers or obstacles before and behind people, preventing them from seeing the truth. This can be interpreted as a metaphor for the spiritual blindness that afflicts those who reject faith and refuse to see the signs of Allah"s existence and guidance. The barriers represent the mental and emotional obstacles that prevent them from understanding and accepting the divine message.
orig: وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون

translation: It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the act of warning or not warning the disbelievers does not make a difference in their faith. They are firm in their rejection of the truth and unwilling to believe, regardless of whether they are warned or not. The verse emphasizes the stubbornness and closed-mindedness of those who refuse to accept the message of Islam, highlighting that their disbelief is a matter of choice rather than lack of information or guidance.
orig: وسواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: You can only warn those who follow the Reminder and fear the Most Merciful unseen. So give them tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet's (peace be upon him) mission is to warn and guide those who are willing to accept the divine guidance and have reverence for Allah, the Most Merciful, even though they cannot see Him. Those who heed the Reminder (the Quran) and fear Allah in their hearts will be granted forgiveness and a noble, generous reward in the Hereafter.
orig: إنما تنذر من اتبع الذكر وخشي الرحمن بالغيب فبشره بمغفرة وأجر كريم

translation: Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritor. And We have already written in the Scripture [of the previous peoples] whatever they had done, and [everything] they have done is in written records.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah (God) is the sole Creator and Sustainer of life and death. He alone has the power to give life and to take it away. Additionally, this verse suggests that Allah keeps a detailed record of the deeds and actions of all people, which will be used to judge them on the Day of Resurrection. The phrase "in a clear register" implies that this record is clear, comprehensive, and accessible to Allah, who will hold people accountable for their actions.
orig: إنا نحن نحيي الموتى ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين

translation: And present to them the example of the companions of the city, when the messengers came to it.
interpretation: This verse presents a parable to illustrate the importance of responding positively to the messengers of God. The "companions of the city" refers to the people of a town who were visited by God's messengers, but they rejected the message. This serves as a warning that those who reject the divine guidance brought by the messengers will face consequences, just as the people of that town did.
orig: واضرب لهم مثلا أصحاب القرية إذ جاءها المرسلون

translation: When We sent to them two [messengers] but they denied them, so We strengthened [them] with a third, and they said, "Indeed, we are [all] to you messengers."
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah sent two messengers to a people, but they rejected them. So Allah then sent a third messenger to strengthen the message and reinforce it. The people then acknowledged that all three were messengers sent to them. This highlights how Allah supports His messengers and the message of truth, even when it is initially rejected, in order to establish it firmly among the people.
orig: إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين فكذبوهما فعززنا بثالث فقالوا إنا إليكم مرسلون

translation: They said, "You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has not revealed anything. You are only telling lies."
interpretation: This verse reflects the attitude of those who reject the message of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). They dismiss the divine revelation as mere human fabrication, denying the existence of God and the authenticity of the Qur'an. This represents a fundamental rejection of faith and a refusal to acknowledge the signs of God's existence and the truth of the Qur'anic teachings.
orig: قالوا ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا وما أنزل الرحمن من شيء إن أنتم إلا تكذبون

translation: They said, "Our Lord knows that we are messengers to you."
interpretation: The messengers of God are affirming that their Lord, the Almighty, is fully aware of their mission to convey the divine message to the people. This verse emphasizes the messengers' unwavering faith in God's knowledge and their own commitment to fulfill their responsibilities as His emissaries, regardless of the response they may receive from the people they are sent to.
orig: قالوا ربنا يعلم إنا إليكم لمرسلون

translation: And upon us is only [the duty of] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the responsibility of the Messenger and those who convey the divine message is to deliver it clearly and unambiguously, without any obfuscation or deception. The ultimate decision and judgment rests with the people to whom the message is delivered. The Messenger's duty is to convey the message, not to force or coerce acceptance of it.
orig: وما علينا إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: They said, "Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you from us a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the reaction of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad and his followers. They accused the Prophet and his followers of being a bad omen, threatening to stone them and inflict a painful punishment if they did not stop preaching the message of Islam. This reflects the hostility and rejection the early Muslim community faced from the disbelievers, who were unwilling to accept the new faith and wanted to silence its message by force.
orig: قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم

translation: They said, "Your omen is with you. If you are reminded, [yet] you persist, then you are a transgressing people."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the response of the disbelievers when the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) warned them about the consequences of their actions. They dismissed his warning, claiming that their misfortunes were not due to their own wrongdoing, but rather were a result of the Prophet's presence with them. This verse condemns their arrogance and refusal to take responsibility for their transgressions, instead blaming the messenger of God for their own misdeeds. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of self-reflection and accountability, rather than shifting blame onto others.
orig: قالوا طائركم معكم أئن ذكرتم بل أنتم قوم مسرفون

translation: And there came from the farthest part of the city a man, running. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers"
interpretation: This verse describes a man who came rushing from the outskirts of the city to call his people to follow the messengers of God. It emphasizes the urgency and importance of heeding the divine message, even if it requires great effort and sacrifice to do so. The man’s haste and determination to convey this call to his people reflects the gravity of the situation and the need for them to respond accordingly.
orig: وجاء من أقصى المدينة رجل يسعى قال يا قوم اتبعوا المرسلين

translation: Follow those who ask of you no reward, and they are [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to follow those who do not seek any material reward or personal gain from their guidance and teachings, but are instead genuinely focused on leading others to the right path. The interpretation suggests that such people, who are disinterested in worldly benefits, are more likely to be truly guided and to guide others effectively.
orig: اتبعوا من لا يسألكم أجرا وهم مهتدون

translation: And why should I not worship He who created me and to whom you will be returned?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping the One who created us, as we will all eventually return to Him. It is a rhetorical question that highlights the logical and natural duty to worship the Creator, who has power over our lives and our ultimate destination. The verse encourages us to recognize God's sovereignty and our dependence on Him, and to dedicate our worship and service to the One who brought us into existence.
orig: وما لي لا أعبد الذي فطرني وإليه ترجعون

translation: Shall I take [for worship] deities other than Him, [when], if the Most Merciful intends for me an adversity, their [claimed] intercession will not avail me whatsoever, nor can they save me?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping any deity other than Allah, the Most Merciful. It suggests that seeking help or intercession from any other source will be of no benefit if Allah intends to inflict harm or adversity. The verse highlights the supreme power and authority of Allah, and the inability of any other deity or intermediary to provide salvation or protection. The interpretation underscores the importance of worshipping Allah alone and placing one's trust in Him, as He is the only true source of help and deliverance.
orig: أأتخذ من دونه آلهة إن يردن الرحمن بضر لا تغن عني شفاعتهم شيئا ولا ينقذون

translation: Indeed, I was in evident error.
interpretation: This verse expresses a person's acknowledgment of their previous state of being misguided and lost. It suggests a realization of one's past mistakes or misjudgments, and a willingness to admit and correct them. The verse conveys a sense of humility and a desire to move away from a state of evident error or deviation, towards a more enlightened path.
orig: إني إذا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me.
interpretation: This verse expresses the speaker's firm belief in God and their desire for others to listen and heed their message. It conveys a sense of conviction and a call for others to accept the same faith. The interpretation suggests that the speaker has found the truth in God's teachings and wants to share this with those around them, urging them to listen and accept it as well.
orig: إني آمنت بربكم فاسمعون

translation: It will be said, "Enter Paradise." [Abraham] will say, "I wish my people could know"
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the Prophet Abraham, who will be welcomed into Paradise after his death. However, he will express a wish that his people, who had rejected his message during his lifetime, could have known the truth and joined him in Paradise. This highlights the Prophet Abraham's compassion and concern for his people, even after his own salvation has been secured. The verse emphasizes the importance of guiding people to the truth and the desire of the righteous to see their loved ones also attain salvation.
orig: قيل ادخل الجنة قال يا ليت قومي يعلمون

translation: Because my Lord has forgiven me and made me of the honored ones
interpretation: This verse expresses the speaker's gratitude to God for forgiving their sins and elevating them to a position of honor and esteem. The interpretation suggests that the speaker has been granted divine forgiveness and has been bestowed with a high status or rank, which they attribute to the mercy and favor of their Lord. The verse conveys a sense of humility, appreciation, and recognition of God's grace in the life of the speaker.
orig: بما غفر لي ربي وجعلني من المكرمين

translation: And We did not send down upon his people after him any soldiers from the heaven. And We had not been sending down [soldiers].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people of Prophet Lot (peace be upon him). It states that after the destruction of Lot's people, Allah did not send down any army or soldiers from the heavens to punish any other people. This emphasizes that the punishment of Lot's people was a unique and specific event, and that Allah does not indiscriminately send down armies from the heavens to destroy people. The verse also highlights that Allah is the sole decision-maker when it comes to meting out punishment, and that He does not act hastily or without wisdom.
orig: وما أنزلنا على قومه من بعده من جند من السماء وما كنا منزلين

translation: Indeed, it is but one shout, and at once they are [all] brought into sight.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when a single blast of the trumpet will cause all people to be resurrected and brought before God for judgment. The verse emphasizes the swiftness and finality of this event, with the dead being "brought into sight" immediately after the single shout. This highlights the certainty and urgency of the Resurrection, which will come upon humanity suddenly and without warning.
orig: إن كانت إلا صيحة واحدة فإذا هم خامدون

translation: Alas for My servants! There comes not to them a messenger but they mock him.
interpretation: This verse expresses the regret and sorrow of God over the attitude of His servants towards the messengers He sends to guide them. Despite the messengers coming with clear guidance and wisdom, the people mock them and reject their message. This highlights the human tendency to dismiss and ridicule the truth when it does not align with their preconceived notions or desires. The verse serves as a warning that such an attitude will only lead to their own detriment and distance from God.
orig: يا حسرة على العباد ما يأتيهم من رسول إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We have destroyed before them, and that they (the destroyed ones) will not return to them?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the disbelievers who deny the Day of Resurrection and the Hereafter. It reminds them that countless generations before them have been destroyed, and that those destroyed people will never return to the living. This is meant to convey the certainty of the Hereafter and the consequences of disbelief. The verse encourages the disbelievers to reflect on the fate of previous nations and to believe in the Resurrection and the Hereafter.
orig: ألم يروا كم أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون أنهم إليهم لا يرجعون

translation: And indeed, all [of creation] that is in the heavens and the earth will come to [Allah] as subjects.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all of creation, whether in the heavens or on earth, will ultimately be gathered before Allah on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder that we are all accountable to our Creator and will be held responsible for our actions in this life. The verse underscores the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah, who has dominion over all things.
orig: وإن كل لما جميع لدينا محضرون

translation: And a sign for them is the dead earth. We have brought it to life and brought forth from it [some] grain, and from it they eat.
interpretation: This verse points to the power and wisdom of God in reviving the dead earth and bringing forth sustenance for His creation. The dead earth, which appears lifeless, is brought back to life through the rain and growth of vegetation. This is a sign of God's ability to resurrect the dead and provide for all of His creatures. The verse encourages reflection on the divine design and care evident in the natural world.
orig: وآية لهم الأرض الميتة أحييناها وأخرجنا منها حبا فمنه يأكلون

translation: And We placed therein gardens of palm trees and grapevines and caused to burst forth therefrom springs
interpretation: This verse describes the bountiful provisions that God has created on Earth, including gardens of date palms and grapevines, as well as springs of fresh water. This imagery conveys the abundance and fertility that God has bestowed upon the world, highlighting His power and generosity. The interpretation suggests that these natural resources are a testament to God's creation and a means by which He sustains and nourishes His creation.
orig: وجعلنا فيها جنات من نخيل وأعناب وفجرنا فيها من العيون

translation: So that they may eat from its fruit, and their hands have not produced it. Then will they not be grateful?
interpretation: This verse encourages people to be grateful for the blessings that Allah has provided, such as the fruits and crops that they are able to consume, which are not the result of their own labor. It reminds us that the true source of these blessings is Allah, and that we should express our gratitude to Him for these gifts.
orig: ليأكلوا من ثمره وما عملته أيديهم أفلا يشكرون

translation: Exalted is He who created all pairs - from what the earth grows and from themselves and from that which they do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the glory and power of God, who has created all things in pairs, including what grows on the earth, what is within human beings, and things that humans do not yet know about. This highlights God's omnipotence and the wonders of His creation, which extend far beyond human knowledge and understanding.
orig: سبحان الذي خلق الأزواج كلها مما تنبت الأرض ومن أنفسهم ومما لا يعلمون

translation: And a sign for them is the night. We remove from it the [light of the] day, and suddenly they are in darkness.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the cyclical nature of day and night, and how this is a sign of Allah's power and control over the universe. The night is mentioned as a "sign" (آية) for the people, indicating that it is a clear evidence and a lesson for them to reflect upon. The verse describes how Allah "removes" (نسلخ) the day from the night, causing the night to become dark. This is a metaphor for how Allah brings about the alternation of day and night, demonstrating His sovereignty and the perfection of His creation. The people are then described as being "in darkness" (مظلمون), which can be interpreted as a state of ignorance, confusion, or heedlessness if they fail to recognize the significance of this natural phenomenon and what it points to in terms of Allah's power and wisdom.
orig: وآية لهم الليل نسلخ منه النهار فإذا هم مظلمون

translation: And the sun runs [on course] toward its stopping point. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the orderly and systematic movement of the sun, which follows a precise and predetermined path. The sun"s journey is not haphazard, but rather guided by the will and knowledge of Allah, the Exalted in Might and the All-Knowing. This suggests that the universe operates according to a divine plan, with each element fulfilling its role and serving a greater purpose. The sun"s movement is a testament to Allah"s power and wisdom, and a reminder that all of creation is subject to His control and guidance.
orig: والشمس تجري لمستقر لها ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: And the moon - We have determined for it phases, until it returns [appearing] as the old [and withered] palm branch.
interpretation: This verse describes the phases of the moon, which the Qur'an states have been determined by God. The moon goes through a cycle of waxing and waning, until it appears as a thin, curved crescent, likened to an "old and withered palm branch". This highlights the precision and order in the celestial bodies, which are a sign of God's power and wisdom in creating the universe.
orig: والقمر قدرناه منازل حتى عاد كالعرجون القديم

translation: The sun must not catch up with the moon, nor does the night outpace the day. And all [heavenly bodies] are, in an orbit, swimming.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfect order and harmony in the universe, where each celestial body follows its own course without interfering with the others. The sun and moon, day and night, all move in their own orbits without disrupting the balance of the cosmos. This is a testament to the wisdom and power of the Creator, who has established this intricate system that functions with precision and regularity.
orig: لا الشمس ينبغي لها أن تدرك القمر ولا الليل سابق النهار وكل في فلك يسبحون

translation: And a sign for them is that We carried their forefathers in the laden ship.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Nuh (Noah) and the Flood. It is a sign and a reminder for the people that just as Allah saved Nuh and his followers in the laden ship, He has the power to guide and protect those who believe in Him. This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and submission to Allah, as He is the One who can save us from calamities and guide us to the right path.
orig: وآية لهم أنا حملنا ذريتهم في الفلك المشحون

translation: And We have created for them the like thereof [i.e. the sailing ships or cattle] on which they ride.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has created various means of transportation and conveyance for humans, such as ships and animals, to facilitate their movement and travel. The interpretation is that God has provided these resources to serve the needs and ease the lives of His creation.
orig: وخلقنا لهم من مثله ما يركبون

translation: And if We willed, We could drown them, and there would be no one to respond to their call, nor would they be saved
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute power and control over the universe. If God wills, He can easily destroy even the most powerful of His creation, and there would be no one who could save them or come to their aid. This serves as a reminder to humans that they are entirely dependent on God and should submit to His will, as He is the Sovereign and All-Powerful.
orig: وإن نشأ نغرقهم فلا صريخ لهم ولا هم ينقذون

translation: Except as a mercy from Us and as a provision for a specified term.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the punishment or trial that believers may face is not an end in itself, but rather a temporary test or trial that is ultimately a mercy from God. The verse indicates that these trials are not meant to be permanent, but rather a "provision for a specified term", implying that they have a limited duration and purpose. The interpretation is that God's mercy and wisdom are behind even the difficulties that believers may face, and that these trials are not arbitrary but serve a higher purpose in the believer's spiritual growth and development.
orig: إلا رحمة منا ومتاعا إلى حين

translation: And when it is said to them, "Avoid what is in front of you and what is behind you so that you may receive mercy,"
interpretation: This verse encourages people to be mindful of their actions, both in the present and in the future. It suggests that by avoiding wrongdoing and being conscious of the consequences of their choices, they may be granted Allah's mercy and forgiveness. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of being accountable for one's deeds and seeking Allah's guidance to live a righteous life.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اتقوا ما بين أيديكم وما خلفكم لعلكم ترحمون

translation: And there does not come to them any sign from the signs of their Lord except that they were from it turning away.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being referred to here are those who stubbornly refuse to acknowledge the signs and evidence of God's existence and power, even when they are presented with clear proofs. They turn away from these signs, choosing to remain in their state of disbelief and ignorance. The verse emphasizes the unwillingness of these individuals to accept the guidance and wisdom that comes from God, and their persistent rejection of the divine messages.
orig: وما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين

translation: And when it is said to them, "Spend from that which Allah has provided for you," those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Should we feed one whom, if Allah had willed, He would have fed? You are not but in clear error."
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of those who reject faith towards the believers when they are called upon to spend from the wealth that Allah has provided them. The disbelievers question the rationale behind feeding others, arguing that if Allah had willed, He would have provided for them as well. This response reflects their lack of understanding of the purpose of wealth and their responsibility to help those in need. The interpretation suggests that the disbelievers are in a state of clear misguidance, as they fail to recognize the true nature of wealth and the obligation to share it with others as per the teachings of Islam.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم أنفقوا مما رزقكم الله قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أنطعم من لو يشاء الله أطعمه إن أنتم إلا في ضلال مبين

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who are skeptical about the promise of the Day of Judgment and the afterlife. They are challenging the believers to provide evidence for the reality of this promise, as they do not believe in it. The verse emphasizes that those who are truthful in their faith will witness the fulfillment of this promise, while the disbelievers will be held accountable for their rejection of it.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: They are waiting for but a single blast, which will seize them while they are disputing.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the final trumpet will be blown, and all people will be resurrected for the final reckoning. The verse suggests that the disbelievers are merely waiting for this single, decisive moment, which will come upon them unexpectedly while they are still engaged in their disputes and arguments against the truth of God's message. The interpretation is that the disbelievers will be caught off guard by the sudden arrival of the Day of Judgment, and will have no time left to continue their denials and objections.
orig: ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون

translation: So they will not be able to make a bequest, nor can they return to their families.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the fate of those who disbelieve and reject the message of Islam. It indicates that they will not be able to make any final arrangements or bequests, nor will they be able to return to their families, as they will be facing the consequences of their disbelief in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the finality and irreversibility of the punishment that awaits those who turn away from the guidance of Allah.
orig: فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون

translation: And the Horn will be blown, and at once they will be from the graves hastening to their Lord.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Resurrection, when the trumpet will be blown and the dead will be resurrected from their graves to be judged by their Lord. The verse emphasizes the swiftness with which the people will emerge from their graves and rush to stand before their Creator, highlighting the urgency and gravity of that momentous day.
orig: ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون

translation: They will say, "Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?" [This is] what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers had told the truth."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection when they are resurrected from their graves. They will be shocked and dismayed, wondering who has awakened them from their slumber. This verse affirms that the resurrection and the Day of Judgment are the truth promised by the Most Merciful God, and that the Prophets and Messengers have conveyed this truth faithfully.
