orig: قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون

translation: Indeed, it is but one shout, and suddenly they will all be brought present before Us.
interpretation: This verse conveys the swiftness and finality of the Day of Resurrection. It suggests that the entire human race will be gathered before God in an instant, with no time for delay or excuses. The "one shout" refers to the blast of the trumpet that will signal the end of this world and the beginning of the Hereafter, when all people will be held accountable for their actions. This emphasizes the urgency and gravity of preparing for the Afterlife, as we will all stand before the Almighty to face the consequences of our choices in this life.
orig: إن كانت إلا صيحة واحدة فإذا هم جميع لدينا محضرون

translation: So this Day no soul will be wronged at all, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice and accountability on the Day of Judgment. It assures that no one will be wronged or treated unfairly, and that each person will be recompensed solely based on their own deeds and actions in this life. The interpretation underscores the importance of personal responsibility and the fact that individuals will be held accountable for their choices and behaviors, without any external factors influencing the outcome.
orig: فاليوم لا تظلم نفس شيئا ولا تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: Indeed, the companions of Paradise, that Day, will be amused in [joyful] occupation.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that the inhabitants of Paradise will be fully engaged in pleasurable and fulfilling activities, free from any worries or burdens. They will be in a state of blissful occupation, enjoying the fruits and delights of Paradise without any distractions or concerns. This highlights the eternal joy and contentment that awaits the righteous in the Hereafter.
orig: إن أصحاب الجنة اليوم في شغل فاكهون

translation: They and their spouses will be in shades, reclining on thrones.
interpretation: This verse describes the blissful state of the believers in Paradise. They and their spouses will be resting comfortably in the shades, reclining on elevated couches or thrones. This imagery conveys a sense of peace, tranquility, and the fulfillment of their desires in the Hereafter.
orig: هم وأزواجهم في ظلال على الأرائك متكئون

translation: For them therein is fruit and for them is whatever they request.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the believers in Paradise will have access to a variety of delicious fruits, as well as anything else they desire. It suggests that the blessings of the Hereafter are not limited, and the inhabitants of Paradise will have their every wish fulfilled.
orig: لهم فيها فاكهة ولهم ما يدعون

translation: Peace - a word from a Merciful Lord.
interpretation: This verse conveys a message of peace and mercy from the Almighty Lord. It suggests that true peace and tranquility can only be attained through the mercy and compassion of the Divine. The verse emphasizes that the Lord, in His infinite wisdom and kindness, extends a greeting of peace to His creation, inviting them to seek refuge in His mercy and guidance.
orig: سلام قولا من رب رحيم

translation: And today, O criminals, distinguish yourselves.
interpretation: This verse is a command to the wrongdoers to set themselves apart from the righteous on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that they will be clearly identified and separated from the believers, as a consequence of their misdeeds in this life. The verse emphasizes the accountability that the criminals will face on the Day of Reckoning, where they will be distinguished and singled out for their crimes.
orig: وامتازوا اليوم أيها المجرمون

translation: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - [for] indeed, he is to you a clear enemy?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question from Allah to the children of Adam, reminding them that He had clearly commanded them not to worship Satan, as he is their sworn enemy who seeks to lead them astray. The verse emphasizes the importance of obeying Allah and avoiding the temptations of Satan, who is described as a "clear enemy" to humanity.
orig: ألم أعهد إليكم يا بني آدم أن لا تعبدوا الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: And that you worship Me. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone, as He is the only true God worthy of worship. The phrase "This is a straight path" indicates that the path of worshipping Allah is the right and direct way to achieve success in this life and the hereafter. It is a clear and unambiguous directive, calling upon believers to devote themselves solely to the worship of the Almighty.
orig: وأن اعبدوني هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And certainly We have destroyed many of you (disbelievers) in the past; so have you not understood?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the disbelievers that Allah has destroyed many nations and communities in the past due to their disbelief and rejection of the truth. The question "so have you not understood?" is meant to make them reflect on the consequences of their actions and to urge them to accept the message of Islam before they suffer a similar fate.
orig: ولقد أضل منكم جبلا كثيرا أفلم تكونوا تعقلون

translation: This is the Hell which you were promised.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers and wrongdoers will be confronted with the reality of Hell, which they were warned about during their earthly lives. The Qur'an emphasizes the certainty of the Hellfire as a consequence for those who reject faith and engage in sinful behavior. This serves as a powerful reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and righteous deeds, in order to avoid the eternal punishment of the Hereafter.
orig: هذه جهنم التي كنتم توعدون

translation: Enter it this Day, for that [disbelief] you were rejecting.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who rejected the truth and disbelieved in God's signs. They are being told that they will be punished for their rejection and disbelief, and that they will now have to face the consequences of their actions. The interpretation suggests that the Day of Judgment has arrived, and those who denied the truth will now have to enter the fire of Hell as a result of their rejection.
orig: اصلوها اليوم بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: This Day We will seal up their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness about what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers will be unable to deny their misdeeds. Their mouths will be sealed, preventing them from making excuses, while their limbs will testify against them, bearing witness to the sins they committed in life. This emphasizes the futility of denying one's actions on that day, as everything will be made clear and the consequences of one's choices will be inescapable.
orig: اليوم نختم على أفواههم وتكلمنا أيديهم وتشهد أرجلهم بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And if We willed, We could have covered over their eyes, so they would race to the path, and how could they see?
interpretation: This verse suggests that if Allah willed, He could have blinded the disbelievers so they would have no choice but to follow the straight path. However, Allah has given them the ability to see and choose their own path. The implication is that Allah does not force belief upon people, but gives them the freedom to accept or reject faith. The verse highlights the idea that true faith comes from one's own choice and conviction, not from coercion.
orig: ولو نشاء لطمسنا على أعينهم فاستبقوا الصراط فأنى يبصرون

translation: And if We willed, We could have deformed them [i.e., the disbelievers] in their places, and they would not have been able to precede [i.e., flee] or return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute power and sovereignty. If He willed, He could transform the disbelievers into something else, preventing them from moving forward or returning. This serves as a warning to those who reject faith, that they are completely at the mercy of God and cannot escape His punishment if He so decides. The verse highlights the futility of resisting God's will and the importance of submitting to Him.
orig: ولو نشاء لمسخناهم على مكانتهم فما استطاعوا مضيا ولا يرجعون

translation: And whoever We grant long life to - We reverse him in creation; so will they not understand?
interpretation: This verse suggests that as people grow old, their physical and mental faculties decline. This is a part of the natural cycle of life that God has ordained. The verse encourages people to ponder and reflect on this process, and to use their God-given intellect to understand the wisdom behind it, rather than being heedless or complacent.
orig: ومن نعمره ننكسه في الخلق أفلا يعقلون

translation: And We have not taught him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is not but a message and a clear Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not a poet, nor was the Qur'an a work of poetry. Rather, the Qur'an is a divine message and a clear, authoritative scripture revealed to him by God. The verse serves to distinguish the Qur'an from mere human poetry, highlighting its unique status as a revelation from the Almighty.
orig: وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له إن هو إلا ذكر وقرآن مبين

translation: That he may warn him who is alive, and that the Word may be justified against the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purpose of the Qur'an and the mission of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The Qur'an is revealed to warn those who are alive and receptive to guidance, so that they may believe and be saved. It also confirms the inevitability of the punishment for those who stubbornly reject the truth and persist in disbelief. The "Word" refers to the divine decree that the disbelievers will be held accountable for their rejection of faith.
orig: لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين

translation: Have they not seen that We have created for them from what Our hands have made, [other] animals, and they [i.e., the people] are their owners?
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the blessings that God has provided for them, such as the creation of domestic animals that they can utilize and benefit from. The implication is that if people can recognize God's providence in creating these useful animals, they should also acknowledge His sovereignty and worship Him alone.
orig: أولم يروا أنا خلقنا لهم مما عملت أيدينا أنعاما فهم لها مالكون

translation: And We have made them tractable unto them, so that some of them they have for riding and [some] of them they eat.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the domestication of animals, such as camels, cattle, and sheep, for the benefit of humankind. The verse indicates that Allah has made these animals subservient to humans, allowing them to be used for transportation ("for riding") as well as for sustenance ("of them they eat"). This highlights the blessings and bounties that Allah has provided for humanity, and the responsibility we have to use these resources responsibly and with gratitude.
orig: وذللناها لهم فمنها ركوبهم ومنها يأكلون

translation: And for them therein are [other] benefits and [numerous] drinks; so will they not be grateful?
interpretation: This verse highlights the many blessings and provisions that God has bestowed upon humanity. The "benefits and drinks" refer to the various resources and sustenance that God has made available for our use and enjoyment. The rhetorical question "so will they not be grateful?" emphasizes the importance of expressing gratitude and appreciation to God for these abundant gifts. The interpretation encourages us to recognize and be thankful for the countless blessings we have been granted, rather than taking them for granted.
orig: ولهم فيها منافع ومشارب أفلا يشكرون

translation: And they have taken besides Allah gods that they might be helped.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the practice of polytheism, where people worship multiple deities besides Allah. The verse suggests that the purpose of this practice is to seek help and support from these other gods, in the belief that they will provide assistance and protection. However, the Qur'an emphasizes that Allah is the only true God, and that seeking help from any other deity is futile and misguided.
orig: واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة لعلهم ينصرون

translation: They are unable to help them, and they themselves are a host brought up before them.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who seek help from false deities or idols will be disappointed, as these entities are unable to provide any real assistance. They are merely a host or army that has been summoned, but they have no power to actually help their worshippers. The verse emphasizes the futility of relying on anything other than the one true God, Allah, for support and guidance.
orig: لا يستطيعون نصرهم وهم لهم جند محضرون

translation: So let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he should not be saddened by the disbelievers' rejection of his message or their attempts to conceal their true intentions. Allah knows everything that they hide in their hearts as well as what they openly express. The Prophet should remain steadfast in his mission, confident that Allah is in control and that the ultimate truth will prevail.
orig: فلا يحزنك قولهم إنا نعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون

translation: Has not man seen that We have created him from a [mere] sperm-drop? Then he is an open adversary.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humble origins of man, created from a mere sperm-drop, to highlight the arrogance and defiance that can arise in man towards his Creator. It serves as a reminder of man's dependence on God and the need for humility, rather than becoming an "open adversary" against the divine plan.
orig: أولم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين

translation: And he has set forth for Us a parable and has forgotten his [own] creation; he says, "Who will give life to bones while they are disintegrated?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to forget the power of God and the reality of the afterlife. When faced with the concept of resurrection, some people may express doubt and question how it is possible for decayed bones to be brought back to life. However, the verse reminds us that the same God who created us in the first place has the power to resurrect us, and that we should not underestimate His abilities. The verse serves as a reminder to have faith in God's omnipotence and to not be swayed by our own limited understanding of the world.
orig: وضرب لنا مثلا ونسي خلقه قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم

translation: Say, "He will give life to them who created them the first time, and He is, of all creation, Knowing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Creator, is the one who can give life and resurrect the dead. Just as He created life the first time, He has the power to bring it back again. This serves as a reassurance that the Day of Resurrection will indeed come to pass, and that Allah has full knowledge and control over all of His creation.
orig: قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة وهو بكل خلق عليم

translation: It is He who has made for you from the green trees, fire, and then from it you ignite.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power and creativity in providing us with natural resources that can be used for our benefit. The green trees, which are a part of God's creation, can be used to produce fire, which is an essential element for human survival and development. This verse reminds us that we should be grateful for the blessings that God has bestowed upon us and use them in a responsible and productive manner.
orig: الذي جعل لكم من الشجر الأخضر نارا فإذا أنتم منه توقدون

translation: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth Able to create the likes of them? Yes, [and] He is the Supreme Creator, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the One who created the vast universe and all that is in it is certainly capable of creating the likes of it. The rhetorical question "Is not He who created the heavens and the earth Able to create the likes of them?" is meant to affirm that God, the Supreme Creator, has the power and knowledge to create anything He wills. The interpretation is that there is no doubt about God's ability to create, for He is the Omnipotent and All-Knowing Creator.
orig: أوليس الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بقادر على أن يخلق مثلهم بلى وهو الخلاق العليم

translation: Indeed, His command is but [that] when He intends a thing, He says to it, "Be," and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah. When Allah wills something to come into existence, He merely says the word "Be" and it immediately comes into being. This highlights Allah's supreme control over all creation, as He can bring anything into existence with a single command. It also underscores the ease and effortlessness with which Allah creates, as there is no struggle or difficulty involved in His acts of creation. This verse serves to reinforce the belief that Allah is the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe, and that nothing can come into being without His will and permission.
orig: إنما أمره إذا أراد شيئا أن يقول له كن فيكون

translation: So exalted is He in whose hand is the realm of all things, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of God over all creation. It affirms that God alone is the true Owner and Ruler of the entire universe, and that all things ultimately belong to and return to Him. This serves as a reminder of God's supreme authority and the fact that human beings will be held accountable to Him on the Day of Judgment.
orig: فسبحان الذي بيده ملكوت كل شيء وإليه ترجعون

translation: And [by] those [angels] lined up in rows
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who are arranged in orderly rows, signifying their obedience and submission to Allah. It suggests that the angels are organized and disciplined in their worship and service to the Almighty. This verse emphasizes the concept of divine order and hierarchy within the celestial realm, where the angels are positioned and aligned in a structured manner to carry out their duties.
orig: والصافات صفا

translation: By the [winds] that blow violently
interpretation: This verse is referring to the angels who forcefully drive the clouds and winds. The interpretation is that the Almighty God has appointed angels to control and direct the winds, which play a crucial role in the cycle of life on Earth. These winds are instrumental in bringing rain, dispersing clouds, and maintaining the balance of the environment. The verse emphasizes the power and precision with which these angels carry out their duties, highlighting the intricate design and control of the natural world by the Creator.
orig: فالزاجرات زجرا

translation: And the remembrance (of Allah)
interpretation: This verse is referring to the remembrance and recollection of Allah. It emphasizes the importance of keeping Allah in one's thoughts and constantly remembering Him. This act of remembrance is a means of connecting with the divine, seeking guidance, and maintaining a spiritual awareness in one's life.
orig: فالتاليات ذكرا

translation: Indeed, your God is one
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and unity of God (Allah). It conveys the idea that there is only one true and supreme deity, and that all forms of polytheism or associating partners with God are rejected. The verse affirms the core tenet of Islamic monotheism, which is the foundation of the faith.
orig: إن إلهكم لواحد

translation: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and the Lord of the sunrises.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and dominion of Allah over all of creation. He is the Lord (Rabb) of the heavens and the earth, as well as everything that exists between them. He is also the Lord of the sunrises, which can be interpreted as referring to the different points of sunrise throughout the world, or the rising and setting of the sun itself. This highlights Allah's power, authority, and control over the entire universe and all that it contains.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما ورب المشارق

translation: Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with the stars
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has beautified the nearest heaven, which is the sky we see, with the stars. The stars serve as adornments and decorations in the heavens, showcasing the power and artistry of the Creator. This is a testament to Allah's magnificent creation and a sign for those who reflect upon it.
orig: إنا زينا السماء الدنيا بزينة الكواكب

translation: And protection from every obstinate devil
interpretation: This verse refers to seeking refuge and protection from the evil influences of Satan, who is described as a "stubborn devil" or "obstinate devil". The interpretation suggests that one should seek Allah's protection and guidance to be safeguarded from the temptations and deceptions of the devil, who is persistent and relentless in his efforts to lead people astray.
orig: وحفظا من كل شيطان مارد

translation: They do not listen to the highest assembly and are pelted from every side.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who reject the message of the Qur'an and turn away from it. They do not listen to the guidance and wisdom of the highest assembly, which is a reference to the angels in heaven. Instead, they are pelted or attacked from every side, meaning they face opposition, ridicule, and rejection from all quarters for their refusal to accept the truth.
orig: لا يسمعون إلى الملإ الأعلى ويقذفون من كل جانب

translation: And they will have a constant punishment
interpretation: This verse refers to those who reject the truth and turn away from the guidance of Allah. They will face a constant and unrelenting punishment in the Hereafter, as a consequence of their disbelief and misdeeds. The phrase "constant punishment" suggests that this punishment will be eternal and unending, a fitting recompense for their stubborn rejection of the divine message.
orig: دحورا ولهم عذاب واصب

translation: Except [for] one who snatches [some words] by theft, and they are pursued by a burning flame.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who try to eavesdrop on the divine revelation and steal some of its words or meanings. However, they are immediately pursued by a bright, piercing flame that exposes and punishes their deceit. The interpretation suggests that the Qur'an is a divine revelation that should be approached with reverence and humility, not with attempts to misappropriate its contents.
orig: إلا من خطف الخطفة فأتبعه شهاب ثاقب

translation: So ask them, [O Muhammad], are they a stronger [and more difficult] creation or is the [previous creation of the] ones We have created? Indeed, We created them from sticky clay.
interpretation: This verse is inviting the disbelievers to reflect on their own creation and compare it to the creation of others. It suggests that the disbelievers are not more difficult to create than the previous creations of Allah, as they were all created from the same basic material of sticky clay. The purpose is to demonstrate Allah's power and ability to create, and to remind the disbelievers that they are not immune to His will and judgment.
orig: فاستفتهم أهم أشد خلقا أم من خلقنا إنا خلقناهم من طين لازب

translation: Nay, but they wonder; and they scoff.
interpretation: This verse expresses the reaction of the disbelievers to the message of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). They are amazed and amused by the message, rather than taking it seriously and reflecting on it. The verse suggests that their scoffing and derision will not deter the progress of the divine message, and that they will ultimately be held accountable for their rejection of the truth.
orig: بل عجبت ويسخرون

translation: And when they are reminded, they do not remember.
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people are heedless and forgetful, even when they are reminded of important matters. They fail to internalize and act upon the guidance or reminders they receive, perhaps due to a lack of focus, sincerity, or willingness to change. The verse highlights the need for people to be attentive and receptive to reminders, in order to maintain a connection with the divine and live according to righteous principles.
orig: وإذا ذكروا لا يذكرون

translation: And when they see a sign, they ridicule it
interpretation: This verse refers to the attitude of those who reject faith and dismiss the signs and miracles of God. They mock and scoff at the evidence of God's existence and power, rather than reflecting on them and accepting the truth. This verse highlights the closed-mindedness and arrogance of those who refuse to acknowledge the divine signs around them.
orig: وإذا رأوا آية يستسخرون

translation: And they say, "This is not but evident magic."
interpretation: This verse refers to the reaction of the disbelievers towards the Qur'an and the message of Islam. They dismissed the Qur'an as nothing more than "evident magic", implying that it was a work of sorcery or deception, rather than a divine revelation. This reflects their unwillingness to accept the truth and their refusal to acknowledge the miraculous nature of the Qur'an.
orig: وقالوا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: Is it [not true] that when we have died and become dust and bones, we will [then] be resurrected?
interpretation: This verse poses a rhetorical question that challenges the idea of resurrection after death. The question suggests that the disbelievers find it hard to believe that after their bodies have decomposed into dust and bones, they will be brought back to life. The interpretation is that this verse is addressing the skepticism of those who deny the resurrection, and it serves to affirm that indeed the dead will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment.
orig: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمبعوثون

translation: Or our forefathers of old?
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between the disbelievers and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The disbelievers are questioning the message of Islam, asking whether they should follow the religion of their forefathers instead. The interpretation is that the disbelievers are clinging to the traditions and beliefs of their ancestors, rather than being open to the new guidance brought by the Prophet. This highlights the importance of not blindly following the ways of the past, but rather seeking the truth and being willing to change one's beliefs if presented with a more compelling message from God.
orig: أوآباؤنا الأولون

translation: Say, "Yes, [but you are] humbled."
interpretation: This verse is a command from God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to respond to those who deny the truth of Islam. The phrase "and you are humbled" refers to the fact that those who reject the truth will ultimately be humbled and submissive before God on the Day of Judgment. The interpretation suggests that the believers should confidently affirm their faith, even in the face of opposition, knowing that the truth will prevail in the end.
orig: قل نعم وأنتم داخرون

translation: And it will be but one shout, and at once they will be observing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Day of Resurrection will occur suddenly, without warning. The "one shout" refers to the single, powerful call that will awaken all people from their graves and cause them to witness the events of the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the swiftness and unexpectedness of this momentous event, highlighting the need for people to be prepared and attentive to the signs of the coming Day.
orig: فإنما هي زجرة واحدة فإذا هم ينظرون

translation: And they will say, "Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, when they will realize the consequences of their actions in this life. They will lament and express their regret, acknowledging that this is the day when they will be held accountable for their deeds. The interpretation suggests that the Day of Judgment is a reality that all people will face, and that it is crucial to prepare for it by living a righteous life in this world.
orig: وقالوا يا ويلنا هذا يوم الدين

translation: This is the Day of Separation about which you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when people will be separated into those who believed and those who disbelieved. It emphasizes that this day, which the disbelievers had denied, is now a reality that they will face. The interpretation underscores the importance of belief and righteous conduct, as the Day of Judgment will reveal the consequences of one’s actions in this life.
orig: هذا يوم الفصل الذي كنتم به تكذبون

translation: Gather those who did wrong, and their companions, and what they used to worship
interpretation: This verse is calling for the gathering and accountability of those who committed wrongdoing, along with their associates and the objects of their worship. It suggests that on the Day of Judgment, all those who engaged in evil deeds will be brought together to face the consequences of their actions, including the people and things they revered. The interpretation is that there will be a reckoning for those who strayed from the righteous path and the accountability will extend to all aspects of their lives and beliefs.
orig: احشروا الذين ظلموا وأزواجهم وما كانوا يعبدون

translation: Other than Allah, so guide them to the path of Hell.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that there is no deity worthy of worship besides Allah. It calls upon the believers to guide those who worship false gods or idols towards the path of Hell, which is the ultimate punishment for those who reject the oneness of Allah and associate partners with Him.
orig: من دون الله فاهدوهم إلى صراط الجحيم

translation: And stop them; indeed, they are to be questioned.
interpretation: This verse commands that people should be held accountable for their actions and beliefs. It suggests that on the Day of Judgment, all individuals will be questioned about their deeds and the choices they made in life. The verse emphasizes the importance of personal responsibility and the need to answer for one"s conduct before God.
orig: وقفوهم إنهم مسئولون

translation: What is [the matter] with you that you do not aid [the cause of] Allah?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question addressed to those who are not supporting the cause of Allah and the believers. It is a call to action, urging them to fulfill their duty of assisting and defending the faith. The interpretation suggests that it is a moral obligation for the believers to aid and support the cause of Allah, and those who fail to do so are being questioned about their inaction.
orig: ما لكم لا تناصرون

translation: Nay, they are this Day (the disbelievers) surrendering (to Allah's Decree)
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers, who were previously arrogant and defiant, will ultimately surrender to Allah's decree on the Day of Judgment. It implies that no one can escape the inevitable consequences of their actions, and that they will be held accountable for their choices in life.
orig: بل هم اليوم مستسلمون

translation: And they will approach one another inquiring of each other
interpretation: This verse describes the scene on the Day of Judgment, where people will be gathered and will start questioning each other about their deeds in the worldly life. It suggests a state of confusion and uncertainty, as people try to understand their own and others' actions and their consequences.
orig: وأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون

translation: They will say, "Indeed, you used to come at us from the right."
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, who will accuse the believers of misleading them and turning them away from the truth. The phrase "from the right" suggests that the disbelievers will claim that the believers had authority, influence, and power, and they used these to lead them astray. The interpretation is that the disbelievers will try to shift the blame for their own choices and actions onto the believers, rather than taking responsibility for their own rejection of the truth.
orig: قالوا إنكم كنتم تأتوننا عن اليمين

translation: They said, "Rather, you were not believers."
interpretation: This verse refers to a dialogue between the disbelievers and the believers. The disbelievers are denying the faith of the believers, claiming that they were never true believers in the first place. This highlights the conflict between those who accept the message of Islam and those who reject it. The interpretation suggests that the disbelievers are dismissing the faith of the believers, challenging their sincerity and commitment to the religion.
orig: قالوا بل لم تكونوا مؤمنين

translation: And we had no authority over you, but you were a transgressing people.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who rejected the message of Islam. It states that the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the believers had no coercive power or authority over the disbelievers, but the disbelievers were a people who transgressed and exceeded the proper bounds. The interpretation is that the disbelievers were responsible for their own rejection of the truth, and could not blame the believers for their misguidance.
orig: وما كان لنا عليكم من سلطان بل كنتم قوما طاغين

translation: And it has become binding upon Us to save the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is incumbent upon Allah to support and protect the believers. It is a promise from Allah that He will save and deliver the believers from any harm or hardship they may face. This verse provides the believers with a sense of security and reassurance that Allah will always be there to aid and support them.
orig: فحق علينا قول ربنا إنا لذائقون

translation: So We led you astray. Indeed, We had [all the while] been astray.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the deception of Satan, who led humans astray from the path of righteousness. The verse suggests that Satan himself was misguided, and in turn, he misguided humanity as well. The interpretation is that we should be wary of the temptations of Satan and strive to stay on the righteous path.
orig: فأغويناكم إنا كنا غاوين

translation: And so they will be, on that Day, sharers in the punishment.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all those who disbelieved and rejected the truth will be held accountable and will share in the punishment that awaits them. The message is that there will be no escape from the consequences of one's actions, and that all who have denied the signs of God will face the same fate on that fateful day.
orig: فإنهم يومئذ في العذاب مشتركون

translation: Indeed, We thus deal with the criminals.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah deals with those who commit sins and crimes in a just and appropriate manner. It suggests that the punishment or consequences faced by the wrongdoers are a result of their own actions, and that Allah's judgment is fair and in accordance with their deeds. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in criminal or sinful behavior, and encourages them to repent and reform their ways.
orig: إنا كذلك نفعل بالمجرمين

translation: Indeed, they used to be, when it was said to them, "There is no deity but Allah," arrogant
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who would refuse to accept the oneness of God (Allah) and instead remained arrogant and prideful. The verse highlights how they would reject the fundamental Islamic belief in the existence of only one true God, displaying an attitude of superiority and unwillingness to submit to the divine truth.
orig: إنهم كانوا إذا قيل لهم لا إله إلا الله يستكبرون

translation: And they say, "Are we to abandon our gods for a mad poet?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who mocked the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and accused him of being a "mad poet" for abandoning their pagan gods and idols in favor of worshipping the one true God, Allah. The verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers, who refused to accept the message of Islam and were unwilling to give up their false deities. The interpretation emphasizes that the Prophet was neither a mad poet nor someone who should be abandoned, but rather a messenger of God bringing the truth to humanity.
orig: ويقولون أئنا لتاركو آلهتنا لشاعر مجنون

translation: But he has come with the truth and confirmed the [previous] messengers.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Prophet Muhammad came with the truth and confirmed the messages and teachings of the previous prophets and messengers of God. It highlights the continuity of the divine message and the truthfulness of the Prophet Muhammad as the final messenger in the line of prophethood.
orig: بل جاء بالحق وصدق المرسلين

translation: Indeed, you will be tasting the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from God to those who reject His message and disobey His commands. It conveys the certainty that those who persist in their disbelief and wrongdoing will ultimately face a severe and painful punishment in the Hereafter. The emphasis on "tasting" the punishment suggests that it will be a direct and visceral experience, leaving a lasting impact on the condemned. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to strive to please God, lest they suffer the same fate as the disbelievers.
orig: إنكم لذائقو العذاب الأليم

translation: And you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, people will be held accountable for their actions in this life. They will be rewarded or punished based on the deeds they performed, not on their status, wealth, or other external factors. It serves as a reminder that we must be mindful of our actions and strive to do good, as the consequences of our choices will ultimately determine our fate in the Hereafter.
orig: وما تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: Except the sincere servants of Allah
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have devoted themselves wholeheartedly to the worship and service of Allah. They are the ones who have purified their intentions and actions, and have submitted themselves completely to the will of Allah. These sincere servants of Allah are the ones who will be spared from the punishment and torment that will befall the disbelievers and the wicked.
orig: إلا عباد الله المخلصين

translation: Those, for them is a known provision.
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who have faith in God and do righteous deeds. They will be provided for by God in the Hereafter with a known, guaranteed sustenance or reward. This suggests that the believers will receive their just due from God, which is a reward that is predetermined and certain.
orig: أولئك لهم رزق معلوم

translation: And fruits, and they will be honored
interpretation: This verse suggests that the righteous and faithful will be provided with delicious fruits in the Hereafter as a sign of their elevated status and the honor bestowed upon them by Allah. The fruits symbolize the bountiful rewards and pleasures that await those who have lived virtuous lives and submitted to the will of God.
orig: فواكه وهم مكرمون

translation: In the Gardens of Pleasure
interpretation: This verse refers to the eternal abode of the righteous in the Hereafter, known as the Gardens of Paradise. It suggests that the believers who have lived a virtuous life will be rewarded with a state of blissful existence, free from any suffering or hardship. The Gardens of Pleasure represent the ultimate fulfillment and joy that awaits those who have submitted to the will of Allah and followed the guidance of the Qur'an and the teachings of Islam.
orig: في جنات النعيم

translation: Upon thrones facing each other
interpretation: This verse describes the setting of the afterlife, where the righteous will be seated on thrones facing each other in a state of contentment and harmony. It suggests a sense of community, togetherness, and mutual appreciation among the inhabitants of Paradise.
orig: على سرر متقابلين

translation: They will be given to drink from a cup [filled] from a flowing spring
interpretation: This verse describes the blessings and delights that the righteous will enjoy in the Hereafter. The "flowing spring" represents a pure, abundant source of refreshment and sustenance, free from any impurities or unpleasantness. The image of being "given to drink" from this spring conveys the idea of being nourished and satisfied, both physically and spiritually, by the bounties of Paradise. This verse highlights the contrast between the eternal bliss of the Hereafter and the fleeting and imperfect pleasures of this world, encouraging believers to strive for the attainment of the everlasting rewards in the Afterlife.
orig: يطاف عليهم بكأس من معين

translation: White, delightful for those who drink
interpretation: This verse is likely referring to a description of pure, clean water that is delightful and refreshing for those who drink it. The whiteness could symbolize the purity and clarity of the water, while the delightfulness suggests its pleasant taste and ability to quench thirst. This verse could be understood as a metaphor for the spiritual nourishment and delight that can be found in the guidance and teachings of the Qur'an.
orig: بيضاء لذة للشاربين

translation: Neither will they hear therein ill speech nor any sinfulness
interpretation: This verse from the Qur'an describes the nature of Paradise, where the believers will reside. It emphasizes that in Paradise, there will be no harmful or evil speech, nor will the inhabitants experience any exhaustion or depletion of their energy and resources. The verse conveys a sense of peace, tranquility, and the absence of any negative or unpleasant experiences in the Hereafter.
orig: لا فيها غول ولا هم عنها ينزفون

translation: And with them will be women limiting [their] glances, with large, [beautiful] eyes
interpretation: This verse describes the companions of the righteous in the Hereafter. Among them will be chaste and modest women, with beautiful and captivating eyes. This suggests that the pleasures of the Hereafter will include the companionship of virtuous and pure spouses, who will be a source of delight and comfort for the believers.
orig: وعندهم قاصرات الطرف عين

translation: As if they were hidden pearls
interpretation: This verse is describing the beauty and purity of the women in Paradise. The comparison to "hidden pearls" suggests that they are delicate, precious, and protected, like pearls that are hidden away. This conveys the idea that the women in Paradise are of the highest quality and value, and are treated with the utmost care and reverence.
orig: كأنهن بيض مكنون

translation: Then some of them approached others, questioning.
interpretation: This verse describes a scene where people are engaging in dialogue and inquiry with one another. The interpretation is that it encourages open and inquisitive discussion, where individuals are willing to approach each other and ask questions to gain a better understanding. This promotes an atmosphere of learning, exchange of ideas, and collective exploration of issues.
orig: فأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون

translation: One of them will say, "Indeed, I had a companion [in the world]"
interpretation: This verse refers to a situation on the Day of Judgment, where one of the disbelievers will lament the loss of a close companion from the worldly life. The companion could have been a friend, family member, or someone the person was close to. This verse highlights the regret and sorrow the disbeliever will feel on that day, as they realize the true consequences of their actions and the relationships they had in the world.
orig: قال قائل منهم إني كان لي قرين

translation: He says, "Are you indeed of those who believe [in it]?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to a disbeliever who is questioning the faith of the believer. The disbeliever is casting doubt on the sincerity of the believer's faith, implying that the believer's claim to believe may not be genuine. The verse highlights the skepticism and challenge that believers often face from those who reject the message of Islam.
orig: يقول أإنك لمن المصدقين

translation: Is it when we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?
interpretation: This verse expresses the skepticism of some people regarding the concept of resurrection after death. They question whether, after their bodies have decomposed and turned to dust and bones, they will truly be brought back to life and held accountable for their actions. The verse challenges this skepticism and affirms that the resurrection and judgment are inevitable realities that all people will face.
orig: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمدينون

translation: He said: "Are you then aware (of what you are doing)?"
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Ash-Shu'ara (The Poets), verse 217. The speaker is referring to the disbelievers who were challenging the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and questioning his message. The interpretation is that the speaker is asking the disbelievers if they are aware of the consequences of their rejection of the truth and their opposition to the Prophet. It is a rhetorical question meant to make them reflect on their actions and the potential consequences they may face.
orig: قال هل أنتم مطلعون

translation: Then he looked and saw him in the midst of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Abraham and his encounter with the tyrant king Nimrod. After Abraham broke the idols in his people's temple, Nimrod ordered him to be thrown into a great fire. However, by the power of God, the fire did not harm Abraham and he emerged unscathed. This verse describes how Nimrod looked into the fire and saw Abraham sitting calmly, unaffected by the flames. This miracle was a clear sign of God's power and Abraham's close relationship with the Divine.
orig: فاطلع فرآه في سواء الجحيم

translation: He (i.e. the chief) said: 'By Allah, you were about to lead me astray'
interpretation: This verse is from the Quran, Surah Al-A'raf, verse 150. It describes a scene where Prophet Moses returns to his people after receiving the Ten Commandments, only to find them worshipping a golden calf. The chief of the people, in this case, accuses Prophet Moses of almost leading them astray by leaving them for so long. The interpretation is that the chief is acknowledging the power of Prophet Moses' influence over the people, and is trying to shift the blame for their wrongdoing onto him.
orig: قال تالله إن كدت لتردين

translation: And had it not been for the favor of my Lord, I would have been of those brought in [to Hell].
interpretation: This verse expresses the Prophet Muhammad"s (peace be upon him) gratitude to Allah for saving him from the punishment of Hell. It suggests that without Allah"s guidance and blessings, the Prophet would have been among those destined for eternal damnation. The verse emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and being thankful for Allah"s grace and mercy, as it is only through His favor that one can be saved from the consequences of their sins and mistakes.
orig: ولولا نعمة ربي لكنت من المحضرين

translation: Then are we not to die
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, implying that death is inevitable for all human beings. The interpretation is that we are all mortal and will eventually die, and this is a fundamental fact of our existence that we must accept and prepare for.
orig: أفما نحن بميتين

translation: Except our first death, and we shall not be punished
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being addressed will only experience their first death, and will not be subjected to any further punishment or torment. It implies that the afterlife will not involve any additional suffering or retribution, beyond the initial death that all people must face.
orig: إلا موتتنا الأولى وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: Indeed, this is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the great success and triumph that is achieved by those who believe in and follow the teachings of the Qur'an. It suggests that the ultimate goal and reward for the faithful is a grand and magnificent victory, both in this life and the hereafter.
orig: إن هذا لهو الفوز العظيم

translation: For the like of this let the workers work
interpretation: This verse encourages people to work diligently and strive towards achieving their goals. It suggests that the reward or outcome of one's efforts is worthy of the work put in. The verse emphasizes the importance of hard work and perseverance, as the fruits of one's labor will be commensurate with the effort exerted.
orig: لمثل هذا فليعمل العاملون

translation: Is that [Paradise] better as hospitality or the tree of Zaqqum?
interpretation: This verse is comparing the blessings and delights of Paradise with the torment and punishment of Hell, represented by the tree of Zaqqum. The implication is that the blessings of Paradise are far superior to the suffering in Hell. The verse is challenging the disbelievers to consider which state is truly better - the eternal bliss of Paradise or the eternal torment of Hell.
orig: أذلك خير نزلا أم شجرة الزقوم

translation: Indeed, We have made it [i.e., the Qur'an] a trial for the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Qur'an serves as a test or trial for those who are unjust or oppressive. The Qur'an, with its clear guidance and moral teachings, challenges the beliefs and actions of those who choose to act wrongfully. It is a means by which they are held accountable for their choices and deeds. The Qur'an provides a standard by which their behavior can be judged, and it serves as a reminder of the consequences of their transgressions.
orig: إنا جعلناها فتنة للظالمين

translation: Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the bottom of the Hellfire
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Zaqqum tree, which is described in the Quran as a tree that grows in the depths of Hell. It is a symbol of the torment and suffering that the inhabitants of Hell will experience. The interpretation is that the Zaqqum tree represents the ultimate manifestation of the punishment and torment that awaits those who reject faith and engage in sinful behavior.
orig: إنها شجرة تخرج في أصل الجحيم

translation: Its (fruit) stalks are like the heads of devils
interpretation: This verse is describing the appearance of a particular fruit, likely referring to a type of date palm. The description of the fruit stalks being "like the heads of devils" suggests that they have a strange, twisted or unappealing appearance, perhaps resembling the horns or heads of demons. This could be a metaphorical way of highlighting the unusual or intimidating nature of the fruit, even though it may still be edible or useful. The verse invites the reader to consider the diverse creation of God, where even something that may seem unattractive can serve a purpose.
orig: طلعها كأنه رءوس الشياطين

translation: And indeed, they will eat from it and fill their bellies with [it]
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and the Day of Judgment. They will indulge in the pleasures of this worldly life, eating and filling their bellies, without any concern for the Hereafter. This highlights the temporary nature of the worldly life and the importance of preparing for the eternal life in the Hereafter.
orig: فإنهم لآكلون منها فمالئون منها البطون

translation: Then indeed, for them will be a boiling drink
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject faith and do not follow the guidance of the Qur'an will face a severe punishment in the Hereafter. The "boiling drink" is a metaphor for the torment and suffering they will experience as a consequence of their actions in this life. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of believing in and submitting to the teachings of Islam to avoid such a fate.
orig: ثم إن لهم عليها لشوبا من حميم

translation: Then indeed, their [final] return is to the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the ultimate destination for those who reject faith and do not live righteously is the Hellfire. It serves as a warning to humans to be mindful of their actions and choices in this life, as they will be held accountable in the Hereafter.
orig: ثم إن مرجعهم لإلى الجحيم

translation: Indeed, they found their fathers astray.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people had inherited their misguided beliefs and practices from their ancestors, who were themselves misguided. It implies that blindly following tradition without critical examination can lead to perpetuating error. The verse encourages individuals to think for themselves and not simply accept what has been passed down, but to seek the truth through their own reflection and understanding.
orig: إنهم ألفوا آباءهم ضالين

translation: So they are hastening upon the traces
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people are rushing to follow in the footsteps of those who came before them, without much thought or reflection. It implies a sense of haste and a lack of careful consideration, where individuals are simply imitating the actions and behaviors of others without fully understanding the reasons or implications behind them.
orig: فهم على آثارهم يهرعون

translation: And certainly, most of the former peoples had gone astray before them.
interpretation: This verse suggests that many of the previous generations had strayed from the right path and fallen into disbelief or immoral practices before the advent of the Prophet Muhammad. It serves as a warning to the people of the Prophet's time that they should not repeat the mistakes of their predecessors and should instead heed the guidance of the Qur'an and the Prophet.
orig: ولقد ضل قبلهم أكثر الأولين

translation: And We have certainly sent [messengers] among every people a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has sent messengers and warners to all people throughout history, in order to guide them to the right path and warn them against disbelief and disobedience. The purpose of these messengers is to convey the divine message and call people to worship Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him. This is a testament to Allah's justice and mercy, as He does not leave any people without guidance.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا فيهم منذرين

translation: So look how was the end of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse encourages us to reflect on the fate of those who were warned by the Prophets and Messengers, but they rejected the message and persisted in their disbelief and disobedience. The implication is that we should learn from their example and heed the warnings of Allah, lest we suffer a similar end.
orig: فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المنذرين

translation: Except the chosen servants of Allah
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who are sincere and devoted servants of Allah. They are the ones who have purified their hearts and actions, and have dedicated themselves completely to the worship and service of Allah. These are the people who will be saved from the punishment and will be granted eternal bliss in the Hereafter.
orig: إلا عباد الله المخلصين

translation: And Noah had certainly called Us, and [We are] the best of responders.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the prophet Noah called upon Allah, and that Allah is the best of those who respond to the prayers and supplications of His servants. This highlights the importance of turning to Allah in times of need and having faith that He will answer our calls, as He is the Most Merciful and the Most Responsive.
orig: ولقد نادانا نوح فلنعم المجيبون

translation: And We saved him and his family from the great distress.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Lot (Lut) in the Quran. It describes how Allah saved Lot and his family from the great punishment that befell the people of Sodom and Gomorrah due to their immoral and unrighteous behavior. The "great distress" mentioned in the verse refers to the destruction that came upon the people of Lot's community as a result of their rejection of the message of monotheism and their indulgence in sinful acts. The verse highlights Allah's mercy and protection for the believers who follow His guidance, even in the face of widespread corruption and evil.
orig: ونجيناه وأهله من الكرب العظيم

translation: And We made his descendants as those remaining [on the earth]
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has made the descendants of the prophet as those who will remain on the earth and carry on his legacy. It implies that the prophet's lineage will continue and his teachings will be preserved through his followers and future generations.
orig: وجعلنا ذريته هم الباقين

translation: And We left for him [favorable mention] among the later generations.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has left a lasting and positive legacy for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) among future generations. The interpretation is that the Prophet's teachings, example, and impact have endured and continue to be revered by Muslims and others throughout history.
orig: وتركنا عليه في الآخرين

translation: Peace be upon Noah among the worlds.
interpretation: This verse is a salutation and blessing upon the Prophet Noah, who was sent as a messenger to guide his people. The phrase "among the worlds" suggests that Noah's prophethood and message were not limited to his own people, but were intended for all of humanity. The verse highlights the high status and honor accorded to the Prophet Noah, and serves as a reminder to believers to emulate his example of steadfastness, patience, and devotion to the divine message.
orig: سلام على نوح في العالمين

translation: Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah rewards those who do good deeds and act righteously. It is a reassurance that those who strive to please Allah and benefit others will be compensated for their efforts. The interpretation suggests that Allah's justice and mercy extend to those who live virtuously, and that they will be justly rewarded in the afterlife.
orig: إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Indeed, he is of Our believing servants.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a righteous and faithful servant of God. It emphasizes that this individual is among the believers who have truly submitted to God and have demonstrated their faith through their actions and devotion. The verse conveys a sense of divine approval and favor towards this believer, highlighting their piety and closeness to God.
orig: إنه من عبادنا المؤمنين

translation: Then We drowned the others
interpretation: This verse refers to the drowning of Pharaoh and his army after they pursued the Israelites across the Red Sea. It signifies that those who oppose the message of God and oppress the righteous will ultimately face divine punishment and destruction.
orig: ثم أغرقنا الآخرين

translation: And indeed, among his followers was Abraham.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the followers of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It states that among those followers was the Prophet Abraham, one of the most revered figures in Islam. This highlights the continuity of the message of Islam, which can be traced back to the teachings of Abraham. The verse emphasizes the shared heritage and connection between the followers of the Prophet Muhammad and the earlier prophets, such as Abraham, who came with the same essential message of worshiping one God.
orig: وإن من شيعته لإبراهيم

translation: When he came to his Lord with a sound heart.
interpretation: This verse refers to the prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), peace be upon him, who came before his Lord with a pure, sincere, and righteous heart. The "sound heart" (qalbun saleem) represents a heart that is free from any impurities, doubts, or attachments to anything other than Allah. This signifies the importance of having a pure and devoted heart when approaching and worshiping Allah, the Almighty.
orig: إذ جاء ربه بقلب سليم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) questioning his father and people about their worship of idols. It highlights Abraham's rejection of idolatry and his search for the true God. This verse encourages critical thinking and the importance of questioning one's beliefs and practices in order to find the true path of worship.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه وقومه ماذا تعبدون

translation: Do you then desire other gods besides Allah?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the desire to worship other gods besides the one true God, Allah. The implication is that worshipping false gods or idols is a form of deception and misguidance. The verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the belief in the oneness of God, as opposed to polytheism or the worship of multiple deities.
orig: أئفكا آلهة دون الله تريدون

translation: So what do you think about the Lord of the Worlds?
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the nature and attributes of God, the Lord of all creation. It prompts us to ponder deeply about the power, wisdom, and benevolence of the Divine, and to develop a proper understanding and reverence for the Almighty. The verse invites us to contemplate God's sovereignty, His control over the entire universe, and His role as the Sustainer and Provider for all beings. Ultimately, this verse urges us to have the right perception and belief about God, which is crucial for our spiritual growth and relationship with the Creator.
orig: فما ظنكم برب العالمين

translation: Then he looked at the stars
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah As-Saffat, verse 88. It describes the Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) reflecting on the wonders of the universe and the signs of God's existence and power. The verse suggests that by contemplating the stars and the celestial bodies, one can gain a deeper understanding of the divine creation and the greatness of the Creator. This encourages us to ponder over the signs of God's majesty in the natural world around us, as a means of strengthening our faith and connection with the divine.
orig: فنظر نظرة في النجوم

translation: And he said, "Indeed, I am ill."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah As-Saffat, verse 89. The verse describes a scene where the prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) tells his people that he is ill, as a way to avoid participating in their idolatrous practices. The interpretation is that the verse highlights Ibrahim's unwavering faith and commitment to the worship of the one true God, even when faced with social pressure and expectations from his community.
orig: فقال إني سقيم

translation: So they turned away from him, retreating.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the reaction of the disbelievers when the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) called them to believe in the oneness of God. Instead of accepting the message, they turned away and fled from him. This verse highlights the stubborn rejection of the truth by those who are unwilling to submit to God's guidance.
orig: فتولوا عنه مدبرين

translation: Then he turned to their gods and said, "Do you not eat?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) who, upon discovering the futility of worshipping idols, confronted the people and questioned why they worshipped gods that could not even eat or benefit them in any way. The verse highlights the absurdity of idolatry and calls upon the people to reflect on the true nature of their deities and to turn to the One true God who is worthy of worship.
orig: فراغ إلى آلهتهم فقال ألا تأكلون

translation: What is [the matter] with you that you do not speak?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, implying that the people being addressed are not speaking up or expressing themselves. The verse suggests that they should be more vocal and engaged, rather than remaining silent. The interpretation is that the verse is encouraging people to speak up, voice their opinions, and participate actively in discussions and decision-making.
orig: ما لكم لا تنطقون

translation: Then strike them over the necks with your right hand.
interpretation: This verse is often interpreted as a command to the Prophet Muhammad to strike his enemies with force and decisiveness. The "right hand" is a symbol of power and authority, suggesting that the believers should act with strength and determination in defending their faith. The verse is seen as a call to confront those who oppose Islam, but some scholars also emphasize that this should be done with justice and restraint, and only as a last resort when peaceful means have been exhausted.
orig: فراغ عليهم ضربا باليمين

translation: And they came to him hastening.
interpretation: This verse describes people rushing towards a person, likely a prophet or messenger of God, with eagerness and haste. The interpretation suggests that the people were eager to receive guidance, knowledge, or teachings from this individual, and they approached him with a sense of urgency and excitement.
orig: فأقبلوا إليه يزفون

translation: He said, "Do you worship what you [yourselves] carve?"
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between the prophet Abraham and his people who were idolaters. Abraham is questioning the logic and rationality of worshiping idols that they themselves have carved or sculpted, as these are merely human-made objects without any divine power or agency. The implication is that the true God is the one who created the universe and all that is in it, not the lifeless statues that people have fashioned with their own hands. The verse encourages critical thinking and challenges the blind adherence to traditional practices that lack sound reasoning.
orig: قال أتعبدون ما تنحتون

translation: And Allah has created you and that which you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the Creator of all things, including human beings and their actions. It serves as a reminder that our existence and everything we do is ultimately under Allah's control and sovereignty. This should instill in us a sense of humility, gratitude, and accountability before our Creator.
orig: والله خلقكم وما تعملون

translation: They said, "Build for him a structure and throw him into the Blaze."
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) and his confrontation with the disbelievers who worshipped idols. The disbelievers wanted to punish Abraham for his rejection of their false deities, so they decided to build a structure or pyre to throw him into the fire (the Blaze). This verse highlights the intolerance and cruelty of the disbelievers towards those who challenge their beliefs and call them to the worship of the One True God.
orig: قالوا ابنوا له بنيانا فألقوه في الجحيم

translation: And they planned a plan, but We made them the lowest of the low
interpretation: This verse refers to the attempts of the disbelievers to plot against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers. However, God foiled their schemes and made them the most humiliated and defeated. The interpretation suggests that those who try to undermine the truth and the righteous will ultimately be brought low, as God's plan prevails over all human machinations.
orig: فأرادوا به كيدا فجعلناهم الأسفلين

translation: And he said, "Indeed, I will go to [the place of] my Lord; He will guide me."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah As-Saaffaat, verse 99. It is spoken by the Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) as he is preparing to sacrifice his son, as commanded by Allah. The verse expresses Ibrahim's trust and faith in Allah, that He will guide him and show him the right path, even in this difficult situation. It highlights the unwavering belief of the Prophets in Allah's wisdom and plan, and their willingness to submit to His commands.
orig: وقال إني ذاهب إلى ربي سيهدين

translation: My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication from the Prophet Abraham, asking God to grant him a righteous child. It reflects the deep desire of a faithful servant to have offspring who will continue his legacy of righteousness and devotion to God. The interpretation suggests that the Prophet Abraham is seeking a child who will be a source of blessing and a means of perpetuating his noble lineage and spiritual inheritance.
orig: رب هب لي من الصالحين

translation: So We gave him the good news of a forbearing son.
interpretation: This verse refers to the birth of Prophet Ishmael, the son of Prophet Abraham. The Qur'an describes Ishmael as a "forbearing" son, indicating his patience, self-control, and wisdom. This highlights the noble character and virtues that were bestowed upon him by God. The verse conveys the good news of this blessed child, who would go on to become a prophet and a righteous leader.
orig: فبشرناه بغلام حليم

translation: And when he (Isma'il) reached (the age of) working with him, he (Ibrahim) said: "O my son! I have seen in a dream that I am slaughtering you (offer you in sacrifice to Allah), so look what you think!" He (Isma'il) said: "O my father! Do that which you are commanded (i.e. slaughter me), and you will find me of the patient ones, if Allah wills."
interpretation: This verse describes the account of Prophet Ibrahim being commanded by Allah to sacrifice his son Isma'il. The interpretation is that this was a test of Ibrahim's faith and obedience to Allah. Isma'il's response shows his own submission and willingness to be sacrificed, demonstrating the faith and patience of both father and son. This event is seen as a pivotal moment in the lives of these Prophets, and a lesson in complete devotion and trust in Allah's commands, even when they may seem difficult to comprehend.
orig: فلما بلغ معه السعي قال يا بني إني أرى في المنام أني أذبحك فانظر ماذا ترى قال يا أبت افعل ما تؤمر ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصابرين

translation: And when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when Prophet Abraham was about to sacrifice his son, as commanded by God. When both Abraham and his son had submitted to God's will, Abraham laid his son down on his forehead, ready to carry out the sacrifice. This represents the ultimate test of faith, where Abraham was willing to give up his most precious possession - his son - in obedience to God's command. The verse highlights the importance of complete submission and trust in God, even in the face of the most difficult trials.
orig: فلما أسلما وتله للجبين

translation: And We called to him: "O Abraham!"
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment when God called out to the prophet Abraham, summoning him and addressing him directly. This represents a profound spiritual experience where God communicated with Abraham, establishing a close and personal relationship. The interpretation is that God reaches out to His righteous servants, engaging with them in a direct and intimate manner to guide them and entrust them with important missions.
orig: وناديناه أن يا إبراهيم

translation: Certainly have We fulfilled the vision. Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fulfillment of a vision or dream that was seen by one of the Prophets, likely Prophet Abraham. It indicates that God has brought to fruition what was shown in the vision, as a reward for the righteous deeds of the one who had the vision. The verse emphasizes that God rewards those who do good and live righteously.
orig: قد صدقت الرؤيا إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Indeed, this is the clear trial
interpretation: This verse refers to the difficulties and tribulations that believers may face in their lives. It suggests that these trials are a clear sign or manifestation of God's test of faith. The interpretation is that the believer should remain steadfast and patient in the face of such challenges, as they are a means by which God distinguishes the sincere from the insincere, and strengthens the faith of the true believers.
orig: إن هذا لهو البلاء المبين

translation: And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Abraham and his son, where Abraham was commanded by God to sacrifice his son. However, God intervened and provided a ram as a substitute, which was a great sacrifice. This event symbolizes the willingness to sacrifice one's most precious possessions for the sake of God and the ultimate trust in His divine plan.
orig: وفديناه بذبح عظيم

translation: And We left for him [i.e., Jesus] among the later people [this]
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah left a lasting legacy and influence of Prophet Jesus among the later generations of people. The interpretation implies that the teachings and impact of Jesus continued to resonate and shape the lives of people long after his time on Earth.
orig: وتركنا عليه في الآخرين

translation: Peace be upon Abraham
interpretation: This verse is a statement of blessing and reverence for the Prophet Abraham, a revered figure in Islam. It conveys the idea that peace, blessings, and honor are upon him as one of the great prophets of God. The verse emphasizes the high status of Abraham and the importance of remembering and honoring him as a spiritual leader and role model for Muslims.
orig: سلام على إبراهيم

translation: Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah rewards those who do good deeds and act righteously. It suggests that those who strive to be virtuous and perform acts of kindness and charity will be recompensed by Allah. The interpretation conveys the idea that the Almighty recognizes and appreciates the efforts of the righteous, and will provide them with suitable recompense in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Indeed, he was of Our believing servants.
interpretation: This verse refers to a righteous and faithful servant of Allah. It suggests that the person being described was a true believer who dedicated themselves to the worship and service of Allah. The verse conveys a sense of approval and praise for this individual, highlighting their piety and devotion.
orig: إنه من عبادنا المؤمنين

translation: And We gave him the good news of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse refers to the birth of Isaac, the son of the prophet Abraham. It is a message of glad tidings, informing Abraham that he will be blessed with a righteous son who will become a prophet. This highlights the importance of the lineage of prophets and the continuity of divine guidance through successive generations of righteous individuals.
orig: وبشرناه بإسحاق نبيا من الصالحين

translation: And We blessed him and Isaac. And among their descendants are doers of good and those who are clearly unjust to themselves.
interpretation: This verse refers to the blessings bestowed upon Prophet Abraham and his son Isaac, and their descendants. It highlights that among their offspring, there will be those who do good deeds and those who are clearly unjust to themselves. This suggests that the outcome of one's actions, whether good or bad, is a matter of individual choice and responsibility, and that the blessings of the Almighty extend to all, but the ultimate consequences are determined by one's own conduct.
orig: وباركنا عليه وعلى إسحاق ومن ذريتهما محسن وظالم لنفسه مبين

translation: And We had certainly conferred favor upon Moses and Aaron
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the blessings and favors that Allah bestowed upon the Prophets Moses and Aaron. It is a reminder that Allah chooses His messengers and grants them special status and divine guidance to lead their people. The verse emphasizes the importance of acknowledging and being grateful for the blessings that Allah bestows upon His chosen servants.
orig: ولقد مننا على موسى وهارون

translation: And We saved them and their people from the great distress.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Lut (Lot) and his people. It describes how Allah saved Lut and his followers from the great punishment that befell the people of Sodom and Gomorrah due to their immoral and wicked ways. The "great distress" mentioned in the verse likely refers to the destruction that came upon the cities in the form of a devastating storm or natural disaster. This verse highlights Allah's mercy in saving the righteous believers from the consequences of the sins of their people.
orig: ونجيناهما وقومهما من الكرب العظيم

translation: And We supported them, and so they became the predominant.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the believers who were supported by Allah and emerged victorious over their opponents. It suggests that when one has faith and trust in Allah, they will be granted success and triumph, even if they are initially weak or outnumbered. The interpretation is that through divine assistance, the believers were able to overcome their adversaries and establish their dominance.
orig: ونصرناهم فكانوا هم الغالبين

translation: And We had given them the clear Book
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine scriptures that were revealed to the prophets, such as the Torah given to Moses and the Gospel given to Jesus. These scriptures were clear and unambiguous in their guidance, serving as a source of enlightenment and direction for the people.
orig: وآتيناهما الكتاب المستبين

translation: And We guided them to the straight path.
interpretation: This verse indicates that God has guided the believers to the right and righteous path, the path of truth and virtue. The "straight path" refers to the path of guidance and salvation, as opposed to the path of error and misguidance. This guidance comes from God, and it is a blessing that He bestows upon those who seek to follow His commands and live according to His teachings.
orig: وهديناهما الصراط المستقيم

translation: And We left for them (a remembrance) among the later people
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has left a lasting legacy or remembrance of the previous nations and their fates for the later generations to learn from. It implies that the stories and lessons of the past serve as guidance and reminders for those who come after, so that they may avoid the same mistakes and be inspired to live righteously.
orig: وتركنا عليهما في الآخرين
