translation: Peace be upon Moses and Aaron
interpretation: This verse expresses a greeting and blessing upon the two prophets, Moses and Aaron, who were sent by God to guide the Israelites. It signifies the high status and reverence that these two prophets hold in the Islamic tradition. The verse emphasizes the importance of honoring and respecting the messengers of God, who were instrumental in delivering divine guidance to humanity.
orig: سلام على موسى وهارون

translation: Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah rewards those who do good deeds and act righteously. It suggests that just as Allah has rewarded the previous righteous individuals, He will also reward those who follow in their footsteps and strive to be virtuous and benevolent. This verse encourages believers to perform good actions and seek Allah's pleasure, as they will be duly recognized and compensated for their efforts.
orig: إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Indeed, they were of Our believing servants.
interpretation: This verse is referring to two individuals who were righteous and faithful servants of Allah. The verse emphasizes that they were among the believers, indicating that they had accepted the message of Islam and lived their lives in accordance with the teachings of the Qur'an and the example of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse highlights the importance of faith and righteous conduct, and serves as an encouragement for believers to strive to be among the faithful servants of Allah.
orig: إنهما من عبادنا المؤمنين

translation: And indeed, Elias was among the messengers.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the prophet Elias (Elijah) was one of the messengers sent by God to guide humanity. It highlights the status of Elias as a divinely appointed messenger, emphasizing the importance of his role and message in the context of the Quranic narrative of the prophets.
orig: وإن إلياس لمن المرسلين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when he said to his people, "Will you not fear [Allah]?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the prophet Shu'ayb, who called his people to worship Allah and abandon their corrupt practices. He reminded them of the need to fear and revere Allah, in order to avoid His punishment and earn His pleasure. The verse emphasizes the importance of being God-conscious and righteous in one's conduct.
orig: إذ قال لقومه ألا تتقون

translation: Do you call upon Ba'al and forsake the Best of creators?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the polytheistic beliefs of the people, who were worshipping the false god Ba'al and neglecting the one true God, the Best of creators. The verse is criticizing this practice and calling upon the people to abandon their worship of Ba'al and instead turn to the one true God, who is the Best of creators.
orig: أتدعون بعلا وتذرون أحسن الخالقين

translation: Allah is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah is the one and only true Lord, not only for the people being addressed, but for all of their ancestors as well. It establishes Allah's sovereignty and divinity, and calls upon the people to worship and submit to Him alone, as He is the Lord of all creation, past and present.
orig: الله ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين

translation: But they denied him, so they will be presented [for punishment]
interpretation: This verse refers to the rejection of the prophets by their people. It indicates that those who deny the truth and reject the messengers of God will ultimately be brought forth for judgment and held accountable for their actions. The interpretation suggests that denial of the divine message has consequences, and that the disbelievers will face the consequences of their rejection on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: فكذبوه فإنهم لمحضرون

translation: Except the sincere servants of Allah
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the sincere and devoted servants of Allah are the only ones who will be spared from the punishment and torment that will befall the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. The "sincere servants" refers to those who worship Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him, and who strive to live their lives in accordance with the teachings of Islam.
orig: إلا عباد الله المخلصين

translation: And We left for him [favorable mention] among the later generations.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the righteous deeds and legacy of a person will be remembered and honored by future generations. It implies that those who live a virtuous life and leave a positive impact on the world will be remembered and respected long after they are gone. The verse highlights the importance of living a life that is worthy of being remembered and that can inspire and guide others even after one's passing.
orig: وتركنا عليه في الآخرين

translation: Peace be upon the family of Yasin
interpretation: This verse is a greeting of peace and blessings upon the family of the Prophet Yasin, which is believed to be a reference to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It expresses the importance of honoring and respecting the family of the Prophet, who were instrumental in the spread of Islam and the guidance they provided to the faithful.
orig: سلام على إل ياسين

translation: Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah rewards those who do good deeds and act righteously. It suggests that just as Allah has rewarded the previous righteous individuals, He will also reward those who strive to do good in the present time. The interpretation conveys the message that good deeds are recognized and appreciated by Allah, and that those who engage in such acts will be duly compensated.
orig: إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Indeed, he was of Our believing servants.
interpretation: This verse refers to a believer who was devoted to Allah and lived a righteous life. The verse emphasizes that this person was among the faithful servants of Allah, who had accepted the message of Islam and submitted to the will of the Almighty. The interpretation suggests that such believers are highly regarded and cherished by Allah, and that their devotion and faith are a source of pride and honor.
orig: إنه من عبادنا المؤمنين

translation: And indeed, [Lot] was of the messengers.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the prophet Lot was one of the messengers of God, sent to guide his people. It highlights Lot’s status as a divinely appointed messenger, entrusted with conveying God’s message and calling people to righteousness. The verse serves to validate Lot’s prophethood and the divine origin of his teachings.
orig: وإن لوطا لمن المرسلين

translation: When We saved him and all his family
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Nuh (Noah) and the great flood. Allah saved Nuh and his family from the flood, while the rest of the people were destroyed for their disbelief and rejection of Nuh's message. This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and power, as He protected the believers and destroyed the disbelievers.
orig: إذ نجيناه وأهله أجمعين

translation: Except an old woman among those who remained behind
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the destruction of the people of Lut (Lot). It indicates that only an old woman, who was the wife of Lut, was left behind and did not perish with the rest of the disbelieving people. This serves as a lesson that those who reject the message of the prophets and persist in their disbelief will face severe consequences, while those who believe and submit to Allah will be saved.
orig: إلا عجوزا في الغابرين

translation: Then We destroyed the others
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah's (God's) destruction of those who rejected the message of the Prophets and persisted in their disbelief and wrongdoing. It suggests that after giving people multiple chances to repent and believe, Allah ultimately destroys those who stubbornly refuse to accept the truth and continue on a path of corruption and oppression. The interpretation highlights Allah's justice in punishing those who persistently reject His guidance and warnings.
orig: ثم دمرنا الآخرين

translation: And indeed, you pass by them in the morning
interpretation: This verse is referring to the ruins of the settlements of the ancient people of 'Aad, who were destroyed for their arrogance and rejection of God's message. The verse suggests that the people of Prophet Muhammad's time would pass by these ruins in the morning, serving as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and disobedience to God.
orig: وإنكم لتمرون عليهم مصبحين

translation: And by the night when it departs,
interpretation: This verse encourages us to reflect and ponder upon the wonders of the night, and to use our intellect to understand the signs of Allah's creation. The night, with its tranquility and darkness, is a reminder of the temporary nature of this world and the need to prepare for the Hereafter.
orig: وبالليل أفلا تعقلون

translation: And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the prophet Jonah (Yunus in Arabic) was one of the messengers sent by Allah. It emphasizes the status of Jonah as a prophet and a messenger who was entrusted with conveying Allah's message to the people. This verse serves to validate Jonah's prophethood and his role in the divine plan of guidance and salvation.
orig: وإن يونس لمن المرسلين

translation: When he ran away to the laden ship.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the prophet Jonah (Yunus in Arabic), who fled from his people and boarded a ship. The verse describes the moment when Jonah, having disobeyed God's command to preach to his people, decided to escape on a ship that was heavily laden with passengers and cargo. This act of fleeing from his divine duty led to the subsequent events, where Jonah was swallowed by a whale and eventually returned to fulfill his mission. The verse highlights Jonah's initial reluctance and the consequences of his actions, serving as a lesson about the importance of obedience to God's will.
orig: إذ أبق إلى الفلك المشحون

translation: So he drew lots with them, and he was of the disappointed.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Jonah (Yunus) in the Quran. When Jonah left his people without God's permission, a storm arose at sea. The sailors cast lots to determine who was responsible for the storm, and the lot fell on Jonah. This verse indicates that Jonah was among those who lost or were disappointed, as he had disobeyed God's command by leaving his people before being granted permission.
orig: فساهم فكان من المدحضين

translation: And the fish swallowed him, while he was blaming himself.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the prophet Jonah (Yunus in Arabic), who was swallowed by a large fish (or whale) after disobeying God's command. The verse suggests that Jonah realized his mistake and took responsibility for his actions, even as he was being punished. This reflects the idea that true repentance and accountability are important in the eyes of God.
orig: فالتقمه الحوت وهو مليم

translation: And if it were not that he was of those who exalt [Allah]
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the prophet Jonah, who was swallowed by a whale. The verse suggests that if Jonah had not been among those who glorify and exalt Allah, he would not have been saved from the whale's belly. The interpretation is that those who remember and praise Allah are more likely to be protected and saved from difficult situations.
orig: فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين

translation: For him to remain in its belly until the Day they are resurrected
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Jonah (Yunus) who was swallowed by a whale. The verse indicates that Jonah remained in the belly of the whale until the Day of Resurrection, when all people will be brought back to life. This is a metaphorical expression to emphasize the miraculous nature of Jonah's survival and his eventual return to his people, as a sign of God's power and the certainty of the Resurrection.
orig: للبث في بطنه إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: And We cast him into the wilderness, and he was [as if] cast aside.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the prophet Jonah, who was swallowed by a whale after abandoning his people. The verse describes how Jonah was cast out into the wilderness in a weakened and vulnerable state, after being expelled from the whale. This represents a period of trial and purification for Jonah, as he faced the consequences of his actions and was forced to confront his own shortcomings.
orig: فنبذناه بالعراء وهو سقيم

translation: And We caused to grow over him a gourd vine.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of the prophet Jonah, who was swallowed by a whale. After being freed from the whale, God caused a gourd vine to grow over Jonah to provide him shade and comfort. This can be interpreted as a sign of God's mercy and care for His servants, even in times of great trial and tribulation.
orig: وأنبتنا عليه شجرة من يقطين

translation: And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Shu`ayb, who was sent by Allah to a large community of people, numbering a hundred thousand or more. The verse highlights the vastness of the community that the Prophet Shu`ayb was tasked with guiding and preaching to. It emphasizes the importance of the message and the scale of the responsibility entrusted to the Prophet Shu`ayb, as he was sent to a large and populous community. The verse underscores the expansive reach of the divine message and the Prophet's mission to convey it to a significant number of people.
orig: وأرسلناه إلى مائة ألف أو يزيدون

translation: So believe, for We will give you enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to have faith in God, as they will be granted the blessings and pleasures of this life for a period of time. It suggests that those who believe will be rewarded, even if only temporarily in this world, before facing the ultimate judgment in the Hereafter.
orig: فآمنوا فمتعناهم إلى حين

translation: So ask them [O Muhammad], "Is it for your Lord the daughters and for them the sons?"
interpretation: This verse is questioning the polytheistic Arabs who believed that angels were the daughters of God, while they preferred to have sons for themselves. The verse challenges this belief, implying that such a notion of God having daughters is illogical and inconsistent with the concept of a perfect, all-powerful deity. The interpretation suggests that the Quranic message rejects the idea of God having any offspring, as this would contradict the fundamental Islamic belief in the absolute oneness and transcendence of God.
orig: فاستفتهم ألربك البنات ولهم البنون

translation: Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the belief that angels are female. The implication is that such a belief is absurd, as the angels were present as witnesses to their own creation. The verse challenges the notion that the angels could have been created as females, as that would be contrary to the rational and logical nature of their existence as divine messengers and servants of God.
orig: أم خلقنا الملائكة إناثا وهم شاهدون

translation: Unquestionably, they are the ones who lie about Allah.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who spread false rumors and fabrications about Allah and His commands. It emphasizes that they are the ones who are engaged in deceit and falsehood, and their claims are baseless. The verse serves as a warning against those who try to misguide people by making up lies and attributing them to Allah.
orig: ألا إنهم من إفكهم ليقولون

translation: And they say, "Allah has taken a son," and they are liars.
interpretation: This verse refutes the belief that Allah has a son. It emphasizes that the claim of Allah having a son is a falsehood, and those who make such a claim are being deceptive. The Qur'an strongly rejects the notion of Allah having any offspring, as it is considered a blasphemous and polytheistic belief that contradicts the fundamental Islamic teaching of the absolute oneness and transcendence of Allah.
orig: ولد الله وإنهم لكاذبون

translation: He has chosen daughters over sons
interpretation: This verse is often interpreted as a criticism of the pre-Islamic Arab practice of preferring sons over daughters. The verse suggests that God has chosen daughters over sons, challenging the prevailing cultural bias against female children. The interpretation emphasizes that all human beings, regardless of gender, are equal in the sight of God and should be treated with equal dignity and respect.
orig: أصطفى البنات على البنين

translation: What is [the matter] with you? How do you judge?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the people's judgment and decision-making process. It suggests that the way they are making judgments or decisions is flawed or misguided. The verse encourages the people to re-examine their thought processes and the basis for their judgments, as they may not be in line with the principles of justice and righteousness.
orig: ما لكم كيف تحكمون

translation: Then will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that encourages people to reflect and remember the signs of Allah's power and wisdom in the universe. It is a call to use one's intellect and not be heedless of the clear evidence of God's existence and His guidance. The verse implies that if people would only pause and ponder, they would remember and be guided to the truth.
orig: أفلا تذكرون

translation: Or do you have a clear authority?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, challenging the notion that those who disbelieve in God have any clear authority or justification for their beliefs and actions. The implication is that they do not have any such clear authority, and that their beliefs and actions are baseless. The verse is emphasizing the importance of having a clear, divinely-revealed basis for one's beliefs and actions, rather than relying on personal whims or the traditions of one's ancestors.
orig: أم لكم سلطان مبين

translation: Then bring your scripture if you should be truthful.
interpretation: This verse is a challenge to those who dispute the truth of the Qur"an and the message of Islam. It calls on them to produce their own scripture or evidence that can match the Qur"an in its eloquence, wisdom and guidance. The implication is that they will not be able to do so, as the Qur"an is the word of God and cannot be replicated by human beings. This verse emphasizes the divine origin and authenticity of the Qur"an.
orig: فأتوا بكتابكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And they have made a relationship between Him and the jinn, but the jinn know that they will be brought [before Him].
interpretation: This verse refers to the false belief held by some people that there is a relationship or kinship between God and the jinn (supernatural beings). The verse clarifies that the jinn themselves know that they will be held accountable before God on the Day of Judgment, rejecting the notion of any special relationship with the Divine. The interpretation emphasizes that God is the sole Creator and Sovereign, and that all creation, including the jinn, will be brought before Him for judgment.
orig: وجعلوا بينه وبين الجنة نسبا ولقد علمت الجنة إنهم لمحضرون

translation: Exalted is Allah above what they describe [concerning Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute perfection and transcendence of Allah. It refutes any attempts to anthropomorphize or ascribe human attributes to the Divine. The verse reminds us that Allah is far above and beyond any limited human conceptions or descriptions. It calls us to glorify and exalt Allah, and to avoid making comparisons between the Creator and the created.
orig: سبحان الله عما يصفون

translation: Except the sincere servants of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the sincere and devoted servants of Allah are the only ones who will be spared from the punishment and torment that will befall the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. The "sincere servants" are those who worship Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him, and who strive to please Him through their actions and deeds. They are the ones who have purified their faith and devotion, and will be rewarded with eternal bliss in the Hereafter.
orig: إلا عباد الله المخلصين

translation: And indeed, you and what you worship other than Allah are but [subjects of] trial for Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the worship of anything other than Allah is merely a trial or test from Allah. It suggests that the true focus should be on worshipping and submitting to Allah alone, as all other forms of worship are ultimately futile and will be judged by Allah.
orig: فإنكم وما تعبدون

translation: You are not upon them with [a power of] control.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not a coercive force over people, compelling them to believe. Rather, his role is to convey the message of Islam, and people have the freedom to accept or reject it. The verse emphasizes that faith is a matter of individual choice, not something that can be forced upon others.
orig: ما أنتم عليه بفاتنين

translation: Except he who is to burn in the Blaze
interpretation: This verse refers to those who will be condemned to the Hellfire, the eternal punishment for those who reject faith and commit grave sins. The phrase "he who is to burn in the Blaze" signifies that only those who have earned the wrath of God through their disbelief and misdeeds will face this severe consequence in the Hereafter.
orig: إلا من هو صال الجحيم

translation: And there is none of us (angels) but has his known place (or position)
interpretation: This verse suggests that every created being, including angels, has a specific role and position assigned by God. It emphasizes the order and hierarchy in the divine creation, where each entity has a known and defined purpose. This highlights the idea that God has a plan and design for all of His creation, and that nothing is left to chance or without purpose.
orig: وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم

translation: And indeed, We are the ones who stand in rows [for prayer].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of standing in rows for prayer, which is a fundamental practice in Islam. It suggests that the believers are united in their worship, standing together as a community before God. The interpretation is that this collective act of prayer demonstrates the unity and discipline of the believers, and their willingness to submit to the will of God.
orig: وإنا لنحن الصافون

translation: And indeed, it is we who exalt [Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is the believers who glorify and praise Allah. It is a statement of the Muslims' devotion and commitment to worshiping and honoring the Almighty. The verse conveys the idea that the believers are the ones who engage in acts of remembrance, glorification, and exaltation of Allah, as this is a fundamental part of their faith and relationship with the Divine.
orig: وإنا لنحن المسبحون

translation: And indeed, they do say
interpretation: This verse suggests that people often make claims or statements, which may or may not be true. The verse implies that it is important to carefully examine the validity and truthfulness of what people say, rather than accepting it at face value.
orig: وإن كانوا ليقولون

translation: If only we had a reminder from the former peoples
interpretation: This verse expresses a desire for guidance and wisdom from previous generations. It suggests a longing for the knowledge and experience of those who came before, as if that could provide a solution or insight to the current challenges faced. The verse implies a recognition that the past can offer valuable lessons and perspectives that could benefit the present, if only we had access to that "reminder" or guidance from earlier peoples.
orig: لو أن عندنا ذكرا من الأولين

translation: But we are the sincere servants of Allah
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the true believers are the devoted and sincere servants of Allah, who have dedicated themselves completely to worshiping and obeying Him. It suggests that the believers should not be swayed by the disbelievers' claims or temptations, but remain steadfast in their faith and in their service to the Almighty.
orig: لكنا عباد الله المخلصين

translation: But they disbelieved in it, and soon they will know.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who reject the message of the Quran and the teachings of Islam. Despite the clear signs and evidence presented, they choose to disbelieve. The verse suggests that their rejection will eventually lead to their own demise, and they will come to realize the consequences of their actions. The interpretation emphasizes that those who turn away from the truth will ultimately face the consequences of their choices.
orig: فكفروا به فسوف يعلمون

translation: And the word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has already decreed and predetermined the fate of His messengers, and that their mission and success is assured. It suggests that the word of Allah is immutable and that His plan for the guidance of humanity through His messengers will come to fruition, regardless of any obstacles or opposition they may face.
orig: ولقد سبقت كلمتنا لعبادنا المرسلين

translation: Indeed, they are the ones who will be victorious.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who believe in God and follow His teachings will ultimately be successful and triumphant. It suggests that the faithful will be granted divine support and protection, allowing them to overcome their challenges and achieve their goals. The verse emphasizes the certainty of this outcome, conveying a message of hope and encouragement to the believers.
orig: إنهم لهم المنصورون

translation: And indeed, Our soldiers [i.e., the believers] - they will be the predominant.
interpretation: This verse conveys a message of reassurance and victory for the believers. It suggests that those who are on the side of Allah (God) and follow His guidance will ultimately prevail, even if they may face challenges or opposition. The interpretation is that the believers, who are considered Allah's soldiers or supporters, will be the victorious ones in the end. This verse instills a sense of confidence and hope in the faithful, assuring them that their cause is just and that they will emerge triumphant.
orig: وإن جندنا لهم الغالبون

translation: So turn away from them for a time
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to turn away from those who are rejecting the message of Islam and give them time, as their hearts and minds may not be ready to accept the truth. The interpretation is that one should be patient and allow people the opportunity to reflect on the message, rather than force it upon them.
orig: فتول عنهم حتى حين

translation: And they will see you, [O Muhammad], and they will not recognize you. And they will say, "Is this the one whom Allah had sent as a messenger?"
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers will eventually see the truth of the Prophet Muhammad's message, but they will not recognize him as the messenger of God. They will be surprised and question whether he is truly the one sent by Allah as a prophet. This indicates that the truth will become apparent to them, but their own biases and preconceptions will prevent them from accepting it.
orig: وأبصرهم فسوف يبصرون

translation: Then do they seek to hasten Our punishment?
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people are impatient and eager for the punishment or consequences of their misdeeds, rather than seeking forgiveness and repentance. The interpretation is that one should not rush towards punishment, but rather focus on improving one"s actions and seeking Allah"s mercy.
orig: أفبعذابنا يستعجلون

translation: And when it descends upon their territory, then evil is the morning of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment or calamity that befalls those who have been warned but have ignored the warnings. When the punishment arrives, it is a terrible morning for those who were warned but did not heed the warnings. The verse emphasizes the consequences of disregarding the warnings and the importance of heeding the guidance provided.
orig: فإذا نزل بساحتهم فساء صباح المنذرين

translation: And turn away from them for a time.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to turn away from the disbelievers and ignore them for a period of time. This could mean to avoid engaging with them in debate or confrontation, and instead focus on those who are receptive to the message of Islam. The interpretation suggests that sometimes it is best to disengage from those who are resistant to the truth, and wait for a more opportune time to continue the dialogue.
orig: وتول عنهم حتى حين

translation: And see, for they are going to see.
interpretation: This verse is a call to reflect and contemplate. It suggests that those who are blind to the truth will eventually come to see it, either in this life or the next. The repetition of the word "see" emphasizes the importance of vision, both physical and spiritual. The verse encourages people to open their eyes and minds to the signs of God's existence and the wisdom of His creation.
orig: وأبصر فسوف يبصرون

translation: Exalted is your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme majesty and power of God, the Lord of all creation. It conveys the idea that God is far above and beyond any human attempts to define or describe Him. The phrase "the Lord of Might" underscores God's absolute sovereignty and authority, which is beyond the comprehension of His creation. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to worship God with humility and reverence, acknowledging His transcendence and the limitations of human understanding.
orig: سبحان ربك رب العزة عما يصفون

translation: And peace be upon the Messengers.
interpretation: This verse expresses a greeting and salutation upon all the Prophets and Messengers of God, who were sent to guide humanity towards the path of righteousness and truth. It signifies the high status and reverence that the Messengers of God deserve, and the importance of recognizing and honoring their role in conveying the divine message to mankind.
orig: وسلام على المرسلين

translation: And all praise is [due] to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse expresses gratitude and praise to Allah, the Lord and Sustainer of all creation. It acknowledges that all praise, honor, and glory belong to Allah alone, as He is the Sovereign of the entire universe. This verse reminds us to be thankful to Allah for His blessings, guidance, and mercy, and to worship Him alone without associating partners with Him.
orig: والحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Ṣād. By the Qur'an, full of reminding
interpretation: This verse is calling attention to the Qur'an, which is described as "full of reminding." The letter Ṣād at the beginning is one of the isolated letters that appear at the start of certain Quranic chapters, the meaning of which is not entirely clear. However, the overall message is that the Qur'an is a source of important reminders and guidance for humanity.
orig: ص والقرآن ذي الذكر

translation: But those who disbelieve are in pride and dissension.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who reject faith and deny the truth of Islam are arrogant and in a state of constant conflict and opposition. They are prideful and unwilling to submit to the guidance of Allah, instead choosing to remain in a state of defiance and discord.
orig: بل الذين كفروا في عزة وشقاق

translation: And how many generations have We destroyed before them? And they [i.e., the people of the past] called out, but there was no escape.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the fate of previous nations and civilizations that were destroyed by Allah due to their disbelief, disobedience, and rejection of the divine message. When the punishment of Allah came upon them, they cried out for help, but there was no escape or way to avoid the consequences of their actions. This serves as a warning to the people of the present time to heed the lessons of history and submit to the will of Allah, lest they suffer a similar fate.
orig: كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من قرن فنادوا ولات حين مناص

translation: And they wondered that there has come to them a warner from among themselves. And the disbelievers said, "This is a magician and a liar."
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of the disbelievers to the coming of a warner from among themselves. They were surprised and skeptical, dismissing the warner as a magician and a liar. This reflects the tendency of some people to reject the truth and resort to personal attacks and accusations when faced with a message that challenges their beliefs and worldviews. The verse suggests that the disbelievers were more concerned with discrediting the messenger than engaging with the message itself.
orig: وعجبوا أن جاءهم منذر منهم وقال الكافرون هذا ساحر كذاب

translation: Do you make [all] the deities one God? Indeed, this is a curious thing.
interpretation: This verse expresses surprise and incredulity at the idea of worshiping multiple gods, when there is clearly only One true God worthy of worship. It is a rhetorical question that challenges the notion of polytheism, and affirms the fundamental Islamic belief in the Oneness and Uniqueness of God (Tawheed).
orig: أجعل الآلهة إلها واحدا إن هذا لشيء عجاب

translation: And the eminent among them went forth, saying, "Go and be patient over your gods. Indeed, this is a thing intended."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the elite and influential people in a society when their religious beliefs are challenged. They urge their followers to remain steadfast in their worship of their deities, as they perceive this challenge as a deliberate attempt to undermine their faith. The interpretation suggests that the powerful often try to maintain the status quo and resist change, even in the face of new ideas or perspectives that may challenge their long-held beliefs.
orig: وانطلق الملأ منهم أن امشوا واصبروا على آلهتكم إن هذا لشيء يراد

translation: We have not heard of this in the last religion. This is not but an invention.
interpretation: This verse is expressing skepticism about a new religious claim or teaching that the people have not encountered before. The implication is that this new idea is not part of the established religious tradition and is merely an invention or fabrication, rather than something authentically revealed or transmitted. The verse suggests a reluctance to accept novel religious concepts without grounding them in the recognized teachings of the past.
orig: ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة إن هذا إلا اختلاق

translation: Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us? Nay, but they are in doubt about My Reminder. Nay, but they have not [yet] tasted My punishment.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who question the revelation of the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse asserts that the Qur'an is not a product of Muhammad's own mind, but a revelation from God. The disbelievers are in doubt and skepticism about the Qur'an, but they have not yet experienced the punishment that will befall them if they persist in their rejection of the divine message.
orig: أأنزل عليه الذكر من بيننا بل هم في شك من ذكري بل لما يذوقوا عذاب

translation: Or do they have the treasures of the mercy of your Lord, the Exalted in Might, the Bestower?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers should not think that they have control over the blessings and mercy of God. The mercy of God is not something that can be hoarded or possessed by anyone. It is the sole prerogative of God, the Exalted in Might and the Bestower of all bounties. The implication is that the disbelievers should not be arrogant or assume that they can withhold God's mercy from others. Instead, they should humbly submit to God and seek His forgiveness and grace.
orig: أم عندهم خزائن رحمة ربك العزيز الوهاب

translation: Or do they have a share in the dominion of the heavens and the earth and [in] what is between them? Then let them ascend [to the heaven] by [any] means.
interpretation: This verse is questioning whether the disbelievers have a share in the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them. It is challenging them to try to ascend to the heavens by any means, implying that they do not have the power or ability to do so, and that true sovereignty belongs to Allah alone.
orig: أم لهم ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما فليرتقوا في الأسباب

translation: The soldiers (of faith) will be defeated here (or on that occasion).
interpretation: This verse suggests that there may be times when the believers or the forces of faith face defeat or setbacks. However, this should not be seen as a permanent or final outcome, as the Qur'an often emphasizes the ultimate triumph of the truth and the righteous. The verse encourages patience, perseverance, and trust in God's plan, even in the face of temporary difficulties or losses.
orig: جند ما هنالك مهزوم من الأحزاب

translation: The people of Noah and 'Ād and Pharaoh, the owner of stakes, denied [the messengers] before them
interpretation: This verse is referring to the rejection of previous prophets and messengers by the people of Noah, 'Ād, and Pharaoh. These groups had denied and rejected the divine messages brought to them, despite the clear signs and warnings. The mention of "the owner of stakes" in reference to Pharaoh likely alludes to the practice of impaling or crucifying disbelievers, highlighting the severe punishment they faced for their rejection of the truth.
orig: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح وعاد وفرعون ذو الأوتاد

translation: And [We destroyed] Thamud and the people of Lot and the companions of the thicket - and those were the [various] regions.
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of various communities that had rejected the message of God's prophets. Thamud was a people who were destroyed for their rejection of the prophet Salih, the people of Lot were destroyed for their immoral practices, and the companions of the thicket were a group that rejected the prophet Shu'ayb. These communities are described as "the [various] regions" that were destroyed due to their disbelief and disobedience to God's commands.
orig: وثمود وقوم لوط وأصحاب الأيكة أولئك الأحزاب

translation: Indeed, all [the messengers] were but liars, so the punishment has become due.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of believing in and following the messengers of God. It suggests that those who reject the messengers and consider them to be liars will face the consequences of their disbelief. The interpretation is that one should have faith in the divine messages and messengers, and not dismiss them as falsehoods, as that would lead to a deserved punishment.
orig: إن كل إلا كذب الرسل فحق عقاب

translation: And these [disbelievers] are waiting for nothing but a single blast [of the Horn], which will seize them while they are disputing.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Resurrection, when the disbelievers will be seized by a single, overwhelming blast of the trumpet that will signal the end of this world. They will not have time to dispute or argue, as the punishment will come upon them swiftly and without warning. The verse emphasizes the suddenness and finality of the coming of the Last Hour, which the disbelievers refuse to believe in despite the clear signs. It serves as a warning to those who deny the reality of the Hereafter and the accountability that awaits them.
orig: وما ينظر هؤلاء إلا صيحة واحدة ما لها من فواق

translation: And they say, "Our Lord, hasten for us our share [of the punishment] before the Day of Account."
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who are impatient for the punishment they believe will come upon them on the Day of Judgment. They are arrogantly demanding that their punishment be brought forward, rather than waiting patiently for the Day of Reckoning. This reflects their lack of faith and their desire to avoid the consequences of their misdeeds. The interpretation is that those who reject faith and mock the idea of accountability will ultimately face the consequences of their actions, even if they try to rush it.
orig: وقالوا ربنا عجل لنا قطنا قبل يوم الحساب

translation: And be patient over what they say and remember Our servant David, the possessor of strength; indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension, all believers, to be patient and steadfast in the face of criticism and opposition from those who reject the message of Islam. It reminds them to take solace in the example of the Prophet David, who was a man of great strength and devotion, constantly turning back to Allah in repentance and worship. The verse emphasizes the importance of perseverance, faith, and reliance on Allah, even when faced with adversity and the taunts of disbelievers.
orig: اصبر على ما يقولون واذكر عبدنا داوود ذا الأيد إنه أواب

translation: Indeed, We subjected the mountains [to praise] with him, [and] the birds, and We were constant therein.
interpretation: This verse is referring to Prophet David (peace be upon him) and his ability to praise and glorify Allah through his beautiful voice. The mountains and the birds are mentioned as joining him in this act of worship, as a sign of the power and majesty of Allah, who has control over all of creation. The interpretation suggests that when a righteous person engages in the remembrance and praise of Allah, even the inanimate objects of nature can be inspired to join in this act of worship.
orig: إنا سخرنا الجبال معه يسبحن بالعشي والإشراق

translation: And the birds assembled, all to Him they turn.
interpretation: This verse suggests that all creatures, including the birds, are ultimately accountable to Allah. The birds are described as being "assembled" or gathered, indicating that they will be held responsible for their actions on the Day of Judgment. The phrase "all to Him they turn" implies that all beings, including the birds, will eventually return to Allah and be judged by Him.
orig: والطير محشورة كل له أواب

translation: And We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom and discernment in speech.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet David (peace be upon him). God strengthened his kingdom, granting him authority and power. Additionally, God bestowed upon him wisdom and the ability to speak eloquently and make sound judgments. This highlights the importance of both political and spiritual leadership, where a ruler is guided by divine wisdom to lead their people justly and effectively.
orig: وشددنا ملكه وآتيناه الحكمة وفصل الخطاب

translation: And has the story of the adversaries reached you, when they climbed over the chamber?
interpretation: This verse refers to a story in the Qur'an about two adversaries who entered the private chamber of a prophet, likely Prophet David (peace be upon him). The verse suggests that this story was well-known, and the audience would have been familiar with the details. The interpretation is that this verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of our actions, even in private, as Allah is aware of all that we do.
orig: وهل أتاك نبأ الخصم إذ تسوروا المحراب

translation: When they entered upon David and he was alarmed by them, they said, "Fear not. [We are] two litigants, one of whom has wronged the other, so judge between us in truth and do not exceed [it] and guide us to the sound path."
interpretation: This verse describes a situation where two people came to seek judgment from the Prophet David (peace be upon him). They were in a dispute, and one of them had wronged the other. The two men recognized David's authority and wisdom, and asked him to judge between them fairly, without exceeding the bounds of justice. They also requested that he guide them to the right path. This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking justice through proper channels, and of the leader's responsibility to judge impartially and guide the people towards what is right.
orig: إذ دخلوا على داوود ففزع منهم قالوا لا تخف خصمان بغى بعضنا على بعض فاحكم بيننا بالحق ولا تشطط واهدنا إلى سواء الصراط

translation: Indeed this, my brother, has ninety-nine ewes, while I have [only] one ewe; so he said, "Entrust it to me," and overpowered me in speech.
interpretation: This verse is part of a parable told by the Prophet Nathan to King David. It illustrates how the rich can take advantage of the poor and how a person in a position of power can abuse that power. The verse shows how the rich man, who already has 99 ewes, demands the one ewe that the poor man has, demonstrating greed and a lack of compassion. The interpretation is that those in positions of power and wealth should use their resources to help the less fortunate, not to take advantage of them.
orig: إن هذا أخي له تسع وتسعون نعجة ولي نعجة واحدة فقال أكفلنيها وعزني في الخطاب

translation: He said: "Surely he has wronged you in demanding your [other] sheep [to add] to his [own] sheep; and indeed, many partners oppress one another, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds - and few are they." And David became certain that We had tried him, and he asked forgiveness of his Lord and fell down bowing [in prostration] and turned [to Him in repentance].
interpretation: This verse describes a parable told by the prophet Nathan to King David, in which a rich man unjustly takes a poor man's only sheep to add to his own flock. The verse emphasizes that many people oppress one another, except for those who have true faith and do good deeds, who are few in number. It then states that David realized he had been tested by God, and he sought forgiveness and turned to God in repentance. The key lessons are the condemnation of injustice and oppression, the praise of true faith and righteous deeds, and the importance of repentance when one realizes their mistakes.
orig: قال لقد ظلمك بسؤال نعجتك إلى نعاجه وإن كثيرا من الخلطاء ليبغي بعضهم على بعض إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وقليل ما هم وظن داوود أنما فتناه فاستغفر ربه وخر راكعا وأناب

translation: And We forgave him that. And indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good place of return.
interpretation: This verse refers to the forgiveness granted by God to one of His servants. The interpretation is that when a person sincerely repents and turns back to God, God will forgive their past transgressions and grant them a close relationship with Him as well as a favorable outcome in the Hereafter.
orig: فغفرنا له ذلك وإن له عندنا لزلفى وحسن مآب

translation: O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow [your own] desire, as it will lead you astray from the way of Allah. Indeed, those who go astray from the way of Allah will have a severe punishment for having forgotten the Day of Account.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the Prophet David, peace be upon him, and it emphasizes the importance of just and righteous leadership. The key message is that those in positions of power and authority must rule with fairness, integrity, and adherence to the truth, rather than being swayed by their own personal desires or biases. The verse warns against following one's own whims, as that can lead one astray from the path of Allah. It also highlights the severe consequences that await those who stray from the way of Allah, having forgotten the Day of Judgement. The overall lesson is that leaders must be mindful of their responsibilities and accountable to Allah, ruling with wisdom, justice, and a commitment to the well-being of the people.
orig: يا داوود إنا جعلناك خليفة في الأرض فاحكم بين الناس بالحق ولا تتبع الهوى فيضلك عن سبيل الله إن الذين يضلون عن سبيل الله لهم عذاب شديد بما نسوا يوم الحساب

translation: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the creation of the heavens, the earth, and all that is between them is not without purpose or in vain. It is a refutation of the notion held by those who reject faith that the universe is meaningless and devoid of purpose. The verse warns those who disbelieve that they will face the consequences of their disbelief, which is the punishment of the Fire. The interpretation highlights that the universe has a higher purpose and meaning, which those who deny faith fail to recognize.
orig: وما خلقنا السماء والأرض وما بينهما باطلا ذلك ظن الذين كفروا فويل للذين كفروا من النار

translation: Or do We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like corrupters in the land? Or do We treat the righteous like the wicked?
interpretation: This verse poses a rhetorical question, suggesting that it would be unjust to treat the believers who do good deeds the same as those who spread corruption and wickedness in the land. The implication is that Allah will not equate the righteous with the wicked, but will rather distinguish between them and reward the believers accordingly. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and righteous actions, and the certainty that Allah will judge people based on their deeds, not merely their claims of belief.
orig: أم نجعل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات كالمفسدين في الأرض أم نجعل المتقين كالفجار

translation: This is a blessed Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that they might reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding would be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and significance of the Qur'an, which has been revealed by God to the Prophet Muhammad. The Qur'an is described as a "blessed Book", indicating its divine origin and the blessings it contains. The purpose of revealing the Qur'an is twofold: first, to encourage people to reflect deeply on its verses and teachings, and second, to serve as a reminder for those who possess understanding and wisdom ("those of understanding"). The Qur'an is not merely a book to be read, but a guide that requires contemplation and reflection in order to fully comprehend its profound messages and lessons.
orig: كتاب أنزلناه إليك مبارك ليدبروا آياته وليتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: And We granted to David, Solomon - an excellent [servant] - indeed, he was one who often returned [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtues of Prophet Solomon, the son of Prophet David. It praises him as an "excellent servant" of Allah, and describes him as "one who often returned" to Allah in repentance and devotion. This suggests that Solomon possessed great qualities of piety, obedience, and closeness to Allah, which made him a model servant and a worthy successor to his father, the Prophet David.
orig: ووهبنا لداوود سليمان نعم العبد إنه أواب

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when he displayed to him the swift horses at evening
interpretation: This verse refers to a time when Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was shown a display of swift and powerful horses. The verse suggests that these horses were presented to him in the evening, which may have been a demonstration of the military might and preparedness of the early Muslim community. The interpretation is that this event was a sign of Allah's favor and support for the Prophet and the believers, as they were being equipped with the means to defend their faith and spread the message of Islam.
orig: إذ عرض عليه بالعشي الصافنات الجياد

translation: He said, "Indeed, I have loved the love of good things instead of remembering my Lord until [the sun] disappeared behind the veil."
interpretation: This verse expresses the regret of a person who became so engrossed in the love of worldly pleasures and material possessions that they neglected the remembrance of Allah. The "love of good things" refers to the person's attachment to the temporary delights of this world, which caused them to forget their duty to worship and remember their Creator. The "veil" symbolizes the person's distraction from the spiritual realm and their failure to maintain a constant awareness of Allah's presence. This verse serves as a reminder to prioritize the remembrance of Allah over the pursuit of worldly pleasures, as the latter can lead to a disconnection from the divine and ultimately deprive one of the true and lasting fulfillment.
orig: فقال إني أحببت حب الخير عن ذكر ربي حتى توارت بالحجاب

translation: Return it to me, and he began to stroke [their] legs and necks.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him) when his brothers returned his stolen shirt to him. The verse describes how Joseph began to examine the shirt, stroking the legs and necks of his brothers, as a way of testing them and seeing if they were telling the truth about what had happened. This verse highlights Joseph's wisdom and discernment in dealing with his brothers, and how he sought to uncover the truth through careful observation and examination.
orig: ردوها علي فطفق مسحا بالسوق والأعناق

translation: And We had certainly tried Solomon, and We placed on his throne a body; then he returned [to Us].
interpretation: This verse refers to a test or trial that God subjected the Prophet Solomon to. According to the interpretation, God placed a "body" on Solomon's throne, which is understood to mean that God replaced Solomon's physical form with something else, perhaps a demonic or satanic entity. This was a test of Solomon's faith and obedience to God. The verse then states that Solomon "returned [to Us]", indicating that he ultimately repented and returned to the worship of God after this trial.
orig: ولقد فتنا سليمان وألقينا على كرسيه جسدا ثم أناب

translation: He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, chapter 38, verse 35. It is a supplication made by the Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him) to his Lord, Allah. In this verse, Solomon is asking Allah to forgive him and grant him a kingdom that will not belong to anyone else after him. The interpretation of this verse is that Solomon is acknowledging his need for Allah's forgiveness and seeking a special kingdom from Him, one that is unique and unparalleled. This reflects Solomon's humility and his recognition that all blessings and powers come from Allah, the Bestower (Al-Wahhab).
orig: قال رب اغفر لي وهب لي ملكا لا ينبغي لأحد من بعدي إنك أنت الوهاب

translation: And We subjected to him the wind, blowing gently by his command, wherever he directed.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah made the wind subservient to Prophet Sulaiman (peace be upon him), allowing it to carry out his commands with ease. The wind would blow gently and obediently, going wherever Sulaiman wished, in order to assist him in his affairs. This was a sign of Allah's power and Sulaiman's status as a prophet, demonstrating how even natural forces were made to serve him.
orig: فسخرنا له الريح تجري بأمره رخاء حيث أصاب

translation: And the devils, [who were] builders and divers
interpretation: This verse refers to the devils, who were involved in building structures and diving into the depths of the sea. It suggests that the devils were not only engaged in tempting and misleading humans, but also possessed skills and abilities that were used for worldly pursuits. The verse highlights the multifaceted nature of the devils and their influence, which extends beyond just spiritual deception.
orig: والشياطين كل بناء وغواص

translation: And others bound in fetters
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are bound in chains or fetters, likely a metaphorical reference to those who are constrained by their own sins, desires, or attachments to the material world. The interpretation suggests that there are others, in addition to those mentioned in the previous verses, who are spiritually or metaphorically bound and in need of liberation.
orig: وآخرين مقرنين في الأصفاد

translation: This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the provisions and blessings bestowed by God are a gift, not an entitlement. It encourages people to be grateful for what they have been given, and to be generous in sharing their wealth and resources with others, without expecting any reward or accounting. The interpretation suggests that one should give freely and without conditions, as God provides for His creation without measure.
orig: هذا عطاؤنا فامنن أو أمسك بغير حساب

translation: And indeed, for him is nearness to Us and good place of return.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who believe in God and do good deeds will be granted a close relationship with God and a favorable outcome in the afterlife. The "nearness to Us" implies a spiritual closeness and connection with the divine, while the "good place of return" suggests a positive and rewarding destination in the hereafter.
orig: وإن له عندنا لزلفى وحسن مآب

translation: And mention, [O Muhammad], your servant Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment."
interpretation: This verse refers to the prophet Job (Ayyub in Arabic) and his steadfastness in the face of trials and tribulations. The verse highlights how Job turned to Allah (God) for help when he was afflicted by the hardship and torment inflicted upon him by Satan. This serves as an example of how believers should remain patient and seek refuge in Allah during times of difficulty, just as Job did.
orig: واذكر عبدنا أيوب إذ نادى ربه أني مسني الشيطان بنصب وعذاب

translation: Strike with your foot - this is a cool ablution and a (refreshing) drink.
interpretation: This verse is instructing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to strike the ground with his foot, which would cause a spring of cool, refreshing water to emerge. This water could be used for ablution (wudu) and as a drink. The verse highlights God's power to provide sustenance and purification for His servants, even in the most barren of environments.
orig: اركض برجلك هذا مغتسل بارد وشراب

translation: And We granted him his family and a like [number] with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Job (Ayyub) in the Quran. After enduring a series of trials and tribulations, God restored Job's wealth and family to him as a sign of mercy and a reminder for those who use their intellect to reflect on God's power and wisdom.
orig: ووهبنا له أهله ومثلهم معهم رحمة منا وذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: And take in your hand a bundle [of grass] and strike with it and do not break your oath. Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to take a bundle of grass and strike with it, but not to break his oath. It praises the Prophet's patience and obedience, describing him as an "excellent servant" who frequently turns back to Allah in repentance. The verse emphasizes the importance of keeping one's promises and oaths, even in the face of difficulty, and highlights the virtues of patience and devotion to Allah.
orig: وخذ بيدك ضغثا فاضرب به ولا تحنث إنا وجدناه صابرا نعم العبد إنه أواب

translation: And mention Our servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob - possessors of strength and [religious] vision.
interpretation: This verse calls for the remembrance and mention of the prophets Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who were known for their strong faith, piety, and spiritual insight. They were endowed with the physical and spiritual strength to carry out their divine missions, as well as the vision and insight to comprehend the deeper meanings of Allah's signs and guidance. This verse emphasizes the importance of following the example of these righteous individuals and drawing inspiration from their lives in order to strengthen one's own faith and relationship with the Almighty.
orig: واذكر عبادنا إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب أولي الأيدي والأبصار

translation: Indeed, We have purified them with an exclusive remembrance of the Abode [of the Hereafter].
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has purified and cleansed the believers by granting them a special remembrance and understanding of the Hereafter. The "exclusive remembrance of the Abode" refers to the believers' deep contemplation and focus on the eternal life in the Hereafter, which helps them to purify their intentions and actions in this world. This spiritual purification enables them to attain a higher level of faith and closeness to Allah.
orig: إنا أخلصناهم بخالصة ذكرى الدار

translation: And they are, with Us, of the chosen and the best.
interpretation: This verse refers to a group of people who are considered to be among the chosen and the best in the sight of God. The verse suggests that these individuals have been selected and distinguished by God, and they hold a special status in the divine hierarchy. The interpretation implies that these people have been purified, righteous, and virtuous, and they are held in high regard by God.
orig: وإنهم عندنا لمن المصطفين الأخيار

translation: And mention Ishmael and Elisha and Dhul-Kifl, and all [of them were] among the good.
interpretation: This verse is instructing the reader to remember and mention the prophets Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhul-Kifl, as well as all the other righteous and virtuous individuals. The mention of these prophets and righteous people serves to remind us of their exemplary lives and the importance of following their guidance. The verse emphasizes that these individuals were "among the good", highlighting their moral and spiritual excellence, which should inspire us to emulate their virtuous qualities.
orig: واذكر إسماعيل واليسع وذا الكفل وكل من الأخيار

translation: This is a reminder. And indeed, for the righteous is a good place of return.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to humanity, highlighting that the Quran is a source of guidance and wisdom. It then emphasizes that those who are righteous, who fear and obey Allah, will have a favorable and blessed destination in the Hereafter. The "good place of return" refers to the reward of Paradise that awaits the pious and God-fearing individuals in the afterlife.
orig: هذا ذكر وإن للمتقين لحسن مآب

translation: Gardens of Eden, the gates will be opened for them.
interpretation: This verse refers to the eternal paradise that awaits the righteous believers in the Hereafter. The "Gardens of Eden" represent the highest level of paradise, where the gates will be open for those who have lived a life of faith, righteousness, and good deeds. This signifies the welcoming and unhindered access the believers will have to this blissful abode, free from any obstacles or restrictions.
orig: جنات عدن مفتحة لهم الأبواب

translation: Reclining therein, they will call for abundant fruit and drink
interpretation: This verse describes the blissful state of the believers in Paradise. They will be reclining on comfortable couches, enjoying an abundance of delicious fruits and refreshing drinks. This imagery conveys the idea of complete comfort, satisfaction, and the fulfillment of all desires in the Hereafter.
orig: متكئين فيها يدعون فيها بفاكهة كثيرة وشراب

translation: And with them will be women limiting [their] glances, companions of equal age.
interpretation: This verse describes the companions that the righteous will have in the Hereafter. The women mentioned are described as "qaasirat-ut-tarf", which means that they will be modest and chaste, lowering their gaze and not looking at anything except their spouses. They will also be of the same age, "atrab", meaning they will be of equal age and maturity, creating a harmonious and compatible relationship.
orig: وعندهم قاصرات الطرف أتراب

translation: This is what you are promised for the Day of Reckoning.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs. The message conveys that the events and consequences that are being foretold will indeed come to pass on that momentous day. It serves as a reminder to humanity to prepare for this inevitable day by living righteously and in accordance with the teachings of Islam.
orig: هذا ما توعدون ليوم الحساب

translation: Indeed, this is Our provision; for it there is no ending.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the abundance and perpetuity of the sustenance and provision that Allah (God) grants to His servants. The interpretation suggests that the sustenance and blessings from Allah are infinite and everlasting, with no possibility of depletion or exhaustion. This reinforces the idea of Allah's boundless generosity and the fact that He is the sole Provider who ensures the continuous flow of provisions for His creation.
orig: إن هذا لرزقنا ما له من نفاد

translation: And indeed, for the transgressors is an evil place of return.
interpretation: This verse conveys a stern warning to those who transgress against the laws and commands of Allah. It indicates that those who reject faith and engage in sinful and oppressive acts will face a terrible and undesirable end or consequence in the Hereafter. The interpretation suggests that there is a grave and unpleasant destination awaiting the transgressors, which serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and righteous conduct.
orig: هذا وإن للطاغين لشر مآب

translation: They will enter Hell. And wretched is that settlement.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment of Hell that awaits those who reject faith and do evil deeds. It emphasizes that Hell is a terrible and unpleasant abode, where the disbelievers will be condemned to suffer eternal torment. The phrase "wretched is that settlement" underscores the severity and undesirability of this final destination for those who have strayed from the path of righteousness.
orig: جهنم يصلونها فبئس المهاد

translation: This let them taste - scalding water and [a foul, purulent] discharge
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment awaiting the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The "scalding water" and "foul, purulent discharge" symbolize the severe and unpleasant torment that awaits those who reject faith and deny the truth. The imagery conveys the idea that the disbelievers will have to endure excruciating and repulsive forms of punishment as a consequence of their misdeeds in this life.
orig: هذا فليذوقوه حميم وغساق

translation: And [the last of the creatures] of its form are mates.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even the last of God's creations, whatever that may be, are created in pairs or as mates. This emphasizes the divine wisdom and order in the universe, where everything is created in a balanced and complementary way, including the final creatures. The interpretation points to the universal principle of duality and pairing that permeates the natural world, as ordained by the Almighty.
orig: وآخر من شكله أزواج

translation: This is a host rushing headlong (to their doom); with them is no (friendly) welcome: for they shall burn in Hell-Fire.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a group of people who are rushing headlong towards their own destruction, without any welcome or hospitality. They are destined to burn in the Hellfire, due to their own misdeeds and rejection of the truth. The verse emphasizes the severe consequences that await those who choose to disbelieve and act in a manner that is displeasing to God.
orig: هذا فوج مقتحم معكم لا مرحبا بهم إنهم صالو النار

translation: They say, "Nay, but you (yourselves) are no welcome; thus have you brought this upon us (this disgrace, ignominy, torment, etc.). So evil is this place to which you have assigned us."
interpretation: This verse describes the response of the disbelievers when they are confronted with the consequences of their evil deeds. They try to shift the blame onto others, claiming that it is the believers who have brought this punishment upon them. However, the verse makes it clear that the disbelievers are responsible for their own actions, and that the place they have been assigned to is indeed a terrible one, as a result of their own choices.
orig: قالوا بل أنتم لا مرحبا بكم أنتم قدمتموه لنا فبئس القرار

translation: They will say, "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us - give him a double punishment in the Fire."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They will blame someone for leading them astray and causing them to end up in the punishment of Hell. Their request for a "double punishment" for this person reflects their intense regret and desire for vengeance, as they recognize the gravity of their own misdeeds and the consequences they now face.
orig: قالوا ربنا من قدم لنا هذا فزده عذابا ضعفا في النار

translation: And they say, "Why do we not see men that we used to count among the wicked?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the bewilderment of the disbelievers who used to consider certain righteous people as wicked, but now they cannot find them. It suggests that the disbelievers had a distorted view of reality, and failed to recognize the true nature of the righteous individuals they had condemned. The verse implies that the disbelievers judgment was flawed, and that they were unable to see the truth about those they had deemed as evil.
orig: وقالوا ما لنا لا نرى رجالا كنا نعدهم من الأشرار

translation: Have We taken them as (our) gods besides Him? Or did they (think) that they are a host to help them?
interpretation: This verse is asking whether the disbelievers have taken other gods besides Allah, or whether they think that their own strength and numbers will help them against Allah. The implication is that they are mistaken in either case, as Allah alone is the true God and He has power over all things. The verse is challenging the disbelievers' beliefs and calling them to submit to the one true God.
orig: أتخذناهم سخريا أم زاغت عنهم الأبصار

translation: Indeed, that is the truth about which they dispute.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the dispute and argument among the inhabitants of Hell is a reality. It emphasizes that the truth about which they argue and disagree is indeed the truth, and there is no doubt about it. The verse serves as a reminder that the disputes and disagreements that arise in the Hereafter are based on the undeniable truth, and that the disbelievers will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs.
orig: إن ذلك لحق تخاصم أهل النار

translation: Say, "I am only a warner, and there is no deity except Allah, the One, the Prevailing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the core Islamic belief in the oneness and sovereignty of God (Allah). The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to convey that he is merely a messenger, a warner, and that there is no other deity worthy of worship besides the One true God, who is all-powerful and dominant over all creation. The verse serves to affirm the fundamental tenet of monotheism (Tawheed) in Islam, rejecting any form of polytheism or associating partners with God.
orig: قل إنما أنا منذر وما من إله إلا الله الواحد القهار

translation: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them - the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and power of God, who is the Lord and Creator of the entire universe, including the heavens, the earth, and all that exists between them. He is described as "the Exalted in Might," indicating His supreme authority and dominion, and "the Perpetual Forgiver," highlighting His endless mercy and willingness to forgive those who seek His forgiveness. This verse reinforces the belief that God is the ultimate source of all creation and the sole object of worship and devotion.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما العزيز الغفار

translation: Say, "It is a great news,"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Qur"an, which is a great news or message that Allah has revealed to humanity. It is a profound and significant revelation that contains guidance, wisdom, and the path to salvation. The verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to convey this great news to the people, as it is a matter of utmost importance that deserves their attention and consideration.
orig: قل هو نبأ عظيم

translation: You are turning away from it.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the people who are neglecting or ignoring the message of the Qur"an. It suggests that they are turning away from the guidance and teachings it provides, and are not giving it the attention and consideration it deserves.
orig: أنتم عنه معرضون

translation: I had no knowledge of the highest assembly when they were disputing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the speaker (likely the Prophet Muhammad) had no direct knowledge or involvement in the proceedings of the heavenly assembly when they were engaged in a dispute or disagreement. It implies that the knowledge of such celestial affairs is limited to God and the angels, and that the speaker was not privy to these divine deliberations.
orig: ما كان لي من علم بالملإ الأعلى إذ يختصمون

translation: I am only a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is a messenger sent by God to warn people about the consequences of their actions and to guide them towards the right path. He is not claiming any special powers or divinity, but rather that he is a clear warner, delivering the message of God to humanity.
orig: إن يوحى إلي إلا أنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay."
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of Adam, the first human being, by Allah. It emphasizes that Allah, as the Creator, has the power and authority to bring into existence whatever He wills, including a human being fashioned from clay. This highlights the divine origin of mankind and the fact that we are dependent on Allah for our very existence. The verse also suggests that the angels were present when Allah announced His intention to create a human, demonstrating the significance of this event.
orig: إذ قال ربك للملائكة إني خالق بشرا من طين

translation: And when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul, then fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of Prophet Adam (peace be upon him). It describes how God fashioned Adam and breathed into him a part of His divine spirit, giving him life and consciousness. This act of God breathing His spirit into Adam is a profound symbol of the divine origin of human life and the special status of humanity as God's vicegerents on earth. The command to the angels to prostrate before Adam signifies the exalted position of humanity and the honor bestowed upon us by our Creator.
orig: فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين

translation: So the angels prostrated - all of them entirely.
interpretation: This verse describes the angels prostrating themselves before Adam, as commanded by God. The prostration of the angels signifies their obedience and submission to the will of God, and their acknowledgment of Adam’s elevated status as the first human being created by God. This event highlights the special position and honor bestowed upon Adam, and the reverence the angels have for God’s creation.
orig: فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون

translation: Except Iblees (Satan), he refused and was arrogant, and he was of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the creation of Adam, where all the angels prostrated before Adam except for Iblees (Satan). Iblees refused to prostrate, out of arrogance and pride, and thus became a disbeliever. This verse highlights the importance of humility and obedience to Allah, and the danger of arrogance and disobedience, which can lead to disbelief and eternal damnation.
orig: إلا إبليس استكبر وكان من الكافرين

translation: He said, 'O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? Were you arrogant [then], or were you [already] among the haughty?'
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the creation of Adam and the refusal of Iblis (Satan) to prostrate before him. The question posed by Allah to Iblis highlights the underlying reason for his disobedience - was it due to arrogance and a sense of superiority, or was he already among the haughty and prideful? The verse emphasizes the importance of humility and submission before the Creator, and the consequences of succumbing to arrogance and pride.
orig: قال يا إبليس ما منعك أن تسجد لما خلقت بيدي أستكبرت أم كنت من العالين

translation: He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of the creation of Adam and Iblis (Satan). Iblis refused to prostrate before Adam, claiming that he was superior because he was created from fire, while Adam was created from clay. This act of arrogance and disobedience led to Iblis' expulsion from the divine presence and his subsequent transformation into Satan. The verse highlights the importance of humility and obedience to God, even in the face of perceived superiority or differences in creation.
orig: قال أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين

translation: He (Allah) said: "Get out from this (Paradise) for verily, you are Accursed."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the expulsion of Satan (Iblis) from Paradise after he refused to prostrate to Adam. The interpretation is that Satan was cursed and banished from Paradise due to his arrogance and disobedience to Allah's command. This serves as a lesson that pride and defiance of Allah's will leads to one's downfall.
orig: قال فاخرج منها فإنك رجيم

translation: And indeed, My curse is upon you until the Day of Recompense.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from God to those who reject His signs and guidance. It suggests that those who persist in disbelief and defiance will be under God's eternal curse, which will continue until the Day of Judgment when they will be held accountable for their actions. The interpretation emphasizes the gravity of rejecting God's message and the consequences that will follow.
orig: وإن عليك لعنتي إلى يوم الدين

translation: He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, where the disbeliever is pleading with God to delay his punishment until the Day of Resurrection. The interpretation is that the disbeliever is seeking more time, hoping that he can avoid the consequences of his disbelief and wrongdoing. However, the Qur'an teaches that the Day of Judgment is inevitable, and that one should prepare for it by living a righteous life in this world.
