orig: قال رب فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: He said, "Then indeed, you are of those reprieved."
interpretation: This verse is from the Qur'an, Surah Al-A'raf, verse 15. It is part of the dialogue between God and Iblis (Satan) when God asked Iblis to prostrate before Adam. Iblis refused and was granted a respite until the Day of Judgment. The interpretation of this verse is that Iblis was given a temporary reprieve, a delay in his punishment, for his disobedience to God's command.
orig: قال فإنك من المنظرين

translation: Until the Day of the Appointed Time
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions. The "Appointed Time" is a reference to the predetermined time when the world will come to an end and the final reckoning will take place. This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment and the importance of being prepared for it through righteous deeds and faith in God.
orig: إلى يوم الوقت المعلوم

translation: He (Iblees) said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all,"
interpretation: This verse is a quote from Iblees (Satan) in response to Allah's command not to mislead or misguide the people. Iblees swears by Allah's might that he will mislead all of humanity, showing his arrogance and defiance against Allah's will. This highlights the ongoing struggle between good and evil, and the need for humans to seek guidance from Allah and resist the temptations of Satan.
orig: قال فبعزتك لأغوينهم أجمعين

translation: Except Your devoted [righteous] servants among them.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fact that on the Day of Judgment, all people will be gathered before Allah, except for those who were sincere and devoted servants of Allah. These devoted servants are the ones who will be spared from the punishment and torment that will befall the disbelievers and wrongdoers.
orig: إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين

translation: He said: "The truth I do indeed speak."
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between Prophet Musa (Moses) and Pharaoh. Pharaoh had accused Musa of being a sorcerer, but Musa responded by affirming that he was speaking the truth. This verse emphasizes the importance of truthfulness and honesty, and that a person of faith should always strive to convey the truth, even in the face of opposition or skepticism.
orig: قال فالحق والحق أقول

translation: I will surely fill Hell with you and those who follow you from among them all.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from God to those who reject the message of Islam and instead follow the path of disbelief and evil. It suggests that those who choose to turn away from God's guidance and lead others astray will be condemned to the eternal punishment of Hell. The interpretation emphasizes the gravity of the consequences for those who reject the truth and the importance of following the righteous path.
orig: لأملأن جهنم منك وممن تبعك منهم أجمعين

translation: Say, "I do not ask you for any payment, and I am not of the pretentious."
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to tell the people that he does not seek any reward or payment for conveying the message of Islam. He is not pretentious or seeking worldly gains, but rather he is a sincere messenger of Allah, delivering the divine message without any ulterior motives. This emphasizes the pure and selfless nature of the Prophet's mission, which was solely to guide humanity towards the worship of the One True God.
orig: قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر وما أنا من المتكلفين

translation: Indeed, it (the Qur'an) is but a reminder to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine message and guidance for all of humanity, not just for a specific group or nation. It is a reminder that calls people to reflect on the signs of God's power and wisdom, and to submit to His will. The Qur'an is a universal reminder that transcends time and place, serving as a source of guidance and inspiration for all who seek to live in accordance with the principles of Islam.
orig: إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: And you will surely come to know [the truth of] its information after a time.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance that the truth about a certain matter will eventually become known, even if it is not apparent or understood in the present moment. It suggests that patience and perseverance are required, as the full understanding of a situation or event may only become clear over time. The verse encourages people to have faith that the truth will eventually be revealed, rather than rushing to judgment or making assumptions before all the facts are known.
orig: ولتعلمن نبأه بعد حين

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an, the revealed book, is from Allah, the Almighty and All-Wise. It highlights the divine origin of the Qur'an, which is not the work of any human being, but a revelation from the All-Powerful and All-Knowing God. This establishes the authority and reliability of the Qur'an as the word of God, deserving of our utmost respect, study, and obedience.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth. So worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, which has been revealed to Prophet Muhammad as the true and final scripture. It calls upon the believers to worship Allah alone, with sincerity and devotion, making their faith and obedience to Him the sole purpose of their lives.
orig: إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق فاعبد الله مخلصا له الدين

translation: Unquestionably, for Allah is the pure religion. And those who take protectors besides Him [say], "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position." Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allah does not guide he who is a liar and [confirmed] disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true worship and devotion should be directed solely towards Allah, the One God. It condemns those who associate partners with Allah and worship other deities, claiming that they do so in order to seek closeness to Allah. However, the verse makes it clear that Allah will judge between them and those who have gone astray. It also states that Allah does not guide those who are liars and disbelievers, implying that true guidance can only be found through sincere belief and submission to the One God.
orig: ألا لله الدين الخالص والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى إن الله يحكم بينهم في ما هم فيه يختلفون إن الله لا يهدي من هو كاذب كفار

translation: If Allah had willed to take a son, He could have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Exalted is He; He is Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and oneness of Allah. It states that if Allah had desired to have a son, He could have chosen any of His creations to be that son. However, Allah is exalted above such human attributes and is the One, the Prevailing, who has no need for a son or any other partner. This verse rejects the concept of Allah having a son or any kind of offspring, and affirms His unique and unparalleled divinity.
orig: لو أراد الله أن يتخذ ولدا لاصطفى مما يخلق ما يشاء سبحانه هو الله الواحد القهار

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night, and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and sovereignty in creating the universe and governing the natural phenomena such as the alternation of day and night, and the movement of the sun and moon. It highlights that all of this is done with truth and purpose, not in vain. The verse also reminds us of God's attributes of might and forgiveness, which should inspire awe, reverence and hope in the believers.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق يكور الليل على النهار ويكور النهار على الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى ألا هو العزيز الغفار

translation: He created you from one soul. Then He made from it its mate, and He produced for you from the cattle, eight mates. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, within three darknesses. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you averted?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of origin of all human beings, as they were created from a single soul. It then goes on to mention the creation of mates for humans, as well as the creation of various animal species in pairs. The verse also highlights the process of human development within the mother's womb, which takes place in three distinct stages or "darknesses". The overall message is to acknowledge the power and sovereignty of Allah as the sole Creator, and to not be diverted from worshipping Him alone.
orig: خلقكم من نفس واحدة ثم جعل منها زوجها وأنزل لكم من الأنعام ثمانية أزواج يخلقكم في بطون أمهاتكم خلقا من بعد خلق في ظلمات ثلاث ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك لا إله إلا هو فأنى تصرفون

translation: If you disbelieve, then indeed, Allah is Free from need of you. And He does not approve of disbelief for His servants. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you; and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is self-sufficient and does not need the worship or belief of His servants. If people choose to disbelieve, it does not diminish Allah's glory or power in any way. However, Allah disapproves of disbelief and desires that His servants be grateful and thankful. Each person is responsible for their own actions and will be held accountable for them on the Day of Judgment. Allah is all-knowing and aware of the innermost thoughts and intentions of people.
orig: إن تكفروا فإن الله غني عنكم ولا يرضى لعباده الكفر وإن تشكروا يرضه لكم ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ثم إلى ربكم مرجعكم فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And when adversity touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow on him a favor from Us, he says, "I have only been given it because of [my] knowledge." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know. Say, "Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire."
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to turn to God in times of hardship, but to then become complacent and forgetful of God's blessings when they are granted ease and prosperity. It warns that such ingratitude and associating partners with God is a grave sin that will lead to the Fire in the Hereafter. The verse encourages the disbelievers to enjoy their disbelief for a little while, as their ultimate fate is the Fire. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of maintaining gratitude and devotion to God, regardless of one's circumstances.
orig: وإذا مس الإنسان ضر دعا ربه منيبا إليه ثم إذا خوله نعمة منه نسي ما كان يدعو إليه من قبل وجعل لله أندادا ليضل عن سبيله قل تمتع بكفرك قليلا إنك من أصحاب النار

translation: Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [like one who does not]? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only they will remember [who] are people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse contrasts two types of people: those who are devoted to worship and seeking God's mercy, and those who do not have this level of devotion and knowledge. The first group spends the night in prayer, both prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for God's forgiveness and compassion. The second group lacks this deep spiritual awareness and connection. The verse then poses a rhetorical question, asking if these two groups can be considered equal. The answer is that only those with understanding and wisdom ("people of understanding") will truly comprehend the difference between these two states. This highlights the importance of seeking knowledge, spiritual devotion, and a consciousness of the Hereafter as a path to God's mercy.
orig: أمن هو قانت آناء الليل ساجدا وقائما يحذر الآخرة ويرجو رحمة ربه قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون إنما يتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: Say, "O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world is good, and the earth of Allah is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account."
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to be mindful of Allah and to do good deeds in this life. It promises that those who do good will be rewarded, and that the earth is vast, so they should not be deterred by hardship or difficulty. The verse also emphasizes the importance of patience and steadfastness, stating that the patient will be rewarded without measure.
orig: قل يا عباد الذين آمنوا اتقوا ربكم للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنة وأرض الله واسعة إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب

translation: Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping Allah (God) with sincerity and devotion. The command to worship Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him, is a fundamental tenet of Islam. The interpretation is that true worship must be done with a pure and sincere heart, dedicated solely to Allah, and not for any other purpose or motive. This is the essence of "being sincere to Him in religion."
orig: قل إني أمرت أن أعبد الله مخلصا له الدين

translation: And I have been commanded to be the first [among you] of the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse expresses the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) commitment to being the first to submit to the will of God and embrace Islam. It reflects his role as the final prophet, sent to guide humanity towards the path of righteousness and obedience to the One true God. This verse emphasizes the importance of being the first to accept and follow the divine teachings, setting an example for others to follow.
orig: وأمرت لأن أكون أول المسلمين

translation: Say, "Indeed, I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah (God) and the fear of facing severe punishment on the Day of Judgment. The speaker, who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad, expresses his deep reverence for Allah and his dread of incurring Allah's wrath through disobedience. The "tremendous Day" refers to the Day of Resurrection, when all people will be held accountable for their actions in life. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to strive to please Allah in all their deeds.
orig: قل إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Say, "Allah I worship, being sincere to Him in my religion."
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to declare that he worships Allah alone, with complete devotion and sincerity. It emphasizes the importance of worshiping Allah exclusively, without associating any partners with Him, and maintaining a pure and sincere faith. The interpretation suggests that true worship of Allah requires an unwavering commitment and a heart that is devoted solely to Him, without any form of idolatry or polytheism.
orig: قل الله أعبد مخلصا له ديني

translation: So worship whatever you wish besides Him. Say, "Indeed, the losers are the ones who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that one should worship only God, and not any other deities or objects. It warns that those who worship anything besides God will be the ultimate losers, as they will lose both themselves and their families on the Day of Judgment. This is the clearest and most evident form of loss, as they have forsaken the true path of worshiping the One God in favor of false idols or deities.
orig: فاعبدوا ما شئتم من دونه قل إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة ألا ذلك هو الخسران المبين

translation: They will have canopies of Fire above them and canopies [of Fire] below them. With this [threat] Allah frightens His servants. O My servants, then fear Me.
interpretation: This verse warns the disbelievers of the punishment they will face in the Hereafter. They will be surrounded by the Fire of Hell, both above and below them. This is a terrifying prospect that Allah uses to frighten His servants and urge them to be mindful of Him and avoid His wrath by obeying His commands and staying away from sins. The verse is a call to the believers to fear Allah and be conscious of Him in all their actions.
orig: لهم من فوقهم ظلل من النار ومن تحتهم ظلل ذلك يخوف الله به عباده يا عباد فاتقون

translation: And those who avoid the Worship of false gods, and turn to Allah (in repentance), for them are glad tidings: so announce the glad tidings to My Servants
interpretation: This verse encourages people to refrain from worshiping false deities or idols ("the Taghut") and instead turn to Allah in repentance and devotion. Those who do so are promised glad tidings and blessings from Allah. The interpretation is that true faith and submission to the One God, Allah, is the path to salvation and divine favor.
orig: والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها وأنابوا إلى الله لهم البشرى فبشر عباد

translation: Those who listen to speech and follow the best of it. Those are the ones Allah has guided, and those are people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to be discerning listeners, who do not blindly accept everything they hear, but carefully evaluate it and follow what is most beneficial and righteous. It suggests that those who do so are the ones truly guided by Allah, and are people of wisdom and intelligence.
orig: الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه أولئك الذين هداهم الله وأولئك هم أولو الألباب

translation: Then is one who is deserving of the decree of punishment [to be guided]? Then, can you save one who is in the Fire?
interpretation: This verse poses a rhetorical question, implying that those who have earned the punishment of Allah cannot be guided or saved from the Fire of Hell. The interpretation suggests that it is not within the power of any human being to rescue someone who has been condemned to the eternal punishment of the Hellfire, as that is solely in the hands of Allah, the Almighty.
orig: أفمن حق عليه كلمة العذاب أفأنت تنقذ من في النار

translation: But those who fear their Lord will have gardens [in Paradise] above them, beneath which rivers flow, [it is] a promise of Allah, [which] Allah does not fail in [His] promise.
interpretation: This verse describes the rewards and blessings that await those who are righteous and fear Allah. They will be granted lofty and spacious gardens in the Hereafter, with rivers flowing beneath them. This is a promise from Allah that He will not fail to fulfill. The interpretation emphasizes that those who obey and revere Allah will be rewarded with the highest levels of Paradise, a place of eternal bliss and contentment.
orig: لكن الذين اتقوا ربهم لهم غرف من فوقها غرف مبنية تجري من تحتها الأنهار وعد الله لا يخلف الله الميعاد

translation: Have you not seen that Allah sends down rain from the sky, and We produce thereby gardens of varied colors? Then in them are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on the signs of Allah's power and wisdom in the natural world. The rain that falls from the sky nourishes the earth, producing a variety of crops and vegetation. This diversity in color and form is a testament to the creative might of the Creator, and a reminder for those who possess insight and intellect to ponder upon Allah's signs in the universe.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض ثم يخرج به زرعا مختلفا ألوانه ثم يهيج فتراه مصفرا ثم يجعله حطاما إن في ذلك لذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: Then is one whose heart Allah has expanded to [accept] Islam and he is upon [i.e., guided by] a light from his Lord [like one whose heart rejects it]? So woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse contrasts those whose hearts have been opened to accept Islam, guided by the light of faith, with those whose hearts have become hardened against the remembrance of Allah. The former have embraced the truth, while the latter are in a state of clear misguidance. The verse emphasizes the importance of a receptive and humble heart in order to receive the guidance of Allah, and warns against the dire consequences of a hardened heart that rejects the divine message.
orig: أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه فويل للقاسية قلوبهم من ذكر الله أولئك في ضلال مبين

translation: Allah has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book wherein is reiteration. The skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts relax at the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills. And one whom Allah leaves astray - for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and impact of the Qur'an, which is described as "the best statement" revealed by Allah. The Qur'an is a consistent and coherent book, with repeated themes and lessons. When those who fear Allah hear the Qur'an, it causes their skin to shiver, as they are deeply moved by its message. However, as they continue to reflect on the Qur'an, their hearts and minds become calm and receptive to the guidance it provides. This guidance is a direct gift from Allah, who chooses to guide whomever He wills. Conversely, those whom Allah leaves astray will have no one to guide them, as Allah alone has the power to guide or misguide.
orig: الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا متشابها مثاني تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله ذلك هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: Is he who will guard himself with his face from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection (like one who disbelieves)? And it will be said to the wrongdoers: "Taste what you used to earn."
interpretation: This verse draws a contrast between those who fear and seek protection from the punishment of the Hereafter, and those who wrongfully commit sins. The former will be saved from the torment, while the latter will be made to taste the consequences of their misdeeds. The verse emphasizes the importance of being righteous and fearing Allah, in order to avoid the severe punishment that awaits the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment.
orig: أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة وقيل للظالمين ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون

translation: Those before them also rejected (the truth), so the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the fate of previous nations and peoples who rejected the truth and the message of the Prophets sent to them. They were punished by Allah in ways they did not expect or anticipate, as a consequence of their disbelief and rejection of the divine guidance. This serves as a warning to those who similarly reject the truth, that they too will face the consequences of their actions, even if they do not foresee or comprehend the nature of the punishment that will befall them.
orig: كذب الذين من قبلهم فأتاهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون

translation: So Allah made them taste the disgrace in the worldly life, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they had known.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who deny the truth and reject faith will face the consequences of their actions, both in this life and the Hereafter. In this world, they will experience the shame and disgrace that comes with their disbelief. However, the punishment in the Hereafter is even greater, as it is eternal and far more severe. The verse suggests that if these people had known the true nature of the consequences they would face, they might have reconsidered their rejection of faith and chosen to believe in God.
orig: فأذاقهم الله الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example that they might remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an contains a wide variety of examples, parables, and lessons that are meant to guide and remind people. The purpose is to help people reflect, ponder, and ultimately remember the teachings of the Qur'an and apply them in their lives. The diversity of the examples provided in the Qur'an caters to the different levels of understanding and backgrounds of the people, making the divine message accessible and relatable to all.
orig: ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: A Qur'an in Arabic, without any crookedness, that they might become righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is revealed in the Arabic language, and it is free from any inconsistencies or contradictions. The purpose of this is to guide people towards righteousness and God-consciousness (taqwa). The Qur'an is a clear and straightforward message, and if people ponder over it and follow its teachings, they will be able to attain the state of righteousness and God-consciousness.
orig: قرآنا عربيا غير ذي عوج لعلهم يتقون

translation: Allah presents an example: a man [who is] owned by quarreling partners and a man [who belongs] exclusively to one man - are they equal in comparison? Praise to Allah! But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse presents a parable to illustrate the difference between worshipping multiple gods versus worshipping one God. The first man is owned by "quarreling partners" - representing the polytheistic belief in multiple deities. The second man belongs "exclusively to one man" - representing the monotheistic belief in one God. The verse emphasizes that these two states are not equal, and that praising the one true God is the correct path, even though most people do not understand this.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا رجلا فيه شركاء متشاكسون ورجلا سلما لرجل هل يستويان مثلا الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, you are to die, and indeed, they are to die.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal truth of mortality - that all human beings, including the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and those around him, will eventually die. It serves as a reminder that life is fleeting and that we should focus on preparing for the Hereafter, where our true and eternal existence lies.
orig: إنك ميت وإنهم ميتون

translation: Then, indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be disputing before your Lord.
interpretation: This verse indicates that on the Day of Resurrection, all people will be gathered before Allah (God) to be held accountable for their actions and beliefs. They will dispute and argue with one another, and ultimately, Allah will judge them based on their deeds and make the final decision about their fate in the Hereafter.
orig: ثم إنكم يوم القيامة عند ربكم تختصمون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a [fitting] residence for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse condemns those who fabricate lies about Allah or reject the truth when it is presented to them. It emphasizes that the ultimate destination for such disbelievers is Hell, which is a fitting abode for those who turn away from the guidance of Allah and the truth. The verse underscores the gravity of rejecting the truth and the consequences that follow.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه أليس في جهنم مثوى للكافرين

translation: And the one who has brought the truth and [those who] believed in it - those are the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of believing in and acting upon the truth. The one who brings the truth, which refers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the message of the Qur'an, and those who sincerely believe in it, are considered the righteous (al-muttaqun). This highlights that true righteousness is not just about outward actions, but also about the sincerity of one's faith and belief in the divine truth. It encourages believers to wholeheartedly accept and follow the guidance of the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet in order to attain the status of the righteous.
orig: والذي جاء بالصدق وصدق به أولئك هم المتقون

translation: For them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the righteous and virtuous people will be granted whatever they desire from their Lord in the Hereafter. This is the just reward for those who have done good deeds and lived righteously in this world.
orig: لهم ما يشاءون عند ربهم ذلك جزاء المحسنين

translation: That Allah may expiate from them the worst of what they did and reward them their due for the best of what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah will forgive the believers for their past misdeeds and reward them for their good deeds. It implies that Allah is merciful and just, and that He will judge people based on their actions, forgiving the worst and rewarding the best. The interpretation suggests that believers should strive to do good deeds, as they will be rewarded for them by Allah.
orig: ليكفر الله عنهم أسوأ الذي عملوا ويجزيهم أجرهم بأحسن الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: Is not Allah enough for His servant? And they would frighten you with those [false deities] other than Him. And whoever Allah leaves astray - for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone is sufficient for His servants, and that one should not be afraid of or intimidated by those who worship false deities other than Allah. It also states that whoever Allah leaves astray, there is no one who can guide them back to the right path.
orig: أليس الله بكاف عبده ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: And whomever Allah guides, there is no one who can misguide him. Is not Allah Exalted in Might, the Owner of Retribution?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the guidance and power of Allah. It states that if Allah guides someone, no one can lead them astray. This is because Allah is All-Powerful and the One who has the ability to punish those who disobey Him. The verse is a reminder that Allah's guidance is the only true path, and that those who follow it will be protected from being misled. It also serves as a warning to those who reject Allah's guidance, as they will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: ومن يهد الله فما له من مضل أليس الله بعزيز ذي انتقام

translation: And if you ask them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they will surely say, "Allah." Say, "Then have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended me harm, are they able to remove my harm; or if He intends me mercy, are they able to withhold His mercy?" Say, "Sufficient for me is Allah; upon Him [alone] rely the [wise] reliers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the belief in the oneness and supremacy of Allah as the Creator of the heavens and the earth. It challenges the notion of worshiping or invoking any other deities besides Allah, as they have no power to either harm or benefit the believer. The verse encourages reliance and trust in Allah alone, as He is the sole source of protection and mercy. The interpretation highlights the importance of monotheism and the futility of seeking help from anyone or anything other than the Almighty Allah.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله قل أفرأيتم ما تدعون من دون الله إن أرادني الله بضر هل هن كاشفات ضره أو أرادني برحمة هل هن ممسكات رحمته قل حسبي الله عليه يتوكل المتوكلون

translation: Say, 'O my people, work according to your position; [for] indeed, I am working. And you are going to know'
interpretation: This verse is a command from God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to tell his people to act according to their abilities and circumstances. It implies that each person has a role to play and should strive to fulfill their responsibilities to the best of their capabilities. The verse also suggests that the outcome of their actions will be made known to them in due time, as God is the ultimate judge of their deeds.
orig: قل يا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل فسوف تعلمون

translation: Whoever is given the punishment (of Allah), he will indeed be disgraced and the lasting punishment will be inflicted on him
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject faith and disobey the commandments of Allah. It indicates that those who are subjected to Allah's punishment will not only be humiliated and disgraced, but will also face a lasting and eternal punishment. The phrase "the lasting punishment" suggests that this punishment will be everlasting, without any relief or end. This serves as a strong deterrent against turning away from the path of righteousness and submitting to Allah.
orig: من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ويحل عليه عذاب مقيم

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth for mankind. So whoever is guided - it is for [the benefit of] his soul; and whoever errs only errs against it. And you are not a manager over them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an has been revealed by God to guide humanity towards the truth. It is up to each individual to choose whether to accept this guidance and benefit from it, or to reject it and suffer the consequences. The Prophet Muhammad is not responsible for the choices of the people, but rather he has been entrusted with conveying the message of the Qur'an. Ultimately, each person is accountable for their own actions and decisions.
orig: إنا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب للناس بالحق فمن اهتدى فلنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: It is Allah who takes the souls at the time of their death, and [also] the souls [of those] who do not die [at that time] during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others for a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse describes Allah's power over life and death. He takes the souls of those who die, and also temporarily takes the souls of those who are sleeping, but then releases them until their appointed time of death. This demonstrates Allah's sovereignty and the temporary nature of our earthly existence, which should inspire people to reflect on the deeper meaning of life.
orig: الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها والتي لم تمت في منامها فيمسك التي قضى عليها الموت ويرسل الأخرى إلى أجل مسمى إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say, "[Even if] they do not possess [any power] to benefit or harm themselves, and they do not possess [any power of] guidance?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of worshipping or seeking intercession from deities other than Allah. It emphasizes that these supposed "intercessors" have no power to benefit or harm anyone, nor do they have the ability to guide people. The verse encourages believers to recognize Allah as the sole deity worthy of worship and to seek guidance and assistance directly from Him, rather than relying on intermediaries that have no real power or authority.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دون الله شفعاء قل أولو كانوا لا يملكون شيئا ولا يعقلون

translation: Say, "To Allah belongs [all] intercession. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all intercession and supplication belongs to Allah alone. He is the Sovereign of the heavens and the earth, and ultimately, all will return to Him for judgment. This affirms the absolute power and authority of Allah, and the need for people to turn to Him directly in worship and seeking help, rather than relying on any intermediaries or intercessors.
orig: قل لله الشفاعة جميعا له ملك السماوات والأرض ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: And when Allah is mentioned alone, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink with aversion, but when those [worshipped] other than Him are mentioned, immediately they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the reaction of those who believe in the Hereafter and those who do not when the name of Allah is mentioned. The believers find comfort and joy in the remembrance of Allah, while the disbelievers feel aversion and their hearts shrink away. This is because the disbelievers place their trust and allegiance in other deities or worldly pursuits, and the mention of the one true God, Allah, threatens their false beliefs and attachments. In contrast, the believers find solace and affirmation in the remembrance of Allah, the only worthy object of worship and the source of all blessings.
orig: وإذا ذكر الله وحده اشمأزت قلوب الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وإذا ذكر الذين من دونه إذا هم يستبشرون

translation: Say, "O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme power and knowledge of Allah as the Creator of the universe and the one who has knowledge of both the seen and the unseen realms. It also highlights Allah's role as the ultimate judge who will resolve the differences and disputes among His servants on the Day of Judgment. The verse encourages believers to turn to Allah and seek His guidance and judgment, as He is the only one who can truly and fairly resolve the conflicts and disagreements that arise among people.
orig: قل اللهم فاطر السماوات والأرض عالم الغيب والشهادة أنت تحكم بين عبادك في ما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: And if those who have wronged had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it, they would [attempt to] ransom themselves thereby from the worst of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not expected.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Resurrection, even if the wrongdoers had all the wealth and resources of the earth, they would not be able to ransom themselves from the severe punishment they will face. It highlights that the punishment of the Hereafter is far greater than any worldly possessions or means. Additionally, the verse suggests that the wrongdoers will be confronted with aspects of Allah's judgment that they had not anticipated, further underscoring the gravity of their situation and the need to seek forgiveness and repentance in this life.
orig: ولو أن للذين ظلموا ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه لافتدوا به من سوء العذاب يوم القيامة وبدا لهم من الله ما لم يكونوا يحتسبون

translation: And the evil [consequences] of what they did will appear to them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who engage in evil deeds and mock the teachings of Islam will ultimately face the consequences of their actions. Their misdeeds will be made manifest to them, and they will be encompassed by the very thing they had previously ridiculed. This serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and engage in sinful behavior, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their choices.
orig: وبدا لهم سيئات ما كسبوا وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And when adversity touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We have bestowed on him a favor from Us, he says, "I have only been given it because of [my] knowledge." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of human beings to turn to God in times of hardship, but then to become arrogant and self-centered when they are granted blessings and favors. The verse suggests that the true nature of these blessings is a test or trial, but that most people fail to recognize this and instead attribute their good fortune to their own knowledge or abilities. The interpretation is that we should remain humble and grateful to God, recognizing that all blessings come from Him and not from our own merits.
orig: فإذا مس الإنسان ضر دعانا ثم إذا خولناه نعمة منا قال إنما أوتيته على علم بل هي فتنة ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Those before them had already said the same, yet what they were doing did not benefit them in the least.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the fact that disbelievers and those who reject the truth have made similar claims and excuses in the past, but their actions and deeds did not save them from the consequences of their rejection. It serves as a warning that merely making claims or following in the footsteps of previous generations is not enough, and that one must be accountable for their own actions and beliefs.
orig: قد قالها الذين من قبلهم فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And the evil consequences of what they earned struck them. And those who have wronged of these [people] will be struck by the evil consequences of what they earned, and they will not be able to escape.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who do evil deeds will face the consequences of their actions. It emphasizes that the wrongdoers will not be able to escape the punishment for their misdeeds, as they will be "struck by the evil consequences of what they earned". The verse serves as a reminder that our actions have consequences, and that we are accountable for our choices in life.
orig: فأصابهم سيئات ما كسبوا والذين ظلموا من هؤلاء سيصيبهم سيئات ما كسبوا وما هم بمعجزين

translation: Do they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone has control over the provision and sustenance of His creation. He grants abundance to some and restricts it for others, as He wills. This is a sign for those who believe in Allah's power, wisdom and sovereignty. The verse encourages people to have faith in Allah's divine plan and to trust that He knows what is best for them, even if they do not fully understand His ways.
orig: أولم يعلموا أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."
interpretation: This verse encourages those who have committed sins not to lose hope in Allah's mercy and forgiveness. It emphasizes that Allah is the Most Forgiving and Merciful, and that He is willing to forgive all sins if the person sincerely repents and turns back to Him. The verse provides a message of hope and reassurance, reminding us that no matter how grave our sins may be, Allah's mercy and forgiveness are boundless.
orig: قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And turn to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, for then you will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to repent and submit to Allah before facing the consequences of their misdeeds. It emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness and guidance before it is too late, as once the punishment arrives, there will be no one to help or save them. The verse highlights the urgency of turning back to Allah and surrendering to His will, as the alternative is facing the inevitable punishment without any means of escape or assistance.
orig: وأنيبوا إلى ربكم وأسلموا له من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب ثم لا تنصرون

translation: And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes to you suddenly while you do not perceive
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to follow the best teachings and guidance revealed in the Qur'an from God, before facing the consequences of their actions. It emphasizes the importance of being mindful and proactive in one's faith, rather than being caught off guard by divine punishment. The interpretation suggests that by adhering to the most virtuous and righteous teachings, one can avoid the sudden and unexpected arrival of divine retribution.
orig: واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب بغتة وأنتم لا تشعرون

translation: That a soul may say: "Alas, [what] I neglected in [my] responsibility to Allah and how I ridiculed [Him]"
interpretation: This verse warns against neglecting one's duties to Allah and mocking or ridiculing Him. It suggests that on the Day of Judgment, a soul will regret its failure to fulfill its obligations to Allah and its arrogant rejection of faith. The verse emphasizes the importance of taking one's relationship with Allah seriously and avoiding the path of those who scoffed at the signs of Allah.
orig: أن تقول نفس يا حسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله وإن كنت لمن الساخرين

translation: Or [you might] say, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous."
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of some people to shift the blame for their own shortcomings onto Allah, by claiming that if only they had been guided by Allah, they would have been among the righteous. However, the Qur'an emphasizes that each individual is responsible for their own actions and choices, and that guidance from Allah is available to all who sincerely seek it. The interpretation of this verse is that one should not make excuses for their own failings, but rather take responsibility and strive to become righteous through their own efforts, with the help and guidance of Allah.
orig: أو تقول لو أن الله هداني لكنت من المتقين

translation: Or [you might say], "If only I had a second chance, I would be among the doers of good."
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who delay repentance and good deeds until they are faced with the punishment of the Hereafter. It suggests that when people witness the consequences of their actions, they may wish they had another chance to rectify their mistakes and do good. However, this verse implies that such regret will be futile, as the opportunity for repentance and reform is in this life, not the Hereafter.
orig: أو تقول حين ترى العذاب لو أن لي كرة فأكون من المحسنين

translation: Yes, My verses have already come to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning from God to those who reject His signs and evidence, and who are arrogant in their rejection. It suggests that God has already provided clear guidance and proofs, but some people choose to disbelieve and turn away from the truth out of pride and arrogance. The verse emphasizes that such an attitude of disbelief and arrogance will lead to being counted among the disbelievers, who will face the consequences of their rejection.
orig: بلى قد جاءتك آياتي فكذبت بها واستكبرت وكنت من الكافرين

translation: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah [with] their faces blackened. Is not in Hell a residence for the arrogant?
interpretation: This verse speaks of the consequences of arrogance and lying about Allah on the Day of Resurrection. Those who were arrogant and lied about Allah will have their faces blackened, indicating their disgrace and humiliation. The verse then poses a rhetorical question, asking if Hell is not the fitting abode for such arrogant individuals. This serves as a warning to those who would dare to be arrogant and lie about Allah, as they will face severe punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: ويوم القيامة ترى الذين كذبوا على الله وجوههم مسودة أليس في جهنم مثوى للمتكبرين

translation: And Allah will deliver those who feared Him by their attainment; no evil will touch them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are righteous and fear Allah will be saved from harm and distress. They will be granted success and deliverance by Allah, and will be spared from the negative consequences that befall the wicked. This is a promise of protection and peace for the God-fearing, who will not have to experience the sorrow and grief that afflicts those who reject faith.
orig: وينجي الله الذين اتقوا بمفازتهم لا يمسهم السوء ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is, over all things, a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah (God) is the sole Creator of the entire universe and everything in it. He is the All-Powerful and All-Knowing, and has complete authority and control over all of His creation. As the Disposer of affairs, Allah governs and manages the affairs of the universe according to His divine wisdom and plan. This affirms the belief that Allah is the supreme and omnipotent deity, to whom all creation is subservient.
orig: الله خالق كل شيء وهو على كل شيء وكيل

translation: To Him belongs the keys of the heavens and the earth. And those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah - it is those who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone has control and authority over the heavens and the earth. Those who reject or deny the signs and revelations of Allah will be the ultimate losers, as they have turned away from the truth and the path to salvation.
orig: له مقاليد السماوات والأرض والذين كفروا بآيات الله أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: Say, "Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?"
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to ask the disbelievers who are worshipping idols and false deities, whether they are ordering him to worship anything other than the one true God, Allah. The verse refers to the disbelievers as "ignorant ones" because they have rejected the message of monotheism and the worship of the one God, and instead have chosen to worship false gods and idols. The verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping anything other than Allah, the Creator and Sustainer of the universe.
orig: قل أفغير الله تأمروني أعبد أيها الجاهلون

translation: And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you that if you should associate [anything] with Allah, your work would surely become worthless, and you would surely be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone and not associating any partners with Him. It warns that if one engages in polytheism or idolatry, their good deeds and efforts will be rendered worthless, and they will be among the losers in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a strong admonition against shirk (associating partners with Allah) and a reminder to maintain a pure and sincere faith in the Oneness of Allah.
orig: ولقد أوحي إليك وإلى الذين من قبلك لئن أشركت ليحبطن عملك ولتكونن من الخاسرين

translation: Rather, worship Allah and be among the grateful.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to worship Allah alone and be thankful for His blessings. It emphasizes that the true object of worship is Allah, not any other deity or creation. Being grateful to Allah for His guidance, provision, and mercy is an essential part of one's faith and relationship with the Divine.
orig: بل الله فاعبد وكن من الشاكرين

translation: And they have not appraised Allah with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be [within] His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over the entire universe. It conveys that humans cannot fully comprehend the greatness and majesty of Allah, as His power and control over all creation is beyond our limited understanding. On the Day of Resurrection, the earth and the heavens will be subject to Allah's complete dominion, with the earth being in His grasp and the heavens being folded in His right hand. This serves as a reminder of Allah's transcendence and the futility of associating partners with Him, as He is exalted and free from any such associations.
orig: وما قدروا الله حق قدره والأرض جميعا قبضته يوم القيامة والسماوات مطويات بيمينه سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.
interpretation: This verse describes the events of the Day of Resurrection. The blowing of the Trumpet signals the end of the world, and all living beings in the heavens and on earth will die, except those whom Allah wills to spare. Then, the Trumpet will be blown again, and all the dead will be resurrected and stand before Allah, ready to be judged for their deeds in life.
orig: ونفخ في الصور فصعق من في السماوات ومن في الأرض إلا من شاء الله ثم نفخ فيه أخرى فإذا هم قيام ينظرون

translation: And the earth shone with the light of its Lord, and the Book was placed, and the Prophets and the witnesses were brought, and it was judged between them with truth, and they were not wronged.
interpretation: This verse describes the events of the Day of Judgment, when the earth will be illuminated by the light of Allah, and the Book of Deeds will be presented. The Prophets and those who bore witness to the truth will be brought forth, and a fair judgment will be passed upon all people, with no one being wronged. This emphasizes the ultimate accountability and justice that will prevail on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: وأشرقت الأرض بنور ربها ووضع الكتاب وجيء بالنبيين والشهداء وقضي بينهم بالحق وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And every soul will be recompensed [in full for] what it did, and He is best aware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, each person will be held accountable for their actions in this life. Allah, being all-knowing, is fully aware of everything that people do, whether it is good or bad. This serves as a reminder to believers to strive to do righteous deeds, as they will be rewarded for them, and to refrain from sinful actions, as they will be held responsible for them.
orig: ووفيت كل نفس ما عملت وهو أعلم بما يفعلون

translation: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates are opened and its keepers will say to them, "Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who have rejected faith and disbelieved in God. They will be driven to Hell in groups, and when they reach it, the gates of Hell will be opened. The keepers of Hell will ask them if messengers did not come to them, reciting the verses of God and warning them about the Day of Judgment. The disbelievers will acknowledge this, but they will also say that the decree of punishment has been established upon them due to their rejection of faith. This verse highlights the accountability that the disbelievers will face on the Day of Judgment for their rejection of God's message and warnings.
orig: وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم زمرا حتى إذا جاءوها فتحت أبوابها وقال لهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم رسل منكم يتلون عليكم آيات ربكم وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا قالوا بلى ولكن حقت كلمة العذاب على الكافرين

translation: It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the arrogant and those who reject the message of Islam. It describes the fate of those who are prideful and refuse to submit to the will of God. The verse emphasizes that the punishment of Hell is eternal, and that it is a wretched and undesirable place to reside. The message is clear that arrogance and refusal to accept the truth of Islam will lead to a terrible and unending punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: قيل ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups until, when they reach it, while its gates have been opened and its keepers say, "Peace be upon you; you have become pure; so enter it to abide eternally therein."
interpretation: This verse describes the reward for those who have been righteous and feared their Lord. They will be gathered in groups and led to Paradise, where the gates will be opened for them. The keepers of Paradise will greet them with the words "Peace be upon you; you have become pure", welcoming them to enter and dwell there eternally. This highlights the honor, dignity and eternal bliss that awaits the righteous in the Hereafter as a result of their faith and good deeds in this life.
orig: وسيق الذين اتقوا ربهم إلى الجنة زمرا حتى إذا جاءوها وفتحت أبوابها وقال لهم خزنتها سلام عليكم طبتم فادخلوها خالدين

translation: And they say, "Praise to Allah , who has fulfilled for us His promise and made us inherit the earth [so] we may settle in the Garden wherever we will. And excellent is the reward of [righteous] workers."
interpretation: This verse expresses the gratitude and praise of the believers towards Allah for fulfilling His promise and allowing them to inherit the land and settle in Paradise as they wish. It highlights the reward and blessings that await the righteous workers who have been steadfast in their faith and deeds.
orig: وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقنا وعده وأورثنا الأرض نتبوأ من الجنة حيث نشاء فنعم أجر العاملين

translation: And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, exalting [Allah] with praise of their Lord. And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said, "[All] praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse describes the angels surrounding the Throne of Allah, glorifying and praising their Lord. It emphasizes that all judgments are made with justice and truth, and that ultimately, all praise and glory belongs to Allah, the Lord of all the worlds.
orig: وترى الملائكة حافين من حول العرش يسبحون بحمد ربهم وقضي بينهم بالحق وقيل الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Ha, Mim.
interpretation: This is one of the 'Mysterious Letters' (al-Muqatta'at) that appear at the beginning of some chapters of the Qur'an. The exact meaning and significance of these letters is not fully known, but they are believed to be part of the divine wisdom and knowledge contained within the Qur'an. They serve to emphasize the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and to draw the reader's attention to the deeper meanings and messages within the text.
orig: حم

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation from Allah, the Almighty and All-Wise. It emphasizes that the Qur'an is not the work of man, but a direct communication from the All-Powerful and All-Knowing God. This affirms the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, and calls upon the believers to accept and follow its teachings with unwavering faith and submission.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم

translation: The Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, the Severe in punishment, the Possessor of abundance. There is no deity except Him; to Him is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse describes the attributes of Allah as the One who forgives sins, accepts repentance, is severe in punishment, and possesses abundant blessings. It affirms the oneness of Allah and that the final destination of all people is to return to Him.
orig: غافر الذنب وقابل التوب شديد العقاب ذي الطول لا إله إلا هو إليه المصير

translation: None argue concerning the Revelations of Allah but those who disbelieve, so let not their [ostentatious] movement in the cities deceive you.
interpretation: This verse warns against being deceived by the outward appearance and movements of those who disbelieve in Allah's signs and revelations. Their apparent wealth, power and influence in the world should not distract one from the reality that they are in fact rejecting the truth of Allah's message. The true believers should not be swayed by the temporary success of the disbelievers, as their ultimate fate will be the punishment of Allah.
orig: ما يجادل في آيات الله إلا الذين كفروا فلا يغررك تقلبهم في البلاد

translation: The people of Noah and the factions after them denied (the truth) before them, and every nation intended to seize their messenger, and they argued by [using] falsehood to [attempt to] invalidate thereby the truth. So I seized them, and how [terrible] was My penalty.
interpretation: This verse highlights how previous nations and communities rejected the divine messages brought by the prophets sent to them. They sought to undermine and discredit the truth, arguing with falsehood in an attempt to invalidate it. However, God ultimately seized them and punished them for their rejection and hostility towards the truth. This serves as a warning that those who reject the truth and argue against it with falsehood will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح والأحزاب من بعدهم وهمت كل أمة برسولهم ليأخذوه وجادلوا بالباطل ليدحضوا به الحق فأخذتهم فكيف كان عقاب

translation: And thus the word of your Lord has come into effect upon those who disbelieved - that they will be the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the decree of Allah has been established against those who reject faith and disbelieve in Him. They will be consigned to the Fire of Hell as a consequence of their rejection of the truth. This is a just and inevitable outcome, as Allah’s word is absolute and cannot be changed. The verse serves as a warning to those who turn away from the guidance of Allah, reminding them of the grave consequences of their actions.
orig: وكذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين كفروا أنهم أصحاب النار

translation: Those who bear the Throne and those around it exalt [Allah] with praise of their Lord and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who have believed, [saying], "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire."
interpretation: This verse describes the angels who bear the Throne of Allah and those around it, who constantly glorify and praise Allah, and pray for the forgiveness of the believers. It emphasizes that Allah's mercy and knowledge encompass all things, and that He forgives those who repent and follow His path, protecting them from the punishment of Hell. The verse highlights the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness, as well as the role of the angels in interceding for the believers.
orig: الذين يحملون العرش ومن حوله يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويؤمنون به ويستغفرون للذين آمنوا ربنا وسعت كل شيء رحمة وعلما فاغفر للذين تابوا واتبعوا سبيلك وقهم عذاب الجحيم

translation: Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse expresses a supplication to Allah, the Lord, to admit the believers into the eternal Gardens of Paradise which He has promised them. The supplication extends to include the righteous among their forefathers, spouses, and offspring, acknowledging that it is Allah alone who is the Almighty and the All-Wise, and that He alone has the power to grant this request.
orig: ربنا وأدخلهم جنات عدن التي وعدتهم ومن صلح من آبائهم وأزواجهم وذرياتهم إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: And protect them from evil deeds. And whoever is protected from the evil of that Day - [i.e., the Day of Resurrection] - then indeed, he has attained mercy. And that is the great success.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking protection from Allah against evil deeds and the consequences of the Day of Resurrection. It promises that those who are protected from the evil of that Day will attain Allah's mercy, which is the greatest success one can achieve. The interpretation suggests that through seeking Allah's protection and guidance, one can be saved from the punishment and trials of the Hereafter and instead earn Allah's forgiveness and eternal bliss.
orig: وقهم السيئات ومن تق السيئات يومئذ فقد رحمته وذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve will be called to [enter] the Fire, [while] their time [in this world] has been prolonged. [This is so] that they may warn others, and that they [themselves] may be warned, so that they will turn [to God].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith in God will ultimately be called to face the punishment of the Hellfire. Their time in this world has been extended, not out of mercy, but so that they may serve as a warning to others and have the chance to reflect and turn back to belief in God. The verse conveys the gravity of disbelief, as the punishment of God is far greater than any self-imposed suffering or regret that the disbelievers may experience.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ينادون لمقت الله أكبر من مقتكم أنفسكم إذ تدعون إلى الإيمان فتكفرون

translation: They will say, "Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and given us life twice, and we have acknowledged our sins. So is there to [any] exit from this [predicament]?"
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, when they will acknowledge their sins and ask God if there is any way for them to escape the punishment they deserve. The "two deaths" refer to their initial death in this world and their second death in the Hereafter, while the "two lives" refer to their life in this world and their resurrection for the Final Judgment. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of acknowledging one's sins and seeking forgiveness from God, as there is no escape from the consequences of one's actions on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: قالوا ربنا أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين فاعترفنا بذنوبنا فهل إلى خروج من سبيل

translation: That is because when Allah alone is invoked, you disbelieve; but if others are associated with Him, you believe. So the judgement is with Allah, the Most High, the Grand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping Allah alone, without associating any partners with Him. It states that when people are called to believe in the Oneness of Allah, they often reject it and disbelieve. However, when they are called to believe in associating others with Allah, they readily accept it. The verse then affirms that the ultimate judgement and decision-making belongs to Allah, the Most High and the Grand, who is the only true deity worthy of worship.
orig: ذلكم بأنه إذا دعي الله وحده كفرتم وإن يشرك به تؤمنوا فالحكم لله العلي الكبير

translation: He it is who shows you His signs and sends down for you from the sky, provision. And none will remember except he who turns back [in repentance].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and power, as He is the One who reveals His signs and provides sustenance from the heavens. It also highlights the importance of remembrance and turning back to God in repentance, as only those who do so will truly benefit from God's guidance and provision.
orig: هو الذي يريكم آياته وينزل لكم من السماء رزقا وما يتذكر إلا من ينيب

translation: So call upon Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, although the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to call upon Allah (God) with sincerity and devotion, even in the face of opposition or dislike from those who reject faith. It emphasizes that one's worship and devotion to Allah should be pure, without any taint of hypocrisy or ulterior motives, regardless of what others may think or say. The verse reminds us that our duty is to remain steadfast in our faith and worship of Allah, even if it is unpopular or displeasing to those who do not believe.
orig: فادعوا الله مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون

translation: The Exalter of Degrees, Owner of the Throne; He places the inspiration of His command upon whom He wills of His servants, to warn [them of] the Day of Meeting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme power and authority of God, who is the "Exalter of Degrees" and the "Owner of the Throne". He is the one who sends down the revelation ("the inspiration of His command") to whomever He chooses among His servants, in order to warn them about the Day of Judgment when they will have to account for their deeds. This highlights God's absolute sovereignty and control over the affairs of the universe and mankind.
orig: رفيع الدرجات ذو العرش يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده لينذر يوم التلاق

translation: The Day they will [all] emerge, not a thing about them will be concealed from Allah. [And it will be said], "To whom belongs [all] sovereignty this Day?" [To] Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Judgment, when all people will be resurrected and stand before Allah. On that Day, nothing about them will be hidden from Allah, who is the Sovereign and the Prevailing. The verse emphasizes that Allah alone has dominion and control over all things on that momentous Day.
orig: يوم هم بارزون لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء لمن الملك اليوم لله الواحد القهار

translation: This Day every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. No injustice this Day. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, every person will be held accountable for their actions and deeds in this life. There will be no injustice, as Allah is swift and precise in His reckoning. It serves as a reminder to believers to live righteously and do good, as they will be rewarded for their efforts, and to avoid wrongdoing, as they will be held responsible for their misdeeds.
orig: اليوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت لا ظلم اليوم إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the hearts will [cut] up to the throats, filled with distress. For the wrongdoers there will be no devoted friend and no intercessor [to be] obeyed.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers about the Day of Judgment, when they will be filled with regret and their hearts will be filled with distress. On that day, the wrongdoers will have no one to help them or intercede on their behalf, as they will have no devoted friend or intercessor whose plea will be accepted.
orig: وأنذرهم يوم الآزفة إذ القلوب لدى الحناجر كاظمين ما للظالمين من حميم ولا شفيع يطاع

translation: He knows the [deceptive] looks of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and all-knowing nature. He is aware of the hidden thoughts, intentions and deceptions that people try to conceal, even the subtle glances and expressions that betray their true feelings. Nothing can be hidden from Allah, the All-Knowing.
orig: يعلم خائنة الأعين وما تخفي الصدور

translation: And Allah judges with the truth. And those they invoke besides Him judge not with any [legal] judgment. Indeed, Allah - He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the only true and just judge, and that any other deities or powers that people may invoke have no real authority or ability to judge. It highlights that Allah alone is all-hearing and all-seeing, and thus the only one qualified to make fair and righteous judgments. The verse serves to reinforce the belief that Allah is the supreme and sole authority, and that one should not seek judgment or guidance from any other source besides Him.
orig: والله يقضي بالحق والذين يدعون من دونه لا يقضون بشيء إن الله هو السميع البصير

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power and in impressions [left] upon the land, but Allah seized them for their sins, and they had from Allah no protector.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the fate of previous generations who were more powerful and influential than the present one. Despite their strength and impact, they were ultimately destroyed due to their sins and transgressions. This serves as a warning that no one is immune from the consequences of their actions, and that only Allah can truly protect and save them. The verse emphasizes the importance of learning from history and recognizing the futility of relying on one's own power or worldly achievements, as true protection and salvation can only come from Allah.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين كانوا من قبلهم كانوا هم أشد منهم قوة وآثارا في الأرض فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم وما كان لهم من الله من واق

translation: That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Powerful and severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences faced by those who reject the clear signs and messages brought by the prophets of Allah. When the people stubbornly refuse to believe and heed the guidance, they incur the wrath of Allah, who is all-Powerful and metes out severe punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who turn away from the truth and choose to disbelieve, despite the availability of clear evidence and divine guidance.
orig: ذلك بأنهم كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فكفروا فأخذهم الله إنه قوي شديد العقاب

translation: And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah sent the Prophet Moses with clear signs and proofs to establish the truth of his message and the divine origin of his mission. The "clear authority" refers to the miracles and evidence that Allah granted to Moses to substantiate his prophethood and to compel the Pharaoh and his people to believe in the One God. This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the message brought by Moses and the clarity of the proof he presented to the people.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

translation: To Pharaoh, Haman, and Qaroun, and they said: 'A lying sorcerer.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the response of Pharaoh, Haman, and Qaroun (Korah) to the message of Prophet Moses. They dismissed him as a "lying sorcerer", rejecting his call to worship only Allah and to free the Israelites from their oppression. This highlights the arrogance and disbelief of the powerful leaders who refused to submit to the truth of God's message, preferring to maintain their own authority and worldly status.
orig: إلى فرعون وهامان وقارون فقالوا ساحر كذاب

translation: And when he came to them with the truth from Us, they said, "Kill the followers of him who are with him and keep them alive." But the plan of the disbelievers is not [except] in error.
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when the Prophet came to them with the truth from God. Instead of accepting the message, they plotted to kill the believers and spare the women. This shows the evil and misguided nature of the disbelievers' plan, which is doomed to fail as it is based on error and misguidance rather than truth and guidance.
orig: فلما جاءهم بالحق من عندنا قالوا اقتلوا أبناء الذين آمنوا معه واستحيوا نساءهم وما كيد الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: And Pharaoh said, "Leave me to kill Moses and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he may change your religion or that he may cause corruption in the land."
interpretation: This verse depicts Pharaoh's fear and hostility towards Moses. Pharaoh wanted to kill Moses, fearing that Moses would influence the people to change their religion or cause disorder and corruption in the land. The verse highlights Pharaoh's tyrannical and oppressive nature, as he sought to eliminate a perceived threat to his power and control over the people.
orig: وقال فرعون ذروني أقتل موسى وليدع ربه إني أخاف أن يبدل دينكم أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد

translation: And Moses said, "Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account."
interpretation: This verse expresses Moses` reliance on God and his plea for protection from those who are arrogant and do not believe in the Day of Judgment. It highlights the importance of humility, faith, and accountability before God. Moses seeks refuge in the Lord, who is the Lord of all, including the arrogant who deny the Day of Reckoning. This verse encourages believers to turn to God for guidance and protection against those who are prideful and lack faith in the ultimate judgment.
orig: وقال موسى إني عذت بربي وربكم من كل متكبر لا يؤمن بيوم الحساب

translation: And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh who concealed his faith said, "Do you kill a man [merely] because he says, 'My Lord is Allah' and has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? And if he is a liar, then upon him is [the consequence of] his lie; but if he is truthful, there will strike you some of what he promises you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar."
interpretation: This verse highlights the courage and faith of a believer from the family of Pharaoh, who spoke up in defense of Prophet Moses. Despite the risk to his own life, he questioned the intention to kill a man solely for professing belief in Allah and presenting clear evidence from Allah. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of impartial judgment, where one should not condemn a person based on their claim of faith, but rather assess the truthfulness of their message. The verse also warns against being a "transgressor and a liar", as such individuals will not be guided by Allah.
orig: وقال رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون يكتم إيمانه أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله وقد جاءكم بالبينات من ربكم وإن يك كاذبا فعليه كذبه وإن يك صادقا يصبكم بعض الذي يعدكم إن الله لا يهدي من هو مسرف كذاب

translation: O my people, yours is the kingdom today, you being dominant in the land. But who will save us from the punishment of Allah if it comes to us?" Pharaoh said: "I show you only that which I see (correct), and I guide you only to the path of right policy."
interpretation: This verse describes a dialogue between the Pharaoh and his people. The Pharaoh boasts of the power and dominance of his kingdom, implying that they have no need for God's help. However, he acknowledges the possibility of God's punishment befalling them, to which he responds by claiming that he can guide them to the right path through his own wisdom and policies, without need for divine guidance. This verse highlights the Pharaoh's arrogance and rejection of God's authority, as well as his attempt to portray himself as self-sufficient and all-knowing.
orig: يا قوم لكم الملك اليوم ظاهرين في الأرض فمن ينصرنا من بأس الله إن جاءنا قال فرعون ما أريكم إلا ما أرى وما أهديكم إلا سبيل الرشاد

translation: And the one who believed said, "O my people, indeed I fear for you [a fate] like the day of the [former] companies"
