interpretation: This verse refers to a believer who warns his people of a fate similar to that of the previous nations who rejected the message of God's messengers. The "day of the [former] companies" likely refers to a day of judgement or punishment that befell previous disbelieving communities. The believer is cautioning his people to heed the message of God and avoid a similar fate of destruction and ruin.
orig: وقال الذي آمن يا قوم إني أخاف عليكم مثل يوم الأحزاب

translation: The example of the people of Noah and 'Aad and Thamud and those after them. And Allah intends no injustice to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse draws a parallel between the fate of previous nations who rejected the message of God's Oneness and the ultimate justice that will befall those who persist in disbelief and wrongdoing. It serves as a warning to humanity that Allah does not intend any injustice or oppression towards His servants, but will hold them accountable for their actions. The lesson is that those who turn away from the truth and oppress others will face the consequences of their choices, just as the peoples of Noah, 'Aad, and Thamud did in the past.
orig: مثل دأب قوم نوح وعاد وثمود والذين من بعدهم وما الله يريد ظلما للعباد

translation: And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Summons
interpretation: This verse expresses the Prophet's concern and warning for his people about the Day of Resurrection, when all people will be gathered and held accountable for their actions. The "Day of Summons" refers to the Day of Judgment, when everyone will be called to stand before God and answer for their deeds in life. The Prophet is urging his people to prepare for this momentous day by believing in God, doing good, and avoiding evil, so that they may be saved from the punishment that awaits the disbelievers.
orig: ويا قوم إني أخاف عليكم يوم التناد

translation: The Day you turn your backs and flee, there will be no protector from Allah, and whomever Allah sends astray - for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse warns that on the Day of Judgement, when people try to flee from the reckoning, there will be no one to protect them from Allah's punishment. It emphasizes that those whom Allah leaves to go astray will have no one to guide them back to the right path. The verse underscores the futility of trying to escape Allah's judgment and the importance of following the guidance provided by Him.
orig: يوم تولون مدبرين ما لكم من الله من عاصم ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: And Joseph had already come to you before with clear proofs, but you remained in doubt of that which he brought to you, [so] until when he died, you said, "Never will Allah send a messenger after him." Thus does Allah leave astray he who is a transgressor and a doubter.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) in the Quran. It highlights how the people of Yusuf's time initially rejected his message and the clear signs he brought, even though he was a prophet of God. They remained in doubt until Yusuf passed away, at which point they stubbornly claimed that God would never send another messenger after him. This verse serves as a warning that God can lead astray those who are excessive in their transgression and doubt, refusing to accept the truth even when it is made clear to them.
orig: ولقد جاءكم يوسف من قبل بالبينات فما زلتم في شك مما جاءكم به حتى إذا هلك قلتم لن يبعث الله من بعده رسولا كذلك يضل الله من هو مسرف مرتاب

translation: Those who dispute about the verses of Allah without [any] authority having come to them - great is [their] disgust in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who have believed. Thus does Allah seal over every heart [belonging to] an arrogant tyrant.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who argue against the verses of the Quran without any legitimate basis or authority. Their arrogance and rejection of the divine signs is seen as abhorrent by Allah and the believers. The verse suggests that Allah seals the hearts of those who are arrogant and tyrannical, preventing them from accepting the truth.
orig: الذين يجادلون في آيات الله بغير سلطان أتاهم كبر مقتا عند الله وعند الذين آمنوا كذلك يطبع الله على كل قلب متكبر جبار

translation: And Pharaoh said, "O Haman, construct for me a tower that I may reach the ways -
interpretation: This verse depicts Pharaoh's arrogance and desire for power. He commands his minister Haman to build him a tower, likely to symbolize his might and reach the "ways" or means to achieve his ambitions. This reflects Pharaoh's belief in his own superiority and his attempt to control and dominate, rather than submit to the will of God.
orig: وقال فرعون يا هامان ابن لي صرحا لعلي أبلغ الأسباب

translation: And the causes of the heavens, so let me look at the God of Moses, and I think he is a liar. And thus, the evil of his deeds was made fair-seeming to Pharaoh, and he was averted from the (right) way. And the plot of Pharaoh led only to ruin.
interpretation: This verse describes the arrogance and disbelief of Pharaoh, who refused to believe in the signs of God and the message of Moses. Pharaoh claimed that he could not see the evidence for the existence of God, and he dismissed Moses as a liar. Furthermore, Pharaoh's evil deeds were made to seem fair and justified to him, causing him to turn away from the right path. However, the verse makes it clear that Pharaoh's plot and scheming ultimately led to his downfall and ruin. This serves as a warning against arrogance, disbelief, and turning away from the guidance of God.
orig: أسباب السماوات فأطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه كاذبا وكذلك زين لفرعون سوء عمله وصد عن السبيل وما كيد فرعون إلا في تباب

translation: And he who believed said, "O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the way of sound judgment."
interpretation: This verse is referring to a believer who is calling his people to follow him and the path of guidance and wisdom. The interpretation is that the believer is urging his people to listen to him and follow the righteous path, as he can guide them towards what is best and most beneficial for them.
orig: وقال الذي آمن يا قوم اتبعون أهدكم سبيل الرشاد

translation: O my people, this worldly life is only [temporary] enjoyment, and indeed, the Hereafter - that is the Home of [Permanent] Settlement.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the life of this world is temporary and fleeting, and that the true and permanent abode is the Hereafter. It encourages people to not be deceived by the allure of this world and to instead focus on preparing for the eternal life in the Hereafter, which is the true "Home of [Permanent] Settlement." This serves as a reminder that the ultimate purpose of our existence is the Hereafter, and that we should strive to do good deeds in this life in order to attain success in the Hereafter.
orig: يا قوم إنما هذه الحياة الدنيا متاع وإن الآخرة هي دار القرار

translation: Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except by the like thereof, but whoever does a righteous deed, whether male or female, while he is a believer - those will enter Paradise, being given provision therein without account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of just retribution in Islam. It states that whoever commits a wrongful act will be punished accordingly, but whoever performs a good deed, whether a man or a woman, and is a believer, will be rewarded with entry into Paradise and will be provided for without limit. This highlights the importance of faith and righteous actions, and that both men and women are equally accountable before God and can earn His pleasure through their deeds.
orig: من عمل سيئة فلا يجزى إلا مثلها ومن عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فأولئك يدخلون الجنة يرزقون فيها بغير حساب

translation: And O my people, why do I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question posed by a prophet or messenger of God, addressing his people. It expresses the prophet's bewilderment and frustration at the fact that he is calling his people to the path of salvation and righteousness, but they are instead inviting him to the Fire of Hell. The verse highlights the contrast between the prophet's sincere efforts to guide his people towards God's pleasure and their rejection of his message, which leads them towards the punishment of the Hereafter.
orig: ويا قوم ما لي أدعوكم إلى النجاة وتدعونني إلى النار

translation: You call me to disbelieve in Allah and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, and I call you to the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse expresses the Prophet's rejection of the polytheistic beliefs and practices of his people. He makes it clear that he cannot accept their call to disbelieve in the One true God and to associate partners with Him, as he has no knowledge or evidence to support such beliefs. Instead, he invites them to worship the Almighty, All-Forgiving God, who alone deserves worship and obedience.
orig: تدعونني لأكفر بالله وأشرك به ما ليس لي به علم وأنا أدعوكم إلى العزيز الغفار

translation: Assuredly, that to which you call me has no [legitimate] call in this world or in the Hereafter, and that our return is to Allah, and that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the beliefs and practices that the disbelievers are inviting the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to are false and have no validity in this world or the Hereafter. It affirms that the ultimate destination for all people is Allah, and that those who exceed the proper bounds (i.e. the transgressors) will be the inhabitants of the Fire (Hell). The verse serves as a warning against following falsehood and a reminder of the importance of submitting to the truth of Islam and the worship of the one true God.
orig: لا جرم أنما تدعونني إليه ليس له دعوة في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة وأن مردنا إلى الله وأن المسرفين هم أصحاب النار

translation: Then you will remember what I have told you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to remember the message and teachings conveyed to them, and to entrust their affairs to Allah, the All-Seeing and All-Knowing. It emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah and submitting to His will, as He is fully aware of the conditions and needs of His servants.
orig: فستذكرون ما أقول لكم وأفوض أمري إلى الله إن الله بصير بالعباد

translation: So Allah protected him from the evils they plotted, and the people of Pharaoh were enveloped by the worst of punishment.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah protected the Prophet Moses from the evil plots and schemes of Pharaoh and his people. Despite their efforts to harm Moses, Allah shielded him from their plots and instead brought down a severe punishment upon Pharaoh and his followers. This highlights Allah's power to protect His messengers and the ultimate defeat of those who oppose the truth.
orig: فوقاه الله سيئات ما مكروا وحاق بآل فرعون سوء العذاب

translation: They will be exposed to the Fire morning and evening, and on the Day the Hour appears [it will be said], "Make the people of Pharaoh enter the severest punishment."
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal punishment in the Hellfire that will be inflicted upon the people of Pharaoh as a consequence of their disbelief, arrogance and oppression. They will be subjected to the torment of the Fire continuously, morning and evening, and on the Day of Resurrection, they will face the severest of punishments. This serves as a warning to those who defy Allah and His messengers, and a reminder of the dire consequences of rejecting faith and engaging in wrongdoing.
orig: النار يعرضون عليها غدوا وعشيا ويوم تقوم الساعة أدخلوا آل فرعون أشد العذاب

translation: And when they will dispute in the Fire, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers, so can you avail us anything against the Fire?"
interpretation: This verse describes a scene on the Day of Judgment, where the arrogant and the weak will be disputing in the Hellfire. The weak, who had blindly followed the arrogant in this world, will ask the arrogant if they can do anything to help them or reduce their share of the punishment in the Hellfire. The implication is that the arrogant will be unable to help the weak, as each person is accountable for their own deeds. This highlights the futility of following others blindly and the importance of taking responsibility for one’s own actions.
orig: وإذ يتحاجون في النار فيقول الضعفاء للذين استكبروا إنا كنا لكم تبعا فهل أنتم مغنون عنا نصيبا من النار

translation: Those who were arrogant will say, "Indeed, we are all [within] it [i.e., Hell]. Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants."
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the arrogant and proud who rejected the truth of God's message. On the Day of Judgment, they will be forced to acknowledge that they were wrong and that God has justly judged between them and the believers. Their arrogance and pride will be of no avail, and they will be humbled before the Almighty. This serves as a warning against the dangers of arrogance and a reminder to submit humbly to God's will.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا إنا كل فيها إن الله قد حكم بين العباد

translation: And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Invoke your Lord to lighten for us [even] a day from the punishment."
interpretation: This verse describes the desperate plea of the inhabitants of Hell to the angels guarding it, asking them to intercede with Allah to lessen their torment, even if for just a single day. It highlights the immense suffering and regret experienced by those who rejected faith and are now facing the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment in Hell and the futility of seeking relief once one has been condemned to it.
orig: وقال الذين في النار لخزنة جهنم ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب

translation: They said, "Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs?" They said, "Yes." They [the disbelievers] said, "Then call [to your aid], and the call of the disbelievers is not [at all] but in error."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and rejection of the disbelievers, even in the face of clear proofs and signs from the messengers of God. The disbelievers acknowledge that the messengers came with clear evidence, yet they still refuse to believe and instead challenge the believers to call upon their own gods, implying that the call of the disbelievers is futile and misguided. This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and submission to God, even in the face of opposition and rejection from those who deny the truth.
orig: قالوا أولم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبينات قالوا بلى قالوا فادعوا وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah will support and aid His messengers and those who believe in them, both in this life and on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that the believers will be victorious and their faith will be vindicated, even in the face of opposition and persecution from disbelievers. The "Day when the witnesses will stand" refers to the Day of Resurrection, when all people will be held accountable for their beliefs and actions, and the messengers of Allah will testify to the truth they conveyed.
orig: إنا لننصر رسلنا والذين آمنوا في الحياة الدنيا ويوم يقوم الأشهاد

translation: The day when the wrongdoers' excuse will not benefit them, and they will have the curse and the worst home.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the wrongdoers will not be able to offer any valid excuse for their misdeeds. They will be condemned and cursed, and will face the worst possible consequences for their actions in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes that there will be no escape or justification for those who have oppressed others or committed sins, and they will be held accountable for their choices in life.
orig: يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the guidance, and We had inherited the Children of Israel the Scripture
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God had bestowed upon Moses the guidance and revealed to him the divine scripture, which was then passed down to the Children of Israel. This highlights the continuity of God's revelation and the importance of the scriptures in guiding the people of Israel.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الهدى وأورثنا بني إسرائيل الكتاب

translation: Guidance and a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a source of guidance and a reminder for those who possess wisdom and intellect. It is a divine revelation that provides direction and insight for those who are willing to ponder and reflect upon its teachings. The Qur'an is not merely a book of rules, but a comprehensive guide that helps individuals navigate the complexities of life and develop a deeper understanding of the divine.
orig: هدى وذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: So be patient. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And ask forgiveness for your sin and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be patient and steadfast, as the promises of Allah are true and will come to pass. It also instructs them to seek forgiveness for their sins and to glorify and praise Allah throughout the day, both in the evening and the morning. This emphasizes the importance of maintaining a constant connection with Allah and seeking His guidance and forgiveness.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق واستغفر لذنبك وسبح بحمد ربك بالعشي والإبكار

translation: Indeed, those who dispute concerning the verses of Allah without [any] authority having come to them - there is not [anything] within their breasts except [ostentatious] pride, [the extent of] which they cannot reach. So seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who argue against the verses of the Qur'an without any valid justification or evidence. Their arguments stem from arrogance and pride, not from a sincere search for the truth. The verse encourages seeking refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing and All-Seeing, who is aware of the true intentions behind such disputes.
orig: إن الذين يجادلون في آيات الله بغير سلطان أتاهم إن في صدورهم إلا كبر ما هم ببالغيه فاستعذ بالله إنه هو السميع البصير

translation: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vastness and complexity of the creation of the heavens and the earth, which is greater than the creation of mankind. However, most people are unaware of this fact and do not fully comprehend the magnitude of Allah's creation. This serves as a reminder of the power and wisdom of the Creator, and encourages people to reflect on the signs of Allah's existence and the purpose of their own creation.
orig: لخلق السماوات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And not equal are the blind and the seeing, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer. Little do you remember."
interpretation: This verse draws a distinction between those who are spiritually blind and those who can see the truth, as well as between those who believe and do good deeds and those who do evil. The implication is that the former groups are not equal in status or worth before God. The verse serves as a reminder to reflect on and remember this fundamental truth, as indicated by the final phrase "Little do you remember."
orig: وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ولا المسيء قليلا ما تتذكرون

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming - there is no doubt about it, but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment (the Hour) and the fact that it will inevitably come to pass. However, it also highlights the lack of faith and belief in this truth among the majority of people. The interpretation suggests that people should prepare for the Hereafter and have faith in God's promise, as the Hour will come regardless of whether they believe in it or not.
orig: إن الساعة لآتية لا ريب فيها ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you." Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] contemptible.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to call upon and invoke Allah, the Lord, as He promises to respond to their prayers and supplications. It also warns that those who are arrogant and refuse to worship Allah will enter the hellfire in a state of humiliation and disgrace.
orig: وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين

translation: Allah is the one who has made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day giving sight. Indeed, Allah is to the people full of bounty, but most of the people do not show gratitude.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's blessings upon humanity by creating the cycle of night and day. The night provides a time for rest and tranquility, while the day brings light and visibility. This is a manifestation of Allah's grace and generosity towards His creation. However, the verse also notes that most people fail to appreciate and be thankful for these blessings, which is a shortcoming on their part.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of Allah as the sole Creator of the universe. It challenges the people to reflect on how they can be misled and deceived into worshipping other deities when it is so clear that Allah alone is worthy of worship. The verse serves as a reminder to turn away from false beliefs and submit to the one true God.
orig: ذلكم الله ربكم خالق كل شيء لا إله إلا هو فأنى تؤفكون

translation: Thus does Allah delude the one who is a habitual liar and a denier of the Signs of Allah.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who persistently reject and deny the signs and revelations of Allah. It suggests that such people are led astray and deluded by their own arrogance, stubbornness and refusal to accept the truth. The verse conveys a warning that those who deny Allah's signs will ultimately be misguided and face the consequences of their rejection.
orig: كذلك يؤفك الذين كانوا بآيات الله يجحدون

translation: Allah is the One who made for you the earth a place of settlement and the sky a structure and formed you and perfected your forms and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord; then blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the attributes of Allah as the Creator who has provided for humanity in numerous ways. It highlights Allah's power in creating the earth and the sky, as well as shaping and perfecting the forms of human beings. Additionally, it mentions that Allah has provided sustenance and good things for people. This serves to remind us of Allah's blessings and to encourage gratitude and worship of the Lord of all the worlds.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الأرض قرارا والسماء بناء وصوركم فأحسن صوركم ورزقكم من الطيبات ذلكم الله ربكم فتبارك الله رب العالمين

translation: He is the Living, there is no deity except Him, so call upon Him, [being] sincere to Him in religion. [All] praise is [due] to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and eternal existence of Allah, the only true God worthy of worship. It calls upon believers to devote themselves completely to Allah, with sincere faith and obedience. The verse also expresses gratitude and praise to Allah as the Lord and Sustainer of all creation.
orig: هو الحي لا إله إلا هو فادعوه مخلصين له الدين الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you call upon besides Allah once the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to declare that he has been forbidden from worshipping any deity other than Allah, the one true God. This is because the clear proofs and signs from Allah have come to him, leaving no doubt about the oneness and sovereignty of the Lord of the worlds. The Prophet is then commanded to submit completely to Allah and to call others to do the same.
orig: قل إني نهيت أن أعبد الذين تدعون من دون الله لما جاءني البينات من ربي وأمرت أن أسلم لرب العالمين

translation: It is He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot; and He brings you out as a child; then [He develops you] that you may reach your [full] maturity, then [further] that you may become elders. And among you is he who is taken in [early] death, and [among you] is he who is returned to the most decrepit [old] age so that he knows, after [once having] knowledge, nothing. And when the earth has taken on its lights and has sprouted and grown [various] beautiful kinds [of flora].
interpretation: This verse describes the stages of human creation and development, from being created from dust, to developing from a sperm-drop, to a clinging clot, to being born as a child, and then reaching full maturity and old age. It also acknowledges that some die before reaching old age, while others live to become decrepit in their old age, losing the knowledge they once had. This highlights God's power in creating humans and controlling their lifespan, as well as the importance of using our faculties of reason and understanding ("that you may think") during our lives.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم يخرجكم طفلا ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم ثم لتكونوا شيوخا ومنكم من يتوفى من قبل ولتبلغوا أجلا مسمى ولعلكم تعقلون

translation: He is the One who gives life and causes death, and when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over all creation. He alone has the power to give life and to take it away, and when He decides on a matter, it simply comes into existence without any delay or resistance. This highlights the supreme control and sovereignty of Allah, and the fact that all things are subject to His will and command. The verse reinforces the idea that Allah is the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe, and that all existence ultimately depends on His divine decree.
orig: هو الذي يحيي ويميت فإذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: Have you not considered those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah? How are they averted?
interpretation: This verse is questioning those who argue against the clear signs and evidence of Allah's existence and power. The verse suggests that despite the overwhelming proof of Allah's sovereignty, some people still stubbornly refuse to accept it and turn away from the truth. The interpretation is that people should reflect on the signs of Allah's creation and not be misguided by their own desires or biases, but rather submit to the divine truth.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين يجادلون في آيات الله أنى يصرفون

translation: Those who deny the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers - they will [eventually] know.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who reject the divine revelation (the Qur'an) and the messages conveyed by God's messengers. It warns that they will eventually come to realize the truth, either in this life or the Hereafter, when they face the consequences of their denial and disbelief. The verse emphasizes that denying the divine guidance has serious repercussions, and that the truth will ultimately prevail.
orig: الذين كذبوا بالكتاب وبما أرسلنا به رسلنا فسوف يعلمون

translation: When the shackles are around their necks and they are dragged
interpretation: This verse is describing the fate of those who reject the truth and are condemned to a life of humiliation and subjugation in the afterlife. The "shackles" and "chains" symbolize the bondage and confinement that awaits those who stubbornly refuse to submit to the will of God. The imagery of being "dragged" conveys a sense of helplessness and the inability to escape the consequences of their actions. This verse serves as a warning to those who turn away from the guidance of the Qur'an and the teachings of Islam, reminding them of the dire consequences that await them in the hereafter.
orig: إذ الأغلال في أعناقهم والسلاسل يسحبون

translation: Then in the Scorching Fire they will be stoked
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the disbelievers in the Hereafter. They will be subjected to the intense heat and burning of the Hellfire, where they will be continuously tormented and suffering will be inflicted upon them without end.
orig: في الحميم ثم في النار يسجرون

translation: Then it will be said to them, 'Where are those you used to associate [with Allah]?'
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when those who associated partners with Allah will be questioned about their false deities and idols that they used to worship. The implication is that on that day, their false gods will be of no help or avail to them, and they will be left alone to face the consequences of their actions.
orig: ثم قيل لهم أين ما كنتم تشركون

translation: They say, "We have gone astray from you, and we have not worshipped anything besides Allah." Thus Allah leaves astray the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of idolatry and the consequences of disbelief. The disbelievers claim that they have abandoned their false deities and have not worshipped anything besides Allah. However, the verse states that Allah leaves the disbelievers astray, indicating that their previous idolatry was a result of their own misguidance and that Allah is the one who ultimately guides or misguides people. The interpretation suggests that true guidance can only be found in the worship of Allah, and that those who reject faith will be left to wander in their own delusions.
orig: من دون الله قالوا ضلوا عنا بل لم نكن ندعو من قبل شيئا كذلك يضل الله الكافرين

translation: That is because you exulted upon the earth without right and boasted.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who were arrogant and boastful in their worldly affairs, rejoicing in their wealth, power, and status without any righteous basis. The Qur'an condemns such behavior, as it is a rejection of God's authority and a deviation from the path of righteousness. The interpretation suggests that such arrogance and boastfulness will be met with consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: ذلكم بما كنتم تفرحون في الأرض بغير الحق وبما كنتم تمرحون

translation: Enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who are arrogant and prideful. It states that the fate of the arrogant is to enter the gates of Hell and remain there eternally. The interpretation is that arrogance and pride are sinful traits that will lead to a severe punishment in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the wretched nature of the abode of the arrogant, highlighting the dire consequences of this behavior.
orig: ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: So be patient, indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And whether We show you [the realization of] some of what We have promised them or take you in death, to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse encourages patience and steadfastness, as the promise of Allah is true. It suggests that the fulfillment of Allah's promise may come in this life or the next, but ultimately all will return to Allah for judgment. The verse emphasizes the importance of trusting in Allah's plan and remaining faithful, regardless of the outcome in this world.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق فإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإلينا يرجعون

translation: And We have certainly sent [messengers] before you, [O Muhammad], among them those [whose stories] We have related to you, and some of them We have not related to you. And it was not for any messenger to come with a sign except by permission of Allah. So when the command of Allah comes, it will be concluded [i.e., decided] in truth, and the falsifiers will thereupon lose [all].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has sent many messengers before Prophet Muhammad, some of whose stories are mentioned in the Qur'an and some are not. It further clarifies that no messenger can bring a sign or miracle except by Allah's permission. When Allah's decree comes, it will be concluded in truth, and those who have been denying the truth will be the losers.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك منهم من قصصنا عليك ومنهم من لم نقصص عليك وما كان لرسول أن يأتي بآية إلا بإذن الله فإذا جاء أمر الله قضي بالحق وخسر هنالك المبطلون

translation: Allah is the One who has made for you the grazing livestock, that you may ride them and [from] them you may eat.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has created the livestock animals for the benefit of humanity. They can be used for transportation, and their meat can be consumed as food. This highlights Allah's provision and care for His creation, and the way He has made the natural world to serve the needs of humans.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الأنعام لتركبوا منها ومنها تأكلون

translation: And for you in them are [numerous] benefits and [that] from them you eat. And upon them and upon ships you are carried.
interpretation: This verse highlights the various benefits and uses that humans can derive from animals, such as using them for transportation, food, and other needs. It suggests that animals are created to serve the needs of humans, and that humans should use them responsibly and with gratitude to Allah.
orig: ولكم فيها منافع ولتبلغوا عليها حاجة في صدوركم وعليها وعلى الفلك تحملون

translation: And He shows you His signs, so which of the signs of Allah do you deny?
interpretation: This verse encourages us to reflect on the signs and wonders of Allah that are all around us in the universe. It challenges us to consider the miracles of creation and not to deny or reject the clear evidence of Allah's power and majesty. The verse invites us to open our eyes and hearts to the abundant manifestations of Allah's divine attributes, so that we may increase in faith and gratitude.
orig: ويريكم آياته فأي آيات الله تنكرون

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power and in impression on the land, but they were not availed by what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the fate of previous nations and civilizations. It suggests that those who came before were more powerful and had a greater impact on the land, but ultimately, their worldly possessions and achievements did not save them. The implication is that one should not be overly attached to material gains and should instead focus on righteous deeds that will benefit them in the Hereafter.
orig: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم كانوا أكثر منهم وأشد قوة وآثارا في الأرض فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they [merely] rejoiced in the knowledge they had. But that at which they used to scoff surrounded them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and close-mindedness of those who reject the truth when it is presented to them clearly. Instead of humbly accepting the guidance of the messengers, they take pride in their own limited knowledge and mock the divine signs. Ultimately, they are enveloped by the very consequences they sought to dismiss, as their rejection of the truth leads to their own undoing.
orig: فلما جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فرحوا بما عندهم من العلم وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and we are disbelievers in that which we used to associate [with Him]."
interpretation: This verse describes the response of the disbelievers when they witnessed the punishment of Allah. In the face of Allah's might and power, they were forced to acknowledge their error and declare their belief in the Oneness of Allah, renouncing the idols and false deities they had previously worshipped. This highlights the fact that true faith and submission to Allah can only be attained when one is confronted with the reality of His sovereignty and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: فلما رأوا بأسنا قالوا آمنا بالله وحده وكفرنا بما كنا به مشركين

translation: But their faith could not avail them when they saw Our punishment. [It is] the established way of Allah which has preceded among His servants, and the disbelievers thereupon lost [all].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that faith alone is not enough to save people from the consequences of their misdeeds. Even if they believe, when they face the punishment of Allah, their faith cannot protect them. This is the established way of Allah - that those who disbelieve and reject His signs will ultimately be the losers. The verse serves as a warning that true faith must be accompanied by righteous deeds and submission to Allah, otherwise one's belief will not be of any benefit.
orig: فلم يك ينفعهم إيمانهم لما رأوا بأسنا سنت الله التي قد خلت في عباده وخسر هنالك الكافرون

translation: Ha, Mim.
interpretation: The letters 'Ha, Mim' are among the 'Muqatta'at' (Disjointed Letters) that appear at the beginning of some chapters of the Quran. Their exact meaning is not definitively known, but they are believed to be part of the divine code used by Allah to emphasize the miraculous nature of the Quran and to draw the reader's attention to the deeper meanings and messages within the text.
orig: حم

translation: A revelation from the Beneficent, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse introduces the Quran as a divine revelation from God, the Beneficent and the Merciful. It emphasizes that the Quran originates from God, the All-Compassionate and the All-Merciful, and that its message is a blessing and guidance for humanity.
orig: تنزيل من الرحمن الرحيم

translation: This is a Book whose verses are perfected and then presented in detail from [One who is] Wise and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divinely-revealed book, whose verses are perfectly structured and explained in detail. It is intended for people who possess knowledge and understanding, as they will be able to appreciate the depth and wisdom of its teachings.
orig: كتاب فصلت آياته قرآنا عربيا لقوم يعلمون

translation: As a bearer of good tidings and a warner, but most of them turn away, so they do not hear.
interpretation: This verse is describing the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger of God. He was sent as a "bearer of good tidings and a warner" - to convey the message of Islam and warn people of the consequences of rejecting it. However, the verse indicates that most people "turn away" and "do not hear" this message, either out of arrogance, stubbornness or lack of understanding. The interpretation is that people have a choice to accept or reject the guidance brought by the Prophet, and those who reject it will face the consequences of their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: بشيرا ونذيرا فأعرض أكثرهم فهم لا يسمعون

translation: And they say, "Our hearts are within coverings from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a partition, so work; indeed, we are working."
interpretation: This verse describes the attitude of those who reject the message of Islam. They claim that their hearts are covered and their ears are deaf to the call of the Prophet, and that there is a barrier between them and the believers. This suggests a willful rejection of the truth, rather than an inability to understand it. The verse encourages the believers to continue their efforts in spreading the message, despite the resistance they face, as those who reject it are still "working" in their own way.
orig: وقالوا قلوبنا في أكنة مما تدعونا إليه وفي آذاننا وقر ومن بيننا وبينك حجاب فاعمل إننا عاملون

translation: Say, "I am only a man like you, to whom it has been revealed that your god is but one God. So take the straight path to Him and ask forgiveness of Him. And woe to those who associate others with Him,"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity of the Prophet Muhammad and the oneness of God. It calls upon people to worship only God, the one true deity, and to seek His forgiveness. The verse also warns against associating partners with God, which is considered a grave sin in Islam.
orig: قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فاستقيموا إليه واستغفروه وويل للمشركين

translation: Those who do not give zakah and they, concerning the Hereafter, they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who refuse to pay the obligatory charity known as zakah. It states that such people are disbelievers in the Hereafter. The interpretation is that zakah is a fundamental pillar of Islam, and those who neglect it are considered to be denying a core tenet of the faith, which is tantamount to disbelief. The verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's financial obligations to the less fortunate as a way of demonstrating true faith and commitment to the teachings of Islam.
orig: الذين لا يؤتون الزكاة وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is a reward uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have faith in God and do good deeds will be rewarded by God without any limitation or end. The "reward uninterrupted" suggests that the blessings and bounties bestowed upon the righteous believers will be continuous and everlasting, without any interruption or cessation. This verse provides encouragement and motivation for believers to maintain their faith and righteous conduct, as they can look forward to a perpetual and unfailing reward from God in the Hereafter.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم أجر غير ممنون

translation: Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who deny the existence of God and ascribe partners to Him. It emphasizes that the One who created the earth in two days is the true Lord of all the worlds, and it is foolish to associate partners with Him. The interpretation highlights the power and sovereignty of God, the Creator, and the absurdity of worshiping false deities alongside Him.
orig: قل أئنكم لتكفرون بالذي خلق الأرض في يومين وتجعلون له أندادا ذلك رب العالمين

translation: And He placed on the earth firmly set mountains over its surface, and He blessed it and determined therein its [creatures'] sustenance in four days - equal for [all] seekers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's creation and provision for the earth. The mountains are described as "firmly set" to provide stability and resources for the earth's inhabitants. God has also "blessed" the earth and "determined" the sustenance or nourishment for all the creatures on it, all within a period of four days. This highlights God's power, wisdom and care in creating the world and providing for all who seek their sustenance from it.
orig: وجعل فيها رواسي من فوقها وبارك فيها وقدر فيها أقواتها في أربعة أيام سواء للسائلين

translation: Then He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We have come willingly."
interpretation: This verse describes God's creation of the heavens and the earth. After creating the primordial matter, God then directed Himself to the heavens, which were initially in a state of smoke or vapor. God then commanded the heavens and the earth to come into existence, giving them the choice to do so willingly or by compulsion. The heavens and the earth responded by saying they came into being willingly, indicating their obedience and submission to God's will.
orig: ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين

translation: And He completed them as seven heavens within two days and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse describes how God created the seven heavens in two days, and appointed a command for each heaven. He also adorned the nearest heaven with lamps (such as the sun, moon, and stars) as a protection for the earth and its inhabitants. This demonstrates God's power, wisdom and knowledge in creating the universe in an orderly and purposeful manner.
orig: فقضاهن سبع سماوات في يومين وأوحى في كل سماء أمرها وزينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح وحفظا ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: And if they turn away, then say: 'I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt [that struck] 'Aad and Thamud.'
interpretation: This verse is a warning from God to the people who reject the message of the Quran. It states that if they turn away from the guidance of the Quran, they will be struck by a severe punishment, similar to the thunderbolt that destroyed the ancient tribes of 'Aad and Thamud. This serves as a reminder that God's punishment can be swift and severe for those who persistently reject His signs and guidance.
orig: فإن أعرضوا فقل أنذرتكم صاعقة مثل صاعقة عاد وثمود

translation: When their messengers came to them from before them and from behind them, [saying], "Do not worship except Allah," they said, "If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down the angels, so indeed we are, in that with which you have been sent, disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse describes the response of the disbelievers when the messengers of Allah came to them, calling them to worship Allah alone. The disbelievers rejected the message, claiming that if Allah had willed, He would have sent down angels instead of human messengers. This interpretation suggests that the disbelievers were unwilling to accept the message of the prophets, preferring to maintain their existing beliefs and practices rather than submitting to the will of Allah.
orig: إذ جاءتهم الرسل من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم ألا تعبدوا إلا الله قالوا لو شاء ربنا لأنزل ملائكة فإنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون

translation: And as for Aad, they were arrogant upon the earth without right and said, "Who is greater than us in strength?" Did they not see that Allah who created them was greater than them in strength, but they were rejecting Our signs.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the people of Aad, who were destroyed by Allah due to their arrogance and rejection of His signs. The verse emphasizes that despite their perceived strength and power, they were no match for the might of Allah, who created them. The lesson here is that true power and strength come from submission to Allah, not from arrogance and a refusal to acknowledge His sovereignty.
orig: فأما عاد فاستكبروا في الأرض بغير الحق وقالوا من أشد منا قوة أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلقهم هو أشد منهم قوة وكانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: Then We sent against them a screaming wind during days of misfortune to make them taste the punishment of disgrace in this worldly life, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah sent a severe and destructive wind against the disbelievers as a punishment for their rejection of faith and moral transgressions. The "days of misfortune" refer to a period of calamity and hardship that afflicted them as a consequence of their actions. The purpose was to make them experience the humiliation and disgrace of this worldly punishment, which is but a precursor to the even more severe and demeaning punishment they will face in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes that they will not be able to find any help or support to save them from this divine retribution, as they had none to turn to but Allah.
orig: فأرسلنا عليهم ريحا صرصرا في أيام نحسات لنذيقهم عذاب الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أخزى وهم لا ينصرون

translation: And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance, so the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the people of Thamud, who were guided by God but chose to reject the guidance and prefer blindness and disbelief. As a result, they were struck by a severe punishment, which is described as a "thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment". This serves as a warning to those who turn away from the truth and persist in their wrongdoing, that they will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وأما ثمود فهديناهم فاستحبوا العمى على الهدى فأخذتهم صاعقة العذاب الهون بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have faith in Allah and are righteous, pious, and God-fearing will be saved from the punishment and calamities that befall the disbelievers. It highlights that belief in Allah and practicing righteousness are the keys to attaining salvation and deliverance.
orig: ونجينا الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: And the Day when the enemies of Allah will be gathered to the Fire, so they will be [popularly] assembled.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the enemies of Allah will be gathered and brought to the Fire of Hell. They will be assembled and arranged in a way that emphasizes their humiliation and punishment for their rejection of faith and opposition to Allah and His teachings.
orig: ويوم يحشر أعداء الله إلى النار فهم يوزعون

translation: Until, when they reach it, their hearing and their eyes and their skins will testify against them for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when people will be held accountable for their actions in life. Their own senses - hearing, sight, and skin - will bear witness against them, confirming the deeds they committed. This emphasizes that on that day, there will be no escape from the consequences of one"s actions, as even the body itself will testify to the truth.
orig: حتى إذا ما جاءوها شهد عليهم سمعهم وأبصارهم وجلودهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they will say to their skins, "Why have you testified against us?" They will say, "We were made to speak by Allah , who has given speech to everything; and He created you the first time, and to Him you are returned."
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when people will be held accountable for their deeds. The disbelievers will try to shift the blame to their own bodies, arguing that their limbs and organs testified against them. However, Allah will make those very body parts speak up and testify to the truth, declaring that they were created by Allah and will return to Him. This emphasizes that each person is responsible for their own actions, and cannot escape accountability before Allah.
orig: وقالوا لجلودهم لم شهدتم علينا قالوا أنطقنا الله الذي أنطق كل شيء وهو خلقكم أول مرة وإليه ترجعون

translation: And you were not covering yourselves, lest your hearing testify against you or your sight or your skins, but you assumed that Allah does not know much of what you do.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against the notion that one can hide their misdeeds from Allah. It emphasizes that Allah is all-knowing and that our senses, bodies, and actions will all testify against us on the Day of Judgment. The verse encourages us to be mindful of Allah's omniscience and to refrain from sinful acts, as we cannot hide anything from Him.
orig: وما كنتم تستترون أن يشهد عليكم سمعكم ولا أبصاركم ولا جلودكم ولكن ظننتم أن الله لا يعلم كثيرا مما تعملون

translation: And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord. It has brought you to ruin, and you have become among the losers.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against having negative assumptions or doubts about Allah. The people had assumed the worst about Allah, that He would not provide for them or help them, and this assumption led them to ruin. The interpretation is that we should not make such negative assumptions about Allah, as it can lead us astray and cause us to lose out in the end.
orig: وذلكم ظنكم الذي ظننتم بربكم أرداكم فأصبحتم من الخاسرين

translation: And if they are patient, the Fire will be a home for them; and if they seek to please [their desires], they will not be of those who are given success.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and steadfastness in the face of trials and temptations. It suggests that those who remain patient and steadfast in their faith will be rewarded, while those who succumb to their desires and seek to please themselves will not find success. The verse encourages believers to focus on their spiritual growth and to resist the allure of worldly pleasures, which can lead them astray from the path of righteousness.
orig: فإن يصبروا فالنار مثوى لهم وإن يستعتبوا فما هم من المعتبين

translation: And We have assigned to them companions (in the Hereafter), who have made attractive to them what is before them and what is behind them (of sins), and the word has come into effect upon them among nations which had passed on before them of jinn and men. Indeed, they (all) were losers.
interpretation: This verse describes how Satan and his followers have been assigned to mislead and tempt humans, making their sins and wrongdoings appear attractive to them. This has been the pattern throughout history, with previous generations of humans and jinn also being led astray. The end result is that all those who succumb to these temptations are ultimately losers, having failed to achieve the true purpose of their creation and the eternal success in the Hereafter.
orig: وقيضنا لهم قرناء فزينوا لهم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم وحق عليهم القول في أمم قد خلت من قبلهم من الجن والإنس إنهم كانوا خاسرين

translation: And those who disbelieve say: "Listen not to this Qur'an, and make noise in the midst of its (recitation) that you may overcome."
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who refused to listen to the Qur'an and instead tried to drown out its recitation with their own noise and distraction. The interpretation is that the disbelievers were afraid of the power of the Qur'an and its ability to guide people, so they attempted to prevent others from hearing and being influenced by it.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لا تسمعوا لهذا القرآن والغوا فيه لعلكم تغلبون

translation: So We will surely let those who disbelieve taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them for the worst of what they had been doing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and engage in evil deeds. It promises that they will be made to experience a severe punishment as a consequence of their disbelief and wicked actions. The interpretation suggests that those who turn away from the guidance of the Qur'an and engage in sinful practices will be held accountable and face the consequences of their wrongdoing.
orig: فلنذيقن الذين كفروا عذابا شديدا ولنجزينهم أسوأ الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah, the Fire. For them therein is the Home of Eternity, as recompense for what they used to deny of Our verses.
interpretation: This verse is describing the punishment that awaits the enemies of Allah in the Hereafter. It states that the ultimate abode for them will be the Fire, which will be their eternal dwelling place, as a consequence of their denial and rejection of the signs and revelations of Allah. The interpretation suggests that those who persistently reject the truth and guidance of Allah will face the severe and lasting punishment of the Hellfire as a just retribution for their actions.
orig: ذلك جزاء أعداء الله النار لهم فيها دار الخلد جزاء بما كانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: And those who disbelieve will say, "Our Lord, show us those who misled us of the jinn and humans [so] we may put them under our feet that they may be of the lowest."
interpretation: This verse describes the attitude of those who rejected faith in Allah. They will demand on the Day of Judgment that Allah show them those from among the jinn (spiritual beings) and humans who led them astray, so that they may humiliate and subjugate them. This reflects the arrogance and lack of accountability of the disbelievers, who wish to take revenge on those they blame for their own misguided choices. However, the true judgment belongs to Allah alone, and He will decide the fate of all based on their deeds and faith.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا ربنا أرنا اللذين أضلانا من الجن والإنس نجعلهما تحت أقدامنا ليكونا من الأسفلين

translation: Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast - the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith. Those who declare their belief in Allah and then remain steadfast in their commitment will be granted the good news of Paradise by the angels. This indicates that true faith is not just a matter of verbal declaration, but requires unwavering adherence to the principles of Islam. The verse also conveys a message of reassurance and comfort, as the angels will allay the fears and sorrows of the believers, and instead give them the glad tidings of the eternal bliss that awaits them in the Hereafter.
orig: إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا تتنزل عليهم الملائكة ألا تخافوا ولا تحزنوا وأبشروا بالجنة التي كنتم توعدون

translation: We are your allies in this worldly life and in the Hereafter. And you will have in it whatever your souls desire, and you will have therein whatever you request.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the true protector and guardian of the believers, both in this life and in the Hereafter. It assures the believers that they will be granted all that their souls desire and all that they ask for, as long as they remain steadfast in their faith and obedience to Allah. The verse highlights the blessings and rewards that await the believers in the Hereafter, which far exceed the temporary pleasures of this world.
orig: نحن أولياؤكم في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ولكم فيها ما تشتهي أنفسكم ولكم فيها ما تدعون

translation: It is sent down from the All-Forgiving, the All-Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, the All-Forgiving and the All-Merciful. It conveys the message that Allah, in His infinite wisdom and compassion, has sent down this guidance for humanity, despite their shortcomings and sins. The Qur'an is a testament to Allah's boundless mercy and willingness to forgive those who turn to Him in repentance and seek His guidance.
orig: نزلا من غفور رحيم

translation: And who is better in speech than one who calls [people] to Allah and does righteousness and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of not only calling people to the worship of Allah, but also of practicing righteousness and declaring one's faith as a Muslim. It highlights that the best speech is that which invites others to the path of Allah, while the speaker themselves lives according to the teachings of Islam. This verse encourages believers to combine their words with deeds, and to openly profess their faith, in order to be truly praiseworthy in the sight of Allah.
orig: ومن أحسن قولا ممن دعا إلى الله وعمل صالحا وقال إنني من المسلمين

translation: And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] by that [deed] which is better; and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity [will become] as though he was a devoted friend.
interpretation: This verse encourages us to respond to evil with good, and to overcome enmity with kindness. It suggests that by repelling evil with a good deed, we can transform the relationship with our adversary, turning them into a devoted friend. The key message is that meeting negativity with positivity is the best way to resolve conflicts and promote harmony.
orig: ولا تستوي الحسنة ولا السيئة ادفع بالتي هي أحسن فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم

translation: And none will receive it (the highest bliss) except the patient, and none will receive it except the greatly fortunate.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the reward for those who are patient and steadfast in their faith. It suggests that the greatest bliss and fortune in the Hereafter is reserved for those who endure trials and tribulations with patience and perseverance. The interpretation is that true success and happiness in the life to come can only be attained by those who are willing to make sacrifices and overcome difficulties in this world for the sake of their beliefs and values.
orig: وما يلقاها إلا الذين صبروا وما يلقاها إلا ذو حظ عظيم

translation: And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse instructs us to seek refuge in Allah when we are tempted by the whispers or suggestions of Satan. Satan tries to lead us astray, but by turning to Allah and asking for His protection, we can overcome these evil influences. Allah is all-Hearing and all-Knowing, and He is able to shield us from the schemes of Satan.
orig: وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ فاستعذ بالله إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: And of His signs are the night and day and the sun and moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him that you worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the sun, moon, night and day are all signs of Allah's creation, and that they should not be worshipped, but rather Allah who created them should be worshipped. It is a call to monotheism and to direct all worship and reverence towards the One true God, Allah, and not to any of His creations, no matter how impressive or powerful they may seem.
orig: ومن آياته الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر لا تسجدوا للشمس ولا للقمر واسجدوا لله الذي خلقهن إن كنتم إياه تعبدون

translation: And if they are arrogant, then those who are with your Lord [i.e., the angels] exalt Him by [night and] day, and they do not tire.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even if people are arrogant and refuse to submit to God, the angels who are close to God are constantly praising and glorifying Him without any fatigue. This implies that God is worthy of worship and obedience, regardless of how people respond to Him. The verse encourages humility and a willingness to submit to the Almighty, as opposed to arrogance and pride.
orig: فإن استكبروا فالذين عند ربك يسبحون له بالليل والنهار وهم لا يسأمون

translation: And of His signs is that you see the earth stilled, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and grows [plants of] every [kind of] beautiful species.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and wisdom of God in creating the natural world. The earth, which appears lifeless and still, is transformed when God sends down rain upon it. The rain causes the earth to quiver and grow a diverse array of beautiful plants and vegetation. This demonstrates God's ability to give life and sustain all of creation, even that which seems inanimate. The verse reminds us that God is the Giver of life and has power over all things.
orig: ومن آياته أنك ترى الأرض خاشعة فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت إن الذي أحياها لمحيي الموتى إنه على كل شيء قدير

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses - We will drive them into a Fire. [Whenever] their skins are burned, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse warns those who disbelieve in the signs and messages of Allah that they will be driven into the Fire of Hell. When their skins are burned, they will be replaced with new skins so that they can continue to feel the punishment. This emphasizes that Allah is all-Powerful and All-Wise in His judgment and retribution against those who reject faith and defy His commands. The verse also conveys that one should act according to one's will, but Allah is All-Knowing of our deeds and will judge us accordingly on the Day of Resurrection.
orig: إن الذين يلحدون في آياتنا لا يخفون علينا أفمن يلقى في النار خير أم من يأتي آمنا يوم القيامة اعملوا ما شئتم إنه بما تعملون بصير

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder [i.e., the Qur'an] when it has come to them [are the losers], and indeed, it is a [mighty] Book.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an and the consequences of disbelieving in it. It states that those who reject the Qur'an, which has been revealed to them, will be the losers. The Qur'an is described as a "mighty Book", indicating its power, authority, and the invaluable guidance it provides. This verse serves as a warning to those who turn away from the Qur'an and encourages believers to hold fast to its teachings.
orig: إن الذين كفروا بالذكر لما جاءهم وإنه لكتاب عزيز

translation: No falsehood can approach it from before or behind it: It is sent down by One Full of Wisdom, Worthy of all Praise.
interpretation: This verse affirms the divine origin and infallibility of the Qur'an. It states that the Qur'an is free from any falsehood, error, or contradiction, as it is a revelation from the All-Wise and All-Praiseworthy God. The Qur'an is protected from any alteration or corruption, whether from the past or the future, and its teachings are entirely true and trustworthy. This emphasizes the Qur'an's divine nature and its reliability as a source of guidance for humanity.
orig: لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه تنزيل من حكيم حميد

translation: Nothing is said to you, [O Muhammad], except what was already said to the messengers before you. Indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness and the possessor of painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that the opposition and rejection he faces from his people is not unique to him, but is a common experience shared by all the messengers of God throughout history. It reminds him that his Lord, Allah, is the One who has the power to forgive those who repent and believe, as well as to punish those who stubbornly reject the truth. This verse encourages the Prophet to remain steadfast in his mission, knowing that the ultimate outcome rests in the hands of the Almighty.
orig: ما يقال لك إلا ما قد قيل للرسل من قبلك إن ربك لذو مغفرة وذو عقاب أليم

translation: And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, "Why are its verses not explained in detail [in our language]? Is it a foreign [recitation] and an Arab [messenger]?" Say, "It is, for those who believe, a guidance and cure." And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is upon them blindness. Those are being called from a distant place.
interpretation: This verse addresses the objections of those who rejected the Qur'an because it was revealed in the Arabic language. The verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a guidance and cure for those who believe, while for those who reject it, it is like deafness and blindness, as they are being called from a distant place. The verse reassures the believers that the Qur'an is revealed in the Arabic language, which is the language of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the people to whom it was first addressed. The message is universal, but the language is chosen to be accessible to the initial audience.
orig: ولو جعلناه قرآنا أعجميا لقالوا لولا فصلت آياته أأعجمي وعربي قل هو للذين آمنوا هدى وشفاء والذين لا يؤمنون في آذانهم وقر وهو عليهم عمى أولئك ينادون من مكان بعيد

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, but it came to be disputed. And if not for a word that had preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them. And indeed they are, concerning the Qur'an, in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: This verse highlights that even after being given the scripture, the people still disputed and disagreed about it. However, Allah had already decreed that the Qur'an would be revealed, and this decree would not be changed. Despite the doubts and uncertainties that some people had about the Qur'an, it would remain as the final and definitive scripture revealed by Allah.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فاختلف فيه ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم وإنهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: Whoever does righteousness - it is for his [own] soul, and whoever does evil - it is against it. And your Lord is not at all unjust to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the consequences of one's actions, whether good or bad, are borne by the individual themselves. If a person does righteous deeds, the benefit is for their own soul, and if they commit evil, the harm is upon themselves. It also affirms that God is not unjust in His dealings with His servants, and that each person is responsible for their own choices and actions.
orig: من عمل صالحا فلنفسه ومن أساء فعليها وما ربك بظلام للعبيد

translation: To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour. And no fruits emerge from their coverings and no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. And the Day He will call to them, "Where are My 'partners'?" they will say, "We announce to You that none of us is a witness [to that]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and sovereignty of God. It states that only God has knowledge of the Hour of Judgment, and that all natural phenomena, such as the growth of fruits and the conception and birth of living beings, occur according to His knowledge and will. The verse also refers to the Day of Judgment, when God will call upon those who associated partners with Him, and they will admit that they have no evidence to justify their polytheism. This underscores the fact that God alone is the Creator and Sustainer of all things, and that He has no partners or equals.
orig: إليه يرد علم الساعة وما تخرج من ثمرات من أكمامها وما تحمل من أنثى ولا تضع إلا بعلمه ويوم يناديهم أين شركائي قالوا آذناك ما منا من شهيد

translation: And lost from them is what they used to invoke before, and they assumed that for them there is no defender.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers will be abandoned by the false deities they used to worship, and they will realize that they have no way to escape the consequences of their actions. It emphasizes the futility of relying on anything other than the one true God, and the importance of seeking refuge in Him alone.
orig: وضل عنهم ما كانوا يدعون من قبل وظنوا ما لهم من محيص

translation: Man is not weary of invoking [Allah for] good [things], but if evil touches him, he is hopeless and despairing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of human beings to be quick to ask for good things from Allah, but to become despondent and lose hope when faced with difficulties or hardships. The verse suggests that people should maintain their faith and trust in Allah even in times of adversity, and not become discouraged or give up. It encourages steadfastness and perseverance in the face of life's challenges.
orig: لا يسأم الإنسان من دعاء الخير وإن مسه الشر فيئوس قنوط

translation: And if We let him taste mercy from Us after an adversity has touched him, he will surely say, "This is [all] my [due]" and never thinks it is the Hour [of Resurrection]; and if I am returned to my Lord, indeed for me there will be with Him the best [reward]". So We will surely inform those who disbelieved about what they did, and We will surely make them taste a massive punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of human beings to become arrogant and self-centered when they experience Allah's blessings and mercy after facing hardship. The verse suggests that when a person is granted relief from difficulties, they may attribute it to their own efforts or deservedness, rather than acknowledging it as a gift from Allah. The verse also warns that such people may not believe in the reality of the Hereafter and the Day of Resurrection. However, the verse assures that those who disbelieve and act arrogantly will be informed about their deeds and will be subjected to a severe punishment.
orig: ولئن أذقناه رحمة منا من بعد ضراء مسته ليقولن هذا لي وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رجعت إلى ربي إن لي عنده للحسنى فلننبئن الذين كفروا بما عملوا ولنذيقنهم من عذاب غليظ

translation: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; and when evil touches him, he is ever full of lengthy supplication.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of human beings to be ungrateful and neglectful of God's blessings, while being quick to turn to Him in times of hardship. When people are blessed with good fortune, they often become arrogant and forget their dependence on God. However, when faced with adversity, they become desperate and make lengthy supplications, seeking God's help. This verse serves as a reminder to maintain gratitude and humility in both good and bad times, and to remain steadfast in one's relationship with the Almighty.
orig: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه وإذا مسه الشر فذو دعاء عريض

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if it [i.e., the Qur'an] was from Allah and you disbelieved in it, who would be more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?"
interpretation: This verse challenges those who reject the Qur'an, despite it being from Allah. It suggests that those who disbelieve in the Qur'an are in a state of profound misguidance, further from the truth than those who are in deep, ongoing conflict with it. The implication is that rejecting divine guidance is the ultimate form of straying from the right path.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن كان من عند الله ثم كفرتم به من أضل ممن هو في شقاق بعيد

translation: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is to all things a Witness?
interpretation: This verse speaks of the various signs and proofs that Allah will show to people, both in the external world (the "horizons") and within themselves ("within themselves"), in order to make it clear that the Qur'an and the message of Islam is the truth. The verse emphasizes that Allah is a Witness to all things, and that His testimony and evidence should be sufficient for people to recognize the truth.
orig: سنريهم آياتنا في الآفاق وفي أنفسهم حتى يتبين لهم أنه الحق أولم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Unquestionably, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. Unquestionably, He is of all things Encompassing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who deny the Day of Judgment and the meeting with their Lord are in a state of doubt and uncertainty. It affirms that Allah is All-Encompassing, meaning that He has knowledge and control over all things, and nothing is hidden from Him. This serves as a reminder that people will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment, and that they cannot escape Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and power.
orig: ألا إنهم في مرية من لقاء ربهم ألا إنه بكل شيء محيط

translation: Ha, Mim.
interpretation: The letters "Ha" and "Mim" are among the "Muqatta'at" or "Disconnected Letters" that appear at the beginning of certain chapters of the Qur'an. Their precise meaning is not entirely clear, and various interpretations have been offered by scholars. One common view is that these letters are a part of the divine language, and their inclusion serves to emphasize the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, reminding the reader that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, not the work of a human being.
orig: حم

translation: Alif, Lam, Sad.
interpretation: The exact meaning of these letters at the beginning of the verse is not entirely clear, but they are believed to be part of the 'mysterious letters' (al-muqatta'at) found at the beginning of some surahs in the Qur'an. These letters are thought to have symbolic or metaphorical meanings, though their precise significance is not definitively known. The presence of these letters serves to emphasize the divine nature and miraculous qualities of the Qur'an.
orig: عسق

translation: Thus Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise, reveals to you, [O Muhammad], and to those before you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the revelation of the Quran to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is part of a continuous chain of divine guidance that has been sent to previous prophets as well. It highlights that the source of this revelation is Allah, the Almighty and All-Wise, who has chosen to guide humanity through His messengers throughout history. The verse serves to reassure the Prophet and the believers that they are following a divinely-ordained path, just as those before them have.
orig: كذلك يوحي إليك وإلى الذين من قبلك الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and dominion of Allah over the entire universe, both in the heavens and on the earth. He is the Almighty, the Possessor of all power and authority, and the All-Wise, whose actions and decrees are guided by infinite wisdom. This affirms the belief that Allah alone is worthy of worship and obedience, and that all creation is subject to His will and control.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العلي العظيم

translation: The heavens are almost rent asunder from above them (by His Majesty), and the angels celebrate the Praises of their Lord, and ask for forgiveness for those on the earth. Verily, Allah is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the awe-inspiring nature of Allah and His supreme power. The heavens are described as being "almost rent asunder" by the magnitude of Allah's majesty, indicating the overwhelming power and grandeur of the divine. The angels, in response, are depicted as celebrating the praises of their Lord and seeking forgiveness for those on earth. This suggests that even the most exalted of Allah's creations, the angels, are in a constant state of reverence and supplication before Him. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah is the Oft-Forgiving and the Most Merciful, emphasizing that despite His immense power, He is also compassionate and willing to forgive those who seek His forgiveness.
orig: تكاد السماوات يتفطرن من فوقهن والملائكة يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويستغفرون لمن في الأرض ألا إن الله هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And those who take allies other than Allah - [but] Allah is the Protector, and He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.
