interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the only true protector and guardian, and that taking any other allies or authorities besides Him is misguided. It reminds us that Allah has power over all things, including the ability to give life to the dead, and that He alone is worthy of our devotion and reliance.
orig: والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء الله حفيظ عليهم وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: And thus We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], a Qur'an in Arabic that you may warn the Mother of Cities [Makkah] and those around it and warn [all] of the Day of Assembly, about which there is no doubt. [One] party will be in Paradise and [one] party in the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the Arabic language, so that he may warn the people of Makkah and the surrounding areas about the coming Day of Judgment. On that day, there will be two distinct groups - one in Paradise and the other in the Hellfire. This verse highlights the importance of heeding the Qur'anic message and preparing for the inevitable reckoning on the Day of Resurrection, where each person's fate will be determined based on their beliefs and deeds in this life.
orig: وكذلك أوحينا إليك قرآنا عربيا لتنذر أم القرى ومن حولها وتنذر يوم الجمع لا ريب فيه فريق في الجنة وفريق في السعير

translation: And if Allah had willed, He could have made them [of] one religion, but He admits whom He wills into His mercy. And the wrongdoers have not any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has the power to guide all of humanity to a single faith, but in His wisdom, He allows people to choose their own path. Those who do wrong will find no one to protect or assist them, as they have strayed from the right guidance provided by Allah.
orig: ولو شاء الله لجعلهم أمة واحدة ولكن يدخل من يشاء في رحمته والظالمون ما لهم من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Or have they taken allies besides Him? [O Muhammad], but it is Allah who is the Protector, and it is He who gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of Allah. It condemns the practice of taking allies or deities besides Allah, and affirms that Allah alone is the true Protector and Sustainer. The verse also highlights Allah's power to give life to the dead, underscoring His absolute authority and control over all things.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دونه أولياء فالله هو الولي وهو يحيي الموتى وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And in anything over which you disagree - its ruling is [to be referred] to Allah. [Say, O Muhammad], "That is Allah, my Lord; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that in matters where there is disagreement, the ultimate judgment and decision should be referred to Allah. The speaker, who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad, affirms his trust and reliance in Allah as his Lord, and his commitment to turning back to Him. This underscores the importance of submitting to the divine will and authority, rather than relying on one's own opinions or desires when faced with differences of opinion.
orig: وما اختلفتم فيه من شيء فحكمه إلى الله ذلكم الله ربي عليه توكلت وإليه أنيب

translation: The Creator of the heavens and the earth has made for you from yourselves, mates, and among the cattle, mates; He multiplies you thereby. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and majesty of God as the Creator of the heavens and the earth. He has created pairs and mates for humans and animals, which allows for the multiplication of life. This demonstrates God's infinite wisdom and ability to sustain and propagate His creation. The verse also affirms that God is unlike any of His creations - He is the Hearing and the Seeing, with attributes that are incomparable to His creatures.
orig: فاطر السماوات والأرض جعل لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا ومن الأنعام أزواجا يذرؤكم فيه ليس كمثله شيء وهو السميع البصير

translation: To Him belongs the keys of the heavens and the earth. He enlarges provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed, He is to all things Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone has control over the heavens and the earth, and that He alone determines the provision and sustenance of all His creation. He grants provision to whomever He wills, in whatever measure He deems appropriate. This is a reflection of His absolute power, knowledge, and wisdom, as He is "Knowing of all things". The interpretation suggests that we should trust in Allah's divine plan and not be overly concerned with material provisions, as He alone controls and distributes them according to His infinite wisdom.
orig: له مقاليد السماوات والأرض يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إنه بكل شيء عليم

translation: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus - to establish the religion and not be divided therein. Difficult for those who associate others with Allah is that to which you invite them. Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the divine message that has been revealed to the prophets throughout history. It highlights that the core of the religion - to establish the worship of the One God and to live in accordance with His teachings - has been a consistent theme across the various prophetic missions. The verse also underscores the challenge of this message for those who associate partners with Allah, as it calls for a complete devotion and surrender to the One God. Ultimately, it is Allah who chooses whom He wills to guide to the truth, and those who turn back to Him with sincerity will find the path to His pleasure and acceptance.
orig: شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا والذي أوحينا إليك وما وصينا به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى أن أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه الله يجتبي إليه من يشاء ويهدي إليه من ينيب

translation: And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord [postponing it] until a specified term, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, those who were granted the Scripture after them are, concerning it, in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the divisions and disputes that arose among people were not due to a lack of knowledge, but rather due to jealousy and animosity between them. The verse suggests that if it were not for the decree of God, delaying the final judgment, the matter would have been settled between them. It also indicates that even those who were granted the Scripture after the previous communities were in doubt and uncertainty about it.
orig: وما تفرقوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك إلى أجل مسمى لقضي بينهم وإن الذين أورثوا الكتاب من بعدهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: So to that [religion, then, O Muhammad], invite, and remain steadfast as you are commanded and do not follow their inclinations. And say, "I believe in what Allah has revealed of the Qur'an, and I have been commanded to do justice among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you your deeds. There is no [need for] argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the [final] destination."
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to invite people to the true religion of Islam, to remain steadfast in his faith, and to not follow the desires of those who reject the message. He is commanded to declare his belief in the Qur'an as the revealed word of God, and to call for justice and fairness among all people. The verse emphasizes that each person will be held accountable for their own deeds, and that ultimately, it is God who will judge and bring all people together. The key message is to call others to the truth of Islam, while maintaining one's own faith and righteousness, and leaving the final judgment to God.
orig: فلذلك فادع واستقم كما أمرت ولا تتبع أهواءهم وقل آمنت بما أنزل الله من كتاب وأمرت لأعدل بينكم الله ربنا وربكم لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم لا حجة بيننا وبينكم الله يجمع بيننا وإليه المصير

translation: And those who dispute concerning Allah after [the matter of] His response has been accepted [by some] - their argument is invalid with their Lord, and upon them is [His] wrath, and for them is a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who argue and dispute against the truth of Allah after it has been clearly established and accepted by others. Their arguments are considered invalid and baseless in the sight of Allah, and they will face His wrath and severe punishment as a result of their rejection of the truth.
orig: والذين يحاجون في الله من بعد ما استجيب له حجتهم داحضة عند ربهم وعليهم غضب ولهم عذاب شديد

translation: Allah is the One who has sent down the Book with the truth, and the Balance. And what will make you know that perhaps the Hour is near?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the One who has revealed the Qur'an, the divine scripture, with truth and justice. It also mentions the "Balance", which could refer to the concept of justice and fairness that is central to Islamic teachings. The verse then poses a rhetorical question, asking what could make one know that the Day of Judgment (the Hour) is near. This serves as a reminder to be prepared for the inevitable coming of the End Times, as its arrival is known only to Allah.
orig: الله الذي أنزل الكتاب بالحق والميزان وما يدريك لعل الساعة قريب

translation: Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in extreme error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the different attitudes towards the Day of Judgment (the Hour) between the believers and the disbelievers. The disbelievers, out of their lack of faith, try to rush or hasten the arrival of the Day of Judgment, perhaps out of a desire to prove it false. In contrast, the believers are filled with a sense of reverence and fear, knowing that the Day of Judgment is the truth and a reality they must prepare for. The verse concludes by stating that those who dispute or argue against the coming of the Hour are in grave error, far removed from the truth.
orig: يستعجل بها الذين لا يؤمنون بها والذين آمنوا مشفقون منها ويعلمون أنها الحق ألا إن الذين يمارون في الساعة لفي ضلال بعيد

translation: Allah is Subtle with His servants; He gives provision to whom He wills. And He is the Powerful, the Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power, wisdom, and care for His creation. It suggests that Allah, in His infinite wisdom, provides for His servants in ways that may not always be apparent or understood by us. The verse reminds us that Allah is the Powerful and Exalted, and that He bestows provision upon whomever He chooses, according to His divine plan. This encourages us to trust in Allah's judgment and to be content with the sustenance He provides, even if it does not align with our own desires or expectations.
orig: الله لطيف بعباده يرزق من يشاء وهو القوي العزيز

translation: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We will increase for him in his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world - We will give him thereof, but there will be for him no share in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who seek the rewards of the Hereafter and those who seek the pleasures of this world. It suggests that those who focus their efforts on the Hereafter will be rewarded with an increased harvest, both in this life and the next. In contrast, those who prioritize the worldly life will receive their share in this world, but will have no portion in the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to orient their lives towards the eternal reward of the Hereafter, rather than the fleeting pleasures of this temporal existence.
orig: من كان يريد حرث الآخرة نزد له في حرثه ومن كان يريد حرث الدنيا نؤته منها وما له في الآخرة من نصيب

translation: Or have they partners (of Allah) who have prescribed for them a religion to which Allah has not consented? And if not for the decisive word, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the polytheists who have associated partners with Allah and prescribed for themselves a religion that Allah has not sanctioned. It emphasizes that if not for Allah's decree to delay the final judgment, the matter would have been settled between the believers and the disbelievers. However, the wrongdoers will ultimately face a painful punishment for their transgressions.
orig: أم لهم شركاء شرعوا لهم من الدين ما لم يأذن به الله ولولا كلمة الفصل لقضي بينهم وإن الظالمين لهم عذاب أليم

translation: You see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned, and it will [certainly] befall them. And those who have believed and done righteous deeds will be in the Gardens of Paradise; they will have whatever they wish from their Lord. That is what is the great bounty.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the fate of the wrongdoers and the believers. The wrongdoers are described as being "fearful of what they have earned", meaning they are anxious and worried about the consequences of their misdeeds. In contrast, the believers who have done righteous deeds will be rewarded with the Gardens of Paradise, where they will have whatever they wish from their Lord. This highlights the vast difference between the fate of the two groups, with the believers receiving the "great bounty" of Allah's pleasure and eternal bliss in the Hereafter.
orig: ترى الظالمين مشفقين مما كسبوا وهو واقع بهم والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات في روضات الجنات لهم ما يشاءون عند ربهم ذلك هو الفضل الكبير

translation: That is the one whom Allah gives good tidings to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say, "I do not ask you for this message any payment [but] only good will through kinship." And whoever commits a good deed - We will increase for him good therein. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah rewards those who believe in Him and do good deeds. It encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to convey this message to the people without asking for any material compensation, but only seeking their goodwill and love. The verse also promises that Allah will increase the reward for those who do good deeds, as He is Forgiving and Appreciative of the efforts of His servants.
orig: ذلك الذي يبشر الله عباده الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات قل لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إلا المودة في القربى ومن يقترف حسنة نزد له فيها حسنا إن الله غفور شكور

translation: Or do they say, "He has invented about Allah a lie"? But if Allah willed, He could seal over your heart. And Allah eliminates falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who accuse the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of fabricating the Qur'an and falsely attributing it to Allah. The verse asserts that if Allah willed, He could prevent the Prophet from receiving revelation and seal his heart. However, Allah instead eliminates falsehood and establishes the truth through the words of the Qur'an, for He is All-Knowing of what is in the hearts of people.
orig: أم يقولون افترى على الله كذبا فإن يشإ الله يختم على قلبك ويمح الله الباطل ويحق الحق بكلماته إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds, and He knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of God. It states that God accepts the repentance of His servants and pardons their misdeeds or sins. This highlights that God is willing to forgive those who sincerely turn to Him and seek His forgiveness. The verse also reminds that God is all-knowing, and is aware of everything that His servants do, both good and bad. This encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and to seek God's forgiveness when they err, as He is the Most Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: وهو الذي يقبل التوبة عن عباده ويعفو عن السيئات ويعلم ما تفعلون

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - He will increase them in [good] guidance and give them their [due] rewards in full.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have faith in God and do good deeds will be rewarded by God. He will increase their guidance and give them the full measure of their rewards. In contrast, the disbelievers will face a severe punishment. The verse highlights the importance of combining belief and righteous action, which leads to God's pleasure and blessings.
orig: ويستجيب الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ويزيدهم من فضله والكافرون لهم عذاب شديد

translation: And if Allah had extended [excessively] provision for His servants, they would have committed tyranny throughout the earth. But He sends [it] down in an amount which He wills. Indeed, He is to His servants Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that if Allah were to provide unlimited wealth and resources to people, they would become arrogant and oppressive, misusing their wealth and power. Instead, Allah sends down provision in a measured and controlled manner, as He knows best what is suitable for each of His servants. This teaches us that we should be grateful for what we have been given, and not seek to accumulate wealth and power excessively, as that can lead to corruption and injustice.
orig: ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض ولكن ينزل بقدر ما يشاء إنه بعباده خبير بصير

translation: And it is He who sends down the rain after they had despaired and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and mercy of God. It states that God is the one who sends down rain, even after people have lost hope and given up. This demonstrates God's ability to provide for His creation, even in the most dire of circumstances. The verse also describes God as the "Protector" and the "Praiseworthy", highlighting His role in guiding and supporting His servants, as well as the fact that He is worthy of all praise and worship.
orig: وهو الذي ينزل الغيث من بعد ما قنطوا وينشر رحمته وهو الولي الحميد

translation: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your languages and your colors. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and wisdom of God in creating the heavens, the earth, and the diversity of life within them. It suggests that the existence of this vast and intricate universe, along with the diversity of human languages and physical attributes, are all signs of God's might and design. This should inspire contemplation and knowledge among those who seek to understand the wonders of creation.
orig: ومن آياته خلق السماوات والأرض وما بث فيهما من دابة وهو على جمعهم إذا يشاء قدير

translation: And whatever disaster befalls you is because of what your hands have earned. And He pardons much.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the difficulties and misfortunes that people face are often a consequence of their own actions and choices. It suggests that we should take responsibility for our deeds, as they can have consequences. However, the verse also highlights God's mercy and forgiveness, indicating that He pardons many of our transgressions. This encourages us to seek repentance and strive to make better choices, while also finding solace in the knowledge that God is forgiving and merciful.
orig: وما أصابكم من مصيبة فبما كسبت أيديكم ويعفو عن كثير

translation: And you will never be able to escape [your punishment] upon the earth, and you have not besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that humans cannot escape the consequences of their actions and that they have no one to protect or help them besides Allah. It serves as a reminder that we are accountable to Allah for our deeds, and that we should seek His guidance and protection rather than relying on our own strength or the help of others.
orig: وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And of His signs are the ships sailing in the sea like mountains.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and might of Allah, the Creator, in creating the vast oceans and the ships that sail upon them. The ships, which are compared to mountains in their size and grandeur, are a testament to Allah's ability to create things of immense scale and beauty. This serves as a sign for those who reflect and recognize the glory of the Almighty.
orig: ومن آياته الجوار في البحر كالأعلام

translation: If He wills, He can cause the wind to be still, so that they would become motionless on its back. Indeed, in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute power and control over the natural world. He can cause the wind, which is normally in motion, to become still and the waves to become motionless. This is a sign of God's might and sovereignty for those who are patient and grateful in their faith. The interpretation suggests that even in the face of life's trials and tribulations, one should remain steadfast in their belief and thankful to God, for He has the power to calm the storms and provide tranquility.
orig: إن يشأ يسكن الريح فيظللن رواكد على ظهره إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: Or He may destroy them [i.e., the wives] for what they have earned; and He pardons much.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has the power to punish or destroy the wives for their misdeeds, but He also has the capacity to forgive and pardon many of their transgressions. The verse highlights the dual nature of Allah's judgment - He can hold people accountable for their actions, but He is also merciful and forgiving towards those who seek His pardon.
orig: أو يوبقهن بما كسبوا ويعف عن كثير

translation: And those who dispute concerning Our verses may know that for them there is no [way of] refuge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who argue against or reject the signs and messages of Allah will have no escape or refuge from the consequences of their actions. They cannot avoid the ultimate judgment and accountability for their denial of the truth revealed in the Qur'an.
orig: ويعلم الذين يجادلون في آياتنا ما لهم من محيص

translation: And whatever you have been given is but [a passing] enjoyment of the worldly life. And what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who have believed and upon their Lord rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the material possessions and wealth of this world are temporary and fleeting. The true and lasting rewards are those that come from Allah, for those who believe in Him and put their trust in Him. It encourages believers to focus on the eternal life in the Hereafter rather than being overly attached to the transient pleasures of this world.
orig: فما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وما عند الله خير وأبقى للذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, and when they are angry, they forgive.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to abstain from major sins and immoral acts, and to exercise self-control and forgiveness even when they are provoked to anger. It suggests that true faith is not just about avoiding wrongdoing, but also about cultivating virtues like mercy, compassion and the ability to pardon others. This teaches us that a righteous person is not defined solely by their lack of sins, but also by their positive qualities and actions, such as forgiving those who have wronged them.
orig: والذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش وإذا ما غضبوا هم يغفرون

translation: And those who have responded to their Lord and established prayer and whose matter [i.e., affairs] is [determined by] consultation among themselves, and from what We have provided them, they spend.
interpretation:
This verse highlights several important characteristics of the believers:
1) They have responded to the call of their Lord and submitted to His guidance.
2) They are steadfast in their prayer, fulfilling this fundamental religious obligation.
3) They consult with one another in their affairs, valuing collective decision-making.
4) They are generous in spending from the provisions that God has granted them, using their wealth for good purposes.
orig: والذين استجابوا لربهم وأقاموا الصلاة وأمرهم شورى بينهم ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And those who, when tyranny strikes them, they defend themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the right of people to defend themselves against oppression and injustice. It suggests that when faced with wrongdoing or tyranny, it is permissible and even encouraged for individuals to stand up for their rights and seek redress. The interpretation highlights the importance of self-preservation and the rejection of passivity in the face of oppression.
orig: والذين إذا أصابهم البغي هم ينتصرون

translation: And the recompense for an evil act is an evil one like it, but whoever pardons and makes amends - his reward is [due] from Allah. Indeed, He does not like wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse teaches that the appropriate response to an evil deed is not necessarily retaliation, but rather forgiveness and reform. While it is natural to want to punish those who have wronged us, this verse encourages us to exercise restraint and pardon the offender. In doing so, we will be rewarded by Allah, who does not love those who engage in wrongdoing. The message here is one of mercy, compassion, and the transformative power of forgiveness.
orig: وجزاء سيئة سيئة مثلها فمن عفا وأصلح فأجره على الله إنه لا يحب الظالمين

translation: And for whoever avenges himself after having been wronged - those, there is not against them any cause [for blame].
interpretation: This verse encourages those who have been wronged to seek justice and redress, but in a measured and proportionate way. It suggests that there is no blame or sin upon those who seek to defend themselves or their rights after having been unjustly treated, as long as they do not exceed the bounds of what is right and fair. The emphasis is on restoring balance and equity, not on engaging in excessive retaliation or vengeance.
orig: ولمن انتصر بعد ظلمه فأولئك ما عليهم من سبيل

translation: The blame is only against those who oppress people and transgress in the earth without right. For them will be a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the blame and punishment are only for those who oppress and wrong others, and who seek to cause corruption and disorder on the earth without any just cause. The verse conveys that those who engage in such unjust and oppressive acts will face a painful and severe punishment.
orig: إنما السبيل على الذين يظلمون الناس ويبغون في الأرض بغير الحق أولئك لهم عذاب أليم

translation: And whoever is patient and forgives - indeed, that is of the matters [requiring] determination.
interpretation: This verse encourages patience and forgiveness. It suggests that those who are able to exercise patience and forgive others, despite the difficulties they may face, are demonstrating strength of character and determination in dealing with the challenges of life. The interpretation is that true strength lies not in retaliation or holding grudges, but in the ability to rise above adversity through patience and compassion.
orig: ولمن صبر وغفر إن ذلك لمن عزم الأمور

translation: And whomever Allah leaves astray - for him there is no protector after Him. And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying, "Is there for us any way to [get out]?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those whom Allah has led astray have no one to guide them or protect them. When the wrongdoers see the punishment they face, they will realize the futility of their actions and desperately seek a way out, but there will be no escape for them. This highlights the importance of following the guidance of Allah and avoiding wrongdoing, as the consequences are grave and inescapable.
orig: ومن يضلل الله فما له من ولي من بعده وترى الظالمين لما رأوا العذاب يقولون هل إلى مرد من سبيل

translation: And you will see them being presented to it (i.e., the Fire), humbled from the [various] disgrace, looking from [behind] a concealed glance. And those who believed will say, "Indeed, the [true] losers are the ones who lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in a lasting punishment."
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They will be presented to the Fire, humbled and disgraced, looking at it with fear and trepidation. In contrast, the believers will recognize that the true losers are those who have lost themselves and their families by rejecting faith and doing evil deeds. This emphasizes that the wrongdoers will face a lasting and severe punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: وتراهم يعرضون عليها خاشعين من الذل ينظرون من طرف خفي وقال الذين آمنوا إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة ألا إن الظالمين في عذاب مقيم

translation: And they had no allies to help them besides Allah, and whomever Allah leaves astray - for him there is no way [of guidance].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that there is no one who can help or guide those whom Allah has left astray. It highlights the complete reliance on Allah and the lack of any other source of support or guidance for those who have been led astray by Allah. The interpretation suggests that one's ultimate destiny is in the hands of Allah, and there is no alternative path or assistance available outside of Allah's guidance.
orig: وما كان لهم من أولياء ينصرونهم من دون الله ومن يضلل الله فما له من سبيل

translation: Respond to your Lord before a Day comes from Allah for which there is no repelling. You will have no refuge that Day, nor for you will there be any denial.
interpretation: This verse urges people to respond to the call of their Lord before the Day of Judgment arrives, a day from which there is no escape. On that day, people will have no place to seek refuge and no way to deny their misdeeds. The verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and submission to Allah before it is too late.
orig: استجيبوا لربكم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا مرد له من الله ما لكم من ملجإ يومئذ وما لكم من نكير

translation: But if they turn away, We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], as a guardian over them. Upon you is only [the duty of] notification. And indeed, when We let the human taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it; but if harm afflicts him because of what his hands have put forth, then indeed, the human is ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad's role is to convey the message of Islam, not to force people to believe. If people choose to reject the message, the Prophet is not responsible for that. The verse also highlights the human tendency to be grateful when experiencing God's mercy, but ungrateful when facing hardship, despite the fact that hardship is often a consequence of one's own actions.
orig: فإن أعرضوا فما أرسلناك عليهم حفيظا إن عليك إلا البلاغ وإنا إذا أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة فرح بها وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدمت أيديهم فإن الإنسان كفور

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He creates what He wills. He gives to whom He wills female [children], and He gives to whom He wills male [children].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the sole Sovereign and Creator of the entire universe. He has complete power and authority over all of creation, including the ability to bestow children of either gender upon whomever He wills. This highlights Allah’s absolute sovereignty and the fact that all things in the heavens and the earth belong to Him alone.
orig: لله ملك السماوات والأرض يخلق ما يشاء يهب لمن يشاء إناثا ويهب لمن يشاء الذكور

translation: Or He may marry them to men and women, and He makes whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's absolute power and sovereignty in determining the outcomes of human lives. He has the authority to unite people in marriage, whether male and female or same-sex couples, and He also has the power to make some people childless, if that is His will. This demonstrates that God is all-knowing and all-powerful, and that His decisions are based on His infinite wisdom, even if they are not always apparent to us.
orig: أو يزوجهم ذكرانا وإناثا ويجعل من يشاء عقيما إنه عليم قدير

translation: And it is not [possible] for any human being that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a partition or that He sends a messenger to reveal, by His permission, what He wills. Indeed, He is Most High and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is not possible for any human being to directly communicate with Allah, the Almighty, except through three means: 1) Revelation (Wahy), where Allah directly inspires the message to the prophet, 2) From behind a veil or partition, where the communication is indirect, and 3) Through a messenger (Rasool) whom Allah sends to convey His message. This highlights the greatness and majesty of Allah, who is "Most High and Wise" in His dealings with humanity.
orig: وما كان لبشر أن يكلمه الله إلا وحيا أو من وراء حجاب أو يرسل رسولا فيوحي بإذنه ما يشاء إنه علي حكيم

translation: And thus We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], a Spirit from Our command. You did not know what is the Book or [what is] faith, but We have made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed, [O Muhammad], you guide to a straight path
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an and the faith it represents were revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by God's command, even though he did not have prior knowledge of them. The Qur'an is described as a "light" that guides those whom God wills among His servants. This suggests that the Qur'an provides clear guidance and direction to those whom God chooses to guide, leading them to the straight path.
orig: وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان ولكن جعلناه نورا نهدي به من نشاء من عبادنا وإنك لتهدي إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: The path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Unquestionably, to Allah are [all] matters returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the sole Creator and Sustainer of the entire universe, both in the heavens and on the earth. All matters, affairs, and ultimate destinies are under His control and will return to Him. This underscores the need for humans to follow the straight path laid out by Allah, as it is the only path that leads to the ultimate purpose of our existence - returning to Allah.
orig: صراط الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ألا إلى الله تصير الأمور

translation: Ha. Mim.
interpretation: The letters "Ha" and "Mim" at the beginning of this Quranic chapter are known as "Muqatta'at" or "Disconnected Letters". Their exact meaning and significance are not fully understood, but they are believed to be part of the divine communication, serving as a reminder of the mysteries and complexities of the Quran. The interpretation is that these letters are a way for God to emphasize the divine nature of the Quran and to draw the reader's attention to the profound and intricate nature of the divine message.
orig: حم

translation: By the clear Book
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an, which is described as the "clear Book". The Qur'an is a divine revelation that provides clear guidance and instructions for humanity. It is "clear" in the sense that its message is unambiguous and its teachings are easily understandable for those who seek to understand and follow them. The Qur'an is a source of wisdom, knowledge, and spiritual enlightenment, and its clarity is a testament to its divine origin.
orig: والكتاب المبين

translation: Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an that you might understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an has been revealed in the Arabic language so that the people, to whom it was first addressed, could comprehend its message and teachings. The use of the Arabic language facilitates a deeper understanding of the Qur'an, as it allows the original meaning and nuances to be conveyed effectively. The verse suggests that by understanding the Qur'an in its original Arabic form, the believers can gain a more profound appreciation of its wisdom and guidance.
orig: إنا جعلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون

translation: And indeed, it [i.e., the Qur'an] is in the Mother of the Book [i.e., the Preserved Tablet] with Us, [and] indeed it is [that] exalted [in position]; [and] wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an is preserved with Allah in the Preserved Tablet, which is the source of all divine scriptures. The Qur'an is exalted in its position and content, and it is full of wisdom. This emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, and its superiority over all other scriptures.
orig: وإنه في أم الكتاب لدينا لعلي حكيم

translation: So shall We then turn away the Reminder from you, because you are a people transgressing?
interpretation: This verse suggests that if people persist in their excessive and wasteful behavior, God may withdraw the guidance and reminders provided through the Qur'an. The interpretation is that those who transgress and exceed proper bounds may be deprived of the divine guidance if they do not heed the warnings and teachings contained in the Qur"an.
orig: أفنضرب عنكم الذكر صفحا أن كنتم قوما مسرفين

translation: And how many a prophet did We send among the former peoples
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has sent numerous prophets throughout history to guide and instruct humanity. It suggests that the message of Islam is not a new or isolated phenomenon, but rather part of a long tradition of divine guidance and revelation. The interpretation is that Allah has consistently provided guidance to people in all eras, through the sending of prophets, in order to lead them towards righteousness and the worship of the one true God.
orig: وكم أرسلنا من نبي في الأولين

translation: And there has not come to them a prophet except that they used to ridicule him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of some people to mock and ridicule the prophets sent by God, rather than accepting their message with sincerity. It suggests that this has been a recurring pattern throughout history, where people have often been resistant to the guidance and teachings brought by the messengers of God. The verse serves as a warning against such arrogance and rejection of divine wisdom, and encourages believers to approach the prophets with an open and receptive mindset.
orig: وما يأتيهم من نبي إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And We destroyed those stronger than them in [physical] power, and the example of the former peoples has previously passed.
interpretation: This verse is referring to how Allah has destroyed previous nations and civilizations that were more powerful and dominant than the people being addressed. The verse is a warning that just as Allah destroyed those who came before, He can also destroy the current people if they do not heed His message and guidance. The interpretation is that no one is too powerful or mighty to escape the consequences of their actions if they defy Allah and His commandments.
orig: فأهلكنا أشد منهم بطشا ومضى مثل الأولين

translation: And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, "[They were created by] the Exalted in Might, the Knowing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that even those who do not believe in the oneness of God (Allah) acknowledge that the creation of the heavens and the earth is the work of a powerful and all-knowing Creator. It serves as a reminder that the signs of God's existence and power are evident in the universe, and that those who deny Him are willfully ignoring the truth.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن خلقهن العزيز العليم

translation: It is He who made the earth a bed [spread out] for you and inserted therein for you roadways [pathways] that you might be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God has created the earth as a comfortable and habitable place for humanity, and has provided us with the means to navigate and find our way upon it. The "pathways" mentioned can be interpreted as both physical routes and metaphorical paths that guide us, allowing us to be "guided" both physically and spiritually. The verse suggests that by recognizing and appreciating God's provision, we may be led to the right path and find our way.
orig: الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا وجعل لكم فيها سبلا لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And it is He who sends down rain from the sky in measured amounts, and We revive thereby a dead land - thus will you be brought forth [from the graves].
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and wisdom of God, who sends down rain from the sky in precise quantities to revive dead and barren lands. Just as God brings life to the earth through rainfall, He will also resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment, demonstrating His absolute control and authority over all creation. This serves as a reminder of the afterlife and the need for humans to prepare for the Day of Reckoning.
orig: والذي نزل من السماء ماء بقدر فأنشرنا به بلدة ميتا كذلك تخرجون

translation: And it is He who created the pairs - all of them - and made for you from the ships and from the livestock that which you ride.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and wisdom in creating all things in pairs, including the ships and livestock that humans use for transportation. It suggests that God has provided us with the means to travel and move about, which is a sign of His care and provision for humanity.
orig: والذي خلق الأزواج كلها وجعل لكم من الفلك والأنعام ما تركبون

translation: That you may mount firmly upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you have mounted thereon and say, "Exalted is He who has subjected this to us, and we could not [otherwise] have subdued it."
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the blessings of Allah and give thanks to Him for the ability to ride and control animals. It reminds us that it is only through Allah's power and favor that we are able to subdue and utilize these creatures for our benefit. The verse calls us to glorify and praise Allah for granting us this capability, which we could not have attained on our own.
orig: لتستووا على ظهوره ثم تذكروا نعمة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه وتقولوا سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين

translation: And indeed, to our Lord we will return.
interpretation: This verse expresses the fundamental belief in Islam that all human beings will ultimately return to God, their Creator, for judgment and accountability. It highlights the transient nature of this world and the certainty of the Hereafter, where each person will be held responsible for their actions and beliefs. This verse serves as a reminder to live a life that is pleasing to God, as we will all face Him on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون

translation: And they have attributed to Him from His servants a portion. Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse refers to the practice of idolatry, where people associate partners with God and worship them alongside Him. The verse condemns this practice, stating that it is a clear display of man's ingratitude towards the One true God who created him. The interpretation is that people should worship and submit to God alone, without ascribing any partners to Him.
orig: وجعلوا له من عباده جزءا إن الإنسان لكفور مبين

translation: Or has He taken daughters out of what He creates and chosen for you sons?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the practice of the pagan Arabs who used to consider female children as inferior and would sometimes bury them alive. The verse challenges this notion by asking whether God, the Creator, has chosen daughters for Himself and only sons for humans. The implication is that God's creation of both males and females is equal and that there is no basis for discriminating against women.
orig: أم اتخذ مما يخلق بنات وأصفاكم بالبنين

translation: And when one of them is informed of [the birth of] a female, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief.
interpretation: This verse condemns the pre-Islamic Arab practice of considering the birth of a daughter as a misfortune. The verse highlights the negative reaction and suppressed anger that some people had towards the birth of a female child, as they viewed it as a sign of weakness or shame. The interpretation emphasizes that this attitude is unacceptable and goes against the teachings of the Quran, which views all human life as sacred and deserving of equal respect, regardless of gender.
orig: وإذا بشر أحدهم بما ضرب للرحمن مثلا ظل وجهه مسودا وهو كظيم

translation: Or is one who is brought up in ornaments while they are not clear in dispute?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, comparing someone who is brought up in luxury and adornment, but is unclear or ambiguous in their arguments and disputes, to someone who is more grounded and straightforward. The implication is that the former is less worthy or reliable than the latter, as their outward appearance and status does not necessarily reflect the substance or clarity of their character and reasoning.
orig: أومن ينشأ في الحلية وهو في الخصام غير مبين

translation: And they have attributed to the angels who are the servants of the Most Merciful female [gender]. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the pagan Arabs who believed that the angels were female deities. The verse emphasizes that the angels are servants of God, the Most Merciful, and that they did not witness their own creation. Their testimony about the nature of the angels will be recorded, and they will be questioned about their false beliefs on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وجعلوا الملائكة الذين هم عباد الرحمن إناثا أشهدوا خلقهم ستكتب شهادتهم ويسألون

translation: And they say, "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have of that no knowledge. They are not but falsifying.
interpretation: This verse addresses the claim made by some people that if God (referred to as the Most Merciful) had willed, they would not have worshipped idols. The Qur'an responds by stating that they have no real knowledge to support this claim, and that they are merely speculating or making unfounded assertions ("they are not but falsifying"). The verse emphasizes that people are responsible for their choices in worship and cannot blame God for their actions.
orig: وقالوا لو شاء الرحمن ما عبدناهم ما لهم بذلك من علم إن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: Or have We given them a Book before this (the Qur'an) to which they are holding fast?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Qur'an is not the first divine scripture revealed to humanity. It raises the question of whether the people were previously given another scripture that they were holding onto, implying that the Qur'an is a continuation and confirmation of that earlier revelation. The interpretation suggests that the Qur'an is not something entirely new, but rather builds upon and affirms the teachings of previous divinely-revealed scriptures.
orig: أم آتيناهم كتابا من قبله فهم به مستمسكون

translation: Rather, they say, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon [a particular] religion, and we are in their footsteps [rightly] guided."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the attitude of those who blindly follow the religious beliefs and practices of their ancestors, without critically examining the validity and soundness of those beliefs. The verse suggests that such people justify their adherence to their ancestral religion simply because they found their forefathers following it, without any deeper understanding or personal conviction. The implication is that this is an insufficient basis for religious belief and practice, and that one should strive to seek the truth through independent inquiry and reflection, rather than relying solely on tradition and custom.
orig: بل قالوا إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مهتدون

translation: And similarly, We have not sent before you any warner into a city except that its affluent said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and we are in their footsteps [following].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that throughout history, whenever a prophet was sent to a community, the affluent and powerful members of that society would resist the message and claim to be following the religion of their forefathers. They would refuse to accept the new guidance brought by the prophet, insisting on adhering to the beliefs and practices of their ancestors. This highlights the human tendency to cling to tradition and resist change, even in the face of divine guidance. The interpretation suggests that one should not blindly follow the ways of the past, but rather be open to receiving and accepting the truth, even if it goes against established norms.
orig: وكذلك ما أرسلنا من قبلك في قرية من نذير إلا قال مترفوها إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون

translation: They said: "If you have brought a better [religion] than that upon which we found our fathers, [then we will follow it]." [The disbelievers] said: "Indeed, we are in regarding you disbelievers [in that which you have brought]."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the resistance of the disbelievers to accepting the new message of Islam, even when presented with a superior way of life. They stubbornly cling to the traditions and beliefs of their forefathers, refusing to acknowledge the truth of the Qur’an. This highlights the human tendency to reject change and new ideas, even when they are clearly better, due to blind adherence to the past. The interpretation underscores the importance of being open-minded and willing to critically examine one’s beliefs, rather than rejecting them outright based on tradition or familiarity.
orig: قال أولو جئتكم بأهدى مما وجدتم عليه آباءكم قالوا إنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون

translation: So We took retribution from them, and see how was the end of the deniers.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the consequences faced by those who reject and deny the truth of God's message. It suggests that those who stubbornly refuse to believe and continue in their denial will ultimately face divine punishment and a dire end. The verse encourages the reader to reflect on the fate of the deniers, as a lesson and a warning to those who persist in their disbelief.
orig: فانتقمنا منهم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am disassociated from that which you worship"
interpretation: This verse highlights Abraham's rejection of the idolatrous practices of his father and people. Abraham clearly states that he is free from and disassociated with the worship of false deities, emphasizing his monotheistic belief in the one true God. This verse demonstrates Abraham's courage and conviction in standing up for his faith, even in the face of opposition from his own family and community.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه وقومه إنني براء مما تعبدون

translation: Except for He who created me; and indeed, He will guide me.
interpretation: This verse expresses the belief that the only one who can truly guide a person is the one who created them, i.e. God. It suggests that true guidance and direction in life can only come from the Creator, not from other sources. The interpretation is that one should rely on God's guidance and wisdom, as He is the ultimate source of guidance and direction for the faithful.
orig: إلا الذي فطرني فإنه سيهدين

translation: And He made it a lasting word in his descendants that they might return [to obedience].
interpretation: This verse refers to the promise of Allah to make the message of Islam a lasting legacy that would be passed down through the generations of Prophet Abraham's descendants. The purpose of this is to encourage them to return to the worship and obedience of Allah, so that they may find guidance and salvation.
orig: وجعلها كلمة باقية في عقبه لعلهم يرجعون

translation: Rather, these [disbelievers] and their forefathers had enjoyed [worldly] pleasures until there came to them the truth and a clear Messenger.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who have been indulging in worldly pleasures and ignoring the truth. It suggests that they and their ancestors had been enjoying the comforts of this life, but now the truth has come to them in the form of a clear Messenger. The implication is that they should now turn away from their worldly pursuits and embrace the guidance brought by the Messenger, as the truth has been made manifest to them.
orig: بل متعت هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى جاءهم الحق ورسول مبين

translation: And when the truth has come to them, they say, "This is magic, and indeed we are disbelievers [in it]."
interpretation: This verse refers to the response of the disbelievers when the truth of the Qur'an and the message of Islam was presented to them. They dismissed it as mere sorcery or magic, and refused to accept it, declaring their disbelief. This highlights the stubborn rejection of the truth by those whose hearts are hardened and who are unwilling to submit to the guidance of Allah.
orig: ولما جاءهم الحق قالوا هذا سحر وإنا به كافرون

translation: And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from [one of] the two cities?"
interpretation: This verse addresses the objection raised by the disbelievers regarding the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). They questioned why the Qur'an was not revealed to a prominent and influential person from the two major cities of Mecca and Taif, rather than to a simple man like the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). This objection stemmed from their arrogance and desire for status, as they believed that the Qur'an should have been revealed to someone of high social standing. However, Allah chose the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), who was humble and of modest means, to receive the final revelation, demonstrating that the message of Islam is for all of humanity, regardless of social status or wealth.
orig: وقالوا لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم

translation: Or do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? It is We who have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world and have raised some of them above others in degrees [of rank] that they may make use of one another for service. But the mercy of your Lord is better than whatever they accumulate.
interpretation: This verse addresses the notion that some people may think they can decide how Allah's mercy is distributed. The verse clarifies that it is Allah who has apportioned the means of livelihood among people in this world, and has raised some above others in degrees of rank. This is so that people may utilize one another's skills and services. However, the mercy of Allah is greater than any worldly possessions or status that people may accumulate. The verse emphasizes that Allah's wisdom in distributing provisions and status is superior to human perceptions or attempts to control it.
orig: أهم يقسمون رحمت ربك نحن قسمنا بينهم معيشتهم في الحياة الدنيا ورفعنا بعضهم فوق بعض درجات ليتخذ بعضهم بعضا سخريا ورحمت ربك خير مما يجمعون

translation: And if it were not that the people would become one community, We would have made for the ones who disbelieve in the Most Merciful - for their houses - ceilings of silver and stairways upon which they would mount.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God did not grant excessive wealth and luxury to the disbelievers in order to prevent them from becoming a unified community against the believers. The implication is that if the disbelievers were given such lavish provisions, they would have become arrogant and united in their rejection of the faith, which would have been detrimental to the believers. Thus, God in His wisdom chose to withhold such material bounties from them in order to maintain a balance and prevent the believers from being overwhelmed.
orig: ولولا أن يكون الناس أمة واحدة لجعلنا لمن يكفر بالرحمن لبيوتهم سقفا من فضة ومعارج عليها يظهرون

translation: And for their houses are doors and couches [of repose] upon which they recline
interpretation: This verse describes the luxurious and comfortable dwellings of the people in the Hereafter. The doors and couches symbolize the grandeur and opulence of their abodes, where they can rest and relax in peace and tranquility. The verse emphasizes the idea that the righteous will be rewarded with a life of comfort and ease in the Afterlife, in contrast to the hardships and trials they may have faced in this world.
orig: ولبيوتهم أبوابا وسررا عليها يتكئون

translation: And adornment. And indeed, all of that is but the enjoyment of worldly life, and the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly possessions and adornments. It reminds us that the material pleasures of this life are temporary and that the true and lasting reward is with God in the Hereafter, which is reserved for the righteous and God-fearing individuals.
orig: وزخرفا وإن كل ذلك لما متاع الحياة الدنيا والآخرة عند ربك للمتقين

translation: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful - We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion.
interpretation: This verse warns against turning away from the remembrance of Allah (the Most Merciful). It states that if someone neglects the remembrance of Allah, the Almighty will assign a devil to be their constant companion. This devil will then lead that person further astray, tempting them and making their evil deeds seem attractive to them. The interpretation is that maintaining a connection with Allah through His remembrance is crucial to avoid falling under the influence of Satan and being led down a path of misguidance.
orig: ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن نقيض له شيطانا فهو له قرين

translation: And indeed, they avert [people] from the way, while they think that they are [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who mislead others and prevent them from following the right path, while they themselves believe that they are on the correct path. It highlights the danger of self-deception and the importance of seeking guidance from reliable sources and not being misled by those who claim to have the answers, but in reality, are leading people astray.
orig: وإنهم ليصدونهم عن السبيل ويحسبون أنهم مهتدون

translation: Until, when death comes to one of you, he says, 'My Lord, send me back that I might do righteousness in that which I left behind.' No! It is only a word he is saying; and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the regret that a person may feel at the time of death, wishing to be sent back to the world to make amends and do good deeds. However, the verse emphasizes that this is merely a plea, and there is a barrier that prevents the dead from returning to the living world until the Day of Resurrection. The interpretation highlights the finality of death and the importance of making the most of one's life before it is too late.
orig: حتى إذا جاءنا قال يا ليت بيني وبينك بعد المشرقين فبئس القرين

translation: And it will not benefit you that Day when you have wronged [i.e., sinned]. You will [all] be partners [i.e., sharers] in the punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, when people are held accountable for their actions, it will not be of any benefit to those who have wronged others or committed sins. They will all be equally punished and share in the torment, regardless of their status or position in this world. The verse serves as a warning to people to refrain from wrongdoing and to seek forgiveness and repentance before it is too late.
orig: ولن ينفعكم اليوم إذ ظلمتم أنكم في العذاب مشتركون

translation: Then will you make the deaf to hear, or guide the blind or him who is in clear error?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and challenging the notion that he can guide those who are spiritually deaf, blind or in clear error. The implication is that it is ultimately Allah who guides people, and the Prophet's role is to convey the message, not to force belief upon those who are unwilling to accept it. The verse emphasizes the limits of the Prophet's abilities and the need for people to willingly choose to accept the guidance of Allah.
orig: أفأنت تسمع الصم أو تهدي العمي ومن كان في ضلال مبين

translation: So if We should will, We could take you away. Then We would surely be the ones to take retribution against them.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if God wills, He can take the Prophet away from his people and punish them for their rejection of the message. It emphasizes God's power and sovereignty, and His ability to hold people accountable for their actions. The interpretation highlights the idea that God is the ultimate judge and can mete out punishment to those who defy His commands.
orig: فإما نذهبن بك فإنا منهم منتقمون

translation: Or We show you that [destruction] which We have promised them, for indeed, We are over them perfect in ability.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has the power to show the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) the destruction that He has promised to the disbelievers. It implies that Allah is all-powerful and can bring about the consequences He has warned of for those who reject faith. The verse reinforces the notion that Allah is in control and can fulfill His promises, whether of reward for the believers or punishment for the disbelievers.
orig: أو نرينك الذي وعدناهم فإنا عليهم مقتدرون

translation: So hold fast to that which is revealed to you. Indeed, you are on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain steadfast in his adherence to the divine revelation he has received from God (Allah). It assures him that he is following the right and righteous path, and that he should not deviate from it. This message is also applicable to all believers, who are called to hold firmly to the teachings of the Qur'an and the guidance of Islam, and to walk steadfastly on the path of truth and righteousness.
orig: فاستمسك بالذي أوحي إليك إنك على صراط مستقيم

translation: And indeed, [O Muhammad], it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a reminder and guidance not only for the Prophet Muhammad, but also for his people and all of humanity. It serves as a reminder of the teachings of Islam and the responsibility that comes with being a believer. The verse also suggests that on the Day of Judgment, all people will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs, and will be questioned about how they lived their lives in accordance with the guidance provided in the Qur'an.
orig: وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك وسوف تسألون

translation: And ask those [prophets] We sent before you, [O Muhammad], 'Did We ever appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?'
interpretation: This verse instructs Prophet Muhammad to ask the previous prophets if they were ever commanded to appoint gods to be worshipped alongside Allah, the Most Merciful. The implication is that there is only one true God worthy of worship, and that the worship of any other deities is forbidden. This reinforces the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and supremacy of God.
orig: واسأل من أرسلنا من قبلك من رسلنا أجعلنا من دون الرحمن آلهة يعبدون

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, and he said, "Indeed, I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse describes how God sent the prophet Moses with clear signs and evidence to Pharaoh and his people, and Moses declared that he was a messenger sent by the Lord of all the worlds. This emphasizes that Moses was not acting on his own accord, but was divinely commissioned to convey God's message to the powerful ruler of Egypt at the time. The verse highlights Moses' role as a messenger of the one true God, in contrast to the false deities worshipped by Pharaoh and his followers.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا إلى فرعون وملئه فقال إني رسول رب العالمين

translation: And when Our signs came to them, they laughed at them.
interpretation: This verse refers to the reaction of the disbelievers when the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) presented them with the clear signs and miracles of God. Instead of accepting the truth, they mocked and ridiculed the signs, showing their arrogance and rejection of the divine message. This highlights the importance of having an open and receptive heart when encountering the teachings of God, rather than dismissing them out of hand.
orig: فلما جاءهم بآياتنا إذا هم منها يضحكون

translation: And We do not show them a sign except that it is greater than its sister [sign], and We seized them with punishment that perhaps they might return [to faith].
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah (God) shows people signs and miracles to guide them towards faith and belief in Him. However, even when these signs are shown, the people often fail to heed them or return to faith. The verse implies that the signs shown by Allah are progressively greater and more compelling, yet people remain heedless. The purpose of this is to lead them to repentance and a return to the right path, so that they may be saved from punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: وما نريهم من آية إلا هي أكبر من أختها وأخذناهم بالعذاب لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And they said, "O you sorcerer, invoke for us your Lord by what He has promised you. Indeed, we will be guided."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who demanded that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) invoke his Lord to prove the truth of his message. They claimed that if he did so, they would believe and be guided. However, this was merely a ploy, as they had no intention of truly believing. The verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of those who reject the truth, even in the face of clear signs and evidence.
orig: وقالوا يا أيه الساحر ادع لنا ربك بما عهد عندك إننا لمهتدون

translation: And when We remove the punishment from them, at once they are rebellious.
interpretation: This verse suggests that when people are relieved from a trial or punishment, they may become arrogant and disobedient. It highlights the tendency of some individuals to forget the lessons learned during difficult times and to revert to their previous sinful ways. The interpretation suggests that true faith and obedience should not be contingent on the presence or absence of hardship, but should be a constant state of being.
orig: فلما كشفنا عنهم العذاب إذا هم ينكثون

translation: And Pharaoh called out among his people, saying, "O my people, is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Then do you not see?"
interpretation: This verse highlights Pharaoh's arrogance and his belief in his own power and authority. He boasts about his control over Egypt and its resources, suggesting that his people should recognize and submit to his sovereignty. The verse emphasizes Pharaoh's delusion of grandeur and his failure to acknowledge the true power and sovereignty of God.
orig: ونادى فرعون في قومه قال يا قوم أليس لي ملك مصر وهذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي أفلا تبصرون

translation: Or am I better than this one who is despised and can hardly make [his] point?
interpretation: This verse is questioning whether the speaker is better than someone who is despised and can hardly express themselves clearly. The implication is that the speaker may not be superior to this other individual, despite any perceived differences in status or ability. The verse encourages humility and not judging others based on outward appearances or perceived shortcomings.
orig: أم أنا خير من هذا الذي هو مهين ولا يكاد يبين

translation: Why then was he not given bracelets of gold, or why have [not] the angels come with him in procession?
interpretation: This verse is questioning why the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not given outward signs of wealth and status, such as golden bracelets, or why he was not accompanied by angels in a grand procession. The implication is that some people expected the Prophet to have such outward displays of power and grandeur, but this was not the case. The Qur'an is emphasizing that true guidance and faith do not depend on material wealth or outward displays, but rather on the message and teachings the Prophet brought.
orig: فلولا ألقي عليه أسورة من ذهب أو جاء معه الملائكة مقترنين

translation: So he made his people see it as trivial, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a people defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse describes the people of the prophet Pharaoh, who were easily swayed by his manipulative tactics and followed him despite his clear wrongdoing. The interpretation is that people can sometimes be easily misled by those in positions of power, even when the leader is clearly acting in a sinful or unjust manner. This serves as a warning against blindly following authority figures without critical examination of their actions.
orig: فاستخف قومه فأطاعوه إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all.
interpretation: This verse describes how the people who angered Allah were punished by being drowned. The interpretation is that those who defy and disobey Allah will face consequences for their actions, as Allah has the power to enact retribution against those who turn away from Him.
orig: فلما آسفونا انتقمنا منهم فأغرقناهم أجمعين

translation: And We made them a precedent and an example for the later [generations].
interpretation: This verse suggests that the previous nations and peoples who rejected the divine guidance and faced consequences serve as a lesson and example for future generations. Their fate is a warning to those who may be tempted to follow a similar path of disbelief and disobedience. The Qur'an encourages learning from the mistakes of the past in order to avoid similar fates and to remain steadfast in faith and righteous conduct.
orig: فجعلناهم سلفا ومثلا للآخرين

translation: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, immediately your people turn aside from it
interpretation: This verse refers to the reaction of the people when the Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) is mentioned or used as an example. The verse suggests that the people turned away from him and rejected him, rather than accepting his teachings and message. This highlights the resistance and opposition that the Prophet Jesus faced from his own people, the Children of Israel, when he called them to the worship of the one true God and to righteous conduct.
orig: ولما ضرب ابن مريم مثلا إذا قومك منه يصدون

translation: And they say, "Are our gods better, or is he?" They do not present that [comparison] except for [mere] argument. But, [in fact], they are a people intent on dispute.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the polytheists who would argue that their gods are superior to the one true God. The Qur'an refutes this claim, stating that their argument is merely a dispute without any real substance or evidence. The polytheists are portrayed as a people who are contentious and argumentative, more interested in debating than seeking the truth.
orig: وقالوا أآلهتنا خير أم هو ما ضربوه لك إلا جدلا بل هم قوم خصمون

translation: He is not but a servant upon whom We have bestowed favor, and We have made him an example for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse refers to Jesus (peace be upon him), who was a servant of God and a prophet sent to guide the Children of Israel. The verse emphasizes that Jesus was not divine, but rather a human being upon whom God had bestowed His favor and made an example for the Israelites to follow. The interpretation highlights the Islamic belief that Jesus was a prophet, not the son of God, and that he was sent as a messenger to guide humanity towards the worship of the one true God.
orig: إن هو إلا عبد أنعمنا عليه وجعلناه مثلا لبني إسرائيل

translation: And if We willed, We could have made from you angels succeeding [one another] on the earth.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if Allah so willed, He could have created humans as angels to inhabit the earth instead. However, Allah chose to create humans with free will, who can worship and serve Him, rather than angels who have no choice but to obey. This highlights the unique status and responsibility of humans as Allah's vicegerents on earth.
orig: ولو نشاء لجعلنا منكم ملائكة في الأرض يخلفون

translation: And indeed, it [i.e., the Qur'an] is knowledge of the Hour, so have no doubt about it, and follow Me. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an contains knowledge about the coming of the Hour of Judgment, and that one should not doubt its occurrence. The verse instructs the believers to follow the guidance of Allah ("Follow Me") which is the straight and righteous path to salvation. The interpretation suggests that the Qur'an provides certainty about the inevitability of the Day of Resurrection, and that believers should have unwavering faith in it and adhere to Allah's commands to achieve eternal success.
orig: وإنه لعلم للساعة فلا تمترن بها واتبعون هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And let not Satan avert you. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse warns against being misled by Satan, who is a clear and open enemy of mankind. It emphasizes that we should not allow Satan to divert us from the right path or lead us astray, as he is an avowed adversary seeking to lead us into error and temptation.
orig: ولا يصدنكم الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said, "I have come to you with wisdom and to make clear to you some of that over which you differ, so fear Allah and obey me."
interpretation: This verse speaks of the coming of Jesus (peace be upon him) with clear signs and proofs of his prophethood. He came to the people with wisdom and to clarify some of the matters over which they differed. The verse encourages the people to fear Allah and obey Jesus, as he was a messenger sent by God to guide them.
orig: ولما جاء عيسى بالبينات قال قد جئتكم بالحكمة ولأبين لكم بعض الذي تختلفون فيه فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God, and calls upon all people to worship and submit to Him alone. It establishes that Allah is the sole deity worthy of worship, and that following His path is the only way to true guidance and salvation. The verse encourages believers to remain steadfast on this "straight path" and to direct all their devotion and obedience to the Almighty.
orig: إن الله هو ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And the parties disputed among themselves, and woe to those who disbelieved from the punishment of a painful Day.
interpretation: This verse refers to the divisions and conflicts that arose among the various factions and groups during the time of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It warns those who disbelieved and oppressed others that they will face a painful punishment on the Day of Judgment. The interpretation suggests that unity, harmony, and justice should prevail among people, and that those who engage in oppression and wrongdoing will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: فاختلف الأحزاب من بينهم فويل للذين ظلموا من عذاب يوم أليم

translation: Do they await except that the Hour should come upon them unexpectedly while they perceive not?
interpretation: This verse is encouraging people to be prepared for the Day of Judgment, which will come suddenly and unexpectedly. It reminds us that we should not be heedless or complacent, but rather be vigilant and ready for that momentous event. The interpretation is that we should not wait passively for the Hour to come, but actively work to prepare ourselves spiritually and morally for that day.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا الساعة أن تأتيهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: Close friends, on that Day, will be enemies to one another, except for the righteous
interpretation: This verse highlights that on the Day of Judgment, close relationships and friendships that people had in this world will no longer matter. All connections will be severed, and people will turn against each other, except for those who were righteous and God-fearing. The verse emphasizes that the only bond that will remain is the one between the righteous, as they will be protected from the discord and enmity that will engulf others.
orig: الأخلاء يومئذ بعضهم لبعض عدو إلا المتقين

translation: O My servants, no fear will there be concerning you this Day, nor will you grieve.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the believers, reassuring them that on the Day of Judgment, they will not experience any fear or grief. It is a message of comfort and reassurance, indicating that those who have truly submitted to God and followed His guidance will be protected and saved from the trials and tribulations of the Hereafter.
orig: يا عباد لا خوف عليكم اليوم ولا أنتم تحزنون

translation: Those who believe in Our verses and were [in fact] Muslims
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have accepted the truth of the Qur'anic revelations and submitted themselves to the will of God. They are described as "believers" in the signs or verses of God, and as being "Muslims" - those who have surrendered themselves to the divine guidance. This highlights the importance of both faith and righteous conduct in the Islamic tradition, where belief must be accompanied by the practical implementation of one's faith in one's life.
orig: الذين آمنوا بآياتنا وكانوا مسلمين

translation: Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, in happiness.
interpretation: This verse is an invitation to the believers to enter Paradise, the eternal abode of the righteous, along with their spouses. The emphasis on entering Paradise "in happiness" suggests that the believers will experience a state of joy, contentment, and bliss in the Hereafter, free from any sorrow or suffering. The verse highlights the importance of maintaining righteous relationships and companionship, as the believers and their spouses will be reunited and celebrate their eternal life in Paradise together.
orig: ادخلوا الجنة أنتم وأزواجكم تحبرون

translation: Circulated among them will be plates and vessels of gold. And therein is whatever the souls desire and [what] delights the eyes, and you will abide therein eternally.
