interpretation: This verse describes the delights and pleasures that will be enjoyed by the righteous in Paradise. The mention of gold plates and vessels symbolizes the grandeur and opulence of the eternal abode. The phrase "whatever the souls desire and [what] delights the eyes" suggests that the inhabitants of Paradise will be provided with everything they could wish for, fulfilling their every desire and bringing them endless joy and satisfaction. The final phrase "and you will abide therein eternally" emphasizes the permanence and everlasting nature of this blissful state, in contrast to the fleeting nature of worldly pleasures.
orig: يطاف عليهم بصحاف من ذهب وأكواب وفيها ما تشتهيه الأنفس وتلذ الأعين وأنتم فيها خالدون

translation: And that is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the eternal Paradise that has been promised to the righteous believers as a reward for their good deeds and righteous actions in this life. It emphasizes that the Paradise is an inheritance that they have earned through their virtuous conduct, not something that is given freely. The verse highlights the concept of accountability and the idea that one's actions in this world will determine one's ultimate destination in the Hereafter.
orig: وتلك الجنة التي أورثتموها بما كنتم تعملون

translation: For you therein is much fruit from which you will eat.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the abundance of fruits that will be available in Paradise for the believers. The phrase "for you therein" indicates that these fruits are a reward and blessing for those who have faith and do righteous deeds. The mention of "much fruit" suggests a wide variety and plentiful supply, while the phrase "from which you will eat" implies that the believers will be able to freely partake of these fruits and derive nourishment and enjoyment from them. This verse highlights the bountiful provision and delights that await the faithful in the Hereafter.
orig: لكم فيها فاكهة كثيرة منها تأكلون

translation: Indeed, the criminals will be in the punishment of Hell, abiding eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who commit grave sins and transgressions will be eternally condemned to the punishment of Hell. It serves as a stern warning to those who persist in wrongdoing, reminding them of the dire consequences they will face in the Hereafter if they do not repent and reform their ways.
orig: إن المجرمين في عذاب جهنم خالدون

translation: They will not be relieved from it, and they will be plunged in it.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment in the Hellfire, where the disbelievers will be trapped without any relief or escape. They will be in a state of despair and hopelessness, unable to find a way out of their torment.
orig: لا يفتر عنهم وهم فيه مبلسون

translation: And We did not wrong them, but they were [themselves] the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah did not wrong or oppress the people, but rather, they were the ones who wronged themselves by rejecting the truth and committing sins. It serves as a reminder that the consequences of one's actions are a result of one's own choices and deeds, not due to any injustice from Allah. The verse highlights the principle of individual accountability, where each person is responsible for their own actions and the resulting outcomes.
orig: وما ظلمناهم ولكن كانوا هم الظالمين

translation: And they will call, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us." [Malik] will say, "Indeed, you will remain."
interpretation: This verse describes the desperate pleas of the disbelievers in the Hereafter, who will call out to the angel Malik (the keeper of Hell) to end their torment. However, Malik will inform them that they are doomed to remain in Hell forever as a punishment for their rejection of faith and evil deeds in the worldly life. The verse highlights the finality and permanence of the punishment in the Afterlife for those who denied God's signs and guidance.
orig: ونادوا يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك قال إنكم ماكثون

translation: We have certainly brought you the truth, but most of you to the truth are averse.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has revealed the truth to humanity through the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad. However, despite this clear guidance, many people choose to reject the truth and turn away from it. This suggests that faith and acceptance of the truth is a matter of individual choice, and that those who refuse to believe are responsible for their own disbelief.
orig: لقد جئناكم بالحق ولكن أكثركم للحق كارهون

translation: Or have they devised a plan? But indeed, We are the planners.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who oppose the truth may have devised a plan against it, but Allah is the ultimate planner and will foil their schemes. It emphasizes that Allah is in control and that those who plot against the truth will not succeed, for Allah's plan is superior and will prevail.
orig: أم أبرموا أمرا فإنا مبرمون

translation: Or do they think that We hear not their secrets and their private counsels? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah is all-knowing and aware of the secrets and private conversations of people. It serves as a reminder that even our most private thoughts and actions are known to Allah, who has appointed angels to record them. This emphasizes the importance of being righteous and accountable for our deeds, as Allah is ever-present and observing our conduct.
orig: أم يحسبون أنا لا نسمع سرهم ونجواهم بلى ورسلنا لديهم يكتبون

translation: Say, "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of [his] worshippers."
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that denies the notion of God having a son. It emphasizes that the concept of God having a son is incompatible with the idea of God being the Most Merciful. The verse is a declaration that the speaker would be the first to worship God if He had a son, which is a way of rejecting this idea. The interpretation is that the Qur'an is asserting the absolute oneness and uniqueness of God, and that the idea of God having a son is a false and unacceptable belief.
orig: قل إن كان للرحمن ولد فأنا أول العابدين

translation: Exalted is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, [far] above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and transcendence of Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. It declares that He is far above and beyond any human attempts to describe or comprehend Him. The verse serves to remind us of Allah's infinite power, majesty, and perfection, which are beyond the limitations of our human understanding. It calls upon us to glorify and revere Allah, acknowledging that He is the supreme Lord who is not bound by the constraints of His creation.
orig: سبحان رب السماوات والأرض رب العرش عما يصفون

translation: So leave them to plunge in [idle] talk and amuse themselves until they meet their Day which they are promised.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet to ignore the mockery and ridicule of the disbelievers, and to let them continue in their idle talk and amusement until they face the Day of Judgment that they have been warned about. The interpretation suggests that the disbelievers will be held accountable for their actions on that Day, and that the Prophet should focus on his mission rather than engage with their frivolous behavior.
orig: فذرهم يخوضوا ويلعبوا حتى يلاقوا يومهم الذي يوعدون

translation: And He it is Who in the heaven is God and in the earth is God. And He is the Wise, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse affirms the oneness and supremacy of God, who is the sole deity in both the heavens and the earth. It emphasizes that God is the Wise, the All-Knowing, and that His dominion and authority extend over the entire universe. This verse underscores the monotheistic nature of Islam and the belief that there is only one true God worthy of worship.
orig: وهو الذي في السماء إله وفي الأرض إله وهو الحكيم العليم

translation: And blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and with Him is knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and power of God, who owns and controls the entire universe, from the heavens to the earth and all that exists in between. It also highlights God's knowledge of the Hour, or the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions and return to Him. This verse serves as a reminder of God's supreme authority and the importance of worshiping and submitting to Him, as well as the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the need to prepare for it.
orig: وتبارك الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما وعنده علم الساعة وإليه ترجعون

translation: And those whom they invoke besides Him do not possess [power of] intercession, except [for] one who testifies to the truth [and] they know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the only beings who can intercede on behalf of others are those who have witnessed the truth and have knowledge of it. It denies the ability of false gods or idols to provide intercession, as they do not possess the necessary authority or knowledge to do so. The verse reinforces the concept of God's absolute sovereignty and the futility of seeking help from anything other than the One True God.
orig: ولا يملك الذين يدعون من دونه الشفاعة إلا من شهد بالحق وهم يعلمون

translation: And if you ask them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they will surely say, "Allah." Then how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that even those who deny the existence of God or associate partners with Him, when asked directly about the Creator of the heavens and the earth, will acknowledge that it is Allah. However, despite this acknowledgment, they still turn away from the truth and are deluded, refusing to submit to the One True God. The verse serves as a reminder that the existence of God is self-evident, and those who deny it are willfully turning away from the truth.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله فأنى يؤفكون

translation: And it will be said, "O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers will be presented before Allah. The verse expresses the plea of the Messenger or the angels, who will say to Allah that these people did not believe in the message of Islam during their lifetime on earth. This highlights the consequences of disbelief and the importance of having faith in Allah and His teachings.
orig: وقيله يا رب إن هؤلاء قوم لا يؤمنون

translation: So turn away from them and say, "Peace." And they are going to know.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to be patient and forgiving towards those who reject his message, and to simply wish them peace. It suggests that in time, the rejecters will come to understand the truth of the message, even if they do not accept it immediately.
orig: فاصفح عنهم وقل سلام فسوف يعلمون

translation: Ha, Mim.
interpretation: The letters 'Ha' and 'Mim' are part of the group of 'Muqatta'at' or 'Disconnected Letters' that appear at the beginning of some chapters of the Quran. Their exact meaning and significance are not entirely clear, but they are believed to be a way of emphasizing the divine nature of the Quran and to draw the reader's attention to the deeper meanings and messages within the text.
orig: حم

translation: And the clear Book.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an, which is described as the "clear Book". The Qur'an is considered the clear and unambiguous revelation from God, providing guidance and wisdom to humanity. The phrase "the clear Book" emphasizes the clarity, lucidity, and straightforwardness of the Qur'anic message, which is free from any ambiguity or contradiction.
orig: والكتاب المبين

translation: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn [mankind].
interpretation: This verse refers to the revelation of the Qur'an, which was sent down to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) during the blessed night of Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Power). This night is considered one of the most sacred nights in the Islamic calendar, as it is the night when the first verses of the Qur'an were revealed. The verse emphasizes that the Qur'an was sent down as a warning and guidance for all of mankind, to warn them of the consequences of their actions and to guide them towards the path of righteousness.
orig: إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة إنا كنا منذرين

translation: Therein [i.e., in that Record] is distinguished every precise matter
interpretation: This verse indicates that in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), every precise and wise matter is distinguished and recorded. It suggests that God has perfect knowledge and wisdom, and that everything in the universe is precisely determined and organized according to His plan.
orig: فيها يفرق كل أمر حكيم

translation: A command from Us. Indeed, We have been sending [messengers].
interpretation: This verse is indicating that the Qur'an and the message it contains is a command from Allah, the Almighty. It is a divine revelation that has been sent down through the messengers of Allah, such as the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse emphasizes that Allah has been sending His messengers throughout history to guide humanity and convey His message.
orig: أمرا من عندنا إنا كنا مرسلين

translation: A mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that the guidance and teachings in the Qur'an are a mercy from God, the All-Hearing and the All-Knowing. It suggests that the Qur'an is a divine revelation that provides wisdom and guidance to humanity, as God is the One who hears our prayers and knows our innermost thoughts and needs. The interpretation is that the Qur'an is a gift from the Merciful Lord, who is All-Aware and All-Wise.
orig: رحمة من ربك إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you should be certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and omnipotence of God, the Creator of the heavens, the earth, and everything in between. It calls upon the believers to have unwavering faith and certainty in God's power and authority. The verse serves as a reminder that all of creation is under the dominion of the Almighty, and that one should strive to live in accordance with God's will and commandments.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إن كنتم موقنين

translation: There is no deity except Him. He gives life and causes death. [He is] your Lord and the Lord of your first [forefathers].
interpretation: This verse affirms the fundamental belief in Islam - the oneness of God (tawhid). It states that there is no other deity worthy of worship besides the one true God, Allah. He alone has the power to give life and cause death, and He is the Lord and Sovereign Ruler not only of the present generation, but also of all their ancestors. This verse underscores the supreme and absolute authority of Allah, and the importance of submitting to Him as the sole object of worship and devotion.
orig: لا إله إلا هو يحيي ويميت ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين

translation: But they are in doubt, playing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being referred to are in a state of uncertainty or confusion, and are engaging in frivolous or meaningless activities instead of focusing on matters of importance. The interpretation is that they are distracted from the truth and are not taking their spiritual responsibilities seriously.
orig: بل هم في شك يلعبون

translation: So watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a major event that will occur on the Day of Judgment, where the sky will produce a visible smoke that will cover the earth. This smoke is seen as a sign of the imminent arrival of the Day of Resurrection and the final judgment of all mankind. The interpretation is that this smoke will be a clear and undeniable sign that the end times are near, and that people should prepare themselves spiritually and morally for the coming of that momentous day.
orig: فارتقب يوم تأتي السماء بدخان مبين

translation: This is a painful punishment that will envelop the people
interpretation: This verse refers to the severe and painful punishment that will befall the people on the Day of Judgment. The use of the word "يغشى" (to envelop or cover) suggests that this punishment will be all-encompassing, leaving no one untouched. The phrase "عذاب أليم" (a painful punishment) emphasizes the intensity and severity of the torment that the people will face. This verse serves as a warning to humanity to repent and seek forgiveness from Allah before facing this dreadful punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: يغشى الناس هذا عذاب أليم

translation: Our Lord, remove from us the punishment, indeed we are believers.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication by the believers, asking Allah to remove the punishment or affliction that they are experiencing. The verse emphasizes their faith and belief in Allah, as the basis for their request for relief from the punishment. The interpretation suggests that when one is facing difficulties or trials, the proper response is to turn to Allah in sincere belief and seek His mercy and forgiveness.
orig: ربنا اكشف عنا العذاب إنا مؤمنون

translation: How can there be for them a reminder, and there has come to them a clear messenger?
interpretation: This verse is questioning how the disbelievers can ignore the guidance and reminders that have come to them through the clear and evident message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse suggests that the people have no excuse for their rejection of faith, as they have been provided with clear guidance from a messenger sent by God. The implication is that they will be held accountable for their rejection of the truth.
orig: أنى لهم الذكرى وقد جاءهم رسول مبين

translation: Then they turned away from him and said, "A madman."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of some people towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) when he conveyed the message of Islam. Rather than accepting the truth, they dismissed him as a "madman", showing their arrogance and unwillingness to listen to the divine guidance. This highlights the importance of an open and receptive mind when encountering the teachings of the Quran, and the need to avoid prejudice and preconceptions.
orig: ثم تولوا عنه وقالوا معلم مجنون

translation: Indeed, We will remove the punishment [from you] for a little. Indeed, you [disbelievers] are going to return [to disobedience].
interpretation: This verse suggests that God will temporarily relieve the punishment of the disbelievers, but they will eventually return to their disbelief and disobedience. The interpretation is that God is merciful and gives people chances to repent, but those who persistently reject faith will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: إنا كاشفو العذاب قليلا إنكم عائدون

translation: The day We seize [the disbelievers] with the greatest seizure, indeed, We are the Avenger.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when Allah will inflict the ultimate punishment upon the disbelievers for their rejection of faith and their misdeeds. The "greatest seizure" signifies the severity and finality of the retribution that will be meted out to those who denied the truth and refused to submit to Allah. The verse emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate Avenger, who will not let the transgressions of the disbelievers go unpunished.
orig: يوم نبطش البطشة الكبرى إنا منتقمون

translation: And We had certainly tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) being sent to the people of Pharaoh. The verse highlights that the people of Pharaoh were also tested by Allah, just as the later generations were tested. The use of the word "noble" in describing the messenger (Prophet Moses) suggests his high status and the importance of his message. This verse serves as a reminder that Allah has sent messengers to guide people throughout history, and that those who reject the message will be held accountable.
orig: ولقد فتنا قبلهم قوم فرعون وجاءهم رسول كريم

translation: That I should deliver to the servants of Allah. Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of delivering Allah's message to His servants with honesty and trustworthiness. The messenger is charged with conveying the divine teachings and guidance to the people, and must do so faithfully and without any deception. The verse underscores the responsibility of the messenger to be a reliable and credible representative of Allah, serving the people with sincerity and integrity.
orig: أن أدوا إلي عباد الله إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: And do not exalt yourselves above Allah. Indeed, I have come to you with clear authority.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the people not to consider themselves superior to Allah or to elevate themselves above Him. It emphasizes that the messenger has been sent with clear proof and authority from Allah, and the people should submit to Allah's will and guidance rather than exalting themselves.
orig: وأن لا تعلوا على الله إني آتيكم بسلطان مبين

translation: And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me.
interpretation: This verse is spoken by the prophet Jesus, who is seeking protection from his Lord (God) against the persecution and harm that may come to him from the people. The verse expresses Jesus' reliance on God and his trust that God will protect him from those who wish to harm him.
orig: وإني عذت بربي وربكم أن ترجمون

translation: And if you do not believe me, then keep away from me.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the disbelievers who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It instructs them to distance themselves from the Prophet if they refuse to accept his message and believe in the oneness of God. The verse emphasizes that those who reject the truth should not interfere with or obstruct the mission of the Prophet, and should leave him alone to convey the divine message.
orig: وإن لم تؤمنوا لي فاعتزلون

translation: So he called upon his Lord, "Indeed, these are a people who are criminals."
interpretation: This verse describes a prophet or messenger of Allah calling upon his Lord to judge a people who have rejected the truth and committed grave sins. The interpretation is that when faced with a community that has turned away from the guidance of Allah and persisted in wrongdoing, the righteous servant of Allah can appeal to the Almighty for justice and punishment of the evildoers.
orig: فدعا ربه أن هؤلاء قوم مجرمون

translation: So set out with My servants by night. Indeed, you are to be pursued.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to lead his followers out of Mecca at night, as they were being pursued by their enemies. The verse emphasizes the need for the believers to take action and flee from persecution, while putting their trust in God. The interpretation suggests that when faced with adversity, believers should seek refuge in God and take the necessary steps to protect themselves, while remaining steadfast in their faith.
orig: فأسر بعبادي ليلا إنكم متبعون

translation: And leave the sea at rest. Indeed, they are a drowned soldiers.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Prophet Moses and the Israelites crossing the Red Sea, as described in the Qur'an. The verse commands Moses to leave the sea alone, as the Pharaoh and his army have been drowned in it, becoming a "drowned soldiers". The interpretation suggests that the sea should be left in peace, as the enemies of God have been defeated and destroyed, and there is no need to further disturb the waters.
orig: واترك البحر رهوا إنهم جند مغرقون

translation: How many gardens and springs did they leave behind?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question about the material wealth and comforts that the disbelievers had left behind when they perished. The implication is that they had enjoyed abundant blessings in this world, but ultimately these were temporary and they were unable to take them with them. The verse serves as a reminder that the true and lasting wealth is that of the Hereafter, which is attained through faith and righteous deeds.
orig: كم تركوا من جنات وعيون

translation: And gardens and lofty places
interpretation: This verse refers to the blessings and rewards that await the righteous in the Hereafter. The "gardens" symbolize the verdant and beautiful paradise, while the "lofty places" represent the elevated and prestigious positions that the faithful will be granted in the afterlife. This verse conveys the idea that those who believe and do good deeds will be rewarded with a magnificent and honorable abode in the Hereafter.
orig: وزروع ومقام كريم

translation: And the favor in which they were previously living.
interpretation: This verse refers to the blessings and comforts that the people were enjoying prior to the trials and tribulations they were facing. It suggests that they had been living in a state of ease and contentment, which they had now lost. The verse serves as a reminder that worldly pleasures and comforts are fleeting, and that one should not become complacent or overly attached to them.
orig: ونعمة كانوا فيها فاكهين

translation: And thus We caused it to be inherited by another people.
interpretation: This verse suggests that when a people reject the guidance and blessings bestowed upon them by God, He may transfer those blessings to another people who are more deserving and willing to uphold His teachings. It is a reminder that God's will prevails and that no one can claim ownership over His gifts - they are meant to be appreciated and utilized in the service of the greater good.
orig: كذلك وأورثناها قوما آخرين

translation: And the heaven and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they given respite.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers who rejected the truth and faced punishment did not receive any sympathy or compassion from the heavens and the earth. They were not given any more time or chance to repent and change their ways. The lack of intervention from the celestial and terrestrial realms indicates the gravity of their transgressions and the finality of their fate.
orig: فما بكت عليهم السماء والأرض وما كانوا منظرين

translation: And We had certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Israelites, who were saved by Allah from the humiliating punishment and oppression they faced in Egypt. It is a testament to Allah's power and mercy, as He delivered the Israelites from their suffering and allowed them to escape the tyranny of the Pharaoh.
orig: ولقد نجينا بني إسرائيل من العذاب المهين

translation: From Pharaoh, indeed, he was arrogant among the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse refers to the tyrannical ruler Pharaoh, who was known for his arrogance and oppression of the people. The verse highlights that Pharaoh was among those who exceeded the bounds of what is right and just, and indulged in excessive and wasteful behavior. This serves as a warning against the dangers of pride, arrogance, and abuse of power.
orig: من فرعون إنه كان عاليا من المسرفين

translation: And We have chosen them, out of knowledge, over [all] the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has chosen certain individuals, such as the Prophets, out of His divine knowledge and wisdom, to be superior over all of creation. This selection is not based on arbitrary preference, but on Allah's perfect understanding of what is best for humanity. The chosen ones are endowed with the knowledge and guidance to lead others towards the path of righteousness and success in both this life and the Hereafter.
orig: ولقد اخترناهم على علم على العالمين

translation: And We gave them from the verses [clear] signs, and We destroyed them with [total] destruction.
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of previous nations and peoples who disbelieved the signs and messages sent to them by God. It suggests that despite being given clear and unambiguous signs and proofs, they persisted in their rejection of the truth, leading to their ultimate demise. The verse serves as a warning to those who choose to ignore the guidance and evidence provided by God, as they too may face severe consequences for their actions.
orig: وآتيناهم من الآيات ما فيه بلاء مبين

translation: Indeed, it is they who say
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who deny the truth of the Qur'an and the message of Islam. The Qur'an is addressing them directly, acknowledging that they are the ones who make such claims against the faith. The implication is that their statements are unfounded and that the truth of Islam will prevail.
orig: إن هؤلاء ليقولون

translation: Indeed, it is not but our first death, and we will not be resurrected.
interpretation: This verse expresses the skepticism and denial of the disbelievers regarding the concept of resurrection and the afterlife. They believe that death is the end and that there is no life after this world. The verse emphasizes their rejection of the idea of being resurrected, suggesting that they view death as a final and permanent state rather than a transition to another form of existence.
orig: إن هي إلا موتتنا الأولى وما نحن بمنشرين

translation: Then bring our forefathers, if you are truthful.
interpretation: This verse challenges those who deny the resurrection and the afterlife to produce their ancestors if they are indeed truthful in their claims. It suggests that the ability to bring back the dead would be a clear proof of the truth of their beliefs. The verse emphasizes the importance of accountability and the need to substantiate one's claims, rather than relying on mere speculation or denial.
orig: فأتوا بآبائنا إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Are they better or the people of Tubba' and those before them? We destroyed them, for they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse is comparing the disbelievers addressed in the Qur'an to the people of Tubba' and those who came before them. The implication is that the disbelievers are not better than those previous nations who rejected the message of God and were consequently destroyed for their crimes and transgressions. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers that they will face a similar fate if they persist in their rejection of the truth.
orig: أهم خير أم قوم تبع والذين من قبلهم أهلكناهم إنهم كانوا مجرمين

translation: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and that between them in play.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the creation of the universe was not a random or meaningless act, but rather a purposeful and deliberate act by God. The universe was not created in jest or play, but with a divine plan and intention. This refutes the notion that the world is the result of chance or that it has no deeper meaning or purpose. The verse underscores the idea that the universe and all that it contains are imbued with divine wisdom and significance, and that humans have a responsibility to seek to understand and fulfill the purpose of their existence within this divinely-ordained creation.
orig: وما خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما لاعبين

translation: We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them except with truth. But most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the creation of the heavens, the earth, and all that is between them is not without purpose or in vain. It was created with truth, wisdom, and justice. However, most people are unaware of the true nature and purpose of this creation, and they fail to appreciate the profound meaning and significance behind it.
orig: ما خلقناهما إلا بالحق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, the Day of Separation is the appointed time for them all.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions. It emphasizes that this day is the predetermined time when all of humanity will be gathered and judged by God. The "Day of Separation" implies that on this day, the righteous will be separated from the wicked, and each will receive their just reward or punishment.
orig: إن يوم الفصل ميقاتهم أجمعين

translation: The Day when no soul will possess [power to do] anything for another soul, and the [sole] command, that Day, is [entirely] with Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgement, no one will be able to help or support another, as each person will be held accountable for their own actions. All power and authority will belong to Allah alone on that day, and no one will be able to intervene or intercede on behalf of another. This serves as a reminder that we must strive to do good deeds in this life, as we will not be able to rely on others to save us on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: يوم لا يغني مولى عن مولى شيئا ولا هم ينصرون

translation: Except those on whom your Lord has bestowed His Mercy - and for this did He create them: and the Word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will fill Hell with Jinns and men all together."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the only ones who will be saved from the punishment of Hell are those upon whom Allah has bestowed His Mercy. It suggests that Allah has created human beings and jinn with the intention of showing them His Mercy, but those who reject faith and disobey Him will be condemned to Hell. The verse highlights the absolute sovereignty and justice of Allah, as well as the importance of seeking His Mercy through faith and righteous deeds.
orig: إلا من رحم الله إنه هو العزيز الرحيم

translation: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum
interpretation: The tree of Zaqqum is mentioned in the Qur'an as a tree that grows in the depths of Hell, bearing bitter fruit that is likened to the heads of devils. This verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them of the torment that awaits them in the Hereafter if they persist in their rejection of faith and righteous deeds.
orig: إن شجرت الزقوم

translation: The food of the sinner
interpretation: This verse refers to the unrighteous and sinful behavior of those who consume unlawful or ill-gotten food. The "food of the sinner" implies that the sustenance of those who engage in immoral or unethical practices is tainted and unacceptable in the sight of God. The Qur'an emphasizes the importance of acquiring wealth and provisions through lawful and righteous means, as the food and sustenance of the righteous is blessed, while that of the sinner is considered impure and devoid of divine blessing.
orig: طعام الأثيم

translation: Like scalding water that boils in the bellies
interpretation: This verse is a metaphor describing the punishment of the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The "scalding water that boils in the bellies" is a vivid depiction of the intense and agonizing torment they will experience. The imagery conveys the unbearable pain and suffering they will endure as a consequence of their rejection of faith and righteous deeds in this life.
orig: كالمهل يغلي في البطون

translation: Like the boiling of scalding water
interpretation: This verse is a metaphor used to describe the intense and severe punishment that awaits the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The boiling of scalding water is used to convey the extreme heat and torment that they will experience in Hell. The intensity of this punishment is meant to serve as a warning to those who reject faith and turn away from the guidance of Allah.
orig: كغلي الحميم

translation: Seize him and drag him into the midst of the Blaze
interpretation: This verse is a command to seize and punish the wrongdoer, casting him into the depths of Hell. The interpretation suggests that those who commit grave sins and transgressions against God and others must face the consequences of their actions, which is eternal punishment in the Hellfire.
orig: خذوه فاعتلوه إلى سواء الجحيم

translation: Then pour upon his head the punishment of scalding water.
interpretation: This verse is describing the punishment of the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The "scalding water" is a metaphor for the intense and painful torment that awaits those who rejected faith and lived in disobedience to God. The imagery conveys the severity and unrelenting nature of the punishment they will face as a consequence of their evil deeds in this life.
orig: ثم صبوا فوق رأسه من عذاب الحميم

translation: Taste, you are the Mighty, the Generous.
interpretation: This verse is a command from God to a person, likely a prophet or a righteous individual, to "taste" or experience the consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes that the person addressed is "the Mighty, the Generous", which suggests that they have been bestowed with power and nobility by God. The interpretation is that the person should be mindful of their actions and responsibilities, as they have been granted a high status by God, and they should use their power and influence in a generous and benevolent manner.
orig: ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم

translation: Indeed, this is what you used to dispute about.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when people will be confronted with the reality of their beliefs and actions in life. The verse suggests that the disputes and arguments that people engaged in during their earthly lives will be shown to be futile, as the truth will be revealed on that day. The interpretation is that we should not be preoccupied with disputes and arguments, but rather focus on living a righteous life in accordance with the teachings of the Qur'an.
orig: إن هذا ما كنتم به تمترون

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure place
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are pious and God-fearing will be in a position of honor, trust and security in the Hereafter. The "secure place" refers to the abode of Paradise, where the righteous will enjoy a state of peace, tranquility and protection from any harm or distress.
orig: إن المتقين في مقام أمين

translation: In gardens and springs
interpretation: This verse refers to the eternal paradise that awaits the righteous believers in the Hereafter. The gardens and springs mentioned symbolize the lush, abundant, and refreshing nature of this abode, which is in contrast to the hardships and trials of the worldly life. This verse conveys a message of hope and the promise of a blissful afterlife for those who believe and do good deeds.
orig: في جنات وعيون

translation: They will be adorned with garments of fine green silk and brocade, and they will face each other.
interpretation: This verse describes the luxurious garments that the inhabitants of Paradise will wear. The mention of "satin" and "brocade" suggests the finest and most beautiful fabrics. The fact that they will "face each other" indicates that they will be gathered together, enjoying each other's company and conversation in the blissful afterlife.
orig: يلبسون من سندس وإستبرق متقابلين

translation: And We will marry them to fair women with large, [beautiful] eyes.
interpretation: This verse is describing the rewards in the Hereafter for the righteous believers. They will be married to pure, beautiful women with wide, lustrous eyes. This is a metaphor for the spiritual and physical bliss that the believers will experience in Paradise, as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this life.
orig: كذلك وزوجناهم بحور عين

translation: They will call therein for every [kind of] fruit - [being] secure.
interpretation: This verse describes the bountiful provisions and peaceful state of the inhabitants of Paradise. They will be able to freely enjoy all kinds of delicious fruits without any fear or worry. The verse conveys the idea that the people of Paradise will be in a state of complete security and tranquility, able to indulge in the pleasures of the eternal life without any hindrance or disturbance.
orig: يدعون فيها بكل فاكهة آمنين

translation: They will not taste death therein except the first death, and He will have protected them from the punishment of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers in the Hereafter, who will be spared from the torment of Hell. They will only experience the first death, which is the death of this worldly life, and will be saved from the eternal punishment of the Afterlife. This emphasizes the mercy and protection of Allah towards the righteous, who will be rewarded with eternal life in Paradise, free from the suffering of Hellfire.
orig: لا يذوقون فيها الموت إلا الموتة الأولى ووقاهم عذاب الجحيم

translation: That is a bounty from your Lord. And that is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the blessings and bounties bestowed upon a person are a gift from God, the Lord. The "great attainment" refers to the ultimate success and triumph in the Hereafter, which is the true and lasting reward for those who believe and do good deeds. This verse encourages people to be grateful for God's favors and to strive for the eternal rewards in the Afterlife, which are far greater than any worldly gains.
orig: فضلا من ربك ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: So We have only made it [i.e., the Qur'an] easy in your tongue [O Muhammad] that they may remember.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Qur'an has been made easy to understand and remember through the Arabic language, which was the native tongue of the Prophet Muhammad and his people. The purpose is to facilitate the remembrance and contemplation of the Qur'anic teachings, so that people may reflect on its message and be guided by it.
orig: فإنما يسرناه بلسانك لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: So wait expectantly; indeed, they are waiting expectantly.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad and the believers to be patient and steadfast in the face of opposition and persecution from the disbelievers. It suggests that the disbelievers are also waiting and expecting something, perhaps a change in the Prophet's message or the collapse of his movement. However, the believers are instructed to remain firm in their faith and await the ultimate triumph of the truth, as promised by God.
orig: فارتقب إنهم مرتقبون

translation: Ha, Mim.
interpretation: The letters "Ha, Mim" are part of the group of "mysterious letters" that appear at the beginning of some chapters of the Qur'an. Their exact meaning is not fully understood, but they are believed to be a part of the divine knowledge and a way for God to emphasize the importance and the miraculous nature of the Qur'an. This opening serves to draw the reader's attention and to prepare them for the profound teachings that will follow.
orig: حم

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an is a divine revelation from Allah, the Almighty and All-Wise. It emphasizes that the Qur'an is not the work of a human being, but rather a book that has been sent down from the All-Mighty and All-Wise God. This establishes the Qur'an's divine origin and authority, and calls for its acceptance and obedience as the word of the Sovereign and All-Knowing Creator.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed, in the heavens and earth are signs for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the wonders and marvels of the universe, including the heavens and the earth, are clear signs and evidence of the existence, power, and wisdom of God for those who have faith and believe in Him. These signs invite people to reflect on the Creator and to recognize His sovereignty and divine attributes.
orig: إن في السماوات والأرض لآيات للمؤمنين

translation: And in your creation and what He disperses of moving creatures are signs for people who are certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse points to the signs of God's power, wisdom, and oneness that are evident in the creation of human beings and the diversity of living creatures. It encourages people to reflect on these signs and to have firm faith and certainty in God's existence and attributes. The verse emphasizes that the signs of God's power and majesty are clear for those who have the capacity to perceive and understand them.
orig: وفي خلقكم وما يبث من دابة آيات لقوم يوقنون

translation: And [in] the alternation of the night and the day and [in] what Allah sends down from the sky of provision and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness and [in] the [changing of the] winds are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights several natural phenomena as signs of Allah's power, wisdom, and mercy. The alternation of night and day, the provision of sustenance from the sky, the revival of the earth after its lifelessness, and the changing of the winds are all evidence of Allah's creative ability and the need for people to reflect and use their reasoning faculties to understand the divine signs around them. These natural occurrences point to the existence, oneness, and attributes of the Creator, and should lead people to worship Him and submit to His will.
orig: واختلاف الليل والنهار وما أنزل الله من السماء من رزق فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها وتصريف الرياح آيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you, [O Muhammad], in truth; so in what statement after Allah and His verses will they believe?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'anic verses and Allah's signs. It suggests that if people do not believe in the Qur'an and Allah's revelations, then in what else will they believe? The implication is that the Qur'an is the ultimate source of truth and guidance, and those who reject it have no other reliable basis for their faith.
orig: تلك آيات الله نتلوها عليك بالحق فبأي حديث بعد الله وآياته يؤمنون

translation: Woe to every slanderous backbiter
interpretation: This verse warns against the evil traits of slander and backbiting. It condemns those who spread false and malicious rumors about others, thus harming their reputation and character. The Qur'an emphasizes the importance of maintaining good character, honesty and respect for others in one's speech and conduct.
orig: ويل لكل أفاك أثيم

translation: He hears the verses of Allah recited to him, then persists arrogantly as if he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse describes the attitude of those who are arrogant and reject the message of the Qur'an, even after hearing the clear signs and verses of Allah. They stubbornly refuse to acknowledge the truth and continue in their wrongdoing. The verse warns that such people will face a painful punishment for their rejection and arrogance.
orig: يسمع آيات الله تتلى عليه ثم يصر مستكبرا كأن لم يسمعها فبشره بعذاب أليم

translation: And when he knows [something] of Our verses, he takes them in ridicule. Those will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns those who mock or ridicule the signs and verses of Allah. It indicates that those who are aware of the truth and evidences of Islam, yet choose to reject and make fun of them, will face a humiliating punishment from Allah. The verse emphasizes the gravity of rejecting and mocking the divine revelations, and calls upon people to approach the Qur'an and its teachings with sincerity, reverence and an open mind.
orig: وإذا علم من آياتنا شيئا اتخذها هزوا أولئك لهم عذاب مهين

translation: Over them is Hell, and what they had earned avails them not, nor what they had taken besides Allah as allies. And for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that those who reject faith in Allah and instead rely on worldly wealth, power, or alliances will face the eternal punishment of Hell. Their material gains and worldly connections will be of no avail on the Day of Judgment, as they have turned away from the true source of protection and salvation - Allah. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits those who persist in disbelief and disobedience to Allah.
orig: من ورائهم جهنم ولا يغني عنهم ما كسبوا شيئا ولا ما اتخذوا من دون الله أولياء ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: This is guidance, and those who disbelieve in the verses of their Lord will have a punishment of a painful torment.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Qur'an as a source of guidance for humanity. It contrasts those who accept and believe in the Qur'anic verses, with those who reject and disbelieve in them. The latter group will face a severe and painful punishment from Allah for their rejection of the divine guidance.
orig: هذا هدى والذين كفروا بآيات ربهم لهم عذاب من رجز أليم

translation: It is Allah who has subjected to you the sea so that ships may sail upon it by His command and that you may seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who has made the sea subservient to humanity, allowing ships to sail upon it by His command. This is a sign of Allah's power and a means for people to seek His bounty, whether through trade, exploration, or other economic activities. The verse encourages people to be grateful to Allah for this blessing and to recognize His sovereignty over the natural world.
orig: الله الذي سخر لكم البحر لتجري الفلك فيه بأمره ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth - all from Him. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all the wonders and resources in the universe, both in the heavens and on Earth, have been subjugated and made available for the benefit of humankind. It is a reminder that these blessings are from God, and that reflecting on them should lead people to contemplate the power, wisdom, and generosity of the Creator. The verse encourages people to ponder and reflect deeply on the signs of God's creation, which can strengthen their faith and guide them towards a deeper understanding of the divine.
orig: وسخر لكم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض جميعا منه إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: Say to those who have believed that they [should] forgive those who hope not for the days of Allah so that He may recompense a people for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to forgive those who do not believe in the Day of Judgment, so that Allah may reward the believers for their good deeds. The interpretation suggests that believers should not seek vengeance against non-believers, but rather show mercy and forgiveness, as this will be rewarded by Allah on the Day of Judgment.
orig: قل للذين آمنوا يغفروا للذين لا يرجون أيام الله ليجزي قوما بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Whoever does righteousness - it is for his [own] soul, and whoever does evil [does so] against it. Then to your Lord you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the personal responsibility of each individual for their actions. It states that whoever does good deeds, the benefit of those deeds will be for their own soul. Conversely, whoever commits evil, the consequences of that evil will be upon their own soul. Ultimately, all people will be held accountable for their actions before God on the Day of Judgment, when they will return to Him.
orig: من عمل صالحا فلنفسه ومن أساء فعليها ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون

translation: And We had certainly given to the Children of Israel the Scripture and judgement and prophethood and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and favors that Allah (God) bestowed upon the Children of Israel. He granted them the revealed Scripture (the Torah), the ability to make sound judgements, the gift of prophethood, and provided them with good and pure sustenance. Furthermore, Allah preferred and distinguished the Children of Israel over all other people in the world. This verse emphasizes the special status and privileges that the Children of Israel enjoyed due to Allah's grace and mercy.
orig: ولقد آتينا بني إسرائيل الكتاب والحكم والنبوة ورزقناهم من الطيبات وفضلناهم على العالمين

translation: And We had certainly given them clear proofs from the matter [of religion], but they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah had provided clear guidance and proofs to the people, but they still differed and disputed with one another after receiving this knowledge. This discord and disagreement arose not from a lack of evidence, but rather from jealousy and animosity among themselves. On the Day of Judgment, Allah will judge between them regarding the matters over which they used to differ.
orig: وآتيناهم بينات من الأمر فما اختلفوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم إن ربك يقضي بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: Then We put you, [O Muhammad], on an ordained way concerning the matter [of religion]; so follow it and do not follow the inclinations of those who do not know.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to follow the divinely ordained path of Islam and not to be swayed by the desires and ignorance of those who reject the truth. It emphasizes the importance of adherence to the teachings and commandments of Allah, and not to be influenced by the whims and fancies of those who lack knowledge and understanding.
orig: ثم جعلناك على شريعة من الأمر فاتبعها ولا تتبع أهواء الذين لا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, they will not avail you against Allah at all. And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another, but Allah is the Protector of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that no one can protect or save the wrongdoers from the punishment of Allah. It also highlights that the wrongdoers are united in their support for one another, while Allah is the Protector and Guardian of the righteous. The message is that one should seek refuge in Allah and strive to be among the righteous, as He alone can provide true protection and guidance.
orig: إنهم لن يغنوا عنك من الله شيئا وإن الظالمين بعضهم أولياء بعض والله ولي المتقين

translation: This is a clear proof for the people and a guidance and mercy for a people who are certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a clear source of guidance and mercy for those who have firm belief and certainty in the teachings of Islam. It serves as a beacon of light to illuminate the path for humanity, providing clear evidence and direction for those who seek the truth. The Qur'an is a gift of divine wisdom that can lead people to a life of faith, righteousness, and inner peace if they approach it with an open and sincere heart.
orig: هذا بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لقوم يوقنون

translation: Or do those who commit evils think We will make them [equal] to those who have believed and done righteous deeds - [equal in] their life and their death? Evil is that which they judge.
interpretation: This verse poses a rhetorical question, challenging the notion that those who commit evil deeds can be considered equal to those who believe and do righteous works, either in their life or in their death. The implication is that such a judgment would be unjust and erroneous. The verse emphasizes that the ultimate outcome for the evildoers and the righteous is not the same, and that the judgment of those who equate the two is flawed and misguided.
orig: أم حسب الذين اجترحوا السيئات أن نجعلهم كالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سواء محياهم ومماتهم ساء ما يحكمون

translation: And Allah created the heavens and earth in truth, and to give you [reward for] what you have done, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the creation of the heavens and the earth by Allah is with a purpose - to hold people accountable for their deeds. It suggests that on the Day of Judgment, every soul will be justly rewarded or punished based on their actions in this life, and no one will be wronged. This serves as a reminder to believers to live righteously and prepare for the Hereafter.
orig: وخلق الله السماوات والأرض بالحق ولتجزى كل نفس بما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Have you seen the one who takes as his god his own desire, and Allah has sent him astray due to knowledge and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart and put over his vision a veil? So who will guide him after Allah? Then will you not be reminded?
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who worship their own desires and impulses instead of worshiping Allah. It suggests that such people have been led astray by Allah due to their own willful ignorance, and that their faculties of hearing, seeing, and understanding have been sealed or veiled. The implication is that only Allah can guide such people back to the right path, and the rhetorical question "Then will you not be reminded?" is meant to spur the reader to reflect on this and turn back to Allah.
orig: أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه وأضله الله على علم وختم على سمعه وقلبه وجعل على بصره غشاوة فمن يهديه من بعد الله أفلا تذكرون

translation: And they say, "There is not but our worldly life; we die and live, and nothing destroys us except time." And they have of that no knowledge; they are only assuming.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the belief held by some people that our worldly life is all there is, and that death and life are merely natural processes without any higher meaning or purpose. It states that they have no real knowledge to support this view, and are merely speculating or making assumptions. The verse suggests that there is more to existence than just the material world, and that the true nature of life and death is not fully understood by those who deny the afterlife.
orig: وقالوا ما هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا نموت ونحيا وما يهلكنا إلا الدهر وما لهم بذلك من علم إن هم إلا يظنون

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their only argument is that they say, "Bring [back] our forefathers, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who reject the clear signs and messages of Allah, the Almighty. When the unbelievers are presented with the undeniable proofs and evidences of the Qur'an, they do not have any valid argument against it. Their only response is to demand that the Prophet bring back their forefathers, as if that would somehow disprove the truth of the Qur'an. This verse highlights the stubbornness and unwillingness of the rejecters to accept the truth, even in the face of clear and compelling evidence.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات ما كان حجتهم إلا أن قالوا ائتوا بآبائنا إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "Allah gives you life, then causes you to die; then He will gather you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt, but most of the people do not know."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over life and death. It reminds us that Allah is the one who gives us life, takes it away, and will ultimately gather us on the Day of Resurrection, a day that is certain to come. The verse also highlights the ignorance of most people, who do not fully comprehend the magnitude of Allah's power and the inevitability of the Hereafter.
orig: قل الله يحييكم ثم يميتكم ثم يجمعكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And the Day the Hour appears - that Day the falsifiers will lose.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah alone has sovereignty over the heavens and the earth, and that on the Day of Judgment, those who have denied the truth or engaged in falsehood will be the losers. The message is that one should submit to the will of Allah and live righteously, as the ultimate reckoning will come on the Day of Resurrection.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض ويوم تقوم الساعة يومئذ يخسر المبطلون

translation: And you will see every nation kneeling [from fear]. Every nation will be called to its record [of deeds], [and it will be said], "Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when all people will be gathered before God to be held accountable for their actions in life. The imagery of every nation "kneeling" conveys a sense of humility, reverence, and fear as they face the reckoning of their deeds. The verse emphasizes that on that day, each nation will be called to account for what they did in the world, and they will be recompensed accordingly. This highlights the importance of living a righteous life and doing good deeds, as one will ultimately be held responsible for their actions before God.
orig: وترى كل أمة جاثية كل أمة تدعى إلى كتابها اليوم تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

translation: This is Our record; it speaks about you in truth. Indeed, We were having recorded whatever you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an, as the revealed book of God, is a record that speaks the truth about people's deeds and actions. It serves as a witness against them on the Day of Judgment, as God has been keeping track of everything they have done in their lives. This underscores the importance of being accountable for one's actions and the need to live righteously, as all of one's deeds will be brought forth and judged by God.
orig: هذا كتابنا ينطق عليكم بالحق إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون

translation: But as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them to His mercy. That is the clear attainment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for those who have faith in God and do good deeds. It promises that God will admit them into His mercy, which is the ultimate success and triumph. The interpretation suggests that true believers who live righteously will be granted divine forgiveness and the eternal bliss of the Hereafter.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيدخلهم ربهم في رحمته ذلك هو الفوز المبين

translation: And as for those who disbelieved, 'Were not My verses recited to you, but you were arrogant and became a people of criminals?'
interpretation: This verse addresses those who have rejected faith and turned away from the guidance of the Quran. It questions them, asking whether the verses of the Quran were not recited to them, and yet they remained arrogant and became criminals. The implication is that they had no excuse for their disbelief and wrongdoing, as they were presented with the clear signs and teachings of the Quran, but chose to reject them out of arrogance and a criminal mindset. This verse serves as a warning to those who refuse to accept the truth and guidance of the Quran, and highlights the consequences of such rejection.
orig: وأما الذين كفروا أفلم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم فاستكبرتم وكنتم قوما مجرمين

translation: And when it is said to them, "Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth and the Hour [is coming] - no doubt about it," you say, "We know not what is the Hour. We assume only assumption, and we are not convinced."
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who are skeptical about the Day of Judgment and the coming of the Hour. Despite being told that the promise of Allah is true and that the Hour is certain, they express uncertainty, claiming that they do not know what the Hour is and that they can only speculate about it. The verse emphasizes that they have no real conviction about the reality of the Hereafter, and are merely making assumptions without any firm belief.
orig: وإذا قيل إن وعد الله حق والساعة لا ريب فيها قلتم ما ندري ما الساعة إن نظن إلا ظنا وما نحن بمستيقنين

translation: And the evil [consequences] of what they did appeared to them, and they were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who engage in evil deeds will eventually face the consequences of their actions, even if they initially mocked or dismissed the idea of punishment. The verse implies that people who scoff at the idea of accountability will ultimately be confronted with the reality of their misdeeds, which will become clear to them. This serves as a warning to those who think they can escape the consequences of their wrongdoings.
orig: وبدا لهم سيئات ما عملوا وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And it will be said, "Today We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours, and your refuge is the Fire, and for you there are no helpers."
interpretation: This verse conveys a stern warning to those who neglect their duties towards Allah and fail to prepare for the Day of Judgment. It suggests that on the Day of Resurrection, those who disregarded the signs of Allah and the importance of the Hereafter will be forgotten by Allah, just as they had forgotten the significance of that momentous day. Their only refuge will be the Fire of Hell, and they will have no one to support or defend them on that day.
orig: وقيل اليوم ننساكم كما نسيتم لقاء يومكم هذا ومأواكم النار وما لكم من ناصرين

translation: That is because you took the verses of Allah in ridicule, and the worldly life deluded you. So today they will not be removed from it, nor will they be given a chance to make amends.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who have mocked and ridiculed the signs and messages of Allah. It warns that they have been deluded by the fleeting pleasures of this worldly life, and that on the Day of Judgment, they will not be able to escape the consequences of their actions nor will they be given a chance to seek forgiveness and make amends. The verse emphasizes the importance of taking the guidance of Allah seriously and not treating it with contempt, as doing so will lead to a severe punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: ذلكم بأنكم اتخذتم آيات الله هزوا وغرتكم الحياة الدنيا فاليوم لا يخرجون منها ولا هم يستعتبون

translation: So, [all] praise is [due] to Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and lordship of Allah over the entire universe. It affirms that all praise, gratitude, and worship belong to Allah alone, as He is the Creator, Sustainer, and Ruler of the heavens, the earth, and all that exists between them. This verse reminds us to acknowledge Allah's supreme power, wisdom, and benevolence, and to direct our devotion and thanksgiving solely to Him.
orig: فلله الحمد رب السماوات ورب الأرض رب العالمين

translation: And to Allah belongs [all] grandeur within the heavens and the earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all grandeur, majesty, and sovereignty belong to Allah alone, both in the heavens and on the earth. He is the Almighty, the All-Wise, whose power and wisdom are unparalleled. This serves as a reminder to believers that they should direct all praise, reverence, and submission to Allah, the One true God, and not to any other created being or entity.
orig: وله الكبرياء في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: Ha, Mim.
interpretation: The letters Ha and Mim are part of the 'Muqatta'at' (Mysterious Letters) that appear at the beginning of some Quranic chapters. Their exact meaning is not definitively known, but they are believed to be a way for God to emphasize the divine origin and miraculous nature of the Quran. These letters serve as a reminder of the Quran's supernatural qualities and the importance of reflecting on its message.
orig: حم

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, the Almighty and All-Wise. It highlights the divine origin of the Qur'an, which is not the work of any human being, but a direct communication from the All-Powerful and All-Knowing Creator. The attributes "the Exalted in Might" and "the Wise" emphasize that the Qur'an is revealed by a Sovereign and Omniscient God, whose commands and guidance are worthy of our utmost respect and obedience.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and [for] a specified term. And those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord will not obtain [salvation].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the creation of the heavens, the earth, and all that is between them was not without purpose or in vain. Rather, it was created in truth, with wisdom and justice, and for a specific duration. Those who reject the signs and messages of Allah will not attain salvation, as they have turned away from the guidance provided to them.
orig: ما خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وأجل مسمى والذين كفروا عما أنذروا معرضون

translation: Say, "Have you considered that which you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth. Or do they have partnership [with Him] in the heavens? Bring me a scripture [revealed] before this or a [single] trace of knowledge, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists to provide evidence for their belief in multiple deities. It asks them to show what the other gods they worship have created, or what role they have in the creation and governance of the heavens. The verse demands that the polytheists produce a scripture revealed before the Qur'an or any credible evidence to support their claims, if they are indeed truthful in their beliefs.
orig: قل أرأيتم ما تدعون من دون الله أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض أم لهم شرك في السماوات ائتوني بكتاب من قبل هذا أو أثارة من علم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, [those] who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, about their call, are unaware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping or seeking help from anything or anyone other than Allah. It highlights that those who call upon deities, idols, or other created beings will not receive any response from them, even on the Day of Resurrection. This is because only Allah has the power to respond to the prayers and supplications of His creation. The verse also suggests that those who engage in such false worship are unaware of the true nature of their actions and the consequences they will face on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ومن أضل ممن يدعو من دون الله من لا يستجيب له إلى يوم القيامة وهم عن دعائهم غافلون

translation: And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them, and they will be deniers of their worship.
interpretation: This verse describes a scenario on the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity will be gathered together. At that time, the people will be hostile towards one another, and they will reject and deny the acts of worship they had performed in their worldly lives. This suggests that the relationships and allegiances in the afterlife will be fundamentally different from those in this life, and that people will be held accountable for their beliefs and actions.
orig: وإذا حشر الناس كانوا لهم أعداء وكانوا بعبادتهم كافرين

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, "This is obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of those who disbelieve when confronted with the clear and evident signs and messages of God as revealed in the Quran. Rather than acknowledging the truth and guidance contained therein, they dismiss it as "obvious magic", denying the divine origin and nature of the Quran. This highlights the stubborn rejection of the truth by those whose hearts and minds are closed to faith, preferring to cling to their own preconceptions and desires rather than submitting to the guidance of God.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين كفروا للحق لما جاءهم هذا سحر مبين

translation: Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "If I have invented it, you possess not for me [the power of] anything against Allah. He is most knowing of that in which you are involved. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusation that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) had fabricated the Qur'an. The response given is that if he had indeed invented it, then he would have no power or authority over Allah. Allah, being the All-Knowing, is fully aware of the truth of the matter. He is the Witness between the Prophet and his accusers, and He is the Forgiving and Merciful. This verse establishes the divine origin of the Qur'an and refutes any claims of human authorship, affirming the Prophet's honesty and the authenticity of the revelation.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل إن افتريته فلا تملكون لي من الله شيئا هو أعلم بما تفيضون فيه كفى به شهيدا بيني وبينكم وهو الغفور الرحيم

translation: Say, "I am not the first of the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not the first messenger sent by God, and that he does not know the ultimate fate of himself or his people. His role is simply to convey the divine revelation he has received, and to warn people clearly about the consequences of their actions. It underscores the Prophet's humility and his reliance on God's guidance, rather than any personal knowledge or power.
orig: قل ما كنت بدعا من الرسل وما أدري ما يفعل بي ولا بكم إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي وما أنا إلا نذير مبين

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if it [i.e., the Qur'an] is from Allah and you disbelieved in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something similar and believed while you were arrogant [about it]? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse addresses those who reject the Qur'an despite its divine origin. It points out that even a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to the truth of a similar revelation, and believed in it. Yet, the rejecters of the Qur'an have remained arrogant and unwilling to accept it. The verse emphasizes that Allah does not guide those who do wrong by rejecting the truth, out of arrogance and stubbornness.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن كان من عند الله وكفرتم به وشهد شاهد من بني إسرائيل على مثله فآمن واستكبرتم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: And those who disbelieve say of those who believe: "If it had been [any] good, they would not have preceded us to it." And when they are not guided by it, they say: "This is an ancient falsehood."
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of the disbelievers towards the believers. The disbelievers argue that if the faith and beliefs of the believers were truly good, they would have been the first to accept them. However, when they are unable to find guidance in the message, they dismiss it as an "ancient falsehood". This reflects the arrogance and close-mindedness of the disbelievers, who are unwilling to accept the truth even when presented with it.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا لو كان خيرا ما سبقونا إليه وإذ لم يهتدوا به فسيقولون هذا إفك قديم

translation: And before it was the Book of Moses as a guide and a mercy. And this is a confirming Book in an Arabic tongue to warn those who have wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse draws a connection between the Quran and the previous scripture revealed to Prophet Moses. It states that the Quran is a confirming Book in the Arabic language, meant to warn those who have wronged and to give good tidings to the righteous. The verse highlights the Quran's role as a guide and a mercy, similar to the Book of Moses, and its purpose of guiding humanity towards righteousness.
orig: ومن قبله كتاب موسى إماما ورحمة وهذا كتاب مصدق لسانا عربيا لينذر الذين ظلموا وبشرى للمحسنين

translation: Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained on a right course - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who have sincerely accepted Allah as their Lord and then steadfastly adhered to the right path, will be free from fear and sorrow. It suggests that true faith in Allah, combined with a consistent commitment to righteousness, leads to a state of spiritual security and tranquility, where one is protected from the anxieties and sorrows that often afflict those who stray from the right way.
orig: إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding eternally therein as a reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous believers who will be granted eternal life in Paradise as a reward for their good deeds and righteous actions in this world. The phrase "those are the companions of Paradise" indicates that these individuals will be part of a community of believers who have attained the highest level of spiritual and moral achievement. The phrase "abiding eternally therein" emphasizes the permanence and perpetuity of their reward, suggesting that their blissful state in Paradise will last forever. The final clause "as a reward for what they used to do" highlights that this reward is a direct consequence of their righteous conduct and good works during their lives on earth.
orig: أولئك أصحاب الجنة خالدين فيها جزاء بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents. His mother carried him, [increasing her] in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years. Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the [final] destination. And if they strive to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them but accompany them in [this] world with appropriate kindness and follow the way of those who turn back to Me [in repentance]. Then to Me will be your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honoring and caring for one's parents. It describes the hardship a mother goes through in bearing and raising a child, and instructs the child to be grateful to both parents. The verse also warns against obeying parents if they try to make the child associate partners with God, but encourages treating them with kindness in this life. Ultimately, the child's return is to God, who will judge their actions.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه إحسانا حملته أمه كرها ووضعته كرها وحمله وفصاله ثلاثون شهرا حتى إذا بلغ أشده وبلغ أربعين سنة قال رب أوزعني أن أشكر نعمتك التي أنعمت علي وعلى والدي وأن أعمل صالحا ترضاه وأصلح لي في ذريتي إني تبت إليك وإني من المسلمين

translation: Those are the ones from whom We will accept the best of what they did and will overlook their misdeeds, [their being] among the companions of Paradise. [That is] the promise of truth which they had been promised.
