interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who have done good deeds and repented from their sins. Allah will accept the best of their actions and forgive their misdeeds, allowing them to enter Paradise. This is the true promise that was made to them, which they will receive.
orig: أولئك الذين نتقبل عنهم أحسن ما عملوا ونتجاوز عن سيئاتهم في أصحاب الجنة وعد الصدق الذي كانوا يوعدون

translation: And he who says to his parents, "Uff to you; do you promise me that I will be brought forth [from the earth] when generations before me have already passed on?" While they call to Allah for help [and to their son], "Woe to you! Believe, for indeed, the promise of Allah is truth." But he says, "This is not but legends of the former peoples,"
interpretation: This verse condemns the disbelief and disrespect shown by a person towards his parents. The verse describes a situation where a person scolds his parents in a derogatory manner ("Uff to you") and expresses skepticism about the promise of resurrection and accountability in the Hereafter. The parents, on the other hand, exhort their son to believe in Allah's promise, which is the truth. However, the son dismisses this as mere "legends of the former peoples", exhibiting arrogance and rejection of faith. This verse highlights the importance of honoring and respecting one's parents, as well as the necessity of believing in the Hereafter and Allah's promise of accountability.
orig: والذي قال لوالديه أف لكما أتعدانني أن أخرج وقد خلت القرون من قبلي وهما يستغيثان الله ويلك آمن إن وعد الله حق فيقول ما هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: Those are the ones upon whom the word has come into effect, [who will be] among nations which had passed on before them of jinn and men. Indeed, they [all] were losers.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have been condemned by God due to their disbelief and wrongdoing. They are part of the communities of jinn and humans that have come before, all of whom were destined for failure and eternal loss because of their rejection of the truth and their evil deeds. The "word" that has come into effect against them is God's decree of punishment and eternal damnation.
orig: أولئك الذين حق عليهم القول في أمم قد خلت من قبلهم من الجن والإنس إنهم كانوا خاسرين

translation: And for all there are degrees [of reward or punishment] for what they have done. And your Lord is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everyone will be judged and rewarded or punished according to their deeds. It suggests that there are varying levels or "degrees" of reward or punishment in the afterlife, commensurate with the nature and extent of one"s actions in this life. The verse also affirms that God is fully aware of everything people do, and will judge them accordingly without any injustice.
orig: ولكل درجات مما عملوا وليوفيهم أعمالهم وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And the Day when those who disbelieved will be exposed to the Fire. [They will be told], "You consumed your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them, so this Day you will be recompensed with the punishment of [extreme] humiliation because you were arrogant upon the earth without right and because you were defiantly disobedient."
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when those who rejected faith will be brought before the Fire. They will be reminded that they had enjoyed the good things of this world, but now they will be punished with humiliation for their arrogance and disobedience. The interpretation emphasizes that the punishment is a consequence of their own actions in this life - they indulged in worldly pleasures without regard for the rights of others or obedience to God, and now they will face the consequences of their choices.
orig: ويوم يعرض الذين كفروا على النار أذهبتم طيباتكم في حياتكم الدنيا واستمتعتم بها فاليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تستكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق وبما كنتم تفسقون

translation: And remember the brother of ʿĀd, when he warned his people in the Ahqāf - and warners had already passed away before him and after him - [saying], "Do not worship except Allāh. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day."
interpretation: This verse refers to the prophet Hūd, who was sent to the people of ʿĀd. It emphasizes the importance of worshipping only Allah and warning the people about the impending punishment on the Day of Judgement. The verse highlights that Hūd was not the first or the last prophet to warn his people, but that the message of worshipping only Allah has been consistent throughout history. The interpretation underscores the need to heed the warnings of the prophets and turn to Allah in order to avoid the severe punishment on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: واذكر أخا عاد إذ أنذر قومه بالأحقاف وقد خلت النذر من بين يديه ومن خلفه ألا تعبدوا إلا الله إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: They said, "Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful."
interpretation: This verse depicts the reaction of the disbelievers when confronted by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding their worship of idols. They challenged him to bring the punishment he had warned them about if he was indeed truthful in his message. The interpretation suggests that the disbelievers were unwilling to abandon their false deities and demanded tangible proof of the consequences of their rejection of the true faith.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لتأفكنا عن آلهتنا فأتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said: "The (true) knowledge is with Allah (alone). And I convey unto you that with which I have been sent, but I see that you are a people given to ignorance."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true and complete knowledge resides with Allah alone. The speaker, likely a prophet or messenger of Allah, conveys the message that has been entrusted to them, but they observe that the people they are addressing are in a state of ignorance or lack of understanding. The interpretation suggests that the speaker is trying to impart divine knowledge, but the people are not receptive or willing to learn.
orig: قال إنما العلم عند الله وأبلغكم ما أرسلت به ولكني أراكم قوما تجهلون

translation: And when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain." Rather, it is that [thing] which you were impatient for - a wind containing a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the people when they saw a cloud approaching their valleys. They initially thought it was a rain-bearing cloud, but it turned out to be a wind carrying a painful punishment. This serves as a lesson that one should not be hasty in their judgments and should wait for the true nature of events to unfold, rather than making assumptions based on appearances.
orig: فلما رأوه عارضا مستقبل أوديتهم قالوا هذا عارض ممطرنا بل هو ما استعجلتم به ريح فيها عذاب أليم

translation: It [i.e., the town] destroys everything by the command of its Lord, and they [i.e., the people] became such that nothing is to be seen except their dwellings. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of a town that was destroyed by the command of God. The town was completely devastated, leaving behind only the empty dwellings of its inhabitants. This is presented as an example of how God punishes the wrongdoers and criminals, depriving them of their homes and livelihood. The interpretation suggests that this is a warning to those who disobey God's commands, as they will face a similar fate of total destruction.
orig: تدمر كل شيء بأمر ربها فأصبحوا لا يرى إلا مساكنهم كذلك نجزي القوم المجرمين

translation: And We had certainly given them power in [matters of] the earth, and We had granted them hearing and vision and hearts, but their hearing and vision and hearts availed them not at all [from the punishment] when they were [continually] rejecting the signs of Allah, and they were enveloped by that which they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ingratitude and disbelief of those who were given great blessings and abilities by Allah, but they rejected His signs and mocked His message. Despite having the senses of hearing, sight, and understanding, they chose to disbelieve and were ultimately punished for their rejection. The verse emphasizes that the mere possession of these faculties is not enough, but they must be used to recognize and submit to the truth of Allah's revelations.
orig: ولقد مكناهم فيما إن مكناكم فيه وجعلنا لهم سمعا وأبصارا وأفئدة فما أغنى عنهم سمعهم ولا أبصارهم ولا أفئدتهم من شيء إذ كانوا يجحدون بآيات الله وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And We have already destroyed what surrounds you of [those] cities, and We have diversified the signs that perhaps they might return [to guidance].
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has destroyed the previous civilizations and communities around the people of Mecca, as a warning and lesson for them. The signs and messages of Allah have been made clear, so that the people may reflect and return to the path of guidance and righteousness.
orig: ولقد أهلكنا ما حولكم من القرى وصرفنا الآيات لعلهم يرجعون

translation: So why did those who disbelieved not prevent them? But they were only astray, and they were not able to find a way.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who worship idols and false gods instead of the one true God, Allah. It questions why those who disbelieve in the oneness of God do not prevent others from this false worship. The verse then states that those who worship idols are "astray" and unable to find the right path. This emphasizes that idolatry is a deviation from the truth and that only by worshipping the one God can one find the correct way.
orig: فلولا نصرهم الذين اتخذوا من دون الله قربانا آلهة بل ضلوا عنهم وذلك إفكهم وما كانوا يفترون

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an. And when they attended it, they said, "Listen quietly." And when it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners.
interpretation: This verse describes an incident where a group of jinn (spiritual beings) listened to the recitation of the Qur'an by the Prophet Muhammad. When they heard the Qur'an, they were captivated by it and asked others to listen quietly. After hearing the Qur'an, they returned to their people to warn them about its message. This verse highlights the profound impact the Qur'an had on the jinn, and their subsequent role in conveying its message to their own communities.
orig: وإذ صرفنا إليك نفرا من الجن يستمعون القرآن فلما حضروه قالوا أنصتوا فلما قضي ولوا إلى قومهم منذرين

translation: They said, 'O our people, indeed we have heard a [recited] Book revealed after Moses confirming what was before it which guides to the truth and to a straight path.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an, which the people acknowledged as a revealed book from God that confirms the previous scriptures and guides people to the truth and a righteous path. It emphasizes the Qur'an's authority and divine origin, and its role in providing guidance and direction for believers.
orig: قالوا يا قومنا إنا سمعنا كتابا أنزل من بعد موسى مصدقا لما بين يديه يهدي إلى الحق وإلى طريق مستقيم

translation: O my people, respond to the Caller of Allah and believe in Him. He will forgive for you your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is an exhortation from the Prophet to his people to heed the call of Allah and believe in Him. It promises that by doing so, Allah will forgive their sins and protect them from a painful punishment in the Hereafter. The key message is the importance of responding to the divine call and having faith in Allah, which will lead to forgiveness and deliverance from a severe punishment.
orig: يا قومنا أجيبوا داعي الله وآمنوا به يغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ويجركم من عذاب أليم

translation: And whoever does not respond to the Caller of Allah will not cause failure [to Him] upon the earth, and he will not have besides Him any protectors. Those are in clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of responding to the call of Allah. It states that those who do not heed the call of Allah will not be able to escape His power or authority, and they will not have any protectors or allies besides Him. Ultimately, those who reject the call of Allah are in a state of clear misguidance and error.
orig: ومن لا يجب داعي الله فليس بمعجز في الأرض وليس له من دونه أولياء أولئك في ضلال مبين

translation: Have they not considered that Allah who created the heavens and earth and did not become wearied by their creation is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed, He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse encourages us to reflect on Allah's power and ability. Despite creating the vast and complex universe, Allah is not weary or diminished in any way. This demonstrates His infinite power and capability. The verse then highlights His ability to give life to the dead, which is a clear sign of His omnipotence. The interpretation is that we should have faith in Allah's power and not doubt His ability to resurrect us on the Day of Judgment, as He is capable of all things.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض ولم يعي بخلقهن بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى بلى إنه على كل شيء قدير

translation: And the Day when the disbelievers will be exposed to the Fire. [They will be told], "Is this not the truth?" They will say, "Yes, by our Lord." [Allah] will say, "Then taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve."
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers will be confronted with the reality of the Hellfire. They will be forced to acknowledge the truth of their disbelief, and will be commanded to taste the punishment they had denied during their earthly lives. The interpretation emphasizes the inevitability of the consequences for those who rejected faith and the justice of Allah in meting out the appropriate punishment.
orig: ويوم يعرض الذين كفروا على النار أليس هذا بالحق قالوا بلى وربنا قال فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad], as were those of determination among the messengers and do not be impatient for them. It will be - on the Day they see that which they are promised - as though they had not remained [in the world] except an hour of a day. [This is] notification. And will [any] be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad and his followers to be patient and steadfast in the face of adversity, just as the previous prophets were. It reminds them that the Day of Judgment will come, and on that day, the disbelievers will feel as if they had only remained in this world for a short time. This is a warning to the defiant and disobedient, that they will be destroyed for their refusal to believe and submit to God.
orig: فاصبر كما صبر أولو العزم من الرسل ولا تستعجل لهم كأنهم يوم يرون ما يوعدون لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من نهار بلاغ فهل يهلك إلا القوم الفاسقون

translation: Those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah - He will waste their deeds.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who reject faith in Allah and actively prevent others from following the path of Allah. The interpretation is that their actions and deeds will be rendered worthless and wasted, as they have turned away from the guidance of Allah.
orig: الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله أضل أعمالهم

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds and believe in what has been sent down upon Muhammad - and it is the truth from their Lord - He will remove from them their misdeeds and amend their condition.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and righteous actions. It promises that those who believe in God and the Prophet Muhammad, and who do good deeds, will have their sins forgiven and their lives improved. The key elements are: 1) belief in God and the Prophet, 2) doing good works, and 3) God’s forgiveness and betterment of their situation. This highlights the path to salvation and a better life in this world and the next for those who sincerely follow the teachings of Islam.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وآمنوا بما نزل على محمد وهو الحق من ربهم كفر عنهم سيئاتهم وأصلح بالهم

translation: That is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood, while those who believe follow the truth from their Lord. Thus does Allah present to the people their comparisons.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the paths of those who disbelieve and those who believe. The disbelievers follow falsehood, while the believers follow the truth revealed by their Lord. This comparison is presented by Allah to guide people and help them discern the right path from the wrong.
orig: ذلك بأن الذين كفروا اتبعوا الباطل وأن الذين آمنوا اتبعوا الحق من ربهم كذلك يضرب الله للناس أمثالهم

translation: So when you meet those who disbelieve [in battle], strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds, and either [confer] favor afterwards or [accept] ransom until the war lays down its burdens. That [is the command]. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them [Himself], but [He ordered armed struggle] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah - never will He allow their deeds to be lost.
interpretation: This verse outlines the rules of engagement for Muslims in battle against those who disbelieve. It instructs them to strike the necks of the disbelievers until they have been thoroughly defeated, at which point they should either show them favor by releasing them or accept ransom for their release. This is to be done until the war has ended. The verse emphasizes that Allah could have taken vengeance Himself, but instead ordered this armed struggle as a test for the believers. It also reassures that the deeds of those killed in Allah's cause will not be lost.
orig: فإذا لقيتم الذين كفروا فضرب الرقاب حتى إذا أثخنتموهم فشدوا الوثاق فإما منا بعد وإما فداء حتى تضع الحرب أوزارها ذلك ولو يشاء الله لانتصر منهم ولكن ليبلو بعضكم ببعض والذين قتلوا في سبيل الله فلن يضل أعمالهم

translation: He will guide them and amend their condition
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah will guide the believers and improve their situation. The interpretation implies that Allah will provide guidance and support to those who follow Him, helping them to overcome their challenges and achieve a state of well-being.
orig: سيهديهم ويصلح بالهم

translation: And He will admit them to Paradise that He has made known to them.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah will grant the believers entry into Paradise, which He has already informed them about and made known to them through the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The believers have been told about the blessings and delights of Paradise, and they have the promise of attaining it if they remain faithful and obedient to Allah. This verse reinforces the idea that Paradise is a real and tangible reward for the believers in the Hereafter.
orig: ويدخلهم الجنة عرفها لهم

translation: O you who believe, if you support Allah, He will support you and make your foothold firm.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to support and aid the cause of Allah, through their faith, actions, and devotion. In return, Allah will support and strengthen the believers, making their position and resolve steadfast. The interpretation suggests that by supporting the divine will and purpose, the believers will be rewarded with divine assistance and guidance to remain firm in their faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تنصروا الله ينصركم ويثبت أقدامكم

translation: And those who disbelieve - for them is destruction, and He will waste their deeds.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject faith in Allah and His guidance. It states that those who disbelieve will face a wretched end and that their deeds, no matter how good they may seem, will be rendered worthless on the Day of Judgement. The implication is that true success and salvation can only be attained through faith and righteous actions done in accordance with Allah's commands.
orig: والذين كفروا فتعسا لهم وأضل أعمالهم

translation: That is because they disliked what Allah revealed, so He rendered their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who reject the guidance and teachings of Allah as revealed in the Quran. Their rejection of the divine revelation leads to the nullification of their good deeds, as they have turned away from the path of righteousness. The interpretation suggests that true faith and obedience to Allah's commands are essential for one's actions to be accepted and rewarded in the Hereafter.
orig: ذلك بأنهم كرهوا ما أنزل الله فأحبط أعمالهم

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed [everything] over them, and for the disbelievers is something similar.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the fate of previous generations who rejected the truth and were destroyed as a consequence of their disbelief. It serves as a warning to the disbelievers that they will face a similar fate if they persist in their rejection of God's message. The verse emphasizes the importance of learning from history and not repeating the mistakes of those who came before.
orig: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم دمر الله عليهم وللكافرين أمثالها

translation: That is because Allah is the Protector of those who believe, but the disbelievers have no protector.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the guardian, supporter, and protector of those who believe in Him. In contrast, the disbelievers have no such divine protection or assistance. This highlights the fundamental difference between the believers and the disbelievers, and the importance of having faith in Allah as the source of divine guidance and protection.
orig: ذلك بأن الله مولى الذين آمنوا وأن الكافرين لا مولى لهم

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow, while those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as grazing livestock eat, and the Fire is a residence for them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the distinction between the fate of the believers and the disbelievers. The believers, who have faith and do good deeds, will be admitted to the gardens of Paradise where they will enjoy eternal bliss. In contrast, the disbelievers will indulge in worldly pleasures, like animals grazing, but their ultimate abode will be the Fire of Hell. This highlights the importance of faith and righteous actions, and the consequences of disbelief and rejection of God's guidance.
orig: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار والذين كفروا يتمتعون ويأكلون كما تأكل الأنعام والنار مثوى لهم

translation: And how many a city have We destroyed that was stronger in power than your city which has driven you out? So there is none to help them.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the fate that befell previous nations and civilizations that were more powerful than the city from which the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was driven out. It serves as a warning that no power or might can withstand the will of Allah, and that those who oppose the truth and persecute the believers will ultimately be destroyed. The verse encourages the believers to have faith in Allah's plan and to not be discouraged by the apparent strength of their enemies, for Allah's help and support will ultimately prevail.
orig: وكأين من قرية هي أشد قوة من قريتك التي أخرجتك أهلكناهم فلا ناصر لهم

translation: Is then one who is on a clear (Path) from his Lord, no better than one to whom the evil that he does appears pleasing, and such follow their own lusts?
interpretation: This verse contrasts two types of people: those who have clear guidance from God, and those who are misled by their own desires and see their evil deeds as attractive. The implication is that the former, who follow the truth, are superior to the latter, who blindly follow their own whims and fancies. The verse encourages believers to seek clear guidance from God rather than being swayed by their own selfish impulses.
orig: أفمن كان على بينة من ربه كمن زين له سوء عمله واتبعوا أهواءهم

translation: The description of Paradise which the righteous are promised: In it are rivers of water unaltered, rivers of milk the taste of which never changes, rivers of wine delightful to those who drink, and rivers of purified honey. And they will have therein all kinds of fruits and forgiveness from their Lord. [Are such] like those who abide eternally in the Fire and are given to drink scalding water that will sever their intestines?
interpretation: This verse paints a vivid picture of the blessings and delights that await the righteous in Paradise. The description of the pure, unaltered rivers of water, milk, wine, and honey emphasizes the perfection and purity of the pleasures in Paradise. This is contrasted with the torment of the disbelievers in the Hellfire, who are forced to drink scalding water that tears apart their insides. The verse highlights the stark difference between the eternal bliss of the righteous and the eternal punishment of the wicked, making clear the high stakes and the importance of following the path of righteousness.
orig: مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون فيها أنهار من ماء غير آسن وأنهار من لبن لم يتغير طعمه وأنهار من خمر لذة للشاربين وأنهار من عسل مصفى ولهم فيها من كل الثمرات ومغفرة من ربهم كمن هو خالد في النار وسقوا ماء حميما فقطع أمعاءهم

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, [O Muhammad], until, when they leave you, they say to those who have been given knowledge, "What has he said just now?" Those are the ones over whose hearts Allah has sealed, and they follow [only] their [own] desires.
interpretation: This verse describes a group of people who outwardly appear to listen to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the teachings of Islam, but their hearts are sealed by Allah due to their following of their own desires and whims rather than the truth. They do not truly comprehend or retain the message, and instead ask others about what was said, indicating a lack of sincere engagement and understanding. This verse serves as a warning against such hypocrisy and the danger of allowing one's desires to overshadow the pursuit of true knowledge and guidance.
orig: ومنهم من يستمع إليك حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك قالوا للذين أوتوا العلم ماذا قال آنفا أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم واتبعوا أهواءهم

translation: And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their [i.e., the guided ones'] righteousness.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who have been guided by Allah and have accepted the truth of Islam, Allah will increase their guidance and strengthen their faith and righteous conduct. The more they strive to follow the path of guidance, the more Allah will bless them with additional guidance and a deeper sense of piety and God-consciousness.
orig: والذين اهتدوا زادهم هدى وآتاهم تقواهم

translation: Do they then await [anything] except the Hour [of judgement] that it should come upon them suddenly? But already its signs have come, and when it is upon them, how [will it be] for them when their reminder has come to them?
interpretation: This verse is encouraging people to be prepared for the Day of Judgement, which will come suddenly and unexpectedly. It suggests that the signs of the Hour have already begun to manifest, and when it arrives, those who have ignored the reminders and guidance will be in a difficult situation. The verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of the impending Judgement and preparing oneself accordingly.
orig: فهل ينظرون إلا الساعة أن تأتيهم بغتة فقد جاء أشراطها فأنى لهم إذا جاءتهم ذكراهم

translation: So know, [O Muhammad], that there is no deity except Allah and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. And Allah knows of your movement and your resting place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental belief in the oneness of God (tawhid) and the importance of seeking forgiveness not only for oneself but also for all believers. It reminds the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension all believers, that God is all-knowing and aware of our every movement and resting place. The verse encourages humility, repentance, and a deep awareness of God's omniscience and sovereignty.
orig: فاعلم أنه لا إله إلا الله واستغفر لذنبك وللمؤمنين والمؤمنات والله يعلم متقلبكم ومثواكم

translation: And those who believe say, "Why has a surah not been sent down? But when a precise surah is revealed and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with a look of one overcome by death. And more [suitable] for them [would have been]
interpretation: This verse is addressing the believers who were questioning why a new surah (chapter) of the Quran had not been revealed. When a clear and decisive surah was revealed that mentioned fighting (i.e. the obligation of jihad), those whose hearts were diseased with hypocrisy and doubt looked at the Prophet with the gaze of one who is about to die, filled with fear and aversion. This verse condemns the hypocrisy of such people and suggests that it would have been better for them to accept the Quranic teachings wholeheartedly rather than show such resistance.
orig: ويقول الذين آمنوا لولا نزلت سورة فإذا أنزلت سورة محكمة وذكر فيها القتال رأيت الذين في قلوبهم مرض ينظرون إليك نظر المغشي عليه من الموت فأولى لهم

translation: Obedience and good speech. But when the matter has been decided, then if they were true to Allah, it would be better for them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and good speech. It suggests that when a decision has been made, it is better for people to be truthful and faithful to Allah, as this would be more beneficial for them. The interpretation highlights the value of sincerity and devotion to Allah in one's actions and words, even when faced with difficult decisions.
orig: طاعة وقول معروف فإذا عزم الأمر فلو صدقوا الله لكان خيرا لهم

translation: Then, is it to be expected of you, if you were put in authority, that you would do mischief in the land and sever your ties of kinship?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the reader to consider the consequences of their actions. It suggests that if one is given power or authority, they should use it responsibly and not abuse it by causing corruption and severing family ties. The verse serves as a warning against misusing power and a call to uphold moral and ethical values for the betterment of society.
orig: فهل عسيتم إن توليتم أن تفسدوا في الأرض وتقطعوا أرحامكم

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He deafened them and blinded their sight.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have been condemned by Allah due to their rejection of faith and persistent disbelief. The verse suggests that Allah has deprived them of the ability to hear the truth and see the guidance, as a consequence of their own choices and actions. This interpretation highlights the idea that those who willfully turn away from Allah's signs and guidance will be deprived of the ability to perceive and understand the truth.
orig: أولئك الذين لعنهم الله فأصمهم وأعمى أبصارهم

translation: Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon [their] hearts?
interpretation: This verse encourages people to ponder and reflect deeply upon the Qur'an, God's revealed scripture. It suggests that some people may have hardened hearts and closed minds, preventing them from truly understanding the profound wisdom and guidance contained in the Qur'an. The implication is that people should open their hearts and minds to the Qur'an, and strive to comprehend its teachings, in order to attain spiritual enlightenment and a closer connection with the divine.
orig: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن أم على قلوب أقفالها

translation: Indeed, those who reverted back [to disbelief] after guidance had become clear to them - Satan enticed them and prolonged hope for them.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who had previously accepted the guidance of Islam, but then later turned away from it and reverted to disbelief. The verse explains that Satan (the devil) tempted them and made their return to disbelief seem appealing, giving them false hope and delaying their repentance. The message here is that one must be steadfast in their faith, as Satan is ever-ready to lead people astray, even those who had once been guided.
orig: إن الذين ارتدوا على أدبارهم من بعد ما تبين لهم الهدى الشيطان سول لهم وأملى لهم

translation: That is because they said to those who dislike what Allah has sent down: "We will obey you in part of the matter." And Allah knows their secrets.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who would outwardly claim to follow Islam, but in secret would obey the disbelievers and go against the teachings of the Qur’an. The verse emphasizes that Allah knows the true intentions and secrets of these hypocrites, and that they cannot hide their deception from Him.
orig: ذلك بأنهم قالوا للذين كرهوا ما نزل الله سنطيعكم في بعض الأمر والله يعلم إسرارهم

translation: Then how [will it be] when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the dire consequences that the disbelievers will face on the Day of Judgment. When the angels of death come to take their souls, they will strike the disbelievers' faces and backs, signifying the humiliation and punishment they will endure for their rejection of faith and their misdeeds in life. The verse serves as a warning to those who turn away from God's guidance and a reminder of the ultimate accountability that awaits them.
orig: فكيف إذا توفتهم الملائكة يضربون وجوههم وأدبارهم

translation: That is because they followed what angered Allah and disliked [what earns] His pleasure, so He rendered worthless their deeds.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who have turned away from the path of righteousness and instead followed that which displeases Allah. By rejecting Allah's pleasure and guidance, they have rendered their deeds and actions worthless in the sight of Allah. The key message is that true success and salvation can only be achieved by following the will of Allah and seeking His pleasure, not by pursuing one's own desires and whims.
orig: ذلك بأنهم اتبعوا ما أسخط الله وكرهوا رضوانه فأحبط أعمالهم

translation: Or do those in whose hearts is disease think that Allah will never expose their [feelings of] animosity?
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who harbor ill-intentions and malice in their hearts. It suggests that such people should not assume that Allah will not reveal their true feelings and hidden animosity. The verse implies that Allah is aware of the hidden thoughts and emotions of people, and He has the power to expose the true nature of those who try to conceal their ill-will and hostility.
orig: أم حسب الذين في قلوبهم مرض أن لن يخرج الله أضغانهم

translation: And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would know them by their mark; and you will surely know them by the tone of [their] speech. And Allah knows your deeds.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has the power to reveal the true nature of people to us, as He knows their innermost thoughts and actions. However, He chooses not to do so, as it is part of the test of faith that we judge people based on their outward behavior and speech, rather than making assumptions about their character. The verse reminds us that Allah is all-knowing and will judge us according to our deeds, not our appearances or words.
orig: ولو نشاء لأريناكهم فلعرفتهم بسيماهم ولتعرفنهم في لحن القول والله يعلم أعمالكم

translation: And We will surely test you until We make evident those who strive among you [for the cause of Allah ] and the patient, and We will test your affairs.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah will test and try the believers in order to distinguish those who strive and struggle in His cause from those who are patient and steadfast. The trials and tribulations faced by the believers serve to purify and strengthen their faith, and to demonstrate their true character and commitment to the religion. Through these tests, Allah will make known those who are sincere in their devotion and those who are merely pretenders.
orig: ولنبلونكم حتى نعلم المجاهدين منكم والصابرين ونبلو أخباركم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah and oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them - never will they harm Allah at all, and He will render their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject faith and actively work to turn others away from the path of Allah. It emphasizes that their actions, no matter how harmful they may seem, will not truly affect Allah in any way. Rather, their own deeds will be rendered meaningless and ineffective, as Allah is in control and will not allow their efforts to succeed. The key message is that those who oppose the truth and the Messenger will ultimately fail, for Allah's guidance and plan cannot be thwarted.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله وشاقوا الرسول من بعد ما تبين لهم الهدى لن يضروا الله شيئا وسيحبط أعمالهم

translation: O you who believe! Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not invalidate your deeds
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger (Muhammad, peace be upon him) for the believers. It warns against invalidating one's good deeds by disobeying the commands of Allah and the Messenger. The verse encourages believers to strive to fulfill their religious obligations and to align their actions with the teachings of Islam, in order to ensure the acceptance and reward of their deeds in the Hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول ولا تبطلوا أعمالكم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah and then die while they are disbelievers - for them Allah will not forgive.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of disbelief and turning others away from the path of Allah. It states that those who die in a state of disbelief will not be forgiven by Allah. The interpretation is that rejecting faith and actively hindering others from the way of Allah is a grave sin that has severe consequences in the Hereafter, as Allah will not forgive such individuals.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله ثم ماتوا وهم كفار فلن يغفر الله لهم

translation: So do not weaken and do not call for peace while you are superior and Allah is with you, and He will never deprive you of [the reward of] your deeds.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast and not to show weakness or call for peace when they are in a position of strength and superiority. It reminds them that Allah is with them and will not diminish the reward for their righteous deeds. The interpretation suggests that the believers should maintain their resolve and confidence in Allah's support, even in the face of adversity, as long as they are on the path of truth and justice.
orig: فلا تهنوا وتدعوا إلى السلم وأنتم الأعلون والله معكم ولن يتركم أعمالكم

translation: Verily, the life of this world is but a pastime and play. And if you believe and guard against evil, He will grant you your rewards, and will not ask of you your possessions.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the life of this world is temporary and fleeting, like a game or play. It encourages believers to focus on their faith and righteousness, as God will reward them for their deeds and does not demand their wealth or possessions in return. The verse reminds us that the true value lies in our spiritual development and relationship with God, not in the material pursuits of this world.
orig: إنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وإن تؤمنوا وتتقوا يؤتكم أجوركم ولا يسألكم أموالكم

translation: If He were to ask you for it and press you, you would be niggardly, and He would expose your malice.
interpretation: This verse warns against being stingy and holding back when asked to give or contribute. It suggests that if God were to demand something from people, they would be reluctant to give, and this would reveal the malice or ill-will that they harbor within themselves. The verse encourages generosity and openness, rather than selfishness and hidden resentment.
orig: إن يسألكموها فيحفكم تبخلوا ويخرج أضغانكم

translation: Here you are - those invited to spend in the cause of Allah, but among you are those who withhold [wealth]. And whoever withholds is only withholding from himself. And Allah is the Free of need, while you are the needy. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the believers, reminding them that they are being called upon to spend and give in the way of Allah. However, some among them are being stingy and withholding their wealth. The verse emphasizes that whoever withholds is only depriving themselves, as Allah is self-sufficient and does not need their wealth, while the believers are in need of Allah's provision. The verse also warns that if the believers turn away from this obligation, Allah will replace them with another people who will be more obedient and willing to spend in His cause. The interpretation highlights the importance of generosity and spending in the way of Allah, as well as the consequences of stinginess and turning away from this duty.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء تدعون لتنفقوا في سبيل الله فمنكم من يبخل ومن يبخل فإنما يبخل عن نفسه والله الغني وأنتم الفقراء وإن تتولوا يستبدل قوما غيركم ثم لا يكونوا أمثالكم

translation: Indeed, We have given you, [O Muhammad], a clear conquest.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the conquest of Makkah by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers. It is a promise from Allah that He has granted the Prophet a clear and decisive victory, which marked a significant turning point in the spread of Islam. The interpretation suggests that this victory was a divine gift and a manifestation of Allah's support for the Prophet and his mission.
orig: إنا فتحنا لك فتحا مبينا

translation: That Allah may forgive you your sins of the past and the future, and complete His Favor on you, and guide you on the Straight Path
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and is a supplication for him. It indicates that Allah has forgiven the Prophet's past and future sins, and has completed His favor upon him by guiding him to the Straight Path. This verse highlights the high status of the Prophet and the extent of Allah's forgiveness and guidance for him. It serves as an encouragement for believers to seek Allah's forgiveness and guidance, just as the Prophet did.
orig: ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر ويتم نعمته عليك ويهديك صراطا مستقيما

translation: And Allah will help you with a mighty victory.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the believers that He will grant them a decisive victory over their enemies. The phrase "a mighty victory" suggests that the victory will be complete, overwhelming, and empowering for the believers. This verse encourages the believers to have faith in Allah's support and to remain steadfast in their struggle, as Allah will ultimately grant them success.
orig: وينصرك الله نصرا عزيزا

translation: It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers that they may have increased in faith along with their [present] faith. And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, and ever is Allah Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who instills a sense of tranquility and peace in the hearts of the believers, which in turn strengthens their faith. The believers" faith is not static, but rather it can increase and grow stronger. This divine tranquility is a blessing from Allah, who is the Sovereign of the heavens and the earth, and who is All-Knowing and All-Wise in His actions and decisions.
orig: هو الذي أنزل السكينة في قلوب المؤمنين ليزدادوا إيمانا مع إيمانهم ولله جنود السماوات والأرض وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: That He may admit the believing men and the believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally, and remove from them their misdeeds - and ever is that, in the sight of Allah, a great attainment.
interpretation: This verse promises the believers, both men and women, that they will be admitted to the gardens of Paradise, where they will live eternally. Additionally, their sins and misdeeds will be forgiven and removed from them. This is a great and tremendous success in the sight of Allah, the Almighty.
orig: ليدخل المؤمنين والمؤمنات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ويكفر عنهم سيئاتهم وكان ذلك عند الله فوزا عظيما

translation: And [Allah will] punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women - and Allah will turn in forgiveness to the believing men and believing women. And Allah is Ever All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who are hypocrites and polytheists, who harbor ill thoughts about Allah. They will be punished for their disbelief and evil intentions. In contrast, the believing men and women will be forgiven by Allah, for He is the Most Forgiving and Merciful. The verse emphasizes the consequences of harboring negative thoughts about Allah, and the importance of true faith and submission to Him.
orig: ويعذب المنافقين والمنافقات والمشركين والمشركات الظانين بالله ظن السوء عليهم دائرة السوء وغضب الله عليهم ولعنهم وأعد لهم جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Ever All-Mighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the Sovereign Lord who commands the armies of the heavens and the earth. He is Almighty, possessing supreme power and authority, and He is All-Wise, governing the universe with perfect wisdom and purpose. This verse reinforces the belief that Allah is the ultimate source of all power and that He alone deserves worship and obedience.
orig: ولله جنود السماوات والأرض وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger of Allah. He was sent as a "witness" to testify to the truth of the divine message, a "bringer of good tidings" to those who believe, and a "warner" to those who reject it. The verse highlights the Prophet's responsibility to convey the message of Islam to all of humanity.
orig: إنا أرسلناك شاهدا ومبشرا ونذيرا

translation: That you [believers] may believe in Allah and His Messenger and honor him and respect him and exalt Him morning and afternoon.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have faith in Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad (peace be upon him). It calls for honoring, respecting, and exalting Allah through remembrance and glorification throughout the day, both in the morning and the evening. The purpose is to strengthen the believers" commitment to their faith and to Allah, and to demonstrate their reverence and devotion.
orig: لتؤمنوا بالله ورسوله وتعزروه وتوقروه وتسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, [O Muhammad] - they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So he who breaks his pledge breaks it only to the detriment of himself. And he who fulfills that which he has promised Allah - [Allah] will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that when people pledge allegiance to the Prophet Muhammad, they are in fact pledging allegiance to Allah. The phrase "the hand of Allah is over their hands" suggests that Allah is witness to and oversees this pledge. The verse then warns that those who break their pledge will only harm themselves, while those who fulfill their pledge to Allah will be greatly rewarded. The interpretation is that one's allegiance should be to Allah above all else, and that keeping one's word and fulfilling one's obligations to Allah is of utmost importance.
orig: إن الذين يبايعونك إنما يبايعون الله يد الله فوق أيديهم فمن نكث فإنما ينكث على نفسه ومن أوفى بما عاهد عليه الله فسيؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: The bedouins who lagged behind will say to you, "Our possessions and our families occupied us, so ask forgiveness for us." They say with their tongues what is not within their hearts. Say, "Then who could prevent Allah at all if He intended for you harm or intended for you benefit? Rather, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted."
interpretation: This verse addresses the bedouins who made excuses for not participating in the battles and expeditions with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They claimed that their wealth and families preoccupied them, and they asked the Prophet to seek forgiveness for them. However, the Qur'an states that their words did not reflect their true intentions, as their hearts were not sincere. The verse then emphasizes that no one can prevent Allah from bestowing harm or benefit upon them, for He is fully aware of their actions and intentions. This serves as a reminder that one cannot make excuses for neglecting their religious duties and that Allah is the ultimate judge of our deeds.
orig: سيقول لك المخلفون من الأعراب شغلتنا أموالنا وأهلونا فاستغفر لنا يقولون بألسنتهم ما ليس في قلوبهم قل فمن يملك لكم من الله شيئا إن أراد بكم ضرا أو أراد بكم نفعا بل كان الله بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: Nay, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and that was made fair-seeming in your hearts. And you thought an evil thought, and you became a people doomed.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who doubted the return of the Prophet Muhammad and the believers after a battle or expedition. It condemns their evil thoughts and assumptions that the Messenger and the believers would never come back to their families. This was a harmful and misguided notion that took root in their hearts. The verse warns that such evil thoughts and assumptions will lead to their own doom and destruction.
orig: بل ظننتم أن لن ينقلب الرسول والمؤمنون إلى أهليهم أبدا وزين ذلك في قلوبكم وظننتم ظن السوء وكنتم قوما بورا

translation: And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of belief in Allah and His Messenger (Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him). It warns that those who reject this belief will face the punishment of the Hellfire, which is described as a "Blaze". The interpretation is that faith in Allah and His Messenger is a fundamental requirement, and those who deny it will be subjected to the eternal torment of the Hereafter.
orig: ومن لم يؤمن بالله ورسوله فإنا أعتدنا للكافرين سعيرا

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over the entire universe. He alone has the authority to forgive or punish whomever He pleases, for He is the All-Forgiving and the Most Merciful. This highlights the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness and mercy, and submitting to His will, as He is the ultimate Judge and Ruler.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: Those who lagged behind will say, when you set out to take the spoils, "Allow us to follow you." They wish to change the words of Allah. Say, "You shall never follow us. This is what Allah has decreed beforehand." Then they will say, "You are jealous of us." Indeed, they rarely understand.
interpretation: This verse addresses the attitude of those who were reluctant to participate in the military campaigns of the early Muslim community. When the believers went out to acquire war spoils, the laggards would ask to be allowed to join them, not out of sincere faith, but out of a desire to share in the material gains. The verse condemns their attempt to change the teachings of Allah, and states that they will not be allowed to follow the believers. Their true motive is jealousy, not a desire to follow the truth. This highlights the importance of sincerity and commitment in faith, rather than being motivated by worldly gains.
orig: سيقول المخلفون إذا انطلقتم إلى مغانم لتأخذوها ذرونا نتبعكم يريدون أن يبدلوا كلام الله قل لن تتبعونا كذلكم قال الله من قبل فسيقولون بل تحسدوننا بل كانوا لا يفقهون إلا قليلا

translation: Say to the desert Arabs who lagged behind: "You will be summoned (to fight) against a people given to vehement war: then shall you fight, or they shall submit. Then if you show obedience, Allah will grant you a goodly reward, but if you turn back as you did before, He will punish you with a grievous Penalty."
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the desert Arabs who were reluctant to join the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in his military campaigns. It is a call to them to prepare for battle against a formidable enemy. They are given a choice: either fight the enemy or they will submit. If they obey and join the fight, they will be rewarded handsomely by Allah. But if they turn back as they did before, they will be punished severely. The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and fighting for the cause of Islam, even if it means facing a strong adversary. It is a call to the believers to be steadfast in their faith and to fulfill their duty to defend the religion.
orig: قل للمخلفين من الأعراب ستدعون إلى قوم أولي بأس شديد تقاتلونهم أو يسلمون فإن تطيعوا يؤتكم الله أجرا حسنا وإن تتولوا كما توليتم من قبل يعذبكم عذابا أليما

translation: There is not upon the blind [any] constraint nor upon the lame constraint nor upon the ill constraint. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, but whoever turns away - He will punish him with a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Islam does not place undue burdens or hardships on those who are physically impaired or ill. It establishes that those with disabilities or sickness are not held to the same standards as the physically able. The verse also highlights that the ultimate reward for those who obey Allah and His Messenger is admission into Paradise, while those who turn away from faith will face a painful punishment. The message is one of compassion, flexibility and the promise of eternal bliss for the faithful.
orig: ليس على الأعمى حرج ولا على الأعرج حرج ولا على المريض حرج ومن يطع الله ورسوله يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ومن يتول يعذبه عذابا أليما

translation: Certainly was Allah pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you, [O Muhammad], under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with a near conquest
interpretation: This verse describes the event of the Pledge of Allegiance (Bayat ar-Ridwan) that took place under a tree during the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. Allah was pleased with the believers who pledged their loyalty to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) at that time, as He knew the sincerity in their hearts. In return, Allah sent down a sense of tranquility and peace upon them, and promised them a near victory, which was the conquest of Makkah a few years later.
orig: لقد رضي الله عن المؤمنين إذ يبايعونك تحت الشجرة فعلم ما في قلوبهم فأنزل السكينة عليهم وأثابهم فتحا قريبا

translation: And [they obtained] many war prisoners whom they took [as spoils], and Allah is Ever All-Mighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse refers to the spoils of war that the believers were able to obtain through their victories. The verse emphasizes that the believers were able to acquire many war prisoners and other spoils, which was a sign of Allah's power and wisdom. The interpretation is that Allah grants victory and spoils to the believers as a reward for their faith and struggle in His cause, and that He is All-Mighty and All-Wise in His decisions and actions.
orig: ومغانم كثيرة يأخذونها وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: God has promised you many gains that you will capture, and He has hastened for you this one and withheld the hands of people from you so that it may be a sign for the believers, and that He may guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the conquest of Mecca by the Prophet Muhammad and his followers. God had promised the believers that they would gain many victories and spoils of war. In this particular instance, God facilitated the conquest of Mecca for the believers and protected them from the hands of their enemies. This victory was a sign for the believers, affirming God's support and guidance. The verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast on the straight path that God has shown them.
orig: وعدكم الله مغانم كثيرة تأخذونها فعجل لكم هذه وكف أيدي الناس عنكم ولتكون آية للمؤمنين ويهديكم صراطا مستقيما

translation: And [He created] another [creation] which you have not been able [to produce]; and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the creation of something that humans have not been able to replicate or produce, which is a testament to the power and omnipotence of Allah. It suggests that there are aspects of the universe and creation that are beyond human understanding and capability, and that Allah alone has the power and knowledge to create all things. The verse emphasizes that Allah is "over all things competent," meaning that He has complete control and authority over the entire creation.
orig: وأخرى لم تقدروا عليها قد أحاط الله بها وكان الله على كل شيء قديرا

translation: And if those who disbelieve were to fight you, they would turn [their] backs; then they would not find a protector or a helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the disbelievers who fight against the believers will ultimately be defeated and forced to retreat. They will not find any protector or helper to support them, as Allah is the ultimate Protector of the believers. This verse serves as a reassurance and encouragement for the believers, reminding them that their faith in Allah will prevail over the disbelievers.
orig: ولو قاتلكم الذين كفروا لولوا الأدبار ثم لا يجدون وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: The established way of Allah which has gone before, and you will not find in the way of Allah any change.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immutability and consistency of Allah's laws and ways. It suggests that the divine principles and patterns that have governed the universe and human affairs in the past will continue to do so in the future. The verse implies that one should not expect or seek changes to Allah's established ways, as they are constant and unchanging. This can provide a sense of stability, predictability and trust in the divine order of things.
orig: سنة الله التي قد خلت من قبل ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا

translation: And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them within [the area of] Makkah after He had made you victorious over them. And ever is Allah of what you do Seeing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslims were prevented from entering Makkah and performing the pilgrimage, despite having the upper hand. However, Allah prevented the hands of the disbelievers from harming the Muslims, and the hands of the Muslims from retaliating, in order to establish a truce and pave the way for future reconciliation. This demonstrates Allah's wisdom and foresight, as He is all-seeing and aware of the consequences of our actions.
orig: وهو الذي كف أيديهم عنكم وأيديكم عنهم ببطن مكة من بعد أن أظفركم عليهم وكان الله بما تعملون بصيرا

translation: They are the ones who disbelieved and obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Haram while the offering was prevented from reaching its place [of sacrifice]. And if not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know - that you might trample them - and there would reach you from them [some] ill-will without [your] knowledge - [you would have been permitted to enter Makkah]. [This was so] that Allah might admit to His mercy whom He wills. If they had been apart [from them], We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the disbelievers who prevented the Muslims from entering the Sacred Mosque in Makkah and obstructed the pilgrims from reaching the place of sacrifice. However, Allah prevented the Muslims from attacking the disbelievers indiscriminately, as there were believing men and women among them whom the Muslims did not know. This was to protect the believers from harm and to allow Allah to show His mercy to whomever He wills. The verse suggests that if the believers and disbelievers had been separated, Allah would have punished the disbelievers with a painful punishment.
orig: هم الذين كفروا وصدوكم عن المسجد الحرام والهدي معكوفا أن يبلغ محله ولولا رجال مؤمنون ونساء مؤمنات لم تعلموهم أن تطئوهم فتصيبكم منهم معرة بغير علم ليدخل الله في رحمته من يشاء لو تزيلوا لعذبنا الذين كفروا منهم عذابا أليما

translation: When those who disbelieved harboured in their hearts [feelings of] pride and haughtiness - the [pride of the] time of ignorance - then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers and imposed upon them the word of righteousness, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse describes a situation where the disbelievers harboured feelings of pride and arrogance, similar to the arrogance of the pre-Islamic period of ignorance. In response, Allah sent down His tranquillity and calmness upon His Messenger and the believers, and imposed upon them the word of righteousness, which they were more deserving and worthy of. This highlights how Allah protects the believers from the arrogance of the disbelievers, and guides them towards righteousness and humility.
orig: إذ جعل الذين كفروا في قلوبهم الحمية حمية الجاهلية فأنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين وألزمهم كلمة التقوى وكانوا أحق بها وأهلها وكان الله بكل شيء عليما

translation: Verily, Allah has fulfilled His Messenger's vision with truth. You shall certainly enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in safety, with your heads shaved and hair cut short, without any fear. He knew what you did not know, and He has granted, besides that, a near victory.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Prophet Muhammad's vision of entering the Sacred Mosque in Mecca was fulfilled. It indicates that the Muslims would be able to enter the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, which was under the control of the Quraysh at the time, in safety and without fear. The verse also suggests that this would be achieved through Allah's will and that the Muslims would be in a state of ritual consecration, with their heads shaved or hair cut short. Furthermore, the verse implies that Allah had knowledge of events that the Muslims did not know, and that He had granted them a near victory, likely referring to the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, which paved the way for the eventual conquest of Mecca.
orig: لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رءوسكم ومقصرين لا تخافون فعلم ما لم تعلموا فجعل من دون ذلك فتحا قريبا

translation: He is the One who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religions, and sufficient is Allah as a Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has sent the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) with the true guidance and the religion of Islam, which is the final and complete revelation from God. The purpose is for Islam to prevail over all other religions and belief systems. Allah Himself bears witness to the truth of this message, and it is sufficient as a testimony.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating [in prayer], seeking bounty from Allah and [His] pleasure. Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their description in the Torah. And their description in the Gospel is as a plant which produces its offshoots and strengthens them so they grow firm and stand upon their stems, delighting the sowers - so that He may enrage by them the disbelievers. Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of the believers who follow the Prophet Muhammad. They are firm and resolute against the disbelievers, yet merciful and compassionate towards each other. They are constantly engaged in worship, bowing and prostrating, seeking Allah's pleasure and bounty. Their devotion is evident on their faces, as they bear the marks of frequent prostration. This description is found in both the Torah and the Gospel, comparing the believers to a thriving plant that delights its cultivator. Allah has promised forgiveness and a great reward for those believers who do righteous deeds, in order to enrage the disbelievers.
orig: محمد رسول الله والذين معه أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم تراهم ركعا سجدا يبتغون فضلا من الله ورضوانا سيماهم في وجوههم من أثر السجود ذلك مثلهم في التوراة ومثلهم في الإنجيل كزرع أخرج شطأه فآزره فاستغلظ فاستوى على سوقه يعجب الزراع ليغيظ بهم الكفار وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات منهم مغفرة وأجرا عظيما

translation: O you who believe! Do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to not act or speak in a way that places themselves above Allah and His Messenger. It emphasizes the need for humility and reverence before Allah, and to be mindful that Allah is all-hearing and all-knowing. The believers are called upon to fear and submit to Allah, and to not try to put themselves first or act arrogantly in relation to the commands of Allah and His Messenger.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقدموا بين يدي الله ورسوله واتقوا الله إن الله سميع عليم

translation: O you who believe! Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds should become worthless while you perceive not.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to be respectful and humble in the presence of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It cautions against raising one's voice above his or speaking loudly to him, as this could be seen as a sign of disrespect. The verse emphasizes that such behavior could render one's good deeds worthless, even if the person is unaware of it. The underlying message is to maintain a reverent and attentive attitude when interacting with the Prophet, out of recognition of his status and the importance of his teachings.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا ترفعوا أصواتكم فوق صوت النبي ولا تجهروا له بالقول كجهر بعضكم لبعض أن تحبط أعمالكم وأنتم لا تشعرون

translation: Indeed, those who lower their voices before the Messenger of Allah - they are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for righteousness. For them is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of showing respect and humility when interacting with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Those who speak softly and humbly in his presence are the ones whose hearts have been tested and purified by Allah. As a result, they are granted forgiveness and a great reward in the Hereafter. This teaches us that outward actions can reflect the state of one's inner spiritual condition, and that true faith is manifested through humble and respectful behavior towards Allah's chosen messengers.
orig: إن الذين يغضون أصواتهم عند رسول الله أولئك الذين امتحن الله قلوبهم للتقوى لهم مغفرة وأجر عظيم

translation: Indeed, those who call you, [O Muhammad], from behind the chambers - most of them do not use reason.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the companions of the Prophet Muhammad who would call out to him from outside his private quarters, without proper etiquette and consideration. It suggests that most of these people were lacking in understanding and wisdom, and did not fully comprehend the appropriate way to interact with the Prophet. The verse encourages people to exercise reason, patience and respect when communicating with religious leaders and authorities.
orig: إن الذين ينادونك من وراء الحجرات أكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And if they had been patient until you [could] come out to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages patience and restraint, even in the face of adversity. It suggests that had the people been more patient and waited for the Prophet (peace be upon him) to come out to them, it would have been better for them. The verse also emphasizes that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, indicating that those who exercise patience and restraint will be forgiven and shown mercy by Allah.
orig: ولو أنهم صبروا حتى تخرج إليهم لكان خيرا لهم والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to verify information, especially from questionable sources, before acting upon it. It cautions against hasty judgments or actions based on incomplete or unreliable information, which could lead to unintended harm and subsequent regret. The verse emphasizes the importance of diligence, caution, and seeking the truth in order to avoid making decisions that could negatively impact others.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن جاءكم فاسق بنبإ فتبينوا أن تصيبوا قوما بجهالة فتصبحوا على ما فعلتم نادمين

translation: And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty, but Allah has endeared to you the faith and has made it pleasing in your hearts and has made disbelief, defiance and disobedience hateful to you. Those are the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the wisdom behind it. Even though the Prophet could have easily complied with the wishes of his people, he remained steadfast in delivering the message of Islam as revealed to him by Allah. This is because Allah has made the faith dear to the hearts of the believers and has made disbelief, disobedience, and sinful acts displeasing to them. Those who follow this guidance are the ones who are rightly guided.
orig: واعلموا أن فيكم رسول الله لو يطيعكم في كثير من الأمر لعنتم ولكن الله حبب إليكم الإيمان وزينه في قلوبكم وكره إليكم الكفر والفسوق والعصيان أولئك هم الراشدون

translation: by the grace of Allah and His favor. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that any good that comes to a person is by the grace and favor of Allah, the All-Knowing and All-Wise. It reminds us that we should be grateful to Allah for His blessings and not attribute our success or good fortune to our own efforts alone. The verse also suggests that Allah's knowledge and wisdom are perfect, and that He bestows His grace and favor upon people according to His infinite wisdom.
orig: فضلا من الله ونعمة والله عليم حكيم

translation: And if two factions among the believers should fight, then make settlement between the two. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the ordinance of Allah. And if it returns, then make settlement between them in justice and act justly. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on how to resolve conflicts and disputes among believers. It emphasizes the importance of seeking reconciliation and making peace between disputing factions. However, if one side oppresses the other, then the believers are instructed to fight against the oppressors until they return to the command of Allah. Once the oppression has ceased, the believers should then make a just settlement between the parties and act with equity, as Allah loves those who are just and fair.
orig: وإن طائفتان من المؤمنين اقتتلوا فأصلحوا بينهما فإن بغت إحداهما على الأخرى فقاتلوا التي تبغي حتى تفيء إلى أمر الله فإن فاءت فأصلحوا بينهما بالعدل وأقسطوا إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: The believers are but brothers, so make settlement between your brothers. And fear Allah that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity and brotherhood among believers. It calls upon Muslims to resolve any conflicts or disputes between them, and to fear and be mindful of Allah, so that they may receive His mercy and blessings. The verse encourages Muslims to see each other as brothers, and to work towards reconciliation and harmony within the community.
orig: إنما المؤمنون إخوة فأصلحوا بين أخويكم واتقوا الله لعلكم ترحمون

translation: O you who believe! Let not a group scoff at another group, it may be that the latter are better than the former; nor let (some) women scoff at other women, it may be that the latter are better than the former. Nor defame one another, nor insult one another by nicknames. How bad is it to insult one's brother after having faith. And whosoever does not repent, then such are indeed the Zalimun (wrong-doers, etc.).
interpretation: This verse urges believers to avoid mocking, ridiculing or looking down on others, whether individuals or groups, as we cannot know who is truly better in the sight of God. It prohibits defamation, insults and the use of derogatory nicknames, as this is unbecoming of those who have faith. The verse emphasizes that such behavior is sinful and that those who do not repent are considered wrongdoers.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا يسخر قوم من قوم عسى أن يكونوا خيرا منهم ولا نساء من نساء عسى أن يكن خيرا منهن ولا تلمزوا أنفسكم ولا تنابزوا بالألقاب بئس الاسم الفسوق بعد الإيمان ومن لم يتب فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: O you who believe! Avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite each other. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah ; indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding negative assumptions, spying, and backbiting among believers. It warns against acting on unfounded suspicions, as some assumptions can be sinful. The verse also condemns the practice of backbiting, which is compared to the undesirable act of eating the flesh of a dead brother. The verse encourages believers to fear Allah and seek His forgiveness, as He is the One who accepts repentance and is Merciful.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم ولا تجسسوا ولا يغتب بعضكم بعضا أيحب أحدكم أن يأكل لحم أخيه ميتا فكرهتموه واتقوا الله إن الله تواب رحيم

translation: O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the common origin of all humanity, created from a male and a female, and the diversity of peoples and tribes as a means for mutual understanding and recognition. It stresses that the most noble and esteemed in the sight of God are not those of high social status or lineage, but rather the most righteous and God-fearing. This underscores the importance of virtue, piety and moral conduct over worldly distinctions, as God is all-knowing and fully aware of the true nature of each person.
orig: يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل لتعارفوا إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم إن الله عليم خبير

translation: The bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not [yet] believed; but say [instead], 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you from your deeds of anything. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse addresses the bedouins who claimed to have believed, but their faith had not yet fully entered their hearts. The verse emphasizes that true faith goes beyond just verbal proclamation, it requires a deep conviction that manifests in one's actions and obedience to Allah and His Messenger. The verse reassures that if they truly submit and obey, Allah will not diminish the reward for their good deeds, for He is Forgiving and Merciful towards those who sincerely believe and follow His commands.
orig: قالت الأعراب آمنا قل لم تؤمنوا ولكن قولوا أسلمنا ولما يدخل الإيمان في قلوبكم وإن تطيعوا الله ورسوله لا يلتكم من أعمالكم شيئا إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then doubt not, but strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is those who are the truthful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the true characteristics of believers. It states that the believers are those who have wholeheartedly accepted faith in Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad (peace be upon him), without any doubt or hesitation. Furthermore, they are willing to strive and make sacrifices, both with their wealth and their lives, in the cause of Allah. These are the people who are considered truthful and sincere in their faith.
orig: إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا وجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله أولئك هم الصادقون

translation: Say, "Do you [claim to] teach Allah about your religion, while Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the all-knowing Creator, and no one can teach Him about religion or faith. It serves as a reminder that we should not claim to have superior knowledge of the divine or try to instruct Allah, as He is the Omniscient One who knows everything in the heavens and the earth. Our role is to humbly submit to Allah's guidance and wisdom.
orig: قل أتعلمون الله بدينكم والله يعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: They consider it a favor to you that they have accepted Islam. Say, "Do not consider your Islam a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred favor upon you that He has guided you to the faith, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse addresses the attitude of some people who had recently converted to Islam and considered it a favor to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that they had accepted the faith.
