The verse instructs the Prophet to tell them that it is not they who have done him a favor by accepting Islam, but rather it is Allah who has guided them to the faith, and this is the true favor. The verse emphasizes that if their conversion to Islam was sincere, then the guidance they received from Allah is the true blessing, not their own act of accepting the faith.
orig: يمنون عليك أن أسلموا قل لا تمنوا علي إسلامكم بل الله يمن عليكم أن هداكم للإيمان إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Indeed, Allah knows the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has knowledge of all that is hidden and unseen in the heavens and the earth. He is all-knowing and aware of everything, including the thoughts, intentions and actions of all people. This serves as a reminder that we should be mindful of our conduct, as Allah is ever-watchful and will hold us accountable for our deeds.
orig: إن الله يعلم غيب السماوات والأرض والله بصير بما تعملون

translation: Qaaf. By the Glorious Qur'an (this is the oath of Allah).
interpretation: This verse begins with the letter 'Qaaf', which is one of the 'Muqatta'at' or 'Isolated Letters' found at the beginning of some Quranic chapters. The purpose of these letters is not entirely clear, but they are believed to be a part of the divine wisdom and mystery of the Quran. The verse then affirms the majesty and glory of the Quran, swearing by it as an oath. This emphasizes the importance and divine origin of the Quran, which is the word of Allah revealed to humanity through the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
orig: ق والقرآن المجيد

translation: But they wondered that there has come to them a warner from among themselves. And the disbelievers say, "This is an amazing thing."
interpretation: This verse expresses the reaction of the disbelievers to the coming of the Prophet Muhammad, who was one of their own people, as a warner to them. They were surprised and amazed that someone from among them would be chosen by God to convey the divine message, rather than someone from a foreign or higher social status. This verse highlights the human tendency to be skeptical of prophets and messengers who are from their own community, even when the message they bring is the truth from God.
orig: بل عجبوا أن جاءهم منذر منهم فقال الكافرون هذا شيء عجيب

translation: Is it when we have died and become dust, that is a distant return?
interpretation: This verse is posing a rhetorical question, challenging the idea that death and returning to dust is a distant or unlikely event. The implication is that resurrection and the return to the afterlife is a certainty, not something remote or impossible. The verse emphasizes the reality of death and the afterlife, refuting the notion that our existence ends with the physical body. The message is that we will indeed be resurrected and held accountable for our actions in this life.
orig: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا ذلك رجع بعيد

translation: We certainly know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserving record.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has complete knowledge of all that the earth consumes or takes away from people, whether it is their physical bodies after death or their deeds and actions. The "preserving record" refers to the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) in which Allah has recorded everything that has happened and will happen in the universe. This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and the fact that nothing escapes His knowledge and record.
orig: قد علمنا ما تنقص الأرض منهم وعندنا كتاب حفيظ

translation: But they have denied the truth when it has come to them, so they are in a confused condition.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people have rejected the truth (the message of the Qur'an) when it was brought to them. As a result, they are in a state of confusion and disarray, unable to comprehend the guidance that has been provided to them. The verse emphasizes the importance of accepting the truth and following the path of guidance, rather than rejecting it and falling into a state of uncertainty and disarray.
orig: بل كذبوا بالحق لما جاءهم فهم في أمر مريج

translation: Have they not looked at the sky above them - how We have structured it and adorned it, and [how] it has no rifts?
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the wonders of the universe and the signs of God's power and wisdom in the creation of the heavens. The emphasis is on the perfect and flawless structure of the sky, which has been beautifully adorned by God. This is meant to inspire awe and belief in the Oneness and Majesty of the Creator.
orig: أفلم ينظروا إلى السماء فوقهم كيف بنيناها وزيناها وما لها من فروج

translation: And the earth - We have spread it out and cast therein firmly set mountains and caused to grow therein [something] of every beautiful kind
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's creation of the earth and its diverse features. The "spreading out" of the earth refers to the expanse and vastness of the planet, while the "firmly set mountains" symbolize the stability and structure of the earth's surface. The verse also highlights the abundance and beauty of the natural world, with the growth of "every beautiful kind" of plant and life on the earth. This points to the richness and diversity of God's creation, which is a testament to His power, wisdom, and benevolence.
orig: والأرض مددناها وألقينا فيها رواسي وأنبتنا فيها من كل زوج بهيج

translation: A reminder and an admonition for every penitent servant
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the signs of Allah and to remember Him, as this will benefit those who turn back to Him in repentance. The "penitent servant" refers to those who sincerely seek forgiveness and strive to improve their relationship with Allah.
orig: تبصرة وذكرى لكل عبد منيب

translation: And We have sent down blessed water from the sky and made grow thereby gardens and grain from the harvest
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of water as a blessing from God that enables the growth of vegetation and crops. The "blessed water" refers to the rain that God sends down from the sky, which is essential for the development of gardens, orchards, and agricultural produce. The verse highlights God's provision and the role of water in sustaining life on Earth.
orig: ونزلنا من السماء ماء مباركا فأنبتنا به جنات وحب الحصيد

translation: And the date-palms having fruit-stalks piled one over another
interpretation: This verse describes the date-palms, which have tall, towering trunks and clusters of ripe, hanging dates. The imagery conveys the abundance and beauty of God's creation, reminding us of His power and the blessings He provides for humanity.
orig: والنخل باسقات لها طلع نضيد

translation: And We have sent down rain from the sky and given life thereby to a dead land. Thus will be the resurrection.
interpretation: This verse draws a parallel between the revival of a dead land through rain and the resurrection of the dead on the Day of Judgment. Just as a barren, lifeless land is revived and brought back to life through the descent of rain, so too will the dead be resurrected and brought back to life on the Day of Reckoning. This serves as a reminder of God's power and the certainty of the Hereafter, where all will be held accountable for their actions in this world.
orig: رزقا للعباد وأحيينا به بلدة ميتا كذلك الخروج

translation: The people of Noah and the companions of the Well and Thamud denied [the messengers] before them.
interpretation: This verse is referring to previous nations and peoples who rejected the message of the Prophets sent to them, such as the people of Prophet Noah, the companions of the Well (Al-Rass), and the people of Thamud. It serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, as they will face a similar fate as those who came before them.
orig: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح وأصحاب الرس وثمود

translation: And [We destroyed] 'Aad and Pharaoh and the brothers of Lot
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of several communities that rejected the message of God's prophets. 'Aad and Pharaoh represent the arrogant and oppressive societies that were destroyed for their disbelief and injustice. The "brothers of Lot" refer to the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, who were punished for their moral depravity and sexual perversions. The verse serves as a warning that those who defy God's commands and persist in their wrongdoing will face divine retribution.
orig: وعاد وفرعون وإخوان لوط

translation: And the companions of the thicket, and the people of Tubba’; every one of them denied the messengers, so My threat was justly fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse refers to various groups of people who rejected the messengers of God, including the companions of the thicket (a place in Arabia) and the people of Tubba’ (an ancient kingdom in Yemen). The verse emphasizes that each of these groups denied the messengers, and as a result, the divine punishment that was threatened against them was justly fulfilled. The interpretation highlights that rejecting the messengers of God has consequences, and those who do so will face the just consequences of their actions.
orig: وأصحاب الأيكة وقوم تبع كل كذب الرسل فحق وعيد

translation: Have We [not] exhausted [i.e., tired] by the first creation? But they are in confusion about a new creation.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers are confused and doubtful about the concept of resurrection and the afterlife. They find it hard to believe that after death, they will be created anew. The verse implies that the creation of the first life is not a difficult task for Allah, and that the creation of a new life in the afterlife is equally within His power. The verse encourages the believers to have faith in Allah's ability to bring about a new creation, despite the doubts and confusion of the disbelievers.
orig: أفعيينا بالخلق الأول بل هم في لبس من خلق جديد

translation: And We have certainly created man and know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer to him than [his] jugular vein.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's intimate knowledge and closeness to each human being. It suggests that God is aware of the innermost thoughts and inclinations of the human soul, and that His presence and guidance are closer to us than our own selves. The imagery of the jugular vein conveys the idea of God's all-encompassing awareness and nearness to the individual, reminding us that we can never escape His watchful eye and that we should strive to live in accordance with His will.
orig: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان ونعلم ما توسوس به نفسه ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد

translation: When the two receivers receive, one on the right and one on the left.
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who record the deeds of people. They are positioned on the right and left of each person, recording their actions, words, and thoughts. The verse emphasizes the constant observation and documentation of a person's behavior by these celestial witnesses, who will present the record of one's life on the Day of Judgment.
orig: إذ يتلقى المتلقيان عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد

translation: He utters not a word but there is a watcher by him, ready (to record it).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that every word a person speaks is recorded by a vigilant observer, implying that we are accountable for our speech and actions. It serves as a reminder to be mindful and cautious in our words, as they are documented and will be judged on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: ما يلفظ من قول إلا لديه رقيب عتيد

translation: And the intoxication of death will bring the truth; that is what you were trying to avoid.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the moment of death, when the veil of this world is lifted and the truth becomes clear. The "intoxication of death" is a metaphor for the profound experience of facing one's own mortality. At that moment, the person can no longer deny or avoid the reality of their situation, and they are confronted with the truth of their existence. This verse serves as a reminder that we cannot escape the ultimate truth, which is that we will all face death one day.
orig: وجاءت سكرة الموت بالحق ذلك ما كنت منه تحيد

translation: And the Trumpet will be blown. That is the Day of the [promised] Threat.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when the Trumpet will be blown to signal the end of the world and the beginning of the Hereafter. This day is described as the "Day of the [promised] Threat" because it is the day when all people will be held accountable for their actions in life and face the consequences, whether reward or punishment, as promised by Allah. This verse serves as a reminder to humanity to prepare for this momentous and inevitable event.
orig: ونفخ في الصور ذلك يوم الوعيد

translation: And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when every person will be held accountable for their actions. The "driver" represents the person's own conscience and deeds, which will compel them to face the consequences of their choices. The "witness" represents the angels or other evidence that will testify to the person's actions in life. This emphasizes the individual responsibility and accountability that each person will face on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: وجاءت كل نفس معها سائق وشهيد

translation: You had been in heedlessness of this, but We have removed from you your cover, so your sight, this Day, is sharp.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the person had been unaware or heedless of the truth, but God has now removed the veil or cover from their eyes, enabling them to see clearly and perceive the reality. The sharpness of their sight on this Day implies a newfound clarity and understanding, which allows them to grasp the truth that was previously hidden from them.
orig: لقد كنت في غفلة من هذا فكشفنا عنك غطاءك فبصرك اليوم حديد

translation: And his companion will say, "This [record] is what is present with me."
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when a person's companion (i.e., their guardian angel) will present the record of their deeds. The interpretation suggests that on that day, the person's own actions and choices will be held accountable, as the record kept by the companion angel will be a testament to their life and the choices they made.
orig: وقال قرينه هذا ما لدي عتيد

translation: Cast into Hell every obstinate disbeliever
interpretation: This verse is a command to cast every stubborn and persistent disbeliever into the hellfire. It emphasizes the fate that awaits those who stubbornly reject faith and refuse to submit to the will of God. The interpretation suggests that those who adamantly reject the truth and persist in their disbelief will be condemned to the eternal punishment of Hell.
orig: ألقيا في جهنم كل كفار عنيد

translation: Hinderer of good, aggressor, doubter
interpretation: This verse describes a person who is an obstacle to good deeds, who acts aggressively and arrogantly, and who is suspicious and doubtful. The interpretation suggests that this person is someone who hinders the progress and well-being of others, acts in a hostile manner, and is not to be trusted due to their suspicious nature.
orig: مناع للخير معتد مريب

translation: The one who takes with Allah another deity - so [both of] you cast him into the severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of associating other deities with Allah, the One true God. It warns that those who do so will face severe punishment. The interpretation is that true faith and worship should be directed solely towards Allah, without any partners or intermediaries. Associating others with Allah is a grave sin that leads to eternal damnation.
orig: الذي جعل مع الله إلها آخر فألقياه في العذاب الشديد

translation: His companion will say, "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, but he [himself] was in extreme error."
interpretation: This verse describes a scenario on the Day of Judgment, where a person's close companion (such as a friend, family member, or leader) will try to absolve themselves of responsibility for the other person's misguided actions. The companion will claim that they did not compel the other person to go astray, but that the other person was already in a state of profound misguidance. This highlights the individual accountability for one's own choices and actions, even if influenced by others.
orig: قال قرينه ربنا ما أطغيته ولكن كان في ضلال بعيد

translation: He said: 'Do not dispute with Me while I had already presented to you [the evidence] with the threat.'
interpretation: This verse is referring to a dialogue between God and the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. God is reminding them that He had already warned them about the consequences of their disbelief and disobedience, so they have no excuse to argue or dispute with Him on that day. The interpretation is that God's warnings and threats to the disbelievers should be taken seriously, as they will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: قال لا تختصموا لدي وقد قدمت إليكم بالوعيد

translation: The word is not changed with Me, and I am not unjust to the servants.
interpretation: This verse conveys that Allah's decree and judgement are immutable and cannot be changed. He is just and fair in His dealings with His servants, and does not wrong them in any way.
orig: ما يبدل القول لدي وما أنا بظلام للعبيد

translation: The Day when We will say to Hell, "Have you been filled?" and it will say, "Are there some more?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the punishment of Hell will be fully realized. The verse suggests that Hell will be so vast and its capacity so immense that even after being filled with the souls of the wicked, it will still have the capacity to hold more. This emphasizes the severity and vastness of the punishment awaiting the unbelievers on that Day, and the insatiable nature of Hell.
orig: يوم نقول لجهنم هل امتلأت وتقول هل من مزيد

translation: And the Garden will be brought near to the righteous, not far.
interpretation: This verse conveys that on the Day of Judgment, the Garden (Paradise) will be brought close to the righteous, those who feared and obeyed Allah. It suggests that the reward of Paradise will be easily accessible and not distant for the God-fearing believers, as a result of their righteous deeds and devotion to Allah in this life.
orig: وأزلفت الجنة للمتقين غير بعيد

translation: This is what you are promised for every penitent and observant [servant].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the promise of reward and punishment in the Hereafter. It is addressed to those who are 'awwab' (penitent, constantly turning to Allah in repentance) and 'hafidh' (observant, guarding their deeds and faith). The verse suggests that the promise of Paradise is for those who continuously seek forgiveness and strive to obey Allah's commands.
orig: هذا ما توعدون لكل أواب حفيظ

translation: Whoever fears the Most Merciful in the unseen and comes with a repentant heart,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fearing and revering Allah, the Most Merciful, even in the unseen or private realm of one's thoughts and actions. The one who comes to Allah with a repentant, humble, and sincere heart is praised, as this demonstrates a deep spiritual connection and a desire to seek forgiveness and guidance from the Almighty.
orig: من خشي الرحمن بالغيب وجاء بقلب منيب

translation: Enter it in peace. This is the Day of Eternity.
interpretation: This verse is a command to enter Paradise in a state of peace and tranquility. It emphasizes that the Day of Resurrection is a day of eternal life, where the righteous will be rewarded with the bliss of Paradise. The interpretation suggests that those who live a righteous life and believe in God will be granted eternal life in the Hereafter, where they will experience a state of complete peace and serenity.
orig: ادخلوها بسلام ذلك يوم الخلود

translation: For them is whatever they wish therein, and with Us is more.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the believers in the Hereafter will have all that they desire, and that Allah has even more rewards and blessings in store for them beyond what they can imagine. It emphasizes the abundance and generosity of Allah's provision for the righteous in the afterlife.
orig: لهم ما يشاءون فيها ولدينا مزيد

translation: And how many a generation have We destroyed before them who were greater than them in [striking] power and had explored throughout the lands. Is there any place of escape?
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of previous civilizations that were more powerful and advanced than the people of the Prophet's time, yet they were destroyed due to their disbelief and wrongdoing. The verse suggests that no one can escape the consequences of their actions, and that the people should learn from the lessons of history. It encourages reflection on the transient nature of worldly power and the importance of faith and righteous conduct.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أشد منهم بطشا فنقبوا في البلاد هل من محيص

translation: Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or who listens while he is present [with an attentive heart].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having a receptive and attentive heart when reflecting on the signs and wonders of God's creation. It suggests that those who possess a heart, meaning an intellect and spiritual awareness, or who listen with an open and present mind, will find guidance and reminders in the various manifestations of God's power and wisdom. The verse encourages people to be mindful and engaged, rather than heedless, when contemplating the divine signs around them.
orig: إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب أو ألقى السمع وهو شهيد

translation: And indeed, We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six [creative] days, and there touched Us not any fatigue.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God created the heavens, the earth, and all that is between them in six days, and that this creative process did not cause any tiredness or fatigue to God. This highlights the ease and effortlessness with which God brings about the creation, as He is all-powerful and not limited by physical constraints. The verse serves to reinforce the belief that God is the sole Creator, who has complete control and sovereignty over the universe.
orig: ولقد خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام وما مسنا من لغوب

translation: So be patient over what they say and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to be patient and steadfast in the face of the criticism and opposition he faced from his people. It instructs him to glorify and praise Allah before the rising and setting of the sun, which represents the beginning and end of the day. This is a call to maintain a constant state of remembrance and worship of Allah, regardless of the circumstances. The interpretation suggests that true patience and steadfastness in the face of adversity can only be achieved through a strong connection with the divine and a commitment to worshipping and praising Allah at all times.
orig: فاصبر على ما يقولون وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل الغروب

translation: And from the night, glorify Him and after the prostrations.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to engage in remembrance and glorification of God during the night, even after completing the obligatory prayers and prostrations. It suggests that one should not limit their worship to the prescribed prayers, but continue to engage in additional acts of devotion and remembrance of God throughout the night.
orig: ومن الليل فسبحه وأدبار السجود

translation: And listen on the Day when the Caller will call from a place that is near.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when a caller will summon all of humanity to account for their deeds. The emphasis on the caller being "from a place that is near" suggests that the reckoning will be immediate and inescapable, as God is always close and aware of our actions.
orig: واستمع يوم يناد المناد من مكان قريب

translation: The Day they hear the Blast [of the Horn] in truth. That is the Day of Emergence [from the graves].
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when all people will hear the Blast of the Trumpet, signaling the end of this world and the beginning of the Hereafter. On that Day, the truth will be revealed, and people will emerge from their graves to be held accountable for their deeds in life. The interpretation emphasizes the certainty and finality of this event, which will mark the transition from the temporal world to the eternal afterlife.
orig: يوم يسمعون الصيحة بالحق ذلك يوم الخروج

translation: Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah alone has the power to give life and cause death. All creation and all affairs ultimately return to Him. This emphasizes the sovereignty of Allah and the need for humans to submit to Him, as He is the source of all life and the final destination for all.
orig: إنا نحن نحيي ونميت وإلينا المصير

translation: The Day the earth will split open for them [emerging], hastening forth. That is a gathering [of creation] upon Us, [which is] easy.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Resurrection, when the earth will split open and people will emerge from their graves hastily to be gathered for judgment before God. This event, though momentous, is described as being easy for God to orchestrate, as He is all-powerful and in complete control of the universe and the afterlife.
orig: يوم تشقق الأرض عنهم سراعا ذلك حشر علينا يسير

translation: We are most knowing of what they say, and you are not over them a tyrant, so remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My threat.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah knows best what people say and think, and that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not a dictator over them, but rather a reminder for those who fear Allah's punishment. The verse encourages the Prophet to continue reminding people through the Qur'an, as it is a means of guidance for those who are mindful of Allah's warnings.
orig: نحن أعلم بما يقولون وما أنت عليهم بجبار فذكر بالقرآن من يخاف وعيد

translation: By the wind that scatters
interpretation: This verse is referring to the wind that scatters and disperses things. It is often interpreted as a metaphor for the spreading of knowledge, the dissemination of the message of Islam, or the transient nature of worldly possessions and attachments. The implication is that one should not cling too tightly to the material world, but should focus on the eternal and spiritual aspects of life.
orig: والذاريات ذروا

translation: And [by] the [pregnant] ones who bear [a burden]
interpretation: This verse refers to pregnant women who bear the burden of carrying a child within them. The interpretation is that Allah is swearing by the pregnant women as a sign of His power and the miracle of life. The bearing of a child is a profound and sacred process, and the Qur'an emphasizes the importance and dignity of this role.
orig: فالحاملات وقرا

translation: And [by] the racers, panting
interpretation: This verse refers to the swift and powerful movement of forces or events, which may be interpreted as the rapid progress of the divine plan or the unstoppable march of justice and truth. The "racers" could symbolize the angels, the forces of nature, or the unfolding of historical events that are driven by the will of God. The "panting" suggests the intensity and urgency of these forces, emphasizing the relentless and inescapable nature of the divine decree.
orig: فالجاريات يسرا

translation: And [by] those who divide [their command] with determination
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who are responsible for carrying out Allah's commands with precision and determination. The interpretation suggests that the angels carry out their duties with unwavering commitment, ensuring that Allah's will is executed with utmost care and efficiency.
orig: فالمقسمات أمرا

translation: Indeed, that which you are promised is true
interpretation: This verse affirms that the promises and warnings made in the Qur'an are true and will certainly come to pass. It is a reassurance to the believers that the Day of Judgment and the rewards or punishments they will receive are not mere fabrications, but a reality that they will face. The verse emphasizes the truthfulness of God's word and the certainty of the events that are to come.
orig: إنما توعدون لصادق

translation: And indeed, the religion is true and established.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the religion of Islam is the true and established religion. It is a declaration of the certainty and validity of the Islamic faith. The verse emphasizes that the principles and teachings of Islam are not mere beliefs or opinions, but rather a true and established way of life that has been revealed by God. This verse serves to strengthen the faith of the believers and reassure them that they are following the right path.
orig: وإن الدين لواقع

translation: And the heaven with its complex formation
interpretation: This verse is referring to the intricate and complex structure of the heavens, which is a testament to the power and wisdom of the Creator. The heavens, with their celestial bodies, orbits, and intricate systems, demonstrate the extraordinary design and engineering behind the creation of the universe. This serves as a reminder of the greatness of God and the need for mankind to reflect on the signs of His existence and power in the world around us.
orig: والسماء ذات الحبك

translation: Indeed, you are in a conflicting speech.
interpretation: This verse indicates that people are often divided in their opinions and beliefs, leading to disagreements and conflicts. It suggests that individuals should strive to find common ground and seek to understand different perspectives, rather than engaging in divisive rhetoric or behavior.
orig: إنكم لفي قول مختلف

translation: He is averted from it who is (himself) averse.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who turn away from the truth or are averse to it will be led astray. The implication is that those who are open-minded and willing to consider the message of the Qur'an are more likely to accept it, while those who are closed-off or resistant will be turned away from it.
orig: يؤفك عنه من أفك

translation: The liars have been killed
interpretation: This verse condemns those who spread false information and lies. It suggests that those who engage in deception and falsehood will face consequences for their actions. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of honesty, truthfulness and accountability in Islamic teachings.
orig: قتل الخراصون

translation: Those who are in [a state of] heedlessness
interpretation: This verse refers to those people who are neglectful, indifferent, or unaware of their spiritual responsibilities and the realities of the afterlife. They are engrossed in the distractions and pleasures of the material world, and have become heedless of the remembrance of God and the preparation for the Hereafter. The Qur'an encourages believers to be mindful, alert, and actively engaged in seeking guidance and doing good deeds, rather than being in a state of spiritual negligence.
orig: الذين هم في غمرة ساهون

translation: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival?
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions. The question "when is its arrival?" suggests that people are eager to know the exact timing of this momentous event, even though the Qur'an emphasizes that only God has knowledge of the Hour. The interpretation encourages believers to focus on preparing for the Day of Judgment, rather than obsessing over its timing, which is known only to God.
orig: يسألون أيان يوم الدين

translation: The day they will be tormented over the Fire
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers and wrongdoers will be subjected to the torment of the Fire. It suggests that they will be tested and tried on that day, facing the consequences of their misdeeds in this life. The interpretation is that this verse serves as a warning to mankind to repent and do good deeds, lest they face the punishment of the Hellfire on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: يوم هم على النار يفتنون

translation: Taste your trial. This is what you were impatient for.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who have been demanding or rushing towards a punishment or trial, as if they are eager for it to happen. The verse tells them to "taste" or experience the trial that they have been hastily anticipating, as a consequence of their actions or behavior. The message is that they should not be hasty in wishing for punishment, as they will ultimately have to face the consequences of their own deeds.
orig: ذوقوا فتنتكم هذا الذي كنتم به تستعجلون

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are righteous and God-fearing will be rewarded with eternal bliss in the Hereafter. The "gardens and springs" symbolize the lush, abundant, and serene environment that the righteous will enjoy in Paradise. This verse conveys the message that if one leads a life of piety, devotion, and obedience to God, they will be granted the ultimate reward of eternal peace and happiness in the Afterlife.
orig: إن المتقين في جنات وعيون

translation: Taking what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous believers who have been granted blessings and rewards from their Lord. They were previously known for their good deeds and righteous conduct, and now they are receiving the fruits of their piety and obedience to Allah. The verse emphasizes that the rewards they receive are a result of their own efforts and God's grace, not something they are entitled to by default. It serves as a reminder that doing good and pleasing Allah should be the ultimate goal for believers, as it leads to the attainment of blessings in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: آخذين ما آتاهم ربهم إنهم كانوا قبل ذلك محسنين

translation: They were but little of the night they slept.
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous people who would spend a significant portion of the night in worship, prayer, and reflection, leaving little time for sleep. The verse highlights their devotion and dedication to their faith, as they prioritized spiritual nourishment over physical rest. This exemplifies the importance of seeking closeness to Allah and the willingness to make sacrifices for the sake of one's spiritual growth.
orig: كانوا قليلا من الليل ما يهجعون

translation: And in the hours before dawn, they would ask forgiveness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness from God during the early morning hours, a time often associated with spiritual reflection and closeness to the divine. The act of asking for forgiveness at this time suggests a sincere desire to purify one’s soul and seek guidance from the Almighty. This practice is encouraged in Islam as it allows individuals to start their day with a renewed sense of purpose and a cleansed heart, ready to face the challenges and temptations of the day ahead.
orig: وبالأسحار هم يستغفرون

translation: And in their wealth there is a known right for the beggar and the deprived
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to set aside a portion of their wealth for the benefit of those in need, such as the beggar and the deprived. It establishes a moral and religious obligation to share one's resources with the less fortunate members of society. This encourages a spirit of compassion, generosity, and social responsibility within the Muslim community.
orig: وفي أموالهم حق للسائل والمحروم

translation: And in the earth are signs for those who are certain [in faith]
interpretation: This verse points to the various signs and wonders in the earth that serve as evidence of God's power, wisdom and divine creation. For those who have firm belief and conviction in the oneness of God, these natural phenomena are a testament to the existence and attributes of the Creator. The verse encourages reflection and contemplation on the marvels of the earth, which can strengthen one's faith and certainty in the divine.
orig: وفي الأرض آيات للموقنين

translation: And within yourselves; then will you not see?
interpretation: This verse encourages self-reflection and introspection. It suggests that the signs of God's power and wisdom are evident within the human being itself, if only one would pause to observe and ponder. The verse invites the reader to look inward, to contemplate the complexities and marvels of the human body and mind, and to recognize the divine hand behind their creation. By reflecting on the self, one can gain a deeper understanding of the Creator and the purpose of existence.
orig: وفي أنفسكم أفلا تبصرون

translation: And in the heaven is your provision and [that] which you are promised.
interpretation: This verse refers to the blessings and sustenance that Allah provides for His creation, both in the physical world and in the hereafter. The "heaven" here represents the higher realm, where Allah resides and where the ultimate rewards and promises for the believers will be fulfilled. The verse emphasizes that the true and lasting provisions, both material and spiritual, come from Allah, and that the believers should have faith in the promises of the Hereafter.
orig: وفي السماء رزقكم وما توعدون

translation: So by the Lord of the heaven and earth, indeed it is truth - just as [sure as] it is that you are speaking.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the truthfulness and certainty of the Quranic message. By swearing by the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the verse establishes that the message being conveyed is an absolute truth, just as certain as the fact that the listeners are speaking. This serves to strengthen the faith and conviction of the believers, and to challenge the disbelievers to accept the truth of what is being said.
orig: فورب السماء والأرض إنه لحق مثل ما أنكم تنطقون

translation: Has the story of the honored guests of Abraham reached you?
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Abraham (peace be upon him) being visited by angels who brought him the good news of a son, despite his old age. The verse is asking if the listener has heard this important story from the Quran, which highlights Abraham's hospitality, faith, and the power of God to grant him a child in his old age. The interpretation is that this story serves as an example of God's mercy, the importance of hospitality, and the need to have faith in God's plan, even when it may seem impossible.
orig: هل أتاك حديث ضيف إبراهيم المكرمين

translation: When they entered upon him and said, "Peace." [Abraham] said, "Peace, [you are] a people unknown."
interpretation: This verse describes a scene where some visitors come to Prophet Abraham and greet him with the salutation of "Peace." Abraham responds by saying "Peace, [you are] a people unknown." This suggests that Abraham did not immediately recognize these visitors, and was cautious in his response, perhaps because he was unsure of their intentions or identity. The verse highlights Abraham's wisdom and discernment in dealing with strangers, and his ability to respond appropriately even in uncertain situations.
orig: إذ دخلوا عليه فقالوا سلاما قال سلام قوم منكرون

translation: So he went to his family and came with a fat [roasted] calf
interpretation: This verse describes the hospitality and generosity of the prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) when he received guests. Upon seeing the visitors, he quickly went to his family and brought them a delicious, fat calf to serve as a meal, demonstrating the importance of welcoming and providing for one's guests in Islamic teachings.
orig: فراغ إلى أهله فجاء بعجل سمين

translation: Then he presented it to them and said, "Will you not eat?"
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) offered his guests a meal, and encouraged them to partake of it. The invitation to eat serves as a sign of hospitality and a means of building rapport with the guests. The interpretation is that we should be generous and welcoming towards others, and provide for their needs, as this is a praiseworthy quality in the sight of God.
orig: فقربه إليهم قال ألا تأكلون

translation: But he felt apprehension toward them. They said, "Fear not," and gave him good tidings of a learned child.
interpretation: This verse describes the angels' visit to the Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) to inform him of the impending birth of his son Isaac. Initially, Abraham felt some apprehension towards the visitors, but the angels reassured him and gave him the good news of a son who would be knowledgeable and wise. This verse highlights the importance of trust and faith in God, even when faced with uncertainty or fear. It teaches us to have confidence in God's plan and to receive His blessings with gratitude.
orig: فأوجس منهم خيفة قالوا لا تخف وبشروه بغلام عليم

translation: Then his wife came forward with a cry of alarm. She smote her face and said, "[I am but] an old, barren woman!"
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the wife of the Prophet Abraham upon being told that she would give birth to a son, despite her advanced age and being barren. Her initial reaction was one of disbelief and alarm, expressed through her cry, striking her face, and declaring herself to be an "old, barren woman". This highlights the miraculous nature of the announcement, which went against the natural order of things. The verse conveys the human element of the story, where even the pious can initially struggle to accept God's plan, but ultimately submit to it.
orig: فأقبلت امرأته في صرة فصكت وجهها وقالت عجوز عقيم

translation: They said, "Thus has your Lord said, 'It is He who is the Wise, the Knowing.'"
interpretation: This verse is referring to a dialogue between the Prophet Muhammad and the disbelievers. The disbelievers are conveying that God, the Lord of Muhammad, has declared that He is the Wise and the Knowing. This emphasizes that God's knowledge and wisdom are absolute, and that He is the ultimate authority who determines what is true and just. The verse reinforces the concept of God's omniscience and omnipotence, and that He alone possesses the perfect knowledge and wisdom to guide humanity.
orig: قالوا كذلك قال ربك إنه هو الحكيم العليم

translation: He said, "What is your mission, O messengers?"
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) and the angels who were sent to him. Ibrahim asks the angels about their purpose, indicating his curiosity and desire to understand their mission. This verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding, even from those who are sent by God. The interpretation suggests that we should approach religious teachings and messages with an open and inquisitive mind, seeking to comprehend the deeper meaning and purpose behind them.
orig: قال فما خطبكم أيها المرسلون

translation: They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a people of criminals."
interpretation: This verse refers to the messengers of God who were sent to warn and guide people, but were met with rejection and hostility from the wrongdoers. The messengers acknowledge that they were sent to a community of sinners, who refused to heed the divine message. This highlights the challenge faced by the prophets in conveying the truth to those who are steeped in corruption and evil deeds.
orig: قالوا إنا أرسلنا إلى قوم مجرمين

translation: We will send down upon them stones from clay.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has the power to punish those who reject His guidance and disobey His commands. The reference to "stones from clay" may symbolize a severe and unforgiving form of punishment, as clay stones can be harsh and unyielding. The interpretation is that Allah has the ability to deliver a decisive and uncompromising retribution against those who turn away from the truth and refuse to heed His warnings.
orig: لنرسل عليهم حجارة من طين

translation: Decreed by your Lord, [and forbidden] to them, are the excessively prideful.
interpretation: This verse is warning against the sin of arrogance and excessive pride. It indicates that Allah has decreed and forbidden such behavior, as it is displeasing to Him. The interpretation is that those who are excessively proud and arrogant will be held accountable for their actions before Allah.
orig: مسومة عند ربك للمسرفين

translation: And We extracted whoever was in it [i.e., the city] of the believers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of a city that had disbelievers, but the believers were saved and extracted from it. The interpretation is that God protects the faithful and rescues them from the consequences of the wrongdoings of the disbelievers in a community. This is a testament to God's mercy and justice, as He does not punish the righteous along with the wicked.
orig: فأخرجنا من كان فيها من المؤمنين

translation: But we found not therein any except a [single] house of [the] Muslims.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Abraham and his son Ishmael, who were sent by God to establish a sanctuary in the barren valley of Mecca. When they arrived, they found no one living there except a single household of believers. This verse highlights the significance of this sacred place, which was destined to become the center of Islamic faith and worship.
orig: فما وجدنا فيها غير بيت من المسلمين

translation: And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse refers to a remnant or trace that was left behind in a specific place as a sign or reminder for those who fear the severe punishment of Allah. The interpretation suggests that the remnant serves as an admonition and warning to those who are mindful of the consequences of their actions and the impending punishment they may face if they do not heed the message.
orig: وتركنا فيها آية للذين يخافون العذاب الأليم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We sent Moses to Pharaoh with clear authority.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Moses (peace be upon him) being sent by Allah to confront the tyrannical Pharaoh. The phrase "with clear authority" indicates that Moses was empowered with miracles and divine signs that demonstrated the truth of his message and the falsehood of Pharaoh's claims. This verse sets the stage for the confrontation between Moses and Pharaoh, which ultimately led to the liberation of the Israelites from Pharaoh's oppression.
orig: وفي موسى إذ أرسلناه إلى فرعون بسلطان مبين

translation: So he turned away from them and was amazed. And he said, "A magician or a madman."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers to the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They dismissed him as either a magician or a madman, unable to comprehend the profound truth of the Qur'anic revelation. This reflects the arrogance and closed-mindedness of those who refuse to acknowledge the divine origin of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him).
orig: فتولى بركنه وقال ساحر أو مجنون

translation: And We took him and his soldiers and cast them into the sea, and he was blameworthy.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of Pharaoh and his army being drowned in the sea after pursuing the Israelites. The interpretation is that Pharaoh and his soldiers were punished by Allah for their arrogance, oppression, and rejection of the message of Prophet Moses. The verse emphasizes that Pharaoh was "blameworthy" or deserving of blame for his actions, highlighting the divine justice and retribution that befell him.
orig: فأخذناه وجنوده فنبذناهم في اليم وهو مليم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], the [people of] 'Aad, when We sent against them the barren wind
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of 'Aad, an ancient Arab tribe that lived in the southern part of the Arabian Peninsula. The Qur'an mentions that Allah sent a "barren wind" against them, which is interpreted as a severe and destructive wind that destroyed their homes and crops, leading to their demise. This serves as a lesson and warning to those who reject the message of Allah and refuse to believe in His oneness and authority.
orig: وفي عاد إذ أرسلنا عليهم الريح العقيم

translation: It leaves nothing it comes upon but it makes it like crushed bones.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Day of Judgment will be a time of complete destruction, where everything that exists will be reduced to a state of complete ruin and desolation, like crushed bones. It highlights the absolute power and authority of God, who can effortlessly annihilate all that He has created. This serves as a reminder to humanity of the transience of the material world and the importance of preparing for the Hereafter.
orig: ما تذر من شيء أتت عليه إلا جعلته كالرميم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when it was said to the Thamud, "Enjoy yourselves for a time."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people of Thamud, an ancient Arabian tribe who were destroyed for their rejection of the message of the prophet Salih. The verse indicates that they were given a period of respite and enjoyment before the punishment that befell them. The interpretation is that even those who reject the truth are sometimes given a chance to reform, but if they persist in their disbelief and wrongdoing, they will ultimately face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وفي ثمود إذ قيل لهم تمتعوا حتى حين

translation: But they insolently defied the command of their Lord, so the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking on.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who defiantly reject the commands of God. Despite being warned, they persisted in their arrogance and disbelief, and were ultimately struck down by a devastating punishment as a consequence of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who would similarly defy the will of the Almighty.
orig: فعتوا عن أمر ربهم فأخذتهم الصاعقة وهم ينظرون

translation: But they were not able to rise up, nor could they find help.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who opposed the truth and the message of the Qur'an were unable to stand firm against it, nor could they find any support or assistance to prevail over it. It implies that the truth and the divine message are ultimately victorious, and those who reject it are ultimately powerless and unable to overcome it.
orig: فما استطاعوا من قيام وما كانوا منتصرين

translation: And the people of Noah before them - indeed, they were a people defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disobedience and sinfulness of the people of Prophet Noah. They had rejected the message of monotheism and the call to worship only Allah, instead persisting in their transgressions and disbelief. This serves as a warning to those who turn away from the guidance of the Qur'an and the teachings of the prophets, and a reminder that such defiant disobedience will lead to severe consequences.
orig: وقوم نوح من قبل إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander.
interpretation: This verse speaks of God's power and ability to create the vast and expansive universe. The phrase "We constructed with strength" suggests that the creation of the heavens was an act of great might and power. The subsequent phrase "We are [its] expander" implies that God continues to expand and sustain the universe, demonstrating His limitless capacity and control over all of creation.
orig: والسماء بنيناها بأيد وإنا لموسعون

translation: And the earth - We have spread it out and excellent are the [capable] Disposers [of it].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's creation of the earth and its suitability for human habitation. The earth has been "spread out" or made spacious and hospitable, and those who manage and care for it are praised as "excellent disposers". This suggests the importance of wise stewardship of the earth's resources and environment.
orig: والأرض فرشناها فنعم الماهدون

translation: And of all things We have created pairs; that you may remember [the Creator].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of duality and complementarity in the creation of all things. It suggests that the Creator has designed the universe with pairs, such as male and female, light and dark, good and evil, etc. This diversity and balance in creation is a sign for people to reflect on the wisdom and power of the Creator, and to remember Him and His guidance.
orig: ومن كل شيء خلقنا زوجين لعلكم تذكرون

translation: So flee to Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse calls upon people to turn to Allah and seek refuge in Him, as the Prophet is a clear warner from Allah to guide them towards the right path and save them from the punishment of the Hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's protection and guidance, and heeding the warnings conveyed by the Prophet.
orig: ففروا إلى الله إني لكم منه نذير مبين

translation: And do not make with Allah another deity. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the belief in the Oneness of God (Tawheed), and warns against associating any other deity with Allah. It is a clear message that Allah is the only true God, and that the Prophet is sent as a warner to convey this message to the people. The interpretation is that one should worship and submit to Allah alone, and not associate any partners with Him.
orig: ولا تجعلوا مع الله إلها آخر إني لكم منه نذير مبين

translation: And similarly, no messenger came to those before them but they said, "A magician or a madman."
interpretation: This verse draws a parallel between the response of previous communities to their prophets and the response of the people of Mecca to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Just as the previous prophets were accused of being magicians or madmen, the people of Mecca also dismissed the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in a similar manner. This highlights the consistent pattern of rejection and hostility that prophets have faced throughout history when delivering the divine message. The verse serves as a reminder that the rejection of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not unique, but rather a continuation of a long-standing pattern of opposition to the messengers of God.
orig: كذلك ما أتى الذين من قبلهم من رسول إلا قالوا ساحر أو مجنون

translation: Do they enjoin upon people righteousness while they themselves neglect it and they recite the Scripture? Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who claim to be righteous and preach to others, but do not practice what they preach. They recite the Scriptures but fail to implement its teachings in their own lives. The verse is calling upon people to reflect on the hypocrisy of such individuals and to not be misled by their outward display of piety.
orig: أتواصوا به بل هم قوم طاغون

translation: So turn away from them, for you are not to be blamed.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to turn away from those who reject his message, as he is not to be blamed for their rejection. It suggests that the responsibility for accepting or rejecting the message lies with the people themselves, and the Prophet should not be held accountable for their choices. The verse emphasizes the importance of delivering the message and leaving the outcome to God.
orig: فتول عنهم فما أنت بملوم

translation: And remind, for indeed, the reminder benefits the believers.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to constantly remind themselves and others of the teachings of Islam. The reminder, or the act of recalling and reflecting on the divine guidance, can have a positive impact on the faith and actions of the believers. It serves to strengthen their conviction, guide their conduct, and keep them steadfast on the path of righteousness.
orig: وذكر فإن الذكرى تنفع المؤمنين

translation: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the primary purpose of the creation of jinn and humans is to worship and serve God. It suggests that the ultimate goal of human existence is to acknowledge the oneness of God, submit to His will, and dedicate one's life to pleasing Him through righteous deeds and devotion. The verse underscores the importance of worshiping God as the sole purpose of our creation, and that true fulfillment and success can only be achieved through this divine purpose.
orig: وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون

translation: I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Almighty, is self-sufficient and does not need any provision or sustenance from His creation. He is the Provider, and it is He who sustains all beings. This verse serves to remind us that our worship and obedience to Allah should not be motivated by the desire for material gain or worldly benefits, but rather by our sincere devotion and recognition of His Lordship and Divinity.
orig: ما أريد منهم من رزق وما أريد أن يطعمون

translation: Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of Strength, the Firm.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the sole provider of sustenance and resources for all of His creation. He has the power and ability to provide for all beings, and His provision is firm, steadfast and unshakable. It reminds us to rely on Allah alone for our needs and to have unwavering faith in His ability to care for us.
orig: إن الله هو الرزاق ذو القوة المتين

translation: And for those who have wronged, there will be a punishment like the punishment of those before them, so they should not impatiently urge [you].
interpretation: This verse warns those who have wronged and committed sins that they will face a punishment similar to the punishment that befell those who came before them. It cautions them not to be impatient or hasty in demanding the punishment, as Allah's justice will prevail in due time. The verse emphasizes that the wrongdoers should not rush the consequences of their actions, but rather reflect on their misdeeds and seek forgiveness and repentance.
orig: فإن للذين ظلموا ذنوبا مثل ذنوب أصحابهم فلا يستعجلون

translation: Then woe to those who disbelieve from their Day which they are promised.
interpretation: This verse warns those who disbelieve in God and reject the message of Islam. It foretells a day of reckoning and punishment that awaits them, a day they have been promised. The term "woe" conveys a sense of severe punishment and torment that will befall the disbelievers on that fateful day when they are held accountable for their rejection of faith and misdeeds.
orig: فويل للذين كفروا من يومهم الذي يوعدون

translation: And the mount [of Sinai]
interpretation: This verse refers to the mount of Sinai, where Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) received the Revelation from Allah. It signifies the importance and sanctity of this place, which holds a significant position in the history of divine guidance and the relationship between Allah and His servants.
orig: والطور

translation: And a Book inscribed
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an, the revealed scripture of Islam. The Qur'an is described as a "Book inscribed" to emphasize its divine origin and the permanence of its message. The Qur'an is a book that has been preserved and recorded, serving as a guide and source of wisdom for humanity.
orig: وكتاب مسطور

translation: In a written record
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Qur'an is a divine record, preserved and passed down through writing. It emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a written text that contains the revealed word of God, which is to be studied, preserved, and passed on to future generations.
orig: في رق منشور

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], the Grand House [i.e., the Kaaba]
interpretation: This verse refers to the Kaaba, the sacred house of worship in Mecca. The Kaaba is known as the "Grand House" and is the focal point of Islamic worship, as Muslims face the direction of the Kaaba during their daily prayers. This verse emphasizes the importance and sanctity of this holy site, which serves as a symbol of the unity of the Muslim community and the centrality of their faith.
orig: والبيت المعمور

translation: And the lofty ceiling [of the heavens]
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of the heavens, which are raised high above the earth. It is a reminder of Allah's power and the grandeur of His creation. The interpretation suggests that the elevated and expansive nature of the heavens is a sign of Allah's might and the vastness of His dominion.
orig: والسقف المرفوع

translation: And the sea filled (or kindled)
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the seas will be set ablaze or boiling over. It signifies the dramatic and cataclysmic changes that will take place in the universe as part of the end times. The "sea filled (or kindled)" could be interpreted as the seas being ignited or overflowing, representing the upheaval and destruction that will occur on that momentous day.
orig: والبحر المسجور

translation: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will occur
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of the punishment that will be inflicted by Allah upon those who reject His guidance and disobey His commands. It serves as a stern warning to those who persist in their wrongdoing, reminding them that they will not escape the consequences of their actions. The interpretation suggests that the punishment of Allah is a reality that will undoubtedly come to pass, and that individuals should take heed and repent before it is too late.
orig: إن عذاب ربك لواقع

translation: He has no defender.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the person being referred to has no one to protect or support them. They are alone and without any assistance or intervention on their behalf. The verse implies a sense of vulnerability and lack of recourse for this individual.
orig: ما له من دافع

translation: The Day the sky will shake with [a visible] shaking
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the heavens will be shaken and transformed, signaling the end of the world as we know it. The "shaking of the sky" is a metaphor for the cataclysmic events that will occur on that day, as the universe is reshaped and the old order gives way to the new. This verse is a reminder of the impermanence of the physical world and the need to prepare for the ultimate reckoning that awaits us all.
orig: يوم تمور السماء مورا

translation: And the mountains will proceed [as if] in motion
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, the mountains, which are typically considered immovable and permanent, will be set in motion and appear to be moving. This is a sign of the tremendous upheaval and transformation that will occur during the end times, when the very foundations of the physical world will be shaken. The movement of the mountains symbolizes the instability and impermanence of all worldly things, and serves as a reminder that only the eternal and divine will endure.
orig: وتسير الجبال سيرا

translation: Then woe to those who deny on that Day.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the truth and deny the reality of the Day of Judgment. On that day, they will face severe consequences for their disbelief and rejection of the divine message. The word "woe" conveys a sense of great distress, calamity, and punishment awaiting those who stubbornly refuse to believe in the teachings of the Qur'an and the existence of the Hereafter.
orig: فويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Those who are in [empty] discourse, amusing themselves
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are engaged in idle talk and meaningless pursuits, rather than focusing on more meaningful and productive activities. The interpretation suggests that such people are wasting their time and energy on frivolous matters, instead of dedicating themselves to more important endeavors that could benefit themselves and society.
orig: الذين هم في خوض يلعبون

translation: The Day they will be drawn to the Fire of Hell with [violent] drawing
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers and wicked will be forcibly dragged and compelled to enter the eternal punishment of Hell. The use of the word "drawing" suggests a violent and coercive process, emphasizing the inevitability and severity of their punishment for their misdeeds in the worldly life.
orig: يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا

translation: This is the Fire which you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers will be confronted with the reality of Hell, which they had previously denied and rejected. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the existence of the Hereafter and the punishment of the Hellfire, reminding them that they will ultimately face the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: هذه النار التي كنتم بها تكذبون

translation: Is this magic or do you not see?
interpretation: This verse is asking whether the message of the Qur'an is something that can be dismissed as "magic" or whether the people are simply unable to perceive the truth of it. The implication is that the Qur'an is not magic, but rather a clear and rational message from God, and that those who reject it are doing so not because it is false, but because they are unwilling or unable to see the truth.
orig: أفسحر هذا أم أنتم لا تبصرون

translation: Burn it! So be patient or impatient, it is all the same for you. You will [only] be recompensed for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who have rejected the truth and are being threatened with the punishment of Hell. The command to "Burn it!" refers to the fire of Hell that they will be subjected to. The verse then tells them that whether they are patient or impatient in the face of this punishment, it will not change the fact that they will be held accountable for their misdeeds. The final part of the verse emphasizes that they will only be recompensed for their own actions, implying that they have no one else to blame but themselves for their fate.
orig: اصلوها فاصبروا أو لا تصبروا سواء عليكم إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and pleasure.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the reward for the righteous in the Hereafter. The "gardens" refer to the paradisiacal abodes of the believers, where they will reside in eternal bliss and comfort. The "pleasure" indicates the state of joy, contentment, and fulfillment that the righteous will experience in the Afterlife, free from any pain, suffering, or distress.
orig: إن المتقين في جنات ونعيم

translation: Rejoicing in what their Lord has given them, and their Lord protected them from the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the believers in the Hereafter. They will be rejoicing in the blessings and rewards that their Lord has bestowed upon them, such as eternal life in Paradise, freedom from all suffering and hardship, and the pleasure of being in the presence of Allah. Additionally, their Lord has protected them from the punishment of the Hellfire, which is a torment that no one can truly comprehend. This verse highlights the immense grace and mercy of Allah towards the righteous, and the eternal bliss that awaits them in the Hereafter.
orig: فاكهين بما آتاهم ربهم ووقاهم ربهم عذاب الجحيم

translation: Eat and drink with enjoyment for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to partake of the blessings and provisions that Allah has provided, and to do so with a sense of gratitude and appreciation for the sustenance they have been granted. It suggests that one should enjoy the lawful pleasures of life, while remembering that these blessings are a result of their righteous deeds and the will of the Almighty.
orig: كلوا واشربوا هنيئا بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Reclining on couches arranged in rows and We will marry them to fair women with large, [beautiful] eyes.
interpretation: This verse describes the blissful state of the believers in Paradise. They will be reclining on arranged couches, enjoying the company of their spouses who are described as "fair women with large, beautiful eyes". This imagery conveys the idea of eternal peace, comfort and the fulfillment of all desires in the Hereafter for those who believe and do righteous deeds.
orig: متكئين على سرر مصفوفة وزوجناهم بحور عين

translation: And those who believe and whose descendants follow them in faith - We will join with them their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds. Every person, for what he has earned, is retained [in responsibility].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and righteous deeds being passed down through generations. It suggests that if the parents believe and follow the teachings of Islam, their children will also inherit this faith, and the rewards of the parents" good deeds will extend to their descendants. The verse also highlights individual responsibility, stating that each person will be held accountable for their own actions.
orig: والذين آمنوا واتبعتهم ذريتهم بإيمان ألحقنا بهم ذريتهم وما ألتناهم من عملهم من شيء كل امرئ بما كسب رهين

translation: And We provided them with fruit and meat as they desired.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has abundantly provided the believers with delightful sustenance, both in the form of fruits and meat, which they find pleasing and desirable. It is a testament to Allah's generosity and care for His faithful servants, ensuring that their needs and desires are fulfilled.
orig: وأمددناهم بفاكهة ولحم مما يشتهون

translation: They will exchange among themselves a cup [of wine] wherein is no ill speech or commission of sin.
interpretation: This verse describes the peaceful and harmonious atmosphere in Paradise, where the inhabitants will enjoy drinking wine without any negative consequences or sinful behavior. The absence of "ill speech" and "commission of sin" suggests a state of perfect tranquility and righteousness in the afterlife.
orig: يتنازعون فيها كأسا لا لغو فيها ولا تأثيم

translation: And there will circulate among them [servant] boys [dedicated] to them, as if they were scattered pearls.
interpretation: This verse describes the luxurious surroundings and attendants that will be enjoyed by the righteous in Paradise. The "servant boys" are young, pure, and beautiful, likened to "scattered pearls" in their radiance and perfection. This imagery conveys the idea of the believers being waited upon by these angelic attendants in the blissful afterlife.
orig: ويطوف عليهم غلمان لهم كأنهم لؤلؤ مكنون

translation: And they will approach one another inquiring of each other.
interpretation: This verse describes the scene on the Day of Judgment, when people will gather and question one another about their deeds and beliefs in this life. It suggests that there will be a sense of accountability and a desire to understand each other"s actions and motivations on that momentous day.
orig: وأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون

translation: They said, "Indeed, we were before this in our people fearful [of associating with you]"
interpretation: The people who were previously afraid to associate with the believers have now accepted the faith. They acknowledge that they were once fearful of being part of the believers, but now they have overcome that fear and joined the community of faith.
orig: قالوا إنا كنا قبل في أهلنا مشفقين

translation: So Allah has conferred [His] favor upon us and protected us from the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse expresses gratitude and appreciation to Allah for His blessings and protection. It acknowledges that it is Allah who has bestowed His favor upon the believers and saved them from the punishment of the Hellfire, referred to as "the punishment of the Blaze". The verse highlights the importance of recognizing and being thankful for Allah's guidance and mercy, which shields the faithful from the torment of the Hereafter.
orig: فمن الله علينا ووقانا عذاب السموم

translation: Indeed, We used to invoke Him [in the past]. Indeed, it is He who is the Beneficent, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the Beneficent and Merciful, and that the believers have always invoked Him in the past. It serves as a reminder that Allah is the source of all mercy and kindness, and that it is to Him that we should turn in times of need and distress.
orig: إنا كنا من قبل ندعوه إنه هو البر الرحيم

translation: So remind, [O Muhammad]; you are not, [O Muhammad], a controller over them. But remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My threat.
interpretation: This verse is instructing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to continue reminding people of the message of the Qur'an, as he is not a ruler or a coercive force over them. Rather, his role is to convey the message and remind those who fear the consequences of rejecting it. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet is not a sorcerer or a madman, as some had accused him of being, but a messenger delivering the divine revelation.
orig: فذكر فما أنت بنعمت ربك بكاهن ولا مجنون

translation: Or do they say, "[He is but] a poet for whom we await a misfortune of time?"
interpretation: This verse questions the claim of the disbelievers that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is a poet, for whom they await some calamity or misfortune to befall him. The implication is that the Qur'an is not the word of a poet, but rather the revelation from God, and that the Prophet will be protected by God from any harm that the disbelievers wish upon him.
orig: أم يقولون شاعر نتربص به ريب المنون

translation: Say, "Wait, indeed I am with you among the waiters."
interpretation: This verse is a command from God to the Prophet Muhammad to tell his opponents to "wait" and be patient, for he (the Prophet) is also waiting with them for the outcome of their confrontation. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet is steadfast in his faith and confident that the truth will prevail in due time.
orig: قل تربصوا فإني معكم من المتربصين

translation: Or do their dreams command them to [do] this, or are they a [transgressing] people?
interpretation: This verse raises a question about the source of the unbelievers' beliefs and actions. Are they following their own whims and desires, or are they being driven by deluded dreams and visions? The implication is that their behavior is not based on reason or divine guidance, but rather on their own arrogance and rebellion against the truth.
orig: أم تأمرهم أحلامهم بهذا أم هم قوم طاغون

translation: Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Rather, they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the disbelievers who accuse the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of fabricating the Qur'an. The verse denies this accusation and states that the real reason they do not believe is not because the Qur'an is invented, but because they are unwilling to accept the truth and submit to Allah. The interpretation is that the Qur'an is a divine revelation, not a human invention, and the rejection of it is due to the stubbornness and lack of faith of the disbelievers.
orig: أم يقولون تقوله بل لا يؤمنون

translation: Then let them produce a statement like it, if they should be truthful.
interpretation: This verse challenges those who reject the Qur'an to produce a text of similar eloquence and divine guidance if they claim the Qur'an is not from God. The Qur'an's unparalleled literary and spiritual excellence serves as proof of its divine origin, as no human being could produce a work of comparable quality. This verse emphasizes the Qur'an's miraculous nature and invites skeptics to test its authenticity by attempting to replicate it, which they will inevitably fail to do if they are truthful in their claims.
orig: فليأتوا بحديث مثله إن كانوا صادقين

translation: Or were they created by nothing, or were they the creators [of themselves]?
interpretation: This verse raises the fundamental question of the origin of creation. It challenges the notion that the universe and all that exists within it could have come into being by chance or without a Creator. The verse invites the reader to ponder whether it is more plausible that creation is the result of a conscious and purposeful act, rather than a random occurrence. The implication is that the existence of the universe and all that it contains points to the existence of a Creator, who is the true Originator of all things.
orig: أم خلقوا من غير شيء أم هم الخالقون

translation: Or were they created by nothing, or were they themselves the creators?
interpretation: This verse is posing a rhetorical question, challenging the notion that the universe and everything in it came into existence by chance or were created by something other than God. The implication is that the creation of the heavens and the earth is a clear sign of the existence and power of God, and that those who deny this are lacking in certainty and conviction ("lā yūqinūn"). The interpretation is that the universe is a product of divine creation, not random chance or self-creation, and that this should be evident to those who reflect upon it.
orig: أم خلقوا السماوات والأرض بل لا يوقنون

translation: Or have they the treasures of your Lord with them, or do they have control (over them)?
interpretation: This verse is questioning whether the disbelievers have access to the treasures and resources of God, or if they have control and authority over them. The implication is that they do not, and that all power and resources ultimately belong to God alone. This serves to remind the audience that the disbelievers have no real power or authority, and that they should submit to the will of God.
orig: أم عندهم خزائن ربك أم هم المصيطرون

translation: Or do they have a stairway (to heaven) by means of which they listen? Then let their listener produce a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse is challenging the disbelievers who claim to have a direct connection to God or a special way to access the divine. The Qur'an is asking them to produce clear evidence or authority for their claims, rather than just relying on hearsay or speculation. The implication is that they do not have any such special access or means of communication with God, and that the Qur'an itself is the clear authority from God.
orig: أم لهم سلم يستمعون فيه فليأت مستمعهم بسلطان مبين

translation: Or has He daughters while you have sons?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the belief that God has daughters, while humans have sons.
