The interpretation suggests that one should be mindful and grateful for God's favors, rather than being ungrateful or dismissive of them.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: There emerges from them pearl and coral.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the two bodies of water, the fresh water and the salt water, from which precious gems like pearls and corals are extracted. The verse is highlighting the bountiful resources that Allah has created for the benefit of humanity, and the verse encourages us to appreciate and make use of these natural wonders.
orig: يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ والمرجان

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, challenging the reader to consider the countless blessings and favors that God has bestowed upon them. The implication is that denying or being ungrateful for these blessings is a grave sin. The verse encourages the reader to reflect on God's mercy and to express gratitude and submission to the divine.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: And to Him belong the ships [moving] in the sea like mountains.
interpretation: This verse refers to the power and majesty of Allah, the Creator of the universe. The ships mentioned in the verse are described as "like mountains", conveying their immense size and strength as they traverse the vast oceans. This is a metaphorical expression highlighting Allah's ability to create such massive and impressive vessels, which serve as a testament to His divine power and sovereignty over all of creation.
orig: وله الجوار المنشآت في البحر كالأعلام

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the countless blessings and favors that God has bestowed upon humanity. The implication is that it would be foolish and ungrateful to deny or reject these divine favors. The verse encourages people to reflect on and appreciate the many ways in which God has provided for them, rather than taking these blessings for granted or denying their source.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: All that is on it [i.e., the earth] will perish.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient and impermanent nature of all that exists in this world. It suggests that everything and everyone on the earth will eventually cease to exist, whether through death, destruction, or other means. This serves as a reminder that the material world is fleeting and that one should not become overly attached to it, but rather focus on the eternal and the divine.
orig: كل من عليها فان

translation: And the Face of your Lord, full of Majesty and Honour, will remain forever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal and everlasting nature of Allah, the Lord. It conveys that while all things in the universe will perish, the Face (Essence) of Allah will remain forever, in all its Majesty and Honor. This highlights the permanence and supremacy of the Divine, in contrast to the transience of the created world. The verse inspires a deep reverence and awe for Allah, the Eternal and Sovereign Lord.
orig: ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, challenging the listener to consider the countless blessings and favors bestowed upon them by God. The implication is that to deny or be ungrateful for these blessings would be the height of ingratitude and disbelief. The verse encourages the listener to reflect on and appreciate the abundant grace and mercy of the Lord, rather than taking it for granted or denying it.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and the earth asks of Him. Every day He is in a (new) Manifestation.
interpretation: This verse conveys that all of creation, from the heavens to the earth, is constantly seeking from and relying upon Allah. Every moment, Allah is engaged in a new state of activity, sustaining and governing the universe. This highlights Allah's infinite power, knowledge, and presence, as He attends to the needs of all His creation at all times.
orig: يسأله من في السماوات والأرض كل يوم هو في شأن

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
interpretation: This verse is part of Surah Ar-Rahman, which emphasizes the blessings and favors of Allah upon humanity. The question "So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?" is a rhetorical one, meant to make the listener reflect on the countless blessings they have received from Allah and to acknowledge and be grateful for them. The verse encourages the reader to appreciate and not take for granted the many bounties and provisions that Allah has bestowed upon them.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: We will attend to you, O you two heavy ones.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the two weighty entities, which are often interpreted as referring to jinn (spirits) and humans. The Qur'an is addressing these two groups, indicating that God will pay attention to them and hold them accountable for their actions. The "two heavy ones" implies the significant responsibility and burden that these two creations of God bear, as they are endowed with the ability to make choices and will be held responsible for them.
orig: سنفرغ لكم أيه الثقلان

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
interpretation: This verse is part of a recurring refrain in Surah ar-Rahman (The Most Merciful) that emphasizes the innumerable blessings and favors bestowed upon humanity by God. The question "So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?" is a rhetorical one, meant to make the listener reflect on and appreciate the abundance of God's grace and mercy. The interpretation suggests that we should not take these blessings for granted or deny them, but rather be grateful and mindful of the Almighty's generosity.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. But you will not be able to pass except by authority [from Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all creation. It challenges humans and jinn (spirits) to try to escape the bounds of the heavens and the earth, which they cannot do except by the permission and authority granted to them by Allah. This serves as a reminder of the limitations of human and jinn abilities in comparison to the limitless power of the Creator.
orig: يا معشر الجن والإنس إن استطعتم أن تنفذوا من أقطار السماوات والأرض فانفذوا لا تنفذون إلا بسلطان

translation: Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
interpretation: This verse is part of Surah Ar-Rahman, which emphasizes the blessings and favors of Allah upon humanity. The question "Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?" is a rhetorical one, meant to make the listener reflect on the countless blessings they have received from Allah and to avoid denying or being ungrateful for them. The interpretation suggests that we should be mindful and appreciative of Allah's favors, rather than taking them for granted or denying them.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: He will send upon you a flame of fire and [a cloud of] smoke, and you will not be able to defend yourselves.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to those who disbelieve and reject the message of the Qur'an. The "flame of fire" and "cloud of smoke" symbolize the punishment and torment that will be inflicted upon them in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes that they will be unable to defend themselves against this divine retribution, as they have no power or means to escape the consequences of their disbelief and wrongdoing.
orig: يرسل عليكما شواظ من نار ونحاس فلا تنتصران

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, challenging the listener to consider the countless blessings and favors that God has bestowed upon them. The implication is that denying or being ungrateful for these blessings is a grave sin. The verse encourages the listener to reflect on and appreciate the generosity and mercy of their Lord, rather than taking these gifts for granted or rejecting them.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: And when the sky is split open and becomes rose-colored like oil
interpretation: This verse describes a dramatic celestial event that will occur at the end of time. The splitting open of the sky and its transformation into a rose-colored hue is a sign of the impending Day of Judgment. The comparison to oil suggests a luminous, shimmering quality to the sky, conveying a sense of awe and foreboding at the approach of this momentous occasion. This verse serves as a reminder of the transience of the material world and the inevitability of the Hereafter, calling upon believers to prepare themselves spiritually for the reckoning to come.
orig: فإذا انشقت السماء فكانت وردة كالدهان

translation: Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the countless blessings and favors that God has bestowed upon humanity. It is a call to reflect on and appreciate the numerous ways in which God has provided for us, and to avoid denying or rejecting these blessings. The verse encourages gratitude, humility, and a deeper recognition of God's mercy and generosity.
orig: فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان

translation: And on that Day, no person will be questioned about his sin, [neither] man nor jinn.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all people (humans and jinn) will be held accountable for their actions. On that Day, no one will be able to make excuses or shift blame for their sins, as each person will be responsible for their own deeds. The emphasis is on the finality and impartiality of the reckoning, where no one will be able to escape the consequences of their choices and behaviors in this life.
orig: فيومئذ لا يسأل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان

translation: So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
interpretation: This verse is part of a recurring refrain in Surah Ar-Rahman, where Allah reminds humanity of His countless blessings and favors. orig: في سدر مخضود

translation: And [abundant] fruit, arranged [in layers].
interpretation: This verse is describing the bountiful and plentiful fruits that will be available in Paradise. The phrase "arranged [in layers]" suggests that the fruits will be presented in an organized and aesthetically pleasing manner, further emphasizing the abundance and beauty of the rewards awaiting the righteous in the Hereafter.
orig: وطلح منضود

translation: And a shade extended
interpretation: This verse suggests the idea of a continuous, lasting, and expansive shade or protection that is provided. It could be interpreted as a metaphor for the enduring care, guidance, and shelter that Allah provides to His believers, shielding them from harm and hardship.
orig: وظل ممدود

translation: And a poured-out water
interpretation: This verse refers to the abundant and continuous supply of water that is provided by God. The "poured-out water" symbolizes the generosity and abundance of God's provision, which sustains all life on Earth. This verse highlights the importance of water as a vital resource and a blessing from the Creator.
orig: وماء مسكوب

translation: And [many] fruits
interpretation: This verse refers to the abundance and variety of fruits that will be available in Paradise. It suggests that the believers in the Hereafter will be surrounded by an endless supply of delicious and nourishing fruits, which symbolize the blessings and pleasures that await them in the afterlife.
orig: وفاكهة كثيرة

translation: Neither cut off nor forbidden
interpretation: This verse suggests that something is neither completely prohibited nor completely permitted. It implies a middle ground, where there is some flexibility or nuance in the ruling or guidance. The interpretation could be that there are certain matters that are not strictly black and white, but rather fall into a gray area where context and circumstances play a role in determining the appropriate course of action.
orig: لا مقطوعة ولا ممنوعة

translation: And lofty mattresses
interpretation: This verse refers to the luxurious furnishings and comforts that will be enjoyed by the righteous in Paradise. The "lofty mattresses" symbolize the elevated status and comfort of the inhabitants of Paradise, who will be provided with the finest of accommodations and furnishings as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this life.
orig: وفرش مرفوعة

translation: Indeed, We have created them [i.e., the women] with an [especial] creation
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has created women in a special and unique way, endowing them with qualities and characteristics that are distinct from men. The interpretation suggests that women possess inherent dignity, worth, and a special status in the sight of Allah, which should be recognized and respected by society.
orig: إنا أنشأناهن إنشاء

translation: And We have made them virgins,
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers in Paradise, who will be granted pure and chaste companions. The interpretation is that the believers in the Hereafter will be provided with spouses who are virgins, untouched by any previous partner, as a reward for their faith and righteous deeds in this life.
orig: فجعلناهن أبكارا

translation: Arabs, their equals
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Arabia, who are described as being "Arabs, their equals". This suggests that the Arabs being addressed are of similar status, age, or character. The interpretation is that the verse is emphasizing the unity and cohesion of the Arab people, highlighting their shared identity and characteristics.
orig: عربا أترابا

translation: For the companions of the right hand
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous people who will be rewarded with Paradise on the Day of Judgment. The "companions of the right hand" are those who will receive their record of deeds in their right hand, signifying their acceptance and approval by God. This verse highlights the eternal bliss and rewards that await the faithful and virtuous in the Hereafter.
orig: لأصحاب اليمين

translation: A group of the former (people)
interpretation: This verse refers to a group of the earlier generations of people, likely referring to those who had come before the time of the Qur'an and Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The interpretation suggests that there were groups of people in the past who had beliefs, practices, and ways of life that differed from the teachings of Islam. The verse may be highlighting the distinction between the beliefs and actions of those earlier groups and the guidance provided by the Qur'an and the Prophet.
orig: ثلة من الأولين

translation: And a group of the later ones
interpretation: This verse refers to a group of people who will come after the earlier generations. It suggests that there will be a continuous succession of believers and followers of the faith, with each generation contributing to the preservation and spread of the divine message.
orig: وثلة من الآخرين

translation: And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, where people will be divided into two groups: the companions of the right (the righteous) and the companions of the left (the wicked). The verse is posing a rhetorical question, emphasizing the dire fate of the "companions of the left" - those who will be condemned to the fire of Hell. The interpretation highlights the importance of living a righteous life in order to be among the "companions of the right" on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: وأصحاب الشمال ما أصحاب الشمال

translation: In scalding water and in a burning blaze
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment that awaits the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The "scalding water" and "burning blaze" symbolize the intense and unrelenting torment that they will face as a consequence of their rejection of faith and righteous deeds. The imagery conveys the severity and unimaginable pain of the eternal punishment in Hell.
orig: في سموم وحميم

translation: And there remained from them one who was left behind.
interpretation: This verse refers to a person who was left behind, likely due to some circumstance or hardship. The interpretation suggests that despite the challenges faced, this individual persevered and remained steadfast, continuing on their journey or path.
orig: وظل من يحموم

translation: Neither cold nor [pleasing]
interpretation: This verse suggests that something is neither cold nor pleasant or agreeable. It could be referring to a situation or circumstance that is neither comfortable nor desirable. The interpretation implies a sense of unpleasantness or lack of satisfaction.
orig: لا بارد ولا كريم

translation: Indeed, they were before that indulging [in luxuries]
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people referred to were previously living in a state of affluence and indulgence, before a change occurred in their circumstances. The implication is that their previous lifestyle of luxury and ease may have led them to become complacent or neglectful, and this could have contributed to the challenges or hardships they now face.
orig: إنهم كانوا قبل ذلك مترفين

translation: And they persisted in the great sin.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who stubbornly continued to engage in grave sins and transgressions, despite being warned and urged to repent. The "great sin" likely refers to idolatry, polytheism, and other major violations of God's commands. The verse emphasizes the obstinacy and refusal of the disbelievers to abandon their sinful ways, even in the face of clear guidance from God.
orig: وكانوا يصرون على الحنث العظيم

translation: And they say, "When we have become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism of some people towards the concept of resurrection and the afterlife. They question how it is possible for them to be brought back to life after they have decomposed into dust and bones. This reflects a lack of belief in the power and ability of God to resurrect the dead. The interpretation of this verse is that God has the power to recreate and resurrect the dead, and that the afterlife and the Day of Judgment are inevitable realities that people must believe in and prepare for.
orig: وكانوا يقولون أئذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمبعوثون

translation: Or our forefathers of old?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the belief that the polytheistic practices of the forefathers should be blindly followed. It challenges the notion that something is right just because it has been done for a long time. The Qur'an encourages critical thinking and not just accepting traditions without questioning their validity.
orig: أوآباؤنا الأولون

translation: Say, "Indeed, the former [generations] and the later [ones]"
interpretation: This verse is instructing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to say that the guidance and message of Islam is not just for a specific time or place, but is meant for all people, both those who came before and those who will come after. It emphasizes the universality and timelessness of the divine message revealed in the Quran.
orig: قل إن الأولين والآخرين

translation: Surely, We have gathered them to a well-known Day.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when all people will be gathered before God for the final judgment. The "well-known Day" is a reference to the appointed time when this event will take place, which is known only to God. This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Resurrection and the accountability that all people will face on that momentous day.
orig: لمجموعون إلى ميقات يوم معلوم

translation: Then, indeed you, [you] the deviators [who are] deniers,
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who have strayed from the right path and rejected the truth of the Qur'an and the message of Islam. It is a stern warning to those who have chosen to disbelieve and turn away from the guidance of Allah. The verse emphasizes that these individuals will be held accountable for their actions and will face the consequences of their rejection of the truth.
orig: ثم إنكم أيها الضالون المكذبون

translation: They will eat from the tree of Zaqqum
interpretation: This verse refers to the tree of Zaqqum, which is mentioned in the Quran as a punishment for the disbelievers in the afterlife. The Zaqqum tree is described as a tree that grows in the depths of Hell, bearing bitter and poisonous fruit that the sinners will be forced to consume as a torment. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and engage in wrongdoing, emphasizing the severe consequences they will face in the hereafter.
orig: لآكلون من شجر من زقوم

translation: So they are filled from it, [but only] the bellies.
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people are only concerned with fulfilling their physical desires and worldly pleasures, without considering the deeper spiritual and moral aspects of life. The focus on "filling the bellies" implies a lack of concern for one's spiritual well-being and a preoccupation with material pursuits. The interpretation emphasizes the need to balance physical and spiritual needs, and to not become overly consumed by the pursuit of worldly pleasures at the expense of one's spiritual growth and development.
orig: فمالئون منها البطون

translation: Then they will be given to drink from a boiling fluid
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that awaits the disbelievers in the Hereafter. They will be forced to drink from a boiling fluid, which symbolizes the intense suffering and torment they will endure as a consequence of their rejection of faith and righteous deeds. The "boiling fluid" represents the severity and unpleasantness of the punishment, emphasizing the gravity of their actions in this life.
orig: فشاربون عليه من الحميم

translation: Then they will drink as the camels drink.
interpretation: This verse is describing the intense thirst and suffering that the disbelievers will experience in the Hellfire. Just as camels drink water greedily when they are extremely thirsty, the disbelievers will drink the boiling water and pus of Hell in a similar manner, out of their intense and unquenchable thirst.
orig: فشاربون شرب الهيم

translation: This is their promised day of judgment.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions in life. The "this" in the verse likely refers to the events or signs that will occur on that momentous day. The interpretation suggests that this day of reckoning is the one that has been promised to humanity, a day when the final judgment will take place.
orig: هذا نزلهم يوم الدين

translation: We have created you, so why do you not believe?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah (God) is the Creator of all human beings, and therefore, it is only logical that they should believe in Him and worship Him alone. The question "why do you not believe?" implies that the belief in the Oneness of God is a natural and rational conclusion that should be reached by every person who contemplates the signs of creation around them. The verse encourages people to reflect on the wonders of the universe and the human being's own existence, which should lead them to recognize the existence and Oneness of the Creator.
orig: نحن خلقناكم فلولا تصدقون

translation: Have you considered that which you emit?
interpretation: This verse encourages us to reflect on the nature and purpose of our own actions and desires. It prompts us to consider the consequences of what we choose to pursue or 'emit' into the world, whether it be our thoughts, words, or deeds. The implication is that we should be mindful and intentional in how we direct our energies, as our choices can have a profound impact on ourselves and others.
orig: أفرأيتم ما تمنون

translation: Do you create it, or are We the Creator?
interpretation: This verse is challenging the notion that anything other than Allah (God) can create. It is a rhetorical question that emphasizes that only Allah has the power of creation, not any created being. The verse is a reminder that Allah is the sole Creator, and that all existence is dependent upon Him. It serves to reinforce the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and sovereignty of Allah as the Supreme Creator.
orig: أأنتم تخلقونه أم نحن الخالقون

translation: And We have already determined among you [the time of] death, and We are not to be outdone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has already decreed the time and manner of each person's death, and that no one can escape or outlive their appointed time. It serves as a reminder that life is finite and that we should live it in a way that pleases Allah, as we will all ultimately return to Him.
orig: نحن قدرنا بينكم الموت وما نحن بمسبوقين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], that We will surely change their condition and create them in that which they do not know.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has the power to completely transform the circumstances and nature of the people, even in ways that they cannot comprehend or anticipate. It implies that Allah is not bound by the current state of things and can bring about radical changes, both in individuals and societies, according to His divine will and wisdom. The interpretation suggests that one should remain humble and open to the possibility of Allah’s transformative power, as He may reshape reality in unexpected ways.
orig: على أن نبدل أمثالكم وننشئكم في ما لا تعلمون

translation: And you have already known the first creation, so will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse reminds people that they have already witnessed and experienced the initial creation of the universe and life. It encourages them to reflect on this fact and to use their powers of remembrance and reason to understand the deeper meaning and purpose behind this creation. The verse implies that if one can comprehend the wonders of the first creation, they should also be able to understand and believe in the concept of the afterlife and resurrection.
orig: ولقد علمتم النشأة الأولى فلولا تذكرون

translation: Have you considered that [seed] which you sow?
interpretation: This verse encourages the reader to reflect on the process of cultivation and growth. It prompts us to consider the wonder of how a small seed, when planted and nurtured, can yield an abundant harvest. This serves as a metaphor for the spiritual growth and development of the human being, reminding us to tend to our inner lives with the same care and attention as a farmer tends to his field.
orig: أفرأيتم ما تحرثون

translation: Is it you who grow it, or are We the Growers?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, challenging the notion that humans are the sole creators or "growers" of what they produce. The implication is that it is ultimately God who is the true Creator and Sustainer, and that humans are merely the instruments through which God's creation is manifested. The verse serves to remind us of our dependence on God and to instill a sense of humility and gratitude in the face of the wonders of the natural world.
orig: أأنتم تزرعونه أم نحن الزارعون

translation: If We willed, We could have made it [as] debris, and you would remain in astonishment.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has the power to easily destroy what He has created, but chooses not to do so. It serves as a reminder to people that they should not take the blessings of God for granted or become complacent, but rather remain in a state of wonder and appreciation for the world around them.
orig: لو نشاء لجعلناه حطاما فظلتم تفكهون

translation: Indeed, we are [greatly] in debt.
interpretation: This verse expresses the idea that the people being addressed are deeply indebted or obligated, perhaps to God or to a higher power. The use of the word "greatly" suggests a significant or overwhelming sense of obligation or responsibility that the people feel they must fulfill. The interpretation is that the people recognize their indebtedness and are committed to repaying or honoring that debt.
orig: إنا لمغرمون

translation: Rather, we are deprived.
interpretation: This verse suggests a sense of deprivation or lack of something. It could imply that the speaker or group being referred to feels they have been denied or prevented from accessing something they desire or rightfully deserve. The interpretation suggests a state of being deprived or excluded, which could have social, economic, or spiritual implications.
orig: بل نحن محرومون

translation: Have you considered the water that you drink?
interpretation: This verse encourages us to reflect on the source and nature of the water we consume. It prompts us to ponder the blessings of Allah in providing us with this essential resource for our sustenance and survival. The verse invites us to appreciate the value of water and to use it responsibly, as a gift from the Creator.
orig: أفرأيتم الماء الذي تشربون

translation: Did you bring it down from the clouds, or is it We who bring it down?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the source of the revelation, challenging the notion that it could have been brought down by anyone other than God. It emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation, not something that was fabricated or originated from human sources. The implication is that the Qur'an is of divine origin, and its truth and authority come from God alone.
orig: أأنتم أنزلتموه من المزن أم نحن المنزلون

translation: If We willed, We could make it bitter, so will you not then be grateful?
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has the power to make even the sweetest things bitter, yet He chooses to provide us with blessings. The implication is that we should be grateful for the favors and bounties that Allah has bestowed upon us, rather than taking them for granted.
orig: لو نشاء جعلناه أجاجا فلولا تشكرون

translation: Have you considered the fire that you ignite?
interpretation: This verse is asking the reader to reflect on the fire that they have kindled. It is a rhetorical question that invites the reader to ponder the consequences of their actions and the impact they have on the world around them. The interpretation suggests that the verse is encouraging the reader to be mindful of the effects of their choices and to consider the potential harm or good that can come from the "fires" they choose to light, whether literally or metaphorically.
orig: أفرأيتم النار التي تورون

translation: Did you create it or are We the Creator?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, challenging the notion that anything other than God could have created the tree. The implication is that only God has the power and ability to create such natural wonders, and that to attribute their creation to any other source would be misguided. The verse serves to reinforce the idea of God's absolute sovereignty and the importance of acknowledging Him as the sole Creator.
orig: أأنتم أنشأتم شجرتها أم نحن المنشئون

translation: And We have made the [Qur'an] a reminder and a provision for the seekers [of knowledge and righteousness].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a reminder and a source of guidance for those who seek knowledge and strive to live righteously. It serves as a constant reminder of God's teachings, commandments, and the path to salvation. The Qur'an provides sustenance, both spiritual and practical, for those who sincerely seek to follow its guidance and grow in their faith and understanding.
orig: نحن جعلناها تذكرة ومتاعا للمقوين

translation: So exalt [Him] with praise of your Lord, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to glorify and praise Allah, the Almighty Lord, for His greatness, power, and majesty. It reminds us to constantly remember and worship Allah, the Supreme Being, with utmost reverence and humility. The verse emphasizes the importance of submitting to Allah and acknowledging His supreme authority and dominion over all creation.
orig: فسبح باسم ربك العظيم

translation: But no! I swear by the positions of the stars
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the positions of the stars, which are used as points of reference for navigation, timekeeping, and other purposes. The oath reinforces the significance of these celestial bodies and the knowledge they provide, which is crucial for human guidance and understanding.
orig: فلا أقسم بمواقع النجوم

translation: And indeed, [the Qur'an] is a great oath, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and significance of the Qur'an. It is described as a "great oath", indicating that it is a solemn and weighty declaration from Allah. The verse suggests that if people truly understood the magnitude and gravity of the Qur'an, they would appreciate it more and strive to follow its teachings. The Qur'an is not to be taken lightly, but rather as a profound and sacred text that deserves the utmost respect and attention.
orig: وإنه لقسم لو تعلمون عظيم

translation: Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exalted status and noble nature of the Qur’an. The Qur’an is described as "a noble Qur’an", indicating its high rank, dignity, and excellence. This suggests that the Qur’an is a divine revelation that deserves the utmost respect, reverence, and careful study by believers.
orig: إنه لقرآن كريم

translation: In a hidden record
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an being a divine revelation that is preserved in a "hidden record" or a well-guarded tablet in the heavens. It suggests that the Qur'an is a sacred and protected scripture, revealed by God to humanity through the Prophet Muhammad. The "hidden record" implies that the Qur'an has a divine origin and is not subject to human tampering or alteration, as it is safeguarded by God Himself.
orig: في كتاب مكنون

translation: None shall touch it except the purified.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an, which is the sacred scripture of Islam. It emphasizes that the Qur'an is a pure and holy text, and that only those who have purified themselves, both physically and spiritually, are worthy of handling and studying it. This serves as a reminder to the believers to maintain a state of ritual purity and spiritual cleanliness in order to engage with the Qur'an in a reverent and meaningful way.
orig: لا يمسه إلا المطهرون

translation: Revelation from the Lord of the Worlds
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Qur'an as a revelation from God, the Lord of all the worlds and all creation. It emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and that it is not the work of a human being, but rather a message sent down from the Almighty. This establishes the authority and sacredness of the Qur'an as the word of God, which should be accepted and followed by believers.
orig: تنزيل من رب العالمين

translation: Is it with this discourse that you are being arrogant?
interpretation: This verse is questioning whether the people are being arrogant and dismissive of the message of the Qur'an. The phrase "this discourse" refers to the Qur'an and its teachings. The implication is that the people are not taking the Qur'an seriously and are instead being arrogant and turning away from it.
orig: أفبهذا الحديث أنتم مدهنون

translation: And you make [the sustenance] your denial.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the contradiction between the blessings and sustenance that God provides, and the disbelief and denial of the people. It suggests that the people are ungrateful for the provisions they have been given, and instead use them to deny the existence and power of God. The interpretation is that one should be thankful for God's bounties and not use them as a means to reject the truth of His divine guidance.
orig: وتجعلون رزقكم أنكم تكذبون

translation: Then why, when it (the soul) reaches the throat (i.e. one is about to die)
interpretation: This verse is referring to the moment when a person is about to die, and their soul is reaching their throat. The verse is prompting the reader to reflect on what they will do at that critical moment, when death is imminent. The implication is that one should be prepared for death and make the most of their life before that time comes.
orig: فلولا إذا بلغت الحلقوم

translation: And you, at that time, will be looking on.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when all people will witness the events unfolding before them. It emphasizes that on that momentous day, everyone will be observing what is happening, unable to escape or avoid the consequences of their actions in this life. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of our deeds, as we will ultimately be held accountable for them.
orig: وأنتم حينئذ تنظرون

translation: And We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the closeness and omnipresence of God. It suggests that God is closer to us than we can perceive, and that our limited human senses often prevent us from fully recognizing His proximity. The verse encourages us to seek a deeper understanding of the divine presence in our lives, and to be mindful of the fact that God is always near, even if we cannot directly observe or comprehend His nearness.
orig: ونحن أقرب إليه منكم ولكن لا تبصرون

translation: So why, if you are not indebted?
interpretation: This verse suggests that if one is not in debt or obligation to others, then they should not hesitate to spend in the way of Allah. It encourages a spirit of generosity and selflessness, rather than holding back out of a sense of owing something to someone else. The interpretation is that one should be willing to give and contribute charitably, without the constraint of feeling indebted to others.
orig: فلولا إن كنتم غير مدينين

translation: You will be made to return it if you are truthful.
interpretation: This verse is a challenge to those who make claims or promises, to prove their sincerity by following through on their words. It suggests that if one is truly honest and truthful, they will be held accountable for their statements and actions. The implication is that one should be careful and deliberate in what they say, as they may be called upon to fulfill their promises or declarations.
orig: ترجعونها إن كنتم صادقين

translation: But if he is of the companions of the right hand,
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of individuals on the Day of Judgment. If the person is among the "companions of the right hand", it means they are the righteous and blessed ones who will be welcomed into Paradise. This indicates that their good deeds and faith in life have earned them a favorable outcome in the Hereafter.
orig: فأما إن كان من المقربين

translation: Then [for him is] a pleasant life
interpretation: This verse describes the reward in the Afterlife for those who believe and do good deeds. "Ruh" (soul) and "Rayhan" (sweet-smelling flower) symbolize the tranquility and pleasantness of the eternal life in Paradise. "Jannat An-Na'eem" (Garden of Bliss) refers to the lush, blissful abode that awaits the righteous in the Hereafter.
orig: فروح وريحان وجنت نعيم

translation: And if he is of the companions of the right
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of the righteous and virtuous people in the afterlife. "The companions of the right" are those who will be welcomed into Paradise on the Day of Judgment, due to their good deeds and adherence to the teachings of Islam. This verse suggests that if the person being referred to is among the righteous, they will be granted eternal bliss and happiness in the hereafter.
orig: وأما إن كان من أصحاب اليمين

translation: So peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand.
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous and virtuous people who will be welcomed into Paradise on the Day of Judgment. It conveys a message of peace and blessings upon them, as they will be among those who have earned the pleasure of Allah and will be granted eternal bliss in the Hereafter.
orig: فسلام لك من أصحاب اليمين

translation: And if he is of the deniers, the deviators,
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of those who reject the truth and stray from the righteous path. It suggests that such individuals, who deny the signs of Allah and deviate from the straight way, will face consequences for their actions. The interpretation implies that those who reject faith and guidance will be held accountable for their choices and ultimately face the consequences of their misguided ways.
orig: وأما إن كان من المكذبين الضالين

translation: And he descended from a hot spring
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment and torment that awaits the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The "hot spring" is a metaphor for the intense heat and suffering they will experience in Hell. The imagery of descending from this scorching spring suggests the depth and severity of their torment, as they are plunged into the depths of Hell.
orig: فنزل من حميم

translation: And the burning of Hell
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment of Hell that awaits those who reject faith and do not follow the guidance of Allah. The "burning of Hell" is a metaphor for the intense and eternal suffering that the disbelievers will face in the Hereafter as a consequence of their actions in this life. The Qur'an emphasizes the severity of this punishment to warn people and encourage them to seek forgiveness, repent, and live a righteous life in accordance with the teachings of Islam.
orig: وتصلية جحيم

translation: Indeed, this is the true certainty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute truth and certainty of the Quranic teachings and the Islamic faith. It conveys the idea that the guidance and principles found in the Quran are undoubtedly true and reliable, and that believers can have complete confidence in them. The verse serves to affirm the divine origin and authenticity of the Quran, leaving no room for doubt or uncertainty.
orig: إن هذا لهو حق اليقين

translation: So exalt [Him] with praise of your Lord, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to glorify and praise God, the Almighty, with all sincerity and reverence. It is a call to constantly remember and acknowledge the greatness, majesty, and sovereignty of the Lord, and to worship Him alone without associating any partners with Him. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a mindset of humility, gratitude, and devotion towards the Divine, which should be reflected in one's thoughts, words, and actions.
orig: فسبح باسم ربك العظيم

translation: Exalted is Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over the entire universe, both in the heavens and on earth. It highlights that all things belong to Allah, the Almighty and All-Wise, who deserves to be glorified and exalted. This serves as a reminder to believers to submit to Allah’s will and to acknowledge His supreme authority and wisdom in all matters.
orig: سبح لله ما في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse affirms the absolute sovereignty and power of God over the entire universe. He is the sole Creator and Sustainer of all that exists in the heavens and the earth. He alone has the power to give life and to take it away, and there is nothing that is beyond His control or ability. This emphasizes the need for human beings to submit to God's will and to seek His guidance, as He is the ultimate source of all power and authority.
orig: له ملك السماوات والأرض يحيي ويميت وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Immanent, and He is the Knower of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the attributes of Allah as the Eternal, the Absolute, the All-Knowing, and the All-Encompassing. It highlights that Allah is the First, without a beginning, and the Last, without an end. He is the Evident, meaning He is manifest and visible through His creation, and the Immanent, meaning He is present and close to His creation. Furthermore, the verse affirms that Allah has knowledge of all things, leaving no aspect of existence outside of His divine knowledge and power.
orig: هو الأول والآخر والظاهر والباطن وهو بكل شيء عليم

translation: It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He knows what goes into the earth and what comes out of it and what descends from the heaven and what ascends therein, and He is with you wherever you are. And Allah, of what you do, is Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and omniscience of Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. It highlights that Allah is in control of all that happens in the universe, from what enters and exits the earth, to what descends from and ascends to the heavens. The verse also affirms that Allah is always with His servants, no matter where they may be, and that He is all-seeing and aware of their actions. This serves to instill a sense of awe, reverence, and accountability in the believers towards Allah.
orig: هو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش يعلم ما يلج في الأرض وما يخرج منها وما ينزل من السماء وما يعرج فيها وهو معكم أين ما كنتم والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah is the sole Sovereign and Owner of the entire universe, both the heavens and the earth. It emphasizes that all matters, affairs, and decisions ultimately return to Allah, the Almighty. This serves as a reminder that we are accountable to Allah for our actions and that we should strive to live our lives in accordance with His will and guidance.
orig: له ملك السماوات والأرض وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: He causes the night to enter the day, and He causes the day to enter the night, and He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and knowledge. He controls the alternation of night and day, demonstrating His sovereignty over the universe. Moreover, He has knowledge of the innermost thoughts and feelings of all people, nothing is hidden from Him. This highlights the importance of being conscious of one's actions and intentions, as Allah is aware of them all.
orig: يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وهو عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Believe in Allah and His Messenger and spend out of that in which He has made you successors. For those who have believed among you and spent, there will be a great reward.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have faith in Allah and His Messenger, and to spend from the wealth that Allah has entrusted them with. Those who believe and spend from their wealth for the sake of Allah will be greatly rewarded. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of both faith and charitable giving as a means of demonstrating one's devotion to Allah and earning His pleasure.
orig: آمنوا بالله ورسوله وأنفقوا مما جعلكم مستخلفين فيه فالذين آمنوا منكم وأنفقوا لهم أجر كبير

translation: And why should you not believe in Allah and the Messenger when the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord and He has already taken your covenant, if you should [truly] be believers?
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who have doubts or hesitation about believing in Allah and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes that there is no valid reason to not believe, as the Prophet is inviting you to believe in your Lord, and Allah has already taken a covenant from you to be a believer if you truly are one. The verse is encouraging and exhorting the believers to have firm faith in Allah and His Messenger, as this is the essence of being a true believer.
orig: وما لكم لا تؤمنون بالله والرسول يدعوكم لتؤمنوا بربكم وقد أخذ ميثاقكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: It is He who sends down to His Servant [Muhammad] verses of clear evidence that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light. And indeed, Allah is to you Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Almighty, is the One who reveals the clear signs and guidance (the Qur'an) to His Messenger, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), in order to guide humanity from the darkness of ignorance, disbelief and sin to the light of faith, knowledge and righteousness. It also highlights Allah's compassion and mercy towards His servants, as He desires to save them from the perils of the darkness and lead them to the enlightenment of the truth.
orig: هو الذي ينزل على عبده آيات بينات ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور وإن الله بكم لرءوف رحيم

translation: And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the cause of Allah, while to Allah belongs the heritage of the heavens and the earth? Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest [of Makkah] and fought [and those who did so after it]. They are greater in degree than those who spent afterwards and fought. And to all Allah has promised the best [reward]. And Allah , with what you do, is [fully] Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to spend and contribute financially in the cause of Allah. It reminds them that the wealth and resources of the heavens and the earth belong to Allah, and that those who spent and fought before the conquest of Makkah have a higher status than those who did so afterwards. The verse emphasizes that Allah has promised the best reward to all who contribute to His cause, and that He is fully aware of what everyone does.
orig: وما لكم ألا تنفقوا في سبيل الله ولله ميراث السماوات والأرض لا يستوي منكم من أنفق من قبل الفتح وقاتل أولئك أعظم درجة من الذين أنفقوا من بعد وقاتلوا وكلا وعد الله الحسنى والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him and he will have a noble reward?
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to make charitable donations and good deeds, as Allah will reward them abundantly. The metaphor of "loaning to Allah" suggests that any good we do is ultimately an investment in our relationship with the Divine, which will be reciprocated with a "noble reward". The interpretation emphasizes the importance of generosity and selfless acts, which are seen as a means of drawing closer to Allah and securing a favorable outcome in the afterlife.
orig: من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا فيضاعفه له وله أجر كريم

translation: The Day you see the believing men and believing women, their light proceeding before them and on their right, [it will be said], "Your good tidings today are [of] gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein you will abide eternally." That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse describes the grand reward and status that the believers will attain on the Day of Judgment. Their light, representing their faith and righteous deeds, will be shining brightly before them and on their right side, guiding them towards the eternal gardens of Paradise. This is the ultimate success and triumph that the believers have earned through their sincere devotion to Allah and their righteous conduct in this world. The imagery of the light and the gardens beneath which rivers flow convey a sense of the splendor, tranquility, and everlasting bliss that awaits the faithful in the Hereafter.
orig: يوم ترى المؤمنين والمؤمنات يسعى نورهم بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم بشراكم اليوم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: The Day the hypocrite men and hypocrite women will say to those who believed, "Wait for us that we may acquire [something] of your light." It will be said, "Go back behind you and seek light." And a wall will be placed between them with a door, its interior containing mercy, but on the outside of it is torment.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the hypocrites - those who outwardly professed faith but inwardly harbored disbelief - will seek to share in the light and guidance of the true believers. However, they will be turned away and instructed to seek light for themselves. A barrier will then be erected between the believers and the hypocrites, with mercy on the inside and punishment on the outside. This emphasizes the consequences of hypocrisy and the importance of sincerity in one's faith.
orig: يوم يقول المنافقون والمنافقات للذين آمنوا انظرونا نقتبس من نوركم قيل ارجعوا وراءكم فالتمسوا نورا فضرب بينهم بسور له باب باطنه فيه الرحمة وظاهره من قبله العذاب

translation: They will call to them, "Were we not with you?" They will reply, "Yes, but you led yourselves to temptation, and you waited and doubted, and your vain desires deceived you until the command of Allah came. And the Deceiver (Satan) deceived you in regard to Allah."
interpretation: This verse describes the dialogue that will take place on the Day of Judgment between the disbelievers and the believers. The disbelievers will try to justify their actions by claiming that they were misled, but the believers will respond by pointing out that the disbelievers were responsible for their own downfall. They were tempted by their own desires, and they waited and doubted instead of following the guidance of Allah. Furthermore, they were deceived by Satan, who led them astray from the true path of Allah. This verse emphasizes the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and not blaming others for one's own failings.
orig: ينادونهم ألم نكن معكم قالوا بلى ولكنكم فتنتم أنفسكم وتربصتم وارتبتم وغرتكم الأماني حتى جاء أمر الله وغركم بالله الغرور

translation: So today no ransom will be accepted from you or from those who disbelieved. Your refuge is the Fire. It is most worthy of you, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse conveys a stern warning to those who have rejected faith in God. On the Day of Judgment, no amount of wealth or bargaining will be able to save them from the punishment they have earned through their disbelief. The Fire of Hell will be their eternal abode, a fitting consequence for their rejection of the truth. The verse emphasizes the finality and severity of their fate, leaving no room for escape or redemption.
orig: فاليوم لا يؤخذ منكم فدية ولا من الذين كفروا مأواكم النار هي مولاكم وبئس المصير

translation: Has not the time come for those who believe that their hearts should be humble for the remembrance of Allah and what has come down of the truth? And let them not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and a long period passed over them, so their hearts hardened; and many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have humble and reverent hearts when remembering Allah and reflecting on the revealed truth of the Qur'an. It contrasts the believers with those who were given scripture previously, such as the Jews and Christians, whose hearts hardened over time due to a lack of sincere devotion. The verse exhorts the believers to avoid becoming like those who became complacent and disobedient, and instead to maintain a state of humility and responsiveness to the divine guidance.
orig: ألم يأن للذين آمنوا أن تخشع قلوبهم لذكر الله وما نزل من الحق ولا يكونوا كالذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبل فطال عليهم الأمد فقست قلوبهم وكثير منهم فاسقون

translation: Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death. We have certainly explained in detail the signs for you, that you might understand.
interpretation: This verse encourages us to reflect on the signs of Allah’s power and wisdom in the natural world. Just as Allah can bring life to the dead earth, He has the power to resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes that Allah has made His signs clear, so that we may use our intellect to understand and appreciate His creation and plan for us.
orig: اعلموا أن الله يحيي الأرض بعد موتها قد بينا لكم الآيات لعلكم تعقلون

translation: Indeed, the men who practice charity and the women who practice charity, and [they who] have loaned Allah a goodly loan - it will be multiplied for them, and they will have a noble reward.
interpretation: This verse encourages both men and women to engage in acts of charity and generosity. It promises that those who lend to Allah, by spending their wealth in good causes, will have their rewards multiplied. The "goodly loan" refers to voluntary acts of charity and financial support for righteous endeavors, which are seen as loans to Allah that will be repaid with great rewards in the Hereafter.
orig: إن المصدقين والمصدقات وأقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا يضاعف لهم ولهم أجر كريم

translation: And those who believe in Allah and His messengers - those are the truthful and the witnesses [to the truth] with their Lord. They will have their reward and their light. But those who disbelieve and deny Our verses - those are the companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the distinction between those who believe in Allah and His messengers, and those who reject faith and deny the signs (ayat) of Allah. The believers are described as the "truthful" (as-siddiqun) and "witnesses" (ash-shuhada), implying that their faith is sincere and they will testify to the truth on the Day of Judgment. They will be rewarded with both material ("their reward") and spiritual ("their light") blessings. In contrast, the disbelievers who deny Allah's revelations are destined for the punishment of Hellfire. This verse highlights the importance of true faith and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله أولئك هم الصديقون والشهداء عند ربهم لهم أجرهم ونورهم والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement and adornment and boasting among you and competition in increase of wealth and children, as the example of a rain whose [resulting] plant growth pleases the tillers; then it dries and you see it turned yellow; then it becomes [scattered] debris. And in the Hereafter is severe punishment and forgiveness from Allah and [His] pleasure. And what is the worldly life except the enjoyment of delusion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the life of this world is fleeting and temporary, filled with distractions like play, wealth, and status. It is compared to a rain that initially produces lush vegetation, but then quickly withers and dies. The true purpose is to seek the Hereafter, where there is either severe punishment or the pleasure and forgiveness of Allah. The life of this world is nothing but an illusion, and one should not be deceived by its temporary allures.
orig: اعلموا أنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وزينة وتفاخر بينكم وتكاثر في الأموال والأولاد كمثل غيث أعجب الكفار نباته ثم يهيج فتراه مصفرا ثم يكون حطاما وفي الآخرة عذاب شديد ومغفرة من الله ورضوان وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور

translation: Race towards forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for those who believe in Allah and His messengers. That is the bounty of Allah which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to strive and compete in doing good deeds in order to attain Allah's forgiveness and the reward of Paradise. The vastness of Paradise, described as being as wide as the heavens and the earth, signifies its boundless nature and the abundance of blessings it contains. This is a special gift from Allah, bestowed upon those who have true faith in Him and His messengers. The verse emphasizes that this bounty is granted by Allah to whomever He wills, highlighting the generosity and sovereignty of the Almighty. The final statement reaffirms that Allah is the source of all great bounties and favors.
orig: سابقوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم وجنة عرضها كعرض السماء والأرض أعدت للذين آمنوا بالله ورسله ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into being. Indeed, that for Allah is easy.
interpretation: This verse conveys the concept of divine predestination and the belief that nothing happens in the world or to individuals without Allah's knowledge and permission. It suggests that all events, whether calamities or blessings, are pre-recorded in a divine register before they occur. This emphasizes the belief that Allah is all-knowing and in control of all affairs, and that what befalls us is part of His plan, which is easy for Him to enact. The interpretation encourages acceptance of Allah's will and trust in His wisdom, even in the face of hardship.
orig: ما أصاب من مصيبة في الأرض ولا في أنفسكم إلا في كتاب من قبل أن نبرأها إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: So that you may not grieve over what has eluded you, nor exult [in pride] over what He has given you. And Allah does not love any self-conceited boaster
interpretation: This verse encourages a balanced and humble attitude towards the gains and losses in life. It advises against excessive grief over missed opportunities or undue pride in one's achievements. The underlying message is to maintain equanimity, as Allah does not favor those who are arrogant or boastful. The verse reminds us to be grateful for what we have been given, without becoming conceited, and to accept with grace what we have not been able to attain.
orig: لكيلا تأسوا على ما فاتكم ولا تفرحوا بما آتاكم والله لا يحب كل مختال فخور

translation: Those who are stingy and enjoin upon [other] people stinginess and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty - and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who are miserly and greedy, not only for themselves but also for encouraging others to be stingy and withhold the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon them. It suggests that such behavior is displeasing to Allah, and that those who engage in it will face a humiliating punishment. The interpretation highlights the importance of generosity, gratitude, and using one's wealth and resources in a way that benefits others and pleases Allah.
orig: الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل ومن يتول فإن الله هو الغني الحميد

translation: Indeed, We have sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance that the people may maintain [their affairs] in justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is great military might and [numerous] benefits for the people, and to let Allah make evident those who support Him and His messengers in the unseen. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has sent His messengers with clear proofs, divine scriptures, and the balance of justice to guide humanity. He has also created iron, which has both military might and benefits for the people. The purpose is to make evident those who support Allah and His messengers, even though their support may not be visible. This highlights Allah's power and might, and the importance of upholding justice and supporting the divine message.
orig: لقد أرسلنا رسلنا بالبينات وأنزلنا معهم الكتاب والميزان ليقوم الناس بالقسط وأنزلنا الحديد فيه بأس شديد ومنافع للناس وليعلم الله من ينصره ورسله بالغيب إن الله قوي عزيز

translation: And We had certainly sent Noah and Abraham and placed in their descendants prophethood and Scripture; and among them was he who was guided, but many of them were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of the prophets Noah and Abraham, and the legacy they left behind in their descendants. The verse emphasizes that prophethood and divine scripture were bestowed upon their lineage. However, it also acknowledges that while some of their descendants were guided and righteous, many of them strayed from the path and became defiantly disobedient to God's commands.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا وإبراهيم وجعلنا في ذريتهما النبوة والكتاب فمنهم مهتد وكثير منهم فاسقون

translation: Then We sent following in their footsteps Our messengers and We sent Jesus, son of Mary, and We gave him the Gospel, and We placed in the hearts of those who [claimed to] follow him compassion and mercy and monasticism - which they innovated; We did not prescribe it for them except [that they seek] the approval of Allah . But they did not observe it with due observance. So We gave the believers among them their reward, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse describes how after sending previous messengers, Allah then sent Jesus, son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel. The verse states that Allah placed in the hearts of those who followed Jesus a sense of compassion, mercy, and monasticism, which they innovated themselves and was not prescribed by Allah. However, they did not observe this monasticism properly. As a result, Allah rewarded the true believers among them, but many remained disobedient. The key message is that while Allah may guide people, they must still observe His commands properly and not innovate their own practices, even if done with good intentions.
orig: ثم قفينا على آثارهم برسلنا وقفينا بعيسى ابن مريم وآتيناه الإنجيل وجعلنا في قلوب الذين اتبعوه رأفة ورحمة ورهبانية ابتدعوها ما كتبناها عليهم إلا ابتغاء رضوان الله فما رعوها حق رعايتها فآتينا الذين آمنوا منهم أجرهم وكثير منهم فاسقون

translation: O you who believe! Fear Allah and believe in His Messenger, [and] He will [then] give you a double portion of His mercy and make for you a light by which you may walk and forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have reverence for Allah ("fear Allah") and to have faith in His Messenger ("believe in His Messenger"). In return, Allah will bestow a "double portion of His mercy" upon them, granting them guidance and forgiveness. The "light by which you may walk" symbolizes the divine guidance that illuminates the path for believers. The concluding statement affirms that Allah is "Forgiving and Merciful", emphasizing His compassion towards those who turn to Him in faith and repentance.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وآمنوا برسوله يؤتكم كفلين من رحمته ويجعل لكم نورا تمشون به ويغفر لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: So that the People of the Book may know that they have no power over the bounty of Allah, and that [all] bounty is in the hand of Allah; He grants it to whom He wills. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the blessings and favors of Allah are not limited to any particular group, but are in Allah's hands to bestow upon whomever He wills. It serves as a reminder that the People of the Book, such as the Jews and Christians, do not have any control or power over Allah's bounty. Rather, all good comes from Allah, and He alone decides how to distribute His favors. This verse encourages humility and reliance on Allah, as the ultimate source of all blessings and provisions.
orig: لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب ألا يقدرون على شيء من فضل الله وأن الفضل بيد الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: Allah has heard the speech of the one who argues with you, [O Muhammad], concerning her husband and complains to Allah. And Allah hears your dialogue; indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah is aware of the disputes and complaints that people bring to Him. It emphasizes that Allah hears and sees all that transpires, and that He is attentive to the concerns of His servants. The verse suggests that Allah is a just and merciful God who listens to the pleas of those who turn to Him, and that He is capable of resolving conflicts and providing guidance.
orig: قد سمع الله قول التي تجادلك في زوجها وتشتكي إلى الله والله يسمع تحاوركما إن الله سميع بصير

translation: Those of you who make their wives unlawful to them [by declaring them to be like] their mothers - they are not [in fact] their mothers; their mothers are none other than those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they are saying an offensive word and a falsehood, and indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse addresses the practice of "zihar", which was a pre-Islamic custom where a man would declare his wife to be like his mother, effectively divorcing her. The verse clarifies that a wife is not actually the mother of her husband, and that making such a declaration is an offensive and false statement. However, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving, indicating that those who have engaged in this practice can be forgiven if they repent and make amends.
orig: الذين يظاهرون منكم من نسائهم ما هن أمهاتهم إن أمهاتهم إلا اللائي ولدنهم وإنهم ليقولون منكرا من القول وزورا وإن الله لعفو غفور

translation: And those who pronounce zihar from their wives and then [wish to] go back on what they said - then [there must be] the freeing of a slave before they touch one another. That is what you are admonished thereby, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse addresses the practice of "zihar", where a husband would declare his wife to be like the back of his mother, effectively divorcing her. The verse instructs that if a husband wishes to go back on this declaration, he must first free a slave before being intimate with his wife again. This is a form of atonement and serves as a deterrent against such declarations, as Allah is fully aware of our actions.
orig: والذين يظاهرون من نسائهم ثم يعودون لما قالوا فتحرير رقبة من قبل أن يتماسا ذلكم توعظون به والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: But if he cannot find [or afford], then [the expiation is] a fast for two months consecutively before he may touch her. And if one is unable - then for him is a feeding of sixty poor persons. That is for you to believe [completely] in Allah and His Messenger. And those are the limits [set by] Allah, and for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse outlines the expiation or atonement required for a man who has violated his oath or vow not to have sexual relations with his wife. The options provided are: 1) fasting for two consecutive months, 2) feeding sixty poor people, if the person is unable to fast. This expiation is meant to reaffirm one's faith in Allah and His Messenger, and to uphold the boundaries set by Allah. For those who reject these limits, a painful punishment awaits.
orig: فمن لم يجد فصيام شهرين متتابعين من قبل أن يتماسا فمن لم يستطع فإطعام ستين مسكينا ذلك لتؤمنوا بالله ورسوله وتلك حدود الله وللكافرين عذاب أليم

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are abased as those before them were abased. And We have certainly sent down verses [i.e., evidence] with clear proofs, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns those who oppose Allah and His Messenger that they will be abased and humiliated, just as those who came before them were. The verse emphasizes that Allah has sent down clear evidence and signs, yet the disbelievers will face a humiliating punishment for their rejection of the truth.
orig: إن الذين يحادون الله ورسوله كبتوا كما كبت الذين من قبلهم وقد أنزلنا آيات بينات وللكافرين عذاب مهين

translation: The Day when Allah will resurrect them all, then He will inform them of what they did. Allah has enumerated it, while they have forgotten it. And Allah is, over all things, Witness.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Resurrection, when all people will be gathered before Allah and held accountable for their actions in life. Allah has perfect knowledge and record of everything that people have done, even if they have forgotten or neglected it. On that Day, Allah will inform them of their deeds, both good and bad, and nothing will be hidden from Him as He is the All-Knowing Witness over all things.
orig: يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا فينبئهم بما عملوا أحصاه الله ونسوه والله على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Have you not considered that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth? There is no private conversation of three but that He is the fourth of them, nor of five but that He is the sixth of them - and no less than that and no more except that He is with them [in knowledge] wherever they are. Then He will inform them of what they did, on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is to all things Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and His awareness of all that transpires, even the most private conversations and thoughts of His creation. It conveys that Allah is present with His servants, cognizant of their every word and deed, and that He will hold them accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's infinite knowledge and power, and the importance of being mindful of one's conduct, as Allah is always watching and aware.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثة إلا هو رابعهم ولا خمسة إلا هو سادسهم ولا أدنى من ذلك ولا أكثر إلا هو معهم أين ما كانوا ثم ينبئهم بما عملوا يوم القيامة إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Have you not seen those who were forbidden from private conversation, then they return to that which they were forbidden and converse among themselves about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger? And when they come to you, they greet you with that [word] by which Allah has not greeted you and say among themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?" Sufficient for them is Hell, wherein they will [enter to] burn, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who engage in private conversations that involve sinful, aggressive, and disobedient acts, despite being forbidden from doing so. It highlights their hypocrisy in greeting the Prophet with words that Allah has not sanctioned, and their arrogance in questioning why they are not punished for their misdeeds. The interpretation suggests that these individuals will face the consequences of their actions, as Hell is a sufficient punishment for their transgressions.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين نهوا عن النجوى ثم يعودون لما نهوا عنه ويتناجون بالإثم والعدوان ومعصيت الرسول وإذا جاءوك حيوك بما لم يحيك به الله ويقولون في أنفسهم لولا يعذبنا الله بما نقول حسبهم جهنم يصلونها فبئس المصير

translation: O you who believe! When you converse in private, do not speak about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger, but speak about righteousness and piety. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to engage in righteous and pious conversations when they converse in private. It warns against discussing matters related to sin, aggression, and disobedience to the Messenger of Allah. Instead, believers are urged to talk about righteousness and God-consciousness. This is because all people will ultimately be gathered before Allah, and they should be mindful of their actions and words in preparation for that day.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا تناجيتم فلا تتناجوا بالإثم والعدوان ومعصيت الرسول وتناجوا بالبر والتقوى واتقوا الله الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: The [practice of] private conversation is from Satan that he may grieve those who have believed, but he will not harm them at all except by permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against the temptations of Satan, who tries to sow discord and distress among the faithful through private whisperings and gossip. However, the verse reassures the believers that Satan cannot harm them unless Allah permits it. Therefore, the believers should put their trust in Allah and not be swayed by the machinations of Satan.
orig: إنما النجوى من الشيطان ليحزن الذين آمنوا وليس بضارهم شيئا إلا بإذن الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: O you who believe! When it is said to you, "Make room" in assemblies, then make room; Allah will make room for you. And when it is said, "Arise," then arise; Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be considerate and accommodating towards others in social gatherings. It emphasizes the importance of making room for others and being willing to make way, as this will be reciprocated by Allah with His own blessings and provisions. The verse also highlights that those who believe and seek knowledge will be elevated in degrees by Allah, as He is All-Knowing of our actions and intentions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا قيل لكم تفسحوا في المجالس فافسحوا يفسح الله لكم وإذا قيل انشزوا فانشزوا يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: O you who believe! When you consult the Messenger in private, offer a charity before your private consultation. That is better for you and purer. But if you find not [the means] - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to offer a charitable donation before engaging in a private consultation with the Prophet Muhammad. The purpose is to purify the heart and intention, as well as to demonstrate humility and reverence towards the Messenger. Even if one is unable to give charity, the verse reminds that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, emphasizing that the act of consultation itself is not contingent on the ability to give. The overall message is to approach the Prophet with sincerity, humility and a spirit of giving, in order to please Allah and receive His blessings.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ناجيتم الرسول فقدموا بين يدي نجواكم صدقة ذلك خير لكم وأطهر فإن لم تجدوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Do you fear that you will not (be able to) give in charity before your private consultation? So when you do not do it, and Allah has forgiven you, then establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be generous in charitable giving, even before engaging in private discussions. It warns that failure to do so may incur Allah's displeasure, but also emphasizes that Allah is forgiving. The verse then reminds believers of the importance of performing the obligatory acts of worship, such as prayer and paying zakah, as well as obeying Allah and His Messenger. The final statement underscores that Allah is fully aware of our actions.
orig: أأشفقتم أن تقدموا بين يدي نجواكم صدقات فإذ لم تفعلوا وتاب الله عليكم فأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأطيعوا الله ورسوله والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Have you not seen those who take as allies a people upon whom is [the curse of] Allah ? They are neither of you nor of them, and they swear to untruth while they know [they are lying].
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and all believers. It is referring to those who ally themselves with people who have incurred the wrath of Allah, even though they are neither part of the believers nor the disbelievers.
