They swear falsely, fully aware that they are lying. This is a warning against forming alliances with those who have earned Allah's displeasure, as it can lead one astray from the righteous path.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين تولوا قوما غضب الله عليهم ما هم منكم ولا منهم ويحلفون على الكذب وهم يعلمون

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, evil is what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to those who engage in evil and sinful actions. It conveys that Allah has prepared a severe punishment for those who persist in their wrongdoing, as their actions are displeasing to Him. The interpretation suggests that one should refrain from evil deeds and strive to please Allah through righteous conduct.
orig: أعد الله لهم عذابا شديدا إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: They have taken their oaths as a shield and averted [people] from the way of Allah, so for them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who use false oaths and pretenses to shield themselves from the truth and to prevent others from following the path of Allah. By doing so, they have incurred a humiliating punishment from Allah, as they have betrayed their own faith and misled others.
orig: اتخذوا أيمانهم جنة فصدوا عن سبيل الله فلهم عذاب مهين

translation: Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide in it eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that worldly wealth and children cannot protect one from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Judgment. Those who rely on these material possessions and fail to seek Allah's pleasure will be condemned to the eternal torment of Hell. The verse serves as a reminder that true salvation comes only from submitting to Allah and living a righteous life, not from the accumulation of wealth or the presence of offspring.
orig: لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: The Day when Allah will resurrect them all, and they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they will think that they have [some] basis. Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when all people will be resurrected and brought before Allah. On that day, the disbelievers will swear oaths to Allah, just as they had sworn oaths to people in this world, thinking that their oaths will save them. However, Allah declares that they are the liars, as their oaths and excuses will be of no avail on that Day. This emphasizes the importance of sincerity in one's faith and actions, as Allah knows the true intentions of the heart and will judge people accordingly on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا فيحلفون له كما يحلفون لكم ويحسبون أنهم على شيء ألا إنهم هم الكاذبون

translation: The devil has overcome them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah. Those are the party of the devil. Unquestionably, the party of the devil will be the losers.
interpretation: This verse warns against the influence of the devil, who can make people forget the remembrance of Allah. Those who succumb to the devil's temptations become part of his party, destined for failure and loss. The message is to remain steadfast in the remembrance of Allah and not to be deceived by the devil's schemes.
orig: استحوذ عليهم الشيطان فأنساهم ذكر الله أولئك حزب الشيطان ألا إن حزب الشيطان هم الخاسرون

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger - they will be among the most humiliated.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who defy and oppose Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him). It indicates that those who reject the guidance of the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad will be among the most disgraced and humiliated people. The implication is that they will face severe punishment and disgrace in this life and the Hereafter for their defiance and rejection of the truth.
orig: إن الذين يحادون الله ورسوله أولئك في الأذلين

translation: Allah has decreed: "It is I and My messengers who must prevail." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse conveys the certainty of Allah's ultimate victory and the triumph of His messengers. It affirms that Allah has decreed that He and His messengers will prevail, as Allah is all-Powerful and Exalted in Might. This verse instills confidence in the believers that the truth and the righteous cause championed by the messengers of Allah will ultimately succeed, despite any apparent obstacles or challenges they may face.
orig: كتب الله لأغلبن أنا ورسلي إن الله قوي عزيز

translation: You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day having affection for those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their kindred. Those - He has decreed within their hearts faith and supported them with spirit from Him. And We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah - they are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and loyalty to Allah and His Messenger, even above family ties. It states that true believers will not have affection for those who oppose Allah, regardless of their familial relationship. The verse describes how Allah has instilled faith in the hearts of the believers and supported them with His divine spirit. As a result, the believers will be admitted to eternal paradise, where they will be pleased with Allah and He with them. This highlights that the true party of Allah, the successful ones, are those who prioritize their faith above all else.
orig: لا تجد قوما يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر يوادون من حاد الله ورسوله ولو كانوا آباءهم أو أبناءهم أو إخوانهم أو عشيرتهم أولئك كتب في قلوبهم الإيمان وأيدهم بروح منه ويدخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه أولئك حزب الله ألا إن حزب الله هم المفلحون

translation: Exalted is Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over the entire universe. It declares that everything in the heavens and on the earth belongs to Allah, the Almighty and the All-Wise. This highlights the need for humans to submit to Allah and worship Him alone, as He is the only true deity worthy of worship. The verse also suggests that Allah's wisdom and might are beyond human comprehension, and that we should trust in His divine plan and guidance.
orig: سبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: It is He who expelled the ones who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah; but [the decree of] Allah came upon them from where they had not expected, and He cast terror into their hearts [so] they destroyed their houses by their [own] hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O people of vision.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah expelled the disbelievers among the People of the Scripture (the Jews and Christians) from their homes during the first gathering, referring to the early battles between the Muslims and their opponents. The disbelievers did not expect to be forced out, thinking their fortresses would protect them. However, Allah's decree came upon them unexpectedly, instilling terror in their hearts, causing them to destroy their own homes, both by their own hands and with the help of the believers. This serves as a lesson and warning to those who have insight and vision, that no one can escape the will of Allah.
orig: هو الذي أخرج الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب من ديارهم لأول الحشر ما ظننتم أن يخرجوا وظنوا أنهم مانعتهم حصونهم من الله فأتاهم الله من حيث لم يحتسبوا وقذف في قلوبهم الرعب يخربون بيوتهم بأيديهم وأيدي المؤمنين فاعتبروا يا أولي الأبصار

translation: And if it were not that Allah had decreed exile for them, He would have punished them in [this] world, and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the exile or displacement of a group of people was a decreed punishment from Allah, rather than a random occurrence. If Allah had not ordained this exile, He would have punished them directly in this world. However, their ultimate punishment will be in the Hereafter, where they will face the torment of the Fire.
orig: ولولا أن كتب الله عليهم الجلاء لعذبهم في الدنيا ولهم في الآخرة عذاب النار

translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger - indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who defy and disobey Allah and His Messenger will face severe consequences. It underscores the gravity of opposing the divine commandments and the authority of the Prophet. The strong language used, "Allah is severe in penalty", conveys the message that defiance of Allah and His Messenger will not go unpunished, and that the punishment will be severe and uncompromising.
orig: ذلك بأنهم شاقوا الله ورسوله ومن يشاق الله فإن الله شديد العقاب

translation: Whatever you have cut down of [their] palm trees or left standing on their trunks - it was by permission of Allah and so He would disgrace the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the actions of the Muslims during a military campaign. It states that any destruction or preservation of the enemy's palm trees was done with Allah's permission, in order to disgrace the sinful and disobedient opponents. The interpretation is that Allah sanctions the strategic use of resources, even destruction, when it is necessary to defeat those who defy His laws and commands.
orig: ما قطعتم من لينة أو تركتموها قائمة على أصولها فبإذن الله وليخزي الفاسقين

translation: And whatever [wealth or war gains] Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the cities - it is for Allah and for the Messenger and for [his] near relatives and orphans and the [stranded] traveler - so that it will not be a perpetual distribution among the rich from among you. And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle that the spoils of war and other wealth acquired by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) belong to Allah and should be distributed according to His commands, rather than being kept by the wealthy. It emphasizes that the Prophet's instructions should be followed, and that one should fear Allah, as He has the power to punish those who disobey His commands.
orig: وما أفاء الله على رسوله منهم فما أوجفتم عليه من خيل ولا ركاب ولكن الله يسلط رسله على من يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Whatever [wealth] Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the cities - it is for Allah and for the Messenger and for [his] near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the [stranded] traveler, so that it will not be a perpetual distribution among the rich from among you. And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse outlines the proper distribution of wealth and resources that have been acquired through peaceful means, such as treaties or voluntary submission. It establishes that these resources belong to Allah and should be used for the benefit of the community, including the Messenger, his relatives, orphans, the needy, and travelers. The goal is to prevent the concentration of wealth among the rich and to ensure a more equitable distribution. Muslims are instructed to accept what the Messenger has given them and to refrain from what he has forbidden, out of reverence for Allah and His commands.
orig: ما أفاء الله على رسوله من أهل القرى فلله وللرسول ولذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل كي لا يكون دولة بين الأغنياء منكم وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا واتقوا الله إن الله شديد العقاب

translation: For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and [separated from] their wealth, seeking bounty from Allah and [His] approval and supporting Allah and His Messenger, [they are] the truthful.
interpretation: This verse refers to the early Muslim emigrants who were forced to leave their homes and possessions in Mecca due to persecution, and instead sought refuge in Medina. It highlights their sincerity in their faith, as they prioritized their loyalty to Allah and the Prophet Muhammad over their own material comforts and wellbeing. The verse praises them as "the truthful" for their steadfastness and commitment to the cause of Islam, even in the face of adversity.
orig: للفقراء المهاجرين الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم وأموالهم يبتغون فضلا من الله ورضوانا وينصرون الله ورسوله أولئك هم الصادقون

translation: And [also for] those who were settled in al-Madinah and [adopted] the faith before them. They love those who emigrated to them and find not any want in their breasts of what the emigrants were given but give [them] preference over themselves, even though they are in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse praises the early Muslim community in Medina who welcomed and supported the emigrants from Mecca. It highlights their selflessness and generosity, as they prioritized the needs of others over their own, even when they themselves were in need. The key message is that true success and prosperity come from overcoming one's own selfish desires and greed, and instead focusing on the welfare of the community. This spirit of sacrifice and altruism is a core Islamic virtue.
orig: والذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم يحبون من هاجر إليهم ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And those who came after them say, "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts [any] resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of forgiveness and unity among believers. It highlights the humility and supplication of those who come after the earlier believers, asking Allah to forgive them and their brothers who preceded them in faith. The verse also underscores the need to avoid harboring any resentment or ill-will towards fellow believers, recognizing that Allah is Kind and Merciful. This encourages a spirit of brotherhood, mutual understanding, and compassion within the community of faith.
orig: والذين جاءوا من بعدهم يقولون ربنا اغفر لنا ولإخواننا الذين سبقونا بالإيمان ولا تجعل في قلوبنا غلا للذين آمنوا ربنا إنك رءوف رحيم

translation: Have you not seen those who practice hypocrisy, saying to their brothers [i.e., associates] who have disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, "If you are expelled, we will surely go out with you, and we will not obey, in regard to you, anyone - ever; and if you are fought, we will surely aid you." And Allah testifies that they are liars.
interpretation: This verse is describing the hypocrites, who outwardly profess faith in Islam but inwardly harbor disbelief. It shows how they make false promises to the disbelievers among the People of the Scripture (i.e., the Jews and Christians), claiming they will support them if they are expelled or attacked, when in reality they are liars who have no intention of fulfilling these promises. The verse emphasizes that Allah knows the truth about their hypocrisy and deception.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين نافقوا يقولون لإخوانهم الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب لئن أخرجتم لنخرجن معكم ولا نطيع فيكم أحدا أبدا وإن قوتلتم لننصرنكم والله يشهد إنهم لكاذبون

translation: If they are expelled, they will not go out with them, and if they are fought, they will not be helped. And if they are given victory, they will [then] turn their backs [in flight]. Then they will not be aided.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who pretend to be believers but in reality do not have true faith. It is stating that if the believers were to expel the hypocrites, the hypocrites would not go out with them. And if the believers were to fight against the disbelievers, the hypocrites would not help the believers. Even if the believers were to gain victory, the hypocrites would turn and flee, and they would not be aided or supported. This highlights the duplicity and cowardice of the hypocrites, who do not truly stand with the believers in times of trial and tribulation.
orig: لئن أخرجوا لا يخرجون معهم ولئن قوتلوا لا ينصرونهم ولئن نصروهم ليولن الأدبار ثم لا ينصرون

translation: You (Muhammad) are more worthy of being feared in their hearts than Allah. That is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being addressed have a greater fear and reverence for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) than they do for Allah. This is because they lack understanding and true faith, and are more concerned with worldly matters and social status than with submitting to the will of Allah. The verse highlights the importance of developing a deep and sincere relationship with Allah, rather than being preoccupied with the opinions and perceptions of others.
orig: لأنتم أشد رهبة في صدورهم من الله ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: They will not fight you all except within fortified cities or from behind walls. Their violence among themselves is severe. You think they are together, but their hearts are diverse. That is because they are a people who do not reason.
interpretation: This verse is describing the disbelievers and their tactics in fighting against the Muslims. It suggests that the disbelievers will not engage in open combat with the Muslims, but will instead resort to fighting from within fortified cities or from behind walls. Their internal conflicts and divisions are also highlighted, as the verse states that "their violence among themselves is severe" and "their hearts are diverse". This is because they are a people who do not use their reason and understanding to comprehend the truth of Islam.
orig: لا يقاتلونكم جميعا إلا في قرى محصنة أو من وراء جدر بأسهم بينهم شديد تحسبهم جميعا وقلوبهم شتى ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعقلون

translation: Like those before them, they have tasted the evil consequences of their affair, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is drawing a parallel between the fate of the previous disbelievers and the fate of the current disbelievers. Just as the previous generations faced the dire consequences of their rejection of the truth and disobedience to God, the current generation will also face a painful punishment for their similar actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who persist in their disbelief and wrongdoing, reminding them that they will ultimately be held accountable for their choices and actions.
orig: كمثل الذين من قبلهم قريبا ذاقوا وبال أمرهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Like the example of Satan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse draws a parallel between the actions of Satan and the disbelievers. Satan tempts humans to disbelieve in Allah, but when they succumb to his temptation, he disassociates himself from them, claiming that he fears Allah. This highlights the deceptive nature of Satan, who leads people astray but then abandons them when they face the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to believers to be wary of Satan's schemes and to remain steadfast in their faith in Allah.
orig: كمثل الشيطان إذ قال للإنسان اكفر فلما كفر قال إني بريء منك إني أخاف الله رب العالمين

translation: And the result of their affair was that they were in the Fire, abiding eternally therein. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of wrongdoing and injustice. Those who persist in their wrongful ways will ultimately face eternal punishment in the Fire. This serves as a warning to all people to refrain from oppression, injustice, and other forms of wrongdoing, as they will be held accountable for their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: فكان عاقبتهما أنهما في النار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء الظالمين

translation: O you who believe! Fear Allah and let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and to prepare for the Hereafter. It calls on them to "fear Allah" - to be conscious of Allah and to obey His commands. The verse also instructs each person to "look to what it has put forth for tomorrow" - to reflect on their deeds and to ensure that they are doing good in preparation for the Day of Judgment. The final part of the verse reminds that "Allah is Acquainted with what you do" - that Allah is all-knowing and will hold people accountable for their actions. The overall message is to live a righteous life, be mindful of one's deeds, and prepare for the Hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله ولتنظر نفس ما قدمت لغد واتقوا الله إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: And do not be like those who forgot [i.e., abandoned] Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse warns against becoming like those who neglect or abandon their relationship with Allah. When people turn away from Allah, they end up losing sight of their own true nature and purpose in life. They become "defiantly disobedient" - living in a state of heedlessness and rebellion against the guidance of Allah. The lesson is to remain steadfast in remembering Allah, as this is essential for maintaining one’s own spiritual well-being and moral compass.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين نسوا الله فأنساهم أنفسهم أولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: Not equal are the companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise. The companions of Paradise - they are the attainers [of success].
interpretation: This verse draws a clear distinction between the eternal state of the denizens of Hell and the inhabitants of Paradise. The former, referred to as "companions of the Fire", are in a state of eternal punishment and loss, while the latter, described as "companions of Paradise", have attained the ultimate success and salvation. This highlights the profound consequences of one's choices and actions in this life, and the stark contrast between the fates of the righteous and the wicked in the Hereafter.
orig: لا يستوي أصحاب النار وأصحاب الجنة أصحاب الجنة هم الفائزون

translation: If We had sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of Allah. And these examples We present to the people that they might reflect.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound impact and power of the Qur'an. If the Qur'an were to be revealed upon a mountain, the mountain would become humbled and split apart out of reverence and fear for Allah. This is meant to illustrate the immense spiritual weight and transformative nature of the Qur'anic message. The verse encourages people to reflect deeply on the Qur'an and its teachings, so that they may gain wisdom and understanding.
orig: لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل لرأيته خاشعا متصدعا من خشية الله وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس لعلهم يتفكرون

translation: He is Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of Allah, the Almighty. It affirms that He is the only true God, the Knower of all that is hidden and all that is manifest. He is the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful, conveying the boundless and compassionate nature of Allah's divine attributes. This verse serves as a reminder to worship and submit to Allah alone, the Supreme Creator and Sustainer of the universe.
orig: هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو عالم الغيب والشهادة هو الرحمن الرحيم

translation: He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Perfection, the Bestower of Faith, the Overseer, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Superior. Exalted is Allah above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique and supreme nature of Allah. It highlights the key attributes of Allah, such as being the only true God, the Sovereign, the Pure, the Giver of Faith, the Overseer, the Mighty, the Compeller, and the Superior. The verse also reaffirms that Allah is exalted above any partners or associates that people may ascribe to Him. This serves to reinforce the core Islamic belief in the oneness and unparalleled nature of Allah.
orig: هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر سبحان الله عما يشركون

translation: He is Allah, the Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner; to Him belong the best names. Whatever is in the heavens and earth is exalting Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the attributes and names of Allah, the one true God. It highlights that He is the Creator, Inventor, and Fashioner of all things, and that He has the best and most beautiful names. Everything in the heavens and the earth praises and glorifies Him, for He is the Exalted in Might and the Wise. This verse affirms the absolute sovereignty, power, and wisdom of Allah, and calls upon believers to worship and submit to Him alone.
orig: هو الله الخالق البارئ المصور له الأسماء الحسنى يسبح له ما في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O you who believe! Do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, offering them [your] affection while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth, [having driven out] the Messenger and yourselves [only] because you believe in Allah , your Lord. If you have come out for jihad in My cause and seeking [My] approval, [take them not as friends]. You confide to them affection, but I am most knowing of what you have concealed and what you have declared. And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way.
interpretation: This verse cautions believers against taking the enemies of Allah and their own enemies as allies or confidants. It emphasizes that these disbelievers have rejected the truth that the Prophet brought, and have even driven out the Prophet and the believers. The verse reminds the believers that they have only come out for jihad in Allah's cause and to seek His pleasure. Taking these enemies as friends and confiding in them affection is forbidden, as Allah knows what the believers have concealed and what they have made public. Whoever does this has certainly strayed from the right path.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا عدوي وعدوكم أولياء تلقون إليهم بالمودة وقد كفروا بما جاءكم من الحق يخرجون الرسول وإياكم أن تؤمنوا بالله ربكم إن كنتم خرجتم جهادا في سبيلي وابتغاء مرضاتي تسرون إليهم بالمودة وأنا أعلم بما أخفيتم وما أعلنتم ومن يفعله منكم فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: If they gain the upper hand over you, they would behave to you as enemies, and stretch forth their hands and their tongues against you with evil, and they desire that you should disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers that if their enemies gain power over them, the enemies will become hostile and use both physical and verbal means to harm the believers. The enemies will wish for the believers to renounce their faith in God. This serves as a caution to the believers to be vigilant against the plots and schemes of their adversaries, who seek to undermine their faith and allegiance to God.
orig: إن يثقفوكم يكونوا لكم أعداء ويبسطوا إليكم أيديهم وألسنتهم بالسوء وودوا لو تكفرون

translation: Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. [Allah] will judge between you, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, one's family ties and children will not be of any avail. The only thing that will matter is one's own deeds and actions, which Allah is fully aware of. It serves as a reminder that we should focus on our own righteous conduct and not rely solely on our familial relationships or offspring to save us on the Day of Reckoning. The verse underscores the importance of individual accountability before Allah.
orig: لن تنفعكم أرحامكم ولا أولادكم يوم القيامة يفصل بينكم والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: There has already been for you an excellent pattern in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are disassociated from you and whatever you worship other than Allah. We have denied you, and there has appeared between us and you animosity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone" - except for the saying of Abraham to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you, but I have not [power to do] for you anything against Allah." [Through this], our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have returned, and to You is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary conduct of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) and his followers, who disassociated themselves from the polytheism and idolatry of their people. They declared their belief in the Oneness of God and their rejection of worshipping anything besides Him. This stance led to a lasting enmity between them and their people. However, the verse also mentions that Abraham sought forgiveness for his father, despite his father's rejection of the true faith, demonstrating that one should maintain familial ties even in the face of religious differences. The verse encourages the believers to emulate the steadfastness and reliance on God shown by Abraham and his companions, as they turned to God alone for guidance and support.
orig: قد كانت لكم أسوة حسنة في إبراهيم والذين معه إذ قالوا لقومهم إنا برآء منكم ومما تعبدون من دون الله كفرنا بكم وبدا بيننا وبينكم العداوة والبغضاء أبدا حتى تؤمنوا بالله وحده إلا قول إبراهيم لأبيه لأستغفرن لك وما أملك لك من الله من شيء ربنا عليك توكلنا وإليك أنبنا وإليك المصير

translation: Our Lord, do not make us [objects of] trial for the disbelieving people and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to Allah, asking Him not to make the believers a source of trial or temptation for the disbelievers, and to forgive the believers. The interpretation is that the believers are seeking Allah's protection from being used by the disbelievers as a means to test or tempt the faith of the believers. They are also seeking Allah's forgiveness, acknowledging that He is the Almighty and the Wise, and that He alone can provide the believers with the guidance and strength they need.
orig: ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للذين كفروا واغفر لنا ربنا إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern for anyone whose hope is in Allah and the Last Day and [who] remembers Allah often.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to follow the example and teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a model of righteous conduct. By emulating the Prophet's life and actions, one can find guidance in seeking the pleasure of Allah and attaining success in the Hereafter. The verse also warns against turning away from this path, as Allah is the Self-Sufficient and the Praiseworthy.
orig: لقد كان لكم فيهم أسوة حسنة لمن كان يرجو الله واليوم الآخر ومن يتول فإن الله هو الغني الحميد

translation: Perhaps Allah will put, between you and those to whom you were enemies among them, affection. And Allah is competent, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse expresses the hope that even between those who were once enemies, Allah may create a sense of affection and goodwill. It highlights Allah's power and ability to bring about such reconciliation, as well as His forgiving and merciful nature. The interpretation suggests that even the most difficult relationships can be mended through the grace of Allah, and that one should have hope in His ability to bring about positive change, even in the most challenging of circumstances.
orig: عسى الله أن يجعل بينكم وبين الذين عاديتم منهم مودة والله قدير والله غفور رحيم

translation: Allah does not forbid you from dealing kindly and justly with those who have not fought you because of your religion and have not driven you out of your homes. Verily, Allah loves those who are just.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to treat with kindness and justice those who have not fought against them or driven them from their homes due to their religion. It emphasizes that Allah loves those who are just and fair in their dealings, even towards those who are not of the same faith. The interpretation suggests that Muslims should not discriminate against or mistreat non-Muslims who do not actively oppose them, but rather should strive to maintain peaceful and just relationships.
orig: لا ينهاكم الله عن الذين لم يقاتلوكم في الدين ولم يخرجوكم من دياركم أن تبروهم وتقسطوا إليهم إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: Allah only forbids you from those who fight you because of your religion and expel you from your homes and aid in your expulsion - [forbids] that you make allies of them. And whoever makes allies of them, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims not to ally with or support those who fight against them because of their faith, who expel them from their homes, and who aid in their expulsion. It emphasizes that those who do so are the wrongdoers, and that Muslims should not become their allies. The verse establishes a clear boundary between Muslims and those who persecute them for their religion, prohibiting any alliance or support for the latter.
orig: إنما ينهاكم الله عن الذين قاتلوكم في الدين وأخرجوكم من دياركم وظاهروا على إخراجكم أن تولوهم ومن يتولهم فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. Allah is most knowing as to their faith. And if you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers; they are not lawful [wives] for them, nor are they lawful [husbands] for them. But give the [disbelieving] husbands what they have spent. And there is no blame upon you if you marry them when you have given them their [due] dowries. And hold not to marriage bonds with disbelieving women, but ask for what you have spent and let them [i.e., the disbelievers] ask for what they have spent. That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the status of believing women who migrate to the Muslim community. It instructs the believers to examine the faith of these women to ensure they are true believers. If they are found to be believers, they should not be returned to the disbelievers, as the believing women are not lawful for the disbelievers, nor are the disbelievers lawful for them. The verse also instructs the believers to pay back the dowries that the disbelieving husbands had given to their wives. The believers are then permitted to marry these women, provided they have given them their dowries. The verse emphasizes that the believers should not hold onto marriage bonds with disbelieving women, and both parties should seek reimbursement of what they had spent. This is the judgment of Allah, who is all-knowing and wise.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا جاءكم المؤمنات مهاجرات فامتحنوهن الله أعلم بإيمانهن فإن علمتموهن مؤمنات فلا ترجعوهن إلى الكفار لا هن حل لهم ولا هم يحلون لهن وآتوهم ما أنفقوا ولا جناح عليكم أن تنكحوهن إذا آتيتموهن أجورهن ولا تمسكوا بعصم الكوافر واسألوا ما أنفقتم وليسألوا ما أنفقوا ذلكم حكم الله يحكم بينكم والله عليم حكيم

translation: And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and you have an accession (by the coming over of a woman from the other side), then pay to those whose wives have gone away the equivalent of what they had spent (on their dower). And fear Allah in Whom you believe.
interpretation: This verse addresses a situation where some Muslim women have left their husbands and joined the disbelievers. It instructs the Muslim men whose wives have defected to pay the equivalent of the dowry they had given to those women, as compensation. The verse also emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah, in Whom the believers have faith.
orig: وإن فاتكم شيء من أزواجكم إلى الكفار فعاقبتم فآتوا الذين ذهبت أزواجهم مثل ما أنفقوا واتقوا الله الذي أنتم به مؤمنون

translation: O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor will they steal, nor will they commit unlawful sexual intercourse, nor will they kill their children, nor will they bring forth a slander they have invented between their arms and legs, nor will they disobey you in what is right - then accept their pledge and ask forgiveness for them of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the pledge that believing women make to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It establishes the key principles of faith and righteous conduct that Muslim women commit to upholding. The pledge includes: worshipping Allah alone, abstaining from theft, adultery, and infanticide, avoiding false accusations, and obeying the Prophet in all lawful matters. In accepting this pledge, the Prophet is instructed to seek Allah's forgiveness for the women, as Allah is the Most Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: يا أيها النبي إذا جاءك المؤمنات يبايعنك على أن لا يشركن بالله شيئا ولا يسرقن ولا يزنين ولا يقتلن أولادهن ولا يأتين ببهتان يفترينه بين أيديهن وأرجلهن ولا يعصينك في معروف فبايعهن واستغفر لهن الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who believe! Do not take as allies a people upon whom is [the decree of] Allah 's anger. They have despaired of [any happiness in] the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of [meeting] the companions of the Graves.
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against aligning themselves with those who have incurred the wrath of Allah. It suggests that such people have lost all hope in the Hereafter, just as the disbelievers have lost hope in meeting the inhabitants of the graves. The interpretation is that the believers should be cautious in their associations and not be influenced by those who have been condemned by Allah, as this could jeopardize their own faith and salvation.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتولوا قوما غضب الله عليهم قد يئسوا من الآخرة كما يئس الكفار من أصحاب القبور

translation: Exalted is Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme greatness and power of Allah, the Creator of the entire universe. It declares that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, and that He alone is the Mighty and Wise. This serves to remind us of Allah's absolute sovereignty and the need to submit to Him in all aspects of our lives.
orig: سبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O you who believe! Why do you say what you do not do?
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to practice what they preach and to align their words with their actions. It is a call to be authentic and consistent, avoiding hypocrisy or saying things that they do not intend to follow through on. The verse emphasizes the importance of living up to one's professed beliefs and not merely paying lip service to them.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون

translation: Most hateful is it in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do.
interpretation: This verse condemns hypocrisy and the disconnect between one's words and actions. It emphasizes that Allah greatly dislikes when people claim to believe or support something, but then fail to put those beliefs into practice. The verse encourages individuals to strive for consistency between their speech and their deeds, and to avoid merely paying lip service to virtuous ideals without the accompanying commitment and follow-through.
orig: كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون

translation: Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row as though they are a [single] structure joined [firmly].
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to unite and fight together in the cause of Allah, as a cohesive and disciplined force. The metaphor of a "structure joined [firmly]" suggests that when Muslims stand together in battle, their unity and coordination make them stronger and more effective. The interpretation is that Allah loves and rewards those who fight for His cause with this level of unity and determination.
orig: إن الله يحب الذين يقاتلون في سبيله صفا كأنهم بنيان مرصوص

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Moses said to his people, "O my people, why do you harm me while you know that I am the messenger of Allah to you?" And when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection and hostility that the prophet Moses faced from his own people, despite them knowing that he was a messenger of Allah. It shows how the people's own deviation and disobedience led Allah to turn their hearts away from the truth. This serves as a warning that those who persist in defiance and wickedness will be deprived of Allah's guidance, as He does not guide those who stubbornly reject the truth.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم لم تؤذونني وقد تعلمون أني رسول الله إليكم فلما زاغوا أزاغ الله قلوبهم والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, 'O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad.' But when he came to them with clear evidences, they said, 'This is obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse describes how Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) informed the Israelites that he was a messenger of God, confirming the Torah and bringing good news of a prophet to come after him, whose name would be Ahmad (another name for Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him). However, when Prophet Jesus brought clear proofs, the Israelites rejected him and accused him of practicing magic. This verse highlights the rejection of God's messengers by some people, even in the face of clear evidence, and the importance of accepting the truth with an open mind.
orig: وإذ قال عيسى ابن مريم يا بني إسرائيل إني رسول الله إليكم مصدقا لما بين يدي من التوراة ومبشرا برسول يأتي من بعدي اسمه أحمد فلما جاءهم بالبينات قالوا هذا سحر مبين

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah while he is being invited to Islam? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who knowingly fabricate lies and falsehoods about Allah, the Almighty, while claiming to be followers of Islam. It emphasizes that Allah does not guide those who engage in such unjust and deceitful behavior, as they have strayed from the true path of Islam. The verse serves as a warning to those who would misrepresent the teachings of Islam for their own selfish motives, and encourages believers to be truthful and steadfast in their faith.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله الكذب وهو يدعى إلى الإسلام والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that the disbelievers may try to suppress the truth of Islam, but their efforts will be in vain. Allah's light, which represents the guidance and truth of the Qur'an, will prevail no matter how hard the disbelievers try to extinguish it. The verse emphasizes that Allah's plan will come to fruition, and the truth will ultimately triumph, even if the disbelievers find it unpalatable.
orig: يريدون ليطفئوا نور الله بأفواههم والله متم نوره ولو كره الكافرون

translation: It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, although those who associate others with Allah dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has sent His Messenger, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), with the true guidance and religion of Islam to prevail over all other religions, even if the polytheists and disbelievers object to it. The message of Islam is destined to spread and triumph, as it represents the absolute truth revealed by Allah. This is a reassurance to the believers that their faith will ultimately be victorious, despite any opposition they may face.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون

translation: O you who believe, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?
interpretation: This verse is an invitation from Allah to the believers to engage in a 'transaction' that will save them from a painful punishment in the Hereafter. The 'transaction' refers to the act of believing in Allah, following His commands, and doing good deeds. By doing so, the believers will be saved from the torment of the Afterlife and will instead be rewarded with eternal bliss in Paradise.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا هل أدلكم على تجارة تنجيكم من عذاب أليم

translation: You believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you should know.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have faith in Allah and His Messenger, and to strive in the cause of Allah through their wealth and lives. The interpretation is that this is the best course of action for the believers, if they understand the true value and benefits of such an approach.
orig: تؤمنون بالله ورسوله وتجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالكم وأنفسكم ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: He will forgive you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow and good, pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eternity. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse promises forgiveness of sins and entry into the eternal Gardens of Paradise for those who believe in and submit to God. The key message is that through God's mercy and grace, believers will be rewarded with the ultimate success and bliss of Paradise. This emphasizes the importance of seeking God's forgiveness and doing righteous deeds to attain this great reward in the Hereafter.
orig: يغفر لكم ذنوبكم ويدخلكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And [there is] another [favor] that you love - victory from Allah and an imminent conquest; and give good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse promises the believers two additional blessings that they will love - victory from Allah and a coming conquest. The "victory from Allah" refers to the help and support that Allah will provide to the believers, allowing them to triumph over their enemies. The "imminent conquest" likely refers to the expansion of Islamic rule and the spread of the faith. This verse encourages the believers by assuring them of Allah's assistance and the eventual success of their cause, which should fill them with joy and hope.
orig: وأخرى تحبونها نصر من الله وفتح قريب وبشر المؤمنين

translation: O you who believe! Be helpers of Allah, as said Jesus, son of Mary, to the disciples, "Who are my helpers to (the cause of) Allah?" The disciples said, "We are the helpers of Allah." Then a faction of the Children of Israel believed and a faction disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to be helpers and supporters of Allah's cause, just as the disciples of Jesus (peace be upon him) declared themselves to be. It highlights how a group from among the Children of Israel believed in the message, while another group rejected it. As a result, Allah supported the believers against their disbelieving opponents, allowing them to prevail. The key message is the importance of being steadfast supporters of Allah's religion and cause, as this leads to divine assistance and victory.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا أنصار الله كما قال عيسى ابن مريم للحواريين من أنصاري إلى الله قال الحواريون نحن أنصار الله فآمنت طائفة من بني إسرائيل وكفرت طائفة فأيدنا الذين آمنوا على عدوهم فأصبحوا ظاهرين

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and the earth exalts Allah. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal worship and glorification of Allah by all of creation - the heavens, the earth, and everything within them. It highlights that Allah is the Sovereign, the Pure, the Mighty, and the Wise. This indicates that all of existence is subject to Allah's dominion and that He alone is worthy of worship and praise, as He possesses the attributes of perfection, power, and wisdom.
orig: يسبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض الملك القدوس العزيز الحكيم

translation: It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although they were before in clear error.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), who was sent by God to the unlettered people of Arabia. The verse highlights the following key points: 1) God sent a Messenger from among the unlettered people themselves, making him relatable and accessible to them. 2) This Messenger (Muhammad) recites God's verses to the people, purifying and teaching them the Book (the Qur'an) and wisdom. 3) Prior to the Prophet's mission, the people were in a state of clear misguidance and error, but through the guidance of the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet, they were led out of that darkness.
orig: هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم يتلو عليهم آياته ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين

translation: And [there are] others among them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have not yet embraced the faith, but will do so in the future. It emphasizes that Allah, the Exalted in Might and the Wise, is in control of all things and will guide those who have not yet accepted the message to the right path in due time.
orig: وآخرين منهم لما يلحقوا بهم وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the blessings and favors bestowed by Allah are a result of His divine will and grace, not something that can be earned or demanded by human beings. It reminds us that Allah is the ultimate source of all bounty and that He bestows His favor upon whomever He chooses, out of His infinite wisdom and mercy. This verse encourages us to be grateful for the blessings we receive, and to recognize that they are a gift from Allah, rather than something we are entitled to.
orig: ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not take it on is like that of a donkey who carries volumes [of books]. Wretched is the example of the people who deny the signs of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse draws a metaphor between those who were entrusted with the Torah (the Jews) but did not act upon its teachings, and a donkey that carries books without understanding their content. The verse condemns those who received divine guidance but failed to live by it, and instead rejected the signs (verses) of Allah. The interpretation is that true guidance comes from not just possessing knowledge, but putting it into practice. Those who neglect or deny Allah's revelations will not receive His guidance and are considered wrongdoers.
orig: مثل الذين حملوا التوراة ثم لم يحملوها كمثل الحمار يحمل أسفارا بئس مثل القوم الذين كذبوا بآيات الله والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Say, "O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of Allah, excluding [all] the people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the Jews who claimed to be the exclusive allies and chosen people of God, excluding others. The verse challenges them to wish for death if they are truly sincere in their claim, as wishing for death is a test of one's conviction in their faith and closeness to God. The implication is that their claim of being God's chosen people is false, and they should be willing to face the consequences of their false claim if they are truly confident in their position.
orig: قل يا أيها الذين هادوا إن زعمتم أنكم أولياء لله من دون الناس فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And they will never wish for it, ever, because of what their hands have put forth. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the wrongdoers will never wish for death or the Hereafter, because they are aware of the consequences of their misdeeds. Their actions have condemned them, and they know that Allah is fully aware of their transgressions. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in wrongdoing, reminding them that they cannot escape the reckoning of Allah, who is All-Knowing.
orig: ولا يتمنونه أبدا بما قدمت أيديهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: Say, "Indeed, the death from which you flee - indeed, it will meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you about what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that death is inevitable and that no one can escape it. It reminds us that we will all eventually return to Allah, the All-Knowing, who is aware of both the seen and unseen realms. On that day, He will inform us about our actions and hold us accountable for what we have done in this life. This serves as a reminder to live our lives in a way that pleases Allah, as we will all be held responsible for our deeds.
orig: قل إن الموت الذي تفرون منه فإنه ملاقيكم ثم تردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who believe! When the call is proclaimed to prayer on Friday (the day of congregational prayer), hasten earnestly to the Remembrance of Allah, and leave off business (and traffic): That is best for you if you but knew.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to prioritize the remembrance of Allah and attending congregational prayers on Fridays over worldly affairs and commercial activities. It emphasizes that this is the best course of action for the believers, if they only knew the true value and importance of this act of worship.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله وذروا البيع ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to engage in worldly pursuits and economic activities after fulfilling their religious obligations, such as the obligatory prayers. It emphasizes the importance of seeking the bounty and provision of Allah, as well as remembering and glorifying Him frequently, in order to attain success and prosperity both in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: فإذا قضيت الصلاة فانتشروا في الأرض وابتغوا من فضل الله واذكروا الله كثيرا لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And when they see a transaction or a diversion, [O Muhammad], they turn away to it and leave you standing. Say, "What is with Allah is better than diversion and than a transaction, and Allah is the best of providers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing the remembrance of Allah over worldly pursuits such as business transactions or entertainment. It cautions against being distracted by these temporary pleasures and encourages believers to focus on the eternal rewards that Allah has in store. The interpretation suggests that the true and lasting sustenance comes from Allah, who is the best provider, rather than from the fleeting pleasures of this world.
orig: وإذا رأوا تجارة أو لهوا انفضوا إليها وتركوك قائما قل ما عند الله خير من اللهو ومن التجارة والله خير الرازقين

translation: When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceitful nature of the hypocrites, who outwardly profess belief in the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) but inwardly harbor doubts and opposition. Despite their false claims, Allah knows the truth about the Prophet's prophethood, and He will expose the hypocrisy of those who try to undermine it. The verse serves as a warning against the danger of hypocrisy and a reminder that Allah's knowledge and judgment are supreme.
orig: إذا جاءك المنافقون قالوا نشهد إنك لرسول الله والله يعلم إنك لرسوله والله يشهد إن المنافقين لكاذبون

translation: They have taken their oaths as a cover, so they have averted [people] from the way of Allah. Indeed, it was evil that they were doing.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who use oaths and religious pretenses as a means to conceal their true intentions and actions, which are in fact harmful and against the way of Allah. It suggests that such individuals are engaged in evil deeds, despite their outward display of piety or righteousness.
orig: اتخذوا أيمانهم جنة فصدوا عن سبيل الله إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so a seal was set upon their hearts and they do not understand.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who initially had faith, but then later turned away from it and rejected it. The verse suggests that their hearts were sealed, meaning they lost the ability to comprehend the truth and understand the message of Islam. This is a consequence of their own actions in first believing and then disbelieving, which resulted in their hearts being hardened and their minds being closed to the guidance of God.
orig: ذلك بأنهم آمنوا ثم كفروا فطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يفقهون

translation: And when you see them, their bodies please you, and if they speak, you listen to their speech. [They are] as if they were pieces of wood propped up - they think that every call is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse warns against being deceived by the outward appearance and eloquent speech of the hypocrites, who pretend to be believers but are inwardly enemies of the faith. Their bodies may seem impressive, and their words may sound persuasive, but they are like lifeless wooden posts, having no true substance or sincerity. They are paranoid, seeing every call to the truth as a threat against them. The verse urges the believers to be cautious of such people and to recognize them as the true enemies, seeking divine help to expose their deception.
orig: وإذا رأيتهم تعجبك أجسامهم وإن يقولوا تسمع لقولهم كأنهم خشب مسندة يحسبون كل صيحة عليهم هم العدو فاحذرهم قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون

translation: And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to [the words of] the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turning away from you in aversion.
interpretation: This verse describes the attitude of the hypocrites when they are called to repent and seek forgiveness from Allah through the Messenger. Instead of heeding the call, they turn away arrogantly, refusing to submit to the guidance of the Messenger. This verse highlights the stubborn and prideful nature of the hypocrites, who are unwilling to acknowledge their sins and seek Allah's forgiveness.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا يستغفر لكم رسول الله لووا رءوسهم ورأيتهم يصدون وهم مستكبرون

translation: It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who persistently reject faith and engage in sinful behavior will not be forgiven by Allah, regardless of whether the Prophet (peace be upon him) asks for their forgiveness or not. Allah's guidance is only for those who are willing to submit to Him and turn away from their transgressions, not for those who stubbornly persist in their defiance and disobedience.
orig: سواء عليهم أستغفرت لهم أم لم تستغفر لهم لن يغفر الله لهم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those [i.e., the believers] with the Messenger of Allah so that they will disperse." And to Allah belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who discourage others from spending in the cause of Allah and supporting the Messenger. They argue that by not spending, the believers will eventually disperse and leave the Messenger. However, the verse emphasizes that all the treasures of the heavens and the earth belong to Allah, and it is He who provides for all. The hypocrites fail to understand this fundamental truth and instead try to undermine the believers' support for the Messenger.
orig: هم الذين يقولون لا تنفقوا على من عند رسول الله حتى ينفضوا ولله خزائن السماوات والأرض ولكن المنافقين لا يفقهون

translation: They say, "If we return to Medina, the more honored [for power] will surely expel therefrom the more humble." But to Allah belongs [all] honor, and to His Messenger, and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the hypocrites who were making claims about the people of Medina. They were saying that if they were to return to Medina, the more powerful and influential people would expel the weaker ones. However, the verse states that all honor and power belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers. The hypocrites do not understand this fundamental truth, and their claims are misguided.
orig: يقولون لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة ليخرجن الأعز منها الأذل ولله العزة ولرسوله وللمؤمنين ولكن المنافقين لا يعلمون

translation: O you who believe! Let not your wealth and your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that - then those are the losers.
interpretation: This verse cautions believers against being overly consumed by their material possessions and familial responsibilities, to the point that they neglect their spiritual obligations and connection with Allah. It emphasizes that one should not allow worldly affairs to distract from the remembrance and worship of Allah, as those who do so are considered the true losers, having prioritized the temporary over the eternal.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله ومن يفعل ذلك فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And spend [in the way of Allah ] from what We have provided you before death approaches one of you and he says, "My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so I would give charity and be among the righteous."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to spend from the wealth that Allah has provided them, before death comes to them. It warns against procrastinating and delaying charitable giving until it is too late. The interpretation is that one should not wait until the last moment to do good deeds, but should strive to be among the righteous by spending from one's wealth in the way of Allah while one has the opportunity to do so.
orig: وأنفقوا من ما رزقناكم من قبل أن يأتي أحدكم الموت فيقول رب لولا أخرتني إلى أجل قريب فأصدق وأكن من الصالحين

translation: And Allah will not delay [the punishment of] a soul when its time has come. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's decree and timing are absolute. When a person's appointed time of death arrives, Allah will not delay it, as He is all-knowing of our actions and has perfect wisdom in determining the duration of each life. This serves as a reminder to live righteously, as we are accountable to Allah for our deeds.
orig: ولن يؤخر الله نفسا إذا جاء أجلها والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allah, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over the entire universe. Everything in the heavens and on the earth, whether animate or inanimate, glorifies and praises Allah. This is a declaration of Allah's complete dominion, authority, and control over all creation. The verse also highlights Allah's wisdom and ability to do all things, for He is the Exalted in Might and the Wise.
orig: يسبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: It is He who created you, and among you is the disbeliever and among you is the believer. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah who has created all people, both those who believe and those who disbelieve. It serves as a reminder that Allah is all-knowing and all-seeing, and that He is aware of the actions and beliefs of each individual. This highlights the importance of faith and righteous deeds, as Allah will judge each person according to their beliefs and actions.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم فمنكم كافر ومنكم مؤمن والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth and formed you, and made good your forms; and to Him is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God is the Creator of the universe, and that He has created all things in a just and purposeful manner. It also highlights that God has created humans in the best of forms, and that ultimately, all will return to Him. This verse encourages us to reflect on the perfection of God's creation and to strive to live in accordance with His will, as our final destination is with Him.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق وصوركم فأحسن صوركم وإليه المصير

translation: He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you declare. And Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, the Almighty. He has knowledge of all that exists in the heavens and the earth, and He is aware of both the secrets we keep hidden and the things we openly express. Nothing is hidden from His knowledge, for He is the All-Knowing, the Knower of what is in the hearts and minds of His creation. This verse serves as a reminder that we cannot hide anything from Allah, and that we should strive to live our lives in a manner that is pleasing to Him.
orig: يعلم ما في السماوات والأرض ويعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون والله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Has there not come to you the news of those before you - the people of Noah and 'Aad and Thamud and those after them? And none but Allah knows them. Their Messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they returned their hands to their mouths and said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed we are, about that to which you invite us, in disquieting doubt."
interpretation: This verse reminds the disbelievers of the fate that befell previous nations who rejected the message of the Prophets sent to them. It serves as a warning that those who reject the truth and persist in their disbelief will face a painful punishment. The verse emphasizes that Allah alone knows the full extent of those who have denied the truth, and that the Messengers came to them with clear proofs, yet they stubbornly rejected the message, expressing doubt and disbelief. This is a lesson for all who are invited to believe in the oneness of Allah and follow His guidance.
orig: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين كفروا من قبل فذاقوا وبال أمرهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they said, "Shall we believe in mere mortals?" and they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was not in need. And Allah is Free of all wants, Worthy of all praise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disbelief of the people who rejected the messengers sent to them by Allah. Despite the clear proofs and guidance provided by the messengers, the people refused to believe, questioning how they could follow mere mortals. This verse emphasizes that Allah is not in need of the people's belief or worship, for He is the Sovereign, the Praiseworthy. It serves as a reminder that those who reject the truth will be held accountable, while Allah's power and wisdom are beyond any need or dependence on His creation.
orig: ذلك بأنه كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فقالوا أبشر يهدوننا فكفروا وتولوا واستغنى الله والله غني حميد

translation: Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will surely be informed of what you did. And that for Allah is easy."
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers who deny the concept of resurrection and the afterlife. It affirms that they will indeed be resurrected and held accountable for their actions in this world. The emphasis on "by my Lord" and "you will surely be resurrected" conveys the certainty of this event. The verse then states that they will be informed of their deeds, highlighting the idea of judgment and accountability. Lastly, it asserts that this is an easy matter for Allah, underscoring His power and ability to resurrect and judge all of humanity.
orig: زعم الذين كفروا أن لن يبعثوا قل بلى وربي لتبعثن ثم لتنبؤن بما عملتم وذلك على الله يسير

translation: So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Light which We have sent down. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse commands believers to have faith in Allah, His Messenger (Muhammad), and the divine guidance (the Qur'an) that has been revealed. It emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of the thoughts, intentions, and actions of all people, and will judge them accordingly.
orig: فآمنوا بالله ورسوله والنور الذي أنزلنا والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: The Day He will gather you for the Day of Gathering - that is the Day of Disillusionment. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness - He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Judgement, when all people will be gathered before Allah to be held accountable for their deeds. It is called the "Day of Disillusionment" because on that day, people will realize the true consequences of their actions in this life. The verse emphasizes that those who believe in Allah and do good deeds will be forgiven of their sins and granted eternal life in Paradise. This is the greatest success and achievement one can attain.
orig: يوم يجمعكم ليوم الجمع ذلك يوم التغابن ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يكفر عنه سيئاته ويدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of disbelief and rejection of God's signs. Those who reject the truth and deny the revelations of Allah will be condemned to an eternal abode in the Hellfire, which is a terrible and undesirable end. This serves as a warning to those who turn away from the guidance provided in the Quran and choose to live in denial of God's existence and message.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب النار خالدين فيها وبئس المصير

translation: No disaster strikes except by permission of Allah. And whoever believes in Allah - He will guide his heart. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all events, whether good or bad, happen by the will and permission of Allah. It encourages believers to have faith in Allah, as He guides the hearts of those who believe in Him. The verse also highlights that Allah has knowledge of all things, which should instill a sense of trust and reliance on Him in the hearts of the faithful.
orig: ما أصاب من مصيبة إلا بإذن الله ومن يؤمن بالله يهد قلبه والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, but if you turn away - then upon Our Messenger is only [the duty of] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to both Allah and His Messenger, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It suggests that if people turn away from this obedience, the responsibility of the Messenger is to clearly convey the message, not to force compliance. The verse highlights the need for believers to submit to the divine guidance and teachings of the Prophet, as this is the path to Allah's pleasure and salvation.
orig: وأطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول فإن توليتم فإنما على رسولنا البلاغ المبين

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse affirms the oneness and sovereignty of Allah, the one true God. It calls upon the believers to put their trust and reliance solely in Allah, as He is the only worthy object of worship and the ultimate source of guidance and support. This encourages a strong and unwavering faith in Allah, and a complete dependence on Him in all matters of life.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: O you who believe! Indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse warns believers that even their closest family members - spouses and children - can sometimes become their enemies, either by opposing their faith or through their actions. The verse advises believers to be cautious and vigilant. However, it also encourages believers to show forgiveness, mercy and compassion towards their family members, even if they are antagonistic. This is because Allah Himself is Forgiving and Merciful, and believers should strive to emulate these divine attributes.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم وإن تعفوا وتصفحوا وتغفروا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Your wealth and your children are but a trial, and Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse reminds us that our material possessions and our children are a test and trial from Allah. They can distract us from our spiritual obligations and lead us to become attached to the temporary pleasures of this world. However, if we remain steadfast in our faith and use our wealth and children in the service of Allah, then we will be rewarded with a great reward in the Hereafter. The true success lies not in the accumulation of wealth or the number of children, but in our devotion to Allah and our commitment to living a righteous life.
orig: إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة والله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: So fear Allah as much as you are able and listen and obey and spend [in the way of Allah] - it is better for your selves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fearing and obeying Allah, as well as being generous and spending for the sake of Allah. It suggests that those who are able to overcome their own selfishness and stinginess will be the ones who achieve success and prosperity in this life and the hereafter. The key message is that true success comes from submitting to Allah's will and putting the needs of others before one's own desires.
orig: فاتقوا الله ما استطعتم واسمعوا وأطيعوا وأنفقوا خيرا لأنفسكم ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: If you lend to Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you, and Allah is the Most Appreciative, the Most Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to make charitable donations and good deeds, as these will be rewarded by Allah. The metaphor of "lending to Allah" suggests that any good we do is an investment in our relationship with the Divine, which will be returned to us many times over. The attributes of Allah mentioned - "the Most Appreciative, the Most Forbearing" - indicate that He is gracious and forgiving towards those who strive to please Him through their righteous actions.
orig: إن تقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا يضاعفه لكم ويغفر لكم والله شكور حليم

translation: The Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the attributes of Allah as the All-Knowing, the Omniscient, who has knowledge of both the seen and the unseen realms. He is the Mighty, the Wise, whose power and wisdom are unparalleled. This verse highlights the absolute sovereignty and authority of Allah, and the need for believers to submit to His will and seek guidance from Him.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة العزيز الحكيم

translation: O Prophet, when you [Muslims] divorce women, divorce them for [the commencement of] their waiting period and keep count of the waiting period, and fear Allah, your Lord. Do not turn them out of their [husband's] houses, nor should they [themselves] leave [during that period] unless they are committing a clear immorality. And those are the limits [set by] Allah. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has certainly wronged himself. You know not; perhaps Allah will bring about after that a [different] matter.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the proper procedure for divorcing women in Islam. It instructs the Prophet and believers to divorce women during their waiting period ('iddah), to keep track of this period, and to fear and be mindful of Allah. It prohibits expelling divorced women from their homes or allowing them to leave, unless they have committed a clear immorality. These are the limits set by Allah, and anyone who transgresses them has wronged themselves. The verse also suggests that Allah may bring about a different matter or outcome after the divorce, which the believers cannot foresee.
orig: يا أيها النبي إذا طلقتم النساء فطلقوهن لعدتهن وأحصوا العدة واتقوا الله ربكم لا تخرجوهن من بيوتهن ولا يخرجن إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة وتلك حدود الله ومن يتعد حدود الله فقد ظلم نفسه لا تدري لعل الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرا

translation: And when they have [nearly] fulfilled their term, either retain them according to acceptable terms or part with them according to acceptable terms. And bring to witness two just men from among you and establish the testimony for [the acceptance of] Allah. That is instructed to whoever should believe in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah - He will make for him a way out
