interpretation: This verse provides guidance on how to handle the end of a marriage relationship. It instructs that when the waiting period (iddah) is nearly complete, the couple should either reconcile and continue the marriage on good terms, or part ways amicably. It also requires that the decision be witnessed by two just people, to establish the testimony before Allah. This is meant to encourage believers to act righteously, fearing Allah and the Day of Judgment, and to provide a way out of difficult situations for those who are mindful of Allah.
orig: فإذا بلغن أجلهن فأمسكوهن بمعروف أو فارقوهن بمعروف وأشهدوا ذوي عدل منكم وأقيموا الشهادة لله ذلكم يوعظ به من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجا

translation: And He will provide for him from [sources] he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allah - then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has already set for everything a [decreed] proportion.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to trust in Allah and rely on Him, as He will provide for them from unexpected sources. It emphasizes that Allah is sufficient for those who put their trust in Him, and that He will accomplish His will and decree for all things. The verse highlights the importance of faith, reliance on Allah, and understanding that everything is subject to Allah's divine plan and measure.
orig: ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه إن الله بالغ أمره قد جعل الله لكل شيء قدرا

translation: And those who no longer expect menstruation among your women - if you doubt, then their waiting period is three months, and [also for] those who have not menstruated. And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth. And whoever fears Allah - He will make for him of his matter ease.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the waiting period ('iddah) for different categories of women, including those who have stopped menstruating, those who have not yet started menstruating, and those who are pregnant. The purpose of this waiting period is to ensure clarity regarding paternity and to allow for the possibility of reconciliation. The verse also emphasizes that those who fear and obey Allah will be granted ease in their affairs.
orig: واللائي يئسن من المحيض من نسائكم إن ارتبتم فعدتهن ثلاثة أشهر واللائي لم يحضن وأولات الأحمال أجلهن أن يضعن حملهن ومن يتق الله يجعل له من أمره يسرا

translation: That is the ordinance of Allah which He has sent down to you, and whoever fears Allah - He will remove for him his misdeeds and make great for him a reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the commandments and ordinances of Allah are to be followed by the believers. It promises that those who fear and revere Allah, and obey His commands, will have their sins forgiven and will be granted a great reward in the afterlife. The key message is that righteous conduct and devotion to Allah will lead to forgiveness and a blessed outcome.
orig: ذلك أمر الله أنزله إليكم ومن يتق الله يكفر عنه سيئاته ويعظم له أجرا

translation: Lodge them [in a space] from where you [O people] are dwelling out of your means. And do not harm them in order to oppress them. And if they should be pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth. And if they breastfeed for you, then give them their payment and confer among yourselves in the acceptable way. And if you are in discord, then breastfeed [the child] for another woman.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on how to treat and support divorced women, especially those who are pregnant or breastfeeding. The key points are: 1) Provide them with housing and financial support according to your means, without causing them harm or distress. 2) If they are pregnant, continue to financially support them until they give birth. 3) If they breastfeed the child, pay them for their services. 4) Resolve any disputes between the parties in a respectful manner. 5) If the parents cannot agree, arrange for another woman to breastfeed the child. The overall emphasis is on caring for the welfare of the divorced woman and ensuring the child's needs are met, even in difficult circumstances.
orig: أسكنوهن من حيث سكنتم من وجدكم ولا تضاروهن لتضيقوا عليهن وإن كن أولات حمل فأنفقوا عليهن حتى يضعن حملهن فإن أرضعن لكم فآتوهن أجورهن وأتمروا بينكم بمعروف وإن تعاسرتم فسترضع له أخرى

translation: Let the wealthy person spend from his wealth, and he whose provision is restricted - let him spend from what Allah has given him. Allah does not charge a soul except [according to] what He has given it. Allah will bring about, after hardship, ease.
interpretation: This verse encourages the wealthy to be generous in spending their wealth, and those with limited means to spend from what Allah has provided them. It emphasizes that Allah does not burden a person beyond their capacity, and that after hardship, Allah will bring about ease. The overall message is one of compassion, moderation, and trust in Allah's plan.
orig: لينفق ذو سعة من سعته ومن قدر عليه رزقه فلينفق مما آتاه الله لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا ما آتاها سيجعل الله بعد عسر يسرا

translation: And how many a township have We destroyed while it was given to wrongdoing - so it is [now] fallen into ruin - and [how many] an abandoned well and [how many] a lofty palace.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of disobedience and rebellion against the commands of God and His messengers. It describes how Allah has destroyed many societies and civilizations that persisted in their wrongdoing, despite being warned. The verse suggests that the destruction of these communities was a severe punishment, as they were "given to wrongdoing" and then "fell into ruin". This serves as a warning to those who defy the will of God, that they too may face a similar fate if they do not repent and return to the righteous path.
orig: وكأين من قرية عتت عن أمر ربها ورسله فحاسبناها حسابا شديدا وعذبناها عذابا نكرا

translation: And she tasted the bad consequence of her affair, and the outcome of her affair was loss.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of someone who engaged in a harmful or unwise course of action. The verse suggests that the person experienced the negative consequences of their actions, which resulted in a loss or failure. The interpretation is that when one makes poor decisions, they will ultimately suffer the detrimental effects, which can lead to a state of loss or ruin.
orig: فذاقت وبال أمرها وكان عاقبة أمرها خسرا

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. So fear Allah, O you of understanding who have believed. Verily, Allah has sent down to you the Reminder.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who have rejected faith and turned away from the guidance of Allah. It emphasizes that a severe punishment awaits them in the Hereafter. The verse then exhorts the believers, those with sound intellect and understanding, to be mindful of Allah and to fear Him. It also affirms that Allah has revealed the Qur'an as a reminder and guidance for humanity.
orig: أعد الله لهم عذابا شديدا فاتقوا الله يا أولي الألباب الذين آمنوا قد أنزل الله إليكم ذكرا

translation: A messenger who recites to you the clear verses of Allah that He may bring out those who believe and do righteous deeds from darknesses into the light. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness - He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Allah has certainly given him an excellent provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger who conveys the clear and unambiguous revelations of Allah. The purpose of this divine guidance is to lead those who believe and do good deeds out of the darkness of ignorance, disbelief and sin, and into the light of faith, knowledge and righteous conduct. Those who truly believe in Allah and do what is right will be rewarded with eternal life in the Gardens of Paradise, where they will enjoy Allah's excellent provision. This verse highlights the transformative power of faith and righteous action, and the eternal blessings that await those who embrace them.
orig: رسولا يتلو عليكم آيات الله مبينات ليخرج الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من الظلمات إلى النور ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا قد أحسن الله له رزقا

translation: Allah is the One who created seven heavens and of the earth, the like of them. [His] command descends among them so you may know that Allah has power over all things and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of Allah. He has created the seven heavens and the earth, and His command flows between them. This demonstrates that Allah has power over all things, and that His knowledge encompasses all of creation. The purpose of this is so that people may know and understand the greatness and sovereignty of Allah.
orig: الله الذي خلق سبع سماوات ومن الأرض مثلهن يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما

translation: O Prophet, why do you prohibit [yourself from] what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and questioning why he has prohibited himself from certain lawful things, seeking to please his wives. The verse emphasizes that Allah has made these things lawful, and the Prophet should not restrict himself from them. The verse also reminds the Prophet that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, indicating that he should not feel guilty for enjoying the lawful things that Allah has provided. The interpretation suggests that the Prophet should not feel obligated to restrict himself from lawful things in order to please his wives, as Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: يا أيها النبي لم تحرم ما أحل الله لك تبتغي مرضات أزواجك والله غفور رحيم

translation: Allah has already ordained for you [Muslims] the dissolution of your oaths. And Allah is your protector, and He is the Knowing, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the believers, informing them that Allah has already prescribed a way for them to be absolved from their oaths. It emphasizes that Allah is the protector and guardian of the believers, and that He is all-knowing and all-wise in His rulings and guidance. The interpretation suggests that Allah provides a path for the believers to rectify any unintended oaths they may have made, out of His mercy and wisdom.
orig: قد فرض الله لكم تحلة أيمانكم والله مولاكم وهو العليم الحكيم

translation: And [O Muhammad], when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement; and when she informed [others] of it and Allah showed it to him, he made known part of it and avoided part. And when he informed her about it, she said, "Who told you this?" [The Prophet] said, "I was informed by the Knowing, the Aware."
interpretation: This verse describes a situation where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) confided a private matter to one of his wives. She then revealed this information to others, which Allah made known to the Prophet. In response, the Prophet acknowledged that he knew part of what she had done, but chose not to address the rest. When the wife asked him how he knew, he replied that it was the Knowing and Aware (i.e. Allah) who had informed him. This verse highlights the importance of discretion and the divine knowledge that the Prophet possessed, even in his personal affairs.
orig: وإذ أسر النبي إلى بعض أزواجه حديثا فلما نبأت به وأظهره الله عليه عرف بعضه وأعرض عن بعض فلما نبأها به قالت من أنبأك هذا قال نبأني العليم الخبير

translation: If you two (wives) turn in repentance to Allah, [it is best], for your hearts have deviated. But if you cooperate against him - then indeed Allah is his protector, and Gabriel and the righteous of the believers and the angels, moreover, are [his] assistants.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) who were involved in a dispute. It emphasizes the importance of repentance and turning back to Allah if their hearts have deviated from the right path. It also highlights that if they were to cooperate against the Prophet, then Allah, the angels, and the righteous believers would support and protect him. The verse encourages the wives to seek forgiveness and reconciliation, and to maintain unity and loyalty to the Prophet and the teachings of Islam.
orig: إن تتوبا إلى الله فقد صغت قلوبكما وإن تظاهرا عليه فإن الله هو مولاه وجبريل وصالح المؤمنين والملائكة بعد ذلك ظهير

translation: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you [all], will substitute for him wives better than you - submitting [to Allah ], believing, devoutly obedient, repenting, worshiping, and traveling [for His cause] - whether previously married or virgins.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if a husband divorces his wives, Allah may provide him with better wives who are more righteous and devoted to their faith. The verse describes the qualities of these potential replacement wives, including being submissive to Allah, believing in Him, obedient, repentant, worshipful, and striving in His cause - whether they were previously married or virgins. This implies that a husband should seek wives who prioritize their spiritual devotion and relationship with Allah, rather than focusing solely on worldly or physical attributes.
orig: عسى ربه إن طلقكن أن يبدله أزواجا خيرا منكن مسلمات مؤمنات قانتات تائبات عابدات سائحات ثيبات وأبكارا

translation: O you who believe! Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are [appointed] angels, harsh and severe; they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them but do what they are commanded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of protecting oneself and one's family from the punishment of the Hellfire. The Hellfire is described as being fueled by people and stones, and guarded by severe and harsh angels who strictly follow the commands of Allah. This serves as a warning to believers to be vigilant in their faith and actions, and to guide their families towards righteousness, in order to avoid the eternal torment of the Hellfire.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا وقودها الناس والحجارة عليها ملائكة غلاظ شداد لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون

translation: O you who have disbelieved, make no excuses this Day. You will only be recompensed for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who have rejected faith in God and His teachings. It warns them that on the Day of Judgment, they will not be able to make any excuses for their disbelief and wrongdoings. They will only be held accountable for their actions and deeds in this life, and will be recompensed accordingly. The message emphasizes the importance of taking responsibility for one's choices and actions, as there will be no escape from the consequences on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: يا أيها الذين كفروا لا تعتذروا اليوم إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who believe! Turn to Allah with sincere repentance. It may be that your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, on the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believe with him. Their light will run before them and on their right hands. They will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent."
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to sincerely repent to Allah and turn back to Him. It promises that if they do so, Allah may forgive their sins and admit them into Paradise. The verse also highlights the honor that will be bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers on the Day of Judgment, when their light will guide them and they will be exalted. The believers' supplication at the end of the verse reflects their humility and desire for Allah's continued guidance and forgiveness, as they recognize that He has power over all things.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا توبوا إلى الله توبة نصوحا عسى ربكم أن يكفر عنكم سيئاتكم ويدخلكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار يوم لا يخزي الله النبي والذين آمنوا معه نورهم يسعى بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا واغفر لنا إنك على كل شيء قدير

translation: O Prophet, fight against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to fight against those who disbelieve in Allah and Islam (the disbelievers), as well as those who outwardly claim to be believers but inwardly harbor doubts and opposition (the hypocrites). The Prophet is instructed to be firm and stern in dealing with them, as their ultimate destination is the Fire of Hell, which is a terrible abode.
orig: يا أيها النبي جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: Allah has set forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants but they betrayed them, so they [i.e., those prophets] did not avail them from Allah at all, and it was said, "Enter the Fire with those who enter."
interpretation: This verse presents the example of the wives of the Prophets Noah and Lot, who despite being married to righteous men, betrayed their husbands by disbelieving and rejecting their message. Their relationship with the Prophets did not protect them from the punishment of Allah, as they were judged based on their own actions and beliefs. This serves as a warning that one's close association with pious individuals does not guarantee salvation if one does not truly believe and follow the path of righteousness.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا للذين كفروا امرأت نوح وامرأت لوط كانتا تحت عبدين من عبادنا صالحين فخانتاهما فلم يغنيا عنهما من الله شيئا وقيل ادخلا النار مع الداخلين

translation: And Allah has set forth an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, "My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds and save me from the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse presents the example of the wife of Pharaoh, who was a believer in God despite living in the household of a tyrant. She prayed to God, asking Him to grant her a house in Paradise and to save her from the oppression of Pharaoh and his people. This example illustrates that even in the most challenging circumstances, one can maintain faith in God and seek His protection and guidance. It encourages believers to steadfastly hold onto their faith, no matter the external pressures they may face.
orig: وضرب الله مثلا للذين آمنوا امرأت فرعون إذ قالت رب ابن لي عندك بيتا في الجنة ونجني من فرعون وعمله ونجني من القوم الظالمين

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], Mary, the daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity [i.e., private parts], so We blew into [her garment] through Our angel [Gabriel], and she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures and was of the devoutly obedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the piety and virtue of Mary, the mother of Jesus. It describes how she remained chaste and pure, and how God breathed life into her through the angel Gabriel, allowing her to conceive Jesus without a father. The verse also emphasizes her faith and obedience to God, as she believed in the divine words and scriptures. This portrayal of Mary serves as an example of righteousness and devotion to God.
orig: ومريم ابنت عمران التي أحصنت فرجها فنفخنا فيه من روحنا وصدقت بكلمات ربها وكتبه وكانت من القانتين

translation: Blessed is He in Whose hand is the dominion, and He is Able to do all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of God. He is the one who possesses all dominion and authority, and He has the ability to do anything. This serves as a reminder that God is the ultimate ruler and that all things are under His control. It encourages believers to put their trust in God and to recognize His supreme power and might.
orig: تبارك الذي بيده الملك وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: The One who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed - and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God is the Creator of both life and death, and that He has created them to test and evaluate the deeds of human beings. The purpose is to determine who among them is best in conduct and righteous actions. God is the Almighty, Powerful and Forgiving, and He will judge people based on their deeds in this life.
orig: الذي خلق الموت والحياة ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا وهو العزيز الغفور

translation: It is He who created the seven heavens in layers. You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency. So return [your] vision [to the sky]; do you see any breaks?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfection and consistency of Allah's creation. The seven heavens, created in layers, are a testament to the Almighty's power and wisdom. The verse invites the reader to observe the sky and ponder the absence of any flaws or inconsistencies in this magnificent creation, which is a reflection of the Mercy and Oneness of the Creator. The invitation to "return [your] vision" suggests that one should contemplate and reflect deeply on the signs of Allah's divinity and the seamless nature of the universe He has created.
orig: الذي خلق سبع سماوات طباقا ما ترى في خلق الرحمن من تفاوت فارجع البصر هل ترى من فطور

translation: Then look again and again, your sight will return to you humbled and fatigued.
interpretation: This verse encourages the reader to contemplate and reflect deeply on the signs of God's power and wisdom in the universe. The repeated act of looking and returning one's gaze is a metaphor for the process of careful observation and contemplation. The verse suggests that through this process, one's sight or understanding will become humbled and fatigued, recognizing the limitations of human perception in fully comprehending the vastness and complexity of God's creation. This humility and awe before the Almighty is a key aspect of the spiritual journey described in the Qur'an.
orig: ثم ارجع البصر كرتين ينقلب إليك البصر خاسئا وهو حسير

translation: And We have certainly beautified the nearest heaven with stars and have made [from] them what is thrown at the devils and have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah has adorned the lowest heaven with stars, which serve as projectiles to drive away the devils when they attempt to eavesdrop on the heavenly realm. The stars are used as a deterrent against the devils, and Allah has also prepared a painful punishment of the Blaze for them.
orig: ولقد زينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح وجعلناها رجوما للشياطين وأعتدنا لهم عذاب السعير

translation: And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse warns those who reject faith in God and deny His Lordship that they will face the eternal punishment of Hell, which is a terrible and undesirable end. It emphasizes that disbelief in God and rejection of His guidance will lead to a grave and unfortunate consequence in the Hereafter.
orig: وللذين كفروا بربهم عذاب جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: When they are thrown into it, they will hear it blaring while it boils up.
interpretation: This verse describes the torment of Hell, where the disbelievers will be cast. They will hear the intense and terrifying sound of the flames as the fire rages and boils. This emphasizes the severe punishment and suffering that awaits those who reject faith and deny the signs of God.
orig: إذا ألقوا فيها سمعوا لها شهيقا وهي تفور

translation: It almost bursts with rage. Whenever a group is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, "Did there not come to you a warner?"
interpretation: This verse is describing the intense fury and anger of Hell, which is ready to burst forth with rage whenever more people are cast into it. The keepers of Hell, the angels tasked with guarding it, ask the damned souls whether they were not warned beforehand about the consequences of their misdeeds. This suggests that the punishment of Hell is not unjust, as the people who enter it had been warned by the Prophets and Messengers sent by God, but they chose to reject the message and persist in their evil ways.
orig: تكاد تميز من الغيظ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم نذير

translation: They say, "Yes, a warner has come to us, but we denied and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything. You are not but in great error.'"
interpretation: This verse describes the response of those who rejected the message of the Prophet Muhammad. They acknowledged that a warner (the Prophet) had come to them, but they rejected his message and claimed that Allah had not revealed anything. This reflects their arrogance and refusal to accept the truth, as they were in a state of profound misguidance.
orig: قالوا بلى قد جاءنا نذير فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء إن أنتم إلا في ضلال كبير

translation: And they will say, "If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers will regret their past actions and wish that they had used their faculties of hearing and reasoning to guide them towards the truth. They will acknowledge that had they listened to the guidance of the Qur’an and used their intellect to ponder over the signs of Allah, they would not have ended up in the hellfire. This highlights the importance of using our God-given faculties to seek the truth and follow the right path, rather than succumbing to desires and whims.
orig: وقالوا لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل ما كنا في أصحاب السعير

translation: So they acknowledged their sin, but [for the inhabitants of] the Blaze, [is] ruin.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who acknowledge their sins. They will face the punishment of the Hellfire, which is described as a place of utter ruin and destruction. The acknowledgment of one's sins is the first step towards seeking forgiveness and redemption, but it does not guarantee salvation. The ultimate punishment for those who persist in their wrongdoing is the eternal torment of the Blaze.
orig: فاعترفوا بذنبهم فسحقا لأصحاب السعير

translation: Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fearing and revering God in one's heart, even when no one else is watching. Those who maintain this sincere and unwavering faith in God, without the need for external validation or recognition, will be granted forgiveness for their sins and a great reward in the Hereafter. This highlights the value of having a genuine and personal relationship with the Divine, rather than a superficial display of religiosity.
orig: إن الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: And conceal your word or announce it; indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to be mindful of their thoughts and words, as Allah is All-Knowing and is aware of what is in their hearts. It suggests that one should be careful in expressing their thoughts and intentions, whether they are kept private or shared publicly. The verse highlights that Allah has knowledge of the innermost thoughts and feelings of people, and that they will be accountable for their words and actions.
orig: وأسروا قولكم أو اجهروا به إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Does He who created not know, while He is the Subtle, the Acquainted?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God, the Creator, is all-knowing and fully aware of His creation. The terms "the Subtle" and "the Acquainted" suggest that God has an intimate and deep understanding of all things, even the most subtle and intricate details. This verse serves to remind us that God's knowledge is comprehensive and that He is aware of even the smallest aspects of our lives and the universe He has created.
orig: ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير

translation: It is He who made the earth tame for you - so walk among its [various] slopes and eat of His provision, and to Him is the [final] resurrection.
interpretation: This verse encourages us to explore and utilize the resources of the earth that God has provided for us. It reminds us that the earth is a place of sustenance and comfort, and that we should make use of its bounties while remembering that our ultimate return is to God. The verse emphasizes the idea of gratitude and appreciation for the blessings of the earth, and the responsibility we have to use them wisely and in moderation.
orig: هو الذي جعل لكم الأرض ذلولا فامشوا في مناكبها وكلوا من رزقه وإليه النشور

translation: Have you ˹believers˺ been assured that the One in the heavens will not cause the earth to swallow you up, and then it would shake?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the belief of those who feel secure and safe from the punishment of God. The verse suggests that the believers should not feel complacent or overconfident, as God has the power to cause the earth to swallow them up or shake beneath them. The interpretation is that one should remain humble and conscious of God's might, and not become arrogant or heedless of the consequences of their actions.
orig: أأمنتم من في السماء أن يخسف بكم الأرض فإذا هي تمور

translation: Or have you felt secure that [instead] He will not send against you a storm of stones from the sky, and you would then know how [severe] was My warning?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who feel secure and complacent, thinking that they are safe from the consequences of their actions. It suggests that God has the power to send down a devastating punishment, like a storm of stones from the sky, to remind people of the seriousness of their transgressions and the importance of heeding the warnings of the prophets. The verse emphasizes the need for people to be vigilant and to take the warnings of God and His messengers seriously, lest they face severe consequences.
orig: أم أمنتم من في السماء أن يرسل عليكم حاصبا فستعلمون كيف نذير

translation: And those before them certainly denied, and how [terrible] was My reproach.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fact that previous nations and peoples who rejected the message of the Prophets sent to them were severely punished for their disbelief and denial. The phrase "how [terrible] was My reproach" emphasizes the severity of the consequences they faced for their rejection of the truth. This serves as a warning to those who would similarly deny the message of Islam, that they too will face the wrath and punishment of Allah if they persist in their rejection.
orig: ولقد كذب الذين من قبلهم فكيف كان نكير

translation: Have they not observed the birds above them, [with wings] outspread and [sometimes] folded in? None holds them [aloft] except the Most Merciful. Indeed He is, of all things, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse invites people to reflect on the remarkable abilities of birds, which are able to spread their wings and fly effortlessly through the sky. This is a sign of God's power and wisdom, as it is the Most Merciful who sustains and controls the birds without any visible means of support. This serves as a reminder that God is all-seeing and all-knowing, and that He alone has the power to create and sustain all things in the universe.
orig: أولم يروا إلى الطير فوقهم صافات ويقبضن ما يمسكهن إلا الرحمن إنه بكل شيء بصير

translation: Is this [god] who is a soldier for you to aid you against the Most Merciful [any god]? Indeed, the disbelievers are not but in delusion.
interpretation: This verse is questioning the belief in false gods or idols that the disbelievers worship, implying that they are powerless to help or protect them. It suggests that the only true source of help and support is the Merciful God (Allah), and that those who reject this truth are deluded. The verse emphasizes the futility of relying on anything other than the one true God for assistance and guidance.
orig: أمن هذا الذي هو جند لكم ينصركم من دون الرحمن إن الكافرون إلا في غرور

translation: Is He [not best] who provides for you if He should withhold His provision? But they have persisted in insolence and aversion.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the power and providence of God. It asks whether the one who provides for you (i.e. God) is not the best, even if He were to withhold His provision. The verse then states that the people have persisted in arrogance and aversion, refusing to acknowledge God's blessings and power. The interpretation is that we should recognize God as the true provider and not be arrogant or turn away from Him, even if our circumstances change.
orig: أمن هذا الذي يرزقكم إن أمسك رزقه بل لجوا في عتو ونفور

translation: Is one who walks fallen on his face better guided or one who walks upright on a straight path?
interpretation: This verse contrasts two types of people - one who is lost and wandering, walking with his face down, and one who is guided and walking upright on a straight path. The implication is that the one who is guided and walking the straight path is better and more rightly guided than the one who is lost and aimless. The verse encourages believers to strive to be on the straight path, following the guidance of God, rather than being lost and misguided.
orig: أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه أهدى أمن يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم

translation: Say, "It is He who created you and made for you hearing and vision and hearts; little are you grateful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is God who has created human beings and endowed them with the faculties of hearing, sight, and understanding (the heart). However, despite these blessings, people often fail to be truly grateful to God for these gifts. The verse encourages people to reflect on and appreciate the wonders of their own creation and the abilities they have been granted.
orig: قل هو الذي أنشأكم وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: Say, "He is the One who has created you from the earth, and to Him you will be gathered."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the One who has created all of humanity and that we will all be gathered before Him on the Day of Judgment. It reminds us of our ultimate accountability to Allah and the importance of living our lives in a way that pleases Him, as we will all return to Him in the end.
orig: قل هو الذي ذرأكم في الأرض وإليه تحشرون

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who mock the believers and challenge them to bring about the promise of the Day of Judgment, if the believers are indeed truthful in their faith. The verse highlights the arrogance and skepticism of the disbelievers, who refuse to believe in the reality of the Hereafter and the accountability that will take place on that Day. The interpretation is that the believers should remain steadfast in their faith, and not be deterred by the mockery of the disbelievers, as the promise of Allah is certain and will be fulfilled in due time.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "Indeed, the knowledge is with Allah, and I am but a clear warner."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true knowledge and wisdom ultimately reside with Allah, the Almighty. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is instructed to convey this message, that he is simply a messenger sent to clearly warn and guide people, but the source of all knowledge is Allah alone. This serves to remind people not to blindly follow the Prophet or any other human, but to seek knowledge and guidance from the divine source, Allah.
orig: قل إنما العلم عند الله وإنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: And when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain!" Rather, it is that for which you were impatient - a wind containing a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they witness the impending punishment from Allah. Initially, they think it is a cloud that will bring them rain, but then they realize it is the punishment they had been warned about. The interpretation is that the disbelievers will be dismayed and distressed when they see the consequences of their rejection of faith and Allah's warnings.
orig: فلما رأوه زلفة سيئت وجوه الذين كفروا وقيل هذا الذي كنتم به تدعون

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should kill me and those with me or if He should [instead] have mercy upon us, who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?"
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have faith in Allah's divine plan and wisdom. It reminds them that even if they or their companions face hardship or death, Allah is the ultimate protector and can show mercy. The verse also highlights the futility of the disbelievers seeking protection from Allah's punishment, as only He can provide refuge from a painful torment.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أهلكني الله ومن معي أو رحمنا فمن يجير الكافرين من عذاب أليم

translation: Say, "He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied. And you will [soon] know who it is that is in clear error."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to have faith in Allah, the Most Merciful, and to place their trust in Him. It also warns those who reject the truth that they will soon realize their error and misguidance. The verse emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah and having unwavering faith in Him, as He is the source of all mercy and guidance.
orig: قل هو الرحمن آمنا به وعليه توكلنا فستعلمون من هو في ضلال مبين

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if your water was to become sunken [into the earth], then who could bring you flowing water?"
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that challenges people to consider the possibility of their water supply being depleted. It is meant to make them reflect on their dependence on a reliable source of water and to appreciate the importance of preserving and managing this precious resource. The interpretation is that we should be mindful of our water usage and take steps to ensure a sustainable water supply, as we cannot take it for granted that water will always be available to us.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أصبح ماؤكم غورا فمن يأتيكم بماء معين

translation: Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.
interpretation: This verse is the opening of Surah Al-Qalam (The Pen), the 68th chapter of the Qur'an. The letter "Nun" is one of the Arabic letters that appears at the beginning of some Quranic chapters, and its meaning is not entirely clear. The verse then mentions the "pen" and "what they inscribe", which is interpreted as a reference to the importance of writing, knowledge, and the recording of deeds. This verse emphasizes the significance of the written word and the act of recording, which are essential for the preservation and transmission of knowledge, wisdom, and the teachings of the Qur'an.
orig: ن والقلم وما يسطرون

translation: And by the grace of your Lord, you are not a madman.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and affirming that he is not a madman, despite the claims of his detractors. It is a reassurance from God that the Prophet's message and teachings are divinely inspired, and that he is not acting out of madness or delusion. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet's guidance and wisdom are a reflection of God's grace and favor upon him, not a sign of mental instability.
orig: ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون

translation: And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the righteous and steadfast believers will be rewarded by Allah without any interruption or end. The "uninterrupted" reward suggests that the blessings and bounties bestowed upon the believers in the Hereafter will be continuous and eternal, without any cessation or diminishment. This verse serves as a promise and encouragement for the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and good deeds, as they will be generously rewarded by Allah in the Afterlife.
orig: وإن لك لأجرا غير ممنون

translation: And indeed, you are of a great moral character.
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and affirming that he possesses a great and noble character. It is a testament to his exemplary moral conduct, which was a reflection of the sublime teachings of Islam. The interpretation suggests that the Prophet’s character and behavior were of the highest standard, serving as a model for all believers to emulate.
orig: وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم

translation: And you will surely see, and they will surely see.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance that the truth will become clear and evident, both to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and to his opponents. It suggests that the ultimate reality will be made manifest, and that those who have been denying the truth will eventually see and acknowledge it.
orig: فستبصر ويبصرون

translation: Which of you is bewitched?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, challenging the people who have been misled or bewitched. The implication is that they have fallen under the influence of false beliefs or deceptions, and are being called upon to recognize and overcome this state of being "bewitched". The verse serves as a wake-up call, urging the people to critically examine their beliefs and actions, and to return to the right path.
orig: بأييكم المفتون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way, and He is most knowing of [who is] the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah (God) has the perfect knowledge and understanding of who has strayed from the right path and who is following the guidance. It serves as a reminder that Allah is all-knowing and that our ultimate guidance and judgment rests in His hands, not in the hands of any human being. This verse encourages us to seek Allah's guidance and to trust in His wisdom, rather than relying on our own limited understanding.
orig: إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: So do not obey the deniers.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers not to follow or listen to those who deny the truth of the Qur'an and the message of Islam. It is a call to stand firm in one's faith and not be swayed by the arguments or influence of those who reject the divine revelation. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining one's conviction and not being misled by those who oppose the teachings of Islam.
orig: فلا تطع المكذبين

translation: They wish that you would soften [in your position], so they would soften [toward you].
interpretation: This verse refers to the desire of the disbelievers for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to compromise his principles and beliefs in order to gain their favor. However, the verse makes it clear that the Prophet should not yield to their wishes, as that would lead them to also compromise their stance. The interpretation is that the believer should remain firm in their faith and convictions, even if it means facing opposition or rejection from those who wish for them to be more accommodating.
orig: ودوا لو تدهن فيدهنون

translation: And do not obey every worthless habitual swearer
interpretation: This verse advises against blindly following or obeying those who frequently take oaths and make empty promises. It cautions against placing trust in those who lack integrity and character, as they are likely to betray or deceive. The interpretation is that one should be discerning and not be easily swayed by the words of those who are known to be dishonest or dishonorable.
orig: ولا تطع كل حلاف مهين

translation: A slanderer, a backbiter
interpretation: This verse describes a person who engages in malicious gossip, spreading rumors and undermining others. The Qur'an condemns such behavior, as it can cause great harm to individuals and disrupt the harmony of society. The interpretation suggests that we should refrain from engaging in this type of behavior and instead strive to be kind, compassionate, and truthful in our interactions with others.
orig: هماز مشاء بنميم

translation: A hinderer of good, a transgressor, a wicked person
interpretation: This verse describes a person who is an obstacle to good deeds, who oversteps the bounds of what is right, and who is sinful and wicked. The Qur'an is warning against such individuals who use their influence or power to prevent others from doing good and who engage in immoral or unethical behavior.
orig: مناع للخير معتد أثيم

translation: Obstinate, after that, ignoble
interpretation: This verse describes a person who is stubborn, arrogant, and of low character. The term "عتل" refers to someone who is obstinate and difficult to deal with, while "زنيم" suggests someone of ignoble or dishonorable lineage. The verse conveys a sense of condemnation for such a person, highlighting their undesirable qualities and the need to avoid or distance oneself from them.
orig: عتل بعد ذلك زنيم

translation: If he is a man of wealth and children
interpretation: This verse is referring to a person who has been blessed with wealth and offspring. The implication is that such a person may become arrogant and feel self-sufficient, forgetting that all blessings come from God. The verse serves as a reminder that wealth and children are not the true measures of a person's worth, and that one should remain humble and grateful to God for His bounties.
orig: أن كان ذا مال وبنين

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Legends of the former peoples."
interpretation: This verse refers to those who reject the Qur'an and dismiss it as mere "legends of the former peoples". They fail to recognize the divine origin and truth of the Qur'anic revelations, choosing instead to dismiss them as fabrications or stories of the past. This verse highlights the arrogance and closed-mindedness of those who refuse to accept the guidance and wisdom contained in the Qur'an, preferring to cling to their own preconceptions and biases.
orig: إذا تتلى عليه آياتنا قال أساطير الأولين

translation: We will brand him upon the snout.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from God to those who reject faith and engage in wrongdoing. The "branding upon the snout" is a metaphorical expression indicating that the consequences of their actions will be clearly marked upon them, like a brand or stamp. This suggests that there will be a clear and visible punishment for those who persist in disbelief and sin.
orig: سنسمه على الخرطوم

translation: Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the companions of the garden, when they swore to cut it down in the morning
interpretation: This verse is referring to a parable in the Qur'an about a group of people who owned a prosperous garden. They swore to harvest all of its fruits in the morning, without leaving anything for the poor. However, their plan was disrupted by a calamity that destroyed the garden. This parable is used to illustrate how God tests the faith and intentions of people, and that one should not be overly confident or arrogant about their worldly possessions and wealth. The interpretation is that God may test the believers in various ways, just as He tested the companions of the garden, to see if they remain steadfast in their faith and act with compassion and justice towards others.
orig: إنا بلوناهم كما بلونا أصحاب الجنة إذ أقسموا ليصرمنها مصبحين

translation: And they do not make exceptions.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being referred to do not make any exceptions or allowances. They are rigid and unyielding in their beliefs or actions, refusing to consider alternative perspectives or make exceptions even in special circumstances. The verse conveys a sense of inflexibility and an unwillingness to compromise or show leniency.
orig: ولا يستثنون

translation: And there passed by upon it a [decrée of] punishment from your Lord while they were asleep.
interpretation: This verse refers to a divine punishment that befell a people while they were sleeping, unaware of the impending doom. The interpretation suggests that Allah's judgment can come swiftly and unexpectedly, even when people are in a state of oblivion or complacency. It serves as a warning that one should always be vigilant and prepared, as the consequences of one's actions can manifest at any time, even when one is least expecting it.
orig: فطاف عليها طائف من ربك وهم نائمون

translation: And it became like a withered stalk.
interpretation: This verse is describing the fate of something that was once vibrant and prosperous, but has now become dry, withered, and devoid of life. It suggests a transformation from a state of vitality to one of decay and decline, often used to symbolize the transient nature of worldly possessions, power, or even human life itself. The imagery of a "withered stalk" conveys a sense of fragility, impermanence, and the inevitability of change that all things in this world must face.
orig: فأصبحت كالصريم

translation: So they called one another at early morning
interpretation: This verse describes a scene where people call out to one another in the early morning. It suggests a sense of urgency or a shared purpose that brings them together at the start of the day. The interpretation is that the verse highlights the importance of communication, coordination and collective action, even at the earliest hours, to achieve a common goal or address a pressing matter.
orig: فتنادوا مصبحين

translation: That you may go early to your fields if you would take charge.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to be diligent and hardworking in their endeavors. The phrase "if you would take charge" suggests that those who are disciplined and determined in their efforts will be rewarded. The instruction to "go early to your fields" emphasizes the importance of starting one's work early in the day, which is a sign of dedication and commitment. The overall message is that success comes through hard work and perseverance.
orig: أن اغدوا على حرثكم إن كنتم صارمين

translation: So they set out, conversing in secret
interpretation: This verse describes a group of people secretly discussing and conspiring, likely about something they do not want others to know. The use of the word "conversing in secret" suggests an element of secrecy, conspiracy, or plotting that is being carried out discreetly.
orig: فانطلقوا وهم يتخافتون

translation: That no poor person shall enter upon you this day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being hospitable and welcoming to the less fortunate. It suggests that one should not turn away or deny access to those in need, but rather should be open and generous in providing for them. The interpretation is that we should be compassionate and care for those who are less privileged than ourselves.
orig: أن لا يدخلنها اليوم عليكم مسكين

translation: And they set out early in the morning with [full] power.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the believers were determined and capable of accomplishing their goals. They set out early, indicating their eagerness and preparedness to take action. The phrase "with [full] power" implies that they were equipped with the necessary resources, strength, and resolve to carry out their plans. This verse encourages believers to approach their endeavors with a similar sense of purpose and capability.
orig: وغدوا على حرد قادرين

translation: And when they saw it (the sea), they said: "Indeed, we are lost."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of Pharaoh and his army when they saw the sea parting before them, as Moses and the Israelites were escaping. The verse suggests that the sight of the sea opening up made Pharaoh and his men realize that they were in a hopeless situation, and that their pursuit of the Israelites was misguided. The interpretation is that this verse highlights the sudden realization of those who are arrogant and oppressive that their plans have gone awry, and that they are now in a state of confusion and loss.
orig: فلما رأوها قالوا إنا لضالون

translation: But we are deprived
interpretation: This verse suggests that the speaker feels a sense of deprivation or being denied something. It could be interpreted as a lament over a lack of provision, resources, or opportunities. The verse implies a feeling of being excluded or marginalized, perhaps from something that others have access to. The interpretation suggests a state of being denied or deprived of something necessary or desired.
orig: بل نحن محرومون

translation: Their most moderate said, "Did I not tell you, 'Why do you not exalt [Allah]?'"
interpretation: This verse is from Surah Al-Qalam (The Pen), verse 28. It describes a dialogue between people who are arguing about belief in Allah. The "most moderate" among them is reminding the others that he had previously urged them to engage in remembrance and glorification of Allah, but they had refused to do so. The interpretation is that the verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping and glorifying Allah, and that those who neglect this are being rebuked for their lack of faith and devotion.
orig: قال أوسطهم ألم أقل لكم لولا تسبحون

translation: They will say, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse describes the remorseful acknowledgment of the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment. They will recognize their transgressions and express their glorification of God, admitting that they had been unjust to themselves and others. This highlights the importance of self-reflection and repentance, as well as the humility to accept one's mistakes before the Almighty.
orig: قالوا سبحان ربنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: And they turned to one another, blaming each other.
interpretation: This verse describes a scene where a group of people are engaged in mutual recrimination and blame-shifting, perhaps after a disagreement or conflict. The interpretation suggests that the verse highlights the tendency of people to avoid taking responsibility for their own actions and instead point fingers at others, which often exacerbates tensions and prevents resolution.
orig: فأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتلاومون

translation: They will say, "Woe to us! Indeed, we have been tyrants."
interpretation: This verse describes the remorseful state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They will realize the gravity of their sins and transgressions, and will lament their past actions, acknowledging that they were indeed oppressors and transgressors who went beyond the bounds set by God. This serves as a warning to humanity to avoid such behavior and to seek forgiveness and guidance from God.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا إنا كنا طاغين

translation: Perhaps our Lord will give us something better than it. Indeed, we are toward our Lord desiring [His pleasure].
interpretation: This verse expresses hope and trust in Allah's wisdom and mercy. The believers acknowledge that whatever befalls them, whether good or bad, is ultimately from Allah. They have faith that if they are faced with a difficult situation, Allah may replace it with something better. The key message is to maintain a positive attitude, seek Allah's pleasure, and have confidence that He will provide what is best for us, even if we cannot see it at the time.
orig: عسى ربنا أن يبدلنا خيرا منها إنا إلى ربنا راغبون

translation: Thus is the punishment, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the punishment in this life is just a precursor to the greater punishment in the Hereafter. It suggests that if people truly understood the gravity of the punishment that awaits them in the Afterlife, they would be more inclined to avoid sinful behavior and strive to please Allah. The verse serves as a warning to mankind to take heed and prepare for the Day of Judgment, when the consequences of their actions will be fully realized.
orig: كذلك العذاب ولعذاب الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, for the righteous with their Lord are [gardens of] Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the reward that the righteous and God-fearing people will receive in the Hereafter. The "gardens of Pleasure" is a metaphorical description of the Paradise that Allah has prepared for those who believed in Him and lived a righteous life. This suggests that the righteous will be granted a blissful and eternal abode in the Afterlife, where they will experience complete contentment, peace, and joy in the presence of their Lord.
orig: إن للمتقين عند ربهم جنات النعيم

translation: Then, should We treat the Muslims like the criminals?
interpretation: This verse poses a rhetorical question, implying that it would be unjust and unacceptable to treat the believers (Muslims) in the same manner as the criminals or wrongdoers. The underlying message is that the believers and the disbelievers cannot be equated, as they are fundamentally different in their faith, actions, and moral standing. The verse emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and not discriminating against the faithful simply because of their beliefs.
orig: أفنجعل المسلمين كالمجرمين

translation: What is [the matter] with you? How do you judge?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that expresses surprise and disapproval at the way people make judgments or decisions. It suggests that the way they are judging or deciding is flawed or unjust. The verse encourages critical self-reflection on one's decision-making process and the basis for one's judgments.
orig: ما لكم كيف تحكمون

translation: Or have you a Book wherein you learn,
interpretation: This verse is inquiring whether the addressees have a revealed scripture or book from which they are learning and deriving guidance. The implication is that if they do not have such a divinely-revealed book, then they should accept the Qur'an as the true guidance from God.
orig: أم لكم كتاب فيه تدرسون

translation: Indeed, for you in it is [what gives] choice.
interpretation: This verse suggests that in the Qur'an, there is guidance and wisdom that allows people to make choices and decisions that are beneficial for them. The Qur'an provides clear principles and teachings that enable individuals to discern right from wrong, and to choose a path that leads to their wellbeing and success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: إن لكم فيه لما تخيرون

translation: Or have you oaths with Us, lasting until the Day of Resurrection, that you will have whatever you demand?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the notion that the disbelievers have any lasting promises or oaths with Allah that would entitle them to whatever they demand on the Day of Resurrection. The implication is that they have no such oaths or guarantees, and that they will be held accountable for their actions on that Day.
orig: أم لكم أيمان علينا بالغة إلى يوم القيامة إن لكم لما تحكمون

translation: Ask them, 'Which of them is responsible for that?'
interpretation: This verse is instructing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to ask the disbelievers who among them is responsible for the accusations and false claims they make against him and his message. It is a rhetorical question, challenging them to take responsibility for their statements and actions. The interpretation is that the Prophet should confront the disbelievers and hold them accountable for their hostility towards the truth of Islam.
orig: سلهم أيهم بذلك زعيم

translation: Or do they have partners who have legislated for them a religion to which Allah has not given permission?
interpretation: This verse is questioning the polytheists who associate partners with Allah. It challenges them to bring forth their supposed partners or deities if they are truly truthful in their beliefs. The implication is that they have no legitimate basis for their polytheism, as Allah alone has the authority to legislate a religion or way of life for mankind. The verse encourages the polytheists to re-examine their beliefs and acknowledge the oneness and sovereignty of Allah.
orig: أم لهم شركاء فليأتوا بشركائهم إن كانوا صادقين

translation: The Day when the shin shall be laid bare and they shall be summoned to prostrate themselves, but they shall not be able to do so.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the true nature of reality will be revealed, and people will be called upon to prostrate themselves before God. However, those who have not lived righteous lives will be unable to do so, as they will be overwhelmed by the weight of their sins and the magnitude of the occasion.
orig: يوم يكشف عن ساق ويدعون إلى السجود فلا يستطيعون

translation: Their eyes will be humbled before them, humiliation will cover them. And they had been invited to prostrate while they were sound.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of those who rejected the truth and refused to submit to God. On the Day of Judgment, their eyes will be downcast, filled with shame and humiliation, as they realize the consequences of their disbelief. Despite being invited to prostrate and submit to God during their lifetimes, they remained arrogant and did not heed the call, even when they were physically and mentally capable of doing so.
orig: خاشعة أبصارهم ترهقهم ذلة وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون

translation: So leave Me [to deal] with the one who denies this statement. We will progressively lead them [to punishment] from where they do not know.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to those who deny the message of the Qur'an. Allah states that He will gradually lead them to punishment, in a way that they do not expect or anticipate. The implication is that those who reject the truth will face the consequences of their actions, even if they think they can escape it. The verse emphasizes the power and authority of Allah, and His ability to deal with those who defy His commands.
orig: فذرني ومن يكذب بهذا الحديث سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون

translation: And I will give them respite. Indeed, my plan is firm.
interpretation: This verse expresses Allah's (God's) power and control over all affairs. It suggests that even though the disbelievers may plot against the believers, Allah's plan is unshakable and He will give the disbelievers a chance to repent before delivering His punishment. The interpretation conveys the message that Allah is in full command and His decree will prevail, no matter what the disbelievers scheme.
orig: وأملي لهم إن كيدي متين

translation: Or do you ask them for payment, so they are by debt burdened down?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not seeking any material gain or payment from the people he was calling to Islam. Rather, the people were burdened by the debts and financial obligations they had taken on. The verse implies that the Prophet's message was not motivated by a desire for wealth or personal gain, but rather by a sincere concern for guiding people to the truth.
orig: أم تسألهم أجرا فهم من مغرم مثقلون

translation: Or have they the unseen, so they write [it] down?
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who claim to have knowledge of the unseen or hidden realities are not truly in possession of such knowledge. The implication is that they are merely fabricating or writing down their own speculations, rather than conveying authentic divine revelation. The verse challenges the notion that anyone can claim to have direct access to the unseen without the authority of God.
orig: أم عندهم الغيب فهم يكتبون

translation: So be patient for the decision of your Lord and be not like the companion of the fish when he called out while he was distressed.
interpretation: This verse encourages patience and steadfastness in the face of trials and tribulations. It refers to the story of the prophet Jonah (the companion of the fish), who became impatient and left his people before God had commanded him to do so. The verse warns against following Jonah's example and urges the listener to patiently await God's judgment and decree, without becoming distressed or despairing.
orig: فاصبر لحكم ربك ولا تكن كصاحب الحوت إذ نادى وهو مكظوم

translation: And had it not been for a favor from his Lord upon him, he would have been thrown onto the [barren] ground, and he would have been blamed.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and how he was saved from being cast out and blamed, due to the grace and mercy of God. It highlights the importance of divine guidance and protection, without which even the most righteous individuals would be vulnerable. The interpretation suggests that the Prophet was saved from a fate that would have been seen as shameful, highlighting God's constant care and support for His messengers.
orig: لولا أن تداركه نعمة من ربه لنبذ بالعراء وهو مذموم

translation: And his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), peace be upon him. It indicates that God (referred to as "his Lord") selected Ibrahim and made him one of the righteous and pious individuals. This highlights God's guidance and favor towards Ibrahim, choosing him to be a prophet and a role model for humanity.
orig: فاجتباه ربه فجعله من الصالحين

translation: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the message, and they say, "Indeed, he is a madman."
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of those who disbelieve in the message of the Qur"an. It indicates that they would try to unsettle or distract the Prophet (peace be upon him) with their intense gazes when they heard the recitation of the Qur"an, and they would dismiss him as a madman. This highlights the stubborn rejection and hostility of the disbelievers towards the divine revelation and the messenger who brought it.
orig: وإن يكاد الذين كفروا ليزلقونك بأبصارهم لما سمعوا الذكر ويقولون إنه لمجنون

translation: And it (the Quran) is not but a reminder to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Quran is a message and a reminder from God to all of humanity, not just a specific group or nation. It serves as a guidance and a source of wisdom for all people in the world, regardless of their background or circumstances. The Quran is a universal message that transcends time and place, providing a reminder and guidance for all who seek to understand and follow the path of truth and righteousness.
orig: وما هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: The Inevitable
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, which is an inevitable and undeniable event that will occur. It serves as a reminder to humanity to be prepared for this momentous day when they will be held accountable for their actions in this life.
orig: الحاقة

translation: The Inevitable
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, which is an inevitable and undeniable event that will occur. The Qur'an emphasizes the certainty of this day, and calls upon people to prepare for it by living a righteous life and believing in the oneness of God. The interpretation of this verse is that the Day of Judgment is a reality that all people must face, and that they should strive to be ready for it through their faith and good deeds.
orig: ما الحاقة

translation: And what may make you know [what] the Striking Calamity [is]?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, emphasizing the magnitude and significance of the "Striking Calamity" (al-Haqqah). The implication is that the Striking Calamity is an event of immense and awe-inspiring proportions, the scale and nature of which is beyond human comprehension. The verse serves to draw the reader's attention to the gravity of this impending event, which is often interpreted as a reference to the Day of Resurrection or Judgment Day.
orig: وما أدراك ما الحاقة

translation: The Thamud and 'Aad [people] denied the Striking Calamity.
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of the ancient peoples of Thamud and 'Aad, who rejected the warnings and signs of God. The "Striking Calamity" is a reference to the divine punishment that befell them, which is described in the Qur'an as a devastating natural disaster or cataclysmic event. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and disobedience, and the power of God to punish those who reject His guidance.
orig: كذبت ثمود وعاد بالقارعة

translation: And as for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Overwhelming [Calamity].
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of the people of Thamud, a historical tribe that lived in Arabia. They were destroyed by a severe calamity or punishment, known as the "Overwhelming" or "Taghiyah" in Arabic. This punishment is believed to have been a natural disaster, such as a thunderstorm or earthquake, that wiped out their entire community as a consequence of their rejection of the message of the Prophet Salih and their persistent disbelief and disobedience to God.
orig: فأما ثمود فأهلكوا بالطاغية

translation: And as for 'Aad, they were destroyed by a screaming, violent wind
interpretation: This verse is referring to the ancient people of 'Aad, who were destroyed by a severe and violent storm as a punishment from God for their arrogance and rejection of the message of the prophet Hud. The "screaming, violent wind" is a metaphor for the powerful and destructive nature of the storm that wiped out their civilization. This serves as a warning to those who defy God's commands and a reminder of God's power and justice.
orig: وأما عاد فأهلكوا بريح صرصر عاتية

translation: And He imposed it upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, and you could see the people therein fallen as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees.
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment that was inflicted upon the people of 'Aad, who had rejected the message of the Prophet Hud. The punishment took the form of a severe and prolonged storm that lasted for seven nights and eight days, leaving the people dead and their bodies scattered like the hollow trunks of palm trees. This serves as a warning to those who disbelieve and reject the signs of God, and a reminder of the consequences of such actions.
orig: سخرها عليهم سبع ليال وثمانية أيام حسوما فترى القوم فيها صرعى كأنهم أعجاز نخل خاوية

translation: So do you see for them any remnant?
interpretation: This verse is asking whether there is any lasting or remaining trace of the disbelievers and their deeds. The implication is that their disbelief and rejection of faith will not leave any lasting impact, and that their worldly efforts and accomplishments will be ephemeral and ultimately perish. The verse suggests that the true and lasting legacy belongs to those who believe and do righteous deeds.
orig: فهل ترى لهم من باقية

translation: And Pharaoh and those before him and the overturned cities came with sin.
interpretation: This verse refers to the arrogance and disbelief of Pharaoh and those who came before him, as well as the people of the destroyed cities like Sodom and Gomorrah. They all rejected the signs and messages of God, and instead chose to engage in sinful and wicked behavior. This serves as a warning to those who defy the teachings of God and choose to live in a state of unbelief and disobedience.
orig: وجاء فرعون ومن قبله والمؤتفكات بالخاطئة

translation: But they disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a severe seizing.
interpretation: This verse describes the consequences faced by those who disobeyed the Messenger of God. The phrase "so He seized them with a severe seizing" indicates that they were punished severely for their disobedience, which could refer to various forms of divine retribution or punishment. The interpretation suggests that when people reject the guidance and teachings of God's Messengers, they invite upon themselves the wrath and punishment of the Almighty.
orig: فعصوا رسول ربهم فأخذهم أخذة رابية

translation: Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the Flood, where Allah saved the believers by instructing them to board the ship built by Prophet Noah. The verse emphasizes that when the floodwaters rose and overwhelmed the land, Allah took care of the believers by providing them a means of salvation in the form of the sailing ship. This serves as a reminder of Allah's power and mercy, and His ability to protect those who have faith in Him even in the face of great calamity.
orig: إنا لما طغى الماء حملناكم في الجارية

translation: And We will make the Qur'an a reminder for you, so will any who has a heart or gives ear while he is present [at it] listen?
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the Qur'an and listen attentively to its message. The Qur'an is a reminder and guidance for those who have a receptive heart and are willing to listen and understand its teachings. It emphasizes the importance of being present and mindful when engaging with the Qur'an, so that its wisdom and lessons can be fully absorbed and applied in one's life.
orig: لنجعلها لكم تذكرة وتعيها أذن واعية

translation: Then when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when the trumpet will be blown to signal the end of the world and the beginning of the afterlife. The "single blast" indicates that this will be a sudden and decisive event, with no gradual transition. This verse emphasizes the finality and inevitability of the coming Judgment Day, when all people will be held accountable for their actions in life.
orig: فإذا نفخ في الصور نفخة واحدة

translation: And the earth and the mountains will be lifted and leveled as one single (smooth) plane.
interpretation: This verse describes the cataclysmic events that will occur at the end of the world, when the earth and mountains will be completely transformed. The earth and mountains will be lifted up and leveled, becoming a flat, smooth surface. This signifies the total destruction and re-creation of the physical world, as part of the final judgment and the transition to the afterlife.
orig: وحملت الأرض والجبال فدكتا دكة واحدة

translation: And on that Day the Occurrence will occur.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the ultimate reality will unfold and the consequences of people's actions in this life will be revealed. The "Occurrence" (al-Waqi'ah) is a term used in the Qur'an to describe the Day of Resurrection, a momentous event that will transform the world as we know it. On that Day, all people will be held accountable for their beliefs and deeds, and the ultimate truth will become manifest.
orig: فيومئذ وقعت الواقعة

translation: And the sky breaks apart, and on that Day it will be fragile
interpretation: This verse describes the dramatic events that will take place on the Day of Judgment, when the sky will split apart. The sky, which is normally strong and stable, will become fragile and weak on that momentous day. This signifies the complete transformation of the natural order and the ushering in of a new reality in the Hereafter.
orig: وانشقت السماء فهي يومئذ واهية

translation: And the kingdom on that Day will be the True [dominion], belonging to the Most Merciful. And it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse speaks of the Day of Judgment, when the true sovereignty will belong to Allah, the Most Merciful. On that day, the disbelievers will face a difficult reckoning for their rejection of faith and righteous deeds. The verse emphasizes that the ultimate power and authority rests with Allah alone, and that the disbelievers will be held accountable for their actions on that momentous day.
orig: والملك على أرجائها ويحمل عرش ربك فوقهم يومئذ ثمانية

translation: That Day, you will be exhibited [for judgment]; not hidden among you is anything concealed.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when all people will be presented before Allah for judgment. On that day, nothing will be hidden or concealed from Allah, as He has full knowledge of all that we have done, said, and even thought. This serves as a reminder to be mindful of our actions and to strive to live righteously, as we will be held accountable for everything on that momentous day.
orig: يومئذ تعرضون لا تخفى منكم خافية

translation: And as for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, "Here, read my record!"
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when people will be divided into two groups based on their deeds in life. Those who have done good and are given their record (of deeds) in their right hand will joyfully invite others to read their record, confident in the knowledge that they have lived a righteous life. This verse highlights the importance of doing good and being accountable for one's actions, as the outcome on the Day of Judgment will be determined by one's own deeds.
orig: فأما من أوتي كتابه بيمينه فيقول هاؤم اقرءوا كتابيه

translation: Indeed, I was certain that I would [have to] account [for my deeds].
interpretation: This verse expresses the speaker's deep conviction that they would have to face the consequences of their actions and be held accountable for their deeds before God. It reflects a sense of responsibility and a recognition of the need to prepare for the Day of Judgment, where each person will be held accountable for their choices and actions in life.
orig: إني ظننت أني ملاق حسابيه

translation: And he will be in a pleasant life.
interpretation: This verse refers to the state of the righteous believer in the Hereafter. The phrase "in a pleasant life" suggests that the believer will be in a state of contentment, satisfaction, and bliss in the afterlife. This is a reward for their faith, good deeds, and righteous conduct in this world.
orig: فهو في عيشة راضية

translation: In an elevated Garden
interpretation: This verse refers to the reward for the righteous in the afterlife. It describes a lofty, elevated Garden, which is a metaphor for the paradise that awaits those who have lived a virtuous life. The elevated nature of this Garden suggests its exalted status, signifying the high rank and honor bestowed upon the inhabitants of this eternal abode.
orig: في جنة عالية

translation: Its fruit is near [to being picked]
interpretation: This verse from the Qur'an is describing a bountiful garden, where the fruit is easily accessible and ready to be picked. It suggests a state of abundance and ease, where the rewards are within reach. The interpretation is that when one is steadfast in their faith and good deeds, the blessings and rewards of the Hereafter will be readily available to them, as if the "fruit" of their efforts is "near" and easily attainable.
orig: قطوفها دانية

translation: Eat and drink with good cheer because of what you used to do [in days past].
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to enjoy the blessings and provisions that Allah has bestowed upon them, as a reward for their righteous deeds and obedience in the past.
