translation: To a known extent
interpretation: This verse suggests that everything in the universe, including the life of every living being, is created and governed by God according to a predetermined plan and measure. It implies that there is a divine order and purpose behind the creation and existence of all things, and that nothing happens by chance or without a specific reason or limit set by God.
orig: إلى قدر معلوم

translation: And We have measured, and excellent [are We] to measure.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that God has measured and determined all things with perfect wisdom and precision. It suggests that God's power and control over the universe is absolute, and that He is the best of all those who have the ability to measure, plan, and execute. This verse emphasizes the perfection and completeness of God's creation and His dominion over all things.
orig: فقدرنا فنعم القادرون

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse conveys a warning of a severe punishment on the Day of Judgment for those who deny the truth of God's message and reject faith. The term "woe" suggests a state of great distress, calamity, and suffering that will befall the disbelievers on that momentous day. The interpretation emphasizes the gravity of the consequences faced by those who stubbornly reject the divine guidance and refuse to believe in God's signs and teachings.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Have We not made the earth a resting place?
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has created the earth as a place of rest and comfort for humanity. The earth is a habitable and hospitable place that provides for our needs and allows us to live and thrive. This verse encourages us to appreciate the blessings of the earth and to use its resources responsibly, as a trust from Allah.
orig: ألم نجعل الأرض كفاتا

translation: The living and the dead
interpretation: This verse refers to the concept of life and death in the Qur'an. It suggests that there are two states of being: the living and the dead. The living are those who are alive and actively engaged in the world, while the dead are those who have passed away. This verse emphasizes the idea that life and death are both part of the divine plan, and that all people will ultimately return to Allah, the Creator, after their earthly existence.
orig: أحياء وأمواتا

translation: And We have placed within the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with you, and We have made therein [mountain] passes and highways that you might be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's creation of the earth and its features, particularly the mountains which serve to stabilize the earth and provide pathways for people to travel. The mountains are described as "firmly set" and "lofty", indicating their strength and permanence. The verse also mentions that God has provided "sweet water" for the people, a reference to the rivers and other sources of fresh water that sustain life on earth. The overall message is one of God's power, wisdom and provision for His creation.
orig: وجعلنا فيها رواسي شامخات وأسقيناكم ماء فراتا

translation: Woe that Day to the deniers!
interpretation: This verse conveys a stern warning to those who reject and deny the truth of God's message and the Day of Judgment. On that fateful day, the deniers will face a terrible fate, filled with anguish, regret, and divine punishment for their disbelief and refusal to submit to the will of the Almighty. The verse emphasizes the gravity of the consequences that await those who turn away from the guidance of the Qur'an and choose to live in denial of the ultimate accountability before God.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Go to that which you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse is a command from God to the disbelievers, instructing them to confront the consequences of their rejection of faith. It suggests that they will be held accountable for their denial of God's signs and messages, and will be faced with the realities they had previously dismissed. The interpretation emphasizes the notion that one's actions and beliefs have consequences, and that denying the truth does not absolve one from responsibility.
orig: انطلقوا إلى ما كنتم به تكذبون

translation: Go you to a shadow (of smoke ascending) in three columns,
interpretation: This verse is inviting the disbelievers to seek refuge in the shade or protection of God, which is described as having three distinct qualities or characteristics. The "three columns" may symbolize the three main attributes of God: His power, His mercy, and His guidance. The invitation suggests that the only true protection and refuge is to be found in God, and not in the false deities or worldly pursuits that the disbelievers were following.
orig: انطلقوا إلى ظل ذي ثلاث شعب

translation: There is no shade and no protection from the blaze
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and intensity of the punishment in the Hellfire. It suggests that there will be no refuge or shelter from the scorching heat and flames of the Hellfire. The verse conveys a sense of the complete lack of comfort or relief for those who are condemned to the Hellfire, highlighting the unrelenting and inescapable nature of this punishment.
orig: لا ظليل ولا يغني من اللهب

translation: Indeed, it [i.e., the fire] throws sparks [as huge] as a fortress.
interpretation: This verse is describing the intensity and magnitude of the fire in Hell. The sparks emitted from this fire are likened to the size of a large fortress, emphasizing the terrifying and overwhelming nature of the punishment awaiting those who disbelieve and disobey God. The imagery conveys the severity and unimaginable scale of the torment that awaits the wrongdoers in the Hereafter.
orig: إنها ترمي بشرر كالقصر

translation: As if they were tethered yellow camels.
interpretation: This verse is using a vivid metaphor to describe a group of people who are lifeless, motionless, and devoid of any energy or vitality. The comparison to "tethered yellow camels" evokes a sense of stagnation and inertia, suggesting that these individuals are passive, unresponsive, and lacking in any meaningful purpose or direction. The imagery conveys a sense of desolation and a lack of dynamism, highlighting the spiritual or psychological state of the individuals being described.
orig: كأنه جمالت صفر

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who deny the truth of God's message and reject the Day of Judgment. It conveys a sense of impending doom and calamity that will befall the disbelievers on the Day of Reckoning. The term "woe" ("wail" or "alas") suggests intense suffering, regret, and anguish that the deniers will experience on that fateful day when they are held accountable for their actions and beliefs.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: This is a Day on which they will not speak.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when people will not be able to speak and make excuses for their actions. On that day, all will be held accountable for their deeds, and their silence will be a testament to the truth of their record. The inability to speak represents the finality and gravity of the situation, where no one can escape the consequences of their choices in life.
orig: هذا يوم لا ينطقون

translation: And they will not be permitted to apologize.
interpretation: This verse indicates that on the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers and wrongdoers will not be given the opportunity to make excuses or apologize for their misdeeds. They will be held fully accountable for their actions, and no justification or plea for forgiveness will be accepted from them.
orig: ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse warns of a dire fate on the Day of Judgment for those who reject the truth of God's message and refuse to believe in it. The term "woe" conveys a sense of severe punishment and torment that will befall the deniers on that momentous day. The verse emphasizes the gravity of the consequences for those who stubbornly deny the divine revelations and guidance.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: This is the Day of Judgement. We have gathered you and the former (generations).
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when all of humanity will be gathered before God for the final judgment. It emphasizes the universality of this event, as both the present and former generations will be held accountable for their actions. The "Day of Judgement" is a pivotal moment when the fate of each individual will be determined based on their beliefs and deeds in this life.
orig: هذا يوم الفصل جمعناكم والأولين

translation: And if you have a plan, then plan against me.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who plot and scheme against the believers. It suggests that if the disbelievers have a plan to undermine the faith, then they should go ahead and execute it, but the believers should also devise their own plan to counter their schemes. The verse emphasizes the importance of vigilance and strategic planning in the face of adversity, and encourages the believers to be proactive in defending their faith and their community.
orig: فإن كان لكم كيد فكيدون

translation: Woe that Day to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and the Day of Judgment. On that fateful day, the disbelievers will face severe punishment and torment for their denial of the truth. The word "woe" conveys a sense of immense suffering and calamity that awaits them. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to strive to guide others towards the truth.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in the midst of gardens and springs
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the righteous, those who fear Allah and follow His commands, will be rewarded in the Hereafter with a blissful abode in the Gardens of Paradise, surrounded by shades and flowing springs. This imagery conveys a sense of tranquility, comfort, and abundance that awaits the pious in the Afterlife.
orig: إن المتقين في ظلال وعيون

translation: And fruits from whatever they desire.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the inhabitants of Paradise will be provided with a wide variety of delicious fruits that they desire and enjoy. The emphasis on "whatever they desire" implies that the fruits in Paradise will cater to the individual tastes and preferences of its inhabitants, providing them with a fulfilling and satisfying experience.
orig: وفواكه مما يشتهون

translation: Eat and drink with enjoyment for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to consume food and drink with a sense of gratitude and contentment, as a reward for their righteous deeds. It suggests that the blessings of sustenance should be enjoyed with a spirit of appreciation, rather than with greed or excess. The verse emphasizes that the true pleasure in life comes from living righteously and being grateful for God's provisions.
orig: كلوا واشربوا هنيئا بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah rewards those who do good deeds and act righteously. It suggests that just as Allah has rewarded the previous good-doers, He will also reward those who continue to do good in the present and future. The interpretation conveys the message that those who strive to please Allah and benefit others will be compensated for their efforts.
orig: إنا كذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the truth and deny the Day of Judgment. It conveys a sense of impending doom and calamity that will befall the disbelievers on that fateful day. The term "woe" suggests a severe punishment and suffering that awaits those who refuse to believe in the divine message and the accountability that comes with it. This verse serves as a reminder to humanity to embrace faith, repentance, and righteous deeds in order to avoid the dire consequences of disbelief.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Eat and enjoy yourselves a little. Indeed, you are criminals.
interpretation: This verse is addressing those who have committed sins and transgressions. It is a warning to them that their enjoyment and indulgence in worldly pleasures is only temporary, and that they will be held accountable for their misdeeds. The verse emphasizes that their actions are criminal in nature, and that they should not be complacent or feel secure in their wrongdoings.
orig: كلوا وتمتعوا قليلا إنكم مجرمون

translation: Woe on that Day to the deniers!
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the message of the Qur'an and the teachings of Islam. On the Day of Judgment, those who denied the truth will face severe punishment and suffering. The word "woe" conveys a sense of sorrow, distress, and impending doom for the deniers. This verse emphasizes the importance of believing in and accepting the divine guidance revealed in the Qur'an, as the consequences of rejecting it will be grave.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: And when it is said to them, "Prostrate," they do not prostrate.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who refuse to submit to the will of God and obey His commands. They are arrogant and unwilling to humble themselves before the Almighty. This attitude of defiance and lack of humility is displeasing to God and can lead to spiritual downfall and loss in the Hereafter.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اركعوا لا يركعون

translation: Woe that Day to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse warns those who reject the truth and deny the Day of Judgment. It conveys a sense of impending doom and calamity that will befall the disbelievers on that fateful day when they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse emphasizes the severity of the consequences faced by those who stubbornly refuse to acknowledge the divine message and the reality of the Hereafter.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Then in what statement after it will they believe?
interpretation: This verse is posing a rhetorical question, implying that if people do not believe in the Qur'an, the word of God, then what other message or statement will they believe in? It suggests that the Qur'an is the ultimate truth and guidance, and that rejecting it means rejecting the very foundation of faith and belief.
orig: فبأي حديث بعده يؤمنون

translation: About what are they asking?
interpretation: This verse is asking about what the disbelievers are questioning or inquiring about. It suggests that they are raising questions or doubts about the message of the Quran and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse invites the reader to contemplate the nature of their questions and the underlying motivations behind them.
orig: عم يتساءلون

translation: About the great news
interpretation: This verse is referring to the news of the Day of Resurrection, which is a momentous and awe-inspiring event. The Qur'an often emphasizes the importance of believing in and preparing for the Hereafter, as it is the ultimate destination for all human beings. This "great news" is a call to reflect on the significance of the Afterlife and to live one's life in a way that is pleasing to God.
orig: عن النبإ العظيم

translation: That wherein they differ
interpretation: This verse refers to the differences and disputes that people have regarding matters of faith, belief, and religious practices. The Quran acknowledges that there are diverse perspectives and disagreements among people, but it encourages them to seek common ground and to resolve their differences through dialogue and mutual understanding, rather than through conflict and division.
orig: الذي هم فيه مختلفون

translation: Nay, they shall soon know.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who deny the truth and reject the message of Islam. It suggests that they will soon come to realize the consequences of their actions, either in this life or the Hereafter. The verse conveys a sense of certainty and determination, indicating that the truth will prevail, and those who oppose it will be held accountable.
orig: كلا سيعلمون

translation: Then, no! They are going to know.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who have denied the truth or turned away from it will eventually come to know the consequences of their actions. It implies that there will be a day of reckoning when they will be held accountable for their deeds. The phrase "Then, no!" emphasizes the certainty of this outcome, and the expression "They are going to know" indicates that they will come to realize the error of their ways, either in this life or in the Hereafter.
orig: ثم كلا سيعلمون

translation: Have We not made the earth a resting place?
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the blessings of Allah in creating the earth as a comfortable and habitable place for human beings. The earth, with its vast expanse and diverse landscapes, is likened to a "resting place" or a place of repose and tranquility. This suggests that the earth has been designed and prepared by Allah to provide a suitable environment for human life and habitation, where people can find rest, sustenance, and the means to live and thrive.
orig: ألم نجعل الأرض مهادا

translation: And the mountains, [He created them] as pegs
interpretation: This verse is referring to the mountains and their role in providing stability and anchoring the Earth. The mountains are described as "pegs" which suggests that they serve as a foundation, keeping the Earth stable and preventing it from shaking or moving excessively. This is a metaphorical way of highlighting the important geological function of mountains in maintaining the Earth's equilibrium and providing a solid base for the land.
orig: والجبال أوتادا

translation: And We have created you in pairs
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has created human beings in pairs, male and female. This indicates the natural complementarity between the sexes and the importance of the institution of marriage in Islamic teachings. The pairing of humans reflects the divine wisdom and design in creation, where each individual is meant to find fulfillment and completion through their relationship with their spouse.
orig: وخلقناكم أزواجا

translation: And We have made your sleep [a means for] rest
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that sleep is a blessing from God, as it provides rest and rejuvenation for the human body and mind. Sleep is described as a "saba	an", which means a state of rest, tranquility, and repose. This suggests that sleep is not merely a passive state, but a purposeful and restorative function that God has created for the benefit of humanity.
orig: وجعلنا نومكم سباتا

translation: And We have made the night as a covering
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has created the night as a covering or a veil for people, providing rest and respite from the activities of the day. The night is a time for sleep, relaxation, and introspection, allowing people to rejuvenate and prepare for the next day's tasks. The interpretation suggests that Allah has designed the natural cycle of day and night for the benefit and well-being of His creation.
orig: وجعلنا الليل لباسا

translation: And We have made the day for livelihood
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has created the day for people to seek their sustenance and engage in various activities to earn a living. The day is a time of activity, work, and productivity, in contrast to the night which is a time of rest and repose. The verse highlights Allah's provision and care for His creation, ensuring that humans have the means to support themselves and their families through the opportunities presented during the day.
orig: وجعلنا النهار معاشا

translation: And We have built over you seven firmaments
interpretation: This verse refers to the seven heavens or layers of the universe that Allah has created above us. The term "seven firmaments" suggests that the universe has a layered structure, with each layer or heaven serving a specific purpose in the overall divine plan. This verse emphasizes the vastness and complexity of Allah's creation, and the idea that the universe is not a simple, single-layered entity but a multi-dimensional, intricate system designed by the Almighty.
orig: وبنينا فوقكم سبعا شدادا

translation: And We have made [therein] a burning lamp
interpretation: This verse is referring to the sun, which is described as a "burning lamp" that provides light and warmth to the earth. The sun is a crucial part of God's creation, serving as a source of illumination and sustenance for all living beings. This verse highlights the sun's importance and the wisdom behind its creation as a guiding light for humanity.
orig: وجعلنا سراجا وهاجا

translation: And We have sent down from the rain-laden clouds pouring water
interpretation: This verse is referring to the provision of water from the clouds, which is essential for sustaining life on Earth. The word "المعصرات" (al-mu'asirāt) means "the rain-laden clouds" that pour down water in abundance. This is a metaphor for God's bountiful provision and care for His creation. The interpretation is that God, in His infinite wisdom and power, has provided a vital resource - water - to sustain all living beings on the planet.
orig: وأنزلنا من المعصرات ماء ثجاجا

translation: That We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation
interpretation: This verse is referring to the process of growth and cultivation, where water (from the rain) is used to produce crops and vegetation. The interpretation is that Allah provides the means for sustenance and life to flourish on Earth through the natural cycle of water and plant growth.
orig: لنخرج به حبا ونباتا

translation: And gardens of grapevines
interpretation: This verse refers to the gardens of Paradise that are filled with grapevines. The mention of "gardens of grapevines" suggests a bountiful and lush environment in the Hereafter, where the believers will enjoy the fruits of their righteous deeds. The imagery of grapevines evokes a sense of abundance, beauty, and tranquility that awaits those who have faith and lead a virtuous life.
orig: وجنات ألفافا

translation: Indeed, the Day of Separation was an appointed time.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, which is the day when people will be separated and held accountable for their actions in life. It emphasizes that this day is a predetermined and inevitable event, set by Allah (God) as a time for reckoning and the final judgment of all human beings. The "Day of Separation" underscores the finality and irreversibility of this momentous occasion, where the righteous will be distinguished from the wicked, and each person will receive their just reward or punishment.
orig: إن يوم الفصل كان ميقاتا

translation: The Day the Horn is blown - and you will come forth in multitudes
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when the Trumpet will be blown and all people will be resurrected and gathered before God for Judgment. The imagery of people coming forth "in multitudes" conveys the vastness of the gathering, as all of humanity will be present to account for their deeds in life. This emphasizes the gravity and finality of the Day of Judgment, when each person will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: يوم ينفخ في الصور فتأتون أفواجا

translation: And the heaven will be opened and will become gateways
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the heavens will be opened and the gates of the afterlife will become accessible to people. It signifies the transition from the worldly life to the eternal life in the hereafter, where the souls will pass through the gates of heaven to face their final judgment and the consequences of their deeds in this life.
orig: وفتحت السماء فكانت أبوابا

translation: And the mountains are moved and become a mirage
interpretation: This verse describes the dramatic changes that will occur on the Day of Judgment, when the mountains - which are often seen as symbols of permanence and stability - will be uprooted and become like a mirage, an illusion that appears real but has no substance. This signifies the complete transformation of the physical world as we know it, highlighting the temporary nature of this earthly existence and the inevitability of the Hereafter.
orig: وسيرت الجبال فكانت سرابا

translation: Indeed, Hell has been in wait
interpretation: This verse conveys the message that Hell is a place that is always ready and waiting to receive those who disbelieve in God and reject His guidance. It suggests that the punishment of Hell is inevitable for those who choose to live a life of sin and disobedience. The verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of the punishment that awaits the wrongdoers in the Hereafter.
orig: إن جهنم كانت مرصادا

translation: For the transgressors is a [final] destination
interpretation: This verse is referring to the ultimate destination and fate of those who transgress the limits set by God, who reject faith, and who engage in wrongdoing. The "transgressors" (at-tagheen) are those who overstep the bounds of what is right and lawful, and they will face a dire and unpleasant end as a consequence of their actions. The Qur'an emphasizes that there is a reckoning and a final abode for those who choose to deviate from the path of righteousness.
orig: للطاغين مآبا

translation: Abiding therein for eons
interpretation: This verse refers to the eternal nature of the punishment in Hell for those who reject faith and do evil deeds. The term "eons" ("ahqaban") suggests an extremely long, indefinite period of time, indicating that the punishment in Hell is not temporary but everlasting. The interpretation conveys the gravity and permanence of the consequences for those who choose to live in defiance of God's guidance.
orig: لابثين فيها أحقابا

translation: They will not taste therein any coolness or [any] drink
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment and suffering of the disbelievers in the Hereafter. They will not experience any comfort, relief or refreshment in Hell, but only the torment of its intense heat and thirst. This emphasizes the severity of the punishment awaiting those who reject faith and turn away from the guidance of Allah.
orig: لا يذوقون فيها بردا ولا شرابا

translation: Except scalding water and a foul discharge
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishments that await the disbelievers in the Hereafter. "Scalding water" and "foul discharge" are metaphorical descriptions of the torments they will face in Hell. The verse emphasizes the severity and unpleasantness of the punishment that the unrighteous will endure as a consequence of their rejection of faith and righteous deeds.
orig: إلا حميما وغساقا

translation: In proportion to (their) deeds
interpretation: This phrase suggests that the reward or punishment in the Hereafter will be commensurate with one's actions and deeds in this life. It indicates that there is a direct correlation between how one lives their life and the consequences they will face. The interpretation is that individuals will be held accountable for their choices and actions, and they will receive a just and fitting recompense based on their conduct.
orig: جزاء وفاقا

translation: Indeed, they were not expecting a reckoning
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people being referred to were heedless of the Day of Judgment and the consequences of their actions. They did not believe in or anticipate being held accountable for their deeds in the Hereafter. This highlights the importance of having faith in the Afterlife and being mindful of one's actions, as we will all be held responsible before Allah on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: إنهم كانوا لا يرجون حسابا

translation: And they denied Our signs with [an absolute] denial.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who stubbornly reject the signs and messages of Allah, denying them completely without any consideration or willingness to understand. It conveys the idea that they dismissed the divine revelations and evidence presented to them, refusing to acknowledge the truth with an absolute and adamant denial.
orig: وكذبوا بآياتنا كذابا

translation: And everything We have enumerated in a register.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive knowledge and record-keeping of Allah. It suggests that Allah has perfect knowledge and account of all things, both seen and unseen. This highlights the omniscience and sovereignty of Allah, as He is aware of every detail and has everything documented in His eternal record. This verse serves as a reminder that we are accountable to Allah for our actions, as He keeps track of all that we do.
orig: وكل شيء أحصيناه كتابا

translation: So taste [the penalty], and never will We increase you except in punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who persist in their disbelief and disobedience. It suggests that they will face the consequences of their actions, and that their punishment will only increase if they continue on this path. The interpretation is that those who reject the truth and refuse to believe in God will be subject to an ever-worsening punishment, as a result of their own choices and actions.
orig: فذوقوا فلن نزيدكم إلا عذابا

translation: Indeed, for the righteous is attainment
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who are righteous, who fear and obey Allah, will attain a great success or triumph in the Hereafter. The term "mafazan" suggests a place of safety, security, and ultimate fulfillment, which the righteous will deserve and receive as a reward for their piety and good deeds in this life.
orig: إن للمتقين مفازا

translation: Gardens and grapes
interpretation: This verse likely refers to the bountiful and lush gardens and vineyards that will be part of the rewards in the Hereafter for the righteous believers. The mention of "gardens and grapes" symbolizes the abundance, beauty, and pleasures that await those who have lived virtuous lives and submitted to the will of God.
orig: حدائق وأعنابا

translation: And youthful companions (of equal age)
interpretation: This verse refers to the delightful companions that the righteous will have in Paradise. These companions will be of the same age, beautiful, and full of vigor, providing each other with joy and companionship in the eternal abode.
orig: وكواعب أترابا

translation: And a brimming cup
interpretation: This verse is describing the delights and pleasures that await the righteous in the Hereafter. The "brimming cup" is a metaphor for the abundant and overflowing bounties that the believers will enjoy in Paradise. It signifies the fulfillment of their desires and the quenching of their spiritual thirst with the purest and most delightful of drinks.
orig: وكأسا دهاقا

translation: They will not hear therein any ill speech or any sinful talk
interpretation: This verse indicates that in the Hereafter, in Paradise, the believers will be free from hearing any kind of harmful, false or sinful speech. They will only hear that which is good, pure and truthful, as they will be in a state of complete bliss and tranquility.
orig: لا يسمعون فيها لغوا ولا كذابا

translation: A recompense from your Lord, a [generous] gift [made due by account]
interpretation: This verse suggests that the rewards and blessings bestowed by God upon the righteous are not arbitrary, but are rather the result of a careful and just reckoning. The phrase "a [generous] gift [made due by account]" implies that these rewards are not merely random acts of generosity, but are earned through one's deeds and actions. This emphasizes the idea that the rewards of the Hereafter are commensurate with one's conduct in this life, and that God's judgment is fair and based on a comprehensive accounting of one's words and deeds.
orig: جزاء من ربك عطاء حسابا

translation: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them - the Most Merciful, they possess not from Him [any] power of speech.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and supremacy of Allah (God), the Creator of the heavens and the earth. It states that the Most Merciful, Allah, has no equal and no one can challenge His authority or speak to Him on equal terms. This verse serves to remind us of Allah's unparalleled power and the need to submit to Him in all matters.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما الرحمن لا يملكون منه خطابا

translation: The Day when the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, they will not speak except for whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is correct.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Resurrection, when the souls of the deceased and the angels will stand in orderly rows before the Almighty. On that momentous day, no one will be able to speak unless they are granted permission by the Most Merciful, Allah. Those who are given permission will only utter the truth and what is right, as they will be under the direct guidance and authority of the Divine.
orig: يوم يقوم الروح والملائكة صفا لا يتكلمون إلا من أذن له الرحمن وقال صوابا

translation: That is the true Day, so he who wills may take to his Lord a [way of] return.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgement, which is the true and inevitable day when all people will be held accountable for their actions in life. On that day, those who have lived righteously and believed in God will have the opportunity to return to their Lord and attain eternal bliss in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes that this is a matter of individual choice - whoever wills may choose to seek a way back to God through faith and good deeds.
orig: ذلك اليوم الحق فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه مآبا

translation: Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment on the Day when a person will observe what his hands have put forth and the disbeliever will say, "Oh, I wish that I were dust!"
interpretation: This verse warns of the impending punishment that will come on the Day of Judgment. On that day, every person will be held accountable for their actions and deeds in this life. The disbeliever, realizing the consequences of their rejection of faith, will wish they had never existed and were just dust. This emphasizes the importance of righteous conduct in this life, as the ultimate reckoning is inevitable.
orig: إنا أنذرناكم عذابا قريبا يوم ينظر المرء ما قدمت يداه ويقول الكافر يا ليتني كنت ترابا

translation: By those (angels) who pull out (the souls of the wicked) with violence;
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who forcefully extract the souls of the wicked from their bodies on the Day of Judgment. The interpretation suggests that the wicked will be subjected to a painful and violent process of being separated from their earthly existence, as a consequence of their misdeeds in life.
orig: والنازعات غرقا

translation: And [by] the racers, racing
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels or other celestial beings who race swiftly to carry out the commands of Allah. The interpretation suggests that these beings are diligent, energetic, and eager to fulfill their duties, moving with speed and vigor in service of the divine will.
orig: والناشطات نشطا

translation: And [by] those who swim [i.e., the angels]
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who glorify and praise Allah constantly. The angels are described as "those who swim" to convey the idea of their swift and effortless movement as they carry out Allah's commands. This verse emphasizes the devotion and submission of the angels to Allah, and serves as a reminder for humans to emulate their example in worshiping and glorifying the Almighty.
orig: والسابحات سبحا

translation: And the foremost [in faith] - the foremost.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are the first and foremost in accepting the message of Islam and striving in the way of Allah. They are the ones who have taken the lead in faith, good deeds, and obedience to Allah. This group is praised and given a special status in the Quran, as they have set the example for others to follow and have earned the pleasure of Allah through their unwavering commitment and dedication.
orig: فالسابقات سبقا

translation: By those [angels] who arrange [each] matter
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who are responsible for managing and executing the commands of Allah. They are the ones who arrange and direct the affairs of the universe according to Allah"s will. This verse emphasizes the role of the angels in carrying out the divine plan and serving as intermediaries between Allah and His creation.
orig: فالمدبرات أمرا

translation: The Day the Quaking [Earthquake] Occurs
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the earth will be shaken and trembling will overtake all beings. It is a warning to humanity to prepare for the inevitable reckoning that will take place on that momentous day, when all actions will be accounted for and the true nature of each person will be revealed. The interpretation emphasizes the gravity and solemnity of that day, and the need for individuals to live righteous lives in anticipation of it.
orig: يوم ترجف الراجفة

translation: Then follows her the Rādifah
interpretation: This verse refers to the concept of the Rādifah, which is often interpreted as the second blast of the trumpet on the Day of Resurrection. The Rādifah is believed to be the event that will follow the first blast, which will cause the death of all living beings. The Rādifah is then understood to be the second blast that will resurrect all the dead and gather them for the final Judgment.
orig: تتبعها الرادفة

translation: The hearts that Day will be trembling
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when people will be filled with fear and anxiety as they await the final reckoning. The "hearts that Day will be trembling" suggests a state of deep unease and uncertainty, as individuals confront the consequences of their actions in life. This verse serves as a reminder of the gravity of the Day of Judgment and the importance of living a righteous life in preparation for that momentous occasion.
orig: قلوب يومئذ واجفة

translation: Their eyes will be humbled
interpretation: This verse refers to the state of the people on the Day of Judgment, where they will be in a state of awe and humility before the Almighty. Their eyes, which were once filled with pride and arrogance, will be lowered in a submissive manner, acknowledging the greatness and power of God.
orig: أبصارها خاشعة

translation: They say, "Is it true that we will be brought back to life (after death)?"
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who deny the concept of resurrection and the afterlife. They question whether they will be brought back to life after death, as the Quran teaches. The interpretation is that this verse is highlighting the skepticism and denial of the disbelievers regarding the resurrection and the return to God for judgment.
orig: يقولون أإنا لمردودون في الحافرة

translation: Is it when we are decayed bones?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question that challenges the notion of resurrection and the afterlife. It suggests that when a person's body has decayed and turned into mere bones, how can they be resurrected? The verse is meant to make the reader ponder the power of God and the reality of the afterlife, which may seem impossible from a human perspective but is entirely possible for the Almighty.
orig: أإذا كنا عظاما نخرة

translation: They say, "That, then, would be a losing return."
interpretation: This verse is referring to the disbelievers who reject the idea of resurrection and accountability in the Hereafter. They consider the concept of returning to God and being held accountable for their actions as a "losing return" - something that would be detrimental to them. The verse highlights their shortsighted and dismissive attitude towards the truth of the Hereafter, which they perceive as a loss rather than an opportunity for eternal success.
orig: قالوا تلك إذا كرة خاسرة

translation: Then it will be but a single cry
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when a single, powerful call from God will resurrect all of humanity from their graves. The interpretation suggests that the process of the Resurrection will be swift and decisive, with no drawn-out events, but rather a single, overwhelming command from the Almighty that will bring about the end of this world and the beginning of the Hereafter.
orig: فإنما هي زجرة واحدة

translation: And then they will be in the open plain
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, people will be gathered in an open, vast plain to be held accountable for their actions in life. The "Sahira" (the open plain) refers to the place where the resurrection and the final reckoning will take place. This verse emphasizes the magnitude and gravity of the event, as people will be exposed and vulnerable in this vast, open space before God.
orig: فإذا هم بالساهرة

translation: Has the story of Moses reached you?
interpretation: This verse is asking if the story of the Prophet Moses has reached the listener. The story of Moses is one of the most prominent narratives in the Qur'an, as it provides guidance and lessons for believers. This verse serves as an introduction to the detailed account of Moses' life and mission that follows in the Qur'an, highlighting its importance and encouraging the listener to reflect on this significant story.
orig: هل أتاك حديث موسى

translation: When his Lord called him in the sacred valley of Tuwa
interpretation: This verse refers to the time when God called Prophet Moses in the sacred valley of Tuwa, which is believed to be located in the Sinai Peninsula. This event marks the beginning of Moses' prophethood, where God commissioned him to go to Pharaoh and deliver the message of monotheism and freedom for the Israelites. The verse emphasizes the sacred nature of the location, signifying the importance and gravity of the divine call that Moses received.
orig: إذ ناداه ربه بالواد المقدس طوى

translation: Go to Pharaoh, indeed he has transgressed.
interpretation: This verse is commanding the Prophet Moses to go to the tyrannical ruler Pharaoh and confront him, for he has exceeded all bounds of justice and oppression. The verse highlights the need to stand up against tyranny and injustice, even in the face of powerful oppressors. It encourages believers to have the courage to challenge those in authority who abuse their power and violate the rights of the people.
orig: اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى

translation: So say, "Is there any way for you [to be guided]?"
interpretation: This verse is encouraging the listener to reflect on their own spiritual state and seek guidance from God. The phrase "Is there any way for you [to be guided]?" suggests that there is a path to purification and spiritual growth available, if one is willing to seek it out. The interpretation is that the verse is a call to self-reflection and a reminder that the opportunity for spiritual development is present, if one chooses to pursue it.
orig: فقل هل لك إلى أن تزكى

translation: And I will guide you to your Lord, and you shall fear [Him]
interpretation: This verse encourages the listener to submit to and worship Allah (God) with reverence and awe. The guidance mentioned here refers to the divine guidance provided through the teachings of the Quran and the Prophet Muhammad. By following this guidance, one will develop a deep sense of fear and reverence for the Almighty, which is essential for a righteous life and attaining salvation.
orig: وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى

translation: And he showed him the Greatest Sign.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) being shown the "Greatest Sign" during his Night Journey (al-Isra' wal-Mi'raj). The "Greatest Sign" is believed to be a vision or experience of the highest levels of the divine presence, which strengthened the Prophet's faith and connection with Allah. This event was a profound spiritual experience that affirmed the Prophet's role as the final messenger of God.
orig: فأراه الآية الكبرى

translation: But he denied and disobeyed
interpretation: This verse refers to a person who rejected the truth and rebelled against the commands of God. The interpretation suggests that this person chose to disbelieve and disobey, despite being presented with the truth. This behavior is condemned in the Quran, as it leads to spiritual and moral downfall.
orig: فكذب وعصى

translation: Then he turned back, walking swiftly.
interpretation: This verse is describing the reaction of a person who has been admonished or warned. After receiving the message, he turns away and walks off quickly, as if trying to avoid further discussion or confrontation. This suggests a dismissive or evasive attitude, where the person is unwilling to engage with the message or consider it seriously.
orig: ثم أدبر يسعى

translation: And he gathered [his people] and called out,
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Salih, who was sent to the people of Thamud. When they rejected his message and continued in their disbelief, he gathered them and called out to them, warning them of the impending punishment they would face if they did not heed his message and repent.
orig: فحشر فنادى

translation: And [Pharaoh] said, "I am your lord, the Most High."
interpretation: This verse refers to the arrogance and delusion of Pharaoh, who claimed divinity and superiority over his people. It highlights the danger of egotism and the rejection of God's true sovereignty. The interpretation is that such hubris and false claims of supremacy are condemned in Islam, as only God is worthy of worship and obedience.
orig: فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى

translation: And Allah seized him with an exemplary punishment in the Hereafter and the first [life].
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that Allah inflicts upon those who reject His guidance and persist in their wrongdoing. The phrase "an exemplary punishment" suggests that the punishment serves as a lesson and a warning to others, deterring them from similar transgressions. The punishment is said to be experienced both in the Hereafter and in this life, indicating that there are consequences for one's actions in both the spiritual and temporal realms.
orig: فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى

translation: Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever fears [Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that in the events and signs of the universe, there is a lesson and a reminder for those who fear and revere Allah. It encourages people to reflect on the wonders of creation and to draw lessons from them that can guide them towards righteous living and a deeper relationship with the Divine.
orig: إن في ذلك لعبرة لمن يخشى

translation: Are you a more difficult creation or is the heaven He constructed?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question to highlight the power and might of Allah in creating the heavens. The implication is that the creation of the heavens is a far greater feat than the creation of human beings, who are questioning Allah's authority. The verse serves to remind us of the immense power and sovereignty of the divine Creator, and to humble ourselves before His grandeur.
orig: أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء بناها

translation: He raised its ceiling and proportioned it
interpretation: This verse refers to God's creation of the universe. It suggests that God raised the heavens and gave them their proper form and structure. The interpretation is that God has created the cosmos in a perfectly balanced and proportioned manner, demonstrating His power, wisdom and artistry.
orig: رفع سمكها فسواها

translation: And [by] the night when it covers [the world in] darkness, And [by] the day when it emerges in brightness
interpretation: This verse is referring to the cycle of day and night, and the contrast between the darkness of night and the brightness of day. The interpretation is that Allah is the One who created this cycle, and it is a sign of His power and wisdom. The alternation of day and night is a reminder of the order and regularity in the universe, which points to the existence of a Creator who controls and sustains all things.
orig: وأغطش ليلها وأخرج ضحاها

translation: And the earth after that He extended.
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of the earth, and how after its initial formation, God "extended" or spread it out. This can be interpreted as a reference to the expansion of the earth, either through the geological processes that shaped the planet's surface, or through a more metaphorical sense of God's power to create and shape the world. The verse suggests the earth's development was a deliberate and purposeful act of God.
orig: والأرض بعد ذلك دحاها

translation: He brought forth from it its water and its pasture
interpretation: This verse refers to God's creation of the earth and its resources. It suggests that God is the one who has brought forth the water and vegetation that sustain life on earth. This is a testament to God's power and providence, and a reminder that all of creation is dependent on Him.
orig: أخرج منها ماءها ومرعاها

translation: And the mountains - He has firmly fixed them,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and wisdom in creating the mountains and firmly establishing them on the earth. The mountains provide stability and balance to the earth's surface, and their presence is a sign of God's creative might. This verse invites us to reflect on the wonders of God's creation and to appreciate the order and purpose that underlies the natural world.
orig: والجبال أرساها

translation: A provision for you and your cattle
interpretation: This verse refers to the provision of sustenance and resources not only for humans but also for their livestock. It suggests that Allah has made available various means of sustenance and livelihood not just for people, but also for the animals under their care. This highlights the divine care and provision for all of Allah's creation, and the responsibility humans have to manage and utilize these resources responsibly.
orig: متاعا لكم ولأنعامكم

translation: And when the greatest Catastrophe comes
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, the greatest catastrophe that will occur when the world as we know it ends. It signifies the arrival of the final hour, when all of humanity will be gathered for the reckoning of their deeds and the ultimate judgment by God. This verse serves as a reminder to be prepared for this momentous event and to live a righteous life in anticipation of that day.
orig: فإذا جاءت الطامة الكبرى

translation: The Day when man will remember what he strove for
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when every human being will be held accountable for their actions and deeds in this life. On that day, each person will remember and reflect upon the efforts they made, whether good or bad, and the consequences of their choices. The interpretation suggests that this verse serves as a reminder to humanity to strive for righteous and meaningful actions during their lifetime, as they will be held responsible for them on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: يوم يتذكر الإنسان ما سعى

translation: And Hell will be brought into sight for [all] those who see,
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the reality of Hell will become clearly visible to those who denied the truth and lived a life of sin. It serves as a warning to humanity to turn away from wrongdoing and embrace the path of righteousness, for the consequences of their actions will be laid bare before them on that momentous day.
orig: وبرزت الجحيم لمن يرى

translation: But as for he who transgresses
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who reject faith and engage in wrongdoing. The interpretation is that those who exceed the limits set by God, who are arrogant and oppressive, will be held accountable for their transgressions.
orig: فأما من طغى

translation: And he preferred the life of this world
interpretation: This verse suggests that the person in question has prioritized the temporary, material pleasures of this world over the eternal rewards in the Hereafter. It implies a lack of concern for spiritual development and a focus on worldly pursuits, which may lead to a neglect of one's duties and responsibilities towards God and others.
orig: وآثر الحياة الدنيا

translation: Then indeed, Hell will be the refuge.
interpretation: This verse is a warning that if one rejects faith and denies the truth, then the ultimate destination for them will be Hell, which is a place of eternal punishment and suffering. It emphasizes the importance of believing in God and following the guidance of the Qur'an in order to avoid the torment of the Hellfire.
orig: فإن الجحيم هي المأوى

translation: And as for one who had feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination
interpretation: This verse describes the righteous person who is mindful of standing before their Lord on the Day of Judgment. Such a person restrains their desires and impulses, and does not indulge in unlawful or sinful acts. They are conscious of their accountability to God and strive to live a life pleasing to Him.
orig: وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى

translation: And so the Garden, it is the refuge.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Paradise (the Garden) is the ultimate destination and refuge for the righteous believers. It emphasizes that the Garden is where they will find peace, comfort, and eternal abode in the Hereafter, after having lived a life of faith and good deeds in this world.
orig: فإن الجنة هي المأوى

translation: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the question that people were asking him about the timing of the Day of Judgment, also known as the Hour. The interpretation is that people were curious and eager to know when the Day of Resurrection would occur, but Allah, the Almighty, has kept the exact timing of this event hidden from us. The verse emphasizes that the knowledge of the Hour belongs to Allah alone, and no one else can determine its arrival.
orig: يسألونك عن الساعة أيان مرساها

translation: In what (condition) are you from remembering it?
interpretation: This verse encourages the reader to reflect on their state of remembrance of God and the hereafter. It suggests that one should be mindful of their connection to the remembrance of God, and consider how they are positioned in relation to this vital aspect of faith. The verse prompts self-reflection and a deeper engagement with one's spiritual state.
orig: فيم أنت من ذكراها

translation: To your Lord is the final destination.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that all things and all people will ultimately return to God, their Creator and the Source of all existence. It suggests that our lives and actions are not meaningless, but have a higher purpose and destination in the Hereafter. This verse encourages believers to focus on their relationship with God and to strive to please Him, as everything will be accounted for on the Day of Judgment.
orig: إلى ربك منتهاها

translation: You are but a warner of those who fear it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is a warner, sent to guide and remind those who fear the consequences of their actions and the Day of Judgment. His role is not to compel or force belief, but to convey the message of Islam and warn those who are receptive to it.
orig: إنما أنت منذر من يخشاها

translation: As if they had not stayed [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning.
interpretation: This verse is describing the fleeting nature of this worldly life. It suggests that the Day of Judgment will come so suddenly that it will seem as if people had only lived in this world for a very short period, like just an afternoon or a morning. This emphasizes the importance of preparing for the Hereafter, as our time in this world is limited and can end at any moment.
orig: كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا إلا عشية أو ضحاها

translation: He frowned and turned away
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) when a blind man came to him seeking guidance, and the Prophet was engaged in a conversation with some influential leaders of Makkah. The verse is a gentle reprimand, indicating that the Prophet should not have frowned and turned away from the blind man, as all people deserve equal attention and respect, regardless of their status or influence. This teaches us the importance of compassion, patience, and treating all people with dignity.
orig: عبس وتولى

translation: That the blind man came to him
interpretation: This verse is referring to an incident in the life of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) where a blind man came to him seeking guidance. The verse highlights the importance of being attentive and compassionate towards those who are in need, even if they may interrupt or distract from other matters. The interpretation is that one should not turn away from those who are seeking knowledge or help, but rather make time for them and treat them with kindness and respect.
orig: أن جاءه الأعمى

translation: And what can make you know [O Muhammad] that perhaps he [i.e., the addressee] will purify himself [through belief]?
interpretation: This verse is asking the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) what could make him know whether the person he is addressing will choose to purify themselves through belief and righteous deeds. It suggests that the outcome of a person's spiritual journey is ultimately known only to God, and that we should not be quick to judge others, but rather focus on our own spiritual growth and purification.
orig: وما يدريك لعله يزكى

translation: Or he might remember, and the reminder would benefit him.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even a person who has been heedless or forgetful may still be reminded and benefit from the remembrance (of God and His guidance). The verse implies that there is always a chance for guidance and positive change, as long as one is open to being reminded and taking heed. The interpretation emphasizes the merciful and forgiving nature of God, who provides opportunities for people to return to the right path.
orig: أو يذكر فتنفعه الذكرى

translation: As for he who is self-sufficient
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are arrogant and feel self-sufficient, not in need of God or others. The interpretation is that such people who are arrogant and think they are self-sufficient will be held accountable on the Day of Judgment, as they have turned away from God and failed to acknowledge their need for Him.
orig: أما من استغنى

translation: Then you are responsible for it
interpretation: This verse suggests that one is accountable for their actions and decisions. The implication is that the person addressed has taken on a responsibility or task, and they are now responsible for seeing it through. The verse emphasizes the importance of taking ownership and being held accountable for one's choices and their consequences.
orig: فأنت له تصدى

translation: And it is not upon you [to cause] their growth.
interpretation: This verse conveys that it is not the responsibility of the Prophet (peace be upon him) to ensure the spiritual growth and purification of people. Rather, it is Allah who guides and purifies the hearts of the believers. The Prophet's role is to convey the message of Islam, and it is up to the individuals to accept and act upon it.
orig: وما عليك ألا يزكى

translation: And as for he who comes to you striving [for knowledge]
interpretation: This verse refers to a person who comes to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) with a sincere desire to learn and understand the teachings of Islam. The phrase "comes to you striving" implies a person who is actively seeking knowledge, making an effort to acquire it. This verse encourages such individuals and highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding the divine message.
orig: وأما من جاءك يسعى

translation: And he fears [Allah]
interpretation: This verse refers to a person who is righteous and God-fearing. He is someone who is conscious of Allah and strives to please Him through his actions. This attitude of fearing and revering Allah is a sign of faith and piety, as it motivates the person to avoid sins and do good deeds. The interpretation suggests that this individual is mindful of his accountability before Allah and seeks to live his life in a manner that is pleasing to the Divine.
orig: وهو يخشى

translation: So you are distracted from him.
interpretation: This verse suggests that one can become distracted from the remembrance and worship of God. It serves as a reminder to stay focused on one's spiritual obligations and not to be sidetracked by worldly pursuits or distractions.
orig: فأنت عنه تلهى

translation: No! Indeed, it is a reminder
interpretation: This verse is a response to those who may dismiss or ignore the Qur'an as something insignificant. The word "كلا" (No!) is used to emphatically reject this notion. The Qur'an is described as "تذكرة" (a reminder), meaning it is a source of guidance, wisdom, and admonition for those who seek to live a righteous life. This verse underscores the importance and value of the Qur'anic revelation, which should not be taken lightly or disregarded.
orig: كلا إنها تذكرة

translation: So whoever wills may remember it.
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on and remember the teachings of the Qur'an. It suggests that those who desire guidance and wisdom can choose to heed the divine message and incorporate it into their lives. The verse emphasizes the idea of individual responsibility and free will in seeking spiritual enlightenment.
orig: فمن شاء ذكره

translation: In honored scriptures
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an, which is described as being in "honored scriptures." This emphasizes the high status and reverence given to the Qur'an as a divine revelation. The interpretation is that the Qur'an is a sacred text that deserves the utmost respect and honor from believers.
orig: في صحف مكرمة

translation: Exalted and purified
interpretation: This verse likely refers to the status and purity of the Qur'an or the believers. It suggests that the Qur'an or the believers are elevated and purified, free from any impurities or flaws. The interpretation implies that the Qur'an or the believers have a high standing and are cleansed from any undesirable qualities.
orig: مرفوعة مطهرة

translation: By the hands of scribes
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an being preserved and transmitted by diligent scribes or scholars. It emphasizes the care and attention with which the divine revelation has been safeguarded throughout history, ensuring its authenticity and purity.
orig: بأيدي سفرة

translation: Noble, pious
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous and virtuous people who are held in high esteem by Allah. They are described as "noble" and "pious", indicating their elevated status and their devotion to living a life of righteousness and virtue. This verse encourages believers to emulate the qualities of these noble and pious individuals, as they are the ones who are beloved by Allah and will be rewarded in the Hereafter.
orig: كرام بررة

translation: Man is [truly] ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to be ungrateful and unappreciative of the blessings and favors bestowed upon them by God. It suggests that mankind often forgets or denies the Creator's benevolence, and instead becomes consumed by materialism, arrogance, and a sense of self-sufficiency. The verse serves as a reminder to remain humble, thankful, and cognizant of one's dependence on the Almighty.
orig: قتل الإنسان ما أكفره

translation: From what has He created him?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the creation of man. It is asking the rhetorical question of what material or substance God used to create the human being. The implication is that man was created from something insignificant or lowly, emphasizing the power and ability of God to create life from the most basic of elements.
orig: من أي شيء خلقه

translation: From a sperm-drop He created him and destined him
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah (God) created man from a humble beginning - a sperm-drop. It highlights Allah's power and ability to create life from the most basic of elements. The verse also suggests that Allah has a plan and purpose for each individual, having "destined" or predetermined their fate. This reinforces the belief that Allah is in control and that our lives are part of a greater divine plan.
orig: من نطفة خلقه فقدره

translation: Then He will make the way easy for him
interpretation: This verse suggests that once a person has made the effort and commitment to follow the path of righteousness, Allah will facilitate and make that path easier for them. It implies that with sincere intention and effort, Allah will provide the guidance, support, and means to help the person progress on the spiritual journey.
orig: ثم السبيل يسره

translation: Then He causes him to die and provides a grave for him.
interpretation: This verse refers to the cycle of life and death, where God is the one who gives life and then takes it away. The interpretation is that God is the ultimate authority over life and death, and that He will provide a resting place, or grave, for the deceased. This emphasizes the belief in the afterlife and the importance of submitting to God's will.
orig: ثم أماته فأقبره

translation: Then when He wills, He will resurrect him
interpretation: This verse suggests that the resurrection of the dead is entirely in the hands of God. He alone has the power and authority to bring back to life those who have passed away. The use of the word "then" implies that the resurrection will happen according to God's will and timing, not according to human desires or expectations. The interpretation is that the resurrection is a matter of divine decree, not human control or manipulation.
orig: ثم إذا شاء أنشره

translation: No! When it (i.e., the soul) reaches the collar bones
interpretation: This verse is referring to the moment of death, when the soul is about to depart the body. The verse is emphasizing that there is no escaping death, as it is an inevitable reality that every person will face. The interpretation suggests that when the soul reaches the collar bones, signifying the imminent departure from the physical world, there is no turning back or avoiding this final journey.
orig: كلا لما يقض ما أمره

translation: So let man look at his food
interpretation: This verse encourages mankind to reflect on the origin and source of their sustenance. It prompts us to ponder the process by which our food is provided, whether it is through agriculture, animal husbandry, or other means. This reflection can lead to a deeper appreciation of the Creator's blessings and a sense of gratitude for the nourishment we receive.
orig: فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه

translation: Indeed, We have poured forth the water in abundance
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the abundance and generosity of God's provision, as He has poured forth water in great measure. It is a reminder of God's power and the blessings He bestows upon His creation, particularly in the form of water, which is essential for life.
orig: أنا صببنا الماء صبا

translation: Then We split the earth, [separating it from] the heavens
interpretation: This verse is referring to the creation of the universe, where the earth was initially joined with the heavens, and then they were separated. This separation allowed for the formation of the earth and the heavens as we know them today. The splitting or separation of the earth from the heavens is a metaphorical way of describing the process of creation, highlighting the divine power and orchestration behind the formation of the universe.
orig: ثم شققنا الأرض شقا

translation: And We produced therein grain
interpretation: This verse is referring to the ability of Allah to create life and sustenance from the earth. By producing grain, Allah demonstrates His power to provide for His creation and sustain life on Earth. The verse emphasizes the bounty and fertility of the land, which is a sign of Allah's divine providence and care for His creation.
orig: فأنبتنا فيها حبا

translation: And grapes and herbage
interpretation: This verse refers to the blessings and bounties that God has provided for humanity. The mention of "grapes" and "herbage" symbolizes the abundance of nourishing and enjoyable sustenance that God has created for our benefit. The interpretation suggests that we should be grateful for these provisions and use them responsibly and in moderation.
orig: وعنبا وقضبا

translation: And [by] the olive and [by] the palm tree
interpretation: This verse is referring to the olive tree and the palm tree, which are two of the most important and valuable plants mentioned in the Qur'an. The olive tree is known for its nutritious fruit and oil, which have been used for centuries in the Middle East and Mediterranean regions. The palm tree, on the other hand, is a symbol of prosperity and sustenance, providing food, shelter, and other useful products. The mention of these two plants in the Qur'an is a reminder of the blessings and abundance that Allah has provided for humanity, and the importance of appreciating and caring for the natural resources that sustain us.
orig: وزيتونا ونخلا

translation: And gardens of abundance
interpretation: This verse refers to the gardens of paradise that await the righteous in the Hereafter. These gardens are described as being in abundance, indicating that they are vast, plentiful, and overflowing with blessings. The interpretation suggests that the faithful will be rewarded with an abundance of delights, comforts, and provisions in the afterlife, as a reward for their righteous deeds in this world.
orig: وحدائق غلبا

translation: And fruit and [its] father.
interpretation: This verse refers to the bountiful provisions that Allah has created for the people in the Hereafter. The "fruit" symbolizes the delicious and nourishing sustenance that the inhabitants of Paradise will enjoy, while the "father" likely refers to the source or origin of this fruit, which is the will and power of Allah. This verse emphasizes the completeness and abundance of the blessings that await the righteous in the Afterlife.
orig: وفاكهة وأبا

translation: A provision for you and your livestock
interpretation: This verse is referring to the resources and sustenance that Allah has provided for both humans and their livestock. It suggests that the bounties of the earth are meant to be enjoyed and utilized by people, as well as the animals under their care. The interpretation is that Allah has created the world and its resources to serve the needs of His creation, and that we should use these resources responsibly and with gratitude.
orig: متاعا لكم ولأنعامكم

translation: And when the Deafening Blast occurs,
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the trumpet will be blown to signal the end of the world. The "Deafening Blast" or "Saakhah" is a term used in the Quran to describe the cataclysmic event that will mark the beginning of the Resurrection. This verse suggests that when this momentous event takes place, it will be a profound and overwhelming experience for all of humanity.
orig: فإذا جاءت الصاخة

translation: The Day when a person will flee from his brother
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when people will be so overwhelmed by the horrors of that day that they will even flee from their closest relatives, seeking to save themselves. It emphasizes the severity and intensity of that momentous day, when worldly ties and relationships will become insignificant in the face of the ultimate reckoning.
orig: يوم يفر المرء من أخيه

translation: And his mother and his father
interpretation: This verse refers to the importance of respecting and honoring one's parents. It emphasizes the duty of a person to be kind, obedient, and dutiful towards their mother and father. This is a central teaching in Islam, as the Quran and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) place great emphasis on the rights of parents and the obligation of children to care for and support them.
orig: وأمه وأبيه

translation: And his companion and his sons
interpretation: This verse refers to the importance of family and companionship in Islam. The companion mentioned could be a spouse, close friend, or other loved one who provides support and companionship. The sons represent the continuation of one's lineage and the importance of raising children according to Islamic principles. The verse emphasizes the value of maintaining strong familial and social bonds, which are integral to a fulfilling and meaningful life.
orig: وصاحبته وبنيه

translation: For every person among them that Day is [a matter] he will be concerned with.
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, each person will be preoccupied with their own affairs and the reckoning of their deeds. It emphasizes the individualistic nature of the accountability process, where each person will be solely responsible for their actions and will not be able to rely on or be distracted by the affairs of others. The interpretation highlights the personal and introspective nature of the Judgment Day, where each person will be focused on their own standing before God.
orig: لكل امرئ منهم يومئذ شأن يغنيه

translation: On that Day, [some] faces will be radiant
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when some faces will be bright and shining, indicating the joy and happiness of those who have lived righteous lives and have been forgiven by Allah. This radiance is a sign of their spiritual purity and their reward in the Hereafter.
orig: وجوه يومئذ مسفرة

translation: Laughing, rejoicing
interpretation: This verse describes a person who is in a state of happiness and joy, indicated by their laughter and cheerful demeanor. It suggests a positive and optimistic outlook, where the person is filled with a sense of contentment and anticipation for what lies ahead.
orig: ضاحكة مستبشرة

translation: And [some] faces, that Day, will be dust-colored
interpretation: This verse describes the state of some people on the Day of Judgment, where their faces will be covered in dust and grime, reflecting their spiritual and moral decay. This suggests that those who have lived a life of sin and neglect of their duties will face a humiliating and dreadful fate on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: ووجوه يومئذ عليها غبرة

translation: It will cover them with humiliation
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers will be covered in humiliation and disgrace for their rejection of faith and righteous deeds. The "it" in the verse refers to the overwhelming state of shame and degradation that will befall them on that day, as a consequence of their misdeeds in this world.
orig: ترهقها قترة

translation: Those are the disbelievers, the wicked.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who have rejected faith and chosen a path of wickedness. The term "disbelievers" (al-kuffar) denotes those who have consciously turned away from the truth of God's message, while "the wicked" (al-fajira) suggests that they have also engaged in immoral and sinful behavior. The verse is a strong condemnation of those who have forsaken their spiritual and moral obligations, and serves as a warning to believers to guard against such a fate.
orig: أولئك هم الكفرة الفجرة

translation: When the sun is wrapped up [in darkness]
interpretation: This verse refers to the end times, when the sun will be darkened and lose its light. This is a sign of the coming of the Day of Judgment, when the world as we know it will come to an end and all people will be held accountable for their actions before God. The verse conveys a sense of the vastness and power of God, who controls even the heavenly bodies, and the inevitability of the final reckoning.
orig: إذا الشمس كورت

translation: And when the stars become dim
interpretation: This verse suggests that when the celestial bodies, represented by the stars, begin to lose their luster or disappear, it signifies a major cosmic event or a significant change in the natural order. This could be interpreted as a metaphor for the upheaval and disruption that will occur at the time of the Day of Judgment, when the world as we know it will come to an end and a new, eternal existence will begin.
orig: وإذا النجوم انكدرت

translation: And when the mountains are made to move
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the mountains - which are typically seen as permanent and immovable - will be set in motion. This signifies the profound changes and upheavals that will take place on the Day of Resurrection, when the entire physical world as we know it will be transformed. The movement of the mountains represents the scale and magnitude of the cosmic events that will unfold, emphasizing the power and might of God and the finality of the Judgment Day.
orig: وإذا الجبال سيرت

translation: And when the she-camels, ten months pregnant, are abandoned
interpretation: This verse refers to the practice of burying female infants alive, which was common in pre-Islamic Arabia. The "she-camels, ten months pregnant" symbolize the valuable and precious nature of these girls, who were nonetheless abandoned and killed. The verse condemns this practice and calls for the protection and care of all human life, regardless of gender.
orig: وإذا العشار عطلت

translation: And when the wild beasts are gathered
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all living creatures will be gathered together. The "wild beasts" symbolize the wicked and sinful people who have lived like animals, without morals or conscience. On that day, they will be held accountable for their actions and face the consequences of their misdeeds.
orig: وإذا الوحوش حشرت

translation: And when the seas are filled with flame
interpretation: This verse speaks of the end times, when the oceans and seas will be set ablaze, signaling the approach of the Day of Judgment. The "seas being filled with flame" is a metaphorical description of the cataclysmic events that will precede the final reckoning, when the world as we know it will be transformed. This verse serves as a reminder of the impermanence of the material world and the importance of preparing for the hereafter.
orig: وإذا البحار سجرت

translation: And when the souls are paired
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all souls will be paired and held accountable for their actions in life. The pairing of souls suggests that each person will be reunited with their deeds, both good and bad, and will face the consequences of their choices.
