This verse emphasizes the importance of living a righteous life, as we will all be held responsible for our actions on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: وإذا النفوس زوجت

translation: And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked
interpretation: This verse refers to the practice of female infanticide that was common in pre-Islamic Arabia, where newborn girls were often buried alive. The verse condemns this practice and suggests that on the Day of Judgment, these girls will be asked about the injustice done to them. The interpretation is that this verse serves as a warning against such inhumane practices and calls for the protection and equal treatment of girls and women.
orig: وإذا الموءودة سئلت

translation: By what sin was she killed?
interpretation: This verse from the Qur'an refers to the practice of female infanticide that was common in pre-Islamic Arabia. The question "By what sin was she killed?" expresses condemnation of this practice, highlighting the injustice and cruelty of killing infant girls. The interpretation suggests that this verse calls for the protection and preservation of human life, particularly the vulnerable lives of young girls, and rejects any justification for such an abhorrent act.
orig: بأي ذنب قتلت

translation: And when the scrolls are spread
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the records of people's deeds will be revealed. The "scrolls" or "pages" represent the records of people's actions, which will be unrolled and made public on that day. This signifies the accountability that all people will face for their choices and actions in life.
orig: وإذا الصحف نشرت

translation: And when the heaven is split open
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the heavens will be split open and the angels will descend. It signifies the end of the world as we know it and the beginning of the afterlife, where people will be held accountable for their actions in this life. The splitting of the heavens is a dramatic and awe-inspiring event that will mark the start of a new, eternal existence.
orig: وإذا السماء كشطت

translation: And when the Hellfire is kindled to a blaze
interpretation: This verse describes the intense heat and raging flames of Hell, which will be ignited on the Day of Judgment. The imagery conveys the severity of the punishment awaiting those who have rejected faith and lived sinful lives. It serves as a warning to humanity to turn to righteousness and seek salvation before facing the torment of the Hellfire.
orig: وإذا الجحيم سعرت

translation: And when Paradise is brought near
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when Paradise will be brought near for the righteous believers. It signifies that the eternal abode of the faithful will be within their reach, and they will be able to witness its splendor and beauty. This verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate reward that awaits those who have lived righteously and submitted to the will of God.
orig: وإذا الجنة أزلفت

translation: Every soul will know what it has prepared.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of personal accountability and the consequences of one's actions. It suggests that on the Day of Judgment, every person will be held responsible for their deeds, and will be fully aware of what they have done in this life, whether good or bad. This serves as a reminder to individuals to be mindful of their actions and to strive to do what is right, as they will ultimately be held accountable for their choices.
orig: علمت نفس ما أحضرت

translation: But nay! I swear by the [stars] that run their course [and] disappear
interpretation: This verse is an oath taken by God, swearing by the stars that rise and set. The purpose of this oath is to emphasize the truth and importance of the message that follows, which is likely related to the Day of Judgment and the accountability of human actions. The "stars that run their course and disappear" may symbolize the transient nature of this world and the certainty of the Hereafter.
orig: فلا أقسم بالخنس

translation: The neighboring houses
interpretation: This verse refers to the importance of maintaining good relationships with one's neighbors. It emphasizes the need to be respectful, kind, and considerate towards those who live in close proximity. The term "الجوار" (al-jiwār) implies a sense of community and mutual responsibility, while "الكنس" (al-kinas) suggests the idea of cleanliness and order in one's surroundings. The interpretation is that maintaining harmonious relationships with neighbors, and ensuring a clean and well-kept living environment, are important aspects of Islamic teachings.
orig: الجوار الكنس

translation: And by the night when it covers,
interpretation: This verse refers to the night when it covers the earth with its darkness. The interpretation is that the night is a time of rest, reflection, and contemplation, when one can escape the busyness of the day and find solace in the tranquility of the night.
orig: والليل إذا عسعس

translation: And [by] the dawn when it breathes
interpretation: This verse refers to the dawn, the time when the day begins to break and the sun starts to rise. The verse uses the metaphor of the dawn "breathing" to convey the idea of the gradual and natural transition from night to day. This can be interpreted as a reminder of the cyclical nature of time and the regularity of the natural world, which are signs of God's power and wisdom. The dawn is also a symbol of hope and new beginnings, as it marks the start of a new day.
orig: والصبح إذا تنفس

translation: Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger.
interpretation: This verse affirms that the Qur'an is the word of a noble and honorable Messenger, namely the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, as it was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad through the angel Gabriel. The verse highlights the noble and esteemed status of the Prophet Muhammad as the recipient of this divine revelation, which is the Qur'an.
orig: إنه لقول رسول كريم

translation: The one of power and having an honored position near the Owner of the Throne [i.e., Allah]
interpretation: This verse refers to the Angel Jibreel (Gabriel), who is a powerful and honored messenger of Allah near the Divine Throne. It emphasizes the high status and authority of Jibreel, who is entrusted with conveying revelations from Allah to the Prophets. This highlights the importance of the Qur’anic message and the divine origin of the scripture.
orig: ذي قوة عند ذي العرش مكين

translation: Obeyed and trusted
interpretation: This verse describes a righteous and trustworthy leader or person who is worthy of obedience and respect. The phrase "Obeyed and trusted" suggests that this individual has earned the confidence and loyalty of those around them through their consistent and reliable conduct. This could refer to a prophet, a ruler, or any person of authority and influence who has demonstrated integrity and wisdom in their actions.
orig: مطاع ثم أمين

translation: And your companion is not [at all] mad.
interpretation: This verse is referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and addressing the disbelievers who accused him of being insane or possessed. The verse affirms that the Prophet is not mad, but rather a sane and rational individual who has been chosen by God to convey the divine message of Islam. The interpretation emphasizes that the Prophet's teachings and actions are not those of a madman, but of a divinely-guided messenger.
orig: وما صاحبكم بمجنون

translation: And he certainly saw him in the clear horizon.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Muhammad’s vision of the Angel Gabriel in the clear horizon. It is believed to be a reference to the event known as the “Mi’raj”, where the Prophet was taken on a night journey to Jerusalem and then ascended to the heavens. This vision of the Angel Gabriel in the clear horizon was a significant spiritual experience for the Prophet, affirming his prophethood and connection with the divine.
orig: ولقد رآه بالأفق المبين

translation: And he is not stingy with the unseen
interpretation: This verse conveys that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not stingy or miserly with the knowledge of the unseen that has been revealed to him by Allah. He freely shares this knowledge and guidance with his people, out of compassion and a desire to lead them to the truth.
orig: وما هو على الغيب بضنين

translation: And it is not the word of a cursed Satan.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing that the Qur'an is not the word of a cursed Satan, but rather the word of God. It is refuting the claim that the Qur'an is the work of the devil or some other supernatural being. The Qur'an is divine revelation, not the product of a cursed or evil entity. This serves to establish the Qur'an's authenticity and divine origin.
orig: وما هو بقول شيطان رجيم

translation: So where are you going?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, prompting the listener to reflect on the purpose and direction of their life. It suggests that we should be mindful of where we are heading and the choices we make, as they will ultimately determine our destination. The verse encourages us to consider the consequences of our actions and to align our path with the guidance provided in the Quran.
orig: فأين تذهبون

translation: Verily, this (Qur'an) is no less than a Reminder to (all) the Worlds
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine reminder and guidance for all of humanity, not just a specific group or nation. It is a universal message that calls people to worship God alone and live according to His teachings. The Qur'an is a source of wisdom, knowledge, and moral guidance that is relevant and applicable to all people, regardless of their background or circumstances.
orig: إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: For whoever among you wills to follow a straight course.
interpretation: This verse encourages individuals to choose a righteous and upright path in life. It suggests that the decision to follow a straight course is a personal choice, and those who desire to do so will be guided accordingly. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of individual agency and responsibility in seeking a virtuous life.
orig: لمن شاء منكم أن يستقيم

translation: And you do not will except that Allah wills, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of God's sovereignty and control over all affairs. It suggests that human will and desires are ultimately subject to the will of God, the Lord of all creation. The interpretation is that we should recognize our dependence on God and submit to His divine plan, as our own wishes and intentions are ultimately dependent on His will.
orig: وما تشاءون إلا أن يشاء الله رب العالمين

translation: When the sky is cleft asunder
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the heavens will be split open and the world as we know it will come to an end. It is a powerful image that conveys the magnitude and awe-inspiring nature of this momentous event. The interpretation suggests that on that day, all human beings will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs, and the true nature of reality will be revealed.
orig: إذا السماء انفطرت

translation: And when the stars are scattered
interpretation: This verse is referring to the events of the Day of Judgment, when the stars will be dispersed and scattered, signaling the end of the world as we know it. This is a metaphorical description of the cosmic upheaval and chaos that will precede the final reckoning, when all of creation will be transformed and the old order will give way to the new. The scattering of the stars is a sign of the unraveling of the natural order, a prelude to the ultimate judgment of humanity by God.
orig: وإذا الكواكب انتثرت

translation: And when the seas are burst forth
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the oceans and seas will be split open and their contents will be released, causing widespread destruction. This signifies the end of the world as we know it and the beginning of the afterlife. The bursting forth of the seas is a powerful metaphor for the upheaval and chaos that will precede the final reckoning of humanity.
orig: وإذا البحار فجرت

translation: And when the graves are turned upside down
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when the graves will be opened and the dead will be resurrected. It signifies the end of the world as we know it and the beginning of the afterlife, where all people will be held accountable for their deeds in this life. The "turning upside down" of the graves symbolizes the profound changes that will take place, as the physical world gives way to the spiritual realm.
orig: وإذا القبور بعثرت

translation: Every soul will know what it has put forth and [what it has] withheld.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual accountability on the Day of Judgment. Each person will be held responsible for their own actions, both the good deeds they have done and the misdeeds they have committed. There will be no shifting of blame or responsibility onto others, as each soul will be fully aware of its own choices and the consequences that follow. This verse serves as a reminder to strive for righteous conduct in this life, as we will ultimately be answerable for our choices before the Almighty.
orig: علمت نفس ما قدمت وأخرت

translation: O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the human being to reflect on what has led them to become heedless of their Lord, the Generous. It suggests that the human being has been deceived by something, whether it is their own desires, worldly temptations, or a misunderstanding of the nature of their relationship with God. The verse encourages the individual to re-evaluate their priorities and to recognize the true generosity and benevolence of their Lord, who deserves their utmost reverence and gratitude.
orig: يا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم

translation: The One who created you and proportioned you and balanced you
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the sole Creator who has fashioned the human being in a precise and balanced manner. It highlights the perfection and harmony in the creation of the human being, which is a testament to Allah's power, wisdom and artistry. The interpretation suggests that the human being should recognize and appreciate the blessings of this creation, and strive to maintain the balance and equilibrium that Allah has established within them.
orig: الذي خلقك فسواك فعدلك

translation: In whatever form He willed, He assembled you.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah (God) has created humans in the form that He willed, implying that our physical appearance and attributes are determined by the divine will. It emphasizes that we should accept and embrace our unique characteristics, as they are part of Allah's plan for us. This verse encourages us to have gratitude and humility towards our Creator, who has fashioned us according to His wisdom and design.
orig: في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك

translation: Nay! But you deny the Judgment
interpretation: This verse is a rebuttal to those who deny the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that the disbelievers are not simply unaware of the Judgment, but actively reject and deny its existence. The verse serves as a warning that denying the reality of the Hereafter and the accountability that comes with it is a grave sin that will have severe consequences.
orig: كلا بل تكذبون بالدين

translation: And indeed, over you [i.e., the people] are keepers [i.e., angels].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that there are angels appointed by Allah to watch over and guard people. These angels record the deeds, actions, and words of individuals, and they will present this record before Allah on the Day of Judgment. This serves as a reminder to people to be mindful of their behavior, as they are constantly being observed and held accountable for their actions.
orig: وإن عليكم لحافظين

translation: Honourable recorders
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who record the deeds of human beings. It suggests that these angels are noble and trustworthy in their duty of recording our actions, both good and bad, which will be presented before God on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of our actions, as they are being meticulously recorded by these "honourable recorders".
orig: كراما كاتبين

translation: They know what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Almighty, is all-knowing and is aware of the actions and deeds of His creation. It serves as a reminder that we should be mindful of our actions, as Allah is watching over us and has knowledge of everything we do, both in public and in private.
orig: يعلمون ما تفعلون

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who lead a righteous and virtuous life will be rewarded with a state of eternal bliss and contentment in the Hereafter. The term "al-Abrar" refers to those who have purified their souls, performed good deeds, and upheld their responsibilities towards God and others. This verse provides a reassurance that the pious and God-fearing individuals will be granted a life of comfort, joy, and fulfillment in the Afterlife.
orig: إن الأبرار لفي نعيم

translation: And indeed, the wicked are in Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who engage in wicked and immoral deeds will be punished in the Hereafter by being placed in the torment of Hell. It serves as a warning to those who stray from the righteous path and encourages them to repent and seek forgiveness from Allah.
orig: وإن الفجار لفي جحيم

translation: They will be exposed to it, the Day of Judgment
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions during their lifetime. On that day, they will be exposed to the consequences of their deeds, whether good or bad. The verse emphasizes the gravity and certainty of the Day of Judgment, when everyone will face the ultimate reckoning before God.
orig: يصلونها يوم الدين

translation: And they are not [at all] from it absent.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the disbelievers are not unaware or heedless of the signs of Allah and the warnings of the Quran. They are fully aware of the message, but they choose to turn away from it out of arrogance and stubbornness.
orig: وما هم عنها بغائبين

translation: And what will make you know what is the Day of Recompense?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question to emphasize the gravity and importance of the Day of Judgment, also known as the Day of Recompense. It is implying that the Day of Judgment is a momentous and awe-inspiring event, the true nature and magnitude of which cannot be fully grasped or comprehended by human beings. The verse serves to instill a sense of reverence and urgency in the reader to prepare for this inevitable day when all will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: وما أدراك ما يوم الدين

translation: And what can make you know what is the Day of Recompense?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question to emphasize the gravity and importance of the Day of Judgment, also known as the Day of Recompense. It is suggesting that the Day of Judgment is an event of such magnitude and significance that it is beyond human comprehension. The verse is meant to instill a sense of awe and reverence in the reader towards this momentous day when all people will be held accountable for their actions in life.
orig: ثم ما أدراك ما يوم الدين

translation: The Day when no soul will possess [power to do] anything for another soul, and the command, that Day, is [entirely] with Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to help or intercede for another person. All authority and decision-making will belong solely to Allah, the Almighty. This highlights the absolute sovereignty of Allah and the individual responsibility that each person will face on that momentous day.
orig: يوم لا تملك نفس لنفس شيئا والأمر يومئذ لله

translation: Woe to those who give less [than due]
interpretation: This verse condemns those who cheat or defraud others, particularly in commercial transactions. It warns that those who short-change or under-measure goods will face severe consequences in the Hereafter. The interpretation is that one should always be fair, honest and upright in their dealings with others, and not try to take advantage or deceive them.
orig: ويل للمطففين

translation: Those who, when they have to receive by measure from men, demand full measure
interpretation: This verse is referring to people who are fair and honest in their dealings with others. When they are receiving something from others, they make sure to measure it accurately and take only what is due to them, without trying to take more than their fair share. This is a praiseworthy quality, as it shows integrity and a commitment to justice.
orig: الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون

translation: And when they measure for them or weigh for them, they cause loss.
interpretation: This verse refers to the practice of cheating or defrauding others in transactions involving measurement or weighing of goods. The verse condemns such dishonest practices, which deprive people of what is rightfully theirs and lead to a loss for those being cheated. The interpretation is that one should be fair and honest in all dealings, and not try to take advantage of others through deceptive means.
orig: وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون

translation: Do those not think that they will be resurrected
interpretation: This verse is asking whether those who deny the resurrection and the afterlife truly believe that they will not be held accountable for their actions. It is a rhetorical question that challenges the notion that people can simply live without consequences. The implication is that everyone will be resurrected and judged by God, and that denying this reality does not change the fact that it will occur.
orig: ألا يظن أولئك أنهم مبعوثون

translation: For a mighty Day
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, which is a momentous and awe-inspiring event that all people will face. The "mighty Day" suggests the grandeur, significance, and gravity of this day when all will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs. It emphasizes the importance of preparing for this pivotal day by living a righteous life and seeking forgiveness and guidance from God.
orig: ليوم عظيم

translation: The Day when the people will stand before the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity will be held accountable before God, the Lord of the entire universe. On this momentous day, people will stand in reverence and awe before the Almighty, awaiting the judgment of their deeds and the determination of their eternal fate. This serves as a reminder to live a righteous life in preparation for this pivotal day.
orig: يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين

translation: Nay, surely the record of the wicked is in Sijjin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the deeds of the wicked are recorded in a place called "Sijjin", which is understood to be a place of punishment or reckoning in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in sinful and immoral acts, reminding them that their actions are being documented and they will be held accountable for them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: كلا إن كتاب الفجار لفي سجين

translation: And what can make you know what is Sijjin?
interpretation: This verse refers to the concept of "Sijjin" in the Qur'an, which is believed to be a place or record where the deeds of the wicked are recorded. The verse is asking a rhetorical question, emphasizing the importance and gravity of this concept. The interpretation is that the nature and significance of Sijjin is beyond human comprehension, and it is a matter of great importance that should not be taken lightly.
orig: وما أدراك ما سجين

translation: A well-preserved Record.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an as a well-preserved and meticulously recorded scripture. It emphasizes the divine preservation and protection of the Qur'an, ensuring its authenticity and integrity throughout the ages. This underscores the reliability and trustworthiness of the Qur'anic text, which has been safeguarded from any alterations or distortions.
orig: كتاب مرقوم

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers!
interpretation: This verse conveys a stern warning to those who reject and deny the truth of God's message and the reality of the Hereafter. On the Day of Judgment, those who refused to believe in God's signs and the accountability of their actions will face a terrible fate, marked by divine displeasure and severe punishment. The word "woe" suggests a state of profound distress, anguish, and loss that will befall the deniers on that momentous day.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Those who deny the Day of Judgment
interpretation: This verse refers to those who reject the concept of the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions. The interpretation is that those who deny this fundamental belief in Islam will face consequences for their disbelief and rejection of this core tenet of the faith.
orig: الذين يكذبون بيوم الدين

translation: And none will deny it except every sinful transgressor.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the truth of God's message will not be denied except by those who are habitual sinners and transgressors. It suggests that those who reject the divine guidance are characterized by their arrogance, wickedness, and disregard for moral and ethical standards.
orig: وما يكذب به إلا كل معتد أثيم

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Legends of the former peoples."
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who reject the Qur'an and dismiss it as mere "legends of the former peoples". They refuse to acknowledge the divine origin and truth of the Qur'anic revelations, dismissing them as mere stories or myths of the past. This attitude reflects a lack of faith and an unwillingness to reflect on the deeper meaning and guidance contained in the Qur'an.
orig: إذا تتلى عليه آياتنا قال أساطير الأولين

translation: No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the wrongdoings and sins committed by people have a negative impact on their hearts, causing them to become hardened and unable to perceive the truth. The "ран" (ran) mentioned in the verse refers to a spiritual veil or covering that obscures the heart and prevents it from accepting guidance. The interpretation is that one's own actions and misdeeds can lead to a state of spiritual blindness, where the heart is no longer receptive to the truth and guidance of Allah.
orig: كلا بل ران على قلوبهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Nay! Surely they shall be debarred from (seeing) their Lord on that Day.
interpretation: This verse indicates that on the Day of Judgment, those who disbelieved and denied the signs of Allah will be prevented from seeing or attaining the presence of their Lord. They will be barred from the divine vision and the blessings of the Hereafter due to their own misdeeds and rejection of faith in this life.
orig: كلا إنهم عن ربهم يومئذ لمحجوبون

translation: Then indeed they will be within the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who reject the message of Islam and persist in their disbelief will ultimately end up in the Hellfire, which is the place of eternal punishment for the unbelievers. The use of the phrase "then indeed they will be" suggests that this is an inevitable outcome for those who turn away from the guidance of Allah.
orig: ثم إنهم لصالو الجحيم

translation: Then it will be said, "This is what you used to deny."
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the disbelievers will be confronted with the reality they had denied during their worldly lives. It serves as a warning that there will be consequences for rejecting the truth and refusing to believe in Allah and the Hereafter. The interpretation suggests that on that day, the disbelievers will be reminded of their past denial and disbelief, and they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: ثم يقال هذا الذي كنتم به تكذبون

translation: Nay, verily the record of the righteous is (preserved) in 'Illiyyun.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the record of the righteous is preserved in a lofty place, referred to as 'Illiyyun. It suggests that the deeds and actions of the righteous are meticulously recorded and will be accounted for on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder that the righteous will be rewarded for their virtuous lives, and that their record is kept in a high and esteemed place, indicating the importance and value of their good deeds.
orig: كلا إن كتاب الأبرار لفي عليين

translation: And what can make you know what is 'Illiyun'?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the highest and most exalted station in the afterlife, known as 'Illiyun'. It is a rhetorical question, asking the reader what can convey the true nature and magnificence of this lofty abode reserved for the righteous. The implication is that the reality of 'Illiyun' is beyond human comprehension, and its splendor and blessings can only be truly understood in the hereafter.
orig: وما أدراك ما عليون

translation: A well-guarded record.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an, which is a divinely-revealed scripture that is well-preserved and protected by Allah. It suggests that the Qur'an is a sacred and authoritative text that contains the eternal and unchanging words of God, preserved in its original form for all of humanity.
orig: كتاب مرقوم

translation: It is witnessed by the brought near [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse refers to the fact that the closest and most devoted servants of Allah, known as the "brought near" (al-muqarrabun), are witnesses to the truth and majesty of Allah. They have a deep and intimate connection with the divine, and are able to perceive and comprehend the signs of Allah's power and presence in a way that others cannot. This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking closeness to Allah and striving to be among those who are "brought near" to Him through righteous deeds and sincere devotion.
orig: يشهده المقربون

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who live a righteous and virtuous life will be rewarded with eternal bliss and happiness in the Hereafter. The term "al-abrar" refers to the pious and God-fearing individuals who strive to do good deeds and avoid sins. The word "na`im" denotes a state of complete comfort, joy, and satisfaction. This verse serves as a motivator for believers to lead a righteous life in order to attain the ultimate reward of eternal pleasure in the Afterlife.
orig: إن الأبرار لفي نعيم

translation: Upon the thrones they will be looking
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who will be resting on elevated couches or thrones in Paradise, looking around and enjoying the blessings and delights that Allah has bestowed upon them. It suggests a state of comfort, contentment, and contemplation in the afterlife for those who have lived righteous lives.
orig: على الأرائك ينظرون

translation: You will recognize in their faces the radiance of pleasure
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who will be granted eternal bliss in the Hereafter. Their faces will radiate with joy and contentment, reflecting the blessings and pleasures they will experience in Paradise. This is a promise of the ultimate reward for those who have lived righteous lives and have faith in God.
orig: تعرف في وجوههم نضرة النعيم

translation: They are given to drink from a sealed nectar.
interpretation: This verse describes the rewards awaiting the righteous in the Hereafter. The "sealed nectar" refers to a pure, delicious drink that is untouched by impurities, signifying the perfection and exclusivity of the blessings in Paradise. This drink symbolizes the spiritual and physical delights that the believers will enjoy in the afterlife as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world.
orig: يسقون من رحيق مختوم

translation: Its conclusion is musk, and for that let the competitors compete.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ultimate reward and conclusion of the righteous believers. The phrase "its conclusion is musk" suggests that the end result or destination for the believers is one of purity, sweetness, and delight, like the fragrance of musk. The verse encourages the believers to strive and compete with one another in good deeds and righteous actions, as the ultimate prize is the pleasure of Allah and the bliss of the Hereafter.
orig: ختامه مسك وفي ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون

translation: And their drink is a drink from Tasneem,
interpretation: This verse refers to the drink that the righteous will be given in Paradise. Tasneem is a spring in Paradise, whose water is described as pure, delightful, and refreshing. This drink symbolizes the spiritual and physical nourishment that the believers will enjoy in the afterlife, as a reward for their faith and good deeds in this world.
orig: ومزاجه من تسنيم

translation: A spring from which those brought near [to Allah] will drink.
interpretation: This verse refers to a spring or fountain in Paradise that is reserved for the righteous and those who are closest to Allah. It suggests that the most honored and favored servants of Allah will have exclusive access to this pure and refreshing water in the Hereafter, as a reward for their piety and devotion.
orig: عينا يشرب بها المقربون

translation: Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disdain of the disbelievers towards the believers. The disbelievers, who were engaged in sinful and criminal acts, would mock and ridicule the believers for their faith and righteous conduct. This verse serves as a warning that the disbelievers' scornful attitude towards the believers will not go unpunished, and that they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions.
orig: إن الذين أجرموا كانوا من الذين آمنوا يضحكون

translation: And when they pass by them, they wink at one another.
interpretation: This verse describes the behavior of the disbelievers towards the believers. They would secretly mock and look down upon the believers, indicating their arrogance and disdain for the believers and their faith. This verse highlights the need for the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be deterred by the mockery and derision of the disbelievers.
orig: وإذا مروا بهم يتغامزون

translation: And when they return to their people, they return jesting.
interpretation: This verse suggests that when the hypocrites return to their people, they do so in a mocking and derisive manner, rather than with sincerity and humility. The verse implies that their outward display of faith is not matched by their inner conviction, and that they are more concerned with appearances and social status than with true devotion to God.
orig: وإذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم انقلبوا فكهين

translation: And when they see them, they say, "Indeed, those are truly lost."
interpretation: This verse refers to those who reject faith and mock the believers. When they see the believers, they look down upon them and consider them to be misguided. The interpretation is that the disbelievers arrogantly view the believers as being in a state of loss and misguidance, when in reality, it is the disbelievers themselves who are truly lost.
orig: وإذا رأوهم قالوا إن هؤلاء لضالون

translation: And We have not sent over them as a keeper.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has not appointed any guardian or watcher over the people to compel them to believe or to punish them for their disbelief. Instead, Allah has granted them free will to choose their own path, whether to believe or disbelieve. The responsibility for their choices lies with them, and they will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وما أرسلوا عليهم حافظين

translation: So today those who believe will laugh at the disbelievers
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, the believers will be triumphant over the disbelievers. The believers, who have accepted faith in God, will be able to rejoice and laugh at the fate of those who rejected faith. This indicates that the ultimate victory belongs to those who have true faith, while the disbelievers will face humiliation and punishment for their rejection of God's guidance.
orig: فاليوم الذين آمنوا من الكفار يضحكون

translation: They will be [reclining] on thrones, observing.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the righteous in the Hereafter, where they will be reclining on comfortable couches or thrones, observing the blessings and wonders of Paradise. It suggests a state of peace, tranquility, and contemplation, as the believers enjoy the rewards of their faith and good deeds in the Afterlife.
orig: على الأرائك ينظرون

translation: And the disbelievers' wealth and children will not avail them against [the punishment of] Allah. And those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein [forever].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the wealth, possessions, and children of the disbelievers will not protect them from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Judgment. Their material assets and worldly ties will not be able to save them from the eternal torment of the Hellfire, which they will be condemned to for their rejection of faith and righteous deeds.
orig: هل ثوب الكفار ما كانوا يفعلون

translation: When the sky is split open
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the heavens will be split apart and the angels will descend. It is a sign of the end times and the beginning of the afterlife. The splitting of the sky symbolizes the dramatic and cataclysmic nature of this event, which will signal the end of the world as we know it and the start of a new, eternal existence.
orig: إذا السماء انشقت

translation: And she inclined towards her Lord, and she was of the ones in compliance.
interpretation: This verse refers to the submission and obedience of the Blessed Virgin Mary to the will of God. She accepted her role and destiny with humility and devotion, becoming a model of faith and piety for all believers. The verse highlights her willingness to submit to the divine plan, even in the face of societal challenges and personal difficulties.
orig: وأذنت لربها وحقت

translation: And when the earth is spread out
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, when the earth will be flattened and expanded, signifying the end of the world as we know it. This event will mark the beginning of the afterlife, where all people will be held accountable for their actions in this life.
orig: وإذا الأرض مدت

translation: And it [i.e., the earth] threw out its contents and became [empty and] leveled.
interpretation: This verse describes the events that will occur during the Day of Resurrection. It indicates that the earth will expel all that is within it, such as the dead bodies and treasures, and become completely flat and devoid of any features. This signifies the end of the world as we know it and the beginning of the Hereafter, where all people will be held accountable for their actions in life.
orig: وألقت ما فيها وتخلت

translation: And she [i.e., the earth] has been authorized by her Lord and was allowed [to appear].
interpretation: This verse refers to the earth being granted permission by God to emerge and be manifested in its creation. It signifies that the earth came into existence by the will and authorization of the Lord, and that its appearance was in accordance with the divine plan.
orig: وأذنت لربها وحقت

translation: O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with [great] exertion and will meet Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all human beings are on a journey towards their Creator, and that this journey requires great effort and dedication. The phrase "laboring toward your Lord" suggests that the path to spiritual fulfillment and closeness to God is not an easy one, but one that requires constant striving and exertion. The verse also reminds us that we will ultimately be held accountable for our actions and beliefs before God, as indicated by the phrase "will meet Him". This serves as a call to live a purposeful and righteous life in preparation for the final reckoning.
orig: يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا فملاقيه

translation: But as for he who is given his record in his right hand
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous believers who will be given their record of deeds on the Day of Judgment in their right hand, signifying that they have earned a place in Paradise through their good works and faith. The right hand symbolizes honor, acceptance and reward, in contrast to those who will receive their record in their left hand, which represents disgrace and punishment.
orig: فأما من أوتي كتابه بيمينه

translation: And soon will he be judged with an easy reckoning
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, those who have lived righteous lives and done good deeds will face an "easy reckoning" or a lenient accounting of their actions. The implication is that Allah will be merciful and forgiving towards those who have strived to please Him, and their judgment will be straightforward and not overly burdensome.
orig: فسوف يحاسب حسابا يسيرا

translation: And he returns to his people, rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of a person who has been successful in their endeavors. After facing challenges or difficulties, they return to their family and community with a sense of joy and satisfaction. The interpretation suggests that when one achieves their goals or overcomes obstacles, it brings a feeling of happiness and contentment, which is then shared with their loved ones.
orig: وينقلب إلى أهله مسرورا

translation: And as for him who is given his record behind his back
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are given their record of deeds on the Day of Judgment, but it is given to them from behind their backs. This signifies that they have turned away from the guidance of Allah and have instead chosen to follow their own desires and worldly pursuits. The placement of the record behind their backs suggests that they have turned their backs on the truth and have become heedless of their accountability before Allah.
orig: وأما من أوتي كتابه وراء ظهره

translation: Then he will call for destruction
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of those who reject faith and turn away from the guidance of Allah. They will ultimately call out for destruction, as they will face the consequences of their own choices and actions. The interpretation suggests that those who reject faith will be left with no choice but to face the punishment they have earned through their own misdeeds.
orig: فسوف يدعو ثبورا

translation: And he will [enter to] burn in a Blaze
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment in the Hereafter for those who disbelieve in God and reject His guidance. The "Blaze" symbolizes the intense and eternal torment that awaits those who choose to live a life of disbelief and disobedience to God. The interpretation suggests that those who turn away from the path of righteousness will face the consequences of their actions in the form of a severe and unrelenting punishment in the Afterlife.
orig: ويصلى سعيرا

translation: Indeed, he was [proud] among his people, exultant.
interpretation: This verse describes a person who was arrogant and boastful among his people. He took pride in his status and wealth, and was overly pleased with himself. This attitude of self-importance and lack of humility is condemned in the Quran, as it leads to a disconnect from God and a disregard for the rights of others.
orig: إنه كان في أهله مسرورا

translation: Indeed, he thought that he would never return [to Us].
interpretation: This verse refers to a person who was arrogant and thought that he would never have to return to God for judgment. The implication is that such a person is deluded and that everyone will ultimately be held accountable for their actions before God.
orig: إنه ظن أن لن يحور

translation: Yes, indeed, his Lord is ever of him Fully Aware.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah is All-Knowing and All-Seeing. It conveys that Allah is fully aware of the individual and their actions, thoughts, and intentions. This emphasizes the concept of divine omniscience and that Allah has complete knowledge and oversight over His creation. The verse serves as a reminder that we are accountable to Allah, who is aware of everything we do.
orig: بلى إن ربه كان به بصيرا

translation: But nay! I swear by the twilight
interpretation: This verse is swearing by the twilight, which is the glow of light that remains in the sky after the sun has set. The purpose of this oath is to emphasize the importance of the message that follows, which is likely related to the Day of Judgment or some other profound truth. The oath serves to draw the listener's attention and underscore the gravity of the matter at hand.
orig: فلا أقسم بالشفق

translation: And by the night when it covers,
interpretation: This verse refers to the night and its encompassing nature. It suggests that the night, with its darkness and tranquility, covers and envelops the world, providing a sense of peace and rest. The interpretation is that the night, with its soothing and calming presence, is a sign of Allah's creation and a reminder of the cycle of day and night that He has established.
orig: والليل وما وسق

translation: And [by] the moon when it becomes full
interpretation: This verse is referring to the moon and its phases. When the moon is full, it is in a state of 'itsaaq' or completeness, shining brightly in the night sky. This is a sign of the power and precision of Allah's creation, as the moon follows a precise cycle that is essential for the functioning of the universe and the lives of humans and other creatures. The verse invites us to reflect on the wonders of the natural world and the perfection of Allah's design.
orig: والقمر إذا اتسق

translation: You shall surely climb from stage to stage.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of gradual progress and development. It suggests that one must strive to continuously improve and elevate oneself, moving from one level or stage to the next, rather than remaining stagnant. The metaphor of "climbing from stage to stage" implies a journey of personal growth and transformation, where each step taken leads to a higher level of understanding, wisdom, or achievement.
orig: لتركبن طبقا عن طبق

translation: So what is [the matter] with them that they do not believe?
interpretation: This verse expresses Allah's wonder and questioning as to why some people do not believe in Him and His message, despite the clear signs and guidance He has provided. It suggests that the lack of faith is a matter of choice and responsibility, not due to any deficiency in the evidence or message. The interpretation encourages reflection on one's own beliefs and the reasons behind them.
orig: فما لهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate [in worship].
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection and lack of reverence towards the Qur'an by some people. It suggests that despite the Qur'an being recited to them, they do not humble themselves and prostrate in worship, indicating their arrogance and unwillingness to submit to the divine teachings. The verse serves as a warning against such attitudes and emphasizes the importance of accepting and obeying the Qur'an.
orig: وإذا قرئ عليهم القرآن لا يسجدون

translation: But those who disbelieve deny the truth.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who reject and deny the message of Islam. It suggests that they are willfully rejecting the truth, rather than simply being unaware of it. The interpretation is that the disbelievers are actively denying and dismissing the teachings of the Qur'an and the Prophet Muhammad, despite the evidence presented to them.
orig: بل الذين كفروا يكذبون

translation: And Allah knows best what they conceal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah, the Almighty, has full knowledge and awareness of what people keep hidden in their hearts and minds. It serves as a reminder that we cannot hide anything from Allah, and that He is the All-Knowing, the One who is aware of all that we think, say, and do, whether it is revealed or concealed.
orig: والله أعلم بما يوعون

translation: So give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a command from God to the Prophet Muhammad to warn those who reject the message of Islam and persist in their disbelief and wrongdoing. The "painful punishment" refers to the severe consequences they will face in the Hereafter for their rejection of faith and their misdeeds in this life. The verse emphasizes the importance of delivering this message of warning to those who have turned away from the truth, so that they may have a chance to repent and change their ways before it is too late.
orig: فبشرهم بعذاب أليم

translation: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is a reward uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the only ones who will be saved from punishment and granted a continuous, uninterrupted reward are those who have true faith in God and do good deeds. It highlights the importance of both belief and righteous action, as faith without good works is incomplete. The "reward uninterrupted" suggests a lasting, eternal reward in the Hereafter for those who fulfill these conditions.
orig: إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم أجر غير ممنون

translation: By the heaven containing constellations
interpretation: This verse refers to the grandeur and magnificence of the heavens, which are adorned with the celestial bodies and constellations. It invites us to reflect upon the intricate and ordered nature of the universe, which points to the existence and power of the Creator. The verse encourages us to ponder the signs of Allah's creation and to draw closer to Him through contemplation and worship.
orig: والسماء ذات البروج

translation: And the promised Day
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, the day when all people will be held accountable for their actions in life. It emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of this event, which has been promised by God. The interpretation suggests that individuals should prepare for this momentous day by living a righteous life and doing good deeds, as they will be judged accordingly on that day.
orig: واليوم الموعود

translation: And the witness and that which is witnessed
interpretation: This verse refers to the concept of testimony and witnessing in the context of Islamic teachings. The "witness" could refer to a person who testifies or bears witness to something, while the "that which is witnessed" could refer to the event, action, or circumstance that is being testified to. This verse emphasizes the importance of bearing witness and providing testimony, which is a central aspect of Islamic jurisprudence and the pursuit of justice.
orig: وشاهد ومشهود

translation: The companions of the trench were killed
interpretation: This verse refers to a historical event where a group of believers were persecuted and killed for their faith. It is a reminder that standing firm in one's beliefs can sometimes come at a great personal cost, but that those who remain steadfast in the face of adversity will be rewarded by God. The "companions of the trench" were likely early Christians or other religious minorities who were martyred for their faith, and this verse serves as a call to Muslims to be willing to make similar sacrifices if necessary.
orig: قتل أصحاب الأخدود

translation: The Fire, [whose fuel is] people and stones
interpretation: This verse refers to the hellfire, which is fueled by the disbelievers and their evil deeds. The "stones" mentioned could refer to idols or other objects of worship besides Allah. The interpretation is that the hellfire is a severe punishment for those who reject faith and engage in sinful behavior.
orig: النار ذات الوقود

translation: When they were sitting on it.
interpretation: This verse refers to a specific situation where a group of people were sitting on something, likely a place or an object. The interpretation suggests that the verse is describing a particular scene or event, without providing additional context about the nature of the situation being described.
orig: إذ هم عليها قعود

translation: And they are witnesses over what they do to the believers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who persecute the believers are fully aware of their actions and will be held accountable for them. It implies that the oppressors of the faithful will not be able to escape the consequences of their misdeeds, as they are being observed and their actions are being recorded.
orig: وهم على ما يفعلون بالمؤمنين شهود

translation: And they resented them not except because they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the disbelievers persecuted the believers solely because of their faith in the Almighty and All-Praiseworthy God. It suggests that the believers' unwavering commitment to their belief in the one true God was the sole reason for the animosity and resentment they faced from the unbelievers. The verse emphasizes the steadfastness of the believers in the face of persecution and their refusal to abandon their faith, which was ultimately rooted in their recognition of Allah's power and worthiness of praise.
orig: وما نقموا منهم إلا أن يؤمنوا بالله العزيز الحميد

translation: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is over all things a Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and omnipotence of Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. It affirms that Allah is the sole Ruler and Owner of the entire universe, and that He is a Witness to all that transpires in His creation. This serves as a reminder that Allah is All-Knowing, All-Seeing, and that He is the ultimate authority to whom all will be held accountable.
orig: الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض والله على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Indeed, those who have tortured the believing men and believing women and then have not repented will have the punishment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the Burning Fire.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who persecute and torment the believers, whether men or women. It warns that unless they repent, they will face the severe punishment of Hell and the burning fire. The verse emphasizes the gravity of oppressing the faithful and the need for sincere repentance to avoid eternal damnation.
orig: إن الذين فتنوا المؤمنين والمؤمنات ثم لم يتوبوا فلهم عذاب جهنم ولهم عذاب الحريق

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse promises a great reward in the Hereafter for those who have true faith in God and do good deeds. The gardens with flowing rivers symbolize the eternal bliss and abundance that awaits the righteous in Paradise. This "great attainment" is the ultimate success and triumph, as it represents salvation from the punishment of the Hellfire and the achievement of the highest level of eternal bliss in the Afterlife.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ذلك الفوز الكبير

translation: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and power of Allah's punishment for those who disobey and reject His commands. It serves as a warning to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to avoid sinful actions that may incur Allah's wrath. The interpretation suggests that the consequences of defying Allah are severe and should not be taken lightly, as He has the absolute authority and ability to punish those who stray from the righteous path.
orig: إن بطش ربك لشديد

translation: Indeed, it is He who begins [creation] and repeats [it]
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah is the sole Creator who initiates the creation of all things and then reproduces or repeats that creation. It is a declaration of Allah's power and sovereignty, as He alone has the ability to bring things into existence and then re-create them. This verse emphasizes the concept of resurrection and the afterlife, as Allah who created life in the first place has the power to bring it back again after death.
orig: إنه هو يبدئ ويعيد

translation: And He is the Forgiving, the Affectionate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes two of Allah's attributes - His forgiveness and His love. It conveys that Allah is merciful and compassionate towards His creation, readily forgiving those who repent and seek His pardon. The attribute of "al-Wadud" (the Affectionate) suggests that Allah has a deep and abiding love for His servants, and desires their love and devotion in return. This verse encourages believers to seek Allah's forgiveness and to cultivate a loving relationship with Him.
orig: وهو الغفور الودود

translation: The Possessor of the Glorious Throne
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah, the Almighty, as the Possessor of the Glorious Throne. It emphasizes Allah's sovereignty, power, and majesty. The Throne represents the highest level of creation, and Allah's possession of it signifies His supreme authority and control over the entire universe. This verse reminds us of Allah's grandeur and the need to submit to His will and worship Him alone.
orig: ذو العرش المجيد

translation: The Doer of what He intends
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is the One who does whatever He wills and nothing can prevent Him from accomplishing His plans. It suggests that Allah is All-Powerful and His will is absolute, and that He is not bound by any external constraints or limitations. The interpretation is that Allah is the Sovereign Ruler who acts according to His wisdom and purpose, and His actions are not subject to the will or control of any other entity.
orig: فعال لما يريد

translation: Has the story of the soldiers reached you?
interpretation: This verse is asking if the story or account of the soldiers has reached the listener. It is likely referring to a specific historical event or narrative that was well-known at the time, and the question is meant to draw the listener's attention to this important story. The interpretation is that the verse is inviting the listener to reflect on this significant tale, which may contain lessons or insights relevant to the listener's own life and faith.
orig: هل أتاك حديث الجنود

translation: Pharaoh and Thamud
interpretation: This verse is a reference to two historical figures and communities mentioned in the Qur'an - Pharaoh, the tyrannical ruler of ancient Egypt, and Thamud, an ancient Arabian tribe. The verse likely serves as a warning and lesson, highlighting the consequences faced by those who rejected the message of God's prophets and engaged in oppression and wrongdoing. It reminds us of the importance of heeding the guidance of the Qur'an and submitting to the will of the Almighty.
orig: فرعون وثمود

translation: Rather, those who disbelieve are in denial.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject faith and deny the truth of the Qur'an and the teachings of Islam are the ones who are truly in a state of denial. They are unwilling to accept the guidance and wisdom that is being presented to them, and instead choose to remain in their state of disbelief and rejection.
orig: بل الذين كفروا في تكذيب

translation: And Allah encompasses them from behind.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge and control over all things, including those that may seem hidden or out of sight. It suggests that no one can escape the watchful gaze and power of Allah, as He encompasses and surrounds all of creation from every direction. This is a reminder of Allah's omniscience and omnipotence, and that one should always be mindful of His presence and authority.
orig: والله من ورائهم محيط

translation: Nay, it is a Glorious Qur'an,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the grandeur and majesty of the Qur'an. It is not merely a book, but a "Glorious Qur'an" - a divine revelation that is sublime, magnificent, and worthy of the highest respect and reverence. The verse serves to highlight the Qur'an's exalted status and the importance of engaging with it as a source of guidance and wisdom.
orig: بل هو قرآن مجيد

translation: In a preserved tablet
interpretation: This verse refers to the concept of the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) in Islamic theology. The Preserved Tablet is believed to be a celestial record where Allah has inscribed all that has happened and will happen in the universe. This verse suggests that the knowledge and decrees of Allah are preserved and protected in this divine tablet, which is beyond the reach of human alteration or corruption.
orig: في لوح محفوظ

translation: By the heaven and the night-comer (i.e. the night-visitant).
interpretation: This verse is referring to the heaven and the night-comer, which is understood to be a celestial object or phenomenon that appears in the night sky. The interpretation is that Allah swears by the heavens and this night-comer, emphasizing the importance and significance of what is to be conveyed in the subsequent verses.
orig: والسماء والطارق

translation: And what can make you know what is the Tariq?
interpretation: This verse refers to the concept of "Tariq" or the "Knocker", which is believed to be a celestial body or phenomenon that is mentioned in the Qur'an. The interpretation of this verse is that it is posing a rhetorical question, asking the reader what they know about the Tariq, implying that it is a profound and mysterious entity that is beyond human understanding. The verse is inviting the reader to reflect on the wonders of the universe and the signs of Allah's creation.
orig: وما أدراك ما الطارق

translation: The piercing star
interpretation: This verse refers to the star, which is described as "piercing" or "penetrating." This could be interpreted as a metaphor for the brightness and intensity of the star, which is able to pierce through the darkness of the night sky. Alternatively, it could be a reference to the star's ability to provide guidance and direction, like a beacon that cuts through the darkness. The verse may also be a metaphor for the power and might of God, whose creation of the stars is a testament to His greatness and sovereignty.
orig: النجم الثاقب

translation: Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that each person has a guardian or watcher over them, who is responsible for recording their deeds and actions. This guardian could refer to the angels assigned to each person, or to Allah Himself, who is aware of and observes everything that a person does. The implication is that we are accountable for our actions and will be held responsible for them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: إن كل نفس لما عليها حافظ

translation: So let man observe from what he was created.
interpretation: This verse encourages humans to reflect on the origin of their creation and the process by which they came into being. It invites us to ponder the wonders of our own creation, which can lead to a deeper appreciation of the power and wisdom of the Creator. By understanding our origins, we can develop a greater sense of humility, gratitude, and purpose in our lives.
orig: فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق

translation: He created [man] from a liquid semen
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of human beings from a flowing liquid, which is a reference to semen. It highlights the origin of human life and the role of procreation in the continuation of the human species. The Qur'an often uses such scientific facts to point to the power and wisdom of the Creator, and to encourage reflection and contemplation on the marvels of creation.
orig: خلق من ماء دافق

translation: It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the origin of human creation. It is describing the process of how a human being is formed, emerging from between the backbone and the ribs. This suggests that the essence of a human being is something that is hidden and protected, coming from a place deep within the body. The interpretation is that the creation of a human being is a miraculous and intricate process, guided by the divine.
orig: يخرج من بين الصلب والترائب

translation: Indeed, [O Muhammad], He is over his return [i.e., resurrection] competent.
interpretation: This verse affirms that Allah has the power and ability to resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that nothing is impossible for Him, and that He can bring back to life all of His creation, no matter how long they have been dead. This serves as a reminder of the certainty of the Hereafter and the need for people to prepare for it by living righteous lives.
orig: إنه على رجعه لقادر

translation: The Day when secrets will be revealed.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all the hidden secrets and intentions of people will be made known. On that day, nothing will remain concealed, and all will be held accountable for their actions, both good and bad. This emphasizes the importance of living a righteous life, as our innermost thoughts and deeds will be laid bare before the Almighty.
orig: يوم تبلى السرائر

translation: And he has no power nor any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the person being referred to has no power or support to help them. It suggests that they are completely helpless and without any means of assistance or protection. The interpretation implies that one should not rely on their own strength or on the help of others, but rather seek support from Allah, the Almighty, who is the true source of power and aid.
orig: فما له من قوة ولا ناصر

translation: And the heaven with [its] returning [rain]
interpretation: This verse refers to the cyclical nature of the heavens and the rain. It suggests that the sky has a constant cycle of returning rain, which is a sign of God's power and the regularity of the natural world. The interpretation is that the heavens have a regular pattern of rainfall, which is a blessing from God and a testament to His wisdom and control over the universe.
orig: والسماء ذات الرجع

translation: And the earth, with its swelling [therein]
interpretation: This verse describes the earth and its expansive nature. It suggests that the earth is constantly expanding and undergoing changes, similar to how a swelling or bulging occurs. This can be interpreted as a reference to the scientific concept of the expansion of the universe and the dynamic nature of the Earth's geological processes.
orig: والأرض ذات الصدع

translation: Verily, this is a decisive word
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authoritative and definitive nature of the Qur'anic message. It conveys that the Qur'an is a clear and decisive statement from God, not something to be taken lightly or doubted. The Qur'an provides clear guidance and judgement on matters of faith, morality, and the human condition. This verse assures the reader that the Qur'an is a reliable and trustworthy source of divine wisdom.
orig: إنه لقول فصل

translation: And it is not a jest.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the message of the Qur'an is not something to be taken lightly or treated as a jest. It is a serious revelation from God that deserves our utmost attention and contemplation. The Qur'an is not mere entertainment or a trivial matter, but a guide for humanity that should be approached with reverence and sincerity.
orig: وما هو بالهزل

translation: Indeed, they are plotting a scheme
interpretation: This verse suggests that those being referred to are engaged in a deceitful or manipulative plot or plan. The use of the word "kaid" (scheme, plot) implies that their actions are calculated and intended to achieve a specific, perhaps nefarious, end. The verse conveys a sense of caution and wariness towards the actions of these individuals.
orig: إنهم يكيدون كيدا

translation: And I will surely plan a plan [against them].
interpretation: This verse suggests that God will devise a plan or strategy to deal with those who reject His message and oppose Him. It implies that God has the power and wisdom to overcome any schemes or plots against Him. The interpretation suggests that God's plan is certain and will ultimately prevail, as He is the All-Knowing and All-Powerful.
orig: وأكيد كيدا

translation: So give a respite to the disbelievers. Leave them for a while.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet (peace be upon him) to be patient and give the disbelievers a respite, allowing them time to reflect and potentially turn to faith. It suggests that forcing belief upon them is not the way, but rather allowing them the freedom to choose their own path, while continuing to convey the message of Islam. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of tolerance, compassion and allowing people the space to make their own decisions regarding faith.
orig: فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويدا

translation: Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to glorify and revere the name of God, the Highest and Most Exalted. It reminds us to constantly remember and praise Allah, the Supreme Lord, who is above all creation. This act of glorification and reverence is a fundamental aspect of worship and devotion in Islam.
orig: سبح اسم ربك الأعلى

translation: The One who created and [then] proportioned
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah as the One who created the universe and all that is in it, and then perfectly proportioned and ordered it. It speaks to Allah's power, wisdom, and control over all of creation. The interpretation is that Allah is the sole Creator and Sustainer of the cosmos, and that He has designed and arranged everything with precision and purpose.
orig: الذي خلق فسوى

translation: And the One who destined and [then] guided
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah, the Almighty, who has decreed and determined all things, and then guided His creation towards the right path. It emphasizes that Allah is the One who plans, ordains, and directs the affairs of the universe, and that His guidance is essential for humanity to find the right way. This verse encourages believers to trust in Allah's wisdom and to seek His guidance in all aspects of their lives.
orig: والذي قدر فهدى

translation: And the One who brings forth the pasture,
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah, the Creator, who provides sustenance for all living beings by bringing forth the vegetation and greenery that serves as food and grazing grounds for animals. It is a testament to Allah's power, provision, and care for His creation.
orig: والذي أخرج المرعى

translation: And He made it [i.e., the dead vegetation] scattered debris.
interpretation: This verse is describing the fate of dead vegetation, which is reduced to scattered debris or worthless material. The Arabic word "ghuthaa'" refers to the light, dry, and scattered remnants of something that has decayed or been destroyed. This verse is a metaphor for the transient nature of worldly things and the ultimate fate of all that is created. It serves as a reminder that all material things will eventually perish, and that one should focus on the eternal and lasting values in life.
orig: فجعله غثاء أحوى

translation: We will make you recite, [O Muhammad], and you will not forget,
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that Allah will make him recite the Qur'an, and he will not forget its words. It is a promise of divine assistance and preservation of the Qur'an, which was revealed to the Prophet over a period of 23 years. This verse highlights the importance of the Qur'an and the role of the Prophet in its transmission, as well as the divine protection and guidance afforded to him in this task.
orig: سنقرئك فلا تنسى

translation: Except as Allah wills. Indeed, He knows what is declared and what is hidden.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that everything occurs according to the will of Allah. He is all-knowing, and nothing is hidden from Him - He is aware of both what is openly declared and what is kept hidden. This serves as a reminder that we must submit to Allah's will and that we cannot act independently of His knowledge and control.
orig: إلا ما شاء الله إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى

translation: And We will ease you toward ease.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that He will make his path easy and facilitate his affairs. It suggests that despite the challenges and difficulties the Prophet may face, Allah will provide him with the means and support to overcome them. The interpretation is that Allah will guide the Prophet and his followers towards ease, comfort, and success in their endeavors, as long as they remain steadfast in their faith and obedience to Him.
orig: ونيسرك لليسرى

translation: So remind, [O Muhammad], if the reminder should benefit [the people].
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to continue reminding and guiding people, as the reminder may benefit those who are receptive to it. It suggests that the role of a messenger is to convey the message, and the ultimate impact is in the hands of the people. The reminder or admonition can have a positive effect on those willing to listen and heed the guidance.
orig: فذكر إن نفعت الذكرى

translation: He will be reminded who fears [Allah]
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who fear and revere Allah will be reminded of His guidance and teachings. The implication is that those who are mindful of Allah and live with a consciousness of Him will be the ones who receive divine reminders and teachings to help them on their spiritual journey.
orig: سيذكر من يخشى

translation: And the most wretched will avoid it.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Hellfire, which the most wretched and sinful people will avoid and stay away from. The interpretation suggests that those who lead a life of sin and wickedness will be fearful of the punishment of the Hereafter and will try to distance themselves from it.
orig: ويتجنبها الأشقى

translation: The one who will burn in the Great Fire
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment that awaits those who reject faith and engage in evil deeds. The "Great Fire" is a metaphor for the eternal hellfire that awaits the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. The interpretation suggests that those who turn away from God and choose to live a life of sin and unrighteousness will face the severe consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: الذي يصلى النار الكبرى

translation: Then he neither dies therein nor lives.
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal punishment of the disbelievers in the Hereafter. They will neither die to find relief from their torment, nor will they live a life of comfort and ease. Instead, they will be in a state of perpetual suffering and anguish, unable to escape the consequences of their rejection of faith and righteous deeds.
orig: ثم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى

translation: Certainly he has succeeded who purifies himself,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of self-purification and moral reform. The one who has purified their soul from vices and adorned it with virtues has truly succeeded in life. This purification is not merely an outward act, but a deep, inward transformation that leads to a righteous and God-conscious life.
orig: قد أفلح من تزكى

translation: And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself [to Him] with complete devotion.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to constantly remember and invoke the name of God, the Lord, and to dedicate oneself fully to Him through sincere worship and obedience. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong connection with the Divine and making one's devotion to God the central focus of one's life.
orig: وذكر اسم ربه فصلى

translation: But you prefer the worldly life
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the human tendency to prioritize and indulge in the pleasures of the worldly life, rather than focusing on the hereafter and spiritual matters. It suggests that people often choose to pursue material gains, status, and temporary enjoyments over the more lasting and meaningful aspects of life. The interpretation is that this verse serves as a reminder to not get overly attached to the fleeting nature of this world and to instead strive for the eternal rewards of the afterlife.
orig: بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا

translation: And the Hereafter is better and more lasting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the superiority and permanence of the Hereafter over the fleeting nature of this worldly life. It encourages believers to focus on the eternal rewards and blessings of the Afterlife, which are far more valuable and enduring than the temporary pleasures of this world. The Hereafter represents the true and lasting abode for the righteous, where they will find everlasting peace, joy, and fulfillment in the presence of Allah.
orig: والآخرة خير وأبقى

translation: Indeed, this [Qur'an] is in the former scriptures
interpretation: This verse affirms that the message of the Qur'an is not something new, but rather it is in continuity with the divine revelations that were sent down to the previous prophets. The Qur'an is the final and complete scripture that confirms and preserves the essential teachings found in the earlier divine books. This emphasizes the unity of the divine message and the fact that the Qur'an is the culmination of God's guidance to humanity.
orig: إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى

translation: The scriptures of Abraham and Moses
interpretation: This verse refers to the sacred scriptures revealed to the Prophets Abraham and Moses. It suggests that the Qur'an contains teachings and guidance that are consistent with the earlier revelations given to these great Prophets of God. The mention of these scriptures underscores the continuity of the divine message and the unity of the Abrahamic faiths.
orig: صحف إبراهيم وموسى

translation: Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming [event]?
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, also known as the "Overwhelming [event]". It is asking whether the news of this momentous and awe-inspiring day has reached the listener.
