The "Overwhelming [event]" is a reference to the cataclysmic events that will take place on the Day of Judgment, when the entire universe will be transformed, and all people will be held accountable for their actions in life. This verse serves as a reminder to be prepared for this inevitable day, and to live one's life in a way that is pleasing to God.
orig: هل أتاك حديث الغاشية

translation: On that Day, [some] faces will be humbled
interpretation: This verse describes the state of people on the Day of Judgment, when they will be humble and submissive before the Almighty. The faces of the people will be downcast, reflecting their awe and reverence for the divine presence. This suggests that on that momentous day, all human pride and arrogance will be stripped away, and people will be humbled by the sheer magnitude and power of the divine.
orig: وجوه يومئذ خاشعة

translation: A toiling woman
interpretation: This verse refers to a woman who is engaged in hard work and labor. It suggests that she is diligent and industrious in her efforts, striving to fulfill her responsibilities and contribute to her family or community. The verse highlights the value and dignity of hard work, regardless of one's gender.
orig: عاملة ناصبة

translation: It will burn in a Fiercely Blazing Fire
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment in the Hereafter for those who reject faith and do not believe in God. The "fiercely blazing fire" is a metaphor for the intense and unrelenting torment that awaits them in the Afterlife. The interpretation is that those who turn away from the guidance of the Quran and live a life of disbelief and sin will face the consequences of their actions in the form of a severe and eternal punishment.
orig: تصلى نارا حامية

translation: It is watered from a source [named] Ayniyya.
interpretation: This verse refers to a source of water that is described as "Ayniyya", which could be the name of a specific spring or well. The implication is that this water source is pure, clean, and readily available to those who need it. This could be interpreted as a metaphor for the guidance and blessings that are provided by Allah to those who seek them.
orig: تسقى من عين آنية

translation: They will have no food except from a bitter thorn tree
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment and suffering that the disbelievers will face in the Hereafter. They will have no access to the delicious and nourishing foods that the believers will enjoy, but instead will be forced to consume only the bitter and thorny plants that grow in the hellfire. This emphasizes the stark contrast between the rewards of the righteous and the torment of the wicked.
orig: ليس لهم طعام إلا من ضريع

translation: It neither fattens nor avails against hunger.
interpretation: This verse is often interpreted as a metaphor for actions or deeds that do not provide any real benefit or sustenance. It suggests that certain actions or behaviors, no matter how much they may be done, do not actually fulfill one's needs or provide any meaningful nourishment. The verse encourages people to focus on more substantial and beneficial actions that can truly satisfy their needs, rather than engaging in futile or superficial activities.
orig: لا يسمن ولا يغني من جوع

translation: On that Day, [some] faces will be radiant
interpretation: This verse describes the faces of the righteous on the Day of Judgment. Their faces will be radiant, reflecting their inner peace, joy and contentment with having lived a virtuous life. This is a promise of reward and success in the Hereafter for those who have believed and done good deeds in this world.
orig: وجوه يومئذ ناعمة

translation: Pleased with her endeavor
interpretation: This verse suggests that the person is content and satisfied with their efforts and achievements. It implies a sense of fulfillment and contentment with the work they have put in, regardless of the outcome. The verse conveys the idea that the person is at peace with the results of their endeavors, knowing that they have given their best.
orig: لسعيها راضية

translation: In an elevated garden
interpretation: This verse refers to the eternal abode of the righteous in the Hereafter. The "elevated garden" symbolizes the lofty and exalted nature of the Paradise that awaits those who have lived virtuous lives and believed in God. This verse conveys the promise of a blissful and exalted existence in the Afterlife for the faithful.
orig: في جنة عالية

translation: You will not hear in it [i.e., Paradise] ill speech or commission of sin.
interpretation: This verse conveys that in Paradise, the believers will be free from any kind of vain, idle or sinful speech. The environment of Paradise will be one of purity, tranquility and righteousness, where nothing impure or harmful will be present. This highlights the perfection and serenity that awaits the righteous in the Hereafter.
orig: لا تسمع فيها لاغية

translation: Therein is a flowing spring.
interpretation: This verse refers to the gardens of Paradise, where there will be a flowing spring of pure, refreshing water. The presence of this spring symbolizes the abundance and tranquility that the righteous will enjoy in the Hereafter. The flowing spring represents the perpetual blessings and delights that await those who believe and do good deeds.
orig: فيها عين جارية

translation: In it are thrones [of dignity], raised up.
interpretation: This verse refers to the luxurious furnishings and elevated status of the dwellings in Paradise. The "sururun marfu'atun" or "thrones raised up" symbolize the elevated, dignified position of the inhabitants of Paradise, who will be seated on comfortable, elevated seats as a sign of their high status and honor in the Hereafter.
orig: فيها سرر مرفوعة

translation: And cups set in their places
interpretation: This verse describes the luxurious setting of Paradise, where cups or vessels are placed in an orderly manner, ready to be served to the inhabitants of Paradise. The implication is that the inhabitants of Paradise will be provided with all that they desire, in a beautifully arranged and organized manner, reflecting the perfection and abundance of the blessings of the Hereafter.
orig: وأكواب موضوعة

translation: And cushions set in rows
interpretation: This verse is describing the luxurious furnishings and comfortable seating arrangements that will be provided for the inhabitants of Paradise. The "cushions set in rows" suggests a setting of elegance and opulence, where the believers will be able to recline and enjoy the blessings of the Hereafter. This verse highlights the rewards and comforts that await those who have lived righteous lives and earned the pleasure of Allah.
orig: ونمارق مصفوفة

translation: And [extensive] carpets [are spread].
interpretation: This verse is describing the lavish furnishings and decorations that will be present in Paradise. The "carpets" referred to here likely symbolize the luxurious and comfortable environment that the inhabitants of Paradise will enjoy. The term "mabthuthah" suggests that these carpets are spread out extensively, conveying a sense of grandeur and abundance. This verse is meant to evoke a vision of the splendor and comfort that await the righteous in the Hereafter.
orig: وزرابي مبثوثة

translation: Then do they not look at the camels - how they are created?
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the wonders of God's creation, specifically the camel. The camel is a remarkable animal that is well-suited to the harsh desert environment, and its unique features, such as its ability to store water in its hump, are a testament to the wisdom and power of the Creator. By contemplating the intricate design of the camel, people are invited to recognize the signs of God's existence and the perfection of His creation, which should lead them to worship and obey Him.
orig: أفلا ينظرون إلى الإبل كيف خلقت

translation: And [consider, O Mankind], the heaven - how it was raised?
interpretation: This verse encourages people to reflect on the creation of the heavens, and how they were raised above the earth in a magnificent and orderly manner. It is a call to ponder the power and wisdom of the Creator, and to recognize the signs of His existence and divine attributes in the wonders of the universe.
orig: وإلى السماء كيف رفعت

translation: And [consider, O worshiper], the mountains - how they are set up?
interpretation: This verse encourages the reader to reflect on the creation of the mountains and how they were firmly established by God. The mountains, with their towering presence and immovable foundations, are a testament to the power and wisdom of the Creator. This verse invites the reader to ponder the grandeur of God's creation and to recognize the signs of His existence and might in the world around them.
orig: وإلى الجبال كيف نصبت

translation: And [consider, O Mankind], the earth - how it is spread out?
interpretation: This verse invites us to reflect upon the creation of the earth and how it has been spread out for the benefit of humanity. It is a call to appreciate the wonders of Allah's creation and to recognize the blessings that the earth provides for us. The interpretation suggests that we should be grateful for the resources and opportunities that the earth offers, and use them responsibly and in accordance with the teachings of Islam.
orig: وإلى الأرض كيف سطحت

translation: So remind, [O Muhammad], for you are only a reminder.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad's role is to convey the message of Islam and remind people of their duty to God. He is not responsible for guiding or compelling people to believe, as that is ultimately up to each individual. The verse encourages the Prophet to continue his mission of reminding and guiding people, without feeling burdened by their choices.
orig: فذكر إنما أنت مذكر

translation: You are not a controller over them.
interpretation: This verse conveys that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not a dictator or a coercive authority over the people. His role is to deliver the message of Islam, not to force its acceptance. The people have the free will to choose whether to believe or not, and the Prophet's responsibility is to guide them, not to compel them.
orig: لست عليهم بمصيطر

translation: Except for those who turn away and disbelieve
interpretation: This verse refers to those who reject faith and turn away from the guidance of the Qur'an. It suggests that the consequences of disbelief and turning away from God's message will be severe, and that those who do so will not be granted the same rewards as those who believe and submit to God.
orig: إلا من تولى وكفر

translation: Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who reject the message of Islam and turn away from the guidance of Allah. The "greatest punishment" likely refers to the eternal punishment in the Hereafter, which is far more severe than any worldly punishment. This serves as a warning to those who persist in their disbelief and disobedience, as they will face the gravest consequences in the Afterlife.
orig: فيعذبه الله العذاب الأكبر

translation: Indeed, to Us is their return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all people will ultimately return to God for judgment and accountability. It serves as a reminder that our actions and choices in this life have consequences in the Hereafter, and that we will be held responsible for them before God.
orig: إن إلينا إيابهم

translation: Then indeed, upon Us is their account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that ultimately, all people will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs before God. It suggests that the final reckoning and judgment of people's deeds lies with God, not with any human authority. The verse conveys a sense of divine sovereignty and the inevitability of being answerable to the Almighty.
orig: ثم إن علينا حسابهم

translation: By the dawn
interpretation: This verse is referring to the dawn or the first light of the day. It is often interpreted as a call to reflect on the cycles of nature and the importance of starting each day with a fresh perspective. The dawn is a symbol of new beginnings, a time to renew one's intentions and commitment to living a righteous life.
orig: والفجر

translation: And [by] the ten nights
interpretation: This verse refers to the first ten days of the Islamic month of Dhul-Hijjah, which are considered sacred and blessed days. These days are associated with the pilgrimage (Hajj) and various acts of worship and devotion. The interpretation of this verse is that Allah swears by these ten nights, emphasizing their importance and sanctity.
orig: وليال عشر

translation: And the even and the odd
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of the universe in pairs, with both even and odd numbers. It suggests that there is a balance and harmony in the universe, with opposing forces coexisting. The interpretation is that the even and the odd represent the duality and complementarity of all things in the universe, which is a reflection of the divine wisdom and power of God.
orig: والشفع والوتر

translation: And by the night when it covers,
interpretation: This verse refers to the night when it covers the earth with its darkness. It is a reminder that the night is a time of rest, reflection, and contemplation, as the darkness envelops the world, providing a respite from the bustling activities of the day. The night is a time to seek solace, to ponder upon the signs of God's creation, and to reconnect with one's inner self.
orig: والليل إذا يسر

translation: Is there in that [sign] a [compelling] oath for one of perception?
interpretation: This verse from the Qur'an is asking whether there is a compelling oath or evidence in the signs of Allah's creation for those who use their intellect and perception. The implication is that the wonders of the universe and the intricate design of creation should serve as a powerful proof and reminder of the existence and majesty of the Creator for those who reflect deeply and use their faculties of reason and understanding.
orig: هل في ذلك قسم لذي حجر

translation: Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with \"Aad?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the destruction of the ancient people of \"Aad, who were known for their arrogance and rejection of God's guidance. The verse invites the reader to reflect on how God dealt with this civilization, as a lesson and warning for those who defy His commands. The destruction of \"Aad serves as a reminder of God's power and the consequences of turning away from the path of righteousness.
orig: ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بعاد

translation: Iram, [that had] lofty pillars
interpretation: This verse refers to the ancient city of Iram, also known as Iram of the Pillars, which was a prosperous and advanced civilization mentioned in the Qur'an. The phrase "ذات العماد" or "that had lofty pillars" suggests that Iram was known for its impressive architectural structures and grandeur. This verse serves as a reminder of the power and might of past civilizations, and the importance of not becoming arrogant or complacent, as their fate can serve as a lesson for the present day.
orig: إرم ذات العماد

translation: That which has not been created the like of it in the lands
interpretation: This verse refers to the uniqueness and unparalleled nature of God's creation. It suggests that there are aspects of the universe or certain phenomena that are truly one-of-a-kind, with no equal or equivalent to be found anywhere in the world. This highlights the extraordinary power and wisdom of the Creator, who has fashioned the cosmos in a way that defies duplication or replication by human beings. The interpretation emphasizes the idea that God's creation is singular, remarkable, and beyond the capacity of mortals to fully comprehend or replicate.
orig: التي لم يخلق مثلها في البلاد

translation: And [We destroyed] Thamud, who had carved out [large] rocks in the [Nubian] valley
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of the ancient people of Thamud, who were known for their impressive architectural feats, including carving out large rocks in the valley. This serves as a reminder of the consequences of arrogance, disbelief, and disobedience to God's commands, as the Thamud people were ultimately destroyed for their rejection of the Prophet Salih and their transgressions.
orig: وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], Pharaoh of the stakes.
interpretation: This verse refers to the tyrannical ruler Pharaoh, who is described as "of the stakes" or "with the stakes". This could be interpreted as a reference to Pharaoh's practice of impaling or crucifying his enemies on stakes as a means of punishment and intimidation. The verse highlights Pharaoh's cruelty and the oppressive nature of his rule over the Israelites.
orig: وفرعون ذي الأوتاد

translation: Those who transgressed in the land
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have committed acts of oppression, injustice, and excess in the land. It condemns those who abuse their power and authority, and who disregard the rights of others. The interpretation suggests that such behavior is unacceptable and will be held accountable before God.
orig: الذين طغوا في البلاد

translation: And they spread corruption in it.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who engage in destructive and harmful activities within a society or community. The interpretation suggests that they are responsible for causing disorder, chaos, and unrest, and their actions lead to the deterioration of the social fabric. The verse condemns such behavior and calls for individuals to refrain from engaging in activities that can harm the well-being of others and the overall stability of the community.
orig: فأكثروا فيها الفساد

translation: So your Lord poured upon them a punishment from above
interpretation: This verse is referring to the divine punishment that was inflicted upon a group of people who had rejected the message of God and engaged in wrongdoing. The imagery of God "pouring" down punishment suggests the severity and overwhelming nature of the retribution. The interpretation is that those who persistently defy God and refuse to heed His guidance will face the consequences of their actions, which can be severe and unrelenting.
orig: فصب عليهم ربك سوط عذاب

translation: Indeed, your Lord is in observation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God is all-knowing and ever-watchful over the actions and deeds of His creation. It serves as a reminder that we are accountable for our conduct, as God is constantly observing and keeping track of our behavior. This should inspire us to live righteously and be mindful of our actions, knowing that we will be held responsible for them before the Almighty.
orig: إن ربك لبالمرصاد

translation: As for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] is generous to him and favors him, he [begins to] say, "My Lord has honored me."
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to become arrogant and self-satisfied when they are blessed with prosperity and favors from God. The verse suggests that when God tests a person and then bestows upon them His grace and blessings, the person may become complacent and attribute their good fortune to their own merits, rather than recognizing it as a gift from God. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of humility and gratitude in the face of God's blessings, and the need to avoid arrogance and self-aggrandizement.
orig: فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه ربه فأكرمه ونعمه فيقول ربي أكرمن

translation: And as for him whom He tries and [thereby] restricts his provision, he says, 'My Lord has humiliated me.'
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of someone who has been tested by Allah through a restriction of their provision or wealth. Instead of accepting this trial with patience and gratitude, they complain that Allah has humiliated them. This attitude reflects a lack of understanding that Allah's tests and trials are part of His wisdom and are meant to strengthen one's faith and reliance on Him. The interpretation encourages the believer to respond to hardship with humility and trust in Allah's plan, rather than with ingratitude and a sense of being wronged.
orig: وأما إذا ما ابتلاه فقدر عليه رزقه فيقول ربي أهانن

translation: Nay! But you do not honor the orphan
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who do not honor and care for orphans. The verse emphasizes that the true test of one's faith and morality is how they treat the most vulnerable in society, such as orphans. The verse is calling on people to show compassion and kindness towards orphans, and to not neglect or mistreat them.
orig: كلا بل لا تكرمون اليتيم

translation: And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to be compassionate and to help those in need. It criticizes the practice of not urging one another to provide food and assistance to the poor and destitute. The interpretation is that Muslims should actively promote and support efforts to feed and care for the less fortunate in society.
orig: ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين

translation: And you consume inheritance, devouring [it] altogether.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of consuming inheritance in an excessive and unjust manner. It suggests that people should not greedily devour the wealth and possessions left behind by others, especially their family members. The verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and moderation in dealing with inheritance, rather than selfishly appropriating it all for oneself.
orig: وتأكلون التراث أكلا لما

translation: And you love wealth with immense love.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to be overly attached to and obsessed with the accumulation of wealth. It suggests that people often love wealth excessively, placing it above other important priorities in life. The verse serves as a reminder to maintain a balanced perspective and not let the love of wealth consume one's values and priorities.
orig: وتحبون المال حبا جما

translation: Nay, when the earth is ground to powder,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when the earth will be completely destroyed and reduced to dust. The term "dukkat" (ground to powder) suggests a violent, cataclysmic event that will completely transform the physical world as we know it. The repetition of the word "dukkan" emphasizes the finality and totality of this destruction, leaving no trace of the current earth behind. This serves as a reminder of the impermanence of the physical world and the inevitability of the Hereafter, where all will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: كلا إذا دكت الأرض دكا دكا

translation: And your Lord comes and the angels, rank upon rank.
interpretation: This verse conveys the majesty and power of God, as well as the obedience and submission of the angels to Him. It suggests that on the Day of Judgment, God Himself will come, accompanied by the angels in perfect order and alignment, to judge humanity. This emphasizes the grandeur and awe-inspiring nature of the final reckoning, where God's authority and sovereignty will be fully manifest.
orig: وجاء ربك والملك صفا صفا

translation: And Hell will be brought forth that Day. On that Day will man remember, but how will that remembrance [then] avail him?
interpretation: This verse describes the events of the Day of Judgment, when Hell will be presented before the people. On that day, the human being will remember and reflect on their actions in life, but this remembrance will be of no benefit to them at that point. The interpretation is that the opportunity to remember and repent has passed, and the consequences of one's deeds must now be faced.
orig: وجيء يومئذ بجهنم يومئذ يتذكر الإنسان وأنى له الذكرى

translation: He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent forth [some good] for my life."
interpretation: This verse refers to the regret that a person will feel on the Day of Judgment when they realize that they did not do enough good deeds during their lifetime. The person wishes they had prepared for the afterlife by performing righteous actions. This serves as a reminder to us to live our lives in a way that pleases God and benefits ourselves and others, so that we do not have to feel this deep regret on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: يقول يا ليتني قدمت لحياتي

translation: And that Day no one will punish [as severely] as His punishment.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when Allah will mete out punishment to the disbelievers and wrongdoers. The punishment on that Day will be unparalleled in its severity, as no one else can inflict such a punishment. This emphasizes the absolute authority and power of Allah, and the finality and inevitability of the reckoning on the Day of Judgment.
orig: فيومئذ لا يعذب عذابه أحد

translation: And no one can be trusted with his affair
interpretation: This verse suggests that one should not blindly trust or rely on others, as no one can be fully trusted with one's affairs. It emphasizes the importance of being cautious and self-reliant, as ultimately, one is responsible for their own decisions and actions.
orig: ولا يوثق وثاقه أحد

translation: O reassured soul
interpretation: This verse addresses the soul that has found peace and contentment through faith in God. It encourages the believer to remain steadfast in their trust and reliance on God, as this is the path to true inner tranquility and fulfillment.
orig: يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة

translation: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to return to God in a state of contentment and satisfaction. The interpretation suggests that the person has lived a life pleasing to God, and now is invited to return to their Lord, having earned His pleasure and approval. It signifies the end of one's earthly journey and the beginning of eternal bliss in the Hereafter.
orig: ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية

translation: So enter among My [righteous] servants
interpretation: This verse is an invitation from God to the righteous to enter into His service and join the company of His devoted servants. It suggests that those who have lived a life of faith, obedience, and good deeds will be welcomed into the fold of God's chosen people and granted the honor of being counted among His righteous servants. The verse emphasizes the importance of submitting to God's will and aligning one's actions with His divine guidance in order to attain this esteemed status.
orig: فادخلي في عبادي

translation: And enter My Paradise
interpretation: This verse is an invitation from God to the righteous believer to enter the eternal abode of Paradise. It signifies the reward and eternal bliss that awaits those who have lived a life of faith, obedience and good deeds. The verse emphasizes the grace and generosity of God in welcoming the believer into the blissful gardens of Paradise, which is the ultimate destination for the faithful.
orig: وادخلي جنتي

translation: I swear by this city [i.e., Makkah]
interpretation: This verse is an oath taken by God, swearing by the city of Makkah, which was the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad and the site of the Ka’bah, the most sacred place in Islam. The oath emphasizes the importance and sanctity of this city, and serves to draw attention to the message that follows in the subsequent verses.
orig: لا أقسم بهذا البلد

translation: And you are settled in this land
interpretation: This verse suggests that the person being addressed is established or settled in a particular land or place. The interpretation could be that the person has found a stable and permanent residence in this location, or that they have a strong connection and sense of belonging to this specific region or country.
orig: وأنت حل بهذا البلد

translation: And by the father and that which was born [of him]
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the father and his progeny. It suggests that the father and his offspring are worthy of respect and honor. The verse may be interpreted as a call to cherish and nurture familial relationships, as the father and his children are intrinsically linked and deserve to be valued.
orig: ووالد وما ولد

translation: We have certainly created man in hardship.
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that the human being is created in a state of difficulty, struggle, and trial. The word "hardship" ("kabad") suggests that life is not easy for humans, and that they face various challenges, burdens, and tribulations. This verse reminds us that the human experience is not one of constant ease and comfort, but rather a journey filled with obstacles and hardships that must be overcome. The Qur'an encourages believers to have patience, perseverance, and faith in the face of these difficulties, as they are part of the human condition and a test from God.
orig: لقد خلقنا الإنسان في كبد

translation: Does he think that no one has power over him?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the arrogant and self-conceited person who believes that they are beyond accountability and that no one has power over them. The interpretation suggests that such an attitude is misguided, as everyone is ultimately accountable to God and subject to His power and judgment.
orig: أيحسب أن لن يقدر عليه أحد

translation: He says, 'I have destroyed wealth in abundance.'
interpretation: This verse expresses the regret of a person who has squandered their wealth in an excessive and wasteful manner. The interpretation suggests that the person is lamenting the fact that they have lost their wealth through extravagance and lack of prudence. The verse serves as a cautionary tale, highlighting the importance of managing one"s resources responsibly and avoiding excessive spending.
orig: يقول أهلكت مالا لبدا

translation: Does he think that no one has seen him?
interpretation: This verse is asking a rhetorical question, implying that the person being referred to believes that no one has seen his actions or behavior. The implication is that this person is acting in a way that they think is hidden from others, but in reality, their actions are being observed and witnessed by Allah. The verse suggests that this person should be aware that their deeds are not hidden and that they will be held accountable for them.
orig: أيحسب أن لم يره أحد

translation: Have We not made for him two eyes?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the creation of man and the blessings bestowed upon him. The two eyes are a sign of Allah's power and wisdom, as they allow man to see the world around him and appreciate the beauty of Allah's creation. The verse suggests that the ability to see is a gift from Allah, and that we should use our eyes to reflect on the signs of Allah and to guide our actions in this life.
orig: ألم نجعل له عينين

translation: And a tongue and two lips
interpretation: This verse refers to the human faculty of speech, highlighting the physical components involved - the tongue and the two lips. The Qur'an emphasizes the importance of speech and communication, as it is a key aspect of the human experience and a means of conveying ideas, expressing emotions, and interacting with others. The mention of these anatomical features underscores the divine creation and the intentional design behind the human ability to speak and communicate.
orig: ولسانا وشفتين

translation: And We have shown him the two ways (of good and evil)
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has guided humanity to the two paths of good and evil, and it is up to each individual to choose which path to follow. The "two ways" refer to the path of righteousness and the path of sin or wrongdoing. This verse emphasizes the free will that Allah has bestowed upon humans, allowing them to make their own choices and be responsible for their actions.
orig: وهديناه النجدين

translation: But he has not broken through the difficult pass.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the difficulty of attaining spiritual growth and closeness to God. The "difficult pass" represents the challenges and obstacles that one must overcome in order to achieve this goal. The verse is encouraging the listener to persevere and not be deterred by the difficulty of the task at hand, as the ultimate reward of spiritual fulfillment is worth the effort.
orig: فلا اقتحم العقبة

translation: And what will make you know what is the obstacle?
interpretation: This verse poses a rhetorical question, inviting the listener to ponder the nature and significance of "the obstacle". The interpretation suggests that this "obstacle" refers to a challenging or difficult task that requires great effort and perseverance to overcome. The verse encourages the listener to reflect deeply on the nature of this obstacle, and to seek understanding of what it entails in order to successfully navigate it.
orig: وما أدراك ما العقبة

translation: To free a neck
interpretation: This verse is often interpreted as a call to free a slave or to help someone in need. It is seen as a moral and ethical imperative to assist those who are oppressed or in difficult circumstances, and to work towards their liberation and freedom. The "freeing of a neck" is a metaphorical reference to the act of emancipating someone from bondage or servitude.
orig: فك رقبة

translation: Or [the] feeding on a day of severe hunger
interpretation: This verse is referring to one of the ways to atone for breaking an oath, which is to feed the poor and needy. The phrase "a day of severe hunger" emphasizes the importance of providing sustenance to those who are in dire need, as this act of charity and compassion is seen as a means of seeking forgiveness and making amends for one's actions.
orig: أو إطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة

translation: An orphan who is of near kin
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of caring for and supporting orphans, especially those who are closely related to the caretaker. The term "ذا مقربة" implies that the orphan has a close familial connection, perhaps a nephew or niece, and thus deserves special attention and protection from their kin. The Qur'an often highlights the duty of Muslims to care for the vulnerable, including orphans, and this verse underscores that responsibility, particularly when the orphan is a close relative.
orig: يتيما ذا مقربة

translation: Or [feeding] a needy person in hardship
interpretation: This verse is referring to one of the righteous deeds that is pleasing to Allah. It encourages feeding a poor or needy person who is in a state of hardship and difficulty. The interpretation is that performing acts of charity and compassion towards those in need is a virtuous and praiseworthy act in the sight of Allah.
orig: أو مسكينا ذا متربة

translation: Then he was among those who believed and advised each other to patience and advised each other to mercy.
interpretation: This verse describes the transformation of a person who initially did not believe, but later became a believer. It highlights two important qualities that believers should possess - patience and mercy. The verse suggests that true believers not only have faith themselves, but also encourage and support one another in being patient and merciful. This is a testament to the strength of their faith and their commitment to upholding the teachings of Islam.
orig: ثم كان من الذين آمنوا وتواصوا بالصبر وتواصوا بالمرحمة

translation: Those are the companions of the right.
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous and blessed people who will be on the right side on the Day of Judgment, indicating their success and salvation. The "companions of the right" are those who have lived virtuous lives, followed the teachings of Islam, and will be rewarded with eternal bliss in the Hereafter.
orig: أولئك أصحاب الميمنة

translation: And those who disbelieve in Our verses - they are the companions of the Wretched Abode.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who reject and deny the signs and messages of Allah (God) as revealed in the Qur'an. They are described as "the companions of the Wretched Abode", which indicates that they will be destined for the hellfire or a place of eternal punishment in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the consequences of disbelief and rejecting the guidance provided by Allah through His revelations.
orig: والذين كفروا بآياتنا هم أصحاب المشأمة

translation: Upon them is a Fire, well-kindled.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment of those who disbelieve and reject the message of Islam. The "Fire, well-kindled" is a metaphor for the eternal torment and suffering that awaits them in the Hereafter. The intensity of the Fire is emphasized by the word "مؤصدة" which suggests that it is constantly stoked and maintained, leaving no chance of escape. This serves as a warning to those who turn away from the guidance of Allah and choose to live a life of disbelief and wrongdoing.
orig: عليهم نار مؤصدة

translation: By the sun and its brightness
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and significance of the sun, which is a prominent feature of the natural world. The sun"s brightness and warmth are essential for life on Earth, and this verse invites us to reflect on the Creator"s power and wisdom in creating such a magnificent celestial body.
orig: والشمس وضحاها

translation: And [by] the moon when it follows [the sun]
interpretation: This verse refers to the phases of the moon, which follow a regular pattern as it orbits the Earth. The moon"s phases, from new moon to full moon and back, are a sign of God"s power and the orderly workings of the universe. The verse encourages reflection on these natural phenomena as evidence of divine creation and wisdom.
orig: والقمر إذا تلاها

translation: And [by] the day when it reveals [the sun]
interpretation: This verse refers to the day when it becomes clear and bright, revealing the sun. It is a reminder of the constant cycle of day and night, and the regularity and order in the universe created by God. The day is a time of activity, clarity, and enlightenment, in contrast to the night which is a time of rest and introspection. This verse encourages us to reflect on the signs of God's power and wisdom in the natural world around us.
orig: والنهار إذا جلاها

translation: And the night when it covers her
interpretation: This verse refers to the night when it covers the earth with its darkness. The interpretation is that the night, with its tranquility and stillness, provides a sense of peace and serenity, allowing for contemplation and introspection. The night is a time when the hustle and bustle of the day subsides, and one can reflect on the deeper aspects of life and the universe.
orig: والليل إذا يغشاها

translation: By the sky and [what] constructed it
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the grandeur and majesty of the creation of the heavens. It invites us to reflect on the intricate design and perfect order of the celestial bodies, which point to the existence and power of the Creator. The interpretation suggests that we should contemplate the wonders of the universe and use them as a means to strengthen our faith and deepen our relationship with the Almighty.
orig: والسماء وما بناها

translation: And [by] the earth and what expanded it
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of the earth and its expansion. It suggests that the earth was created and then expanded, which is consistent with the scientific understanding of the formation and expansion of the universe. The interpretation is that the Qur'an points to the expansive nature of the earth, which is a testament to the power and wisdom of the Creator.
orig: والأرض وما طحاها

translation: And [by] the soul [as] and what proportioned it
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the human soul and its inherent nature. The soul is a creation of God, and it is endowed with the ability to be shaped and proportioned according to the individual's choices and actions. The interpretation suggests that the human being has the capacity to develop their soul and align it with the divine purpose, through their own free will and moral conduct.
orig: ونفس وما سواها

translation: And [its creator] inspired it [with discernment of] its wickedness and its righteousness
interpretation: This verse speaks of the human soul and its innate capacity for both good and evil. Allah has instilled within each person the ability to discern between right and wrong, virtue and vice. The choice to follow the path of righteousness or the path of wickedness lies within the individual. This verse emphasizes the responsibility we have to nurture our God-given potential for moral and spiritual growth.
orig: فألهمها فجورها وتقواها

translation: Certainly he succeeds who purifies it,
interpretation: This verse from Surah Ash-Shams (The Sun) refers to the success and prosperity of the one who purifies their soul and character. The act of "زكاها" (purifying it) implies a conscious effort to cleanse oneself from vices, sins, and negative traits, and instead cultivate virtues, good deeds, and a righteous character. The interpretation is that the person who undertakes this spiritual and moral purification will achieve true success, both in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: قد أفلح من زكاها

translation: And he has certainly failed who instills it [i.e., the soul] with corruption.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who corrupt their souls or lead others to corruption will ultimately fail and be deprived of success. It serves as a warning against engaging in immoral or unethical acts that can taint one's soul and lead to spiritual downfall.
orig: وقد خاب من دساها

translation: Thamud denied [the truth] through their transgression
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Thamud, an ancient Arabian tribe, who rejected the message of the prophet Salih and denied the signs of God due to their arrogance and excessive pride. The verse highlights how their rejection of the truth was a result of their own transgression and rebellion against the divine guidance.
orig: كذبت ثمود بطغواها

translation: When the most wretched of them arose
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the Prophet Salih and the people of Thamud. It describes the emergence of the most wicked and rebellious individual among the people, who then proceeded to hamstring the she-camel that was a sign and miracle from God. This act of defiance and destruction led to the ultimate destruction of the people of Thamud as a consequence of their rejection of the Prophet Salih and his message.
orig: إذ انبعث أشقاها

translation: And the Messenger of Allah said to them, "[This is] the she-camel of Allah, [so let her] drink."
interpretation: This verse refers to an incident in the life of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) where he was sent to the people of Thamud as a messenger of Allah. The people of Thamud were instructed by the Prophet to let a she-camel, which was a sign from Allah, drink from the water source. This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting the signs and miracles sent by Allah and obeying the commands of His messengers.
orig: فقال لهم رسول الله ناقة الله وسقياها

translation: But they denied him and hamstrung her, so their Lord brought down upon them destruction for their sin and leveled them [with their dwellings].
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the people of Prophet Salih who rejected his message and killed the she-camel that was a sign from God. As a result, God punished them by sending a severe destruction that leveled their homes and settlements. The interpretation is that those who defy the signs and messengers of God will face severe consequences for their sins and transgressions.
orig: فكذبوه فعقروها فدمدم عليهم ربهم بذنبهم فسواها

translation: And he does not fear its consequence.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the righteous individual does not fear the consequences of their actions, as they have faith in Allah and trust that their deeds will be judged fairly in the Hereafter. The person who lives according to the teachings of the Qur'an and follows the path of righteousness need not worry about the outcome of their actions, for they know that Allah is the Just and Merciful Judge.
orig: ولا يخاف عقباها

translation: And the night when it covers [with darkness]
interpretation: This verse refers to the night when it envelops the world with its darkness. It suggests the tranquility and calmness that comes with the night, as well as the need for rest and reflection during this time. The verse invites us to contemplate the wonders of the night and the role it plays in the natural cycle of day and night.
orig: والليل إذا يغشى

translation: And by the day when it appears in brightness
interpretation: This verse speaks of the day when it shines brightly, illuminating the world. It is a reminder of the power and grandeur of Allah's creation, and the cycle of day and night that He has established. The day's appearance in brightness is a sign of Allah's wisdom and the order in the universe, and a call for humans to reflect on the wonders of the divine creation.
orig: والنهار إذا تجلى

translation: And He created the male and female
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah (God) is the Creator of all things, including the male and female genders. It suggests that the distinction between the sexes is part of Allah's divine plan and wisdom. The verse highlights the fundamental equality of men and women, as they are both created by the same Creator.
orig: وما خلق الذكر والأنثى

translation: Indeed, your efforts are diverse.
interpretation: This verse suggests that people's efforts and pursuits in life are varied and diverse. Each individual has their own unique path, goals, and ways of seeking fulfillment. The verse highlights the diversity of human endeavors and the fact that there is no single, uniform way to live one's life. It encourages an appreciation for the multitude of ways in which people strive to find meaning and purpose.
orig: إن سعيكم لشتى

translation: As for he who gives and fears [Allah]
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are righteous and God-fearing. They are the ones who give charitably from their wealth, and they do so out of their reverence and obedience to Allah. This verse highlights the virtues of those who combine faith and good deeds, as they are the ones who will be successful in the Hereafter.
orig: فأما من أعطى واتقى

translation: And he believed in the best [reward].
interpretation: This verse refers to a righteous person who has faith in the promise of the best reward from Allah in the Hereafter. It suggests that this person has a strong belief in the goodness and justice of Allah, and that they are confident in receiving the most favorable outcome in the afterlife as a result of their righteous deeds and beliefs.
orig: وصدق بالحسنى

translation: And We will ease him towards ease.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah will make the path of righteousness and salvation easy for the one who believes and does good deeds. It indicates that with faith and righteous actions, the journey towards the Hereafter will be facilitated, and the individual will be guided towards the path of ease and prosperity.
orig: فسنيسره لليسرى

translation: And as for he who is stingy and self-sufficient
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are miserly and arrogant, thinking they are self-sufficient and do not need to rely on Allah or help others. The Qur'an condemns this attitude, as true faith requires humility, generosity, and dependence on God.
orig: وأما من بخل واستغنى

translation: And he denies the good
interpretation: This verse is referring to someone who rejects or denies the good that has been promised by Allah. It suggests that this person does not believe in the rewards and blessings that Allah has promised for those who do good deeds and live righteously. The interpretation is that this person is rejecting the concept of divine justice and the hereafter, and instead chooses to focus only on the material world and its pleasures.
orig: وكذب بالحسنى

translation: And We will ease him toward the easy [path].
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah will make things easy for the person who faces difficulties or hardships. The interpretation is that Allah will provide guidance and support to help the person overcome their challenges and find the right path, which is the easy path.
orig: فسنيسره للعسرى

translation: And his wealth will not avail him when he falls [into Destruction]
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that one's wealth and material possessions will not be able to save them from the consequences of their own actions or from the punishment they face on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that true success and salvation lie not in the accumulation of wealth, but in one's faith, good deeds, and righteous conduct.
orig: وما يغني عنه ماله إذا تردى

translation: Indeed, [the responsibility] is upon Us to guide
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that it is Allah's responsibility to guide people to the right path. It suggests that guidance comes from Allah, and that He is the source of true direction in life. The verse implies that people should turn to Allah and seek His guidance, as He is the one who can lead them to the straight path.
orig: إن علينا للهدى

translation: And indeed, for us is the Hereafter and the first [life].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Hereafter, or the life after death, is as real and important as the present, worldly life. It suggests that the believers should not only focus on the immediate, material concerns of this world, but also keep in mind the eternal life in the Hereafter, which is the ultimate destination for all human beings.
orig: وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى

translation: So I have warned you of a Fire which blazes
interpretation: This verse is warning people about the punishment of Hell, which is described as a blazing fire. The interpretation is that the Qur'an is warning people to avoid the eternal punishment of Hell by believing in God and following His commands.
orig: فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى

translation: None shall have to endure it but the most wretched
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment of Hell, which will only be experienced by the most wretched and sinful individuals. It suggests that those who have led righteous lives and avoided the path of wickedness will be spared from the torment of the Hellfire. The interpretation emphasizes that the punishment of the Hereafter is reserved for those who have persistently engaged in evil deeds and rejected the guidance of the Almighty.
orig: لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى

translation: The one who denied and turned away
interpretation: This verse refers to a person who rejected the truth of God's message and turned away from it. The interpretation is that such a person will be held accountable for their denial and rejection of faith.
orig: الذي كذب وتولى

translation: And the most righteous one will be averted from it.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, where the most righteous and God-fearing individuals will be spared from the punishment and torment that will befall the wicked. The verse emphasizes that those who have lived a life of piety, righteousness, and devotion to God will be protected and saved from the consequences of their sins on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: وسيجنبها الأتقى

translation: He who gives his wealth to purify himself
interpretation: This verse is referring to the act of giving charity and spending one's wealth in the way of God. The one who gives his wealth, not out of show or pride, but with the sincere intention of purifying his soul and seeking the pleasure of God, is the one who will be successful and attain spiritual growth and closeness to the Divine.
orig: الذي يؤتي ماله يتزكى

translation: And there is no one who has a favor to be requited
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that no one has any favors or good deeds that can be repaid by God. It suggests that all blessings and bounties come from God alone, and that we should be grateful to Him without expecting any reward or return. The verse highlights the idea that we should worship and serve God out of sincere devotion, not out of a desire for reciprocation or repayment.
orig: وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى

translation: Except as a desire for the Face of his Lord, the Most High
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the only motivation for a true believer should be the desire to please and attain the pleasure of Allah, the Highest and Most Exalted. It suggests that one's actions and intentions should be solely driven by the aim of seeking Allah's approval and nearness, without any worldly or selfish motives. The "Face of his Lord" refers to Allah's pleasure and acceptance, which should be the ultimate goal for a believer.
orig: إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى

translation: And He will be pleased with them
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who believe in God and do good deeds will be rewarded with God's pleasure and approval. The interpretation conveys the idea that the ultimate goal for believers should be to seek God's satisfaction and contentment, as this is the highest and most fulfilling outcome one can achieve.
orig: ولسوف يرضى

translation: By the morning brightness,
interpretation: This verse is referring to the morning time, which is a symbol of hope, new beginnings, and the start of a new day. The "morning brightness" is a metaphor for the light and guidance that comes with the dawn, both physically and spiritually. This verse encourages us to make the most of the opportunities and blessings that come with each new day.
orig: والضحى

translation: And by the night when it covers and conceals
interpretation: This verse refers to the night when it envelops the world in darkness, covering and concealing the earth. It is a reminder of the cycle of day and night, and the way in which the night can provide a sense of tranquility and rest. The interpretation suggests that the night, with its soothing and concealing qualities, is a sign of God's power and wisdom in creating the universe.
orig: والليل إذا سجى

translation: Your Lord has not abandoned you, nor has He become displeased.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that his Lord has not forsaken him nor become displeased with him. It is a message of comfort and reassurance, reminding the Prophet that Allah is with him and has not abandoned him, even during times of difficulty or trial. The interpretation suggests that the Prophet should not feel alone or that Allah has turned away from him, but rather that the divine support and guidance remain constant.
orig: ما ودعك ربك وما قلى

translation: And the Hereafter is better for you than the first [life].
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to focus on the Hereafter, which is eternal and better than the temporary life of this world. The Hereafter represents the true and lasting success, compared to the fleeting pleasures and trials of this life. The interpretation suggests that the believer should prioritize the Hereafter and work towards achieving eternal bliss in the Afterlife, rather than being solely consumed by the pursuits of this world.
orig: وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى

translation: And your Lord will give you, and you will be satisfied.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God will bestow upon the believer all that they desire, and they will be content and pleased with what they receive. It implies that those who put their trust in God and follow His guidance will be rewarded with fulfillment and satisfaction, both in this life and the hereafter.
orig: ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى

translation: Did He not find you an orphan and give [you] refuge?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and how Allah guided him and provided for him, even when he was an orphan. The interpretation is that Allah takes care of those who are in need, and that He will guide and protect those who put their trust in Him, even in the most difficult of circumstances.
orig: ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى

translation: And He found you lost and guided [you]
interpretation: This verse refers to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and how Allah guided him from being lost and misguided to being rightly guided. It is a testament to Allah's mercy and guidance, as He took the Prophet from a state of ignorance and led him to the path of truth and enlightenment. This verse highlights the transformative power of Allah's guidance and the importance of seeking it in one's life.
orig: ووجدك ضالا فهدى

translation: And He found you poor and made [you] self-sufficient.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Muhammad's life and how Allah provided for him and made him self-sufficient. It signifies that Allah takes care of those who are in need and elevates them, just as He did for the Prophet Muhammad. The interpretation is that Allah can transform one's circumstances from poverty to wealth and self-sufficiency, which is a testament to His power and mercy.
orig: ووجدك عائلا فأغنى

translation: As for the orphan, do not oppress [him]
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to treat orphans with kindness and compassion, and not to exploit or mistreat them. The orphan, who has lost one or both parents, is to be protected and cared for by the community. This verse emphasizes the importance of safeguarding the rights and well-being of the vulnerable in society.
orig: فأما اليتيم فلا تقهر

translation: And as for the petitioner, do not repel [him]
interpretation: This verse encourages kindness and compassion towards those who seek help or request something. It advises against turning them away or being harsh with them, but rather to treat them with gentleness and understanding. The interpretation suggests that one should be patient and welcoming towards those who come to you with a need, and not dismiss or rebuke them.
orig: وأما السائل فلا تنهر

translation: And as for the favor of your Lord, report [it].
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to express gratitude and appreciation for the blessings and favors bestowed upon them by God. It is a call to acknowledge and speak about the grace, mercy, and bounties that one has received from the Almighty. The believer should not be silent about the favors of their Lord, but rather proclaim and share them with others, as a way of showing thankfulness and glorifying God.
orig: وأما بنعمة ربك فحدث

translation: Did We not expand for you, [O Muhammad], your breast?
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad and asking if God has not expanded his chest, or his heart and mind, to receive and bear the weight of the message of Islam. The expansion of the Prophet's chest is a metaphor for the spiritual and intellectual enlightenment he received, which prepared him to receive and convey the divine revelation. This verse is a reassurance to the Prophet that he has been chosen and equipped by God to fulfill his role as the final messenger.
orig: ألم نشرح لك صدرك

translation: And We have removed from you your burden
interpretation: This verse is referring to the removal of the burden or sin from the Prophet Muhammad. It suggests that Allah has forgiven him and relieved him of the weight of his past mistakes or transgressions. The interpretation is that through Allah's grace and mercy, the Prophet's soul has been purified and he has been freed from the burden of sin.
orig: ووضعنا عنك وزرك

translation: The One Who has eased for you [your task]
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah, the Almighty, who has made your life and responsibilities easier for you. It suggests that Allah has relieved you of burdens and difficulties, and has provided you with the means and strength to carry out your duties. The interpretation implies that Allah is the One who supports and guides you, making your path smoother and more manageable.
orig: الذي أنقض ظهرك

translation: And We have raised for you your repute.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance from God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that his status and reputation have been elevated. It signifies that the Prophet's name and teachings will be remembered and revered for all time, and that his legacy will continue to inspire and guide humanity. This verse is a testament to the Prophet's profound impact and the enduring nature of his message.
orig: ورفعنا لك ذكرك

translation: For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.
interpretation: This verse conveys the message that every difficulty or hardship is accompanied by ease and relief. It suggests that no matter how challenging a situation may be, there is always a way out and a path towards resolution. This verse encourages believers to have faith and perseverance, as Allah will provide relief and ease even in the midst of hardship.
orig: فإن مع العسر يسرا

translation: Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.
interpretation: This verse conveys the message that even in the face of difficulty and hardship, there will be ease and relief. It suggests that no matter how challenging a situation may be, Allah (God) will provide a way out and make things easier for the believer. This verse encourages patience, perseverance, and trust in Allah during times of adversity, as the ultimate outcome will be one of comfort and ease.
orig: إن مع العسر يسرا

translation: So when you have finished [your duties], then stand up [for worship].
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to complete their tasks and duties, and then to devote themselves to worship and remembrance of God. It suggests that one should not become too engrossed in worldly affairs, but rather balance them with spiritual contemplation and connection with the divine.
orig: فإذا فرغت فانصب

translation: And to your Lord be your inclination.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to turn to Allah (God) with sincerity, devotion, and a desire to please Him. It suggests that one should focus on Allah as the ultimate source of guidance, provision, and fulfillment, rather than seeking satisfaction elsewhere. The interpretation is that the believer should aspire to have a strong connection with Allah, directing their hopes, prayers, and actions towards Him.
orig: وإلى ربك فارغب

translation: By the fig and the olive
interpretation: This verse is an oath taken by God, swearing by the fig and the olive. The fig and olive are believed to be symbolic of prosperity, abundance, and nourishment. The interpretation is that God is emphasizing the importance and significance of these two fruits, which have great value and benefits for humanity. This oath serves to draw attention to the divine message that follows, and to underscore its importance and truthfulness.
orig: والتين والزيتون

translation: By the Mount Sinai
interpretation: This verse refers to the sacred Mount Sinai, where Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) received the Ten Commandments from Allah. It is a place of great significance in Islamic tradition, as it represents the divine revelation and the establishment of a covenant between God and His people. The verse invokes this holy mountain as a symbol of the profound spiritual connection between the Creator and His creation.
orig: وطور سينين

translation: And this is the secure city
interpretation: This verse refers to the city of Mecca, which was considered a sacred and secure place in the time of the Prophet Muhammad. The term "البلد الأمين" (al-balad al-amin) emphasizes the sanctity and inviolability of Mecca, where the Kaaba, the most sacred site in Islam, is located. The interpretation suggests that Mecca was a place of safety and protection, where people could seek refuge and practice their faith without fear of harm or persecution.
orig: وهذا البلد الأمين

translation: Indeed, We have created man in the best of stature
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has created human beings in the best and most perfect form. It suggests that the human being is the pinnacle of Allah's creation, endowed with the most excellent physical, mental, and spiritual faculties. This highlights the inherent dignity and worth of the human being, and calls upon us to recognize and appreciate the blessings bestowed upon us by the Creator.
orig: لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم

translation: Then We return him to the lowest of the low
interpretation: This verse suggests that after a person's life on Earth, they will be returned to the lowest and most degraded state, which is often interpreted as a reference to the afterlife and the punishment for those who have lived a life of sin and disbelief. The "lowest of the low" is understood to mean the lowest level of Hell, where the most wicked and unrepentant souls will be consigned.
orig: ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين

translation: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the only ones who will be saved from eternal punishment are those who have true faith in God and do good deeds. Their reward in the Hereafter will be continuous and uninterrupted, as opposed to the punishment of the disbelievers which will be eternal. This verse encourages believers to maintain their faith and do righteous acts, as this is the only way to attain God's pleasure and eternal bliss.
orig: إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فلهم أجر غير ممنون

translation: And what will make you know [the nature of] the Recompense?
interpretation: This verse is asking what will make you know or understand the nature of the Day of Judgment and the final reckoning. It is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the importance and gravity of the Hereafter, which people often deny or ignore. The interpretation is that one should take the concept of the Hereafter and final accountability seriously, as it is a fundamental aspect of the religion of Islam.
orig: فما يكذبك بعد بالدين

translation: Is not Allah the wisest of judges?
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the wisdom and justice of Allah as the ultimate Judge. It suggests that Allah, being the All-Wise, makes decisions and judgments that are perfectly fair and just, far surpassing the wisdom and judgment of any human being. The verse is a rhetorical question that affirms Allah's supreme authority and unparalleled wisdom in all matters.
orig: أليس الله بأحكم الحاكمين

translation: Read in the name of your Lord who created
interpretation: This verse encourages the reader to begin any task or endeavor in the name of God, the Creator of all things. It emphasizes the importance of acknowledging God's sovereignty and seeking His guidance and blessings before undertaking any action. The verse also implies that true knowledge and understanding can only be attained through the remembrance of God and seeking His wisdom.
orig: اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق

translation: He created the human being from a clinging substance.
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of the human being from a clinging substance, which is a scientific description of the embryonic stage of human development. The interpretation suggests that Allah, the Creator, has designed the process of human creation with precision and detail, and that the Qur'an provides insights into the natural world that are consistent with scientific understanding.
orig: خلق الإنسان من علق

translation: Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous
interpretation: This verse encourages the reader to seek knowledge and engage in the act of reading, as it is a path to gaining wisdom and understanding. The reference to "your Lord" emphasizes that the ultimate source of this generosity and guidance is God, the Most Generous, who provides us with the means and the ability to learn and grow. The verse suggests that by reading and seeking knowledge, one can draw closer to the divine and attain a higher level of spiritual and intellectual enlightenment.
orig: اقرأ وربك الأكرم

translation: The One who taught by the pen
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah, the Almighty, who has taught humanity the skill of writing and recording knowledge through the use of the pen. The pen is a symbol of knowledge, education, and the preservation of information. This verse emphasizes the importance of learning, literacy, and the acquisition of knowledge, which are essential for the advancement of human civilization. It also highlights Allah's role as the ultimate source of all knowledge and the One who has endowed humanity with the capacity to learn, discover, and create.
orig: الذي علم بالقلم

translation: He taught man that which he knew not.
interpretation: This verse highlights the remarkable capacity of the human being to acquire knowledge. It suggests that the Almighty Creator has endowed man with the ability to learn and understand things that were previously unknown to him. This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge, as it is a means for human beings to expand their understanding of the world around them and to grow intellectually and spiritually. It encourages the pursuit of education and the constant acquisition of new knowledge, which can lead to personal and societal progress.
orig: علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم

translation: Nay, indeed, man does transgress [all bounds]
interpretation: This verse is a warning against the tendency of humans to overstep their limits and engage in arrogance, pride, and oppression. It emphasizes that mankind is prone to transgression and excess, and must be mindful of their actions and stay within the bounds of morality and righteousness. The verse serves as a reminder to humans to humble themselves, seek guidance, and avoid falling into the trap of self-aggrandizement and unrestrained desires.
orig: كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى

translation: That he sees himself as self-sufficient
interpretation: This verse refers to the tendency of some people to become arrogant and self-absorbed when they perceive themselves as wealthy or successful. The verse suggests that such an attitude can lead to a detachment from the realities of life and a lack of gratitude towards God. The interpretation is that one should not become complacent or self-satisfied, but rather remain humble and appreciative of the blessings bestowed upon them.
orig: أن رآه استغنى

translation: Indeed, to your Lord is the ultimate return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all people will ultimately return to God, their Creator, on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder that our actions and choices in this life will be held accountable before God, and that we should strive to live righteously in preparation for the final reckoning.
orig: إن إلى ربك الرجعى

translation: Have you seen the one who forbids
interpretation: This verse is referring to a person who forbids or prevents others from doing something. The interpretation is that this verse is calling on the reader to reflect on the actions of someone who tries to stop or hinder others, and to consider the motivations and consequences of such behavior.
orig: أرأيت الذي ينهى

translation: A servant when he prays
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prayer and the reverence with which a servant should approach it. When a person prays, they should do so with humility, sincerity, and a deep awareness of their relationship with the Divine. The verse suggests that the act of prayer should be carried out with the utmost respect and devotion, as it represents a direct communication between the servant and their Creator.
orig: عبدا إذا صلى

translation: Have you seen if he is upon guidance
interpretation: This verse is asking the reader to consider the situation of someone who is following the right path and guidance. The implication is that if someone is on the right path, then they should be respected and their actions should be judged accordingly. The verse encourages the reader to reflect on the guidance and righteous conduct of others, rather than making hasty judgments.
orig: أرأيت إن كان على الهدى

translation: Or [he] instructs to righteousness
interpretation: This verse suggests that a righteous person is one who instructs others to be God-conscious and to live a virtuous life. The emphasis is on the importance of guiding others towards righteousness, which is a praiseworthy quality. The interpretation is that a true believer should not only strive for their own spiritual development but also actively encourage and support others in their journey towards righteousness and devotion to God.
orig: أو أمر بالتقوى

translation: Have you seen if he denies and turns away?
interpretation: This verse is asking the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to consider the case of someone who rejects the message of Islam and turns away from it. The implication is that such a person will be held accountable for their rejection and will face the consequences of their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: أرأيت إن كذب وتولى

translation: Does he not know that Allah sees?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the fact that Allah is all-knowing and all-seeing. It is a reminder that Allah is aware of everything, including the thoughts, actions, and intentions of human beings. The implication is that one should be conscious of Allah's presence and act accordingly, since He is witness to all that we do.
orig: ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى

translation: No! If he does not desist, We will surely drag [him] by the forelock
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to those who persist in their disbelief and wrongdoing. It suggests that if a person does not heed the call to repentance and reform, they will face severe consequences. The "dragging by the forelock" is a metaphor for the humiliation and punishment that will befall them. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of heeding the guidance of the Qur'an and turning away from sinful behavior, lest one face the wrath of Allah.
orig: كلا لئن لم ينته لنسفعا بالناصية

translation: A lying, sinful forelock
interpretation: This verse is referring to a person who is deceitful and sinful. The "lying, sinful forelock" is a metaphor for the person's character, suggesting that their outward appearance and behavior are not a true reflection of their inner nature. The Qur'an is warning against such individuals who try to deceive others through their words and actions.
orig: ناصية كاذبة خاطئة

translation: Then let him call his council (of associates)
interpretation: This verse encourages the person who is being challenged or opposed to gather his supporters and allies to help him in his cause. It suggests that seeking help and counsel from one's social network and community can be an effective way to address difficulties or opposition.
orig: فليدع ناديه

translation: We will call the keepers of Hell
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when Allah will summon the angels responsible for guarding and punishing the inhabitants of Hell. It suggests that on that day, the wicked will be held accountable for their misdeeds and face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.
orig: سندع الزبانية

translation: No! Do not obey him, and prostrate and draw near [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to not obey the one who calls you to disobedience, but rather to prostrate in worship and draw closer to Allah. It is a reminder to prioritize one's relationship with the Creator over any worldly temptations or influences. The interpretation encourages the believer to resist the urge to submit to the demands of the one who seeks to lead them astray, and instead focus on submitting to Allah through acts of devotion and drawing nearer to Him.
orig: كلا لا تطعه واسجد واقترب

translation: Indeed, We sent it [i.e., the Qur'an] down during the Night of Decree.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), during which the Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The Night of Decree is considered one of the most important nights in the Islamic calendar, as it marks the beginning of the revelation of the Qur'an, which is the divine guidance and source of wisdom for Muslims. This night is believed to be blessed, and Muslims are encouraged to engage in extra acts of worship and reflection during this time.
orig: إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر

translation: And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and mystery of the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr). It poses a rhetorical question, implying that the true nature and significance of this night are beyond human comprehension. The verse encourages reflection on the profound spiritual significance of this night, which is considered one of the holiest nights in the Islamic calendar.
orig: وما أدراك ما ليلة القدر

translation: The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), which is considered one of the most sacred nights in the Islamic calendar. It is believed that on this night, the first verses of the Qur'an were revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse emphasizes the immense value and significance of this night, stating that it is "better than a thousand months" - meaning that the rewards and blessings of worshiping and seeking forgiveness on this night are far greater than a lifetime of worship during regular months. This highlights the importance of seeking closeness to Allah and engaging in spiritual practices during this blessed time.
orig: ليلة القدر خير من ألف شهر

translation: The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter.
interpretation: This verse describes the descent of the angels and the Spirit (Gabriel) upon the earth, with the permission of Allah, to carry out His commands and decrees. It suggests the constant communication and interaction between the heavenly and earthly realms, with the angels and the Spirit serving as intermediaries between God and His creation. The verse emphasizes the divine authority and control over all matters, as nothing happens without Allah's permission.
orig: تنزل الملائكة والروح فيها بإذن ربهم من كل أمر

translation: Until the break of dawn
interpretation: This verse is referring to the time period during which fasting is observed in Islam. Muslims are required to refrain from eating, drinking, and sexual relations from dawn until sunset during the month of Ramadan. The phrase "until the break of dawn" signifies the end of the night and the beginning of the new day, when fasting commences.
orig: سلام هي حتى مطلع الفجر

translation: Those who disbelieve from among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not [to be] separated [from disbelief] until there had come to them clear evidence.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the disbelievers, whether from among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) or the polytheists, were not going to abandon their disbelief until they were presented with clear and undeniable proof of the truth of Islam. It suggests that faith is not something that can be forced upon people, but rather it requires sincere conviction based on evidence and understanding.
orig: لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين حتى تأتيهم البينة
