translation: A messenger from Allah, reciting purified scriptures
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Muhammad, who was sent by Allah to recite and convey the purified scriptures of the Qur'an to humanity. The Qur'an is described as "purified" to emphasize its divine origin, purity, and freedom from any human alteration or corruption. The role of the Prophet Muhammad is to faithfully deliver this divine message to guide and enlighten people.
orig: رسول من الله يتلو صحفا مطهرة

translation: Therein are Valuable Writings
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an, which is described as containing "Valuable Writings". This suggests that the Qur'an is a source of profound wisdom, guidance, and teachings that are of immense value to humanity. The Qur'an is not merely a collection of stories or rules, but a comprehensive scripture that provides insights into the nature of God, the purpose of human existence, and the path to spiritual and moral fulfillment. The "Valuable Writings" in the Qur'an are seen as a precious gift from the Divine, offering invaluable guidance and wisdom to those who seek it.
orig: فيها كتب قيمة

translation: And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided until after there had come to them clear evidence.
interpretation: This verse refers to the divisions and disagreements that arose among the followers of the previous revealed scriptures, such as the Jews and Christians, after clear evidence and guidance had come to them. The implication is that unity and agreement should have prevailed, but instead they allowed differences and disputes to emerge, often for selfish or worldly reasons rather than adhering to the truth. The Qur'an calls for unity and adherence to the guidance provided, rather than falling into disunity and disputation.
orig: وما تفرق الذين أوتوا الكتاب إلا من بعد ما جاءتهم البينة

translation: And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and to establish prayer and to give zakah. And that is the correct religion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental purpose of human existence, which is to worship Allah alone with sincerity and devotion. It highlights the core tenets of Islam: belief in the oneness of God, performing the obligatory prayers, and paying the mandatory charity (zakah). The verse also affirms that this is the true and upright religion, in contrast to any other belief system or way of life. The message is clear - the ultimate goal of a Muslim is to live a life dedicated to the worship and service of the Almighty, while fulfilling the religious duties and obligations prescribed by Him.
orig: وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين حنفاء ويقيموا الصلاة ويؤتوا الزكاة وذلك دين القيمة

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve from among the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the Fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. Those are the worst of creatures.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith, whether they are from the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) or polytheists, will be condemned to the eternal punishment of Hell. They are described as the "worst of creatures" due to their stubborn rejection of the truth and their unwillingness to submit to the divine guidance. This serves as a stern warning to those who persist in their disbelief and highlights the grave consequences of turning away from the path of righteousness.
orig: إن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين في نار جهنم خالدين فيها أولئك هم شر البرية

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - those are the best of creatures.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the true believers, those who have faith in God and do good deeds, are the best of all created beings. They are superior to all others because of their spiritual and moral excellence. This highlights the importance of both faith and righteous actions, as they go hand-in-hand in determining one's worth and status in the sight of God.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك هم خير البرية

translation: For them will be Gardens of Eternity beneath which rivers flow. They will abide therein forever. Allah will be pleased with them, and they with Him. That is for whoever has feared his Lord.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward in the Hereafter for those who have feared and obeyed Allah. They will be granted eternal abode in the Gardens of Paradise, where they will live forever in peace and contentment. Allah will be pleased with them, and they will be pleased with Him. This is the ultimate reward for those who have been conscious of their Lord and lived righteously.
orig: جزاؤهم عند ربهم جنات عدن تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه ذلك لمن خشي ربه

translation: When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Resurrection, when the earth will be shaken violently and dramatically, signaling the end of the world as we know it. The interpretation is that this shaking of the earth is a sign of the coming of the Day of Judgment, when all people will be held accountable for their actions and the world as we know it will come to an end.
orig: إذا زلزلت الأرض زلزالها

translation: And the earth has cast out its contents
interpretation: This verse refers to the earth disgorging or expelling its contents, which can be interpreted as the earth revealing or exposing what it has been concealing, such as buried treasures, ancient ruins, or the remains of past civilizations. This can symbolize the uncovering of hidden knowledge, the unearthing of long-forgotten histories, or the emergence of truths that have been buried and suppressed. The verse suggests a sense of revelation, of the earth unveiling its secrets and disclosing what has been hidden from view.
orig: وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها

translation: And the human says, "What is [wrong] with her?"
interpretation: This verse expresses the human tendency to be impatient and to question the wisdom behind Allah's decrees. It suggests that sometimes, humans may be quick to judge or complain about the circumstances they find themselves in, without understanding the deeper purpose or reasoning behind them. The interpretation encourages us to have faith in Allah's plan and to approach life's challenges with humility, patience and trust in the divine wisdom.
orig: وقال الإنسان ما لها

translation: That Day, it will report its news.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when the earth will bear witness to all that happened upon it. The "news" or "information" of the earth will be revealed, and nothing will be hidden. This suggests that on that Day, all of our deeds, both good and bad, will be made known and we will be held accountable for them.
orig: يومئذ تحدث أخبارها

translation: That your Lord inspired [to the bee]
interpretation: This verse indicates that God has inspired the bees with the knowledge and instinct to build their hives, produce honey, and carry out their various tasks. It suggests that the remarkable abilities of bees are not due to chance or evolution alone, but are a result of the divine guidance and inspiration bestowed upon them by the Creator.
orig: بأن ربك أوحى لها

translation: That Day, the people will depart separated [into categories] to be shown [the result of] their deeds.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when people will be divided into different groups based on their actions and beliefs in this life. They will be presented with the consequences of their deeds, whether good or bad, so that they can see the results of how they lived their lives. This emphasizes the importance of living righteously and doing good in this world, as we will all be held accountable for our actions on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا ليروا أعمالهم

translation: So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that even the smallest good deed will be acknowledged and rewarded by God. It encourages people to do good, no matter how small, as it will not go unnoticed. The interpretation is that even the smallest act of kindness, charity, or righteousness will be recognized and rewarded by God in the Hereafter. This verse serves as a motivator for people to strive to do good deeds, no matter how insignificant they may seem.
orig: فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره

translation: And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of one's actions, no matter how small. It conveys the idea that even the slightest wrongdoing will not go unnoticed and will have consequences. The message is that individuals are accountable for their actions, and they will be held responsible for even the smallest transgressions. This serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's behavior and to strive to do good, as even the smallest deeds can have a significant impact.
orig: ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the racers, panting,
interpretation: This verse, known as the opening of Surah Al-'Adiyat, takes an oath by the charging war horses. The interpretation suggests that the verse is emphasizing the importance of being steadfast, determined, and unwavering in the face of challenges, just as the war horses charge into battle with unwavering resolve.
orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم والعاديات ضبحا

translation: And [by] the racers panting
interpretation: This verse refers to the horses or camels that race swiftly, their hooves striking the ground and creating sparks. The imagery evokes a sense of power, speed, and determination, which can be seen as symbolic of the strength and steadfastness of the believers in their pursuit of righteousness and their struggle against the forces of evil.
orig: فالموريات قدحا

translation: And [by] the dawn-breakers
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels or other celestial beings that bring about the dawn, signifying the start of a new day. The interpretation is that these dawn-breaking forces are a sign of God's power and the regularity of the natural world, which point to the existence and wisdom of the Divine.
orig: فالمغيرات صبحا

translation: And they raise thereby much dust
interpretation: This verse is describing a scene of battle, where the horses or vehicles raise up a cloud of dust as they move. The dust being raised is a metaphor for the chaos and turmoil of war. The interpretation is that this verse is highlighting the disruptive and unsettling nature of conflict, where the normal order of things is disrupted and obscured by the violence and upheaval.
orig: فأثرن به نقعا

translation: And they all came to him together
interpretation: This verse refers to a group of people coming together to see or approach someone. The interpretation suggests that a collective or unified action is taking place, where multiple individuals come together for a common purpose or to engage with a particular person or entity.
orig: فوسطن به جمعا

translation: Indeed, mankind is ungrateful to his Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the tendency of humans to be ungrateful and unappreciative of the blessings and favors bestowed upon them by their Creator. It serves as a reminder that we should be thankful and acknowledge the countless gifts and opportunities we have been granted, rather than taking them for granted or even denying them. The verse encourages us to cultivate a grateful heart and to express our gratitude to Allah (God) through our words and actions.
orig: إن الإنسان لربه لكنود

translation: And indeed, he is a witness over that
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a witness over the truth of the message of Islam. The Qur'an is a witness to the truth of God's oneness and the guidance it provides, and the Prophet Muhammad is a witness who testifies to the divine origin of the Qur'an and the validity of its teachings. This verse emphasizes the credibility and trustworthiness of the Qur'an and the Prophet as authoritative sources of guidance for humanity.
orig: وإنه على ذلك لشهيد

translation: And indeed, he is in love with wealth to an extreme.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the love of wealth and material possessions can be an extreme and excessive desire in some individuals. It cautions against being overly attached to the accumulation of wealth, as this can lead to a neglect of more important spiritual and moral values. The interpretation encourages a more balanced approach to wealth, where it is seen as a means to an end rather than an end in itself.
orig: وإنه لحب الخير لشديد

translation: Does he not know when that which is in the graves is scattered?
interpretation: This verse is asking whether the disbeliever does not realize that when the Day of Resurrection comes, the contents of the graves will be scattered and the dead will be resurrected. It is a reminder that everything is known to God and that the Day of Judgment is inevitable, when all people will be held accountable for their actions in life.
orig: أفلا يعلم إذا بعثر ما في القبور

translation: And [all] that is within the breasts has been disclosed.
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, all that people have kept hidden in their hearts and minds will be revealed. Nothing will remain concealed, and all secrets and intentions will be made known. This emphasizes the idea of accountability and the fact that we cannot hide anything from God, who is All-Knowing.
orig: وحصل ما في الصدور

translation: Indeed, their Lord with them, that Day, is [fully] Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, Allah, the Lord of all creation, is fully aware of and knowledgeable about the deeds and intentions of every individual. He is not unaware of anything, and will judge each person with perfect justice and wisdom based on their actions in this world.
orig: إن ربهم بهم يومئذ لخبير

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. The Striking Calamity
interpretation: This verse introduces the chapter known as 'Al-Qari\'ah' or 'The Striking Calamity'. The interpretation of this verse is that it calls attention to a momentous, earth-shattering event that will occur, which will have a profound impact on all of humanity. This event is referred to as 'The Striking Calamity', which signifies its tremendous and overwhelming nature. The verse emphasizes the attributes of Allah as the Entirely Merciful and the Especially Merciful, indicating that even in the face of this calamity, His mercy and compassion will still be present
orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم القارعة

translation: What is the Striking Event?
interpretation: The Qur'anic verse "What is the Striking Event?" (al-Qari'ah 101:1) refers to the Day of Judgment, which is a momentous and earth-shattering event that will occur in the future. This verse serves as a wake-up call, urging people to reflect on the inevitability of this momentous day and to prepare for it by living a righteous life. The "Striking Event" is a metaphor for the overwhelming and cataclysmic nature of the Day of Judgment, which will shake the foundations of the entire universe and bring about a profound transformation in the lives of all human beings.
orig: ما القارعة

translation: And what can make you know what is the Striking Calamity?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, also known as the "Striking Calamity" or "al-Qari'ah". It is emphasizing the immense magnitude and gravity of this event, asking the rhetorical question "And what can make you know what is the Striking Calamity?". This is to underscore the incomprehensible nature of the Day of Judgment, which will be a tremendous and earth-shattering occurrence that will shake the very foundations of existence. The verse is meant to instill a sense of awe and reverence in the listener, and to prompt them to reflect on the importance of preparing for this momentous day.
orig: وما أدراك ما القارعة

translation: The Day when the people will be like scattered moths
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all of humanity will be gathered and scattered like moths, disoriented and without purpose or direction. It suggests the fragility and insignificance of people in the face of the overwhelming power and majesty of God on that momentous day.
orig: يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث

translation: And the mountains will be as tufts of wool [that have been fluffed up].
interpretation: This verse is describing the Day of Judgment, when the mountains will be uprooted and scattered like tufts of wool that have been fluffed up. This imagery conveys the immense power and upheaval that will occur on that momentous day, as the very foundations of the earth are shaken. The comparison to wool highlights the lightness and ease with which the mountains will be transformed, emphasizing the absolute authority and control of God over all creation.
orig: وتكون الجبال كالعهن المنفوش

translation: And as for one whose scales are heavy [with good deeds]
interpretation: This verse refers to those whose good deeds outweigh their bad deeds on the Day of Judgment. Their scales will be heavy with the weight of their righteous actions, indicating that they will be successful and enter Paradise.
orig: فأما من ثقلت موازينه

translation: Then he will be in a pleasant life.
interpretation: This verse refers to the state of the righteous believer in the afterlife. The phrase "في عيشة راضية" (fee 'eeshatin radhiyyah) translates to "in a pleasant life", indicating that the righteous will be granted a blissful and satisfying existence in the hereafter. This interpretation suggests that the reward for those who believe and do good deeds is a life of contentment, peace, and fulfillment in the Afterlife.
orig: فهو في عيشة راضية

translation: And as for one whose scales are light,
interpretation: This verse refers to those whose good deeds are outweighed by their bad deeds on the Day of Judgment. Their scales will be light, indicating that their righteous actions were insufficient to outweigh their sins. This implies that they will face punishment and consequences for their misdeeds in the Hereafter.
orig: وأما من خفت موازينه

translation: And his mother will be [in] Hawiyah.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fate of a disbeliever in the afterlife. "His mother will be [in] Hawiyah" suggests that the disbeliever's mother will be in the depths of Hell, a place of severe punishment and torment for those who rejected faith and lived a life of sin. The verse emphasizes the consequences of disbelief and the importance of following the guidance of the Quran to avoid such a fate.
orig: فأمه هاوية

translation: And what can make you know what [i.e., who] it is?
interpretation: This verse is expressing the greatness and grandeur of the subject being referred to, which is not specified. It is conveying a sense of awe and mystery, suggesting that the true nature of this thing is beyond human comprehension. The implication is that it is something of immense importance and significance, the full extent of which is unknown to us.
orig: وما أدراك ما هيه

translation: A Blazing Fire
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment of Hell, which is described as a "blazing fire". The interpretation is that those who reject faith and commit sins will be subjected to the torment of the Hellfire, which is a severe and unrelenting punishment.;نار حامية

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Wealth and children have diverted you.
interpretation: This verse warns against being preoccupied with the pursuit of wealth and material possessions, as well as being distracted by one's children, to the point that it diverts one from the remembrance of Allah and the hereafter. The true purpose of life is not the accumulation of wealth or the raising of children, but rather the worship and remembrance of the Almighty. This verse encourages believers to prioritize their spiritual well-being over worldly matters and to not let the desire for more wealth or the care of one's family distract them from their ultimate purpose.
orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ألهاكم التكاثر

translation: Until you visit the graves
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the inevitability of death and the importance of preparing for the afterlife. It encourages people to reflect on their mortality and the transient nature of this world by visiting the graves, where the remains of those who have passed away are laid to rest. The verse serves as a call to action, urging individuals to use the reminder of death as a motivation to live a righteous life and seek the pleasure of God.
orig: حتى زرتم المقابر

translation: Nay, you shall soon know,
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to those who deny the truth and disbelieve in the Resurrection and the Hereafter. It suggests that they will soon come to know the consequences of their actions, either in this life or in the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the disbelievers, as they will ultimately be held accountable for their choices.
orig: كلا سوف تعلمون

translation: Then no! You are going to know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and a promise of future knowledge. It suggests that those who deny or disbelieve will eventually come to understand the truth, either in this life or the Hereafter. The emphasis on "then no!" implies a rejection of the previous statement or claim, and the following "you are going to know" suggests that the truth will become apparent, regardless of one's current beliefs or actions.
orig: ثم كلا سوف تعلمون

translation: No! If you only knew with certainty [the truth].
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who deny the truth of the Hereafter and the Day of Judgment. It suggests that if they truly understood the reality and certainty of the Hereafter, they would not be so heedless and would instead strive to prepare for it. The verse is meant to awaken them to the gravity of their situation and the importance of believing in and acting upon the truth.
orig: كلا لو تعلمون علم اليقين

translation: You will surely see the Hellfire
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to mankind about the reality of the Hellfire, which is the eternal abode of those who reject faith and commit grave sins. The verse emphasizes the certainty of seeing the Hellfire, implying that it is an inescapable reality that everyone will witness, either in this life through the eyes of faith or in the Hereafter through direct observation. This serves as a powerful reminder to believers to strive for righteousness and to avoid the path that leads to the Hellfire.
orig: لترون الجحيم

translation: Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, when people will witness the reality of the afterlife with their own eyes. The "eye of certainty" implies a direct and undeniable knowledge of the truth, rather than just believing or having faith. This verse emphasizes the certainty and clarity that will be experienced on that day, leaving no room for doubt or uncertainty about the existence of the Hereafter.
orig: ثم لترونها عين اليقين

translation: Then, on that Day, you will surely be asked about the pleasures (you indulged in).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, people will be held accountable for how they utilized the blessings and pleasures that were bestowed upon them in this life. It serves as a reminder to be mindful of how we spend our time and resources, and to ensure that we use them in a way that is pleasing to God and beneficial to ourselves and others.
orig: ثم لتسألن يومئذ عن النعيم

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. By time,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of time and how it should be utilized. The oath "By time" indicates that time is a precious commodity that should not be wasted. The interpretation is that one should strive to make the most of their time, engage in righteous deeds, and not squander the opportunities that life presents.
orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم والعصر

translation: Indeed, mankind is in loss
interpretation: This verse conveys the idea that human beings are in a state of loss and deprivation unless they believe in God, do righteous deeds, and encourage one another to truth and patience. It suggests that without faith and good works, a person's life is ultimately futile and devoid of true success.
orig: إن الإنسان لفي خسر

translation: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and enjoin upon one another truth and enjoin upon one another patience.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the only ones who will be saved from the punishment and granted eternal bliss are those who have true faith, do good deeds, and encourage each other to uphold the truth and practice patience. It highlights the importance of both belief and righteous action, as well as the mutual support and exhortation within the community of believers.
orig: إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وتواصوا بالحق وتواصوا بالصبر

translation: Woe to every scorner and mocker
interpretation: This verse is a warning against those who mock, slander, and ridicule others. It condemns those who take pleasure in belittling and humiliating people. The "every scorner and mocker" refers to those who engage in such behavior, and the "woe" indicates that they will face a severe punishment in the Hereafter for their actions.
orig: ويل لكل همزة لمزة

translation: He who hoards wealth and counts it
interpretation: This verse refers to a person who accumulates wealth and is obsessed with counting and keeping track of it. The Qur'an is cautioning against such behavior, as it can lead to greed, selfishness, and a lack of concern for others. The true purpose of wealth is to be used for the betterment of society and to help those in need, not to be hoarded and counted endlessly.
orig: الذي جمع مالا وعدده

translation: He thinks that his wealth has made him immortal.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a person who is deluded by his wealth and believes that it will protect him from death and make him immortal. The verse is highlighting the common human tendency to become arrogant and complacent when one becomes wealthy, forgetting that wealth and material possessions are ultimately transient and that death is inevitable. The interpretation suggests that true success and lasting fulfillment come not from worldly wealth, but from spiritual and moral development, as well as from serving others and seeking the pleasure of God.
orig: يحسب أن ماله أخلده

translation: No! Indeed, he will be thrown into the Crusher.
interpretation: This verse is a warning against arrogance and disbelief. The 'Crusher' (Al-Hutamah) refers to one of the levels of Hell, where those who deny the truth and indulge in arrogance will be punished. The verse emphasizes that there will be severe consequences for those who reject faith and engage in wrongdoing, and that they will be cast into the Crusher, a place of intense torment and destruction.
orig: كلا لينبذن في الحطمة

translation: And what can make you know what is the Crusher?
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Day of Judgment, specifically the punishment that awaits those who deny the truth and engage in sinful behaviors. The "Crusher" is a metaphorical term used to describe the intense and overwhelming nature of the punishment that will be inflicted upon the disbelievers on that day. The verse is intended to instill a sense of awe and reverence in the reader, and to emphasize the gravity of the consequences that await those who reject the message of Islam.
orig: وما أدراك ما الحطمة

translation: The fire of Allah, kindled,
interpretation: This verse refers to the eternal fire of Hell that Allah has kindled for those who reject His guidance and disobey His commands. The fire of Hell is described as being "kindled" by Allah, emphasizing its intensity and the divine origin of this punishment for the unbelievers. This serves as a stern warning to those who turn away from the path of righteousness and choose to live in defiance of Allah's will.
orig: نار الله الموقدة

translation: That which comes up to the hearts
interpretation: This verse is referring to the concept of the heart and its connection to the spiritual realm. The heart is seen as the center of human emotions, desires, and spiritual awareness in Islamic teachings. The phrase "that which comes up to the hearts" suggests that there is something that has the ability to penetrate and influence the innermost thoughts and feelings of a person. This could be interpreted as a reference to the divine guidance, revelation, or spiritual experiences that can touch and transform the human heart.
orig: التي تطلع على الأفئدة

translation: Indeed, it will be closed upon them.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject faith and turn away from the guidance of Allah will be trapped and confined, with no way out. The imagery of a door being closed upon them conveys a sense of finality and the consequences of their choices. The interpretation is that those who refuse to believe and follow the path of righteousness will be sealed off from the mercy and blessings of Allah, facing the consequences of their own actions.
orig: إنها عليهم مؤصدة

translation: In extended columns
interpretation: This verse is describing the creation of the heavens and the earth, emphasizing that they were created in an organized and structured manner, like extended columns. This suggests the perfection and intentionality behind the divine creation, which is a common theme in the Qur'an. The interpretation is that the universe was created by God in a deliberate and purposeful way, not haphazardly.
orig: في عمد ممددة

translation: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?
interpretation: This verse refers to the event known as the 'Year of the Elephant', when an Abyssinian army, led by the Abyssinian king Abraha, attempted to attack the Kaaba in Mecca with a large army that included elephants. However, the army was miraculously destroyed by flocks of birds that pelted them with stones, protecting the sanctity of the Kaaba. This event is seen as a demonstration of God's power and protection over the holy site of Mecca.
orig: ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بأصحاب الفيل

translation: Has He not made their plot go astray?
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has foiled the schemes and plots of those who seek to mislead and deceive others. It implies that Allah's power and wisdom are superior to the machinations of those who wish to lead people astray, and that He is ultimately in control and can thwart their efforts.
orig: ألم يجعل كيدهم في تضليل

translation: And He sent against them birds in flocks
interpretation: This verse refers to an event in Islamic history where a flock of birds was sent by God to defend the city of Mecca from an invading army. The birds carried small stones that they dropped on the enemy, causing them to be destroyed. This event is seen as a miraculous intervention by God to protect the holy city and its inhabitants.
orig: وأرسل عليهم طيرا أبابيل

translation: He throws stones at them from clay (that has been baked into hard stones)
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment that will be inflicted upon the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. The imagery of throwing stones at them suggests a severe and relentless form of punishment, where the stones are made from a hard and durable material like clay that has been baked into a solid form. This conveys the idea that the punishment will be harsh, inescapable, and designed to inflict maximum pain and suffering upon the disbelievers for their rejection of faith and their misdeeds in this world.
orig: ترميهم بحجارة من سجيل

translation: And He made them like consumed straw.
interpretation: This verse is a metaphor that describes the fate of those who reject faith and oppose the truth. The image of "consumed straw" suggests that they will be destroyed and reduced to nothing, like straw that has been burned and consumed. The interpretation is that those who deny God's signs and messages will ultimately face a severe and irreversible consequence for their actions.
orig: فجعلهم كعصف مأكول

translation: For the accustomed security of the Quraysh
interpretation: This verse refers to the custom of the Quraysh tribe of Mecca, who enjoyed a privileged position and security due to their control of the Kaaba and the annual trading caravans. The verse suggests that this security and prosperity was a source of pride and comfort for the Quraysh, which they should not take for granted and should instead be grateful to Allah for.
orig: لإيلاف قريش

translation: For the accustoming of the Quraysh, [specifically] the accustoming of them for the caravan journeys of winter and summer.
interpretation: This verse refers to the custom of the Quraysh tribe, who would undertake trade journeys during the winter and summer seasons. The verse highlights how the Quraysh were able to travel and conduct their commerce safely and without fear, due to the protection and alliances they had established. This stability and prosperity allowed the Quraysh to focus on their trading activities and maintain their economic and social standing.
orig: إيلافهم رحلة الشتاء والصيف

translation: So let them worship the Lord of this House
interpretation: This verse is calling upon the people to worship and serve the Lord who is the Creator and Sustainer of the Kaaba, the sacred house of worship in Mecca. The verse emphasizes the importance of worshipping the one true God, as the Kaaba is a symbol of monotheism and the unity of God. The interpretation suggests that the people should dedicate themselves to the worship and obedience of the Lord, who is the sole object of worship and the source of all blessings.
orig: فليعبدوا رب هذا البيت

translation: He who has fed them against hunger and has made them safe from fear.
interpretation: This verse refers to God as the one who provides sustenance and protection for His creation. It emphasizes that God is the ultimate source of nourishment and security, and that He alone can alleviate the hunger and fear that people may face. The verse encourages believers to trust in God's providence and to seek refuge in Him, as He is the one who can truly satisfy their needs and grant them peace of mind.
orig: الذي أطعمهم من جوع وآمنهم من خوف

translation: Have you seen the one who denies the Judgment?
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who reject the concept of the Day of Judgment and the accountability of one's actions. It is a rhetorical question that challenges the reader to reflect on the mindset of those who deny the existence of a divine reckoning. The interpretation suggests that such denial of the Deen (religion) or the Judgment is a grave error that deserves contemplation and guidance.
orig: أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين

translation: And that is the one who drives away the orphan
interpretation: This verse refers to a person who mistreats or neglects the orphan. The interpretation is that such a person who does not care for the orphan and instead drives them away is condemned, as the Qur'an places great emphasis on the care and protection of orphans.
orig: فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم

translation: And they do not encourage the feeding of the poor.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of caring for and providing for the less fortunate members of society. It condemns those who do not encourage or promote the feeding and nourishment of the poor and needy. The interpretation suggests that believers have a moral obligation to support and assist those who are struggling, rather than ignoring or neglecting them.
orig: ولا يحض على طعام المسكين

translation: So woe to the worshippers
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who perform their prayers in a perfunctory manner, without sincerity and devotion. It suggests that those who pray merely out of habit or for show, without truly connecting with Allah, will face a painful punishment in the Hereafter. The interpretation emphasizes the importance of performing one's prayers with a sincere heart and a deep reverence for the divine.
orig: فويل للمصلين

translation: Those who are neglectful of their prayers
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are careless, indifferent or negligent in performing their obligatory prayers. It highlights the importance of being attentive and dedicated in one's religious duties, as prayer is a fundamental pillar of the Islamic faith. The interpretation suggests that those who are heedless or lax in their prayer life are displeasing to God and may be at risk of spiritual decline.
orig: الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون

translation: Those who are hypocrites
interpretation: This verse refers to those who outwardly display acts of piety and righteousness, but their true intentions are to be seen and praised by others rather than to please Allah. They seek worldly recognition and status rather than the pleasure of Allah. This hypocritical behavior is condemned in the Qur'an as it demonstrates a lack of sincerity and true faith.
orig: الذين هم يراءون

translation: And they withhold [simple] assistance.
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who are miserly and unwilling to help others in need. The term "al-ma'un" in the verse refers to small acts of kindness and assistance, such as lending a tool, sharing food, or offering help to those who are in need. The verse condemns those who are stingy and unwilling to perform these small but important acts of charity and compassion towards their fellow human beings.
orig: ويمنعون الماعون

translation: Indeed, We have granted you, [O Muhammad], al-Kawthar.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the blessing of al-Kawthar, which is interpreted as a river in Paradise. The verse is a promise from Allah that He has bestowed upon the Prophet a great abundance of good, both in this life and the Hereafter. This can be understood as a spiritual blessing, as well as the large number of followers and descendants the Prophet was granted.
orig: إنا أعطيناك الكوثر

translation: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice [to Him alone].
interpretation: This verse is calling upon the believer to devote themselves fully to Allah (God) in worship and submission. The first part "So pray to your Lord" emphasizes the importance of establishing a direct connection with Allah through regular prayer and supplication. The second part "and sacrifice [to Him alone]" instructs the believer to make sacrifices, whether material or spiritual, solely for the sake of Allah and not for any other entity. This verse encourages the believer to purify their intentions and actions, focusing solely on pleasing Allah.
orig: فصل لربك وانحر

translation: Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off [from good].
interpretation: This verse is referring to those who harbor enmity and hatred towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his message. It is a warning that such people will be the ones who are deprived of any good and ultimately, they will be the ones who are "cut off" from any blessings or success in this life and the Hereafter. The interpretation suggests that the true loss is for those who reject the truth and oppose the Prophet, as they will be the ones left without any legacy or lasting impact.
orig: إن شانئك هو الأبتر

translation: Say, 'O disbelievers,
interpretation: This verse is a call for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to address the disbelievers and reaffirm his faith in the oneness of God. It marks a clear distinction between the believers and the disbelievers, emphasizing that there can be no compromise when it comes to the fundamental belief in God's unity. The verse serves as a declaration of the Prophet's unwavering commitment to his faith and a rejection of the polytheistic beliefs of the disbelievers.
orig: قل يا أيها الكافرون

translation: I do not worship that which you worship.
interpretation: This verse expresses the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) rejection of the polytheistic beliefs and practices of his people. It signifies his firm commitment to worshiping only Allah, the One true God, and his refusal to participate in the worship of false deities or idols. This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle of monotheism and the rejection of any form of idolatry or polytheism.
orig: لا أعبد ما تعبدون

translation: And you are not worshippers of what I worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental differences between the beliefs and practices of the Prophet Muhammad and those of his opponents. It suggests that the Prophet and his followers worship God alone, while the opponents worship multiple deities or idols. The verse highlights the irreconcilable nature of these two worldviews and the need for the Prophet's followers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the practices of the unbelievers.
orig: ولا أنتم عابدون ما أعبد

translation: And I am not a worshipper of that which you worship
interpretation: This verse expresses the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) rejection of the polytheistic beliefs and practices of the Quraysh in Mecca. He declares that he does not worship the idols and gods that they worship, as he is a monotheist who believes in the One true God, Allah. This verse emphasizes the fundamental difference between the Prophet's belief in the oneness of God and the polytheistic beliefs of the people he was sent to guide.
orig: ولا أنا عابد ما عبدتم

translation: And you are not worshippers of what I worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental differences between the beliefs and practices of the Prophet Muhammad and those of his opponents. It suggests that the Prophet and his followers worship God alone, while the opponents worship multiple deities or idols. The verse highlights the exclusivity of the Islamic faith and the need for a clear distinction between the true believers and those who reject the message of Islam.
orig: ولا أنتم عابدون ما أعبد

translation: For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of religious freedom and tolerance. It suggests that each person is free to follow their own faith and beliefs, without interference or coercion from others. The verse highlights the importance of respecting and accepting different religious practices and convictions, as long as they do not harm or infringe upon the rights of others.
orig: لكم دينكم ولي دين

translation: When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest
interpretation: This verse refers to the time when Allah grants victory and conquest to the believers. It signifies that when the help and support of Allah comes and the believers achieve a decisive victory over their enemies it is a sign that the promise of Allah has been fulfilled. This verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast in their faith as Allah's help and victory are assured for those who follow His path.
orig: إذا جاء نصر الله والفتح

translation: And you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes
interpretation: This verse suggests that the religion of Islam will spread rapidly and that many people will convert to it. It reflects the idea that the message of Islam will resonate with people and they will embrace it in large numbers. The interpretation is that the growth and expansion of Islam will be swift and widespread as people recognize its truth and accept it.
orig: ورأيت الناس يدخلون في دين الله أفواجا

translation: So exalt [Him] with praise of your Lord and ask forgiveness of Him. Indeed He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to glorify and praise God, and to seek His forgiveness. The phrase \"exalt [Him] with praise of your Lord\" suggests that we should express our gratitude and reverence for God through acts of worship and remembrance. The phrase \"ask forgiveness of Him\" indicates that we should humbly acknowledge our shortcomings and seek God\'s mercy and pardon. The verse also emphasizes that God is \"a Perpetual Forgiver,\" meaning that He is always ready to forgive those who turn to Him in sincere repentance.
orig: فسبح بحمد ربك واستغفره إنه كان توابا

translation: May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he.
interpretation: This verse is a curse directed towards Abu Lahab, an uncle of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) who was a staunch opponent of Islam. The verse expresses that Abu Lahab's hands and his entire being will be destroyed due to his rejection of the message of Islam and his persecution of the Prophet and his followers. This verse serves as a warning to those who choose to reject the truth and oppose the divine teachings.
orig: تبت يدا أبي لهب وتب

translation: What will his wealth and his gains avail him?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the futility of worldly wealth and gains in the face of the Hereafter. It suggests that on the Day of Judgment, a person's material possessions and acquisitions will not be of any use or benefit to them. The underlying message is that one should focus on spiritual and moral development, rather than being preoccupied with the pursuit of wealth and material gain, as these worldly things will not help a person in the Afterlife.
orig: ما أغنى عنه ماله وما كسب

translation: He will [enter to] burn in a Fire of [blazing] Flame
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment in the Hereafter for those who reject faith and commit sins. The "Fire of [blazing] Flame" is a metaphor for the intense and eternal torment that awaits the disbelievers in the Afterlife. The phrase "He will [enter to]" suggests that this punishment is inevitable for those who turn away from the guidance of Allah and choose to live a life of disbelief and wrongdoing.
orig: سيصلى نارا ذات لهب

translation: And his wife, the carrier of firewood
interpretation: This verse refers to the wife of one of the disbelievers mentioned in the Qur'an. It portrays her as a carrier of firewood, which was likely a difficult and laborious task. This description suggests that she was of a low social status and had to perform menial tasks, highlighting the hardships faced by some women in that society. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of treating all people, regardless of their social standing, with dignity and respect.
orig: وامرأته حمالة الحطب

translation: In her neck is a rope of [twisted] fiber
interpretation: This verse is often interpreted as a metaphor for the fate of those who reject faith and engage in evil deeds. The "rope of [twisted] fiber" symbolizes the consequences and punishment that await them, as they have chosen to entangle themselves in a web of their own making. The imagery suggests that their actions will lead to their own undoing, much like a noose around their necks. This verse serves as a warning to those who stray from the righteous path and a call to repentance and reform.
orig: في جيدها حبل من مسد

translation: Say, "He is Allah, [who is] One,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah. It affirms that Allah is the sole, supreme, and indivisible deity, without any partners or equals. The interpretation is that Muslims should declare and believe in the absolute monotheism of Allah, rejecting any notion of polytheism or associating partners with Him.
orig: قل هو الله أحد

translation: Allah, the Self-Sufficient
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the attribute of Allah as the Self-Sufficient, the One who is independent and in need of nothing. He is the Eternal, the Absolute, the One who has no need for a partner, offspring, or anything else. This highlights Allah's perfection and the fact that He alone is worthy of worship and devotion, as He is the source of all existence and the sustainer of all creation.
orig: الله الصمد

translation: He neither begets nor is He begotten
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah. It states that Allah is not born, nor does He give birth to anyone. This underscores the idea that Allah is the eternal, self-sufficient, and uncreated Creator who is free from any need or association with other beings. The verse rejects the concept of God having offspring or being part of a divine family, which was common in many ancient religions. Instead, it affirms Allah's absolute sovereignty, power, and independence.
orig: لم يلد ولم يولد

translation: And there is none comparable to Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute uniqueness and incomparability of Allah (God). It affirms that there is no one or nothing that can be equal to or comparable to the Divine Being. This reinforces the concept of the absolute Oneness and Uniqueness of Allah, which is a fundamental tenet of Islamic belief. The verse underscores that Allah is the One and Only, without any partners, equals or similitudes, and that He is Transcendent, Incomparable and Unparalleled in His Essence, Attributes and Actions.
orig: ولم يكن له كفوا أحد

translation: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak,"
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to seek protection and refuge in the Lord of the daybreak, who is Allah. The term "daybreak" (al-Falaq) refers to the beginning of the day, when the first light appears, and it symbolizes the emergence of good and the dispelling of darkness and evil. By seeking refuge in the Lord of the daybreak, the believer is asking Allah for protection from all forms of harm, whether physical, mental, or spiritual, and for guidance towards what is good and righteous.
orig: قل أعوذ برب الفلق

translation: From the evil of that which He created
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to seek refuge in Allah from the evil or harm that may come from His creation. It implies that even though Allah has created everything, including things that may be harmful or evil, the believer should turn to Allah for protection and seek His refuge. The interpretation suggests that the ultimate source of all evil and harm is not the creation itself, but rather the misuse or abuse of that creation by human beings. The verse encourages the believer to rely on Allah's protection and guidance to navigate the complexities of the created world.
orig: من شر ما خلق

translation: And from the evil of the darkening (night) as it approaches
interpretation: This verse refers to seeking refuge from the evil that may occur during the night. The "darkening (night) as it approaches" is a metaphor for the onset of darkness and the potential dangers that may arise during this time. The interpretation suggests that one should seek protection from Allah against any harm or evil that may manifest itself during the night.
orig: ومن شر غاسق إذا وقب

translation: And from the evil of the blowers in knots
interpretation: This verse refers to the practice of sorcery or witchcraft, where individuals would blow into knots to cast spells or curses. The interpretation is that one should seek refuge from the evil or harm that can be caused by such practices.
orig: ومن شر النفاثات في العقد

translation: And from the evil of an envier when he envies
interpretation: This verse is a seeking of refuge from the harm and mischief of an envious person. Envy is a dangerous trait that can lead to resentment, malice, and even attempts to harm others who are perceived as more successful or fortunate. The Qur'an warns against this destructive emotion and encourages believers to focus on their own spiritual growth and development rather than comparing themselves to others or wishing for what they do not have.
orig: ومن شر حاسد إذا حسد

translation: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind,"
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to seek refuge in the Lord of all people. It emphasizes that the true source of protection and safety is Allah, the Lord and Sustainer of all humanity. This verse encourages believers to rely on Allah alone for protection from all harm, whether physical, emotional, or spiritual.
orig: قل أعوذ برب الناس

translation: The Sovereign of Mankind
interpretation: This verse refers to God as the Sovereign or Ruler of all people. It emphasizes that God alone has dominion over all of humanity, and that all people are ultimately accountable to Him. This highlights the idea that God is the supreme authority and that we must submit to His will and judgment. The interpretation suggests that we should seek God's pleasure and guidance, and not be swayed by the temporary powers or authorities of this world.
orig: ملك الناس

translation: The God of mankind
interpretation: This verse refers to Allah, the one and only true God who is the Creator and Sustainer of all humanity. It emphasizes that Allah is the sole object of worship and devotion, and that all people should turn to Him alone for guidance, protection, and salvation. The verse highlights the universality of Allah's divinity, as He is the God of all people, regardless of their race, nationality, or beliefs.
orig: إله الناس

translation: From the evil of the retreating whisperer
interpretation: This verse refers to seeking refuge in God from the evil of the "retreating whisperer", which is interpreted as the devil or any source of persistent negative thoughts and temptations that try to lead one astray. The "retreating whisperer" is believed to whisper evil suggestions to people, then retreat and hide, only to return again. This verse encourages believers to seek God's protection from such persistent and deceptive influences that can undermine one's faith and wellbeing.
orig: من شر الوسواس الخناس

translation: The one who whispers [evil] into the breasts of mankind
interpretation: This verse refers to the devil or Satan, who whispers temptations and doubts into the hearts and minds of people, trying to lead them astray from the path of righteousness. The interpretation suggests that we must be vigilant against the subtle and insidious influence of the devil, who seeks to undermine our faith and moral resolve through his whisperings.
orig: الذي يوسوس في صدور الناس

translation: From the jinn and mankind
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of two types of sentient beings - the jinn (supernatural creatures) and humans. The Qur'an emphasizes that both jinn and humans have been created by God and are accountable to Him. This verse suggests that the message of the Qur'an is intended for both groups, highlighting the universal nature of the divine guidance.
orig: من الجنة والناس
